“Beastification has broken out! They are like zombies. All this time, what has the Lighthouse Kingdom been doing? Why didn’t they issue warnings and set up defenses beforehand…”
“Damn it, we’ve been betrayed!”
“Sever the conduit of benefits between the Lighthouse and enemies from the Other World.”
Hiss…
All of it is worrisome.
“There certainly is worry in that regard, but it’s not important; catching him now, while he’s on guard, won’t be an easy task. Moreover, in the short to medium term, there is no need for excessive concern. As for the reason, it involves some core company secrets that I can’t disclose to you for the time being.”
“Alright, if you guys think it’s not an issue, then it’s not an issue.”
Upon hearing this, Colin let it go; after all, if the sky were to fall, there would be taller people to hold it up; his concern as a lowly employee wouldn’t be of much use.
“Is there anything else you need to ask?”
Colin’s mind spun, and he asked about the “Interaction Hall”—the robots there might be clumsy, but sometimes they strangely unnerved him.
Upon hearing this question, Lady Bunny, who was perusing documents, responded without lifting her head, “This is information that only those with Level C Clearance or above have the privilege of accessing.”
“Level C and above?”
Colin wasn’t surprised, but what level was this Lady Bunny in front of him?
The tone of her voice felt as if it exceeded D Level…
“Yes, on that matter, all I can tell you is that you don’t have to worry about them as long as you don’t expose your immediate coordinates. They only become dangerous if you verbalize your immediate coordinates.”
“Furthermore, if you’re confident, you can use a method to expose your location indirectly to lure out and kill other ill-intentioned fish; this won’t attract their attention. However, I suggest that you have at least D Level clearance and the ability to use the Book of Fate as a reference without wholly relying on it; be fully prepared, especially for escaping.”
Immediate coordinates refer to those “robots,” and indirect exposure means luring some ill-intentioned fellows? Colin nodded thoughtfully.
He didn’t press further, but seeing that he had no more queries, Lady Bunny took out a thick stack of files from a drawer: “These are some people’s profiles; you can pick three from here to be on your team for your next entry into code number 13.”
To choose teammates?
Colin eagerly took the files, which contained a hundred or so people, who unlike him, seemed to truly possess capabilities.
Some were real war-seasoned elite soldiers, balding young academic experts, business-savvy geniuses… and the list went on.
These resumes almost made me feel inferior, Colin wondered if his selection was due to his parents, whom he’d never met, perhaps being high-ranking officials in the company like in the novels?
Or did he have some legendary supreme lineage?
Could it really just be because he was handsome?
Oh, maybe he was simply chosen to be expendable, the one to roll the dice for luck, whoever rolled luck would go.
It was somewhat akin to Russian roulette; he didn’t know how many had died before him.
Shaking his head to dismiss the thoughts, Colin continued to read on.
Lady Bunny didn’t disturb him; instead, she took out another document and began to write in silence—she seemed to have endless paperwork, not stopping once since Colin had arrived.
After an uncertain amount of time and having read through all the resumes, Colin discovered that these people, each formidable in their own right, had one thing in common: they all suffered from terminal illnesses, disabilities, psychological disorders, blood diseases, genetic defects, cancers, some even had the legendary pancreatic cancer…
Bonfire Company really liked to hire those not long for this world.
Colin sighed and then selected three individuals: a woman with achievements in surgery but was in the middle stage of pancreatic cancer, a retired person with a special background but missing limbs, and an average civil engineer with a good mentality.
They weren’t the best among the profiles, but their mentality and adaptability were the best.
As for their physical conditions, Colin wasn’t worried, for Bonfire Company would likely arrange for them to undergo “Soul Transference.”

chapters.title: Chapter 31 - 31 31 Probably Really Dead._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 31: Chapter 31: Probably Really Dead._1 Chapter 31: Chapter 31: Probably Really Dead._1 “I will notify them, but I can’t guarantee I’ll bring everyone, sometimes people refuse the company’s invitation, preferring to die rather than accept.”
You guys never explain things clearly, so it’s normal for them not to accept…
Colin looked through the list of over a hundred names again, and selected five alternative plans.
“Alright, the details of the next event will be conveyed to you in the form of a task.”
Lady Bunny said, “Additionally, as the executor of the mission for ‘World Code 13’, I will grant you office privileges. By Sunday, you can make first contact with them through the office, and the specific usage details will be provided to you upon activation.”
There are perks like that? Colin was startled for a moment, then nodded to show he understood.
“Alright, one last thing…”
Lady Bunny said without blinking an eye, “Today, the company was invaded by The Descender, and some countermeasures will be issued, probably in the form of tasks. Don’t worry about these tasks too much, they’re not something you can complete.
“Secondly, the company isn’t sure what will happen next internally, so you might need to be more alert, reduce your use of the ‘Interaction Hall’, you can read messages, but don’t send more than thirty a day.”
The company was invaded? Colin didn’t understand why he needed to limit sending messages, but still nodded to show he understood.
After a brief exchange, he returned to reality.
In the blink of an eye, he was back in his familiar little room.
He glanced at the wall clock.
April 1st, Wednesday, three o’clock in the afternoon.
“Ah, I forgot to ask Lady Bunny about the time issue. Why does it feel like the timing isn’t quite right, this time it was obviously longer than last time, why does it feel like it’s always the same duration, always three hours?”
But according to the current guess, every Monday from twelve noon to three o’clock, then without mishaps, it should be equivalent to one day of activity in the Other World.
It probably wouldn’t be more than that.
“It’s quite relaxing, working four days a month, earning over a million. But speaking of which, it seems I forgot to ask Lady Bunny about the authority level.”
Colin muttered to himself, suspecting that she might be one of those elusive C level or above employees spoken of in legends within the ‘Interaction Hall’.
He didn’t pay too much attention to these minor details, though.
Picking up the parchment from the nightstand next to his bed.
The summary of his mission had already appeared on it.
[“The ‘Call from Afar’ event has been completed.”]
[“In this event, your rating was: B+.”]
[“Below is the settlement for this event’s tasks—’Bonfire Points*1000′, ‘Bonfire Points*1600’, ‘Silver Clearance Certificate*1’.”]
[“All items have been transferred to the ‘Storage Room’, please collect them.”]
…
“Not as many rewards this time, but the points are quite a lot. Is this thousand the additional minimum points reward Miss Bunny mentioned?”
Colin was somewhat surprised, having thought that the guaranteed minimum would only start from next week, but it was counted now.
Including the fifteen points he had left previously, he now had a total of 2623 points.
As for the rating, he felt it was already quite high.
After all, even if he came up with more reasons to defend himself, two people had died this time, and six were half-dead, not yet out of danger.
Taking a deep breath, Colin didn’t rush to buy equipment, but instead got out of bed, sat in his wheelchair, and let the sunlight from the window shine on his skin. He closed his eyes, intending to do a simple recap.
To review the flaws and omissions in this action.
But as soon as he closed his eyes, Colin’s expression became increasingly pale, his throat churned, and nausea surged in his stomach.
The blood-red menus from the kitchen flashed through his mind, and Colin’s face turned ugly, eventually unable to help but retch a few times.
“Aside from some things about the ‘Book of Fate’, there wasn’t much worth reviewing.”
Colin placed a hand on his stomach and rubbed it, repeatedly swallowing saliva.
During Beast Transformation Syndrome, he had no reaction to the scenes in the kitchen, even thought of taking a taste, but now, back in human form, all he felt was nausea and the urge to vomit.
He could handle death, but that scene was a bit too much for the normal him.
After taking several deep breaths, Colin took out the parchment and looked at his colleagues’ ridiculous messages, only to notice they were discussing some mission.
“Unyielding Guardians,” the blood-red font was unsettling to look at.
“Ss, a million points, super rare item, a straight pass to B level… big spender.”
Colin couldn’t help but be tempted himself.
Unfortunately, Lady Bunny had informed him in advance that the task was a no-go, and he didn’t even know who “The Descender” was; otherwise, even just providing a little clue would have guaranteed him an entry of ten thousand points, which would have been simply delightful.
Shaking his head and sighing, he started looking for equipment worth buying.
Now that he had money in his hands, his inflated desire to spend was almost uncontrollable.
But, after not looking for long, he unexpectedly found a post related to himself—
The Ephemeral “Golden Legend”.
“Lifecoach Kawaii-many”: Brother Shunzi has been silent for three days, has anyone seen his messages?
“East Wind in the small building last night”: He’s probably dead.
“Sea God007”: It’s a pity that a golden artifact had just appeared and then disappeared. Let’s mourn the vanished golden legend, wishing that in its next life, it will have a more sedate master, like me for example.
“Fish Pond Master”: He hasn’t shown up for so long, my golden legend! Just like that, gone! I can’t accept it!
“Two-Faced”: Fake, all fake. There was never any golden equipment; it’s all you guys conspiring to lie to me, right?!
“Arsonist Tao Tie”: It doesn’t matter if he’s dead, but what about the hundred points he owes me! It upsets me, feel like I’ve been freeloaded…
…
You guys really don’t wish me any good at all.
He had been busy with preparations for his missions in the past few days, so he hadn’t interacted much. To his surprise, they were all holding funerals for him, no, for his equipment.
His gaze lingered on the ID of “Arsonist Tao Tie”.
“The rest of you forget it, what fuss are you joining, you’re afraid I won’t go online, right?”
Colin muttered to himself; he had been interacting privately with this Jailbreak Series brother these past few days, who knew whether he was dead or alive better than anyone else.
However, he hadn’t seen this guy around and nearly forgot about the hundred points he owed.
He didn’t intend to renege on the debt; Colin directly interacted with him through private chat.
“You finished the task and returned so quickly?” The Jailbreak Series brother expressed surprise, but not too much surprise, mainly because he knew Colin had a lot of equipment.
Just after joining, he had as much equipment as those who had been fishing around for a year.
The quality was completely overwhelming.
A single Golden Legend would allow him to strut through the regular F Level tasks; he was almost guaranteed to be safe.
What a pity, the other party had taken up a “Descender project”.
The more money, the quicker the death.
“How should I pay you the hundred points?” Colin went straight to the point.
“Wait a sec, I’ll probably just list some unremarkable special material for you to buy, that’s all.”
“Don’t use ordinary items?”
“Nope, ordinary items can’t pass the review to be listed in the auction house. Only special materials obtained from task events work, otherwise what you’d see most in the auction house would be weapons, not those junk items. Oh right, make sure you confirm the name when you make the purchase.”
“Got it.”
It wasn’t long before he received the name from the Jailbreak Series brother; Colin searched for it in the auction house.
[“A Slightly Hard Stone”, price: 100 points.]
[Quantity: 1.]
[Note: The item cannot be taken out in the real environment without application.]
[Description: A stone picked up during a museum event, the core component of a figurine. Seemed useful at the time, so I grabbed it, but later on, it seemed to have no use.]
[Seller: “Arsonist Tao Tie”.]
…
Colin quickly confirmed the name and directly made the purchase, with the item going straight into his storage bag. He planned to casually use it as a hidden weapon to throw at someone next time he entered a “dungeon”.
It was worth a hundred points after all.
After that, Colin took another look at the threads posted by those people, adhering to the joy of sharing good things with others.
He casually edited a title—
[What? How did you guys know I got another orange-colored equipment? Just got the “Revolver Contrarian”, seems alright.]
As soon as the post was made, many online colleagues came sniffing around, attracted by the scent.

chapters.title: Chapter 32 - 32 32 A Good Person Will Be Rewarded_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 32: Chapter 32 A Good Person Will Be Rewarded_1 Chapter 32: Chapter 32 A Good Person Will Be Rewarded_1 “….Can we chat offline?”
“It’s killing me, don’t send any more, seeing you get equipment is even more painful than actually killing me, damn it, ahhhh!!!”
“Two items, my god! One gold and one orange, what kind of dogshit luck is this! Why can’t I have such luck!”
“Front row, I’m soaking up the luck.”
“Who said Brother Shunzi is dead? Come out and apologize! @XiaoLou ZuoYe You DongFeng.”
“Boss Shunzi, three hundred million US dollars, three hundred million for your two items. We can negotiate if you’re not willing, I’ll even buy the orange one for a hundred million. You’re dead, no big deal, but you wouldn’t want your family…”
“@Unnamed123456, Brother Shunzi is begging for help, please come to the ‘Non-Existent Hospital’ on floor eighteen and save me, six thousand points, I beg you, boss, to save this dog’s life…”
“Brother Shunzi, take me with you to the Other World, I can be your assistant.”
…
Colin smiled as he read these messages. Although the revolver didn’t seem to play any special role in this incident, he believed that there must be a good reason for it to be rated as rare and second only to gold in quality.
Besides further repairs, he also hadn’t activated its special properties yet.
He probably had to wait until it was fully repaired and all abilities were activated to see the full power of this item.
Then, his attention was briefly drawn to that “Non-Existent Hospital”, but he just glanced at it.
He had seen this guy several times, either calling for help or on his way to do so.
But the problem was.
This guy was an Employee Level E, in terms of physical strength he was a whole realm above him, even if he wanted to help, he was incapable.
As for why this guy was stuck in that place.
Colin had seen others mention that he was forced to use three fragments of the Book of Fate in one day during a dangerous mission.
Although he broke through the crisis, he rolled misfortune at that time and then “accidentally” accepted a D Level Mission, entering the event “Non-Existent Hospital”.
He then managed to barely survive, surviving for half a year, during which time it wasn’t that no D Level Personnel tried to rescue him in that event.
But as soon as they heard this guy had gone as deep as the eighteenth floor, they all gave up.
“Respect others’ fate, let go of the compulsion to help, avoid being moved by oneself.”
Colin reluctantly took his eyes off the six thousand points.
After a while, he opened the post he had made a few days ago to scam equipment, preparing to gather some new items for his next mission.
Soon, he made some discoveries.
[Name: Gluttony Power Mark]
[Quality: Defective.]
[Status: Stable (Integrity 48%).]
[Energy Level: F Level (Suitable for Employees F-E Level).]
[Effect “Gluttony Power”: When holding the mark, nutrients can be absorbed from consumed food to rapidly recover physical strength and injuries, and this power can be transferred to others through contact.]
[Effect “Special Taste”: When holding the mark, taste buds will grow in the small intestine, allowing the taste of digested food remnants to be discerned, and to know which foods have more nutrients or waste.]
[Negative Effect “Excessive Hunger”: Prone to eating oneself to death.]
[Price: 1400 points.]
[Note: “Our evaluation department discovered the ‘Special Taste’ ability could be used in the mouth, but you chose to use it in the small intestine.”]
[“Was it intentional or an accident?”]
[“I did it on purpose. (Proud.jpg)”]
[“The mouth only serves to initially digest and break down food and is not optimal for nutrient analysis. Therefore, to better utilize this ability, I moved it from the mouth to the small intestine!”]
[“Anger.jpg”]
…
“What sort of freaks and monsters are working at Bonfire Company to make equipment?”
Colin was silently overwhelmed by the effect of the item.
But, to be fair,
“On the trading floor, items with healing effects seem to always be priced a bit higher than other types. The commotion caused by that person’s equipment last time was also due to this reason; this one here is already the cheapest available.”
Colin briefly looked it over – 1400 points, enough to buy an energy level E item.
But for healing types, you could only get a poor quality energy level F.
Right, with such a low grade, there’s likely some personal grudge involved.
Putting aside some abilities that cause physiological discomfort, this item, despite its lower energy level, could almost be considered an excellent item without any negative effects, just based on the description.
However.
“Special taste” was somewhat off-putting.
Colin didn’t want to know what it felt like for the small intestine to have a sense of taste, nor did he want to have such an experience.
But after watching for a while, he decided to buy it anyway.
After all, he had subordinates.
If he couldn’t use it himself, it was still perfect for his subordinates, and this thing could even transfer its effects to teammates—in a sense, almost without side effects.
To earn those few thousand points from saving people, this item was essential.
When the item arrived at the “Storage Room,” Colin observed it through the “Storage Room.” It seemed to be a sticker-like mark.
The mark was shaped like a mouth.
“This item is fated for my teammate.”
Colin muttered to himself, then glanced at his remaining 1115 points and couldn’t help feeling that spending it was almost irresistible.
A simple change of equipment and more than half was gone.
Latter, he browsed the auction for a while and found a “Book of Fate: Fragment,” without hesitation, he snapped it up right away.
Although Lady Bunny told him that three were always provided at a time, such an item wouldn’t expire, and when the opportunity arose, it was still best to gather more.
Most importantly, Colin wanted to confirm the differences between what he could buy here and what Lady Bunny offered.
After storing the item, Colin browsed some more, and when he didn’t find any more suitable items, he activated both features “Quick Draw Slash (American Style)” and “Adaptive Aiming” of the “Revolver Contrarian.”
[“Quick Draw Slash (American Style)”: In 0.2 seconds, complete the series of actions from drawing the gun to firing. The gun must be reholstered after each use.]
[Exclusive Feature “Adaptive Aiming”: With this, even a three-year-old can easily blow off the head of a quite well-off enemy from over eighty meters away with one shot.]
“Great, there go another six hundred dollars.”
With 323 points left, Colin stocked up on 33 bullets, paying 99 points.
And with 224 left….
He planned to save the remaining money to wait for a chance at the “Book of Fate: Fragment.”
Next was preparing material resources for reality.
This wasn’t a big issue; he still had quite a bit of cash on hand.
A few days ago, the kindhearted Colin didn’t forget the hardworking masses and specifically went to a charitable event in a wheelchair, donating a certain amount of money. Although it wasn’t much, it was still a sincere gesture. Afterwards, he participated in a scratch-off game organized by the store, and by accident, he won a grand prize of two hundred thousand dollars. This shows that good deeds do indeed bring good fortune.
This had nothing to do with “Dice of Probability’s” luck; it was solely because of his kindness.
After deducting forty thousand for taxes and spending several tens of thousands more on equipment for buying various refined blended oils, he still had a few tens of thousands of dollars in hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 33 - 33 33 When the Night Comes..._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 33: Chapter 33 When the Night Comes…_1 Chapter 33: Chapter 33 When the Night Comes…_1 Three days passed, and it was Sunday at twelve noon.
Colin received a message on the parchment right on time.
[The “Office” permission has been activated, which can be used in reality when not on a mission, allowing you to bring subordinates who have signed contracts with you into the office.]
[Currently, you have signed with 3 people, and you can let them enter the office at any time.]
“Li Ming, Lin Yilan, Tang Ken, all three of those guys agreed?”
Colin thought for a moment and did not rush to call them in, instead deciding to familiarize himself with this function first.
The moment he activated the function, his mind went blank. When he came to his senses, he was already in an office that was almost identical to Miss Bunny’s.
However, this time, he was sitting at the rear of the office, and the desk did not have those mountainous piles of various company files.
With a single thought, the desk drawer slid out and then snapped shut on its own.
It seemed that he could control everything here at will.
Colin ran his finger over the armrest of his chair, looking around with a sense that the entire office was under his control.
“It’s a pity though, this office is quite large, but the decoration is lacking; too plain. Meeting with the three employees later would seem a bit shabby, not ideal for impressing them.”
Colin shook his head and sighed in disappointment.
If it could become grand and magnificent, imposing enough to dazzle newcomers at a glance, that would be great.
However, no sooner had this thought surfaced than the whole office abruptly began to vibrate.
Following that, the entire scene quickly blurred, and then a beam of orange light fell from above. Colin looked up and his pupils shrunk to pinpoints upon seeing a gigantic fireball hanging in midair, constantly spewing out immense flames.
Under its radiant light, the entire sky turned a deep, twisted red.
It was like a celestial body crashing into this place, making anyone who gazed upon it feel insignificance and awe.
The appearance of the surrounding office changed drastically, transforming into a mysterious and solemn hall filled with the traces of war and rust, within which stood a damaged gray stone long table.
Outside the hall, smoke from gunfire filled the air, obscuring visibility.
Colin sat at the head of the gray stone long table, completely stunned. He hadn’t expected the entire place to transform so dramatically just because of his casual complaint.
The giant fireball on the dome seemed at least over a thousand meters in diameter, continuously spewing out flames.
If this were real, just the distance of less than a hundred meters would be enough to broil him beneath it, sizzling with oil, and bursting with aroma.
After a long while, Colin turned his gaze away from the fireball and reflected:
“In terms of special effects, I’m willing to call it the strongest.”
He also couldn’t understand what was going through Lady Bunny’s mind, making the office so flashy when it could have just been a simple cubicle set up like in a small company.
At this moment, a task message appeared in Colin’s mind:
[The “Unfamiliar World” task has been changed to “World Code-13,” with a series update. Please check the task bar for details.]
“It’s almost the same as when I’m on a mission, the function of the parchment transfers to my mind. However, when on a mission, there is nothing like the Interaction Hall, only a task and Storage Room. The office doesn’t have those restrictions.”
Colin stroked his chin, curious about why the Bonfire Company bothered with the parchment scroll in reality, questioning why they didn’t just directly upload everything into the brain?
The text on the parchment could only be seen by the holder in reality.
Not understanding and without overthinking it, Colin checked the task bar to see the new events added:
[Event One (Priority): After returning to “World Code-13,” establish a Bonfire Sacrificial Site by stacking and burning the corpses of “Bonfire Church” personnel and their follower believers at the altar in the church.]
…
[Event Two: Due to technical reasons, employees cannot be precisely dropped into the Bonfire Sacrificial Site. Please guide the employees to the Bonfire Sacrificial Site for marking after entering that world.]
…
[Event Three: Carry “Token-13” to “World Code-13” to investigate any anomalies that might relate to “Hunger.”]
…
[Event Four: Complete the containment of a Phase Three “Beastification individual contaminated with the Ancient God’s Aura.”]
…
[Event Five: Survive in that world for seven days.]
..
“Bonfire Church?” Colin was startled by the name, and then, under the guidance of the mission’s revelation, he immediately realized that it referred to the dense accumulation of corpses in the church.
And he could be quite certain that this “Bonfire Church” was very likely established by a former colleague who had died.
Or could it mean that there were more former colleagues in that world?
“To establish a church in another world, to do such a thing… that colleague seems to be more than an F Level, at least a D Level. Miss Bunny seemed especially concerned about the whereabouts of a certain containment subject he had with him, but who knows what it is.”
Colin thought the former colleague’s experience must have been quite interesting.
All alone, somehow ending up in another world, then gradually establishing a foothold, founding a church, rising to the pinnacle of life, and then… having his head chopped off to be made into a ritual artifact.
Tragic indeed.
After death, his name in the company’s missions became ‘former employee,’ and even work-related compensation was waived.
Afterward, Colin collected his thoughts and looked at “Event Three.”
“Investigate all abnormal events related to hunger? Could ‘Beastification’ count?”
“Beastification” gave him two major impressions: one was a constant desire to tear people apart, filled with inner tyrannical brutalities, and a flame in the belly.
The other was a relatively strong sense of hunger, although the hunger felt weaker than the tyranny.
However, the specific situation would only be known after entering “World Code 13” tomorrow.
Another point is…
What exactly is this “Token-13”?
No sooner had Colin thought this than a rusty badge appeared on the gray stone table.
He was familiar with this object; it was one of the three items on the church altar, besides the badge in front of him, the other two were his colleague’s head and the Orange Named Revolver.
Looking at the object, Colin’s retina displayed information related to it—
‘A tool manufactured by Bonfire Company through special means using designated items. While you possess it, you will continuously approach your target under either indirect or direct invisible influences. Every second you exist in that zone, every breath of air you take, every step you walk, will lay the groundwork for your eventual face-to-face interaction with the investigative target.’
Upon seeing this description, Colin’s first impression was: Yet another profound and mysterious object related to fate.
Somewhat similar to the red string of destiny in mythological stories.
One end with him, the other end unknown, but following the red string, there would eventually be a day when the two sides meet each other.
Without giving it much thought, he reached out to pick up the “Token-13” from the stone table to examine it.
It was shaped like an eight-pointed star.
The front depicted an imprint of a figure holding up a torch.
Somehow, upon seeing this pattern, Colin couldn’t help but conjure an image in his mind.
Someone raising their right hand high, clutching in it a burning, throbbing heart, like a torch, dispelling the darkness…
Creepy.
Colin shook his head to dispel the image in his mind, noticing that the torch pattern was indeed composed of three critical elements: “an arm,” “a heart,” and “a flame.”
Then, he flipped over the badge in his hand.
On the back of the rusty copper badge, there was a short phrase—
‘When The Night comes, there must be one to light the flame, to shine across all directions.’

chapters.title: Chapter 34 - 34 34 Megalophobia_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 34: Chapter 34 Megalophobia_1 Chapter 34: Chapter 34 Megalophobia_1 “Time is almost up, I should call the three employees over for a meeting to discuss tomorrow’s matters,”
Colin put away the badge that had been made into a “token” and then looked at the three personal resumes, feeling somewhat speechless.
Compared to him, these three seemed to have a much more comfortable start.
For one, they were granted “G Level Authority (Temporary Special Provision)” by Miss Bunny, although the authority only extended to a 10-liter Storage Room.
What’s more outrageous is that they were endowed with a trait—”Reset.”
Simplistically put, it is a special ability akin to resurrection.
In order to ensure they could successfully convene in front of the Bonfire, these people had three “Reset” opportunities in the first week.
Only after using up all three “resurrection” chances and dying again would they truly die.
“Why is that ability given to them and not also fashioned for me?”
Colin felt somewhat aggrieved.
He started with just three pieces of paper, all of which were truncated; if it were not for landing on “Luck,” it might be another person sitting here now.
Even if he wasn’t given it at the start, it would be fine to compensate him now.
Unfortunately, he didn’t know how to contact Lady Bunny and could only wait for her to call on him unilaterally.
“But, come to think of it, Lady Bunny’s clearance seems higher than I’d imagined. What she’s shown, offices and the like, those folks on the forums haven’t even heard of, and as for methods like ‘resurrection,’ it’s the same—they seem likely to be higher than the C Level clearance I’d imagined.”
Over the past two days, Colin also tried to gather information about Lady Bunny, to no avail; her every detail was shrouded in mystery.
In his mind, some associations formed faintly…
But before these associations could take concrete shape, they vanished.
Colin felt as if he had momentarily forgotten something, but after careful thought, it seemed as though nothing was missing.
Shaking his head, he clutched the resumes in his hand, half-closing his eyes in contemplation, and soon felt three distinct “threads” emerge in his mind.
His thoughts extended like hands, gently tugging on these three “threads.”
…
Near Black Forest Park, in a hospital’s intensive care unit, Lin Yilan lay on the bed with a breathing tube, dressed in blue and white striped hospital garb.
Her complexion was deathly pale, her body extremely emaciated, skin stretched tight over bone, with scant hair left on her head and only a few teeth remaining. Her arms and limbs were nearly devoid of muscle.
Not even thirty, and her life was already on its last legs.
Even her once-bright eyes had dulled, clouded over from repeated chemotherapy and surgeries.
Her once-decent looks had turned gollum-like, akin to those from The Lord of the Rings.
Cancer cells had already spread throughout her body, making each moment of existence an immense agony.
Though her face bore little expression, her body shuddered with immense internal pain.
At this point, pain medication was almost ineffective for her.
Her current endurance was solely because she wished to die in her fight against the sickness, not yield to it.
In her mind, this period would not be very long, three to six months more and everything would return to tranquility, eternal tranquility.
Until the day before, when a mysterious letter suddenly appeared beside her—
[Bonfire Company Employment Invitation]
Beep beep beep~
The alarm on her phone vibrated beside her ear, waking her from her frail slumber.
She opened her eyes; everything was unchanged, and the invitation mentioned in the letter had not appeared.
“It seems, indeed, that I was hallucinating, what was I expecting,”
Lin Yilan gave a difficult self-mocking smile.
How could she believe in such unscientific things?
What completing tasks can get rewards, obtain the chance to survive…
Now that he was awake, he thought it did seem a bit…
“Hmm?!”
Lin Yilan suddenly startled, as a surge of grey fog came rolling in from all directions and swallowed her up in an instant.
Then, tendrils of deep red light fell from the sky.
A massive fireball, like the break of dawn, banished all that was blurred and shadowy.
Whew…
She held her breath, lifting her head in shock to look at the gargantuan fireball above her that was spewing flames, her heart shaking violently.
At that moment, she felt a suffocation as though she had megalophobia because of looking directly at the sun from too close.
“My body…”
Lin Yilan touched herself and was horrified to find the pain inside her was gone, her body restored as before, as if it was never ill.
“Thump thump~”
The tapping sound on the desk brought her back, and then she noticed that she was sitting on a stone chair at that moment.
The one who tapped the desk was a man sitting at the end of an oval table, on a high-backed chair against the backdrop of the sun.
His body seemed covered in a layer of gunpowder smoke, indistinct and full of mystery.
Lin Yilan took a deep breath and deeply felt that the individual before her was no ordinary human.
A powerful aura was emanating from the person behind the curtain of smoke.
When she vaguely felt his gaze, almost tangible, casting over her from behind the smoke, Lin Yilan couldn’t help but feel a surge of fear and awe, and she modestly lowered her head, not daring to meet his eyes.
“Hello, I am Tang Ken. Are you the Agent of the Bonfire mentioned in the invitation? What do we need to do?” a voice came from beside her.
Lin Yilan followed the sound and only then did she notice that, aside from herself, there were two other people sitting at the inferior seats.
One seemed to be a lively young man in his twenties with slightly dark skin, while the other seemed to have the composed temperament of a middle-aged person in his forties or fifties.
However, for some reason, Lin Yilan felt she could see them, but she was unable to form a concrete memory of their faces in her mind.
It was a bit weird…
…
Agent of the Bonfire? Is that how Miss Bunny described me in the invitations she sent to them? Colin thought, then nodded his head.
Leaning against the chair, he mulled over the information about these individuals and then spoke, “Your task is very simple. Find a place to sleep by twelve o’clock tomorrow, wait for the descent, and then cooperate with the company’s work on the other side. Specific details will be provided after you enter.”
As he spoke, the details of the three individuals’ clearance levels flashed through their minds, and they immediately understood that their first task was to go to the “Bonfire Sacrificial Site” to register.
Then there was nothing else to do, it mainly depended on what the team leader would require at the time.
At this moment, Colin saw Lin Yilan slightly raise her hand. After a slight gesture, she spoke up:
“Sir Bonfire Agent, may I ask you, upon arriving in that world, will I be in this current body from the gathering or in my original form from reality?”
If it was her real form, no matter what she did, there was no chance.
Right now, she couldn’t even walk after getting out of bed.
The other two held their breath as well; they were unaware of Lin Yilan’s situation but knew about their own, which was equally grim.
“Neither, there will be another body for you to use,” Colin answered simply.
Upon hearing this, they all breathed a sigh of relief. Although they did not know what the other body would be like, it was good enough not to be in their own bodies.
Tang Ken, who appeared composed and reserved to others, raised his hand and, after being acknowledged, asked:
“Mr. Agent, may I inquire about the environment there? I would like to know what kind of items I should bring that would be appropriate. Are there any restrictions on the items we can carry?”
As he finished speaking, the other two adjusted their seating postures and listened attentively, as this was also of concern to them.

chapters.title: Chapter 35 - 35 35 Saving the Fallen Hero_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 35: Chapter 35: Saving the Fallen Hero_1 Chapter 35: Chapter 35: Saving the Fallen Hero_1 “That area is relatively desolate, with some people possessing magic-like abilities. There’s the danger of encountering unknown high-risk monsters, food is scarce, and there’s special and unusual weather, so I suggest starting from these aspects. As for restrictions on the items you can carry, there aren’t any,”
Magic, high-risk monsters, scarce food, strange weather… Tang Ken nodded and sat back down, “Understood, thank you for your answer.”
He wasn’t surprised by the talk of monsters.
After arriving here, even if the person in front of him said tomorrow was the end of the world, he would believe it.
Seeing that both of the others had asked questions, the fellow in construction, Li Ming, hesitated, wondering if he should also ask something. Thus, he raised his left hand and asked an inconsequential question.
“Sir Bonfire Agent, will we be asked to do inhumane, bloody, and cruel things?”
To this question, Tang Ken didn’t seem particularly concerned. In his view, going to other worlds and even foreseeing conflicts that could result in death was to be expected, while Lin Yilan seemed to care but apparently didn’t have a strong resistance to it.
Colin took note of their expressions. If he were to quantify their moral compass, it would probably be Li Ming—Lin Yilan—Tang Ken.
Then, he shook his head and responded:
“Basically, no.”
After briefly answering everyone’s questions, Colin dismissed the meeting and told everyone to start preparing from now on.
When the last person disappeared from the office, Colin also returned to reality.
“These five incidents, it seems, indeed didn’t mention that Human Patchwork Monster. The threat that, in my opinion, reached the sky actually didn’t have much of a follow-up.”
Colin sat in his wheelchair, thinking over today’s updated tasks.
It appeared that the Bonfire Company really didn’t care much about this…
But on further thought, the Bonfire Company had already mastered the method of descent across worlds and could even create items related to time.
The things it showed far exceeded reality.
The only uncertainty was where it came from, which side it belonged to. Colin didn’t naively think that this was something Earth people could come up with.
If it were possible, Earth would have already entered an interstellar civilization society.
After a moment of meaningless speculation, Colin collected his thoughts.
…
The next day, Monday, eleven fifty-nine in the morning.
Colin’s gaze drifted away from the clock on the wall, and then he lay on the bed, eyes closed, silently waiting for a while until the distant and ancient sound rang in his ears on schedule.
“Dong— Dong— Dong—”
When Colin opened his eyes, he saw the overwhelming gray mist slowly receding, revealing the familiar interior of a church in front of him.
This descent didn’t bring any unexpected incidents.
The dark church, the myriad of bodies sprawled across the floor, the stifling air, and the locked doors… Colin looked around. Everything was much the same as when he left last week.
“My body is back to its normal state, but upon feeling it now, it’s not my body, although it’s healthy, it still feels a bit uncomfortable.”
Colin looked at his own hands. Aside from the pale skin and slightly longer body hair, there was almost no sign that he was a patient with Beast Transformation Syndrome.
However, he felt deep down the “quality” of the Beast Transformation Syndrome had grown more pronounced.
“If I use this power, I’ll need to be cautious. Otherwise, I might suddenly go crazy. The task is the company’s, but the life is mine, and I certainly don’t want the next successor’s task to mention me with ‘Former Company Employee’.”
Colin took a deep breath, reined in his thoughts, and noticed his clothes, torn to tatters, much like fragments. He pursed his lips, glad that he had anticipated this and had taken underwear and a set of pajamas from the “Storage Room” to wear.
Afterward, he casually grabbed a set of villager’s clothes to put on over his, covering up the clothes that were out of place in this world.
“The people here seem to have a habit of not wearing underwear.”
Last time Colin was in prison, there was nothing inside his trousers, which felt somewhat improper.
This time he brought a few extra pairs.
Then, he silently recited the name of Bonfire Company in his heart to strengthen the connection, before preparing to complete that task to establish a “Bonfire Sacrificial Site”.
But as soon as he reinforced the connection, he noticed that the “task bar” in his mind was flashing continuously.
This seemed to indicate that some tasks had already been completed.
“That’s strange, I haven’t even started on any tasks yet.”
Colin opened it subconsciously and was taken aback by the information inside.
To his surprise, the task column, which he thought had only five tasks, suddenly had over a dozen new tasks, with nearly half of them already completed.
[Event 17 “Take a breath of fresh air from ‘World Code-13′” completed: 20 Bonfire Points.]
[Event 18 “Observe the architectural style of ‘World Code-13′” completed: 50 Bonfire Points.]
[Event 21 “Take the first step of a human from Earth onto ‘World Code-13′” completed: 20 Bonfire Points.]
[Event 9 “Encounter the forms of life activity on ‘World Code-13’…”]
…
“Fuck, can you even do tasks like this? Is this the benefit of having a leader?”
Colin was dumbstruck. He had barely been here for two minutes and had already earned nearly three hundred points.
Miss Bunny really went all out when she helped apply for the side tasks!
The uncompleted tasks, most of them are not difficult either, belonging to the kind that one could easily finish naturally after staying for a while.
That means, at the very least, there’s a guaranteed five hundred points just from being here.
As for those tasks with specific requirements, like [Event 6 “Find the child of the mother with Beast Transformation Syndrome”] or [Event 7 “Kill the guarding monster outside the door”], they’d require a bit more thought.
Colin checked the tasks with certain demands and found those related to the “Brave Ones”.
[Event 9: “Rescue the fallen Brave Ones”].
This task was similar to the one during his first descent when he was tasked to find a former colleague. When he focused on it, Colin could feel a signal emitting from a direction one and a half hour clock position away from him.
The distance was uncertain, but definitely much farther than the first time.
It might take two or three days of nonstop travel to reach there.
“Even if they can’t survive for a month, they should last for ten days or more, so there’s no need to hurry. However, this time, only by completing Event 5 can I return to reality, there’s no mention of being able to go back if anything else is accomplished…”
Colin frowned slightly, the remaining time for Event 5 had refreshed, now it showed “167 hours 57 minutes 31 seconds” until the end.
Doesn’t that mean he has to stay for seven full days before returning?
What a headache…
“Forget it, it’s not like it was in prison last time. I won’t be sent to the Holy Healing Church again, nor will I encounter that shitty priest or ‘him’, so if I just lie low, there shouldn’t be any problems.”
Colin smacked his lips, feeling the only issue might be that the food wouldn’t be enough.
But conserving a bit, he should manage for seven days with no problems.

chapters.title: Chapter 36 - 36 36 Bonfire Sacrificial Site_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 36: Chapter 36 “Bonfire Sacrificial Site”_1 Chapter 36: Chapter 36 “Bonfire Sacrificial Site”_1 He took a deep breath, and Colin turned around to look at the large pit filled with a massive amount of ashes at the deepest part of the church, deciding to pile all the people right here.
Establishing a Bonfire Sacrificial Site, what followed was getting the employees to start descending.
The task of stacking the corpses wasn’t complicated, but as he lifted the bodies, there was an innate aversion in the depths of his heart towards the dead, or perhaps towards death itself.
Almost an hour later, Colin had piled all the corpses into the large pit of the church.
“A total of one hundred and ninety-seven people, fewer than I had originally guessed…”
Colin dusted off his hands, looking at the huge pile of corpses before him, the bodies dried up and devoid of moisture, intertwined and stacked like old kindling, forming a large circle.
The stacked corpses, reaching three meters in height, did not emit any peculiar scent, not even a foul odor, only presenting death before the eyes, silent and absolute.
While handling these bodies, Colin discovered something—that there wasn’t anything of value on them.
It was one thing for their clothes to be patched, but even some wearing red cult robes with flame patterns had nothing valuable. It could only mean that someone beat him to it, or that they had passed on their valuable belongings to someone else before this.
Considering there were no apparent signs of the bodies being disturbed.
Colin leaned towards the latter possibility.
“What a pity, not a single thing to scavenge, not even something left for me.”
While Colin pondered this, he lifted the last few corpses and threw them on top of the pile.
Thus, the accumulation of all the followers’ bodies from the Bonfire Church at the scene was completed.
The incident was only left with the final step of igniting the fire and burning it.
He pulled out a bottle of Blended Oil from his pocket, about to pour it on, but thinking better of it, it didn’t seem quite right to use such a thing inside a church. He switched to alcohol instead.
With a snap.
The distinctive blue-transparent flame of the alcohol whooshed into life.
The moment the flame ignited, a particular atmosphere escaped from the corpses used as kindling. The flame, as if under some control, instantly enveloped the entire pile, turning it into a massive bonfire several meters high in the blink of an eye.
The blue light of the fire simultaneously turned to orange-red, blazing fiercely.
Amazingly, the fire, almost reaching the top of the church, didn’t burn anything. Even standing next to it, where the flames soared much higher than himself, Colin didn’t feel any scorching heat hitting his face.
Moreover, if he listened carefully, it was as if one could hear the indistinct murmurs of prayers coming from within the flames.
It was like hearing the voices of those long dead resounding once more.
The church, abandoned for who knows how long, thus became tinged with an indefinable eeriness and sanctity.
At the same time, in Colin’s heart, it seemed as if this world now had an additional “coordinate.”
As long as he was in this world, no matter where he was, he could feel the location of this bonfire, and use it as a mark to determine his current direction.
“If this were a game, wouldn’t this just be like a save point or something?”
Colin looked up at the enormous flame and suddenly remembered, the church is sealed tight now, isn’t it…
Would he die from carbon monoxide poisoning?
Although his body had been enhanced, it still hadn’t reached that ultimate living organism form that could survive without the need for air.
Just at that moment, a line of text appeared on his retina.
[“Bonfire Sacrificial Site” has been established.]
In Colin’s mind, information related to the “Bonfire Sacrificial Site” surfaced.
[A special flame ignited with special kindling authorized by the Bonfire Company can be used as a coordinate reference system for the “Descend Project G-1”.]
[Furthermore, it possesses all the beautiful imaginations people have of flames: including but not limited to “warmth”, “brightness”, “driving away the darkness”, and so on…]
[In addition, it has a multitude of properties geared towards the mystic, such as anti-prophecy and anti-spying, and in most cases, it can only be observed through conventional physical methods.]
“Seems quite impressive, but there’s no explanation on whether I will die of carbon monoxide poisoning.”
Colin snorted, finding that his mind was suddenly filled with additional data.
[“Bonfire Sacrificial Site”: Level 1.]
[Remaining burn time: 29 days, 23 hours, 57 minutes.]
[Note: The bonfire is about to extinguish, yet kindling is not added, you need to bring more powerful creature carcasses as fuel to burn and extend the time.]
[—Sacrificing a containment subject assessed at a threat level 2 beast (reference: Stage Three “Beast Transformation Syndrome”) +3000 points, can upgrade the bonfire level and unlock more functions.]
[—A “Murky Energy Block” will be produced after 23 hours and 57 minutes.]
…
“Has a game designer or something infiltrated the Bonfire Company?”
Colin blinked, his curiosity piqued about what exactly a “Murky Energy Block” was.
Unfortunately, there was no further explanation, he could only wait a day to find out.
Nevertheless, although he still didn’t have information about the current flame, based on its size, if there were any issues, the oxygen should have been almost consumed by now. The fact that he wasn’t suffocating suggested that there wasn’t a major problem.
“Next up, it’s time to summon the employees to deal with the thing outside the door.”
…
Dong——Dong——Dong——
The distant and ancient bell tones slowly faded away.
Li Ming propped himself up, shook his head, opened his eyes, and looked around with slight confusion, but he soon froze.
Surrounding him was an unfamiliar wasteland.
What was chilling was that beside him lay four or five corpses in disarray.
They had died an unknown time ago, their flesh long since decayed, leaving only bones wrapped in rotten cloth.
“So intense right from the start?”
Li Ming’s scalp tingled for a moment, and it a deep breaths before he could steady himself.
Then, he noticed his previously missing right hand, his amputated right leg, and some burns on his body had all miraculously healed.
No, to be more precise, the body he now inhabited was not his own.
Was this the ‘Soul Transference’ mentioned in the meeting?
Li Ming savored the feeling of a whole body for the first time in a long time.
At that moment, a message suddenly surged into his mind: “Can you see this?”
Li Ming was taken aback, and then realizing something, he instinctively responded in his mind with a “Yes.”
Having received a response, Colin sent another message.
“Alright, then sense the mission and start making your way over. It shouldn’t be far, I’ll wait for you here.”
“Okay.”
Li Ming was about to ask where the other person was, but then a message emerged in his brain.
[Mission One: Locate the “Bonfire Sacrificial Site”.]
[Description: Your squad leader is waiting for you there. Please act swiftly to rendezvous.]
When he focused on this, he, like Colin, sensed a signal coming from a certain direction.
He was like a signal receiver.
Even with his eyes closed, he could feel a bright flame in that place.
But when he opened his eyes, nothing special was visible. A bit further away, everything was blurred, as if a thin veil-like mist shrouded everything.

chapters.title: Chapter 37 - 37 37 Will This Be Dangerous_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 37: Chapter 37 Will This Be Dangerous?_1 Chapter 37: Chapter 37 Will This Be Dangerous?_1 “It feels like it’s a bit too far away, I should find some sort of handy weapon for self-defense before hitting the road.”
Li Ming wasn’t exactly unarmed, but his defensive item wasn’t quite suitable for the situation at hand, and it wouldn’t do much good in an unexpected emergency either.
He looked around and quickly found himself embarrassingly realizing that not even a sizable rock could be found in the vicinity—there were no useful weapons at all.
However, at that moment, he noticed a pair of bleached leg bones scattered on the ground.
Uh, this…
As Li Ming eyed the remains of these so-called Good Brothers, he suddenly realized that perhaps all was not lost.
It just seemed a bit unconscionable, morally speaking.
“Friend, you wouldn’t want to just lie here exposed to the wilderness, never finding a burial place, right?”
Li Ming muttered under his breath, seeing no objections, he squatted down, “Don’t worry, I guarantee with the name of my squad leader that once I succeed and have the chance, I’ll come back to bury you and erect a tombstone.”
After saying that, Li Ming chose a femur—one of the hardest bones in the human body—from each of the fellow kind-hearted Good Brothers and then left the place without looking back.
He trudged towards his destination with his head down for a solid half-hour before he slowed down and glanced back…
Good, nothing unclean was following him.
After catching his breath, he looked at the four sturdy and slightly burdensome femurs he was carrying on his back and silently thanked nature’s bounty.
Then, he tossed three of them beside the road.
He originally only wanted to carry one, but fearing that if he turned around halfway and saw the “Good Brothers” bringing “others” after him, he had taken one from each corpse.
Now that everything was fine, there was no need to carry so many.
After all, they were quite heavy.
Later, on his way, Li Ming looked around at the eerie “death” scene and developed the same confusion that Colin initially had.
What exactly had happened here to cause such complete death?
There was no answer.
A couple of hours later, an exhausted Li Ming spotted a desolate small town.
“Captain, I think I see the small town you mentioned. Are you inside?”
“Yeah, there’s a white church building in the town, head straight here.”
Li Ming, looking at an enormous, non-human footprint on the ground, swallowed hard: “Boss, could there be any danger?”
“Of course, there would be—why else would I be sitting here waiting for you to come?”
Colin didn’t try to hide the fact that there was danger outside the door; after all, these men had multiple lives to spare, and if they weren’t going to sacrifice one now, when would they?
If he remembered correctly, when that monster made a move, it would certainly expose itself for a brief moment.
Using Time Stasis at that moment and five seconds of concentrated fire should pose no problem…
At least the “Book of Fate: Fragment” displayed no issues.
Thinking of this, Colin closed his eyes and sensed the messages he had received through the Life Paper while the other was making his way here.
[You’re waiting for your subordinate employee to reach the church door, touch it, and then, taking advantage of the instant he’s attacked, decisively use “Time Stasis” to freeze the scene, stab the assailant with that dagger, and defeat it under a round of concentrated fire.]
After this, the Book of Fate said he and Li Ming would meet and then successfully find the next employee.
This prediction did not end in death.
It ended when the third day came, and the paper was full and vanished.
‘The Book of Fate occasionally ends with death; otherwise, if all is normal, the predictions continue until there’s no more blank space on the paper, and it disappears.’
Colin recalled what he had read in the company’s internal communication group.
However, just as he had guessed before, the information given by the Life Paper became less accurate the further ahead it predicted, generally becoming unreliable for events more than seven days away.
For that was what would occur under some ideal condition…
It’s like someone planning their future during the holidays, deciding to wake up to brush teeth, wash face, read books, go for a run, have breakfast on time, exercise, meet friends to hike, and return to sleep at nine o’clock… and so on for a healthy lifestyle.
But in reality, if most people wake up without having to go to school or work and have no pressing matters, the first thing they do is check their phones, then go back to sleep for a bit more, get up, meet friends to play games, and play throughout the night…
However, under normal circumstances, most company employees using this thing wouldn’t end up dead.
Only for him, so far he had used it five times, and died four times.
Without giving it much thought, Colin put on the Third-Level helmet, had “Time Stasis” in his left hand and held “Revolver Contrarian” in his right hand from his pocket, then he approached the church gate.
About ten or so minutes later, some noises arose in the quiet town.
At the same time, information transmitted from Li Ming came into his mind.
“Captain, I can see the church now, what should we do next?”
“Continue to approach, first come to the front of the gate.”
Colin remembered that he was attacked the last time because he opened the door; before that, knocking or shouting did not seem to affect him.
Soon, Li Ming’s footsteps could be heard not far from the door.
Colin held his breath, his hand clenching the Golden Card, ready to use the card at any moment.
But just as he thought…
As long as he didn’t try to open the door, the fatal attack would not come.
Outside the door, the footsteps stopped about two meters from the gate, with only a door separating Colin from his subordinate employee.
After Li Ming stopped walking, Colin quickly received information in his mind.
“What should we do next?”
“Get ready to open the door, remember, to open the door swiftly in one motion, and be as careful as possible of your back during the opening because it’s highly likely there will be an attack.”
Colin silently sent a message to his subordinate who was two or three meters away.
Having received the message, Li Ming wasn’t scared; he knew he had three lives, although he wasn’t sure if they were real or fake, but not cooperating to return to reality meant a slow death…
Moreover, various signs indicated that the company indeed possessed technology beyond normal human imagination – the Descent Protocol, Soul Transference, those enormous frightening fireballs, and so on.
Each one was a testament to the company’s terrifying nature…
Gathering his thoughts, Li Ming placed his hands on the door crack and pushed as hard as he could.
The heavy doors were only pushed open a slight gap.
…
Now is the time!
An intuition flashed through Colin as a ripple appeared, the assailant, whether invisible or employing some other technique, had made a move!
He used “Time Stasis” without any hesitation.
In the instant that the scene before him froze, Colin drew his gun, aimed, and fired in 0.2 seconds, shooting three bullets towards the seemingly empty space behind Li Ming.
However, Colin was taken aback as the bullets went through unimpeded.
Not behind him?! If there was a physical body, this would never have happened!
But at that very moment, while he was in the frozen space, he suddenly felt something within a distance of ten to fifteen meters trying to break free from the Time Stop Effect!

chapters.title: Chapter 38 - 38 38 Tainted Virtue_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 38: Chapter 38 Tainted Virtue_1 Chapter 38: Chapter 38 Tainted Virtue_1 Something’s escaping at eleven o’clock!
Although Colin saw and smelled nothing, he trusted his instincts, decisively pulling out a bone spur filled with cracks and charging towards that location!
This was the item that had pierced his side in the last incident.
Once stabbed by it, one’s organs would rapidly fail due to swelling, even in his Beast Transformation Syndrome State, he couldn’t withstand it.
Ratatat…
Just as he came within ten meters, he heard the sound of the Time Stop Effect coming to an end.
But, he had already reached the position in front of the target!
Relying on some kind of combat intuition, Colin gripped the handle of the bone spur tightly and stabbed forcefully into the “air” ahead of him.
Crack—
Vaguely, it felt as though the sharp end of the bone spur had penetrated a layer of hard protection, then smoothly stabbed into something with the texture of flesh.
In the blink of an eye, without time to think, an image suddenly appeared in Colin’s head…
In the picture, his head flew off, as if he had undergone a beheading once more.
Right then, before the Time Stop Effect completely faded, Colin decisively let go of the knife and rolled to the left.
Hum…
A fatal, yet secret sound flew over his head.
Colin didn’t immediately get up after the roll but instead lay flat on the ground, instantly drawing his gun and aiming at an area that seemed to be empty.
As the trigger was pulled, the flame flashed, and several bullets flew out, then disappeared instantly.
“Did it hit?”
Colin didn’t hear the sound of bullets hitting anything, and normally, they definitely would hit the building behind.
There was only one possibility for this.
The bullets had hit…
But, since he couldn’t see the target, he had no idea what the effect was.
“Damn, this feeling of punching cotton is really frustrating.”
Colin cursed softly, then pushed himself off the ground with his right hand, getting up while cautiously reloading his revolver and staying alert all around.
Being stabbed by that dagger would definitely have an effect!
All he had to do was wait.
Sure enough, after a dozen seconds, there was a sound of liquid dripping at three o’clock!
Colin immediately turned his head, seeing a human silhouette emerging in the air, becoming increasingly visible.
The opponent’s ability akin to invisibility was failing!
Colin’s spirit lifted, realizing that this was because the bone spur was taking effect!
With guarded attention, he saw a being clad in broken armor, with a clean bone spur sticking out from its chest, gradually take shape.
Under its armor was not flesh and blood but a mass of black, eerie gelatinous material; no helmet, its head was wrapped round and round with a filthy burlap like that of a mummy, with dark blood seeping out from the cloth, obscuring any features.
In its only remaining left hand, it held a rusty, broken sword.
Colin even saw the holes his bullets had made in its body, but those holes seemed to have almost no effect on it.
At this moment, perhaps because the dagger was still having an effect, its body was becoming more swollen and filled with water, resembling a body that had floated up in a pool after being soaked.
The air was thick with a sickening and putrid stench.
“It should no longer belong to the living.”
Colin’s eyelids drooped slightly, his body leaning forward, with a Golden Card in his left hand and a gun in his right, striking a hunting leopard’s pose ready to attack.
It was then that this creature in broken armor, dragging its rusty, broken sword, started walking towards him, step by step, preparing for a final charge.
However, before it could take two steps, its body, swollen from edema, seemed to reach its limit, like an overinflated balloon; black pus oozed from its pores, mixing into streams dribbling onto the ground.
With a body swollen like Giant’s Lookout, charging would be difficult, let alone walking.
Nonetheless, to avoid any accidents, Colin used the Golden Card once more when it was within effective range.
This time, the loaded bullets again fired, leaving six holes on the surface of the monster.
After the Time Stop effect ended, Colin first felt an intense disorientation from the distortion of time, and then he noticed that the humanoid monster had fallen to the ground at some point, with black pus that made one’s stomach churn oozing incessantly from the six holes.
It was like a rotten watermelon poked with holes…
The foul-smelling liquid spread all over the ground…
“Does getting stabbed by this dagger result in such a miserable fate?”
Colin’s breath hitched, he estimated that even if he did not finish it off with another stab, the monster wouldn’t last long before exploding.
The first combat use of this dagger had left him feeling deeply alarmed.
Meanwhile, as it fell, a mission update flashed in Colin’s mind.
[You have successfully slain a “Fallen Virtue Knight”.]
[Event 7 “Slay the Guardian Monster Outside the Gate” is completed. The reward will be settled upon return.]
“Fallen Virtue Knight?”
Colin finally learned the name of the monster, and he also breathed a sigh of relief.
Although the exchange, excluding the ten seconds of Time Stop, lasted less than a minute in normal time, the psychological pressure it brought was quite significant.
It wasn’t that it was very strong, but its abilities were just too strange…
Luckily, everything was now over.
However, after glancing at the corpse on the ground, Colin’s eyes flickered, and he turned his head, wanting to signal his cheap subordinate to help pick up the bone spurs.
But when he turned around, he saw that his subordinate’s expression was off. Staring at him, his lips moved a few times as if trying to say something, but before any sound could come out, his head suddenly dropped from his neck.
With a thud, it smashed into the ground.
Blood sprayed from the severed neck like a cloud of mist, splashing high into the air, as if a blood rain had fallen.
This… didn’t make it in time to save him!
Colin was stunned. He felt that his reaction at that moment had been fast enough, possibly just one-tenth of a second.
But even then, he failed to save Li Ming…
Was the sword that fast?
And why did it take so long for the head to fall off?
This makes no sense.
However, the blood rain did not continue for long. Li Ming’s body quickly disintegrated into grey mist, sweeping toward the flames inside the church.
“Going back to respawn?”
Colin guessed the reason and didn’t know how long the process would take. Out of helplessness, he turned back to look at the mushy corpse on the ground and took out a monocle from his pocket.
[This was a being that could actively lower its own presence and converge its breath, making it difficult to be perceived. In life, it could indeed have been called extraordinary.]
[Judging from the formal name “Virtue Knight”, one can guess its ability is associated with the “eight virtues”, perhaps representing “Humility”.]
“Does ‘Humility’ here refer to an actual force rather than just a moral honor?”
Colin reflected thoughtfully. He now noticed that, with the creature dead, there was actually a large number of footprints and a distinctive smell present at the scene. It had not only reduced its own presence but also lowered the presence of all related things.
Compared to mere invisibility, this ability would be much more troublesome to deal with.
“Tch, if one virtue represents one power, then I wonder what other kinds of effects the other virtues have. One is already this terrible; what if someone had all eight combined?”
Colin felt a headache considering the possibility.
At the same time, he also felt curious about whether the world’s eight knightly virtues had any connection to the eight virtues on Earth.
Is it just a coincidence? Or is it something an ex-employee created?
Unfortunately, limited by his insufficient knowledge of this world, Colin could not speculate much.
It was then that another message suddenly appeared in his mind.
[Agree to hand over the “Fallen Virtue Knight” corpse to receive an additional one thousand points, as well as an item characteristic of it.]
[Would you like to submit?]

chapters.title: Chapter 39 - 39 39 Lost Contact_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 39: Chapter 39 Lost Contact_1 Chapter 39: Chapter 39 Lost Contact_1 “Yes.”
Colin agreed decisively, after all, there was no use holding onto the creature that had turned into black pus on the ground.
After making the decision.
In the air, a transparent vortex appeared.
Under its suction, every drop of liquid and debris from the corpse on the ground was sucked in and disappeared.
“One Thousand Points, plus an item with the corresponding properties of this creature.”
“Do all the items with special effects within Bonfire Company come about this way?”
“Capturing various anomalies and then using their powers to create items through special means?”
Colin stood still, observing the lingering traces around him, with a thoughtful look in his eyes.
He glanced at the Golden Card in his hand, not knowing what had been contained to create it.
It must not be something easy to handle.
Shaking his head and collecting his thoughts, Colin’s gaze shifted to the ground where the Bone Spur had played a significant role.
He did not rush to pick it up, after all, it had just been soaking in the pus. Who knew if it was contaminated with viruses?
Colin cautiously took out the “Analytical Lens” again, pinched the top and bottom of the lens with his right hand, brought it to his left eye, and gave the Bone Spur a close-up view.
[A dagger made from the simple processing of the remains of a female clergy member after her death. If stabbed by it, one would experience the horror she faced in life, continually being infused with foul water until they felt like they were dragged into the deep sea, suffocating to death.]
[Holding it for too long will also cause the body to swell gradually, and within thirty minutes, a slight mishap could lead to death from organ failure triggered by the swelling.]
“There’s no mention of contamination or the like, so it should be okay. I just wonder why the description seems much more detailed than before.”
Colin put away the “Analytical Lens,” speculating that the reason might be that he had come to understand more about this world, so he knew more.
However…
Was the female clergy member mentioned above Talisa?
Was she drowned?
No… simply being drowned didn’t seem to warrant this kind of outcome.
Colin wondered curiously for a moment, then cautiously stepped forward to pick up the object and put it into the “Storage Room.”
Then, he turned and glanced back at the church behind him.
There was still no stir.
“The resurrection bar mustn’t have finished yet.”
Colin pursed his lips, then walked back into the church.
At this moment, there was no change in the flames inside the church, but all the corpses had turned to ash, the ashes of nearly two hundred bodies piled up like a small hill.
And outside the Bonfire, wisps of ash were gathering and dispersing, seemingly coalescing into a human silhouette.
Seeing that the resurrection wouldn’t happen anytime soon, Colin first closed the door and then found a place to sit after looking around. He took out some food from his pocket and silently dealt with the negative effect of the Golden Card “temporal perception disorder.”
Having used the ability twice in a row, symptoms were slightly pronounced, as if time was speeding up or slowing down. Even the short walk into the door felt like several days had passed, or in the blink of an eye, it seemed as though time had flown by in the space of a dream.
But looking at Task Five on the clock… only two minutes had actually gone by.
Fortunately, with a few uses, the symptoms were manageable, and the negative effects slowly wore off as time went on…
Twenty actual minutes later, there was some movement inside the church. Colin, who was sitting by the altar, turned his eyes and saw that in front of the Bonfire, the ashen silhouette had finally coalesced into Li Ming, who looked utterly bewildered and at a loss standing before the massive Bonfire.
Touching his neck with lingering fear, it seemed as if his death was just a moment ago.
“Reviving takes about half an hour?”
Colin calculated the time, then stuffed the chocolate into his mouth and stood up, looking at the other person, “How do you feel?”
Li Ming now looked to be in his twenties or thirties, with brown hair and a medium build that leaned toward the shorter side. His skin was dark, probably no taller than one meter seventy.
“Not too bad, just feeling a bit off in a way that’s hard to describe, but it doesn’t affect my movement…” Li Ming twisted his neck.
“That’s probably something the company did on purpose to keep you from getting too immersed here and then not being able to distinguish between reality and the Other World when you get back. Anyway, since it doesn’t affect anything, there’s no need to worry about it, but that’s just my guess. I’m not sure if that’s really the case.”
Colin gave a simple explanation, but to be honest, if one stayed here too long and then suddenly returned, it really could happen.
By then, Li Ming might desperately run down the road, screaming: I can’t tell, I really can’t tell which is real…
Nevertheless, Colin didn’t dwell on it too much and briefly introduced himself to the other person.
Only then did he realize…
This guy apparently hadn’t recognized his identity as an Agent of the Bonfire, and that’s why he used the title “Captain.”
“Captain, what are we going to do next?” asked Li Ming.
Colin didn’t let on but simply said, “You stay here and guard the Bonfire. I should go look for the other colleagues. I have a feeling they might have run into some trouble.”
While speaking, he silently sensed the positions of the other two in his mind. The signal of one was intermittent; the messages were sent but he didn’t know if they were received since there was no response.
The other’s signal couldn’t even be described as intermittent, more like ‘broken broken broken broken’; they had basically been “out of contact” from the start.
Colin couldn’t even pinpoint the latter’s location precisely.
He could only be sure that the two were generally in the same direction, though how close or far they were was something he would likely only find out after he got there.
“But come to think of it, is the signal quality related to the distance?”
Colin pursed his lips, feeling that the technology of Bonfire Company sometimes seemed impressive, but at other times, lacking…
Especially this “Descent Protocol” – to say it wasn’t impressive would be an understatement; it could cross who knows how many thousands of light-years to transport a person to a strange world.
To say it was impressive, well, it seemed like every time it would mishandle the transport…
“No problem, but Captain…”
After a pause, Li Ming asked, “Shouldn’t we stick together to look for people at a time like this?”
“No need, they’re not close by. Even on my own, it might take half a day to get there; if I take you along, it would likely take even longer.”
Colin turned down Li Ming’s suggestion, because unlike him, Li Ming couldn’t endure a long journey and maintain his condition without rest.
If he brought him along, they might not even make it by tomorrow…
And most importantly, the “Book of Fate” predicted smooth sailing ahead, so there was nothing to be afraid of.
It was better to act efficiently in everything.
After making arrangements, Colin prepared to leave, but at that moment, he noticed Li Ming standing to one side looking troubled as if he had something to say.
Colin directly spoke up, “If you have something to say, just say it.”
“Captain, do you have any food with you?”
“You didn’t bring any food?”
Seeing him nod, Colin frowned. Hadn’t the situation been explained during the meeting? How could he not bring any food?
However, without making it difficult for the other person, Colin pulled a Snickers from his pocket and asked, “What did you bring with you?”
After speaking and seeing the assortment of items Li Ming took out of his ten-liter space, Colin fell silent.

chapters.title: Chapter 40 - 40 40 Childrens Rifle_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 40: Chapter 40 Children’s Rifle_1 Chapter 40: Chapter 40 Children’s Rifle_1 A pile of metal parts of various sizes rapidly assembled in Li Ming’s hands, turning into a somewhat compact black rifle.
Then, Li Ming, holding the gun, said somewhat helplessly, “I only brought some local specialties from the Americas…”
Well, talk about Teammate stockpiling food while you’re stockpiling guns, huh?
Colin looked at the gun in his hand, fell silent for a few seconds, then passed over the family pack Snickers he was holding and said, in a low voice,
“If I remember correctly, you went abroad for further studies after college, self-funded, wasn’t it? At what’s-its-name Bashinama Pineapple University in civil engineering?”
Li Ming wasn’t surprised that the captain knew about his background and continued the conversation, “San Polo University. I got into some trouble and just got out.”
Colin didn’t know much about that university, but he had heard of some of the industries in that region. However, he didn’t give it much thought and reached out his hand:
“This gun, let me have a look at it…”
Li Ming nodded and passed the firearm over. He didn’t feel threatened by the idea of his captain taking his weapon.
After all, before his head got chopped off, he saw his boss actually Flash!
And he Flashed twice!
That ability was something only legendary superpower users were supposed to have. If he had any ill intentions toward him, he wouldn’t need a gun at all.
While Colin was weighing and handling the gun, Li Ming took the initiative to introduce its specifications to the captain. It was a modified AR15, about 78 centimeters in length, weighing only two kilograms. Moreover, it had an imposing name in its place of origin – the Child Assault Rifle.
As he spoke, Li Ming pointed at a mark on the side of the gun, a cartoon image of a skull with a pacifier in its mouth, beside which was a short phrase in English.
Translated, it roughly meant: Shoot like Mom and Dad to give kids more confidence.
Colin couldn’t help but remark on the unvarnished local customs from across the Ocean, cultivated from a young age.
“Aside from the gun, I only brought a dagger and the rest are bullets, over two hundred rounds, so I didn’t bring any food…”
Li Ming scratched his head with his left hand, saying awkwardly, “I thought there would be some basic food supplies here…”
“Heh.”
Colin, holding the gun, didn’t know how to respond, but suddenly felt that his earlier decision to prioritize Li Ming’s moral standing might have been a bit premature.
He held the gun and couldn’t help asking, “You studied civil engineering, how come you seem quite good with guns?”
The speed at which the other party had assembled the parts into a firearm was certainly not slow, and it didn’t look like a last-minute cramming job.
“When we were in class, the employee guidance counselor took us to the shooting range in the first week and told us that in this place, before civil engineering students go to the construction site to sling concrete, you need to know how to sling lead, otherwise, not to mention slinging concrete, even the shovels used for it would be stolen…”
Who the hell would steal a shovel for slinging concrete?
