[The “Beast Transformation Syndrome” within you becomes even more uncontrollable, and at this point, you realize that if you don’t find a way to solve the root of the problem, you’re heading down a dead end.]
[Carrying this thought, you head towards the source of the terrible threat you feel a kinship with, intending to resolve it in order to escape from this place.]
[You make your way to the Holy Healing Church, forcefully break in, and there you see a monstrous entity beyond your imagination, radiating an aura of tyranny, the strongest creature you have encountered in this world so far.]
[Its body is impaled with various weapons, bathed in blood, indicating that a battle had occurred before you arrived, one that ended with its victory.]
[In this battle, you exhausted all your strength, yet you couldn’t withstand his power.]
[After desperately fleeing the battlefield, “he” didn’t leave, instead controlling other sufferers of Beast Transformation Syndrome to hunt you down. You kept running within the city, enduring until the next day when you were exhausted and finally killed.]
[In the end, you became a part of him during a ritual that wasn’t complete.]
…
“Damn it!”
Colin couldn’t help but curse softly, using the “Book of Fate” to finally remember there was a problem lurking nearby.
A big problem!
“He”!
The first two times he used the “Book of Fate,” he died at the hands of this guy, no, to put it more accurately, he became a part of “him.”
“I shouldn’t have entered this city this afternoon!”
Colin felt somewhat of a headache, closed his eyes, and scanned the information again. If nothing went wrong, the source of danger was supposed to be a legendary Beast Transformation Syndrome that exceeded the Third Order.
No, it might even surpass the Third Order!
“I just absorbed a Second Order Beast Transformation Syndrome fluid, and it was already overwhelming. Who knows how much this guy has collected by now, the usual ranking of orders can’t even be applied to him.”
“I thought after that ‘Virtue Knight’ left, I would be invincible, but I didn’t expect this to be the real invincibility.”
“No, I can’t fight this battle, even if I give it my all.”
Colin pinched his forehead, feeling that the only thing he could do was immediately get out of this troubled place, carrying Tang Ken through the night.
“Book of Fate: Fragment” mentioned that he relied on good fortune and attempted to escape after daylight and failed.
But it didn’t say whether or not you could succeed at night…
“Why does it feel like I’m back in jail again, only that the jail has shifted to another place?”
Colin sighed. The last time, he was able to conjure some “Luck” with “The Dice of Probability,” but now everything was uncertain.
But this one could be used as the last resort.
For now,
he would first try to escape under the cover of night. If he could get away, then they would make a run for it; if not, then they’d have to come back and rally the others to fight.
Seeing Colin stand up, Tang Ken promptly asked, “What happened?”
He had noticed that his captain’s expression had been growing increasingly solemn, feeling that the situation might be developing in an ominous direction.
“Getting ready to run. Let’s see if we can escape the city tonight; if not, we’ll discuss other options.”
Colin picked up the robe on the bed, slipping it on, and confirmed through “Event 5” how much time had been activated this time.
The remaining time is 150 hours 27 minutes 34 seconds.
“I remember the earliest I used a ‘Book of Fate’ around 167 hours. Counting the time, to be safe, I can use the third one by 143 hours, which leaves me with a little over seven hours.”
Colin silently calculated in his heart, got ready, and headed downstairs.
Tang Ken quickly followed behind him.

chapters.title: Chapter 51 - 51 51 One Glance Kill_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 51: Chapter 51: One Glance Kill_1 Chapter 51: Chapter 51: One Glance Kill_1 Leaving the small inn didn’t encounter much resistance.
Colin and Tang De easily arrived outside, where the cold and quiet air of the night carried a faint mix of the local waste and other assorted stenches.
Aside from the occasional patrol team, the streets were almost completely deserted.
Even those folks they saw lying in the streets during the day seemed to have disappeared, likely hiding from the fear of the dark dome above.
Although Colin now felt that the probability of escaping at night was equally slim, it was a waste of time.
But even now he had no choice but to try…
“If our attempt fails later, we’ll go to that noble woman and see if we can initiate a siege against ‘him.'”
As Colin pondered this in his head, he swiftly navigated through the streets and alleys.
After easily avoiding some of Black Stone City’s patrolling guards, the two of them once again arrived at the city wall.
After sniffing the various scents in the air, Colin found a spot where the watch was thin and the defenses were weak.
Looking up at the ten-meter-high city wall, he turned to Tang Ken behind him,
“Can you climb it?”
Tang Ken didn’t immediately respond. He looked up, noticed the irregular construction with plenty of gaps, and nodded, “Yes, I can scale a ten-story building with my bare hands if there’s a chance.”
“That’s all we need. We must climb quickly to avoid being discovered.”
Colin cautioned, not saying much more. After looking around to ensure there were no issues, he began to climb.
A minute later, the two successfully scaled the rampart that was, for ordinary people, like a chasm in the sky.
Outside the city wall, a large number of poor gathered. They had no place to live, merely huddling together at the edge of the light radiating from the city, struggling to survive.
Occasionally, some areas had bonfires burning, but the flames were not large.
“If the bonfires inside the city go out, most of these people probably won’t survive the risk and will die, right?”
Colin glanced at them, recalling the content from the “Book of Fate” that mentioned the greatest catastrophe would start here first.
They are the lowest tier of this world, the first group to be sacrificed…
Turning his gaze away, Colin led Tang Ken towards the edge of the world of light, but after only two or three hundred meters, they stopped.
In their field of vision, at the edge of the light, there was a thin layer of black fog.
It clung to the boundary of light, blending with the outer darkness and was hardly noticeable. Had they not approached it closely, it would have been difficult to see.
Crack!
Colin took out a bottle of blended oil and threw it towards the black fog, expecting it to pass through easily. But it was instead repelled upon impact and shattered on the ground.
Without a second thought, he pulled out a lighter, casually lit a tissue, and tossed it over.
Boom!
A massive blaze erupted, with a heatwave coming straight at them.
However, the raging flames had no effect on the “black fog.”
“What exactly is this layer?” Tang Ken couldn’t help but ask.
“I don’t know for now.”
Colin hesitated for a moment, then reached into his pocket and took out a monocle, holding it by the edges and slowly bringing it to his left eye socket.
Thump~
The moment the lens touched his eye, his heart skipped a beat, and a strong sense of foreboding surged within him.
His mind conjured an image: his eyes bulged, and he fell down, bloodied.
Right then, Colin swiftly closed his eyes and flung the lens away.
But even so, before discarding it, he glimpsed through the lens a vast and terrifying form behind the thin black fog.
Its body was as large as half a mountain, constantly emitting an enormous wail full of rage.
“Ah!!!”
Colin clutched his left eye, blood continuously spilling from between his fingers, his brain throbbing unbearably, feeling as if his soul were trembling, and his body involuntarily squatted down in pain.
Meanwhile, Tang Ken, at a loss, wanted to step forward to help, but suddenly noticed that blood-red long hairs were sprouting quickly on his captain’s body, like bamboo shoots after the rain…
An invisible tyrannical aura spread rapidly.
Even more illogical was that the shadow beneath the captain writhed continuously, as if something was swelling to burst forth from within.
“What’s happening?” Tang Ken gasped, unsure of what to do.
“Don’t, don’t come near me…”
With difficulty, Colin managed to utter a sentence before tensing his body, struggling against the intense wave after wave of pain in his mind.
After a while, the blood-red fur on his skin retracted, his breathing gradually steadied, he regained a certain but limited clear-headedness, and realized immediately.
His left eye was ruined.
It was just a casual glance.
And he had lost an eye.
Drenched in a cold sweat, like someone who had been dragged out of water, Colin took a couple of deep breaths, his ears constantly buzzing.
Tang Ken was saying something beside him, but he couldn’t make it out…
He glanced at the “Analytical Lens” tossed on the ground, only to see it riddled with cracks, evidently damaged beyond use.
And pulling up information related to it…
[Analytical Lens (Severely Damaged, Unusable): Restoring to minimum usable condition requires 813 points.]
[Note: I’m cracked…]
[Warning: This item is contaminated. Contamination type “Ancient God’s Aura.” Holding it for over ten minutes may attract the gaze of an unknown existence and cause the holder to contract “Beast Transformation Syndrome.”]
“It’s done for.”
Colin took a deep breath, never expecting that he was only trying to see if there was a breakthrough in the black mist, and almost died for it.
He didn’t even dare to contemplate what that mountain-sized thing he had seen was…
He could only divert his attention to avoid thinking too much about it.
After that, he checked his personal profile again and his mouth twitched.
On the status section, a list of debuffs had appeared.
Including but not limited to “Physical Weakness,” “Nervous Weakness,” “Left Eye Congested and Burst,” “Dizziness,” “Temporary Tinnitus”…
“It’s uncomfortable.”
Sitting on the ground, Colin could not stop his body from swaying, shook his head, feeling his brain was shaking like jelly, making it hard to think clearly.
After sitting for a good while, his body recovered a bit.
“Captain? Captain?” Tang Ken’s voice seemed to come from beside him.
“It’s nothing, just a minor injury.”
Colin waved his hand, picked up the cracked Analytical Lens from the ground, and pocketed it.
Then, he took out a bar of nut chocolate and put it in his mouth.
The sweet flavor slowly spread in his mouth…
He then took out the “Gluttony Power Mark” and held it in his hand.
While holding it, Colin could feel the food he had just eaten quickly transforming into nutrients and being distributed throughout his body.
HIs bodily functions recovered rapidly within minutes…
Unfortunately.
Using this item, Colin had a complex expression, as if contemplating something.
In this moment, he felt a deep and unspeakable empathy for the fate of that “Evaluation Department” judge.
However, before he had time to dwell on it further, a new task appeared in his mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 52 - 52 52 Seeking Help_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 52: Chapter 52 Seeking Help_1 Chapter 52: Chapter 52 Seeking Help_1 [Event 23: By all means, persist in surviving until the countdown for “Event 5” ends.]
Remark: A special reward will be granted upon completion of this event.
…
“Hiss, a task within a task? What’s the point of this task appearing, though? It’s not helpful at all, no, wait…”
Colin was seated on the ground, eating something while holding the “Gluttony Power Mark,” and he diverted his attention from the strange sensation in his stomach by thinking.
He quickly realized that this event seemed to be guiding him in some way.
It was as if it were indicating, “Don’t try to escape, don’t try to fight, just endure, and all problems will be resolved on the seventh day.”
This gave Colin, who had just been seriously injured and didn’t know what to do next, some ideas.
“If there’s no need for a direct confrontation or escape, and I just have to hold on, then, seven days might not be out of reach.”
“First, I need to make the soldiers in the city on guard, so we can avoid being ambushed by the uncontrollable Beast Transformation Syndrome refugees outside the city tomorrow…”
“Then I have to figure out a way to interfere with that ceremony tonight, if it could be directly prevented, everything might be simply solved.”
As one thought after another flashed through his brain, Colin’s bodily functions gradually recovered, and aside from his eyes, the other parts were mostly back to normal. Thus, he stood up.
He planned to find that noblewoman first.
At this moment, only through her could he have a chance to indirectly mobilize the city’s power.
“But speaking of which, I’m starting to suspect whether this noblewoman was arranged to come here from the start, too coincidental, in all sorts of ways…”
Colin was somewhat suspicious, but he couldn’t afford to ponder it now, as either way, he definitely needed their assistance.
Just as he was about to act, he seemed to remember something and turned to Tang Ken beside him, “I didn’t ask, what did you bring in with you?”
Tang Ken was startled, not expecting Colin to suddenly ask this. After thinking for a bit, he replied, “Three days’ worth of military rations, a multifunctional shovel, a mini pistol, and over a hundred bullets.
“I was planning to bring a Mini Uzi, but there was no room for it, so I didn’t.”
After a pause, he continued, “I didn’t know I’d be staying here that long; if I had known, I would’ve brought more food. But if I’m careful with it, it shouldn’t be a problem.”
Good, he’s much more reliable than that Li Ming… Colin wasn’t surprised that he could get his hands on a pistol, given that this guy was retired and had his own channels.
Li Ming, that guy studying civil engineering, didn’t bring anything useful, just whipped out a children’s rifle, and that was when Colin really lost it.
But now there’s been a mishap; they can’t go back, so whether that guy can stay alive is down to fate.
With some luck, maybe he’ll find something like dried rats in the church to tide him over.
If not, he shouldn’t starve to death in seven days…
Even if he starves to death, he still has another life, no panic.
“By the way, how did you get caught by that group if you had a gun?” Colin noticed this detail.
If he had used the gun back then, he would likely have had a good chance to escape.
Tang Ken’s face showed some embarrassment, “To fit things in the Storage Room, my gun was disassembled. I intended to assemble it after getting through the crowd, but I was knocked out before I could get out…”
“Then get it ready now; there’s probably going to be all sorts of trouble coming up, be prepared, prepared to kill.”
Although he knew that this guy probably had blood on his hands, Colin still gave a reminder.
Seeing the other nodded, Colin didn’t say anything more and returned to the base of the city wall that he had just scaled.
Before attempting to climb the wall again, he looked back over his shoulder.
“Still, I didn’t feel the scent of ‘Beastification’ on these people, so, the ‘Book of Fate’ mentions a massive outbreak of ‘Beastification’… Is it man-made or due to some other unknown reason?”
A few seconds later, Colin withdrew his gaze and sighed, deciding not to dwell on it for now. He planned to return and speak with the other party first to understand the situation better.
After easily scaling the city wall, Colin, accompanied by Tang Ken, quickly headed towards the inn where Helena was staying.
Compared to the small inns they rented, Helena’s place was much more luxurious, and at night, soldiers were arranged to protect this noble, ensuring that no harm would come to her.
“Halt! Who goes there?!”
As Colin approached, someone immediately issued a stern challenge.
Several more people emerged from the other side…
“It’s me, go inform Helena that I have urgent business with her.”
Colin walked forward slowly yet decisively, not concealing his identity.
“You? Who are you to casually call out a noble’s name? Do you think visiting a noble of such status is something anyone can do, especially at this late hour?”
The guard frowned suspiciously, thinking Colin was up to no good, slowly drew his long sword to drive the person away, but another member of the noble’s personal guard recognized him.
“Wait, don’t act rashly. Are you the Thunder Priest from earlier today?”
“Yes.”
Colin nodded, not denying the identity others had given him.
After all, as the saying goes, those who know, know…
Thunder Priest?
The soldier who wanted to draw his sword was taken aback, and then filled with anxiety, fearing that he would be held in contempt by Colin. He wanted to say something in explanation but relaxed only when Colin gestured that it was not a concern.
Your society seems to have quite strict class notions…
Observing his reaction and combining his experiences from entering the city today, Colin got a general understanding of the societal structure here.
About a dozen seconds later, footsteps were heard coming from upstairs, and the noble guard returned with a message:
“Honored Priest, Miss Helena is already waiting for you upstairs. Please follow me.”
After saying that, he led the way.
Colin followed behind, reaching the third floor where Helena, seated in a large chair in the spacious living room, awaited as nobility.
Her old butler stood beside her, weary yet trying to appear energetic, his eyes bloodshot, evidently just awakened.
After pointing to a seat nearby, Helena, still shrouded in her grey robe, began speaking only after Colin was seated:
“Sir, what brings you to us at this hour?”
The tone sounded a bit irritable, but that was understandable. In their view, they had finally arrived at a safe location, only to be woken in the middle of their rest – indeed quite vexing…
Colin let the thought pass and didn’t beat around the bush, saying directly:
“I’ve noticed that a disaster is approaching and that everyone in this city may struggle to survive.
“If we don’t react, neither I nor you,
“All of us will die, no exceptions.”
As his words ended, the entire room fell into a silent stillness, so quiet you could hear a pin drop.

chapters.title: Chapter 53 - 53 53 Assembling the Troops_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 53: Chapter 53 Assembling the Troops_1 Chapter 53: Chapter 53 Assembling the Troops_1 The scene fell silent for a few seconds as if everyone was stunned by the information, taking a while to register what had been said.
The old butler, with his temples streaked with grey and his face weary, opened his mouth uncertainly, “Your Excellency, if I heard you correctly, did you just say that a disaster is going to befall our city?”
As he spoke, he couldn’t help but glance out of the window, where all was tranquil under the light, seemingly not a place where any disaster would strike.
Moreover, they were already thousands of miles away from the “Magic Fog calamity” zone. Even if it were to spread, it shouldn’t be so rapid.
“Yes, that’s why I need your help to mobilize the city’s defenses, to prepare for the oncoming disaster over the course of this night before it becomes unstoppable.”
Colin pondered for a moment; if he remembered the previous foresights correctly, they had several key points.
The first wave of substantial charges would occur after daylight…
Next was that “he,” who apparently could not leave the Holy Healing Church. The notes mentioned that his charge on the church failed and he was ultimately routed without pursuit from the other side.
However, “he” could control the Beast Transformation Syndrome to attack, perishing in the inexhaustible onslaught, sapped of his strength.
But now that Colin had that mission guidance, he would not engage in head-on confrontations anymore…
In addition, it appeared that a group of people had discovered the issue with the Holy Healing Church before him and had launched an attack before he could get there, dealing certain damage to the adversary.
Any team capable of injuring such formidable creatures was obviously a strong one.
Although unclear who they were, he must seize this opportunity and not let it go to waste.
At this moment, the old butler wore a conflicted expression. He seemed about to speak but then, thinking of something, turned to look at Miss Helena.
“Are you sure?” Helena’s voice came from beneath the gray hood.
Her tone was much steadier this time.
“Absolutely.”
Colin’s tone was firm and decisive.
The person behind the scenes conducting the ritual would absolutely not stop now.
Otherwise, they wouldn’t have locked down the entire city.
One reason would certainly be the desire not to let the outside world know, not wishing to be disturbed; the second was an indication that the individual was also in a last-ditch effort, with no turning back.
As for why “he” did not choose to perform the ritual in the wilderness in secrecy.
Clearly, he needed the whole city’s population for the sacrifice.
Of course, framing it that way wouldn’t be enough to gain trust due to insufficient evidence.
So as he spoke, Colin lifted his grey robe to reveal his current state: a pale and weak face, the left half covered in blood, with one eyeball sunken in, and traces of blood still seeping out.
When this scene came into view, everyone present, whether Helena, the old butler, or the guards, couldn’t help but gasp.
Colin looked much more miserable than when they had seen him during the day.
After a while, the old butler with greying temples broke the silence:
“What has… happened here?”
What has happened? Young and foolish, suffered for seeing what he shouldn’t have… Colin muttered to himself. Indeed, he had only looked out of habit and had not expected that glance to nearly cost him his life.
Of course, that wasn’t what he could say out loud. Taking a slight breath, with a grave expression, he said, “It’s the price paid for glimpsing the disaster that is about to unfold.
“Besides, there is one more thing that can confirm the veracity of my words…
“From now on, it will be impossible to leave the city. A powerful force has sealed it off, and you can try to go outside to verify it for yourselves.
“However, I advise against going now, as it would lead to us being discovered.”
After speaking, neither Helena nor the old butler spoke immediately.
After a few seconds, Colin was about to urge them when Helena said, “Please allow me to step away for a while before I can make a decision.”
I’ve already made it so clear, and still, she needs to consider? Doesn’t she know that time is life right now…
Without waiting for Colin to respond, Helena rose and walked into the study next door.
Upon entering the study, Helena turned to close the door and then took out a gold ring from a delicate pouch at her waist.
Embedded in the ring was a pure white crystal stone.
Helena put the ring on the middle finger of her right hand and then took out a piece of shaped gold, painted with a sun composed of a circle and straight lines.
Then, she bowed her head, clasped her hands in front of her chest in a praying gesture, and seemed to be chanting someone’s revered name.
Quickly, the piece of gold burned like a piece of paper, but what burned was a pure white radiance.
Helena rapidly reviewed in her mind the words she had just heard from Colin combined with the anomalies that had occurred that day.
Before long, a faint, pale light appeared on her, as if she were draped in a sacred, translucent veil.
“I sense the breath of catastrophe, yet I am still here, unable to leave easily, unable to provide much help…”
“There are some problems with his words, but they’re not important…”
“Assist him, he should have a solution, and can be trusted…”
“But the condition is, if possible, to save more people, regardless of their status, regardless of their nobility or commonness…”
“Of course, everything depends on the situation; no need to force it.”
A series of light, melodious, and divine-sounding female voices rose to her ear, making one’s heart feel at peace, unable to harbor any emotion.
“Yes, Your Grace.”
Helena responded in a low, devout voice, and when she opened her eyes again, the piece of gold seal on the desktop had completely evaporated.
She carefully removed the ring, put it back in her pocket, and then turned to walk out.
In the hall, several minutes had already passed, and Colin looked a bit better than before. At the sight of Helena coming out, he looked over at her.
“I will assist you with all matters, but I have one condition.”
“What condition?”
Colin asked curiously. Although he wondered why the noblewoman’s attitude had changed after a trip to the study, he couldn’t afford to dwell on that now.
“In this disaster, save as many people as possible.”
“Save more people?”
I can hardly save myself; how can I save more people? Are you overestimating me?
Do you really regard me as some almighty savior?
If I had that power, why would I even come to you?
If it weren’t that he needed her help, Colin would have liked to say, you might as well find someone more capable.
Seeing Colin frown, Helena continued, “Of course, it’s only about trying our best to do so; it’s okay if we really can’t save everyone.”
That makes more sense, Colin nodded, “I can only say I’ll do my best.”
Helena didn’t say anything more but went on, “What should we do next? What do I need to do?”
“Right now, our forces are too scattered, and the battle situation is not in our favor. We need to start by assembling our troops.”

chapters.title: Chapter 54 - 54 54 Summoning_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 54: Chapter 54: Summoning_1 Chapter 54: Chapter 54: Summoning_1 “Assembling forces will take some time, how soon will the disaster occur?”
Colin didn’t ponder the old butler’s words for too long and responded a few seconds later, “We have at least about seven hours to prepare, and how well we handle certain matters on this first day will determine if we can survive smoothly through the next seven days.”
“Seven days?” Helena interrupted, picking up on the term.
“Yes.”
Colin nodded, not waiting for a reply, and asked, “I have a question, during this time, do you have a way to seek assistance from the outside world?
“Like finding some ‘Virtue Knights’.”
If there was a “Humility” to act in concert, his pressure would be greatly reduced.
That kind of extremely reduced presence was just too BUG…
Most of the time, it really wouldn’t be noticed until a head was actually chopped off.
Unfortunately, Helena shook her head, “We cannot make contact, this place is indeed closed off by some kind of power, and we are no longer able to seek help from the outside world.
“Besides, you haven’t answered my question yet.”
“Alright then, forget it, I can’t explain too much as to why insisting on surviving seven days will ensure safety, but you just have to trust me—by then, I can guarantee the disaster will be resolved.”
After pausing, Colin continued,
“Now, we should quickly gather forces.”
Reluctant to speak, huh? It’s just as His Highness said, this man has many mysteries… Helena pondered briefly before saying, “The power of a city is usually managed jointly by the Church, the Knight Legion, and the City Lord, but currently, due to a cult’s affair, both the ‘Virtue Knight’ and the City Lord are absent. We can seek help from the Holy Healing Church, and I will help you contact Archbishop Laurenson stationed here…”
It’s this bishop that I’m worried about… Colin sighed and interrupted her, “If things go as anticipated, the source of the disaster will occur within the ‘Holy Healing Church’…”
“How could that be? The Holy Healing Church is supposed to be…”
Helena’s voice suddenly faltered as she spoke, only now realizing something was amiss when she combined it with Colin mentioning tomorrow’s disaster.
Immediately after, she realized that things had just gotten complicated.
That was a regional bishop!
On par with a member of the “Virtue Knights” who wielded one or two powers of virtue!
Underneath her gray hood, Helena’s expression grew serious. She was unclear about the specifics, but at this moment, her focus was not on questioning but on quickly thinking things through before she continued,
“Without considering the Church, we need the help of Warden Calder. Even though he’s just a regular warden, he has enough knowledge of Black Stone City. He was part of numerous missions to eradicate the Magic Fog when he was younger…
“He may not be the strongest in Black Stone City, but he has considerable prestige, which is why he was assigned to reception duties today. To understand more, it’s best to bring him here.”
“Then let’s fetch him quickly.”
Colin could no longer care about what might be exposed; to be honest, he actually had a fairly good impression of this warden.
After all, aside from being slippery and artful, there weren’t any major issues with him.
Before long, a portly middle-aged man with a beaming smile on his face arrived at the small inn. Just as he walked in, he sensed the heavy atmosphere and then noticed the familiar figure from the afternoon seated there.
Helena repeated the information about the disaster to him but did not mention the Church.
After listening, Warden Calder’s eyebrows twitched, and he suddenly thought of something. Although still uncertain, he cooperatively replied, “A terrible disaster? This catastrophe couldn’t have come at a worse time…
“Knight Ail has taken his elite away, and the City Lord also mobilized a portion of the town’s guards. Currently, including the city defense and various other soldiers, we barely have a total of seventeen hundred men. Therefore, I suggest that Miss Helena…
“You could use your rights as a noble to request assistance from Archbishop Laurenson. As far as I know, although he is not a primary combatant, his realm is sufficiently high. Even “Virtue Knight” Ail Knight might not be able to confront him. It would be much easier with him intervening.”
“Indeed, we do need to visit Bishop Laurenson next, but before that, we need to make some preparations, preparations for potential conflicts that may arise.”
“Conflicts?”
What kind of conflicts could arise? Calder was taken aback, about to say something, when he suddenly sensed that something was amiss, and quickly realized there was something deeper at play.
Miss Helena was not unaware of the situation in Black Stone City; knowing about the disaster, her first port of call ought to have been the Church to seek help.
Yet, in our conversation just now, this noble lady prompted me to contact other defense forces and subtly suggested that I take charge, while she didn’t mention the Church, which would obviously be the best to contact. Then there’s the matter of the conflicts…
Considering this, and recalling the recent events surrounding Beast Transformation Syndrome, Calder—whose sensitivity to matters outstripped Helena’s—suddenly had a bold but not very clear idea—
The disaster is related to the Holy Healing Church!
As Warden Calder’s mind was whirling, Colin spoke up, “The first thing we should do is to check Bishop Laurenson’s status. We need ample preparation and strength because the disaster probably originates from there.”
Just as I expected, there’s something wrong with the Holy Healing Church!
Calder was struck with a feeling of surprise that was not entirely unexpected, as if a weight had finally been lifted from his heart—he had long harbored suspicions about the Holy Healing Church.
He then realized that the simultaneous departure of Knight Ail and the City Lord was probably not solely attributable to the Gluttonous Feast; these people were likely causing trouble behind the scenes.
But before he could say anything, an epiphany flashed through Warden Calder’s mind. Hearing Colin’s voice, he suddenly remembered something and looked at Colin with a ghost-seen expression—
It was you, you little rascal that cost me a year’s salary and made me lie in bed for a couple of days unable to set foot on the ground!
“You, you are…”
“At times like this, let’s not worry about those things. We had better deal with the ‘Holy Healing Church’ first.”
Having been previously admonished, Helena now spoke up, “I am willing to vouch for Lord Colin in the name of the Heddon Family.”
As soon as she spoke, the most intense reaction came from the old butler standing behind her, but before he could say anything, he was cut off by a wave of Helena’s hand.
The Heddon Family, indeed it is them. This way, even if there are issues, they cannot be blamed on me. What can I do in the face of these nobles other than agree?… Calder mused to himself, standing up with a pleasing smile on his face and a bow of the head, he uttered, “Yes.”
He did not hesitate in the slightest with his self-effacing compliance, because at this moment, even if the City Lord or Knight Ail were here, he could only say, “Yes, Miss Helena.”
“Take this and gather a group of people. In the process, we must not alert the Holy Healing Church.”
Helena handed over an exquisite badge, engraved with a half-man, half-horse creature, to Warden Calder.
Taking the badge with extreme caution, Calder confirmed its authenticity and then turned to leave, ready to swiftly inform some of Black Stone City’s other officers and the like.
‘Miss Helena’s status seems to be even more distinguished than I thought. When she brought up the Heddon Family, the warden seemed quite shocked.’ Colin thought to himself, sitting on a soft fur-covered chair.
Meanwhile, the aged butler who stood behind Helena inadvertently glanced at her draped in a grey robe. Recalling her skeptical approach to the study and then her one-sided attitude after coming out, he couldn’t help but sigh softly to himself.

chapters.title: Chapter 55 - 55 55 Do Not Question God_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 55: Chapter 55 Do Not Question God_1 Chapter 55: Chapter 55 Do Not Question God_1 Using the “Heddon Family” as a guarantor was no trivial matter.
In the old butler’s view, this “Colin” was shrouded in mystery, using unknown methods from a non-majority church, possibly a member of some dangerous secret organization.
Yet she did not hesitate to vouch for him in the name of “family,” which could lead to serious consequences for Miss Helena if the family pursued accountability.
Clearly, it was all because of the Saintess Her Highness.
Perhaps, the formerly proud and cold Miss Helena, indifferent to everything, had really been trained by the Saintess Her Highness into obedient submission…
For her, she had fallen into danger several times, nearly losing her life.
Alas.
The old butler sighed quietly, hoping only that once he returned to the family, he could report the situation to the City Lord who might be able to resolve it.
And now, as a butler, all he could do was to obey.
On the other side, Colin, oblivious to these thoughts, was constantly pondering his next move, crafting his plan for the upcoming challenge.
The living room fell quiet for a moment.
It wasn’t until ten or so minutes later that footsteps could be heard from the street, and Warden Calder, accompanied by a dozen people, came upstairs.
“Miss Helena, one thousand seven hundred and sixty defenders of Black Stone City are willing to follow your commands,” said Warden Calder.
Hearing these people declare their loyalty, Colin on the other side began to arrange—
It wasn’t so much an arrangement.
It was to ambush a group of people outside the “Holy Healing Church,” then they would come up with an excuse to enter inside the “Holy Healing Church” to see if they would be allowed through.
The rest of the soldiers would head to the City Lord’s residence in Black Stone City, where they could retreat to the small castle of the City Lord’s family if things didn’t go well with the Holy Healing Church incident.
“What about the ordinary people?” Helena opened mouth to ask, noticing that ordinary people did not seem to be included in Colin’s arrangements.
“The disaster will not erupt too intensely at the first moment. At that point, we can try to save as many people as possible, exactly how many is just a matter of doing our best.”
Colin replied, had it not been for the demands of saving people, he had even entertained the idea of letting a majority perish in a fire to tackle the problem at its root.
Because doing so would fundamentally prevent the outbreak of “Beast Transformation Syndrome.”
By this time, he had learned that in this world, during The Night, even those Virtue Knights or Bishops, if exposed outdoors without any light or fire for too long, would die immediately.
No one knew what would happen the moment darkness enveloped them…
Because almost everyone who tried ended up dead, leaving nothing behind but bloodstains.
However, putting that idea aside, perhaps catching a couple of Holy Healing Priests later to figure out how Beast Transformation Syndrome actually spreads could also solve the problem…
Shaking his head, Colin reined in the surging thoughts in his heart, then stood up and went out the door with Helena and the others.
At that moment, downstairs, a dozen people were ready, holding lanterns and swords at their waists.
Without further communication, under the escort of their guards, Colin and Helena headed towards the largest “Great Cathedral of Holy Healing” in Black Stone City.
Fifteen minutes later, Colin saw the cathedral, which seemed somewhat similar to a “Church of Light” cathedral but decorated largely in red, with a symbol of a praying person holding a cup in their hands.
Outside the church, Colin saw five or six unusually tall figures robed in white with silver masks and bearing huge iron swords measuring one meter seventy-eight in length.
Beneath their cult robes, the iron boots of their lower limbs faintly suggested that they were armed to the teeth.
From these few, Colin felt a very strong sense of threat.
“What on earth do these people eat to grow so strong?” Colin mumbled to himself, grateful for the moment that they merely seemed to be extremely robust.
All muscle.
A single bullet would suffice to disable half their combat effectiveness.
And this time, he did not come alone….
With just one cannon strike, Calder would lead at least five hundred soldiers to charge forth.
However, more oppressive than these people to Colin’s heart was the invisible presence within the church that made him feel suppressed.
This suppression originated from the “Beast Transformation Syndrome” within him, from something even higher in rank.
At this moment, as soon as Colin and his companions arrived, a church cleric, also dressed in white cult robes and a pure silver mask, slender in build, stepped forward.
“Who are you?”
The old butler stepped up, “I am of the Heddon Family, and this lady is Helena Heddon, the third daughter of the Heddon Family. We have urgent matters that require an audience with Archbishop Laurenson, please go and inform him immediately.”
“The Heddon Family?”
Father Alenna, who originally intended to send the visitors away, was taken aback. He had not expected an offspring of such important stature to appear here, akin to a country farmer meeting a royal minister.
After a few seconds of shock, just as he began to doubt, he saw the other party present a badge depicting a centaur…
The spiritual imprint on it made him feel as if he were standing before a towering beast holding a black scythe, surrounded by an endless aura of death.
It was a massive fog formed from the congregation of countless departed souls…
A mythological centaur creature who was said to have fought alongside the King of Knights, carving out a kingdom upon this dark land!
Beneath its feet were the bones of countless dead, a testament to its exploits.
While Father Alenna was lost in the vision for a moment, a ray of Purification Light emerged on his body, and all the illusions disappeared…
Only then did he snap back from the shock of the momentary glance.
It’s true!
Damn it!
Why would the offspring of such an influential figure appear in this place?
Father Alenna roared.
“I…”
Under normal circumstances, Father Alenna would find it difficult to refuse the request of such an important person’s offspring, but now, the Archbishop’s ritual was ongoing and could not be disturbed!
“I apologize for the offense, but Archbishop Laurenson is dealing with important matters and cannot meet with you.”
With great determination in his voice, Father Alenna spoke, gesturing with his hand as he did so.
Behind him, several towering Sanctuary Punishers reached for the large swords on their backs, and at that moment, the atmosphere dropped to freezing point.
“Are you sure you want to refuse my request? Are you questioning my identity?”
Helena’s icy voice rang out, “Is that how I should interpret this? You are questioning my identity! Questioning the authenticity of this badge?”
“No, I wouldn’t dare question the legitimacy of your identity, but right now, Archbishop Laurenson is devising a way to solve the key issue of the Beast Transformation Syndrome, and it cannot be disrupted.”
Father Alenna’s forehead was covered in cold sweat, and at that moment, he did not use any excuses to claim the badge was fake or such.
Because even if he killed Helena, there probably wouldn’t be a problem, but questioning the authenticity of that badge was almost equivalent to questioning the mythological creature itself.
It was a strong act of blasphemy that really could trigger something to happen…
You must not question God!
Even if it is just a Sub-God.
Meanwhile, Colin was about to give the signal for the “Axemen” to summon five hundred soldiers, but a sudden disturbance occurred.
A scream suddenly emanated from within the church.

chapters.title: Chapter 56 - 56 56 Stage Three Beast Transformation
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 56: Chapter 56: Stage Three Beast Transformation Syndrome_1 Chapter 56: Chapter 56: Stage Three Beast Transformation Syndrome_1 “Enemies!”
Shouts erupted from the massive church, urgent peals of bells sounding simultaneously from within.
Meanwhile, a cacophony of screams, roars, and the clash of metal upon metal emanated from inside.
Clearly, a battle had burst forth in an instant.
Colin and his companions looked at each other in bewilderment, clearly uninvolved in the unfolding situation inside.
“Damn! What’s happened? How could enemies have suddenly entered?”
Father Alenna glanced at Helena and the others, noting their apparent shock, and realizing they seemed unaware of the interior situation.
“If you can guarantee that under no circumstances will you interfere with Bishop Laurenson’s ritual, I can take you inside. Please, regardless of anything, trust that our ultimate purpose is to solve ‘Beast Transformation Syndrome’ and… save more people!”
Upon hearing the noise from within, Father Alenna gritted his teeth and ultimately made this decision.
As he spoke, he glanced over the shoulders of the group, catching faint glimpses of figures moving in the streets beyond.
He worried that if he didn’t grant passage, these people might forcibly break through, which would only lead to greater chaos and trouble.
“I will have Mr. Colin and some guards go in my stead. If they encounter Bishop Laurenson, Mr. Colin will act on my behalf.”
Helena raised a hand, pointing toward Colin, who was clad in a grey robe.
Agitated like an ant on a hot pan, Father Alenna could not afford to dwell on it any longer. In such a situation, it was indeed not suitable for nobility to enter.
“That’s acceptable, as long as you can make that promise.”
“Rest assured, we’re mainly here to look. We absolutely won’t interfere unless necessary.”
Colin stepped forward to speak, and inwardly he added…
The precondition is that there really is no problem inside.
He too was curious about these sudden intruders and who they might be, daring to interfere at such a time.
The “Book of Fate” had mentioned that before him, others had tried to deal with that “Him,” but he had always thought these people should be Warden Calder and his allies…
Now that these individuals stood on his side, it was clear his previous guess was incorrect.
Furthermore, he had noticed something else—a seemingly scant understanding of “Beastification” on the part of Father Alenna.
“Alright, follow us, but only your group may come.”
Finally conceding, Father Alenna turned and hurried towards the massive church, resembling a palace, with the church’s armed forces following closely behind him.
“Keep up.”
Colin, along with Tang Ken and several guards, followed behind them.
“Being one-eyed does make things a bit difficult to adapt to, but luckily, I can still ‘see’ by relying on my nose…”
Colin sniffed the air as various scents flooded in, forming a picture in his mind.
The battle seemed to be taking place in a large hall behind the church, where the Holy Healing Church’s guards were clashing with a group of odd invaders… the oddness stemming from the fact that…
“Mmm, how tantalizing, what’s with these people?”
A strong sense of hunger welled up in Colin’s stomach, an impatient desire to lay eyes on those treats… no, those people.
Before long, as they crossed the church’s atrium and turned into a hall through a side entrance, Colin observed the chaotic scene within, his expression turning bemused.
He saw a horde of short but sturdy individuals continuously charging towards the church’s rear doors.
They appeared to be an angry mob from outside the city, though it was unclear how they had made it inside.
Scattered across the floor were numerous bodies lying in disarray.
Among the crowd, Colin spotted a particularly conspicuous person, thin in stature, with a red and yellow silk-forged gown draped diagonally across his shoulder, exposing the upper half of his left chest.
He had no hair upon his head, but it was covered with growths that resembled fatty tumors, densely packed together like clusters of flesh.
A strong and incomparable scent of meat radiated from him, and upon smelling it, Colin rapidly salivated, developing a strong desire to eat.
“Eat him!”
“Eat him!”
“Eat him!”
In his mind, bloodthirsty thoughts bubbled up.
Colin tried hard to suppress this absurd notion, biting his tongue, and a sharp pain spread from his mouth, which finally subdued his eating urge, and his right eye regained rationality.
At the same time, when he saw the other, that person seemed to sense something, turned to glance at Colin, but after a mere glimpse, he averted his gaze.
“Damn it, what kind of walking humanoid pastry is this guy? What’s going on with him?”
Colin, observing the individual whose style clashed with the locale, understood why Tang Ken had mentioned seeing a traveler before.
In this perfectly good fantasy world, how did a monk manage to barge in?
The only explanation seemed to be “transmigration.”
At that moment, upon arriving here, Father Alenna quickly assessed the situation, immediately led his people to charge, and engaged with that group.
“What do we do?” Tang Ken’s message came through Colin’s mind.
Colin frowned. His original plan was to find and ally with those who had broken in, to work together and see if they could get to the root of the problem.
However, now that he had seen that fellow, he felt that they likely weren’t on the same path.
Still, even if they weren’t on the same path, their current objective was presumably to open the large door that led to the rear.
“Find a way to open that door at the far end, deal with the rest on the fly…”
Colin had an idea, his goal was to see if he could strike “him” with a Bone Spur.
Even if it didn’t kill, it could severely wound the monster, buying himself time.
However, just as he was about to act, a heavy set of footsteps thundered from behind the church’s door.
Without waiting for anyone to react…
With a “bang,” the door at the rear of the church was smashed open from the inside out by a formidable force.
This sudden event seemed to catch everyone off guard; they all just stared dumbfounded at the breached door, peering into the darkness beyond.
It wasn’t until a monstrous figure emerged, accompanied by the sound of dragging chains, that everyone gasped.
“Hiss… damn it.”
Colin’s heart skipped a beat, watching as a monster taller than three meters with a massive physique and body covered in coarse long fur, resembling a giant beast, stepped out.
As it appeared, an air of tyrannous bloodlust burst forth within the church!
At this very moment, an inspiration flashed across Colin’s mind.
The creature before his eyes…
It was at least a horrendous beast with the aura of third-stage “Beastification”!
No, it seemed even more than that!
But, if it were just that, it wouldn’t be unmanageable.

chapters.title: Chapter 57: Chapter 57: Misjudgment_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 57: Chapter 57: Misjudgment_1 Chapter 57: Chapter 57: Misjudgment_1 Colin sized up the variety of items on his person and the people present, concluding that there was a chance to take on a third-stage “Beast Transformation Syndrome.”
Without delay, he took out the golden card, held the bone spur filled with black cracks in his right hand, ready to spring into action, planning to first stick it with a DEbuff Continuous Needle.
“Indeed, coming here ahead of time does present an opportunity to stop everything.”
As this thought just emerged, he heard the three-stage “Beast Transformation Syndrome” patient violently emit a deafening, inhuman roar.
Hearing the roar, Colin was startled, not because the sound was horrifying.
But because the roar conveyed one message…
“Run!”
“Run?”
As he wondered, Colin’s scalp tingled, his eyes widened with horror as he saw a monstrous hand, devoid of skin, its blood vessels and muscles exposed to the air, reach out from behind the pitch-black door.
The hand effortlessly grabbed the “Beast Transformation Syndrome” monster, which was roaring, like picking up a rag doll and dragged it back into the darkness behind the door.
Craaaack, crunch…
From the shadows beyond the door, the sound of chewing and swallowing echoed, and rapidly approached the door. Before long, everyone saw a gigantic beastly face appear behind it.
The three to four meters high church door could only reveal the upper half of its face.
In the half-face’s constantly chewing mouth, the three-stage Beast Transformation Syndrome—just like a small rat bitten in a cat’s mouth—was evident as the creature that had rushed out to warn the others to flee.
“Damn! What the hell kind of monster is this?!”
Colin was profoundly shaken, feeling as though he himself was the little rat under the bed, with a huge head stretching down from above.
He couldn’t even begin to imagine the massive body of that flesh-and-blood, skinless goliath behind the door.
Not only him, but everyone present was also stunned by this terrifying scene.
Some even lost their strength and collapsed…
Run!
The only thought possible in Colin’s mind was to escape.
He was even starting to doubt the “Book of Fate,” which had indicated that after fighting desperately with the monster, he would ultimately escape. Could he actually have a physical altercation with this thing?
Perhaps the premonition was too flattering towards him…
However, before Colin could even move to flee, a figure broke the terrifying silence before anyone else, the peculiar man in red who seemed like an outsider, as if he had not arrived through company channels.
The man in red quickly rushed towards the colossal half-face emerging behind the door, his hands pressed together in a prayer-like gesture.
His speed was like that of a cheetah.
Just as Colin thought he had some trump card to counter the monster that was probably larger than a three to five-story building, the man in red leapt and plunged into the mouth of the giant beast behind the door.
Crunch, crunch…
The skinless beast’s lower jaw masticated, and the man in red was crushed like a sugary tangerine, his bright red juices spilling all over the ground.
Buddy, are you here to be a clown?
Colin didn’t know whether to laugh or cry, unable to comprehend the perplexing human behavior.
But before he could think further, a strong sense of crisis welled up within him.
In that moment, Colin realized something and without any hesitation, he used “Time Stasis.”
Almost simultaneously, a giant, flesh-exposed hand, much like a train emerging from a tunnel, stretched forth from behind the three-meter-tall door.
It extended dozens of meters in an instant, aiming straight for Colin at the center of the hall.
Its speed was so fast that most people couldn’t react…
Some people in front of Colin were merely touched and died on the spot.
But as it reached within fifteen meters, the entire arm’s speed suddenly slowed, clearly under the influence of “Time Stasis.”
“It can be confirmed as Beast Transformation Syndrome, but this limb extension… Is it a new ability?”
Colin glanced at the huge blood-red beast’s claw without much thought, grabbed Tang Ken’s shoulder beside him, and quickly retreated.
As for the other guards, he simply couldn’t afford to care about them right now.
Ratatatat…
The moment the Time Stop effect wore off, the giant palm slammed down causing a noticeable vibration in the entire Church hall.
“Run!”
After dodging the sudden attack, Colin turned and ran without a moment’s hesitation.
When the wind is tight, it’s time to bolt!
The situation had somewhat exceeded his expectations; the enemy was far more terrifying than he had imagined.
He had assumed his opponent would be a creature affected by Beast Transformation Syndrome, likely in the third stage or perhaps a bit higher.
But seeing just the tip of the iceberg that emerged from behind the door, it seemed that the creature’s size alone likely exceeded ten meters.
Not something that could be dealt with by ordinary means…
Indeed, only such a form could match the description “an unimaginably terrifying life form.”
And only such a form could enforce a complete lock down of an entire city.
Colin felt that to deal with a creature of this size, they would probably need to deploy the military, tanks, fighter jets, and whatnot.
No, even then it might not be enough to kill it, because it also had the ability “Deadly Insight”, making it extremely difficult to achieve a one-hit kill.
“Bishop Laurenson has failed! At all costs, control it! It must not be allowed to leave, or the whole Southern Border will face a horrific catastrophe!”
The roar of Father Alenna came from behind.
Colin was somewhat surprised to hear this voice, and at that moment, he realized…
The battle mentioned in the Book of Fate had been fought by these priests, who likely had prepared for failure even before the ceremony began.
That’s why the unprecedented Beast Transformation Syndrome monster had been bound within the hall, unable to escape for now.
But this was only temporary…
Colin could see that the monster was currently in an incomplete state.
Once it reached its full form, he feared nothing in the town would be able to contain it any longer!
“It’s impossible to start with the monster itself, need to find a way to control the outbreak of Beast Transformation Syndrome outside; at the very least, find the cause of the outbreak!”
As Colin ran wildly, he made rapid decisions in his mind.
However, halfway through his escape, he realized something was off.
The Holy Healing Church’s members weren’t running, which was one thing, but why weren’t the rioters running either?

chapters.title: Chapter 58: Strengthen_1
chapters.content:
Chapter 58: Strengthen_1
“Could it be that those people were sent here on purpose?”
Colin harbored a suspicion; aside from the guy who had slipped and provided a sizable meal for the monstrous creature, the other rioters hadn’t been attacked and some could have easily escaped.
Yet it seemed as if not one had fled. In fact, they appeared rather excited, charging forward as if they were deliberately seeking their own demise.
Colin couldn’t help but suspect they were sent intentionally.
Moreover, it looked like they used some secret passage to get in, which would have been nearly impossible without someone from inside the Church to guide them.
On top of that, there was the “Gluttonous Feast” that drew people away.
All of this hinted at a bigger scheme that had been set up behind the scenes, one that they were witnessing unfold, incomprehensible as it might be to them and likely part of the plan.
But before he could think further, another violent vibration came from behind, chunks of cracking stone falling from the ceiling. Colin promptly adjusted his position, narrowly avoiding the fallout.
“Forget it, no matter what their plans and conspiracies are, when facing a monster of that size, all I can do is choose to trust,” he thought.
Colin felt that there was a chance the Bonfire Company would directly intervene, as described in the mission briefing.
He had a fair amount of trust in the Company’s capabilities to handle the terrifying creature within the church, except for the Descent Protocol.
God knows if they actually intervened, how far off course things might go because of that protocol…
Hopefully, the Company would prove effective when the time came…
Colin took a deep breath, adjusted his breathing, and continued walking. He soon left the crumbling church behind and escaped to the outside.
Aside from Tang Ken, of the six guards who had initially set out with him, only two remained. Behind him, some panicked Church personnel were also scrambling out.
“What happened?”
No sooner had Colin emerged than Helena and others surrounded him, with several hundred soldiers following behind her, faces filled with horror as they observed the church that was still sending out vibrations.
What on earth could cause such earth-shaking rumbles?
“Run first,”
Colin didn’t waste words; a single phrase conveyed his attitude.
On the way, he quickly and briefly shared with Helena what he had witnessed inside the church.
“A formless entity over ten meters tall?”
The old butler’s face mirrored disbelief, a chill running down his spine as if recalling the giant beings emerging from the Magic Fog during the Mist Disaster and the fear they inspired.
And the one in the church was probably even more terrifying than those from the Mist Disaster.
“It wants to sacrifice everyone in the entire city to truly descend? Such a grand-scale ritual… Has Laurenson lost his mind? Does he not realize what he’s summoning?”
The old butler cursed: “An Evil God could be summoned because of this!”
“It’s likely that he orchestrated everything, but it’s too late to discuss that now. That thing, as it stands, is not something we can handle,”
Colin and the others made their way quickly towards the castle structure in the city’s center: “At least for the next few days, it should not be able to break through. Our main issue now is handling the common people infected with Beast Transformation Syndrome.”
On this front, he also had no clue why regular people were suddenly falling ill.
Warden Calder, who was accompanying the group, spoke up: “I’ll take some of the Holy Healing Church members in for questioning later. I don’t believe they’ve come up with absolutely nothing over these past few months… ”
“Good.”
Colin nodded. Whether it was finding the source of infection, methods of protection, or even just identifying who was infected with “Beastification” beforehand, any of these three methods were vitally important to him!
If these were not possible, saving people in the upcoming actions would be nothing but a harm to himself.
Suddenly, a towering figure emerged from an alley and blocked their path.
A pair of eyes glowed with a greenish light, staring at the group.
“Mid-to-Late First Stage ‘Beastification’.”
Warden Calder, standing nearby, saw a tall, skinny man who gripped a cross sword in his right hand, his body crouching as he focused on the monster, “Leave it to me!”
As soon as he finished speaking, he didn’t wait for the warden beside him to intervene. He surged forward, fast as an accelerating cheetah, and in an instant, he was at the monster’s side.
His sword swung, aiming to behead the “Beastification” sufferer.
“This sudden burst move is somewhat interesting…”
Colin silently assessed, hoping to learn it if the opportunity arose.
His current strength relied entirely on various artifacts, and what belonged to his body itself was not significant.
However, just as he finished his assessment, an abrupt change occurred ahead of him.
Bang.
Crack.
The clear sound of breaking bones echoed.
The tall, skinny man screamed, his body flying backward. His right hand was broken, dangling from his chest by skin and flesh, and as for the sword, it had already fallen to the ground.
But he couldn’t worry about that now; seeing the Beast Transformation Syndrome sufferer that had just countered successfully and was now lunging at him, he held his breath, his pupils shrinking.
Bang!
In that moment, a glimmer of light appeared behind him, and a bullet entered the enemy’s forehead.
The Beast Transformation Syndrome sufferer’s attack came to an abrupt halt, but he didn’t fall; instead, his body stiffened in place.
Then another robust figure rushed out; it was Calder, whose fat had transformed into muscle.
Dragging his heavy sword, he cleaved the monster in two on the spot.
“What are you still hiding there for?”
Colin scolded the one who was still in a daze, putting away his smoking revolver. He frowned, looking at the Beast Transformation Syndrome sufferer with the bullet hole in his forehead.
Others might not have grasped what had just happened.
But Colin saw it quite clearly; the mid-to-late first-stage Beast Transformation Syndrome sufferer had narrowly ducked his head a step earlier, narrowly avoiding the decapitating strike.
In the ensuing counterattack, had the tall, skinny man not reacted promptly, he might have been impaled through the heart by the creature’s hand.
And the ability used by the Beast Transformation Syndrome sufferer was something he was familiar with—”Deadly Insight”!
It could allow a person to detect a fatal attack coming one or two seconds in advance.
In life-or-death combat, this ability was simply a killer move.
Its weakness was also quite prominent: with short, frequent, deadly threats, it could not provide insight, and it wouldn’t work when the mind was affected.
When fighting the Human Patchwork Monster, Colin had his “Deadly Insight” disrupted by a psychic attack. For someone prepared and aware, this passive ability wasn’t difficult to counter.
However, that wasn’t the key point; the key was that Colin remembered that mid-to-late first-stage “Beastification” shouldn’t have such an ability!
“Could it be that because of that thing’s appearance, all of the ‘Beastification’ have been enhanced?”
While Colin speculated inwardly, Calder also came to the side of his assistant, pulling him up, “I told you, don’t go rushing in like that. Even if you don’t think about yourself, you should at least think about your dad. He most likely wouldn’t want to see his son die the same way he did…”
“Thank you,” the assistant said, not saying much else.
“You should thank that guy…”
Warden Calder pointed to Colin; it was largely due to Colin’s timely intervention that he could rescue the man in one piece.
Even though he already knew Colin’s identity at this moment, there still was an unbroken veil of pretense between them.
And at this time, other places were filled with more screams and low growls.

chapters.title: Chapter 59 - 59 59 Hunger_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 59: Chapter 59 “Hunger”_1 Chapter 59: Chapter 59 “Hunger”_1 “Let’s get moving.”
Colin sniffed the air, detecting various scents, and could clearly sense the presence of Beast Transformation Syndrome all over the city.
The number was growing more and more.
Moreover, due to the ongoing ritual, the Beast Transformation Syndrome had become stronger than usual.
When he reached the former City Lord’s home, Colin immediately ordered the questioning of the church officials from the Holy Healing Church who had just fled with him.
Soon, he learned some news.
“The infection mechanism of ‘Beastification’ is still unclear, but one thing is certain; it’s very likely to erupt in people who feel extremely hungry and can’t find food.”
“Therefore, ‘Beastification’ mostly happens outside the city, and only a small part inside, because as long as there is enough food to fill the stomach, the probability of illness is low.”
“And under this extreme hunger, if emotions run high, like rage, then the possibility of an outbreak is even higher.”
Extreme hunger plus intense negative emotions?
Colin hadn’t expected the symptoms to erupt so simply, and he now understood why it was usually said to only break out among the poorer populations.
Because only those who couldn’t satisfy their hunger would face such trouble.
“It targets the weak, no wonder the ‘Book of Fate’ mentioned a massive outbreak of Beast Transformation Syndrome among the refugees outside the city tomorrow…”
Colin sat in a room in the castle, sighed, and looked at the Holy Healing Church officials tied up by the soldiers:
“Besides that, what exactly is ‘Beastification’? Is it something you are spreading?”
“No, we’re not sure where it came from either. Besides hunger, coming into contact with too much blood from Beast Transformation Syndrome patients, or accidentally allowing it to seep into wounds, can also lead to infection, as happened to Father Laurenson.”
“So, according to you, as long as people are well-fed, a large-scale outbreak of ‘Beastification’ can be prevented?”
“Yes, if people are not hungry, the likelihood of infection will be reduced.”
Hearing this, Colin paused for a moment and then turned to Warden Calder: “How many more days can the city’s food supply last?”
“If all the food in the city were collected and provided only to the people in the castle, even if we add another ten thousand people, it could last at least half a month…”
Colin waved his hand to cut him off: “No, I mean the entire Black Stone City as well as the refugees outside.”
“Then… if distributed smoothly, about a week.”
After a pause, Warden Calder added, “But that’s almost impossible, there are tens of thousands of people in the city, and nearly as many outside…”
He implied that such a massive distribution task could not possibly go well on the spot.
Having participated in various punitive campaigns and been responsible for logistics, Calder knew very well that such distribution was extremely difficult.
There would surely be people hoarding food, there would be uneven distribution…
If those inside knew that their food was being allocated to the undesirable refugees outside the city, it would only trigger a terrible riot.
Moreover, the constant fear imposed by “Beastification” would only add to the chaos.
“This is troublesome. If we can’t distribute the food well, and if those people all turn into beasts, we probably won’t be able to withstand it…”
Colin couldn’t help but pinch the bridge of his nose, as he was not familiar with this sort of thing and could not provide effective advice.
He also hadn’t expected that in dealing with these ‘Beastification’ cases, his biggest problem wouldn’t be how to kill them, but the shortage of supplies.
If handled poorly and famine ensued, it would directly lead to a large-scale outbreak of “Beastification.”
This thing, one or two might not be so bad…
But once the numbers increased, and considering there was no escape, it would be a deadlock situation.
“Do your best, while ensuring our own food supply.”
Pausing momentarily, Helena added, “The conversations here are strictly forbidden from being leaked. If I find out, I will hang whoever is responsible.”
“Now, have those soldiers start going out to collect food, and stop any gluttonous behavior with the severest of measures.”
“Yes.”
Warden Calder said nothing more. Under normal circumstances, he would certainly try to push these troublesome matters onto others.
But at such a time, he too was deeply involved, and he was indeed a ‘tall man’.
So, he was even less inclined to entrust the matter to anyone else.
He had already attempted to send people outside the city to try, and now it was truly sealed off, with no escape possible.
“Rest assured, once this crisis is over, I will ask my father to convey your achievements to His Majesty the King and have you made a member of the ‘Virtue Knights’.”
“Yes.”
Calder nodded, took his leave with a quick stride.
“I’ll go too.”
Colin was somewhat uneasy and followed, intending to see how they would handle the situation.
If he didn’t take action, he would feel a strong sense of unease.
It was as if he could feel the Holy Healing Church’s entity constantly watching him…
“Your Excellency, are you certain that after seven days, the situation will truly take a turn for the better?” Calder couldn’t help but ask out of skepticism, as he honestly doubted the claim.
Because he really couldn’t imagine any way to deal with the creature that might have been summoned by an ancient god summoning ritual.
But… it seemed that the man before him was the only exception since “Beastification” had begun to appear.
His case was just as mysterious…
After escaping from the dungeon, he inexplicably returned, and then miraculously reverted to his normal human form.
He then began to speak as though he was the savior, claiming that the crisis would be resolved within a few days.
Honestly, if it wasn’t for Helena, a noble heir vouching for him, Colin would have seemed the most suspicious.
According to him, if they just waited a few days, in an unrestricted situation, the entity within the church might fully descend.
At that time, there would be nothing that could stop it.
Everybody would die, without exception!
Better to try and fight while they still had the chance.
“I can’t tell you the specifics, but you just need to believe that when the time comes, the problem will be effectively resolved,” said Colin, who himself did not dare to make promises too confidently.
He was unclear on how the Bonfire Company planned to intervene, unsure whether they would deal with the issue directly or once again use him as a means to solve it.
One thing he was certain of was that in a few days, he would be able to return to reality.
Then, he needed to rush to consult his colleagues at the company: in an era of cold weapons, how to deal with a terrestrial creature likely larger than a blue whale.
And then, during those seven days, he should work hard to improve himself, possibly acquiring some lethal weapons.
Before long, a thousand soldiers within the castle were divided into over a dozen teams, moving throughout various parts of the city.
Their single purpose was to collect food.
Meanwhile, Colin took a group of people loaded with a large quantity of food, heading straight for the city gates, planning to start by attempting to address the refugee problem outside the city.

chapters.title: Chapter 60 - 60 60 Relief and Manifestation of Holiness_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 60: Chapter 60 Relief and Manifestation of Holiness_1 Chapter 60: Chapter 60 Relief and Manifestation of Holiness_1 “First, summon some of the leaders among them and then make unified arrangements to distribute food,”
Colin began attempting to make contact with these refugees, having known beforehand that most refugees tended to form groups, with apparent leaders among them.
If he truly wanted to launch a relief effort, it was best to start with these individuals, persuade them, and then, through them, reach out to the refugees behind them to deliver effective aid.
Otherwise, trying to assist everyone at once would definitely lead to utter chaos.
Moreover, Colin set the initial relief group at around a thousand people. He planned to save these individuals first and then use food as a lure to let them “share” the good news with others.
In this way, he could achieve the goal of “saving one to inspire the saving of many,” and spread the word widely.
Of course, this was Tang Ken’s advice.
Colin planned to follow it.
However, there had to be some selectivity in choosing the refugees. At his suggestion, Colin had soldiers who were normally garrisoned outside the city pick out individuals.
These soldiers, who manned their posts year-round, understood the refugee groups better than most.
Soon, a group of refugees was selected from the crowd. Perhaps due to their higher status, they seemed to be in noticeably better condition than the others.
Although still dressed as refugees, their attire was not as wretched—they wore a tangle of tattered, indifferent scraps of cloth.
At that moment, they did not dare to meet Colin’s gaze, standing beside him apprehensively and respectfully.
“If it weren’t for the refugees, I would have thought they were a beggar gang…”
Colin murmured in his heart, then announced his intention to promise bread to everyone, but only those who were sincerely in need would receive the boon of food.
Next, he casually picked a dozen or so “sincere people” and distributed several wagonloads of bread on the spot.
The group of refugees, witnessing this scene, were suddenly taken aback—was this for real?
In the past, “nobles” would occasionally show great charity, but it was usually empty talk without any follow-through, tricking them into mining labor. Although there really was food in the mines, the work was likely to kill them from exhaustion.
Who would have thought that this one would start by distributing food…
As the wagons loaded with dark bread parked nearby, some less “sincere” individuals looked on with envious eyes.
“Thank you, my lord! Praise be to you, my lord! I will go now and call over people from our tribe…”
“I will too, praise be to you, my lord…”
“Sweet holy water! Crisp bread!”
Colin, hearing their praises, nodded with a smile and a kind look on his face.
The bread was, of course, the kind of dark bread that made him feel nauseous, and the “holy water” was a type of concentrate brought by Tang Ken which, when added to well water, tasted sweet.
Compared to Colin and Li Ming, Tang Ken clearly understood better what kind of food should be brought along.
So, in addition to the basic provisions for a few days, he also brought several bottles of the most important thing—a mix of nutritional supplements and high-concentration sugar syrup as a concentrated liquid.
The nutrient-deprived refugee leaders felt an immediate revitalization and a surge of strength with just one sip, leading them to believe it was holy water blessed by the divine. They fell in love with the taste of this scientific concoction: cheap dietary fiber mixed with a high volume of vitamins diluted in the concentrated syrup.
With each gulp, what reached their bellies was all science and hard work!
Of course, amidst the praise, there were a few discordant voices—
“You must be sent by the ‘Light Saintess’ herself to save us. I knew it, I knew it. Praise to you, praise to the Saintess.”
Uh, Her Saintess? Why not thank nature’s bounty instead?
Colin’s smile held a trace of awkwardness as the credit was oddly shared.
But this wasn’t the first time he had heard the title “Saintess”; it seemed to most often refer to the current saint of the Church of Light, a living saint according to legend.
She seems to have a good reputation among the middle and lower tiers of society.
However, according to information obtained from Helena’s guard, the living saint is currently in the south, amidst the most terrifying Catastrophe of the Magic Fog.
No one knows whether she is alive or dead…
Colin wasn’t very concerned, he simply thought for a moment before allowing these people to take some bread back and bring others to collect food.
Then, he turned his attention to some other less “sincere” individuals:
“You still have a chance to get food.”
“You need to tell more people, spread my name, my kindness.”
“I will bring you bread and water that flows with honey…”
“Go, let more people know that the world is not hopeless, I will bring food to satisfy your hunger, bring true goodwill.”
“But!”
At this point, Colin spoke seriously, and Tang Ken, seeing this, hurriedly and quietly lit a basin filled with Blended Oil.
In an instant, a huge flame roared into existence.
Colin, with the Ring of Flame Dominance on his right hand, waved, and the flame, as if controlled, converged in mid-air, forming a surging fireball three meters in diameter.
The scorching hot air spread instantly, and the atmosphere on site turned tense immediately.
All those who saw the heart-like flame pulsating in mid-air could think of only destruction.
And Colin, standing below, with his back to the light, his face obscured and his silhouette wrapped in the smoke spreading from the fire, looked as though a god had descended.
How could the refugees present have ever seen this?
The light from the fire reflected on their faces, scaring them into shivering, their first instinct was to flee, but soldiers stationed nearby blocked them, preventing any movement.
Not just them, even the soldiers who had followed Colin were taken aback, having not expected him to have such a trick up his sleeve.
Good, it seems this special effect isn’t bad…
On the surface, Colin looked dignified, a trace of approval in his eyes, pleased with their reaction.
But in reality, if there weren’t so many people…
Colin thought he might actually be unable to resist rolling on the ground.
Pain!
Such pain!
Too painful!
Colin felt as if his entire body were being licked by the light and fire, his figure under the gray robe trembling involuntarily.
The burning sensation was so intense that he felt as if he were being roasted on a stove.
“The Ring of Flame Dominance,” this damned thing was only sold for a few hundred points for a reason, I’d like to sell it too, it’s indeed a bit unbearable…
It’s way too damn painful.
Bearing the agony, he said what needed to be said, and after a minute, Colin, trembling, waved his hand to disperse the light and then stood with his hands behind his back, eyes fixed on them—he was in too much pain and needed to catch a breath.
Of course, to the ordinary locals who hadn’t been treated to any special effects, he, who had displayed a “miracle,” didn’t show any sign of discomfort, and standing still only made him seem more mysterious and unfathomable.
Even though the light had dissipated, they still lowered their gaze, trembling inside and not daring to speak, the greed for food seen earlier returning to rationality.
After a long while, filled with immense respect, they heard Colin’s words again.

chapters.title: Chapter 61 - 61 61 Do Not Question My Words _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 61: Chapter 61: Do Not Question My Words! _1 Chapter 61: Chapter 61: Do Not Question My Words! _1 “Very well, I have discovered several more ‘sincere’ individuals.”
Colin casually pointed to two or three people, having thrown them a sweet date at the beginning, followed by a cudgel, and now offered them a sesame seed, reigniting their longing for food.
“Go forth, spread my name, spread my goodwill, and inform those tormented by famine that the good news arrives with my coming.”
“Remember, do not question my words, do not misconstrue my goodwill.”
Having said that, Colin waved his hand, signaling the soldiers to take the group of people away.
No outsiders remained around.
‘Hiss, my goodness….’
Colin sucked in a breath of cold air, his expression hidden under the grey robe finally becoming somewhat difficult to maintain.
After taking a few breaths and adjusting his status, Colin felt the remaining burning sensation slowly dissipate before he turned to Tang Ken:
“Where did you learn all this stuff? How come you’re so adept at it?”
Although performing this “miracle” was quite uncomfortable, the effects seemed quite good so far.
At the very least, much better than his own ideas.
