After entering the house, Colin tore away the facade of “The False Powerhouse.” His confidence faded, and a sudden, inexplicable fear welled up in his heart.
It wasn’t that he had faced any great danger, but he had believed he could control his emotions—yet, to his surprise, he found that they were not as manageable as he had thought.
However, since he had only used it for less than ten minutes, the impact was not too severe.
If he had used it for over an hour…
The situation might have been completely different.
Gathering his thoughts, Colin followed Hu Xiaoyuan and the others upstairs. Upon reaching the second floor, he saw that there were quite a few survivors present. Most of them were local residents looking haggard, clearly having not fared well during this period.
“Please follow me, I’ll help you clear out a room for you to rest for a while…” Hu Xiaoyuan had someone take the few survivors that came with Colin into a room, then she led Colin to a hall.
Looking around, Colin saw a few injured people but nothing else; assured there were no ambushes, he sat down on a solid wood sofa in the hall:
“Can we talk now? What exactly happened here? Explain in detail, and make sure there are no omissions.”
“To be specific, it all started over a month ago…”
Hu Xiaoyuan saw Colin nod for her to continue, took a deep breath, and started recounting the events that had occurred during this time.
About a month ago, the person in charge of the local “health station” received a notification that something abnormal had occurred at a construction site, where a group of construction workers had vanished. Therefore, a three-person team was sent to investigate.
Initially, no one paid much attention because the site had experienced issues before, with construction workers mysteriously disappearing en masse.
However, upon investigating, they found these so-called “mysteriously vanished” construction workers actually learning “foreign languages” in a less-than-reputable barbershop.
If it weren’t for someone vouching for them, considering the impact on the construction progress, they probably would have been detained for a while.
So, when they vanished this time, nobody took it seriously until the investigation team disappeared, which caught the station’s attention.
Later, considering the severity of the situation, Hu Xiaoyuan personally led a team to the site and found the problem originated from an unearthed underground temple.
For some reason, pollution had leaked from the inside, resulting in shadowy monsters attacking anyone under the light at night. Once embraced, the touched area would quickly assimilate.
Most of the disappeared probably met with misfortune, and what was more troublesome was that after entering, they found they couldn’t handle the threat in the temple, nor could they leave. They were forced to seek rescue…
Luckily, an elite squad from “The Great Wall” was passing by at the time and stopped to help.
But the threat in the underground temple was more troublesome than they had anticipated…
Moreover, they had not realized at the time that this wasn’t just an ordinary resurgence of anomalies but a premeditated plot by someone with an ulterior motive.
The “Frontier Guard” team leader used thirteen “Books of Fate” to seal the threat in the temple.
It was thought that the matter was resolved, but it turned out that the trouble was just beginning.
A group of Cultists, seemingly from nowhere, suddenly appeared and blockaded the entire town, attacking them and making them realize that they had fallen into a well-designed trap.
These people were very familiar with the “Book of Fate” and managed to avoid being observed through the books.
Since then, both parties have been fighting over the entity inside the temple. The “Frontier Guards,” in order to prevent further disaster, had to deal with the anomaly while also fighting against them, suffering heavy losses.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 93 - 93 93 Lost Containment Subject Shadow Stone
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 93: Chapter 93: Lost Containment Subject “Shadow Stone Buddha” _1 Chapter 93: Chapter 93: Lost Containment Subject “Shadow Stone Buddha” _1 “Wait, thirteen ‘Books of Fate’ in a row?”
Colin was startled when he heard the name, and immediately raised his hand to interrupt Hu Xiaoyuan’s speech, “Are you saying that the ‘Frontier Guard’ squad captain used thirteen ‘Books of Fate’?”
Thirteen of them! Aren’t the official forces being a little too extravagant?
You should know that he didn’t manage to get even one for his mission this time.
“Yes.”
The tall vice-captain of the Cleanup Squad nodded, “That anomaly was very dangerous before; what we are encountering now has been weakened at the source, which is why their movements are so stiff and slow. Otherwise, it would be very troublesome to deal with.”
After a pause, she added, “Later, that squad captain sent out a team to break through and send a distress signal, but the breakout team disappeared, and we thought it had failed until the remaining ‘Books of Fate’ were used, and then we knew it was successful.
“From the ‘Book of Fate’, we learned that in three days, you would appear from the predesignated direction on time…”
Sure enough, they weren’t suspicious of me because of the ‘Book of Fate’…
After hearing about the ‘Book of Fate’, Colin immediately understood the reason, so he was not surprised at all.
What really made him curious was the relationship between the official forces and the Bonfire Company?
“Could it be that the ‘Books of Fate’ are so scarce because there are also official personnel in the company, and so they were all taken? No wonder I couldn’t find any these past days; an individual can’t compete with a group…”
Colin muttered to himself, he had a simple reason for not guessing that the Bonfire Company was an official force.
If that thing belonged to any country on Earth…
With those few “agreements”, Earth would most likely have entered the interstellar era a long time ago, and spaceships might have been heading toward other worlds one after another, gathering resources, instead of fighting amongst themselves in the Solar System every day.
Various thoughts flashed through his mind, but Colin did not say anything on the surface. Instead, he asked,
“So, what’s the deal with those anomalies? You just said that once stepping outside under the light, one would be immediately attacked, so why was the light kept on all the time?”
“That’s the biggest problem here…”
Hu Xiaoyuan gave a wry smile, “Turning on the lights leads to trouble that we can resolve, but turning them off brings even weirder issues. In the dark, our bodies grow cold, and usually, we can’t last for more than a minute…
“The only luck we have now is that these dangers only occur at night, and as long as you stay inside a completely enclosed building, you won’t be subjected to unknown attacks.”
That mysterious, huh? Turning on the lights leads to attacks, and turning them off does too…
Colin was somewhat surprised to hear this, but he suddenly remembered that during his time in “World Code-13”, strange things seemed to happen at night too.
“Mr. Lin, we learned from the last prediction that you resolved this crisis, may I ask how you plan to resolve it? Although we don’t have any special means ourselves, we will try our best to provide some cooperation if needed.”
How to resolve it? How would I know how to resolve it…
Colin felt a headache coming on when he heard this; the Cleanup Squad member in front of him didn’t know what was happening inside the underground temple.
After the arrival of the “Frontier Guard,” her responsibility was to help evacuate the periphery; she actually knew very little.
Whether it was the identities of the cultists or the specifics of the underground temple, she knew very little.
To get a clear understanding of the situation, it might be necessary to go deeper into the construction site and find that group of “Frontier Guards” to learn more.
However, just as Colin was about to suggest going to the core area where the problem erupted to take a look, a piece of information suddenly popped up in his mind.
[Single Player · Trial Task (2/3) — “Anomaly in the Township” has been completed.]
Huh? It’s completed just like that? Colin stopped in mid-sentence.
[Single Player · Trial Task — “Recovery of Lost Low-risk Containment Subject ‘Shadow Stone Buddha'” has been issued.]
The message in his mind made Colin pause, then he quickly made an excuse to go to the restroom. He stepped back a few paces, sat on the toilet, and pulled out the parchment from his pocket.
[Single Player · Trial Task — “Recovery of Lost Low-risk Containment Subject ‘Shadow Stone Buddha'”.]
“Description”: An item that was lost within the company a long time ago, its actual form is a shadow-type strange entity in a bizarre city, sealed by a monk through special means into a stone Buddha sculpture and placed inside Bonfire Company’s containment hall, but due to a previous invasion incident, the containment subject was lost.
“Requirement”: Carry a “Level 2 Containment Sphere (already placed in the ‘Storage Room’)”, and collect all shadows by shattering.
“Hint”: Shadows can only be observed when under the light.
“Event Reward”: “Bonfire Points * 300”.
“Note”: This task has a time limit. If containment is not completed by six o’clock tomorrow morning, when the sun rises, it will be considered a task failure.
…
“Nice one, so the problem here is actually related to you, huh?”
Colin couldn’t help but make a snide remark internally.
He initially thought it was just an emergency caused by the mysterious resurgence of an ancient evil deity and that some cultists wanted to seize it, but he hadn’t expected there to be such hidden details…
“Wait a second, does that mean the real masterminds are actually a group of cultists? So, that underground temple was just a trick to fool the eyes devised by those cultists? Was their actual target the ‘Frontier Guards’ who happened to pass by?”
Colin had a sudden flash of insight, as if guessing many things.
If it weren’t deliberately arranged, this group would have definitely been discovered by the ‘Book of Fate’ by now, so their aim is obviously at the official forces.
Wait, could they have been the ones who invaded Bonfire Company? Otherwise, how would they possess a containment subject lost by Bonfire Company?
Colin was terribly alarmed by the idea but quickly dismissed it, because if that were the case, this task wouldn’t be an “F Level” trial task—it would have to be “C Level” or above.
And now, Bonfire Company, knowing about the existence of the cultists, still hadn’t dispatched reinforcements.
That must mean the situation isn’t too serious…
Everything is still within his capacity to handle.
“However, why would those cultists attack the official personnel? They can’t possibly just be bored, can they? Why do I have this eerie feeling that I’m being sucked into a much bigger vortex?”
Muttering to himself, Colin opened the “Storage Room” and took out the “Level 2 Containment Sphere”.
[“Level 2 Containment Sphere”: Capable of containing a large number of Level 2 low-threat non-physical special entities.]
The “Level 2 Containment Sphere” was roughly the size of a fist, divided into an upper and lower section, the upper part red, the lower part white, with a line in the middle, and on that line, a small circular button featuring the number 2—
This is basically an Elf Ball, isn’t it?
Colin stared at it, unable to stop himself from pondering.
Such an offbeat design could only be a product of some company’s manufacturing department employee’s bad taste in humor.

chapters.title: Chapter 94 - 94 94 Mole_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 94: Chapter 94 Mole_1 Chapter 94: Chapter 94 Mole_1 “So, how am I supposed to use this thing? Wait until after I’ve killed it and then throw the ball over to see it shake three times?”
Colin weighed the ball in his hand and thought back to when he had killed those Shadow Monsters; it seemed they would directly split apart and disappear in an instant, with no way to be contained.
However, at this moment, a timely “inspiration” appeared, resolving his confusion—
Using it didn’t require throwing; simply keeping it in an open state and killing the black figures while it was active would be enough.
“Using it is quite convenient, though.”
Colin muttered to himself and then glanced over the mission description again. “No wonder that ‘Frontier Guard’ is now bogged down in a tough battle. Who would have thought that the real body of the monsters is not the assumed Stone Buddha, but those Shadow Monsters thought to be insignificant fodder?
“It’s like fighting a boss. You battle your way to the boss chamber, only to find that the boss can’t be killed, and at best, you can only seal it, but there are also the endlessly respawning minions, which really is a headache.
“But it’s no wonder they missed it, with a group of Cultists interfering; it’s normal that they didn’t realize…
“But they’ve been going in the wrong direction. Lacking this piece of information, all their efforts are in vain.”
During his contemplation, Colin guessed most of the situation regarding the abnormity in the area.
It’s possible that even now the ‘Frontier Guard’ hasn’t realized this point, or perhaps they have, but because they’ve wasted too much energy on the statue, they no longer have the strength to deal with the other shadows and are now just barely hanging on.
Of course, whether they know it or not, the Cultists behind the scenes are certainly aware of this fact.
If he targets the black shadows later, the Cultists will definitely notice and then come over to attack him…
If nothing unexpected happens, he will definitely become the focus of their attacks.
“I’m not sure about the strength of the ‘Frontier Guard’, but if the Cultists are all like that Wu Sheng guy, then they’re not too strong. If they’re all of that caliber, even if a hundred of them come at me, I could take my time hunting them down…”
Colin pressed his hand to his forehead, but considering that the ‘Frontier Guard’ and his team used thirteen ‘Book of Fate’ cards and still didn’t manage to detect these people, it was enough to show how cunning they were.
So it’s still better to be a little cautious…
At that moment, a breeze slipped through the gaps in the windows into the bathroom.
Colin turned his head and glanced outside the window. By now, the sun had completely set, and outside, everything was enveloped in darkness, barely distinguishable by silhouette.
The time displayed on his phone indicated it was already seven in the evening.
Without much thought, he reached out to tug the window, ensuring it was firmly closed.
In fact, Hu Xiaoyuan hadn’t meant completely sealing off without leaving any gaps, but rather simply ensuring that the doors and windows were properly shut; otherwise, the people inside the building could have suffocated.
Afterward, he tucked the parchment into his pocket, stood up to take care of his physiological needs, washed his hands, and left the bathroom.
At this moment, in the hall, a few white candles, whereabouts unknown, had been lit. Under the dim light of the flames, the surroundings took on an indescribably eerie atmosphere.
Better off without lights, at this point my vision is worse than my sense of smell… Colin muttered to himself internally and returned to his seat on the sofa with an impassive face.
Before the cleaner from the sanitation station could continue asking him about his plans, Colin took the initiative to question Hu Xiaoyuan about the strength of those Cultists.
“They worship an entity known as ‘Mother of the Red Moon’, commonly referred to as ‘Church of the Red Moon’…
“Furthermore, their powers range approximately from Level 1 to Level 3. The group you just killed earlier was likely a small squad that split off, led by a Level 2, while the rest were all Level 1…”
Another set of standards different from Bonfire Company’s, why can’t they just unify it… Colin felt a bit of a headache, but at least now he had a reference.
The ‘Hemorrhoid Spirit’ was Level 2, the rest were Level 1…
“According to this calculation, wouldn’t an ordinary Second Order ‘Beastification’ without vampirism be Level 3? Could I be Level 4 or even Level 5? If the enemy leader is just Level 3, that’s pretty weak…”
As thoughts flickered through his mind, Colin spoke, “Right, do you know the exact content of the last ‘Book of Fate’?”
“Yes, I’ve brought it with me…”
Hu Xiaoyuan took out a yellowed piece of rice paper and passed it over; Colin took the paper and glanced at it.
On it, in very neat red handwriting, were written some matters that would “happen” in the future.
Broadly speaking, it stated that as the situation here grew increasingly dire, a supporter entered the sealed township from the square by unknown means.
He called himself “Mr. Lin” and arrived with five burdens in tow, deterring those present with his fierce methods.
But unfortunately, it seemed that due to various probing attempts, “Mr. Lin” had not been able to resolve the issue in time. Consequently, the restrictions around the Stone Buddha were broken, disaster erupted, and in order to save others, the user stayed behind and died while buying time for everyone else.
And “Mr. Lin” led the others to break out and escape…
Colin didn’t see what his own ultimate fate was, but judging from the situation, the reason for the mission’s failure was his inability to complete the containment task in time, not a lack of strength to do so.
According to the paper, after his arrival, he first encountered Hu Xiaoyuan but was mistaken for a cultist; the two sides fought, although not for long, as night arrived and he went deeper in, encountering other people. All in all, because of various alerts and probes, they missed the best opportunity…
It wasn’t until the end that the “Frontier Guards” and the “Cleaners” realized he was an ally, and they had all made a huge blunder.
This time, however, Colin was without these troubles.
“The ‘Book of Fate’ really came in handy, of course, it looks like those cultists don’t have a ‘Book of Fate’ in their hands, or else the situation would be quite different.”
As Colin felt relieved, he also harbored many complaints about the creator of the “Book of Fate: Fragment.”
If the enemy got their hands on this thing, the trouble would be real…
What Colin didn’t notice was that while he was inspecting the content on the “Book of Fate,” Hu Xiaoyuan was also discreetly sizing him up.
Only after confirming that he truly could understand the content, rather than pretending to read, did she somewhat relax.
The ‘Book of Fate’ is one of the three main pathways of power for the ‘Fate Propeller’ ability users within the relevant departments. It is said that the material used to create it is the same as that used for the ancient and mysterious ‘Tui Bei Map,’ but she didn’t know the specifics.
This was among the highest and most central of secrets…
Anyway, she knew that under certain specific restrictions, people unrelated to the pertinent departments could not comprehend the content of the ‘Book of Fate.’ Since this “Mr. Lin” could understand it, that meant he was definitely one of their own…
Although she didn’t know why this person from their side didn’t have any identification, she didn’t have time to think about it now.
Colin scanned the yellow paper again, asked a few questions, then handed the ‘Book of Fate’ back to Hu Xiaoyuan, and said, “I have a general understanding of the situation now. It’s a little after seven thirty, let’s rest a while, and start the operation at eight o’clock…”
“Have a look for someone who can accompany me to the source later; we’ll aim to resolve everything in one go.”
Hearing Colin’s words, Hu Xiaoyuan nodded, “Alright, I’ll accompany you there; I’m the most familiar with the situation here.”
“Hmm, that’s fine, but did you notice one thing?”
Pausing for a moment, Colin looked at her and said, “Haven’t you realized there is a mole among you?”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 95 - 95 95 Violating Rules_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 95: Chapter 95 Violating Rules_1 Chapter 95: Chapter 95 Violating Rules_1 “A mole?”
Hu Xiaoyuan was taken aback, seemingly unable to grasp the meaning behind Colin’s words initially.
Seeing the Cleanup Squad leader’s puzzled expression, Colin’s eyebrows raised slightly. Had the man really not noticed?
Colin didn’t intend to continue speaking in riddles and subtly hinted, “Take another good look at the content on that piece of paper.”
Hu Xiaoyuan unfolded the ‘Book of Fate’ paper she was about to put away and read the contents. With Colin’s deliberate prompting, she quickly noticed something amiss—
Why were the cultists able to appear on the road Mr. Lin had taken before him?
Mr. Lin came from the direction of the square, which was intelligence only they were supposed to know, wasn’t it?
She suddenly remembered that when they had wanted to set up an ambush on the road earlier that afternoon, they had encountered the ‘Mother of the Red Moon’s’ believers. After a skirmish, they had to retreat.
Likewise, if it weren’t for the cameras they had left behind, which had spotted Colin, they might not have been able to meet up with him in time.
“Many people have looked at this piece of paper—the ‘Frontier Guards’ over there, us, and…”
“Your range of suspicion is too broad. If you really can’t figure it out, just let it go.”
Colin waved his hand dismissively, “Right now, I only trust you, and that’s that. Later, you come with me to support the rear. I plan on collaborating with the ‘Frontier Guards’ over there and his squad to thoroughly suppress the Stone Buddha, which is the source of it all. Everything should then come to an end.”
He didn’t disclose that he knew the black figure was the real entity, in case it tipped off whoever was pulling the strings behind the scenes.
As for trusting Hu Xiaoyuan? That was just talk…
Colin hadn’t detected the scent of any cultists in the building or the vicinity, so he wasn’t sure who the mole was. In his view, anyone present could be the mole.
Including the one before him.
And his mention of the issue was just to bluff, but unfortunately, he hadn’t bluffed anything out.
“That cultist named Wu Sheng had always seemed to think I had teammates, but the ‘Book of Fate’ clearly stated I came alone, carrying five bottles of soy sauce. This suggests that the mole either couldn’t transmit much information or hadn’t seen the detailed contents…”
Colin had some guesses in mind, but he wasn’t particularly concerned about it.
“I understand…”
Hu Xiaoyuan nodded, then continued, “If that’s the case, please be careful around me too. It’s possible there’s no mole, just someone who’s been hypnotized and leaking information unwittingly…”
You’re making this more complicated, Colin thought as he interrupted her with a raise of his hand, “Alright, alright, if we start splitting hairs like this, there’ll be no end to it.
“In the face of absolute power, all else is as trivial as chickens and dogs.”
With ‘God Gear’ on his person and undertaking an F Level trial task, Colin still had some confidence.
Now it seemed, indeed, much easier than dealing with a ‘Descent Type’…
Having said that, Colin pulled out a Snickers from his pocket and was about to take a bite when he suddenly heard a number of people approaching from outside the hall.
Colin put the Snickers into his mouth and glanced at the group, instantly determining they were all ordinary people.
They must be survivors from the local towns…
“What’s going on?” Hu Xiaoyuan furrowed her brow and stood up to meet the people.
At that moment, the crowd exchanged uncertain looks until finally, a woman spoke up.
“Commander Hu, I overheard you say you’re going to deal with some trouble…”
“Yes, what about it? With the support we’ve received from outside, once he resolves the issue, everyone will be safe.”
Hu Xiaoyuan briefly said a sentence, but this did not reassure everyone. The woman glanced at Colin, then continued:
“It’s not that I don’t trust him, but could we be sent out of here before departing? Otherwise, what if—what if it fails?”
“Exactly, you’re capable. Even if it fails, you can survive, but we can only wait to die…”
“Right, right, if it fails, we might even become a burden. Could you please let me out first? That young man is powerful, we all saw him hacking his way here…”
“It’s not that we’re being inauspicious, Hu Team, but… protecting us is your duty, isn’t it? You can’t just abandon us, right?”
Watching the crowd’s growing clamor, Hu Xiaoyuan furrowed his brows, not quite knowing how to respond.
“Everybody, everybody…”
Colin called out twice, but seeing the crowd did not quiet down, he drew his revolver and fired a shot in an unoccupied direction.
Bang.
Finally, everyone quieted down, each looking at Colin with fear.
“First, I have to tell you that I can’t leave before the problem is resolved.”
As Colin spoke, his gaze swept over them, trying to spot the mole hidden among them.
He felt that at a time like this, a group of people suddenly making trouble…
It seemed too much of a coincidence.
Unfortunately, apart from being somewhat out of control emotionally, he didn’t seem to observe anything out of the ordinary in their faces. And them being trapped here for half a month and breaking down was within the realm of normal.
In fact, if they had been trapped for so long and still acted as if nothing happened, that would be abnormal.
Still, he suspected that the reason these people came out might be due to someone inciting them from behind.
“How could it be? We just saw you, with a kitchen knife, casually hacking your way through to rescue us. Isn’t saving us a piece of cake? Please, I beg you, we don’t want to die here, wuwu…”
As she spoke, one of the women, looking to be in her sixties, couldn’t help but start crying.
“Young man, that kitchen knife must be something powerful, right?”
“With that kitchen knife! We could leave by ourselves!”
“Why don’t you leave that thing with us? If you fail, we can still give it a try…”
Damn, Hu Xiaoyuan felt a sudden chill in her heart as she suddenly remembered one of the internal rescue guidelines:
If ordinary people are present at an abnormal site, when circumstances permit, please avoid showing the special nature of the special items you have in front of them, or the transgressor will bear the corresponding responsibility for the adverse consequences caused by this reason.
This rule seemed perplexing, but she knew that each one was established through various sacrifices bit by bit.
It was precisely because Colin had shown his tool that trouble arose.
Colin didn’t know the rescue guidelines, but looking at this group of people emotional breakdowns, he did remember something.
There was a child in the orphanage whose father was a firefighter. When his father went into a fire to rescue people and was about to succeed during a corridor evacuation, one of the disaster victims lost their breathing mask…
Then, that person snatched the child’s dad’s breathing mask and managed to escape.
Afterward, the child’s family collapsed, and he was taken to the orphanage by the old Dean…
Of course, according to the final reports, the child’s father died a hero, “voluntarily” giving others the chance to live.
Colin never thought he’d encounter something like this one day.

chapters.title: Chapter 96 - 96 96 Divine Strike_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 96: Chapter 96 “Divine Strike”_1 Chapter 96: Chapter 96 “Divine Strike”_1 “A bit interesting…”
Colin didn’t get angry, after all, getting mad at a group of people who had lost their sanity wasn’t very meaningful.
He was just slightly curious about the possible mastermind behind the scenes…
As it stood, these people had been incited to come here; there might not be any supernatural elements involved.
Of course, it wouldn’t be difficult to find out who the mastermind was, but given these people’s mental status, it was probably going to take a lot of effort and time…
Remembering that this mission seemed to have a time limit, Colin wondered if once the time was up, their objective would be achieved?
‘Are they trying to divert my attention to the traitor, using this to stall for time? Is the traitor planning to self-destruct?’
‘If it were an ordinary person, at this point, they might really consider finding the mastermind or the traitor first, but unfortunately, I have already obtained the most critical information and know how to resolve this incident. There’s no need to play their werewolf game.’
Colin guessed some of the situation.
At that moment, the alarm on his cell phone suddenly rang.
He took his gaze from the crowd in front of him, pulled out his cell phone to turn off the alarm, and at the same time checked the time—eight o’clock had arrived.
“It’s time to take action.”
Colin tilted his head to Hu Xiaoyuan next to him and said.
After speaking, he prepared to bypass the crowd and leave the apartment directly.
“Don’t you dare leave!” a man with a fierce expression blocked Colin’s path.
If it weren’t for other members of the Cleanup Squad holding him back, he might have already charged forward.
At this moment, after Colin turned his gaze toward him, the man shouted with a red face:
“Either way, you must rescue me today, or else you won’t be able to leave alive!”“We don’t care how the rest of you plan to act! We have to save people first!”
“Otherwise, if we die, we won’t let you off the hook even as ghosts!”
The others also surged forward, their emotions highly charged.
Having their spirits suppressed for the better part of a month, they finally found an outlet for release at this moment and suddenly became somewhat irrational, frenzied like madmen, foam flying from their mouths, seemingly determined to fight to the bitter end if their demands were not met.
Watching the crowd trying to come forward to demand a kitchen knife but being held back by the outstretched hands of other Cleanup Squad members, Colin sighed, took out a lens from his pocket, placed it against his left eye socket, and took a quick look at the crowd.
He wanted to know which part of the human body would sustain the least damage when hit.
After getting the answer, Colin put the Analytical Lens back in his pocket and raised his Revolver, aiming at one of the most vociferous individuals in the crowd.
“Last warning, move aside,” Colin said calmly.
“Come on, shoot! You think you’re great because you have a gun?! I’ll tell you, I’m not afraid of you! I’ve risked everything today, I don’t believe you dare…”
The man pointed at Colin with his hand, seemingly fearless.
Bang!
Bang!
Bang!
The sound of three flashes of gunfire, like a splash of cold water, instantly quieted the crowd.
He actually shot? Hu Xiaoyuan turned her head in shock, met Colin’s eyes, and couldn’t help but feel a chill at the bottom of her heart.
Because she suddenly noticed that Colin’s eyes at the moment were not human-like, but vertical pupils filled with anger, and the reddish glow reflected in those pupils was chilling—what kind of power was this?
“Don’t worry, he’s not dead,” Colin responded quietly.
Three bullets, one went through the man’s palm, and two “missed” killing him, hitting a television behind them instead, leaving it covered with spider-web-like cracks.
The man didn’t feel the pain immediately, just numbness in his hand. But when he came to his senses and saw his bloodied palm, his face showed terror, and he fainted.
Without looking further, Colin walked toward the stairwell, reloading three bullets into the chambers of his Revolver as he went.
Hu Xiaoyuan followed behind Colin somewhat dazedly, although she knew that the rescue code mentioned special actions for special times. However, actually seeing someone take action, she still felt a sense of shock.
However, accordingly, after Colin made his move, nobody else dared to play the hero, nor did there remain a voice about not letting them off the hook even as ghosts…
The survivors present seemed to have finally regained their lost rationality, as their eyes became much clearer.
Colin was not at all surprised by this. Were these people really that fierce, or were they still so desperate they turned on their own people in anger?
However, just as he reached the stairway entrance, Colin suddenly remembered something. He reached into his pocket, felt around, and tossed out a kitchen knife.
“Here, the kitchen knife you wanted.”
Colin threw the kitchen knife out as if he was discarding trash, then turned around and headed downstairs without a second glance.
Everyone looked at each other, but no one dared to step forward to pick it up right away.
“Mr. Lin, is this really okay? To just throw that kitchen knife away like that…” Hu Xiaoyuan, who was half a head taller than Colin, caught up and asked in a low voice next to Colin’s ear.
If she wasn’t mistaken, that kitchen knife was the very one that had easily knocked over the shadowy figure before.
“Huh, you don’t seriously think I need a kitchen knife, do you?”
Colin chuckled. When he got to the front door, he pulled out a folded black tactical shovel from his pocket.
Following behind, Hu Xiaoyuan couldn’t help but pause again—where did that tactical shovel come from?
She clearly hadn’t seen Colin carrying that thing around.
Although curious, she did not ask further. Holding a high-wattage flashlight in her hand, she followed Colin out of the rented park, which served as their base.
“By the way, Mr. Lin, are we just going to go like this, without using a ‘Book of Fate’?”
Hu Xiaoyuan turned on the flashlight and asked curiously.
Usually, before official personnel started their operations, they would use such artifacts to test whether the upcoming event would go smoothly.
It seemed that “Mr. Lin” did not intend to use one.
I would also like to use it, but the problem is that I need to have one for that, “Books of Fate” were all snatched up by you, and I didn’t get any… Colin complained inwardly, but his expression did not change:
“‘Book of Fate’? I never need such things.”
Not using it? Hu Xiaoyuan was initially taken aback by the answer but quickly noticed something from the disdainful tone.
Among the three great powers of the official institutions, the one that despises the “Book of Fate” the most is “Divine Strike,” which is listed alongside it.
Through a special means, they invite the “God” into their bodies to gain strength…
Of course, it’s not a real “God”; the power’s essence comes from the broad masses’ cognition and trends of thought.
Specifically, it is the borrowing from a widely recognized “idol” imagery and not from some deceased who has been dead for who knows how many years and whose true nature is uncertain.
Borrowers can only derive power from a few specific positive figures that are legally recognized and permitted by the officials, such as Guan Gong, Zhong Kui, Pure Yang True Man, Dragon King, and so on…
When executing tasks, what to borrow usually depends on the local beliefs…
Different images are used to cope with different situations.
When “Mr. Lin” used his power, the change in his demeanor indeed matched the characteristics of “Divine Strike.”
Only, it appeared that the entity he borrowed from didn’t match any of the figures she recognized.
“Could it be a new variety from overseas?”
Hu Xiaoyuan remembered that there had been an exchange learning event among the domestic and foreign ability users, bringing forth some new “images.”
For example, the most famous one was “Newton”…
This figure, well recognized worldwide, had been fashioned into a legal “image” by the officials for “Divine Strike” practitioners to use.
But…
It didn’t quite seem right, an “idol” newly created by the officials?
…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 97 - 97 97 Insight into Secrets_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 97: Chapter 97 Insight into Secrets_1 Chapter 97: Chapter 97 Insight into Secrets_1 Colin didn’t know Hu Xiaoyuan was trying to guess his strength, but at this moment, as the two opened the apartment door and stepped outside, they were immediately surrounded by numerous dark figures.
They seemed to be following an instinct, reaching out their arms and walking slowly towards the two.
Colin didn’t waste any time, he pressed the “Elf Ball” in his pocket and stealthily attached “The False Powerhouse” to a concealed part of his body.
Upon using it this time, he felt the presence of over thirty “valid recognitions”.
These “valid recognitions” quickly transformed into tangible strength, swelling within him accompanied by a surge of confidence.
“Heh…”
Colin flashed a confident smile, the military shovel in his hand gleaming brilliantly, as if it were a blessed Holy Relic.
He dashed forward in just a few strides, gripping the handle of the military shovel with both hands, swung it, and fiercely slapped it down on the head of a dark figure.
With a clang, the shadow’s head was smashed into its chest cavity, its form rapidly dissipating.
However, this time it didn’t vanish into the air but was instead pulled invisibly into Colin’s pocket.
“Good, got one.” Colin nodded to himself, lifting the military shovel that emitted dazzling light, and charged towards the next target.
Clang, clang, clang~
Within the stronghold, the sound of striking echoed continuously, leaving the survivors in the other apartments standing at their windows in shock.
More and more faces appeared behind the windows, staring in amazement.
The monsters that had once driven them to despair were now being dispatched one by one with the shovel, as easy as chopping melons and slicing vegetables.
“Damn, what’s going on, how is he doing that?”
“I thought the guys who came to support us earlier were invincible, but this guy’s even fiercer. Who is this big shot?”
“We’re saved! We’re finally saved!”
“Big brother, take us with you, let’s charge together!”
Voice came from the nearby buildings, many people excited by Colin’s performance, and even wanted to join him.
But Colin ignored these shouts.
How could he possibly contain the monsters well while in the company of these vermin?
“Hahaha, come on, let me have a bit more fun!”
Colin laughed wildly, swinging his military shovel, slaying the approaching monsters with a single strike.
As more and more “valid recognitions” appeared, his strength became even more formidable, his physical condition surpassing even that of Beast Transformation Syndrome.
His whole being radiated with a glowing aura, making him seem like a god descended from the heavens.
The battle with the aberrations could only be described as utterly devastating.
However, Hu Xiaoyuan, following behind, was somewhat distressed as he watched Colin’s rampage because, after thirty minutes, they had barely made it five hundred meters.
“But with Mr. Lin’s strength, at the very least he’s at the ‘Agent’ level, or even a high-level ‘Agent’, right?”
Hu Xiaoyuan watched the wild slaughter, his eyes glittering in wonder.
Some practitioners on the path of “Divine Strike,” after borrowing the power of their “idols” to a certain extent, could be referred to as “Agents.”
Just like those on the path of Fate Propeller who, even without the “Book of Fate,” could predict the future through their own abilities.
Such people truly belonged to the extraordinary realm…
Clang!
“One hundred sixteen!”
Colin slapped one dark figure with his right hand, shattering it, while his left hand reached out and grabbed the head of another, his fingers exerting force and crushing its skull.
“Mr. Lin, it’s this way…” Hu Xiaoyuan reminded him from behind.
“What do you mean ‘this way’? It doesn’t matter where! I’ll clear the creatures here first!”
“How can you clear them all? These things can’t be killed, they are endless, it’s impossible…”
“What do you mean ‘endless’? You haven’t noticed it’s because you’re weak. Where I am, that’s where the depths are!”
“This…”
Hu Xiaoyuan suddenly paused, realizing with a start that the number of dark silhouettes nearby seemed to have significantly decreased!
The chilly sensation from the surrounding darkness had also noticeably lessened…
What’s going on?
Could it be that they’ve actually all been killed?
At that moment, she saw the terrifying aura of Colin suddenly halt, then he turned around and gave her a kick.
Hu Xiaoyuan didn’t even have time to react before she was kicked away to the side…
“Is he out of control?”
Midair, her first thought was exactly this—borrowing the power of an “idol” certainly wasn’t without risk, and the greatest risk was the possibility of losing one’s sense of self and ultimately being assimilated by the “idol.”
The stronger the power, the higher the tendency for assimilation…
However, just as she hit the ground, she abruptly saw the ground explode into a crater beside Colin.
Following that, a rumbling sound came from afar—
A heavy sniper rifle!?
The instant she heard the sound, Hu Xiaoyuan’s pupils shrank, and she immediately recognized the source of the noise.
The enemy has this kind of weapon?
Without a second thought, she dashed behind a building to find cover.
Afterward, she looked worriedly at Mr. Lin, wanting to shout to him to stop being reckless.
Bullets might not be very effective against anomalies, but they’re certainly efficient at killing people, even more so than using superpowers.
Even an elephant couldn’t withstand a shot from a heavy sniper, not to mention the human body, even if it was enhanced…
“Hahaha, they’ve finally shown themselves.”
Colin turned around, looking towards a figure on the rooftop of a building hundreds of meters away, barely discernible.
He was not surprised in the least. If he had been reaping so many “dark silhouettes” and these people had not responded, then he would really have to question their intelligence.
Then, he touched his right ear and looked at his hand; there was some blood on it.
“Heh, not bad, they’ve actually managed to injure my skin. However, compared to enemies I’ve encountered in the past, you’re not even worth a second glance, not to mention a mention!”
Colin turned and shoveled another dark silhouette, containing it on the spot.
Bang!
Another heavy sniper shot came, the bullet piercing the asphalt road, causing the ground to tremble.
“Too slow, too weak, disappointing.”
Colin shook his head with a sigh, waving the shovel in his hand, and before their very eyes, contained another dark silhouette.
At this time, the “Level 2 Containment Sphere” already held more than two hundred of them, and looking at the progress bar above, it seemed that two-thirds had already been contained.
“Damn it! He just arrived, he hasn’t even been near the construction site—how did he discover this?”
Some cultists hiding in the shadows gritted their teeth in frustration.
They had laid many traps around the construction site, but to their dismay, he hadn’t shown up.
Not only had he not shown up, but the concentration of anomalies in the entire town was decreasing!
They immediately realized that someone had discovered this critical secret and was not coming over; they wouldn’t fall for the trap, rendering all the traps and ambushes useless!
Then, a few more bullets fell empty, and they became visibly agitated.
“What’s happening! What exactly is happening! Which figure did he borrow from?! Why is it that as soon as he makes a move, he can directly complete the containment?!”
The cultists hidden in the darkness also evidently considered Colin a user of the “Divine Strike” power.
They just didn’t understand which figure he was using.
But no matter what, feeling the continuous decrease of strange powers around them, they knew they couldn’t drag this out any longer. If they continued to be killed off like this, they would be left with only one path—death!
“No, we can’t keep hiding! Even if we’re discovered, it doesn’t matter!”
“We’re all in! Hold them off, bet our lives on it—we can’t let them get away from here before twelve o’clock!”
A few cultists behind the scenes gritted their teeth, ready to step into the fray.

chapters.title: Chapter 98 - 98 98 My strength is all my own_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 98: Chapter 98 My strength is all my own!_1 Chapter 98: Chapter 98 My strength is all my own!_1 duang!
The shovel struck the black figure’s head, emitting a crisp vibration that echoed endlessly in the pitch-black street.
Colin retracted the shovel, easily containing another shadowy figure.
Once the true nature of these dark figures was discovered, dealing with them wasn’t difficult.
However, just as Colin was about to continue disposing of the black shadows in front of the enemy, he suddenly stopped and, with a smile on his face, turned to a certain direction:
“Can’t sit still? Come on, come on! Let me have a little more fun!”
No sooner had the words fallen than a blood-colored whip lashed out viciously from the darkness.
Colin laughed out loud, with a casual wave he used the shovel to effortlessly slash the bloody whip from midair.
But within that whip seemed to be something else hidden…
A palm-sized oval metal object.
Fragmentation grenade.
“Heh, it’s all these boring weapons. Security should tighten their checks.”
Colin showed no fear, winding up with the shovel, his muscles tensed, and, like playing tennis, he aimed at the grenade and swung the shovel with force.
Bang!
The moment the shovel’s face struck the grenade, it exploded instantly. Yet, the truly lethal fragments hadn’t scattered before the shovel flicked them away, igniting sparks as they spread out over the ground.
And the shovel, recognized by the superior fighters, didn’t even dent from a mere grenade.
Colin himself was completely unharmed.
Even more, he had the spare energy to free up one hand and casually kill one of the dark figures approaching him.
Bang!
Another sniper bullet whizzed past Colin, missing by just a hair’s breadth, always just missing its mark.
The other cultists weren’t idle either; they kept launching attack after attack from the shadows, but to no avail.
That guy was like a bystander strolling through a hail of gunfire, virtually untouched.
And what infuriated them even more was his taunting words.
“Is this really all you’ve got? You think you can hurt me with such petty tricks? Aren’t you being a little too confident? But then again, this really is the limit of what you as weaklings can muster.”
“Even if I need to spare a hand for the shadows and stand in darkness, I’m still not the despair you can confront directly.”
“Let your ‘Mother’ hiding behind you come out…”
His tone, full of arrogance and superiority, turned the eyes of the ones behind the scenes bloodshot, grinding their teeth in fury.
Some of them had roughed it out everywhere and encountered numerous enemies.
But they’d never seen someone who could talk so much shit!
What was even more infuriating was that they really couldn’t take him down right now!
Not only could they not take him down, but they also realized that this guy was getting stronger and stronger!
Some of the guys in the darkness couldn’t sit still any longer.
“It’s one thing to insult us, but to insult our Master… I can’t listen to this anymore! I can’t stand it! I’m going to fight him!”
“No, don’t go, he’s deliberately provoking us! His strength has already exceeded Level 5! Only the Priest can deal with him!”
“What the heck, Level 5? I don’t believe in this evil! I’m fighting a Level 5!”
“Wang Zhi! Where the hell is your mother’s umbilical cord blood injection? Inject me now!”
Soon after, a cultist with Level 2 strength but not in good mental condition roared angrily and suddenly burst out from a corner of the street.
His figure emitted a red light as he charged, his head splitting apart to reveal the huge tumor rooted beneath his skull.
Compared to the “Hemorrhoid Spirit” Colin first encountered, it was obviously a lot stronger.
“I’m going to kill you!”
The tumor trembled, waving a blood-red tentacle covered with thorns.
“Ho ho, knowing how powerful I am, you chose not to run away but to charge at me head-on instead?”
“Do you also want to dance in the air like those ‘leaves’ I’ve sent flying?”
“Fine, consider this a reward for your courage to face me. Savor it, this last moment before death arrives.”
Colin lifted his chin, admiring the ants’ meaningless attempts.
Looking at that terrifying, non-human creature.
Then, he swung his shovel at the creature rushing towards him, and with a whoosh of a splitting air, the opponent burst into countless pieces like a watermelon hit on the spot, arcs of blood and flesh traced through the air before falling to the ground, shattering everywhere.
“You see, I only need to lift my hand to turn you into rubbish on the ground…”
Colin waved his hand to shake off the blood clinging to the shovel.
At this moment, he could easily pick up even a car as if it were foam.
More and more “valid recognitions” had endlessly pushed his strength to the physiognomic standard of a Bonfire Company C level.
These “valid recognitions” included not only the onlookers but also the cultists!
The boost from “The False Powerhouse” enabled him to kill at will in this place.
But…
On the surface, that indeed seemed to be the case.
In reality, Colin didn’t see it that way. He believed that his strength relied entirely on himself—what did that artifact have to do with anything?
He was strong because he was inherently strong!
That so-called mark was nothing more than a catalyst.
Colin felt that the role of “The False Powerhouse” wasn’t actually significant. What he truly relied on was completely himself.
“Feel my strength, face my strength, those who don’t grasp how powerful I am cannot comprehend or recognize just how weak and pitiful they themselves are.”
“Before me, I can no longer see any enemies!”
Colin’s smile faded as he sighed helplessly, suddenly feeling a hint of loneliness.
Hearing this sigh, Hu Xiaoyuan couldn’t help but twitch:
“Damn, I really want to beat you up. Mr. Lin, just who exactly are you borrowing this ‘Divine Strike’ from…”
As she felt a darkness before her eyes, she also silently took note of those hair-raising words, planning to look into the specifics later.
After a long use of an “idol’s” power, an “agent’s” style of speech would also draw close to that of their counterpart.
So sometimes, through this, it’s possible to guess who might be the “ambassador” of whom.
However, Hu Xiaoyuan was also curious about this peculiar speaking style that seemed like it could easily get one killed. No, it was unique…
This “idol” should be famous; why did it seem like she hadn’t heard of them?
But before she could ponder further, she suddenly noticed some figures stealthily moving towards the base.
“Planning to strike at the common people?”
Hu Xiaoyuan gathered her thoughts.
Although the base had some mechanisms left by the Frontier Guards, if there was no one to lead and if the correct course of action wasn’t understood, one would fall into the anomaly called “Project 3-87 Infinite Staircase” while climbing stairs…
Thinking of possible accidents, she decided to return to assist in protecting the civilians, so Mr. Lin wouldn’t be distracted here.
At this point, she had realized that this supporter might have mastered the solution to the dilemma long ago.
Otherwise, those cultists hidden behind the scenes wouldn’t have surfaced.
Just then, she suddenly felt a vibration in the ground.
It seemed like some enormous creature was approaching from afar…
…

chapters.title: Chapter 99: From Now On, I Will Stand at the Top_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 99: Chapter 99: From Now On, I Will Stand at the Top_1 Chapter 99: Chapter 99: From Now On, I Will Stand at the Top_1 Thump…
The ground trembled slightly.
What was that noise?
Colin squinted his eyes and turned to look in the direction of the vibration. Through the pitch-black veil of the night, he could barely make out the silhouette of a massive creature looming over the town.
A faint stench of blood began to pervade the air…
“It’s here, it’s here! The Priest Lord has arrived!”
“Perfect! As long as he’s here, everything will get back on track!”
In the darkness, a group of cultists, enraged by Colin yet helpless, showed ecstatic expressions on their faces.
The arrival of the priest meant victory was within reach!
Meanwhile, as the vibration drew closer, Colin finally saw what that thing looked like—
A gigantic tumor bigger than a dump truck by a whole size.
The tumor was riddled with crimson veins, adorned with countless tendrils of flesh, and shrouded in a faintly glowing red mist.
Under it were six thick legs; barring the absence of wings and skin, it closely resembled the mythological creature “Chaos” from The Classic of Mountains and Seas.
With its emergence, the number of shadowy figures around multiplied suddenly.
“Good, finally something decent has shown up!”
Colin seemed to have finally found some enjoyment, a hint of a smile appearing at the corner of his mouth.
However, feeling a streak of approval wavering due to its appearance, he involuntarily furrowed his brow…
The power that had been steadily growing within him had diminished slightly.
It was only a slight reduction, but it was enough to cause him significant displeasure.
Because this meant that there were already people around who doubted whether he could deal with that monster as he had before!
“My power will not be questioned! Such an extraordinary creature has no place in this town.”
Colin waved his hand, and with absolute power, shattered the surrounding shadows…
He then stood in the middle of the road, hands behind his back, watching the enormous creature charging at him as swiftly as a dump truck, without any intention of dodging.
On the other side, Hu Xiaoyuan, who was planning to retreat, was shocked at the scene and hurriedly warned:
“Mr. Lin! Be careful of that monster! It has been blessed and is difficult to deal with!”
Colin’s figure was dwarfed by the giant creature, like a watermelon to a sesame seed.
The sheer scale of the difference made her hold her breath involuntarily.
Especially seeing that Colin didn’t seem to plan on moving aside, her concern deepened, fearing that Colin might encounter misfortune…
This “idol” was strong, but perhaps a bit too… arrogant and prideful.
“Hmph.”
Colin ignored her, his gaze fixed on the rapidly approaching behemoth, standing as immovable as a rock.
His aura erupted further, spreading swiftly like oil on water, eventually giving rise to a gale.
Such an action reaffirmed the “approval” of many onlookers.
And the behemoth, as gargantuan as a dump truck, hastened its six-legged pace, its veins bursting open to emit a mist of blood.
Colin noticed that this bloody mist, upon touching anything around it, whether organic or inorganic, caused a striking transformation.
Cars grew limbs, metal melded with flesh emitting strange growls, walls sprouted eyes and mouths, vegetation uprooted itself, charging forth alongside the monstrous globe of flesh.
The entire world was mutating, filled with unforgivable corruption and desecration.
In this moment, not only Colin but the gargantuan tumor itself seemed eager to resolve the battle in a single move rather than dragging it out.
After a brief moment of thought, Colin understood why.
Most likely, this blessed power was not meant to last.
The priest had broken free from the “Frontier Guard” and was rushing over, obviously not without some cost.
If things were dragged out, it might have collapsed and disintegrated on its own, and then everything would have settled like dust.
But…
For Colin, that was impossible.
He wouldn’t allow anything more eye-catching than himself to exist in this place!
This matter had to be resolved by his own hands!
“Especially when it dares to harbor thoughts of killing me, how arrogant is that?”
Colin’s gaze was icy as he watched the other approach swiftly, casually reaching into his pocket to pull out something.
Fifty meters.
Thirty meters.
Ten meters.
Five meters.
“The World! Halt!”
Colin stretched out his hand and pointed forward, and a flash of golden light passed, instantly freezing everything in stasis.
Meanwhile, outside the field, just when everyone was holding their breath, waiting for the moment when the two would truly meet, they suddenly found…
The scene before them had abruptly frozen.
Whether it was Colin standing in the middle of the road like a rock or the massive tumbling hunk of flesh in a mad sprint, everything had come to a standstill.
“What’s happened?!”
The crowd was stunned, wondering if there was some bug in the world before them that had caused this lag.
But before they could figure anything out, the scene in front of them started moving again.
A blood-red haze swallowed everything present, the gigantic figure stood in place, and that incessant show-off no longer knew where he was.
“No way…” Hu Xiaoyuan felt a chill in her heart and was a bit frantic.
She was unclear about what the blood-red tumor was, but the fact it had come from the “Frontier Guard” indicated a problem.
If Mr. Lin were dead, they too wouldn’t survive, as they no longer had the capability to deal with those cultists…
“Did we win?! Finally killed that guy?!”
Some cultists cried tears of joy, having had enough of the guy who could neither be beaten nor killed.
However, before their joy lasted long, a sudden wail emanated from the blood-red tumor.
Following that, with a loud thump, the tumor with six large legs collapsed to the ground.
It convulsed continuously, as if trying to stand up again, but a layer of frost quickly spread across its body.
At first, it could still tremble slightly, but eventually, even the trembling disappeared, and within less than a minute, the cold frost had frozen the mass of flesh, almost the size of a large truck.
The temperature of the surrounding environment also plummeted at this moment, making people feel as if they had fallen into an ice cellar, cold to the bone…
Tap, tap, tap…
Clear footsteps emanated from the hunk of flesh.
“Indeed, you possess some strength, but regrettably… challenging me is an imprudent decision.”
A figure stepped on the huge frozen mass of flesh, walking step by step upwards, and to one’s surprise, it was Colin, whom they’d thought to be dead!
“Before my arrival, you might have been equally matched, pulling at each other, with no one capable of standing at the decisive position.”
“However, it’s a pity that such a window of opportunity has already ended.”
Colin put away the Bone Spur in his hand, stretched out his hand, and swept his hair back, his eyes brimming with unabashed arrogance and pride.
With a calm tone, he announced to everyone:
“From now on, I shall stand at the apex.”

chapters.title: Chapter 100 - 100 100 Where is the person How did they
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 100: Chapter 100 Where is the person? How did they disappear?_1 Chapter 100: Chapter 100 Where is the person? How did they disappear?_1 The vast street was empty and silent as people looked on in shock at the man who had crushed the giant tumor under his foot.
“Is the Priest Lord… dead?”
“How is that possible…”
Some of the hidden Red Moon Cultists couldn’t believe it.
In just those few seconds, they didn’t even know exactly what had happened; everything seemed to have come to an end.
Even faced with their murmuring, many people were already too scared to respond.
Not just them, even their own comrades were shocked by the situation in front of them.
In their eyes, the appearance of this thing was most likely to lead to a tough battle, but after just a “pause,” all crises seemed to have been resolved.
At this moment, Colin stood on the corpse of the giant monster that had been hunted like a trophy, becoming the undeniable focal point of the scene.
His power also reached its peak at this moment.
The glowing aura pulsed and swelled again, spreading like a hurricane in all directions, carrying bone-chilling cold with it.
“Very good, that’s how it should be.”
Colin lifted his chin, looking around at the crowd with satisfaction, as if he was inspecting subjects who had submitted to him.
He waved his hand, seemingly wanting to say something more, but a message suddenly popped up in his mind—
[Solo Trial Task (3/3)— “Recover the lost low-risk Containment Subject ‘Shadow Stone Buddha’,” completed.]
[This “Solo Trial Task” has been fully completed.]
[Would you like to return to the initial task acceptance location via the company’s pathway?]
[Time remaining to decide: 5 minutes 37 seconds.]
[Note: If you choose not to return via the company pathway, the task reward will be processed in one hour.]
“Heh, Bonfire Special Containment Subject Company…”
Colin narrowed his eyes, highly dissatisfied with this message that suddenly arrived, interrupting his further proclamation.
After reading the contents, he decided to return via the company’s pathway but did not plan to return immediately.
“Some people who are courting death haven’t been dealt with yet, they need to be handled before I can leave; never mind five minutes, three minutes is enough.”
Colin’s words fell, and he raised his right hand, which wore a ring with a large eyeball on it.
Then, with a thought, a beautiful blue figure drifted from the cold mist and merged into his body…
The next instant, his body seemed to defy gravity as he dove toward those hidden cultists…
Many Red Moon Cultists only reacted at this point, but, unfortunately, it was already too late.
A massive bone-chilling coldness arrived with the howling of the wind, and within the area shrouded by the ice fog, the temperature plummeted to negative degrees, with icicles forming mid-air, secretly striking those who wanted to retaliate.
All those struck by these icicles turned into lifelike ice statues in an instant.
The place covered in ice and snow seemed like it had entered an Arctic world.
“He’s so strong, what kind of tactic is this?”
Hu Xiaoyuan’s eyes widened in shock, along with her clean-up crew companions.
They gained a deeper understanding of Mr. Lin’s strength.
At that moment, the walkie-talkie on her chest suddenly emitted a “zzt zzt” electrical noise, followed by a weak man’s voice:
“What’s going on? I’m ‘Frontier Guard’ Luo Wenhao, what happened here? Can anyone hear me… ”
“Yes, it’s me, Hu Xiaoyuan, the anomaly has been dealt with…”
“Dealt with?” The man on the other end of the limitless walkie-talkie clearly sounded shocked.
Immediately after, his voice came again quickly: “The anomaly indices around here are indeed dropping rapidly, what happened, did you see that monster? Did it run away?”
In the eyes of the ‘Frontier Guard,’ that giant monster was clearly impossible to defeat, so its current silence obviously meant it had fled.
“He didn’t run away because… it has been resolved.”
Without waiting for Luo Wenhao to ask, Hu Xiaoyuan quickly explained, “Our support arrived, a very strong ‘Agent.’ He settled all the problems in no time…”
She paused for a moment, then added with a sigh, “Almost with an air of overwhelming power.”
“Where is he now? Let me contact him…”
“He… disappeared!”
Hu Xiaoyuan was about to say something, but suddenly noticed that the “Agent,” who stood out with his surging energy, was gone!
What happened?!
How did a person who was just fine a moment ago vanish into thin air?
“Maybe he left after resolving the issue?”
A voice suddenly appeared behind Hu Xiaoyuan; she was startled and almost fell down the stairs.
When she turned around, she saw a man about one meter eighty, dressed in a white suit, wearing a white hat, with a somewhat pale complexion appearing behind her—
An elite from the “Great Wall” department, the leader of the “Frontier Guard!”
“Leader Luo! When did you get here…”
“I, cough cough…”
Luo Wenhao in the white suit coughed twice, with blood on the corner of his mouth. He pulled out a handkerchief from his pocket to wipe it before he continued, “My situation isn’t important. If nothing unexpected happened here, this must have been a Level 7 ‘Agent.'”
“When I arrived, I confirmed that all the problems around had indeed been resolved.
“The power of a Level 7 ‘Agent’ is terrifying.”
Luo Wenhao looked at the fog slowly drifting above the street, shock evident in his eyes, as he murmured to himself.
If not for a Level 7, this could not have been done with such ease.
As far as he knew, leaving aside the titles and positions, there were roughly nine levels from 1 to 9, with higher numbers indicating stronger energy levels.
Level 7 is one in ten thousand; the total number in the country is less than three hundred, not enough to allocate to each city.
Normally, only important cities or regions would have the chance to see one, and he didn’t expect to encounter one here…
“It’s a pity, it seems like he had something else to attend to, or maybe he didn’t want to draw attention, so he left in a hurry. It’s a shame I couldn’t meet him and learn something…” Luo Wenhao shook his head.
Not wanting to draw attention… Hu Xiaoyuan heard this and almost couldn’t keep a straight face.
“Mr. Lin hasn’t gone far…”
“No need, such individuals are always rushed for time; let’s not disturb him.”
Luo Wenhao rationalized Colin’s disappearance for him and then waved his hand as if he thought of something. He paused and said, “Right, do you have the records of the recent fight? Let me have a look…”
He was just one step away from being a resident Level 5 ‘Agent’; perhaps taking a look could lead to a breakthrough.
“Yes, I do… Huh?”
Hu Xiaoyuan took out her recorder, but as she turned it on, she found that the content she had just recorded seemed to have vanished.
It was not only her, but the recordings of others and even those of the onlookers with mobile phones had disappeared.
“That shouldn’t be, what happened…”
“This must be the result of carrying some special Containment Subject…”
Luo Wenhao, with the experience of someone who has been through it all, offered a reasonable explanation for the phenomenon.
“By the way, can you sketch?”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 101 - 101 101 Social Death_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 101: Chapter 101 Social Death_1 Chapter 101: Chapter 101 Social Death_1 “Will do…”
“Then see if you can draw it out, let me take a look. Just mentioning Mr. Lin’s name isn’t jogging my memory…”
“I seem to… have forgotten, I only remember that his name was Mr. Lin.”
“Uh, no worries, looks like this mysterious object still has a profound influence. But it seems like you haven’t forgotten the events, so write a report later.”
Luo Wenhao said it was not a big issue.
At that moment, the walkie-talkie crackled to life, as if someone was trying to make contact.
“This is the Special Operations Support Battalion, can you hear me? We’ve broken through the abnormality on the outskirts of the town, support is on the way, please hold on…”
“Old Lu? This is Luo Wenhao, the issue has been resolved…”
“Resolved?” The voice on the other end of the walkie-talkie also paused in surprise.
“What’s there to be surprised about? You came with that Level 7 ‘Agent’ right? You’re really lucky…”
“Level 7 ‘Agent’? Wait, are you saying a Level 7 ‘Agent’ just came by?”
“Yeah, don’t tell me you didn’t know.”
“Impossible, absolutely impossible. There is no way a Level 7 ‘Agent’ would be here; even a Level 6 is unlikely…”
Hearing this firm statement, Luo Wenhao was startled, “What do you mean?”
“I’ll explain the specifics later. For now, just know that there was a recent command from above, an emergency mobilization of all personnel above Level 6 to stop whatever they are doing and head to the capital of our province. They wouldn’t be here now, and we might even be called over after a while…”
“So, that Level 7 ‘Agent’ is a bit suspicious…”
Luo Wenhao, feeling a chill in his heart, exchanged looks with Hu Xiaoyuan, growing increasingly silent.
We’ll leave Mr. Lin’s situation aside for now…
What truly made Luo Wenhao apprehensive was the mobilization order mentioned by the other party.
If nothing goes wrong…
It predicted that some kind of natural disaster, threatening the country or even the world, was likely to occur, and all capable individuals must start mobilizing for it.
…
Dong——Dong——Dong——
The distant and ancient chimes of the clock echoed in his ears.
When Colin came to, he found himself back inside the house, surrounded by darkness.
The digital clock on the wall showed the current time was: 00:37:59.
Still night…
The heavy sound of the chimes seemed to suppress the negative effects within him, slightly.
Colin casually turned on the light and then seemed to remember something, “My strength doesn’t need this kind of thing to prove it.”
As he spoke, he reached into his neckline and with a swoosh, tore off a sticker, carelessly throwing it onto the floor.
Then, Colin’s expression stiffened, and he slowly sat down on the sofa. As he recalled his recent memories, the confident smile at the corner of his mouth gradually faded, growing stern…
After who knows how long, he couldn’t help but draw in a cold breath.
“Shit, what the hell did I just say? How could I say something like that?!”
A strong sense of “aftereffect” exploded within him.
Colin was restless, his heels arching, his toes curling on the floor awkwardly twitching, and goosebumps sprouting all over his body.
“It’s over, it’s over. I remember many people were filming with their phones just now, dammit! I actually forgot to conceal myself, didn’t even wear a mask, now I’m done for, I…”
Thinking about the possibility of his words being recorded and uploaded to the internet, then being seen by friends who might call him…
Just the thought made Colin feel as though ants were crawling all over his body.
If that were truly the case…
He might as well let Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis make a comeback and take him for a reboot.
However, it seemed like he remembered something, he quickly plugged in his phone to charge and then turned on the computer, starting to search for related topics.
Luckily, no related videos have surfaced for the time being…
This allowed Colin to breathe a sigh of relief.
Then, when he thought about the experiences of the Bonfire Company’s evaluation department employees who initially tested this item, he consoled himself, and his embarrassment was alleviated once again.
After all, no amount of trash talk can compare to live-streaming an affair with an electric fan in front of the public.
If he had done something like that…
Then there really wouldn’t be anything left in life worth clinging to.
“Right, looking at the big picture, the unusual incident hasn’t appeared massively in the public eye, which means the authorities are suppressing it – even if there’s a compromising video of me, it probably won’t leak that easily…”
“The thing is, without a disguise, it’s highly likely that the government officials can find me, no, it’s certain – even if the video isn’t clear, they can still learn about me through those five survivors…”
“Sigh, is my life of hiding in plain sight coming to an end?”
Colin sighed, guessing that there was a very high chance of him being co-opted to become an insider.
True gold can’t be hidden forever, even when concealed…
Damn, why am I still having such narcissistic thoughts? Is the negative effect not fully worn off yet?
Colin shook his head and pondered the possible situations that might arise if he were found.
Though many people joke about special ability holders potentially being thrown into a lab for dissection, it appears that the relevant departments have been established, so they probably wouldn’t do anything so counterproductive.
The likelihood of him being co-opted was the greatest.
It’s just that after being co-opted, the secrets of “Bonfire Company” would probably not be safe.
“Although there’s no direct evidence, it seems that there are also official personnel inside Bonfire Company, who have been co-opted as well?”
Colin speculated there might be some kind of connection between the two sides, but he couldn’t guess much with so little information.
However, what mattered more than these was that, once his emotions had stabilized, he pulled out the parchment.
At this moment, it had begun to settle the task at hand.
[In this incident, your evaluation is: A-.]
[The following is the task settlement for this incident – “Bonfire Points*1200”, “Silver Clearance Certificate*1”.]
[All items have been transferred to the “Storage Room”, please check.]
“What, that’s all the reward I get for this task?”
Colin grumbled, feeling that although the task was overall simple, he had done quite well, but to his surprise, the task rewards were indeed just that.
Aside from that, he did learn quite a bit from this task.
For instance, he hadn’t expected that Earth’s problems seem to be not so small, especially that dark city…
The sense of oppression that place gave him could be said to be unprecedented.
Moving a bit further to the prairie…
Though he didn’t know what was up there, it looked just as dangerous.
Of course, aside from those two, the overall difficulty of the task was not high, truly within the F Level scope.
That final village…
“As long as you figure out the pattern and convey it to those relevant people, then set up a few more traps, and finally avoid facing that massive meatball’s desperate attack, the issue gets resolved.”
Colin felt that even if his inventory was halved, he could easily clear the task.
However, before he could continue reflecting deeper, he suddenly noticed.
A line of blood-like text had emerged on the parchment.
.
.
.
Update first, then revise

chapters.title: Chapter 102 - 102 102 Out-of-Control Copy Script
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 102: Chapter 102 Out-of-Control Copy “Script City—Passionate Paradise”._1 Chapter 102: Chapter 102 Out-of-Control Copy “Script City—Passionate Paradise”._1 [Team Trial Task—”Script City: Passionate Paradise”]is now open, please check the [Task Bar]for details.
“‘Passionate Paradise’? What a unique name, it doesn’t sound like anything serious. I have been looking at various F Level team promotion copies, but I don’t seem to recall this one…”
Colin was initially curious about the strange name, and then he began to ponder another matter—
Why is the font name of this task blood red?
You should know that the current task display, even for the “Descent” projects, is in normal black color; this situation has not yet occurred.
“Could this be…”
Colin blinked, considered some possibilities, and suddenly felt a bit anxious…
Not dwelling on that, he opened the [Task Bar]with a glimmer of hope and flipped through it until he found that red-titled task.
[Team Trial Task—”Script City: Passionate Paradise”]
“Description”: This is a Utopia as anticipated by normal heterosexual men, filled with all kinds of beautiful romantic encounters, where all fantasies of desire can be fulfilled. Come on, enter “Passionate Paradise” and test the weaknesses of being a man, experiencing the thrill of being coveted and embraced from both sides…
“Requirement”: Enter the copy on November 3rd and survive for seven days.
“Hint”: Be cautious of anything that happens in “Script City: Passionate Paradise”!
“Event Rewards”: “Advanced Talent Lottery Ticket*1”, “Bonfire Points*500”.
“Notice”: Prohibited from using… within “Script City: Passionate Paradise”, otherwise bear the consequences yourself.
…
“This description, it honestly doesn’t seem very serious either, is this really a task?”
Colin, looking at the above content, felt his unease growing stronger for no apparent reason. He took a deep breath to suppress that indescribable feeling.
Then, he looked at the event reward information.
“Advanced Talent Lottery Ticket, Talent… this thing seems only to be unlocked after reaching E Level, right?”
Colin remembered seeing in the Interaction Hall’s explanatory posts that when you’re promoted to E Level permissions, a Talent Grid will be unlocked in your “personal resume”. This Talent Grid can be equipped with a “Talent Skill” made internally by the Bonfire Company.
Talent Skills enhance oneself, some even manipulate electricity and such…
Anyway, they sound pretty powerful.
What’s most important is that if the Talent feels unsuitable, it can be changed at any time for a small amount of points.
Furthermore, once D Level permissions are reached, the number of Talent Grids increases to two. If the two acquired Talents synergize well, the effect of 1+1 is far greater than 2, which can be considered a qualitative change.
However, this is still a bit far off for Colin. He gathered his wandering thoughts and looked at the last notice.
“…What’s going on here? Prohibited from using what? C’mon, finish your sentence. What’s the deal with erasing the key information?”
Colin scratched his head in annoyance. After scanning the notice a few times, he decided to consult his colleagues when in doubt.
Although those guys sometimes joke about his death, when he asks them something, they really do provide earnest answers, and most of the time their advice is quite useful.
‘I hope this task isn’t what I think it is…’
Colin silently prayed in his heart and then opened the Interaction Hall. Despite the late hour, it was as bustling as ever.
“Unnamed123456”: Does anyone know what’s up with the F Level promotion task “Script City·Passionate Paradise”? I have a friend…
“Unnamed114514”: @Unnamed123456, I know, I know. I’m quite familiar with this task, but due to some reasons, it’s not good to talk about “it” rashly. If you’re curious about it, so I suggest we chat privately…
…
Seems like you really know your stuff, but you guys, aren’t I going to be dead by the time we chat privately?
Colin grumbled and waited a few seconds before quickly seeing replies from other colleagues.
“The east wind blew again last night in the small building”: Oh shoot, Passionate Paradise? Your friend is probably done for…
“Son of Sadomasochism”: @Unnamed123456, all I can say is, mourn your loss, that’s a place even I, the master of sadomasochism, wouldn’t dare to set foot in lightly…
“Son of Doom”: Brother Shunzi, is this ‘friend’ you’re talking about actually yourself?
“Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦”: What’s happening, mourn what, what’s with this copy? I haven’t been promoted yet, so I don’t know…
“Professor Cute Cuddle”: @Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦, it’s an Out-of-Control Copy from the F Level promotion task list, a copy specifically targeting men, I heard it’s hard even without being out of control, let alone now…
“Loafing Immortal”: Wuu wuu wuu, targeted at men? I didn’t expect to encounter such things in this era, tears fall as I shiver with anger, when will we men be able to stand up…
“Son of Sadomasochism”: Tch, Brother Shunzi, if you have any last wishes just spill them. Remember to @ me when you’re doing the task, so I can time my card drawing…
“Lifecoach Kawaii-many”: @Unnamed123456, whether it’s your friend or you, all I can say is mourn your loss. Normally with regular “Copies,” even if you fail, you can come back; at most, you just restart the task, there’s no real death. But with “Out-of-Control Copies,” once you go in, you won’t come out, no one knows what really happens inside. There are currently fourteen types of copies for the F Level promotion, only two of which are out-of-control. One is “Lightless Zone,” and the other is the very “Script City·Passionate Paradise” that Brother Shunzi is talking about…
“Wave Rider Seek Pig”: What’s said above is true, “The Descent Project” still gives a chance to see someone who completed the first loop come back and hop around; “Out-of-Control Copies,” once you go in, I’ve never seen anyone come back…
“Anonymous135”: Too bad, I thought I was going to witness the rise of a big shot, but didn’t expect…
“Wave Rider Seek Pig”: Indeed a pity, I mean the Golden Card…
