Colin murmured to himself, looked for a while longer, then suddenly jumped into the conversation and said, “The plans are pretty good, it’s just, based on some intel I’ve gathered, if you really go ahead like this, most of you will probably die once you’re in.”
As the message was sent out, the discussion group, which had been somewhat quiet, suddenly erupted again.
“Miss Nell’s Dog”: What do you mean? Everyone will die?
“Loafing Immortal”: Why is that?
“Soul Lock Warden”: Brother Shunzi, does this mean… is there some inside information?
“Wandering Speedy Lad”: Brother Shunzi, don’t hesitate to be more explicit…
Clearly, Colin’s words were like a bucket of cold water poured on their heads, sending them into panic all at once.
Seeing this, Colin didn’t hold back and quickly drafted a message to send in.
“From what I know, this Out-of-Control Copy was initially created by Bonfire Company to deal with some special existence. As for what that is, maybe some people with connections can figure it out without me saying, so it’s not important…”
Not important? How is it not important? You might as well explain clearly what it is, and how does it relate to our dead-end situation, Shunzi, focus on the essentials for God’s sake!!!
As the few people anxiously awaited, Colin sent the next message.
“Here comes the crucial part, the purpose behind its creation was to train employees’ self-will. Therefore, the key to conquering this copy lies in relying solely on oneself, not on any items that could affect one’s mental state, so preparing mental items and drugs is the wrong choice…”
“Of course, another key point is that this Out-of-Control Copy conflicts with a certain item, so you absolutely must not use this item once inside…”
With this, Colin paused, and the employees, seeing the next part not appearing, were almost itching with frustration — if we can’t use what item, just spit it out!
They hated those who spoke in half-truths the most!
They felt like rushing through the parchment to give that guy a whack on the head.
But Colin didn’t leave them hanging for long and quickly sent another message.
“The name of this item is ‘Book of Fate: Fragment.’ Once you use it, it will trigger extremely severe consequences that you all are definitely not able to bear. This point was also mentioned in the mission prompt, only it was erased due to some reasons.”
What?! We can’t use the “Book of Fate: Fragment”?
Upon reading the message, a mix of disbelief and sudden clarity arose in everyone’s heart, as if they understood a lot more in an instant.
In fact, they had guessed as much, but were never certain…
After all, if the guess turned out wrong, it would be like cutting off their own arm, the strongest and most robust one at that.
And even when Colin spoke of the matter with certainty, they still weren’t quite sure.
“Miss Nell’s Dog”: Wait a second? We can’t rely on external objects?! Then what, did I take medicine for nothing?
“Wandering Speedy Lad”: Holy shit, were my estrogen pills taken in vain?
“Loafing Immortal”: @Unnamed123456, is your source reliable? Where did you get this information from?
“Soul Lock Warden”: Right, do you have any evidence to back up what you’re saying?
“Unnamed123456”: I can’t prove anything to you guys like you want. All I can tell you is the copy is about cooperative adventuring and not competition… As for the rest, all you have to do is think about why I’ve survived multiple descents from the “Advent Project.”
…
After sending this message, Colin wanted to release information about a few special items as well, but after some thought, he decided against it.
Because he figured that this bunch would probably check his “household register.”
As someone slightly famous within the company, the messages he posted recently would still be searchable.
Discovering information on their own would be more credible to them than just being told directly.
However, what Colin didn’t expect was…
In the next few days, the developments among this group seemed a bit off.
Colin had thought that his maneuvers would convince them, but while they believed him, they didn’t believe him entirely.
The group knew he might truly have internal channels, but they doubted whether what he revealed was the whole truth…
After all, without absolute proof, the possibility of Colin deliberately sending them to their deaths wasn’t low.
But as much as they doubted, what if—Brother Shunzi really did have good intentions?
After pondering for a while, someone, confused by the possibilities of truth and lies, couldn’t help but feel perplexed: It’s unclear, really unclear…
Suddenly, things became more complicated.
This matter concerned their very lives, and they had to be extra cautious with any choices they made.
No one wanted to be blindly deceived into death, and they were no exception.
Then, Colin saw that for the five-person copy, there were more than a dozen discussion subgroups, some with four people, some with three, some with just two…
It was only at this moment that Colin realized that these four individuals discussing mutual help with great enthusiasm in the group…
Didn’t agree on everything, each harboring their own doubts and calculations.
“You guys really— don’t have as much cunning as a girls’ dormitory…”
Colin, seeing that “Wandering Speedy Lad” and “Soul Lock Warden” had sent invites to a three-person discussion group, couldn’t help but raise his hand to rub his forehead.
Without even thinking, he knew that the two excluded individuals were likely their “suspects.”
“Damn, there’s a seismic drill going on outside, and you guys are also having a drill of seeking enemies in the void, huh…”
Colin sighed heavily. After several rounds, he was becoming a bit neurotic; to keep his composure, he simply decided to ignore these messages from now on.
He had done what he could, and for the rest—whatever will be, will be. He’s done playing server!
Time passed by slowly, and after two more drills, the day that they had all been obsessing over, November 3rd, finally arrived.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 114 - 114 114 Entering Passionate Paradise _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 114: Chapter 114 Entering “Passionate Paradise” _1 Chapter 114: Chapter 114 Entering “Passionate Paradise” _1 November 3rd, 11:21:57 AM, inside the room.
“There are 39 minutes left until twelve o’clock…”
Colin withdrew his gaze from the electronic wall clock and then glanced over at the small discussion group on the parchment.
After a few days of working together, everyone had chosen to follow his advice, meaning they no longer used any drugs or items, and they had abandoned the idea of giving “Script City·Passionate Paradise” a tiny bit of shock from the “Book of Fate.”
At least that was the case on the surface; what they chose to do privately, Colin wasn’t clear about, and he couldn’t force them…
To be honest, he felt that this group was starting to go mad.
And it seemed that this crazed way of thinking was a bit contagious…
“This is making me wonder if there’s a traitor or a water ghost from ‘Passionate Paradise’ among you four, deliberately leading you astray… Hiss, no, no, I can’t start going crazy with you.”
Colin put away the parchment. A boat won’t sink because of the water around it, but it will because of the water inside it.
Then, he began the routine check of his equipment and items to reinforce his impression.
This time around, some equipment was banned in the instance, which could be seen as a nerf.
Currently, he could use… “Servant of Money,” “Ring of Flame Dominance,” “Fusion Card: Smiling Mountain of Corpses,” “Revolver Contrarian,” “Widow Yukionna,” “Murky Energy Shard,” “Analytical Lens” —
Well, excluding those “The False Powerhouses,” it didn’t seem like he had been nerfed much; he could still use his core equipment.
Colin took a deep breath and looked up again at the electronic wall clock, making sure he still had some time. He casually opened his computer and deleted all his study files, intending to leave his innocence in this world…
After completing all this, he lay back on his bed, somewhat nervously.
This mission didn’t require him to go himself. Like the “Ascension Project,” all he had to do was lie on the bed and wait for the transport at the start of the mission.
As time ticked by, not knowing exactly how many seconds had passed, Colin suddenly looked blank.
A distant and ancient bell tolled in his ears, and a surge of dense fog rolled in.
He felt his body continuously falling.
Not knowing how much time had gone by, Colin came to his senses, blinked, sat up, and found himself in a somewhat unfamiliar small room.
“Is this… the world inside ‘Passionate Paradise’?”
Colin propped himself up from the bed and looked around the room, examining the unfamiliar décor.
The room was half the size of his bedroom, seemingly just over ten square meters.
Importantly, this tiny ten-square-meter room incredibly contained bookshelves, a television, a sofa, a desk, a computer, and even a small bathroom. The surrounding pink decorations also exuded an inexplicably warm feeling…
The entire room of just over ten square meters, though small, was completely equipped.
“It’s also a rarity for the designer, managing to fit so many things into such a small room…”
Colin watched with admiration, though the décor style looked somewhat familiar, as if he had seen it somewhere before, yet he couldn’t quite recall where.
Not dwelling too much on the room’s layout, as soon as he was sure there was no danger, he immediately checked whether his “Storage Room” and other functions were still usable.
“Everything should be functioning normally; that information from the Two-Faced guy wasn’t wrong…”
Colin pondered the information he had received at the time.
He was told that after arriving, he would be assigned a new identity and be required to act according to assigned tasks, but a mission had yet to appear…
However, at this very moment, a line of white text suddenly emerged on Colin’s retinas.
[You are awake…]
[Your name is Colin, and you remember being a kindhearted high school student with a non-blood-related sister whom you’ve depended on since childhood, living in this small room left behind by your parents…]
[Today is yet another serene day with a gentle breeze and a warm sun. You, as usual, wake up from your nap, ready to brush your teeth, wash your face, tidy up your appearance, and eat the breakfast made by your sister. You’ll go to school before 1:30 PM, return home at 6 PM, and finally sleep before 9 PM, passing peacefully through this ordinary day.]
[You know that you! Must! Not! Break! This! Daily! Routine!!!]
Is this the narrator? Colin sensed something, certain that this had little to do with Bonfire Company—the style of the text output was just different.
Then, he briefly looked at the contents above…
“A high school student? A sister not related by blood? Orphaned?”
“No wonder I felt this room layout seemed familiar. A high school student in Neon, although it seems somewhat out of place. The books on the shelf are all in Chinese—’A Brief History of Time’, ‘Calculus’, ‘Mysteries of Survival’, ‘Terrifying Marine Depths’. Oh, they cover quite a range…”
“Brushing teeth, washing face, having breakfast prepared by my sister, going to school and coming home, another tranquil day… Is this what today’s task requires?”
Colin contemplated thoughtfully, but upon seeing the last line of text, particularly the narrator that seemed paler by a few shades, he couldn’t help but mock in his mind: “If I shouldn’t break it, then I shouldn’t, but what’s with all these exclamation marks?”
However, speaking of which, with the information at hand, he temporarily couldn’t spot what was amiss about this “narrator”…
The mission seemed ordinary as well, skimming over everything without going into detail, so it’s possible that the dangerous aspects would only be encountered during its execution…
“I have no idea what roles the other four got, hmm, it surely can’t be that they all turned into girls… But I can’t contact them now, so I just hope they don’t end up doing something fatal.”
Colin silently prayed for them for three seconds before something came to mind. He glanced over at the digital clock on a simple-style shelf formed by a few wooden sticks—12:07 PM, without seconds.
“Judging by the feeling of time passing, it has indeed been about seven minutes, so does this time align with reality?”
He remembered the brief mentioning to be mindful of the mission time, so he made a mental note of it.
Then, Colin rose from the bed, ready to get up and brush his teeth and wash his face as required, to begin today’s task.
But just at this moment, some mission information appeared in his mind.
[Team Promotion Mission—”Script City: Passionate Paradise”.]
[Event One: Survive seven days in ‘Passionate Paradise’ with remaining time 167:52:31.]
Note: Completing this event will be considered as completing this round of promotion missions and will result in a certain amount of reward upon return.
[Event Two: Investigate the various anomalies in “Passionate Paradise” to gather substantial information.]
Note: Upon your return, rewards will be given according to the completion status of the mission.
[Event Three: There exists a certain special, conflict-free path to life enhancement in “Passionate Paradise”, a route specifically left behind by a former senior executive of the company in this instance. Please try to understand it and take it out of “Passionate Paradise”.]
Note: Completing this event will earn a significant reward and unlock additional special feature access.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 115 - 115 115 The Yukionna Miss Who Doesnt
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 115: Chapter 115: The “Yukionna” Miss Who Doesn’t Understand Human Emotions_1 Chapter 115: Chapter 115: The “Yukionna” Miss Who Doesn’t Understand Human Emotions_1 “The task from Bonfire Company, late but finally here…”
Colin pursed his lips, glanced briefly at it, and saw that the task rewards were written all over it, but there was not a word on how to get back.
So, the biggest problem with “Passionate Paradise” is not being able to go home?
“The time for event one aligns with reality, didn’t see any issues there; event two is probably about investigating and collecting abnormal information or something, an optional task that doesn’t have to be completed; actually, what seems interesting is this event three…”
Colin pondered as he headed towards the small restroom—some kind of special life enhancement path without conflict?
It seemed like it was left by that high-level employee…
Colin didn’t know how ‘high-level’ this ‘high-level’ was, since it was the first time he encountered the term ‘high-level’ being used in the company description.
“Could it be by the founder of ‘Script City,’ the holder of the advanced item ‘Script Book’?”
Colin made some associations, but unfortunately, once cooled, they all uniformly had a “former company” prefix…
“Poor guy, got fired as soon as he died.”
Colin sighed at the fate of the “former company” employees, then continued to focus on this event three.
He was quite curious about what the life enhancement without conflicts would be like.
And the task rewards seemed to be quite substantial; the appearance of the word “huge” indicated that Bonfire Points would start at least at ten thousand.
Not to mention it seemed to unlock some additional special function privileges…
Unfortunately, just being able to get out alive would be good enough; Colin simply looked at it without much intention to complete it.
Shaking his head slightly, Colin looked at the toothbrush and face cloth in the small restroom that seemed to be new and unopened.
“Good thing, I definitely couldn’t stand it if I had to use something that someone else used before; who knows how many people have traveled through this cabin before…”
Colin muttered to himself, opened the packaging, and incidentally glanced at the mirror in front of the washbasin.
Black hair, black eyes, with a fair complexion, he looked much younger than in reality, dressed in a black suit-like school uniform for boys, appearing very placid, now showing the “gentle” quality mentioned by the Narrator—
This appearance seemed to be his own but with some unnecessary minor adjustments.
One can only say, good basics, the flaw does not obscure the virtues.
After a simple brushing and face washing, Colin was tidying up his appearance when suddenly he felt a piece of information emerge in his mind.
[Event Four: Before leaving the room, please wear “Widow Yukionna” on the ring finger of your right hand, and try to obtain its help.]
Note: “Yukionna” possesses a certain level of self-awareness, and upon realizing “Passionate Paradise,” it will inevitably exhibit emotions. Please find a way to calm and gain its forgiveness; furthermore, it has minimal contact with people, with very simple cognition, so you can reasonably obtain help through this point.
…
“Should I take it out at this time?”
Colin was startled, almost forgetting about it, but looking at the content of this task, it didn’t seem like it was issued by “Bonfire Company,” otherwise it would have popped up together with the previous three.
Without surprises, it felt more like a hint hurriedly sent by “Bunny” madam amidst her busy schedule.
Without thinking too much, he took out a ring with a large gemstone from his pocket.
No sooner had he taken it out and put it on his finger, than he felt an intense bone-chilling cold emanating from it.
The pain came in waves, like the vibration of sound…
Clearly, “Yukionna” had sensed something amiss and knew she was back in “Passionate Paradise,” so she was trying to interact with him, which likely meant none of her words were particularly nice…
“Probably calling me trash, fucking trash bastard shit or something… tsk, need to lower the standards…”
Colin endured the piercing chill on his ring finger from “Yukionna,” waiting for her to continue venting her anger.
He waited for several minutes until the stabbing pain slowly subsided…
Then, he began to sense an indescribable mix of negative emotions like “grievance,” “despair,” and “fear.”
Vaguely, he could even hear indistinct sobbing…
“‘Yukionna’s’ activity is higher than I thought; having a certain self-awareness is one thing, but to also have such rich emotions… previously, seeing only a blurry shadow, I thought she was like those thoughtless automatons akin to servants.”
Colin was slightly surprised and waited a while longer before raising his right hand to look at the large gemstone and speaking:
“I can feel your rejection, but you never mentioned it early, so I didn’t know you were so repulsed by this place; though, looking at the situation, it seems you, like me, don’t want to stay here either…”
“Why don’t we open our hearts and work together to escape.”
“Miss Yukionna, you wouldn’t want to be taken in by this cursed place again, would you?”
No sooner had he spoken when Colin suddenly saw a burst of snowy white breath spray out from the giant eyes directly onto his face.
It was chillingly cold…
But, the breath didn’t seem dangerous.
After thinking it over, Colin spoke up again:
“To make up for my mistake, I’ll do everything I can to get you out again, and when the time comes I will also break your seal, so you can be free again. Consider it my reparation to you, I guarantee it with my life…”
After whispering this, Colin added silently to himself, ‘After all, I never said I wouldn’t capture you again and reseal you after you’re free…’
Miss Yukionna, who hadn’t had much contact with humans, seemed unaware of human treachery and the complexities involved. After Colin gave his promise, he could feel the coldness from the ring diminishing significantly.
Clearly, she was somewhat persuaded…
A wave of emotion flowed through the ring.
“Good, I’m glad you’ve agreed to help. As long as it can make up for the harm I’ve caused you, I’m willing to do anything.”
Colin ‘CUPped’ (pua) the words, aiming to gain more favor.
Feeling the malice in the ring diminish further, he couldn’t help but mutter to himself—haven’t you already been caught once? How can you still be so naive? Have you turned foolish from being in the ring for too long…
Colin, standing in front of the mirror and straightening his appearance, spoke up:
“By the way, you’ve escaped from here once before; can the same method be used to escape again?”
After he finished speaking, he felt a thread of consciousness carrying a chill pass into his hand.
This consciousness wasn’t any spoken language or text, but it was directly comprehensible—
Don’t know?
You don’t know how you escaped…
Colin pursed his lips and didn’t say any more, finally he wiped his face and looked at the time.
12:18 PM.
The time matched up with the remaining task time in his mind.
“The so-called task of paying attention to time, what exactly does that entail?”
Colin murmured to himself and looked around the room, preparing to search for any notes left by his predecessors.
At that moment, there was a gentle knock at the door. Startled, he stopped what he was doing and turned to look toward the door. Before he could sense anything, he immediately heard a girl’s voice coming from downstairs—
“Brother, it’s time to eat.”
Is this… the sister who is supposed to depend on me, as the Narrator said?
Colin also remembered what the Two-Faced brother had said, that he mustn’t let them notice anything odd about themselves.
So after hesitating for a couple of seconds, he responded, and with a few steps reached the door, ready to go downstairs.
However…
The moment he opened the door, Colin suddenly remembered something important: if it was his sister who had called him down for a meal, then who was it that knocked…
Who else could it be?
A sense of indescribable absurdity enveloped him in an instant.
And it was at that moment, he suddenly heard a trembling, fearful voice at his ear.
“Brother, don’t answer, that’s not me…”
..
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 116 - 116 116 Sister Says Downstairs Is Dangerous_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 116: Chapter 116: Sister Says Downstairs Is Dangerous_1 Chapter 116: Chapter 116: Sister Says Downstairs Is Dangerous_1 Colin felt as if a bloody character had appeared above his head.
“Danger”!
“Damn it, what’s going on, which one is the right one…”
Colin cursed inwardly, feeling a chill running up his spine, and subconsciously wanted to turn his head. The whispered voice was identical to the one downstairs, it was also “sister’s” voice.
Obviously, the one who had just knocked on the door must be the one who was speaking…
But Colin couldn’t determine which one was real; he had a premonition that picking the wrong one would definitely be a fatal question.
“My instinct tells me that the one downstairs is real, and this one on the second floor is fake! After all, the Narrator’s initial request was to go eat with the one downstairs, anyway, no matter what, I must not turn back…”
Colin’s scalp tightened, forcibly stopping the thought of turning his head.
At this moment, although he hadn’t turned his head, he could “sense” an image in his mind: a petite figure huddled in the corner of the hallway, seemingly trembling as it stared at him, its pitch-black gaze without any whites, as tangible as reality.
He didn’t know exactly what that thing was, but it seemed to be waiting for him to look at it, and once he looked at it…
Colin suspected that would directly trigger some kind of fatal attack, turning his head would be to “go”.
But…
Was the one calling him to eat downstairs really real?
Colin couldn’t be sure, and he paused at the doorway for a few seconds, motionless.
What troubled him the most was that he had just responded to the other party, not knowing if that would cause trouble.
Just then, some information suddenly appeared before his eyes…
[You heard your sister’s frightened voice. Imagining your sister scared and anxious, as a sister-complex person, you cannot sit idly by. You immediately want to turn your head, to comfort your cute and innocent sister, telling her not to be afraid of anything when you are here…]
When he saw this message, Colin’s eyelid twitched, don’t make decisions for me!
However, before he could think further, this line of text seemed to have a strange magic, arousing in him a strong protective desire to turn around and protect his “sister”, unwilling to see her suffer the slightest grievance…
To make everything proceed according to the “script”.
“Get lost…”
Colin resisted this inexplicable influence, his whole body tensing up, trembling in place as if he was combating something.
If he was uncertain before about what would happen if he turned his head, now he was sure that turning many heads would not result in anything good…
It was at this time of indecision that a piercing pain shot through his right middle finger, as if a cat had bitten him.
This snapped him back to reality, freeing him from the demonic influence of the text…
“Go downstairs…”
Colin interpreted Yukionna’s message and immediately headed toward the stairs.
And just as he made his decision, the entire second floor instantly became dark, and from behind came a voice repeatedly murmuring in a low tone—
“Brother, don’t go down, don’t leave me!”
“Brother, do you not want me anymore?”
“Have you gone mad?! Brother, have you gone mad?! It’s dangerous down there!”
“Stop! Quick, stop! I don’t want you to die!”
“Brother, don’t trust the monster downstairs, follow me, let’s be together forever, I can satisfy all your wishes, any wish…”
“Brother, only I truly care for you, melt into me…”
The monster behind him, using “sister’s” voice, issued repeated, pleading sounds, trying to stop Colin’s footsteps.
But even so, seeing that Colin still did not stop, that voice gradually turned to frenzy.
“Don’t go!”
“Don’t you dare walk away!”
“Stop right now, or I’ll kill you!”
His “sister” let out one piercing scream after another. The corridor grew increasingly heavy with a putrid smell in the air, and mold rapidly spread across the walls. The world in front of him was aging swiftly, and the wooden floorboards creaked under the stress as if they couldn’t bear his weight.
This space, once filled with warmth, seemed to be revealing its true nature…
Colin heard footsteps chasing after him more than once, even feeling something filthy dragging on the hem of his clothes, trying to force him to stop.
If it weren’t for the reminder from “Yukionna,” he would have turned around several times already, exclaiming “Mighty Heavenly Dragon” in a loud voice.
However, if he had done so, he probably would have found himself in even greater trouble…
“What can be confirmed now is that although the terrifying things in ‘Passionate Paradise’ are of high rank, they all must follow the rules, just like NPCs,” he thought.
“I have no idea what the thing behind me is, but the pattern should be: if I don’t turn around or respond, nothing will happen…”
Colin ignored the changes in front of him and the odd movements by his side, step by step, he walked toward the staircase.
At this moment, the corridor on the second floor seemed as if it had been stretched, Colin’s progress was slow, but after a while, he finally reached the top of the stairs.
And just then, all the abnormalities suddenly disappeared.
The sweet, yet chilling, calls of “brother” that had been echoing in his ears finally stopped.
[You didn’t find anything strange. You suspect that you have just experienced a hallucination upon waking from a nap. Your sister is clearly downstairs, so how could she be upstairs? Shaking your head, you don’t take these events to heart…]
[——Unfortunately, such a mundane course of events takes away some of the necessary conflict and tension from the story.]
“Damn it…”
Colin got a bit irritated at the “Narrator” written on his retina. If it weren’t for Yukionna raising a hand, he almost looked back.
Even if he didn’t look back, it wouldn’t be so easy to break free; he would have needed to resort to some measures.
Then after that…
Other things might become completely disrupted, turning things extremely troublesome.
“Is this what that person meant about being wary of the Narrator? It seems to have some kind of bewitching power, but it’s still within the range of resistance. More importantly, it doesn’t seem to care much about the ring in my hand. Can it not perceive it, or does it not care enough to bother with it?”
As Colin pondered, he continued down the stairs.
Halfway through, he seemed to remember something, took out a piece of gauze from his pocket, and wrapped the ring in it, making a simple disguise.
After that, he finally felt safe to walk downstairs and saw his real “sister,” described by the Narrator, below.
She sat behind a table, dressed in her middle school uniform with a dress, and draped in an apron she hadn’t had time to take off from cooking. Her hair was tied into a ponytail, draped over one shoulder. Even with her petite form, youthful face, and innocent appearance, she seemed to exude a gentle and capable charm.
“Sis, that hairstyle can be dangerous…”
Colin mumbled to himself internally and then turned his gaze to the table.
On the table were ready dishes: stir-fried tomato and eggs, blanched hollow vegetables, and stir-fried beef – a meal that had both meat and vegetables.
“I got your meal ready there for you, brother. What took you so long to come down… oh, your hand, what happened?”
His sister was taking off her apron while speaking, and then quickly noticed the gauze on Colin’s right hand, showing concern.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 117 - 117 117 Passionate Paradise No Paranormal
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 117: Chapter 117: Passionate Paradise? No, Paranormal Paradise!_1 Chapter 117: Chapter 117: Passionate Paradise? No, Paranormal Paradise!_1 [Seeing the girl in front of you, you know she is your sister, Ke Xiaoya, a junior high school student.]
“It’s nothing, just tied up for fun…”
Colin naturally walked over and sat down at the dining table, skipping over the topic, discreetly taking a glance at his “sister.”
It has to be said…
The girl in front of him looked human, spoke with a gentle voice, was pretty, and could cook, stirring up a protective desire that would be the dreamgirl of many homebodies.
But Colin was well aware that such girls didn’t exist in reality…
Every individual in “Passionate Paradise” was a containment subject.
They were shaped into the form of humans through some means and then imprisoned in “Script City,” just like NPCs, deceiving fatties into their doom according to the “script’s” demands…
Yet, Colin suddenly remembered, why did this method feel vaguely familiar?
“Is that so… If brother likes it, then I’m happy.”
As a good “sister,” she didn’t ask more, removed her apron and sat down at the side.
“I wonder what kind of monster is under this appearance.”
Colin muttered to himself, and took another look at the three dishes before him that seemed quite decent.
However, when he carefully sniffed the air, he always felt that something about the smell was slightly off.
“Yukionna” hadn’t given any hints, and he hadn’t felt any danger, so the food should be edible…
But having said that, Colin thought it over and still felt that he should find a way to avoid eating if possible.
And if he did eat, he’d have to find a way to throw it up…
Colin still didn’t know exactly where “Passionate Paradise,” this “Out-of-Control Copy,” had gone wrong; like that door killing earlier, it didn’t seem like the direct and fundamental cause of the loss of control.
Just then…
[Clearly, compared to the dull meals, your junior high school sister before you piques your curiosity even more. The glances you throw her way are filled with an indescribable desire to know more, making you unable to resist wanting to find out more about her, and there’s still about an hour left until it’s time to go to school…]
[Some thoughts begin to arise in your mind…]
“Fuck, I’m not, I didn’t, I’m just curious what kind of monster she is, don’t fucking improvise for me.”
Colin’s expression froze, and he couldn’t help but clench his fist, suppressing those thoughts that were not his own.
Everything was fine until that damned narrator made a comment, and the whole atmosphere mysteriously changed.
At that moment, his sister’s voice came.
“Brother, why aren’t you eating? Don’t you have an appetite?”
“No…”
As the sister was about to speak, she suddenly remembered something and quickly stood up: “Oh, that’s right, I also made chicken soup, wait a moment…”
With that, she hurriedly stood and ran to the kitchen.
Seeing her rush away, Colin didn’t dilly-dally, took some vegetables and rice, and promptly put them into the “Storage Room.”
Then, he took out his phone to check, finding it still seemed to work…
However, he didn’t pay attention to that, quickly operated it for a bit, and then put the phone back into his pocket.
Right after he finished all this, he saw his sister return in a timely fashion, holding a bowl of chicken soup.
“Chicken soup is ready…”
“Brother, come and drink the chicken soup, try the taste and see how it is…”
“This is the hen I bought with half a month’s pocket money, you are growing, brother, have a taste quickly…”
Colin looked at the golden-yellow chicken soup brought before him, sniffed discretely, and noticed a slight unpleasant odor.
Then, he looked at the sister next to him, her face full of expectation.
Her moist eyes seemed to say: Drink it quickly, why aren’t you drinking?
After thinking for a moment, he made an excuse, “I just finished eating and I’m a bit too full, can’t drink any more, you have it.”
“You ate?”
Only then did his sister notice that Colin’s rice bowl had been emptied at some point.
She didn’t speak, but gave Colin a strange look, first patted Colin’s pocket, didn’t find anything, and then suspiciously walked towards the garbage bin at the side, as if to confirm something…
It was at this moment that Colin felt an inexplicable sense of crisis rising within him.
“Nice one, leaving the chicken soup was intentional, huh?”
Colin realized this, but luckily, he had directly hidden the stuff in the “Storage Room,” so he wasn’t afraid his sister would discover anything.
“There’s nothing in the trash can, brother, you really ate it…”
His sister rummaged through the trash can, didn’t see any discarded food, and only then did the inexplicably tense atmosphere in the room start to ease.
“Brother, the chicken soup…”
Before she could finish, Colin’s phone rang and he quickly stood up, turning off the music player at an angle where his sister couldn’t see.
“I’m eating, oh, okay, I’ll be right there, yes, yes, yes, I’ll be quick…”
Speaking, Colin walked outside the cabin, and when he reached the door, he hung up the phone and said to his sister with a look of apology, “Sorry, I made plans with a classmate, need to go to the school right away…”
After walking some distance from the door, Colin could feel that there was a gaze locked on him from behind…
He glanced over his shoulder and saw that his sister was standing at the door, apparently not intending to follow.
This made him breathe a sigh of relief, finally managing to avoid drinking the chicken soup in a legitimate way…
Thinking this, Colin gave his sister a slight smile.
Upon seeing this, his sister placed her hands over her mouth, making a megaphone shape, and yelled, “Be careful on the road,” followed by a gentle smile that gradually turned hideous, her mouth stretching to her ears…
“Hiss…”
Colin’s heart skipped a beat, he blinked, and everything seemed to return to normal.
His sister was smiling sweetly.
“Damn it, what happened to ‘Passionate Paradise’? It’s like a ghost story with no feeling of sweet romance at all, no weak point to challenge…”
Colin withdrew his gaze, looked around, the nearby street was deserted, but seemed normal enough, only the sky was overcast, clouds covering the sky, as if it was a cloudy day, the air felt heavy.
It felt like the prelude to rain…
Right, where is the school, how should I go again?
[You remember that taking the bus no. 2 from the stop across the street, which comes every half hour, will get you to school quickly, but more than that, the sight of a girl lying under the streetlight ahead grabs your attention…]
A girl?
Only now did Colin notice that under the streetlight not far ahead, indeed lay a girl in a black school uniform.
Just from a cursory glance at her figure, he knew she was a very pretty girl.
By her clothing, she seemed to be from his school…
[You recognize her as the class beauty of your class, very beautiful, but for some reason, right now, she lies there defenseless, smelling faintly of alcohol, apparently very drunk, you know, even if you were to carry her into the deserted alley nearby, she probably wouldn’t resist much…]
[Facing this situation, you know you can’t just stand by and do nothing!]
[Looking at her exposed pale long legs, you feel increasingly restless inside, wanting to do something. So, you decide…]
Colin, expressionless, took a phone out of his pocket and tried calling a number, and a few seconds later, the call actually went through. He brought the phone to his ear—
“Hello, is this Spirit Spirit?”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 118 - 118 118 Whips Uniforms and Buses._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 118: Chapter 118: Whips, Uniforms, and Buses._1 Chapter 118: Chapter 118: Whips, Uniforms, and Buses._1 “Drip-drop, drip-drop…”
An open-top patrol car slowly approached, with three smartly dressed female officers seated inside.
Once at the intersection, one of the shapely policewomen stepped out, her sharp gaze sweeping the area. Spotting Colin waiting, she moved towards him.
“Was it you who made the call?” asked the buxom policewoman as she approached, clutching a leather whip in her hand, handcuffs and a baton hanging at her waist. Her scrutiny-filled gaze fixed on Colin.
“Yes, the person is over there. I just stepped outside and saw her lying there motionless.”
Colin nodded and glanced at the objects in her hand—Where on earth did this scenario come from? Which police officers actually carry whips with them?
The person who set up “Passionate Paradise” must have never seen any real officers, right?
But as much as he scoffed inwardly, he dared not look too long for fear of triggering something else; then he pointed towards the “class beauty” under the streetlight.
Although the female class beauty was quite attractive, dangerously aligning with his fetishes…
Clearly…
This was not something decent.
“Alright, I got it…”
The policewoman went over, took a quick look, then confirmed in a firm tone, “She’s indeed drunk, seems she drank too much, had a blackout and fainted here. Come over and help me lift her, we’ll take her back to the public security office.”
After speaking, she turned to Colin: “Do you know her?”
He didn’t know her… Colin wanted to say this to avoid further trouble, but before the words could leave his mouth, his right eyelid suddenly twitched, and a bad feeling surfaced from within.
Do they have the ability to verify truth from lies?
Colin’s thoughts shifted, and what he said was: “I know her, she’s a girl from our class, but I don’t know her name.”
“Is that so,” the policewoman asked a few more simple questions before she stopped the inquiry.
At the same time, Colin felt the strange unease disappear…
By normal logic, he would have lied just now, saying he didn’t know her, right? Damn it, playing shady games, aren’t they…
Colin cursed inwardly and then tentatively spoke up:
“Then I should go to school now, I’m almost late…”
After finishing, he prepared to leave, but the female officer said, “Wait, don’t rush off to school just yet.”
“What’s the matter?”
Colin’s heart skipped a beat, then suddenly remembered, don’t callers usually have to give a statement?
Would there still be time to go to school after making the report?
Wait, maybe not necessary…
Colin recalled that when the Dean’s late wife’s gold ring went missing, they made a report, and after it was found, no statement was needed, and they just left.
But… Colin wasn’t very familiar with this; he only knew that if they used this as an excuse to take him to the security office, things could get troublesome.
If that happened, he wouldn’t be able to follow the Narrator’s instructions for “an uneventful day,” and who knows what twists could occur.
“You’re quite commendable, knowing to call the police, instead of acting like human scum, taking advantage of someone in a vulnerable state and causing other societal harms…”
The policewoman nodded approvingly at Colin, her sharp gaze softening considerably.
“Of course, of course, this is the moral principle taught to us since childhood by the school.”
Colin nodded repeatedly, knowing full well that if he had really entertained some unsavory thoughts and dragged this unfamiliar class beauty to the small woods behind the alley, truth be told, who would have taken advantage of whom was not a sure thing…
‘In a dangerous world, boys must learn to protect themselves and say no to bad temptations!’
Colin muttered to himself, his eyes shifting away from the female officers dressed in wildly inappropriate attire that clearly didn’t conform to conventional norms.
However, just at that moment, he suddenly saw some information pop up on his retina…
[Clad in a dashing uniform, the female officer who resembled an older sister showed immense appreciation for your character, noting it is a rare sight these days to come across flowers as pure as you.]
[Clearly, she seemed to want to personally cultivate you, to safeguard your future…]
Colin’s eyelid twitched as he finished reading the information, just in time to see the voluptuous female officer tuck a whip between her breasts, before she asked:
“By the way, your school uniform matches hers, you are students from the same school, aren’t you?
“Do you have a contact? What is it, could you leave one? If there’s anything, it would be good for us to get in touch with you.
“Of course, if there are other matters, you might also come directly to me for assistance.”
There was really no need… Colin almost vehemently refused, turning his mind swiftly, he responded, “I… I don’t have any contact information.”
“What about your mobile number?”
“I just changed my SIM card, I can’t remember the number…”
“Then…”
“Ah, I’m sorry Sister, my bus has arrived. If there’s nothing else, I need to go to school. If I miss this one, I’ll have to stand as punishment from the teacher…”
Seeing a bus with a “2” on top approaching from the distance, Colin hastily looked for an excuse to leave.
“Hmm, alright then, remember to tell your teacher about what happened here.”
“Yes, of course.”
Hearing that the woman did not pursue further, Colin once again breathed a sigh of relief internally.
He felt that if their contacts were taken by her, it might lead to other unsavory developments.
Although he was not sure what would happen specifically, it was very likely not to be anything good.
Fortunately, at the crucial moment, the bus on route 2 arrived like a savior, and the Narrator did not continue to cause trouble…
“What in the world is going on here? It feels like traps are everywhere, making it impossible for one to live in peace. It’s been less than an hour, and so many troublesome things have already happened.”
Colin felt that if other employees from his company encountered similar situations, especially the ones with setups as lethal as the door they faced earlier, they would likely be in grave danger.
They might be caught off guard at first.
Moreover, the subsequent conversations were filled with language traps so subtle they were hidden within seemingly ordinary sentences, and giving the wrong answer could easily spell trouble.
“The anomalies I’ve encountered now, the fake sisters, the class beauty, the female officers… they all give me an extremely dangerous feeling, with a threat level I’m afraid none lower than third-stage ‘Beastification’… This place is really outrageous.”
Colin shook his head inwardly.
It seems these Containment Subjects still require “evidence” to act, everything has to follow the rules, according to that “script”…
But in a few days, things might not be the same.
If by then these creatures no longer needed to find “evidence” to act…
Colin felt his scalp tingle with just the thought.
However, before he could ponder further, the bus on route 2 slowly came to a halt in front of him.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 119 - 119 119 The Girl on the Bus_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 119: Chapter 119 The Girl on the Bus_1 Chapter 119: Chapter 119 The Girl on the Bus_1 “WeChat Pay received 2 yuan.”
After paying, Colin glanced at the bus carriage—quite a number of people onboard, the seats all occupied, and about a dozen standing in the aisle. It looked rather crowded.
Luckily, he was the only one getting on at this stop, so he didn’t have to worry about someone pointing a gun at his back.
He found a spot to stand, and the bus began to move.
At this moment, some information appeared on Colin’s retinas.
[Suddenly, it seems you notice something amiss in the crowd, and you look towards the source…]
As soon as that appeared, Colin subconsciously turned his head to look.
Then, he saw a girl not far from where he stood—dressed in a black school uniform skirt, not very tall, squeezed amongst the crowd.
She wore a pair of glasses, had a gentle and frail aura, but now displayed a troubled expression, clutching the handrail and curling her body up as though enduring something.
Several men beside her kept squeezing toward her each time the bus swayed, occasionally trying to graze against her.
Although they hadn’t succeeded yet…
Seeing the girl not reacting, their actions gradually became more brazen.
What is this, some sort of Indian bus scenario playing out?
The moment Colin saw this scene, he immediately grasped what was happening.
This godforsaken place, why are there so many manga-esque storylines unfolding? Could the script of “Passionate Paradise” have been inspired by some kind of paradise, or some pink application perhaps?
He felt that the former senior employee of his company was quite conscienceless, turning the containment subject into a character from an adult manga, then letting the employees trigger it…
No wonder “Yukionna” had such a big issue with this place.
Without giving it much thought, the girl caught in the middle of the crowd seemed to notice Colin’s gaze, and she turned to look back at him.
When she saw Colin, her expression first froze, then noticing they wore the same uniform, her face immediately showed a look of plea, seemingly asking for help…
[The introverted literary girl surrounded by perverts recognizes you, and after realizing you’re a classmate from the same class, she quickly sends a signal for help.]
[You know that once you act, this girl who you barely know will suddenly have a great deal of affection for you, willing to do anything for you.]
[Perhaps, this could put an end to your years of singledom…]
[Or maybe, you plan to turn a deaf ear and do nothing, letting the events on the bus naturally progress, possibly leading to something even more thrilling?]
[You stand there, unsure which option is the more appropriate choice…]
“Another classmate? How come I can’t take two steps outside without running into so many classmates? And all of them in trouble, too. Seriously, assess for yourself whether this ‘script’ of yours is reasonable or if it seems like some third-rate screenplay?”
Colin cursed inwardly and let out a sigh.
The situation seemed a bit different this time; regardless of his choice, trouble seemed inevitable…
He was indeed indecisive, not sure whether to intervene.
Of course, his hesitation had nothing to do with the “narrator” mentioning wanting to see more stimulating scenes—it was purely a contemplation of which choice’s consequences he could accept.
Based on his previous experiences, he was inclined to be like Teflon—uninvolved in everything…
If he ignored her, the “plot” would presumably just end right there.
But if he got involved…
Those men might strip away their human guise on the spot, transform into terrifying monsters, and kill him right there and then.
Colin was certain that those people were some kind of unknown monsters.
No, more precisely, not a single one of the dozens of people on the bus was a real human being…
And as he pondered, a chilly feeling transmitted from his right middle finger…
“Need help?”
Colin lifted his hand, covered his mouth with it, and, pretending to rest his chin on his hand, he asked in a low voice.
The icy chill spread quickly…
“Yukionna” reaffirmed the previous answer and relayed more information—
If he didn’t help, something very exciting might happen on the bus soon, but the excitement might not be the kind he was thinking of…
Once the young girl’s mental state collapsed, her true form would appear. Its humanity was not fully shaped, and it could easily become frenzied.
Although Colin didn’t understand what “humanity being fully shaped” meant, he still made a decision.
Just as he was about to act, he saw more information from the Narrator appearing on his retina.
[Seeing your hesitation, the desperation in the girl’s eyes behind her glasses grew more intense. She clung to the bus railing, her options to evade dwindling. Several passengers smirked triumphantly, closing in step by step. One of them even couldn’t resist reaching towards her skirt…]
[But just at that moment, you suddenly pushed through the crowd, bumped into the man, and stood behind the girl, protecting her.]
[Several passengers were seething inside…]
“Kid, mind your own business about what’s happening here,” a man threatened.
Colin glanced at him, then shouted, “Ah, help, there’s a pervert…”
No sooner had he spoken than the expressions of the men changed. The bus stopped and the doors opened at that moment. Taking the chance, they rushed down the bus without a second thought.
“Colin, thank you. If it hadn’t been for you…”
As the girl spoke, a scared expression crossed her face; her cheeks flushed red, and then she snuggled into Colin’s embrace.
Could you not repay kindness with enmity…
Colin felt discomfort in his body and took a half step back.
[The girl looked at you admiringly, her expression filled with a certain infatuation. It seemed that she had a liking for you a long time ago, she already liked you a lot, and now… she likes you even more.]
Stop adding settings at will! She was clearly just an unfamiliar classmate a moment ago, why add this forced setup?!
Colin was annoyed, but he had no time to dwell on that as more “Narrator” information emerged.
[The girl’s body pressed against yours, her form so soft, the scent coming off her so enticing. With the swaying of the bus, your bodies occasionally rubbed against each other, unintentionally stirring up some romantic thoughts in you…]
???
Question marks formed in Colin’s mind, followed by the sensation of inappropriate thoughts emerging.
Fortunately, having experienced various things by now, he easily suppressed those thoughts, preventing undesired reactions from happening in this inappropriate place…
Later, after another bus stop, Colin seized the opportunity to grab a seat and quickly let the girl sit down.
[The height at which she sat was just at your waist level. Looking at that pretty head below you, you couldn’t help but recall some scenes from educational materials. If…]
What in the world is all this, is my innocence going to be ruined here?
Colin gasped a breath of cold air, feeling a slight tingling on his scalp, and gained a new understanding of the Narrator’s lack of limits.
But luckily, “Yukionna” provided timely support.

chapters.title: Chapter 120 - 120 120 The Mores Degenerate Day by Day..._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 120: Chapter 120 The Mores Degenerate Day by Day…_1 Chapter 120: Chapter 120 The Mores Degenerate Day by Day…_1 A cold breath emanated from the ring, gradually calming his mind, enabling him to resist the script arranged by the “Narrator”.
“Thankfully, the arrangements of this thing can be fought against, otherwise it would really be troublesome…”
Colin sighed with relief.
So far, he felt that the most challenging aspect of this eerie place was not the willpower, but the resistance to social death…
After all, if the things mentioned above actually happened in reality, they would indeed lead to social death.
“Is this how they train willpower?”
Colin couldn’t understand; he had been informed that this “Passionate Paradise” was initially created by Bonfire Company to cultivate something to counter a particular type of anomaly, but after entering, he had faced a few crises, yet he didn’t feel significantly trained…
Could it be because he hadn’t stayed long enough?
But without thinking too much, Colin’s eyelid suddenly twitched, and he saw a line of information appear before him.
[The bus will soon arrive at Maple Leaf School, where you and a companion girl will get off together and return to class, starting this afternoon’s lessons.]
[You vaguely remember that today is Friday, and the three afternoon classes are mathematics, physics, and politics.]
[Once today’s classes are over, tomorrow will be the weekend, and thinking of this, a wave of joy rises inside you…]
Phew, lucky they didn’t concoct some weird stuff this time…
Seeing that the “Narrator” didn’t mess around for once, Colin instantly relaxed.
Then he took a closer look at the second sentence…
“Math, physics, politics, what’s the content for high school again, hiss, wait, what grade am I? It keeps hinting that I’m a high school student, but it never specifies which year…”
Colin’s brows knitted instantly, sensing something was amiss.
This season, oh, that’s not right, how do you say it, semester, he actually didn’t know which grade he was in, nor did he know if it was the first or second semester.
And predictably, according to the script of “Passionate Paradise”, there was a high chance he would be put on the spot during class.
This was a common scenario in many stories, and Colin didn’t believe that the “Narrator” who liked to play with melodrama would pass up this plot device…
However, if he were called upon and couldn’t answer the question…
He might well be dragged into the office to see if his development was normal.
But at this point, Colin noticed that the girl sitting on the bus seat seemed to be holding a small bag filled with books, which apparently were textbooks.
After a moment’s thought, Colin tried to ask, “Are those… textbooks you’re carrying?”
“No,” said the girl with glasses, shaking her head and volunteering, “Some study materials, extracurricular readings…”
“Study materials? Do you have any for math or physics? Oh, others are fine too, I can’t seem to recall some things clearly.”
Colin’s main goal was to determine which year he was in.
Startled by Colin’s request, she hesitated and then clumsily opened the small bag, “Yes, there’s one, there’s a book on interpretation outside of class, Colin, just wait, I’ll find it for you…”
In no time, she handed him a thick book.
[The small interaction secretly delighted her, and although she seemed unmoved on the surface, she was very happy inside that she could help you…]
There it was again, messing with the love stories… Colin glanced at it, didn’t see any danger, and so he didn’t think much of it.
Afterward, he took the supplemental reading book and flipped through it casually.
He quickly understood the current semester – second year of high school, second half.
Looking at the mathematical terms in the table of contents, Colin just felt a headache coming on; it had been years since he graduated from high school, who the hell could remember all that stuff?
And the most important thing was, his science grades had never been that great.
Colin pursed his lips, took a cursory glance in desperation, hoping to remember something, anything, just to scrape by for a while longer.
But…
Sometimes life can be fudged, language can be fudged, but mathematics can’t be, because if you don’t know math, you really don’t know it…
“Colin, is there anything you don’t understand? You can tell me, I… Don’t judge by my looks, I’m actually quite confident in the combined sciences…”
Seeing Colin’s troubled expression, the girl with glasses mustered the courage to speak.
She seemed to “recall” that Colin’s scores were decent in the arts, but his science grades weren’t too good…
Having said that, she added, “If, if you need it, I can teach you.”
“Uh, I shouldn’t need it for now…”
Colin sighed inwardly, already contemplating what strategy to use when “the teacher” pulled him into the office later.
If he wanted to guess what the teacher would ask, the best option would be to use the “Book of Fate: Fragment”.
But…
Based on the information he had so far, using that thing would probably only make matters worse.
Having glanced through a few pages, Colin resigned himself to returning the book.
At that moment, the bus pulled up to the stop.
Outside the bus window, it was possible to see quite a few students dressed in black uniform suits, and in the direction where these students were heading, sprawled out like a slumbering giant beast, was the school.
“We’re here.”
Colin announced, then alighted from the bus, with his female classmate following him out.
As soon as he stepped off, he saw, not far away, a couple kissing in an alley by the roadside.
“Morals decline, public displays of lewdness…”
Colin shook his head slightly. Seeing their behavior, he couldn’t help but reminisce about his real high school days, when he, too, had seen a couple of high schoolers kissing on the street.
He didn’t linger, shifting his gaze away, fearful that looking any longer might trigger trouble.
Who knows whether the “Narrator” would suddenly have a brain fart and saddle him with a new identity, forcing him to barge in and enact some juvenile drama in front of them…
As for the moral bottom line of the “Narrator”, it was best not to look too much.
The girl with glasses who was following him peeked in the direction of his gaze, let out a little “yah”, quickly averted her eyes, then stole another glance at Colin, her face somewhat flushed, seemingly lost in thought.
However, just when Colin thought he had managed to sidestep one issue, the “Narrator” spoke up again.
[At this moment, across the street, outside the school, some idle loafers were eating, their eyes lighting up the moment they saw the girl by your side…]
Colin’s vision darkened.
Following the Narrator’s intrusion, he saw a few boys with bleached hair start walking over to them.
The girl with glasses also noticed the people across the street, and her expression changed.
With so many good-looking people around, they just have to look at the one next to me, forcing the plot, huh!
Colin cursed inwardly.
And from inside the ring, “Yukionna” offered a tip…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 121 - 121 121 Hidden Mission_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 121: Chapter 121 Hidden Mission_1 Chapter 121: Chapter 121 Hidden Mission_1 “I’m going to be late, hurry up…”
Colin took a deep breath, grabbed the girl’s wrist, and walked quickly toward the campus that gave him a bad feeling.
Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the road, a few blond punks cursed at the sight. They wanted to pursue, but when they saw him enter the school gates, they ultimately cursed a few more times and did not continue the chase.
[You successfully avoided an incident…]
Are you disappointed?
Colin felt a bit better. He thought the only thing worth being happy about right now was that the “Narrator” seemed unhappy.
“Um, Colin…” a voice as soft as a mosquito’s buzz reached his ears.
“What’s up?”
Colin turned his head and saw the still unnamed female classmate looking at him, then remembered to let go of her hand.
The bespectacled girl retracted her hand like a startled bunny…
Without further observation, Colin followed the “Narrator’s” guidance to his second-floor classroom.
Class 802.
By this moment, two-thirds of the class had already arrived.
[As soon as you entered, you chose your seat, the fourth row from the back, the one next to the window, the sorrowful lookout point reserved for male protagonists in various works of fiction, where you could gaze at the sky at a forty-five-degree angle—unfortunately, you might have been able to see the Femme Fatale that Mr. Treeman mentioned calling your name, but now, you will never see her again…]
“Femme Fatale?”
Colin paused, recalling the equipment “Miss Bunny” had mentioned, which included “Femme Fatale.”
Did it break free from “Script Heaven’s” containment right here in the past?
Does this mean there might be some kind of loophole to escape this place?
While pondering, Colin took his seat.
Surprisingly, the bespectacled girl was sitting right in front of his assigned seat…
[Because of the slight run you just had, as soon as you sat down, the girl took off her jacket, revealing a white summer school uniform underneath. Through the plain uniform, you caught a glimpse of a black horizontal strap on her back, and you knew she must be wearing a black bra…]
[This makes you…]
[Due to your experiences having shallow engagements with anomalies multiple times, you seem to have activated something, earning a discretionary point.]
“Hm? Discretionary point? What does that mean?”
Colin was contemplating the “Narrator’s” lack of boundaries when suddenly the conversation shifted, introducing concepts he didn’t understand.
At that moment, however, he saw that the “Narrator’s” messages continued to appear.
[Hidden task limited to the instance “Experience five events in any ‘Script City’ script” has been completed.]
[—The “Gene Compensation Panel Version 1.0” will now be unlocked for you.]
“Five events?”
Colin guessed at something, then saw a panel resembling a resume for a Bonfire Company employee appear on his retina…
[Name]: Colin.
[Strength]: 5.1. (Exceeding the strength of a bear!)
[Constitution]: 6.9. (A terrifying body that wouldn’t easily die even if it fell from the eighteenth floor.)
[Agility]: 5.4. (You could even catch up to a sedan and ask if they’re selling anything.)
[Discretionary Points]: 1 (Each point added can be as low as 0.1.)
[Note]: If an attribute breaks through 10, perhaps something will happen?
[Note]: An F Level Employee can get up to ten discretionary points, moreover, a “Firebearer” at this stage can gain an additional 2 discretionary points.
[Description]: The successful development of the “Gene Compensation Medicine” offered mankind a new possibility, but the overall strength of the current company employees was still too weak to preserve themselves in the impending apocalypse, much less take on the responsibility of continuing civilization.
For this reason, led by employee “Boss Huang He,” a group of high-level employees deeply explored the basis of the “Gene Compensation Medicine.” By combining a variety of dangerous substances, many employees paid a heavy price with their lives in the collection of materials and research, eventually developing a new means of enhancement for all employees, the “Gene Compensation Panel Version 1.0.”
Its manner of use was extremely simple—interacting with any anomaly within “Script City” gave one the opportunity to earn a certain number of discretionary points freely chosen for enhancement.
…
“Is this the unique promotion method mentioned in the task?”
Colin immediately thought of a requirement from a “Bonfire Company” task upon seeing this, which said that within “Script City” there existed a special, conflict-free method of reinforcement.
He hadn’t expected to unlock it so soon.
Colin took a careful look and quickly acquired a relatively complete understanding of it.
According to what was written, as long as he encountered an event, he had the chance to earn “discretionary points” and become stronger.
The extent of this increase in strength was considerable, and it was direct and brutal.
[An ordinary F Level Employee who has injected three doses of F Level Gene Compensation Medicine, if he doesn’t experience anything too drastic, then his three attributes would typically hover around “2”…]
The Narrator, for some reason, took up the role of a proper narrator this time.
“The average F Level Employee has full attributes around 2? Looks like I’ve far exceeded that, averaging almost three times more…”
Colin thought for a moment that if his physical attributes were reduced to a third during a solo Trial Task…
Then that task would be quite difficult.
“But this ‘Boss Huang He’ name… why does it feel so familiar? Wait a minute…”
Colin squinted his eyes and suddenly remembered—wasn’t this the creator of “The False Powerhouse”?
He’s actually a high-level employee?
Colin had always thought he was some third-rate creator, after all, the thing was useful, but it was somewhat unscrupulous; to put it simply, it could be summed up as randomly selecting a person for social death…
However, what he was more curious about right now, compared to “Boss Huang He,” was the “impending apocalypse” mentioned in the description.
“Unable to preserve oneself before the upcoming apocalypse?”
Colin frowned, if it were a random passerby mentioning the “apocalypse,” he would definitely not believe it, but given the context…
He had to give it some thought.
Yet, reflecting on recent events, he seemed to not see the slightest sign of the so-called apocalypse.
Just then, before he could ponder further, a harsh class bell sound suddenly rang out.
“Forget it, just focus on getting stronger, if there really is an apocalypse, it isn’t something I can control anyway.”
Colin took a deep breath and snuffed out the information in his mind.
And at this moment, after the bell rang and then quieted down, a tall, intelligent-looking female teacher with a ruler and compass walked in from outside the door.
“Students, stand up!”
A boy who seemed to be the class president stood up and called out.
Colin’s expression became distant upon hearing this sound after so many years, then he stood up along with the others.
“Good morning, teacher.”
“Good morning, students.”
“Please sit down. Today we will continue with yesterday’s knowledge. Now, I will pick a few students to discuss the concept of complex numbers…”

chapters.title: Chapter 122 - 122 122 The Scent of Blood on the Note_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 122: Chapter 122: The Scent of Blood on the Note_1 Chapter 122: Chapter 122: The Scent of Blood on the Note_1 I can’t be seen, I can’t be seen, I can’t be seen…
Colin lowered his gaze and kept his eyes on the back of a female classmate’s head, endlessly chanting in his mind.
Although he had anticipated this segment, he couldn’t help feeling a bit nervous when it arrived.
“Very few students! Knowing what class it is and yet not even taking out your textbooks, it seems you are quite confident about the upcoming lesson, well then, very good…”
The female teacher, holding a long ruler and clutching a plastic protractor, surveyed the room with a sharp gaze and began to speak in a cold tone:
“First row, table seven, the student on the right, please stand up and answer the teacher’s question.”
Could it really not be me?
Colin felt a tingling sensation on his scalp when he heard the teacher mention “very few students,” recalling the fear once dominated by teachers.
And it was only then he noticed that he, too, seemed to have forgotten his book, being too preoccupied with the “Gene Compensation Panel” to remember these things…
However, to his surprise, the first person to be called upon wasn’t him.
His seat was in the fourth row from the back, near the window, a far cry from the other person’s…
Colin glanced sideways and saw a male student hesitantly stand up—another employee?
But it was at first glance that he made out this particular detail…
First, although the person had the appearance of a student, his demeanor didn’t seem youthful, having a kind of maturity that’s typically… worn smooth with age.
Second, Colin could faintly distinguish through the smell that, among the monsters in the class, it was this called-up classmate who smelled like a human…
But he didn’t know which employee this person was precisely.
“If he can’t answer, it’s hard to tell what kind of punishment will be triggered. Will it be an instant death on the spot or a trip to the office to be bent over?”
As Colin pondered, he quietly pulled out a brand-new-looking math textbook from his drawer.
Meanwhile, the other “employee” struggled to answer the teacher’s question; the relevant knowledge had likely been gradually returned to his high school teachers over four years of college…
Answering some details of sophomore knowledge was clearly not possible.
“What’s the matter? Can’t remember or something?” the teacher with the imposing demeanor tapped the blackboard twice with the ruler.
The employee held his breath, his hand reaching into the jacket pocket of his uniform. After a moment of silence, he finally said, “I… don’t know.”
“Hmm.”
The teacher nodded and said nothing more but suddenly shifted her gaze to the other side: “Fourth row, the last desk, by the window there, you seemed rather pleased when you saw a student unable to answer the question?
“Come on, since you appear so confident, answer the teacher’s question.”
Upon hearing this, Colin’s expression froze. He was just looking, how was he ‘rather pleased’?
He wished he hadn’t looked at all…
[Clearly, the math teacher had noticed your little actions and used a trivial excuse to have you answer a question. Although your mind is blank, without any content, you know…]
[Answering incorrectly might cause trouble, but not answering at all would definitely cause trouble.]
Following this piece of narration, Colin felt an alertness in his heart, as if staying seated a moment longer would lead to something bad happening immediately.
Reluctantly, he slowly stood up from his chair, preparing to admit his ignorance just like the other employee had done.
As he was about to speak, his hand also slipped into his pocket, quietly gripping “Time Stasis,” ready to trigger a Time Stop at the first sign of danger…
However, at that moment, Colin suddenly saw the female classmate in front of him quietly raise her math textbook…
There was a section of text marked with a red line on it, concerning the knowledge about complex numbers…
Colin fell silent for a moment, then proceeded to answer according to the text.
“Not bad, take a seat.”
Upon hearing the teacher’s words, Colin breathed a sigh of relief and plopped back into his seat, feeling a sense of fortunate survival despite the current scene not seeming too terrifying—yet the sense of danger he felt was no less than in the Other World.
However, Colin’s brow furrowed slightly right after. Had he been saved by an “abnormality”?
This…
Was it part of the “script’s” plan?
Colin was unsure, not knowing if there was some other, more dangerous arrangement behind the scenes.
Meanwhile, after Colin sat down, the female teacher did not stop but chose another student to stand and be questioned…
“Third row, fourth desk on the right, you seem to understand as well. I’ll change the question for you, do you know…”
Another colleague? When Colin saw the person stand up, he quickly distinguished through his sense of smell that this person was also one of the monsters among them.
“Are the monsters here intentionally singling all of us out? I didn’t notice before, but there are already several classmates, no, several colleagues in the class.”
Colin thought to himself, quietly noting the two who were called to stand, planning to confirm their identities after class.
Considering the difficulty of the task at hand, he didn’t expect that the other employees were still alive…
When the third colleague was called out, Colin saw that the fourth person chosen was a girl, and to his surprise, she seemed to be human.
“Wasn’t it said that only men could enter?”
Colin’s expression was puzzled as he continued to observe secretly.
Before long, the question session before class ended. Of the four who were called out, one answered correctly, while three did not…
This “Passionate Paradise” had also come prepared…
Colin shook his head inwardly; the four of them should have been enough to take down a third-stage Beast Transformation Syndrome creature.
Unexpectedly, they all crashed out on some simple math knowledge.
It seems that everyone’s knowledge reinforcement was done well.
“Alright, you can sit down too. Pay attention to the class. High school is a bit more pressing. When you get to university, it will relax, and then you can play however you want without us managing you…”
“I won’t say more; learning is for you, not for me.”
“Now, everyone take out your textbooks; today, we will learn the last unit of the second semester of the senior year.”
After a few cold remarks, the math teacher let the two sit down without mentioning any punishment, but this made them all the more uneasy, suspecting she might be planning something more sinister…
But there was no time to dwell on these thoughts, as the math class had already begun.
Colin listened while opening his textbook, scanning the math book for key points.
He had already learned these things before, and now, going through them again, he understood many concepts immediately.
However, while flipping through the middle of the book, he suddenly found a small piece of paper tucked inside…
A scent of blood came from the note.
Colin pursed his lips, used his peripheral vision to check his surroundings, and after confirming no one was paying attention, he picked up a ballpoint pen and, under the pretense of writing, opened the note that smelled of blood.
On it, in writing as small as a mosquito’s, was densely packed text.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 123 - 123 123 Code_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 123: Chapter 123 Code_1 Chapter 123: Chapter 123 Code_1 “He who can open this piece of paper must be a normal human, because the ‘Containment Subject’ would ignore these things. I don’t care how you got in here or what faction you belong to, but you must be careful…”
“Never trust the ‘Narrator’! Do not do as it asks, or you will merge into this world and become part of its vast puppetry!”
“Do not use the ‘Book of Fate’, or you will get noticed by the ‘Script Book’, and face its direct targeting!”
“Then, the only way out before it arranges for your death is to immediately head to ‘Rain City’…”
“‘Passionate Paradise’ has lost control; it is being contaminated by the ‘Crimson’, be very careful, we could be assimilated by ‘Passionate Paradise’!”
“Also, be cautious at one o’clock in the morning every Friday, pay attention to time, the real time…”
“If you cannot withstand the ‘Crimson’ and are at your limit, then you can shout ‘Praise the eternal night’ to call forth the heavy rain, and try to run to where it is raining; the last survivors are there…”
“We have established the last shelter here, we are benevolent and willing to exchange secrets with everyone…”
“One last thing, ‘Passionate Paradise’ cannot escape due to some reasons, but we have found a way out…”
…
“Left by someone ahead? Was it the official team from the Sino-American joint production, or other colleagues?”
Colin never expected that he would still find a note left by predecessors here…
The richness of information on it surprised him somewhat.
“They not only discovered the ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’, but they also know the name ‘Script Book’, and even know about its opposition to the ‘Book of Fate’; there’s indeed some substance…”
Colin felt that if he hadn’t already received the corresponding intel from Lady Bunny, he would have been greatly surprised.
“‘Passionate Paradise’ is being contaminated by the crimson?”
“What does this sentence mean, the crimson? What does that signify? I’m so annoyed with these people and their riddles, I just want to kill them all!”
“Forget it, skip ahead—be careful at one o’clock in the morning every Friday, today is Friday, and time has already passed…”
“No, the real time, is that referring to the real-world time?”
Colin pondered for a moment, recalling that today was Thursday, and Friday was tomorrow.
Reality seems to be one day behind the world of the copies…
But then, what’s the point of paying attention to this?
However, he did remember something else, something ‘Two-Faced’ had mentioned in the messages he sent out…
He had safely made it through the first day with no issues, but something happened at dawn during the first night which led to the absence of any messages on the second day, until finally, there was a reply on the third day.
It was unclear what he had encountered during that intermediate time.
“It seems he must have called out this… eternal night and entered that shelter?”
Colin frowned, thinking of ‘Two-Faced’s words, and felt that this shelter might not necessarily be a good place.
“Sigh, this place is truly full of mysteries, there’s a pile of problems in front of me yet to be solved, and now a bunch more troubles pop up…”
He sighed and jotted down the content of the note before putting the note back in its original place within the book.
Then, he searched through other books and soon realized that other books also contained a similar note, almost every book had one, but the content was the same.
Seeing this, he didn’t want to waste any more time there…
“These notes, they kind of make me feel like I’m involved in a pyramid scheme… I’ll talk to the others later and see if they’ve collected any other information.”
Colin muttered, meticulously replacing the books back to their original spots, and then he began to patiently “attend class”.
A few minutes later, the bell signaling the end of class suddenly rang.
The female teacher, with a ruler in her left hand and chalk in her right, turned her head towards the doorbell, and after it stopped, she tapped the blackboard with her ruler, saying indifferently:
“Let’s just finish this one problem, it’s quick, won’t take two minutes.”Damn, dragging out the lesson to the last as well…
Colin was speechless inside, but still listened patiently, and as promised, it really did not take more than two minutes to finish the last problem.
“Next class your physics lesson will be switched with next Tuesday’s physical education…”
The female teacher with the long ruler hadn’t finished speaking when a cheer suddenly erupted in the classroom. All the students seemed very excited. Once everyone calmed down, the teacher gestured for quiet with a slight press of her hand in the air and said expressionlessly:
“However, your P.E. teacher is sick, so the next class will still be math. Alright, class dismissed. Go to the bathroom…”
After finishing her sentence, she turned around and left, leaving behind a deflated classroom.
“That’s brutal. They’re a bunch of monsters, and they still have to attend classes…”
Colin muttered to himself. Seeing that the female teacher had disappeared into the corridor, he stood up and walked over to his colleague, who had just been scolded:
“Sky King…”
“Covering Earth Tiger…”
“Going to the bathroom?”
“Sure.”
A colleague from the first row also spoke up, “Wait, take me with you…”
“You… Big Hammer…”
“80.”
“Got it, let’s go.”
After confirming their code words, Colin nodded and glanced uncertainly at the only girl in the room.
“The milky white Xuezi…” the girl said to the three of them.
At these words, including Colin, all three fell silent for a moment—so she was one of them.
It’s just that no names were mentioned, so none of them actually knew who the others were.
“I… I mean, let’s talk outside, it’s not appropriate to speak here.”
As she spoke, the only girl who had been called upon to answer questions in class was the first to leave the room.
Colin and the others looked at each other, hesitated for a few seconds, and followed her out together.
