They didn’t actually go to any bathrooms, but instead, found a spot in the corridor to huddle together.
“Dude, what’s your situation? If I remember correctly, isn’t this place only accessible to males?”
One of the colleagues couldn’t help but ask first.
“I don’t know, I seem to be a girl, yet also, not…”
“What do you mean?”
“I… have both male and female… stuff, but there are only girls’ clothes at home, so I can only dress like a girl.”
Well, that’s androgynous…
Colin and the others were taken aback, for this was something they had only seen on TV.
“How can this be? Which one are you? If you don’t come clean, we can’t trust you…”
“I’m Dog Brother.”
The girl spoke up, awkwardly saying, “Uh, maybe there was some ambiguity in my gender characteristics when I came in, causing a bug. This issue is pressing for time, so let’s not talk about it now, it shouldn’t affect things…”
“True.”
“Indeed.”
Colin nodded in agreement, then noticed a complex expression on the other two’s faces, a mixture of relief and apprehension.
“Right, is it just us here, or is there another person?”
“Nothing bad happened to them, did it?”
“Let’s not worry about them for now, our matter here is urgent. How are things on your side?”
The girl known as “Dog Brother” said, “On my way here, I seem to have made some special discoveries.”

chapters.title: Chapter 124 - 124 124 This is a slide that must not be
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 124: Chapter 124 This is a slide that must not be touched!_1 Chapter 124: Chapter 124 This is a slide that must not be touched!_1 “Dog Brother, spill the details about your special discovery…”
“It’s nothing much, just that in the small room next to mine, where my aunt stays, I saw a message that must’ve been left by a previous employee. He mentioned that unknown dangers could arise tonight, and if we want to survive, we should head to a place called ‘Rain City’…”
“Rain City? What’s that?”
“I’m not sure, I didn’t get the chance to look more closely, my aunt came back…”
Meanwhile, hearing Dog Brother’s words, Colin paused, reminded of the note he’d just received—
Could this be the rainy place mentioned on the note?
It mentioned the same location, “Rain City”…
Just as Colin was about to ask for more details, the bell for class rang.
“Damn it, did we even get five minutes of break?” Dog Brother’s pretty face showed anger as he cursed softly.
But curse as they might, they dared not delay, hurrying into the classroom and back to their seats, fearing anything that might be triggered by lagging behind.
Before entering the door, Colin, remembering something, pulled everyone aside and reminded them, “Right, later, check your textbooks to see if there’s anything tucked inside.”
The others didn’t say much but nodded their heads.
Just as he returned to his seat, Colin saw the bespectacled girl in front of him turn around.
“You and that girl… no, what were you guys just talking about?” she began, then remembered it seemed to involve several others.
[The girl named Liu Yun tried to cover up the slip in her speech. Of course, that’s not the point. The point is she’s showing a tinge of jealousy towards the girl you were chatting with. If you can’t produce a plausible explanation, perhaps something dangerous might occur?]
Do I need to give explanations for speaking now? What’s up with this new yandere twist…Colin looked at the narrator who had just settled down and was now stirring things up again, somewhat speechless, but he noticed from the information above that it finally decided to give the girl a name after such a long time.
Before, it was just “sister,” “class beauty,” “female cop,” “female teacher”—it couldn’t even be bothered to come up with a name…
And it seems like Liu Yun has somehow become attached to him.
Colin could clearly feel the difference between her and the other “NPCs”; compared to the beginning, she had become more spirited…
Was it because the “Narrator” was constantly setting her up with characteristics?
After pondering for a moment, Colin carefully said, “Nah, I had an emergency earlier and borrowed twenty bucks from him. I was just paying him back…”
The sense of impending danger hadn’t been triggered, which likely meant that the person before him didn’t possess special abilities like the female cop.
There was no need to worry about being cut for lying.
“Oh, is that right?” The quiet Liu Yun with glasses looked dubious.
“What else could it be?”
Colin pursed his lips, slightly annoyed by her skepticism. What, did she really think he could have an inappropriate relationship with Dog Brother, a straight man of steel?
Thinking about the two sets of equipment Dog Brother was carrying, just the thought made Colin’s skin crawl.
“You know, you…”
“The teacher’s coming, stop talking.”
Seeing Liu Yun finally turn obediently back around, Colin breathed a sigh of relief. He truly felt as if he were on the verge of being confronted with a Divine Skill at any moment.
Without further thought, with another command for the students to stand up, what was supposed to be PE class now officially began as a math class.
Seeing the female teacher raise the ruler in her hand, only a very small portion of “top students” in the class showed no reaction. The others, especially the “illiterate” group led by Colin, all shifted uneasily…
They quickly reviewed the bare essentials, knowing that if called up to solve a problem, it would likely spell trouble.
Although it seemed okay just now, if they were called up again, it was uncertain whether troubles would arise.
‘Damn it, I’m an outstanding employee who has made commendable contributions to the Bonfire Company by entering and exiting the Other World three times, and yet I’m afraid of solving a math problem…’
Colin felt his mood inexplicably a bit subtle and shitty.
Fortunately, the icy-tempered female teacher didn’t make everyone do exercises this time; instead, she picked up the ruler, tapped it on the blackboard, and continued the content from the last lesson.
Seeing this, Colin and the others all breathed a sigh of relief, feeling lucky to have survived a disaster.
Then, as the dry and tedious lecture resumed, Colin quietly lifted his right hand, propped up his chin, and pretended to study attentively.
“Yukionna, Yukionna, please tell me, what is ‘Rain City’?”
Colin asked in a low voice, not knowing what “Rain City” was, but “Yukionna” should know…
A chill slid up from his middle finger.
Corresponding thoughts unfurled in his mind…
“A very dangerous area within ‘Passionate Paradise’ that one can travel to whenever it rains? One of the locations where the initial invasion occurred?”
Colin was stunned. How dangerous must it be for “Yukionna” to consider it a threat?
“Let’s not worry about the danger for now. Is there really a way to escape that place?”
Colin’s current guess was that “Passionate Paradise” had become inoperable for some unknown reason, preventing a mechanism akin to “Descent Protocol G-2” from triggering and allowing one to return to reality…
Therefore, if one wanted to go home, they had to rely on their own Divine Skills.
Soon, a cold message came through.
“You don’t know? You only know that there is an important factor there that caused the loss of control in ‘Passionate Paradise’?”
Colin was somewhat surprised by this but not overly so. Thinking it over, he changed the question.
“Right, do you know what ‘Crimson’ is? It was mentioned on a note I just saw, something about ‘Crimson’…”
No sooner had the words left his mouth did Colin feel the “Yukionna” ring squeeze tightly, reacting violently as if poked in a sensitive spot, turning his finger red from the pressure.
What’s happening? Is this necessary? It’s just a name, could it be going mad?
Colin’s brow furrowed slightly. He could sense that “Yukionna” was experiencing an intense fear of the name “Crimson,” so much so that even mentioning it caused such a reaction.
Several minutes passed, and not until his finger had swollen to a purplish hue did the ring slowly relax its grip.
However, before Colin could ask again, he felt a cool breath arrive, bringing with it a message that almost seemed like a plea.
Don’t mention anything related to “Crimson” anymore!
In Colin’s mind, it was as if a scene formed of “Yukionna” kneeling and kowtowing to him—
Stop talking, I’m begging you!
For the sake of staying alive, don’t speak of it again!
This is a topic not even to be touched upon!
‘Not even to be mentioned? Is it that dangerous? This… it’s a bit like that old ‘Hunger’ and ‘Tyrant’…’
Colin rubbed his darkened fingers, encouraging blood flow to return them to their normal color.
He remembered, back in the Other World, that “Hunger” and “Tyrant” were so intense that a mere glance could nearly explode, and they forced everyone to not dare sleep or dream at night, almost to the point where sleep meant death…
But at least they could be spoken about, while this “Crimson” seemed even more special, too dangerous to even be mentioned…
Just mentioning a name had frightened “Yukionna” into such a cowardly state.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 125 - 125 125 Some Ridiculous Things. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 125: Chapter 125: Some Ridiculous Things. _1 Chapter 125: Chapter 125: Some Ridiculous Things. _1 He didn’t think much of it and took a quick glance at the female teacher. Seeing that she hadn’t noticed what was going on here, he continued to ask,
“So speaking of which, do you know why ‘Passionate Paradise’ was invaded in the first place?”
If he could figure out why “Passionate Paradise” was invaded, the whole incident’s context would become much clearer…
This time the question wasn’t too dangerous, and he quickly got a response…
But this response left Colin completely baffled.
“What do you mean? To catch mothers? What on earth are ‘mothers’? No, wait, mother is a mother, what’s with the plural? Which ‘mothers’ are you referring to? No, that’s not right. Forgive me for being somewhat impolite, but do you even have a mother?”
Colin’s brain CPU was a bit dizzy, and at first, he couldn’t understand the meaning behind Yukionna’s response.
However, after a brief exchange and piecing together the information he had received…
Colin suddenly had a bold thought. He glanced at the classroom and spoke in a voice that others couldn’t hear,
“Your mothers, are they also the mothers of everyone in ‘Passionate Paradise,’ and, is their relationship with each other not very good?”
A cold breath came quickly, affirming Colin’s words.
At the same time, this response helped him roughly understand what “mothers” meant—
“Script Book,” “Decree Book (Rule Book),” “Book of Fate,” and so on…
This… did indeed make sense.
The character “Yukionna” and others like her were essentially monsters, crammed into some “personas” by those high-level artifacts, forcibly transformed from monster female to rational and reborn human females.
So, it wasn’t too much of a stretch for “Yukionna” to refer to these items as “mothers.”
‘In the past, when watching anime, people were turned into monsters, but the folks at the company, they think about turning monsters into people, quite creative indeed…’
Colin felt that he had also opened his eyes a bit more today.
“But looking at it this way, you guys have quite a number of mothers. Do you have a father? No? Oh, so all of you are mothered, but fatherless…”
Colin mostly figured these things out.
At first, based on his perception of people, he didn’t connect “books” with “mothers” straight away.
But thinking about it, the “Script Book,” “Book of Fate,” and so on might not actually be books at all.
They could also be glamorous, mature young women…
Unmarried, but with a bunch of kids.
It seemed that there was also one or more masters…
Shaking his head slightly, without dwelling further on this somewhat wacky idea, Colin refocused and continued to inquire, “So how are your ‘mothers’ doing now?”
As he finished speaking, he paused—not needing to go through Yukionna to have a rough understanding.
For instance…
Names like “Book of Fate: Fragment” and “Decree Book·Fragment” could probably give him a glimpse into their status.
As for “Script Book,” Colin wasn’t too sure, since there was no item like “Script Book·Fragment” available on the company’s market…
But considering the status of the other two, the situation of “Script Book” was probably not great either.
However, compared to his speculations, Yukionna offered a bit more information…
“You can’t really feel the normal ‘mothers’ anymore? Except for ‘Great Mother’ Script Book, the rest of the ‘mothers,’ second mother ‘Book of Fate,’ third mother ‘Rule Book,’ except for some remnants of power, have vanished?”
Colin asked softly, vague images of some past events emerging in his mind—
At first, several “housewives” in “Script City” happily created children, never expecting a group of unknown things to rush in. Without a second word, they kidnapped the local girls, causing “Script City” to spiral out of control…
Huh, this sounds a bit odd.
Colin exhaled slightly. Whether the mystery had been solved wasn’t clear, he just felt that things were getting stranger and stranger.
Of course, the strangeness was mainly due to “Yukionna’s” peculiar names for several objects.
And mainly…
With only this information, Colin still couldn’t find a breakthrough.
“Don’t you remember anything from your escape from ‘Passionate Paradise’? Did your ‘moms’ leave you any messages or something?”
Colin somewhat suspected that “Yukionna” might have some tricks up her sleeve…
After all, the abilities of these few objects were written directly in their names…
Colin had never used the “Script Book,” but from its name, it could surely weave a person’s future path, make events happen as one wished, and manipulate incidents from behind the scenes to achieve the ultimate goal.
Colin was no stranger to the ‘Book of Fate,’ though he had never used its original form, but from the fragment, its capabilities at least included observing the future and penetrating the unknown…
If the two objects were used in combination…
At this thought, Colin suddenly fell silent for a moment—he suddenly realized that a perfectly good employee, suddenly hit by a stroke of extreme misfortune, being brought into “Script City” might just be due to their arrangement?
“No, there were several batches of people who entered before me; it shouldn’t have been done specifically to target me, but I can’t rule out the suspicion that it was arranged. However, what I should be more concerned with now is their purpose for dragging people in here.”
“Is it merely an instinctual harm to others, in need of more sacrifices, or are they trying to find a way to save themselves by pulling in Bonfire employees?”
“Why did the Chinese-American co-production force its way into ‘Passionate Paradise’? What was that for?”
Colin had some guesses…
If it was about pulling people in to save themselves, then “Passionate Paradise” itself wasn’t an enemy but a potential ally…
It’s just that this “ally” had some problems.
“Speaking of which, the whereabouts of properties like ‘Femme Fatale,’ ‘Sister Strategy,’ and other such named books are unknown; it’s quite possible they were brought into ‘Script City,’ not necessarily ‘Passionate Paradise,’ but could be other copies related to ‘Script City.'”
Colin speculated that his initial purchase of “Widow Yukionna” had the significant possibility of being part of a set-up.
After all, this cursed place was supposedly sealed and impossible to leave, yet they could still appear in the outside world.
To say there was no connection at all, Colin found that hard to believe.
“Damn, what a trap, it seems I can’t just buy any prop from Bonfire Company carelessly anymore. If I’m not careful, I might inadvertently fall into their scheme…”
Colin cursed inwardly and then took a long breath out, ending the storm of thoughts in his head.
He had some ideas now, planning to follow up on the information from “Yukionna” to see if there was a way to contact “Great Mother,” and then see if they could form an alliance.
After all… the Great Mother surely wouldn’t want to end up like the second mother, right?
If he could get her support, the pressure of the entire event would become much lighter in an instant.
Even then, Colin might have the chance to think about taking the “Gene Compensation Panel Version 1.0” out with him from the copy.
Thinking it over, he planned to ask more questions, but he noticed “Yukionna” had actively sent a message…
However, as soon as Colin understood what “Yukionna” was saying, his breathing stalled, his scalp tingled with numbness, and his gaze sharpened.
“Mom is here, she’s outside the window…”
.

chapters.title: Chapter 126 - 126 126 Terrifying and Deadly Attack_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 126: Chapter 126 Terrifying and Deadly Attack_1 Chapter 126: Chapter 126 Terrifying and Deadly Attack_1 Right outside the window?
Colin’s heart “thudded,” and then out of the corner of his eye, he saw numerous pink marks next to the classroom window that seemed to have appeared out of nowhere, looking just like cherry blossoms pasted outside…
However, when he came to his senses, he abruptly realized that these were definitely not cherry blossoms.
They were dense clusters of crimson handprints…
These blood handprints rapidly formed on the window, growing ever more vivid, as if still oozing.
Bang, bang, bang!!!
The window suddenly trembled, the pounding sound like raindrops, and he could faintly hear the screams and howls of countless people in his ears.
“Help, let me out, let us out!!!”
“SOS!”
“Help me!!!”
“Save me!!!”
“help!!”
“….”
A surge of cries and screams from different people burst in his ears like a tsunami, causing Colin’s head to throb intensely, his eyes bloodshot and veined.
At that moment, with a crack, the classroom window glass suddenly developed fissures…
Crimson light flooded the classroom in an instant.
“Ah…”
Colin couldn’t help but groan in pain, covering his forehead with his hand.
He felt the world before him turn blood-red, with thick blood flowing everywhere, merging into pools of blood where countless figures struggled and thrashed.
And near him, pale arms emerged from the blood pools, grasping at his body, as if trying to drag him into the pools with them…
Or rather, like a drowning person clutching at the last straw, hoping to grasp him and rise out of the blood lake.
Each hand possessed immense strength; merely being grasped by them, Colin felt immobilized, unable to do anything but watch helplessly as his body was dragged into the pools of blood, becoming the “straw” for these “drowned.”
Even under this sudden assault, he had no chance to use “Time Stasis”!
“Damn it, what the hell is this…”
Colin felt his thoughts grow increasingly faint, unable to move at all.
Just then, he suddenly felt the presence of “Beast Transformation Syndrome” swelling and then contracting back within his body.
Immediately after, a powerful hunger emanated from his stomach…
“Gurgle, gurgle, gurgle~” The rumbling from his belly vibrated, causing the blood-colored, pale arms to stiffen momentarily.
This sudden development startled Colin.
Because he had not at all attempted to trigger the presence of “Beast Transformation Syndrome” just now!
And this power didn’t seem like “Beast Transformation Syndrome”…
But rather like “Hunger”!
“Fuck! When did this thing get inside me!”
Colin was shocked again.
But before he could think further, the rumbling of his belly, almost like a monk chanting in a temple, a thin, ethereal sound, made mouths without teeth grow on the palms of the surrounding pale hands…
Then, as if infected by the intense “Hunger,” they began to bite at the other arms frenetically, devouring each other in a bizarre spectacle.
At the same time, Colin’s ears were filled with what seemed like a monk’s whisper, and he vaguely saw a terrifying Buddha statue sitting in a hall…
“Hear my voice, comprehend my wisdom, follow my teachings…”
“Devour all that is impure and fallen…”
“Great compassion, great…”
An honorable name appeared to be on the verge of being uttered, but at that moment, a line of text appeared before his eyes.
[No one wishes to see Him appear in this world, for He is the nemesis of all creatures with tangible existence. Even “0-9 Hunger” cannot tolerate the presence of His power in reality, hence “0-9 Hunger” instinctively took action—a perfectly normal occurrence…]
[However, due to the minimal amount of power residing within you, after only a brief confrontation to initially resolve the issue, the part of “0-9 Hunger” quickly waned and fell into a temporary slumber.]
[And as for a part of His essence, it, too, could not be sustained after the interference and the crimson essence faded.]
[Everything here will return to normal.]
[Because this incident happened in reality but only in a minor part, your classmates, teachers, and the majority of other things, aside from you, remained unaware of what just transpired.]
As these lines of text appeared, Colin immediately felt the disappearance of the Buddha statue’s image in his mind.
The hunger in his stomach, the crimson world before his eyes, and the overwhelming cries for help resounding beside him like waves crashing—all abnormalities swiftly vanished…
Apart from the lingering pain and the cracked window, everything seemed to return to normal once again.
Then, Colin instantly made sense of something through the “Narrator”.
A terrifying entity had suddenly attacked, nearly killing him, and then the “0-9 Hunger” hidden within the “Beast Transformation Syndrome” had engaged in some resistance. There wasn’t just resistance—it seemed to want to turn him into a Believer.
“Then, they ‘perished together’? That crimson thing is what they call the ‘Rule Book’? No, no…”
Colin rubbed his throbbing forehead and quickly realized that the “Great Mother” mentioned by Yukionna was probably the later “Narrator”.
It hadn’t truly arrived but had created a “Script” through the “Narrator” that provided some aid.
It was like the mantis stalking the cicada, unaware of the oriole behind. In the end, it stepped in and suppressed both parties.
Colin could feel that after the clash with the “crimson” entity, his “Beast Transformation Syndrome” became unprecedentedly “quiet”.
[Clearly, you know you cannot die in “Passionate Paradise”; although it wouldn’t truly kill you, it would signify your utter failure, with no more chances to escape…]
[Clearly, you know you must be cautious of the fallen in “Rain City”. Maybe some are normal, but you simply don’t have the energy to discern…]
[Clearly, you know that from this moment until your death or the end of your mission’s time, you will be able to get some help from “Passionate Paradise”…]
Again, three lines from the “Narrator” appeared before him…
Colin could distinctively feel that the current “Narrator” seemed vastly different from the previous one.
“Can’t die here, be careful with the people of ‘Rain City’, know that ‘Passionate Paradise’ is a source of strength… Is this a reminder? Wait, are you the ‘Script Book’? ”
Colin quickly digested the information before him, and then frowned slightly—was this entity so sure he was going to enter “Rain City” instead of making another choice?
But before he could think further, the “Narrator’s” message disappeared from his view, with no further response.
At the same time, a trembling sensation came from his ring…
“Gone?”
Colin wasn’t too surprised and took a deep breath. Then he felt something odd on his face; he reached out to wipe it and found his fingers covered in blood…
He wiped again and realized that his nose had bled profusely just moments ago.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 127 - 127 127 Before the year 2044..._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 127: Chapter 127 Before the year 2044…_1 Chapter 127: Chapter 127 Before the year 2044…_1 After wiping his face with a tissue and ensuring that there were no problems besides dry eyes, a sore throat, an aching mouth, a hungry stomach, and a throbbing headache, Colin planned to continue inquiring about the “Yukionna.”
He had to understand if the “Script Book” had left behind anything else besides inexplicably getting beaten up and uttering some perplexing words.
Just then, some information emerged in his mind.
[A new event has been added to “Team Promotion Mission.” Please check the “Mission Panel” for details.]
“A new mission from Bonfire Company?” Colin muttered, vaguely realizing that during that recent encounter, Bonfire Company must have obtained some information, otherwise they wouldn’t have issued a new mission.
Without much thought, he willed the “Mission Panel” open and saw the new events added to the team promotion mission.
[Event Four: Strive to enter “Rain City” by 3 a.m. tomorrow morning, taking advantage of the impending anomaly to investigate the level of pollution in that area. Current progress: 0%.]
Note: Please do not die within “Script City.” If you die, it means that you cannot leave this place before 2044.
[Event Five: Go to the home of the “Loafing Immortal” and resolve his current situation.]
Note: Bring along your teammates; although their strength may not match yours, Bonfire Company’s signal will be stronger and the information received more complete when they are present.]
[Event Six: Find and save more employees who have not yet died…]
Note: The company has always been adhering to the principle of not giving up on any employee that could be alive.]
…
After quickly browsing through the content of the new missions, Colin understood what he needed to do next.
“Entering ‘Rain City’ by 3 a.m., no wonder the ‘Script Book’ was so certain I’d go there—it had directly communicated with Bonfire Company?”
Colin guessed that during the encounter, that thing had probably bypassed him and spoken directly to Bonfire Company.
Of course, it could also be because he was like a humanoid camera; whatever he saw, the folks at Bonfire Company knew as well. Combined with their possession of more information, they would know how to proceed.
“But why can’t I leave before 2044? What’s the significance of that year?” Colin was puzzled. There were still a good ten to twenty years left until 2044, and if he were to get trapped here by accident, it would feel no different from being dead.
This time he wasn’t sure whether he had entered with his physical body or if only his soul was present.
If it were just his soul and his body was still lying at home…
Then, waiting a decade or more to get out, his body would probably be nothing but a skeleton by then, no, it would have already been reported by neighbors for reeking, then sent to the crematorium and burned to ashes.
“Event Five… so the one not present is the ‘Loafing Immortal’? And he’s been trapped at home?”
Colin pursed his lips, thinking, out of five people, just this one got stuck at home…
Really weak.
However, looking at the note for Event Five, wasn’t it subtly suggesting that these people were just mobile signal boosters or extra pairs of legs?
“Forget it, as long as they don’t significantly drag me down, it’s not a big issue. Besides, they’re actually not that weak…”
Colin wasn’t too bothered.
In fact, based on his observations, Dog Brother and the others’ strength was actually not weak, slightly stronger than Warden Calder from the Other World. Plus, each of them had some Bonfire Company gadgets, the specifics of which he did not know, so they couldn’t be considered too weak.
Then, his gaze shifted downward, and upon seeing the note for Event Six about “not giving up on any employee,” Colin couldn’t help but laugh—if they were fired, they would no longer be considered Bonfire Company employees, right?
“This Event Six, it feels just like when they built the ‘Bonfire Sacrificial Site,’ just using them to build a signal point?”
His seasoned experience allowed him to see right through the essence of the mission…
Of course, if everything went smoothly, these people could indeed be saved.
“Just don’t know how many survivors are left…”
As Colin spoke, he glanced at the window and noticed that it now had only a few cracks, and these cracks were healing over time, much like the flesh of a living being.
As for the events that transpired here, neither the “students” nor his colleagues seemed to have noticed anything.
Obviously, this must have something to do with the power that “Script Book” had just activated.
By observing their reactions, Colin estimated that the other colleagues, besides him, seemed to have not received any new missions.
“Is this a task Lady Bunny has specifically sent to me?”
Colin had a hunch, but he wasn’t certain.
[As seconds and minutes ticked by, the sound of the school bell signaling the end of classes was about to ring. What made everyone even more delighted was the announcement by the principal, due to certain reasons, that school would be dismissed early today…]
The content of the “Narrator” suddenly appeared before his eyes.
No sooner had Colin finished reading than the sound of a bell “ding-a-ling” rang in his ears, followed by the blast of a loudspeaker.
A gentle, mature female voice emerged from the campus broadcast.
Just as described by the “Narrator,” the principal mentioned that there might be a storm later, so school was ending early and everyone should go home.
“The power of the ‘Script Book’ is truly mysterious,” Colin thought to himself with a slight sense of intrigue, just wondering if using the “Book of Fate: Fragment” in tandem with the “Script Book” under a cooperative condition would still lead to being targeted…
If possible, to combine “Book of Fate: Fragment” with the “Script Book,” that would be invincible…
But without dwelling on it, Colin stood up, called his colleagues, and left the classroom, going to a corner of the corridor.
“Did you guys also find those notes in your textbooks?”
“Yes, but about that stuff—it says some stuff inside, do you think it’s credible?”
“Don’t know, it seems like fishing for bait. It might be a trick by ‘Passionate Paradise’ just to lure us there and kill us…”
“You remember what the brother of ‘Two-Faced’ said, right? Said everything is fake, might be about this…”
“Indeed, I feel our focus should be on tonight’s catastrophe…”
…You guys are behind on the news… Colin thought to himself with a murmur. If this were before, he’d probably be hesitating about whether or not to go…
But with insider information now, he thought for a moment, raised his hand, and when he saw the others stop their discussion and look over puzzled, he finally spoke:
“Folks, what we need to consider isn’t the question of whether to go or not…
“It’s how we should deal with trouble once we get there.”
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 128 - 128 128 May I Ask Who You Are_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 128: Chapter 128: May I Ask Who You Are?_1 Chapter 128: Chapter 128: May I Ask Who You Are?_1 “Wait, wait a minute, dude, how come you decided to head straight to ‘Rain City’?”
Someone couldn’t help but interrupt Colin’s speech.
“Yeah, honestly, based on the current intel, that place is obviously a trap…”
“I agree with that, right now we don’t have a hundred percent certainty about the situation over there. I think, we should gather some more intel before making plans. It won’t be too late…”
“Right, the first day isn’t even over, and our understanding is insufficient. Isn’t it too hasty to set off right away?”
As they had yet to make up their minds, Colin’s words sounded as if he had already made the decision for them, which was somewhat discomforting and instinctively met with resistance.
Of course, aside from that, they genuinely felt that the situation in “Rain City” was troublesome.
Especially when combined with Two-Faced’s brother’s vague information, and almost complete ignorance about the place, the pressure was even greater.
One misstep could easily lead to their demise there…
“A hundred percent certainty?”
Colin’s eyebrows raised, the previous remarks were fair, but that last statement suddenly made him feel out of sync with several employees.
How could there be people who think you must be a hundred percent certain before doing something?
However, after second thoughts, Colin kind of understood. The tasks the company employees took on before were all regular F Level tasks, which mostly had very low completion difficulty and no time pressure, so as long as they were prepared, they indeed could be completed with a hundred percent certainty…
Even if they couldn’t be completed, there was enough margin for error to ensure safety.
But…
“I need to correct you on one thing, the task you are currently undertaking is an Out-of-Control Copy.”
Colin waved his hand, feeling the need to correct their mindset:
“We mustn’t let slip any opportunity, we must firmly grasp every chance we get; otherwise, one wrong step could mean all subsequent steps are wrong, and looking back, we’d find no opportunities left at all.”
“What do you mean? Dude, if you can really give a valid reason, we’re not against going over there,” said Dog Brother, his red lips parting slightly as he stared at Colin with a bizarre expression. “Did you receive some key intel again?”
Before Colin reminded them, they might not have noticed the notes hidden within the books.
It was also quite possible that the other party just acquired some crucial information which is why they said this.
However, before Colin could explain, Dog Brother and the other two’s expressions changed subtly, their mouths shut, their eyes slightly glazed, as if their attention was diverted elsewhere…
“Did they also receive their tasks?”
Seeing this, Colin immediately understood the reason; without a “task” directly requesting it, it would be difficult for him to convince them through normal conversation.
At this moment, Dog Brother was the first to snap back to reality, his expression odd: “Based on the task we just received, it seems we only have one path, that is to investigate ‘Rain City’… Strange, did you receive the task in advance?”
“Seems like it.”
Colin didn’t deny it, and they exchanged the specific content of the tasks they had just received, concluding that everyone got the same thing.
Of course, Colin also noted a small detail that was different.
For instance, the remark for the three of them was to survive in “Rain City” by sticking together as much as possible, rather than just being an eye, a phraseology that left much face.
“That’s not right, usually everyone gets the task at the same time. Why did this happen…” Dog Brother and the others looked utterly puzzled, suspecting that Colin might have taken a shortcut.
However, they didn’t dwell on it too much and started discussing the next step of their plan.
“First, let’s extract ‘Loafing Immortal’ from his house…”
Colin proposed the next step, and this time no one opposed; they had received the same task, only the remark was different from Colin’s, it was just a perfunctory mention of shared hardships and then it was finished.
Seeing everyone nod, Colin didn’t stand on ceremony: “Then, let’s align our thoughts. From now on, follow my instructions for the operation. If you have better ideas, you can also speak up.”
He didn’t want the team to be dragged into greater trouble with everyone having their own ideas.
In a small team, it’s very important to have someone who can make decisions.
Colin compared the situations and felt he was suitable, so he had no intention of hiding his talents.
After all, now is not the time to be hiding his strength…
After inexplicably suffering a brutal beating at the window seat just moments ago, Colin realized that the thing hidden beneath “Passionate Paradise” was simply something he couldn’t handle…
Unlike before, when he could slaughter his way through when he was alone.
Waiting for his teammates to mess up and fall into a desperate situation before playing the role of a pig to eat a tiger wasn’t an option this time…
However, when Colin said this, the others couldn’t help but frown.
“Centered around you?”
“Why should we?”
“Probably, based on strength, I think this is the most appropriate from the perspective of strength.”
“Strength?”
“Would this convince you to agree with my decision?”
Colin casually took out a sticker, and the others looked down to see a line of information appear in their retinas—”The False Powerhouse.”
Although Colin didn’t share further information, they could only see the name without knowing the specific details of the item.
But the purple color of the name was enough to demonstrate its power.
“Purple Gear, impressive indeed, but it still lacks a bit of oomph…”
“How about this then?”
Colin waved his hand and showed off his ring—”Widow Yukionna.”
“Green Gear? This…”
Isn’t this even worse than your previous equipment?
To showcase your strength, have you got the sequence wrong?
Moreover…
There might even be a Brother Shunzi in the team, and the big shot hasn’t even rushed to speak yet, so what turn is it yours…
Dog Brother was about to say this when a piece of information suddenly flashed through his mind, reminding him of the owner of this piece of equipment—Unnamed123456.
The only person currently from Bonfire Company who survived the “Descent Project” and also the only known public holder of a “Golden Artifact,” who had repeatedly taken the top position in Bonfire Company—this mysterious employee.
As he realized this, the other two also paused, and their expressions turned much more serious as they came to the same conclusion.
“May I ask, Bro, your name is…”
“I’ve just luckily completed the ‘Descent Project’ a few times, it’s not worth mentioning.”
Colin replied evasively, yet he had already provided an answer.
Seeing Colin’s acknowledgement, even though it was strange, they felt a weird sense of security: “Alright, although I’m not fond of being arranged by someone else, since it’s Brother Shunzi, it’s okay, you have more experience than I do…”
These words, why do they feel a bit odd…
Colin muttered to himself inwardly, preparing to leave the school with everyone to head for the home of “Loafing Immortal” as instructed by the mission.
If they didn’t set out now, it wouldn’t be good for him to die at home.
“Loafing Immortal” dying was just losing a life, but what Colin was losing was a living signal amplifier.
Just then, at this moment, someone suddenly approached them.
“You three, the math teacher just told me to send for you, she wants to see you in the office, she has something to ask you…”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 129 - 129 129 Self-Contradictory Confrontation_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 129: Chapter 129 Self-Contradictory Confrontation_1 Chapter 129: Chapter 129 Self-Contradictory Confrontation_1 Colin turned around and saw the classmate who sat in front of him, the female student Liu Yun whose name had just been called, appear out of nowhere.
[Because they couldn’t answer the question, three students were summoned to the math teacher’s office, a demand that couldn’t be refused, otherwise, who knows what terrible things might happen?]
“What do we do?” Dog Brother and the others were stunned, not expecting that the female teacher would suddenly do this to everyone.
They all turned to look at Colin.
“You guys go ahead.”
Colin glanced at the remaining “people” in the school and his intuition told him that there were too many “people” here, taking action would be tantamount to seeking death.
At the same time, if it weren’t for the inappropriate timing, he would have liked to ask “Yukionna,” what’s the deal with your mom? Weren’t you supposed to provide help?
He paused before adding, “Just be careful, there might not necessarily be problems inside the office, and if things become unmanageable, then we can talk.”
A few of them nodded their heads and walked towards the teacher’s office, their anxious demeanor as if they feared being caught at any moment.
Seeing the group leave, Colin smiled and thanked Liu Yun—if not for her, everyone might have been caught in one fell swoop, with none spared.
“It’s nothing.”
Liu Yun raised her hand to tuck her hair behind her ear, looked up with a blush coloring her expression, and gazed at Colin:
“By the way, Colin, are you free the day after tomorrow? Your math isn’t good, and, and we’re almost in our senior year, would you like to come to my house, and we can study and discuss together?”
Her tone was somewhat faltering, and after a pause, she added, “No one will be home this Sunday.”
[The bespectacled female student couldn’t contain her inner desire and finally mustered the courage to extend an invitation to study with her in an innocent manner…]
[Immediately, you can’t help but think of a few key phrases flashing across your mind: childhood friend, glasses, man and woman alone, pure love, uncensored…]
[Please do not reject this invitation lightly, otherwise her feelings might swing from one extreme to another?]
Fuck, starting to act up again, aren’t we?
Colin shook his head slightly, dismissing some thoughts from his mind.
He felt the atmosphere was somewhat inexplicably delicate and reckoned, just as the “Narrator” described, refusing would likely cause trouble…
However, after several encounters with these “NPCs,” he’d figured out a few ways to respond…
“If I can make it, I’ll do my best to come.”
Colin made a non-committal promise—if he wasn’t dead by then, he’d be free…
Upon hearing this, the light in Liu Yun’s eyes behind her glasses brightened as she slightly curved the corners of her mouth, “Great, I, I’ll try my best to prepare, and then we can discuss and study together the parts you don’t understand…”
Is this discussion about studying even serious?
Colin complained internally but outwardly agreed with her.
If all went well, he could potentially have a chance to leave “Passionate Paradise” in a few days.
As for finishing the task…
That wasn’t very important after all.
If it couldn’t be completed, they could just start a new “team task”; it’s not possible for them to always be Out-of-Control Copies, is it?
Afterward, Liu Yun started to ask about some other stuff, like his favorite foods.
While Colin verbally responded, he quietly observed the teacher’s office, but things inside seemed relatively stable.
A few minutes later, the three colleagues finally came out, and seeing them, Liu Yun turned red and hurried away…
“You guys made quite a smooth transition there.”
Colin muttered under his breath. When he was conversing with Liu Yun just a moment ago, he had an inexplicable feeling of being manipulated—first, it sidestepped his three colleagues and then brought Liu Yun over, it might have already made some special arrangements for him…
Shaking his head slightly and not dwelling on the thought, Colin noticed the somewhat indescribably odd expressions on the faces of the three returning colleagues.
“Teacher just asked us the questions again, nothing much, but, Brother Shunzi, you definitely don’t know, we seem to have activated something incredible…”
“A points add-on panel?”
“Yeah… Huh?” Dog Brother was about to explain, but upon understanding what was said, he was taken aback, “How’d you know?”
“I started it a bit earlier than you guys.”
Colin explained offhandedly and didn’t linger, walking towards the staircase while saying, “However, this task isn’t easy to do now, to get the disposable points, you need to interact with those ‘NPC’ female characters.
“If it were during normal times in ‘Passionate Paradise’, it would be somewhat manageable, after all, even if you fail the mission you could leave…
“But now, if you don’t want to die here, don’t think too much…”
“That’s true…”
Dog Brother thought it over and indeed that was the case. In the past, dying in the Out-of-Control Copy meant you could start over, but now, death meant truly dead.
The allure of becoming stronger through adding points was tempting, but when compared to one’s life, it was insignificant.
With that, the group followed Colin’s lead and headed upstairs.
But as soon as they reached the school gates, they heard chaos at the entrance…
[Some thugs seemed to have surrounded a few female students, trying to grope them, and as you pass by and witness this scene, you know you can’t just stand by, so…]
[Suddenly, a police car approached from afar, and upon hearing the sound, the thugs scattered like monkeys when a tree falls.]
…
[Passing by a small alley, you hear some faint moaning sounds from within, and these moans seem to come from more than one person. There appears to be some special kind of gathering inside, and the thought crosses your minds—why not join in?]
[But just as you think to do so, you see several warm-hearted young men helping two girls with sprained ankles out of the alley, and only then do you realize it was all a misunderstanding.]
…
[In a secluded corner, inside a pink-lighted hair salon, a sister dressed in scant fabric gazes at you enticingly, seemingly wanting you to patronize her hair washing business so she can afford more clothes…]
[However, for some reason, as the police car makes a sudden return, the sister hastily shuts the salon door in a panic.]
…
“Huh? What’s going on?”
Everyone noticed something was off, the Narrator’s lines seemed different from the ones during the day; the first half of the sentence appeared to be slightly indecent, and the second half took a sharp turn, almost causing them to pull a muscle.
Moreover, different from during the day, when the “Narrator” appeared it seemed to signal incoming trouble…
But now, it seems to resolve itself, baffling everyone.
However, more so than the confusion of Dog Brother and the others, Colin pondered thoughtfully, guessing at something.
The self-contradictory content before his eyes…
Perhaps it was the “Script Book” fighting against itself.
No, more precisely, it should be the normal part of ‘Passionate Paradise’ that was fighting against the contaminated part.
Thanks to this, Colin and his group encountered almost no more obstacles on their way to Loafing Immortal’s place.
..
.

chapters.title: Chapter 130 - 130 130 Little Brother Open the Door Nicely~_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 130: Chapter 130: Little Brother, Open the Door Nicely~_1 Chapter 130: Chapter 130: Little Brother, Open the Door Nicely~_1 At four in the afternoon, as sunset approached, on their way to “Loafing Immortal”‘s house, everyone couldn’t help but sigh while looking at the flood of information scrolling past on their retinas.
“What a pity, what a pity, we can’t truly relax and immerse ourselves in this dungeon…”
Dog Brother lamented with a shake of his head…
People would occasionally discuss a loli succubus event at the roadside, or some gorgeous housewives seemed to always have a blonde trailing behind them, or some decent women that popped up out of nowhere would invite them over for dinner…
Or when passing by a park, they would hear inexplicable noises coming from within the woods.
Alleys, bushes, windows, balconies, stores, almost every place they laid eyes on was the site of various events, some of pure love, and others involving minotaurs, sadly inaccessible for a genuine experience due to pollution.
“If it weren’t for the pollution, I’d even try out this dungeon just for the individual experience,” the “Soul Lock Warden” averted his gaze from a plump woman with a large bosom.
Once Colin revealed his identity, the other two employees no longer concealed theirs and disclosed their identity as well.
However, when it came to what items they possessed, they only told part of the truth, keeping the rest to themselves.
Colin didn’t insist on knowing more and allowed everyone to retain some secrets.
After all, he himself had plenty he couldn’t reveal…
“Speaking of which, what was the situation like for you guys when you started at home?” Dog Brother couldn’t help but ask out of curiosity.
“Not great…”
“Wandering Speedy Lad” thought about what he had encountered initially and shuddered, he had woken up on the couch, surrounded by five girls who looked almost identical except for their figures, clothes, and hairstyles…
“I reckon they must have used ‘The Quintessential Quintuplets’ as a reference. Back then, they asked me which I liked best, and if it weren’t for my quick wits and prior cramming, I would have almost become quintessential for all five of them…”
“As for me, I had a co-renting housewife, and I almost got my neck wrung the moment I stepped out the door, but luckily in a moment of desperation, I offered to tutor her child, which gave me the chance to escape…”
“Soul Lock Warden” said and looked toward Dog Brother, “What about you, what happened again?”
“I ended up in my aunt’s room the moment I entered, and I had her shorts in my pocket, and then there was this diary in front of me…”
Recalling their first encounters, everyone felt a bit of lingering fear, as it was the closest they had felt to death.
‘It seems like every one of us faced a door-opening murder at the start…’
As Colin walked, he listened to their conversation and noticed that these people encountered fewer things after they left their houses.
No, they almost didn’t encounter anything at all and directly arrived at the school.
This made Colin feel like he had been targeted to some extent from the moment he entered…
But fortunately, the problems weren’t too significant.
Before long, under the “mission” guidance, they stopped in front of a villa that occupied hundreds of square meters.
Colin quietly took a breath, analyzing the faint strange scent in the air, and said, “Let’s get ready, it looks like we’re in for a tough battle.”
There was something dangerous about this house…
…
“Dear little brother, where have you hidden yourself this time? Stop playing hide and seek with sister, come on, let’s do something fun~”
On the third floor of the detached villa, a voluptuous woman walked up; her clothes were somewhat disheveled, with many tears revealing glimpses of flesh, as if she had been through a fierce battle…
Upon reaching the third floor, she revealed a grotesquely exaggerated smile on her pale yet beautiful face, stuck out her tempting tongue, and licked the corner of her mouth before approaching a room door.
“Is it here?”
She stretched out her hand to knock but without waiting for a response, suddenly twisted the doorknob and flung open the door…
Behind the door was an ordinary bedroom, fully furnished.
Regrettably, there was no one inside.
“Oh, it seems my dear brother isn’t here….”
She walked out of the room with disappointment and headed for the next room.
“Is it this one, then?”
“Oh, it’s not again…”
She walked out with regret, her smile gradually disappearing, seemingly becoming impatient, as she headed toward the next door.
This time she didn’t even knock, just directly twisted the handle—but it didn’t open.
Instantly, a flushed smile reappeared on her face, one that carried traces of illness and distortion.
“Dear little brother, sister is coming~”
Bang!
A loud crashing sound suddenly came from outside the door.
“Damn! She’s found me again!”
“Loafing Immortal” felt his heart skip a beat at the sound and looked fearfully towards the solid wooden door of the bedroom.
His identity in this instance was that of a high school student, brought up by his sister who was a decade his senior, and then there was a blonde-haired, blue-eyed childhood friend turned maid who adored him…
And then, today the maid confessed her love, and after hesitating, he chose to “accept.”
But to his surprise, after accepting, “Sister” went mad, unable to accept that her beloved little brother was being taken away…
She smashed the maid’s chest to pieces and tore her apart on the spot, pulling out her spine and head with her bare hands…
Afterward, “Loafing Immortal” desperately used many methods to escape from “Sister’s” demonic clutches.
Of course, it was thanks to the “maid’s” protection…
“Damn, I should’ve put off agreeing and gone to school first…”
“Loafing Immortal” regretted deeply in his heart.
He hadn’t expected that one wrong choice would lead to such a perilous situation…
At that time, choosing “Sister” might have been a good option too, as in hindsight, “Sister’s” combat ability was clearly much higher than the maid’s…
If he had chosen “Sister”, even if the “maid” had gone crazy, he probably would have been sheltered and survived.
Bang!
Another terrifying impact came from outside the door, interrupting his memories.
The whole room trembled, and a faint layer of dust fell from the ceiling, showing how intense the impact was.
“Sweet little brother, open the door nicely, sister wants to come in~”
The woman outside hummed softly while lifting her full bosom and slammed it against the wooden door.
Bang!
Once again, a loud noise was heard.
“Loafing Immortal” glanced at the door and saw a yellow talisman that seemed to be losing its effect. Gritting his teeth, he took out another yellow talisman from the Storage Room and pasted it on the solid door—
“Stabilizing Door Talisman”!
Its effect was to strengthen the door’s sturdiness, under normal circumstances, just sticking one on.
Even an RPG rocket launcher might not be able to blast open the door with the talisman on it, and it might not even leave a scratch; it could be said to be a lifesaver in urban alley fights…
A thick, earthy yellow Secret Force spread from the talisman, reinforcing the door once more…
“My adorable little brother, a sister is like a mother, if you’re naughty, I’ll have to punish you properly in a bit~”
“Sister’s” voice came again, becoming somewhat inhuman.
Then, she once again lifted her firm bosom and smashed it against the wooden door—
She believed that as long as she tried hard enough, her little brother would understand her true feelings.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 131 - 131 131 This is the ceremony for Mothers
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 131: Chapter 131 This is the ceremony for Mother’s awakening…_1 Chapter 131: Chapter 131 This is the ceremony for Mother’s awakening…_1 Bang! Bang! Bang!
The solid wooden red door made an increasingly strained noise under violent collisions, as if it wouldn’t take much longer before it was smashed to pieces.
In just under a few minutes, the yellow talisman affixed to the door with the words “Mount Tai” written in special strokes began to slowly fade, looking as though it would disappear soon.
“Damn it!”
The “Loafing Immortal” hid in the room, trembling uncontrollably, knowing that in less than four minutes, the “Stabilizing Door Talisman” would lose its effectiveness, and the other side would break through the door.
This time, he had no more “Stabilizing Door Talismans” left.
“It’s over…”
The “Loafing Immortal” swallowed hard with a look of terror in his eyes, knowing that once the “Stabilizing Door Talisman” failed, he absolutely would not survive!
All his means had been shattered in the confrontation not long ago, and all that was left in his hands was a broken sword with just a stub remaining.
This sword was once his pride, indestructible in the real world. For the past half year, the many tasks were merely a matter of one stroke of the sword.
But, after just a few clashes with the opponent, the blade was actually snapped in half by the opponent’s chest…
Snapped in half by the chest!
This was something the “Loafing Immortal” had never imagined in his life.
“For fuck’s sake, what’s the deal with that chest, it’s like a hydraulic clamp. What kind of monster was the original entity of this thing before it was contained…”
The “Loafing Immortal” was utterly desperate, and the only method he could think of now was to use the “Book of Fate: Fragment”!
No, it wasn’t just about using the “Book of Fate: Fragment” in an ordinary sense, but triggering “The Dice of Probability” through it.
Only if he rolled “Luck,” he might have a chance to survive.
Otherwise, merely using the “Book of Fate: Fragment,” he would at most, learn only three ways he could die.
But…
That mere one percent probability was also daunting and despairing.
Moreover, this instance had an aspect that set it apart from other instances, as it seemed to be one of the rare ones that harbored an unknown malice towards the “Book of Fate.”
Perhaps just using the first page could lead to an unforeseen disaster.
Bang Bang Bang!
The heavy knocking sound came over and over again.
The “Loafing Immortal” was in disarray, his heart sinking ever lower.
At this moment, he was more inclined to abandon all illusions and use the “Book of Fate: Fragment.”
Since he was already in an impasse with no escape, he might as well gamble desperately forward. Despite the many restrictions and only a one percent chance, a full effort might still eke out a sliver of faint hope.
“It’s just death if all else fails!” the “Loafing Immortal” hardened his heart.
But just then, the relentless heavy thudding suddenly stopped, and it did not resume for a couple of seconds.
“What’s going on?” the “Loafing Immortal” froze, momentarily stopping his use of the “Book of Fate: Fragment.”
But before he could think further, he heard the voice come again…
“Why don’t we have an open-hearted talk?”
This sudden change in tone made the “Loafing Immortal” hesitate for a moment. Could there be a turning point in this situation?
After a few seconds of hesitation, he tentatively said, “Then, can you let me go to school?”
If he left, he was absolutely never coming back to this godforsaken place again!
From the information left by predecessors, he knew that as long as he could escape, leave this villa, he would be temporarily safe…
While speaking, “Loafing Immortal” suddenly felt uneasy and carved a few words in a corner with his broken sword—choose Sister, be her licking dog, then leave the house!
He didn’t know who started the habit of leaving messages, but since he had accepted help from others, he didn’t mind leaving some potentially useful information for others who might come in the future.
“Go to school?…”
A strange laugh suddenly came from outside the door, followed by him hearing the other party continue to say:
“You finally spoke to Sister…”
When he heard this sentence, “Loafing Immortal” felt a sudden and intense unease inside—damn, it was a trap, he shouldn’t have replied!
The next second, he suddenly felt a sharp pain in his brain, and then an uncontrollable fear erupted from within.
“Loafing Immortal”‘s spirit was affected, and he lost all rationality, crying his eyes out as if he had broken down, cowering in a corner not daring to look at the door again.
For a moment, he even forgot to use the “Book of Fate: Fragment”.
“Sister is here~”
As the voice fell, a violent collision sound suddenly erupted, and the solid wooden door that had held up for nearly half an hour burst apart.A pair of enormous breasts burst through the door opening, sending wood chips flying.
“Don’t!”
“Loafing Immortal” hugged the broken sword, his body shrinking into the corner, his head against the wall, legs flailing on the floor, and he screamed in utter despair.
Only to see that the huge, full breasts slowly withdrew from the broken hole in the door, revealing the pitch-black corridor outside…
But in a few seconds, a beautiful face stretched in through the breach, her whole head squeezed in the door’s broken hole, seemingly with red glowing eyes turning towards the corner by the door.
“I placed that little bitch’s head on the bedside, later, let her head watch…”
Saying this, she retracted her face and stretched her hand through the broken hole, reaching for the doorknob, ready to open the door from the inside and enter.
“Loafing Immortal,” his face filled with panic and having lost his sanity, didn’t even consider putting up a fight. His rationality had been shattered just now, and even though he knew deep down this was the last chance, that there would be no opportunities left if he didn’t fight, the extreme terror prevented him from taking any action…
He couldn’t even directly use the “Book of Fate: Fragment” in his mind.
Click~
The door to the room was opened.
“Don’t come over here!!!”
“Loafing Immortal” shrieked.
“Sister” stepped forward, grabbed his two legs, and started dragging him out of the room, all the while talking and laughing strangely.
As long as she kept speaking, she could continuously maintain that fear, preventing any accidents from happening…
The babbling suddenly halted.
As “Sister” stepped outside the room, an inconspicuous hanging cord dropped from above the door frame. Before she could react, it looped around her neck and suspended her off the ground in an instant.
.
.
.
This chapter… its original content was probably too explicit; it kept getting deleted and modified by the system, and after changing it, it was deleted again, there’s nothing I could do, so I had to make do. (In fact, there was no special content, I don’t know why it was so sensitive)

chapters.title: Chapter 132 - 132 132 Displaying Divine Skills_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 132: Chapter 132 Displaying Divine Skills_1 Chapter 132: Chapter 132 Displaying Divine Skills_1 “What is this? A rope?”
Suspended above the ground, “Sister” clutched at her neck, only to feel a rough, thin rope. She looked up and saw a rope descending from the darkness, looped around her neck.
Without a chance to take another look, a terrifying force suddenly emanated from the rope around her neck.
Even as a supernatural being, her thoughts began to slow, and she found it difficult to think…
It seemed as if a large hand at the end of the rope was exerting force, lifting her towards the ceiling. The higher her feet left the ground, the stronger the terrifying force became. Sounds of bones crisply breaking could be heard within her body; it was clear that her neck wouldn’t last long before snapping.
Her eyes rolled back to the point where only the whites were visible. Because of the pressure from the rope, her tongue protruded from her mouth, stretching long, with viscous saliva dripping from its tip…
In the case of a normal person, they’d practically be dead by now.
Yet, at that moment, a flash of scarlet light swept across her eyes.
…
“Got it, rush in, act now, save her!”
Outside the stand-alone villa, “Soul Lock Warden” shouted from the courtyard.
At this instant, he held a bamboo fishing rod in his hand. At the end of the rod, there was a somewhat rough, thin rope that extended into the shadows, taut as if it had caught something.
But just as he finished speaking, a strong pull came from the rope below.
He stumbled, nearly being dragged down.
“Damn, such strong force all of a sudden. Hurry up and move, I can’t hold on much longer!”
“Hold on a bit longer!”
After Dog Brother took a deep breath, he looked towards a location on the second floor and retrieved an unsheathed dagger from the Storage Room, which was inlayed with numerous precious stones such as red coral, rubies, sapphires, and pearls on both the handle and scabbard.
After taking out the object, he hesitated for a moment before drawing the blade from its sheath…
At that moment, Colin and the others felt a strange, chilling presence enveloping the area.
Creating an unbearable sensation…
On the exquisitely ornate blade, there appeared to be a lifelike feather pattern crafted with a unique forging technique. The sharp dagger shimmered with a dark light as if under an unknown scrutiny.
“Damascus blade pattern? This energy level… Purple Gear, eh? Going all in with a royal flush right at the start?”
Colin roughly surmised the level of the equipment, unsure of its effects but feeling it must be formidable.
However, as he was thinking this, he suddenly saw Dog Brother turn his head and say to them, “If you see me start to self-harm, Brother Shunzi, remember to stop me…”
“No problem,” Colin nodded.
Dog Brother raised his ornate dagger in his right hand, extended his left hand with the palm facing up. Soon after, he grabbed the hilt with his right hand and quickly thrust it downward, piercing through his palm…
Instantly, blood poured from the center of his palm, converging on the blade and dripping from its tip.
As the blood hit the ground, rings of black mist began to spread from beneath his feet, covering a radius of three meters around him.
What made Colin’s skin crawl was the sight of Dog Brother staring at his bleeding palm with an oddly blissful smile creeping across his handsome face, despite the pain.
But his expression suddenly stiffened as he shook his head, and his high ponytail swung with the motion…
Meanwhile, from the black mist around Dog Brother, strange whispers arose, sounding like the rustling of wind yet also like hushed voices in the shadows.
One by one, dark figures began to stand up within the mist.
They were five in number, resembling but not quite human, with disproportioned limbs and four arms, their hands bearing long claws like scythes…
As they emerged, Dog Brother, resisting the pleasure of cutting himself again, lifted his head and turned his gaze to the second floor.
In his eyes, the world turned gray and transparent, and everything could be clearly seen.
After focusing his gaze on the monster hanging mid-air, emanating a red glow…
Dog Brother’s left hand remained still, while his right hand loosened its grip on the knife handle and slowly stretched out his index finger towards the glowing monster.
“Go!”
As the words fell, five black shadows let out an eerie and piercing screech, rushing toward the monster.
They seemed to ignore the physical material of reality, not abiding by the physics rules understood by most, running through the air and passing through walls, swiftly arriving on the second floor.
Click~
It was at this moment that “Sister” tore off the noose from her neck, touched the ground with her tiptoes, pushed off with force, and leapt backward, avoiding the beheading attack that came sweeping towards her.
However, even though she dodged the lethal strike, the other monsters still left several gashes on her body.
“Interrupting my time with my little brother, you all deserve to die!”
A burst of red light exploded from “Sister” as she turned around, her absurdly large bosom swelling even more and smashing directly onto the head of a four-armed shadow…
With a bang, the shadow exploded on the spot.
“Holy shit, that’s so exaggerated?”
Downstairs, Dog Brother, as if feeling for the shadow, felt like his head had been struck by a club, and he staggered.
These shadows, normally impervious to any attack, now one was killed by a single chest slam…
This was a bizarre death he could never have imagined in his lifetime.
However, as the four-armed shadow vanished, another shadow rose from the darkness beside him.
This item, as long as he himself didn’t die, would keep summoning shadows to carry out orders without end.
Of course, he didn’t know the limit of the item, but his limit was probably the death of ten shadows…
The closer he got to this number, the closer Dog Brother felt to death.
Apart from that, the accompanying negative effects “Pleasurable Self-Harm” and “Bleeding Syndrome” were not much of an issue, just minor superficial wounds.
While Dog Brother took action, the others were not idle either…
“Soul Lock Warden” quickly tied a new loop in his broken fishing line, preparing to continue using it…
“Wandering Speedy Lad” took out a silver-white coin with electricity sparking on its surface, occasionally emitting a crackling arc.
“Everyone’s truly showing off their divine skills…”
Colin silently smacked his lips, thinking their methods weren’t bad.
He couldn’t help but wonder if, for some reason, these three decided to team up against him, whether he could handle it…
On reflection, it seemed a bit troublesome, but not overly so.
The Warden’s straw rope didn’t mean much to him, as it was countered by his inherent ability “Deadly Insight” from “Beast Transformation Syndrome” to the point it wouldn’t even recognize its own mother, perhaps even a late-stage phase one wouldn’t necessarily be caught…
The attack range of “Wandering Speedy Lad’s” coin wasn’t far, and its power didn’t seem to be too great either.
As for Dog Brother, probably the most formidable, as a “Summoner,” once he was approached closely, his life would likely be in grave danger…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 133 - 133 133 The Strange Phenomenon Unaffected by
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 133: Chapter 133 The Strange Phenomenon Unaffected by Time Stop_1 Chapter 133: Chapter 133 The Strange Phenomenon Unaffected by Time Stop_1 Of course, when separated, their strength wasn’t considered too strong.
But combine them, and they could reveal an effect much greater than the sum of their parts, which made dealing with them a little troublesome…
Moreover, Colin knew that besides these overt abilities, these people had other methods at their disposal.
If something really did happen later, whether Yukionna’s mother used the power of the “script” to arrange a defection or some other cause led to an internal conflict, they’d need to be careful…
While thinking, Colin prepared to take action.
He secretly held a golden card in his left hand, and with his right hand, he dragged out a blackened bone spur full of dark cracks from the storage room.
The other few, who seemed to be giving their all but still holding back, occasionally glanced towards Colin. Upon seeing the bone spur, they suddenly felt an indescribable discomfort, as if they had been suddenly submerged in water, making it hard to breathe.
“Absolutely must not be stabbed by this thing.”
The same thought emerged in the minds of all three simultaneously.
Just one look induced such discomfort; actually getting stabbed would likely lead to unimaginable consequences.
However, this sensation was like an illusion, fleeting; the blackened bone spur on second glance seemed to become ordinary again…
[An ominous atmosphere is enveloping this place, you estimate that it might not take long for the one on the second floor to undergo some kind of transformation. Her humanity is unstable and will quickly fade, revealing her original form from before containment.]
[Once this situation arises, the “crimson” gaze will return, and the matter will come to an end.]
Text from the “Narrator” appeared before everyone’s eyes simultaneously.
Seeing those words “crimson”, Colin’s eyelid twitched, knowing he couldn’t delay any longer.
That thing was too buggy…
If it really appeared again, they’d have to release “Loafing Immortal” whether they wanted to or not.
“Let’s take the initiative and go in.”
Colin glanced at the second-floor window; if the monster decided to counter-attack after being struck, it would surely jump out to attack them.
Yet, so far, there was no reaction…
If the other side wouldn’t take the initiative, they would have to do so themselves.
“Why not go straight up from the window?” Brother Xu asked Colin.
However, before Colin could speak, Dog Brother interrupted him, “No, all the houses here have some very weird stuff; don’t know what it is, but it’s best to go up normally. Plus, if the window were an option, Loafing Immortal would have taken the chance to jump out long ago, sss—”
As he was talking, his expression suddenly contorted as if he were under attack.
Clearly, another four-armed shadow had been smashed…
“Might be some kind of curse or something, come on, let’s not drag this out…”
After Colin finished speaking, he took the lead and rushed towards the front door. When he arrived in front of the firmly shut door, he lifted his foot and kicked forcefully. With a bang, the door was kicked halfway open.
[The deep brown door simply couldn’t withstand such force; just one kick opened it halfway. Perhaps with one more, it could be opened fully?]
Colin paused for a moment, then followed the operational prompt and delivered another kick, fully opening the door.
Immediately, a strong smell of blood hit them.
Everyone saw that in the hall behind the door, the walls, ceiling, and floor were all covered with splatters of blood…
Large intestines, internal organs, flesh, shattered bones, and other common materials were blown all over the place.
“All the tissues have burst from individual bodies, the smell here is like a human’s, yet not quite. They’re probably dead…”
Colin sniffed and quickly confirmed this through the scent of the blood.
Then, without much thought, he stepped forward, his feet squishing on the thick blood puddles as he quickly made his way towards the staircase.
He had seen even more bizarre scenes several times before, the downfall of those unfortunate heroes had been even worse than this, so Colin wasn’t about to stop in his tracks over something like this…
The few people behind him couldn’t help but gasp when they saw this scene, feeling a tingling sensation on their scalps.
It wasn’t that they had never seen a dead person, but they had never witnessed such a stimulating scene…
However, seeing Colin take action, they didn’t delay any longer and quickly charged forward.
Not long after, when they reached the third floor, a figure emitting a red glow lunged towards them.
This monster had clearly undergone even more mutations, with two sections of its chest splitting open like mouths from which two crimson tentacles bristling with backwards-facing spines stretched out. One of these blood-red appendages grappled with a hanging rope, while the other thrashed wildly at shadows in the air…
Each hair on its head writhed intensely, like earthworms.
At this moment, except for its two long legs, its upper body barely had any resemblance to a human…
“Boom!”
Brother Xu flicked a silver coin with his thumb, a white bolt of lightning as thick as two fingers flashed by, accompanied by a thunderous noise, striking the monster and freezing it mid-motion.
After the strike, Brother Xu didn’t stop, repeatedly using coins until his hair stood up like an exploding head and his face showed weakness from complete spiritual exhaustion.
However, after the noise dissipated…
“Damn, I couldn’t even break through its defense?!” Brother Xu was stunned, his eyes wide open.
Around the monster, a crimson light shielded it, blocking all the lightning…
“You fucking killed one of my four-armed citizens…” Dog Brother couldn’t help but curse, feeling a numbness all over his body.
It was then that the monster, transformed from “Sister,” enraged by the attack, let out a fierce scream, scattering the persistent four-armed shadows around it, and then lunged at Colin and the others.
“Time, halt!”
Seeing it approaching within a certain range, Colin almost didn’t think before activating the Golden Card, planning to finish it off with a combination of techniques in one go.
In the roar of an invisible engine, the world before his eyes seemed to be dragged into a stance of stillness.
Looking at the monster less than five meters straight ahead of him, Colin picked up the bone spur in his hand, intending to give it a jab…
But as he raised his hand, he couldn’t help but narrow his eyes, pausing his movement.
He saw, within the forbidden scene in front of him, the red glow on the monster’s body seemed to undulate incessantly like the walls of a stomach, unaffected by anything…
Since “Time Stasis” had come into his possession for such a long time, this was the first time Colin had seen such an anomaly.
“Even ‘Time Stop’ can’t hold it? What the hell is this ‘crimson’ thing?”
Colin was internally shocked, unsure of whether to proceed with his planned attack.
However, after less than a second’s hesitation, he clenched his teeth and took two steps forward, at a distance of three meters from the monster, he forcefully threw the bone spur at its head…
Luckily, the red glow seemed not to hinder the bone spur.
Following a whoosh of slicing air, the sharp bone spur pierced directly into the head of the monster…
At the same time, the time stop ended.
The next moment, a shrill scream erupted in the corridor of the third floor.
.
.
.
Post first, then revise

chapters.title: Chapter 134 - 134 134 A Little Shock from Colin_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 134: Chapter 134 A Little Shock from Colin_1 Chapter 134: Chapter 134 A Little Shock from Colin_1 “Ah!!”
The monster’s body jolted, suddenly clutching its head and rolling on the ground, thrashing about and emitting a piercing scream.
“Ahhhhh!!!”
With each scream, its body kept swelling with fluid, resembling a swollen corpse that had bloated with river water at Giant’s Lookout, as streaks of foul and filthy black water oozed from its skin…
And the red light that covered it also faded more and more with the continuous infusion of the filthy black water.
The onlookers felt their hearts pound with alarm…
What on Earth had just happened?
All they remembered was the scene suddenly “freezing,” and by the time they came to their senses, they saw Colin “teleport,” with the Bone Spur already piercing the enemy in his hand. Then, in just a few seconds, everything seemed to be resolved…
The “freeze” they could guess was definitely the Golden Artifact in Colin’s hand, the legendary “Time Stasis.”
And that ghastly, terrifying Bone Spur filled with black cracks…
They knew almost nothing about it; they knew it was powerful, but it was only after a round of fighting that they realized, where was it just powerful?
It was freakishly stronger than they had expected!
Dammit, the monster that hadn’t even been scratched by their combined assault was brought down with just one stab—
Could it be another orange-grade equipment?
Unfortunately, Colin hadn’t disclosed, they couldn’t even begin to fathom the abilities of this artifact, let alone its name.
However, one thing was certain; Colin’s silhouette from the front had become more enigmatic in their eyes.
“That was close…”
Colin breathed a sigh of relief when he saw the red light completely disappear, and the creature on the ground ceased to move.
The red light, which was unaffected by “Time Stop,” had maxed out his stress just a moment ago.
Fortunately, aside from being immune to Time Stop, no other mishaps occurred, and he saw no bloody handprints appear out of nowhere…
‘The sense of oppression this thing brings feels so familiar, yet I can’t quite place it.’
Colin had a vague sense of familiarity with it.
But he didn’t dwell on it too much, as a message appeared before Colin.
[Event Seven: Hand over one “Passionate Paradise” containment failure specimen.]
[Would you like to hand over the corpse in front of you?]
[Note: After completing this task, you will receive a related artifact after a certain period of time.]
[Warning: The creature has not died completely and will revive in a completely uncontrollable manner after some time.]
A containment failure specimen, this one, huh, this warning is quite intriguing…
Colin looked at the creature before him. After its “death,” it finally stopped swelling and became limp like a dead squid on shore, with filthy black water still flowing from its corpse.
That a thing like this could still potentially revive…
One could only say that the creatures contained in “Passionate Paradise” were indeed strange.
However, speaking of which, “Bonfire Company” still owed him a “Humility Virtue Knight” artifact.
“If things go smoothly and I manage to return, they should be able to issue it, right?”
Colin pursed his lips and, without giving it much thought, he agreed to the task’s requirement…
A familiar transparent vortex appeared before everyone’s eyes, sweeping away the mushy corpse on the ground like a puddle of sludge.
“Is this… a mission?” Dog Brother asked Colin uncertainly.
“Yeah, a mission to hand over a corpse, don’t you guys have it?”
Colin asked curiously without concealing anything.
After speaking, he saw the three shake their heads and realized it seemed only he himself had emerged…
“Uh, isn’t this a bit too much favoritism?”
Colin murmured in his heart, guessing it might be Miss Bunny’s fault.
In a certain sense, after all, it was a task they had completed together; it wasn’t quite right for him alone to reap the benefits.
