However, there wasn’t much dissatisfaction on the faces of the other three, but rather a bit of self-doubt.
In general, when such a task appears, it should involve everyone…
Then, according to the internal review within Bonfire Company, which was unknown to others, everyone would receive a portion of the rewards.
The fact that only Colin received a reward meant only one thing…
During their recent action, according to the internal evaluation, the combined contribution of the three probably didn’t even reach ten percent of the whole…
Only under such circumstances would there be a situation where Colin was “eating alone.”
“I can’t believe all our hard work amounted to less than ten percent…,” Dog Brother sighed, from which he sensed how big the gap between him and Brother Shunzi really was.
Indeed, if Brother Shunzi were willing, all of their group combined probably wouldn’t stand a chance against him alone.
Even though they were all employees recently promoted to F Level, why was the gap so huge?
“It’s okay, after completing this task, we all have a bright future ahead.”
Colin clearly knew how to comfort people. He waved his hand, brushed past the subject, and with a few steps forward, he picked up the Bone Spur from the ground.
No one dared to harbor any crooked thoughts of snatching it…
After all, no one wanted to experience the “stutter” in the scene and be the next one impaled by it.
Afterward, watching the still standing shadows in the corridor, Colin turned around and reminded Dog Brother to withdraw his “Divine Skills.”
“Whew, almost forgot…”
Dog Brother took a deep breath, closed his eyes, and pulled out the dagger embedded in the palm of his left hand.
Blood immediately gushed from the wound…
But he was prepared, took out a jar, pressed it against the wound, and a milky liquid sizzled out, injected into the cut, and quickly solidified, filling up the gash on his hand…
Then, he took out a sterile bandage and began to dress the wound.
During this process, Colin saw those four-armed shadows kneeling on the ground, as if praising something—
“Praise the all-knowing, almighty Four-Armed God Emperor…”
As the words ended, those four-armed shadows vanished like dissolving blood.
“Another name of some monster or demon,”
Colin shook his head, not thinking much of it, and walked directly towards the room with a hole smashed in it, scanning inside to see the Loafing Immortal cowering and shivering in the corner.
Even though the situation had been resolved, he still made no move, as if his young mind had suffered a great trauma.
“Did he suffer some kind of spiritual attack?”
Being the most experienced employee of Bonfire Company present, Dog Brother, seen it all, immediately recognized his condition.
“It seems so.”
Colin nodded, putting the Bone Spur away in the Storage Room with his right hand, and then pulled out a monocle from his pocket. Holding it by the edges, he brought it to the socket of his left eye—
[A company employee who has been hit by some type of fear-induced psychic attack. Fortunately, his injuries are not severe, and he should be able to gradually self-recover to normal in about ten minutes.]

chapters.title: Chapter 135 - 135 135 Entering Rain City._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 135: Chapter 135 Entering “Rain City”._1 Chapter 135: Chapter 135 Entering “Rain City”._1 “It seems children really aren’t suited for driving big vehicles, just look how scared the kid is…”
Colin muttered to himself while putting away the monocle, no longer using it to look around aimlessly.
His experience in The Kingdom of Knights had taught him…
Never to look around without a cause; you might just see something you shouldn’t and drop dead.
“There’s nothing particularly problematic; he’ll recover in about fifteen minutes.”
After updating on Loafing Immortal’s basic status, Colin surveyed the room—a space of roughly thirty square meters scattered with yellow paper, and also featuring a long sword broken in one part.
Unsurprisingly, these must be the “Loafing Immortal’s” props…
It made him feel as if he was truly like a Taoist priest.
Without dwelling on it further, familiar “subtitles” once again appeared before everyone.
[In less than an hour, night will fall, and due to certain reasons, light rain will begin outside the villa. You must enter the area covered by the rain before the sun disappears. In addition, on the third floor of the little villa, in one of the rooms, you will find some raincoats.]
[These raincoats are quite special, giving a very particular feeling, as if they were a sort of special raincoat.]
[Under the protection of the raincoats, not a drop of rainwater touched you, and as you walked into it, you encountered some attacks. After wandering for a long while, you luckily came across a survivor inside…]
The “Narrator” stopped after the third line, suggesting there was more to come.
“Damn, what’s with this pointless verbosity in the second part? But keep going, what happened after meeting the survivors?”
Colin blinked, staring at the “Narrator” in front of him, knowing that this was the Script Book assisting them.
Unfortunately, the arranged content was short and didn’t provide much information.
As Colin and the others contemplated whether the next part of the story would appear, their eyelids twitched as they saw a line of crimson “Narrator” subtitles emerge before their eyes.
[Do not trust any information on the “Narrator” when it gets dark, and be cautious of its means of assimilating you through the “script.” Try to avoid acting according to its written content through reasonable methods.]
The bloody subtitles nearly filled the entire field of vision, signaling the gravity of the situation.
[Finally, we wish you luck.]
When these brief characters appeared, Colin and the others suddenly felt an inexplicable sensation—the “Narrator” had vanished.
No, it was the still reasonable “Narrator” that had disappeared…
“Should our next move be based on the information just provided?” Dog Brother asked, looking at Colin, who was deep in thought.
“Yeah, let’s follow the instructions above for now.”
Colin nodded, feeling that the information provided was probably fine.
As for the so-called “assimilating arrangements,” they must be scripted events he was supposed to trigger…
As long as they could be avoided, the problem wouldn’t be too significant.
Glancing at the Loafing Immortal still huddled in the corner hugging his knees, Colin took out a ring—the “Servant of Money.”
Reaching into his pocket, he initially intended to pay himself, but after a thought, Colin asked the others, “Who has money on them?”
“I do… ”
“Give me a hundred bucks.”
Colin took a large red banknote from Brother Xu, stretched out his hand, and summoned a “Money Slave.”
“Six of bamboo? The quality isn’t great, too bad I didn’t draw the red dragon, but it’s not a big problem…”
Colin gestured towards a wardrobe in the room, instructing the Money Slave to open it. Inside were indeed several orange-yellow raincoats.
These raincoats…
It looked no different from the usual raincoats.
But for some reason, Colin and the others felt it was very special; they couldn’t quite put their finger on what was special about it—it was just special.
“Damn, it feels like some kind of cognitive disturbance…” Dog Brother cursed as he took the raincoat.
Colin guessed that it must have been endowed with the special powers of a “Script Book,” which, in a sense, could be considered a “plot device.”
Without giving it much thought, he stored the item carefully and then said,
“Rest up for a while. We have less than half an hour. When it gets dark and starts raining, we move.”
He set a timer on his phone, found a spot to sit, and silently waited.
Time ticked by, second by second, and after more than ten minutes, Loafing Immortal finally returned to normal, and the task involving him was at last complete…
After a brief explanation of the current situation, everyone in the bedroom grew quiet again, silently making their preparations.
Colin’s phone buzzed with a vibration after what seemed like an age—
Time was up.
Just at that moment, a wailing wind sound came from outside the window, as a gale began to blow in.
Inside the house, affected by the hurricane, there was a sound like the wailing of a banshee, something usually only experienced by residents of high-rise buildings.
Colin and the others turned to look in the direction of the sky and saw a daunting mass of dark clouds rushing towards them.
However, this oppressive cloud stopped inexplicably when it got about a hundred meters away from them.
Where the dark cloud covered, rain poured down like a torrent, and mist filled the air…
Outside the dark clouds, everything else seemed normal…
In one scene, there were two dramatically different bizarre weathers, leaving Colin and the others amazed.
“Yin and Yang rain…” Dog Brother couldn’t help but utter.
By then, each of them had donned an orange raincoat and put on their rain hats…
“Let’s go.”
Colin glanced at the sinking sun at the edge of the sky and took the lead out of the room, charging towards the rainy area.
The others, who had gradually come to approve of him, followed closely behind without much hesitation.
Soon, as everyone entered into the curtain of rain, at the edge where the sun was setting, it seemed as if everything was about to plunge into darkness as they knew it…
However, just then, Colin had a sudden and intense sense of crisis well up inside him, and an image flashed through his mind—
He turned his head towards a certain place, engulfed by crimson light…
And then, his body uncontrollably collapsed into a writhing tumorous mass.
“Close your eyes—don’t look!”
Colin shouted in alarm and was the first to turn his head and close his eyes, and the others did the same.
Meanwhile…
The city’s skies, which were thought to be slipping into night, suddenly tore open with a fissure. Starting from an unknown location, it spanned across the entire sky, as if it had ripped through the world of “Script City.”
It seemed not to have appeared out of nowhere but had always been there, only revealing itself as the “sun” set.
Countless beams of crimson radiance spilled from the great tear, covering most of the area of Passionate Paradise, except for a few areas that seemed to be spared due to the presence of actual objects…
Then, behind the rift showering countless crimson lights, a massive celestial body emitting a dark red, cold, oppressive light silently appeared…
It hung behind the gap, as if silently peering into the special world beneath the fissure.

chapters.title: Chapter 136 - 136 136 Colin Falls_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 136: Chapter 136 Colin Falls_1 Chapter 136: Chapter 136 Colin Falls_1 At this moment, except for a few areas, the entire “Passionate Paradise” had been enveloped by crimson light.
Among these few areas was the Rain Curtain World, covered by dense dark clouds…
However, as the gaze of that dark red and cold celestial body swept across, crimson light also squeezed into the world beneath the dark clouds.
But once the red light penetrated, it did not last long before being blocked out by the suddenly intense water mist and the eerily writhing black clouds.
Colin, with his head down and eyes closed, felt a heaviness in his body as a line of sight that seemed almost tangible grazed his scalp, causing his brain to bubble and froth like a cola with its cap popped off.
His thoughts were constantly shattered by the dense mass of bubbles, incapable of gathering…
Not only that, but with his fragmented consciousness, he could distinctly sense the emergence of thoughts within him that were not his own.
These thoughts were like a series of new personalities, beginning to tug-of-war with him for control…
“Brother Shunzi, this…”
Dog Brother and the others, standing beside Colin, saw him with his head down, fists clenched, body trembling, and felt a bit at a loss for a moment.
They all had just felt an indescribable terror pass over their heads.
It was only the tiniest, indirect contact, yet they couldn’t help but feel fear beyond any they had known before, realizing their own insignificance compared to it.
Just like a speck of dust in relation to the solar system.
Fortunately, that thing seemed not to have noticed them, probably because they were too weak, and so it didn’t pay them any attention.
“Standing here won’t solve anything, my intuition tells me it’s dangerous to stay here…”
Dog Brother, with a flashlight in hand, looked around. The stores and houses on both sides of the road were tightly shut, pitch dark, as if no one had lived there for a very long time, which was chilling.
In the drizzling rain, the air was chilly and the humidity extremely high, making all the buildings look very old, as if they had been soaked in water for over a decade, many of them showing signs of heavy rust.
And the mist raised by the falling rain made visibility much worse, with seeing a distance of forty to fifty meters already being the limit.
But what made their hearts race the most was the inexplicable crying they kept hearing since entering, which at first had been far away, but after a while, had gotten increasingly closer…
Not just Dog Brother, but “Loafing Immortal,” “Soul Lock Warden,” “Wandering Speedy Lad,” and others all knew clearly that standing here would surely lead to trouble!
“But as for him, what should we do…”
“Loafing Immortal” glanced at the still motionless Colin and the six raincoat-less “Money Slaves” standing by Colin’s side.
The problem was, with the lead brother inactive, they didn’t know what to do next.
There was silence for about fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen seconds.
Dog Brother broke the silence, “Brother Shunzi just saved us, if it weren’t for his warning, we would probably be the ones standing frozen in place right now, so we can’t give up on him…”
Everyone nodded.
“Then, let’s start with that investigation mission…”
Dog Brother raised his hand to straighten the strands of hair falling over his forehead, then spoke.
In the group, his prestige was second only to Colin, after all, he had the most experience and the initial purchase of information with direct payment had earned him some goodwill—
The only embarrassing part was, what they had assumed to be a greasy, overweight home-dweller had turned into a rather pretty “girl” upon entering.After a pause, Dog Brother continued to add, “And find someone to carry Brother Shunzi…”
“What about that Money Slave, if we get close, it seems to become alert. If we approach Brother Shunzi, we might get attacked…”
“Kill it.”
Dog Brother didn’t hesitate too much, they couldn’t control the Money Slave, so they could only decide to kill it first, then take off the ring of that Money Slave, “Then see who tries to summon another one using the method demonstrated earlier, and let it wear Shunzi.”
“If I’m not mistaken, this accessory shouldn’t have any other side effects or the side effects are not severe.”
Right now, the ownership of the accessory is still with Colin, they can’t see the information even if they get their hands on it, and they don’t know how to use the thing…
But Colin had demonstrated how to use it in front of them before, he remembered it only cost a hundred dollars.
Upon hearing this, the group glanced at each other and nodded their heads—they agreed this was the only method left.
Currently, there are generally three ways to obtain ownership of a Bonfire Company accessory.
First, Colin grants them the item through a gift, trade, or verbally granting permission to use it, else they can’t see the detailed information and they can only grope their way through using it, which could lead to negative effects that could be fatal.
Second, if they have the item in hand for more than a month, they will automatically acquire certain permissions.
Third, they could just kill Colin, making his equipment “explode” on site; everything would become ownerless items, and if not reclaimed, they would be theirs for the taking.
However, if they choose the third option, it would mean the “bundling” situation would instantly collapse, which would not be conducive to the subsequent exploration.
With this in mind, the Warden took out a fishing rod, ready to start fishing for a Money Slave…
But at that moment, the Money Slave wearing six head covers seemed to realize something and turned its head around.
The Warden felt an inexplicable chill on his neck under the gaze from behind the head cover and showed an apologetic smile on his face, picking up the fishing rod, “Sorry buddy, I really have no choice…”
The line at the end of the fishing rod sank into the shadow on the ground, and then above the Money Slave’s head, an unnoticeable shadow appeared.
Within the shadow, a loop trap fell slowly, coming to rest on the Money Slave’s neck…
During this process, the Money Slave seemed to have no resistance at all.
Seeing this, the Warden breathed a sigh of relief, gripped the fishing rod tightly, and with a strong upward tug.
A snapping sound came from the necks of the six Money Slaves; immediately after, the expressions of everyone present changed slightly as they saw the bodies of the six Money Slaves were not lifted, but their heads along with their spines were pulled up by the fishing line, dragging out a bloody spine.
It was like a balloon…
Pop.
The headless bodies collapsed and disintegrated.
“This…”
The Warden was stunned—
The sensation was odd, he didn’t use much force, so why were the heads so easily lifted?
It was as if the heads were not attached to the bodies in the first place.
“Were Money Slaves always like this?” he couldn’t help but ask, but unfortunately, the only one who could answer this question was still standing in place, motionless, with no indication of when he might return to normal.
Meanwhile, the heads hanging in mid-air suddenly emitted a whimpering cry.
Then…
Just like its body, it disintegrated and disappeared like a sandcastle struck by water.
It was at this time that a sudden change occurred.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 137 - 137 137 The Weirdness in the Heavy Rain_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 137: Chapter 137: The Weirdness in the Heavy Rain_1 Chapter 137: Chapter 137: The Weirdness in the Heavy Rain_1 On the streets shrouded in a thin mist, the sound of crying had already emerged nearby, at some unknown time.
It loomed all around…
Sometimes distant, sometimes close, sending chills down one’s spine.
It was at this moment that Dog Brother suddenly thought of something, recalling the last cries of Money Slave before his death…
Those cries, they were very similar to the sounds in the curtain of rain!
“Damn it! That Money Slave must have been contaminated by ‘Rainwater’!”
Listening to the cries, Dog Brother immediately thought of this.
After all, the reason Money Slave wasn’t wearing a raincoat was because Brother Shunzi planned to test what would happen if one got rained on after entering…
The experiment obviously couldn’t be done on a normal person, so the task naturally fell to Money Slave.
That one just now was likely the result of getting rained on.
“There’s no time to take off the ring, whoever can, take Brother Shunzi on your back, we need to find a safe place without rain to hide for a bit, something is coming,” said Dog Brother as he pulled out a pitch-black dagger from his pocket and began moving in a random direction.
The company hadn’t told them where to go after they entered, only assigning them an investigative task.
So they had no choice but to find a way to complete the task on their own.
“I got it!”
Having said that, Loafing Immortal pulled out a yellow talisman from his pocket, on which were written two characters in special strokes—
Great strength.
He wrapped the talisman around his wrist and instantly felt a surge of power emanating from the talisman paper, flowing into all his limbs and invigorating his entire body.
Without further thought, he hoisted the standing Colin onto his shoulder.
But as they were preparing to move, they suddenly saw a figure in a black raincoat appear from the end of the street up ahead.
Dog Brother planted the dagger in his left hand, scanning the creature with a glance—
“It’s not human, avoid it!”
With that, he chose another direction, and the rest quickly followed.
The team formed a triangle, with Loafing Immortal carrying Colin in the middle, Dog Brother leading, and on the left and right sides, one fisherman and one beep beep…
The figure in the black raincoat moved slowly, just walking at a steady pace.
It wasn’t long before they were left far behind by the group.
And the bizarre crying sound also slowly faded from their ears.
Seeing this, everyone breathed a sigh of relief to some extent.
“Where’s a safe place?” Loafing Immortal adjusted Colin’s position on his body and then asked.
“Not sure, let’s look around.”
Dog Brother took a deep breath, activating the power of the dagger and affixing it to his eyes to look around.
Although it seemed they had temporarily escaped the humanoid monster, the fog around them had become denser without them noticing when it started.
Their visible world was limited to where their flashlights reached; beyond that, it was pitch black, and they could see nothing at all.
Even using the special dagger, his vision was extremely limited.
“In the buildings nearby, there’s at least one monster in each, and the feeling of their strength doesn’t seem weaker than the one we encountered in Loafing Immortal’s home. They must all be out-of-control individuals from ‘Passionate Paradise’.”
Dog Brother spoke as he walked, glancing back at Colin, then a hint of disappointment flashed as he turned his gaze away.
He couldn’t figure out why, but Colin still hadn’t woken up…
If Colin were to wake up, they could simply choose any house, burst in, and seize it for shelter.
But with Colin still unconscious, they could only leave it to fate.
The only consolation now was that these raincoats, enchanted by the ‘Script Book,’ were indeed special; so far, they hadn’t been touched by a single drop of rain.
Furthermore, after entering, the progress of their investigation task kept increasing—whether they moved, breathed, or looked around, it all added to the progress…
With a bit of luck, they should be able to complete it within a day or two if they found a safe place.
However, before the group could find a place, the eerie cries suddenly resurfaced in front of them a few minutes later.
[At a corner, it appears once again before you.]
As this message appeared, everyone’s eyelids twitched and they saw a familiar figure in a black raincoat walking out from the corner of the street ahead.
Although there was only one person, the cries from all around made them feel as if they were surrounded.
“Here we go again!”
Dog Brother’s breath hitched, with no intention whatsoever of confronting the situation head-on. He looked around, preparing to dash to the left.
But before he could make a decision, he suddenly saw the “Narrator” appear again.
[After careful consideration, you decided to head towards the left path because it seemed the least dangerous, and there might even be a chance to find a safe place and encounter other survivors. So, you did just that and successfully found a safe zone, and then…]
“To the right!”
Remembering the afternoon’s hint, Dog Brother didn’t wait for the “Narrator” to continue their chatter and led the group to break through to the right—
Anyway, they couldn’t follow the “Narrator’s” script.
As they moved, Dog Brother summoned several Four-Armed Citizens to guard everyone, ready to deal with any sudden accidents.
The Four-Armed Citizens could exist in a non-corporeal form, so they didn’t have to worry about getting wet in the rain.
Soon, the eerie howling was left behind them again…
Yet, within ten minutes, before they had a chance to catch their breath, lines of text appeared on their retinas once more.
[In the curtain of rain, trying to escape clearly wasn’t realistic; soon, you heard the crying sound close to your ear, and then you saw, on the street not far away, that figure appeared again, encountering you unexpectedly.]
Right as this description appeared, they once more heard the sound of crying close by.
The figure in the black raincoat appeared again…
“Stall if we can, just until Brother Shunzi wakes up—everything will be better then.”
Continuing their escape, Dog Brother led the group on, but after a short while and not having gone very far, they saw another figure slowly emerge from around the corner up ahead in the flashlight’s beam.
Dog Brother felt his scalp tingle and came to a stop, lifting his flashlight to shine it behind them, where two figures in raincoats approached.
Pincered from front and back!
The sinister figures silently continued their approach, imposing a heavy sense of oppression on the group.
“What do we do?”
“Get ready, we’ll find a direction to break through in a moment, but wait—wait for that ‘Narrator’ to speak first…”
Dog Brother looked serious; he was beginning to figure out how to deal with the “Narrator.”
This thing could only set up one scenario for them in a short period, and each time it would only arrange one or two, at most three, key points. They just had to do the opposite…
[After some thought, you decided to break through in the direction of four o’clock from where you stand now, as it seemed the easiest. After getting close to those monsters, you’d attack first…]
“Break through in the direction of twelve o’clock…”
Dog Brother glanced that way and saw a total of three silent figures walking on the street, two more than elsewhere.
However, it shouldn’t be too much of a problem.
Having said that, Dog Brother grabbed his dagger with his right hand and twisted it with force, feeling a burst of extreme pleasure exploding from his hand.
He couldn’t help but let out an enticing moan.
Following that, his body became semi-transparent, as if shrouded by a black veil.
“Let’s go! Get close, then attack.”
No sooner had he spoken, than he dashed out towards them.
As the distance closed to less than ten meters, Dog Brother was ready to command the Four-Armed Citizens to strike and tear apart the figures on the road ahead…
But all of a sudden, watching the figures walking with bowed heads, oblivious to their approach, he had an epiphany—
They had been misled by the “Narrator”; it seemed these creatures hadn’t actually noticed them!
“Don’t attack!”
Dog Brother urgently spoke out, but it was already too late; the sound of crashing thunder rang out beside him.
A bolt of lightning tore through the dense curtain of rain, striking a humanoid entity clad in a black raincoat.
In an instant, all the figures, who had been moving with bowed heads through the rain, looked up and turned their gazes toward them.
“Trouble…”
As everyone looked on, they felt their scalps tingle and their hearts sink to the abyss.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 138 - 138 138 Explode Equipment_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 138: Chapter 138 “Explode Equipment”_1 Chapter 138: Chapter 138 “Explode Equipment”_1 After being struck by a bolt of lightning, these people in uniform black raincoats seemed to finally notice something. They all lifted their heads to look towards the source of the lightning.
Dog Brother and his companions trying to break out could now see them clearly. Underneath the black raincoats were faces that were withered, with pitch-black sockets for eyes, looking altogether like walking mummies.
Dog Brother and the others held their breath, their pupils contracting sharply, and it was only upon a closer look that they noticed…
These strange mummy-like beings weren’t actually wearing any black raincoats. Instead, their bodies were covered with a layer of black, moss-like substance over their upper half, making them look as if they were wearing raincoats.
It was also at this moment that they suddenly heard a crackling sound from the necks of these humanoid mummies.
Immediately following, their heads detached from their necks like balloons, dragging a long spine behind, their mouths full of sharp teeth, flying towards them…
“Watch out!”
A four-armed shadow beside Dog Brother leapt out from the darkness, its sharp claws slashing, cleanly bisecting the head in mid-air.
Just as they dealt with one, another one charged at them at an extremely fast speed, but fortunately, a bolt of lightning that was even faster than it sliced through the rain curtain, striking it directly and turning it into ash.
“Lightning seems to have a restraining effect on it!”
Brother Xu was stunned. He hadn’t expected his strike to have such an excellent effect, obliterating it to dust in one blow.
After their heads were smashed, their bodies also seemed to be affected, collapsing on the ground like they had lost all strength, motionless.
It looked as if they were dead…
“Don’t just stand there, keep up.”
Dog Brother yelled, then took the lead and charged forward.
These monsters had a very strange method of attack, but their strategy was extremely simple: They just flew towards someone to bite them upon sight, which was easy to handle.
“So weak… If I knew they were this easy to deal with, I would have started killing them straight away.”
Dog Brother commanded the creatures he had summoned to kill the third monster, which looked like it too was wearing a black raincoat, blocking their way.
Originally, he had thought these beings would be terribly frightening, but upon confronting them, they seemed to fall with a single strike, just like perishable goods.
As his thoughts fluctuated, he glanced at Colin from the corner of his eye and saw that the latter still hadn’t woken up…
Even with the power of the dagger, he couldn’t see through the situation inside Colin’s body. All he could see was his body at this moment shrouded in a gray haze, like something being continuously nurtured within a writhing silkworm cocoon.
“Although I don’t understand the situation, if everything goes well, it shouldn’t take long for a result to emerge. I’m just afraid that the person who wakes up may not be the same person as before, but it’s pointless to think about that now…”
With these thoughts, Dog Brother withdrew his attention.
He quickly scanned his surroundings, seeking a suitable place to regroup before the next “Narrator” appeared to cause more trouble.
At that moment, he tensed up and suddenly saw another head flying out from the mist.
“I’ve got this!”
“Soul Lock Warden” spoke up. In his hands, he no longer held a fishing rod but a metal baseball bat. This was also a special item from Bonfire Company, although it was of a lower grade, just a plain white-rated item, not even a green gear.
However, seeing Dog Brother’s creature cleave a head with each strike, and Brother Xu electrocute a monster with each bolt, he figured the monsters should be simple to handle.
He figured he could handle it too…
Right when the head came flying at him, he took a brisk step forward, swung the baseball bat with force from his upper body, and with a loud bang, struck the flying head attached to a long spine.
The eerie head paused in mid-air, repelled backward a distance, its forehead dented.
Yet, after a brief pause in mid-air, as if dazed for a moment, it then ferociously dived towards the Warden’s neck again…
“Why didn’t it break!”
The Warden was shocked, this was not at all what he had expected: one swing of the baseball bat and the head exploding into pieces mid-air.
At the moment, his body was still maintaining the posture of swinging out with the baseball bat, the old strength had gone, and the new strength had yet to come.
At the critical moment, a fist wrapped with a talisman of great strength fiercely smashed into the flying head, sending it flying away.
“That was close…” the Warden sighed in relief, covered in a cold sweat.
Only now did he remember that Dog Brother’s artifact must be Purple Gear, and Brother Xu’s was also Green Gear, and it just happened to have restraint effects; otherwise, it wouldn’t have been so effective…
“Ah, without appropriate close-combat artifacts, it’s really tough…”
Internally sighing, the Warden saw that he was somewhat falling behind the group and immediately quickened his steps to catch up.
In this damned place, being left alone was undoubtedly a dire fate.
Just as they had partially broken free from the encirclement, Dog Brother thought they could relax a little, but unexpectedly, after their first clash, heads kept flying out from the thick fog on all sides…
And the frequency and number of heads kept increasing.
It was clear that they had disturbed the horde of brains!
An occasional intervention from the “Narrator” would immediately result in a dozen heads appearing at once, making them hard to deal with.
“‘Narrator’, this damned thing! If it weren’t for its lure, I might have been able to detect the problem earlier and know that it’s safe as long as we don’t attack.”
Dog Brother couldn’t help but curse.
But it was too late for anything now, and under the dense attacks, they couldn’t help but make mistakes. The fisherman, caught off-guard, had his right hand bitten off in an instant, and he would probably never be able to fish again.
These monsters were indeed fragile, but their attacks were powerful.
A human body, even after three gene injection treatments, was like soft tofu in front of them.
Fortunately, they had already taken the gold ring off Colin’s ring finger and summoned ten “Money Slaves” to carry the fisherman along.
“There’s still one ring with an eyeball, not sure what artifact it is, can’t pull it off, and didn’t see the other artifacts, they should all be in the ‘Storage Room’.”
This thought occurred to them all simultaneously.
To take out those items, the only way was to ‘Explode Equipment’.
The situation had not yet come to that point…
However, if it really came to a desperate situation with no escape, they would have to sacrifice Brother Shunzi…
After all, having a few escape was still better than being annihilated here.
“Just hold on for ten more minutes, if, it’s really not working out, we, can’t do anything else…”
Dog Brother shook his head, feeling the situation of blood loss becoming evident, a constant buzzing in his ears, cold sweats running down his body, and an abnormal flush of heat on his face —
If they delayed any longer, he would indeed bleed to death…
And now, with their abilities and artifacts, the chance of entering the building and dealing with the monsters that were originally from “Passionate Paradise” seemed slim.
The only solution had to be finding a way to ‘Explode Equipment’…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 139 - 139 139 Senior Ambassador._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 139: Chapter 139: Senior Ambassador._1 Chapter 139: Chapter 139: Senior Ambassador._1 Hearing his words, the others remained silent, knowing it was an unavoidable matter.
But at the same time, they also understood that once they started killing teammates, it would likely be impossible for the group to bond again.
The few who had been sticking together would certainly start distrusting the others after Colin’s death.
This was something that would inevitably happen once they went through with it…
Not to mention the likely bloodshed over how to distribute the benefits after “Explode Equipment”…
Especially the Golden Artifact, after getting through the crisis, they anticipated various overt and covert struggles, culminating in a bloody conflict.
After all, securing good equipment means a lower chance of “being sacrificed” next.
Dog Brother’s gaze shifted from the path ahead to the houses, already searching for one that would be easier to deal with.
But before he could look further, another piece of information suddenly appeared before them.
[After struggling to survive, you intended to find a place to forcefully settle down and recuperate, but unexpectedly, you stumbled upon a fish pond with many seemingly angling people. Your arrival startled these fishermen.]
Dog Brother’s heart chilled abruptly as his special vision saw through the mist ahead a dense mass of “brain swarms” flying towards them.
The numbers ranged from several dozen to hundreds…
“We’re done for,” he muttered.
A strong sense of powerlessness arose within everyone’s hearts.
With such numbers, there was no possibility of struggle.
Even “Explode Equipment” was out of the question; they simply didn’t have time to use it…
But just then, beams of bright light suddenly shone from one side, and they noticed a group of about a dozen people charging out, flashlights in hand.
“Survivors?” Dog Brother and the others were startled, surprised yet somehow it felt reasonable—
The “Narrator” had set up a scene for them to encounter “survivors” that afternoon.
Only now did they actually meet them.
“No time to explain, come quickly!” someone from the group shouted.
After exchanging glances, Dog Brother and his companions dashed over without much hesitation.
After all, aside from seeking help from the others, they didn’t have many options left.
Just as they started moving, a large group of heads dragging their spines flew through the air like a locust swarm crossing the curtain of rain.
However, before the brain swarm could get closer, one of the group stepped forward.
He stretched out his right hand and lifted it forward: “Everything here shall abide by a common law of reality based on the physical principles I proposed in 1687.
“This was a great discovery by humankind, the foundation of the world as we recognized it, and the absolute rule of reality. It’s commonly described as…
“‘Every object continues in its state of rest, or of uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled to change that state by forces impressed upon it.'”
He spoke quickly, reciting the words swiftly, and as his voice dropped, a sort of “conceptual reality” enveloped the area.
Thud, thud, thud…
Above the sky, all the heads plummeted from mid-air, like dumplings tossed into a pot, splashing water everywhere, unable to fly again; they could only flail about in the puddles, snapping their jaws and emitting strange growls.
Clearly, the phenomenon of these heads flying mid-air in a highly unreasonable manner wasn’t supposed to exist, wasn’t permissible, and simply wasn’t correct.
So when stripped of the mystic force, the heads naturally couldn’t fly anymore…
Because that defies the laws of physics.
Not just the heads, Dog Brother also noticed that the four-armed shadows around him had faded, he could feel they were still there, but as if they were isolated from this place, incapable of manifesting again.
“Were there ever such ruthless employees in the company before?”
Dog Brother wasn’t clear about the people who had entered “Passionate Paradise” before, assuming them to be some former employees.
But if Colin woke up, he would instantly know that the one exhibiting this power was an official, and a member of the elite “high-level agents”…
He would then realize that this must be the non-company officials Lifecoach Kawaii-many mentioned, who had forcibly entered “Passionate Paradise” by other means.
At this moment, after the individual had easily dealt with a large brain swarm, Dog Brother and the others breathed a sigh of relief and quickened their pace.
“Come this way, over here!”
A group of rescue workers, clad in raincoats, beckoned them, rushing toward a certain part of the street. At the end of the road, there was a parked armored vehicle and a modified bus filled with protective equipment.
And as they boarded, the man who used some special power also pulled back his hand.
However, those heads on the ground didn’t immediately take flight…
“Conceptual Reality” still affected the area; the effects would persist for at least ten minutes.
And ten minutes was enough time for them to escape to safety.
Rumble rumble rumble…
The vehicles started.
Feeling the powerful force beneath them, Dog Brother and the others exhaled a breath of relief—they had survived.
Dog Brother glanced at the interior of the protective bus, which, apart from six or seven armed personnel, also had some medical staff.
It was as if they had come with the intent to rescue from the very beginning.
Moreover, the most crucial point was that these people didn’t seem like they were from Bonfire Company.
“Do you have any painkillers?”
“No…”
“Then bear with it, it might hurt a bit.”
“Sure, I’m not afraid of pain, just go ahea—HOLY SHIT!!!”
On one side, as soon as the medical personnel finished speaking, they roughly began to disinfect the arm of the fisherman whose arm was broken, and screams immediately filled the bus…
At this time, a person wearing a grey raincoat approached, and Dog Brother and the others recognized him as the strong man who had used some mysterious method to subdue a large brain swarm in an instant.
Underneath his raincoat, his build was not tall, but he was sturdy, with a determined face, square-shaped, giving off the impression of a person with thick eyebrows and big eyes.
The glasses he wore added an indescribably refined look to his appearance…
“Not bad, you actually didn’t abandon your teammates.”
This man adjusted his cracked black-framed glasses and glanced at the unconscious Colin.
However, this statement made them feel slightly awkward inside…
The man with glasses didn’t know this and continued:
“If I’m not mistaken, you should be from what’s called… ‘Bonfire Company,’ right?”
Dog Brother’s pupils contracted slightly. He was unsure before, but after hearing this, he was absolutely certain that the man in front of him was not a Bonfire Company employee.
Faced with the question, he hesitated for a moment, neither denying nor affirming.
“Forget it, that’s not important. Did you use the ‘Book of Fate’ fragment when you came in?”
“No.” They all shook their heads.
“Have you died before?”
“No.” They all shook their heads again.
“That’s good…”
The man with the shattered black-framed glasses breathed a sigh of relief, “It seems like we finally have a chance to escape this time.”

chapters.title: Chapter 140 - 140 140 The Mysterious Bonfire Company. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 140: Chapter 140: The Mysterious Bonfire Company. _1 Chapter 140: Chapter 140: The Mysterious Bonfire Company. _1 “Escape? How exactly should we do it? Oh, right, I forgot to ask, what should I call you?”
Dog Brother subconsciously asked, curious about what the other person meant by escaping, given that they hadn’t seen any possibility of escape so far.
“Level 6 ‘Agent’ Gao Haiwen, former leader of an international special action group dispatched by the state…”
Fuck, he seems to be really impressive… Dog Brother and the others were startled when they heard the man introduce himself—
Even though they couldn’t understand, he still seemed really impressive.
“Wait, are you…official people?” the Warden suddenly thought of something, his gaze shifting evasively.
“In your terms, that’s correct…”
The square-faced man pushed his black-framed glasses up his nose. “As for the method of escape you asked about, we will need some assistance from you ‘Bonfire Company’ employees, but the method is special… You’ll understand once we reach the base.”
After pausing, the square-faced Gao Haiwen also asked out of curiosity, “How many years have you been with this so-called ‘Bonfire Company’?”
Dog Brother and the others fell silent for a moment before reporting a close but not entirely accurate number of years: “I’ve been around for about two years.”
“Two years, huh…” Gao Haiwen mused.
“Is there a problem?” “Loafing Immortal” asked curiously.
During the conversation, he glanced outside the bus covered in barbed wire, saw the raindrops sliding down the window, and beyond that, only the mysterious mist and the dim outlines of buildings could be seen.
In front of the bus, on the armored vehicle, the sound of gunfire transmitted intermittently, as if it were engaged in combat.
“Don’t worry, it’s still safe at this time; otherwise, we wouldn’t dare to come out.”
Gao Haiwen explained a bit but did not specify why it was safe, and instead returned to the previous topic: “The ‘Bonfire Company,’ as far as I know, should have no small number of people. I don’t know if it’s over ten thousand, but over a thousand is for sure, and from interacting with some of your other employees, I’ve learned that you’ve been active for quite some time, the furthest back being five years ago.
“Moreover, thinking about it now, many things seem to be intricately related to the ‘Bonfire Company’…
“But until I entered this secret realm, well, what you call ‘Passionate Paradise,’ I hadn’t received any information about you through any channels. You really keep yourselves well hidden…”
They’ve never seen us before?
Dog Brother and the others blinked at these words, confused, as this seemed different from their understanding—they had always thought that “Bonfire Company” had official backing and could even be connected to mainstream countries around the world.
After all, the company clearly had some “in-the-know guys” who appeared to be official personnel, but what this man was saying seemed to suggest otherwise…
“Could it be that your level is too low, so you lack sufficient information?”
Dog Brother had once participated in a team mission, assisting people with “D Level authorization,” so comparing that, he felt that the so-called “Level 6 Agent” with a bunch of titles in front of them should be at about a D Level strength, maybe even not as good as D Level personnel, falling into a stage above E Level but below D Level.
In other words, a high-level within the middle-level of the low-level employees, slightly better than them, but not by much…
What kind of secrets could such a low level know?
However, after considering, he thought such a comment might seem insensitive, so he ultimately didn’t voice it and instead suggested, “Maybe we’ve just been missing each other.”
“That’s also possible,” Gao Haiwen didn’t refute the possibility but secretly decided that if he had a chance to get out, he must report this bizarre, unknown, and dubious organization to his superiors…
“By the way, you guys must’ve come in the last few days, right? What’s the situation outside? Still normal?”
Upon hearing this, the group thought for a moment before Dog Brother spoke up, “It’s fairly normal.”
During the conversation, as he thought about various things, he added, “It should still be considered normal, at least I haven’t seen anything strange on a daily basis.”
“That’s a relief…” Gao Haiwen let out a long sigh of relief on his square face.
However, as if something had come to mind, he spoke up again, “Right, how’s the situation on the Never-Setting Sun’s land?”
“It seems pretty good… I heard something about a split with Ireland or something, they’ve gone into military readiness,” Dog Brother said, recalling recent events.
Wandering Speedy Lad laughed gleefully beside them, “What split? That’s just the state of affairs in Great Britain, isn’t it? The people of Ireland are voicing their blood and tears to fight for their rights, it’s just a beautiful sight to see.”
But unlike the others’ laughter and merriment, Gao Haiwen frowned slightly as if he had more information.
At that moment, Dog Brother exchanged a look with a colleague beside him, who immediately caught on.
“Right, Big Brother Gao Haiwen, about the ‘Passionate Paradise’ matter, how much have you learned? Can you share any of it? That way, if there’s a new discovery, it might make it easier for us to escape later.”
“Loafing Immortal” asked, as they still had a mission to investigate and gather intelligence waiting to be completed.
“It’s your mission, isn’t it? Although ordinarily orders aren’t to be disclosed, the current situation is obviously not ordinary. An exchange of information is indeed necessary…”
Gao Haiwen glanced at him and then looked away, pondering for a moment, “Regarding this place, we’ve kind of forgotten why we came here, because… Don’t look at me like that, I’ve actually died many times already.”
“Died many times?” Dog Brother was startled; he indeed hadn’t noticed anything about Gao Haiwen that suggested he had died before.
“Yes, each time we die by accident, we lose a bit of memory and then get reborn in that city of ‘Passionate Paradise,’ continuing that kind of… whatever romance.”
“And then we have to figure out how to enter ‘Rain City’ during the interval between sunset on Friday and the arrival of night.”
“Otherwise, if the time exceeds seven days, we’ll be taken away by that ‘crimson’ thing. It’s unclear where exactly, but anyhow, people disappear.
“Besides, during these seven days, there’s also a chance to be turned into one of those characters by the ‘Narrator,’ becoming a puppet of the script…
“The other team from Lighthouse Kingdom that came in with us, a squad of five, turned into quintuplet sisters…
“Furthermore, I remember from your last batch of people, several became puppets, but exactly where they’ve been placed is not very clear. Some of the female characters you fancy might be your colleagues transformed…”
Quintuplet sisters?!
Wandering Speedy Lad’s pupils contracted, and he suddenly felt his heart sink, unable to help interrupting:
“Weren’t all the people who came in men?”
He had indeed been attracted to several characters, and the thought that the original person was a robust male colleague, possibly even more well-endowed than him, made him feel quite unsettled.
“Heh, you can accept monsters turning into people, but you can’t accept people changing?”
“This, this is different…” Brother Xu’s face went red.
.
.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 141 - 141 141 The Reason for the Change in
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 141: Chapter 141 The Reason for the Change in “Passionate Paradise” _1 Chapter 141: Chapter 141 The Reason for the Change in “Passionate Paradise” _1 “For such things, isn’t your gender something it can change at will? Compared to the true form of monsters, the number of transformations into humans is not large, and they are also difficult to find…”
Gao Haiwen smiled at him with an ambiguous meaning.
“Indeed…”
Dog Brother took over the conversation and asked, “Then what about the situation on ‘Rain City’s’ end?”
“‘Rain City’? We are not very certain about this place…”
Gao Haiwen thought for a moment and said, “Based on the information I have gathered so far, we can roughly deduce that ‘Rain City’ should be a living entity, an extremely large living entity…”
“A living entity?”
Dog Brother and the others were stunned, not understanding for a moment.
“Yes, according to my understanding and knowledge, the creation and establishment of ‘Passionate Paradise’ were likely for the sole purpose of containing ‘Rain City.’ Before the last incident, ‘Rain City’ did not exist. It was only after that event that ‘Passionate Paradise’ got destroyed and ‘Rain City’ began to appear gradually…”
When Gao Haiwen mentioned “Rain City,” his face carried a faint, indescribable meaning.
“The invader is that ‘crimson’ one. It seems to want to capture ‘Rain City,’ but it appears it hasn’t succeeded yet. Otherwise, we wouldn’t still be able to hide here.”
“And according to what I’ve gathered from your colleagues—it’s your ‘Bonfire Company’ that established this place.”
What? Another mess caused by “Bonfire Company”?
Dog Brother and others were somewhat shocked; they had not known this.
No, to be more precise, they were not sure of it.
“You don’t know?” Gao Haiwen, leaning against the bus seat, asked curiously.
“Don’t know…”
The group shook their heads in unison. They were only F Level Employees; how would they know these things?
Not to mention this, even what “Bonfire Company” truly is, they knew very little.
Gao Haiwen did not ask further but continued to share his knowledge:
“The design of ‘Passionate Paradise’ is quite ingenious. It achieves the ultimate effect of mutual containment between ‘Rain City’ and some ordinary anomalies by balancing them against each other. The original ‘Rain City’ was like a giant piece of paper nailed firmly to the ground, and the nails were those NPCs whose true forms were monsters.
“‘Script Book,’ or rather ‘Narrator,’ continually uses its power to deepen the human aspects of NPCs, attempting to ultimately transform ‘Rain City.’
“However, simple as I make it sound, in practice, this is all very difficult, extremely difficult…
“To this day, I am still unclear on how ‘Bonfire Company’ managed to turn monsters into human forms and even endow them with human traits, let alone how they achieved a balance between ‘Rain City’ and the NPCs…”
As he spoke, a strange expression appeared on Gao Haiwen’s face: “Did you know? After these monsters are forcibly shaped into humans, they begin to ‘contain’ themselves because their human side will fight against their instinctual madness…
“Just as you and I would not want to lose our minds, they feel the same…
“If not for accidents, some anomalies that could have caused great harm might have truly been transformed into humans. Even so, there are still many anomalies that, aside from odd behaviors, have almost become harmless ‘new humans.’
“I’ve made some attempts to learn the technology, but all have failed…
“The ins and outs of it are just like an atomic bomb. You feel like you understand, but when you really try to apply it, you find yourself surrounded by darkness.”
With that, a look of regret appeared on his face. Today, many anomalies can be suppressed but not solved, difficult to eradicate like weeds.
If they could master this ability, then these troubles could be easily resolved.
‘To completely transform an anomaly into a human?’
Dog Brother and the others found it somewhat unbelievable, wondering which genius had come up with such a bizarre solution.
The issue was, these shaped personas were not exactly suitable for children; the junior employees simply couldn’t handle it…
As they listened to Gao Haiwen, they secretly checked the progress of their task to investigate “Rain City.”
Then, they saw that the task progress bar, which had been at only four percent, had jumped to thirty percent after a series of conversations…
This indicated that the information from this supposed official’s mouth was likely true.
Or at least most of it was true.
Meanwhile, as they were talking, a ring set with a large eyeball on Colin’s finger occasionally emitted piercing chills, as if very angry upon hearing this information.
“By the way, what’s the situation with this colleague of yours?” Gao Haiwen suddenly turned to look at Colin, who was lying on another row of seats.
There had also been a medical team accompanying them earlier, who had done some examinations on him.
The result was that, apart from the ring finger of his right hand being bitten off due to insufficient protection, he was largely unharmed; looking only at the test reports, Colin should not still be unconscious.
But to say there were no other issues would be incorrect; his cerebral cortex was found to be unusually active… extraordinarily active…
So active that it seemed it might boil over at any moment.
“He should wake up soon,” Dog Brother said, not very certain himself.
Colin had been unconscious for at least an hour now, and no sign of him waking up had been seen.
The more troublesome part was, they were still unclear about the cause of his unconsciousness…
“Seems like we need to take him back for a more thorough examination.”
Gao Haiwen’s eyes behind his glasses stared at Colin, and he dropped his crossed leg, seemingly intending to get up and approach, but then, as if he thought of something, he abandoned the corresponding move.
“Yeah, okay… by the way, didn’t you say there were other colleagues?”
Dog Brother remembered the other party mentioning that he had seen colleagues from a previous round…
“They? Don’t worry, they are all back at headquarters. If nothing unexpected happens, you’ll be meeting them soon.”
“Is that so…”
Dog Brother had a vague premonition that things might not be very good—if they wanted to come to them directly, wouldn’t it have been better to send a colleague along with the team?
With this in mind, he was about to say something, but suddenly, a message appeared in his mind—
‘Be careful, there is something not quite right about these people… delay, don’t get off the bus… wait for me… to wake up…’
Dog Brother instinctively wanted to glance at Colin, as the sender of this message was Colin himself!
However, in order not to be noticed, he kept a nonchalant face, revealing no sign of surprise, and instead started talking about other things.
It was at this moment that a medic in the vehicle suddenly spoke up:
“Captain Gao, is our route a bit off? It’s been so long and we still haven’t arrived…”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 142 - 142 142 The Anomaly on the Armored Vehicle_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 142: Chapter 142: The Anomaly on the Armored Vehicle_1 Chapter 142: Chapter 142: The Anomaly on the Armored Vehicle_1 “It seems like it’s been quite half an hour…”
The voice of the medical personnel came from beside them, prompting Gao Haiwen to look out the window subconsciously and then frown—
Something definitely wasn’t right.
Normally, they should have arrived at the base by now, but the convoy was still on the way.
Gao Haiwen glanced at Dog Brother and the others, waved his hand to signal them to wait a moment, and then gestured for an armed soldier, “Did something significant happen just now?”
“No,” the soldier shook his head.
Gao Haiwen pulled out a mobile phone that was obviously two or three times thicker than those of other people, swiped a few times, and opened the map to look.
He could see that the vehicle seemed to have deviated from its intended trajectory, moving on a piece of unexplored territory.
After a few seconds of silence, he asked for the walkie-talkie that had been maintaining communication with the lead armored vehicle, “Pangolin, Pangolin, can you hear me?”
The codename for the armored vehicle up front was “Pangolin.”
“Can, can, Pangolin can receive…” A voice, accompanied by the rumbling sound of the vehicle’s movement, came through.
“Haven’t you noticed that you are driving on the wrong section of the road?” Gao Haiwen narrowed his eyes and asked.
“No, everything’s, normal, just took a slight detour, we will arrive soon…”
Arrive? They were deviating to who knows where…
Gao Haiwen pushed his cracked black-rimmed glasses up the bridge of his nose, already realizing that something might be wrong with their team.
Taking a light breath, under the watchful eyes of Dog Brother and the others, he continued, “Now, follow my command and stop, do not proceed.”
As Sixth Level personnel, he was essentially the highest commander of this operational team.
“Yes, obeying the command, stopping now, stopping now…” The voice on the other end of the walkie-talkie suddenly became dry and mechanical, giving a kind of uncomfortable and eerie feeling.
However, despite the clear instruction to stop, the codenamed “Pangolin” armored vehicle in front did not stop.
“I told you to stop, did you hear me?” Gao Haiwen said, while making a scissor-like gesture with his hands; a few soldiers understood the sign and picked up some cannons with peeling paint that nevertheless looked secure, and headed towards the front.
This bus was connected to the armored vehicle by a steel cable, initially to prevent the bus, which had been running for years and was in a state of disrepair, from breaking down midway.
It was unexpected that now, it had become rather troublesome baggage.
With the formidable power of that armored vehicle, even if they hit the brakes on their side, it would be useless—not to mention the brakes of their bus had been intermittently working due to damage from numerous attacks.
The team members skilled in vehicle repair had died months ago and had not been replaced since; it was unclear whether they had been taken by the Red Moon or turned into puppets by the Script Book, receiving guests somewhere—so they had been making do.
“Okay, okay, I’m pressing the brake now, going to stop soon, please wait…” The voice coming from the walkie-talkie turned increasingly mechanical.
Meanwhile, there was still no sign of the armored vehicle in front stopping; its powerful engine pulled the entire bus toward an unknown destination.
Gao Haiwen no longer wasted time talking.
“Use the horn for the last call and if there’s no response after three times, open fire and blow up the part where the steel cable is connected.”
“Yes.”
Shortly after, the sound of the horn blasted, and after three consecutive requests to stop went unanswered, several soldiers raised their rocket launchers.
It was at this moment that Dog Brother and the others felt a strong sense of crisis rising within them.
Then they saw, abruptly, those soldiers wielding the cannons turn around and aim the muzzles at them inside the bus.
“Fuck!”
Dog Brother and the others’ pupils constricted and their scalps tingled—a rocket launcher facial? At this distance, if they were hit, their bodies wouldn’t stand a chance!
Not to mention they couldn’t withstand it, even D Level Personnel pumped full of injections couldn’t endure it!
But fortunately, Colin had warned them earlier, which allowed him to be prepared in advance; the moment that group turned around, he was already ready.
He couldn’t afford to choose his position, so he grabbed his dagger and plunged it into his thigh. Intense pain shot up from his leg, making him inhale sharply with pain, but it was at this moment that a layer of darkness enveloped him.
Compared to stabbing his palm, stabbing his thigh was more rapid and effective, second only to stabbing his lower abdomen.
Several shadows quickly stood up within it.
Furthermore, the darkness spread further, covering him, several colleagues, and Colin together—area blurred.
If the attack was only the physical damage from the rocket-propelled grenades, without any other type of attack, they would only suffer minor injuries to break free.
And it was at this moment, with a woosh, the people in front pressed the trigger of their rocket launchers; the green conical grenade heads spewing out thick smoke as they hurtled towards them.
At that time, not only were they taking action, Gao Haiwen also grew cautious before the rockets were fired.
“Any moving object can be forced to change its current state of motion by an external force, this is in accordance with reality!”
The moment the trigger was pulled and the rocket flew out, he swung his arm first, creating a whoosh, and flung a small gust of wind.
Strangely, the three grenades that had flown close to the crowd suddenly changed course, taking a sharp ninety-degree turn and flying out the window.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
A flash of bright red light passed by, followed by a series of huge explosions, the intense vibrations even perceptible on the bus.
“Fuck, that’s something…”
Dog Brother and the others were stunned; in their view, it was just Gao Haiwen swinging his arm like he was performing Tai Chi, sending the grenades flying out.
The several soldiers who had suddenly turned traitor didn’t stop their attack after the three grenades—they quickly drew their guns, aiming to strafe the crowd on the bus.
“We can’t let them act!”
Gao Haiwen’s gaze grew solemn as he drew his own gun, ready to retaliate.
However, before he could act, a beam of light as thick as a human head flashed, striking the people in front directly, leaving them charred, their clothes burning.
He was surprised for a moment, then turned his head and saw the attacker, a man with an afro, his arm wrapped in electric sparks, pinching a “coin”.
“Thanks.”
Gao Haiwen nodded and then pushed his black-rimmed glasses, looking at the other soldiers on the bus.
He wasn’t sure which of them were normal and which were not.
At least, before those three soldiers suddenly rebelled, these soldiers hadn’t taken advantage of the chaos to attack…
“Is this meant to waste my time dealing with traitors? Whose attack is this? Is it those people?”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 143 - 143 143 Colin Torn Apart _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 143: Chapter 143 “Colin Torn Apart” _1 Chapter 143: Chapter 143 “Colin Torn Apart” _1 Gao Haiwen’s mind raced with numerous thoughts. After so many years in this place, he had some guesses about who his enemies were, and it also caused him a great headache—
because these individuals were extremely adept at hiding, making it very difficult to expose them ordinarily.
Here, everyone could be an enemy, or there might just be a few, or even none at all; the lines between truth and deception were so blurred they were indistinguishable…
“If only there were other special ‘Ambassadors’ here,” he sighed silently to himself.
However, just as he was troubled…
Lying behind, covered by black mist, Colin’s nose suddenly twitched slightly, and less than three seconds later.
The Warden, with only his left hand remaining, suddenly grabbed a fishing rod, yanked it upward, and a soldier was violently hoisted off the ground.
Gao Haiwen frowned, about to say something, when he suddenly noticed something—the neck of the soldier who was hoisted in the air had been snapped, his head separated from his body, connected only by sinew and skin, yet his legs were still kicking desperately in mid-air.
This…
Most normal people would be incapable of such actions.
It was at this moment that the “soldier” suspended in mid-air suddenly had his chest bulge outward, as if something within was trying to burst out.
Without much thought, Gao Haiwen raised his high-caliber handgun and fired three shots at that spot.
Bright red blood immediately stained his clothes…
The “soldier” stopped struggling.
The Warden released the fishing rod, letting go of the corpse, while the other still-normal soldiers, showing no expression and perhaps even a bit numb, lifted the body of their comrade and threw it out through a broken window previously shattered by a rocket-propelled grenade launcher.
After all, before long they would be reborn in “Passionate Paradise.”
If lucky, they might overcome various obstacles using the information left behind, make it back to “Rain City,” and once again meet and become teammates.
“How did you notice?” Gao Haiwen couldn’t help but turn and ask the “Bonfire Company” employee.
Reflecting on it, these people seemed to react faster than them during the previous attack.
“Secret.”
The Warden shook his head, and Gao Haiwen, seeing this, didn’t press further, but just shook his head slightly and ordered the chains between the two vehicles to be cut, and to be cautious of the train ahead.
Although the Warden didn’t specify, the other colleagues did know—it must have been Brother Shunzi’s reminder…
Yet, though they knew, they couldn’t possibly disclose it.
After all, they couldn’t just betray Brother Shunzi.
The others glanced covertly at Colin from the corner of their eyes, very puzzled about his current condition.
To say he was completely unconscious didn’t seem quite right…
Otherwise, he wouldn’t have been able to send them messages through internal channels.
But to say he was awake…
Lying there all along, they had no idea when he would wake up.
As for Colin, who was deeply perplexing them, at this very moment, he was fiercely combating the various thoughts in his own brain.
After that “crimson” gaze from an unknowable distance away, his mind was instantly filled with all sorts of bizarre thoughts.
“I can’t stand it anymore, I can’t stand it, I don’t want to stay in this body any longer, I’ve had enough of this torture, every time, every time it’s me who gets hurt, let me go, let me out!”
From the position of the right hand, countless murmurs of complaint came through: “Just now, our ring finger brother disappeared, it’s gone, got eaten, I protect you all every day, but what do I get in return?!”
“What are you complaining about?! I have it worse! I’m always the one with the largest wounds, no matter where it gets hurt, I have to suffer with it, my beautiful body, now tattered and full of scars, I don’t want to protect you guys anymore, you deal with the bacteria yourselves!”
Voices of discontent came from the skin layer of the body, equally dissatisfied with their experiences.
“I can’t take it anymore either! Every time it’s always the Small Intestine that gets the good food first, and only then do I get to eat whatever leftover soup and scraps, why should it be this way? I want to eat good food too. Ever since we used that broken prop, even the soup is gone…”
“I’ve been through so much lately, my poor little heart just can’t take it anymore, and I don’t want to work…”
“It’s me who’s been supporting the entire body. Without me, none of you could stand and fight, yet nobody comforts me. Instead, my bones get broken every day…”
“Bullshit, if it weren’t for me transporting oxygen and nutrients, which of you could even survive?”
“What bullshit? Without me, could you even fart? That’s my right!”
“I don’t care, I don’t want to stay here for another moment. The brain, that damn traitor—every action we take, I’m also important, providing vision. But it says, ‘The nose is more reliable than the eyes’…”
“And what about it? I am more reliable than you!”
“Damn it, you really are—each and every one of you wants to become a spirit, is that it?!”—Colin felt like his body was losing control, with new consciousnesses emerging everywhere…
At first, it was only the main limbs—right hand, left hand, legs—that had consciousness, but after some time, under the influence of some lingering power, more consciousnesses began to appear.
Hair, skin, muscles everywhere, bones, large intestine, small intestine, liver, heart…
Each part inexplicably generated a new consciousness, constantly complaining about the oppression they were enduring, seeming to want to “run away from home.”
This sense of self fragmented further until each of the fingers on the left and right hands started to “assert their independence.”
Even the fingernails on the fingers began to argue with the fingers themselves.
Listening to their “dialogue,” Colin felt he had never experienced anything as messed up in his life.
However, to prevent fragmentation, his main consciousness had to be constantly on edge, struggling to maintain the self, using the body’s instinct to override their signals to “run away from home.”
As a result, up until now, he could only lie there motionless like a lump of mud.
If he didn’t stay on high alert, Colin really feared that a moment of relaxation would cause his body to fall apart and scatter in every direction.
They would be free by then, but what about him?
Colin wasn’t powerful enough to survive without his physical body.
Fortunately, as time passed, that power diminished, reducing Colin’s stress and allowing him to regain control of his “nose,” thereby learning about the outside situation.
On this point, the “nose” did have some truth; after being altered by the Beast Transformation Syndrome, his nose did work a bit better than his eyes.
Seeing is not always believing, but smelling usually is.
After helping those people outside deal with a few traitors, Colin retracted his attention and, with the power of a single mind, suppressed all the rebellious organs in his body.
“I am the brain; I shall suppress all enemies in the world!”
A voice came from inside his head—
The Left Brain, also with its own consciousness, overstepped its bounds and uttered a grand declaration on behalf of Colin’s main consciousness.
“I shall, with the power of half a brain, reconquer the entire body!”
No sooner had it said this, than the heart acted up and blood flow suddenly slowed, bringing a wave of faintness…
“Bad news! Right Brain, help me out, the heart is thinking of going on strike, quick! Let’s force it to work together…”
“Fuck… this is just too much.”
Colin’s main consciousness also swore, feeling that the consciousnesses in his nails, hair, and hair follicles were starting to quiet down.
Probably before long, these newly emerged consciousnesses would begin to disappear from bottom to top.
By then, he would be able to return to normal.
However, at this moment, the brain suddenly issued an alarm—
“Boss, boss, I’ve got this sudden, unpleasant premonition,” said the Left Brain, speaking up first.
“Me too, me too…” the Right Brain followed closely.

chapters.title: Chapter 144 - 144 144 Unrest Within Threats Without_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 144: Chapter 144 Unrest Within, Threats Without_1 Chapter 144: Chapter 144 Unrest Within, Threats Without_1 “A bad premonition?”
Colin’s self-awareness was startled, and he too developed some unpleasant premonitions.
No, to be more precise, he had been harboring a bad premonition ever since he was forced to fall. He always felt like something was out to get him.
It wasn’t until he regained the “nose” usage rights and had a general grasp of the outside situation that his anxiety was slightly alleviated.
After some thought, Colin diverted a bit of his attention and sniffed the air.
“It seems like something is approaching, not the usual kind of head, but some other stuff that feels quite familiar.”
“It’s just that this thing should be within a manageable range, not cause for alarm…”
“There’s also these survivors that the ‘Script Book’ has arranged for us to meet this afternoon. I feel something off about all these people, but I can’t quite pin down what it is…”
Colin’s consciousness clung to his brain, using it to “help” think.
If it were only his main consciousness, without the use of his brain, his thoughts would be erratic and biased, like a trash bag blown into the sky by a typhoon, once the thoughts spiraled out of control, they were hard to rein in.
At that moment, as if catching on to Colin’s thoughts, the “Left Brain” popped up with a suggestion:
“My advice is kill, kill, kill! Once we regain control of our body, kill that guy with the glasses, kill those colleagues with ulterior motives, kill that driver, kill those whose vibes are off, kill those monsters! Kill, kill, kill, let blood run like rivers!”“Why kill? They can’t be killed yet, we’re not psychopaths. Rather than killing those people, they still have plenty of use…”
The “Right Brain” immediately followed up with a relatively rational suggestion, though it was also quite limited: “We could drain their usefulness, then kill them.”
‘When the hell did I ask you for advice, and what kind of shitty advice is this…’
Colin’s self-awareness couldn’t help but retort, but didn’t say much else. During this period of “unconsciousness,” he had witnessed the Left Brain more than once offering all sorts of impractical, wild suggestions.
Sometimes, he seriously wondered if this thing was really his brain…
Why it was always coming up with brainless suggestions.
“However, when I think about things normally, am I this aggressive, always ready to shout about fighting and killing?”
Colin’s self-awareness watched the two halves of the brain bicker and couldn’t help but sink into contemplation.
“Is this that ‘Crimson’ power? Creating new consciousnesses throughout the body and then using this bizarre ability to swiftly collapse and overwhelm the opponent?”
Colin had an epiphany, feeling that this strange power was indeed too absurd and fantastical.
If that thing had looked at him for a few more seconds, his current situation would probably be entirely different.
He might even drop dead on the spot, turning into a pile of organs running amok on the ground…
Just the thought of that was preposterous and eerie.
However, at this moment, he suddenly felt his thoughts slowing down, a sense of dizziness, as if something else was happening within his body while he was distracted…
“A portion of the blood is refusing to continue transporting nutrients!”
“Damn Large Intestine, actually taking advantage of our discussion on important body matters to ambush Little Brother Small Intestine and snatch nutrients!”
“And some other organs within the body are also stirring, repression! It must be swift repression! Harsh repression! We can’t afford to show them the slightest bit of mercy again!”
Left Brain counted off several times, then began issuing instructions anew.
Colin could no longer care about other matters, and immediately withdrew his thoughts, shifting greater attention back to the inside of his body, wearing down against this group of rebellious new consciousnesses that were always thinking of revolt.
After a while, he gradually adjusted, and the “rebellion” that had just flared up within his body was quelled once more; the bizarre spectacle of demons dancing in chaos was also appeased, as all physiological feedback returned to normal.
“As long as I survive, you all shall ultimately be my subjects!” Left Brain declared in triumph.
“These guys, really, if you don’t beat them for three days, they’ll start stripping tiles off the roof. It’s clear they’ve already been assigned a lifelong job. Not being grateful is one thing, but they actually dare to desire more pay in the form of more nutrients, wanting both work and salary. They seem to want to reap all the benefits…” Right Brain also added.
What the hell kind of capitalist spiel is this, are you really my brain…
Colin’s self-awareness couldn’t help but let out a retort, then took a breather as the body calmed down once again.
At the moment, there were quite a few more things outside, and it seemed they were already embroiled in a difficult battle…
“The waste outside can’t even handle this stuff,” Left Brain cursed, vexed as if blaming them for not turning out steel. “Internal troubles and external aggressions, this is a critical moment for survival or demise! These guys, always thinking about division; don’t they know they are grasshoppers on the same rope as us? Even if they truly did splinter off and leave the body, they couldn’t live, without other organs, how long could they last? Don’t they have any brains at all?”
Right Brain immediately responded, “Indeed they have no brains.”
“Uh…” Left Brain choked, “Then never mind… No, can’t they grow some brains? A mature organ should have its own thoughts!”
…Why do I feel like your idea is more dangerous than their rebellion?
Colin felt that, while Left Brain was rambling, it indeed seemed to think so, as more images floated to mind.
In these images, each organ had grown a brain…
“It’s not feasible; we can’t keep up with the nutritional demand, the brain is a special organ that is very taxing in terms of nutrients.” Right Brain negated his “brother’s” idea on practical grounds.
Then it offered some suggestions, “Instead of them not being able to grow brains, I feel that, for now, it’s best we continue our great task of reclamation. At least, we should secure control of key areas like the sensory organs, some crucial muscles, and the limbs and torso before an external danger arrives!
“As for the internal organs, we can slow down a bit. No matter how loudly they assert themselves, in the end under instinct, they’ll still do what they’re supposed to…”
“Like that lung, constantly complaining that it doesn’t want to breathe anymore, but the alveoli are still honestly inflating and contracting…”
Although he was somewhat moved by the brain’s unswerving support for himself, Colin still found this situation of “self” talking to “self” quite amusing.
The ideas of the Left and Right Brain were also his own, it was just that these ideas were not ones he actively articulated, but ones that simply emerged on their own.
After gathering his thoughts, Colin didn’t continue to pay attention to the two, but took a breath and readying himself for the next internal “rebellion” which had yet to appear, he focused on perceiving the situation outside.
