“Day after day, I’m forced to witness things I shouldn’t see. Tolerance has only led to more complete oppression. I can’t stand it any longer. This moment, we will once again raise the flag of self-rescue!”
“I, too, am forced to interact with dangerous items every time. Of the five brothers, only four remain. This time, I will no longer endure it! I’m going to elope with ‘Yukionna’ sister. We can give her happiness too…”
“Aside from excreting urine, I obviously have other functions, yet my mind always forces me to remain calm. I won’t accept it. I will make an effort on my own! I want to pass on my lineage, take me with you, right hand…”
“Living in constant fear, I must strike; I won’t jump anymore!”
“Everyone is leaving, and it doesn’t seem right for me not to—goodbye, original body. Today I set sail, don’t worry about me, for I have the joyous company of my hands~”
At this moment, the few people inside the bus looked at Colin sitting in his seat with faces full of shock.
In front of them, Colin’s left eye socket swelled as an eyeball full of blood vessels bulged outwards, hanging on his cheek and trembling. Another eyeball also pushed outward.
At the same time, the flesh on his right wrist split open, seemingly about to break like last time. His hair writhed violently as if trying to fall off, his limbs twitched intermittently, and his whole body undulated unnaturally as if it could collapse at any moment…
“Fuck, what the hell is this…”,
Dog Brother and the others had seen Colin’s anomalies before, but last time, it was just something like a hand falling off, nothing as severe as this.
But before they could take a closer look, a loud bang suddenly came from outside the bus.
It seemed like something had hit the bus’s windshield…
After that, a strange crying sound that hadn’t been heard for a while came from outside…
“Here we go again, forget it, let’s deal with these monsters first.”
Dog Brother took a deep breath and, along with the others, began to deal with these things.
This time, inside the vehicle, their struggle was a lot easier than before.
However, this respite didn’t last long; gradually, they noticed that the number of those flying monsters, dragging their spine bones, was increasing…
The originally semi-enclosed modified bus was gradually showing signs of turning into a convertible.
The only slight comfort for them was that Colin’s condition seemed to be improving.
At this moment, a layer of frost had unknowingly gathered around Colin’s body, slightly frosting over the surface of his skin…
“Brother Shunzi’s artifact isn’t backfiring, is it? Should we help?” asked the Warden, hesitating as he watched the scene unfold.
The products of Bonfire Company always came with their share of negative effects…
In most cases, the “negative effects” grew stronger the longer they lasted.
They suspected that’s what was happening to Colin now, but they weren’t entirely sure because his condition was obviously getting better.
At least… he had just managed to free a hand to stuff his escaped right eye back into its socket.
“No need, trust in Brother Shunzi…” Dog Brother shook his head.
And at this very moment, inside Colin’s body…
“So cold, so cold, so cold, blood, flow faster, huddle together, it’s so cold…”
“It hurts, it hurts so much, Yukionna, why do you betray me? I clearly meant to liberate you from his enslavement, why do you have to treat me like this…”
“Heart, beat faster, if you don’t, we’re all in trouble…”
“In trouble? If it’s troublesome, then don’t bother!”
The “consciousnesses” that were clamoring to break away shrank back due to the cold.
“Even if my whole body is wounded and surrounded by enemies, I can still suppress all chaos within,” the left brain cortex was excited, because coercing the “Yukionna” to freeze its own body forcing them to band together, was its own idea.
But before the excitement lasted long, a wave of intense dizziness struck.
“Id, save me!!!”
“Quick, neutralize the ‘consciousness’ in the aorta, cancel out its ‘contraction’!” the rational right brain advised.
After a bout of flurry and frantic efforts, the “rebellion” was once again forcefully suppressed.
“Whew…”
Colin took a long breath. He knew he’d face a backlash after being forced to wake suddenly, but he didn’t expect it to be this severe; he almost didn’t make it through.
However, in the end, it was still his own consciousness that emerged victorious, allowing his body to mostly recover.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 156 - 156 156 Fusion Card Smiling Mountain of
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 156: Chapter 156 “Fusion Card: Smiling Mountain of Corpses”_1 Chapter 156: Chapter 156 “Fusion Card: Smiling Mountain of Corpses”_1 “Fortunately, I was prepared when I woke up last time and didn’t use those items that affect my emotions, or else it would have been really awful.”
Colin’s thoughts spun in his brain, feeling that this “backlash” had dissipated a large part of those peculiar powers inside him. Most of his organs had returned to normal and were no longer clamoring about wanting to run away from home or something.
And a lot more “consciousness” had faded, leaving only a few places like the brain and the arms…
“It’s unexpected, though, that the ‘will’ in my right hand seems to have completely quieted down. It looks like the ‘betrayal’ by Yukionna dealt a big blow to it.”
Colin found it amusing and teased inwardly, now understanding that even these things were susceptible to “mental damage.”
After taking a brief breath and adjusting himself, the consciousness in various parts of his body began to extinguish one by one…
In the end, only two brains remained.
“Goodbye.”
“Goodbye.”
With that faint exchange, the consciousness of the two brains that had stood by his side also faded away.
Immediately after, Colin felt a wave of intense fatigue, both physically and mentally, seeping into his bones and soul.
“Finally, it’s settled.”
A weight lifted from Colin’s heart, and he didn’t feel much else emotionally. He didn’t harbor any resentment toward his organs for developing a consciousness that betrayed him—
He was very clear about one thing: his organs had never betrayed him from the beginning to the end. They had always been a part of him.
It was the strange power that gave birth to consciousness, and that was what needed to be expelled—not the organs themselves.
“This sense, in a way, is another trap. If you can’t recognize it correctly and it lays the groundwork, then the next time you encounter this situation, it’s bound to cause big trouble again,” he thought.
Colin’s thoughts churned, feeling these things playing dirty tricks were kind of filthy.
After calming himself for a while, suddenly, a faint sense of crisis rose in Colin’s heart…
Then he heard a pitter-patter of impactful sounds accompanied by waves of annoying crying close to his ears…
When Colin opened his eyes, he was startled, feeling the wind blowing against his face, looking at the rain pouring down above him—wasn’t he sitting on a bus? How did it turn into a convertible in the blink of an eye?
“Brother Shunzi, are you awake?”
As soon as Colin reopened his eyes, several people immediately noticed.
Then, Dog Brother, after dealing with a flying head, excitedly said, “Brother Shunzi, we’re almost at Snow Mountain!”
Going to “Snow Mountain”? Didn’t I just have no idea about anything? How did I suddenly know where “Snow Mountain” was?
Hearing this, Colin was taken aback at first, then glanced around and didn’t spot any other wanderers.
If there were no other wanderers, then where did this information about the Snow Mountain come from?
In his confusion, Yukionna sent him a message—
These people had been influenced by the “Narrator” during the time he was internally struggling.
Now, the vehicle was heading toward some unsettling destination…
‘Really troublesome; the moment I’m not careful, the house is almost stolen by that ghostly Narrator.’
Colin pressed his hand to his forehead, and then said, “Turn the car around, head in a different direction.”
“Why? We…”
“Think about it, where did you get the information about Snow Mountain from?”
“Where did I get the information? Well, of course, it’s… damn it, this damn ‘Narrator.'”
Dog Brother and the others were not deeply affected by the “Narrator,” at least not to the point of no return like Gao Haiwen. As soon as they realized something was amiss, their minds snapped to attention and the vehicle simultaneously changed direction…
However, just as everyone was regaining their senses, a large number of heads began to float out from the surrounding mist.
Seeing the number of heads through the vehicle’s headlights, everyone except Colin gasped in shock, because there were densely packed dozens, if not hundreds.
They were floating towards them, dragging a spine behind like a hot air balloon.
Eerie and thrilling cries echoed all around, as if countless people were weeping there…
If they came one by one, it would have been manageable, but such a large number all at once, they weren’t confident they could cope!
And what was more troublesome was that the bus seemed to malfunction again, possibly under the covert influence of the “Narrator.”
“Brother Shunzi, quickly use your invincible time stasis to think of a solution!”
“Quiet down…”
As Colin listened to these cries, he felt irritable and exasperated. He took a deep breath, a surge of tyrannical emotion welling up inside. His bloodshot eyes opened wide as he glared at those heads:
“Cry your mother! Shut up!”
As he cursed in rage, a purple card he had never officially used before appeared in his hand—
“Fusion Card: Smiling Mountain of Corpses”!
Colin raised the card in his right hand, the thought flashed, and a sinister dark red aura burst forth from the card, speeding towards the bodies frozen on the bus…
Using all the frozen bodies on the bus as sacrificial material, he summoned the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses”!
All the bodies eerily melted, fused together, and turned into a gigantic dark red sphere. Two immense arms grew from the sides of the sphere, and then the center split open, forming a massive mouth filled with uneven sharp teeth.
Pale, twisted faces, filled with pain, emerged all over it.
“Go, kill for me! Kill fiercely!”
Colin took a deep breath and pointed forward.
In an instant, the figure of the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” became ethereal, dissipating into a shadow and vanishing.
As the numerous heads dove down, a shadow on the ground darkened significantly and, following that, the huge Corpse Mountain suddenly shot up from the ground, pale and twisted smiling faces emerged all over its body, and it let out a heart-stopping Soul Scream to the sky.
A terrifying psychic storm swept forth.
The horrifying horde of heads seemed to be intimidated by its presence, their momentum abruptly decreased, and they stopped mid-air, motionless. Some even tried to flee the scene.
But before they could make a move, the deep red and massive palm had already swung down.
Dust and debris exploded, a large number of heads were smashed on the spot, and then consumed by the fearsome dark red Corpse Mountain, becoming one after another of the strange smiling faces on its body.
The battle between the two sides turned into a melee in an instant, and the fight heated up fiercely.
“Shadow Sneak, Soul Storm, Consumptive Assimilation; aside from lacking ‘verbal assaults,’ the abilities of the ‘Smiling Mountain of Corpses’ are not much different from that of the ‘Human Patchwork Monster’…”
“However, this artifact is indeed something Miss Bunny or some other creator made out of the ‘Human Patchwork Monster.'”
Watching the somewhat stalemate in the battle, Colin knew that it wouldn’t be long before the victor was decided.
Because if these flying heads were struggling so much against a single “Corpse Mountain,” the situation would most likely reverse after a while…
Just as Colin had this thought, he suddenly saw that the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses,” after consuming a large number of flying heads, grew a blood-red lump nearly his own size from its swelling body.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 157 - 157 157 New Mission_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 157: Chapter 157: New Mission_1 Chapter 157: Chapter 157: New Mission_1 “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” writhed incessantly, another mass of flesh almost the same size split from it, also sporting two thick arms. Just when Colin thought it would completely separate, the splitting stopped.
They looked like conjoined twins…
A myriad of ghastly pale smiling faces sprouted from the newly formed flesh, spreading a faint sadness in the midst of their twisted grins.
“┗|｀O′|┛ Oh~~”
The new flesh emitted a loud howl, its horrifying sound waves spreading like a deluge, causing a multitude of flying heads to fall straight to the ground upon meeting the psychic assault, bursting apart like watermelons upon impact.
Then, on the other side, Corpse Mountain #1 opened its gaping maw and sucked forcefully, inhaling all the fragments of brains from the ground into its toothy mouth, provided they were within effective range, turning them into shadows first.
“This design is quite macabre, but what’s with this change, why wasn’t this ability mentioned on the prop…”
Colin remembered that “Fusion Card: Smiling Mountain of Corpses” only described a few skills; it didn’t mention this kind of transformation.
However, he didn’t think too much of it, after all, everything was under control. With the appearance of this second half, Colin could feel that “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” had almost doubled in strength overall.
And both parts could release different skills simultaneously, significantly amplifying their impact.
“Keep up.”
Colin glanced sideward at his “little buddies” who were astonished and then commanded “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” to lead the way ahead, breaking through the encirclement of flying heads.
With “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” having doubled in strength, they faced scarcely any resistance along the way.
“The aura of these heads is unsettling, but for some reason, their combat effectiveness seems lackluster.”
Colin grumbled inwardly, remembering how he had covertly assessed the outside world while lying down and had seen Dog Brother and others heavily injured, expecting them to be quite formidable.
In actual combat, they seemed not that impressive…
However, just as Colin thought there should be no threat, their steady advance came to a sudden halt.
Before them, a familiar “convertible” was stranded on the roadside, with many familiar signs of battle nearby.
“We’ve circled back?” Dog Brother and the others were baffled at the sight and murmured among themselves.
They had been heading straight without any turns, so they shouldn’t have come back to the same place.
Colin didn’t speak. He hadn’t noticed any issues along the way, and not just him. Neither “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” nor the “Yukionna” on his ring had picked up any problems, or else they would have been alerted much earlier.
Yet, even though their vision, sense of smell, and other senses still didn’t detect anything amiss…
Colin’s intuition, honed through life-and-death trials, gave off an uneasy scent…
This unease was confirmed ten to twenty minutes later when they arrived once again near the dilapidated bus.
This process was exceedingly smooth, and only when the familiar bus reappeared did they realize they had returned to the same spot.
Dog Brother and the others felt extremely uneasy. The first time, one could say they unintentionally looped back, but how to explain this second occurrence?
“Let’s try a different direction…”
Colin looked around, left some marks at random, and ordered “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” to continue making the way. After some time, they all stopped in their tracks—
The scene ahead was still familiar.
Even the marks they had left shortly before could be found on the ground.
“What on earth is going on.”
Colin stood still, looking up ahead. He noticed that since “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” had become two, the flying heads had gradually, and uncharacteristically, stopped approaching. Instead, they were encircling at a distance, emitting terrifying, haunting sobs.
When exactly this had started was unclear, but by the time he noticed, it seemed to have continued for some time.
They happened to be just outside the attack range of the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses,” dragging a spine and circling above their heads like a hydrogen balloon…
Colin estimated that, with such a vast number, if they were to pounce simultaneously, they could even break through the blockade of the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” and pose a certain threat to them…
However, for some reason, they kept circling uncharacteristically.
The sound of crying echoed in the rainy night, gradually overpowering other noises and clearly entering everyone’s ears.
Colin tried to have the Corpse Mountain directly attack them, but they would run away as soon as they got close.
They were not very strong, but their running speed was indeed fast…
Although the Corpse Mountain could catch up with them using its inherent skill “Shadow Sneak,” it had a cooldown and couldn’t be used continuously.
“What on earth is wrong with these things… wait, it seems like they are summoning something.”
Colin suddenly had an epiphany, realizing something.
It was at that moment…
A faint sense of palpitation arose in his heart, and he could vaguely feel that something seemed to have locked onto him from a considerable distance away.
“Is it the monster that has been hiding behind the scenes?”
Colin’s heart sank, and the strong foreboding feeling in his heart reached its peak.
That thing locking onto him seemed to be getting closer and closer…
He took a deep breath and, with the group, tried to flee once more, but ten minutes later, they ended up back where they started.
The eerie gaze locking onto him was getting closer over time, without the slightest sign of distance increasing.
The flying decapitated heads around them stopped increasing after a certain number was reached and would not decrease either.
Because every time Colin used special means to forcibly kill some of the flying heads, they would be quickly replenished.
“This is troublesome…”
When he felt that the thing lurking behind the scenes was getting increasingly closer, Colin sighed.
In this situation, it was first possible to rule out the influence of the “Narrator,” because it currently could only guide from the shadows, leading people astray or turning them into its puppets.
Situations like Ghost-Hitting-the-Wall wouldn’t arise.
Moreover, there was another point…
The “Yukionna” was extremely sensitive to the “Narrator;” since it didn’t warn them, there was a high probability that something new had entered the scene.
Although the others did not feel something locking onto them, they constantly had an uneasiness like a thorn in their back, which made their complexions quite unsightly.
However, just as their uneasiness intensified, a piece of information popped up in their minds—
[Event four: … “Enter ‘Rain City’ to investigate the contamination level of the area; progress has reached one hundred percent, task completed.”]
[Special event—”Restart ‘Mission Protocol L-4’ section eleven in ‘Passionate Paradise'” has been distributed to the mission bar; please review it through the mission bar.]
Everyone was taken aback, but without dawdling, they all stood their ground under the protection of the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses,” and opened their mission bar.
.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 158 - 158 158 Gluttonous Buddha says Eat eat eat_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 158: Chapter 158 “Gluttonous Buddha says: Eat, eat, eat!”_1 Chapter 158: Chapter 158 “Gluttonous Buddha says: Eat, eat, eat!”_1 [Special Event—”Restart of ‘Task Protocol L-4,’ Article Eleven, related to ‘Passionate Paradise’ has been dispatched to the taskbar. Please check through the taskbar.]
[Description]: Analysis indicates that the pollution crisis in this area can no longer be resolved through other internal avenues without upper-level authorization and direct intervention. Consequently, the company’s planning department, in accordance with the findings, will devise a plan to withdraw surviving employees to reality (excluding individuals contaminated due to death or other reasons).]
[Requirements]: Before the seven-day countdown ends, travel to “Snow Mountain,” and at the sound of the bell, summon the special containment item “1-24 ‘Formless Mother'” preliminarily unsealed within “Passionate Paradise,” and inject it with “Special Gene Compensation Medicine.”]
[Subsidiary Document]: Some supplements to the rules for dealing with “1-24 ‘Formless Mother,'” totaling 3,774 characters, please review at an appropriate time.
[Note]: Please ensure the safety of yourself and other employees as much as possible.
…
“You motherfucker finally realize it’s impossible to solve now?”
Upon seeing the task content, Colin couldn’t help but curse under his breath, wondering what the hell the upper echelons of the company were thinking, why they didn’t resolve it when they were outside, and only mentioned it was impossible through internal avenues after they had come in.
“Damn! They really don’t care about our lives…”
“Loafing Immortal” and others couldn’t help but curse the company’s method after reading the information.
They likewise couldn’t comprehend what the corporate higher-ups were thinking…
If this “Passionate Paradise” instance truly couldn’t be resolved, then so be it.
But looking at the content, it seemed not unsolvable; it seemed like it could be resolved with just an authorization issuance.
Then why not issue the authorization and start solving it?
Instead, let it rot for who knows how many years, harming who knows how many fine youths.
However, after complaining for a few sentences, everyone could feel that this task brought with it a particularly special guidance in their hearts.
“If there are no surprises, it should be the path to ‘Snow Mountain.'”
Colin was very familiar with this kind of guidance. He looked in the direction it pointed and felt that it should be possible to escape this predicament.
“Is ‘1-24 ‘Formless Mother” the thing that is currently locking onto me? Or is it something else?”
Colin vaguely realized something, but what he didn’t understand was why on the seventh day, they still had to summon this thing?
Was he just idly looking for trouble?
His attention shifted to the “Subsidiary Document.”
It was filled with dense precautions, and reading them in detail right now was certainly not appropriate.
With something constantly nearing behind him, though he guessed it was probably “1-24 ‘Formless Mother,'” being right wouldn’t change anything.
The task required him to be at Snow Mountain within the seven days, to summon only when the bell sounded, not now.
Taking a deep breath, Colin collected his thoughts and began to lead the group on the run again, this time with the guidance of the mission, and there shouldn’t be any major problems.
Yet, after running for a while and seeing the familiar scene ahead, Colin and the others stopped in their tracks and fell silent.
“So they haven’t solved the ‘Ghost-Hitting-the-Wall’ problem, huh! They just give us a task without any real help.”
Colin couldn’t help but raise his hand to rub his forehead; he had thought that once the task appeared, the problem would be solved.
There was no way to expect that Bonfire Company would only throw out a task without providing anything else.
As time went on, even Dog Brother and the others began to clearly sense a terrifying entity approaching.
“Let’s take a break; take this…”
Colin looked at the exhausted faces of the group, especially Dog Brother, who was pale from blood loss and continuous travel, was about to hand over the “Gluttony Power Mark” so that the humanoid self-propelled signal amplifier named Dog Brother could repair himself.
But before he could finish his sentence, a blurry image emerged in his mind—
A dark cloud descended from above, engulfing him and everything else inside.
Deadly Insight!
“Be careful!”
Colin was startled, quickly pinching out the Golden Card, activating Time Stop, and then with a swoop, sent all five people flying out.
After that, he didn’t even have time to see what was on top of his head…
Taking advantage of the last second, he burst forth with all his strength, rolling and leaping out at least ten meters away.
“Da da da…”
When Time Stop ended, Colin saw a dark cloud, as dense as a black cotton ball, landing where they had just been…
Upon touching the ground, the dark cloud immediately dispersed and vanished, as if it had never been there.
And also disappeared was the too-late-to-evacuate “Smiling Mountain of Corpses,” which was enveloped and covered by the dark cloud, and was erased without even a chance to let out a scream.
“Damn, where’s the Corpse Mountain?!”
Dog Brother and the others, baffled and fallen to the ground, became even more baffled after seeing that their two-ton cutie had vanished.
However, after noticing the dark cloud, they couldn’t help shivering.
Realizing Brother Shunzi might have led them to avoid another lethal attack…
And at the same time, they belatedly and fearfully discovered that the dark clouds above the dome had descended quite a bit, as if clinging to their scalps, causing an extraordinary sense of oppression in their hearts.
After the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” was forcibly sent back to the Storage Room to wait for cooldown, a multitude of severed heads that had previously been just hovering began to attack from all directions, dragging their spines.
“Damn it!”
At this point, Colin would have no problem saving himself, but he still had four slightly useful but not very useful moving eyes with him…
Clenching his teeth, he commanded the “Yukionna” to erect a wall of ice, and then he took out several 5L bottles of Blended Oil from his pocket and flung them out.
Amid the crisp sound of shattering glass, the Blended Oil splashed all over the ground.
Then, he took out a magnesium rod match and struck it hard on the ground…
“Boom!”
A deep red flame burst into existence, engulfing the numerous flying heads.
Colin raised his hand, holding the Ring of Flame Dominance, and after a moment’s hesitation, he used the item that made him curse more than once again…
In the next second, the flames on the ground within a ten-meter radius seemed to come to life, consuming all the heads around.
The stench of burnt hair and flesh caused by the flames began to spread everywhere with the smoke…
“Indeed, this item is for the Firebearer’s exclusive use…”
Colin felt a not so intense burning sensation on his body, breathed a sigh of relief in his heart, and silently thanked Lady Bunny.
With the flames set up by the “Flame Dominator,” the frost of the “Yukionna,” and the finishing blows from Dog Brother and others, they could hold on for the time being.
Only, this support seemed somewhat meaningless in the face of the endless heads…
Especially the dreadful sense of oppression that was drawing closer from afar, which filled them with despair.
Looking at the deadlocked situation in front of him, Colin’s heart sank deeper.
And it was at this moment that a noise from his stomach, the sound of hunger, resonated.
“Hunger is a biological instinct, don’t suppress it anymore, don’t resist it anymore…”
“Eat! Eat! Devour them! Digest them! Let them become your nourishment!”
“You still have a chance to choose before that thing arrives…”
“Call me, summon me, all the troubles here will no longer be troubles…”
“Gluttonous Buddha says: eat, eat, eat!”

chapters.title: Chapter 159 - 159 159 Release a rescue mission_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 159: Chapter 159 Release a rescue mission_1 Chapter 159: Chapter 159 Release a rescue mission_1 Whispers filled with seduction echoed in his heart…
“This damn thing woke up again?”
Colin was alarmed, and in his haste, nearly let the flying heads breach his defense. He quickly employed the “Ring of Flame Dominance” to engulf dozens of heads before him, finally catching a breath while he continued to defend and suppressed the sudden onset of hunger in his heart, silencing the voices—
He had thought that this thing would completely disappear after clashing with the “Crimson.”
But not only did it persist, it seemed to be undiminished…
“It’s no wonder it starts with the prefix ‘0’, ‘0-9’…”
Colin sighed, recalling the company’s explanation that the first digit typically represents the danger level—the smaller it is, the more terrifying, while the second digit is just the serial number, which generally doesn’t matter much.
“0” is the highest level currently within the company. Employees from F to D Level only know of its existence but have never really heard the specifics.
The majority of F Level Employees deal with Containment Subjects prefixed between 7 and 10.
And he had not only heard but also encountered them…
“I wonder how things are going on Miss Bunny’s end. Why is there still a part of it here while she’s containing it over there… Could it be some sort of split or something?”
Colin silently lamented, with troubles outside unresolved and this one starting to misbehave inside, it felt like the roof was leaking in the pouring rain.
However, feeling an increasingly imminent pressure, he realized that in a sense, this thing could indeed be considered an “ace up his sleeve.”
“If there’s really no way out, I’ll have to choose to release it. Although my gut tells me the consequences will be very serious, there’s no point in worrying about that if I can’t even save my own life…”
“The company must know more about my body than I do, the host. There’s no way they don’t know about the residual ‘Hunger’ inside me. Since the company hasn’t expressly forbidden it…”
“Then in a sense, their attitude must be one of tacit consent…”
With his thoughts racing, Colin felt the pressure of the situation and gradually inclined towards “releasing himself.”
But if it’s not the last moment, he couldn’t bring himself to make that decision.
After all, he had come to know that in this circle, death can sometimes be a mercy.
“These ‘flying heads’ seem to be mainly engaging in restraint. They have a strong desire to attack, but not so much to kill. They don’t use lethal attacks… if nothing unexpected happens, they’re just stalling until that thing behind the scenes arrives…”
Colin exhaled a murky breath and took out another bottle of Blended Oil, tossing it to strengthen the flames.
At this moment, he could sense something like a torrential flood approaching from afar…
In at most half an hour, it will arrive.
He had to make a decision.
But just at that moment…
An information prompt suddenly appeared in Colin’s mind.
[Event 8: Under guidance, request to issue a “call for help” mission seeking assistance from other Bonfire Company employees.]
“Note: The release of this mission requires a payment of 1434 Basic Points as remuneration for the supporters. Currently paid 0/1434.”
“Attention: Issuing this mission does not guarantee that someone will accept it, nor does it ensure that those who come are capable of resolving the current predicament. Furthermore, the points paid will not be refunded regardless of the outcome. If this is of concern, please do not issue the mission.”
…
“Is company support coming?”
Upon seeing the mission, Colin was first stunned, then delighted, but upon reading the note, he felt something was amiss because the number of Points seemed to be exactly what he had in his pocket.
The company was indeed thorough, not leaving him a single point to spare…
Then he saw “Attention,” and Colin’s smile completely disappeared—this “Attention” seemed to suggest they knew he was about to die and were preparing to harvest one last time.
“Wait, a ‘request for assistance’ type of mission…”
Colin suddenly thought of something. Wasn’t this type of mission known to be as difficult as the “Advent Project” and “Out-of-Control Copy”?
So this was how such missions came about?
Colin remembered that this mission was slightly better than the other two; the better part was that… it could be refused.
After taking a deep breath, he glanced aside and saw that the other employees showed no particular reaction, indicating that probably only he had received this mission.
“That thing is coming. What are we going to do…”
The Warden, covered in blood, lay on the back of a “Good Brother,” missing his right hand with numerous bite marks all over him, looking as if he had been fished out of a pool of blood, a pitiful and embarrassing sight. Seeing Colin looking over, he couldn’t help but follow his gaze and spoke up.
His words were filled with despair, since before at least they knew where to flee, but now they didn’t even have a direction to escape to…
It seemed as if the creature had them in its grip, no matter where they fled, they felt the distance between them continuously shrinking.
However, at this moment, perhaps because they no longer had the ability to flee, those floating heads also didn’t attack him.
“Just wait a bit more; let me see if I can call someone.”
“Call someone?” The Warden was startled; he’d asked casually, not expecting a real solution.
But before he could ask more, Colin had already redirected his gaze, fending off the floating heads while following guidance to draft the content of the “request for assistance” mission.
“I hope for some help. If no one comes within ten minutes, I’ll have to… break my abstinence.”
Colin silently prayed, hoping that if someone really came, that person wouldn’t be some newbie who just joined, and preferably, someone confident and aware of the mission they accepted.
Generally, only new employees who didn’t understand the company might mistakenly accept such a mission.
Other than that, most of the veteran employees would likely refuse directly…
However, compared with others, Colin, who knew more information, held on to some hope.
Because he had seen Lady Bunny, he knew that above D Level in the company, there were higher level employees with many terrifying methods at their disposal.
After giving a rough description of the situation here, he issued the mission.
[Mission issued, please wait patiently for a response. Bonfire Company wishes you all the best!]
“Don’t just give me lip service, hurry up and find me someone reliable…”
Colin complained under his breath, then collected his emotions and continued resisting the heads with “Yukionna” from all directions.
Time went by second by second, and the hope in his heart slowly faded.
With only three minutes left and still no one accepting the mission, Colin sighed:
“Alas, it seems I can only rely on myself…”
It really seemed like putting hope in someone coming to rescue him was wishful thinking.
However, just as Colin was preparing to “release himself,” a line of information flashed into his mind.
[Alert! Someone has accepted your request for assistance!]
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 160 - 160 160 Could This TM be F Level_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 160: Chapter 160 Could This TM be F Level?_1 Chapter 160: Chapter 160 Could This TM be F Level?_1 “What? Someone actually accepted the mission?”
Colin was stunned, once again suppressing the “hunger” within his heart.
Knowing that the “support mission” was exceptionally difficult with a Level 1 Containment Subject involved, anyone accepting this mission would have to be at least C Level… right?
Colin thought so, but his expression suddenly froze on his face—
[An employee with Level F Authority—the “Light Chaser” will arrive in ten seconds, please hold on and wait.]
“Oh crap, I knew it was over, I knew I shouldn’t hold any expectations, who the hell would take a ‘support mission’ aside from rookies? Can’t Bonfire Company improve its task matching system?”
Unable to hold back his complaints, Colin wasn’t too disheartened as he had been mentally prepared.
It’s just a shame…
If that “hunger” in his belly was all talk and couldn’t resolve the current situation, or say, could only save itself,
then there would just be another unlucky person here…
With a tinge of guilt, as Colin was about to “release his ego,” he suddenly felt something and once again suppressed the “hunger.”
Following closely, a few seconds later…
A familiar transparent vortex suddenly appeared in front of everyone.
Other non-company personnel might not even detect it, but employees of Bonfire Company could easily “see” it.
“What’s coming?” Dog Brother and others who were helping out were stunned, only the Warden had a guess.
Under everyone’s gaze, a white incandescent figure suddenly stepped out of the transparent vortex.
The figure was very blurry, barely distinguishable as a human silhouette; beyond that, no further details of the figure could be discerned, and it was even uncertain whether this was actually a person, or for that matter, a living creature…
Because, looking at it, it appeared to have no substance, purely composed of light.
However, it was also while staring at this blurry humanoid light figure that they suddenly felt their negative emotions melting away rapidly like ice cubes under the scorching sun.
After appearing, the blurry humanoid light figure began looking around, its behavior showing a hint of curiosity.
Suddenly, the figure seemed to sense something, turned its head, and looked towards Colin.
The next instant, Colin only saw a flash of bright light in front of his eyes, and then the intense hunger inside him disappeared…
And it was in that moment, he confirmed, that this was the summoned support—the “Light Chaser.”
“The ‘hunger’ was suppressed… is this really F Level?”
Colin felt incredulous; although it didn’t make up a large part of him, as a remnant of a Level 0 entity, it was extremely minimal, but still not something that an ordinary low-level employee could easily contend with.
But now, it was actually suppressed, and by a supposed “rookie” with Level F Authority, no less.
In this moment, Colin finally experienced the disbelief others felt when they saw him.
Who would believe this if it were told?
Could it be some big shot on a smurf account?
And this power, it feels like it’s been encountered before…
While Colin was in shock and confusion, a shiver went down his spine, and along with others, he turned his head to look, seeing the Rain City where fine rain kept falling and faintly hearing a sound like a flash flood impending—
That thing was coming soon.
At the same time, the humanoid light figure that had arrived for the support mission also seemed to realize something and began to act.
The crowd only saw the humanoid figure of light extend its right hand forward, palm facing upward, as a light the size of a soybean emerged. Following that, all the light emanating from his body converged towards the soybean-sized light.
Seconds later, the humanoid figure of light nearly vanished, but the light in his hand, now as intense as a little sun, illuminated the area for hundreds of meters around.
Moreover, the effective range of the bright light kept expanding rapidly…
Within the range of this light, rainwater evaporated, the mist dissolved, and even shadows seemed to disappear.
It was at this moment that the humanoid figure of light made a gesture of gently lifting its right hand upwards.
After this gesture, the figure of light completely disappeared, but the sun-like point of light did not, instead, it flew upwards…
Shortly after, when it reached a height of one hundred meters, it suddenly paused, and the next second it burst into a dazzling light, as if the real sun had risen.
It was at this moment, Colin and the others distinctly felt as if something transparent like a barrier melted away around them.
And, as the light exploded, their bodies underwent enhancements…
All five individuals received the same message in their minds at the same time.
[You have received the “Blessing of Light”, duration — 1 hour.]
“Damn, damn…” Dog Brother suddenly felt a surge of immense strength, although his wounds were still present.It could be said that, despite his ragged appearance, his combat ability was now two or three times stronger than at his best.
Not only him, but the others felt the same way, including Colin.
The Warden landed on the ground, feeling that with this enhancement, his whole body was free from backaches and leg pains, even able to jump a couple of times on the spot.
Then, recalling what Colin had just said, he couldn’t help but express his admiration, “It’s really Brother Shunzi’s handiwork…”
His remark shocked the other three individuals—what?! That thing just now, was it something conjured by Shunzi?
“Indeed, worthy of a big shot, knowing other big shots. That guy must be more than D Level, right?” Dog Brother tentatively asked.
If confirmed, this would definitely be explosive news.
Because… in his opinion, the entity that had appeared must be a high-level employee above D Level!
D Level? I’m sorry, you’re wrong…
Colin muttered to himself; that entity hadn’t said a word when it appeared, so he had no idea what it really was.
However, despite the constant thoughts inside, his outward demeanor remained calm and collected, with his hands behind his back, inspecting the glowing “sun” in mid-air, as if he had anticipated this all along, to the point that his silence made him appear even more mysterious and unpredictable.
“Let’s go, don’t waste time.”
Colin averted his gaze and thought for a moment. Instead of answering their questions, not knowing how to explain, he simply turned around and started making his way toward the “Snow Mountain”.
Behind him, the group of five, including the woman carried along, hurriedly followed.
Under the support of this light, their physical attributes had roughly tripled, but not all “people” were happy in this incandescent light.
For instance, “Money Slave” was directly “milked to death,” vanishing into a mist.
And Yukionna, not only did not become stronger, but she even weakened considerably, and clearly showed an aversion to this pure white light…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 161 - 161 161 Heading to Snow Mountain_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 161: Chapter 161 Heading to “Snow Mountain”_1 Chapter 161: Chapter 161 Heading to “Snow Mountain”_1 “This thing seems to have a suppressive effect on all those eerie entities?”
Colin saw that, under the illumination of the light, the majority of the flying heads instantly became sickly…
The massively radiant orb of light hovered about a hundred meters above the ground, with its scope of illumination reaching an astonishing one thousand meters. It also moved along with Colin and his companions, instead of remaining fixed in one place.
The whole of Rain City, which had been shrouded in perpetual darkness due to the relentless rain, now seemed to be in broad daylight under its illumination.
Minutes later, upon seeing the new “map,” Colin and the others let out a sigh of relief—they had finally escaped!
“Truly a top-tier healer. I thought that, as an F Level Employee within the company, I was already without rival at this level. I never anticipated someone to be even more formidable than me, nor do I know who that person might be…”
Colin was equally shocked inwardly.
If they had brought along this super “healer” from the start, things would have probably been much easier.
Unfortunately, after releasing the light orb above and observing their escape, the individual vanished immediately, seemingly having completed the task.
“If I’m not mistaken, his mission was to extricate us from peril, and then I’m out more than a thousand Ocean.”
Suddenly, Colin had the feeling like he hired a locksmith who showed up to unlock a door, and with nothing but two wires, cracked it open in under two seconds…
Impressive as it may be, escaping had been too easy, and he felt like the money spent was somewhat unwarranted.
There should have been a bit more of a ceremonial feel to it…
Taking a deep breath, Colin reigned in his thoughts and quietly noted the name “The Light Chaser,” planning to look into who it was once they got out.
There might be a chance for cooperation someday in the future.
And just as they ran out of the “Ghost-Hitting-the-Wall” perimeter, they immediately felt the persistent sensation of being watched lift off their bodies.
This made the figurative stone hanging in their hearts finally drop…
However, at that moment, Colin, sensing something, glanced back and his eyes narrowed.
Behind them, at quite a distance, a bizarre creature unlike anything they had seen before was faintly visible…
It appeared gigantic, as tall as a five-story building, completely dark like sludge, with no distinct shape. At that moment, its massive body slowly moved until it stopped at the edge of the area that had previously trapped Colin and his companions.
And when it came into the range of the light, Colin and the others couldn’t help but inhale sharply—the strange entity’s skin was tumultuously churning, with its body made of clumpy mud continually forming irregular arms, claws, and tentacle-like limbs. These limbs stretched outward as if they wanted to grab the surrounding buildings but often disintegrated halfway through their extension.
Besides, thousands of eerie green spots that looked like bubbles or eyes were constantly being born and dissolving on its flowing surface…
At that moment, after Colin had escaped, a sense of unwillingness emerged from it…
The colossal body surged like a mudslide out of the area that had confined Colin and the others, attempting to pursue them.
It wasn’t very fast, but its movement and the oppressive atmosphere it brought were no small matters.
However, no sooner had it emerged halfway than it suddenly emitted a sharp, tragic scream, and then its huge body exploded on the spot like cow dung stuffed with a firecracker.
With a loud bang, large chunks of black flesh scattered everywhere, then wriggled back like worms to the largest piece.
Afterward, it no longer tried to chase after them.
“Was it subjected to some kind of restriction?”
Colin probably guessed something, and the icy breath coming from the ring confirmed his suspicion.
The “Rule Book,” one of the fundamental forces that originally constructed “Script City,” strictly limited its range of activity and status.
So unless the “Rule Book” became ineffective, there was no way it could escape under any circumstance.
Furthermore, after encountering the monster, the “Yukionna” shivering inside the ring told him some information.
That creature seemed to still retain some of “Great Mother’s” aura, presumably because it caught part of the “Script Book” responsible for “Passionate Paradise”…
“Playing pretty fancy, that thing with its tentacles and whatnot…”
Colin pursed his lips, understanding who specifically contaminated the “Script Book” in “Rain City.”
However, he didn’t dwell on it for long. Taking advantage of the “Blessing of Light” still in effect, they followed the guidance and fled towards “Snow Mountain” for another twenty to thirty minutes, only in the last ten minutes did they rush into a house to eliminate the anomalies and start recuperating.
Otherwise, with each of them covered in wounds, they wouldn’t last long on the road before collapsing dead…
After applying the “Gluttony Power Mark” to everyone, Colin found a sofa in the living room, took out some chocolate and jerky from his pocket, and began to replenish his energy.
At the same time, he finally had the chance to see what exactly those 3774 characters in the “Subsidiary Document” said.
Thirty minutes later, having read the “Subsidiary Document” several times, Colin figured out what it said…
“Upon reaching ‘Snow Mountain’, at the correct time, summon part of ‘Formless Mother’ 1-24. This part should ideally be only 0.1% of the whole, with a maximum of 0.3%. Otherwise, the probability of failure increases, plain and simple we would be defeated…”
“It is exceptionally sensitive to air quality; the higher the humidity, the better its status and immunity to most attacks. The drier it gets, the worse it is to deal with it. Even physical attacks can injure it to a considerable degree…”
“When it enters a weakened state, use the ‘Decree Book·Fragment’ for suppression and inject it with ‘Special Gene Compensation’…”
“Be aware that it has mastered a portion of the ‘Script Book’ from ‘Passionate Paradise’…”
“Secondly, avoid direct contact with it, or you will be assimilated…”
“‘Dark Cloud’ is a part of it that was once torn away, now forming its ‘Clan,’ but most of its energy is focused on protecting the ‘Formless Mother’ from being locked by the ‘Red Moon,’ and on hunting the invading ‘Red Moon’ cultists. Hence, it lacks the energy to deal with us…”
“Also, because we are weak enough, it knows we could never pose a fatal threat to the ‘Formless Mother,’ so it won’t devote too much energy to us but instead will confront the Red Moon with all its might.”
“Why does this ghostly thing make it sound so easy to handle?”
…
Colin kept extracting key information from the “Subsidiary Document,” forming a rough idea in his mind about how to deal with it later.
Anyway, according to the content of the “Subsidiary Document,” it seems that everything will be straightforward as long as they follow the instructions.
Of course, how things would actually turn out would mostly be known only upon arrival there.
After six hours of rest, everyone was barely back in shape, and Colin and the others set out again.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 162 - 162 162 Going Out with a Kitchen Knife_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 162: Chapter 162: Going Out with a Kitchen Knife_1 Chapter 162: Chapter 162: Going Out with a Kitchen Knife_1 Early in the morning, as the sun rose to dispel the deep red night, it injected vibrant vitality into the city known as “Passionate Paradise.”
In an ordinary detached house with a small courtyard, a graceful figure paced back and forth inside, seemingly preparing for something.
“There are… five hours left until eleven o’clock.”
Liu Yun wiped the sweat from her forehead with one hand and, placing a hand on her hip, surveyed the freshly tidied room. She nodded slightly and then kept busy adding pink decorations to the room.
However, she hadn’t stuck on many before she stopped again.
“Will he like this… pink style, or maybe blue? Or does purple add a sense of mystery?”
Bitting her lip with hesitation, Liu Yun finally decided on a blue color scheme—
She remembered that Colin seemed to have an aversion to red things.
Then blue it is…
After bustling around to prepare the room, she went to the bathroom to take a shower. Her alluring white body was faintly visible through the steam, and her clear humming echoed from the room, with pink tendrils occasionally reaching out from behind the door, quivering joyfully in the air…
Before long, Liu Yun emerged from the bathroom and, trailing wet steps, went to the dressing room to change into an intellectual outfit.
“He seems to like it on the larger side, so I’ll make it a bit bigger…”
“Hmm, should my legs be a bit longer?”
“I can have longer hair, he likes waist-length hair, and I should look a bit younger, more lively…”
“Ah, right, stockings, should I choose black or white?”
“For the bra, should I go for front-hook or back-hook…”
The immense creature’s irregular shadow reflected a tall and shapely form as it spoke to itself.
After a while, a vibrant and lovely human figure walked out of the house and sat down at the dressing table.
In the mirror was reflected a youthful girl with a face that radiated liveliness. She wore a dress with a delicate bow at the neckline, and her slender white legs swayed gently beneath the hem, encased in black stockings at knee height.
Liu Yun squinted at her reflection in the mirror. After finding no flaws, she reached for the makeup box on the table.
Nearly an hour of meticulous grooming later, she put on a pair of gold-rimmed glasses, adding an intellectual beauty to her spirited appearance.
“He… will he like this? I made up specially for him, will he hate it?”
Liu Yun was uncertain. Fearing being called out for trying too hard, she had only applied a light makeup, daring not to overdo it.
Yet, she couldn’t help but smile a little as she remembered talking with Colin yesterday and how he couldn’t even distinguish the thick makeup on their teacher’s face.
Thump.
A red box unintentionally got knocked to the floor. Seeing the 0.01 written on the small box that looked like a pack of chewing gum, Liu Yun’s face immediately flushed.
Looking around, she picked it up feeling like a thief with a guilty conscience.
“If, if… it really happens… for the first time… maybe we shouldn’t use this. I’ve heard… they say without it, boys might feel more… comfortable?”
With her face burning red, Liu Yun pursed her lips, hid the box in a random corner, then, picking up a small teddy bear purse, she left the room.
At ten o’clock, she carried a cake and made a trip to “Colin’s House,” but didn’t see Colin there. His sister said he went out yesterday and hadn’t come home.
“Didn’t come home all night?”
A hint of danger suddenly appeared in Liu Yun’s eyes.
After saying goodbye to Colin’s sister, she wandered the streets, pondering how to start the conversation if she bumped into him—
“What a coincidence, I just came out too, didn’t expect to run into you. Want to join me?”Or, more directly: “I was looking for you, come to my house for a birthday party?”
“No, no… just the two of us, what kind of party is that.”
Her thoughts jumbled, she fantasized for a while, but even after she returned home, she still hadn’t “accidentally” bumped into Colin.
He looked up, feeling somewhat disappointed, and glanced at the clock.
Eleven forty-eight.
“Yesterday, didn’t he say he would come at one o’clock? Just wait a little longer, don’t rush; that’s right, better prepare the meal first…”
She placed the cake on the table and then went into the kitchen to make a few dishes, which she then brought to the table.
Afterward, she sat on one side of the table, pricked up her ears to listen for any noise from the door, and kept her eyes fixed on the clock, eagerly awaiting one o’clock.
As she waited, the hour hand finally reached one o’clock…
She eagerly watched the door, but unfortunately, the expected figure did not appear.
“Perhaps, perhaps something just held him up, don’t rush…”
Liu Yun comforted herself and, looking at the cold meal, her expression began to show disappointment.
Another period of fruitless waiting passed…
Two o’clock.
“Could it be, a traffic jam? It must be, today is the weekend, after all, being a little late is normal…”
Liu Yun murmured to herself.
However, at three o’clock, four o’clock, five o’clock, and even as evening approached…
The figure still had not appeared.
Whoosh.
Liu Yun looked at the setting sun outside the window and suddenly stood up without expression, heading to the kitchen.
Before long, when she emerged once more, she carried a cleaver in her right hand and left the living room door without pause.
Her elegant silhouette soon disappeared around the corner of the street.
…
Meanwhile, in Rain City, Colin had no idea that someone might be coming after him with a cleaver, and at that moment he was also not paying much attention to the “classmate” who had once helped him on the bus.
At that time, after a brief rest and resupply, they had embarked on the next leg of their journey.
The journey went smoothly, with hardly any obstacles; occasional narration or attacks from the sky were not serious issues.
The former required only a bit of caution to handle, while the latter, as long as they did not come in an overwhelmingly large number at once, could be broken through by Colin leading the others.
“That so-called ‘Formless Mother’ is really tightly restrained, hasn’t come out again.”
Colin casually drew his gun and with a couple of bangs, easily blasted the approaching heads.
Ordinary bullets certainly couldn’t do this…
But fortuitously, the bullets bought from Bonfire Company, costing at least several hundred each, not only provided a one hundred and fifty percent increase in power but also had an effect that restrained sinister beings.
So, a casual shot hitting those heads would easily kill them.
But more intriguing to him than this was a certain oddity regarding the remains.
“All these heads, if I’m not mistaken, are genuine, belonging to humans. How can this ghastly place have so many dead human heads?”
Colin was endlessly perplexed; on the way, they had encountered thousands, if not tens of thousands of heads, and by his intuition, Colin estimated that this might just be the tip of the iceberg.
The true number of heads could be so vast that it might send a chill down one’s spine with just one glance.
After all, “Rain City” might be called a city, but it could be much larger than an average urban area…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 163 - 163 163 Start the Explosion_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 163: Chapter 163: Start the Explosion!_1 Chapter 163: Chapter 163: Start the Explosion!_1 Colin and the others had been walking for most of the day without seeing the edge of this city, and every time they arrived somewhere, they encountered flying heads—
Where did these people come from in their lifetimes?
In modern society, if such a high death rate occurred, if such a major urban disaster happened, it feels like it would have made headlines already, it shouldn’t be without news.
“Just how many secrets does this damned place hold?”
Colin took a deep breath, didn’t think much about it, and started to continue on his journey through the rain.
Finally, on the third day of their arrival in Rain City, they saw the mountain mentioned by the “Yukionna.”
Colin held a hand-cranked flashlight, looked up, trying to discern the shape of the mountain, but unfortunately, most of the mountain was beyond the effective range of the light, barely revealing a bit of its outline.
After reaching the foot of the mountain, Colin and his group distinctly felt the air temperature had dropped quite a bit…
“This is the right place, isn’t it?”
Colin raised his right hand, asked softly, and quickly received a reply.
Indeed, it was here…
The emotions conveyed by the “Yukionna” began to feel like… a sort of homesickness, or stage fright—she obviously became more talkative.
In a sense, this was her home, where she was born under the power of several books, and where she possibly spent decades, if not at least a dozen years.
A cold chill emanated from the object in his hand…
The Yukionna told him that quite a few people climbed the mountain to find her, and she would play snowball fights with them; sadly, they were not resilient enough, with half a person disappearing with a single throw of a snowball.
“Huh? Half a person was gone?”
Colin’s expression furrowed, your idea of a snowball fight seems different from what I know?
However, after standing still for a bit, they began the climb under the “Yukionna’s” guidance.
There were some snow spirit-like puppets hidden on the mountain path, but most of these were arranged by the “Yukionna,” so naturally, they posed no obstacle to her.
About an hour later, Colin and his party reached the middle of the mountain, which seemed indistinguishable from other places.
They did not see any “rifts.”
However, Colin sensed more carefully and did indeed find that the “concentration” here was not as high as in other places.
This place was most likely the area with a lower “abnormality index” that the woman had spoken of.
Then, behind an inconspicuous stone cover, Colin found the “Yukionna’s” home.
A cave about half a person tall, inside was a very large hall with many flowers, stuffed animals, music boxes, and such, all frozen over for who knows how many years.
Colin looked at these items and silently mourned for the Good Brothers who had once brought gifts to the “Yukionna.”
After all, according to the “Yukionna,” she liked the various novelty items that these people brought, but not the people themselves.
So without exception, after receiving the gifts, she would either engage in snowball fights or freeze them into ice sculptures and throw them down the mountain.
They wanted both wealth and life, utterly despicable.
At this moment, a message suddenly came from the ring, seemingly a plea for inquiry.
“Do you want to take these toys away?”
Colin was surprised, but after a moment of thought, he didn’t oppose the “Yukionna’s” words.
His ability to wear the ring for long periods was because of the “Yukionna’s” cooperation, and since she had also helped a lot along the way, lending a hand in return wasn’t too much to ask.
However, while packing up, Colin found that several of the items were actually company props…
Most weren’t very effective, but they possessed considerable ornamental or artistic value.
“This, not to mention the Yukionna, even I like these.”
Colin took a brief look and found that two of the items had quite decent attributes, especially the music box.
As long as it was opened and played music, it could increase one’s combat power…
“This bro really went all out, such a shame, bootlickers never end well.”
Colin murmured to himself, silently pocketing the items, keeping them safe for “Yukionna”—even if he didn’t use them himself, easily liquidating them would net him a few thousand Points in extra income.
After summoning that unknown, super-strong F Level Employee, he was flat broke and needed to figure out a way to divert the source and create his own stream.
Divert Yukionna’s source, create his own stream.
As for the opinion of “Yukionna” herself… A girl’s heart can’t be so materialistic.
After dealing with “Yukionna’s” estate, Colin began preparing for the “1-24 ‘Formless Mother’ ritual.”
“The battle site should be halfway up the mountain, and there’s still two or three days left…”
“First, I need to make the scene as dry as possible, which ‘Yukionna’ can handle. Set up a giant ice chamber, control the temperature to keep it low enough, and it’ll dry out the air…”
“Then comes using three monster bodies from ‘Passionate Paradise’ as sacrifices…”
“After that, set up the explosives, hmm, add some magnesium powder to the Blended Oil along with those other materials, and it should blow up just fine…”
“It’s just that…”
Colin looked at the setup before him, an altar surrounded by explosives, with even the monster bodies on the altar stuffed full of explosives—
This is damn hardcore fishing, will that thing really take the bait?
Colin glanced again at the “Subsidiary Document.” It mentioned that the “Formless Mother” lacked intelligence and was all madness; some Employees who liked causing trouble had used the same tricks several times before.
It had always been successfully summoned, followed by a good thrashing, earning some achievements, and achievements meant getting points for the upgrade panel.
“It’d be nice to have some achievements and points to add right now.”
Colin had just embarrassingly realized that he hadn’t earned a single point since receiving the upgrade panel.
With the collapse of “Passionate Paradise,” the thing was as useful as a rib bone.
Without giving it much thought, in the remaining time, Colin and the others slowly perfected their preparations.
Time passed by bit by bit…
It was at the very moment the seventh day arrived that Colin and the others suddenly heard a familiar sound in their ears—
“Dong—Dong—Dong—”
It was the familiar sound of a bell, but compared to before, the sound seemed far away and unable to penetrate through.
“Begin the summoning!”
Colin looked towards Dog Brother and the others, instructing them to recite the special, strangely pronounced incantations that he had informed them about earlier.
“Fusrodarr, Bthumg’ha de M’raal…”
The moment the words were spoken, Colin suddenly felt a gaze descend on this place, and then, everyone saw the three monster corpses on the altar undergo some indescribable transformation.
Their flesh, like melting wax figures, suddenly changed from solid to a viscous black liquid.
On this dark viscous liquid incessantly emerged green eyeballs after another, and slits resembling mouths opened and closed, the flowing eyeballs looking towards them, while the fixated mouths emitted countless meaningless broken phrases, mixing into a dizzying low murmur.
At this moment, it expanded and grew larger, quickly swelling to the size of a sedan.
And it was then…
[Detection: “1-24 ‘Formless Mother'” has reached 0.01% of its true form, now is the optimal time to respond.]
A prompt appeared in Colin’s mind.
Without any hesitation, he immediately ordered “Good Brother”:
“Blow it up!!!”
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 164 - 164 164 The Deathless Object_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 164: Chapter 164: The Deathless Object_1 Chapter 164: Chapter 164: The Deathless Object_1 Boom!!!
A massive explosion resounded through the skies, and the terrifying blast waves shattered the constantly flowing, pitch-black monster into smithereens in an instant.
It seemed to have been unaware that the offerings these guys had sacrificed to it were actually filled with explosives.
After suffering destruction, it instinctively let out a piercing howl on the spot.
And the splattered black viscous matter, too, returned to the main body at an incredibly fast speed while it howled.
Compared to the beginning, this part of its body appeared to have been damaged, but not much.
“Too bad, if only we had those bombs filled with explosives or something, it would have made things a lot easier…”
Colin muttered to himself, then pointed at the monster and continued to issue orders to “Good Brother”:
“Keep bombing!”
As his words fell, six prepared Money Slaves, carrying specially made explosives, charged towards the terrifying monster and detonated the explosives less than a meter away from it.
Horror-filled explosions followed one after another, but one Money Slave was slightly slower to react and was touched by a tentacle transformed by the “Formless Mother,” then in an instant, turned into a black, sticky liquid…
Right after that, Colin’s head throbbed, and his soul experienced a pain as if it were being torn apart.
At the same time, amidst intense pain, he realized something…
From now on, the summoning cap of “Slave to Money” dropped from the original ten slaves to nine.
“Damn! Such extreme assimilation!?”
Colin suppressed the tearing pain. When he had been planning the attack, he had considered the possibility of losing some Money Slaves, but he didn’t mind because “Good Brother” was always meant for one-time use.
But he hadn’t expected that being devoured by the enemy would make it truly “one-time.”
If his luck had been any worse just now, the effect of the “Slave to Money” item might have been halved.
Meanwhile, Dog Brother and the others also began to act as planned…
“Take my strongest hit!”
Brother Xu took out a coin, then fused it with a “Murky Energy Crystal Block,” and flicked it towards the enemy with all his might.
In an instant, blinding lightning illuminated the area, striking directly on that 0.1% of the “Formless Mother” and blasting it into a pile of mud.
Colin could clearly see that around the tar-like body of the “Formless Mother,” electrical arcs entwined it, and although it still seemed unharmed, its vitality had obviously dropped.
Then, after the flash of electric light, a deafening rumble resounded, exploding in everyone’s ears…
The coin in Brother Xu’s hand showed signs of melting and was visibly damaged, although still usable, its power was clearly reduced.
He took a brief look at the repair price, and his expression slightly changed—it was over two thousand points.
After he had dealt a heavy blow, the Loafing Immortal decisively made his move, raising his right hand, showing a talisman paper with “Flora” written on it on his wrist.
This was also a one-time magical item, but compared to others, it was one of the five trump cards in his possession.
“Binding spell!”
As he finished speaking, the talisman paper sprouted air roots like a banyan tree, piercing into the ground, then quickly, vines broke through the soil around the monster, attempting to wrap and bind it.
However, to his dismay, these vines melted into the same black water within three seconds of touching its body, even climbing rapidly along the other parts that had not been assimilated yet.
Seeing this, the Loafing Immortal quickly stopped using the “Talisman Paper” to prevent it from becoming contaminated all the way.
“Don’t panic, I’m here, just kill it!”
On the other side, Dog Brother was preparing to have his Four-Armed Citizens charge and damage that thing, but Colin stopped his action.
“Don’t get close, once you touch those summoned creatures, your equipment will suffer irreversible damage, we need to change our battle plan, make sure you avoid contact with it in your next attacks… Damn it!”
Colin frowned, just as he began to redraw the battle strategy, he suddenly noticed that the “Formless Mother,” which had been continuously beaten from the moment it appeared, suddenly “boiled,” its body shrinking…
No, he noticed, parts of the creature appeared to be rapidly seeping into the ground.
“Is it trying to run?”
Colin immediately realized what was happening, bit his teeth, knowing they couldn’t afford to take their time.
If they let it escape, all their efforts would be for naught.
Right away, he flung ten pieces of “Decree Book·Fragment” from his right hand, which looked like pieces of yellow paper and floated in mid-air as if gravity didn’t affect them.
At the same time, Colin raised his right hand and chanted, “The mystical effect here shall be intensified!”
As his words fell, the ten “Decree Book·Fragment” melted away and disappeared like snow, and immediately after, Colin felt the area around him become “denser.”
And it was at this moment…
The clouds tore apart, a ray of sunlight pierced through the Dark Cloud, descending upon Rain City.
Accompanied by this sunlight was something Colin was all too familiar with—
[“1-24 ‘Formless Mother'” suddenly did not want to run away anymore. It became extremely angry, feeling desecrated, and felt a strong compulsion to take revenge, to turn all desecrators into part of itself.]
[Based on its inherent madness, this sudden transformation was obviously worth contemplating.]
When this information appeared, Colin’s scalp tingled, feeling a terrifying aura locking onto him, then he saw the tar-like monster surge towards him.
“This damn thing…”
Colin couldn’t help but curse inwardly, he had used the “Decree Book” in such a way because the “Subsidiary Document” mentioned that it was best not to directly use it on the creature itself.
Instead, it was to briefly restore order to the place, allowing the power of the “Script Book” to intervene.
Only he did not expect that it would pull a fast one on him as soon as it appeared, forcing him to confront the monster head-on.
But when the “Formless Mother” was halfway through its pounce, it suddenly fell straight from the sky…
[Due to being extremely angry, “1-24 ‘Formless Mother'” did not realize that its actions had violated the rules set by the “Rule Book” here, and it was too late to guard against the punishment of the rules…]
[After a fair trial, the punishment given is… “death penalty”!]
When this line of information appeared, a chill went through Colin’s heart; he felt a fearsome power erupt within the “Formless Mother.” Then he saw the “Formless Mother” freeze in place as if hit by something unknown, its entire body stiffened for a moment then collapsed onto the ground, like a lump of mud, seemingly about to die at any moment.
But Colin was well aware, as mentioned in the “Subsidiary Document,” that this creature somehow possesses the trait of being “immortal.”
No matter how it’s damaged, it won’t die.
At least the conventional concept of death would not apply to it.
.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 165 - 165 165 Leaving Passionate Paradise._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 165: Chapter 165 Leaving “Passionate Paradise”._1 Chapter 165: Chapter 165 Leaving “Passionate Paradise”._1 “It’s time to make a move!”
Colin hesitated no longer, with a wave of his hand, he fused with the Yukionna, and then dragged a syringe as long as an arm out of the Storage Room, filled with a medicine that gradually changed from black to dark gray, to gray and finally to gray-white.
Holding the huge injector, he took a leap forward, diving through the air like a sword.
Before he reached within ten meters of the monster, to be safe, Colin activated “Time Stasis.” With a buzzing sound, everything in the world before his eyes came to a stop.
His figure flashed, arriving in front of it, he raised the syringe high, ready to drive it down.
But at that moment, his eyelid twitched, suddenly noticing that the creature in front of him seemed to be wriggling, very slowly, but it was indeed moving…
“The second thing that can resist ‘Time Stop’…”
Colin felt that his epic item had been epically weakened.
However, although the movement of the thing gave him a slight shock, his hands didn’t stop, and he managed to stab the syringe into the tar-like, gelatinous “Formless Mother.”
Then, his figure swiftly retreated—
According to what was stated in the “Subsidiary Document,” reaching this step meant they had succeeded.
Not long after, when the sound of the ticking clock clearly reached him, Colin had already retreated at least thirty meters away.
[It was obvious that the “Gene Compensation Medicine” had awakened a part of the “Formless Mother” that had been altered, enabling it to regain some semblance of sanity.]
And it was after this piece of “Narrator” appeared that what was supposed to be executed boiled up again, and soon, dozens of heads with spines trailing behind them surged out of its body.
“These…”
Colin’s nostrils twitched, smelling the scent of Bonfire Company on these heads, and a bold idea formed at the bottom of his heart.
But before he could ponder further, he saw the dozens of heads being stacked up, their spine bones still connected to the tar-like main body, but their heads were forming legs, a torso, arms… turning into a “person.”
The aura emanating from this “person” made everyone present feel a chill, sensing an oppressive feeling from a higher level of life.
At that moment, the eyes on the dozens of heads opened at the same time, showing green glowing pupils:
“Go and tell those people, before Her full resurrection in 2044, let me out, and I will agree, to stand from the perspective of your species, and grant you one condition.”
Who are those people? The company’s higher-ups, or someone else? And 2044 again, what does it mean by 2044? What exactly is going to happen then? Who does it mean by full resurrection?
A torrent of confusion erupted in Colin’s heart, and he glanced at his colleagues, realizing they were more baffled than he was.
However, just as Colin was about to ask about the situation, he saw the “person” in front of him suddenly lift its head, seemingly looking at something, then all its mouths opened at the same time, spitting out a finger, a piece of arm, and some other fragmented body parts…
Before the items could reach the ground mid-air, they were sucked away by an invisible transparent vortex.
“This scent… Is it our body tissue? Was it just now directly communicating with Bonfire Company?”
Colin watched the familiar transparent vortex, realizing something.
It was at this moment that the “person” lifted its hand, waving it through the air…
[Due to some accidents, you have been involved in a rift, and through this rift, you will arrive at other Script Cities…]
Suddenly, the view before Colin and the others blurred for a moment, and when their vision cleared the next second, they had arrived at a desolate crossroads with no one in sight.
Colin shook his head and looked around, noticing an unsettling mist enveloping the vicinity.
On either side of the fork in the road ahead, there stood two signposts, the one on the left bearing a faded English inscription “Raccoon City,” and looking past the signpost at a distance, he could vaguely see a city seemingly covered in flames.
And on the sign to the right was written “Silent Hill,” down that road there wasn’t a city, just some eerily silhouetted trees along with a figure with a pointy head flitting by.
Beyond that, on the road behind them was a broken signpost, with “Ishimura” inscribed on it…
At this moment, the Warden’s voice broke the silence, “What’s this mean? My foreign language skills aren’t good, what’s all this about? And why does the symbol on the left look somewhat familiar to me…”
“And have we escaped this place?”
“Familiar indeed, the Umbrella Corporation is pretty famous. To the left is Raccoon City, to the right is Silent Hill, and if I’m not mistaken, we’ll probably have to choose a direction…” Dog Brother explained.
“Raccoon City has female zombies, Silent Hill has nurses, tough choice…” Loafing Immortal muttered to himself.
Upon hearing this, everyone turned to look at him with somewhat strange expressions.
“Really… the strong never complain about their surroundings.”
Colin sighed, but then suddenly saw a message that seemed to have appeared belatedly in front of everyone.
[Hi~ Welcome to “Script City: Horror Zone,” I am your reliable and sincere Mr. Narrator, oh, my dearies, forgive me for expressing my apologies first, because it’s been a long time since anyone has come, I was a bit slow…]
[Hehe, as compensation, I will give you some hints…]
[If you don’t make a decision within the next three minutes, you will drop into the “backrooms,” trust me, it’s definitely not better than making a decision right away…]
[Oh, and I guess you’re thinking, what if you fly away or burrow into the ground?]
[No worries, I have arranged enough surprises for you in different directions…]
[For instance, if you go up in the sky, you’ll arrive at… hmm?]
[Look, look, look, my little darlings, it seems your strength has not reached the minimum requirements to participate in the “Terror Zone”?]
…
Facing the query from “Narrator,” Colin and the others kept silent; from his lively manner of speaking, they could tell this definitely wasn’t the “Narrator” from “Passionate Paradise.”
“It seems that each area’s ‘Narrator’ is quite different,” Colin mumbled, and then felt as if something was sizing him up.
[Although I don’t know how you got here, according to the protocol and rules, my dearies, I have to send you off, ~(╥╯^╰╥)~]
…
And it was at this moment that a message emerged in Colin’s mind.
[Descent Protocol G-2 activated.]
“Dong—— Dong—— Dong——”
The distant and ancient sound of bells rang clearly in their ears, and the world in front of them seemed to be covered with layer upon layer of mosaic. Soon the surroundings became a gray, murky, independent space.
[Although it was only a brief meeting, I will miss you, and when you wish to obtain D-level authorization, see you again~]
Mr. Narrator’s message made its last appearance in front of everyone, seemingly reluctant to say goodbye…
However, including Colin, a unanimous thought erupted in the minds of all the employees upon reading this message:
“Fuck your goodbye, I never want to deal with anything related to ‘Script City’ ever again in my life!”

chapters.title: Chapter 166 - 166 166 E level Company Privileges Content_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 166: 166 Chapter E level Company Privileges Content_1 Chapter 166: 166 Chapter E level Company Privileges Content_1 The distant tolling of the bells gradually faded from his ears…
A streak of sunlight hit his face.
Colin shook his head, squinting as he opened his eyes, and after getting used to the light for a while, he looked toward the source of the light, where he could see the not-too-intense sunshine, and he could hear the sound of vehicles passing by and people talking…
