“Not really. It’s just that compared to the others, you might not be miserable enough…”
You’re ranking misfortunes now? Do I have to saw off a leg before you think I’m qualified? Colin pursed his lips and shook the envelope in front of his eyes, “What should I do next, open the envelope?”
As he spoke, he glanced around and noticed that not many people had received an envelope. Out of a thousand people, less than ten…
“Wait a moment…”
Qin Chuan put his hand to his ear, seemingly talking to someone through an earpiece, and after a while, he finally said, “Wait before opening it, let’s change location.”
Saying this, he stood up and pushed Colin away from the scene. Along with them were a few other “old, weak, sick, and disabled” individuals—only eight in total.
Colin also noticed that these people shared one characteristic: they were disabled, but not fully incapacitated—able to move, but not too much.
“By the way, did you hear that dice sound just now?” On the way, Colin casually asked with curiosity.
“That’s the ability of the person in charge.” When mentioning that person, Qin Chuan couldn’t help but speak with respect in his voice.
Colin took the opportunity to ask, “Is that person very powerful?”
“Powerful? Definitely powerful. That’s one of the few Ninth Level Powerhouses that you can’t find in the whole country, no, the whole world. You can’t just simply describe them as powerful…”
Being able to actively roll the ‘Dice of Fate,’ a Ninth Level Powerhouse was indeed terrifying…
Colin smacked his lips in awe, then said, “So out of more than a thousand people, there are only this few of us?”
“It’s still not certain. We’ll only know by this time tomorrow. But there likely won’t be many more.”
“Is it still a 24-hour influence? I’m afraid the specific number won’t be known until tomorrow…”
Colin pondered, wondering how many people would become new employees of the company in the next few days.
Moreover, he was now somewhat curious whether this “Luck” was applied to them to make them “lucky” enough, or if it was some sort of targeting, such as merely increasing their chances of encountering the “Bonfire Company” and not including anything else.
If it was the former, then Colin felt that he should find an opportunity to start “synthesizing”, there might be a chance to synthesize an orange Talent.
But if it was the latter, then that wouldn’t do…
“The problem with the ‘Dice of Fate’ is that even when blessed with good fortune, one cannot feel it.”
Colin sighed inwardly.
A minute or two later, he was wheeled through various corridors, finally entering a room that was clearly arranged for a purpose.
“Just do as the people inside request, and I’ll come to get you after it’s handled,” Qin Chuan said in a soft voice, then left the room.
Colin gave the room a quick look; it was arranged like a reception hall, with a woman dressed in a military uniform sitting in the middle. Her face bore a dignified smile that at first glance seemed innocuous, but a split second later, one could feel an inexplicable discomfort.
After a moment’s thought, Colin was reminded of the smiles found on the statues in temples and shrines.
Such smiles were somewhat acceptable on statues, but seeing them on a human made it rather unsettling.
‘Is this… ‘Divine Strike’?’
Colin speculated, observing the woman’s status, he could faintly sense a hint of pain and struggle beneath that stiff smile.
However, he didn’t dare to stare for long, because she also imparted an indescribable sense of threat.
She must be at least Eighth Level if not Ninth…
“When one climbs to high positions through official means, the negative side effects seem quite significant, creating a semblance of neither human nor ghost.”
Colin recalled the person he saw earlier with his back full of fine wires, and looking at the woman before him, he felt they both seemed to be in great pain, as if their spirits were always tensely stretched.
“Alright, you may now tear open the envelope,” the woman said, her tone carrying an indescribable ethereal quality.
Whoosh…
Without dawdling, Colin promptly tore open the envelope and poured out the letter inside—
It was the familiar script, the familiar countdown, the familiar request to press a fingerprint.
Under the woman’s instruction, Colin didn’t wait for the last few seconds this time and directly pressed down his thumb.
Unlike the last time, upon pressing the thumbprint, he wasn’t transported immediately but instead, a message popped up.
[The official mission initiation is about to begin; your Trial Task is “to investigate the large abandoned sewer under the Black Forest Subway Station, third level.”]
[Bonfire Company (Full name: Bonfire Camp Special Item Containment Company) wishes you all the best on this incident!]
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 177 - 177 177 Investigating Black Forest Subway
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 177: Chapter 177 Investigating “Black Forest Subway Station”_1 Chapter 177: Chapter 177 Investigating “Black Forest Subway Station”_1 Huh? Black Forest Subway Station?
Colin paused for a moment when he read the name because, not long ago, he had boarded the “Mist Train” there.
But he hadn’t expected that there was something off about this damned place.
Wait, Colin suddenly remembered something, and an overview of the “Mist Train” came to mind: an old train that might appear at various abnormal locations, always shrouded in disquieting grey fog when it did.
“Fuck! I didn’t even notice that detail, thinking the train was deliberately waiting for me to board. Turns out it wasn’t, which means that subway station already had issues at that time?”
Colin had a moment of sudden realization.
However, when he went to the subway station back then, he didn’t notice anything peculiar.
There were only two possibilities for this, the first being that things weren’t too serious at the time, everything was still in a hidden phase, and since his attention wasn’t focused there, he didn’t notice…
The second possibility was that the place was more dangerous than he had imagined, which was why he noticed nothing.
Colin felt the former was unlikely because based on current observations, dangers at the train’s destinations were already formed, whether it was that prairie or the town later…
So the second possibility seemed to be the greater one.
“Damn it, this is definitely not your typical entry-level task. I’ve heard them say normal entry-level tasks are very easy; not something that looks complex like this…”
Colin felt like refusing the task. He knew that since he hadn’t accepted the job yet, he could decline and wait for a new task in a few days.
But if he refused, they might realize something was off with him.
After some thought, he decided not to go through with it.
“With my current strength, I can walk sideways among D Level, I should be fine if I’m careful.”
Colin reassured himself internally.
Then, he unfolded the parchment, and the familiar interface appeared before him, only aside from the “Mission” section, everything else was dull and grey, clearly in an inactive state.
Based on Colin’s experience, other features like the “Storage Room” would be unlocked after completing the induction trial.
Without overthinking, he opened the only softly flickering[Mission]tab and saw the specific content of the entry trial.
[Entry Trial—”Investigate the third level of the large abandoned sewer beneath Black Forest Subway Station.”]
[Description: A large sewer whose existence is unreasonable, seemingly undergoing unpredictable changes due to some leakage.]
[Event One: Please collaborate with other new recruits to enter the third level of the large sewer for investigation. Current progress 0%.]
[Participants: 3 people.]
“Note: Upon completion of this event, the next chain mission will be issued based on the results of the investigation.”
…
“A team mission with three people? Uncommon, yet it doesn’t seem too special. What’s puzzling is what lies inside. I feel like Lady Bunny specifically sent me this mission, so it’s probably somewhat challenging. But then, why add two new teammates if that’s the case?”
Just as Colin had this thought, he suddenly recalled that Bonfire Company had the habit of forming teams to strengthen the signal.
If this mission’s difficulty was high, then it’s likely they’d do the same…
Of course, it’s also possible that the mission just looks a bit strange and nothing else.
“Speaking of which, would a subway station really be built next to a large sewer? Isn’t that too weird?”
Colin felt something was not quite right, but he wasn’t knowledgeable about subway systems, nor was he certain whether such city planning was appropriate.
However, he didn’t have much time to ponder as his heart skipped a beat, his vision suddenly blurred, and then he almost leapt out of his wheelchair.
That was because he abruptly saw that the entire room was filled with countless pairs of densely packed eyes; these eyes were fixed in every corner of the room, their gaze on everyone present.
What was even more disturbing to Colin was that the woman inside the room was covered with tightly packed eyes that swept over everyone one by one.
But this eerie scene arrived as suddenly as it had disappeared.
By the time Colin blinked, everything had returned to normal…
“All set,” the woman sitting motionless in her chair from the beginning smiled and then pressed a button.
“Ding-a-ling.”
The clear ring of a bell sounded from inside the hall, followed by footsteps outside, and Colin saw Qin Chuan and others walking in again.
“This feels just like waiting outside the school for parents picking up their kids.”
Colin muttered to himself and then continued to be wheeled out, and before leaving the hall, he caught a glimpse in the corner of his eye of the woman still sitting there motionless with a smile, and after leaving, there came the sound of chains, as if something was being tied up.
“That woman’s status is really bad, feels like she could lose control any moment…”
Thoughts churned in Colin’s head, and at this moment, Qin Chuan who was pushing him said, “If all goes as expected, we’ll be colleagues soon. It’s my first time leading a team, but it shouldn’t be a problem; everyone assigned to this leadership mission is elite, and I’m no exception.”
Uh, is it really appropriate for you to boast about yourself like this when you can’t even cook a meal without burning it?
Colin uttered a noncommittal “hmm” without responding, and Qin Chuan continued, “By the way, what was the task you received?”
“It was something like this…”
Colin didn’t conceal it and showed Qin Chuan the content on the “small” parchment scroll, but as soon as he finished looking, Qin Chuan couldn’t help but furrow his brows.
“What’s wrong?”
“No, not quite sure, just feels a bit off. Hold on, let me ask.”
After speaking, Qin Chuan walked to the side with a puzzled face and started talking into his earpiece, and it was several minutes before he came back over.
Before Colin could ask, he took the initiative to say, “We need to double-check the situation with Black Forest Subway Station, the results will be in shortly, I shouldn’t speculate without them. Also, regarding your other two teammates,
“They’re also people from this batch, right over there, let’s go meet them.”
He gestured toward a nearby spot where a group had gathered, among them two with remarkably grim physical appearances—one was the burn victim Colin had shared a ride with recently, the other a middle-aged man he hadn’t seen before, wearing a mask and coughing occasionally, his complexion ashen.
When Colin arrived, one of the official attendants looked puzzled and said, “Xiao Chuan, since when did Black Forest Subway Station have a sewer? I’m in charge of this area, and I’ve heard nothing about it.
“And besides, a subway station isn’t likely to be built with a large sewer system, right?”
Hearing this, Colin suddenly remembered the task description for this place, “a large sewer system that doesn’t make sense.”
“No idea, I’m an art student, asking me about this is off-topic. But, we’ll know when it’s confirmed by the authorities in a bit.”
Qin Chuan joked, “Maybe it was those German folks who built a sewer system a hundred years ago; if you dig around, you might even find a German engineer wrapped up in oilcloth.”
As the several people chatted, a dozen minutes swiftly passed.
Then, the few who were waiting soon received a message—
There indeed was no such thing as a large sewer system in that place, but just as relevant, someone had reported the discovery of a strange entrance inside the subway station.

chapters.title: Chapter 178 - 178 178 The Invaded Office_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 178: Chapter 178: The Invaded Office_1 Chapter 178: Chapter 178: The Invaded Office_1 In a special office, a woman with an indistinct face, dressed in professional attire and long white legs, sat upright behind a desk.
At the moment, she was holding a list of pending incidents, seemingly perusing it.
Within this list, detailed accounts of some investigations that had been completed, yet due to various reasons, no further action had been taken, were recorded.
“Shadow in the Lake,” “Midnight Empty Bus,” “The Nonexistent Hospital,” “Ancestral Tomb No. 773,” “Desert Blood Lake,” “Abnormality at the Seaside Watchtower,”…
Lady Bunny’s gaze swiftly moved from one name to another, looking for a suitable new task for Colin to execute.
After a while, her eyes stopped on one named “The Hospital That Shouldn’t Exist.”
This task had been shelved for quite some time, and now it was worth considering taking action.
Of course, the main reason was that much of the key intelligence for this task seemed to have already been uncovered by an employee; with careful handling, there shouldn’t be any major screw-ups.
After pondering for a brief moment, she decided to assign this as Colin and others’ “entry trial.”
It was just then that a line of information appeared before her.
[This employee is already executing a task, please avoid assigning two separate tasks at the same time, should you wish to continue this action, please obtain permission before attempting again…]
Seeing this message, Lady Bunny tilted her head, as if making a frown,
“Who is interfering with my affairs?”She reached out and grabbed at the air, then as if pulling out a sheet of A4 paper from nowhere, and on this paper, Colin’s details were clearly recorded.
And it was clear to see that Colin was currently on a task, investigating something about the third layer of the sewer.
It was obvious that this was not a task she had issued.
Seeing this, she seemed to realize something and slowly pulled open a drawer, taking out a stamp, ready to use her authority to forcibly cancel this task.
But it was at this moment that a sharp “squeak squeak squeak” sound began to emerge from the plain office.
Lady Bunny turned to look and saw a gap in the office floor from where palm-sized shadows surged out like a fountain and crawled toward her, seemingly intent on devouring her.
She remained unpanicked, her tone calm as she spoke,
“Returners? Invading my place, are you trying to make an example of me?”
…
Meanwhile, Colin and the others had once again arrived at the Black Forest Subway Station and encountered the so-called entrance inside one of the men’s restrooms.
It was at the very back of the restroom, resembling a door that looked unremarkable. The exact time of its appearance was unclear, as no subway passenger paying a visit would notice it.
It was first discovered by a cleaning lady who was responsible for maintaining the cleanliness of the restroom but found an extra door in the afternoon that seemed out of place when opened out of curiosity.
By now, the subway station had been temporarily closed down, and groups of armed personnel thoroughly blockaded the restroom.
“It’s a shame the door is just this size, too small to expand and bring in something more formidable,” Qin Chuan sighed beside Colin, his arms crossed.
If possible, they would like to drive an armored vehicle in, but unfortunately, that seemed impossible.
After breaking through the wall next to the door, everything appeared normal; they didn’t dare to damage the door, fearing it might cause the anomaly to disappear and then fail the mission.
In addition, they had sent some drones and whatnot in there; the signal was fine, but the images were unclear…
Experts behind the scenes speculated that it might be due to some kind of pollution.
“We’ll have to go in ourselves now,” said Colin.
Colin was still seated in his wheelchair, but this time, the officials had considerately switched it out for the electric wheelchair he had wanted to buy while he was ill but had never been willing to splurge on, which could go up to 30 kilometers per hour at its highest speed.
As he spoke, he glanced at the sewer entrance ahead, which was pitch-black. Even the light that shone in seemed suppressed, unable to illuminate very far.
However, unlike the sewers he remembered, there was no smell coming from inside, nor were there any signs of use.
It seemed, it had been abandoned for quite some time…
“It seems so. But it’s not all bad news; at least electronic devices work inside,” Qin Chuan said as he waved to someone behind him. Eight fully armed people approached, their movements faintly giving off mechanical sounds, presumably wearing some kind of exoskeleton equipment.
“Will it be dangerous for us to go in? Cough cough cough…” A middle-aged man with a grey complexion said, unable to suppress his coughing halfway through his sentence.
“There shouldn’t be any danger. In the hour that we’ve been here, someone has already completed their assignment, and the others are almost done too. This suggests that the first task on the job is relatively easy. Plus, we just used some sort of premonition technique to test, and there’s no problem…”
Don’t say anymore, brother; I feel so sick I could puke…
Colin, watching Qin Chuan talk confidently, felt an inexplicable anxiety at the bottom of his heart. Looking at the entrance, he increasingly felt something was wrong, but couldn’t put his finger on what exactly. After all, there was no sense of danger.
Moreover, the nature of this onboarding task was puzzling, suddenly presenting a countdown.
This forced Colin, who had initially planned to choose a better time to enter the next day, to go in now.
After a while, Colin saw the group bring in three nearly two-meter-tall cylindrical robots.
“Hey, Explorer Type 2 Detection Robots, worth millions each, can analyze the physical and mental status of all present, as well as any environmental dangers in real-time… Alright, strap on the protective gear and let’s get moving,” Qin Chuan explained to everyone, then helped Colin and others prepare their oxygen tanks before giving the others the signal to start the operation.
First, the three cylindrical robots entered, followed by six mechanical dogs carrying a significant amount of supplies, then the eight armed personnel, as well as Qin Chuan, Xia Liufang, and three other unrecognizable people. Colin and his group were the last to enter.
A total of sixteen people.
As Colin entered, he just caught sight of the cylindrical robots’ casings cracking open, extending two machine gun barrels to display their professional ethical standards to everyone.
Operating the mechanical wheelchair from behind, Colin pulled his face mask slightly and took a stealthy breath, faintly detecting the acrid smell of gunpowder lingering in the air.
“Official equipment is just different from private gear. The quantity of these supplies could probably cripple a subway station, couldn’t it?” Colin thought to himself, then looked again at the large sewer in front of him.
The originally dark sewer was now completely illuminated by the lights on the robots.
It was more appropriate to call this a massive underground reinforced concrete hall supported by numerous pillars rather than a sewer. The cold and desolate hall was covered with thick dust and some faded garbage bags.
Yet, whether it was the smell or something else, Colin was sure that there shouldn’t be any danger on this level.
However, although there was no danger, no one dared to let down their guard.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 179 - 179 179 Im Colin when you see this..._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 179: Chapter 179 I’m Colin, when you see this…_1 Chapter 179: Chapter 179 I’m Colin, when you see this…_1 Following the “mission” instructions, Colin and his team kept advancing through the concrete and stone-pillared sewer system for about seven or eight minutes before they finally came across a downward turn, marked by an “↑-2” sign made of special anti-corrosion material.
Still led by the three robust cylindrical robots, the group then turned and entered the second sub-level.
Upon descending, Colin noticed that the second sub-level seemed much more dilapidated than the first, but other than that, there wasn’t much difference.
However, shortly after entering, their protective suits’ built-in earphones started blaring an alarm.
“Anomaly detected! Anomaly detected! Anomaly detected!”
Several infrared rays from the cylindrical robots pointed towards a specific area up ahead.
Following their direction, Colin and the others saw piles upon piles of small animal skeletons on the ground, covered with short, black fur….
They didn’t need the robots to identify what creatures they were.
“Rats?”
Colin was surprised, noting that each heap of skeletal remains held at least thousands, if not tens of thousands of rats, with some areas where the bones were stacked over three meters high, resembling small hills.
“How are we supposed to deal with this?” an employee gasped, speaking with a touch of fear, “What if they come back to life?”
“We can’t deal with it for now,” Qin Chuan was also somewhat worried.
If there were a few hundred or even a few thousand or ten thousand, it wouldn’t be much of a concern, but the sudden appearance of tens or hundreds of millions of rat skeletons was quite frightening.
The main issue was the sheer number; they simply had no way to handle it.
At the same time, they also wondered what could have killed so many rats and piled them up like this.
“Let’s wait for the robotic analysis report,” Qin Chuan reassured everyone.
Then, one of the cylindrical robots picked up a rat skeleton, analyzed it inside its body, and a minute later reported the findings:
“Preliminary estimate, the creature died approximately thirty to fifty years ago, cause of death unknown, no obvious injuries observed, no remnants of internal organs, flesh, or other tissues other than skeleton and fur, appears to have been stripped by unknown means.
“Within a one hundred meter radius of the scene, no living organisms or ‘anomaly indexes’ fluctuations were detected.
“Return route to the alert point is unaffected…
“…
“If you wish to proceed further, it is recommended to install a ‘Reality Stabilization Device’ here to prevent accidents.”
Listening to the robot’s voice in their ears, Qin Chuan, Colin, and the others considered for a moment and decided to continue on.
Soon, Colin saw several silver metallic columns, more than a meter tall and as thick as an arm, being taken out and placed into the ground. After a few seconds, they emitted a “beeping” sound, with green light dots pulsating to indicate normal operation.
“This must be the ‘Reality Stabilization Device,’ after being put in place I feel the tyrannical nature of ‘Beastification’ inside me has been cut right off, my voice silenced. Other items seem to have been sliced as well, and continue to be suppressed…” Colin muttered softly.
After the team finished setting up, a slender employee took out a slightly yellowed piece of paper from his pocket and stared intently at it.
Under his gaze, black text began to emerge on the paper.
“You try to enter the third sub-level underground, and although you encounter even more rat skeletons along the way and face no danger, during the investigation below you make some unexpected and shocking discoveries…”
“After staying a while longer, you’re eager to return, intent on communicating these findings to the outside world.”
“….”
“Eventually, you successfully send the message back.”
Seeing this content, he visibly relaxed, then passed the parchment to Qin Chuan and the other colleagues.
Colin, sitting in his wheelchair, also saw the text displayed on it.
“The ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’? Isn’t the official fragment supposed to be used directly in the mind? And why does it feel like the official ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’ has even more riddlers and nonsensical talk?”
Colin stared at the first line of content, unable to help himself from complaining internally that this thing only mentioned a shocking discovery but never specified what the discovery was…
Not waiting to ponder it for long, Qin Chuan signaled everyone to be cautious and they started moving.
Just like the ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’ had said, along their way they saw even more rat carcasses than before, piling up like continuous small hills throughout the sewage space on level negative two.
The death symbol represented by those bones made Colin and the others feel an overwhelming sense of oppression, as if they couldn’t breathe, even though they hadn’t actually encountered any danger yet.
A few minutes later, Colin and his companions arrived at the entrance leading down to level negative three.
At that moment, aside from the increased number of rat skeletons, there were no other anomalies along the way…
They detected nothing wrong, Colin saw nothing wrong, and considering the “guarantee” from the ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’, along with the thought that Miss Bunny might have specifically arranged this task, he didn’t suggest turning back.
Afterward, glancing back at the dense mountains of rat carcasses, they entered the third level.
Upon entering, before they even started to explore, they found a corpse at the corner—it was a human body!
The body was covered in dust and seated against the mud wall, so long dead that it had become a mummy. Uniquely, its legs weren’t human but rather two mechanical limbs.
At that moment, Colin’s gaze sharpened as he looked steadfastly beside the body and noticed a piece of parchment carelessly cast aside, halfway unfolded.
“Is it a company employee? Who died here?”
Inner shock gripped Colin, and Qin Chuan, noting Colin’s reaction, also looked over and furrowed his eyebrows.
After quickly ensuring there were no issues in the surrounding area, a robot stepped forward, picked up the parchment with its mechanical arm, unfolded and photographed it, then transmitted the photo to a device resembling a mobile phone in Qin Chuan’s hands.
Generally, this was done because the parchment might carry unknown dangers.
But, for some reason, signals like images couldn’t be transmitted inside this sewage space, resulting in a blurry mess when the photo came through.
And as a result, the robot was also disrupted and couldn’t read the content on it.
Left with no choice, an armed individual was sent to take a preliminary look. After a few minutes with no issues detected in him, one of the extraordinary personnel accompanying them was allowed to observe.
However, after reading the content, his face became strange and cautious as he cast a glance at Colin.
“Qin Chuan, come take a look.”
“What’s wrong?”
“Come see for yourself.”
After a while, Colin saw the two men standing shoulder to shoulder, both looking at him with consistent expressions—strange, cautious, and tinged with a hint of hostility.
Could it be that they’ve discovered my secret account? Colin was puzzled and felt it was unlikely.
No matter what, he couldn’t link how parchment left by another employee, dead for who knows how long, could hold any information that revealed his secret…
“Maybe I should take a look too?”
Colin spoke up, curious about what was actually on the parchment.
After some discussion, they agreed to his request. They had the robot bring the parchment to him while covertly aiming their guns at him, ready for any accidents that might occur.
Colin was somewhat displeased internally, but kept quiet. When the robot presented the parchment, he shifted his gaze to see the content written in dark brown ink on it.
At that moment, as he read the first line of text, he was taken aback.
“I am Colin, and by the time you read this paper, I should already be dead…”
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 180 - 180 180 The Future Colin_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 180: Chapter 180: The Future “Colin”_1 Chapter 180: Chapter 180: The Future “Colin”_1 I’m not me, don’t talk nonsense…
Colin’s pupils shrank as he rapidly denied the possibility within his heart. How could he be dead when he was alive and well?
‘No wonder everyone who glanced at this paper then looked at me weirdly. I only read the first sentence and didn’t continue. Even I am starting to doubt if I really am who I think I am.’
After taking a deep breath, he continued to read, to confirm whether it was just a big misunderstanding due to identical names.
“On December 31, 2031, as I write this will, the world has deteriorated to an irreparable state. Multiple S Level Disasters have broken out consecutively, reflecting on each other, and civilization has completely collapsed. The extinction of humanity is just a matter of time…”
“However, before that, relying on the missions from ‘Bonfire,’ we at The Hague Shelter were able to hold on amidst the calamities from ‘Twilight’s Children,’ but unfortunately, as the world fell apart, ‘Bonfire’ seemed to have encountered issues too and stopped assigning missions…”
“We don’t have much time left, so we decided to take a risk by using some methods to open a path to leave this world.”
“Sadly, if you’re reading this parchment, it means our route failed, that guy deceived us, turned us into sacrifices, and even caused a bigger problem, an S Level Disaster related to The Rat…”
“Its purpose is different from other disasters; it has a strong desire to leave this world. In a sense, I even suspect that the dysfunction of ‘Bonfire’ is related to it, and even that all the S Level Disasters were triggered by its planning…”
“The related content, I cannot write here, it remains only in the shelter…”
“If you are just some scavenging survivors who stumbled upon this, you can leave now, there isn’t anything here.”
“If you’re someone from another area who fled here still in search of salvation, I think you can give up already. At least, this region no longer holds that possibility, but of course, you could try to search the shelter to see if there is anything you need.”
“If you are a group of people who are also seeking a path to leave, in the shelter, there are a few other projects that we didn’t get to attempt…”
“My only request is…”
“if you could give some assistance to those inside the shelter, or… at least don’t kill them, that would be enough.”
…
The contents of the parchment were not written in system text, but rather with a kind of dark brown pigment, dabbed on with fingertips in a crooked and twisted manner. The farther down he read, the more erratic and weak the writing became, as if the person who wrote it was losing strength.
“Is it blood?”
Colin took a deep breath, not letting his thoughts wander too far. The contents of the paper were far more significant than whatever material was used to write it, but first, a misconception had to be clarified.
He looked up at the people around him and said, “As you can see, I’m sitting right here, fine and dandy. Aside from the name, I didn’t see anything on that paper that proves it has anything to do with me. Maybe it’s just a coincidence. Can’t your robot perform various checks? Just a DNA test should do it.”
“That’s possible.” They did not object and let the robot proceed to acquire a tissue sample from the body and took a little body fluid from Colin, then began the comparison.
The result came out very quickly—
The DNA of the person sitting in the wheelchair was nearly identical to the one sitting against the wall.
Well, this is awkward…
Upon hearing this result, everyone looked at Colin, and even he fell silent—Could it really be me?
Or could it actually be a future him?
“Could the machine have made a mistake?”
Colin raised his objection, and then two more tests were conducted by other machines, yielding no discrepancies in the results.
This definitely made the atmosphere a bit delicate…
Which means…
“Do you have an identical twin?” Xia Liufang finally asked, seeing as only an identical twin could explain it all.
Otherwise, that body was really unexplainable.
“If I remember correctly, there was none,” he said.
Colin shook his head, slightly annoyed, “But, based on the information above, is there a possibility that the dead one is me from a decade or so in the future, rather than the present me?”
“How is that possible…” The middle-aged uncle in his forties or fifties couldn’t believe it. He had also looked at the parchment while testing DNA but hadn’t looked at it much and didn’t remember some details.
“It is indeed a possibility. Who knows, this place might be a future area that came to the present in an unknowable way, or it might be a Parallel World that is ten years ahead of our world in terms of time…” The person who had been staring at Colin spoke up, and he seemed to be a practioner of the “Fate Propeller” path, now starting to speculate.
Compared to others, they who were adept at predicting the future, were quite open to this kind of possibility.
“Indeed,” Colin agreed, and then glanced at the body on the ground. He felt that the man did indeed look a bit like himself, with thin, slightly curly hair, and on the body, he could vaguely see a shadow of himself.
It’s just…
“Why do I feel like I’m disabled no matter what world it is?”
Colin glanced at the mechanical prosthetics on the corpse’s legs and couldn’t help but complain inwardly.
Afterward, the group analyzed a bit and concluded that there was a certain probability that this suddenly appearing place was a Parallel World from the future.
And that person on the ground could be “Colin” of this world.
“It might be due to some reason that Colin of this world has established a strong connection with our Colin, causing both to approach each other under some guidance. In the study of ‘Fate’…”
The suspected “Fate Propeller” wielder began to speak, attempting to explain the precedents, but was interrupted before finishing,
“Say something we can understand,” Qin Chuan reminded him.
“Oh, it might be related to the Ancient God mentioned above,” the other person finished and furrowed his brows, “Regardless, we must report these messages quickly, because according to the description above, there might be something that slipped from this Parallel World to ours.
“Also, if this Inner World is destroyed by some uncontrollable S Level Disaster, that disaster might appear in our world as well.
“Upon arriving, I discovered something crucial, the ‘Book of Fate’ indeed does not deceive me…” he murmured fervently to himself as he uttered the last sentence.
“So do we continue the investigation, or do we send some people back first?” Colin asked. They had just arrived, and the progress of the investigation regarding this place was less than ten percent.
This suggested there was still much that hadn’t been uncovered…
“The countdown is less than one hour; if we go back now, we won’t have time to return,” they said.
“And… I always feel there is a lot more here that we don’t understand…”
“As for sending some people back, it’s best not to split up at this time.”
After a brief discussion, everyone decided to continue delving into the matter and took “Colin’s” body with them, planning to drag it back for research later on.
Regrettably, Colin did not see items like “Time Stasis” on this body, he didn’t know if they were lost, or if they never were obtained.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 181 - 181 181 Trap Task_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 181: Chapter 181 Trap Task!_1 Chapter 181: Chapter 181 Trap Task!_1 At this point, the third level of the underground sewer no longer showed any sign of rat skeletons; they seemed to have completely vanished.
After advancing deeper for a few minutes, they came upon a group of people seated on the ground, surrounded by others. There were fifteen individuals altogether, sitting motionless.
As they approached, Colin and the rest saw that these people had turned into mummies, much like “Future Colin” had, each seated at a certain distance from the others and seemingly arranged in some sort of formation.
Hesitating for a moment to ensure the anomaly index hadn’t risen, they proceeded to inspect the scene.
Then…
“How is this possible?!”
Exclamation after exclamation echoed through the sewer.
The group discovered that these “corpses” had some identification which matched with each of the fifteen present, which left Colin confused and shocked, yet also relieved.
After all, this meant he was no longer the prime suspect.
With each corpse’s identity confirmed, the progress on Colin’s parchment rapidly increased, giving him an uneasy feeling.
“I feel like this is some kind of evil ceremony orchestrated by the Ancient God mentioned earlier, designed to bring together people from two identical worlds through some means, like connecting magnets…” one official speculated with an air of trepidation.
“That’s not right. I don’t understand how they knew to choose us. We only gathered together today…” Qin Chuan frowned.
At that moment, someone suddenly exclaimed:
“Wait, there seems to be another body over there!”
Hearing this, everyone was momentarily stunned and then felt a chill in their hearts. They had only entered as a group of sixteen—it made no sense for there to be a seventeenth person!
Could someone else have followed them in?
Colin looked in the direction the voice had indicated and saw a body lying not far away.
This corpse was more damaged than the others, reduced to a pile of white bones with no trace of hair or clothing.
Next to it on the ground, there were some hastily scrawled words that looked like they were left behind while the person was still alive:
“…be careful… I have been replaced…”
“Who has been replaced?”
Everyone was puzzled, but only Colin, looking at the pile of white bones in front of him, felt a sense of familiarity. He could tell it was a female, and there was something indescribably familiar about the skeleton, but he couldn’t immediately place who it might be…
His certainty about the gender wasn’t due to any medical knowledge but purely because he had seen enough skeletal remains recently to recognize it.
Soon, a robot took tissue samples, and the results came back within minutes.
“The deceased is Liping, cause of death unknown, suspected to have died within the last three years…”
When the robot reported the name and identity, Colin was certain he didn’t know the person. However, Qin Chuan and five other extraordinary agents looked shocked.
“Two or three years? That’s a joke! How could it be her? She is… She is an Eighth Level Agent! How could she have died here for no reason?”
An Eighth Level Agent?
A flash of insight crossed Colin’s mind, and he remembered a woman with a dignified smile, almost like a stone statue.
“No, a few years ago, it seemed like after returning from a task, she began to excuse herself from appearing publicly due to health reasons, delegating much of her work to others. Even the situation here could possibly be related to this ‘Liping’…” Qin Chuan spoke about some past events.
As he spoke, the others grew increasingly silent.
An Eighth Level Agent, a figure who would typically be the sole authority in a province, might now only be an imposter?
Who replaced her?
“If it is really an impostor capable of attacking an Eighth Level Agent, then it’s definitely beyond our ability to cope with. Take these bones with us.”
“Just in time, the head of the Southern Region is right here, we can report to him first…”
Meanwhile, Colin’s anxiety grew denser, but his unease was not due to the Eighth Level Personnel they mentioned. Instead, it stemmed from the progression of the mission, especially upon seeing that the mission progress had already reached ninety-seven percent. He felt an inexplicable sense of suffocation.
Regardless of his unease, he didn’t actually sense any immediate danger…
However, it was at this moment that he suddenly had an epiphany. While everyone else’s attention was elsewhere, he switched to the “large size” parchment and saw that a new task had been issued.
[ “Escape the sewer area before the investigation task progress reaches one hundred percent!” ]
Upon seeing this task, Colin’s pupils constricted. He suddenly realized that this task might actually have been issued by Lady Bunny.
The previous task was likely a trap!
Immediately looking at everyone else, who were still in shock, Colin knew that convincing them to leave right now would be nearly impossible. He discreetly pulled out a card from his pocket—
“Fusion Card: Smiling Mountain of Corpses.”
The next instant, the robot’s body flashed with red light, and an alarm suddenly went off!
“Warning! The abnormality index is climbing sharply! Warning! The abnormality index is climbing sharply. The threat level has reached C Level and has exceeded our personnel’s capability to handle!”
Several infrared rays aimed at a certain point, and as everyone looked in that direction, they saw that on the ground, the dried flesh and bones of about a dozen of their “future selves” were melting and converging towards the center.
This process was terrifyingly swift, and by the time they snapped back to reality, a massive black flesh orb with two thick arms let out a piercing shriek that shook their hearts.
“Please, Little Fist Stone!”
Colin silently gave the command for it to launch an attack.
“Run! Keep up!”
Qin Chuan and the others didn’t even think, they immediately abandoned the mission and ordered everyone to beat a hasty retreat.
As they retreated, the machine’s guns sprayed gunfire, a barrage of fire raining down upon it, blasting the terrifying flesh orb with the gaping mouth into countless pieces.
It seemed as though they had inflicted fatal damage, but as these pieces hit the ground, they liquified and flowed back to the main body…
But from the beginning, they had not expected ordinary methods to work; the attack was only meant to slow it down.
“┗|｀O′|┛ Ahhh~~”
Enraged screams erupted from Corpse Mountain, and Colin could sense it seemed to hold some grudge, but it had no choice but to maintain a distance from them, as per the requirement, and play a chasing game.
In their frantic escape, everyone was too preoccupied to notice any issues with the acting of “Smiling Mountain of Corpses,” as they were running for their lives.
Only Colin was a bit more relaxed, simply turning his wheelchair’s speed to the maximum and racing along the trail he had left behind.
Time after time, “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” nearly caught them, but fortunately, each time they escaped by the skin of their teeth. Eventually, after about ten minutes, they returned to the door they had initially entered through.
Yet, when they arrived at this spot, they instinctively stopped in their tracks, not proceeding any further, but simply staring ahead blankly.
In their eyes, outside the door was not the lavatory they had come from but a degraded world covered in twilight. It was also at this moment that Colin saw on his “small size” parchment that the onboarding task had been completed.
The price of completion was…
They all seemed to have been displaced.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 182 - 182 182 Mie City._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 182: Chapter 182 Mie City._1 Chapter 182: Chapter 182 Mie City._1 Outside the narrow door, an endless twilight shrouded a strange city devoid of any vitality, where every building standing under the dusk seemed like an old man with one foot in the grave, surrounded by the air of twilight, not yet dead but close to death.
Gurgle…
Colin swallowed hard, his expression extremely unsightly. With his rich experience, he clearly understood that he and the others had unknowingly arrived in another world.
And the fact that there was no “Descent Protocol” prompt during the process indicated that it was not through official channels…
“Was it that suspected ‘Eighth Level Agent’ who did this? What was her purpose? Just to throw me over here? Is it targeting me, or others as well? And what about that thing, that future ‘me’ mentioned, that slipped away?”
A mass of confusion erupted in Colin’s heart.
At that moment, a mechanical voice rang out: “Warning, connection with the outside world is interrupted, the abnormality index of the area outside the door is extremely high, please proceed with caution…”
Any clear-eyed person could see that something was wrong outside. Did that even need to be said?
Colin grumbled internally and discreetly put away the “Fusion Card: Smiling Mountain of Corpses”.
“Lock on ‘temporary number-1’ creature lost, please be careful to avoid surprise attacks.”
“That thing’s gone?” Qin Chuan and the others sighed with relief upon hearing this, remembering that after they ran to the second sublevel, that monster did not continue the pursuit.
They wondered if it was due to some kind of territorial limitation.
But now was not the time to worry about that; the situation at hand was even more troublesome…
“Cough cough cough, where is this place?” The middle-aged man looked ahead with an ashen face.
“I don’t know either, but it seems like it’s not our world. It could be… the future?” Qin Chuan said uncertainly. Now that they were sure the monster behind them had disappeared, they didn’t feel as urgent a need to leave.
“If it really is, what should we do?”
“I…” Qin Chuan looked at the others, exchanging glances. Most had no good ideas, and for the moment, couldn’t think of what to do next.
This was the first time he had encountered such a situation; he had never even seen it before.
Seeing that the group was directionless, Colin spoke up: “That ‘Eighth Level Agent’ you mentioned, what was she doing during the incident, or besides what we’ve already discussed, was there anything unusual?”
If they could figure out this information, then they would not be so passive moving forward.
“The missions that require an ‘Eighth Level Agent’ are highly confidential. We couldn’t possibly know.” someone shook their head.
So, that line of inquiry was at a dead end… Colin rubbed his forehead, about to speak, when the only woman present, Xia Liufang, said, “I do know something unusual; I vaguely remember that she seemed to be going to deal with the followers of the ‘Mother of the Red Moon’…”
The Red Moon, always the damn Red Moon, it feels like every issue on Earth was caused by these bastards… Colin couldn’t help but curse internally.
Indeed, nowadays it seemed that no matter the issue, their shadows could always be seen lurking behind.
Thinking this, Colin asked about the situation with the “Mother of the Red Moon” followers, trying to understand why they were causing trouble…
“I’m not clear on the specifics. According to them, besides wanting to summon the ‘Red Moon’ to save the world, they seem to continuously cause various disasters and troubles. Well, if I have to say, it’s like they’re pure villains—no, to be more accurate, they’re like a bunch of shit-stirrers causing trouble everywhere.” Qin Chuan provided some well-known information.
“Sigh, these details aren’t very helpful…”
Colin massaged his forehead, glanced at the world outside, then picked up the “small” parchment and looked over it.
The words “mission completed” on it seemed almost like a mockery to them.
Moreover, they weren’t sure if it was because they’d come to this place, but although they had completed the mission, it had not been settled.
The parchment seemed stuck, unable to perform any action.
“However, since we were able to come here, there must be a way to leave. That future ‘you’ mentioned it, didn’t he? There should be other projects within their refuge. Maybe we can try that,” Xia Liufang suggested.
“That’s the only option now, to look for information on that refuge,” replied Colin and the others with nods.
After confirming one last time that the bizarre sewer space had only one exit, they passed through the door one by one, leaving the sewer district behind.
The robot led the way without detecting anything, followed by the others. The anticipated scenario where the door would disappear halfway did not occur, and they all emerged successfully.
As he stepped into the world covered by the twilight light, Colin distinctly felt some indescribable discomfort, but he wasn’t sure what it was.
He looked back at the door behind him, seeing it situated atop a building, like a broken bridge, and it didn’t vanish with their exit.
“If we encounter any trouble, we can consider going back to the first sublevel of the sewer,” someone suggested.
It seemed that as long as they stayed on the first sublevel, they wouldn’t suffer attacks.
Of course, Colin knew that the entire sewer district was safe, but apart from being “safe,” there was nothing else there, and he had a feeling that if they stayed, they might never be able to leave.
The longer they stayed, the stronger this feeling became.
Looking away, Colin looked up at the sky where there was no sun to be seen, but judging from the shadows of buildings, it seemed that the yellow light might be falling directly from the center of the sky, making the whole city look desolate and dying.
Then, the team began their move, aiming to find a large mall or a park of some sort.
According to Qin Chuan and other official personnel, if there was a refuge in this place, it was likely built in these types of places, which is why they chose this as their first direction of exploration.
While moving, they tried to stick to the shadows cast by the tall buildings, avoiding direct exposure to the yellow light to prevent any accidents.
After all, the future “Colin” had mentioned that the civilization of this world was destroyed by multiple S Level disasters, and who knows if this eerie twilight could be one of them.
Not much was said along the way. After scanning over buildings, streets, and shattered windows for nearly an hour, they had gained no more information other than the fact that this city was in ruins.
“This place doesn’t seem futuristic either, except for a coconut juice advert that bragged ‘I’ve been drinking it since childhood, for 41 years,’ it doesn’t seem like there’s any evidence of the future here. There are no noticeable changes, no particularly new things.” Colin’s gaze moved away from a faded coconut juice bottle on the ground as he looked forward at a street sign, which referred to ‘Yangcheng’s People’s Park.’ This suggested that they might be in a somewhat renowned southern metropolis of the motherland.
However, as of now, it seemed to have nothing to do with prosperity.
..
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 183 - 183 183 The World Where Humanity is Defeated_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 183: Chapter 183: The World Where Humanity is Defeated_1 Chapter 183: Chapter 183: The World Where Humanity is Defeated_1 Everywhere lay decayed and shattered; plants extinct and devoid of life, the “survivors” mentioned on the parchment were nowhere to be seen.
However, after walking a distance further, they suddenly stopped…
“Fuck, what is this thing?”
Upon hearing the exclamation, Colin turned his head following his gaze and saw, on the ground not too far away, a pair of enormous handprints that looked as though something had fallen from above and left them behind.
Looking up, he indeed saw a huge hole in the building next to the handprints.
In his mind, Colin simulated the scene at the time, thinking that perhaps some gigantic creature had jumped from there, then landed on the road with both hands, smashing a big pit, and then slowly walked towards the distance…
Was this the “Twilight’s Child” that caused this area to be lifeless?
Colin was secretly shocked and glanced at the others’ faces, finding they too seemed thoughtful, clearly sharing a similar guess.
“Analysis in progress, the imprint highly matches the human palm structure, but is abnormally large; depth of the pit is thirty centimeters, width two meters, length five meters, suspected to have fallen from the seventeenth floor, estimated body weight at least three tons…”
The conclusion drawn by the exploration robot’s remote scanning sent a chill through everyone.
Even Colin furrowed his brows, unable to imagine what kind of monster had left this handprint.
Nevertheless, as the investigation continued and they arrived at the city center, they saw more buildings destroyed by some kind of gigantic creature.
“Judging by these marks, the monster that came here seems to have been more than one or two.”
Colin scanned the surroundings and felt that this could be described as the most central and prosperous part of the city, now just like grass gnawed by dogs, disordered without a trace of intactness.
Moreover, they finally saw some traces of the people of this world after combatting the monsters.
And from the robot’s analysis, it was determined that the used weapons included but were not limited to various calibers of bullets, large-caliber shells, and other kinds of common conventional weapons…
“I remember this place, one hundred and fifty thousand per square…”
One of the armed personnel holding his gun couldn’t help but lament.
Traces of humans and other creatures had long disappeared here, leaving only the bare steel-reinforced concrete jungle…
Listining to his lamentation, Colin’s gaze swept over various tanks, armored vehicles, and even the remnants of armed helicopters, faintly feeling the intensity of the battle from the residual smell of gunpowder in the air.
However, unfortunately, from the remaining debris, it seemed that the humans here had not won the fight.
“Have you guys noticed, there are no human remains at all?” someone couldn’t help but speak up.
“Not just human remains…”
Colin shook his head, “No remains of any creatures are to be seen, not just humans, but also no rats, insects, or even trees.”
Animals left no trace behind, and plants disappeared as well, except for those that were turned into “miraculously spared” furniture.
The thing that caused the disaster seemed to have taken away the majority of the biomass.
“The outbreak of a battle here proves our previous guess was not wrong, there is indeed a refuge nearby; otherwise, there wouldn’t have been a defensive battle here.” Colin’s gaze went beyond the military debris, ready to head with the others towards that shopping mall over there.
But it was at this moment that his heart sank, feeling as if something were moving towards them.
In the air, there was a faint smell of a very slight putrefaction…
However, before he could figure out how to warn the others, they all heard a strange roar coming from the back and side direction.
Heavy footsteps followed one after another…
Some enormous creature seemed to be approaching, neither hurriedly nor slowly.
“Abnormal creature detected within a five hundred meter radius! Please evacuate immediately! Please evacuate immediately…”
Three robots simultaneously flashed red lights and sounded alarms.
However, at this moment, Colin suddenly felt the ground tremble and an image emerged in his mind—
A dull yellow hand reached out from underground, grasping him along with the wheelchair in its palm, then squeezing forcefully, his internal organs and bones crushed and spilling out between the fingers along with a tomato-colored sauce.
“Deadly Insight”!
Immediately, Colin paid no mind to whether he would expose himself or not, and like a medical miracle, he “struggled to stand” from the wheelchair. He then lunged at the two people beside him, knocking them aside, and moving several meters away from his original position.
Before Qin Chuan and the others could wonder why Colin’s strength was so great or what he was suddenly doing, in the next second they saw the ground bulge upward and break apart as a dull yellow hand reached out from underneath.
The recently acquired electric wheelchair, caught in its grasp, was crushed with a snap into a tangled mess.
And during this process, something from underground seemed to be crawling towards the surface.
Ratatatatatatata!
Eight elite armed personnel reacted immediately, firing at the thing to suppress it, with dozens of bullets showering down on its massive hand in a short amount of time.
But such an attack was merely an annoyance to it, as the holes created by the gunfire were quickly filled by other flesh.
And within a matter of seconds, they saw a giant, decaying humanoid creature covered with countless gravel emerge from the ground.
For some reason, its body was severed at the navel, leaving only half of it. It supported itself on the ground with its massive hands, its sand-covered body giving off a strong stench of blood and rotting flesh.
And although it had a human form, there were no facial features where the head should be, only a third of the face occupied by a fleshly crevice that contained an eye filled with malice and blood vessels—
“Twilight’s Children”!
At the first sight of it, the word immediately popped into Colin’s mind.
It was at this time that Qin Chuan and others put distance between themselves and the creature, and without any hesitation, they attacked it simultaneously.
Sheets of yellow talismans flew and stuck to its body, causing it to abruptly sink, and on the talismans, one could barely make out the word “gravity.”
The creature suspected of being “Twilight’s Children” let out a strange roar from its chest, then writhed, and another hand stretched out from under its armpit, reaching straight for the people.
At the same moment, the attack from the others arrived.
Large-caliber bullets, grenade launchers, among others, as well as some methods unknown to Colin, struck the monster.
Soon he saw the creature, about three meters high, completely collapse.
Pieces of flesh decayed and fell to the ground, then eerily seeped into the soil and vanished.
“It can’t take a beating?” Qin Chuan held a stack of yellow talismans, ready for another round of attacks, but unexpectedly, the enemy simply disappeared.
Colin, who was standing to the side ready to intervene, furrowed his brow. He was certain that although the monster had been smashed to pieces, it definitely wasn’t dead and might launch a surprise attack later.
However, before he could think further, the sound of more distant footsteps could be heard. They exchanged glances and immediately took out umbrellas they had found in some shops during their exploration. They opened them and dashed toward the location of the shopping mall.
Fortunately, the shopping mall, which occupied a substantial area, seemed to have no more “Twilight’s Children.”
Even more “luckily”…
As soon as they entered the mall, right in the lobby on the first floor, they saw a body hanging from a noose.
..
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 184 - 184 184 Human Future Research Institute_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 184: Chapter 184 Human Future Research Institute_1 Chapter 184: Chapter 184 Human Future Research Institute_1 The corpse had been dead for quite some time, dressed in rags, with skin beneath the clothes dried and wrinkled like old tree bark. Its face was grotesque, presenting a mummified appearance.
A long rope circled his neck, its end tied to the second-floor balcony railing.
After Colin and the others entered, it appeared to be disturbed by the wind, swaying gently like cured meat hanging in a home.
“Death time detected, approximately within the last week. The exact time is indeterminable, cause of death mechanical asphyxiation…” the Robot concluded swiftly after scanning with several beams of light, providing the result within a minute.
“You can turn into this after being dead for a week?”
Listening to its words, everyone reflexively thought of the same word, unsatisfied with the conclusion.
Regardless, right or wrong, the speed at which it delivered results was anything but slow…
Colin sat on the back of the mechanical dog, glancing behind him. Not seeing the “Twilight’s Children” approaching, he turned his gaze back to the corpse hanging in midair.
What was certain was that this was a normal human corpse, with no abnormalities, and no risk of reanimating. Confirming this, Colin let out a sigh of relief.
Next, it was time to investigate why it was hanging there.
“Should we take down the body to have a look?” someone suggested, but as soon as these words were spoken, there was opposition.
“No, something’s off about this place. If we mess around carelessly, it might lead to other problems. Let’s just observe as is, see if we can find any valuable information…”
After a brief discussion, everyone decided to keep things as they were.
Most importantly, since their arrival, “Twilight’s Children” seemed to have no intention of entering the area.
Heaven knows if it was related to this corpse…
It was unlikely, but they didn’t want to gamble.
However, without much inspection, they noticed a cloth strip deliberately tied around the left wrist of the corpse.
On this strip, they saw an irregular circle with a red dot, and underneath it was a phrase: Dragon Bay, D, 801.
“Dragon Bay, D, 801? What does it mean? A specific location? What was his purpose for writing down this thing?”
Colin and the others were puzzled. They could infer from the words “Dragon Bay” that it probably referred to a residential district, then building D, apartment 801?
But there was a question – where was Dragon Bay?
And what was his purpose in leaving this message before dying, and who was it meant for?
In the midst of confusion, Colin suddenly noticed something in the front pocket of the corpse’s shirt. From his angle, he could just make out the corner of a piece of paper sticking out.
“Can one of you check and see if you can get that thing from his chest pocket?” Colin reminded them.
If he had to do it himself, he could have asked Yukionna for help.
But at this point, even though he knew they might suspect him due to his recently displayed strength and reactions, he still didn’t want to expose too much.
He would keep things hidden as long as possible; no matter if it couldn’t stay hidden forever. As long as he didn’t fully reveal himself, they probably couldn’t guess his association with the Bonfire Company.
Soon, with Colin’s prompt, everyone carefully extracted the paper from the chest pocket and had the Robot unfold it. The paper, once unfolded, was quite large, about the size of two A4 sheets, but upon opening, they were met with a big curse—
“Fuck! The! Bastards! In! The! Research! Institute!”
Ah, what kind of grudge was this, starting with such an explosive insult…
Colin muttered internally, his eyes continuing to scan downwards.
“Before setting out in search of supplies this time, the captain asked me to write a will first. I didn’t know what to write originally, since besides my son, I had little else to yearn for. But when I thought of the institute, I knew exactly what to write.”
“If it weren’t for those damned Human Ascension Projects and whatever God-making Plans, things here wouldn’t be so terrible. Everywhere, there are unkillable Twilight’s Children, rats lurking in the darkness, Deep Sea Leviathans. If not for their schemes, none of this would have happened…”
“These big shots messed up the world and ran away. Haha, they were prepared long in advance, escaping into shelters or even leaving this world. But we common people only knew when disaster struck. Damn bastards…”
“Damn Human Ascension Project, those sons of bitches. If there is a hell, when I see those mixed breeds, I will make them die again. Because of them, we’ve lost everything…”
“Don’t let me catch any of those bastards, or else I swear I’d turn their heads into piss pots.”
…
The majority of the will was filled with swearing, cursing the deceit of relevant departments, their irresponsibility, and so on, with holes punctured by the pen indicative of deep resentment towards the institute.
However, despite the cursing, some of the mentioned disasters and the names of various plans set minds wandering.
Beyond that, Colin noticed that the handwriting towards the end of the document was much more disordered than the rest, likely added in the last moments of life.
“If anyone sees this note, I’m sure I’m already dead…”
“I wanted to survive, but unfortunately, I’ve been targeted by a catastrophe-level ‘Twilight’s Child.’ These products of the ‘Human Ascension Project,’ apart from some human resemblance, have long since lost the appearance and cognition of humans.”
“However, luckily, a few friends and I managed to hold out until we reached Shelter No. 21, where we plan to die in an apparent accident.”
“The storage point for the supplies is on the cloth strip in my hand. Inside, there’s essential medicine, enough for the settlement to use for half a year. Besides this, we’ve hidden another important discovery there.”
“Also… I don’t know if anyone will see this will…”
“If so, please tell my son who might still be waiting: Dad is still out looking for Mom. When I find her one day, we’ll come back together, don’t worry.”
“According to exploration rules, I have a box of candies I can distribute myself. I hope the Administrator will give him one each week. Don’t eat too many, it’s bad for your teeth…”
“Last of all, the same old curse…”
“You! Bastards! At! The! Human! Future! Research! Institute! Fuck! Your! Mothers!”
…
Compared to the earlier part of the will, the added text in the latter half appeared much more tranquil, but it was somehow even more weighty, indicating the writer’s acceptance of imminent death and reluctance to leave his child.
Setting aside the emotions, the other information provided was crucially important.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 185 - 185 185 Twilights Children_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 185: Chapter 185 Twilight’s Children!_1 Chapter 185: Chapter 185 Twilight’s Children!_1 “The ‘Son of God Project,’ ‘God Creation Project,’ ‘Human Advancement Project,’—are the Twilight and Twilight’s Children outside the product of the ‘Human Advancement Project’?”
Colin scanned the suicide note back and forth, gaining a preliminary understanding of the state of the world.
Although he did not know the specifics of the “Human Advancement Project,” from what he could see of the outside world, the project had most likely failed…
A large number of humans had turned into terrifying creatures that roamed in the Twilight.
“Human Future Research Institute, from his words, it seems like many of the disasters of this world originated from this institute, but could he be talking about that shelter?”
Colin touched his chin and pondered silently, taking note of these matters.
At that moment, Qin Chuan spoke up, “If this corpse died within the last week, then it indicates that there indeed are survivors around, and judging by his death, it wasn’t by chance. Those survivors might come looking for us.”
“You mean to wait here?” Colin, his mind on other things, asked casually upon hearing this.
Qin Chuan shrugged, “Yeah, first, we don’t know where Dragon Bay is, and second, those ‘Twilight’s Children’ for some reason won’t enter here, so we might as well try lying in wait. The note wasn’t discarded, which means we probably got here first.
“Plus, it says this is Shelter No. 24, who knows, maybe we’ll discover something inside this shelter.”
After he finished speaking, the others nodded, agreeing with him.
Colin didn’t object, but he still reminded, “It’s best to first confirm the situation here and understand why ‘Twilight’s Children’ don’t come in.”
If it had been half a month ago, Colin might have thought this place was some kind of ‘safe zone.’
But now, without delving too deep, he could somewhat sense that the thing capable of deterring ‘Twilight’s Children’ was likely something of the same caliber.
Honestly, this place might not be any better than outside…
And that group dared to enter here, most likely because they were aware of some rule, and by mastering the rules, they could avoid mishaps.
“Yeah, let’s start here and work our way up.”
The group didn’t reject Colin’s suggestion and immediately continued their actions. Soon after, within this rather large area, they found remnants of past battles.
And from some handprints that were clearly made by ‘Twilight’s Children,’ it appeared they used to attack this place.
But for some reason, they no longer set foot in ‘Shelter No. 24’ now.
Then, during their staggered exploration, they came across four hanged corpses.
These corpses, much like the one they first found, all had a strip of cloth tied to their right hands, with coordinates of a certain place written on it, followed by a suicide note in some pocket of the body.
The contents of the suicide notes varied, but all expressed resentment towards the ‘Human Future Research Institute.’
Some were as violent in their writings as the previous one, while others denounced them as traitors.
“Do we have such a research institute on our side?”
After searching the first floor, Colin couldn’t help but ask. If such a malignant organization existed, it needed to be eradicated quickly!
“There shouldn’t be…”
Qin Chuan replied as he thought aloud, “There are only five relevant research institutes on the domestic front, using numerical codes 12345. I’m not sure about international institutes, but famous ones like ‘Eternal Life Society,’ ‘Celestial Research Institute,’ ‘Golden Dawn,’ and so on, don’t seem to be included…”
“Whether it came out later or changed its name, we need to pay close attention to this thing.” A Transcendent who seemed to be ‘Fate Propeller’ said.
From the messages left by the corpses of post-disaster survivors, it seemed that many disasters were related to them.
At this point, Xia Liufang spoke up, “Although there is no research institute with the same name, there are some similar projects aiming at the research of certain terrifying creatures and objects…”
This was not exactly a secret; anyone who joined for a while would understand quickly.
After all, the three official avenues and all the Transcendents in the world stemmed from research into superhuman entities, an indisputable fact.
“There’s no need to be so overly cautious. Just go back and report the facts; decisions aren’t for us to make…”
“I have a question, may I ask?”
At this moment, the man with burn injuries, who had been mostly silent, interrupted the conversation. After receiving a nod, he continued,
“Why conceal these crises? Wouldn’t it be better to face them together with everyone?”
Hearing his words, Colin, who was sitting on a mechanical dog, also pricked up his ears, equally curious about this point.
“Well…”
Qin Chuan was not surprised by this question. After pondering for a moment, he began to speak, “Because experiments have shown that once people in an area become aware of the anomalies, the events happen much more frequently there, with a probability ten to a thousand times higher than before.”
“A thousand times?” Colin was shocked for a moment.
Isn’t that a bit too much of a range?
“Yes, if you’re lucky, the anomalies you encounter are of a simple type that can be resolved quickly, then everything can still be salvaged. If you run into major trouble right off the bat, then the entire area might spiral out of control.”
“According to those experts, human cognition is one of the foundations of maintaining the ‘reality index’ of a region.”
“Our world may not be as materialistic as we imagine… Do you have any other questions?”
Qin Chuan explained at length; all these were basic knowledge, so he had no intention of hiding it.
“No more.” The man with burn injuries shook his head, adding after recalling the content of the previous wills, “As long as I know it wasn’t hidden on purpose, that’s fine.”
“Yeah, I know you have some unresolved issues, but trust us, we would never do anything to betray humanity.”
Qin Chuan nodded, “Then let’s continue the investigation. Let’s check out the second floor.”
Soon enough, they arrived on the second floor and checked carefully, but like the first floor, there were no abnormalities other than the absence of bodies.
Then, after nearly two more hours of investigation, they found nothing amiss on the third, fourth, and fifth floors either.
This brought them some relief.
“We still have the underground area left. I just looked at the guide map; this mall has nine floors in total, five above ground and four below. The original shelter should be on the very bottom floor. Shall we go down?” Qin Chuan asked.
Maybe we shouldn’t go after all… Colin was just about to speak when he suddenly felt a sinking feeling in his heart, followed by a horrific sense of pressure.
It wasn’t just him; everyone present felt an intense pressure.
The direction from which this pressure was coming was crystal clear…
And faintly, they could also hear abnormally heavy “footsteps” reverberating through the air.
Colin and the others turned their heads to look and saw a terrifying sight through the window.
In the distance, several kilometers away, next to a slender tower building that was roughly six hundred meters tall, there appeared a Twilight Giant that was five or six times taller than the tower, very likely over three thousand meters.
It had no lower body, and supported itself on the ground with its immensely large hands, slowly moving among the towering buildings of Mie City.
Above its head, a dirt-yellow ring was continuously emitting a twilight glow, like sunset over a mountain.
And it was at this very moment that Colin and the others felt an overwhelming sense of weariness and exhaustion bursting forth from deep within.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 186 - 186 186 Business Outsourcing_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 186: Chapter 186 Business Outsourcing_1 Chapter 186: Chapter 186 Business Outsourcing_1 “So tired…”
Colin and the others felt an unparalleled weariness throughout their bodies, collapsing to the ground one by one, finding even breathing to be extremely uncomfortable.
In that moment, they seemed to age from their prime to their twilight years, their bodies exuding an air of dusk.
The rich twilight light made everything seem to be in decline…
Outside the window, there was an immense creature supporting the earth with its hands and a earthen-hued halo above its head. Its movements sent faint but horrifying tremors that weighed heavily on the heart.
In the eyes of the people, each time the giant creature lifted its hand, there was a vibration in the air, followed by a booming sound of tearing through the sky, and something like yellow sand continuously poured out from its severed waist.
Unlike the others, Colin could vaguely see that the leaking “gravel” turned into “Twilight’s Children” of various sizes as it hit the ground, continuing their activity within the city.
“Damn it, what the hell did this ‘Human Ascension Project’ create?”
“No wonder the survivors cursed like that, anyone who saw this thing would curse…”
Colin cursed under his breath, seeing beneath the “deity-like” Twilight Children a dense swarm of smaller ones.
The number was countless and merely a glance at them could make one’s scalp tingle.
However, no matter how much it made the scalp tingle, Colin thought that humans had enough firepower to solve it.
But that big one, that Twilight Child that was at least three thousand meters tall with a halo above its head, like an angel…
How are you supposed to fight that?
Without knowing its, no, His capabilities, it would probably not be easy to deal with it.
Fortunately, the giant “Twilight Child” wasn’t paying attention to them. He walked on the broken earth, not knowing where He came from or where He was going.
He simply didn’t care about this group of people here.
But the bad news was, even if He had no malice toward them, His mere appearance and departure could mean that many people around would simply not make it.
“At this rate, for the thing to completely leave, it would take at least three to five minutes, which is very difficult…”
Colin slumped to the ground, his eyelids drooping as if to close, devoid of strength, even the beating of his heart grew sluggish, as if Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis was reviving and erupting within his body.
While feeling miserable, he also realized something; even though ALS no longer affected him in normal times, if the enemy had similar means, they could still cause significant harm via the “dark injury” on him.
Only by advancing to D Level might he finally solve issues related to his body…
But before he could ponder further, he suddenly heard a burst of violent coughing, filled with an indescribable sense of decay and impending death.
“Qin Squad, I… If I die here, will my family still get the insurance? Will they still… get the compensation?” the middle-aged man with a gray complexion suddenly spoke up.
Hearing his words, Colin’s heart jumped, and he noticed that the man’s face was ashen, like a candle in the wind, about to be snuffed out at any moment.
Qin Chuan also thought of something and quickly said, “You… hold on a bit longer.”
As he spoke, he tried to get up but couldn’t even stand.
“Answer me, can you fulfill your promises?”
“We will…” Qin Chuan nodded: “Even if we all don’t make it back, you don’t have to worry about the compensation at all.”
“That’s good.” After saying that, his eyes rolled back, his eyelids closed, and he rapidly deteriorated, his skin wrinkling within a short time, as if a great amount of moisture had been evaporated, turning into a dried corpse, his life extinguished.
Damn it! Colin cursed silently, wanting to save the man but utterly powerless to do so.
The only medically effective thing on him, the “Gluttony Power Mark,” was completely useless in this situation…
“This one can’t be brought back, and there’s another one, I need to think of something. If he dies too, I might not be able to return.”
Colin gritted his teeth, racking his brain for usable items, but sadly—
No.
However, it was at this moment that a line of information suddenly flashed across the retina of his eyes.
[Would you like to issue a special support request? This task will consume 5000 Bonfire Points.]
“…Five thousand points? It’s outright robbery…”
Colin cursed silently to himself, thinking that if he didn’t face that monster for three to five minutes, he should be able to hold on.
After all, no matter how difficult he felt now, he was still Employee Level E, and having injected an E level Gene Compensation, he should definitely be able to withstand it.
But for the others, it wasn’t certain, especially for that last remaining company employee…
If they died, it would most likely mean trouble for him too, so after pondering for a moment, he decided to issue the task and request support.
By the way, he would need to ask Lady Bunny what this support task was all about when he got back. Colin always felt that the task did not seem to be issued by Lady Bunny but by someone else.
However, just as he confirmed it, Colin was suddenly startled.
Because he realized…
This task seemed to have been received and confirmed directly on his retina, not through parchment.
There had never been such a thing before!
“No, this isn’t right…” Colin surreptitiously pulled out a large parchment and checked it. There were no traces of the task on it.
….
Meanwhile, in a land shrouded by endless grey and white fog, tens of thousands of people with withered faces lined up in a long queue, some using crutches, and some bleeding, all walking toward the front.
