And at the front of the queue, a woman with a ball of light hanging over her head, radiating pure white light like a white sun, was leading the way.
The brilliance emanating from the white light above her head sheltered the people caught in the “Catastrophe of the Magic Fog” from its troubles.
And under this light, no shadows existed anymore.
By the woman’s side, a female clad in female armor with blue hair followed her. Her deep blue eyes turned to glance at the Saintess, who had been sheltering the masses for months without any diminishing in her radiant light, and she sighed with a sense of admiration within her heart.
Months ago, they were trapped in the heart of the “Catastrophe of Magic Creatures,” which had led them to despair, but it was then that Saintess Shana, one of the universally acknowledged living holy figures from the Church of Light, descended from the heavens, leading them through various dangers to escape.
“Worried about your sister Helena? Don’t worry, she should have returned to the Royal Capital by now.”
The voice of Saintess Shana rang beside her ear, ethereal and pure, like singing a holy prayer chant, filled with soothing power.
“No, I’m just moved that we finally escaped…”
“Yes, it wasn’t easy.”
The Saintess was about to say something else but suddenly, she changed her words, “Dianas, have everyone stop. There is a ruin not far away; we’ll rest there for today. Also, send some people to explore the ruins to see if they can find any food or water, and we’ll come back during daylight tomorrow.”
“Yes.” Dianas nodded and then stepped back.
Watching her leave, Shana’s right hand moved into the sleeve of her left hand and pulled out a yellowed, tattered piece of parchment.
When she spread it out, the parchment revealed an account balance.
.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 187 - 187 187 Generous Rewards for the Task_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 187: Chapter 187 Generous Rewards for the Task_1 Chapter 187: Chapter 187 Generous Rewards for the Task_1 [Congratulations on completing the task “Support and Repel a Certain Distorted Creature.”]
[The evaluation of this task is: D-.]
“You have obtained ‘Stale, Hard Black Bread*399,’ which has been transferred to your inventory.”
“You have obtained ‘14.34 Bonfire Points,’ which have been transferred to your inventory.”
Glancing at the rewards, Saintess Shana nodded imperceptibly, aware that the rewards for a task she had done last time had been credited.
The task had not been simple, and she had paid a certain price. However, fortunately, the rewards were quite good, several hundred black breads plus a dozen or so points.
“14.34 points…”
Saintess Shana skillfully opened the [Shop], where there were three items for sale, with black bread in the two front rows. However, the one at the back had a “Stale, Hard” prefix.
In terms of price, the former was three for one point, and the latter was over thirty for one point…
Besides black bread, there was also “Pure Water,” roughly one ton for three points.
“I’m not in desperate need of water right now.”
After pondering for a moment and realizing she wasn’t currently short on water, she spent all her points on “Stale, Hard Black Bread.”
Then, in a flash, she appeared in the ruins some distance away, unnoticed in the process of leaving, as everyone saw her as still standing there, shining.
Arriving in the ruins, she took out a large amount of black bread and, uncaring about her image, embraced them in her arms, looking for suitable places to hide them within the wreckage.
Just as she had finished, she suddenly felt something and took out a piece of parchment.
[Special Summoning Task “Request from an Unknown Land.”]
[Task Requirement: Use a clone to provide Purification assistance to some Bonfire members. Ensure they remain uncontaminated for a certain period, with the task duration subject to specific conditions.]
[Task Rewards: “Bonfire Points*50,” “Stale, Hard Black Bread*999.”]
“Huh, a fifty-point task? That much…”
Surprised by the task, she didn’t hesitate and immediately accepted it—
Since she had started handling these parchments, it was rare to see one offering such rich rewards.
Moreover, she wasn’t worried that the tasks posed any danger to herself, as she and the previous generations of Saints could confirm that the tasks were generally not beyond their capabilities.
At that moment, in front of her, a heart-pounding grey fog appeared, and within the fog surfaced a bubble emanating light from within.
From the surface of the bubble, one could glimpse a strange world covered in yellow.
Without much hesitation, she raised her hand and conjured a ball of light, tossing it towards the bubble.
During this process, the ball of light swiftly transformed and stretched, taking on a roughly human shape, and plunged into it.
Then, she faintly “saw” through the haze, fifteen figures.
…
It was also at this moment that a caption appeared in the eyes of all those present, including non-Bonfire Company personnel like Qin Chuan.
[Supporter, Special F Level Employee “The Light Chaser” is about to arrive.]
“Supporter?” A group of people sitting dazed on the ground were momentarily bemused, not quite understanding the meaning.
“The Light Chaser? He’s not dead?”
Colin recalled the name and remembered the exceptionally special employee summoned that day in “Passionate Paradise,” a man whose strength was terrifying enough to confront the “Formless Mother” head-on!
Although it seemed like he fought for only a very short time before vanishing, Colin had always thought he was a goner after that.
He didn’t expect to still be alive…
Then again, only such a big shot would dare to accept the “support mission” that employees spoke of with fear, and although he didn’t know how the other party eventually got away from “Passionate Paradise,” the moment he saw him appear, Colin felt somewhat reassured, and he straightened up.
It was then that he saw “The Light Chaser” appear, wave his hand, and a dozen orbs of light flew towards them, then melted into their bodies like snowflakes.
In an instant, that strong sense of decay and fatigue dissipated rapidly like a sandcastle meeting water.
From everyone’s body, wisps of dim light evaporated and disappeared.
However, after taking this step, “The Light Chaser” did not continue to act, but simply floated in mid-air, as if in a daze.
“Don’t be in a hurry to move, wait until that thing outside leaves…” Qin Chuan said.
He was a bit afraid that acting rashly now would cause that thing outside to cast its gaze this way.
But it was very clear that the terrifying creature didn’t care about anything that was happening here, It didn’t care what came or what It killed in the process of Its activity.
It just moved away slowly with one palm after another towards a certain direction.
After It left, the dusk light around them faded rapidly, and in the distant sky visible to the eye, a black curtain was arriving bit by bit with the disappearance of the dusk.
It probably won’t be long before darkness falls here.
“It seems we should be safe now…”
After saying this, Qin Chuan quickly got up and ran towards the middle-aged man, then saw that, during this time, there wasn’t even a trace of warmth left on the corpse.
“The robots, they seem to be all wrecked…” came the voice of an armed individual.
Colin followed the gaze and saw that even after dusk, there was no sign of life in those robots.
“Ah, let it be if they are wrecked,” Qin Chuan on the other side sighed, put away the parchment, and turned his head to look at the glowing, gender-indistinct vague figure, “Sorry for the delay, are you… a supporter from ‘Bonfire Company’?”
The information previously displayed on their retinas informed them that this person should be “one of our own,” so there was not much hostility.
However, faced with his question, this “one of our own” did not respond at all but seemed to notice something and turned to look in the direction beside him.
Qin Chuan turned his head and saw that the “supporter” was looking at Colin.
He frowned, remembering Colin’s previous abnormal behavior. The tremendous power could be explained by the adrenaline rush in a life-or-death situation, but how did Colin detect the underground attack first?
The Transcendent “Fate Propeller” explanation could be due to the influence of that Ninth Level Big Shot, allowing him to temporarily possess the corresponding power, and it is indeed possible for someone with high inspiration to experience this.
However, Qin Chuan always felt there was something far-fetched about this explanation…
As thoughts flashed through his mind, he paid a little more attention and then asked Colin, “He seems to be from Bonfire Company, do you know him?”
“I’ve just joined Bonfire Company, how could I know anyone inside?”
Colin decisively shook his head, feeling unnerved under the other’s gaze, and touched the goosebumps on his hand. He was equally puzzled as he looked towards the glowing figure and decided to try and see if he could communicate with him.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 188 - 188 188 Automatic Renewal_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 188: Chapter 188: Automatic Renewal_1 Chapter 188: Chapter 188: Automatic Renewal_1 “Hello, I… am also an employee of Bonfire Company.”
Colin “struggled” to his feet from the ground, subconsciously wanting to say, how coincidental, we meet again, but fortunately remembered at the crucial moment that this should be their “first” meeting.
However, in response to his question, the glowing figure just floated a few inches above the ground, silently looking at them, showing no intention of responding.
After some thought, Colin tried asking a few more questions, but still got no response.
“It feels like they can’t see us,” Qin Chuan commented with a puzzled look beside him.
Not just him, Colin felt the same, sensing that the other’s gaze wasn’t on them, but rather looking somewhere else.
“Could the reason we can’t communicate be because this place is too special?”
Colin had a hunch; since arriving here, this eerie place indeed brimmed with all sorts of irregularities.
Just when he thought to try other methods to get a response, the light in front of him suddenly retracted, all the brightness condensed and disappeared all at once.
“They left?” The crowd around the supporter was taken aback.
Not right, they didn’t leave… Colin frowned, although he couldn’t see the Light Chaser, a strong intuition told him that the figure hadn’t moved but had simply stopped glowing and turned completely invisible.
If one’s inspiration was strong enough, they could still sense that someone was there…
Meanwhile, the Transcendent from “Fate Propeller” suddenly spoke up, “They didn’t leave; it seems like they’ve cloaked themselves. Concentrate, and you can sense it.”
Among those present, he claimed to have the second strongest inspiration, and no one dared claim the first… With his reminder, everyone sensed the presence to varying degrees.
“It seems they don’t want to talk with us, it’s fine.” Someone shook their head, no longer fixated on the matter.
After all, the other had just lent a hand to help so they should harbor no ill intentions.
Even if they did, they would have acted by now…
Most importantly, they could still feel the effects of a BUFF on them.
While they were talking, the corner of Colin’s mouth suddenly twitched as he saw a line of information appear on his retinal display:
[Remaining duration of “Purification Light” effect: 11 hours, 51 minutes, 33 seconds.]
[Every 12 hours, 250 points are required to replenish energy once (up to 168 hours max).]
[Do you confirm to automatically extend before the “Purification Light” effect expires? Can be canceled at any time.]
[Note: Charges calculate as full 12 hours even if the period is less.]
“Good heavens, you’ve got to be kidding me, I…”
Colin pursed his lips, taking a deep breath in silence, unsure of what to say for the moment.
He previously thought he had a good understanding of the company’s operations, but now realized his knowledge was quite superficial.
Seeing “automatic renewal” at this time, he was still shocked.
Apart from marveling at the “talents” within the company, he didn’t know what to say for a while…
As for the BUFF.
“Lucky they didn’t get me into some membership program or something with advance payments…”
Colin thought it over; although the fee of 250 points for 12 hours seemed offensive, he still confirmed the “renewal.”
After all, apart from the extortionate cost, the “Purification Light” buff was truly formidable.
Of course, its strength was in protecting sanity and one’s own status; the amplification in other areas was minor, but not insignificant.
But in this world, what was most needed was the protection of sanity and one’s own status.
Afterward, Colin mentally noted the name of the Light Chaser in his notebook, planning to inquire about the details with Miss Bunny once back in reality.
Taking advantage of him to make so much, he’ll have to get payback when he can!
However, he didn’t dwell on it. As the giant “Twilight’s Children” moved away like a moving light bulb, Colin and the others saw their vision gradually darken.
After about ten minutes, the erstwhile twilight world had completely turned into a chilly night.
In the dilapidated Doomsday world now devoid of electricity, not a single light could be seen. Many unspoken oddities seemed to be taking shape invisibly.
Compared to the twilight world, the dark night was equally unsettling, but the sense of oppression was much lessened.
Colin glanced outside, seeing nothing but the receding twilight within his field of vision, no other sources of light, not even a glimmering celestial body in the pitch-black sky.
However, he didn’t dwell on this; he was thinking about how to find other survivors and look for the shelter mentioned by the “future self.” But just then, he noticed that everyone in the dark was looking around, perplexed.
At that moment, Xia Liufang spoke up:
“I think I can see everything clearly in the night?”
Her vision was strange, not like normal sight; it was somewhat like infrared, yet not quite, and the details were fully replicated, clearer than in daylight.
“I thought it was just me, but it seems everyone can… it must be the ‘BUFF’ given by that supporter from Bonfire Company,” Qin Chuan guessed the cause and thanked the Light Chaser again.
This powerful night vision was a significant boost for them.
“There are still a lot of good people at Bonfire Company, unsolicited and selfless help without the need for rewards…” Qin Chuan and others expressed their appreciation.
They had no follow-up subtitles on their retinas, so they knew no more, assuming it was the company’s “uncompensated assistance.”
Listening to this, Colin kept an expressionless face, but silently repeated the name once more.
More than feeling cheated, he was now puzzled because he had secretly checked the parchment earlier, only to find that neither his “large account” nor “small account” had any mission records.
“This ‘support mission’ is a bit strange in how it was given…”
Colin furrowed his brows, suspecting that someone deliberately left him in this place to drain his points.
But they didn’t have time to ponder further; they suddenly noticed in the pitch-black ruins, a few hundred meters away, several flares of light visible, moving swiftly toward Research Institute No. 24, where they were.
“These must be the survivors from after Doomsday.”
Colin realized this; from his perspective, he could see that these people were pale as if they hadn’t seen sunlight for years, dressed in tattered clothes like scavengers.
Clearly, this group must be the people the hanged individual spoke of, who would come specifically to collect their bodies later.
They exchanged glances, deciding to stick to their earlier plan to lie in wait inside the building, waiting for them to come over so they could attempt communication.
But just at that moment, a scream suddenly pierced the darkness.
The group rushing towards them had apparently been ambushed.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 189 - 189 189 Survivor in the Dark_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 189: Chapter 189: Survivor in the Dark_1 Chapter 189: Chapter 189: Survivor in the Dark_1 “Damn it, those freaks are catching up!”
Wang Hu raised his torch, his face flush with anger as he cursed. Ahead in the pitch-black darkness, imperceptible to the outstretched hand, one could see humanoid creatures that walked on all fours like animals.
Their skin was pitch-black, blending into the night; their eyes were bloodshot, and they boasted snow-white, shark-like fangs.
They moved much faster than any normal human. Under the cover of night, they were like gecko-like humanoids scurrying about.
Their movements could be heard everywhere…
At this moment, these monsters didn’t rush them directly but used various items they could find nearby, like stones and glass, to hurl at them.
Of course, their main target wasn’t the people but the peculiar torches in their hands.
These creatures, they feared the light!
Although experiments had been conducted showing that light could not actually harm them unless set aflame, for some unknown reason, they were terrified of flames.
If there was an ordeal, these not-so-intelligent creatures would always prioritize attacking the source of the flames.
For this reason, they held their torches very high, two meters up, so they wouldn’t fear the enemy’s ability to hit them.
“Don’t let them catch you, head to Shelter No. 24, there’s a corpse of that thing there, they wouldn’t dare come close!”
Wang Hu yelled out, then swung the crossbow arrow in his hand at the dark-skinned monsters to fend off their attempts to extinguish the fire.
He then led the other twelve people in his team towards Shelter No. 24.
But he hadn’t taken more than a few steps when Wang Hu suddenly felt alarmed, noticing something flying towards him from the darkness. It wasn’t aimed at the two-meter-high torches but at him…
His pupils contracted, and as he attempted to dodge, he felt a severe pain in his knee.
Crack…
It was the sound of his kneecap shattering.
Wang Hu’s body stumbled due to the inertia of his run and crashed to the ground, falling heavily. The broken lower leg bone was connected to the thigh.
“Ah!”
The intense pain made him let out a wail, veins straining in his neck, but quickly suppressing the pain, he lifted his head in desperation and unwillingness, looking ahead.
At that moment, he felt a pulling force on both arms and, momentarily puzzled, looked up to see two young rookies from the team apparently trying to drag him along.
Although moved inwardly, he knew all too well that with a broken leg at such a time, there was no chance of survival.
Wang Hu tried hard to break free from the grasp of the two men: “How were you taught when we left! Run now! Run fast! Everyone else has already run! Keep up, don’t fall behind!”
His voice was filled with desperate unwillingness but also helplessness.
“No, we’re almost there, just a hundred meters…” the person pulling him refused to let go.
“You… get out of the way!”
Wang Hu was about to curse out loud when he suddenly noticed something was wrong; he saw something in the darkness stand up, getting ready to swing a stone and smash it towards them.
Wang Hu’s breathing paused, ignoring the pain from his broken leg. He forcefully pushed away the rookie trying to drag him to escape.
It was then that another stone came whistling through the air, aimed accurately at them.
However, Wang Hu dodged in time this time, avoiding the attack. He only received minor scrapes with a small piece of flesh sheared off his arm by the stone.
Unstoppable stones smashed behind the people, shattering and exploding on impact, a testament to the tremendous force.
“Forget about me! There’s something wrong with these mutants! Run for it!”
Wang Hu shouted, realizing at that moment that there was definitely something off about these mutants.
From his years of experience, he knew mutants should not be able to cross flames and directly attack humans. The occurrence of such an event meant there was something wrong with this group of mutants.
Although he didn’t know exactly what had happened, he was clear that if this intelligence didn’t get back,
then every night, the search teams would likely suffer heavy casualties.
“Run fast, tell them about the situation here.” Wang Hu stuffed crossbow arrows into the hands of two people, pushed them away, and then saw a humanoid mutant with similarly dark skin in the darkness bending over to pick up a piece of broken stone, ready to strike at him.
He looked up unwillingly at that spot, also picking up a stone, shouting in despair and anger:
“Come on!!!”
In the midst of shouting, he hurled the stone in his hand and saw the other also swing their stone.
However, just as his stone flew out and he was about to despairingly close his eyes, he saw the monster’s head suddenly explode, red sauce, white brain matter, and shattered eyeballs bursting out…
He was stunned by the sight—how could I be this powerful? Could it be that I’ve awakened superpowers?
No, that’s not right, Wang Hu suddenly remembered that his throw was incredibly awkward and hadn’t hit the target at all…
It was at that moment that the intense sound of rapid gunfire erupted; he saw several figures sprinting from the darkness towards Shelter No. 24, holding firearms as they charged out.
Between the flashes of their gun muzzles, he could vaguely make out that these people were wearing combat suits and that there were faint mechanical and hydraulic sounds accompanying their movements.
In just a short span of time, those black humanoid mutants that considered this area their territory after the apocalypse scrambled to escape in panic.
“Special forces?” Wang Hu was startled. He was familiar with these people, having once been one of them.
But equipment this… “sci-fi,” he had never seen before.
“Covering fire!” Someone shouted loudly, and he saw someone from that team dart out at an extremely fast speed, come to his side, grab his shoulder, and drag him towards Shelter No. 24.
Though the figure didn’t look very large, their strength was abnormally great.
Quickly, he was dragged into the middle of this squad that appeared out of nowhere, and then he saw several of the people who had fled towards Shelter No. 24 among them.
However, compared to the original team of thirteen, there were only seven here.
“The others are already inside the shelter, no need to worry,” Colin explained next to him.
Now with the “Purification Heart” BUFF as his cover, he could once again run and jump openly…
“Thanks…” Wang Hu started to say when he suddenly noticed on the second-floor balcony of a building, another black mutant unreasonably picked up a stone and aimed to throw it at them.
He was about to give a warning when he suddenly saw the creature throw the stone, but as it left its hand, it flew in an utterly unnatural direction, smashing right back into its own face and smashing its head…
What was that?
Lifting a stone to smash one’s own head?
And as he stood there in shock, Colin, as if he hadn’t noticed anything, quietly continued the retreat, secretly pinching a golden card in his pocket.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 190 - 190 190 Understanding This World_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 190: Chapter 190 Understanding This World_1 Chapter 190: Chapter 190 Understanding This World_1 “Some suspected human-contaminated creatures turn into black monsters with well-developed limbs and simple minds; they only prioritize attacking fire, not killing people first… And what kind of attack method is this, throwing stones?”
Colin watched the monsters picking up stones and, for some reason, felt like laughing.
Of course, it couldn’t be denied that the stones thrown by these creatures were indeed powerful, but not very efficient, at least not nearly as much as bullets.
“Against ordinary creatures, bullets and the like go ‘rat-tat-tat’, which is more convenient and saves time.”
Colin murmured to himself and didn’t continue to take action, except for the one that tried to sneak attack from the second floor earlier, the rest weren’t very capable.
After being blessed with “Purification Light”, the rescue team completely ignored the darkness, revealing everything in fine detail.
When the battle erupted, it took only a moment for more than twenty black, humanoid creatures to lie dead on the ground.
The stench of blood thick as in a slaughterhouse permeated the area.
Before long, Colin’s support team, except for one who unfortunately suffered a light injury from a thrown stone, all safely returned to Shelter No. 24 in the city center.
As for the group of survivors, out of the original thirteen, only eight remained alive. The other five were smashed to death and then dragged into the darkness by those twisted, black-skinned creatures…
Meanwhile, at the mall’s first floor, both parties stood on opposite sides.
For some reason, Colin could clearly sense an elusive hostility emanating from these people.
Even though they had clearly rescued this group, they could still feel their hostility.
As for the reason for the hostility, Colin and his team could roughly guess — these people might suspect they were from some research facility.
In the silent standoff, just as everyone was thinking about how to explain themselves to avoid being falsely accused by the local nefarious forces, a scream suddenly rang out.
“Ah!”
Wang Hu, who had passed out halfway, suddenly screamed out in pain as the agony of his broken knee woke him up again.
At that moment, his face was flushed red, sweat pouring down, while others around him were helping to urgently dress and straighten his wound.
“Take this, a fast-acting painkiller injection that also stops bleeding and fights infection; just inject it near the wound,” said one of the armed personnel, throwing a portable syringe to him after a nod from Qin Chuan.
Wang Hu, his mind still a bit fuzzy, stiffened for a moment before seeming to realize something, glanced at Colin and the others, then shakily reached out to pick up the syringe from the ground and injected it near his wound.
Given the strength of these people, he didn’t have to worry at all that they might poison the medicine or anything like that.
Because it was completely unnecessary; it was better to accept their help graciously and suffer less…
After a slight prick and less than thirty seconds, he quickly felt the pain signals from his nerves being blocked by the analgesic; other than feeling a bit of swelling at the wound, there was no other discomfort.
Wang Hu took a deep breath and nodded to the group, “Thank you.”
After that, he scanned the armed personnel’s sophisticated equipment before continuing, “Are you from the research facility?”
As these words came out, the breathing of the people behind him stalled, and the atmosphere immediately tensed up.
These people really held deep hatred for that shelter… Colin inwardly sighed; even in this vulnerable situation, they wanted to confirm if they were from the research institution rather than feigning ignorance.
It was evident that the hatred between the two parties might have reached an irreconcilable point.
“No, we are from official forces, the Special Operations Department, but we come from another province.”
Qin Chuan stepped forward to negotiate, but even after he’d finished speaking, the atmosphere hadn’t lightened much.
After all, only the officials had the capability to establish research institutes. Ordinary people simply didn’t have that kind of power on this land.
So, one could imagine what sort of elements the shelters consisted of.
“I understand your possible encounters, but we truly aren’t those people, not even remotely related…”
Qin Chuan glanced at Wang Hu’s attire, “If that military uniform is your own, then you should be able to understand our point, we are different from them.”
Upon hearing this, Wang Hu fell silent for a few seconds before speaking, “The envelopes left here by those people, you’ve found them, haven’t you?”
They weren’t certain, but they could feel that this group was squatting here so conveniently, it was very likely for them.
Otherwise, these people probably wouldn’t have taken action so soon…
Seeing Qin Chuan nod, Wang Hu didn’t hesitate to follow up, “What do you want to obtain from us? Do you require us to deliver undeveloped human embryos each month, or less frequently, or some other special experimental subjects?”
“Huh? Undeveloped human embryos? Less than a month old?”
Qin Chuan was about to speak up about wanting to know the location of the shelter, but he couldn’t help being shocked upon hearing this.
Seeing the surprised expressions on the faces of everyone present, Wang Hu knew that they must truly have little to do with those inhumane shelters.
Latter on, through his explanation, the group finally learned about the depraved acts committed by these shelters.
From time to time they would capture some of the survivors outside the shelters to conduct various experiments, like sending children to parents who had already half lost their sanity to see if they would kill, or providing some protection in exchange for regular delivery of people as experimental material…
And recently, they had heard that one of the shelter research institutes was collecting human embryos that had already been fertilized, requiring collection by their people around the one-month mark.
“This is truly inhuman!” someone cursed angrily.
“What are they collecting these for?” Colin couldn’t help but ask the reason.
“I’m not clear, but when it comes to the anti-human acts of these lunatics, most of the time there’s no good outcome. I’m not sure if there are any good people in other regions, but at least on the land of this region, there are none left…”
Wang Hu shook his head and then continued, “Let’s not talk about this, what do you want to obtain from us?”
Qin Chuan collected his emotions and said, “Find a place called The Hague Shelter, find a way to leave, do you know the exact location…”
“The Hague Shelter?” Wang Hu pondered for a moment and shook his head, “I’ve heard of it, but I don’t know the exact location. No, to be more precise, none of the remaining shelters in this region do we know the exact location of.”
Only a very few individuals knew the exact locations of the shelters, and most of the time, it was those people themselves who would come out.
“Not even one?” Colin inquired.
As long as they knew the location of any shelter, it might be possible to find other shelters through them…
So, for them, it didn’t matter which shelter they found, as long as they found one.
.
.
.
ps: I forgot to include the name of The Hague Shelter in the will of “Future Colin.”

chapters.title: Chapter 191 - 191 191 On this day God made a promise to all
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 191: Chapter 191: On this day, God made a promise to all mankind._1 Chapter 191: Chapter 191: On this day, God made a promise to all mankind._1 “All I know is that there are probably two shelters that still exist in this province, one is the ‘Human Future Research Institute,’ and the other is the ‘Dawn’s Light Foundation,’ but their exact locations are unclear. They are very secretive about their whereabouts.”
Wang Hu shook his head; however, as he spoke, he seemed to think of something, “In our settlement, there might be someone who knows where the shelter is; he seems to have escaped from one.”
“If you can help us and bring back supplies, I can promise to hand him over.”
Nowadays, it’s hardly realistic for them to bring back supplies on their own strength, and without supplies, the settlement won’t last long.
Moreover, the geographical location where the supplies are stored is also in these people’s hands; they can’t obtain it by force.
When he finished speaking, the expressions of some people behind him changed, knowing this could likely expose their own location.
However, a few others showed thoughtful expressions, realizing that since neither party was the enemy and there was no malice, it was better to have a reasoned discussion—after all, it’s always better than resorting to physics.
Wang Hu took note of the expressions of his companions, silently marking those who might be suitable for further development.
“Hmm?”
On the other side, Colin and his group were also taken aback. They hadn’t steered the conversation towards this “sensitive topic,” fearing it would arouse suspicion.
But to their surprise, these folks had brought it up themselves.
“We can…”
Qin Chuan and the others exchanged glances, then took out several pieces of paper wrapped in rotten cloth and passed them over, “This is the information they left behind, and their bodies can be seen just a little further inside the hall…”
“Can you describe the state of their bodies when you saw them?” Wang Hu took the letter and glanced at the address on it, immediately understanding the destination.
“Hanged, mummified…” Qin Chuan added some details.
After an employee of Bonfire Company died, they knew that if one died under the twilight, the body’s moisture would rapidly evaporate, turning into a mummy.
They hadn’t disturbed those hanged mummies, but the mummies of their own people had been simply buried on the spot.
Listening to Qin Chuan’s explanation, Wang Hu and the others nodded—the method of hanging was indeed their arrangement this time.
If these guys suspected to be members of the shelters had made the kill, they most likely wouldn’t know the “hanging” code.
“Then, we’ll rest for a while, and while we’re at it get to know some of the conditions here…”
Qin Chuan looked at the people around him, about to say something, but was suddenly interrupted by Colin from the side.
“Did you guys hear anything?”
Colin cocked his head to the side, looking a bit confused. Something didn’t feel right to him, yet he was not sure, but a sense of indescribable hunger was rising within him.
This made him realize that things might not be so simple.
“What sound?”
Qin Chuan was stunned, about to continue speaking, but suddenly heard three dull thumps near his ear.
“Thump, thump, thump~”
It wasn’t just him; everyone present heard the sound. At first, they were all taken aback, failing to understand what the noise was or where it was coming from. It just felt like some heavy drumbeat resonating, causing the air itself to vibrate.
However, the next second, while everyone paid attention, they heard the dull sound rise again…
“Thump~ Thump thump~ Thump thump~”
The sound seemed to herald the revival of something, and Colin and the others suddenly realized—wasn’t this just the sound of a heartbeat?
Moreover, they could clearly feel that the sound was coming from underground!
Wang Hu’s face suddenly changed, as if he had thought of something, “Bad news! It’s that thing underground in Shelter No. 24! Run for it! Otherwise, once it wakes up, we’re all going to die!”
The fact that the Children of Twilight wouldn’t enter this accursed place had a reason after all…
Colin muttered to himself, ready to flee, yet he felt a strong sense of hunger welling up inside him.
His complexion changed suddenly, and immediately after, he heard a certain sound emanating—
“Eat, eat, the incomplete one born from beneath the ground…”
“Eat, eat, eat! A great tonic…”
“It has been so long since I have eaten…”
Biblical whispers lingered by his ear as a tantalizing scent of meat infiltrated Colin’s nostrils, and it seemed he could “see” clearly with his eyes that the aroma was emanating from beneath the ground.
However, at that moment, the Saintess following Colin, silently trailing and bestowing BUFFs without doing much else, seemed to notice something, directing her gaze towards him.
In her eyes, everything was hazy, unseeable, inaudible, but she felt a familiar and terrifying entity awakening.
Without needing the prompt of parchment, she took the initiative to enhance the BUFF effects on Colin.
“Eat my ass! Eating anything and everything will only harm you!”
Colin regained his rationality, suppressed the voice inside him, and hurried to keep up with everyone’s fleeing pace.
He had only paused for less than three seconds, so no one became suspicious, and as they left, the increasingly clear and, it could be said, deafening heartbeat sound gradually faded away.
“What in the world was that thing?” Colin asked while looking at Wang Hu, who was being carried on a survivor’s back.
“I’m not sure. I heard that Shelter No. 24 was once attacked by ‘Twilight’s Children’ for some unknown reason, and when pushed to utter despair, they conducted a certain experiment. The end result was ‘Twilight’s Children’ left, and that place became something of a forbidden zone.”
Wang Hu explained the situation. To his knowledge, most anomalies wouldn’t actively approach that place, but interestingly, living people wouldn’t come to harm there.
In a sense, it could be seen as a safe haven.
Of course, the condition was not to stay too long, and to leave immediately upon hearing that heartbeat.
Otherwise, one might be trapped there forever…
After roughly understanding that as long as they left in time, they would not be entangled by whatever was there, Colin breathed a sigh of relief and paid no further attention.
Afterward, they made no plans to rest and headed straight for Dragon Bay.
As they hurried on their way, they learned more about this world from the survivors like Wang Hu.
For example, each time the ‘Twilight’s Children’ disappeared, they would return again after about three days, shed light upon this place for a few days, and then leave once more.
This entity was a product of the Human Future Research Institute, and when asked why it only had an upper body, Wang Hu and the others attributed it to divine punishment for humanity.
A survivor carrying Wang Hu spoke through gritted teeth, “Those damned people attempted to create a creature that could rival God, leading to divine judgment. Their blasphemous creation was severed by the dominion of the heavens at the waist, forcing them to walk on hands, perpetually fatigued, as a warning and retribution.”
Why does this sound so heavily infused with religious motifs… Colin guessed that the severing of the creature’s lower body might indeed have happened, but the inside story was likely different from what they were told.
Besides the ‘Twilight’s Children’, they also learned about the situation of the great calamity.
It seemed that, roughly a decade and a half ago at the beginning of the year, daylight turned to The Night in an instant. The sun stopped rising, people went mad and feral, a myriad of bizarre rules emerged, and the world plunged into doomsday.
Later, they gradually came to understand some “truths” and knew that all disasters originated from those research institutes or shelters.
“However, we believe that as long as we persevere and maintain our faith in Him, eventually He will descend from the heavens, send His Angel Envoys, and rescue us all from The Night and disasters, delivering us from this sea of suffering…”
“Him?” Colin asked reflexively, but after asking, he suddenly felt a twinge of regret.
Seeing Colin’s inquiry, the young man carrying Wang Hu showed a hint of fanaticism on his face, not just him, but all the other survivors as well, exuding a fervent and devout look that made Colin and the others feel uneasy.
But he himself did not notice and continued to speak, “If you don’t mind, please allow me to introduce our Master to you, spread His image… This is the only chance for salvation for both you and us. All other attempts are futile, which you will come to understand eventually.
“And He, I have seen Him in my dreams. He symbolizes the white sky, radiates sacred and pure Light, extraordinarily merciful, with twelve beautiful pairs of wings. Despite being supremely great, He still deigns to assuage the hearts of us mortals…
“He told us not to panic, to pray to Him, and that one day, He will pass judgment upon all calamities and bring redemption to us, the innocent…
“He told me His name is… ‘White Night’.”

chapters.title: Chapter 192 - 192 192 Arriving at the Destination _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 192: Chapter 192: Arriving at the Destination _1 Chapter 192: Chapter 192: Arriving at the Destination _1 White Night…
As Colin listened to his sermon and the other party pronounced his real name, he couldn’t help but think of a sacred figure in his mind.
That figure arose from the eternal darkness, floating in mid-air, flapping its wings, scattering blessings and light, dispelling the darkness, and bringing salvation…
In a trance, everyone seemed to hear it as if it wanted to say something.
However, at that very moment, someone suddenly shouted, and the vision came to an abrupt halt.
“Wait, I think we’ve arrived!”
Hearing the voice, Colin paused his steps for a moment and slightly shook his head, looking in that direction.
Under the illumination of light, a dilapidated and declined riverfront skyscraper appeared on their retinas. Visually, there wasn’t anything particularly strange about this place compared to others.
However, taking in a slight breath, Colin detected in the air a fishy smell, not normal by any means.
‘There’s something wrong here.’
Colin hesitated for a moment, uncertain if he should find some way to warn the others, but the Fate Propeller, one of the Extraordinary Ones, suddenly cried out, “My intuition tells me something is off inside. Be careful.”
Although “intuition” wasn’t reliable in gauging good or bad luck, those who followed the path of Fate Propeller were a different story.
Because they were in contact with the power of the Book of Fate, their sixth sense was usually extraordinary.
After he spoke, Colin saw everyone immediately become alert, slowing down and quieting their footsteps.
Another group of survivors, unaware of the reasons, observed nothing out of the ordinary but still followed suit in reducing their noise.
A few minutes later, Colin and the others cautiously moved up to the perimeter of that community.
Upon arriving, they could distinctly feel the air turn moister, and an almost imperceptible scent of sea brine wafted around them.
However, for the moment, they saw nothing unusual; aside from the smell, Colin spotted no threats…
Just then, Wang Hu, who was being carried by someone, smelled the sea brine and seemed to think of something, whispering, “It’s those things from the seabed; they might be nearby.”
“Something from the sea?” Colin asked.
He soon learned this was related to a disaster that occurred at the beginning—a terrifying tsunami.
During that storm, countless coastal cities and island nations disappeared beneath swiftly rising seas, the population plummeting by unknown numbers. Even those who didn’t die immediately could still hear strange sounds from the sea, luring survivors into the depths.
Fortunately, after a while, the tsunami receded back to pre-catastrophe levels.
Sources said that those close to rivers and seas might encounter certain underwater lifeforms…
These beings were suspected to be humans who had been engulfed by the disaster.
The smell in the air now, along with the moistness and some strange, viscous liquid on the ground, matched the descriptions of those beings.
“Over the years, we’ve traded information with survivors from other regions and learned about these monsters, but we’ve never seen them…” Wang Hu shook his head, adding more details.
Said monsters had skin tough as steel, immense strength, and the power to beguile the human heart and more…
“They should have only passed through here; the problem isn’t that big.”
Colin glanced at the ground and clearly saw the foul-smelling stains leading toward a corner of the street, not entering Dragon Bay.
If it wasn’t necessary, they had no desire to confront these beings.
Now, entering the night, as Colin and the others hurried along, they occasionally saw various bizarre things, such as squirming shadows, flesh plants perched atop buildings, and so on…
Perhaps they had discovered them early, so they hadn’t been attacked.
The only monster they had directly confronted was those black-skinned creatures resembling humans in vast numbers…
Without further thought and once assured there was no immediate danger, Colin and his companions entered Dragon Bay and, following directions, arrived at the base of Building D.
In front of them, the stainless-steel gate on the first floor of the community had long been rusted beyond repair due to years of neglect and previous exposure to the sea.
They easily passed through the gate and cautiously made their way to Room 803 on the eighth floor, where they found a large stash of supplies.
Colin scanned the items and noticed most were various canned foods and some mechanical parts. What seemed to be stored most securely was medicine, such as Amoxicillin, cough suppressants, ibuprofen, acetaminophen, Liuwei Dihuang Pills, vitamins, and so on…
“We’re saved! There’s hope for my dad’s illness!” a survivor called out, holding a box in his hands, his dirty face beaming with joy.
It wasn’t just him; other survivors also showed rare smiles.
In this disaster, food wasn’t so hard to come by, after all. The catastrophe had claimed so many lives at once that the grand districts and cities which used to support tens or hundreds of millions of people now had to sustain less than one percent or even one thousandth of that number, making the leftover food more than abundant.
Even in some ruined shelters, the remaining canned goods were plentiful enough that several settlements had eaten for more than a decade without exhausting the supply, not to mention other resources.
And, with makeshift generators and a few light bulbs, they could also grow some vegetables and raise pigs…
Only medicine, even the common cold medicine that used to be everywhere, was beyond their ability to replicate, making it scarce in the aftermath.
“After so many years, are these still good?” Colin couldn’t help but ask, curious.
From what he understood, after the great disaster, except in shelters and such, people generally lacked the means to produce medicine. Therefore, any medicine found here would be at least ten years old, and he wondered if taking it could lead to poisoning.
“The potency might diminish, but most of them should still work, and besides, we don’t have a choice,” explained Wang Hu, lying atop a crate of canned goods.
Taking it might cause a reaction, but not taking it would surely lead to death from an infection.
Without medicine, an ordinary cold could be as devastating as a natural disaster for children or those not in good health…
“Alright, we’ve done what we promised you; now it’s your turn,” Qin Chuan steered the conversation back on track, “Have your people lead us to a ‘refuge shelter’ that is still operational.”
“Don’t worry, give us one day. Once we take these medicines back, we’ll immediately call that person over to lead you to the shelter. During this process, I and three others will stay here with you…” Wang Hu made the promise.
Colin and the others exchanged looks, thought about it, and ultimately did not object.
They could wait one day.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 193 - 193 193 The Return to World Code-13_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 193: Chapter 193: The Return to “World Code-13″_1 Chapter 193: Chapter 193: The Return to “World Code-13″_1 Moreover, after having continuously traveled until now, they really did need to rest and recuperate…
Qin Chuan glanced at Colin and the burn victim. Neither of them were Extraordinary Ones, and they were physically weak. If it hadn’t been for the buff boost from the supporters of Bonfire Company, they probably couldn’t have made it this far.
With that thought, Qin Chuan silently thanked the selfless help of the employees within Bonfire Company.
It would be nice if everyone were as willing to help others as they were.
“You two should find a spot to rest as well, and as for food, there’s some here.” Qin Chuan took off a backpack from an armed person and tossed it over.
Although there was plenty of food at the scene, they were not from this world, so they didn’t plan on trying the local food unless they were absolutely desperate.
Accidentally triggering something that could prevent their departure would not be ideal.
“Mmm, thank you.”
Colin opened the backpack and glanced inside to find an assortment of individual ration bags, with a rich variety of flavors, from pig’s trotters rice to roasted chicken and more.
After quickly solving their hunger problem, he found a corner to lay out some things and leaned back to sit down.
“There’s still about an hour left, and even if they don’t plan to rest, I guess I’ll have to find some excuse in a bit.”
Colin pulled out a “large-size” parchment, looking at it openly. The countdown to “World Code-13” opening had one hour left, meaning that although it was unclear what day of the week it was in this world, it should be around 11 a.m. on Monday in the outside world.
“However, judging from the fact that my thoughts don’t align with the content on the parchment, I should currently be in a non-mission status. Yet, I still can’t access things like the Interaction Hall, as if my network got disconnected, with only a few functions working.”
Suddenly recalling something, Colin pulled out a “will” from his “future self” to look at, which was also a parchment.
It appeared to have been issued by the “Bonfire Company” of this “future world,” but nothing on it could be accessed.
Colin pursed his lips, remembering that his “future self” mentioned that the Bonfire Company of this future or parallel world seemed to have encountered some problem, causing various functions to be disabled, and up to now, it was as good as waste paper.
Considering the events of the past few days, he speculated that the company must have been thoroughly compromised by an invasion.
“Nevertheless, I don’t know what level I’ve reached in this world. If I go by my current rate of progression, after more than ten years, I probably should have at least reached A Level, right?”
Colin made a guess but wasn’t too certain.
If the Storage Room function had still been active, he could have guessed based on the other person’s equipment level, but that obviously wasn’t feasible right now.
“It’s a pity, with some luck, I might have gotten more Golden Artifacts, or even higher-level rare items…”
Colin sighed inwardly; he was quite curious to take a peek at his own inventory to see what was inside.
But without dwelling on it much, he secretly took some food from this world and stashed it in his backpack. He wouldn’t eat it himself, but planned to have the people on the other side try it later.
Afterwards, he quietly put on the “Widow Yukionna” on his finger, silently asking her to take special care of his body during this sensitive time.
Otherwise, he might be clueless if his body got fouled up by something…
“Speaking of which, it’s a good thing those three robots that could detect anomalies broke down, else Yukionna would hardly dare to come out.”
Colin nestled in the corner with his arms folded over his knees, his head buried in his arms as if he had started to rest.
As time passed by, the countdown to “World Code-13” gradually reached its end.
Dong——Dong——Dong——
The distant and ancient bell tolling sounded in his ears after a long absence.
Billowing fog surged from in front of his field of vision…
In a moment of haze, Colin heard the crackling sound near his ears, shook his head, and saw himself in an empty, tidy church, with a large bonfire burning in front of him.
The flame was not fierce but brought an indescribable warmth and comfort.
“Directly inside the church this time?”
Colin was startled for a moment. He remembered that when he had initially fled, he had just left that city and, based on his past experiences, should have awakened nearby.
However, he didn’t dwell too much on this. Upon arriving here, he immediately felt something akin to a smartphone reconnecting to WiFi after a long disconnection.
It was at the very moment this feeling arose that lines of information appeared on my retina…
[Special Event — “Investigate the ‘Hague Research Institute.'” has been issued to the mission list. Please check it through the mission list.]
“Getting a mission right off the bat, and it’s related to the Hague Research Institute. As I suspected, the reason I didn’t receive any missions there last time was due to ‘disconnecting,’ or perhaps some other reason.”
Colin pursed his lips and opened the mission list in his mind to check it.
[Special Event: The scheme from the “Hague Research Institute.”]
[Description: A special Box Garden Space that is almost completely out of control.]
[Requirements: Find the files in the institute that contain reports on the various disaster events of this world.]
[Note: Completing this event will earn a high task reward.]
…
There wasn’t much content in the mission, but Colin was taken aback by the description that Bonfire Company used for that unfamiliar world — it was neither called a “future world” nor a “parallel world.”
Instead, it was referred to as a “special Box Garden Space.”
“‘Box Garden Space,’ if I remember correctly, implies that this world is artificial? Who could be so impressive…”
Colin was greatly shocked, but then again, it might not be “man-made,” it could also be “god-made.”
Right after that thought, he began to wonder, what was the purpose of creating this Box Garden Space?
As soon as this idea emerged, Colin had a vague guess within him — to seal away those various strange entities and keep them away from the normal world.
“However, there is no indication of how to leave this so-called ‘Box Garden World’; that’s troublesome…”
Colin shook his head but didn’t get too discouraged.
After all, according to these requirements, at least he had a direction, and when the time came, leaving should be achievable.
Of course, this assumed that the mission was not a trap.
“This must be a mission from Lady Bunny, but it’s not certain. However, it doesn’t matter, just be careful when the time comes…”
“Sigh, ever since I joined Bonfire Company, I’ve either been trapped here or there. When will I get a normal level assignment? I’m clearly just an E-level rookie.”
Colin let out a slight complaint, then gathered his thoughts and reviewed the mission requirements for “World Code-13.”
This time, aside from those point-earning missions, it was as Lady Bunny had said before, he was to represent Bonfire Company in this place, spreading branches and teaching salvation, collecting faith and such.
Of course, if he had any other ideas, like creating a kingdom, that would be fine too.
Bonfire Company didn’t care in what form he gathered followers, as long as he did not go against humanity, they only cared if he could complete his KPI.
Gathering his thoughts, Colin opened [Event Sixteen: Summon Subordinates] and summoned his three makeshift subordinates.
Whoosh…
Suddenly, pillars of fire in the church surged, spewing out two clumps of ashes at the base, which rapidly transformed into two human figures in mid-air, strikingly similar to his two previous subordinates.
Li Ming, Tang Ken…
After they appeared, they looked each other over, seeming to recognize their identities.
Then, they both looked toward Colin and greeted him simultaneously.
Colin nodded and turned his gaze toward the three o’clock direction; he could sense that another subordinate was probably less than five kilometers from here.
Beyond that, he could faintly smell from the air that there seemed to be a large group of people over there.
“First, lead the people back; ha, this time it’s not like the last, where I had to search far and wide for people.”
Colin breathed a sigh of relief.
This time the damn people were right on his doorstep; surely nothing could go wrong now, could it?

chapters.title: Chapter 194 - 194 194 The Incident that Broke Out in the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 194: Chapter 194 The Incident that Broke Out in the City_1 Chapter 194: Chapter 194 The Incident that Broke Out in the City_1 Creak~
The heavy church doors were pulled open from the inside, and a dim light shone in from outside. Three men stood behind the door, peering out. One of them made to leave, but noticing someone standing still, he seemed to think of something, and his step hung in midair without falling.
It was only after taking a few steps out of the door that Tang Ken realized that there was no one beside him.
Then, he turned back with a puzzled look, “What’s wrong with you guys?”
Behind him, Colin and Li Ming were both at the door, not having stepped out.
This gave him a sudden, rather uneasy premonition.
“It’s nothing, heh heh…” Li Ming let out a nervous chuckle. While speaking, he glanced outside twice and touched his neck, seemingly recalling the memory of his head flying off.
But before he could finish, Colin, who was behind him, suddenly lifted his leg and kicked Li Ming squarely in the butt, sending him flying out.
“Don’t delay.”
Colin retracted his leg and, seeing that there was no problem with the two men, spoke with a stern face, “We still have a lot to do today.”
Through the scents in the air, he could determine that there should be quite a number of people outside this dead city, and these people seemed to be acquaintances— the poor and general populace from the town they had visited before.
“It feels like a lot of people have been driven here. Was it done by that what’s-it-called First Legion of the Zoo?”
Many questions arose in Colin’s mind, like how long had passed in this world and where had the people of the First Legion gone…
He shook his head slightly and collected his thoughts, then walked toward the position of another female subordinate.
“Why didn’t you two come out just now?” Tang Ken asked in a low voice as he walked and bumped Li Ming’s shoulder, waiting for him to turn his head before asking with confusion.
“Uh, about that…” Li Ming hesitated slightly, and seeing that the boss didn’t show any signs of stopping him, briefly mentioned the event with the opening of the door and being attacked.
Of course, he didn’t go into detail about the power of the Virtue Knight, but just told him that at most he got a wound the size of a bowl and it wasn’t a big problem.
“Even if there’s a problem, the boss could easily save you, so don’t worry about it.”
You’d be easily saved before your corpse rots, Li Ming silently added some details in his heart.
Tang Ken was dubious, but remembering Colin’s abilities, he didn’t doubt it much…
Compared to Li Ming, who had spent seven days lazing around in the church until the “grand finale,” trying to find worms and bugs to supplement his protein, Tang Ken had seen even more of the powers of Mr. Colin, the Bonfire Agent.
However, he didn’t say much else because after they walked out of this eerie abandoned city, they saw that the barren woods were filled with people.
Colin stopped in his tracks and took a glance at them. They were a large group of short-statured, ugly and filthy-looking refugees, numbering around three hundred. Unlike what he had seen before, most of these people were draped in large red garments.
Without much thought, he knew that these must have been distributed by the what’s-it-called First Legion when they settled the refugees.
And the moment they saw him, some of the refugees seemed to have remembered something, their eyes lighting up with fervor as they called out and knelt down.
“It’s the Savior! The holy Savior of the Bonfire! The Savior sent by the Legion of God to rescue mortals!” With his cries, a dense mass of refugees knelt down.
“Ah, this…”
Colin blinked, and once these people knelt, he could even see some tags that had not been torn off the red garments, reading “Made-in-China.”
“Tsk… Impressive, my country…”
Colin muttered sarcastically, then shifted his gaze to see some people who had not yet knelt—the tall, skinny young man who was the nephew and assistant to the Warden Calder, but whose name he momentarily forgot…
These people looked around at the fervently kneeling refugees, their expressions somewhat awkward.
Since everyone else was kneeling, wouldn’t it be inappropriate if they didn’t? But then again, they were knights of the kingdom!
Amidst the embarrassment, Colin shook his head subtly as a signal, then turned his gaze to the zealous crowd, raised his hand, wanting to get the people to stand up, but unfortunately, those caught in the fervor didn’t notice his gesture.
“This is… fervor indeed.”
Thinking it over, Colin stealthily took out the “Ring of the Flame Master” and casually spilled some blended oil.
Immediately after, with a “whoosh”, flames burst into existence, forming a huge fireball above his head.
After absorbing a portion of the Firebearer’s essence, he used this accessory; the adverse effects were greatly reduced, at most feeling like he was thrown into an oven of seventy or eighty degrees, something he could withstand for quite a while.
Meanwhile, feeling the enormous glow, everyone finally fell silent, looking at him with devout faces, waiting for him to speak.
Enduring the discomfort of being put in the spotlight, Colin spoke, “Alright, everyone stand up. Next, you will follow the arrangements made by these two.”
Afterward, Colin handed over most of the supplies to Li Ming and Tang Ken, and temporarily lent them equipment like “Slave to Money” and “Gluttony Power Mark”, tasking them with taking charge of this portion of refugees. He also nodded towards the Warden’s nephew, indicating that they should talk elsewhere.
Not long after arriving at another location, the Warden’s nephew couldn’t help but ask, “How come you’re here?”
“It’s quite normal for me to be here, but why are you… How long has it been since that catastrophe? What were the consequences? And what’s the situation now?”
Colin asked out of curiosity.
“About half a month has passed, fifteen days or so,” answered the Warden’s nephew, puzzled by why Colin was unaware, but he quickly provided an answer.
‘Fifteen days, if I calculate carefully, I indeed missed two sessions of not entering…’
Colin thoughtfully pondered, according to this situation, if he didn’t come in every Monday at noon, would this world simply skip a week’s “storyline”?
In the subsequent conversation with the Warden’s nephew, he roughly understood the situation back then.
“The First Legion” evacuated all residents from the city, then fortified the seal again, and fought against “Hunger” inside. No one knew the exact circumstances because everything was sealed off.
Outside, those Bunnies not quite as big but still about two and a half meters tall had saved them afterwards, distributed food and clothes, and then sent them to this place to find the Bonfire Sacrificial Ground.
A few days ago, the Warden’s nephew finally found this peculiar place, an area completely devoid of life, unimaginable what had transpired here.
However, during their investigation, they quickly located the Bonfire Sacrificial Ground and subsequently began to bring the people over.
As for their reason to cooperate with those people, it was simple…
Nowadays, the only place that could accommodate these refugees was “Wheat Spike City”, but it was impossible for “Wheat Spike City” to accept them; the majority within the kingdom either didn’t care about the lives or deaths of the poor.
For them, just enough was sufficient—if there were too many, they would let them fight amongst themselves, if too few, they would command them to reproduce more.
The situation in “Wheat Spike City” was clearly the former.
So, if they didn’t want them to perish in the wilderness, the only solution was to settle them in this manner.
Calder and the others felt that, with the power of those people, it was unlikely they would deceive them.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 195 - 195 195 The Desire to Eat_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 195: Chapter 195: The Desire to Eat_1 Chapter 195: Chapter 195: The Desire to Eat_1 “Lady Helena has already left and should arrive at the Royal City in a few days if all goes well. Meanwhile, Uncle Calder is in Wheat Spike City undergoing punishment and reward, and we are in the process of relocating the common folk…”
“Undergoing punishment and reward?” Colin interrupted curiously while walking towards the position of the third employee.
“Yes, for protecting Lady Helena from danger and for safeguarding most of the nobles and civilians within the city, his merits are sufficient for him to become a first-stage ‘Virtue Knight’. However, the town was leveled, and although not primarily responsible, he cannot escape some blame…”
The Warden’s nephew briefly finished explaining the situation over there and also clarified the current state of the town.
The legions who possessed terrifying powers left around the eighth day, and when they left, the town was once again revealed to everyone, plunging all who saw it into deep shock.
As if recalling something fearsome, the Warden’s nephew looked at Colin with eyes filled with awe, his words laden with palpitations:
“After it reopened, everything turned to dust, the entire city was utterly flattened, and a kilometers-wide, nearly hundred-meters-deep crater appeared at the bottom of which lay magma. Moreover, that area had become a magic-free zone; magic could not operate within it, and someone like me would even be turned into an ordinary person if they approached it…”
And there was a little incident within all this; he thought about it but decided not to mention it—the moment the nobles in Wheat Spike City heard about the incident, they immediately declared the expulsion of all elements detrimental to the kingdom and wanted to put Colin and the other Heretics on trial.
For this purpose, a powerful expeditionary force was organized, swiftly heading towards the town that had been pulverized to dust.
However, when they arrived and sensed the remnants of the aura in the huge crater, the expeditionary force’s captain and everyone else suddenly fell silent. Then, looking at the fearsome pit, they changed their tune, saying perhaps they had misunderstood…
Just by the way they disregarded the act of helping ordinary people, it was apparent they were not bad individuals, and their character must be trustworthy.
They asked Calder to pass on a message, advising him to make good contact with Colin and the others to avoid unnecessary conflicts and misunderstandings that could harm the hard-won friendship between both parties etc…
…
Wow, that’s rough. Did the First Legion drop a nuclear bomb when they fought ‘0-9 Hunger’, or did they keep dropping them over and over?
Colin too was astonished as he listened, eager to see if the place was as exaggerated as the guy described.
At the same time, he couldn’t help but think about the former employee who had been sacrificed at the church.
“What level was that guy, to qualify to bring ‘0-9 Hunger’ here, and what exactly was he doing here? What did he encounter that led to such a pitiable death…”
Colin frowned secretly; he was starting to find the matters of this world a bit complex.
However, he didn’t dwell meaninglessly on these thoughts, quickly gathering his mind and refocusing on the present, knowing that the first thing to do was to take the third employee back to the church.
He would first have her register so that if she were to kick the bucket, she would resurrect at the Bonfire Sacrificial Site, and her future descents wouldn’t be at random locations anymore.
“By the way, where are we heading now, Your Excellency?” asked the Warden’s nephew, suddenly realizing something amiss.
Why does it feel like we’re getting further off course?
However, before he could speak further, Colin raised his hand to interrupt the Warden’s nephew and looked ahead, taking a deep breath.
He could sense that about a kilometer ahead, his third subordinate was there, and there were also numerous refugees close to the subordinate; these refugees were unfamiliar, and some of them emitted an odd scent.
Colin’s expression turned strange for a moment; he wasn’t sure whether the subordinate’s body obtained in the Other World was male or female, but considering some possible situations, he quickened his pace slightly.
Because regardless of gender, if one’s luck were even a bit sour in this ghastly place, their fate wouldn’t be very pleasant.
…
In a long-deserted stone village, a young girl named Vanessa, dressed in the simple white robes of the Church, was kneeling with glowing hands, intently trying to heal a woman lying on the ground.
The woman’s face was pale and her body frail, with injuries all over, appearing as though she was on the brink of death.
The pure white light shining upon her also seemed to have little effect.
Around them, a number of people watched in silence, hoping for a miracle to occur.
But after a while, the holy white light suddenly disappeared, and Vanessa, somewhat weakened, withdrew her hands and looked at the woman lying on the ground, sighing, “I’m sorry, I…”
Through her abilities, she could estimate that the woman on the ground had ruptured organs and widespread failure, and it was very difficult for her to save her with her own powers.
At this moment, only those flesh sages who specialized in this path had a slight possibility of healing her wounds.
Her “Light,” in dealing with the injuries, could only prevent the wounds from festering and decaying, making Thaiveil’s condition slightly better…
“Please, you must save Miss Thaiveil. If she dies, we are finished too; the master will not let us go…” A few men gathered here changed their expression and said in panic upon hearing this.
They had barely escaped from the “Calamity of Monsters,” and now they might be buried along with the death of the young lady.
This was something they couldn’t accept…
Vanessa looked at them, opened her mouth as if to speak, but ultimately couldn’t say “I’m powerless.” Instead, she said, “I’ll do my best, I’ll make sure she lives, as long as we get to Wheat Spike City, just… cough cough cough…”
Before she could finish, she couldn’t help but cough a few times.
“Are you alright?”
“No, I… I may need to rest for a while, sorry.”
Saying this, Vanessa left the room without another word and went to a small hut a short distance away. As she closed the door, she seemed to finally give in to the coughs, her hand covering her mouth while fresh blood seeped through her fingers.
At that moment, she appeared significantly more listless, looking like she could collapse at any second…
After Vanessa left, several servants of the Thaiveil family inside the room looked utterly hopeless.
They faintly felt that Miss Thaiveil might not hold on much longer, which almost certainly meant a dead end for them…
It was at this moment that one of them suddenly showed a fierce expression, with abnormal bloodshot eyes, “Switching to the ‘Gluttonous Feast,’ there’s no other way. We can only do this; otherwise, we’re left with a certain death.”
“But joining the ‘Gluttonous Feast’ requires handing over a sufficient portion of blood food. Are we really going to harm Sister Vanessa? She has helped us a lot. If not for her, we would likely have fallen to corruption…” a servant hesitated, seemingly uncertain about the original plan.
“So what? Without our help, she, a Church nun and an Extraordinary One, wouldn’t have stood a chance to leave. When the young lady was attacked, she was right beside her but didn’t block it. With her physical condition, how could she have failed to block it?” someone said resentfully.
“It’s all because of her selfishness that we are forced to join the ‘Gluttonous Feast’…”
A servant wielding an axe chimed in with agreement, “Exactly, it’s all her fault! Now we’re just making her pay for it! And by handing her over, we might even get a share of her ourselves, taste what she’s like and escape the life of servants for good!”
As he mentioned the “Church of Light” nun, he couldn’t help but lick his cracked, bleeding lips, his eyes revealing a strong desire.
A strong… craving to eat.

chapters.title: Chapter 196 - 196 196 Enchantment Fusion_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 196: Chapter 196 Enchantment Fusion_1 Chapter 196: Chapter 196 Enchantment Fusion_1 “I arrive only to witness an event unfolding…”
Colin’s body was hidden beside a ruined clay house, and he clearly heard the refugees’ planning. If nothing unexpected happened, Lin Yilan was probably lying inside the room, her soul residing in the body of a woman named Thaiveil.
Obviously, considering the “Bonfire Company” only allowed for “Soul Transference” into a corpse.
That woman’s original body must be dead…
“This is still the first one to start off finding a body with an identity; the rest are refugees or refugees.”
Colin pursed his lips and quietly pulled out the “Revolver Contrarian” from his pocket. Using a firearm was evidently a good choice against these ordinary people.
And now he didn’t need to worry about the bullets because, after coming out of “Passionate Paradise” last time, he had spent over three thousand points and a Gold Mission Voucher to repair this revolver.
At this moment, its integrity had reached nineteen percent.
Furthermore, it had acquired a special ability—”Air Compression Bullet.”
The bullet’s effective range was fifty meters, with power equivalent to that of a regular bullet…
As for how many rounds he could shoot, that depended on Colin’s lung capacity because before firing, he needed to take a deep breath to use this special firearm skill.
He had tested it himself; one breath could last for about five to seven shots.
However, just as he was about to make his move, he suddenly noticed a prompt on his “Revolver Contrarian.”
[Prompt: One thousand Bonfire Points + “Ring of Flame Dominance” can be used at “Bonfire Sacrificial Ground” for enchantment synthesis of this item.]
“Enchantment synthesis?”
Colin was momentarily stunned; this was his first time learning about this function of the “Bonfire Sacrificial Ground.”
But before he could think more about it, the people inside the cabin seemed to have finally reached an agreement. Seven or eight individuals emerged from the cabin and headed straight toward Sister Vanessa, not realizing that their conversation had been overheard through the wall just moments ago.
A faint sound of metal friction reached his ears—the Warden’s nephew seemed ready to take action…
“Wait for a moment.”
Colin sniffed, noticing that apart from these people, there appeared to be some other characters with ill intentions nearby.
These characters were releasing a faint fragrance…
‘Damn it, the moment I heard the tasting reference, I sensed something was off; it must be those “The Glutton” followers…’
Colin frowned; he couldn’t precisely locate the cultists by their scent, which was a bit troublesome.
In all fairness, he wasn’t particularly keen on meddling in other people’s business.
But when it came to matters related to “The Glutton,” it was a case of killing one whenever you encounter one!
Otherwise, who knows if they would catch you off-guard with something big, just like before…
“The nun is in danger. Aren’t we going to go up directly?” asked the Warden’s nephew, his hand on the hilt of his sword, slightly puzzled; he hadn’t smelled any fragrance.
“There’s something else, don’t rush, move stealthily.”
Colin motioned with his hand to signal his companions to follow, then trailed behind the traitorous servants.
At the same time, he informed Lin Yilan through the internal channels of the Bonfire Company to lie still and not move.
In just a few steps, Colin saw the group arrive at the door of the nun, knocking on it. First, there came some faint noises from behind the door, then it was pulled open.
There stood Nun Vanessa, with wheat-colored skin, brown hair, blue eyes, gentle facial features, not stunning but fairly pleasant to look at, dressed in the plain white garb of the Church, exuding a mild temperament.
At this moment, her complexion was abnormally pale, making her appear somewhat frail.
“You…” Sister Vanessa looked at the group outside the door, about to say something, when she suddenly saw someone raise an axe towards her head.
And from the front, several people pulled out brightly polished knives and stabbed directly at her.
Quite decisive… Colin also at the same moment drew his gun, ready to rescue Sister Vanessa first…
Bang, bang, bang—
With a few muffled sounds, several servants flew out from the doorway and fell to the ground.
Colin was taken aback because he hadn’t fired his gun yet, but these people had already fallen.
What surprised him even more was that Nun Vanessa, who he thought was so frail, suddenly burst out with incredible speed, knocking out and stunning each attacker with one punch.
Not only that but the most threatening one, the servant with the axe, was now being lifted by the neck with one hand by her.
The situation had swiftly reversed in a matter of seconds.
Colin and the trainee knights at his side were completely stunned.
“Spare me, please spare me…” The servant, hanging midair, pleaded in panic.
“Sorry, forgive me for not realizing in time that you had lost your way. May the Light guide your soul to His kingdom.”
Nun Vanessa’s blue eyes shimmered with white light as she sighed.
The minds of the others present were not completely corrupted yet, so she merely knocked them out with her punches. However, this one person’s mind was utterly enveloped, beyond any chance of salvation.
Then, she clenched her fingers, and the next second, the sound of crushed bones echoed through the air, and the servant’s head drooped lifelessly…
“That’s some strength,”
Colin pondered, his heart skipping a beat. He watched as she nonchalantly dropped the corpse in her hand, her gaze shifting, taking a glance in their direction as if she had spotted them.
Despite seemingly detecting their whereabouts, she did not approach. Instead, she retracted her gaze and sprinted towards another direction like a nimble leopardess.
Where was the sign of any weakness in her movements?
“Damn it!” someone cursed suddenly from that spot, hastily responding to the attack. But they had barely managed to raise a wand for defense before it was smashed to pieces by Vanessa’s punch.
“I knew she was faking it! She wasn’t injured at all! She’s not as frail as she seems! Damn this ‘Church of Light’ bitch, they love to play these games every day—”
Several locals, dressed in robes that looked indecently like cassocks, screamed out loud.
However, before they could finish their swearing, a glowing fist hammered down, the sound of breaking bones silencing their shrieks.
“Hiss… So she was pretending after all? Another fishing tactic? Do people in this damned place love to fish this much…”
Colin watched speechlessly. He had truly believed that the nun had sustained serious injuries, but now it seemed even if she had been hurt, there was no need for her to rush to such a remote room…
Thinking about it now, it was likely a ruse to give these people a “chance to plot.”
In less than a minute, the battle was over. Colin saw her hands emitting light, her punches leaving no quarter as she effortlessly hammered the “The Glutton” believers to death.
The believers did not lack resistance, but all their methods became ineffective upon touching the white light, as if suppressed.
“That light looks familiar…”
Colin squinted his eyes, sensing that by nature, it was almost identical to “The Light Chaser,” yet he was not entirely sure.
Because “The Light Chaser” was far stronger than the one before him…
“Wait, that’s not right, ‘World Code -13’ currently only has me in operation. Besides that, only Lady Bunny’s First Legion was briefly active, but they left quickly… Why would someone bypass me to command this world’s power?”
