Colin’s brow suddenly furrowed as he realized something, could “The Light Chaser” be from this world?
The thought wasn’t impossible.
After all, the former employee had been active here, who knows if he left anything behind?
“Right, ‘The Light Chaser’ seemed to have first appeared at ‘Passionate Paradise,’ exactly when the First Legion arrived in this world, could it be someone newly recruited by Lady Bunny at that time?”
Colin had his theories, but he wasn’t certain.
At that moment, a person clad in a red grid-like cassock charged towards them, his muscles writhing, a look of horror on his face as he tried to escape from this direction.
That woman was too terrifying, one punch after another, no one could withstand her.
However, he only got halfway when he spotted Colin and the others nearby.
“Get out of the way!” His face was ferocious, his mouth gaping wide like a fish, and he lunged at Colin, attempting to take a bite.
Facing a maw that could swallow a head whole, Colin kept his hands in his pockets, expressionless. He merely twitched his hands a little inside his pockets—
A powerful repulsion was suddenly applied to the opponent, flinging him through the air in an arc before he brutally smashed into the ground, dying instantly on impact.
“What happened?”
The Warden’s nephew, who had just drawn his sword, was startled. They hadn’t even seen Colin make a move, nor felt any magic burst.
Watching Colin, hands still in pockets, not surprised in the slightest, they found him increasingly mysterious…
And it was at that moment that Vanessa returned. This time she walked straight towards them, and behind her, the “The Glutton” believers lay in twisted positions, the scene shockingly impactful.
Obviously, they had all been sent to “Heaven” by her little fists.
After some thought, Colin decided not to hide. He stood up openly—not because he was afraid of her, but because there was no need for any conflict between them.
Moreover, if that “The Light Chaser” was really a local and affiliated with the nun’s group, then it was certainly necessary to establish good relations.
“You all…”
Vanessa saw Colin and the others appear without surprise, but before she could finish her sentence, her wheat-colored skin turned white in an instant, and she staggered, bending over to cough a few times against her will.
Her hand covering her mouth, blood seeped through between her fingers…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 197 - 197 197 Equipment Fusion Upgrade_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 197: Chapter 197 Equipment Fusion Upgrade_1 Chapter 197: Chapter 197 Equipment Fusion Upgrade_1 “Ugh.”
Colin and the others didn’t say anything, falling silent for a moment, not knowing what to say—
Big sister, isn’t your acting a bit much? Do you really think our brains are just for show?
Though that was what he thought, Colin wasn’t entirely sure if the other party was “seriously injured,” because the acting was very realistic. Moreover, what was strange was that he couldn’t determine the other party’s physical condition through scent or anything like that.
The only thing he was sure of was that, despite the person coughing up blood severely, there wasn’t the kind of aura that indicated they were on the verge of death.
“Sorry, cough cough, I’ve suffered some injuries. I am a nun from the ‘Church of Light,’ Vanessa. We have just escaped from a disaster…”
Vanessa looked apologetically at everyone, introducing herself while coughing.
After a pause, she asked with a weak and tentative tone, “What are you… here for?”
She looked so frail and vulnerable, as if she might faint at any moment, and as if she were telling any potential enemy: I am almost done for; if you want to make a move, now is the best time. I’m coughing up blood, I can’t stand anymore, come on out…
“Don’t worry, we mean no harm; we’re just looking for someone.”
As Colin spoke, his gaze shifted past her to other refugees who had drawn near, seemingly confused about what was happening here.
Vanessa’s figure shifted slightly, blocking Colin’s line of sight to those innocent bystanders.
Standing in this position, she could ensure that if Colin suddenly attacked those ordinary people, she could block him without delay.
“Who are you looking for?”
“Miss Thaiveil in that room.”
“She… she… I’m very sorry. Although Miss Thaiveil’s body still has some vitality, her soul, in fact, disappeared a long time ago… Ah??”
Vanessa, the nun, was about to say this when she suddenly saw from the door, a person who was supposed to be dead, walking out—
It was Miss Thaiveil!
And no sooner had she come out than she started walking toward that unfamiliar man…
The next second, Vanessa clenched her fist, her eyes swept uncertainly over these people.
“A living corpse? A mutation? Doesn’t seem like it; she must have come back to life, but how come her wounds are gone? No, that’s not right. Is she possessed? That’s not right either; her soul feels the same as when I first met her…”
Vanessa was utterly befuddled. What puzzled her the most was that she didn’t feel even the slightest hint of an evil spirit from the other person nor did she feel much negative emotion. If it hadn’t been for her clear knowledge of Miss Thaiveil’s condition, she might not have noticed anything was off…
“Right, Miss Thaiveil was acting strange before she fainted…”
Vanessa seemed to remember something. Contrary to what those servants had said, Miss Thaiveil, although injured, hadn’t sustained mostly lethal wounds. Vanessa had indeed blocked the attack at the time, but even under those circumstances, Miss Thaiveil had suddenly passed out and remained unconscious until recently.
She had been wondering what kind of attack could cause Miss Thaiveil’s soul to disappear instantly and then return just as suddenly?
Now, what was the best course of action?
At this very moment, it was the first time she had encountered such a situation, and she didn’t know how to respond.
On one side, seeing the awkward atmosphere, the Warden’s nephew suddenly stepped forward and said, “I am an apprentice Virtue Knight from the ‘Virtue Knight Order’ of The Kingdom of Knights. There’s a town nearby that the ‘Bonfire Church’ is establishing, distributing food and medicine. If you don’t mind, you can come over…
“After all, I think your kindness would not allow those ordinary people to continue to endure hunger and the torment of illness.”
“I, I need to think it over…” Vanessa looked at his badge, neither agreeing nor denying.
She was not clear about who these people were and what their intentions might be; her thoughts were a bit slow to catch up.
However, Colin didn’t continue to talk to her. After he finished speaking, he left with Lin Yilan, who on the surface was “Miss Thaiveil” but in actuality was a G Level temporary employee.
“Do you now have the memories of this body?” Colin asked curiously, turning his head.
“Mhm.”
Lin Yilan nodded, with fragments of the body’s memories surfacing in her mind. She knew she was the daughter of a wealthy merchant out on an excursion when she encountered a monster attack known as the “Magic Fog”, in which she died.
And then, her arrival…
“I have been to this world before, but it wasn’t long before I suddenly returned to reality. Then the hospital was suddenly put under lockdown, many people started to go insane, but later on, some individuals came and dealt with the issue…”
“Moreover, it seems like they wiped the ordinary people’s memories, and everyone except me forgot what happened at that time.”
Lin Yilan explained what had happened then.
This roughly matched the intelligence Colin had obtained later on.
“Those details aren’t important, but do you have the ability to treat the locals now?” Colin remembered that Lin Yilan’s medical expertise was high, seeming to specialize in surgery, but he wasn’t clear on the specifics.
“I can.”
Seeing her nod, Colin assigned her a task to treat the injuries of the refugees.
As for the matter of her body’s original identity, that was temporarily put aside. The most important thing now was to settle the refugees and heal their various illnesses.
Not long after, when everyone returned to the dead city, they saw that the formerly deserted town now had the presence of many living people.
Disaster victims in various red garments were lined up in an orderly manner under the arrangements of Li Ming and others to receive food—
Five loaves and two parcels, along with a bowl of concentrated syrup diluted in water, enriched with various ingredients.
After arriving, Colin took Lin Yilan to meet the others, retrieved the “Ring of Flame Dominance”, and handed over some company items like “batteries that make one glow” to them. He let them take free rein before assuming the role of an absentee landlord and entering the church alone.
Colin clearly wasn’t as savvy as Tang Ken in the management of ordinary people, so he didn’t plan to meddle needlessly.
Entering the church, Colin approached the massive Bonfire, taking out two items: a revolver and a bracelet.
[Enchantment conditions are met. Start fusion?]
“This better not downgrade my equipment,” Colin grumbled. But then, thinking it through, even though the revolver was considered orange-quality gear, it was actually useless and already at rock bottom. It didn’t seem like it could get any worse, so he opted to start the fusion…
Then, he saw no changes in the items in his hand.
While puzzled, a flash of insight struck him, and he realized something, tossing both items into the Bonfire.
Soon, he watched as the red bracelet was set ablaze, melted, and wrapped around the revolver. It then seeped into the metal of the revolver, filling the cracks with a lava-like fiery substance.
A scorching breath came at him…
In no time, the Bonfire swelled and spat out the enchanted revolver like a seed.
Colin picked up the revolver that landed at his feet, brought up the “Revolver Contrarian” properties, and saw two new skills added besides “Iai Slash (American Style)”, “Adaptive Aiming”, and “Air Compression Bullet”.
[Exclusive Skill “Fiery Embrace”: When wielding this gun, the user can manipulate flames within a 30-meter radius at will. All bullets fired carry flame attack properties and have a certain suppressive effect on anomalies. Furthermore, when Fiery Bullets hit the same target 33 times, a “Lethal (causing massive damage)” effect will be triggered.]
“Precondition for Use: The user must have a preliminary sense or a certain ‘Firebearer’ aura; otherwise, they will suffer significant negative effects.”
“Note: No matter how strong, what does it matter? Watch as I down you with 33 bullets!!!”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 198 - 198 198 The Fireball in the Office_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 198: Chapter 198 The Fireball in the Office_1 Chapter 198: Chapter 198 The Fireball in the Office_1 “Lethal”? That’s an instant kill effect… Damn, this crappy gun is finally starting to have the attributes an orange-tier weapon should have.”
Colin looked at the revolver in his hand and couldn’t help but reveal a relieved smile.
For a long time, this crappy gun had the name of an orange-tier weapon but didn’t live up to its reputation, which made him feel it was utterly useless. But now, with the addition of the “Lethal” effect, it finally possessed the corresponding power.
With his hand on the gun grip, Colin could somewhat feel that among the monsters he had encountered, even a Stage Three “Beastification” victim would be instantly “Lethaled” after taking thirty-three bullets.
And before that, a single ordinary bullet might not have broken its defense.
“Aside from Stage Three ‘Beastification’, that Hemorrhoid Spirit experience with the super-large meatball could also be slashed, of course, that intensity from ‘Formless Mother’ wouldn’t be enough, it could cause some damage but certainly wouldn’t kill…”
Colin silently felt that, in a way, these bullets were also very sneaky.
Because until the thirty-third bullet hit the target, even if only thirty-two had been fired, the opponent wouldn’t feel a thing. It was only at the moment the thirty-third bullet struck that it would explosively trigger.
After nodding silently to himself, Colin gripped the gun handle and tried out the new skill “Fiery Embrace.”
Whoosh!
The giant pillar of fire inside the church suddenly swelled and burst, hugging the church ceiling and spreading outwards with a roaring sound; the surging flames seemed to ignite the entire church.
And in Colin’s hands, the fire was like a formless giant beast, extending its scorching tongues and licking the church, spreading further out.
Hot currents whirled inside the church, continuous howling sounds from the pressure of the fire.
At the same time, the people outside the church also noticed the commotion here. Li Ming, Tang Ken, and Lin Yilan, who were distributing goods and managing the refugees, showed shock on their faces and rushed into the church.
With such a big fire, what if the boss got burned to death?
Who would then distribute the G Level genetic compensation?
“Save…”
Li Ming, somewhat fearful of the flames, was the first to rush into the church, intending to shout for fire-fighting, but he noticed that Colin was standing calmly at the back of the church, his body covered in raging flames. But these flames did not burn him at all.
So much so that it seemed as if they were emanating from him…
In the face of the incoming heat wave, Colin, augmented by the fire, looked like a Flame Apostle in command of the fire, exuding an oppressive aura.
Tang Ken, Lin Yilan, and others who arrived were also stunned by this sight, and the refugees following them were now kneeling en masse—awkwardly though, some wanted to chant prayers or something, but seemed to remember that Colin, aside from having the title of “Bonfire Messenger,” had never spread any scripture.
Nevertheless, before this point when they would give thanks to the “Bonfire,” they might mention the “Saintess,” but now, after witnessing Colin’s performance like a Flame Apostle, there was only one object of loyalty in their hearts.
And it was in the worship of the congregation of half-believers that Colin vaguely saw, in a position that did not exist in reality, a tremendously huge flame burning in the sky, swallowing countless sparks, almost like an active sun.
He was looking at that sun, and the sun seemed to be looking back at him.
“Isn’t this the background wallpaper of my office?”
Colin pursed his lips, took a deep breath, and without dwelling on it further, slowly retracted the flames, allowing the light to recede back to its original place.
“Fiery Embrace” is a skill that, theoretically, has no usage limitations; however, when he used it, he could still feel a certain drain on his energy. Using it for a minute or two didn’t pose any problems, but extending it to around an hour became strenuous.
“That said, the flames at the ‘Bonfire Sacrificial Ground’ are rather special; if it were ordinary fire, the duration might have been halved,” he explained.
Colin glanced over at the church’s interior; the recent commotion was considerable, but due to the peculiar nature of these flames, nothing actually got burnt. Rather, the flames eradicated accumulated dust and the remnants of decay lingering in the air.
“Boss, is this…” Li Ming cautiously approached and asked.
“It’s alright now, I was just testing out a skill, it feels pretty good.”
Colin waved his hand dismissively, changing the subject, “Let’s continue with the work arrangements then. I’ve got some other things to handle. If there are any issues, you can come to me. Oh, and leave the door open.”
“Understood.” Li Ming and others nodded, leading away the newly converted believers, the refugees.
They had just discussed it, and the work for the day was to systematically register everyone, craft some basic sort of identification documents. If they didn’t get this done now, as more people arrived later, starting then would become much more troublesome.
After tackling that task, they would turn to sanitation and treatment…
After a cursory examination, Lin Yilan found that many people suffered from moderate to severe malnutrition, as well as indigestion from consuming things like grass roots, bark, and even dirt, causing some bellies to bloat as if pregnant for five or six months.
Furthermore, many had wound infections due to various injuries; in the more severe cases, one could even see bones laced with blood through the flesh…
To implement emergency rescue, Lin Yilan took the “Gluttony’s Remnant” into her hands. Its negative effects were at most a mild discomfort for her, with no significant psychological burden.
After all, compared to the intense agony of pancreatic cancer, this was child’s play.
With the trio’s planning, everything proceeded smoothly…
Inside the church, Colin holstered his revolver and took out other pieces of equipment to review one by one, but unfortunately, he did not find any others that could be synthesized.
Currently, the only item that showed a synthesis prompt was the revolver.
“What a pity, so much junk equipment in my possession, nowhere to use it,” he sighed.
Colin had collected a fair amount of gear when the staff were offloading equipment during the peak of ‘storyline instance’ sales.
Many items seemed like a bargain, possibly useful, so he had placed orders, only to find out after the impulse buying that most of them weren’t particularly useful—suddenly owning more than twenty pieces of junk equipment.
However, it’s also possible that at some point, equipment that seems useless could come into play.
Take, for instance, the “Whole-body Fever” prop; to Lin Yilan, it appeared to be a very good medical aid, as controlled body heating could be quite effective.
Shaking his head slightly, Colin didn’t dwell on it. After confirming there weren’t any breakthroughs with his gear, he brought up the Bonfire’s attributes to check again.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 199 - 199 199 Holys Guidance_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 199: Chapter 199 “Holy’s Guidance”_1 Chapter 199: Chapter 199 “Holy’s Guidance”_1 The “Bonfire Sacrificial Site” was still at level one, with less than half a month of burn time remaining.
In addition, he didn’t know if it was because there were some more believers, but Colin noticed that the “Murky Energy Block,” which originally took 24 hours to produce, now only took 20 hours.
“Not bad, if it’s the believers that have reduced the time, then when more refugees come over, this time when I go back, I should be able to get about 10 pieces.”
“For an upgrade, you need a monster at a similar third stage of ‘Beast Transformation Syndrome,’ pity I forgot to collect those…”
“The remaining burn time isn’t a big issue, I just need to hunt something down and toss it in later…”
After briefly checking the information above, Colin withdrew his gaze.
In the following time, he didn’t just sit idly inside the church but went out to help everyone settle these sorrowful locals.
Even if Colin didn’t need to do anything, just his appearance alone significantly boosted the refugees’ morale, and they also became more compliant.
Colin found a place to sit casually and took on the role of a mascot of sorts.
“If every time I come over, I could work like this, lying around and slacking off, it doesn’t seem too bad.”
Pulling out a chocolate bar and putting it into his mouth, Colin squinted his eyes, a trace of contentment on his face.
The first day passed quickly, and the world’s eerie night came once more—Lin Yilan looked at the scene before her with a strange expression. It was her first time seeing such a peculiar phenomenon where the night was brighter than the day, and then the light and the darkness were distinctly separate from each other.
However, she didn’t remain shocked for long; she continued to clean the thick water on a refugee’s leg and pulled out the wriggling parasites inside…
After half a day of healing, she had a clearer idea of what medication she should bring next time.
The night passed without incident, and when day two was only about halfway through, the Warden’s nephew brought another group of over two hundred refugees for Colin to take in, then left again to bring in another batch of people.
“Boss, we’re short on management staff…” Li Ming, seeing Colin sitting in front of the church “doing nothing,” couldn’t help but come over and complain.
It was one thing having three hundred people yesterday, but today several hundred more arrived, and it looked like another batch might come before long…
The key issue was that they only had three employees on the job, plus one slacker; they simply couldn’t manage, let alone handle occasional disturbances among the refugees, such as fighting to get a better spot in line.
At this moment, the main reason he reported to Colin was to hope they could recruit more staff since three of them plus 12 “Money Slaves” were not enough.
‘It’s no use looking at me now, I don’t have the authority to recruit people…’ Colin muttered internally, and said expressionlessly, “I can’t call people right now. It’s a special time; please bear with it. If we’re short on hands, we can train some from the crowd. Don’t always think about relying on external help, use your brain more, rely on yourself…”
People they trained weren’t immediately usable. They already had trouble speaking one or two words, and were troubles themselves… Seeing the boss skillfully push the issue back, Li Ming didn’t say more and returned to his post with dark circles under his eyes, helping those later arrivals write their identity wooden tags.
“Next time I come in, I indeed need to speak with Lady Bunny and see if we can hire more labor.”
Colin took in the situation of his territory.
With the Warden’s nephew’s third arrival, the number of refugees had broken through a thousand. It was indeed challenging to manage them with only three people, even though the refugees were all very obedient.
There would always be this or that minor issue…
And according to the Warden’s nephew, there were at least another seven or eight thousand refugees needing to be relocated, which made everyone’s heads ache.
They only had enough food this time to support just over two thousand people; any more than that would be impossible…
As time ticked by, on the third day, a female practitioner named Vanessa arrived here with a few hundred people—ready to rest in a nearby town, only to find the closest town had been leveled. In the end, she chose to bring her group of “Magic Fog Disaster” survivors here.
However, upon reaching this eerie death land and seeing the church amidst it, Vanessa’s expression became indescribably strange.
She narrowed her eyes and carefully examined the mark on the church—a round sun with lines of varying lengths around it representing rays of light, and the entirely white walls of the church.
“Is this…if I’m not mistaken, isn’t this our church?” Vanessa couldn’t help but say.
However, she had been to the “Knight Kingdom” a few times and had never heard of a church there.
But she didn’t think much of it; seeing those thin but spirited refugees on the territory, she felt that the church wasn’t a big deal in their hands.
After all, under the sanctions of various countries, the “Church of Light” was not allowed to actively recruit believers, so it didn’t matter whether they had a church.
After a brief exchange with Colin, eating the delicious block-shaped food he handed her, and watching the busy figures on the estate, Vanessa suddenly felt a pang of guilt.
“By the way, is there anything I can help with?”
Finally, she spoke up, and since you were the one who offered, don’t blame me for not holding back…
Colin said with a troubled look, “Although I don’t want to bother a guest, as you can see, I really do need some help over here.”
“No problem, just give me some food, I have quite a few people with me, over sixty, plus seven or eight church members…”
“That’s not a big issue; I may have even more people here, around a thousand or so that need your help with settling and distributing food…”
“How many???”
Vanessa was taken aback, pointing to her wheat-colored face, “Over a thousand people? And you want just a few of us to handle this…”
As a grassroots clergy member, she knew what managing a thousand people entailed, but just as she was about to say that might be too much, Colin interrupted her with a grateful look:
“I appreciate it.”
After speaking, he had Li Ming come up to take over the liaison with her.
Vanessa looked at Li Ming’s thick dark circles under his eyes and felt his intense fatigue, becoming involuntarily silent.
She suddenly thought that accepting the “chocolate” from Colin’s hand might have been a hasty decision.
No… more precisely, perhaps coming here under the “Holy’s Guidance” was a bit too hasty.
…
Time passed quickly, and after several days of initial chaos, the situation at the Bonfire Sacrificial Ground finally stabilized, with the number of people settling at around three thousand, leaving the rest for later.
The food they originally brought was almost gone.
However, fortunately…
As time ticked away, Colin managed to hold on till the seventh day, and the “downfall event” was about to end.
Soon, as the chimes rang in his ears, Colin returned to reality.
As soon as he returned, Colin immediately felt his Yukionna issuing continuous warnings on his wrist.
Before he could understand what it was trying to tell him, he opened his eyes to find that in room 801, still filled with a large amount of materials, the atmosphere was somewhat tense. Qin Chuan and others carefully watched outside the window, as if on the lookout for something.
Shaking his head to dispel the trancelike feeling of transitioning between two worlds, Colin took a deep breath.
In the air lingered a strong fishy smell…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 200 - 200 200 Humming in the Waves_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 200: Chapter 200 Humming in the Waves_1 Chapter 200: Chapter 200 Humming in the Waves_1 “You’re awake?”
Qin Chuan saw Colin, who had been sleeping like the dead, finally wake up and breathed a sigh of relief.
When they had first noticed the anomaly, they had quietly started waking people up. Everyone else had awoken, but Colin had been sound asleep, taking almost a minute to respond after they called him…
“What happened? This smell…”
Colin was somewhat bewildered as he quickly recalled the memories from “seven days ago,” and then remembered that during this particular descent mission, they had encountered some creatures that might have come from the sea floor.
The smell seemed to be related to those creatures, and judging by the scent, they must be very close to this location.
At the same time, he felt a bit of pain in his shoulder. He pulled back his sleeve to look and saw two dark red marks, as if he had been pinched by something.
“Sorry, I might have pinched too hard just now,” Xia Liufang apologized from the side.
“It’s nothing.”
Colin pursed his lips, and it was only then that he generally dispelled the strange sense of alienation from having spent seven days in another world while only three hours had passed here, realizing what the “Yukionna” was chirping about—
It was probably about some very disgusting creature nearby.
At the same time, Qin Chuan also explained in a low voice, “The creatures that might come from the sea we encountered earlier are passing by outside, keep your voices down, they haven’t discovered us yet…”
What the hell are these things… Colin didn’t bother to check his rewards, but glanced outside as he spoke and saw a large group of uncanny, upright creatures resembling human beings holding torches as they moved through the darkness of the world below the building.
Squinting slightly, Colin’s pupils underwent some subtle changes. Under the clearer vision that followed, he saw these creatures had a high, scaly ridge on their backs and their skin was covered with deep blue, nearly black, and slightly reflective scales. Their hands had webbing reminiscent of a frog between them.
And their heads were incredibly large; to say they were human seemed more like some sort of fish…
“Not one or two of them have weak life forces…”
Colin looked over the muscles bulging under the scales, feeling the latent power beneath those muscles and it seemed there was some kind of indescribable special secret force over those scales.
As he observed them more closely, it was as if he could hear the sound of the waves in his ear and with each breath, it became somewhat difficult, as if his lungs were suddenly filled with water, dragged into the deep sea.
However, after shifting his gaze and silently invoking the “Beast Transformation Syndrome” tyrannical nature, that uncanny discomfort instantly disappeared, as if it had been devoured by something.
At that moment, the approximately fifty deep sea creatures below had not yet noticed the people stealthily peering from the eighth floor and continued to move amongst the ruins of the dark, destroyed city. Among these creatures, using chains around their necks, they had captured about one or two hundred people…
If Colin hadn’t been mistaken, these appeared to be all women, ranging in age from teenagers to women in their forties and fifties.
Their cries could be faintly heard from below…
“What are these creatures doing…” Qin Chuan couldn’t help asking Wang Hu, who was next to him.
Although he felt sympathy for the plight of the innocent survivors, it was evident that after surreptitiously comparing the strength of both sides, they simply did not possess the ability to attempt a rescue.
“I’m not quite sure…”
Wang Hu lowered his tone and voice, “When we were exchanging information before, I heard that these creatures from the sea seemed to specifically come ashore to capture women. There are generally three conjectures. The first is they capture them to breed their offspring, as female creatures of their kind have not been observed, or at least they can’t be distinguished if there are any. The second is they capture them for food, simply to eat them. The third conjecture is for some kind of special ceremony…
“But as for what exactly they are used for, I’m not clear, because before this, these deep-sea things generally only operated around coastal towns further south and didn’t appear here…”
As he was talking, a sudden disturbance arose from the group of creatures below, and they let out strange roars.
The people inside the room were taken aback, and immediately after, Wang Hu’s expression changed. He noticed the creatures were rushing toward a certain house, as if something was there.
“It’s our people!” Wang Hu exclaimed.
“What? Didn’t you say one day?” Qin Chuan frowned, noticing that it had been just over three hours, far less time than the other party had mentioned.
“I…” Wang Hu opened his mouth, seemingly unsure of how to explain.
But before he could speak, Qin Chuan said with displeasure, “Never mind. Next time, I hope you’ll tell me the truth. I want to tell you once again that I’m not interested in your settlement.”
Even without an explanation, everyone understood why they would say that; it was nothing more than a tactic to keep the location unpredictable.
If it were a normal situation, it wouldn’t be a big deal, but now it was causing complications.
“Which one of you claimed to know the location of the shelter…” An Extraordinary One interjected directly. These monsters were much more powerful than those with black skin; saving everyone was completely unrealistic.
“The girl with white hair…”
“A girl?”
“Yes…”
After he gave an answer, they didn’t delay any longer. Qin Chuan, along with two Extraordinary Ones and five armed personnel, as well as two survivors aside from Wang Hu, set off for a rescue attempt, planning to retreat to Shelter No. 24 afterward.
The remaining members, Xia Liufang and another official Fate Propeller Extraordinary One, along with two armed personnel, hid upstairs, charged with protecting Colin, the burn victim, and Wang Hu—three defenseless, helpless, ordinary people…
“Is this plan really going to work?” Qin Chuan couldn’t help but question.
If those monsters really discovered this place, to put it bluntly, they would have to do without a Fate Propeller, as they had no fighting power before reaching Level 5, only being slightly better than Colin’s group in not being disabled.
“You may not trust me, but you can’t distrust my premonition.”
The official Fate Propeller Extraordinary One said, “I have foreseen that this location is actually the safest. There won’t be any casualties even if there is an accident. I don’t know why this is the case, but compared to us, I think you should be more careful.”
As he spoke, he glanced at Qin Chuan’s forehead. “Do you know that the space between your eyebrows is dark and shining?”
“Say something more auspicious,” Qin Chuan spat, then promptly led the others downstairs.
After they left, the room suddenly felt emptier. The Level 2 official Fate Propeller casually sat on the floor. Seeing Colin, who suffered from Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, with a grave expression, he tried to reassure him:
“Don’t worry. If I say we’re going to be alright, then we definitely will. Trust me; it’s certain…”
Brother, don’t jinx it. Just relying on you, everyone here doesn’t know how many times they would die. They might even get their fill of Meng Po Soup…
Colin muttered to himself, pursing his lips and offering no comment on the other’s words.
Contrary to the man’s intuition, he felt a clear unease at that moment, being able to distinctly smell the “fishy scent” getting stronger.
And whether the intensification of the smell was due to the increasing number of non-human monsters downstairs was unknown…
“La la la la, la la la la, hmm hmm hmm, la la la~”
Suddenly, a soft, nasal hum of a song entered his ears, the gentle voice like a mother’s lullaby, full of a soothing, enticing power that made one want to get lost in it.
Initially, Colin didn’t pay much attention to it because the voice sounded familiar to him—it was Xia Liufang’s. But after listening for two or three seconds, his expression glazed over momentarily, as if he were hearing layers of waves bringing drowsiness to him.
However, in that moment of near indulgence, he violently felt a surge of anger burst forth from deep within. This anger swallowed the foreign sensation that had crept in, snapping Colin back to alertness.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 201 - 201 201 - Fatal Attack_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 201: Chapter 201 – Fatal Attack!_1 Chapter 201: Chapter 201 – Fatal Attack!_1 “Eat, eat, eat! Stinking fish, dare to charm me, I’ll just eat you… no, wait, eat my ass, who’s singing?”
Colin suppressed his anger, his gaze sweeping around. He did not see Xia Liufang opening her mouth; she stood there bewildered and silent, while others seemed to be enthralled.
The next moment, he seemed to sense something and turned his head to see a woman’s silhouette with long hair leaning over the windowsill behind the drawn curtains.
Through the curtains that were slightly blown open by the wind, Colin saw the lower half of a gray-skinned, fanged monster’s face.
At this time, from the slightly parting jaws of the monster, a delightful humming could be heard.
How could such a ghastly thing appear outside the eighth-floor window?!
The instant he saw it, Colin’s eyes flickered, and he immediately realized something.
“Damn it! It’s an ambush!”
Colin’s expression darkened, and while the monster had not yet seen him, he casually grabbed a can of beef from the lunchbox beside him and flung it hard at the creature outside the window.
With no attempt at stealth, the can of beef whistled through the air under his full force attack, shattering the glass and smashing directly into its head.
And it was at that moment that three tall figures burst through the windows around the room.
They were uniformly muscular with giant fish-like heads and frog-like hands and feet, resembling some kind of amphibious creature suited for waterways.
“Be careful, it’s an attack!” Xia Liufang, now alert, immediately drew her gun and fired.
Clang, clang, clang!
Sparks flew and a clear sound rang out when the specially made bullets hit them, causing her eyelids to twitch uncontrollably.
“What the hell are these things!”
Wang Hu, lying to the side, hadn’t finished speaking when he looked up in alarm. A fish-headed monster had already reached him, its palm larger than his head swiping towards his skull.
Without a doubt, being grasped would mean certain death.
However, just then, Colin suddenly grabbed his shoulder and pulled him backward, out of the attack range.
The fish-headed monster let out a screech of frustration, ready to continue the chase, but a blade made of translucent energy materialized and slashed at it, driving it back.
“‘Divine Strike’…”
Colin glanced at Xia Liufang, noting the sudden change in her demeanor as she wielded the large sword, exuding an aura of a heroine unfettered by her gender.
Ratatat!
The dense sound of automatic gunfire suddenly erupted; two armed individuals raised their rifles and fired relentlessly at the three monsters.
The more powerful rifle bullets were significantly stronger than the handgun rounds; while still unable to kill, they could tear through the monsters’ mysterious scales. One fish-headed monster, hit through the eye by chance, collapsed and convulsed with a scream.
“Don’t get bogged down in fighting, retreat quickly!”
The ‘Fate Propeller’ among the Extraordinary Ones shouted, helping to take Wang Hu, who Colin had pulled to safety, and then running out.
Everyone was no fool; once they woke from the charm, they immediately realized they were ambushed.
“Hu Zheng, didn’t you say we’d be perfectly safe up here?” Xia Liufang, wielding her large sword, forced back one of the fish-like monsters that tried to charge at them, and couldn’t help but curse quietly.
Compared to before, her temperament had grown much more fiery after using her ability.
“I, I didn’t know, but it’s normal for predictions to occasionally be incorrect…” The ‘Fate Propeller’ called Hu Zheng defended himself.
He truly had a premonition that his side was relatively safe, but for some reason, it was off.
Of course, cursing is one thing, but fortunately, on this building, whether due to the enemy’s negligence or not, there seemed to be only a few—
What they didn’t know was that Colin had used “Force – Repulsive Force” to throw the other Fishmen, who hadn’t yet jumped into the building, right out. Coupled with the cover of gunfire, no one noticed the sound of anything falling from the building.
“These damned things are really hard to detect when they’re lying in wait…”
Colin felt that their ability to hide was almost as good as that of the “Virtue Knight” he had encountered outside the door…
With his covert assistance, everyone barely managed to make it to the ground floor of Building D and saw Qin Chuan and others trying to rush back to defend. Upon hearing the commotion here, they quickly realized that the monsters had lured them away in a classic misdirection ploy.
However, the number of monsters was too great, and they were unable to come back in time…
Just as Colin had reached the ground floor, his expression darkened as he saw twenty or thirty fish-headed creatures wielding black harpoons, encircling the outside.
But for some reason, they weren’t charging as they had before, resulting in a standoff between the two sides.
“It’s over, there’s no escape…” Hu Zheng’s face changed as he felt a sense of despair.
Given the basic physical abilities of these creatures, they could kill them all just by mindlessly rushing in F2A style.
What made him even more uncomfortable was that, even at this moment, his intuition was still signaling “auspicious”…
“Damn it, ‘Fate Propeller’ is such a piece of crap. No wonder no dog would pick it, and the attrition rate is so high…” Finally, he stopped being stubborn and cursed angrily.
He hadn’t expected the supporter from Bonfire Company to take action, as that person seemed merely like a healer, unlikely to be more powerful than him…
“Why aren’t these monsters attacking, it’s strange…”
Colin didn’t understand why, but before he could think further, Xia Liufang suddenly spoke:
“It seems like I’m their target. I can feel it, they all seem to be watching me…”
Her pair of spirited eyes met those covetous gazes without a hint of retreat or fear, “Their goal seems to be to capture women. In a moment, I will activate the ‘Deification’ Status and draw them away. You all should take the chance to escape…”
This was the trump card of the “Divine Strike” pathway: once used, it would allow the “idol” they draw power from to descend briefly.
In doing so, she would achieve the combat power of a Level 6 “Ambassador.”
Of course, there’s a hefty price to pay for doing this. Without the actual strength of an “Ambassador,” even if it didn’t kill her, it was highly likely to cause her to lose control and forget who she really was…
‘Sigh, for the choices you’re making, you won’t die today. Let’s just reveal what’s behind the mask… I’m done hiding…’ Colin silently sighed and reached into his pocket, clutching a revolver.
But at that moment, his expression suddenly changed—
“Deadly Insight” was triggered!
A blurry image surged into his brain: a huge harpoon suddenly thrust out from the wall, impaling him completely on it, and then pinned him against the wall.
Not dying immediately, he “saw” a very large Fishman rushing out from the depths, releasing lightning, killing everyone except for Xia Liufang.
“Fuck, these bastards aren’t attacking now because they’re wary of me? So they shook me down? How did they lock onto me?”
A thought flashed through Colin’s mind, and the hand holding the revolver turned, gripping the corner of a golden card instead.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 202 - 202 202 Deep Sea Messenger_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 202: Chapter 202 “Deep Sea Messenger”_1 Chapter 202: Chapter 202 “Deep Sea Messenger”_1 Buzz!
The roaring of the invisible engine exploded beside Colin’s ear. Everything seemed to slightly lose color, being dragged into some sort of unseen field, falling into an apparently eternal stasis and solidification.
“That was close.”
Colin’s eyelids twitched as he saw the solid steel-reinforced concrete wall bulge slightly outward.
The tip of a harpoon, glittering with a heart-palpitating, cold sheen, was about to breach the surface like a bamboo shoot ready to emerge.
That harpoon’s tip was directly aimed at the position of his heart…
He was only half a second away from possibly being impaled by this massive harpoon.
But luckily, his “Deadly Insight” once again came in very handy.
As the thought flashed through his mind, Colin’s hands did not slow down in the least, and he used another card, “Force – Repulsive Force.”
With the power of this card, he repelled the people who had been in the direct line of fire and quickly retreated to a comparatively safer position.
“5 seconds is still too short to do much, need to repair it…”
Colin had just hurriedly completed these actions when the sound of a clock’s second hand ticking rapidly rang out beside his ear.
At the same time, several armed personnel, along with Xia Liufang, Hu Zheng, and Wang Hu, found themselves inexplicably flying into mid-air, each wearing a face of shock and uncertainty.
They had no idea what had suddenly happened.
However, it was at that moment that, with a thunderous boom,
A gigantic tri-tipped harpoon broke through the wall with a terrifying force, piercing straight through several walls at the base of the building before finally lodging in a load-bearing wall.
The dreadful noise and the resultant tremors made the entire building shake incessantly.
“Fuck, what kind of monster…”
Colin caught a glimpse out of the corner of his eye of the harpoon in the dust, still quivering. He saw that it was thicker than his thigh and estimated it to be around five meters long, with lots of rust, barnacles, and similar encrustations on it.
But he had no time to think any further, as he suddenly heard a terrible commotion outside. It seemed like some colossal creature had charged over, which, if he was not mistaken, should be the owner of that harpoon.
“You guys hurry and escape… be careful!” Xia Liufang was about to use her trump card, but suddenly saw a monstrous creature with an ugly, massive body, similar to a fish, bursting forth.
Its upper body somewhat resembled those of the Fishmen, but it was more ferocious, and just its upper body alone was two to three meters tall. Unlike other Fishmen, it lacked a bipedal lower body and instead was dragging a bloated, fat tail covered in scales, reminiscent of an eel or snake, as it surged into the building.
At that moment, this terrifying deep-sea creature charged in, and whether intentionally or not, headed straight for Colin, swinging its giant arm, covered in dark blue, nearly grey scales, viciously towards Colin.
“Why me again…”
Colin ran off to one side. If the first harpoon aimed directly at him was a coincidence, then this time it was definitely no stroke of luck!
This monster was coming for him!
Colin could even sense in the creature’s dead fish eyes, which were larger than his own head, a terrifying hatred as profound as avenging the death of one’s father.
Even as Xia Liufang launched an attack at it, it did not respond, still focusing solely on Colin.
In his contemplation, Colin narrowly avoided another attack. Just as he was about to grip the Revolver of the Contrarian to engage in direct combat, he suddenly saw an armed person lying on the ground, not knowing when he had fallen. His helmet was dented in, apparently having been hit in the head by splattered stones from a harpoon attack, and he was now as dead as one could be.
Seeing this corpse, Colin took a silent moment to mourn. Though the thought was somewhat hellish, he realized that with the addition of those Fishmen corpses, there were now enough materials on the scene for a sacrifice.
“Get out of the way quickly!” Xia Liufang’s anxious voice came again as she saw Colin standing still.
She swung her energy longsword, chopping down on the creature, but this time the blade that easily sliced through ordinary Fishmen could only pierce its scales before it could go no further.
“Hiss!!!”
The giant Fishman emitted a serpent-like scream, blowing Xia Liufang away, then continued to charge towards Colin with extreme speed. Sounds of electricity crackling appeared on its body, seemingly intending to use certain organs to unleash a powerful current, ensuring an unavoidable attack.
“You really hate me, don’t you…”
Colin stood still, looking as if he were frozen in fear to the others.
At that moment, watching the loathing-filled monster, reminiscent of a dump truck wrapped in thunder and lightning, charging toward him, a blur of icy blue shadow flew beside him. The frigid air rolled forward, causing the merman-serpent creature’s movements to pause momentarily…
But the pause was brief, and with a rushing sound, it erupted from its body, instantly dispelling all the chill.
Colin heard “Yukionna” let out a miserable shriek as she was electrocuted and flung away. “Yukionna” wasn’t very strong unless she lost control and her humanity was overtaken by instinct, so he didn’t expect her to hold out for long. His hand touched another card—
“Fusion Card: Smiling Mountain of Corpses”!
In an instant, all the corpses around him—friend and foe alike—melted away rapidly. They then gathered at an extreme speed on the body of the armed person lying not far from Colin.
“┗|｀O′|┛Ao~~”
A one-ton heavy, gigantic black flesh orb with the speed of lightning struck the Fishman creature. Two equally thick arms clung to its head, ignoring the crackling electricity, then opened its own mouth wide, unleashing a “Soul Scream” up close.
The merman-serpent creature’s brain vibrated before it quickly regained its senses and began to furiously tear at the smiling face on the black lump of flesh.
In the contest of strength, it easily gained the upper hand.
However, this time, perhaps due to the sufficiently high-quality sacrifice used for the summoning, Colin saw its body rapidly writhing and then splitting into a second equally massive flesh orb, clawing back some of the disadvantage.
Suddenly, two vast beings of flesh collided with passion, grappling desperately with each other…
It was at this point that Colin pulled a bone spur filled with black cracks from the “Storage Room”, planning to hand it to “Yukionna” for a stealth attack, but just as he grasped the bone spur, he abruptly felt an extremely terrifying gaze sweeping over him.
“What?!”
Colin’s scalp tingled, intending to trace the gaze to its source, but found that the sensation had vanished without a trace.
“Ao!!!” Corpse Mountain let out a wail as one of its arms was bitten off by the giant Fish head. Seeing the two flesh orbs of “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” steadily losing the struggle, he couldn’t be distracted with that and handed the bone spur to a nearly invisible “Yukionna”, asking her to find a chance for a secret stab.
While he made these arrangements, the others weren’t watching this scene but were instead staring in shock at the black flesh orb creature.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 203 - 203 203 A Big Misunderstanding_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 203: Chapter 203 A Big Misunderstanding_1 Chapter 203: Chapter 203 A Big Misunderstanding_1 “This damn thing, it followed us here!?”
Xia Liufang, Hu Zheng, and others looked on in astonishment. They were familiar with this sewer, the monster they had encountered for the first time in the sewer was the one before them now.
But, wasn’t this creature supposed to have disappeared on the second sub-level of the sewer? How did it suddenly appear on this level?
Just as the baffling thought arose, they saw the half-mermaid, half-sea serpent creature suddenly leap up, followed by an exceptionally painful scream—
It worked!
Colin shared the five senses with “Yukionna,” and in his mind appeared the image of her driving the Bone Spur into the creature’s wound. He immediately ordered her to stab and run, to quickly return.
If nothing unexpected happened, this monster’s violent backlash was about to follow.
Colin wasn’t sure if a stab like that would kill it immediately, but he could tell that it was not taking it easily after being stabbed…
Crackling arcs of electricity flickered incessantly over its body, but before the arcs could repel, they were all resisted by “Little Fist Stone.”
And amidst the heart-wrenching cries of agony, Xia Liufang and the others also snapped back to reality. Now was not the time to worry about where that damn thing had come from, but to take advantage of the two monsters fighting each other and escape!
“What are you still watching for, run!”
Seeing Colin still standing there “dazed,” she didn’t bother explaining, rushed over, grabbed Colin onto her shoulder, and fled towards another wall that had just been breached.
The remaining armed personnel and Hu Zheng and others also came to their senses. Without time to think further, they each carried the man with burn injuries and Wang Hu, following Xia Liufang, escaping the scene.
During this process, all the Fishmen no longer watched on as idly spectators like before, but rather, as if stimulated by something, they rushed over from their position.
However, they didn’t attack Colin and the others; instead, they charged at the Corpse Mountain that had visibly injured the “Deep Sea Messenger.”
Spear after spear flew from their hands and accurately impaled the Corpse Mountain, instantly turning it into something resembling a hedgehog.
As they continued to struggle, Colin and company had already gotten some distance away.
“What’s going on, what’s the situation with that thing…” Hu Zheng, an official Transcendent of the “Fate Propeller” path, wore a look of astonishment, still somewhat in disbelief—did they just escape?
This escape seemed to him akin to a “Mechanical Descension.”
Because that Black Flesh Orb monster had arrived here in an incomprehensible way…
No, upon closer thought, they didn’t understand what had happened when they were initially launched into the air. And if they hadn’t been thrown, they might have died in an instant—could it be…
Different perspectives converged into a single thought among the group.
“Thanks to the person sent by ‘Bonfire Company’ for their help, I can confirm it was him who made a move just now…” Hu Zheng said with a sincere face, feeling that he had guessed the truth.
He had just seen a partially invisible figure attacking near the monster before coming towards them and then disappearing.
Invisible, unseen, floating, lacking any substance…
Wasn’t that the same person who had aided them before?
Ah, this… Colin fell silent for a moment, suddenly realizing that under those circumstances, “The Light Chaser,” the mysterious individual who had been following them all the way but did nothing other than buffing, indeed fit the conjecture better.
After all, no one knew what other abilities “The Light Chaser” had, so it was natural to apply his capabilities to the other person, completing the logical loop…
And during the fight just now, everyone’s focus was on Corpse Mountain, nobody had noticed him.
“What was the deal with that monster?” Xia Liufang asked, puzzled, trying to get a response from the invisible individual the entire time.
Unfortunately, after lending them a significant hand, the person seemed to have no intention of explaining.
“It’s just a Little Hammer Stone that happened to pass by and decided to lend a helping hand…”
Colin responded silently in his heart. He had originally thought he was exposed, but to his surprise, it turned out to be a mix-up.
But this mess isn’t too bad either…
It was at this time, as the Fishmen were aiding the “Deep Sea Messenger,” that Qin Chuan and the others charged over. Compared to Colin’s side, the intensity of the battle they faced was obviously higher. Two out of the five armed personnel accompanying them had died, and the remaining three were also injured.
The two Extraordinary Ones who were with them were unharmed, although one had a fish spear that had been chopped off embedded in his shoulder, his face deathly pale…
As for the local survivors, aside from a little girl with white hair, only three unfamiliar faces remained, clearly indicating that almost ten other people had all died at the hands of those mermaid monsters.
Qin Chuan’s pale face glared at Wang Hu; if it weren’t for this guy hiding information, they wouldn’t have been so passive.
“Sorry…” Wang Hu spoke.
“Let’s get out of here first,” Qin Chuan, usually jovial, said with a very bad look on his face.
After that, everyone quickly made for Shelter No. 24. That place was safe as long as you didn’t stay too long, and they also needed to go back there to take some of the supplies left behind.
However, less than five minutes after they set off, Colin suddenly felt a jolt in his head, as if some dying voice transmitted into his mind, followed by a certain image—
The “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” was impaled with densely packed fish spears, flesh torn in multiple places, strong muscles slowly drooping, the body no longer sustaining itself, crumbling and dissolving into a thick, dark red sludge…
“This must be the first time Little Fist Stone got torn apart, huh.”
But just as Colin thought this was the end, he suddenly heard something intangible following this returned image to connect to his brain.
Accompanied by the inexplicable sound of tides, one angry roar after another, filled with resentment, arrived simultaneously.
“Colin… Colin… Colin…”
“Contemptible and ignorant fools, deceived and misled…”
“Blasphemous, God-slaying Promise Breakers…”
“Unforgivable villains…”
“The dying curse of the Great Will of the Deep Sea…”
“Shall descend upon thee, eternal and endless…”
“Thy sins shall endure for eons, until the end of time and space!”
The dense and agonized voices of resentment exploded in Colin’s brain, making him feel as if his brain were being torn apart by a terrifying undertow.
The one emitting these sounds seemed to be that horrific creature with the body of a human and the tail of a snake.
Clearly Bone Spur was formidable, but merely stabbing it and leaving, though causing immense damage and suffering, still had not killed it.
However, what puzzled him more than this was the various cryptic contents of the voice that made no sense…
He looked up to make sure no one noticed him and, enduring the headache, tried to analyze the meaning behind the “riddles” the creature had cursed.
“What does ‘contemptible and ignorant fools’ mean, and the ‘blasphemous, God-slaying Promise Breakers’? What does it all mean? Not to mention, how could the term ‘God-slaying’ be connected to me? Anything I’ve encountered related to it has me running for my life…”
“Which of these absurd things has anything to do with me? You can’t just shift the blame like this…”
“Huh? Wait a second…”
Colin’s eyes widened as he suddenly realized something.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 204 - 204 204 The Albinism Girl_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 204: Chapter 204 The Albinism Girl_1 Chapter 204: Chapter 204 The Albinism Girl_1 “Fuck, it must have been that guy causing trouble!”
Colin gritted his teeth, thinking of an inconspicuous figure who nevertheless was the start of this unexpected incident—
“Future me.”
“That’s right, if it wasn’t for him doing something despicable, I wouldn’t have been hit out of the blue. After all, I had truly not come into contact with that so-called Great Will of the Deep Sea, let alone slaying it.”
“And once it’s confirmed that he did it, then it first explains why that monster knew my name, and then targeted my appearance and scent, among other things. After all, we had tested before that we are identical physiologically. It’s based on these similarities that I got misinterpreted, although at first, I didn’t expect that he actually attempted gods… And looking at the results, it seems he was successful and the suspected deity of the Deep Sea most likely has perished.”
Thinking of this, Colin felt a chill in his heart, realizing that he had underestimated that “himself” who died in an unchecked corner of the world.
Of course, combined with the title “Promise Breaker,” Colin guessed that the process of this slaying was not exactly honorable, likely a sneak attack from behind that finally succeeded.
However, even if it was a successful sneak attack, the outcome is shocking enough.
But as for that fucker, he just died, leaving behind the one from this “Parallel World” to take up his misfortunes.
I haven’t even done anything and I’m saddled with a huge blame. I was nearly nailed to the wall…
“If you had the power to slay a god back then, then why didn’t you finish it completely, what the hell was the point of leaving behind all that mess?”
Right now, Colin truly wished he could revive that “Colin,” hang him up, and whip him for three days and nights, then tie him up and deliver him in front of those monsters.
Unfortunately, all this talk is useless now.
Colin took a deep breath in private, slightly reining in his negative emotions, and continued on the road while sorting out the entire sequence of events in his mind.
“Now, the first thing that can be confirmed is that the guy must have escaped successfully at the time. It’s just unclear why he ultimately died in that sewer full of rats. Hm, the other bodies are also quite suspicious. The ones who came out correspond exactly to those of us who went in, which clearly looks like some kind of ritual…”
“Right, that Eighth Level official might have been a mole infiltrated long ago. They just don’t know why they chose me. Plus, what that Deep Sea monster said about ‘the ignorant fools who have been deceived’ is quite interesting…”
“‘Future Colin’ also mentioned in his will that everything most likely started with the scheme of some existence. Whether it’s the disaster of this world or something else, it all comes from him. I just don’t know who this mastermind is, daring to plot against higher beings. It’s probably another higher being. If not, it wouldn’t necessarily be much worse than Miss Bunny…”
Colin’s mind was racing, yet, unfortunately, with a lack of key information, he only knew there was a mastermind behind the scenes, but nothing about this mastermind.
No, not nothing…
“Based on the current situation, that being has likely already escaped this ‘Box Garden World,’ and the creatures of the Deep Sea do not know that ‘I’ am already dead. Hence, with the switch in roles, only I am the unlucky one…”
Colin felt a headache coming on, setting aside the huge blame thrown at him. What was troubling him the most now was the monster’s “Deep Sea Curse.”
Although it seems like there’s nothing wrong at the moment, it still put him on edge for some reason.
But before he could ponder on it further, someone suddenly spoke up:
“We’re here.”We’re here?
On hearing this, Colin stopped walking and looked ahead, only then realizing that while he had been contemplating, everyone had unknowingly returned to the area outside the formerly-known Shelter No.24 Mall.
And behind them, the Fishmen by the sea did not pursue to kill them.
Colin pursed his lips, suddenly feeling a bit thirsty. He grabbed a bottle of water, opened the cap, and tilted his head back to drink. But just as he took a sip, he suddenly choked, bent over, and sprayed the water out, followed by a violent cough…
“Are you okay?” Qin Chuan and the others were about to question Wang Hu when they turned to see Colin choked by the water, tears and snot streaming down his face, as if his lungs were being carved out.
“No, cough cough… I’m fine…”
It took Colin several seconds of severe coughing before he recovered. Then, he raised his hand to wipe his mouth and nose, enduring the discomfort of choking, and looked at the fallen mineral water with a hint of alarm in his eyes—
Just then, for some reason the mineral water had surged into his windpipe and filled his lungs, truly making him feel as though he was choking to death on water.
And as someone with an “E level” physique, this obviously didn’t make sense.
So the only explanation was…
“That curse, it seems to have started working?”
As Colin’s thoughts raced, he realized the problem and after recognizing it, he discovered that if he listened carefully, he could always hear the sound of waves crashing in his ears…
Some deep-sea call seemed to be inviting him to the ocean.
Even Colin himself couldn’t help but feel the desire to set out…
“I must stay calm!”
Colin shook his head, reining in his thoughts. At this moment, he felt a mysterious fear of anything related to water, rivers, and the sea.
But beyond the fear, his organs, tissues, and cells were instilling an innate impulse to return to the sea.
Colin was not unfamiliar with this odd sensation; sometimes when he was on the rooftop, despite his fear of the height of a dozen floors, when he looked down, there would still be a bizarre urge to jump.
It was the same now…
“I need to figure out a way to leave this godforsaken place fast.”
Colin took a deep breath, realizing that something as mundane as drinking water could inexplicably cause him to choke—and he dared not think what might happen next.
“We’ve just come a long way, don’t drink water so hastily,” Qin Chuan, not thinking much of it, advised, since in his eyes, Colin was just an ordinary person suffering an incurable disease, who, despite the “buff”, was still only at the level of an ordinary person. Choking on water was quite normal.
After speaking, he turned his gaze towards Wang Hu and the others and said, “I hope you won’t hide anything this time. Who is this girl? Are you sure she can lead us to those shelters?”
“Don’t worry…”
Wang Hu, sitting on a stone, glanced at the little girl with a head full of white hair, “Actually, whether it’s her or me, we can both find the shelter. We’re both from the ‘Dawn’s Light Foundation’, no, to be more precise, from a branch of this shelter before the disaster. But I also took on some duties transporting goods, so that’s how I knew the general location of this research institute…”
“Never mind about you for now. What’s the deal with this girl?” Qin Chuan looked at the little girl who seemed to have albinism.
The girl had been in a dazed state since their encounter, not appearing to be normal.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 205 - 205 205 Forgotten Heroes _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 205: Chapter 205: Forgotten “Heroes” _1 Chapter 205: Chapter 205: Forgotten “Heroes” _1 “She was an advanced experimental subject of the ‘Dawn’s Light’ research; I’m not clear on what kind of subject, but if it weren’t for her, I probably would have died a long time ago…”
“She herself has some telekinetic superpowers. During the disaster, she took it upon herself to protect everyone, and she would occasionally speak, but after the disaster, for some reason, she became more and more silent and sluggish, and stopped defending herself…”
“Even when torn to shreds she wouldn’t speak, and then after being killed, she would revive and reappear in what she considered a safe place, usually a corner of a refugee settlement…”
“Can revive?” Colin interrupted in surprise.
“I… am not quite certain, but she always vanishes before sustaining a fatal injury, and I don’t know if that’s considered reviving.”
Wang Hu simply narrated, his gaze towards the girl filled with some indulgence, “This time, I want to take her with me to the research institute to see if there is a way to make her recover.”
Qin Chuan was non-committal towards his request, as their goal was to find a shelter that was still operational, then use that refuge to locate the ‘Hague Research Institute’, and finally to find a way to leave; this didn’t clash with the other party’s intentions.
At that moment, Colin spoke up, “Then, what’s the situation with that ‘Dawn’s Light’?”
While speaking, he carefully observed the little white-haired girl. She appeared to be only about ten years old, with her hair, eyebrows, and everything pale, but her eyes were a dark red, seemingly due to a lack of pigment.
And from Wang Hu’s words, it seemed the girl only looked like a child, but her actual age might be even greater than his.
‘No particular scent, no, there’s actually no scent at all…’
Colin found he was seemingly unable to make any effective observations of her.
However, as an unknown advanced experimental subject, having some peculiarities was normal. Since arriving in this world, there were plenty of things he couldn’t effectively observe, and so missing one more wasn’t a big concern for Colin.
“The ‘Dawn’s Light Foundation’ used to attempt to fuse various forces with the human body, creating many monsters. After the disaster, I only know their actions became more extreme, beginning to capture survivors in large numbers to perform some experiments; to date, no one has escaped.”
“However, their relationship with the ‘Human Future Research Institute’, another power within the shelter, is still relatively normal. Conflicts between the two are rare, and they often act together…”
“So, when you go there, there’s a chance they might act against you, but a greater likelihood is that they’ll communicate normally with you.”
Wang Hu had shared all that he knew.
The reason he wanted to take the little girl out was because upon learning that these people came from another unknown shelter, he wanted to leverage their status…
If it were for their own identities, those people would probably kill him without a second thought, and then forcibly take the girl away.
After listening to him, Qin Chuan nodded and said, “When the time comes, we’ll first make contact and see. For now, let’s replenish our supplies and rest for an hour, then head to that ‘Dawn’s Light Foundation’ you mentioned to see what’s going on with those people.”
“No problem, I will cooperate fully.” Seeing that the other party didn’t object to his idea of bringing the little girl, he breathed a sigh of relief.
Without further interaction, everyone first entered the shopping mall together holding torches, went up to the fifth floor to retrieve the supplies left over from the robots, and quickly left, encountering no creatures from the basement level during the brief process.
Then they found a place outdoors to make some simple adjustments, and while resting, Colin took the opportunity to take a glance at the parchment scroll.
“A little over a thousand but close to two thousand points, a silver-grade mission clearance certificate, so little…”
The recent few missions had all been worth tens of thousands of points, making him look down on such a small amount. But then again, it seemed they really hadn’t encountered anything frightening this week, and there was no danger either, so a little over a thousand points was not bad.
It just felt like something was overlooked…
Colin frowned, opened the [Mission Column] to take a look, and quickly twitched—
He discovered that he had seemingly probably perhaps ought to have… forgotten to rescue those seven “Heroes” again.
“Oh man, by my calculations, it seems a month has passed in that other world… They aren’t dead, are they?”
Colin blinked his eyes but quickly noticed that the countdown concerning the seven “Heroes” appeared to have been extended, with still over half a month remaining.
If nothing unexpected occurred, the “First Legion” might have lent them a hand.
Without dwelling on it, to avoid detection, Colin put away the parchment scroll and pondered how he should deal with the upcoming visit to the “Dawn’s Light Foundation.”
At this moment, he was making all his preparations on the assumption that a battle would erupt.
After all, just from Wang Hu’s description, there was a good chance these people had gone mad enough to lose their humanity. Coupled with the terrifying methods they likely possessed, it was best to prepare for the worst from the outset.
“With my strength, as long as I’m not facing Ninth Level Personnel, I can handle others, even if it’s an official Eighth Level Personnel. As for the Ninth Level… it’s unlikely to bump into them right off the bat, after all this isn’t a game of cards where someone starts with the jokers.”
Colin silently reflected on his initial impressions when he had real-life contact with two senior members of the Special Operations Department, and he approximately formed some judgments.
Soon, an hour passed in rest, and without any delay, Colin and his comrades, led by Wang Hu, moved through the deserted town, heading directly towards a certain suburban area outside the city.
Along the way, with a complete view of their surroundings, the group easily avoided a lot of trouble.
Moreover, they also noticed that in the darkness, these monsters, without the aid of their lights, were mostly weak-sighted. With just a bit of extra caution, they could easily bypass them.
They traveled silently, and several hours quickly went by. Except for a few stops to rest and regroup, they encountered no other delays and finally, in an isolated suburb outside the city, they found some traces.
“There’s almost no high-level threat here, just some minor, low-level nuisances. It feels like this place has been ‘pruned,'” Colin said after taking a deep breath, committing the situation of this place to memory through its scent.
“There’s a rather large golden arch nearby, standing alone. Look for it…” Wang Hu reminded them; he didn’t have the “Purification Heart,” so he could only see within the range the torchlight allowed.
And now, aside from the occasional lighting of a torch to discern direction, the group proceeded in the dark.
After all, once a torch was lit, not only could they see, but other monsters could also find them because of it. Being pinpointed could lead to a host of problematic situations…
Therefore, there was no need to add fuel to the fire once the issue of visibility was resolved.
“Found it, what now?”
After scanning the area, Colin found a clown statue under a golden arch at the three o’clock direction. The faded and mottled statue of a clown stood ominously in the dark, its gaping mouth worn with a sinister smile, staring at them.
“About one or two kilometers directly behind it, there’s a villa complex. Enter that area, find a rather large artificial rockery. Right in the middle of it is one of the entrances…” Wang Hu quickly recounted the route from his memory of the last visit.
Not hesitating, Colin and the others bypassed the golden arch and after another fifteen minutes, saw the collapsed area of the villa complex and the artificial rockery within it. They directly entered the fenced area…
“This villa complex, although called such, has actually always been a territory of the ‘Dawn’s Light Foundation.’ It was used as a cover from the beginning, and only very few people know that this place belongs to them. Uh, what the…”
As Wang Hu lay on top of an armed man, explaining the situation of the place, before he could finish, he suddenly noticed everyone had stopped.
While he was puzzled, he abruptly saw dozens of laser sights coming from all around, densely dotting their bodies.

chapters.title: Chapter 206 - 206 206 Mutation_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 206: Chapter 206: Mutation_1 Chapter 206: Chapter 206: Mutation_1 “I really hate it when someone points a gun at me, especially high-caliber rifles, and so many of them…”
Colin frowned, his peripheral vision catching the infrared aiming points on his body, knowing if that many bullets were fired, even with “Deadly Insight” triggered, dodging wouldn’t be easy.
He then seemingly fearfully shuffled his feet, moving behind the others, especially behind Xia Liufang—
During the time they had been together, he had secretly observed that although Xia Liufang was a girl, her physique, enhanced by “Divine Strike,” was actually the strongest among them, unlikely to be easily penetrated by bullets.
With the predictive advantage of “Deadly Insight,” Colin was confident he could react swiftly enough to protect himself.
His hand tightly gripping “Time Stasis,” he took a deep breath and surveyed the group hiding in every direction. He quickly identified a peculiar trait about them—
No breathing.
“Feels like they’re dead, but not actually dead. Their physical strength is clearly not inferior… Have they undergone some kind of modification? However, they hid really well, I only noticed something was off after entering the villa area…”
Once he positioned himself in a “safe” spot, Colin rapidly analyzed the situation and after a simple judgement that he should be able to react, he somewhat relaxed.
Compared to his composure, Qin Chuan and the others felt their scalps tingle, they were Transcendents with strength far surpassing ordinary people, but only at a two or three level, not at the point of ignoring bullets.
Qin Chuan was about to explain when he heard distinct footsteps from a certain direction, deliberately made. When they turned their heads, they immediately saw a person wearing a black suit and a Golden Mask.
“We mean no harm…” Qin Chuan immediately began to explain.
Before he could finish, however, he was interrupted by a gesture from the other person, and an unmistakably synthetic electronic voice emerged from the masked figure, saying:
“Whether you have ill intentions is irrelevant, but how did you find your way here? Confess truthfully, or I will order to have you shot dead right now.”
Qin Chuan nodded and continued, “We were led by a…”
“Wait a second…”
The person with the Golden Mask raised his hand again, interrupting Qin Chuan, giving Colin and the others a careful look as if realizing something, and clicked his tongue, “Oh, it’s you. You actually survived?”
If we hadn’t survived, would we be standing here as ghosts?
Everyone couldn’t help but mutter a sarcastic remark internally, but as soon as they did, they immediately felt something was off. Did this person recognize them?
“However, you didn’t come through this entrance last time, right? Strange, how did you find this place?” the man in the Golden Mask asked again in his strange, electronic tone.
“We were led by a…”
“Wait a second…”
God damn it! Interrupted multiple times, Qin Chuan’s eyelids twitched, feeling an urge to punch that jerk if it weren’t for the special situation— Didn’t anyone teach you how to talk properly when you were a kid?
The man wearing the Golden Mask seemed oblivious to Qin Chuan’s irritation, his gaze drifting to the injured Wang Hu and the others, he began speaking to himself, “If I’m not mistaken, it must be this guy who led you here. Normally, we’d capture you first, especially since allowing ‘Contaminated’ people near is very dangerous, especially that little girl, who doesn’t give me a good feeling…
“But with you all here, we will not act for now.
“Speak, then. What are you here for…”
“We were hoping to find you…”
“Wait a moment!”
Click.
Qin Chuan’s knuckles turned white from clenching, and the expressions of the team members grew harsh, annoyed by the other party’s manner of speaking.
“Before answering your question, I think you should answer a question of ours first,” he said.
“What question?”
“About the outside world. Have you confirmed the existence of other worlds this time? When you passed through here before, I remember you said this world was fake, everything was fake, and you were looking for your true home. I thought you were crazy then, unable to distinguish reality, but now…”
At this point, the man in the Golden Mask seemed to have thought of something, and with a strange laugh, added, “So, what about it? Any news on ‘Parallel World,’ ‘Future World,’ ‘Past World,’ or habitable regions and the like…?”
To confirm the existence of the outside world? Do these Box Garden World people realize something’s off?
Colin pondered within the crowd.
Then he saw that Qin Chuan and the others seemed to realize something too, and after a brief silence they spoke, “Yes, we have confirmed the possibility of other worlds existing, one hundred percent.”
Because they were legitimately from the outside…
From the conversation, they also realized that this group possibly mistook them for people from The Hague Shelter.
“Well, maybe we can discuss in depth later. Since you left three years ago, we’ve made some special discoveries. Let’s see if we can exchange information later.”
Left three years ago? So, the death of “us” in this world occurred at least three years ago? Qin Chuan pondered and nodded, “That’s possible.”
He didn’t refuse the request, nor could he.
However, just from this initial contact, he felt the people from Dawn’s Light Foundation weren’t as crazy as he had imagined.
At least they didn’t seem insane when speaking…
But the very next second, he thought he might have been a bit early with that assumption.
“Then let’s deal with these people’s situation first,” the man with the Golden Mask said, looking towards Wang Hu and the others. The eyes behind the mask squinted, the finger flickering lightly.
Following that, several flashes of gunfire emerged from the darkness, accompanied by the delayed sound of shots. Those in the back of the group, including Wang Hu and several survivors, bulged their eyes and collapsed.
The expressionless young girl with white hair still stood quietly, without any reaction.
“What are you doing?!” one of the Extraordinary Ones in the team exclaimed angrily.
“Don’t worry, I’m not like that bunch of extreme lunatics at the Human Future Research Institute. We don’t kill ‘Contaminated’ who aren’t in the final stages, so we merely used fast-acting anesthetics. After we get their information, they’ll be given a way out…”
