“However, the girl with white hair is an exception. We’ve found our custom chip inside her, which suggests she might be a Containment Subject we’ve once detained, and not just any, but an Ultra-Dangerous Class 1 Containment Subject…”
“We must contain her first while she’s unresponsive!”
Even though it was still a synthetic electronic voice speaking, Colin and the others could distinctly feel that he had become very cautious.
And just as the words fell, an abrupt change occurred.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 207 - 207 207 God is Not Invincible_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 207: Chapter 207 “God” is Not Invincible!_1 Chapter 207: Chapter 207 “God” is Not Invincible!_1 Drip—
A drawn-out siren suddenly blared, and Colin and the others saw a piece of skin on the little girl’s neck suddenly flash red, suggesting through the skin an implanted chip.
The expressionless little girl with white hair flinched, suddenly looked up, and her eyes swirled with a vivid blood red.
An extremely terrifying aura burst forth from her…
In that moment, the faces of those nearby her changed, feeling as though they were facing not a little girl but a terrifying entity rapidly resurrecting…
“This lifeform’s fucking on par with the ‘Formless Mother,’ and they knew it was dangerous yet still provoked her?”
Colin cursed inwardly, wanting to flee but found his body immobile, and his brain quickly becoming blank as if all memories were being erased by some power.
Being this close to the entity was a serious risk; even the effect provided by the “Purification Heart” seemed barely functional.
It was at this moment that the chip on the girl’s neck suddenly burst with an intense electrical surge, apparently activating something that caused red lights to flicker on various parts of her body—a clear indication of some form of restraint.
This prearranged measure directly interrupted her resurgence process…
But that alone wasn’t enough—Colin could clearly feel that she was still not completely restrained, and she might break free from the current standoff if she persisted.
Without further thought, Colin steeled himself, and as he noticed her gaze suddenly turning towards him, her lips slowly began to move as if she wanted to say something…
“Become my serva…”
Before she could finish, a black metal spear flew in suddenly and impaled her through the heart with deadly precision, causing her small body to collapse powerlessly to the ground, like a chunk of skewered meat dropped on the floor, with all signs of life fading away.
“What was she about to say? Become her what?”
Colin looked at the girl on the ground, puzzled. Despite her heart being pierced, not a single drop of blood could be seen flowing out.
If it weren’t for the black spear that had transpierced her small body, she would appear as if she were simply sleeping on the ground.
Just then, someone’s voice suddenly came from one side:
“Phew, that was close, thankfully I caught up in time, it wasn’t in vain that I dragged out our conversation for so long, allowing the ‘Reality Stabilization Spear’ to be delivered…”
The man wearing a golden mask arrived in front of Colin and the others, seeming relieved, and upon seeing their gaze, he let out a laugh with an unpleasant mechanical sound.
But before he could speak, Colin asked first, “What exactly is this thing?”
“I’m not quite sure myself. All I know is that it’s definitely a high-risk containment subject. We will probably have to wait until later, once the Foundation finds the records, to know exactly what she is. Wait a moment, let me give her another ‘Reality Stabilization Spear’ to ensure the effect…”
As the man with the golden mask responded, he reached out to take another metallic spear, roughly one meter eight in length, from his subordinate, and easily carried the hundred-something-pound spear. He aimed it at the temple of the girl who appeared to be fast asleep and impaled it without hesitation.
Crack…
The spear, thick as three fingers, drove through her head, pinning it solidly to the ground.
Even though the little girl still looked as if she were deeply asleep, the indifference and efficiency with which it was done caused a twitch in the eyelids of Colin and the others.
It was at this moment that a modified vehicle arrived, with a snap the door opened, and more than a dozen yellow-clad personnel in protective gear carefully placed the little girl into a cylindrical vessel. They then lifted it onto the vehicle and drove away.
“The people from your Hague Research Institute were quite fussy before, but I didn’t expect that after a round trip, they would appear even fussier. It’s just about enhancing the containment effectiveness, containing a threat—is such a reaction really necessary?”
The man with the golden mask scoffed, shaking his head, his words tinged with a hint of respect: “But then again, it’s hard to imagine that you folks could achieve the ‘God-slaying’ feat. My salute to you, for you have proved a possibility to us!
“The so-called ‘God’ is not invincible.”
A ‘God-slaying’ feat? What ‘God-slaying’ feat?
Qin Chuan and the others were initially startled, then recalled something, their expressions somewhat strange—they had actually done such a thing?
Upon hearing these words, Colin knew his previous guess had been confirmed: his “future self” had indeed performed the act of slaying a god. The question was…
“But looking at this guy’s words, it wasn’t just me involved in that operation. Why single me out?”
After thinking for a moment, Colin could only conclude that perhaps it was he who had delivered the killing blow.
“Alright, enough idle talk. Come with me.”
The man with the Golden Mask made an inviting gesture and led the group for a few minutes to a villa that had collapsed to less than a third of its original structure. He opened a vertical shaft in the villa’s courtyard and, taking the lead, climbed down the handrails along the shaft.
Colin and the others exchanged glances before ultimately deciding to follow the man’s path down the line.
Partway down the shaft was a hole just big enough for someone to stoop and pass through. After squeezing through and walking a few thousand steps, the path suddenly opened up.
A subterranean space with thick walls and a sci-fi feel unfolded before them, filled with soldiers standing guard. They were fully armed, all wearing black masks, showing no excess curiosity towards Colin and the others who were led in, nor any signs of breathing—they genuinely did not breathe.
“What’s up with these people here, not needing to breathe? And why are they all wearing masks—is there an explanation for this?” Colin wondered internally.
However, without dwelling on it and led by the man in the Golden Mask, Colin and the others arrived in a large, spartan hall filled with ammunition.
“Take a seat. There’s water on the table as well as dried worms, a specialty from our ‘Dawn’s Light Foundation’, available in cumin or durian flavors. I suggest trying the snail noodle flavor, which I prefer. A representative from our foundation will be here soon. Before that, let me tell you…”
In the middle of his speech, a woman wearing a Golden Mask as well, but with a “3” written on it, walked in.
She was tall, wearing high heels and a suit that was both stylish and professional. Upon entering and seeing the people sitting in chairs, she used an almost identical electronic synthesized voice to take over the conversation:
“I am the negotiation representative from the Dawn’s Light Foundation. Please forgive the absence of the board members due to some emergent matters, but my presence here also represents their will.
“First, we thank you for bringing us an entity from a high-level project, but concerning this entity’s information, we are not at liberty to disclose it. You may choose some items as remuneration afterward…
“Moreover, there is another matter of urgent concern. We’ll cut to the chase…
“We will agree to your request for help, and the Human Future Research Institute will join us in helping you take revenge on those things that destroyed the Hague Research Institute and prevent a disaster from erupting.
“But on this premise, you must disclose all research findings of leaving this world…
“Or…”

chapters.title: Chapter 208 - 208 208 Identity Exposed_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 208: Chapter 208 Identity Exposed_1 Chapter 208: Chapter 208 Identity Exposed_1 “Or share with us the nanomechanic foundry technology within the ‘Hague Research Institute,’ and if a real path to leave this world exists, I hope the people of our shelter can obtain a certain number of slots to follow and leave…”
“Of course, since the affairs inside the Hague Research Institute have already endangered the entire world, even if you don’t ask for help, we would still proceed to resolve it. Therefore, on this point, we will offer a certain compensation.”
“We will share with you what we have discovered in these three years, about the true state of this world, a secret we uncovered after some investigation prompted by your reminder.”
The woman, wearing a golden mask and uniform, her feet in high heels, spoke unhurriedly.
Although she had said a lot all at once, in a peculiar electronic voice, her words were very clear, allowing time for thought.
However, no matter how much time they had to think, everyone was a bit dumbfounded because they didn’t understand a thing…
What nanomechanical engineering technology, what achievements in leaving the world, and what exactly is going on with the “Hague Research Institute”?
Endangering the entire world?
Is there still anything that can be described as endangering in a world like this?
Colin and others’ minds were boiling like hot water, bubbling up with a multitude of questions, and they were at a loss for words for the moment.
However, to the two people in front of them, their behavior seemed like they were pondering, so for the moment, it went unnoticed.
The hall, filled with a vast amount of ammunition, quieted down.
After six or seven seconds, Qin Chuan finally spoke up after pondering: “Wait, are you saying the ‘Hague Research Institute’ sent out a distress signal to you?”
After this question was asked, the body of the woman with the golden mask froze noticeably, as if the face behind the mask was stunned.
“Wasn’t it you who sent it out?” the woman asked confusedly, “At seventeen days, twenty hours, thirty seconds, our foundation received your distress signal, and after one hour and thirty-three minutes, dispatched an investigation team. Ten days later, we preliminarily clarified the situation and held a joint meeting with the executives of the ‘Human Future Research Institute.’ Three days ago we made a decision…”
At this, she paused, then added, “Didn’t you come for this reason?”
This time her synthesized electronic voice was much faster, but it was still clear enough to be understood.
Big sister, don’t be so detailed… Colin was a bit bewildered as he listened; he felt that the people at this research institute seemed to have some communication problems—they seemed a bit too straightforward.
However, at this moment, a man wearing a golden mask who liked to interrupt others raised his hand: “Wait, it seems it really wasn’t sent by them…”
He briefly explained why Colin and his group had come to them.
“You have already left this world and just recently returned?” the woman with the golden mask emitted a mechanical synthesized female voice from behind the mask.
She tilted her head, eyes behind the mask showing a trace of surprise: “Have you truly confirmed the existence of other worlds?”
To say so wouldn’t be wrong; after all, it couldn’t be said that “us” from this world had died, and we were now from another world…
Colin thought for a moment and decided whether or not to give Qin Chuan a hint when he saw the latter nod slightly before speaking with apparent concern: “What happened at the ‘Hague Research Institute’ during the time we were away?”
As part of the “Hague Research Institute” membership, Qin Chuan felt that he should show the appropriate attitude.
What happened? No matter how you look at it, you should have been able to guess, right?
The two individuals with golden masks didn’t respond immediately, but showed some suspicion, suddenly aware that something was amiss.
However, at that moment, Colin abruptly thought of something and added: “Is it those things from the deep sea?”
If there was anything closely linked to this research institute, it had to be those monsters from the deep sea—
After all, “Colin” had slain the once great will of the deep sea; Qin Chuan and the others didn’t know as much, but he was different.
“Yes, after your departure, the followers codenamed ‘002’ somehow found the ‘Hague Research Institute,’ breached the defenses you left behind, located the god’s corpse remnants, and seem to be trying to resurrect ‘002.’ Despite combining the data you had left, we deem their resurrection’s likelihood extremely low, with a success rate of less than one percent. However, should He be resurrected, the consequences would be unimaginable.”
There was a profound dread in the woman’s voice…
Though “Colin” and his party didn’t involve them in their deed of slaying the god, they had taken away nearly a thousand ‘Reality Stabilization Spears’ from them.
Therefore, should that higher will awaken once again, they—no, everyone within this large area—may be annihilated by the ancient god, should He return, through the power of the ocean.
It was only after she finished that Colin and the others learned about the situation at the “Hague Research Institute”. Thinking back to their recent harrowing encounter with the large fishmen, they exchanged uneasy glances, unsure whether they should proceed or not.
As the main participants in “slaying the Ancient God”, they didn’t need to think too hard to realize that they would face the most resolute attacks from those terrifying creatures.
At this moment, they felt the same sense of being screwed as Colin…
Dammit, none of this had anything to do with them, yet they were inexplicably taking the fall for a giant mess.
“Originally, we were planning a forceful assault, but now that you’re here, things will clearly be a bit easier to handle. Your presence won’t trigger the other defense systems of the ‘Hague Research Institute’…”
The man with the golden mask suddenly spoke up, his gaze sweeping casually over everyone before withdrawing his attention from Colin’s delicate yet intact legs:
“If all goes well, we’ll head to ‘The Hague Shelter’ in two or three days to stop them. What do you guys think?”
What could they think? They obviously had to agree. Qin Chuan glanced at the others, and seeing no objections, nodded his consent:
“No problem.”
Regardless, a trip to “The Hague Shelter” was essential since that was the only place where they could find information on how to leave.
Seeing him nod, Colin also breathed a sigh of relief, for his sole task was to investigate the data at “The Hague Shelter”.
Without sufficient information, “Bonfire Company” would likely be unable to assign them their next task for leaving.
They were originally facing the possibility of confronting the situation on their own, but now they had the assistance of two shelters. It could only be seen as an improvement.
After settling on this, Colin and the others discussed remuneration, which was similar to their initial talks, but now included a request for the “Dawn’s Light Foundation” to assist with post-disaster reconstruction.
Before long, having settled various issues, they agreed to meet in three days. Colin and his companions were then temporarily housed in a three-story underground residence, each level covering about three hundred square meters and including facilities such as a bathroom, library, great hall, and so on…
In the pricey underground district, their accommodations were quite sizable—according to the man, they were places where only senior officials could reside.
“Meals will be delivered every eight hours on schedule. If you have any other requests, you can use the internal phone to contact us. I have some matters to deal with first…”
After saying this, the man with the golden mask bid farewell to Colin and the others, returning to the large hall where they had previously conversed.
The woman was still there, not having left.
As the man entered, she dispensed with any pleasantries and immediately shared her observations about Colin and his companions.
“Their emotions are off… When I spoke of the ‘Hague Research Institute’ being attacked, their initial reaction was almost completely indifferent. Considering the intelligence we’ve gathered about them, they regard the ‘Hague Research Institute’ highly, and even for the sake of the ordinary people there, they shouldn’t be so aloof…”
“Moreover, I did not observe any nanomachinery on their bodies, something that has completely disappeared, and the metal composition ratios on the gear of several armed personnel are unfamiliar to me, as are the models of the equipment…”
“On an even more detailed note, Colin’s legs should be fitted with pre-disaster Model 47 mechanical prosthetics, and Xia Liufang, Qin Chuan, and others should have nanotech hearts instead of their original flesh-and-blood hearts. Also, their contamination index is at 0, which is impossible. Even for people in various research institutes, the average fluctuates between 0.1 and 0.5, while previously, their data showed around 0.3…”
“Wait a minute!”
The man with the golden mask couldn’t help but interrupt his colleague, aware that when she got emotionally agitated, she tended to talk more and try to back her claims with all sorts of data:
“I can guess what you’re trying to say. You mean to suggest that they are definitely not those people, right?”
“Yes,”
The woman nodded, then continued, “But…”
“Wait a minute!”
“Get to the point. You’re trying to say that although you’re certain of this, all the instruments insist that their biological signals, while inconsistent, are matching, and it’s definitely not a case of parasites or the like?”
The man with the golden mask seemed to preempt her words, but he knew if she continued, she might add another ten or so sentences before reaching her ultimate conclusion.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 209 - 209 209 Human Future Research Institute_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 209: Chapter 209 “Human Future Research Institute”_1 Chapter 209: Chapter 209 “Human Future Research Institute”_1 “To be honest, I’m not certain about their situation either. I have some bold ideas, but upon further thought, they might be too bold,” said the man in the golden mask thoughtfully. Just then, a person approached, wearing a silver mask, a surveillance officer. At that moment, he pressed on his neck, emitting a chaotic jumble of static from his mouth.
Of course, this seemed like noise to others, but for those who had implanted the special chip, it was clear that he was conveying some intelligence.
“They seem to be persistently browsing through some encyclopedic books in the library. This behavior is a bit like gathering intelligence, or rather, getting to know…”
“…this world.”
After the man in the golden mask finished speaking, both fell silent for a moment.
“There are two possibilities, one is that they are outsiders, and by coincidence, everything fits. The second possibility is that something happened to them during their last action, causing them to be reprogrammed, but there’s a lot that can’t be explained…”
“Wait a minute, let’s not guess about these things.”
He interrupted the other person and took a half-smoked cigar from his pocket, placed it in his mouth, and lit it: “No matter what, one point can be confirmed, the intelligent machinery cannot detect any errors in their biological signals, and that’s enough.”
What they needed was just that; otherwise, in their next move, they would likely encounter the Hague Research Institute’s defense systems. Thinking of the swarms of nano-machinery and such, they felt a headache coming on.
Based on the available intelligence, those “Clan” members from the sea had opened an unknown passage to get inside, but clearly, they could not take the same route.
So, when it comes time to stop the revival of the Deity, they also had to break through the outer defenses of the Hague Research Institute…
Including the Hague Research Institute, there are only three remaining shelters in this vicinity now; most others have been destroyed for various reasons.
And since they had both cooperation and conflict with The Hague Shelter, they were very clear about how troublesome the nano-machinery-centered defenses of the Hague Research Institute could be.
Originally, they planned a strong attack, but since these people had come, why not see if they could circumvent the defense system and even counterattack those damn stinking fish.
“I understand. I’ll organize our information and submit it to the Foundation’s board of directors.”
“Hmm.” The man in the golden mask nodded and took a puff of his cigar. After cycling the rich tar and nicotine through his lungs, his mind became much calmer.
To savor the pleasure of the cigar, he had even kept a small portion of his original lungs.
Then, his voice synthesizer engaged as he asked, “By the way, what’s the situation with the Human Future Research Institute? What are they planning to do on The Hague side?”
“I’ve received intelligence that they are ready, mobilizing a Level 6 ‘Twilight Angel’ for a sacrifice and preparation.”
“A Level 6 ‘Twilight Angel’? It seems they are indeed taking this operation very seriously. Tsk, it means another deputy director will be sacrificed…”
“Also, upon learning about the situation here, they’ve arranged a delegation that should arrive tomorrow…”
The woman in the golden mask seemed to think of something: “Regarding their identities, perhaps we can help cover for them to avoid any accidents. You and I know these people can be quite mad, sometimes failing to grasp the urgency of situations. After discovering the anomalies with these people, two to three layers of them might attempt an aggressive detention, which in their words, is keeping the accident within control. But there’s no need for that now…”
“I feel the same, heh, if it weren’t for those extreme human supremacists’ ‘Human Ascension Project,’ this apocalypse might not have been so terrible.”
“Not necessarily, if we look at it dialectically without emotion, if it wasn’t for them, possibly everyone in the Asia-Pacific region would be dead by now…”
“Who knows…”
The man in the golden mask was noncommittal, simply bringing the cigar to his lips for another puff, then reached out to the woman in the golden mask: “331, how about it, want a puff? Special supply that only the big shots before the disaster could enjoy.”
“No, I need to put together the report of this conversation.”
…
Meanwhile, as they held their secret conversation, Colin and the others, through various books in the residential library, had come to roughly understand the situation of this world.
“The world before the catastrophe was largely consistent with the history of Earth, but records are sparse, lacking in detail…”
“As for the specific time of the disaster’s outbreak, opinions vary, with some saying it was the 24th year and others the 25th… Now, more than twenty years have passed, and civilization has almost experienced a discontinuity. Currently, optimistic estimates suggest that the total world population might be less than thirty million…”
Reading the content of the popular science book, Colin was shocked by the information provided, not realizing that these books might have been a “trap” specifically left for them by the foundation.
But even if he knew, he still had to read…
At the same time, he also understood what the masked man meant by “the Contaminated”…
These people carried various mysterious contaminations, which were difficult to detect. The Contaminated appeared no different from normal people most of the time, only showing signs when the contamination reached a certain concentration, or under certain special circumstances.
Generally speaking, once a settlement’s population exceeded three thousand people, and they were all Contaminated, aberrations would inevitably occur.
Therefore, the Shelter’s countermeasures were to constantly patrol outside, driving away and suppressing survivors to prevent the emergence of large settlements, and to execute those whose contamination index exceeded a certain value…
“No wonder the settlements Wang Hu mentioned before were all just a few hundred people, at most not exceeding a thousand. Could it be intentional?”
Colin glanced at the page in the book, which mentioned several Shelters like “Da Jiang Shelter,” “Bei Chuan Shelter,” and others, were ultimately destroyed because they failed to properly handle their surrounding situations.
“In that case, Wang Hu and his people do have some problems…”
Colin thought of the abnormal zeal displayed by Wang Hu and the other survivors when they mentioned “White Night” during their journey.
That thing was likely some kind of contamination, just that it hadn’t reached a critical concentration, so it hadn’t caused any noticeable abnormalities yet…
“This world is truly dangerous,” Qin Chuan couldn’t help but express his sentiment.
As an official, he could see that the disaster classification here had some slight differences from the other side, but overall, the disparity was not great. However, Earth had not yet experienced the world-upending “S” Level disasters, while this place had at least five such disasters on record…
As for A Level disasters, the number was frighteningly high, with twenty-seven recorded just in the Asia-Pacific region alone.
What was special, though, was that there weren’t many disasters below A Level.
Everyone initially thought the number was too large to count, but later learned through annotations that most disasters below this level were devoured by others…
“It’s almost like raising gu,” Colin couldn’t help but comment.
With information from Bonfire Company, he was well aware that this world was most likely a “man-made” world.
It remained unknown who was able to capture so many entities and confine them here…
And why was this “man-made” world made to resemble Earth so closely?
“Speaking of which, didn’t those survivors say that a lot of deplorable things happened in those two Shelters? I don’t seem to see much about it, and wasn’t there talk about collecting embryos from pregnant women one month into pregnancy or something…” someone curiously interjected.
“Do you think it’s possible to find the dark secrets of a Shelter while taking refuge in it?”
Colin shook his head helplessly and continued to read. The book introduced many of the Shelters’ research findings, such as the discovery of new material uses and the identification and exploitation of certain Containment Subject’s characteristics, among other things.
Behind these “achievements,” who knows how many lives were sacrificed…
The group sat in the library, constantly perusing one book after another, with time steadily passing by. After more than twenty hours, a group of people dressed in extremely heavy yellow protective suits suddenly entered the residential area.
Getting up from the living room couch, Colin stood and watched these figures, resembling armored humans, with caution.
“Who are you?”
“I am a delegation member of the Human Future Research Institute…”

chapters.title: Chapter 210 - 210 210 Blood Debt Must Be Tasted with Blood
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 210: Chapter 210: Blood Debt Must Be Tasted with Blood! _1 Chapter 210: Chapter 210: Blood Debt Must Be Tasted with Blood! _1 “This is our institute’s second director, Director Chen Guang, and I am the director’s assistant. These here are accompanying researchers, Lü Guang, Huo Jinxiang…”
A person clad in a heavy-duty protective suit moved forward to introduce the group to Colin and his people.
However, aside from the deputy director and the assistant whose protective suits were a bit more lavish and bulkier, equipped with some personalized gear, there was really no obvious distinction between them and the rest.
Each individual looked about a meter and twenty at the very least, resembling elongated, oval-shaped balls with legs.
And among this group of people, the man wearing the golden mask and the female representative were present as well.
“Hello, Director Chen Guang…” As the captain of the team, or at least the apparent captain, Qin Chuan stepped forward, greeted the other party with a genial smile, but he did not extend a hand for a handshake.
In the post-disaster world, handshakes had all but disappeared.
Qin Chuan also refrained from saying things like ‘I’ve long admired your name’ or ‘first time meeting you’—what if in this “future” it wasn’t the first time they had met? That would complicate matters…
“Heh.” Director Chen Guang, enshrouded in a heavy protective suit, looking like an oval tin can with long legs, chuckled sarcastically, “Impressive, impressive. To have survived that incident with so many of your people alive.”
There seems to be a tinge of hostility…not just Qin Chuan, even Colin and the rest could sense something off in the tone.
“Wait a minute…”
The man with the golden mask suddenly chimed in with a synthesized mechanical voice, chuckling, “Director Chen Guang, let’s set aside some personal matters for now. The current situation endangers the future of humanity. I can’t say that the past is the past, but we need to prioritize…”
As he spoke, he couldn’t help but inwardly sneer at having to deal with this stubborn old man, foreseeing complications in today’s negotiations…
“223, there’s no need for you to rush in playing the good Samaritan. My son, daughter-in-law, and son-in-law died in that battle. I hold no grudges, only pride for them, which symbolizes humanity’s truly limitless potential…”
No grudges? Your resentment seems sky-high… The face behind the 223 mask pursed his lips, neither agreeing nor disagreeing, yet still plastered a chuckle on his face to dismiss the issue and prevent any trouble from arising.
“Alright, let’s not dwell on it any further,” said Deputy Director Chen Guang before turning to address Qin Chuan. “Let us now discuss the specifics of this matter.”
“Of course!” Qin Chuan nodded without letting the previous exchange sour his disposition.
Soon, Colin and the others came to understand the specific purpose of their visit. The other party began by asking about the internal defenses of the “Hague Research Institute,” but such details were beyond anybody there to accurately answer.
However, at that moment, the female representative from the Dawn’s Light Foundation spoke up, stating that these matters had been discussed previously and the relevant documents would be handed over later, temporarily deferring the topic.
Then came negotiation over the distribution of benefits after the expulsion of the ocean “affiliates,” an area in which Qin Chuan, Colin, and their people exhibited a grand disposition—after all, it was not theirs to claim, so making a perfunctory effort for appearance’s sake sufficed, manifesting an attitude of indifference typical of someone bargaining with assets they did not own.
Ultimately, almost two hours later, this impromptu meeting came to an end. Watching the rotund members of the “Human Dawn Research Association” depart, Colin and his group let out a sigh of relief.
“Alright, in about 27 hours, we will begin our operation. Adjust your schedules accordingly, and if you need to resupply with any special ammunition or equipment, let us know,” said the man with the golden mask before leaving the place.
“Weird, why do I get the feeling that these people from the Dawn Foundation have suddenly become so amenable?”
Once seated, Qin Chuan threw a yellow talisman on the ground to create a soundproof barrier, then said, “If not for them, today’s conversation might have gone awry.”
On many occasions, it was clear they were smoothing things over, which otherwise could have become quite troublesome.
“Is there a possibility that we’ve been exposed already? Maybe for some reason, they just haven’t pierced the veil yet?” Colin suggested.
That’s impossible, absolutely impossible… Qin Chuan was about to express this conviction but suddenly fell silent, as the possibility wasn’t so small after all.
“It might not necessarily be that they’ve discovered us, but they definitely sense something is off. They probably want to use us to bypass something at ‘The Hague Shelter,’ hence their attitude. After all, we have been through a mechanical check before; biologically, we are identical to ‘ourselves’ in this world,” Xia Liufang suddenly interjected, her insights surpassing Qin Chuan’s—having grown up in a secret base, she knew much more.
Following her speculation, they probably knew there was a good chance their presence had been detected; they just didn’t know to what extent…
“Anyway, if nothing unexpected happens, they have to wait until everything is over before they make a move. We need to make some preparations in case we get stabbed in the back later on…” Qin Chuan analyzed based on the available intelligence.
“Right, at the very least, we have supporters behind us…” Hu Zheng from the official Fate Propeller continued.
“We have supporters backing us up? Who are they? Wait, you mean…”
Qin Chuan was initially startled, but then quickly realized the other party was referring to the Bonfire Company supporters who had always been giving them “buffs.”
From their perspective, their previous escape from the Fishmen’s attack was entirely due to the other party’s intervention; they just didn’t understand why he kept staying hidden instead of showing himself…
Looking at it from Colin’s point of view, however, his emotions were a bit more complex.
Nonetheless, everyone didn’t rely too much on having “supporters behind them,” but tried to take as many precautions as possible on their own.
It was during their discussion that the man wearing the Golden Mask, after having made arrangements for people from the Human Future Research Institute, said to the woman beside him with a puzzled expression, “Have you noticed anything strange about Director Chen Guang?”
“Hmm, according to the information I have, his reaction, at least in eight aspects, seems…”
“Wait, I get what you’re saying. Are you trying to say you also think something is off?”
“Yes, I…”
“Aside from his mindset, there doesn’t seem to be any other issues; he might just be trying to come out.”
The man with the Golden Mask shook his head; he hadn’t even tried to eavesdrop on that group because it was impossible.
To avoid eavesdropping, every resident of the shelter had their own set of methods. It was because Colin and the other “outsiders” were unfamiliar with the local rules that they fell into the pit.
…
At that time, in another resettlement residence, Deputy Director Chen Guang was seated with a group of smaller “cans.”
Rather than speaking directly, they communicated by reading the flickering “dark spots” above the heads of each other’s cans.
Assistant to the Director: “Director Chen, what we can be sure of is that there’s something off about this group. But I’ve cross-referenced their biological gene sampling backups and, aside from some discrepancies in their limbs, everything else matches perfectly, which is strange…”
The others agreed, feeling the situation was bizarre.
Deputy Director Chen Guang: “Since the biological sampling is accurate, then there’s no issue. They are who they are, they can’t be someone else. Sometimes appearances can deceive you, voices can deceive you, but data won’t…”
He paused for a moment, then added more content: “Regardless, as long as they are successfully recognized by the ‘material’ of The Hague Shelter, it shouldn’t be a big problem. Only then can we prevent a tragedy from happening in time… we must prioritize the greater good. If that damn Deity dares to resurrect, then we’ll just have to kill it again!”
“I understand!” the Assistant to the Director responded solemnly.
Unlike the people from Dawn’s Light Foundation, they were also direct participants in the original “Deicide Operation.” In that battle, they had nearly been wiped out, losing three directors (who were promoted from deputy directors after the successful operation).
The Director’s son was one of them, but unexpectedly, he managed to suppress his rage…
“Hmm, rest assured, I have confirmed that there is definitely no problem with the people, absolutely no mistakes… You guys also get ready, we are going to act ahead of schedule very soon.”
Deputy Director Chen Guang dismissed everyone and looked at the now-empty hall, his aged face beneath the protective suit silently muttering to himself.
“Of course, there’s no mistake… because this is the ‘will’ left by the great Deep Sea conveyed to me through God Revelation. Its return demands the fresh blood of these people as a guide for revenge. Blood debt will be paid in blood, and my child shall be resurrected from death!”
…

chapters.title: Chapter 211 - 211 211 Another Encounter with a Mother of the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 211: Chapter 211: Another Encounter with a “Mother of the Red Moon” Believer. _1 Chapter 211: Chapter 211: Another Encounter with a “Mother of the Red Moon” Believer. _1 Twenty-some hours quickly passed, and Colin and his companions were arranged onto an armored vehicle, which then headed straight towards the south of the World of Darkness, without stopping along the way.
Sitting in the vehicle, Colin glanced outside, and could tell that the people from “Dawn’s Light Foundation” took this operation quite seriously.
The variety of vehicles alone numbered over a hundred, including some tank trailers among them.
Since the route had been prepared in advance, avoiding all dangerous projects, the only other things left were some of the black-skinned people who were a local specialty of Mie City.
However, these people, upon seeing such a scale of the convoy, chose to make way for it willingly.
“The intelligence of these things is on the rise. If it had been before, they might have charged up here, but now they actually know to hide. Looks like it’s time for a big cleanup, and to study how they’ve suddenly wised up…” The man in the Golden Mask, sitting next to Colin and the others, looked out the window at those covetous figures and spoke casually.
Amidst the faint sounds of conversation, after about sixteen hours in the vehicle, Colin and the others arrived near the “Hague Research Institute.”
Stepping out of the vehicle, Colin first took a look at the distant “Hague Research Institute,” nestled in a big mountain about thirty kilometers from the coast. Because it was some distance away, the mountain indeed resembled a fang stretching out from the sea, hence the name The Hague…
When he redirected his gaze, Colin noticed that the air was faintly carrying a wet, salty scent…
Among the smells, Colin detected the stench of decaying dead fish, which induced a strong sense of unease.
And the sound of the endless overlapping waves in his head became even clearer…
The lightless sea was exuding a deadly “temptation” towards him.
Suppressing his emotions slightly, Colin’s expression grew solemn; he was sure that the smell of decay floating nearby probably came from some extremely terrifying entity.
“The power contained here is almost equal to that behind ‘Beastification,’ and it’s almost on par with one fifth of ‘Hunger’…”
Colin couldn’t help but inwardly relieve that thankfully this thing was already dead, otherwise, he really didn’t know how to deal with it.
Of course, that was under the premise of stopping those guys’ revival ritual…
After composing himself, Colin looked around. Besides their reinforcement, both “The Human Future Research Institute” and “Dawn’s Light Foundation” had already deployed significant forces here before their arrival.
As per the agreement, they would take a vehicle directly into The Hague Shelter. As long as they could be successfully identified, the two shelters would launch a full-scale attack to stop the evil sacrifice of the Fishmen.
Before long, Colin got back into the vehicle. This time, only three vehicles were headed there, with Colin and his team sitting in the first, beginning their advance.
“Can we really blend in with this…” Qin Chuan and the others were feeling a little uncertain at this moment.
They were well aware that the defenses of “The Hague Shelter” must be incredibly strong to cause such trepidation in the two shelters.
If the verification failed, not to mention whether they could escape or not, even if they did, it wouldn’t be easy to handle the aftermath—
Some matters, although both sides were fully aware, still had room for negotiation until they were explicitly addressed…
Colin was about to say something when he suddenly heard some faint sounds and saw a clump of silver mud-like substance on the ground in front of them arch upwards, forming a metallic pillar over a man’s height, with a blurred human face protruding from its middle.
“You have entered private territory and are within the strike range. Please turn back immediately or move forward five meters and stop for inspection…”
An indifferent voice came from the mouth of this face.
‘Is this nanomachinery?’ Colin wanted to take a closer look but could not discern anything significant.
The people in the vehicle exchanged glances, then continued to drive forward to the designated spot and stopped…
At that moment, a flat blue light shone from the eyes of the face, inspecting the entire vehicle. After a dozen seconds had passed, the face suddenly spoke up, causing everyone to tense up.
“Genetic match correct… Great Wisdom Chip missing… Anomalous situation: 2545712…”
Everyone’s breathing hitched, and the people in the two vehicles trailing behind couldn’t help but ready their weapons, prepared for a preemptive strike.
Otherwise, once these “nanomachines” scattered into the air, it would be troublesome.
However, it was at this moment that Colin noticed the eyes of the human face suddenly moved and looked at him, no, more precisely, at the “Colin” parchment in his pocket.
And then…
“Verification complete, welcome back, Chief of Shelter. May I ask if there is anything I can assist you with?”
Upon hearing this, everyone breathed a sigh of relief, while inside the first vehicle, Qin Chuan followed the direction of the human face’s gaze and couldn’t help but glance at Colin, never expecting that his identity in this world would be the chief of The Hague Shelter.
“It’s probably just a coincidence…”
Colin pursed his lips, not particularly surprised.
Next, they heard a voice from the wireless earpiece, “The System has indeed been hacked. Tell it to bring up the map of the research institute and to perform a high-level deep self-check to identify the problematic area.”
Similar functions exist in every shelter’s smart AI, let alone here.
With the command issued, a 3D holographic map projection appeared in front of Colin. In the projection, there was an area that constantly failed to load.
“Warning! Unable to perform checks on D-3 Area. All ‘Worker Bees’ entering the area have been subject to unknown attacks. Please have the head of the armed section dispatch forces swiftly…”
“Warning! Signs of an A Level life form reawakening detected. Most of the research institute’s personnel are missing in several areas. Head of the armed section, the armed units have been completely annihilated…”
“Warning! Part of the nanomechanics are revolting for unknown reasons…”
“Warning! Please grant highest authority to the chief…”
…
A series of seven or eight warnings appeared on the 3D projection, leaving everyone dumbfounded.
“A revolt? How could this thing possibly revolt?!”
The voice in the earpiece was full of shock, but after a moment of thought, the man in the Golden Mask immediately said, “Don’t grant access to the highest authority, put it on maximum alert, then lead the way, and also allow all of us to have our weapons access authorized.”
Even the mechanical synthetic voice sounded somewhat anxious at this moment.
Because he couldn’t imagine what on earth could make these uncontrollable entities revolt!
Colin did as instructed, and after granting the permissions, the earth trembled, and thousands of armed personnel moved out with their combat vehicles.
Colin and the others immediately got out of their vehicles and raced towards the uncontrollable “D-3” area.
“Something isn’t right,” Colin paused mid-step.
He realized that ever since they had entered, their path had been clear, and apart from seeing traces of past battles, no other enemies had appeared.
However, just as this thought crossed his mind, Colin suddenly saw at the end of The Hague Shelter’s metal corridor, a familiar gigantic figure of a Fishman holding a spear, blocking the path, while behind it, a sizable altar could be faintly seen.
But compared to those bizarre creatures, Colin frowned and glanced at the more familiar entities beside the giant Fishman.
A group of monsters with split bodies and covered in strange flesh orbs.
It was upon seeing those things that Colin immediately understood the reason for the “nanomechanics” losing control.
The followers of “Mother of the Red Moon” were here…
That meant the power of the “Red Moon” was here too!
And it was at that moment, an intense sense of danger exploded in Colin’s mind!
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 212 - 212 212 Betrayal_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 212: Chapter 212 Betrayal_1 Chapter 212: Chapter 212 Betrayal_1 “Deep Sea Messenger?!”
The men and women wearing golden masks clearly recognized what that creature was, their expressions turned ugly, yet not surprised.
These messengers of the Ancient Gods alone, without just those big-headed fish, could never have breached this place.
Before they could think further, the huge Fishman creature lifted an arm to grab a harpoon, and with a forceful thrust, hurled the black-metal-made spear towards Colin. However, due to the narrow passage, at least half of the people were within the striking range of this long spear.
At this moment, without waiting for Colin to act, the man and woman wearing golden masks had already stepped forward, amidst the cries of alarm.
Then they opened their hands, and a Positional Shield made of energy appeared in front of them.
The next instant, the harpoon, carrying tremendous force, slammed into the shield, resulting in a huge sonic boom sound as the harpoon was forcibly stopped.
As the impetus of the harpoon faded, the “Deep Sea Messenger” gestured with his hand, and some force remotely reinforced it, causing the harpoon to fly backward as if to return to its hand.
“Wishful thinking.” The Golden Mask man thought, and the Positional Shield immediately changed shape, extending an invisible hand to tightly grip the front end of the harpoon, making it impossible to retract.
“Not bad at all…”
Colin was surprised for a moment and took the opportunity, as they blocked the attack, to glance over and see those familiar humanoid meatballs. He couldn’t help but twitch his eyelids.
He hadn’t expected that even in another world, he would still encounter these creatures causing trouble.
Almost every time Colin saw them, they were either up to something or on their way to it. They were involved in everything, and this time seemed no exception.
Just what are they planning to do this time…
But there was no time to ponder further; the ground beneath Colin shook, and then he saw the corridor behaving as if it were the stomach and intestines of some giant creature, writhing madly and pushing them toward D-3 Area up ahead.
“Splitting, activating… the power of this damned thing is still as bizarre as ever…”
Colin steadied his footing to avoid falling on the suddenly softened ground.
At the same time, from the direction they had come from, a layer of silver-white nanomachines flowed like water, directly penetrating into the writhing walls. Blood gushed forth from the metal walls as if damaged, and the undulation gradually came to a halt.
“This doesn’t feel right…” Hu Zheng suddenly had a feeling, speaking quickly, “My intuition tells me that if we go forward, we might not only fail to stop the disaster, but everything could become even more troublesome.”
“Then let’s retreat…” Qin Chuan decided to do as the other had said.
So far, Hu Zheng’s intuition had been quite accurate. Although small issues constantly arose in the directions guided by it, the overall direction was largely correct—
And that was also the reason why most teams were willing to include one or two “Fate Propellers,” the Extraordinary Ones with hardly any fighting capability, in their operations.
Sometimes, with their intuitive guidance, problems could be solved much more easily.
However, upon hearing the decision in the conversation of the few, the two people contending in a standoff with the “Deep Sea Messenger” were reluctant.
“Having come this far, just one more step to stop them, and now you’re thinking of retreating?”
The man wearing the Golden Mask didn’t quite understand the concept of “Fate Propeller” and simply couldn’t comprehend why these few were thinking of leaving just because someone said their intuition was off.
At this very moment, shouldn’t they be charging in to break through the defenses, place a beacon, lower the Hague Research Institute’s defense level, and have the Foundation launch missiles to precisely bomb and take care of the evil ritual?!
But the next second, a burst of “static” came through the man in the golden mask’s earpiece, and he looked startled. He then yelled, “Pull out! We have a mole, abort the mission, watch out for Chen…!”
Before he could finish, a giant earthy yellow hand reached up from beneath the ground, grabbed his and another woman’s lower half—who was also wearing a golden mask—and yanked hard.
Crack…
In almost an instant, both of their bodies were crushed, but no blood spilled out. Instead, there were sparks flying, with the cross-sections filled with densely packed, smoking, short-circuited metal components.
Afterward, the earthy yellow hand casually tossed aside the two bodies that seemed to have lost their power.
“Director Chen, what are you doing!?” A member of the “Human Future Research Institute,” dressed in a yellow heavy-duty protective suit akin to a human-shaped tank, incredulously looked back.
Chen Guang, who previously wore a similar protective suit, had at some point removed his protection, and a mutated hand extended into the ground, almost identical to that of “Twilight’s Children.”
And his entire being was rapidly transforming into something inhuman…
As members of the same institute, they were well aware that Deputy Director Chen was turning himself into one of “Twilight’s Children.”
It wasn’t anything strange in itself; transforming into “Twilight’s Children” was a given and also their trump card. However, the problem was that he had started to attack his own people!
“Chen Guang, have you fucking lost your mind?! You’ve betrayed humanity!” shouted 223, who wore a golden mask and had fallen to the ground. He had barely managed to sit up before he began to curse in a rage.
He had never anticipated a traitor among humankind in the “Human Future Research Institute.” Until now, he had always believed that even if the entire board of directors betrayed them, the opposition would never turn.
But to his surprise, just as he had been blocking the “Deep Sea Messenger,” a voice suddenly came through his earpiece—it was another deputy director of the “Human Future Research Institute” warning him to be careful of Chen Guang.
Then, before he could properly react, he was ambushed and had half of his modified body crushed.
“Betray humanity? Hah! I did not betray humanity. It is you who have betrayed us, you who first betrayed the goodwill of the Ancient God!”
Deputy Director Chen Guang glared at Colin and the others with resentment as the thoughts in his mind materialized and projected into everyone’s brain:
“You have no idea how merciful an entity you’ve attacked. If it wasn’t for Him, barely anyone would have survived the global tsunami.
“Without His kindness, I would have died long ago, never to return to land but forever trapped atop the vast ocean…
“Yet you used the bloodline of my son to get close to Him, to backstab Him, to strip away his divinity, leading to His downfall…
“Because of your false lies, my child was killed, and everything was taken from me—my descendants, my faith…
“You are the true traitors, the ones who truly deserve to die a thousand deaths!”
As he spoke, he supported himself with his hands on the ground; his muscles swelled, bursting through his clothing, as a layer of gravel-like growths emerged on his skin, reflecting a light like that of the setting sun.
The others did not stand idly by during his transformation, continually attacking with their weapons attempting to stop him. What a pity that although bullets and bombs at first left some holes in him, as he transformed, conventional firearms were no longer effective.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 213 - 213 213 Even If Its God Ill Kill for You to
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 213: Chapter 213 Even If It’s God, I’ll Kill for You to See!_1 Chapter 213: Chapter 213 Even If It’s God, I’ll Kill for You to See!_1 “Are you fucking stupid? Without these Ancient Gods, where would the damn tsunami come from? If It truly had good intentions, then what’s the deal with those Fishmen? Don’t tell me you don’t fucking know how all this happened!”
The man wearing the Golden Mask cursed angrily, but unfortunately, the heart of Chen Guang, filled with resentment, could no longer take in his words.
He propped himself up with one hand on the ground while lifting the other, readying his stance to attack the other party.
But forget about his current incomplete state, even at full strength, his attack would hardly have any significant effect on a “Twilight’s Child” of at least Level 5.
“Twilight’s Children” are indestructible except by the “Ancient Gods”; the only strategy for others is to stall, to wait until their rationality fades and they voluntarily return to the “Twilight Angel.”
Its body, seemingly made of condensed yellow, couldn’t properly stretch out in the corridor, yet it was able to fill the entire space. Without even attacking, it had already completely blocked everyone’s retreat…
Neither reinforcement troops arriving later nor the nanomachines could break through this defense in a short time.
And yet, Colin and others were truly trapped within the encirclement of the “Twilight’s Child” and the “Deep Sea Messenger.”
Simultaneously, the entire metallic corridor began to squirm again as if it had regained its vitality, indicating that the nanomachines that had just infiltrated it had been eliminated.
Now, working in concert with the “Twilight’s Child” wedged in the corridor, it seemed to want to squeeze people towards the front.
Colin squinted, and another scene emerged in his mind: the “Deep Sea Messenger,” retracting its harpoon, swung the weapon in its hands to hurl it once more with tremendous force. The harpoon, covered with lightning, encompassed everyone in the corridor within its strike range, instantly killing and wounding many.
In this moment, the deputy director of the Human Future Research Institute betrayed them, and the two from “Dawn’s Light” lay on the ground, no longer able to rise. Qin Chuan and the others couldn’t hold back…
“It seems I’ll have to take action myself, and my instinct tells me there’s no escape now. I have to make a quick decision, the longer we wait, the worse things get, the more likely it is that something will resurrect…”
Just as Colin’s thoughts were racing, a thunderous roar exploded at the end of the corridor, and then Qin Chuan and the others saw, with faces of despair, the harpoon glowing with electricity once again in the large hand of the merman, aiming at them.
Xia Liufang gritted her teeth, her demeanor changing abruptly. She stepped forward, pulling a long sword from the air, ready to sacrifice herself to block the incoming attack…
But at that moment, a hazy ice-blue shadow appeared in front of them.
The figure lifted its chin slightly, seemingly contemptuous of everything, and faced with the impending attack, simply stretched out a finger towards it.
And it was at this moment that the giant fishman completed its throwing motion, and the harpoon, wrapped in terrifying lightning, arrived in an instant.
Some even closed their eyes in despair, feeling everything was over…
But just as the harpoon was about to hit the crowd, the blurred figure slightly opened its mouth—
“Spicy to the fill!”
Instantly, a terrifying invisible Repulsion erupted from Colin, directly affecting the harpoon. The force of the Charge and the Repulsion collided on the harpoon, causing it to explode into innumerable fragments that fell to the ground.
This sudden turn of events left everyone stupefied as they turned their gazes—Who is this?
Under the scrutiny of many eyes, Colin’s presence surged, but he offered no response to their questions. Instead, he looked at the scattered fragments on the ground and disdainfully said,
“Is that all?”
As he spoke, the “Twilight’s Child” behind him stretched out a dusky yellow hand. Colin didn’t even look back; with a casual wave, all the black metal shards on the ground were affected by the Repulsion and flew towards the “Twilight’s Child,” momentarily forcing it back.
In just an instant, the problem of being attacked from both front and rear seemed to be effortlessly resolved…
Colin did not expect these metal fragments to kill the enemy, he glanced at the stunned crowd and simply said, “Everyone, follow me.”
After saying that, he headed towards the D-3 Area, but a member of the Human Future Research Institute couldn’t help but say, “But their goal is to drive us there to serve as sacrifices for the ritual. We’d better run. With your strength, maybe…”
Before he could finish, under the immense pressure of Colin’s gaze, his voice gradually ceased, and he swallowed hard, blinking his eyes, not continuing on.
“Don’t tell me how to do my job.”
Colin withdrew his gaze and turned towards the D-3 Area.
Behind him, the others exchanged glances, and finally, gritting their teeth, they picked up the two fallen “Dawn’s Light” members and followed behind.
“Oh no, where’s Colin?”
“I don’t know…”
“Could it be that he has already been saved by that big shot?”
“Maybe…”
The whispered conversations of Qin Chuan and the others could be heard from behind, but Colin didn’t pay any attention. He looked at the “Deep Sea Follower” blocking the doorway, quickening his pace with each step.
When he was less than thirty meters away from the “Deep Sea Messenger,” Colin heard the other emit an angry screech.
It seemed to be another language, which Colin couldn’t understand, but that didn’t matter.
He pulled out “Revolver Contrarian” from his pocket, flames began to burn from his body and spread around from his feet. Inside the corridor space, the terrifying temperature rose instantaneously.
Seeing that the creature didn’t dodge or flinch, its body shimmering with electricity and blood vessels in its dead fish eyes throbbing without retreating, Colin’s mouth formed a slight “√”:
“Good, your courage to challenge the strong is commendable, so next…“You can die in peace.
“Don’t worry, if your god awakens, I’ll be sending him down soon too.
“Anything that’s alive, even a god, I’ll kill it for you to see.”
“Arrogant!”
The “Deep Sea Messenger” was so angry that it spoke in human language, its muscles bulging. With a hissing sound, many small arcs of electricity emerged from its body, then, like arrows of lightning, they shot towards Colin.
If any one of these electric serpents struck an ordinary person, it would be enough to kill him instantly…
However, as soon as the hundreds of electric serpents got close, they were directly engulfed by the flames bursting with terrifying heat.
“How is this possible!” It widened its fish eyes in disbelief.
“There’s nothing impossible, realizing your own weakness through me is your luck.”
Colin’s face was sincere and serious, and his arrogant demeanor nearly caused the massive fishman to burst a blood vessel in its forehead. It then summoned its power again, calling forth a massive amount of electricity, and grabbed it in its hand, forming a sphere of lightning.
“Die!”
It roared, charged with lightning, and rushed towards Colin. The creature’s watery vapor surged to disperse the flames around Colin, and it swung its electrified fist, smashing it down towards his head.
“How will you block this?!”
It roared as the fist came down, but felt no contact with the other, paused for a moment, retracted its hand, and realized that Colin had disappeared from sight.
But it was at that moment, a calm voice suddenly resounded by its ear:
“Farewell.”
“You…”
Before it could finish, a strong repulsive force suddenly erupted inside it.
The mermaid-tailed “Deep Sea Messenger” burst like a firework in an instant, countless pieces of its shattered body flying everywhere, like rain.
This sight made those following behind Colin gasp in shock.

chapters.title: Chapter 214 - 214 214 Major Changes in Destiny._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 214: Chapter 214: Major Changes in “Destiny”._1 Chapter 214: Chapter 214: Major Changes in “Destiny”._1 “This, this strong?”
Xia Liufang’s eyes sparkled with shock; she had once fought a monster nearly like this one and knew how tough its fish scale armor was—it was a terrifying creature whose skin could not even be pierced by a heavy machine gun.
Not to mention the various mysterious protections it had, as well as its own attacks, which made piercing its defense even more unlikely…
But now, in just the briefest of moments, that suddenly appearing fire-bodied figure had managed to instantly kill it, blasting its flesh and blood all over the sky!
It was unimaginable how this was achieved.
“Wait, this figure, it feels somewhat familiar…” blurted out a Transcendent from the team.
If at first they didn’t see it clearly when it appeared as a blurry ice-blue shadow, now that the figure was bursting with flames, they immediately recognized something…
Isn’t that the guy in the wheelchair?!
Right, they indeed couldn’t see this person at the scene right now and didn’t know where he’d gone.
“What do you mean, you know who it is?” asked the Golden Mask man, number 223, who was being carried on the shoulder of an armed person, with surprise.
He and 331 had just been ambushed and hadn’t noticed what was happening here; in their eyes, it was almost as if, when they thought they couldn’t escape, a figure suddenly burst forth, and then the situation of attack and defense changed drastically.
“I’m not sure, but if it really is him, then it must be Bonfire Company’s support arriving again, it’s just that, his aura has changed greatly now, resembling ‘Divine Strike,’ but I have never seen this type of ‘Divine Strike’ before…” The Transcendent half-closed his eyes, as if he had thought of something.
“It’s not without precedent…” Xia Liufang suddenly spoke, “His way of speaking is very similar to a senior I’ve heard of before, who had a similar style and also could manipulate ice…”
Being on the path of ‘Divine Strike’, she naturally had heard some things; some internal documents were distributed a few days ago, seeking the identity of a certain person, initiated by her uncle, Luo Wenhao.
Xia Liufang had seen that file, and the description matched the person in front of her: able to manipulate ice, speaking in exaggerated terms, in possession of many peculiar items, with an extremely strong combined combat capacity…
Each trait matched up one by one.
She wasn’t sure before, but now she was certain that this guy definitely came from Bonfire Company.
But, after searching for a while with no results, everything had been put aside, and she didn’t expect to now see someone fitting that description appear again.
However, she was unsure whether Colin had just had his body borrowed or if there was really something wrong with him.
Qin Chuan was also watching the figure clearing the path ahead, deep in thought, as he recalled some inconsistencies along the way, the most prominent being the time when Colin’s wheelchair was wrecked…
While everyone at the scene couldn’t react, a “normal person” did manage to react.
Then there were various details; this person encountered many things along the way but rarely showed any signs of shock—a part of him even wondered if the man’s calmness was like someone who had lived through World War II…
But now thinking about it, it also felt like he inherently possessed certain confidence, so nothing seemed to unsettle him.
Although there was one time another Bonfire Company supporter arrived, that supporter’s abilities were obviously different from the person before them now.
He was so full of certainty when he first refused them while sitting in the wheelchair, and he still is now; Qin originally thought it might be a personality quirk, but now thinking about it…
Is it possible that as early as that time…
Various contradictions unfolded in his mind.
Of course, he was just suspicious and not entirely certain because there were many other explanations for the current situation.
For example, it wasn’t impossible that Bonfire Company had used some method to have a ‘Divine Strike’ descend.
After all, this power that had suddenly appeared less than a year ago was characterized by the fact that its members always had an astonishing variety of powerful abilities and objects.
However, just as he was about to speak, Hu Zheng on the side suddenly spoke up and reached a conclusion: “It must be right, it certainly is Bonfire Company’s support that has arrived, just like Miss Xia Liufang said, some kind of method akin to ‘Divine Strike,’ and Colin must be the Container for this power!
“Have you heard about possession?” he asked. “It’s like, maybe some old man’s spirit has gotten into him.”
Qin Chuan looked at him thoughtfully. Even he could sense that something was amiss, so Hu Zheng, who was the most sensitive of them all, should definitely have noticed…
At this moment, if not for the friendship that had started in high school and felt as close as brothers, he would have almost suspected his friend of betrayal.
Nevertheless, as someone who knew him well, he could tell that the other was always steering the conversation in a certain direction.
He elbowed Hu Zheng, who clearly realized why he had done so, but just shook his head slightly…
Huh? Does Colin really have an issue? Qin Chuan was taken aback.
“Do you guys think there’s a chance that this guy has always been problematic? To be honest, along the way…” said an official Transcendent who had been seriously injured and seldom spoke, as he couldn’t help but point out that the others always seemed to miss “the main point.”
But before he could finish, Hu Zheng’s eyelid twitched, and he abruptly interrupted, “Aren’t you being a bit too paranoid?”
The man frowned. All along this journey, Hu Zheng had always been covering for the other, leading him to suspect that Hu Zheng might have an ulterior motive. Expanding on that thought, could this incident also be related to him, no, them?
“Are you hiding something?” he asked warily. The situation now was such that, despite clearly heading towards a trap, that guy was still leading them on—the problem was significant.
Hiding something? What can I hide? Boss, weren’t you the one who’ve been hiding things well before? Why are you suddenly being so brazen? At least change your tone of voice… Hu Zheng couldn’t help but grumble inwardly, casting a glance at Colin, who was holding his own against numerous enemies ahead—
In fact, it was only after the Fishmen attack that he had confirmed some things about Colin…
But for some reasons, even with his certainty, he couldn’t point it out.
However, seeing that people were becoming divided on-site because of “Colin’s” undisguised actions at the front, he took out a piece of the “Book of Fate: Fragment” and quickly sensed it before he cautiously said:
“I understand your concerns, but if you don’t want to experience a significant change in the ‘Threads of Fate,’ I advise you to stop saying things that go against unity…”
A major change in the “Threads of Fate”?
Are things really that serious?
Upon hearing this, everyone couldn’t help but gasp, knowing what it signified once it occurred.
The last time it happened, Ao Island was torn asunder, and the entire region fell. In an emergency international mobilization, hundreds of high-level personnel headed to that country under the guise of joint maritime counter-terrorism drills, paying a hefty price to bury nearly half a continent along with part of human memory and recognition of that place.
And the reason for this significant alteration of the “Threads of Fate,” was said to be a member of Fate Propeller who brought an antique there and ultimately forgot to bring it back, causing the incident.
The time before that, the government first discovered Bonfire Company and began their infiltration efforts…
And the time before that…
In any case, once it happened, whether for good or bad, it was not something they could handle.
“So, there are things you may know, but you can’t speak of them,” Hu Zheng said seriously. Not to mention not being able to point it out, even if Colin came forward to say there was a problem, they would have to conjure an excuse to cover for him.
The Transcendent quickly changed his tune, “I suddenly find Miss Xia Liufang’s words quite reasonable…”
He didn’t understand why speaking up could lead to such severe consequences, but obviously, the situation was beyond his control. Instead of pondering over it, it would be better to think of a way to leave when the time came and let the bigwigs handle it.
.
.
.
ps: Actually, it’s not that I never had suspicions, it’s just that I wasn’t sure, and with Hu Zheng forcefully meddling in secret for some reasons… made it even more uncertain.

chapters.title: Chapter 215 - 215 215 Resurrect My Mother Goddess_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 215: Chapter 215: Resurrect, My Mother Goddess!_1 Chapter 215: Chapter 215: Resurrect, My Mother Goddess!_1 “Indeed! Those who dare to face me directly, I will bestow death upon you equally.”
Colin looked at the waves of Fishmen coming towards him, stretched out his right hand, and a huge Flame swept forward like a tiger pouncing on its prey, devouring all the enemies in an instant.
The scent of roasted fish permeated the area.
With “The False Powerhouse” combined with “Revolver Contrarian,” his power level rose once again, and the intensity and range of his flame control significantly increased.
As for the discussions of the people behind him, Colin didn’t care. Even if they truly knew his identity, what could they do?
His own strength was not inferior to anyone; he had no need to hide from anyone!
At that moment, after killing a “Deep Sea Messenger” and tearing through the defenses of those Fishmen and Red Moon believers, Colin directly manipulated the power of “Yukionna” within his body and continued to delve forward.
He could feel something further past several layers of defense that was displeasing to him!
Before long, Colin passed through a large doorway, avoided the landmines within, and entered a hall that could be described as a plaza.
As soon as he entered, a rotten stench akin to a slaughterhouse assaulted his senses.
“This place…”
Colin stood at the entrance of the hall, halted his steps for a moment, and looked up. After seeing the scene inside, even with the effect of “The False Powerhouse,” he still felt a strong sense of crisis explode in his mind—
Before his eyes was an unimaginably grisly scene: Human limbs were brutally dismembered, twisted and strewn throughout the hall. Hearts, brains, intestines, limbs; countless organs floated and wriggled in the air…
They drifted like dust, not in harmony, but constantly tearing at and assaulting each other, breaking into more pieces, or fusing together into distorted monstrosities.
Decomposition and fusion were happening all the time…
The hall itself was already animated, with flesh and steel fused together perfectly, pulsating like a biological stomach and emitting deafening noises.
And in the midst of all this was a giant cylindrical container vessel over thirty meters tall and several meters wide. Within the vessel, filled with a blue solution, floated a pale, nearly decomposed, and shredded corpse…
It was impossible to tell what it once was; it was a rotten mess of flesh.
Thousands of organs, many floating outside the vessel, revolved around this corpse slowly, like angels in heaven, wriggling as they played a cheerful, praising, and humanly incomprehensible broken language…
Looking past these animated organs, Colin’s gaze focused on the decaying body within the containment vessel, sensing the terrifying might emanating from it, he surmised:
“Corpse of the Ancient God.”
Even though it was rotten beyond recognition, riddled with holes like a tattered bag, the lingering dominion of the once-sea ruler still invoked palpitations and even fear.
Moreover, after Colin’s arrival, he immediately felt the corpse in the containment vessel start to stir.
A sharp and dreadful scream resounded in his ears, filled with resentment before death…
The people who followed him, upon witnessing this sight, were stunned, staring blankly at everything before them, emitting hurried breaths.
However, at that moment, a voice came from above.
“It seems that there has been a complication; your people have not brought them here in the correct way…”
A “Red Moon” follower, radiating red light, stepped on the still-living severed female heads, saying somewhat displeased.
Colin glanced at those heads; some of them were still the same hundred-plus female slaves they had encountered earlier when they faced the Fishmen.
And next to the figure emitting red light stood five “Deep Sea Messengers,” one of which immediately turned its eyes blood-red upon seeing Colin, recognizing him as the human who had severely wounded it days ago and had attacked the household of the Great Will of the Deep Sea!
“I will kill him now!” exclaimed the “Deep Sea Messenger” with a hiss.
“No, the sacrifice has already arrived here, and the wrong method doesn’t matter, after all the power of motherhood is sufficient, enough to serve as the bearer of my Mother’s power. What you have to do now is to fight for the Time of Her resurrection, and not let that guy get too close…”
However, before he could finish speaking, Colin, covered in flames, hurtled towards them like a meteor rushing at high speed.
Yet, before he could approach further, thunder and lightning erupted from the bodies of the “Deep Sea Messengers,” who boldly launched an attack. Using electricity or hurling harpoons, their all-encompassing assault forced Colin to retreat temporarily, and he was blasted away…
After finishing his words, this “Red Moon” follower directly pulled out a dagger and stabbed it into his own heart.
“Sovereign of all that lives, ultimate destination of countless lives, pure and flawless Mother, I implore Your gaze to fall upon this place…”
The next second, dazzling red light burst from his body, and a terrifying aura that made everyone present shudder with fear descended.
All the fluttering organs seemingly responded to a call, swarming towards him like moths to a flame, instantly fusing into a monstrous, twisted mass of flesh.
It lay there quietly like a huge, bizarre, blood-flesh pill, emitting red light.
At the same time, the already activated glass container cracked open its mouth on both sides, and the rotten flesh of the Deep Sea Ancient God, long decayed into a lump, crawled out sluggishly like a slug and swallowed the massive blood-flesh pill whole…
At this moment, the suffocating might of the ocean spread out.
The already decaying massive piece of flesh suddenly burst with vitality once more, expanding rapidly and reviving, revealing its originally vigorous state!
And outside, in the sky above, Dark Clouds suddenly gathered densely, the wind and rain intertwined, lightning flickered, the sea waves surged ceaselessly, tidal waters swept up the sky, and the relentless ocean began to swallow the world with the resurgence of resentment.
Those whispers not of human origin seeped out from the depths of the ocean, ringing in everyone’s ears, sounding the death knell for the world.
“Had it not been for the betrayer among humans, who took advantage of Your weakness while You stepped upon the earth and birthed Your divine child, launching a surprise attack, You would never have fallen…”
“Now, rise again! My Mother God!”
“May all traitors never find peace in death, let the world fully enter the era of the Deep Sea!”
The “Deep Sea Messengers” opened their arms wide, shouting excitedly, falling into a fervor, no longer paying attention to Colin, who was charging at them once again.
For, the Master had been resurrected, and even if they were killed, they would be revived from the side of the Master!
That is to say, as long as the “Mother of the Sea” exists in this world, they will attain supreme might, immortal and undying!
All dead “Messengers” will also be brought back to life the moment the Mother opens Her eyes!
However, just as they were loudly proclaiming the return of their ruler, they suddenly heard a tremendously painful moan from the great sovereign of the ancient ocean.
This groan caused them to freeze, stopping their chanting and looking up, only to see a crimson gash unexpectedly tear open at the chest of the ocean sovereign.
Behind the rift lurked a blood-red eye that seemed to be curiously observing this world from its parasitic refuge.
“What’s happening…”
Before they could understand the situation, dozens of tentacles suddenly extended from that horrific body of the Ancient God, engulfing several stunned “Deep Sea Messengers” into itself.

chapters.title: Chapter 216 - 216 216 Strike Hard_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 216: Chapter 216: Strike Hard!_1 Chapter 216: Chapter 216: Strike Hard!_1 “Just a piece of rotten flesh, and it’s actually been resurrected…”
Colin’s gaze flickered across the red eye in the chest of the Ancient God, quickly realizing that this was likely not His original bodily organ.
Without a doubt, it must be the true purpose of the followers of the Red Moon.
“Are these Fishmen really that stupid or just pretending, to believe in the words of the ‘Red Moon’ followers?”
Colin muttered to himself, unlike the desperate Fishmen seeking any remedy, he didn’t believe that the ‘Red Moon’ believers would sacrifice themselves for a Different Race without reason.
What stood before him must be the result the other party wished to achieve…
At this moment, flames danced around him, sheltering him as he faced the might emanating from the resurrected Ancient God. Even with the use of “The False Powerhouse,” he moved prudently and did not rashly advance.
At least for a short time, he figured he probably shouldn’t rush forward and deliver himself…
Then, he discovered the awkward truth: not only was defeating it uncertain, but escaping was also not guaranteed.
“No, that’s not right. The Ancient God might be strong now, but it seems to lack that divine essence. Creatures like ‘Hunger’ and even the ‘Tyrant’ have shown a similar aura, but this guy has none. It’s purely strong on its own…”
Colin suddenly remembered hearing that this “Ancient God” seemed to have been stripped of divinity by “His future self.”
The divinity had not returned with His return.
To put it plainly, He now seemed to be just a ‘knockoff’…”
