The next second, the unsubstantial rat silhouette couldn’t even struggle as it was pulled backward into the air, caught by the chubby hand of the rat’s body, and dragged directly into the transparent vortex.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 245 - 245 245 Chaos and Deadly Attack_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 245: Chapter 245 Chaos and Deadly Attack_1 Chapter 245: Chapter 245 Chaos and Deadly Attack_1 “I have no idea how they’ll handle my situation when they arrive…”
Colin stood to the side, watching the few on the phone. He wasn’t in the mood to listen to what they were saying, just suddenly feeling his mind getting somewhat messy, unsure of how to proceed with things.
From a rational perspective, he thought, the officials should not do anything irrational to him.
But, there was indeed a considerable chance that, under the pretext of research or something else, they would make him surrender his equipment.
And the true combat power of an employee largely came from the various equipment combinations they used, beyond some inherent factors.
Compared to others, Colin was even more reliant on his equipment.
He found that it was either bad luck or some other reason, but he would always get involved in various events, each of which carried a significant degree of danger.
Without sufficiently powerful equipment, that would be almost like being sentenced to death.
He couldn’t achieve what the “Firebearer” did, who, even reduced to nothing but a heart, still possessed power so great it could suffocate the enemy.
However, the best-case scenario would of course be for both sides to set aside prejudices and cooperate in good faith, working towards a win-win situation.
With Lady Bunny’s endorsement from before, he felt the likelihood of the latter was not small…
But, what if some other bad situation really occurred?
“Logically, it shouldn’t happen…”
Colin rubbed his forehead, suddenly feeling overwhelmed by pressure. His mind was muddled by various thoughts, like a ball of yarn without an end, becoming more and more tangled.
After several dozen seconds, the indescribable sense of confusion suddenly vanished, and Colin let out a long sigh of relief.
He felt that his mindset seemed off, as he usually had many thoughts, but they weren’t typically this disordered…
“Forget it, it’s meaningless to think about this.”
Colin pressed his temples with his hand and sorted out his thoughts before looking back at the people present, counting them idly, only then noticing that exactly a hundred and eight children had escaped…
Just the right number for the heroes of the Water Margin.
There were Qin Chuan and the others next, originally five official Extraordinary Ones, eight armed personnel, and three “Bonfire Company” employees including Colin, the lung cancer patient, and the burn victim—sixteen people in total…
Now, four official Extraordinary Ones remained, only three out of the eight armed personnel survived, and among the “Bonfire Company” employees, only two were left. Seven had died, almost more than half of them.
As for injuries, generally speaking, everyone had suffered some to a certain extent.
“This is the first time I’ve seen such a high casualty rate on a mission…”
Colin remarked with a sigh. This incident had been too unexpected, so much so that everyone was unprepared.
However, before he could think further, about ten or so minutes after their return to the real world, the roaring sound of engines approached from not too far away.
Listening to the sound, it seemed that there was more than one vehicle coming…
Then, everyone quickly saw three armored vehicles, painted in green camouflage, emerging from the shrubbery where there were barely any roads by the coast.
The complicated terrain was like flat ground under their wheels, and it didn’t take long before they stopped about fifty meters in front of the crowd—not too close but not too far, either.
Next, the rear door of one armored vehicle swung down from above.
First, a muscular man wearing slippers, beach shorts, and a floral shirt stepped out, followed by twelve fully armed individuals who ran down towards the crowd.
“Haha, congratulations on your return, I am the person in charge of the Anhai Region, Gao Sheng…”
Gao Sheng said with a hearty laugh on his rough face, glancing at Qin Chuan and the others, then at the children in uniform, “And these are?”
“Classified, can’t say for now…” Qin Chuan didn’t immediately offer an explanation.
He felt it was not appropriate to disclose their identities before meeting with higher-ranking officials…
“Alright.”
Gao Sheng, who seemed to have been dragged along halfway through a leisurely activity, didn’t press further and chuckled, then continued, “Then as procedure dictates, hand over any weapons or dangerous items. I’ll take you to ‘Base No. 4’ as required.”
“Base No. 4?” Qin Chuan was taken aback upon hearing this, gradually gaining some awareness of their current location.
There were five super-large bases or research institutes domestically, starting with No. 1 in the north to No. 5 in the south.
The area they had been in was close to Shelter No. 5…
But that wasn’t a big issue.
They just had to cross the Qionghai Strait to get home…
As for surrendering items, he had few doubts, after all, they had just emerged from a dangerous area, and it was indeed possible that they had picked up a dangerous scent.
After confiscating some items from Qin Chuan and the others, Gao Sheng wearing a floral shirt approached Colin.
“You’re an employee of the Bonfire Company, right?” Gao Sheng asked, holding a piece of parchment he had received from the burn victim, yet, unfortunately, without the required clearance, he was unable to access any information.
Without giving it much thought, he handed over the items he had picked up to the armed personnel beside him, then looked at the silent Colin, “Would you mind handing over your items…”
“Sure.”
Colin took out a “small-sized” piece of parchment from his pocket and handed it over to the other party.
After all, this thing wasn’t particularly important to him…
However, after receiving the parchment, Gao Sheng didn’t leave. He glanced at it, handed it to his assistant, and then continued with a smile:
“Sorry, not this one…”
“Is it this one?” Colin took out another parchment with the name “Colin” on it.
The text on it had already been wiped clean by him upon his exit…
“Yeah…”
Gao Sheng took it, looked it over, handed it to someone else, and shook his head, “I’m referring to… the one you use yourself, Mr. Colin.”
When he finished this sentence, the atmosphere suddenly turned cold.
‘Buddy, asking further is becoming impolite, isn’t it?’
Colin squinted at the official Extraordinary One, who returned the gaze with a smile. However, while they made eye contact, he gestured, and the armed personnel began to move, subtly intending to surround Colin.“Sorry, friend, we’re just following protocol, please cooperate, or we won’t be able to avoid an unnecessary conflict…” Gao Sheng’s words contained an implicit warning.
Meanwhile, Qin Chuan, witnessing the situation, first froze—this… isn’t this going about it the wrong way?
In his opinion, they should first calm everyone down rather than provoke a conflict at this moment.
“What’s going on?” He halted his steps toward the armored vehicle and turned to approach.
“This friend here doesn’t want to cooperate with us and hand over the dangerous items, his own piece of parchment…”
“Didn’t I see him hand over two pieces of parchment?”
“No, no, I mean his own piece…” Gao Sheng cheerfully replied.
“There aren’t any more, right? I remember he only had two…”
Qin Chuan’s words seemed to offer a protective edge, not that he especially wanted to help Colin, but that if a real issue arose.
There were no high-ranking personnel on the scene, and they might not be enough to stop Colin if he decided to attack…
Moreover, subsequent to the displeasure here, it could potentially lead to serious issues with the Bonfire Company.
At the same time, Hu Zheng, Xia Liufang, and another person approached to help explain.
“Don’t worry, I can vouch for him here. As a Fourth Level ‘Fate Propeller’ member and ‘Great Wall’ Reservist, I should qualify to offer this assurance…”
“I can also vouch for him, I trust Mr. Colin…”
“Indeed, if there were any issues, he probably would have acted already.”
Listening to the group, Gao Sheng’s expression remained unchanged. Just when Qin Chuan and the others thought that this attempt at communication might be ineffective, Gao Sheng suddenly exclaimed, “Ah, forget it, come with me…”
Upon hearing this, Qin Chuan breathed a sigh of relief, about to speak to Colin, when suddenly a thought struck him, his expression turning suddenly, “Something’s not right!”
He clearly had not yet reported Colin’s situation to the higher-ups, only asking them to send senior employees if possible; how did these people know there was an issue with Colin?
No, if he himself didn’t know how many pieces of parchment Colin had, how could they be certain?
But before he could finish speaking, he suddenly felt a strong sense of impending crisis, followed by a contraction of his pupils as he saw a flash of orange light on the bodies of the dozen or so armed personnel surrounding them—
Damn it, were they wearing bombs instead of bulletproof vests?!
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 246 - 246 246 The Reluctant Smiling Mountain of
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 246: Chapter 246: The Reluctant “Smiling Mountain of Corpses”_1 Chapter 246: Chapter 246: The Reluctant “Smiling Mountain of Corpses”_1 “It’s over…”
The last thought emerged in Qin Chuan and the others’ minds, and then their thoughts stopped abruptly.
However, before the shockwave of the explosion could spread,
a rumbling of engines that ordinary people couldn’t hear exploded at this moment…
The next moment, within a ten-meter radius of this area, everything froze as if in a photograph.
And within this stasis, only Colin could move…
“Damn, that was close, these people were actually a trap…”
Colin held the Time Stop Card in his hand, looking at the objects before him, his heart steely.
There, the bodies of more than a dozen armed men had been torn apart in the horrific explosion, the frozen blaze and fierce shockwave in a state of about to erupt but not yet erupted…
Each of these people was covered in high-performance explosives.
And there was more, Colin saw bullets coming from all directions in the explosion, frozen in mid-air.
Among the multitude of machine gun bullets, there were also a few large-caliber bullets that one could tell at a glance would tear a person in half!
The person behind the attack had been ruthless from the beginning, leaving no room for survival!
If it hadn’t been for the timely Time Stop, Colin estimated he himself would probably be dead by now!
No, even with Time Stop, under such successive fatal attacks, the odds were he could only wait for death…
Because more bullets were continuously being fired, slowing down as they entered a fifteen-meter radius, the numerous bullets densely filling the area nearly trapped Colin without escape…
Once the Time Stop effect ended, these attacks would come, and he would surely die.
But fortunately…
Colin’s face was calm, as he rolled the fingers holding the “Time Stasis” Golden Card from left to right, revealing yet another Golden Card —
“Force – Repulsive Force.”“As long as I can react, I could even deflect lightning, let alone an explosion.”
After swiftly “marking” Qin Chuan and a few others, Colin used the inherent ability of “Repulsion Burst” to its full extent.
The very next instant, a rapid succession of sounds rang out beside his ears…
A terrifying repulsion force, with Colin at the center, sent everything flying away from him, except for a few people—this included the air, the sand beneath their feet, and the shattered limbs and shockwave, everything.
As a top-tier item from Bonfire Company, the Golden Card’s influence on matter was superior to all the things present!
In an instant, a circular crater fifteen meters in both depth and width appeared on the beach.
The group fell into it…
After successfully avoiding this nearly certain death trap, Colin then noticed that in the recent attack, although the people around him had escaped calamity, the other children a bit further away were not so lucky.
Under the attack of machine guns interspersed with some large-caliber bullets, limbs were shattered, blood sprayed…
Nearly no one among the dozens of people at the scene was left with an intact body.
Climbing out of the pit a little, Qin Chuan and the others, who didn’t know how they had escaped death, saw the scattered corpses all around, first their brains went blank, then their eyes filled with blood, their veins popping furiously.
They had protected these children all the way, and some feelings had developed.
Moreover, the great sacrifice made by 331 into getting them out, they thought they were home and everything was over, yet they ended up being betrayed!
“Gao Sheng, you motherfucker!” Qin Chuan looked at a little girl’s head shattered by bullets on the ground, at the milky rabbit candy she clutched in her lifeless hand beside her, and he nearly lost his mind.
He still remembered the childish questions she asked him on the train about what the world was like, what the real sun looked like, the stars, the moon…
He promised to take them to the amusement park.
But now…
Blood soaked the sand before them, while a mist of blood from exploded limbs hung over the battlefield, the smell of blood from a slaughterhouse hitting them in the face.
“Stay calm…”
Hu Zheng hurriedly held him back; the attack from outside hadn’t stopped, and to rashly rush out would mean certain death.
Before reaching the Sixth Level, they didn’t have the ability to disregard these weapons…
“Stay calm my ass, I’m going to fight it out with him!” Qin Chuan struggled free of Hu Zheng’s hold, grabbing a bunch of charms, intending to rush out and fight to the death.
But before he could crawl out, a hand grabbed his neck from behind and flung him backward.
“Get into the pit, protect the others.”
Colin’s face grim and his hand withdrawn, he sensed the situation outside without any delay and pulled out another card—”Smiling Mountain of Corpses”!
The next instant, all the corpses within the effect range melted, converging midair.
“Awooo!!!”
A massive, pitch-black sphere of flesh dropped into the center of the battlefield, emanating indescribable resentment and rage. As soon as it appeared, without waiting for Colin to utter a word, it withstood a barrage of weapon attacks and charged toward the enemies, who were shooting incessantly dozens of meters away, unleashing a piercing “psionic attack” from its mouth.
In an instant, several armed personnel shuddered and fell dead to the ground.
Meanwhile, the surface of Corpse Mountain writhed, and another face full of anger and resentment grew out of it…
Unlike before, the twisted faces that sprouted from it now seemed much more juvenile.
“Come back.”
Colin stopped Corpse Mountain from charging forward; his purpose for summoning it was to block attacks like bullets.
Otherwise, in this open area near the sea, stepping out would be like being used for target practice.
“These guys…”
Seeing the hair-raising barrage of bullets blocked by the massive body of Corpse Mountain, Colin took a ring with a large eyeball from his pocket, slipped it onto his finger, and a blurry ice-blue shadow flew out from it. Sensing his suppressed emotions, it didn’t speak much and cooperated by entering his body…
Afterward, Colin’s body became somewhat blurred, and he acquired the ability to fly quickly at low altitude.
After leaping out of the pit, he used Corpse Mountain’s huge size as cover and charged towards the enemy’s direction.
If there were no tank cannons involved, it would be difficult to completely destroy Corpse Mountain with just these weapons, especially this time, where the Corpse Mountain, seemingly because of an issue with the “sacrifice” source, had terrifyingly sinister smiling faces exuding intense bitterness and rage…
“Loads of enemies, thirty or more? Or even more? There are snipers, too, but no big deal. The most troublesome thing is inside one of those armored vehicles…”
Colin followed behind Corpse Mountain, assessing the enemy’s position.
However, just then, his footsteps halted when he felt a hand grasp at his foot from beneath the sand—it was Gao Sheng, an unknown Extraordinary One of the fifth or sixth level…
In his hand was a charm, which he attached to Colin’s foot.
A face also emerged from the sand and laughed, “Haha, Advanced Anomaly Dispel Talisman. Once stuck on you, all your Extraordinary Powers will be rendered useless…”
Before he could finish, Colin bent down swiftly and grasped the man’s face, pulling him out of the ground like uprooting a radish and holding him aloft.
At the same time, a terrifying chill surged along his arm into Gao Sheng’s body.
“How is this possible, you…” Before Gao Sheng could finish his sentence, his entire body was frozen solid.
“Sorry, I don’t have much in the way of Extraordinary Powers on me.”
With a determined gaze, Colin tightened his grip on the man’s head, crushing the frozen skull to pieces in an instant.
His body, now able to move one-ton objects even in a normal state, had no trouble crushing a brain that had been frozen to tens of degrees below zero.
His corpse was not wasted, directly devoured by Corpse Mountain…
The body of a high-ranking official caused it to almost sprout a third head.
However, Colin paid it no heed, and after killing him, continued to move forward while flashing through thoughts in his brain, guessing who the enemy attacking them might be.
This time, the enemies gave him a strong sense of being specifically targeted, with the initial wave of attacks being fatal had his methods been any less.
From the initial confusion to the subsequent arguments, followed by the narrowly averted multiple deadly attacks that almost rendered his “Deadly Insight” useless…
If it weren’t for a bit of luck and a quick reaction, he might have indeed perished.
“My enemies in reality seem to be only the ‘Red Moon’ believers, but it doesn’t seem like they’re the ones responsible this time, so that means…”
Swiftly, a name emerged in Colin’s mind—Liping.
The Eighth Level Ambassador he had seen when he joined the officials at the base.
And it was at that moment…
Realizing they couldn’t take Colin down by conventional means, several armed personnel opened the rear door of the last armored vehicle.
Behind the door was a woman bound in chains all over her body, her body covered in charms, sitting stiffly like a stone statue with an eerie smile that should not appear on a human face.
.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 247 - 247 247 Eighth Level Agent_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 247: Chapter 247 Eighth Level Agent_1 Chapter 247: Chapter 247 Eighth Level Agent_1 “It’s indeed this guy…”
Standing behind Corpse Mountain and seeing the figure of the woman inside the carriage, Colin’s heart suddenly became clear, and at this moment, he could be certain that the Eighth Level Agent herself must have died long ago.
After all, he had seen this woman’s “skeleton” and her last words in the sewer filled with rat bones before.
He just didn’t know what means the other party had used to take over her characteristics and flesh, even deceiving the insiders.
At the same time, upon observing the other party, he directly used the “Combat Power Observation” ability that came with the “Gene Compensation Panel.”
A set of panel information immediately appeared before his eyes.
[Name]: Liping (uncertain).
[Strength]: 3.9. (Not very strong.)
[Constitution]: 23. (Her horrifying constitution could even let her withstand the Harmonious Express.)
[Agility]: 2.4. (Not very quick.)
[Description]: Its constitution is strong, but even stronger and more bizarre seems to be the evil spirit residing within her.
[Comprehensive Evaluation]: Unkillable.
[Note]: The above data does not represent the final combat power, please refer to the actual contact…
“???”
This information made Colin startled; his strength and agility weren’t much, but was there a dot missing in the middle of that 23 constitution value?
And moreover, judging by the description, it seems her strength doesn’t lie in her constitution…
However, without thinking too much, Colin’s heart chilled as he heard the sound of several chains snapping beside his ear, and then, the woman who had maintained a statue-like eerie smile saw her charms spontaneously combust without flame; she twisted her neck to face Colin.
The next moment.
A terrifying aura poured forth.
This Eighth Level Agent had a vertical crack appear on her forehead, which pulled apart to either side, revealing a blood-red eyeball within…
The world in all directions turned crimson in an instant, making Colin feel as though he was being dragged into some domain.
The “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” also disappeared from his side…
“Fuck, so sinister, what kind of ‘Ambassador’ did it serve as?”
Colin’s scalp tingled. He had previously asked Qin Chuan and the others about the situation of this senior agent.
Unfortunately, due to the low level, they didn’t know much…
Only Xia Liufang, who was walking the same path, roughly knew some intelligence, knowing that Liping, after stepping into the Seventh Level, had in a twist of fate integrated a weird belief that had been activated during an ancient regional licentious priesthood into herself, thus taking a step further to become one of the top-tier personnel.
This was different from ordinary people who merely borrowed power from “belief.”
She genuinely invited a “God” to reside in her body, and if she managed to fully integrate with her own consciousness dominating, she might theoretically have the chance to become Ninth Level Personnel.
Unfortunately, the current situation seemed to be that at some indeterminate point in the past, she was secretly killed during a mission, and then someone took over her body and infiltrated the official rank.
Probably the “Special Operations Department” never expected one of the country’s top powerhouses to die so quietly.
However, without waiting to think further, Colin saw, amidst the crimson sand of the surrounding beach, several “fountains” appeared, and what spewed from the fountains wasn’t water but torrents of fresh blood.
It was like the mumblings of the previous day echoed in his ears, and the strong stench of blood also assaulted his face…
At the same time, Colin’s heart tensed, and an image appeared in his mind—
From amidst a cloud of blood mist above his head, a female hand with sharp claws stretched out through a curtain of flame and slapped onto his head, causing his eyeballs to burst out from the sockets due to immense pressure, his head shattered, and he died on the spot.
Without much thought, Colin lifted his head, his right hand pulled out a white bone spur filled with black cracks from his pocket, and he stabbed towards a cluster of blood mist above that had gathered unknown when.
During this process, a hand with black nails reached out…
“Ah!!!”
The sharp tip of the bone spur easily pierced the skin of the palm. A woman’s agonized scream followed, erupting from above in a cloud of blood that rattled the soul.
The figure within vanished, as if trying to escape…
However,
“Within a thirty-meter radius, you can’t run away,”
Colin’s eyes were cold, and he spread the fingers of his left hand, reaching out to grasp the rapidly receding blood mist from afar.
Boom!
Flames burst violently from his body, engulfing the blood mist like a gaping maw.
As the blood mist dissipated in the blaze, a figure struggled in mid-air, but after fluttering for a few seconds, it turned into a charred corpse and fell from the sky.
After it hit the ground, it turned into a pool of dirty blackened blood and disappeared without a trace.
And the crimson world around remained unchanged…
“It’s not the real body, but even with this move, killing a high-level agent is indeed a bit difficult,”
Colin, unconcerned, surveyed his surroundings warily, noticing more blood mist appearing, each with pairs of eyes watching and moving closer.
It seemed they were planning to overwhelm him with numbers and exhaust him to death in this inexplicable crimson domain…
Moreover, bubbling noises kept coming from the blood pools on the ground, and he could sense something malevolent emerging from beneath the surface…
A sense of dreadful crisis erupted within him.
Intuition told him that being in this domain, his situation was very bad.
If these oddities were to attack at the same time, even his “Deadly Insight” would be futile, leaving him to just watch himself die.
Just then, the eerie blood mists hastened their advance, apparently intending to launch a saturation attack.
Colin narrowed his eyes and, without hesitation, pulled out a Golden Card and infused it with spirit.
“Repulsion Burst”!
The next second, a terrifying repulsion radiated from his body outwards, pushing all the blood mist away…
But just as Colin was pondering how to extricate himself from this place to avoid being drained to death…
Crack.
The crimson domain itself seemed to be affected by the repulsion, riddled with cracks, and shattered on the spot into myriad pieces.
The normal world was once again revealed before his eyes.
“This thing… can it really push away such an eerie domain?”
Colin was momentarily astonished; he genuinely hadn’t expected the card to be this powerful, tearing apart the problematic crimson domain so easily.
“How is that possible?!”
Some who saw Colin’s figure reemerge were even more shocked than him.
The “Domain” was an ability unique to Eighth Level powerhouses, and although it might not work against peers, it was virtually a death sentence for those a level lower or lacking the means to counteract it.
Yet, the man they had just dragged in for less than ten seconds had already escaped?
However, before they could dwell on it, on seeing them, Colin didn’t hesitate to step forward and stomped his foot, as flames erupted from his body, instantly covering everyone in the vicinity for tens of meters.
A few, aflame, started running wildly, attempting to flee the firestorm, but Colin shot them dead with an “Air Bullet” within just a few steps.
At a distance, the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” also charged into the crowd, smashing enemies into pulp.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 248 - 248 248 My Value is Above Yours_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 248: Chapter 248 My Value is Above Yours!_1 Chapter 248: Chapter 248 My Value is Above Yours!_1 “No one’s getting away; you’re all going to die!”
Colin cursed under his breath, raised his gun, and quickly picked off the enemy.
Depending on the “Adaptive Aiming” attribute, nearly every bullet he fired took down an enemy.
Before his flesh could fully withstand rifle bullets, these guys’ harassment was pretty annoying, so it was still best to kill them off…
While firing, his gaze shifted, searching for the figure of the Eighth Level Agent.
After coming out, he discovered that the person had vanished without a trace…
Just then, Colin had a sudden hunch and looked in a certain direction. Aside from the blood mist, it seemed like nothing was there, but upon blinking, when his pupils turned into Beast Transformation Syndrome State, he could see a woman with a blood-red vertical eye on her forehead standing among it.
Her expression was rigid, and when her eyes met Colin’s, she nodded at him and said,
“An Eighth Level Personnel like you being dragged into the blood pool would usually emerge severely injured if they escaped at all. Yet you’re fine, which is quite impressive.
“I can offer you a chance to become a high-level priest of the ‘Red Moon,’ drink the ‘True Crimson Blood,’ and obtain the opportunity to survive the final catastrophe in a decade or so…”
“Red Moon”…
Hearing this term, a strong sense of anger rose within Colin. These people were truly everywhere!
Openly and secretly, their shadows lurked everywhere.
Bang, bang, bang!
Several bullets wrapped in flames shot out, interrupting her speech…
But the bullets caused her no harm as they simply passed through her body.
“These little conflicts between us are insignificant in the face of the future existential crisis of our species. And now, the only way to survive this disaster is to follow the benevolent ‘Mother,’ to achieve ultimate salvation…”
However, before she could finish, Colin’s figure had already charged up, engulfing the figure before him with fierce flames.
Unfortunately, what his attack hit was still just a shadow in the blood mist.
“Don’t waste your effort; you can’t kill me, and I can’t kill you. If you want to flee, I can’t stop you, and it’s the same if I want to leave. So, why not patiently listen to what I have to say, for instance, you don’t have any idea how desperate the situation humanity has to face is, and our only option is…”
Further away, some more blood suddenly misted and a female silhouette appeared, continuing to try to persuade Colin, but halfway through, she suddenly sensed something, turned her head as if she realized something, and glanced somewhere.
“It seems we’ll have to meet again another time.”
With that, her figure turned into a blood mist and disappeared…
Colin frowned and took a deep breath, sniffing the air. He intended to pursue but then heard a strange roar from afar.
The sound came from the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses.”
Suddenly, a crazed figure dripping with blood tore through the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses,” dragging a spine-like “sword” as it charged towards Qin Chuan in the pit.
“That man called Gao Sheng? Didn’t I crush his head and feed it to the Corpse Mountain? Wasn’t he digested properly? No, that doesn’t seem to be Gao Sheng; it’s the monster that was controlling his body; the symbiosis failed…”
Colin saw a writhing mass of flesh where the man’s brain should have been, clearly indicating a core only followers of the “Red Moon” possessed.
At the same time, he immediately checked the panel of the individual.
[Name]: Gao Sheng (False).
[Strength]: 7.4.
[Constitution]: 10.9.
[Agility]: 5.
[Description]: Possesses an exceptionally strong constitution…
[Overall Evaluation]: Not weak.
[Note]: The above data does not represent the final combat capability, please judge based on actual contact…
“About the same stats as me.”
With a frown, Colin knew that Qin Chuan and the others definitely couldn’t handle it; letting it pass would be disastrous. Its sheer statistics were enough to slaughter them.
Without further hesitation, Colin paused for a moment, abandoning the chase after Liping, and turned towards the same direction to charge…
Three seconds later, he caught up to the aberration from behind.
Just then, as if he sensed something, Colin stopped in his tracks and pulled out a bone spur, positioning it in front of him.
Almost simultaneously, “Gao Sheng” turned around, his sword arcing back like a rearward thrust, chopping straight down onto the bone spur that Colin held in front of him.
“Bang!”
In the massive collision, the air itself seemed to tremble.
Small stones under Colin’s feet were sent flying…
Not far away, Qin Chuan and the others felt a buzzing in their ears, their hearts pounding uncontrollably.
If that strike had hit them, none of them could have blocked it!
Colin’s expression was icy as he forcefully deflected the great sword in front of him, then flames burst from his body, engulfing the enemy before him.
Unfortunately, the flames seemed to have little effect on him.
However, this time, even though he didn’t take down his opponent immediately, Colin didn’t consider using the two Golden Cards to kill the enemy on the spot…
Using the “Repulsion” card repeatedly in a short time caused his internal organs to experience “repulsion,” feeling extremely uncomfortable, as if they would burst at any moment.
Using Time Stop again in a short interval would stack two buffs on top of each other, which his body simply couldn’t withstand.
There was also the fact that Gao Sheng’s stats were very high; Qin Chuan and the others would probably be unable to block even one hit.
But…
“My stats are above yours!”
Colin didn’t know much about “swordsmanship,” but relying on his own stronger overall stats was enough to compensate for any shortcomings in that area.
Bang!
Bang!
Bang!
Two men capable of explosive power that could shake tons of weight clashed, producing deafening noises.
The ears of the people behind them were ringing and itching unbearably, almost unable to hear clearly.
“This… these are truly two monsters.”
Hu Zheng muttered to himself as he watched the collision unfold.
However, the high-frequency exchange didn’t last long before Qin Chuan and the others noticed that Gao Sheng was gradually weakening, and several wounds inflicted by Colin’s bone spurs appeared on his body.
These wounds weren’t deep, yet they seemed to cause him great pain.
“It’s time to end this.”
Colin was preparing to take him down directly, but suddenly he felt something, noticing that Gao Sheng’s body was expanding at an abnormal speed.
Although bone spurs could cause swelling, it certainly wasn’t this fast!
Is this guy… planning to self-destruct?
Colin’s brow furrowed as he immediately guessed the opponent’s intention. After a brief thought, he was ready to endure the side effects and use “Repulsion” again to eject the enemy.
But just then, the flesh ball in front of him suddenly trembled, and immediately an open wound on the chest tore open, and a torrent of filthy, foul-smelling black liquid gushed out, turning into a puddle of black pus…
“Died from not being able to endure the curse of the bone spurs?”
Colin was momentarily startled. There was a possibility for this, but it was unlikely to be high since the effect of the bone spur’s curse wasn’t that fast.
However, before he could ponder any further, he suddenly noticed that the figure of an old man had appeared in the middle of the battlefield.
The old man was extremely tall, at least one meter ninety, but his frame was very lean, as if he didn’t have an ounce of body fat, looking like a telegraph pole.
No one knew when he had arrived, and no one knew how long he had been there—it seemed as though he had been standing there for quite some time by the time they noticed him.
‘A Ninth Level “Fate Propeller” expert!’
Colin’s breathing hitched, feeling an overwhelming pressure radiating from the old man.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 249 - 249 249 Many Friends Many Paths_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 249: Chapter 249: Many Friends, Many Paths_1 Chapter 249: Chapter 249: Many Friends, Many Paths_1 “It seems I’ve arrived a bit late…”
The old man swept his gaze around the battlefield, then took another look at the black flesh orb not far away, a strange light flashing in his eyes as if he understood a lot about the situation in an instant.
“Cough, cough, cough!”
A series of coughing sounds came from the trees around, and Colin saw that the enemies who had been hiding in the dark and shooting, who hadn’t been dealt with in time, seemed to have bad luck and accidentally choked on their saliva, unable to suppress the physiological instinct to cough.
Then, within a few seconds, they passed out one after another due to the severe coughing that caused a lack of oxygen in their brain…
‘Is this… this strange?’ Colin was dumbfounded.
He knew it was possible to knock oneself out by choking on water, but it couldn’t happen to these people—they were clearly under the influence of that Ninth Level “Fate Propeller” powerhouse.
“Bad luck looks like this,”
said the old man, summing up the situation in a simple comment. He withdrew his gaze and looked at Colin with a kind countenance, yet it made Colin feel a depressing weight in his heart again.
If he could have taken a swing at the Eighth Level guy earlier, now with this one, if the other party really had any ideas, Colin figured he had no chance of resisting, and even escaping felt forced.
Meanwhile, he also understood why this battle was so hasty and why the enemy had suddenly withdrawn.
The enemy must have known that reinforcements would arrive soon, so they decided to retreat rather than continue trying to capture him.
Especially since among the reinforcements there was a Ninth Level top-tier Extraordinary One!
“You seem to be under a lot of pressure?”
The Ninth Level powerhouse spoke calmly, his tone emotionless, but his gaze didn’t stay on Colin. Instead, he followed Colin’s line of sight to Qin Chuan and the others behind him and pulled out a pair of black sunglasses from his pocket.
“Actually, there’s no need for that, after all, I’m not some kind of demon,”
the old man said as he put on the sunglasses, then looked back at Colin: “In these times, having one more friend to cooperate with is much better than having another enemy, don’t you think?”
Upon hearing this, Colin let out a sigh of relief inside and nodded: “You’re right.”
He knew this basically meant that he wouldn’t have to worry about things like handing over those items.
Because their relationship was “cooperative,” not subordinate…
“The incident with ‘Liping’ is indeed a tragedy. However, have you ever wondered why ‘Liping,’ when inviting you at the end, kept saying things that made no sense?” the old man continued.
“What do you mean?” Colin sensed something.
With this reminder, he indeed noticed that “Liping” had been engaging in pointless actions at the end.
Clumsy persuasion to surrender, clichéd lines, incomprehensible “riddles”…
“Heh, she initially wanted to recite some prayers of the ‘Red Moon’ and instill in you some subtle yet extremely dangerous knowledge contamination… However, I gave her a new script. Otherwise, with your current state, coming into contact with that knowledge might not be such a good thing,”
the tall and lean old man shook his head: “It’s a pity she noticed the issue after only a few sentences, otherwise there really was a chance to capture her.”
‘These lines are so bad, who wouldn’t realize something was off?’
Colin criticized inwardly.
At the same time, he learned of the old man’s ability from his words—to influence a person’s luck, as well as arrange abilities similar to the “Passionate Paradise” Narrator from before.
The old man didn’t elaborate further on this matter, and from behind the sunglasses, his eyes moved to the children: “Where are these people from? Some other unknown region? I can hardly detect their presence in this world.”
Impressive… Colin felt that if the old man looked a few more times, he might see through the disguise of those “The Seventh Box Garden World” seeds.
“They have some issues, but nothing major. Next, we should talk about you…”
The old man seemed completely unaware of what Colin was thinking. Just as he was about to continue speaking, he suddenly noticed something, turned his gaze in a certain direction, and changed the topic:
“I suddenly feel that if I chase after her now, I might be able to catch up with her. The possibility is slim, but what if?
“So, let’s talk about your matter later. Someone else will take over here soon. We’ll meet again afterward.
“By the way, the items you handed over before, you can try looking around nearby. If you’re lucky, they should all be fine.”
After saying this, the old man disappeared without waiting for Colin to reply. No trace of his presence could be found, and everything seemed as if it were just an illusion…
Qin Chuan and the others behind him were still immersed in the “deafening” battle that had just taken place and hadn’t snapped back to reality, not even noticing the old man had been there.
Had it not been for the enemies a distance away, whom he had knocked out with his saliva, Colin might even have doubted that the old man had ever appeared.
He was like “Luck,” difficult to detect unless he deliberately left a trace.
‘Is a “Ninth Level Fate Propeller” really this elusive…’ Colin thought, alarmed. He then moved forward to search and successfully found four parchments; two were his, and the other two belonged to his companions.
Besides that, some of the items that Qin Chuan and the others had handed over were indeed still there…
It seemed like Qin Chuan and the others finally came to their senses. They all uniformly scratched their itchy ears before someone finally spoke up, “Is it over?”
“Yes.”
Colin nodded, and as he began to dissipate the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses,” he started speaking.
However, before he could say much more, he suddenly heard a rumbling noise by his ear.
The group looked up in the direction of the sound and saw several fighter jets streaking across the sky at high speed.
And when the jets reached a certain position, their bomb bays opened, releasing something that flew towards them—
A missile!
Boom!
The missile landed not far from where Colin and his companions were standing, its bay shattering, but instead of explosives, it burst open with a myriad of eerie yellow talisman papers…
What was this now?
As Colin wondered, he saw part of the yellow papers in the sky suddenly come together, forming the shape of a person.
Before long, from among the fluttering yellow papers that never seemed to touch the ground, a paper man figure, clearly made of the talisman papers yet as lifelike as a real human, walked out.
“…This seems to be the garrison general of this province, an ‘Eighth Level powerhouse,’ the ‘Talismanist’ Cao Yixiang,” Qin Chuan explained in a low voice next to Colin, his words filled with respect.
Because he was on the same path as the other—dealing with talismans.
“It looks like the troublesome matter has been resolved,” Cao Yixiang observed, noticing that everything had been settled.
Then, seeing that many people were injured, he waved his hand, and numerous talisman papers quickly flew out, sticking to those people or directly entering their bodies, stabilizing their wounds…
As this Eighth Level powerhouse took charge of the scene, the sky above saw hundreds of parachutes descending rapidly, much smaller than normal parachutes and falling fast, clearly custom-made for those with extraordinary abilities…
In the far distance, at sea, a few ships could be faintly seen approaching. Helicopters flying in mid-air were advancing faster, closing in rapidly.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 250 - 250 250 The Key to Slaughtering God _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 250: Chapter 250: The Key to Slaughtering God “_1 Chapter 250: Chapter 250: The Key to Slaughtering God “_1 “Hiss… official forces always put on quite the show, don’t they? But is all this really necessary?”
Although Colin had seen even grander scenes and more advanced equipment in the “Seventh Box Garden World,” witnessing it in reality felt different.
“From the moment we returned to reality and made contact with these people, to when we were attacked, then the arrival of the super strong individual, followed by the rest of the personnel… The total time might have only been about fifteen minutes.”
Colin silently estimated in his mind; the speed of the support had been very fast indeed.
However, unfortunately, they were still one step slower than that other person—no, that’s not right.
“If the official deployment of combat aircraft was slower than the enemy, how could those ‘Red Moon’ traitors have locked onto our position so quickly and arrived even faster?”
Colin was puzzled and wondered if the enemy had roughly known their location from the start. What was it that kept updating the enemy on their position?
But he couldn’t dwell on that, for the Eighth Level “Talismanist” approached them now.
Up close, he finally noticed something indescribably stiff about the “Talismanist’s” expression, which gave off an unsettling feeling.
“I will escort you to Base No. 4 next. If you have any questions, you can discuss them with me here. Meanwhile, other injured parties will remain; other rescue personnel will take care of them.”
Cao Yixiang looked straight at Colin and the others, his eyes devoid of the spark that should inhabit a person’s gaze, and his voice was just as strangely unnerving.
“Hmm.” Colin nodded, and seeing that Cao didn’t seem interested in further conversation, just brought out a walkie-talkie to start communicating with others.
‘It seems that these high-ranking officials commonly exhibit symptoms of being out of control.’
Colin contemplated as he watched Cao walk away.
From his encounters with them, it seemed that from Sixth Level onward, these individuals began to deteriorate, and by Eighth Level, they overtly seemed less human, lacking a sense of humanity.
As powerful as they were, they also gave off the impression that they could lose control at any moment.
People in Bonfire Company didn’t seem to have this issue…
Colin estimated that under normal circumstances, D Level Personnel would definitely not match up to an Eighth Level official powerhouse, but would be stronger than a Sixth Level, probably around Seventh Level quality.
Yet, in terms of humanity, they seemed completely normal, showing no tendency to lose control.
It was unclear what influenced this condition.
But without giving it much thought, several helicopters had already arrived overhead and dropped ladders.
Assured that it wasn’t a trap this time, Colin and the others each climbed up.
…
Meanwhile, atop a hundred-story skyscraper, a skinny, tall old man wearing sunglasses pushed open the rooftop door and walked to the edge, looking down.
Then, with a grave and puzzled look, he murmured to himself:
“Did the ‘footprints’ disappear here?”
He had told Colin he was leaving to track “Liping,” but in reality, he had noticed something that could bring significant trouble starting from the beach, leaving behind a visible trail of “footprints” all the way here, so he had followed it.
To his surprise, it disappeared halfway.
After a moment’s thought, the old man took off his glasses, revealing mysterious patterns in his eyes, trying to reconstruct what had happened here.
In his mind, images flickered by like shattered glass…
The visions were meaningless, but just as a significant scene was about to surface, he seemed to “see” an amber light appear in his consciousness…
Immediately, he cut off the “observation.”
His instincts told him that from this point on, the matter had become connected with Bonfire Company…
In such a situation, it was nearly impossible to continue delving into it.
Because, just like the followers of the Red Moon, Bonfire Company also had a very strong anti-observation capability. Forcing a deeper look would only lead him to see an eternal and horrific blaze, seemingly capable of consuming the world or even a galaxy.
So rather than waste time here, it would be better to ask the “Spy in the Disc” directly later on.
…
On the other hand, after a thirty-minute flight, Colin and others arrived at Shelter Number Four. They had only been there for a short time when everyone was taken away separately.
Colin was no exception, being led into a sealed room.
There was a chair in the room, and, one meter in front of the chair, there was a thick glass wall, behind which was a table and chairs.
It felt like an interrogation room…
No, to be accurate, it was an interrogation room, except without handcuffs on him.
Once Colin was seated, two men and a woman walked out from behind the glass wall. One man appeared middle-aged with an authoritative face, and the other looked young, probably just over twenty.
The woman, in her early forties, had a face that involuntarily exuded a sense of approachability…
‘There seems to be a system to their selection.’
Colin wasn’t familiar with psychology, but he could tell that these people seemed a bit “typecast.”
Without letting him ponder further, as everyone settled in, the conversation began swiftly.
The stern-faced man was the first to speak gravely:
“Name.”
“Colin.”
“Age.”
“Twenty-three.”
“Gender.”
“Gender?”
Colin was taken aback—what a silly question? Although it felt nonsensical, he answered nonetheless.
Then followed a series of questions about his height and weight.
After seeing Colin answer each one frankly, the young man spoke up:
“Do you know why you’re here?”
“I don’t.”
“Do you know about the believers of the Red Moon? Did your colleagues mention anything about them to you?”
“I know.”
“Then do you know why you were targeted by the ‘Red Moon’ believers?”
“I don’t know, do you?”
Colin also shook his head. To be honest, it seemed he only happened to kill a few of their people when he was doing his tasks, and he shouldn’t be targeted like this just for that, should he?
When faced with Colin’s counter-question, the young man choked for a moment, then shook his head.
“So, can you remember the entire process of this incident? Our people later went to the subway station and did not find a sewer entrance, and as we understand it, those of you who entered seemed to have gone to another world…”
The middle-aged woman’s voice was warm, making one feel a full sense of closeness.
“I can.”
Colin briefly described the situation at that time without revealing his own role.
“Mr. Colin… Your account seems to have many loopholes. For example…”
“Based on the information we have, the dangers you faced far exceeded your capabilities, and from your companion, we learned that many terrible dangers were taken on by you alone…”
“And as a new employee of ‘Bonfire Company,’ where did you get all those things from…”
“And in the final stage, why did you leave some things behind instead of taking everything with you, but continued to let them take the train to the next station…”
“…”
There was no luck involved, one sharp question after another was thrown out.
Some questions were even ones Colin himself hadn’t noticed. Looking at the earphones on the ears of these people, he knew that there must be another team behind them, responsible for receiving information from Qin Chuan’s side and then asking questions.
However, these questions made Colin somewhat troubled. Why did these people seem to feign ignorance and insist on asking difficult questions?
Just as Colin didn’t know how to answer, the people in front of him suddenly stood up all at once.
“Old Master Wu is asking for you in his office.”
Upon hearing this, Colin breathed a sigh of relief, and then it occurred to him—was that old man’s surname Wu?
Without giving it much thought, he was led out again and taken onto a fully enclosed vehicle.
After about ten minutes, the vehicle stopped, and then Colin was taken into an office.
The office was over a hundred square meters large, filled with various mahogany furniture and sculptures, looking very imposing…
Behind a mahogany tea table, wearing a pair of dark sunglasses, sat Old Master Wu—the Ninth Level Powerhouse and the head of the Southern Region. Seeing him come in, he pointed to the seat in front:
“Sit down.”
Once Colin settled in his seat and there were only two people in the room, Old Wu poured him a cup of tea and asked directly:
“Do you know if anything followed you out?”
Something followed them out?
Colin was taken aback; he truly hadn’t realized. In his eyes, their escape, despite heavy casualties from “The Seventh Box Garden World,” could be considered very successful.
Throughout the whole process, no unsavory entities came out, at least none that he had discovered…
‘Wait, if something really did follow us, and kept us in check all the way, then ‘Liping’ would have been able to come to us first to clarify…’
‘Also, that bizarre treeman at the second station—was it actually trying to say that something had followed me?’
In a flash, Colin felt as though he understood much, and at the same time, there was a chill in his heart.
He hadn’t noticed anything along the way!
However, before he could speak of these matters, the old man, after getting his reply, didn’t seem to have the intention to continue questioning. Instead, he began speaking of something else, as if implicating another matter:
“Since it’s not there, let it be. It’s not that important anyway. Now, let’s talk about ‘Bonfire Company’…
“I don’t know much about it, and since you’ve joined this company for some time, you might have learned quite a bit. Can you enlighten me?”
“Please say.”
Colin sat upright in the wooden chair. In the tasks he had taken on before, there was a requirement to understand the demands of the “Special Operations Department.”
Now was a good opportunity…
Old Wu pondered for a moment, then said, “We have no ill intent towards ‘Bonfire Company,’ but we are very interested in some things within it and are willing to pay a certain price to obtain them. For example…
“Do you know about the ‘Gene Compensation Medicine’?”
Under normal circumstances, Colin, who had just completed his mission and was yet to “formally join” the company, should not know about this stuff.
But at this point, Colin didn’t hide anything: “I know.”
The old man said, “Tell me, is there a way we can get a large quantity of the ‘Gene Compensation Medicine’? For instance, thousands or tens of thousands of doses for each level, or even more…the price is negotiable.”
Thousands or tens of thousands for each level? How much would that cost in points and badges?
Colin did a quick calculation and felt it was an astronomical sum; obviously, money wouldn’t suffice.
“What… do you need so much of this for? Its enhancement isn’t that great, is it?”
Colin asked in confusion. The boost from the Gene Compensation Medicine wasn’t strong; much more of the enhancement came from equipment and talents.
But the officials didn’t ask about those powerful pieces of equipment first, nor talents, rather they started with the ostensibly inconspicuous “Gene Compensation Medicine”?
“Heh, you might not know, but this stuff is really good,” said Old Wu as he poured tea and shook his head with a chuckle.
“If we had it, we might not have to worry about losing control, and I probably wouldn’t be left with less than a year of life…
“If there is something that allows humans to truly touch the extraordinary and take these powers, which don’t belong to mankind, into our hands like knives, swords, and firearms, then it is undoubtedly this.
“Its effects might not be immediately noticeable, but its role is irreplaceable.
“Even unreservedly said, if humanity wants to attempt to slay ‘gods,’ then it is a key ‘key’ necessary on the path to slaying gods.”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 251 - 251 251 On the Importance of Gene Compensation
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 251: Chapter 251: On the Importance of “Gene Compensation Medicine”._1 Chapter 251: Chapter 251: On the Importance of “Gene Compensation Medicine”._1 “A key on the path of deicide? That extravagant?”
Colin clicked his tongue upon hearing this; he hadn’t expected the “Gene Compensation Medicine” to hold such a high status in the eyes of this old man, or rather, in the eyes of the officials.
But upon reflection, the strength of “Gene Compensation Medicine” wasn’t due to how much it boosted, rather, its use meant one wouldn’t so easily lose control and go mad…
Thinking back to the status of the official Extraordinary Ones and the senior members of Bonfire Company, it did indeed seem to fall quite short.
As for the less than a year of lifespan the other mentioned…
Colin wasn’t surprised because Old Master Wu appeared to be in his nineties, and due to the specialty of the powers he wielded, there was a kind of indescribable ethereality about him, as if he could “ascend to immortality” at any moment.
“Hmm, saying it’s an exaggeration might indeed be an exaggeration, but the value and importance of this thing might be much higher than you think…”
“We’re unclear how exactly this medicine is made, but without a doubt, after using it, trying to merge with Extraordinary Power, the symptoms of losing control will be greatly reduced.”
Old Master Wu said this while opening a Zisha teapot brewing Pu’er tea, tossing a handful of goji berries and red dates into it:
“Be it domestically or internationally, all power pathways, as long as used, can play a role, and it can almost be considered a universal medicine that Extraordinary Ones wouldn’t even dare to dream of, or to directly call it a golden finger wouldn’t be an exaggeration either. Once used, it can resolve the biggest hidden danger, losing control.
“According to estimates, if an Eighth Level Personnel could use this medicine methodically, then his tendency to lose control would be reduced by at least ninety percent and above.
“This way, we wouldn’t need to counteract our own madness while using our powers, and our strength would also see a much greater increase.”
Under the old man’s patient explanation, Colin finally understood just how powerful the effects of that small vial of medicine really were.
However, the other talking about a transaction of a few thousand or tens of thousands all at once…
Colin felt that the possibility wasn’t very large.
“Getting some ‘Gene Compensation Medicine’ shouldn’t be difficult for you; just follow the process, Bonfire Company will most likely not give you any fake products, but asking for too much…”
Colin honestly expressed his opinion.
He felt that exchanging for the medicine wouldn’t be difficult, but that was only applicable to him personally.
Once the amount reached a unit of thousands or tens of thousands, it felt somewhat unreal…
The required Points and Mission Vouchers would be unimaginably vast.
Plus, many of Bonfire Company’s rules are quite rigid. Lady Bunny indeed has considerable authority, but she might not be able to make decisions on this matter.
Moreover, even if the officials could produce valuables worth that amount of medicine, it was uncertain whether Bonfire Company would have them.
Currently, Colin guessed that the number of people active in the Interaction Hall, excluding those “invaders,” probably wouldn’t exceed five hundred, or even three hundred.
The total amount of medicine acquired by so many people might not even reach a thousand, let alone thousands or tens of thousands…
“The problem isn’t very big, whatever we can get is enough; as long as they are not giving fake goods or something, then it’s fine.”
Old Master Wu didn’t show any sign of regret, quite the opposite; he seemed to adopt an attitude of taking whatever he could get.
“There shouldn’t be any need to worry about fake goods…”
After joining the company and seeing various affairs, Colin suspected that if a “Demon” joined the company and honestly completed missions, earning Points and certificates, they would still be able to obtain genuine medicine.
What the company emphasizes is an indiscriminate teaching, equal treatment for all…
However, while speaking, Colin suddenly thought of something and said:
“Right, there’s another thing, even if you can get the medicine, you will most likely only be able to get D Level and below Gene Compensation Medicine…”
“D Level Gene Compensation Medicine.”
Old Master Wu murmured to himself as if assessing something, then after a while he said, “That should be almost enough; at least it’s still suitable up to Eighth Level, and even at this stage, it has a very large effect…”
If I had these things, the high-level personnel cultivated in the future would no longer be like time bombs that could explode at any moment as they do now.
Incidents like Liping’s, who had to risk encompassing dangerous things before going mad, eventually stepping into a trap, would no longer occur…
“Are you thinking of using it to address the pollution in your body?”
Colin looked at the old man in front of him and asked curiously.
Truth be told, although it seemed like the old man was trying to conceal something, Colin could still somewhat sense the massive, nearly illusory black threads spreading from the old man’s back into the distance, connecting to who knows where, it was disturbing.
And his less than a year of life expectancy was most likely not because his time had come, but because he was out of control and had to solve the problem himself.
“Me? I’m beyond help…”
Old Master Wu shook his head, poured himself a cup of goji berry and red date Pu’er tea, and poured one for Colin as well, “The best way to treat cancer is to deal with it before the word ‘cancer’ ever touches you, not after it appears…
“I’m already gravely ill, this thing might be of use to me, but it wouldn’t make much of a difference…
“There needs to be a sequence to these things, and I, for one, am too late…
“From what I understand through my abilities, it should work well for those at Level Five and below, but from Level Six, the effects are halved, and the efficacy is even worse for Level Seven…
“So, even if we get this thing, the members at Level Seven and above would have to give up using it.”
“That…” Colin opened his mouth, at a loss for words for a moment.
“Heh, it’s not a big deal. Compared to my ancestors, at least I can see some hope, which isn’t bad,” Old Master Wu seemed rather open-minded about the matter and then couldn’t help but sigh, “However, if it had been a few years earlier, perhaps I might have had a chance…”
As he spoke, he did not inquire about getting a higher-level medicine, nor did he ask for more, seemingly having accepted the outcome before even making such a request.
“In a while, once I learn a bit more, I will tell you.”
Colin wasn’t sure when he would be able to speak with Miss Bunny, so he didn’t specify a time.
The old man showed understanding of this.
Latter, rather than delving into the topic of Bonfire Company, the old man casually brought up other matters in what seemed like idle conversation.
“You might not know, but no matter where we are, international or domestic, the ways Extraordinary Ones might gain power are diverse—there are doctrines, inheritances, beliefs, or perhaps bloodlines, races, and much more, quite a variety…”
“But ultimately, Extraordinary Ones are just people contaminated by alien essences. They use the pollution they’ve received to combat anomalies. That’s how we are, and others are similar…”
“Fate Propelling is the same. The more you use things contaminated with a certain essence, the more your body becomes tainted. Of course, if you want a more pleasant way to say it, it’s that you’ve inherited extraordinary power, but in reality, it’s pollution…”
“The human body will break down and go mad as the contamination deepens; it’s just that some do so quickly and others slowly. Those diverse methods can be seen as ways to slow or share the madness, but that’s all they do—slow it down…”
“Only Gene Compensation Medicine can prevent such an outcome and truly allow one to wield the power in their hands. That’s why I told you, if humans want to wield the power to slay gods, this is indispensable.”
Listening to the old man, Colin understood the significance of this item even more deeply.
“By the way, have you ever used a ‘Book of Fate’ fragment?” the old man suddenly changed the subject.
“I have.”
Colin didn’t deny it. Not just him but most people in Bonfire Company had used it; he would often see newcomers getting hold of it and then trying to buy lottery tickets, ultimately learning a lesson and losing their investment.
This wasn’t a secret, and speaking of it wasn’t a big deal.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 252 - 252 252 Prop Production Intentions._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 252: Chapter 252: “Prop” Production Intentions._1 Chapter 252: Chapter 252: “Prop” Production Intentions._1 “Yes, and with this journey, you should be able to discern that our ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’ is quite different from those within the Bonfire Company, and its use would only be by common people or those who are ‘Fate Propeller’…”
“Indeed.”
Colin nodded, remembering that the official ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’ had a physical form, while the company’s did not.
Regarding the users, he only noticed it after the other party mentioned it.
“Hehe, this is the process of becoming a ‘Fate Propeller Teller.’ Once used, one would be contaminated…”
“Use it and be contaminated?” Colin was startled, he had used it quite a lot.
“Yes, but you don’t have to worry.”
Old Master Wu laughed, but his laughter felt somewhat bitter, “I don’t know how the people at Bonfire Company did it, but they have removed the pollution aspect, turning it into a pure tool.”
“Although I hate to admit it, Bonfire Company’s use of the ‘Book of Fate’ is indeed superior to ours.”
This seems normal, the ‘Book of Fate’ itself had leaked from Bonfire Company, it just isn’t known how it ended up in official hands…
Colin didn’t care much about that, and indeed the creators within Bonfire Company were extremely talented at turning various anomalies into tools.
The myriad of tools with diverse effects at the internal Trading Path could also be seen as a history filled with the blood and tears of strange anomalies and evaluators.
Although he knew this, he did not speak it out loud.
“Not only the ‘Book of Fate,’ but Bonfire Company seems to be good at making all sorts of tools,”
The old man put down his empty teacup and popped an almond into his mouth, “Perhaps in this regard, we might have some space for cooperation. Dealing with dangerous containment subjects nationally or worldwide is not a small matter, what do you think?”
Is this the idea of wanting to export ‘raw materials’ for Bonfire Company to process, and then get items in return for the price of the ‘raw materials’?
Upon hearing this, Colin didn’t need to think much to understand the other party’s idea.
After a brief contemplation, he nodded, “That should be possible, I’ll find out more about it later…”
Compared to the vast number of ‘Gene Compensation Medicines,’ the likelihood of this cooperation was much greater.
That’s because Bonfire Company also had a significant demand for those dangerous subjects themselves.
And at the Bonfire Sacrificial Site in Other World “World Code-13”, he still needed a third-stage ‘Beast Transformation Syndrome’ to perform an upgrade.
If a cooperation was established with this regard, he wouldn’t have to risk his life to capture one, after all, a little wastage during official trade with Bonfire Company is very normal, isn’t it?
At this moment, Colin suddenly thought of something and couldn’t help but ask, “Old Master Wu, there are some things I’m not sure if I should ask?”
“Whatever question you have, just ask. It can’t all be me asking and you answering,” the old man said with a smile.
“Do you know what the end of the world in 2044 is about?”
Colin had heard about the events of 2044 more than once through various channels, but with no place to inquire, now seemed an opportune time to question a knowledgeable person.
As a powerhouse whose main abilities included methods like “precognition” and “extrapolation” for observing the future, Old Master Wu must know something.
“The year 2044, hmm? We have always been collecting information on that matter, but…”
Old Master Wu shook his head, “I don’t know.”
“What?”
Colin was stunned, not expecting the old man to be so blunt.
“Although I indeed feel that I’ve observed something, I find it very difficult to actually describe that sensation. So, I can tell you that I haven’t observed anything. But more troubling than this, are the various disasters that may happen before 2044.”
The old man said with certainty, “For us, the end of the world will occur before 2044.”
This… Colin was about to speak when he suddenly remembered the message from that “future self”: Don’t wait for 2044, the world’s end instigated by various Ancient Gods is already upon us.
The Earth now seems to be in a similar predicament; without caution, one wouldn’t need to wait for 2044 to experience the feeling of an imminent apocalypse…
Although still curious about 2044, seeing that Old Master Wu really did not know, he did not press further.
Perhaps Bonfire Company had more information on the matter.
Afterward, the two chatted like friends for a while. Although their ages seemed to differ by decades, Colin found that he could actually converse quite well with the old man, without any generational gap.
However, at that moment, Old Master Wu seemed to suddenly remember something and spoke up:
“Speaking of which, there are some things you also need to be aware of regarding the end of the world…”
“How so?” Colin asked curiously.
“In the future I’ve observed, disaster will definitely strike, though the exact timing is uncertain. It could be in the next few years or in a decade, but it won’t be later than 2044. So if you’re capable, you need to improve yourself as quickly as possible…”
“I understand…” Colin nodded, feeling an impending storm with his growing experiences.
“The severity of the disaster might exceed both of our imaginations. The collapse of civilization might occur overnight. To that end, we might initiate the ‘Spark’ project before these signs emerge, and with your situation, you’re likely to be chosen…”
“‘Spark’?”
“Essentially, it’s about leaving this world to find another place suitable for human survival…”
“This…”
Colin was taken aback, was it already so pessimistic that it hadn’t even started?
He still couldn’t quite imagine that the home he had lived in for decades might soon no longer exist.
“The specifics, I still can’t tell you, but we must be prepared for this. Given your situation, there’s a significant chance you’ll be chosen…”
Old Master Wu’s tone was much lower, seemingly pessimistic about the future.
But soon, he shook his head, his mood became restrained, and he said in an encouraging manner, “Of course, maybe the effort we put in now can change everything for the future. You never know.”
“Alright, we’ve talked long enough, I still have some things to take care of, so let’s end it here for today.”
“Okay.” Colin had no objections.
After a few hours of “heart-to-heart” talk, this first conversation also came to an end.
However, before leaving, Old Master Wu suddenly said, “By the way, regarding the task you’ll be undertaking with us, I’ll provide you with some assistance…”
The task I have to do? Haven’t I not mentioned it yet? Could it be another prediction?
Colin was taken aback, not quite sure if what the other party meant was the same as what he was thinking—investigating the “Book of Fate.”
But before he could think it over, the old man’s figure suddenly vanished, and a few waiting staff members signaled and then took Colin out of the office and into a specially arranged room.
The setup looked like a hotel, although he didn’t know whether there were any hidden listening devices or not. However, Colin didn’t care much about these things and directly sat down on the room’s large bed.
“The official demands are clear now; generally, it’s about ‘Gene Compensation Medicine’ and handing over ‘Containment Subjects’ to the company to turn into tools…”
“But while their demands are resolved, I still don’t know what to do with mine. Is it really what I’m thinking it is…”
“Speak clearly if you have something to say, darn riddler…”
Colin rubbed his forehead. Miss Bunny had given him the task of investigating the “Book of Fate.”
At the time, there hadn’t been a good opportunity, so he hadn’t brought it up, but unexpectedly, it seemed like the other party had started talking about it…
What really troubled him was whether what the other party said was actually what he was thinking.
At that moment, there was a knock on the door.
Colin composed his emotions and stood up to check the room’s door monitor. Seeing that it was Qin Chuan and others outside, he opened the door for them:
“What is it?”
“Nothing much, just to let you know, we’ll be heading back tomorrow.”
“So soon?” Colin was surprised for a moment.
He had thought they would continue to stay here for quite some time.
“Yes, and also, the organization has decided that from now on, you will be the person in charge of our area, leading the local anomalies. We have no objections to this…”
Qin Chuan was internally impressed, but he didn’t really mind, because after all, Colin’s strength was evident to all.
It would actually be a bit wasteful to have someone who could match a Ninth Level Powerhouse just overseeing a single region.
“I’m to be the person in charge?”
“Yes, of course you can refuse…”
“Let me think about it…”
Colin mused for a moment, not rushing to refuse, as this might be the “help” the old man had mentioned.
“Ah, I envy you for being able to talk to Old Master Wu for so long. It’s difficult for me even to get a meeting. If I could get some guidance, maybe I could avoid a lot of mistakes. His ways of maintaining health seem really effective…”
Hu Zheng spoke enviously, “He is one of the youngest among the few Ninth Level Personnel in the world.”
“The youngest? Old Master Wu looks to be in his nineties, and he’s the youngest? But his maintenance is indeed good. By the way, how old are the other Ninth Level Personnel?”
Colin thought about the old man’s condition and felt that he was indeed well-maintained, wise, serene, and knowledgeable about life; just like someone who knows how to live healthily, soaking goji berries and red dates in Pu’er tea.
He should ask for the health maintenance methods if he got the chance, and bring a copy back to the seniors at the welfare institute.
However, what he was now more curious about was how old the other Ninth Level Powerhouses were…
Just as the words left his mouth, he suddenly felt that the expressions of the others looking at him were a bit off.
“What’s wrong?”
“Old Master Wu is only 38 this year…”
“Ah???”
“Oh, I misspoke…”
Just when he thought how it could be possible for him to be only thirty-eight, Colin almost couldn’t help but splutter out a mouthful of water when he heard what Hu Zheng said next.
“Old Master Wu is strictly speaking 37 years old this year, not yet 38.”

chapters.title: Chapter 253 - 253 253 The Fishermans Soliloquy_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 253: Chapter 253: The Fisherman’s Soliloquy_1 Chapter 253: Chapter 253: The Fisherman’s Soliloquy_1 “Cough, cough, cough!”
Colin was choked by these words and couldn’t help coughing a few times before he confirmed after several checks that these people were not joking—
The man who looked to be in his nineties was really only in his thirties, not even forty.
And if appearance were disregarded, he was indeed the youngest “Ninth Level” powerhouse recorded in the world.
“Fate Propeller… Does this job come with so much pressure?”
Colin unconsciously looked at Hu Zheng with a bit of pity in his expression, but Hu Zheng simply shook his head nonchalantly and explained:
“That’s not the case. The side effects of Fate Propeller are the lowest among the three major pathways and even in the global context, it’s one of the practices with lesser negative effects…
“The reason why Old Master Wu looks so old is related to his experiences. He personally deals with up to a hundred incidents a year, whereas in normal circumstances, we would handle maybe a dozen or twenty regular incidents a year…
“In addition, most of the issues he deals with are global disasters, such as the one I went to in Australia, as well as the Great Northwest Land Fissure Incident, the Red Glow of the East Sea, and so on—high-risk incidents he was all involved in…
“These kinds of tasks often require risking one’s life, so even though he is very strong, compared to other Fate Propellers, he looks significantly older.
“In other words, his current state can indeed be said to be a result of exhaustion.”
Exhaustion, huh…
Upon hearing this, Colin put away his joking mindset and a sense of respect welled up inside him.
He was unfamiliar with the incidents mentioned by Hu Zheng, but he had been to the kangaroo island they previously visited. Colin would not want to face such disasters even if his strength were to double, yet there were still people who bravely stepped forward to prevent these disasters from happening.
Even though Colin knew that the authorities had designs on him and felt some discomfort about it, he also had to admit that he, like many ordinary people, lived under the protection that the authorities desperately upheld…
In this regard, what the others did truly deserved everyone’s respect…
Seeing the atmosphere grow somber, Hu Zheng did not say much more.
“By the way, I’ll also return this to you…” Qin Chuan pulled out a piece of parchment and handed it to Colin.
This time, there wasn’t much searching, but they still took away the “alternate identity” parchment along with “Future Colin’s” parchment.
“The other piece has some things that require inspection, so it might be returned to you later…”
“No problem, it doesn’t matter whether or not you give it to me.”
Anyway, it seemed like that piece of parchment was blocked from opening… Colin took his “alternate identity.”
After delivering the items and completing the organization’s mission, Qin Chuan and others left. They were worn out, having finally returned from the “Other World” and undergoing a day of interrogation.
Bang.
After Colin closed the door, he immediately lay back down on the big bed, holding his “alternate identity” parchment to take a look.
The [Mission Section] was flashing.
He skillfully opened it, completed the previous tasks, and then, familiar text once again appeared in his mind.
[Congratulations on becoming a Bonfire Employee, F Level company privileges will be initiated for you, please wait…]
“Ah, this…”
Colin pursed his lips with a strange expression. Initially, he had created the “alternate identity” in order to blend into the authorities, but now, after one incident, the last layer of pretense between them had almost been stripped away. Was there any point in maintaining the alternate identity?
“Forget it, I’ll keep it as a spare. Having an extra hundred cubic meters of storage room isn’t too bad,” he mused.
After a brief check, apart from the few hundred points rewarded for completing the tasks, the most valuable thing was a reward of a magic item lottery ticket. However, Colin didn’t rush to use the lottery ticket this time. He put away his “alternate identity” and took out his “main identity.”
This time, the mission section showed that the task of investigating the “Special Operations Department” demands had been completed.
They only gave me a tiny bit of points, no other rewards…
“Just over two thousand points.”
Colin sighed. With such meager earnings, was he supposed to appease beggars?
However, the overall profits from this whole event weren’t significant, with only the mission points being somewhat satisfactory, plus the share of points from the new round of “Choose-Your-Own-Mission Events”.
Now, he had roughly 35,000 points in rewards in his pocket…
“I’ll need a good upgrade this time. With over 30,000 points, a lot will probably go towards equipment repair, and then there’s ‘Gene Compensation Medicine’…”
“I only used one E level syringe last time; this time I’m using them all, since the point requirements aren’t high and I have enough mission vouchers. If possible, I’ll see if I can advance to D level soon to boost myself. Can’t be caught flat-footed if some doomsday scenario suddenly erupts.”
“Oh, and I should check if I can upgrade that ‘Bonfire Sacrificial Site’ in ‘World Code-13’. That thing seems to have an equipment fusion effect, which is perfect since I’m carrying a bunch of junk equipment…”
Colin had several thoughts flashing through his mind, roughly figuring out what he needed to do next.
Many pieces of equipment should have been upgraded long ago.
But last time, blinded by greed, he jumped into the “Talent” sinkhole, aiming to synthesize a high-level Talent, only to end up wasting a fortune. As a result, aside from a minor repair to his revolver, he hardly had time for anything else.
“Can’t mess with ‘Talent’ synthesis anymore, it’s a damn trap. Old colleagues always used to say how ‘Talent’ ruins lives, and now I think there’s some truth to it…”
