Colin couldn’t help muttering under his breath, then he opened the internal chat channel “Interaction Hall,” not rushing to start on equipment-related tasks right away.
After all, it’s not wise to flaunt wealth; this place isn’t his home, and doing stuff here never feels secure…
Although Colin figured his home was probably full of surveillance by now, it still felt somewhat more secure than this place.
After opening the internal group chat in the “Interaction Hall,” Colin felt inexplicably relaxed upon seeing the “long-lost” employees. His colleague-peers seemed to have an innate sense of humor for some reason.
However, while he was happy to see these colleagues’ messages, he wasn’t thrilled about some of the information mingled within.
As the “D Level staff” he had run into on the train had mentioned, there was a sense of not-too-malicious rivalry against him within the company lobby.
“Son of Doom”: [Tyrant Body: Standard Edition] Speaking of which, why does it feel like there have been a lot of newbies in the company this week? They all seem as curious as babies.
“Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦”: It does seem like that; a bunch of people came in asking all sorts of questions. There seem to be about two hundred new IDs. How come the company suddenly recruited so many people at once?
“Miss Nell’s Dog”: [Tyrant Body: Standard Edition] It’s nice, with them joining, the weekly missions have gone back to just one, at most two. It’s much more relaxed. It’s just that this bunch seems to have ulterior motives…
“Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦”: They all inquire about the company; I guess we’ve been infiltrated again, no big deal. The company isn’t panicking, so we don’t have to either. There’s another thing, @Miss Nell’s Dog, @Son of Doom, can you guys stop posting your damned Talent every time you speak? No one wants to see it, you know, nobody!
“Lifecoach Kawaii-many”: Are you talking about Talent? [Tyrant Body·Limited Edition] Not bad, eighth to complete it. When used, physical capabilities are roughly tripled or quadrupled, and with some drugs, can reach five times. Yeah, not really brag-worthy.
“Anonymous 662”: Here they come, the fishermen’s self-Q&A session is starting again…
“Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦”: Damn, the hundred and first to complete it. Missed a Purple Talent by just one spot, damn it! Annoying as hell. That damn Shunzi took so much of my money without sparing me an extra one.
“Loafing Immortal”: @Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦, dude, don’t blame Shunzi for being incompetent. If you had tried harder, would it have come to this?
“Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦”: @Loafing Immortal, you little shit, you think I don’t know about those few thousand points you scrounged from that guy? Bring your head over here!
“Son of Sadomasochism”: @Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦, [Tyrant Body: Standard Edition] What ability does your head have after transformation? Probably enhanced senses, like being able to bite through 12mm thick steel plates. But generally, you don’t use your mouth after transforming, I’m a bit of a germaphobe…
“White Cute Cuddle”: So frustrating, almost everyone has a Purple Talent except me. But seems like that thing lowers one’s IQ. My master @Lifecoach Kawaii-many doesn’t seem all that bright anymore…
“The Unyielding”: Somebody save me, please! I’ll give whoever rescues me this [Tyrant Body·Limited Edition] and Three Thousand Points. Please, I’m begging, save me…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 254 - 254 254 In the Quagmire of Natural Disasters_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 254: Chapter 254 In the Quagmire of Natural Disasters_1 Chapter 254: Chapter 254 In the Quagmire of Natural Disasters_1 “This… no wonder my reputation is so bad; as soon as I come in, it’s all curses. It’s all because of you little trolls…”
Colin browsed through it briefly, feeling utterly speechless inside. Damn it, with all these seals showing off every day, everyone else was bound to resent him by association. It would be a miracle if his reputation hadn’t suffered…
After all, only a fraction of people obtained Talents; the rest could only watch with envy, jealousy, and hate.
The catch was, these people had spent just as many Points as everyone else, if not more…
Over time, this resentment naturally concentrated on him.
“Sigh, this won’t do. I haven’t even flaunted my original ‘Beastification,’ and you’re all having a great time showing off.”
Colin shook his head and sighed, reflecting on how the youth of today lacked steady temperaments—he made up his mind to ask Miss Bunny if she could come up with a name for his “Beastification” as well.
Preferably a name in orange, to put down these inflated egos.
However, not dwelling on it too much, Colin glanced over their words again, noticing there wasn’t much more discussion about “Gene Compensation Panel 1.0″…
He guessed it probably hadn’t gone into open beta yet; most likely, he was the only one using it.
He then proceeded to check out the various inquiry posts made by the “newcomers.”
There were all sorts of questions in the posts, but most were related to Bonfire Company…
So it was pretty certain that the people who joined recently, if not one hundred percent, then ninety-nine percent of them must be members of the Special Operations Department.
“No, that’s not right; there seem to be similar operations abroad; it’s just that I don’t know which ones they are.”
All the information on the parchment had gone through a high-level translation, and even if it were only a dog reading it afterward, they wouldn’t be able to tell.
Having taken a casual glance, Colin didn’t think much more of it.
If the leaders above didn’t care about people with ulterior motives sneaking in, then he had even less reason to pay attention.
After browsing for a while longer and finding no bigger “news,” he put away the parchment and closed his eyes to rest.
…
Meanwhile, in another land shrouded in grey mist, Shana, acting as a Saintess, was leading tens of thousands of refugees to rest and settle down.
Although this large group moved with great difficulty, sometimes not even managing ten kilometers a day, they had fortunately escaped the center of the disaster.
In another ten days or half a month, they should be able to leave this natural disaster quagmire behind and return to the normal world.
“People in this area really do love their pumpernickel…” Diana, the adjutant following behind the Saintess, couldn’t help but comment.
Lately, almost every rest stop had resulted in finding a considerable amount of pumpernickel within the ruins of towns…
Apart from affection, she really couldn’t think of any other reason why people here would store so much pumpernickel.
But regardless, if it weren’t for those, probably not many would have made it to this point.
Confronted with her adjutant’s remark, the Saintess neither agreed nor denied, simply lifting her delicate yet gaunt face, her ice-blue eyes fixing on a certain direction in the mist:
“Yes, I sense there might be some ruins not far from here. Given the integrity of this area, we might find more food. I’ll go check it out; you maintain order here.
“If there’s danger, I’ll come back quickly.”
Hoping for some other food, even an earthworm cake would do… Diana prayed inwardly while bowing to respond, “Yes.”
It wasn’t that she had anything against the sour-smelling pumpernickel, but… she really had eaten too much of it!
Now she was almost afraid to look at it!
…
Pure, flawless white light raced across the desolate land, arriving at an abandoned town…
Before long, Shana stopped in front of the town, ignoring the dangers within. Instead, she reached her right hand into the left sleeve of her dress and pulled out a yellowed, tattered piece of parchment—
The mission was settled.
[Congratulations on completing this mission.]
[Task evaluation: D.]
“You have earned ‘Bonfire Points*50’.”
“You have received ‘Staled Black Bread*999’.”
“Additional task reward ‘Bonfire Points 65’.”
…
“115 points.”
Shana blinked and smiled, her bad mood somewhat improved.
The overall time for this mission had been quite long, but the rewards were indeed very generous; the points alone could be exchanged for thousands of pieces of black bread, which would probably be just enough to support their departure from the Magic Fog afflicted area.
The main reason the team’s movement had been slow nowadays was due to the famine victims being too weak from hunger; now that they would have enough food to fill their stomachs, their departure time might be reduced by more than half.
Although she had paid a certain price for this mission, it was still within an acceptable range.
However, thinking of a certain person she had encountered during the mission, she closed her eyes slightly, and a thoughtful glint emerged in her exquisite pupils:
She seemed to have sensed the aura of some Holy Relic on that person.
If nothing went wrong, that lost Holy Relic which had not been seen for many years had appeared near Helena not long ago, and now it had showed up on this person, suggesting that the two might be the same…
Only…
After pondering for a moment, Shana shook her head; it was a pity that the other party wasn’t a bad person, so she couldn’t just snatch it away.
“The previous requirements were for an item with a sufficiently powerful offensive effect, but…”
Shana couldn’t help but feel a headache—due to historical reasons, the Church of Light was forbidden by the various holy orders and kingdoms from possessing such artifacts; even if they had them, they were sealed beneath the Great Cathedral of Rest by the Gods, completely inaccessible.
To obtain an item with matching offensive capabilities, she estimated a significant cost would be involved…
Before she could continue wrestling with her headache, Shana suddenly found that an old parchment seemed to have an activated feature—[Interaction Hall].
The feature had been there before, but it was greyed out; now, it seemed accessible.
Thinking it over, to be safe, a blurred shadow clone emerged from her body, took the parchment to another spot, and set up some protections before it opened the function that had suddenly become usable on Shana’s behalf.
Upon activation, it displayed some odd bars and boxes, and aside from that, it was empty…
An invisible guidance made her understand that this device seemed to enable communication with other people who possessed it.
“Are there others out there who have this thing?”
Shana was puzzled for a moment; the parchment had been with the Church of Light for a very long history, only in the distant past, it was sealed by a godly being of great stature, but even such a being could not truly seal it away, much less destroy it.
Because as long as a Saint appeared in the “Church of Light,” it would break through all seals to appear beside the Saint, offering assistance, as it was doing now.
Without the parchment, the number of people who could have survived and made it this far was probably less than one in ten.
For this, her heart was filled with gratitude.
And through various tasks, Shana knew there was likely more than one parchment, yet she had never seen a second one appear; not only had she not seen it, but the descriptions about it from other records were the same.
In this world, it seemed to be truly unique.
At the moment, looking at the empty chat room, out of curiosity, she composed a message and sent it.
“Is anyone there?”
After a long time, the room remained deserted with only that single message and no response whatsoever.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 255 - 255 255 Where the Heart Rests_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 255: Chapter 255: Where the Heart Rests_1 Chapter 255: Chapter 255: Where the Heart Rests_1 The next day, just past nine in the morning, Colin and his companions left Base No. 4 by car, heading to another airport, ready to fly home.
Inside the car, having had breakfast, Colin leisurely sipped a cup of milk tea while looking at the news on his smartphone.
‘Recently, our city held an anti-landing military exercise….’
“So they’ve glossed over the battle on the beach from the day before yesterday already.”
Colin took a sip of his milk tea, swiped his thumb across the phone screen, and glanced at other people’s comments.
There were few comments, and most people didn’t seem to care much…
After all, due to the somewhat unique geography, there had been frequent exercises over the years; initially, people were quite surprised at sights like jet fighters, but it had since become commonplace.
About an hour later, they reached a private airport, and a modified airplane had been waiting for quite some time…
Without delay, the group boarded the camouflaged green airplane.
The interior, in contrast to the rugged exterior, was “refined” with primarily first-class seating, spacious and comfortable.
Colin casually chose a seat and noted several others that were still empty. He thought they would have to wait a bit, but the plane swiftly completed all pre-flight checks and took off at a rapid pace.
“This…is it specially arranged to take us?” Colin asked curiously.
This time taking a plane, no one told him to put his phone in airplane mode, nor instructed him not to wear headphones or anything; there were no warnings about speaking up if he felt unwell—of course, the likelihood of them feeling unwell given their physical condition was very small.
And perhaps due to some related modifications, the noise and vibration from the plane’s takeoff were incredibly quiet…
Qin Chuan nodded, “That should be the case.”
It was also his first time receiving such treatment, and he felt it novel inside, but then thinking about Colin’s strength, it all made sense.
However, what they didn’t expect was that soon after the airplane took off, four jet fighters appeared from elsewhere, closely escorting them on either side.
“Tch, this treatment…”
Qin Chuan smacked his lips, never having thought he’d experience the feeling of being escorted by fighter jets in his lifetime.
Of course, watching those armed combat planes appear and disappear within the clouds, he knew very well that all these honors stemmed from the organization’s high regard for Colin.
The other people on the plane could only enjoy this privilege by riding on Colin’s coattails…
Qin Chuan glanced at Colin, who was sitting by the window, and although he was moved, he also felt puzzled about the officials’ attitude towards Colin.
At Base No. 4, they were only told that they would form a special team under Colin’s leadership to handle anomalies, but aside from that, there were no other arrangements, nor was there any talk of surveillance.
They were simply instructed to fully agree with or assist Colin’s arrangements as long as they didn’t violate any principles.
Before they could figure out the reason for all this, after nearly two hours of flying, the airplane landed at an undisclosed location, less than thirty kilometers in a straight line from the city where Colin lived.
Colin was surprised inwardly, having had no idea that there was an airport near this area…
“Mr. Colin, are you going directly home, or do you have another destination?” asked a staff member politely, as a car waited not far behind him.
Colin first looked at Qin Chuan, “What’s the situation with our work?”
“Things should start officially around next Wednesday. If you have any other plans right now, you can leave first. I’ll go check for any updates and notify you.”
“Okay, so there’s nothing for the next few days?”
“Right, if you have any requests, just contact me on WeChat…”
“Then I’ll head back first.”
Mr. Colin had no plans to take up his post immediately. After parting with Qin Chuan and the others, he left alone in the car.
Qin Chuan, Xia Liufang, and Hu Zheng silently watched the car drive away.
“Feels like I’ve suddenly become a secretary, even though I was the first one to take up a position in this city…”
Qin Chuan couldn’t help but let out a wry smile. Then, his gaze moved past Xia Liufang to Hu Zheng, “Speaking of which, why aren’t you staying put in your area, or applying for better positions, instead of following us and hunkering down in this small place?”
Unlike them, Hu Zheng was originally the second in command for another Extraordinary One. However, this time, he had taken the initiative to transfer here—surprisingly, his application was approved.
At a time when there was a shortage of staff, it seemed a waste for a Fourth Level personnel like Hu Zheng to be here, considering Mr. Colin’s special circumstances.
“You’re not unaware of our unique situation here. I finally have a chance to latch onto a big player, so I’m seizing the opportunity to gain experience and level up. Besides, what good is a Fourth Level ‘Fate Propeller’? I might not be able to beat anyone I encounter, so I might as well blend in until I reach Sixth Level. That’s when our abilities truly begin to assert themselves…” Hu Zheng pursed his lips.
“But you need events to gain experience, right? There’s not that much happening for you to get involved with in this small place…”
Qin Chuan shook his head. The key to advancing in “Fate Propeller” was indeed to ‘blend in’, but sadly, counting the incident at the Black Forest Subway Station, his small city had only seen about five incidents in the last three years—all of them peaceful.
“This…”
Hu Zheng wanted to say “it’s hard to tell,” but after some thought, he decided not to speak.
Anyway, he felt that the key to his promotion depended entirely on Mr. Colin…
“With that look of yours, if you were a girl, you might have thrown yourself at him already,” Qin Chuan muttered, while inwardly he lamented that if he had known about latching onto a big player, he would have followed the “Fate Propeller” path as well.
Lying down while leveling up, isn’t that sweet?
“What did you say?”
“Nothing, just that you have good judgement.”
…
About half an hour later, Mr. Colin arrived at his front door, took out his key to unlock it, and pushed open the door to his home. Everything inside looked the same, but after being away for a while, the room felt somewhat smaller.
This often happened after being away on long trips, and he wasn’t particularly bothered by it…
Then, walking into his house and casually closing the door behind him, Mr. Colin first glanced at the wall clock—
December 2nd, 13:21:55.
He let his gaze wander away and took a deep breath through his nose.
“It’s been gone through once again, huh.”
Mr. Colin wasn’t surprised. He’d guessed that someone had come in about ten days ago when he disappeared in the sewer district.
And after his identity was exposed yesterday, he figured there would be some kind of arrangement.
Shaking his head and gathering his thoughts, Mr. Colin made a round of the house but didn’t spot any surveillance or listening devices.
“Some hidden corners look disturbed, so it’s possible something was installed and then removed.”
Mr. Colin simply chalked this up to official goodwill.
Now, feeling certain that nothing extra had been installed at home, he went back to his bedroom, pulled back the covers on his bed, and lay down heavily. He shifted a few times and finally let out a satisfied groan.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 256 - 256 256 Miss Bunnys Reply_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 256: Chapter 256 Miss Bunny’s Reply_1 Chapter 256: Chapter 256 Miss Bunny’s Reply_1 ‘Lying in my own bed really is the most reliable…’ he reflected inwardly. But just then, a strange smell wafted into his nose, and his expression changed instantly. He sprang out of bed, hurried to the living room window, and pushed it open.
As expected, there was a pile of bird droppings beside the window…
“Damned pigeon!” he exclaimed.
Colin took a deep breath. If only he hadn’t fed it millet back then, it wouldn’t have started coming to his place every day, not to mention waking him up early in the morning and pooping daily.
However, it was at this point that he noticed something round on the air conditioner unit by the window—
A pigeon egg?
The slick pigeon egg lay on the air conditioner unit, and if not for the two sticks, appearing out of nowhere, propping it up, the egg probably would have fallen off the building by now.
“Heh, it sure knows where to lay its eggs,” he said.
Colin looked at the two flimsily makeshift “nests” and casually picked up the egg, which still seemed fresh. Then, a flame sprouted from the palm of his hand.
In no time, the pigeon egg was roasted…
He cracked open the shell, and inside the egg was clear and transparent. Colin tasted it and found it decent; he popped it into his mouth as a way of returning the pigeon’s favor.
As for the bird droppings on the window, he’d deal with them later.
“I should upgrade my gear,” he mused.
Colin closed the window and returned to his bed, intending to ponder over an upgrade for his equipment, but then he had a sudden premonition and took out a scroll to check for new tasks…
A new message appeared on it—”You have a new task ‘Return to the Interior of Your House’ available for acceptance, do you choose to accept?”
“Is this from Lady Bunny?” Colin wondered.
He scanned the contents of the task, and after seeing a particular stamp, he intuitively accepted it.
Upon acceptance, the task was immediately completed, and the tallying began.
Then, to his surprise, he discovered several items at the foot of his bed that hadn’t been there before.
A hefty-looking black briefcase and, weighing down on the briefcase, a slick silver orb.
As soon as Colin saw them, two names appeared on his retina.
[“Leftover Item from The Seventh Box Garden World (Backup)”]
[“Nano Intellectual Core”]
“Were the things I was asked to send over on the train returned?” he pondered.
Thought after thought flashed by as Colin shifted his position and hoisted the several-hundred-pound case to inspect it. It was identical to the one he had sent.
If it weren’t for the notification that it was a backup, he probably wouldn’t have been able to tell the difference.
“Having names displayed like props suggests that the ‘Bonfire Company’ must have thoroughly researched it…” Colin deduced based on his knowledge of the company.
However, what he didn’t anticipate was that the company would return the items so swiftly.
And it was at this moment, the basketball-sized “Nano Intellectual Core” suddenly began to melt, and promptly it took the form of a cat-eared maid, standing by the side of the bed.
“Good evening, no, neural component check, time adjustment…”
“Good afternoon, Mr. Colin. Earlier, you commanded me to protect the children on the train. However, subsequently, I do not know why, but I stopped working. I apologize for not having completed your task,” the nano intellectual maid, composed of nano particles, stood respectfully to the side and spoke.
A complete shutdown? Looking at this, it seemed impossible to find out where the train had gone afterward.
But as he pondered, Colin noticed that there seemed to be a letter on the black briefcase, the contents of which were unknown.
Reaching out, he picked up the envelope and tore it open along the seam, finding inside an emblem and a sheet of letter paper.
“This is…”
Mr. Colin first glanced at the emblem.
The emblem had eight corners, and its pattern was a black circle with eight thorns distributed within. Each thorn appeared to symbolize something different, and overall, it looked less like a circle and more fittingly, a crown.
Moreover, this style seemed somewhat familiar…
“Hm? Isn’t this the thing on the ‘Virtue Knight’s’ armor outside the church?”
Colin quickly remembered where it came from.
However, it now seemed to have been repaired and looked much more exquisite.
At this moment, a line of light purple information appeared on his retina.
[Name: “Emblem of the Humility Knight”]
[Quality: Excellent.]
[Status: Perfect (Integrity 97%)]
[Energy Level: D.]
[Description: When holding it and holding one’s breath, one will enter a “Presence Diminished” state until one breathes again. It is best not to use it for more than thirty minutes at a time, and try not to exceed a total of five hours of use per day.]
[“Presence Diminished”: In this state, the presence of oneself and things associated with oneself will be significantly reduced, making it difficult to be noticed. However, one can still be attacked, and there is a probability of being discovered with every active interaction such as attacking or touching.]
[Note: When holding the item, one will tend toward striking from behind during attacks. After using it continuously for over five hours, it’s possible to be severely affected in one’s judgement.]
[Remark: Be careful when sneaking into an alternate dimension…]
…
“Is this… an item made from that ‘Virtue Knight’ outside the door?”
Colin was at first stunned, then suddenly realized, after so long, he had almost forgotten the equipment that Lady Bunny had promised him…
Now looking at the effects—no wonder that damn thing outside could stay invisible indefinitely. As a creature akin to an “undying monster,” it didn’t need to breathe, did it?
As long as it didn’t breathe, it could maintain that “Presence Diminished” state constantly.
“One can still be attacked when the presence is lost, indeed no problem. Looking at it like this, the wide-area attacks would have been effective against it. The reason I didn’t succeed is simply because the attacks weren’t enough. A big bomb with a large single amount might have been a certain kill…”
Colin rubbed his forehead and glanced again at the information about the equipment, realizing that it almost made up for the shortcomings of his deadliest attack (Bone Spur).
As for the strength of the “Presence Diminished” effect, he wasn’t worried at all…
He believed that even if he took off his clothes and ran naked outside right now, no one would notice.
After all, not just him but a whole bunch of people within the company had a deep understanding of it; even D Level staff, without special means, wouldn’t realize immediately that someone was outside, and each had suffered much because of it.
Colin himself almost had a direct crash because of this thing…
“But now, this power is mine!”
Colin felt joyful, taking a look at the corresponding negative effects. Five hours seemed like it was practically nothing.
“The items from Miss Bunny are always good; the side effects are almost nonexistent, unlike that Mister Huang He; damn, a bunch of side effects that break one’s defenses…”
Colin casually complained.
Afterward, having quickly understood the equipment, he pocketed it and then picked up the letter left by Miss Bunny.

chapters.title: Chapter 257 - 257 257 The Content of the Letter_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 257: Chapter 257 The Content of the Letter_1 Chapter 257: Chapter 257 The Content of the Letter_1 “Congratulations on your safe return. The first issue is the demands of the Special Operations Department, which I am aware of, but unfortunately, it is not possible to directly trade the Gene Compensation Medicine.”
“The rules and agreements on the related aspects are very rigid unless a number of members with the highest authority unanimously vote for it, otherwise, the corresponding clauses cannot be changed or modified.”
“However, this doesn’t mean there is no room for cooperation…”
“I could employ some methods to add or transfer a large number of tasks to them, so they would be able to acquire a substantial amount of Points to exchange for the items they need…”
“Of course, this time it can’t be done like with you, it has to follow the official procedure.”
So it’s through tasks, is Miss Bunny in charge of tasks?
Colin couldn’t help but feel curious as he read the content above, recalling a similar experience he had had in “World Code-13.”
He didn’t ponder too much and continued reading.
Second issue: Earth’s official “raw materials” export—bartering to “purchase” items made by the Company using these “raw materials.”
This was exactly as Colin had guessed; the Company agreed to the trade.
And they told Colin that they would provide him with a detailed list later to discuss the Company’s demands and rules.
“A complete seller’s market, I suppose they would agree to any condition…”
Colin shook his head. Currently, only the “Company” possessed a highly mature capability of turning oddities into artifacts, so they could command any price they wished.
However, from his own interactions, he estimated that the “Company” probably wouldn’t be too ruthless…
He continued to read on.
“If nothing unexpected happens, the Special Operations Department should give you an opportunity to approach the ‘Book of Fate’ when you promote from Fifth Level Personnel to Sixth Level Personnel.”
“Then you can ascertain its current situation. It may not be the fastest method, but relatively speaking, it is certainly a very appropriate one that won’t cause too much reaction from the ‘Book of Fate’…”
“After all, observing it requires a seemingly plausible, albeit loophole-ridden, justification rather than a direct, rash approach.”
“What you need to do is to quickly improve your professional level within the other party.”
“The payment for observing it is that I will assist in smoothing the execution of the first two demands.”
Surely, Old Master Wu might have used an ability similar to the ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’ when talking to me. I didn’t say much, but he probably knew it all and has already started making arrangements…
Colin pursed his lips, looking at the last paragraph of this part of the message with some curiosity.
Why is Lady Bunny so concerned about the status of the ‘Book of Fate’?
Even willing to use the first two items as compensation?
Unfortunately, with just this information, it’s hard to conclude anything. After finishing the issues related to the Special Operations Department, the topic of Lady Bunny’s letter shifted to himself.
“Regarding your matters, the first is that starting today, you will receive an E level Gene Compensation Medicine injection every three days to complete the promotion. Then, if possible, you should initiate the task to obtain Level C Clearance before the Spring Festival arrives next year.”
“The second matter is about the ‘Box Garden Worlds.’ There are nine ‘Box Garden Worlds’ in total, which were once places where the Company contained and stored some rather dangerous things. However, due to certain reasons, many of them have lost control, and we are trying to transform them.”
“The reason you were targeted this time may be related to your possession of the ‘Firebearer’s’ power…”
“We have confirmed that a very troublesome entity has escaped from The Seventh Box Garden World. Not long ago, through the identity of the Administrator of The Seventh Box Garden, it briefly invaded the Company’s interior and took away some things…”
“As for its recapture and containment, it is now certain that all attempts have failed.”
“From what I know about it, it won’t stay quiet for long. Perhaps within the next six months, it will cause a significant disturbance. Its instinct endows it with the ability to observe weak points within balance and use those weaknesses to induce chaos.”
“However, we are still unsure exactly how it plans to proceed. We can only speculate that there is a high probability that it will attack Earth’s ‘cognitive barrier of reality’ to overturn the state of the world, leading everything into chaos.”
“Besides that, you don’t have to worry about it coming after you again before that trouble erupts.”
Colin muttered to himself the term “cognitive barrier of reality,” understanding its meaning just from the name—
He had previously heard from Qin Chuan and others that if people in an area are aware of anomalies, the frequency of anomalies in that region would exponentially increase; conversely, if there’s no awareness, the number of anomalies would decrease…
The hidden “cognitive barrier of reality” probably played a significant role in this.
“Looking at it this way, every ordinary person is a part of the barrier…”
Colin felt a shock within, realizing that overturning this barrier would not be straightforward.
Then, he glanced again at this part of the content: “Did they deliberately choose me because I wield a certain ‘Firebearer’s’ power? But I didn’t expect that, in the end, something would still escape, and it even dared to invade the Company…”
Colin pinched his forehead, the unease about the future increasing within him. He felt an even more urgent need to become stronger.
There were a few more paragraphs at the end of this letter, although not about the year 2044 he was most curious about. It did mention that the “Nano Intellectual Mechanism” was now fully bound to him and he could use it with confidence.
The next topic addressed the situation of The Light Chaser—
In short, it was just one sentence: The Light Chaser targeted him because of the large number of Points on him.
“Is it really for such a mercenary reason?”
Colin fell silent for a few seconds.
But according to Lady Bunny, the problem wasn’t significant, as apparently, The Light Chaser was part of what “Bonfire Company” had lost; it could be seen as a “subsidiary company,” belonging to that particular “Firebearer.”
Bound by agreements, it could only offer him “help” and could not harm him by any means…
In a sense, it could even be seen as an exclusive “special measure” for him.
The only downside was that it was somewhat costly.
Additionally, it would only help him with things within its capabilities. If he wanted to challenge an Ancient God or the like, the people there would turn a deaf ear.
Of course, Lady Bunny also expressed interest in this independent “subsidiary company” and would provide him with Three Hundred Thousand Points on his next entry into “World Code-13” to see if she could lure it out for recovery by the Company’s headquarters…
But that’s just to see if it could be lured. The main focus is still on the other lost “0-9 ‘Hunger.'”
The timing for the next entry remains unchanged, still next Monday, which is three days later, December 5th.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 258 - 258 258 New Mission Star Color Art Academy _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 258: Chapter 258: New Mission: “Star Color Art Academy” _1 Chapter 258: Chapter 258: New Mission: “Star Color Art Academy” _1 “Three hundred thousand points, huh, pity it seems I can only look at them and not use them…”
Colin shook his head, regretting that such a lucrative sum had passed through his hands untouched.
He didn’t dwell on it, though, as he put away the letter and glanced at the black briefcase at his feet, which Lady Bunny had not mentioned how to deal with.
But since it was here, it most likely meant it would be handed over to the authorities without any surprises.
As for the nano intellectual maid by his side, Colin decided to keep her for his own use.
With full access to the maid’s privileges, she was even more loyal than the so-called “external incarnations” in the novels. Whatever he wanted done, she did, and her combat abilities were extremely strong too.
Back when he was “Future Colin,” neither of the two refuges dared to enter rashly without him, relying entirely on this seemingly harmless intellectual maid.
Colin planned to let her guard his home and protect the old man when the time came.
Afterward, he refocused his thoughts, opened the parchment, and immediately bought two doses of “E level Gene Compensation Medicine.” After injecting one for himself, he just waited to inject the third after an interval of three days.
“In three days, I’ll be able to start the ‘D Level Promotion Mission.’ I wonder what kind of weird stuff I’ll encounter this time. Just don’t give me a mission to go to ‘Script City’ again.”
Colin silently prayed, knowing that if he went in again, it was very likely he wouldn’t make it out.
Then, he told “Little Cat” to guard the door well before taking out his equipment one by one—the “Revolver Contrarian,” “Analytical Lens,” “Force – Repulsive Force,” “Time Stasis,” “Smiling Mountain of Corpses,” “Servant of Money,” “Widow Yukionna,” and a bunch of other miscellaneous items…
“Yukionna” seems unwilling to let me upgrade my equipment; that’s understandable, upgrade means strengthening the seal for her, and there’s really no need. “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” is a bit behind in version; to upgrade it requires more “Human Patchwork Monster,” but sadly, it’s hidden too well, and I can’t find it…”
“Servant of Money” and “Analytical Lens”: either they can’t be upgraded, or there’s no need to upgrade them…”
Looking over everything, it seems that only two Golden Cards and a revolver are eligible for an upgrade.
[“Time Stasis (Completion 29%)” — Status repair conditions: Spend three thousand points, and the duration and effect range will both be enhanced.]
[“Force – Repulsive Force (Completion 30%)” — Status repair conditions: Spend five thousand points, and the duration and effect range will both be enhanced.]
[“Revolver Contrarian (Completion 19%)” — Status repair conditions: Spend 8761 points + one Gold Mission Voucher.]
“Yes, yes, yes!”
With the command given, the completion of “Time Stasis” reached 49%, extending the time stop to 7 seconds, its direct effect reaching 30 meters, and the influence range to 45 meters!
The completion of “Force – Repulsive Force” also reached 49%, with its effective range reaching 30 meters as well…
The next repair costs for both became the same: eight thousand points + one Gold Mission Voucher.
And “Revolver Contrarian’s” completion reached 29%, adding two skills: “Expanded Magazine” and “Rapid Fire.”
“Expanded Magazine” adds an extra 18 rounds of ammo storage, even capable of storing my “Air Bullet,” while “Rapid Fire” allows the revolver to shoot 17 rounds in two seconds, although it can only be used once every thirty minutes…”
Colin nodded in satisfaction at the two newly added effects, as these skills applied to the “slay” effect when all 33 bullets hit an enemy.
Now when facing powerful enemies, he wouldn’t have to strain himself by pulling the trigger repeatedly.
“After spending over twenty thousand points and still having more than ten thousand left, the auction hadn’t had any useful equipment in the past few days. Without more ‘Mission Vouchers,’ I have no idea how to spend this excess money…”
Colin sighed.
If only points could buy “Mission Vouchers.”
He then separately bought 3 “Decree Book·Fragments” and 1 “Book of Fate: Fragment.”
Next, he opened his phone’s WeChat, found a selfie of an old man, and messaged Old Master Wu to relay Lady Bunny’s response.
Without an immediate reply from the other end, Colin prepared to continue finding Qin Chuan to have them come over and receive the inheritance of “The Seventh Box Garden World.”
“With these things, the world’s technology should be able to advance by leaps and bounds, right?”
Colin had just finished typing and was about to send the message when, not even half a second later, he suddenly saw a reply from Qin Chuan:
“Are you there?”
Huh? Colin was confused by what that reply meant and then quickly saw the message get retracted by the other party.
“Alright, Mr. Colin, I’ll have someone come by to receive them later. Also, there’s something else; are you free right now? I, Hu Zheng, and Xia Liufang just dealt with an emergency situation, but something went wrong, and now it seems like we’re trapped…”
I just got home and haven’t even been here two hours, and you guys have already managed to get yourselves into trouble?
Colin was somewhat speechless, but then, as if he sensed something, he saw a new message emerge on the parchment:
‘You have a new task “Anomaly at Star Color Art Academy” now listed in [Task Bar], please decide within one hour whether or not to accept.’
“Could this be a coincidence?”
Colin sent a message to Qin Chuan: “Are you guys currently at some Star Color Art Academy?”
Soon, the reply came back.
“Yes.”
“Then hang in there for now.”
Shaking his head helplessly, Colin put away his phone and opened the [Task Bar] to have a look at the newly issued task.
[Weekly Task — “Anomaly at Star Color Art Academy”]
“Description”: Near this location, in an old campus named “Star Color Art Vocational Academy,” some special anomaly seems to have occurred, already resulting in several people’s disappearance…
“Requirement”: Before December 3rd, investigate the situation of the anomaly in the old campus area.
“Hint”: Be cautious of any possible non-human art objects.
…
“An E-level weekly task?”
Colin stroked his chin; being an E-level regular weekly task, it probably wouldn’t be too hard.
However, considering that, aside from the first part of the “Trial Task,” he had barely encountered anything simple lately, he figured he’d better make thorough preparations just to be on the safe side…
Before long, a seemingly ordinary wheelchair buzzed through the streets at an extraordinary speed. He moved so quickly, leaving a trail of lightning sparks behind, and some drivers couldn’t react in time before he was already far ahead, leaving only a stunning and unrivaled view from behind.
“Holy shit, is that a wheelchair?”
“I’m doing 80 kilometers per hour and still got left behind?”
“Awesome, he must be going at least a hundred kilometers per hour, and he doesn’t even slow down for turns…”
“Sitting in a wheelchair isn’t for no reason; if he falls, won’t he end up with a bunch of bruises?”
“No, it’d be bruises here and there!”
…
11 minutes 27 seconds later, when the wheelchair, akin to a chariot, came to a stop, Colin had arrived in front of the old campus of “Star Color Art Academy,” which had been evacuated and quarantined by the staff of the “Special Operations Department.”
.

chapters.title: Chapter 259 - 259 259 Statue of Liberty_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 259: Chapter 259 Statue of Liberty_1 Chapter 259: Chapter 259 Statue of Liberty_1 “So, this is the Star Color Art Academy, right?”
Colin stepped down from his wheelchair and asked a staff member present, but as he got off, the wheelchair behind him suddenly melted into a puddle of silver “water,” seeping into the surface of the concrete and disappearing.
“Uh, yes, you… who are you?”
Caught off guard by Colin’s question, the staff member in his thirties was still trying to process the situation—
Over the years, they had encountered quite a few who appeared like ghosts with a flash or arrived in various special ways, but this was their first time seeing someone speed onto the scene in a wheelchair…
Moreover, in the direction from which Colin had come, one could faintly hear the sound of approaching sirens.
“I’m Colin, newly arrived to handle the current incident. Give me a copy of any reports you have on the situation.”
Colin posed his question directly, his gaze set on the old campus building in front of him. He could distinctly feel that something was off about a large building deep inside, and the air emanating from it gave a strong sense of unease.
And, the scent of Qin Chuan and his group had also disappeared inside it…
‘Intuitively, the threat level doesn’t seem high; after all, the fact that Qin Chuan and the others have survived until now suggests that the problem isn’t too serious. I should be fine even if I barge in, but to be safe, I still have to be cautious…’
Colin’s thoughts flashed by, but after a few seconds, he still hadn’t seen the report from the staff member beside him.
Only when he withdrew his gaze did he notice that several people were staring at him, looking both puzzled and unfriendly.
‘Could it be they haven’t entered my information yet?’
Colin suddenly realized the reason—he had not officially assumed his post since returning, and with only two hours passed, his identity information might not have even been synchronized locally. Therefore, the staff members on site didn’t know much about him.
In fact, it was indeed as he guessed. The staff members were eyeing Colin, wary of this young man who had appeared out of nowhere.
“How can you prove…”
The staff member hadn’t finished speaking when suddenly the walkie-talkie on his shoulder crackled to life, instructing him to immediately cooperate with all of Colin’s actions.
A few moments later, he handed Colin several documents he had just received.
“Besides mentioning that it’s best to dispatch Fourth Level or higher personnel for the abnormal level, it doesn’t seem like there’s much useful information…”
Colin skimmed through the documents quickly and gently shook his head. They stated that roughly two days ago, numerous students had disappeared mysteriously after entering the old campus district, after which police officers were called in, perceived something amiss, and promptly reported it to their superiors.
Subsequently, a Special Operations Department squad consisting of two E-level personnel entered and then got trapped inside…
Qin Chuan and the others got wind of the incident not long before and thought that with Hu Zheng, a Fourth Level member in their team, handling it shouldn’t be too difficult, but unexpectedly, they also ended up trapped, with no word from them since…
‘Probably, through something like ‘Luck’ or other means, he managed to forcefully send me a call. He really knows how to find someone.’
Colin had a rough guess and handed back the documents to the staff member: “Alright, continue maintaining order at the site; I’ll go in and have a look.”
Before the staff member could ask if he needed any assistance, Colin leaned back and, in that process, a mysterious liquid surged up from the ground, solidifying into a silver wheelchair that caught him steadily, then rolled towards the campus.
It accelerated to over a hundred miles per hour in less than a second, vanishing from everyone’s sight and leaving them dumbfounded.
It was at this moment that the traffic police finally arrived belatedly on their motorcycles…
…
Before long, Colin in his wheelchair reached the specific site of the incident: a teaching building with a substantial footprint but obviously abandoned for a considerable amount of time, laid out in the shape of a “well.”
The traces of Qin Chuan and his group ended in front of the teaching building…
Under the sunlight outside, at first glance, there seemed to be nothing special about it.
But after looking at it for a bit longer, Colin felt that the lighting of the teaching building was somewhat off; although it looked normal, it somehow made one feel ominously dim and dizzy.
At that moment, the armrest of the wheelchair sprouted the head of a cat-eared maid: “Detected a special field formed by pollution levels between Third and Fourth Level; the source of the pollution has not been determined…”
“Uh.”
Colin looked at the head on the armrest and felt that this way of appearing was a bit too advanced for him, but he didn’t give it much thought, roughly grasping the concept of the Fourth Level contamination mentioned by the other party.
That level probably corresponded to the “E level” standard, which was a fairly typical difficulty for an E level task…
In Colin’s eyes, the problems were not too significant.
“However, these levels are so chaotic now,” he remarked. “The ‘Box Garden World’ has one set of standards, Earth another, the company its own, and the Other World yet another…
Colin stood up from his wheelchair, thinking that he should unify all the standards if he had the chance.
Otherwise, when people talked about threat levels, he would have to do some calculations before he could understand.
Without much thought, Colin walked into the eerie old school building, while the Nano Intellectual Mechanisms dispersed around him like a gray mist, ready to respond to any trouble at a moment’s notice.
It was just as he stepped through the entrance that Colin first noticed a sudden brightness. The light within the old campus painted a picture that was quite off for his eyes—the dark areas were particularly dark and the light areas extremely bright, with the light twisted and colorful, making him feel dizzy…
Following that, his body seemed to become lighter…
No, more precisely, there was something wrong with the gravity inside the building. All sorts of objects were floating around: white broken statues, torn paintings, wooden frames, paintbrushes stiff with dried paint, and so on…
Most of these objects were common items found in an art academy.
Colin looked back and saw not far from where the entrance was another building with a “well” shape identical to this one, with the only difference being that the other building was reversed, like a reflection in a mirror.
“What’s the situation on that side?”
Colin asked the Little Cat Intellectual Mechanism maid, and then the gray mist around him formed some words:
“Exiting from that side, it seems one would appear in other parts of the school. This is a special spatial area that cannot be left through normal means. However, with your methods, you can tear a rift to leave…”
“Is that so?”
Colin brought out “Slave to Money” and summoned a Good Brother, instructing him to cross the doorway. After a few steps, the Money Slave vanished directly.
The next moment, Colin, via his connection with the “Good Brother,” could feel that it seemed to have appeared somewhere else in the school.
But before he could determine the precise location, the connection with the “Good Brother” disappeared…
“Taken out that quickly?”
Colin shook his head, put away the item, and hesitated whether he should try it himself.
As he contemplated, the sound of footsteps or something falling suddenly came from a corner of the “well” shaped building. Colin’s gaze immediately turned in that direction, and on the third floor of the teaching building, he could vaguely sense traces of human activity.
Simultaneously, the Nano Intellectual Mechanisms provided information: “Life signals detected…”
“Then let’s take a look.”
Without delay, Colin stepped forward towards that direction.
Although gravity seemed to be almost nonexistent around him, and he could easily jump to the third floor if he wished, he decided it was better to take the stairs as usual.
The passageway was eerily quiet, and the distorted, colorful scattered light accentuated a kind of intangible eeriness.
However, just as Colin reached the turning on the second floor, whether by coincidence or for some other reason, a white plaster-made Statue of Liberty, but only the upper half of the body, floated behind Colin.
Then, taking advantage of Colin’s apparent inattention, the human-sized plaster Statue of Liberty silently raised the torch of freedom in its hand and viciously smashed it down towards Colin’s head.
The air even produced a “whoosh” sound from the impact.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 260 - 260 260 Survivors in the Academy_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 260: Chapter 260 Survivors in the Academy_1 Chapter 260: Chapter 260 Survivors in the Academy_1 “Bang!”
Just as the plaster torch touched the silvery-gray mist near Colin, it crumbled into pieces instantly.
“That’s interesting… I didn’t even notice anything was wrong with it before it attacked. There’s something quite unusual about this strangeness…”
Colin tilted his head, pondering the scene that had just occurred, without feeling any sense of danger.
Because that thing posed a very low threat to him, even if he stood still, it might not be able to penetrate his defenses.
Moreover, what made him feel uneasy wasn’t so much the attack from the statue, but rather the brilliant, multicolored dazzle of light that emanated from the Statue of Liberty as it shattered.
This dazzle of light disappeared in less than a second…
But whether it was an illusion or not, when he looked directly at that resplendent light, he always felt as if his life span might have experienced a “-1S,” “-1S” situation.
“Upon analysis, the light seems to have the special ability to absorb the vitality of living beings. It is recommended not to destroy it again to avoid any direct contact…” the Nano Intellectual Mechanism responded.
Can it suck away life? Is this what the mission warning meant by cautioning against non-human art?
Colin nodded thoughtfully, “Let’s do as you suggest.”
Then, he continued toward the third floor, along the way, he saw quite a few eerie statues drifting towards him, only to be repelled before they could get close to Colin.
And unless they got within a certain distance, they seemed not to launch an attack.
“They don’t seem to have a very strong desire to attack…”
Colin guessed it might be because he hadn’t actually triggered anything, or perhaps the time had not come; otherwise, these things probably wouldn’t be so docile.
Before long, he arrived on the third floor. Upon reaching this location, his enhanced senses could clearly detect the presence of several survivors behind what seemed to be the door to a multimedia office.
“Knock, knock, knock.”
Colin knocked on the sturdy door. “Is anyone there?”
As he spoke, he could clearly feel that the people inside seemed to hold their breath.
“I don’t need to come in, just have someone tell me about the situation here. Qin Chuan, um, Xia Liufang, have you seen them? A girl who looks spirited and like a heroine…”
He had intended to use Qin Chuan as an example, but Colin thought it over and figured that if these people were to arrive, Xia Liufang would probably attract more attention.
Unfortunately, there was no response from inside to Colin’s words.
“Being cautious is good, it’s just a pity that it’s misplaced here.”
Colin waved his hand, and a swath of silvery-gray mist surged up, corroding the components of the door lock. Then, he politely reached for the doorknob, preparing to open it, only to find that some force was preventing the door from opening.
“Some kind of seal?”
He frowned, let go of the doorknob, and with flames bursting from his right leg…
Following that,
“Boom!”
The mysterious force on the door melted on contact with the flames and was instantly kicked away.
At the same time, several yellow talisman papers fell from behind the door, appearing to be what had blocked Colin’s entrance.
However, before he could take a closer look, a man holding a shotgun, ready to fire, exclaimed:
“I’ll fight you to the end!”
The shotgun in his hand was peculiar, wrapped in layers of yellow talismans, but before he could pull the trigger, he found a mass of silver around his fingers enveloping his palm, and his entire body stiffened, immobilized…
Unbeknownst to him, the Nano Intellectual Mechanism Little Cat had already taken complete control of him, even filling his entire body.
“What’s all this anger about?”
Colin’s gaze passed over this “Special Operations Department” Extraordinary One and looked inside. He could see six students from the Star Color Art Academy, two males and four females, all huddled in the corner, looking at him with faces as frightened as little chicks.
His eyes swept over them, and from their pale, emaciated faces and scared eyes, it was clear that they were not in good shape.
And in the multimedia office, there was a smell of excrement…
Clearly, these people had been hiding here for more than a day or two.
“Have you calmed down now?”
Colin withdrew his gaze and looked at the Extraordinary One, who was hugging a shotgun and controlled by a Nano Intellectual Mechanism.
Not until then did he confirm that Colin was not an enemy, managing a difficult nod, “It’s okay now.”
“Good.”
Colin did not release the control over the other person, “Were you the first one to come in?”
“Yes.”
“Did you see the person I mentioned?”
“An hour ago, I heard some noises. They could be the ones who came to support later, but I didn’t dare to look, worrying that the enemy would find my position…”
“Enemy?”
“I’m not sure. If you’re active outside for a while, you could get attacked by something inexplicable…”
“Alright, then do you know where those people went?” Colin continued to inquire.
“Most likely they went to the studio on the seventh floor of Building B; that could be the source. But I haven’t seen them come out later. Our current location is D Building…”
“Building B, seventh floor.”
Colin’s vision drifted past a mass of floating objects and looked across, where he could see the top floor’s seventh level, seemingly one particularly large classroom, which indeed gave him an uneasy feeling.
But whether that was actually the source was not so certain…
At that moment, however,
A line of information appeared on his retina: [“Weekly Mission—’Anomaly in the Star Color Art Academy’ has been completed.”]
“Huh? That completes the investigation?”
Colin was taken aback and then saw another line of information emerge.
[If you leave now and proceed with mission clearance, you will receive “Bonfire Points*250” + grade rewards.]
[Continue to the next stage of the mission: “Containing the embryonic embryos in the classroom within seven days,” you will receive an additional guarantee of “Bonfire Points*800” and one “Silver Task Certificate.”]
[Note: The next stage of the mission has certain risks. It is recommended to carry “Excellent (Purple)” grade items with sufficient attack strength or transfer the mission to a “D Level” employee.]
“I can leave now?”
Colin’s expression was odd, only then realizing just how easy a regular weekly mission could be.
Of course, he didn’t hesitate, immediately accepting the next stage of the mission.
Mission Vouchers were hard to come by nowadays; the more he could get, the better.
Even if he didn’t consider the rewards, he had to think about Qin Chuan and the others…
After all, it wouldn’t do if all his subordinates died before he even started his new position.
At once, he gathered his thoughts, Colin released the official Extraordinary One from his bonds and headed towards the studio on the seventh floor of Building B, casually calling out over his shoulder:
“You guys come with me.”
“Us, together? Where to? Wait a minute!”
The official Extraordinary One behind him, whose name he still didn’t know, was stunned and hastily intervened, “The anomaly above hasn’t been investigated yet, and all those who went in haven’t come back out. I suggest waiting for stronger official Extraordinary Ones to arrive…”
Since Colin was not part of the three major paths, he couldn’t sense Colin’s strength, just assuming the other to be around Fourth Level.
But Fourth Level was simply not enough!
“Anomaly?”
Upon hearing this, Colin lifted his right hand above his head, extending an index finger. A burst of flame ignited on the finger, rapidly expanding until its diameter exceeded three meters in an instant. Under the scorching light, all the distorted beams returned to normal.
As he walked forward without looking back, he said:
“I am what you call ‘stronger.’
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 261 - 261 261 The Door to the Seventh Floor_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 261: Chapter 261: The Door to the Seventh Floor_1 Chapter 261: Chapter 261: The Door to the Seventh Floor_1 Boom…
The frightening firelight hovered in the air outside the hallway, letting out a howling sound…
A scorching heat rushed toward them, yet to the surprise of the people behind Colin, they hadn’t expected such a large flame less than two meters away from them to make it intolerably hot…
However, under the cover of the firelight, not only did they not feel too hot, but they could also sense a strange warmth wrapping around them, significantly lessening their fatigue and even improving their mental state considerably.
“This fire…”
An unnamed Extraordinary One felt the changes in himself and was greatly astonished.
He looked at Colin’s back, wanting to ask who the other was, but before he could speak, Colin’s voice came:
“Something is coming, follow me quickly if you don’t want to die.”
Colin’s gaze swept the surroundings; he could see many objects floating in the air, seemingly being drawn towards him.
This sensation was as if there was some special gravity on him…
He suddenly stoked a large fire, not really out of goodwill for the people behind him, but because he felt targeted by some bizarre entity.
“There was no movement just now, until I determined the specific location of the other party, then it reacted? So, it has also noticed me?”
Colin maintained the burning of the flame, returning the world in front of him to reality to avoid being secretly influenced by the other party and getting caught unawares.
The stone statues floating in the air were handled by the Nano Intellectual Mechanism.
However, at that moment, footsteps came from downstairs, heavy and deep, more like the muffled sound of somewhat soft stones colliding with marble.
“It’s those plaster statues!”
The Extraordinary One behind him changed color at the sound.
And then, a dozen stone statues wielding various weapons rushed up, many of which Colin found somewhat familiar, but he could not recall specifically who they were meant to be, only that they were foreign gods or historical figures.
At the forefront, one of the statues had a hanging tag—
Graduation Design Theme of 20XX: Greek Gods.
“Gods or not, aren’t these a bit too much for the eyes?”
Colin looked at the statues with minimal or no clothing at all, feeling it was somewhat indecent.
But without dwelling on it, he raised his hand, aiming at those “Greek Gods.”
“Don’t, don’t shatter them!”
The Extraordinary One behind him saw Colin’s movements, seemed to recall something, and wanted to stop him, but before he could act, Colin’s revolver started to spit sparks.
“Bang bang bang bang—”
A dozen gunshots sounded, leaving him with a stunned expression; what kind of revolver fired like a machine gun?
Each bullet, adorned with flame, accurately shattered a statue, clearing the path ahead and bringing about a “Twilight of the Gods.”
From the broken deity statues, eerie and twisted rainbow light leaked out…
Colin could feel his “life” seemed to be getting drained, but before anything happened, the flames attached to the bullets completely incinerated it.
The shattered statues did not fall to the ground but stayed levitating, continuing to drift closer to Colin.
“These statues, once shattered, release something that weakens us…” The Extraordinary One found his chance to speak and hurriedly began to explain.
“More precisely, it’s not about becoming weaker, but about absorbing our ‘life force.’ However, it’s not a big deal, just follow me…”
Colin took some bullets from his pocket, reloading as he spoke, and continued moving forward.
Since the flame can suppress these contaminations, things shouldn’t be too troublesome…
“The power of a ‘Firebearer’ really is impressive, seeming to have a suppressive effect on all kinds of abnormal and bizarre phenomena. I wonder when I will truly possess this power.”
With a silent sigh in his heart, Colin longed for the scene he had witnessed by the seaside.
However, he didn’t linger on the thought for too long. He led several people towards the seventh floor, ascending two more stories. Along the way, another classroom unleashed a number of plaster statues.
Only, compared to the first time, the statues that rushed out this time were all anime or game characters, such as Shirogane Mashiro, Rem, Violet, Jerusalem, Silvie, Akiyama Eri, Kasugano Sora, Renka, Warden Karin…
Colin didn’t recognize any of these.
After smashing another group of students’ graduation projects, they reached the corner of the seventh floor.
There hung a painting…
A painting from a fairy tale, of White Snow Princess receiving a red apple. When Colin arrived there, the princess in the painting turned her head to look at Colin and his companions, revealing a sinister and chilling smile.
Afterward, the oil painting bulged outwards, with a pair of hands reaching out from the canvas, offering the red apple from fantasy to reality as if wanting to hand it to Colin.
When this red apple appeared, twisted and dazzling colors exploded in front of them…
“If it weren’t for the distinctly different nature of the power, I would have thought it was the influence of the Red Moon causing this kind of animation.”
Colin felt his life dropping by “-1S-1S” again and without any hesitation, he grasped the revolver with his left hand, extending his arm forward, his index finger directly pointing at the canvas.
Boom!
Flame surged, following Colin’s direction, engulfing everything before them in an instant like a flood of flames.
In the midst of the surging firelight, the White Snow Princess in the painting let out a wail like a banshee, with twists of light bursting forth, but in a few seconds, the sound stopped, and everything was consumed in the flames.
Having promptly dealt with the anomaly in front, Colin turned back to glance at that official Extraordinary One and a few people behind him…
Compared to himself, they were much more affected, visibly weakened, with one girl even showing signs of aging.
However, if they would make it back safely, they’d probably recover after a year and a half.
“Let’s continue.”
Colin lifted his foot and stepped forward, after rounding this last corner, he arrived at the seventh floor. Without spending too much time looking around, he headed straight for the final studio.
He was eager to see what kind of monster was really in there.
Behind him, the official Extraordinary One, who seemed to have aged a few more years, thought of Colin’s methods and couldn’t help but inwardly exclaim:
“So powerful…”
What troubled them most in this accursed place weren’t the statues, but the twisted lights that seemed to be draining their life force at every moment. The first team to enter here had aged into dust because they didn’t know about these effects…
It was only after a while that they began to notice these things, but by then it was already too late.
Then came Qin Chuan and his group, who arrived before Colin. He had intended to wait until the other party passed the third floor to confirm the situation before giving them a heads-up.
But somehow, they managed to rush straight to the source on the seventh floor and then never came out.
Shaking his head, the Warden didn’t ponder further. He glanced at Colin ahead of him, then turned to the few students closely following him and said, “Keep up, everyone. If all goes well, we should be able to get out this time.”
Before long, Colin and the others arrived outside the studio, with its doors tightly shut.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 262 - 262 262 Celestial Observation Society_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 262: Chapter 262 “Celestial Observation Society”_1 Chapter 262: Chapter 262 “Celestial Observation Society”_1 “The task, the smell, everything points here, it must be right…”
Colin shoved his hands in his pockets, raised his leg, and a huge flame attached to his leg kicked straight towards the door.
Boom!
The door exploded instantly with that kick.
A swirl of dazzling, distorted colors burst forth but was quickly devoured by a more ferocious blaze; as flames poured ruthlessly into the studio, the scene inside was laid bare for all to see.
“Where are they?”
Colin didn’t find Qin Chuan and the others, but did see many easels, each holding what seemed to be unfinished oil paintings.
However, the next second, as if sensing something, Colin looked at one of the oil paintings.
In that painting, it was Qin Chuan and his companions who seemed to be chased by something, fleeing in terror; the painting was very lifelike, or perhaps… they were really trapped inside.
“They got put into a painting?”
Colin was astonished, but without giving it much thought, he suddenly felt something and turned his head to look deeper into the studio, where a two-meter-tall, gigantic oil painting hung on the wall.
The painting depicted a radiant starry sky, with countless stars emitting mad colors, looking extremely distorted and bizarre…
At that moment, below the canvas, a glowing figure of a woman slowly stood up.
“You are, you also want to, destroy my painting, don’t you? You….”
“You people… all deserve to die!”
“Die, all of you! Become my pigments! Become my… artwork! Ha-ha, ha-ha… he-he-he…”
The woman’s voice and tone became increasingly disordered, and by the end, she devolved into manic laughter.
When she turned to look at Colin, they finally saw her appearance; on her pale face, her eyes were gone, but the eye sockets were not empty because a continuously flowing paint with distorted colors spilled out of them…
From this woman, all Colin could sense was pure madness.
“There seems to be no need for salvation…”
Colin could even see that what flowed through the vessels beneath the woman’s skin was not blood, but an unknown liquid radiating dazzling light…
He drew his handgun, intending to execute a swift and ruthless draw-and-fire maneuver.
But at that moment, a young man abruptly approached from behind: “Chen Wei, Wei, is that you?!”
Hearing his words, the woman’s body shuddered and stopped, the twisted, exaggerated smile freezing.
“It’s really you! I’ve been looking for you for so long!”
The frail-looking young man showed a surprised delight: “We’ve come to save you, don’t be afraid…”
“Wang Hai… Wang Haiwei?” the woman muttered.
“Yes, it’s me! I’m here to save you! I’ve been searching for you since you went missing! Let’s go back together, it doesn’t matter to me what you look like…”
Tears streamed down the young man’s face, who had known something was wrong here all along but still braved his way inside, all to find his beloved girlfriend and fiancée.
After enduring so much hardship, he finally saw her.
“…Couldn’t he really be moved by her?”
Watching the scene unfold, Colin wore a puzzled expression; was this what they called the power of love?
Having always been out of touch with such matters, Colin found it somewhat surreal, yet also pondered if it could really be possible?
However, it was then that he suddenly had a foreboding feeling…
“Hee-hee-hee… Haiwei… Haiwei… my love… you will, surely you will help me finish this beautiful piece, won’t you…”
“Yes! I will do anything for you, so let’s go back first…”
“No, no, I still, I still need some more pigments…”
“Pigments?”
The young man was puzzled and confused, but before he could figure it out, Colin suddenly kicked him away to one side.
In the next instant, the woman who had been tens of meters away dragged a stream of bright, twisted colors at breakneck speed, like a shooting star through the flames, passing between the two men…
Yet, just when Colin thought she would pass straight through, the woman’s figure stopped unnaturally in midair, turned her head, looked at Colin with a sinister smile, stretched out her arms towards him, as if wanting to absorb him into her body…
What baffled her, even in her mania, was that Colin, too, had a smile on his face…
The next second, Colin disappeared before her eyes, and a searing, terrifying pain erupted from her abdomen.
The woman with the multicolored blood looked down to see a pitch-black Bone Spur riddled with cracks, plunged into her abdomen at some unknown time.
“Ah!!!”
The terrible pain overpowered her madness at that moment, and she fell to the ground, writhing in agony.
But after a few seconds, the alien colors on her body faded, putrid, foul-smelling black liquid oozed from her, her body swelled and bloated, and before long, she became still.
“Wei! Stop it! Let me go!”
The young man who was kicked aside finally came to his senses, hurriedly trying to rush over, but this time, another person held him back.
Pinning too many hopes on love proved unwise… Colin wondered whether the young man was truly foolish or pretending to be. After taking care of the woman, he bent down to pick up the Bone Spur, his gaze then turning towards the enormous painting in the depths of the studio.
As the anomaly had not yet dissipated, it suggested that the woman most likely was not the direct source of the contamination…
Without much hesitation, he stepped forward, heading straight towards it.
As he neared the painting, an indescribable sense of crisis grew stronger…
Just as he got within five meters of it, Colin suddenly realized something, sniffed the air, paused, turned to look at a corner of the studio, and noticed a painting blended with a multitude of vivid colors standing there.

chapters.title: Chapter 263 - 263 262 Celestial Observation Society_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 263: Chapter 262 “Celestial Observation Society”_2 Chapter 263: Chapter 262 “Celestial Observation Society”_2 Compared to other paintings, it looked like a bunch of paint had been randomly smeared on it, with nothing special about it.
However…
“There’s something off about this paint…”
Colin detected some issues through his sense of smell.
Just as he was about to go over there and take a look, an image suddenly popped into his mind—
In the twisted cosmic painting not far from him, a nauseatingly brilliant halo burst forth, and within the halo, one could vaguely make out the figure of a woman. In an extremely short amount of time, it completely enveloped him, and then…
Clang.
A new oil painting fell to the ground, depicting none other than Colin himself.
“As expected, the big painting is indeed a trap, and the woman isn’t dead.”
As the corresponding thought flashed past, flames suddenly erupted from Colin’s body, covering him entirely, and then he lifted his hand, palm facing the dazzling halo that had just spewed forth from the cosmic painting canvas…
“Scram.”
As his words fell, a terrifying Repulsion Burst erupted, crushing the brilliant and colorful halo in an overwhelming fashion.
After upgrading “Force Repulsion,” Colin could use it to a higher degree, already able to control the range and strength of the Repulsion Burst relatively freely.
Having repelled the attack from the painting, Colin quickly headed toward the corner.
It was at this moment that the colors in the corner painting writhed and twisted, condensing into a cold, prismatic eye.
Innumerable colors, worthy of being called optical pollution, gathered in front of it, seemingly ready to launch some attack.
Witnessing this scene, Colin not only had no intention of dodging but instead accelerated further, arriving in front of the eye in a very short time.
Facing the dazzling brilliance gathering in its eye, Colin reached out his hand, holding a Bone Spur, and without any mercy, stabbed down at the eye, piercing the painted eye on the canvas.
Clang!
The Bone Spur met resistance.
This seemingly fragile eye, however, possessed an unexpected hardness.
“No wonder it requires a strong enough offensive item; otherwise, even if an ordinary person finds this, they may not be able to break through the defense. To hesitate further would perhaps mean being ground to death by it.”
Colin’s arm exerted force suddenly.
Pop.
With a crisp sound, the Bone Spur pierced the eyeball…
Almost instantly, the eye exploded, and the colorful paint on the canvas melted afterward, trickling down like pus.
Sounds of pitter-patter, objects falling, were heard outside the studio…
Gravity seemed to return to normal.
At the same time, subtitles appeared on Colin’s retina.
Mission completed.
“This…I finished it this easily?”
Colin couldn’t quite believe it. He took out the Parchment and saw that it was indeed completed.
A transparent vortex appeared before him, sucking in the bizarre paint along with the canvas…
[In this event, your rating is: A.]
[You have completed this event with unparalleled speed.]
[The following are your rewards for this event— “Bonfire Points*1200,” “Silver Task Certificate*2”.]
[Do you choose to return (back to the starting point)?]
“Not bad, two Mission Vouchers. But as for returning, I don’t seem to need it for this mission. Hm, there’s one advantage to being publicly known; I don’t have to sneak around when doing things.”
Colin stowed away the Parchment, refused the return, and as he turned, he just caught sight of Qin Chuan and the others escaping from the painting.
Their status was obviously a bit weak, but the problem wasn’t too big.
At the same time, transparent vortices appeared on other canvases, with more people being liberated, until no one was left, and then the canvases began to melt…
The giant cosmic painting also melted, but what fell out wasn’t people, but a colorful female skeleton.
“Did the company help out?”
Colin pondered, raised his hand to let the light spread out, enshrouding more people to prevent them from fainting on the spot.
Then he glanced at the skeleton. Intuitively, this seemed to be the woman’s body, but because the contamination source had been contained, it had lost its activity.
As if sensing something at that moment, Colin turned his head and saw another man being pinned to the ground by official Extraordinary Ones. He was staring at Colin with a gaze filled with unabashed hatred.
‘This…your girlfriend died a long time ago, and she wasn’t killed by me. Hating me is useless, and with that level of madness, even the company might not be able to save her.’
Colin shook his head inwardly, feeling somewhat speechless about the man’s misdirected anger.
“Mr. Colin!” When Qin Chuan and the others saw the fiery Colin, their eyes lit up, and they immediately approached.
Without any pleasantries, Colin spoke of the recent events, and then asked, “How do you usually deal with something like this?”
“You don’t have to worry about this part. We have people who will handle their memories specifically. If it’s a parent or someone close, it might be a bit difficult, but if it’s girlfriends and relationships that aren’t too deep, it will be much easier to handle.”
“Okay then.”
Without dwelling on it further, Colin pocketed the Parchment and said, “Also, investigate the cause of the abnormal events here, and find out more about that woman…
“Lastly, thoroughly examine this school.”
Though the mission was complete, there were still many puzzles, such as the origin of those paints, why some people had been trapped here for far longer than just a few days, with reports only emerging recently.
Colin felt that the events here were not like a mere accident.
“Alright, I’ll let you know if there’s any news,” Qin Chuan nodded.
“Mhm.”
Colin nodded, and after making sure there was nothing else to deal with at the scene, he sped back to his residence in his wheelchair.

chapters.title: Chapter 264 - 264 262 Celestial Observation Society _3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 264: Chapter 262 “Celestial Observation Society” _3 Chapter 264: Chapter 262 “Celestial Observation Society” _3 This time, to avoid drawing attention, Colin used the “Emblem of the Humility Knight” and held his breath all the way home.
“This thing, I’m not sure how useful it is in actual combat, but it’s certainly handy for everyday use.”
Colin put away the badge, took a deep breath, then lay back on the bed, resting while pondering other matters.
“Old Master Wu hasn’t replied yet, so after returning from ‘World Code-13’ on Monday, the day after, it will be just right to inject the third potion and start the next promotion mission…”
“I already have one D Level Potion, the remaining two exchanges shouldn’t be difficult, with official help at that time, promotion will be even easier. If all goes well, I might have a chance to be promoted to C Level in a month…”
“With Lady Bunny’s protection and escort, there shouldn’t be a problem…”
As thoughts flashed through his mind, just as Colin was getting his things in order and preparing to rest, a cellphone ringtone sounded.
He reached for his phone and took a look; it was a message from Qin Chuan.
To be more precise, it was a detailed report on the background of the event.
About ten minutes later, having understood the contents, Colin unraveled quite a few doubts—this school really wasn’t very proper.
At the time of the incident, the school’s leadership “happened” to be abroad, but subsequent investigations revealed they were related to a power overseas named the “Celestial Observation Society.”
It seemed they had been covertly cultivating something for many years, their methods secret and unnoticed.
But recently, there had been some accidents…
