According to the investigation, not long ago, a girl under surveillance accidentally came into contact with some bizarre paint that “escaped” from the principal’s office and immediately turned into an obsessed slave, frantically trying to depict a certain starry sky scene.
By the time the school’s leadership discovered the incident, it was too late to cover up. The authorities had taken notice, so their choice was clear—flee.
“This… what an undeserved disaster.”
Colin sighed. Truly ordinary people are fragile and powerless in the face of the abnormal.
Then, he looked up the “Celestial Observation Society” and found that these people… seemed to be listed as targets to be expelled or even eradicated in most countries.
At first, it was just an ordinary civilian organization, but from who knows when, some of them received overwhelming yet mind-corrupting powers from above the stars, and everything changed.
They held more and more bloody rituals, praying to the stars, seeking twisted power.
But to say they were entirely a cult…
Was not entirely the case, because these people also dealt with abnormal events and had some inexplicable sense of mission, believing themselves to be the saviors of the world.
“Saviors, huh? These people really should let the ‘Human Patchwork Monster’ summon them to the Other World for a lesson…”
Colin shook his head, not dwelling on these matters anymore. Since the regional issue was resolved and the other party had fled, it was unlikely they would have much interaction in the short term.
Soon after, Colin closed his eyes and began his rest.
For the next two days, the city was peaceful, and he had a rare chance to experience a couple of days of leisure before preparing for Monday’s relief work, and then quietly waiting.
…
At the same time, Wang Haiwei returned home, feeling extremely dejected, as he had received the news that his girlfriend, Chen Wei, had died in a car accident.
“Why, why did you have to leave me…”
The more he recalled his girlfriend’s voice and smile, the more he felt despair and couldn’t help but think of going to the rooftop.
But it was at that moment…
In a shadow he didn’t notice, the eerie shape of a rat’s shadow flitted by and slipped into his own shadow.
Immediately after, a voice suddenly emerged in his mind.
“Ding.”
“System activated.”
“Do you confirm you want to accept the System’s offer and start a new life?”
“Note: You will learn the real secret behind your girlfriend’s death, and you will also have the power to bring her back to life!”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 265 - 265 263 A Gift from the Darkness._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 265: Chapter 263 “A ‘Gift’ from the Darkness.”_1 Chapter 265: Chapter 263 “A ‘Gift’ from the Darkness.”_1 “What is this?!”
Wang Haiwen was first startled, sensing some information floating in his mind:
“System? Wait, what do you mean by that? Didn’t Chen Wei die in a car accident?”
As his words fell, more information continued to emerge in his head.
This information was special, as he perceived it, it was as if he directly understood all the content within through “hearing,” “seeing,” “smelling,” and so on.
“Not at all, her death was no accident, but caused by someone else…”
The information ended there, and Wang Haiwen’s face twisted into a ferocious snarl, bellowing, “Caused by someone else? What does that mean! Tell me now!”
“Only if you accept the ‘system’ can I tell you, not before.”
Seeing this, Wang Haiwen felt anger rising but then suddenly fell silent, “No matter what, she’s already dead… Are you saying there’s a way for me to see her again, to bring her back to life?”
“Yes, yes,” the information stored in his mind seemed to have a bewitching quality, making one want to agree involuntarily.
“What are your intentions? And why have you sought me out?”
“Doomsday is approaching, and the world needs more saviors…”
“Doomsday?” Wang Haiwen was taken aback.
“Yes, the world of the future is about to collapse, numerous disasters will erupt, and you have been chosen as one of the members.”
“Are you sure you have no other motives?”
“I am merely a ‘system’ anthropomorphic self-help response program, I only answer what you ask, what bad intentions could I have?”
Hearing this, Wang Haiwen fell silent, and finally, he asked one more question, “Can you really resurrect her?”
He sensed that option in his mind, he had a premonition that once he made the choice, he might step into an abyss.
It didn’t matter if he fell into the abyss, but what if the true target of this “system” was actually Chen Wei and he was approached just to obtain something from her? Then what?
“I can provide the method to resurrect her, but whether you can ultimately bring her back to life, and whether you are willing to pay such a price for her resurrection, is up to you. Maybe you will have forgotten your feelings for her halfway through.”
“Impossible! I could never forget her!”
Wang Haiwen felt his emotions were being questioned and, without any hesitation, immediately chose to agree.
Instantly, some memories that should have been erased resurfaced in his mind.
As he recalled what had happened, his eyes bloodshot with rage, an intense anger exploded, “That damned bastard, I will, I must kill him!”
If this vengeance is not avenged, I swear I’m not human!
Once he became strong, he would certainly kill him, no, kill his entire family!
However, at that moment, another line of information appeared in his mind.
“No, no, no, you shouldn’t hate him, you should thank him!”
“What the fuck are you talking about!?” Wang Haiwei couldn’t accept this. Although he knew it was just an intelligent program that might have ulterior motives, he still couldn’t help the anger that surged.
“If it weren’t for his help, your girlfriend might have become a slave to ‘the stars,’ and then you would never have the chance to resurrect her…”
“What do you mean?” Wang Haiwei’s anger subsided, confused.
But soon, through the information in his mind, he realized that it was all because of a conspiracy by an organization called the Celestial Observation Society, all because of them, his girlfriend and fiancée had suffered like this.
“I blamed the wrong person, those damned cultists,”
Wang Haiwei took a deep breath and sat back down, “So, what am I supposed to do next?”
As his words ended, three pieces of information popped up in his mind.
“1. Head to… find any mainstream church of followers who believe in the grand and exalted ‘Red Moon,’ become its believer, and obtain the ‘True Crimson Blood’ within one month.”
“2. Infiltrate the ‘Celestial Observation Society,’ assassinate the false god, and obtain the ‘Color of Madness’ pigment (must complete Task 1 as a prerequisite).”
“3. Proceed to Base No. 5, find the ‘Corrupted Remains (Chen Wei),’ and commence the resurrection ritual.”
After reviewing the content above, Wang Haiwei stood up, not waiting for daybreak, and left his room immediately.
…
Meanwhile, in a special hospital’s ward in another city, beside a comatose patient who had been bedridden for years, a palm-sized creature that was nothing but a shadow slipped into his body.
Minutes later, the “vegetable patient” suddenly opened his eyes and sat up, staring blankly around:
“Where is this? Didn’t I die from the ‘Celestial Observation Society’s’ conspiracy?”
Memories of a car accident from long ago surfaced, leaving him in shock before he looked incredulously at his own hands: “Is it really only the 2020s? Have I, have I returned to ten years ago?!”
And at that moment, a line of familiar text appeared before his eyes.
[Some force seems to have brought you back to more than a decade ago, where everything feels fresh and new.]
“This is…”
The “vegetable patient” felt baffled for a moment, then, as if receiving a “revelation,” his confusion turned to great joy. It was his former ability, to receive hints from any predicament and break through!
After confirming that this was indeed more than a decade ago, he laughed out loud:
“Hahaha, I can’t believe I was reborn again!
“This time, I will overturn the ‘Celestial Observation Society’s’ conspiracy, kill those who summon the Outer Gods! Annihilate all human traitors!
“This time, I will rewrite all endings!”
…
In another region, a man weighing over two hundred pounds was eating a roasted field mouse when a piece of information appeared abruptly in his mind.
“You have obtained one of the Super Talent Fragments ‘Gluttony of the World,’ just eat, and you will become stronger!”
“Sole mission: Defeat the other holders of this fragment within thirty days, complete all the pieces, and proceed to the ‘Celestial Observation Society’ to consume the false god, obtaining the ‘Color of Madness’…”
“Eat, eat, eat! Devour all your enemies and let them nourish you!”
That night, it seemed countless individuals received ‘gifts’…”
…
Ding—Ding—Ding—
The distant and ancient bell sounds slowly faded away.
Colin once again arrived at ‘World Code-13,’ opened his eyes, and the familiar Bonfire appeared within sight, it was warm, bright, and didn’t evoke the discomfort of being burnt by flames.
Perhaps due to a deepened understanding of the power of ‘Firebearer,’ Colin noticeably felt a vague and indescribable sense of closeness with the flame that was hard to articulate.
[You have obtained “Nearly Pure Colorless Crystal*37.”]
“Huh… the Colorless Crystal, the energy density is higher.”
Colin took out one to inspect, and the effect was evidently more potent than before, allowing for the liberal use of energy for fifteen minutes with just one crystal.
For example, if used on an ordinary person, they could run at full sprint for fifteen minutes.
That effect was still quite impressive…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 266 - 266 264 Saving the Fallen Hero_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 266: Chapter 264 Saving the Fallen Hero_1 Chapter 266: Chapter 264 Saving the Fallen Hero_1 Of course, Colin estimated that if he used it at full strength, its duration would significantly shorten, since the energy he output was much greater than that of an ordinary person. He might need several crystals combined to match the effect on an ordinary person.
The limitations were three times in an hour, ten crystals in a day…
“Not bad, it feels like an extraordinary version of Viagra or Red Bull. Is this the benefit of having more followers?”
Colin tucked the crystal away, feeling that in a fight to the death, it could have a miraculous effect.
However, he didn’t dwell on this matter. He turned around, looked down, and saw three figures appearing in the church.
Li Ming, Tang Ken, Lin Yilan.
The trio of subordinate employees had also arrived…
Having learned what this world truly required, they hadn’t indulged in any fancy tricks like bringing in arms; each had brought various compressed foods.
But with only 10 liters of space, no matter how they packed, they couldn’t carry much…
“If it weren’t for some expansion of my space, entering this time would have been rather troublesome…”
This time, with his large and small spaces combined, he had a total of four hundred liters of independent space, allowing him to carry much more.
But even that extra space probably wouldn’t be enough…
Colin could sense that there were quite a few more people outside today; the total population of the territory probably reached tens of thousands.
As thoughts flickered through his mind, he too took out his items: various sorts of rehydratable compressed foods, medicines, and some dried beef that could double as a knife…
“Hey… these foods.” Tang Ken expressed his surprise, looking up at Colin, then back at the food. He could see the semblance of internal military food processing. These were not items one could buy on the open market.
You didn’t expect that, did you? I invested…
Colin muttered to himself, feeling it was much easier to get things done with official backing. He didn’t need to find suitable items to bring in one by one; he just had to tell Qin Chuan his requirements, and the latter would specifically deliver the items.
Faced with their questions, all he needed to do was mumble vaguely that “it’s part of the plan.”
At the same time, Colin also took some small potato pieces from his pocket… these were also part of the plan.
Given the current situation, with more and more refugees, even if he advanced to D Level and his space increased to one cubic meter, he wouldn’t be able to provide enough food for them all.
It’s better to teach someone to fish than to give them a fish. The only solution was to be self-sufficient by growing food.
“Although there isn’t enough sunlight, these are special improved varieties, so there shouldn’t be much problem. I’m not sure if the Nano Intellectual Mechanisms can assist in farming rice or anything…”
As thoughts continued to race through his mind, Colin handed over the items to Tang Ken to take charge of.
Compared to Li Ming and Lin Yilan, Tang Ken, who was suspected to come from a military background, had not only combat skills but also a good number of life skills.
“By the way, Boss, do we have new employees this time?” Li Ming asked.
As he spoke, the other two subordinate employees also looked towards Colin.
With severe understaffing management, tens of thousands of people might be looked after by just the three of them, along with some soldiers who helped out and a small number of cooperative civilians—it was impossible to manage everything.
With so much going on recently, I’ve forgotten about this. But even if I hadn’t forgotten, I couldn’t do anything without Lady Bunny’s approval…
Thoughts flickered through Colin’s mind, but he kept his face neutral and said, “It won’t be long now. I’ve already asked for authorization, it’s in the process of being approved. As soon as the candidates are confirmed, you’ll have assistants…
“For now, you’ll have to overcome the difficulties and hang in there.”
Upon hearing this, their expressions turned bitter.
“No worries, take these. If you feel a bit exhausted, use one. Don’t wear yourselves out.”
Colin kindly handed out a few “Colorless Crystals” to his employees.
Then, they pushed open the church doors, and a faint smell of excrement wafted through the air. However, compared to last week, the scent was much less intense. After all, there had been improvements in sanitation, and ordinary people now knew not to relieve themselves nearby but rather in a large pit.
Standing on the church steps and looking into the distance, Colin finally felt the place had grown more lively with people.
Thud, thud, thud!
Series of heavy hammering sounds were coming from not far from the church…
Colin looked in the direction of the noise and saw that Nun Vanessa, whom he had met before, was now kneeling on one knee on the ground, with a goat that had four horns pinned beneath her knee, continually hammering down with a mallet in her hand.
With every strike of the hammer, the goat emitted a pitiful “baa” from its mouth.
“What’s going on here?”
Colin squinted his eyes, making the scene a bit clearer for himself, then suddenly felt a chill in his lower body.
He saw that the buck goat had been tied down by its limbs by Vanessa, pinned to the ground, its testicles clamped in a wooden device, with her wielding the mallet, hammering away at the wooden frame clasping the goat’s testicles…
In order not to exert too much force and completely crush the testicular sac, she had to control her strength accurately to shatter the vas deferens and blood vessels within the testicles, which would then lead to the testicles decaying within the sac from lack of sustenance and eventually being reabsorbed by the body.
This process required meticulous attention and not too much force. It was better to err on the side of caution, hence the need for successive hammering.
Colin and the others hadn’t done anything yet after coming out, just watching this made them freeze in shock—
Pain, it was too painful…
In less than two minutes, the goat was sterilized.
“Next one, oh, you’re back?”
Sister Vanessa called out, but when she didn’t see anyone bringing the next goat, she turned around and noticed that Colin and the rest were already there.
‘Hiss, there’s a next one, lady, how many people, no, how many goats have you sterilized…’ Colin silently complained to himself.
From a distance, Lady Bunny seemed a bit uncomfortable as she stood up, intending to walk over directly, but noticing the disarray and dirt on her clothes, she washed her hands with some water and used a “Purification” to clean herself up before she approached:
“Didn’t you say you were going to leave for a few days? You’re back so soon?”
“So soon?”
“Yes, it’s only been a day…”
Only a day?
Colin was surprised but didn’t think much of it after that.
As for the time issue in “World Code-13,” probably only Lady Bunny knew the situation.
“The journey was smooth, so we came back quickly.”
He made an excuse and swiftly changed the topic, briefly asking if anything had happened during the day, but apart from learning that people in the territory had fought over land and Warden Calder’s nephew had sent several thousand more refugees, there was no other significant news.
Ending the conversation, Colin gestured towards the supplies they had just brought:
“These are the materials we just brought in; you can start distributing them now.”
After saying that, Colin handed over the “Slave to Money” task to Li Ming and the others, then opened the side quest named “Rescuing the Fallen Heroes,” following the sensation to look in a specific direction of this world.
First, he’d rescue this group of people…
.
.
.
ps: After coding the last part and going to the bathroom, I came back so sleepy that I thought I’d sent it out, but after not even sleeping for two hours, my brain kept shouting “didn’t post, didn’t post” in my dream. I checked my phone, and it really wasn’t posted….
Sorry…

chapters.title: Chapter 267 - 267 265 Plea Beneath the Colossal Labyrinth_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 267: Chapter 265: Plea Beneath the Colossal Labyrinth_1 Chapter 267: Chapter 265: Plea Beneath the Colossal Labyrinth_1 “It’ll probably take about a day or so if I keep moving day and night without stopping,” Colin said to himself, estimating based on his past experiences. He felt that the problem wasn’t too big.
The only problem was that after a month or so, he didn’t know whether he was going to retrieve bodies or save people.
But without giving it too much thought, Colin finished giving instructions regarding his territory and continued on his rescue journey.
“This damned place always causes a bunch of trouble every time I come here to save people; I hope it won’t this time.”
Colin silently prayed and then set off in the direction of his target.
After about ten or so hours of tedious travel, he suddenly stopped at a small hillside.
It was already night, and Colin held up a torch. Due to the unique phenomena of this world, his surroundings were actually clearer and even more comfortable to see at night than during the day.
The only uncomfortable thing was the darkness beyond the firelight; it was just too oppressive.
Within that depth, it felt as if danger lurked, ready to emerge at any moment…
Colin took a deep breath to shift his focus away from the darkness and scrutinized the hillside that stood about twenty or thirty meters tall, using the light from his torch.
Following the mission instructions, he quickly found an entrance on the hillside.
Without hesitation, Colin entered it, arriving at what appeared to be an ordinary underground cave; he then followed the guide for a while until he came across what looked like a square, neatly repaired man-made underground tunnel.
Colin looked around and then headed towards a road junction.
“This place still feels just as ridiculous as before. I’ve no idea why someone would go to the trouble to build something so huge.”
After about an hour of winding through the pathways, Colin faintly smelled a trace of blood in the man-made tunnel.
After a moment’s thought, he took out the “Analytical Lens” and put it up to his eye.
[You faintly smell a scent of blood tinged with pain and suffering, drifting from this place…]
“Not bad, still as ridiculous as ever.”
Colin pursed his lips, pocketed the lens, and quickened his pace.
This time, even if the “Human Patchwork Monster” appeared again, he had nothing to fear.
With his current strength, it would be an instant kill as soon as he saw it…
“Feels like I’m a high-level returning to the novice village.”
Colin commented to himself, and soon he arrived at a familiar hall. Near the hall, he saw scorch marks from a battle, and he could faintly smell Blended Oil.
After crossing the hall in a few steps, Colin entered the so-called “kitchen” and saw the figures of seven “Brave Ones,” but before he could approach, his movement suddenly halted.
“Who has been here?”
Colin noticed that several of the “Brave Ones” were dressed in blue and white striped clothes, looking like patients rather than the long-haired look he left them in.
Apart from that, in front of these people floated an “Energy Crystal” the size of a human head, from which a certain power was constantly supplied to their bodies like blood vessels.
Upon seeing this item, he understood who had been here because on every face of the square “Energy Crystal”, there were words like “First Corps ‘Bunny’ spare medical supplies”.
“Indeed it is an energy crystal block, but whether it’s the purity or the size, it seems much better than mine…”
Colin had no intention of claiming it for himself; instead, he stepped forward to take a look at the “Brave Ones”. Their status was relatively stable, but it was so stable that it seemed overdone; they looked dead, similar to corpses in a morgue’s freezer.
Clearly, this “Energy Crystal” was only maintaining their status, not healing their injuries.
“Hiss, even the muscles under the skin are not seamlessly joined…”
Colin looked at the strange bulges in their clothes at the limbs, neck, and back and couldn’t help but shake his head.
Given the strength of the “First Corps,” repairing their bodies would definitely be easier than him going out to buy a bottle of cola.
But whether it was because there wasn’t enough time or some other reason, those people did nothing more than put clothes on the wounded and provide them with something to prolong their lives, without making any further efforts to treat the “Heroes'” injuries.
“The muscles and tendons at the joints are completely torn; it seems there’s nothing I can do either.”
Colin pinched his forehead, finding it easier to slay enemies than to mend such injuries.
Moreover, the “Gluttony Power Mark” didn’t seem quite suitable for such a situation.
Without thinking too much, Colin decided to first pack the people up and bring them back to his territory for now, then reconnect their muscles and figure out a way to treat them further afterward…
“Sigh, it’s only I who care about you guys, coming from thousands of miles away to take you back.”
Colin took out a large burlap bag from his pocket, stuffed the people into it one by one, feet down, heads up, with only their heads sticking out of the bag for breathing.
The “Energy Crystal” seemed to possess some kind of intelligence, following on its own.
Then, shouldering this big bundle of people, Colin headed for the exit of this immense underground labyrinth. Once on the surface, with the use of some tools, his movement should speed up a lot.
When back in his territory, he would ask Lin Yilan if she could perform surgery to fix their muscles.
After the repairs, the “Heroes” would immediately be able to start their happy lives in the Other World.
Colin remembered that at the time, several of them were interested in things like “the iron torrent,” and building a beautiful society through farming…
Colin decided that once they woke up, he would help them achieve their dreams.
“Although they are all marginal groups, at least they all have completed nine years of compulsory education. No, wait, seems I’ve forgotten that none of them had actually joined the company, not even as external personnel, so they might not be able to communicate with the locals…”
When the “Human Patchwork Monster” communicated with them, it used Mandarin instead of the local language, which indicated that there was a high probability they could not understand the local language.
To resolve this, they would have to join the company, or at the very least obtain an external authorization from the company like Li Ming and the others, otherwise, it would be quite troublesome.
“Forget it, I’ll see how it goes when the time comes, these people are worth a few thousand Points after all…”
Colin shook his head in secret, swung his hand to adjust the angle of the bag, and continued to drag them away.
However, at that moment, Colin suddenly felt the tunnel floor tremble and an eerie aura seemed to spread up from beneath the earth, arriving at this place in an instant.
Eerie whispers appeared by his ear.
Colin originally wanted to be on guard, but hearing this voice made him have a somewhat strange expression.
“Great Rosen, Holy Rosen, I have realized my mistakes, please let me go…”
“I am willing to change my beliefs and accept the transformation of the ‘Primordial Fire,’ to walk on the earth in human form…”
“Please, take me away…”
“I have recognized all my faults…”
“I promise to suppress my instincts, learn human values and cognition, no longer do evil, do good deeds, and become a true human…”
“I am willing to sign that three-thousand-year Bonfire work contract, as atonement…”
“Holy Walker, Rosen, spare me…”
“I am willing to serve you…”
…

chapters.title: Chapter 268 - 268 266 From the Underground_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 268: Chapter 266: From the Underground_1 Chapter 268: Chapter 266: From the Underground_1 “Ah??”
Colin’s mind raised a huge question, What’s going on here?
He could feel that the presence emanating from the speaker was incredibly powerful, much stronger than the “Father of the Sea” after his “Divine” had been stripped away.
The most critical aspect was the obvious “superiority” about it—that kind of “Divine.”
But…
With such strength, this level of being pleading for mercy, he had never heard of it before.
This made Colin feel a sense of unreality and absurdity…
Every big shot that appeared had an imposing presence, so why was this one’s tone so soft, pleading and apologizing?
“However, who is this Rosen? What is this thing that’s trapped? And why is he calling out to me… Did he mistake me for someone else?”
Colin puzzled inwardly when a sudden illumination made him vaguely realize who the person mentioned by the other party was.
The “former company” employee who died here!
“So, this one is called Rosen…”
Colin seemed to understand and then, with a cold face, ignored the voice by his ear, lifted his foot, and continued walking out—
Perhaps in the eyes of that former colleague, these creatures were nothing but chickens and dogs.
But now, with the roles reversed, if he were to be recognized, there would be big problems!
However, just then, sensing that Colin was not paying attention, the terrifying existence deep below the giant maze seemed to grow impatient…
Under Colin’s feet, the soil squirmed, turning into a pair of hands, reverently stretched out to grasp the hem of his pants.
“I really have repented, I truly have, please release me from your Containment God Kingdom…”
You, son of a…
Colin looked at the hand clutching the hem of his pants, thinking about whether to use “Time Stop: Pause” to escape or to perform a “Tiger’s Body Shake” to make the other let go.
But then, a human face emerged: “Saint Rosen I have acknowledged my wrongs, I beg you… you’re not Rosen!”
The face stared at Colin and screamed!
“No, you are Rosen, you have his power, his weapon, no, no, no, is he… dead?!”
The terrifying existence from beneath the ground seemed to have been tormented for too long, leading to a confused mind, but after a moment, it suddenly realized something and let out wild laughter, causing the entire labyrinth tunnel to vibrate:
“Hahaha, that damned guy, he’s finally dead!
“You, whoever you are, since you’ve inherited his power, release me immediately, or else I’ll kill you!”
The horrifying existence from below changed its tone in an instant.
‘Well, it’s all pleases and thank yous with him, and with me, it’s all fists and threats, huh!’ thought Colin as he understood what was meant by a “Light Speed” change of face.
Immediately, a flame burst forth from his body, enveloping him, and Colin spoke with a tone of doubt, “How do you know he’s dead? Maybe I just came to test you, didn’t I?”
The monster underground definitely had no idea about his purpose for being there, and it likely also didn’t know about the previous “Human Patchwork Monster.”
It had pursued him because it sensed a familiar aura on him.
Therefore, with this unequal information, Colin had some room to maneuver.
However, as he was talking, he was also prepared to use Time Stop and ready to flee.
At this point, the hand withdrew, as if worried about Colin’s suggestion—that guy might not truly be dead—what if this was just a probe?
Otherwise, it would be simply too unreasonable for this person carrying Rosen’s aura to come here alone.
“You… I… I can feel he’s gone, but…” His voice turned weak again, and even though he knew it was a ruse, he didn’t dare try more; in fact, he couldn’t attempt too much.
The seals that bind it to this day still limit it, preventing it from truly using much power.
“Regardless of his situation, I can be sure that you indeed have a significant chance of setting me free…”
“We can make a deal.”
“I can guarantee I won’t lay a hand on you, and I can agree to a request for aid…”
The voice kept reaching his ears, but Colin didn’t stop moving, continuing toward the exit.
“I can sense that although you possess that kind of power, you’re not a ‘Firebearer.’ If you can release me, I can tell you where his traits might remain and where he went last…”
“I can tell you many secrets, about this world…”
“Also, from you, I can see that you’re entangled with many things, many of which are connected to you, many of which are troublesome divine beings…”
“Just solve my predicament, and I can likewise help you resolve one of your troubles…”
The underground voice continuously tried to negotiate, but unfortunately, Colin let it in one ear and out the other, leaving unswervingly.
During this process, Colin encountered no further obstacles.
“Someday, you will agree.”
After Colin had completely left the Underground Giant Great Labyrinth, the last voice reached his ears, and behind him, a human face stretched out from the wall, staring at him intently until it disappeared.
Not long after returning to the surface, Colin finally breathed a sigh of relief.
Reflecting on what that thing said, he pursed his lips:
“Agree my ass. It’s all apologies and servitude with that Rosen, even offering a three-thousand-year contract. When it comes to me, they put on an act. Damn, do they think I’m easy to bully…”
Although Colin was indeed curious about what that creature had said, he also knew that his current strength was nowhere near capable of tracing the past.
The stark difference between that underground being’s past and present personas was proof enough.
This was already the case without releasing it; if he truly set it free and it confirmed the death of its former colleague, given the personality traits it had shown, Colin reckoned there was a not-so-small chance he’d be on the receiving end of its retribution.
Couldn’t overcome the big one, and now can’t handle this smaller one?
“I’ll report this to Miss Bunny later. If she deems it important, I guess the Corps will come talk.”
Colin shook his head, not surprised that his former colleague had such strength.
After all, the two “Firebearers” who had appeared were both dead yet extremely powerful; neither was weak.
Without pondering further, Colin, torch in hand, glanced at the surrounding darkness, confirmed his direction, and started to silently retrace his steps back.
This time, apart from that little surprise underground, nothing else happened.
After several more hours, Colin once again saw the little chapel. Around it, many refugees seemingly heard that they could get food and survive there had come flocking.
Along the way, Colin saw many groups moving toward the chapel as if on a pilgrimage.
However, at that moment, Colin suddenly heard a din of noisy cursing coming from a nearby group.
It looked like something had happened over there.
After thinking for a moment, Colin first gazed from a distance at the town within the Silent Mountains, confirming that nothing had occurred there during his absence, then he walked toward the source of the noise and cursing.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 269 - 269 267 An Unexpected Encounter_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 269: Chapter 267: An Unexpected Encounter_1 Chapter 269: Chapter 267: An Unexpected Encounter_1 “You little brat, hand over the goods quickly!”
“Damn thief, catch him, I want to beat him to death!”
“Surround him, don’t let him get away!”
About seven or eight vagrants launched a pursuit of a young child, their curses filled with venom.
Aside from them, there was a large crowd of onlookers, which made the scene quite lively, but no one noticed a breathless man walking into the crowd.
Through the gaps in the crowd, Colin’s expression changed as he focused on the child being chased:
“Huh… that looks like someone I know.”
A child in tattered clothes, clutching something in his hand, was running fast to escape, while several vicious-looking people chased relentlessly behind him.
Seeing the child being cornered and chased, Colin first felt a sense of familiarity, and then quickly recognized him by scent, realizing this was the kid he had met on the way to find Tang Ken, with whom he shared a brief encounter.
The boy’s distinct black eyes and hair, along with the fact that Colin had given him a couple of glances and been noticed in return, had made a strong impression, which allowed him to recognize the boy immediately now.
Of course, his reason for coming here was not only the desire to see what was happening at the commotion near his home.
There was also a feeling that the “find the child of the mother with Beast Transformation Syndrome” task seemed to have been slightly triggered, though it was very faint, very slight.
For that task, Colin had always wanted to take it on, since his first power came from that child’s mother, leaving him indebted to her.
If it was within his power, he felt that he would be troubled by regrets if he didn’t attempt the task.
Unfortunately, when he previously asked Warden Calder, he too shook his head, indicating he didn’t know the whereabouts of the child.
Although he didn’t find the child, he did learn some information about the mother from other refugees, hearing that her own child had been stillborn and that the precious boy she cared for might have been someone else’s child she found somewhere and raised as her own.
In such cases, where the scent didn’t match her bloodline, it became even harder to find the child.
Moreover, given the hunger at that time, the outcome for orphaned children with no parents was generally not good, with a certain likelihood of being taken for “extra meals,” so Colin always feared the worst for the boy.
But the task remained active and hadn’t indicated failure, which led Colin to pray for a lucky encounter one day.
He did not expect to feel a strange sensation today…
“The sensation is too vague and weak to be sure if it was actually triggered.”
Colin rubbed his forehead.
Before he could ponder further, a vagrant suddenly sprang out on the boy’s escape route, tripping him to the ground. The others quickly pounced, capturing and beating him with a flurry of fists and kicks.
Under the rain of punches, the child didn’t cry out but stubbornly curled up on the ground.
Only his small face began to show a pair of eyes turning gradually from black to red.
“Damn it, he stole our food and dared to throw rocks at us. Break his legs!”
“Hehe, those legs, I really fancy them. Watch me smash them off.”
“Good! I haven’t eaten in so long…”
As they spoke, someone brought over a rock, raising it to smash down on the child’s legs.
But the rock had only dropped halfway when the grinning man realized a hand had blocked its descent.
Following the hand to its owner, he saw a tall, lean man who had appeared out of nowhere in front of them.
Although the single-handed block of the rock’s force astonished him, seeing Colin’s ratty appearance, which wasn’t much different from their own apart from being taller, he figured they outnumbered this new arrival!
And…
The vagrant leader, catching sight of the pair of legs revealed by the bottom of Colin’s trousers, was immediately intrigued; as someone with a fetish for legs, he suddenly got some ideas:
“Dare to interfere with me, I’ll break your legs too, and we’ll roast them for a meal!”“Is that so?”
Colin squinted, his gaze sweeping over the few men. He could smell the stench of blood on them, a clear sign of their not being new to violence.
Even their talk of eating was not an empty threat but an actual plan.
While Colin might turn a blind eye to extreme acts of necessity, he considered actively engaging in cannibalism another matter. If he hadn’t encountered it, that was one thing, but having encountered it, it was a matter of killing every single one!
He would not allow such things on his territory!
The next moment, Colin drew his revolver and used the “Air Bullet,” firing a dozen bullets in rapid succession. Before they could react, he had blown all their heads off.
The bright red blood mist exploded along with brain matter, as one figure after another fell like harvested stalks, blood gushing out.
Seeing this, the onlookers who had come for entertainment were initially stunned, then screamed and scattered in all directions.
“Are there still a few kids who haven’t run away? Are they all together?”
Colin took a breath; he could sense that there were roughly three children who had not left, all small and malnourished-looking, but they were hiding in the back, watching this side with fear and concern.
“It’s a pity, none on the scene are related by blood to her. So many days have passed, and if it’s just a scent, the scent would have faded by now, hard to distinguish, but…”
Colin withdrew his gaze, unable to determine which one was the mother’s child, so he decided to save them all!
Not just the ones here!
If they were still alive, one day he would be able to save them!
“Speaking of which, the old Dean wanted to train me to be his successor, such a pity that ALS ruined those plans. But now it’s not too late to start an orphanage here.”
While pondering, Colin squatted down and looked at the child he had saved.
Dirty, skinny, small, with many bruises on his body and blood flowing from his forehead, yet those eyes were still bright and pure, invoking involuntary compassion…
Colin took out a clean tissue from his pocket, disregarding the filth on the child’s body, and reached out to wipe the blood from his face, then pressed on the wound.
At this moment, perhaps recognizing Colin, the child was not as wary as when they first met and did not run away either, just blinking at Colin, showing a sort of innocence and curiosity.
“Bear with it a moment.”
Colin took out a wet wipe and cleaned around the wound: “Does it hurt?”
The child shook his head, then nodded, then shook his head again.
Uh, what does that mean?
Although confused, since the child didn’t pull away, Colin continued to clean the wound and asked:
“Do you have a name?”
The child blinked his black eyes, staring at Colin as if he’d lost his internet connection, no reaction.
“Then do you know where your home is?”
No reaction.
“What about your mom and dad?”
No reaction.
‘Other than staring at me, he’s utterly unresponsive; is his brain damaged?’ Colin muttered to himself, but his hands did not stop moving. After cleaning the wound, he took out an all-purpose adhesive bandage and applied it to the nail-sized wound on his forehead.
It was then that he noticed what the child was holding in his hands—two plump moles.
As for why he caught them, Colin didn’t need to guess; it was for food.
Without a second glance, Colin searched for a bottle of emergency medicine for contusions and pulled up the child’s hand that was holding the moles, helping him apply the ointment to various swollen and bruised parts of his body.
However, with his hand pulled like that and feeling Colin’s touch roaming over his body, the child’s face suddenly turned a bit red.
And it was at that moment he suddenly heard the man before him continue to ask:
“Why were they bothering you? Did you steal something from them?”
Colin didn’t really expect the child to speak, but to his surprise, after hearing his question, the child with the pure black eyes suddenly became agitated.
..
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 270 - 270 268 Well-Organized Development_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 270: Chapter 268: Well-Organized Development_1 Chapter 270: Chapter 268: Well-Organized Development_1 “I didn’t steal it, I caught it myself!”
The child retorted with a slightly hoarse and childish voice, their little hands involuntarily squeezing tight, the mole’s tongue protruding out.
Colin was about to comfort the child when he suddenly paused:
“You… huh? You’re a girl?”
The kid wasn’t even 1.2 meters tall, with no hint of development, dirty and unkempt. Colin had assumed the child was a boy both times he had seen her, not realizing she was a girl until she spoke.
“Okay, fine, I apologize, I misunderstood you…”
“Ah…” The little girl, about to say something, froze, having braced herself to be hit. She never expected an apology from the other party.
You see, for someone like an “important person,” right or wrong, daring to talk back could even get you killed!
“Hehe, I know what it’s like to be wronged, I went through it myself when I was young. Okay, I offer you a sincere apology, and here’s my apology gift.”
Colin spoke kindly, reaching into his pocket and taking out a milk-flavor candy, stuffing it into the little girl’s mouth before she could react.
He actually always disliked annoying kids, but the well-behaved and sensible ones were a different matter…
And the little girl, just processing what happened, felt the sweet dissolving in her mouth, her whole jaw turning sour—she had never tasted anything so sweet!
That unfamiliar milkiness and sweetness…
“All right, your injuries are not too serious.”
Colin stood up after roughly treating her main wounds, pointing towards his domain in the direction of the small town:
“Would you like to come with me? I’ll provide you with food and shelter. As long as I live, I’ll save more children like you who have nowhere to go, teach you some knowledge, help you grow up, and then, the future is yours to choose.”
This time was different from making empty promises to the employees; Colin truly intended to do this, reminded of his own childhood by these children.
From a broken small family to the large family of the old dean…
Colin felt he had been quite fortunate.
Now, he planned to extend that luck a little longer.
The little girl followed his gesture, seeing only mountains vaguely in the distance a few kilometers away and nothing else, then turned her gaze back to Colin’s side profile, staring at him blankly.
After a while, she suddenly said with dejection,
“But we don’t have any money…”
She looked awkwardly at the two moles in her hands.
Although they were indeed fat, clearly, they could not pay the price, not even enough for the sweet thing in her mouth.
This kind of “good fortune” frightened her…
Yet, feeling the tone in Colin’s words, she didn’t run away as she would have in the past.
“Your growing up will be my reward.”
Colin smiled, reaching out to ruffle her hair. Ever since he had come to “World Code-13,” he had been completing tasks numbly, but having found something he wanted to do, he felt his mood had improved a lot.
And it was then that he turned to look behind him:
“Are those your friends?”
At this moment, those children had moved a bit closer, each carrying a stone as if prepared to give him a hard time.
‘Young in age, but certainly not in courage,’ Colin mused to himself.
“Um… could you take them with you?” the little girl tentatively asked.
“Of course, call them over.”
At his words, the little girl’s eyes lit up; her dark pupils appeared to redden with the change in emotion. Realizing something, she quickly averted her gaze, cocking her head to the side, sneaking another peek at Colin. Seeing that he seemed not to notice, she breathed a sigh of relief.
‘There’s indeed something not quite right with this child, those eyes,’ Colin thought with a hint of suspicion. However, having just comforted her, he didn’t rush to inquire immediately, to avoid upsetting her.
“By the way, what’s your name?” Colin asked again.
Upon hearing the question, the girl first shook her head, then said in a low voice, “I don’t have a name, but they all call me ‘Red’…”
No name; that must be a nickname then?
Colin was not overly surprised by this, as many refugees indeed did not have names or the privilege to have one; they often just had nicknames.
“Then I’ll call you Little Red.”
Without dwelling on the matter, at Little Red’s beckoning, the children who had wanted to “rescue” her jumped out. After Colin explained the misunderstanding, he took out the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses.”
In the next instant, the corpses on the ground melted away, and a huge Black Flesh Orb rose from the ground.
After briefly calming the shocked and frightened children, Colin led them to climb the Corpse Mountain, heading toward his domain:
“Pipi Ball, let’s go!”
The Corpse Mountain extended its thick arms in place of legs, carrying the group towards the domain. Thanks to Colin’s use of the “Emblem of the Humility Knight,” they didn’t cause much of a stir along the way—
It just always felt like something was missing.
“Ah.”
Suddenly, Colin slapped his forehead, remembering that he had yet to pick up the “Heroes” sack he had tossed on the ground. He commanded the Smiling Mountain of Corpses to return to the original spot to collect them before finally heading back to his territory.
After more than a day’s travel, everything in the territory was normal, except for a slight increase in the population.
However, soon Colin noticed that in addition to the refugees, there were several hundred soldiers he had never seen before…
After Colin’s return, Li Ming quickly received the message and temporarily put down his work to come over.
“Those soldiers are brought by Calder’s nephew. They say they’re here to help, but I feel like they harbor ill intentions. Should we drive them away?”
“Drive them away? Why?” Colin was surprised.
“Well… There are traitors among them.”
“Doesn’t matter. We’re indeed short on labor right now, especially the kind that can understand orders. I reckon these ‘traitors’ will probably work harder than other soldiers to gather intelligence.”
Colin waved his hand dismissively, showing he wasn’t too concerned, his strength giving him the confidence to speak like this.
What Li Ming saw as traitorous soldiers were just another source of labor in Colin’s eyes…
“Alright then.” Li Ming nodded, then turned to look at the few children following Colin and at a sack of people being carried by a few “Money Slaves” handed over by Colin.
“These are ‘Heroes’ that I’ve just rescued…”
“You mean those poor sods are them?” Li Ming exclaimed in surprise.
Colin had told them the story of these unlucky “Heroes” before; Li Ming hadn’t expected that Colin’s recent outing was for this reason.
However, upon further thought and rubbing the dark circles under his eyes, Li Ming suddenly got excited, “Then, are they…?”
Having experienced nine years of compulsory education, acting as high-quality labor and contributing to their own well-being shouldn’t be a problem!
“Don’t think about it for now; they didn’t come through official channels and aren’t employees of the Bonfire Company. There’s a language barrier, and they’re injured. Right, their wounds need tending to. Later, ask Lin Yilan to come over.”
“Okay.”
Li Ming resigned himself to the fact and then turned to look at the few kids beside Colin, “By the way, who are these few?”
“You’re not thinking of having them help you with work, are you?” Colin asked with an odd expression.
“No, just asking.” Li Ming shook his head.
Noticing his gaze, Little Red nervously hid behind Colin, anxiously clutching the hem of his clothes.
Her eyes started to turn red again, perhaps due to the emotional changes.
Although there was no evidence, Colin had a premonition that if her eyes remained red, bad things were likely to happen.
‘It seems I’ll have to take care of her myself, otherwise there could be trouble.’ Colin thought to himself, his face betraying nothing as he spoke:
“Well, they’re a few homeless children; I’ll arrange for them to stay in the church for now.”
Colin patted her head to reassure her, made the arrangements, and then casually asked about the others—
Lin Yilan and the Nun were together rescuing people, while Tang Ken had gone out with a group of people to fabricate some basic tools and then attempt to reclaim farmland and develop wasteland.
In this world, there are actually quite a few people who know how to reclaim land and farm, but most of the time, they can’t do so.
Because reclaiming land in such times is heavy labor. Without enough food and protein support, a thousand refugees would go out to reclaim wasteland, and without food or tools, half would likely die from exhaustion or starvation in a few days.
Food and such are controlled by the nobles, and only when they wish to reclaim wasteland, can ordinary people do so.
Colin’s territory was also short on food, but he had that batch of several hundred 25s whose physiques were several times stronger than an ordinary person, so the problem wasn’t too severe.
After getting a brief understanding of the territory’s situation, Colin nodded with satisfaction.
In the following days, just as he had imagined, the 25s worked much harder than ordinary people. With their selfless dedication, the territory finally began to recover some order from the chaos.
Three days passed in an orderly fashion…
But looking at the increasingly dark circles under the eyes of Li Ming and the others, Colin suddenly felt a bit guilty and some ideas began to emerge—
“Is there a way to let them work continuously for seven days without reducing their work efficiency due to fatigue?”
As he pondered, Colin somewhat had a few ideas.
“Now they still need rest, but it’s time to enhance their strength. If they could get injected with F Level Gene Compensation Medicine and combine it with ‘Colorless Crystal,’ even if they work continuously for seven days, they probably won’t develop dark circles.”
In this way, his conscience would also feel much better.
However, just as Colin was thinking of going out to improve his employees’ strengths, Sister Vanessa suddenly rushed over excitedly and told him some big news—
Sometime soon, the highest-ranking figure in the “Light” Church, the first person under God, the Saint walking the earth, may be passing through this area!
.
.
.
ps: Seeking a monthly ticket, let’s see if there’s a chance for a thousand monthly tickets to fulfill the dream of surpassing a thousand monthly tickets after many years of struggling to write.

chapters.title: Chapter 271 - 271 269 Sincerity Leads_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 271: Chapter 269 Sincerity Leads_1 Chapter 271: Chapter 269 Sincerity Leads_1 “Quite a number of titles…”
Colin looked at the excited Vanessa in front of him, and couldn’t help but feel a surge of curiosity about the saint.
After all, when he first took in the source of the “Beast Transformation Syndrome” and those affected by “0-9 Hunger,” Helena was willing to help him selflessly from beginning to end, seemingly influenced by the saintess.
Otherwise, Colin wouldn’t have been able to mobilize the people from that city to assist him.
In that regard, he owed her a favor.
The only thing he couldn’t understand was why she would help a stranger like himself.
Besides, among the refugees Colin had helped, the most prayed-to figure, aside from the four deities of the Knight Kingdom and the Three Teachings, was generally the “Light” Church’s saintess.
Even many lower-class followers of other teachings, in addition to worshiping their own deity, would pray to the “Light” Church’s saintess, almost as if their hearts lay elsewhere despite being in another camp.
This was a situation Colin found himself in often—many refugees thanked the “Saintess” first for their food.
Of course, Colin’s eagerness to think about her was definitely not because he felt slighted seeing refugees consuming the food, drinking the water, and living in the houses he had provided, while praying to someone else.
However, Colin thought that the saintess, as spoken of by the refugees, was a bit mythologized.
He was curious what such a revered individual truly looked like in reality…
“When will she be coming? I ought to treat her well.”
Colin earnestly said, knowing that someone who could escape from a massive disaster with countless burdens must be incredibly strong, without even having to think about it.
And from the bits of information he had gathered, she was indeed one of the strongest individuals in the world.
Plus her exalted status…
Colin could only hope that nothing would go wrong when she visited his domain.
Otherwise, if her zealous believers came after him, Colin didn’t know if he could withstand them.
“I’m not sure, possibly half a month, or maybe a month?”
“Half a month, a month, that’s no rush…”
Colin pursed his lips, calculating: half a month equates to one month, one month equates to two months.
There was plenty of time.
“Yes.” After announcing the safe return of the saintess, Vanessa’s wheat-colored face relaxed quite a bit, and then she took out a small item from her pocket and held it in front of Colin:
“Mr. Colin, do you still have any more of this? I—I’d like to have one, to let Her Saintess try as well. I can compensate with work hours!”
Colin looked down and saw a piece of White Rabbit Creamy Candy with only a third remaining.
He remembered giving it to her last week—it was clear she’d been eating it sparingly.
“You gave me two before, and I intended to save one, but… it was really too delicious, and I’d never tasted anything like it before. I couldn’t help myself.”
Vanessa hung her head, speaking like a child who had done something wrong, almost as if she were about to recite a penitential prayer.
Wouldn’t it seem a bit cheap to entertain that saint with such a thing?
Colin felt a mix of amusement and consternation as he took another few pieces of candy from his pocket: “I’ve run out of that kind of candy for now, but here are some other fruit-flavored ones that also taste quite good…”
“Oh?” Upon hearing Colin’s words, Vanessa looked a bit disappointed, but after giving them a try, her eyes brightened. The sour and sweet flavor, with a touch of unfamiliar fruit, felt good as well.
If she had a choice, though, she’d still prefer the white milk candy.
Then.
The young nun seemed to think of something and closed her eyes sincerely, muttering a few words—though her voice was soft, Colin still caught the gist of it: “Thanks to the saintess’s ‘Revelation’ for leading her here, thanks to Mr. Colin,” and so on…
Good grief, what does my candy have to do with her… Colin squinted slightly, waiting for her to finish praying, before saying:
“I’ll bring some more next time I come. However, compared to a few candies, I think what the saintess might care more about isn’t that…”
“Ah? What might that be?” The young nun asked curiously.
“Given the saintess’s character, I think she’d be happier to see everyone here having houses to live in rather than ruins, having food rather than hunger, all people living and working in peace without pain and suffering from disease. More than a few candies, perhaps she’s more concerned with things like that…”
“It does seem that way,” Nun Vanessa nodded, feeling that Colin’s words made sense, as if he understood the saintess even better than she did.
“But… look at those houses yet to be rebuilt, those wastelands being reclaimed, those people filled with disease—we’re still a long way off. This construction site, oh no, this area needs more people willing to rebuild their homes. If we can quickly build more houses to shelter everyone, regardless of their status or wealth, seeing such a scene, I think the saintess might feel more gratified…”
Colin reached out and patted the little nun on the shoulder. During this period, he had gained some insight into how to inspire her. Despite her naïvety and belief in a certain “righteousness,” she selflessly dedicated herself to the cause, with the great strength to efficiently move more than a dozen bricks alone.
Moreover, compared to her choice to join Lin Yilan in providing medical care to people, Colin truly believed that she would be better suited to working on a construction site or farming.
After all, compared to the high purity of her physical strength, the effect of her so-called “Light” was not as effective as a single Amoxicillin.
However, Colin was surprised when, right after he finished speaking, the little nun suddenly said, “Mr. Colin, is what you said true? To let those people… have their own houses? And to allow them to move in?”
She pointed to the disaster victims who were still gaunt but whose status had improved considerably…
“Yes, we are not able to do that now, but we will work towards that goal,” he nodded. Colin had also noticed these days that the more satisfied the refugees were with their situation, the purer their recognition, the purer that “Colorless Crystal” would be, and the faster the production speed would increase.
Even bathing in such an atmosphere, he felt his control over the “Bonfire” becoming more skillful and effortless.
This was probably the reason Lady Bunny wanted him to do good deeds…
Colin wasn’t sure if continuing like this would make him a “Firebearer,” but… trying it out wouldn’t cost any money.
After hearing his words, the little nun seemed to be struggling with something, with her head bowed. Colin was about to ask to quickly resolve the doubts in her heart—
After all, the silence for the past minute or so may have caused a dozen baskets of clay to be brought over.
At that moment, the little girl appeared to make a decision, “I will write a letter to have some people from the ‘Light’ Church come over and help when the time comes. They are more formidable than I am, maybe dozens of them…”
She wasn’t completely unaware of Colin’s plans, yet she didn’t mind them much either.
Because doing so indeed could help more people, it aligned with the Church of Light’s current reformed idea to eradicate suffering…
Another key point was, as far as she knew, though this place was territory of The Kingdom of Knights, Colin’s demonstrated formidable strength had essentially made it an independent “kingdom.”
Even the discontented nobility could not reach into this place…
“This…”
Colin was momentarily stunned, then catching on he smiled, “That’s, of course, welcome.”
It wasn’t long before the little nun left. Colin then pondered the matter of a few employees, planning to see, upon his return, whether he could upgrade their permissions and use a higher grade of “Gene Compensation Medicine” to boost them or acquire some strength recovery items.
At that moment, his clothing was tugged, interrupting his thoughts. Colin turned his head and noticed Little Red pulling at him.
After having bathed, she was much cleaner and better groomed than she had been two days ago, dressed in patched but whitewashed hemp clothing, with her scalp free from the chaotic mess and visible lice scurrying around.
Although her frame was still diminutive and emaciated from long-term malnutrition, and her face thin, she finally looked a bit like a young girl.
Before getting to the bottom of why her eyes had turned red, Colin had decided to keep her by his side…
“What’s the matter?” He patted her head, pulling out a piece of candy from his pocket, but while the little girl eyed it longingly, she did not take it. Instead, she asked in a childlike voice, “Can I, can I do any work to help you?”
You’re still a child laborer… Colin looked at the little girl who was less than one meter twenty in height and whose exact age he did not know: “In a few days, I will teach you something. For now, just accompany me as we walk around the estate.”
“Okay.” Little Red stared at his face, blinking her eyes.
“Hehe…”
Colin stroked her head, deciding to bring her the children’s favorite “One Lesson Three Practices” when the time came.
“Little Red sis…”
Just then, another child ran over, laughing, but upon seeing Colin, his voice halted with an inexplicable fear.
“What’s the matter?” Little Red let go of Colin’s clothes, standing like a big sister.
“The mole seems to be dying…”
After Colin rescued them, they had temporarily kept the two moles they had caught for extra food.
Unfortunately, today one of them seemed to be on the brink of death…
However, clearly it should be a sad moment for normal children, yet Colin couldn’t help but see the poorly concealed smile on the boy’s face—
It looked like an anticipation for a feast.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 272 - 272 270 Catastrophe of the Magic Fog _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 272: Chapter 270 “Catastrophe of the Magic Fog” _1 Chapter 272: Chapter 270 “Catastrophe of the Magic Fog” _1 “If it’s dead… you guys handle it.”
Little Red didn’t have any particular emotions about it; after all, that thing was meant to be food. She had intended to give it to Colin but realized it wasn’t enough and felt a bit embarrassed to offer it.
“It might have had a heatstroke, see if it can be saved.”
Colin voiced his opinion.
Afterward, spurred by Colin’s initiative, he led the possible heatstroke-afflicted mole to a creek not far from their location.
Unfortunately, they couldn’t save it in the end. Colin could only set up a bonfire, together with a few children, he sprinkled salt and cumin while tearfully sending the mole on its last journey…
In the following days, there was still no clear news about the Saintess’ visit, but they ended up waiting for another piece of information—
Some monsters from the Catastrophe of the Magic Fog were heading their way for unknown reasons.
Based on observations by some people, it was estimated that they may arrive near this area within the next few days…
Even in Colin’s mind, a mission to kill these Catastrophe of the Magic Fog monsters appeared.
“In five days at the earliest, seven at the latest, kill the Fourth Level Mutated Bodies coming nearby to use as kindling for the bonfire…”
Colin sat on a wooden chair inside the Church, stroked his chin, and guessed that this disaster wouldn’t be too difficult as the mission details recommended D Level Personnel for the operation.
He wasn’t a D Level Personnel, but he might as well be!
However, that information would come after five days; he still had more than ten days to prepare, maybe even enough time to ascend to a true D Level…
“If it weren’t for the lack of time, I could go right now to warm wine and slay monsters.”
Colin joked casually, then silently awaited the countdown for this descent’s return to end on his retinal display.
Meanwhile, in a room inside the Church, Little Red stared blankly at the people in front of the bonfire, especially at the figure who had rescued her, lost in thought.
Suddenly, as if sensing something, Colin turned his head. Little Red quickly pulled her head back as if guilty, and it took several seconds before she gathered the courage to peer out from the edge of the door and continue watching.
But this time, she was taken aback; the people in front of the bonfire had disappeared…
“Gone?” Little Red couldn’t hide the disappointment in her voice.
Even though Colin had warned that they might come tomorrow or in a few days, she couldn’t help but feel a sense of loss and even anxiety.
After a while, she dejectedly went back to the straw bed Colin had made for her and picked up a small notebook.
It contained some math homework Colin had translated for her…
“If I finish it, will he come back?”
Little Red used her small hand to count on five fingers, using the arithmetic that Colin had taught her, and frowned as she worked out the addition and subtraction problems within ten on the notebook.
After a while, she finally completed the day’s homework.
Then, noticing that it had become night outside, she ate something casually and went back to her little bed to sleep. But, pausing, she sat up, brought her hands to her chest, and said her evening prayer innocently:
“The most special, the most revered, the kind, all that is good comes from him, who I long for, Mr. Colin… brother.”
She had never believed in gods, but she had heard the prayers of other Cultists; so she modified them for her own use.
Gods wouldn’t provide her with a place to live, food to eat, or a sense of safety.
But, Colin would…
After her simple prayer routine, she crawled back into bed, closed her eyes, and fell into a deep sleep.
…
At a certain distance away, some people, through the vast space and darkness, seemed to gaze towards the nascent town.
Some whispered exchanges arose among them.
“Are you sure we’ve found her…?”
“Not certain, but around a dozen days ago, when the disaster struck here, that presence was indeed detected. It may have been an accidental use of her powers for self-preservation, and if not mistaken, she could have blended in with the inferior humans. That way, she might have gone to the town, and perhaps we could try to look for her directly…”
“The Grand Duke has warned us not to probe carelessly, not to cause any misunderstandings…”
“Is caution really necessary? This is The Kingdom of Knights, our territory, after all. That’s just an unfamiliar wild Church…”
“No, it’s not about whether caution is necessary, but that it’s imperative to proceed cautiously. We must not offend, because the wild Church you speak of has recently initiated a ‘God Descent’.”
This statement was followed by a long silence.
“Is the source of this information reliable…?” the voice asked, growing somewhat hoarse.
“After multiple confirmations, yes. The branches of the Three Teachings have already classified them as orthodox and are preparing to send Ambassadors. The Grand Duke will also soon acknowledge their legitimate status in the Northern Territory.”
Another silence ensued, and they all knew what this meant.
Ahead was a “God”!
And a “God” that could even make the Three Teachings take the initiative to yield!
This meant that whatever their next actions were, they couldn’t cause any misunderstanding with that “Mr. Colin.”
For he represented the voice of “God” on earth!
According to Calder and others’ description, he has the authority to actively trigger a “God Descent,” a position that may be even higher than that of a Saintess!
“However, our target isn’t the Church, nor is it him. When the time comes, using the Catastrophe of the Magic Fog as our cover, we could go in under the guise of offering help, and try to find…”
“Yes.”
“All for our King’s coronation.”
“Praise be to our King!”
The crowd voiced their devotion sincerely.
….
“Still three hours, as unyielding as ever.”
Colin, unaware that in this Other World some saw his status akin to that of a Saint Heir, first checked the wall when he awoke, noting that only three hours had passed in the real world.
“You’ve woken up, Mr. Colin.” A maid with exquisitely near-perfect features and two cat ears politely greeted Colin, “Shall I prepare some afternoon tea?”
‘She’s really like a maid now…’
Colin nodded, indicating he’d like something to eat, feeling that he needed to put on some weight.
Otherwise, at one meter seventy-eight and just over one hundred pounds, his physique and appearance depended entirely on loose clothing to embellish, which was indeed not ideal.
Later, Colin looked over the parchment and saw the mission rewards were quite good: “Four Silver Task Certificates, over six thousand Points, and one Talent Lottery Ticket.
Unfortunately, the lottery ticket drew a rubbish Talent, so it’s as if I got nothing.”
“Besides that newly appeared mission to kill a Mutated Body, there’s also investigating ‘Hunger’; with this, the minor missions of ‘World Code-13’ are mostly cleared up…”
Looking at the much cleaner mission column on the parchment, Colin felt an inexplicable sense of accomplishment.
“I’ve received the rewards from those ‘Brave Ones’ missions too, but calling them up is a bit troublesome.”
Colin rubbed his forehead; Lin Yilan told him that she knew how to perform the surgery but didn’t dare to because she had limited clinical experience, with what little she had being from several years ago.
Moreover, the ‘Heroes’ weren’t just dealing with one or two cut muscle bundles; almost the entire musculature had been severed, so reconnecting it was no minor surgery.
Given the stringent conditions on-site, if bleeding or infection occurred, there was a high likelihood they would die on the spot.
While “Mark of Gluttony” did wonders for minor cuts, healing even cerebral hemorrhages and appendicitis quickly, it couldn’t do much once surgery was needed, even for simple dislocations, fractures, or even hernias.
To put it bluntly, its strength lay solely in healing effects…
Just then,
“Mr. Colin, you seem to be troubled by something. Is there something I can assist you with?” the cat-eared maid asked.
“Not really… Huh?”
Colin suddenly remembered that “Nano Intellectual Mechanisms” could be stored in the “Storage Room,” which would solve the surgery problem, right?
“Actually, there is something. Do you know how to perform surgery?”
“I can, but I specialize in precise surgeries, eradication of viruses or treatment of divine contamination. I don’t have much to offer for genetic diseases or ischemia caused by major bleeding,” she explained.
“This… Isn’t that just right?”
Colin decided to bring this cat-eared maid along next time.
At this moment, he realized he hadn’t properly understood the maid’s capabilities.
After closing the window and having a good understanding, Colin noticed that the capabilities of this “Nano Intellectual Mechanism” were somewhat omnipotent. It could farm, even integrate with plants to assist in nutrient absorption, it could perform medical treatment, even terminal cancer was not a problem for it, and it could help with construction…
The only regret was that he currently lacked the conditions to establish their production line.
Its self-assembling lines, prepared with enough materials, could only manufacture offspring mechs far inferior to itself, and due to their scant numbers here, it would take a considerable amount of time to establish a production line, possibly years.
By the time the line was perfected to copy the Nano Intellectual Mechanism itself, the year might have rolled around to 2044.
And she still had tens of tons of Nano Intellectual Mechanism left in “The Seventh Box Garden World,” which Colin couldn’t retrieve.
“Seems I have to wait until the national level overcomes this technology.”
Colin glanced at the box on the floor, took a deep breath, took out his phone to hurry Old Master Wu to send someone over to collect the goods, but then, feeling something, he looked out the window and locked eyes with someone.
A middle-aged figure in a black hat, black clothes, and black eyes, standing with a cane, with many strange black threads trailing behind him connected to who knows what…
He stood on a streetlamp, nodding to Colin who sat at home.
The people around seemed to not notice this man on the streetlamp.
And in that instant, Colin was certain this was an Eighth Level “Fate Propeller” among the Extraordinary Ones.
.
.
.
ps: A bit unfortunate, not successful, 908 votes, but it was the closest attempt yet.
Also, regarding the feedback from everyone, I will try to pay attention as much as possible.

chapters.title: Chapter 273 - 273 271 Small Win Medium Win Big Win
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 273: Chapter 271: Small Win, Medium Win, Big Win. Chapter 273: Chapter 271: Small Win, Medium Win, Big Win. “I am Xu Duojin, sent here on the orders of Mr. Wu. He told me there is an important matter requiring my presence. May I have the permission to enter the room you’re in?”
Standing atop a street lamp, the “Fate Propeller,” an Extraordinary One, touched his hat and gestured slightly towards Colin. Even though there was some distance between them, it seemed as if Colin could hear his voice.
But upon closer thought, it was as if he hadn’t heard him, yet if he were to say he hadn’t heard, it felt almost the same as if he had.
There was an inexplicably mysterious feeling. Colin pondered for a moment and felt that if he had to describe it, it would be akin to hearing.
He guessed it was probably some technique of the “Fate Propeller.”
‘This question seemed like a request for opinion, fulfilling some mystic requirement. I feel that if I refused, perhaps he would not truly enter.’
The thought flashed through his mind, but Colin did not rush to agree. He took out his cell phone and, after checking that Old Master Wu had indeed replied with a message stating someone would come to retrieve something, he then pointed to a sofa in the living room:
“Please, have a seat there.”
“Thank you, please wait a moment,” the visitor said.
Just when Colin thought he would employ some technique to fly straight in.
Colin saw him jump to the ground and then wait for the pedestrian light at the crosswalk, after which he made his way to the building, somehow opened the complex’s gate, and walked in. Soon enough, there was a “thud” at the living room door.
‘Damn it, if you weren’t going to come in directly, what the hell was the point of climbing up that lamppost…’
Colin muttered in his mind, then instructed the Cat Maid to open the door and let Xu Duojin in.
“Mr. Wu is tied up with some matters and thus sent me to speak with you in his stead. Rest assured, from the moment we met, I am under the influence of his power, and the decisions I make are equivalent to his own.”
Equivalent to his own—could it be a power similar to the “Script Book”? Colin remembered that upon his initial return, Old Master Wu had proactively mentioned that he had implanted a “script” into that displaced Eighth Level “Agent.”
The only issue was that the script was poorly written, and the other party realized it immediately and fled.
‘So, a high-level user of the ‘Book of Fate’ can also use the ‘Script Book’s power to a certain degree? The relationship between these books seems deeper than I thought.’
Colin pondered with intrigue and nodded, “Let’s get straight to the point.”
“This person…” Xu Duojin looked at the cat-eared maid and felt… that she didn’t quite seem human.
But then again, not many of the senior Extraordinary Ones looked human.
“Don’t mind her, just talk,” Colin said, not intending to go into detail about his Nano Maid.
“Alright!” The middle-aged looking Xu Duojin smiled, “Firstly, regarding your proposal of obtaining more points through task-oriented cooperation in exchange for medications, although it differs slightly from our expected exchange, we can accept it.
“Of course, there are some details that should be mentioned, like the extremely difficult side-quests, which we refuse to take part in.”
These past few days, they had roughly understood some of the situations within the Bonfire Company, knowing the high fatality rate of these tasks, and many involved special transportation which the officials could not assist with, so they were better off not accepting.
“No, that won’t do.”
Colin shook his head, about to speak, when he suddenly felt something influence him for a moment, and then he heard the other party say, “If the respective ratio can be pressed down to 0.01%, then we can accept.”
‘Pretty good, that’s nearly what I wanted to say…’
Colin squinted his eyes and thought of the inexplicable sensation of being spied upon, instantly realizing the cause.
He didn’t speak, just stared at the other party, and after a few seconds of a stand-off, Xu Duojin, with an apologetic tone, said, “Sorry, it’s a matter of habit, I assure you I will not use any abilities next time.”
“Fine, I hope our talks can be free from trickery.”
Colin didn’t intend to pursue it further—when Old Wu had used these methods, Colin couldn’t detect them, had no evidence, and only had a vague suspicion afterwards. Even with suspicions, he wasn’t sure, but with this Eighth Level individual, he could feel it.
Afterward, they continued discussing some intricacies, and Colin moved on to the negotiation of the second cooperative project:
About the exchange of raw materials from official personnel to the company for finished prop items,
both parties were inclined to reach an agreement, and negotiations were almost completed without much discussion. Officials would prepare a corresponding inventory and then hand it over to Colin, who would reciprocate through mission assignments to Lady Bunny.
At that time, she would evaluate and inform them of how many props the raw materials could be exchanged for, what kind of props they were likely to be, and the expected delivery cycle.
If they could accept, they would; if not, they would decline.
“You may need many containment subjects of the same level before you can exchange for a single prop, and it’s not a small chance that you’ll need three or four for one. I guess I should give you a heads-up on this,” Colin reminded.
“No problem, five or six for one is fine, not to mention three or four,”
Xu Duojin laughed, appearing very generous—in fact, not just five or six, but the upper echelon had given him a baseline that even eleven would work!
After all, many containment subjects were merely that because they had no solution for them.
Sometimes, while some containment subjects may seem harmless to humans and animals, it’s possible that their execution could lead to unexpected disasters.
For example, the officials once detained an almost unkillable “Wild Boar” with immense destructive power and a strong desire to kill. They thought that executing it would suffice, but after the execution, its blood turned into a pool from which numerous abnormalities emerged…
After the loss of a Level Seven Personnel’s life and the containment of the blood pool, they realized that the “Wild Boar” might be some sort of seal. After that, they became extremely cautious about completely executing certain things.
If they could contain it, they would; if they really couldn’t, they would try to open some special tunnels to throw it into another world…
Now, with the “Bonfire Company” actively willing to deal with such matters, they were too pleased to even consider refusal.
In any case, as long as the trade was concluded, and the trouble resolved, it would be a success. Whatever props they obtained could be considered a bonus, and they could only win big or win small in the end.
Colin was unaware of this, but he was also happy that the trade was concluded; after all, he handled transactions for both parties.
In this exchange, there would always be something for him to gain.
One could say that after the transaction was complete, all three parties were happy, with the only ones likely unhappy being those strange abnormalities destined to become either props or kindling…
“Here is the contract, take a look at the specifics,”
