Of course, if he wanted, he could get one from the official source, but the fragments provided officially always came with a bit of “poison,” contaminating anyone except the ‘Fate Propeller’ who used them.
“I’ll do it. I have two of them.”
Dog Brother closed his eyes slightly, using the fragment to predict what might be encountered if the ship headed in that direction.
[Hours later, the submarine arrives at this piece of seabed land, and as soon as you arrive, you are attacked by a sea anemone creature hundreds of meters in size, with millions of dense tentacles reaching out for you.]
[Despite your combined efforts to kill it using various means, the submarine is severely damaged.]
[At that moment, you also realize that this is not any ordinary seabed land, but a floating underwater island in deep water, with a large number of marine creatures and a self-sustaining biological chain.]
[In the struggle with those creatures, you manage to escape with difficulty, but soon after, you are pulled back into the fray by countless attacks, and the submarine is eventually destroyed, leaving you exposed in the sea, fleeing in all directions.]
[You manage to barely survive for a while using props, and during your escape, you discover traces of civilization buildings, regrettably, they seem to have perished due to some kind of invasion.]
[You don’t know their fate, but you…]
[You die.]
[After reaching the limits of your props, your body is enveloped by a lucky sea star, and for the first time, you understand how a sea star feeds.]
…
“It’s very dangerous over there, with lots of marine creatures. Let’s take a detour,”
Dog Brother relayed the information he had received to the others.
Based on the content above, going there would mean certain death. No, to be precise, others might not be sure, but he definitely was.
“Alright, let’s take a detour.”
Colin was curious about the ruins of that civilization but their mission had nothing to do with it; there was no need to stubbornly head that way.
Under his command, the submarine did not head in that direction…
The game of cards continued, followed by more rounds and blocking.
However, at that moment, Colin’s hand, which was about to place a card, suddenly paused; he felt a danger approaching.
“Warning! An abnormal creature is approaching!”
Little Maid’s warning also reached his ears.
“Stop playing, something’s coming!”
Colin tossed his hand of cards forward with a glance, stepping up to raise the alert to the others.
“Clang clang clang!”
From outside the submarine, the sound of something chipping away could be heard.
And there was a large number of these sounds, at least twenty different sources!
“So many, and so close, yet I only noticed now. It seems the underwater environment does impose significant restrictions on me, and there’s no scent for me to analyze…”
Colin frowned and followed the noises with his eyes, sensing that these creatures were not particularly strong.
He walked swiftly toward the closest source, pressing his right hand against the submarine’s steel wall, and with his left hand on a Golden Card, a force of repulsion burst forth through the wall, pushing the water aside and revealing a strange creature in front of the glass window—
It had three pairs of blood-red eyes, skin as oddly rough as that of a stonefish, and two strong, frog-like hands, one of which held a very sturdy-looking white stone.
“Kill.”
Colin issued orders in a simple and decisive manner.
It was unclear what those things were, but there was something off about that stone—it had managed to dent the outer hull of the submarine!
On one side, Dog Brother decisively pulled out a dagger and stabbed it into his palm, after which two Four-Armed Citizens stood up from the shadows nearby.
First, their figures blurred as they ignored all matter to enter the sea, and then they began the slaughter of the monsters.
One by one, the grotesque corpses of the creatures appeared before everyone’s eyes…
Meanwhile, the Little Maid also abandoned part of the area and began operating the specially made weapons on the submarine to attack these monsters.
“They’re not particularly strong, but they are especially troublesome, and there are a lot of them,” he said.
Colin noticed that within just a few minutes inside the submarine, there were already many pot-holes.
If they didn’t stop them, it was possible that the submarine could actually be breached by those broken stones.
“Dog Brother, Wave Rider, Naming is Hard, you guys go protect the engine room. I’ll handle this side; Tao Tie, stick with me.”
To avoid any accidents, Colin moved people around, because it wouldn’t be good if the nuclear power somehow blew up.
“According to the analysis, they probably discovered us because of the ‘sonar’ and launched the attack. There are about two hundred or more of them, and in addition, many strange creatures seem to be approaching this area.”
“Can we break free?”
“We can, but we’ll need to turn off the sonar and lights and concentrate all Nano Intellectual Mechanisms on some energy transmission lines and the propellers to achieve an overburdened operating effect. During this period, we won’t be able to maintain defense.”
After all, the Nano Maid was only so big and couldn’t cover every area.
“Leave safety to us. For now, just focus on making an escape,” they said.
In a normal environment, Colin could kill these creatures easily, but the situation was special now, and it wasn’t easy for him to make a move, so it was best to avoid them if possible.
Soon, the interior of the submarine suddenly went dark as all the lights were turned off, and power converged on the propellers, which were wrapped by Nano Intellectual Mechanisms.
In the darkness, the speed of the submarine increased rapidly within a minute, leaving the chaotic area in a short time…
Due to the extremely high speed, the temperature in the submarine’s space rose rapidly due to the engine room’s overburdened operation. In the sweltering heat, everyone could still clearly feel the submarine’s incessant vibrations, like a Wuling Hongguang forced to drive at two hundred kilometers an hour, seemingly ready to fall apart at any moment.
Finally, after confirming that they had left the dangerous area, their speed began to slow.
The tension in everyone’s hearts eased slightly…
“Have we left?” a question came.
Colin turned his head to see, in the darkness, Dog Brother’s figure was approaching his own and Arsonist’s side.
“I don’t know, but there’s something I need to tell you…”
Colin faced him and said, but for some reason, right next to Colin, Tao Tie felt as though Colin seemed to be responding to the other person but was actually speaking to himself.
“What is it?”
Colin clenched his fist with his right hand, took a forceful step forward, and threw a punch at Dog Brother’s head, not holding back in the slightest.
A heavy thud.
With that, the head burst upon impact…
A fiery blaze erupted from within the corpse.
“Something has invaded.”
Amid the flickering flames, Colin turned his cold gaze to Tao Tie beside him, causing the latter to catch his breath, his hairs standing on end, fearful that the next second the punch would land on his own head.
.
.
.
ps: The update time is most likely going to be adjusted to during the day.

chapters.title: Chapter 284 - 284 282 Anthropomorphized Deep Sea Creatures
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 284: Chapter 282 Anthropomorphized Deep Sea Creatures. _1 Chapter 284: Chapter 282 Anthropomorphized Deep Sea Creatures. _1 Boom.
The sound of a headless, burning corpse hitting the ground momentarily brought Tao Tie back to reality. Staring at the soft, boneless body writhing on the ground like a mollusk, he realized what Colin had meant.
“You mean something invaded and imitated or replaced him?”
“If nothing’s gone wrong, then it should be correct.”
Colin nodded, took a deep breath, and was fairly certain that there were several independently moving individuals aboard the submarine.
At that moment, the voice of the Nano Intellectual Mechanism Maid resounded in his ear:
“Mr. Colin, I have detected that parts of the submarine have been drilled with tiny breaches. We have now confirmed our departure from the danger zone. Should we prioritize stopping and repairing the submarine’s hull?”
Could it be that they drilled in through these breaches? But these chunks of rock actually punctured the submarine; do the monsters here have some kind of critical hit bonus against the submarine?
As Colin’s thoughts flashed, he immediately ordered the Little Maid:
“Go ahead and fix the hull first, lest the submarine bursts apart later. I’ll take care of the things inside the submarine.”
He first glanced at the hall ahead to ensure no enemies were hiding, then headed straight towards Dog Brother and the others in the engine room, while Tao Tie followed behind him. As for “The Light Chaser,” he had disappeared again without trace.
However, they had only gotten halfway when Colin saw the figure of “Naming is Hard” frantically rushing toward them:
“Not good! Something has broken in!”
“Hmm.”
Colin looked at the figure, nodded, and then raised his fist, striking its head with a punch.
Immediately, the “employee’s” head exploded, and it fell to the ground.
The headless body transformed into some kind of invertebrate mollusk, constantly twisting on the ground like a bizarre humanoid starfish, but it didn’t last long before it quickly dried up under the flames…
With a thud, Colin kicked the corpse away and, as he approached the door of the engine room, heard his own voice:
“Dog Brother, what are you doing? Hurry up and open the door! The danger’s been cleared!”
“This time we are the real deal!”
It wasn’t just his voice; Tao Tie also heard his own voice and saw a suspected clone of himself frantically banging on the door, attempting to deceive the people inside into coming out.
When Colin arrived, the two imposters turned their heads to look at the original, their bodies began to tear, ready to launch an attack; but the next second, a surge of scorching flame engulfed the two monsters in a sea of firelight…
“Counterfeit goods really aren’t much good.”
Colin walked forward at an unhurried pace; it was unclear how strong these monsters were in attack, but their defense seemed pretty low.
Even now, Tao Tie following Colin still didn’t quite understand how Colin managed to instantly identify the enemies upon meeting them. These creatures sounded almost exactly like the originals, and even the scents they emitted were highly deceptive.
But the timing wasn’t right, and he didn’t rashly approach to ask.
“Open the door.”
Colin indeed had no intention of immediately explaining; flames surged around his body, and with his revolver in his right hand, he came to the door and, without a word, kicked the steel-reinforced watertight door twice.
Suddenly, there was a stir from behind the door.
“Are you really going to open it? What if it’s like before…”
“Yeah, hiss, how can you be sure…”
“No, this attitude, this familiar ‘knocking’ method, that’s right, it’s Brother Shunzi, I’ve never seen him use his hands to knock in my life!”
Muffled conversations came from behind the door; it seemed they had learned their lesson, but it looked as though they had solved the issue.
Soon, the sound of the watertight door’s bolts turning could be heard.
Dog Brother and two others appeared behind the door, looking somewhat disheveled. “Naming is Hard” had his arm’s skin corroded, with veins and bones exposed to the air, as if it had been soaked in sulfuric acid, visibly wincing in pain.
Behind them, several soft bodies cut into pieces were wriggling on the ground.
Colin first glanced over their heads to make sure the IDs were all present, then he looked behind them.
“That was close, the power room itself wasn’t too damaged.”
Colin sighed with relief, since the device was somewhat a nuclear one, if it were seriously damaged, who knows how much longer they would be delayed…
Then, a flame flowed out from under Colin’s feet, spreading towards those bodies that had not completely died off yet like ivy, completely eradicating them.
Following behind Colin, Tao Tie had also discerned something notable along the way; he noticed that these impostors all had one thing in common, that although they were well-disguised, they did not display the company’s ID over their heads.
Brother Shunzi probably acted on this basis when he made his move.
‘He’s really decisive. Even if I’d noticed, I might have been on guard, but I wouldn’t necessarily have been 100% sure, at least not so certain.’ Tao Tie reflected internally.
Unaware of what the man behind him was thinking, Colin, having dealt with the remnants of the monsters inside, turned his attention to Naming is Hard. He thought for a moment and took out an item from his pocket:
“Here… take this. Recover a bit on your own, and if possible, buy a BUFF from that guy.”
Naming is Hard took it handily and after seeing the information for the item named “Gluttony Power Mark,” he jerked his head up to look at Colin, his expression somewhat moved—
Although there was a collegial relationship among company employees, they generally wouldn’t really treat each other as comrades during missions.
After all, it’s not uncommon for colleagues to stab each other in the back to burst gold coins.
Colin’s gesture undeniably warmed his heart.
“Hurry up and recover, so you don’t slow us down later.”
Colin reminded with a frown. The reason he was willing to lend the item was simple: first, he didn’t want the other to become a real drag, and second, aside from needing to keep replenishing their stomachs, using the item wouldn’t cause any wear and tear.
In the end, if the other party really had any designs on his item, he had absolute confidence that he could teach these people how to behave in their next life and recover what belonged to him.
If he couldn’t beat those various abnormalities, could he really not beat a few small employees?
Facing Colin’s words, the employee thanked him sincerely, then asked, “How do I buy a BUFF from that F Level Employee?”
He didn’t yet know the specifics of how to go about it, but just as he spoke,
“The Light Chaser” appeared beside them in an unknown manner.
Following that, a considerate piece of information appeared before his eyes.
[Would you like to spend 500 points?]
“Ah, this…”
Colin pursed his lips on the side; this guy would go invisible when in trouble, and even he might not be able to find him, but as soon as someone wanted to shop, he’d appear in an instant.
Quite professional!
“Mr. Colin, the submarine’s hull maintenance has been completed.” The voice of the Little Maid with cat ears appeared at his ear.
“Then run a check on the submarine to see if there’s any fish that slipped through the net. If there aren’t any, continue with the plan.”
Colin silently gave the instruction, then glanced at “The Light Chaser” without a trace, quietly asking, “Still no way to handle him?”
The bodies of all present were more or less infiltrated with some “Nano Intellectual Mechanism,” but “The Light Chaser” was an exception; the nanomachines had never been able to start on him.
And it seemed that the reason they couldn’t get started wasn’t because they were detected, but because they simply couldn’t find his actual existence.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 285 - 285 283 World Code-4_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 285: Chapter 283 “World Code-4″_1 Chapter 285: Chapter 283 “World Code-4″_1 “Still unable to locate its physical entity,” the little maid responded honestly.
“Strange, even entities like Dog Brother who escape into alternate dimensions, or those like me who lower their presence, have a not-so-small chance of being discovered. Yet, this ‘The Light Chaser’ still can’t be touched.”
Colin was secretly surprised, not knowing whether this “The Light Chaser” was truly that powerful or had some kind of powerful artifact at their disposal.
If it was the latter, he guessed it must definitely be a Golden Artifact.
Unfortunately, no information on the matter could be obtained from the other party, so Colin didn’t dwell on it. After giving some commands for their next move, he resumed the exploration mission.
Now the progress of the mission had filled one third, so they should be able to complete the mission after enduring a little longer.
This time, they did not use sonar; even more, not long after sailing, they turned off the lights because just now, Colin and the others had seen a monstrous creature in the sea more than a hundred meters long, seemingly attracted by the light.
The creature was like a gigantic spider, at its center, a massive eyeball.
Colin and his people were ready for combat then, but after turning off the lights, it seemed to lose interest in the area and, stirring the water with its limbs, slowly drifted away…
Thereafter, they did not use any searchlights besides the dim internal lights of the submarine.
Because no one knew how many of these enormous creatures there might be.
With several more like it, even if Colin really got going, he would be penalized.
And as they proceeded in darkness, the exploration progress slowed down significantly. To stave off boredom, Colin let the cat-eared maid become a game controller similar to those used by billionaires on a Titanic-like deep-sea tour, manipulating the submarine in the same manner as operating a game controller.
Unfortunately, there wasn’t much of Titanic to be seen here.
In the dark green deep sea, apart from occasionally spotting some peculiar things, there wasn’t much bizarre activity.
After playing for a while, Colin lost interest and was about to have the little maid take over.
That’s when he heard her say, “Mr. Colin, I’ve received a sonar signal that seems to be a distress call. Should we respond?”
“No need.”
Adhering to the principle that less is more, Colin didn’t even consider using the “Book of Fate: Fragment” to probe further and earnestly focused on the task at hand.
After all, the first part of the mission could be completed without actual contact.
The one thing they needed to be careful about was to keep themselves from being idle; otherwise, if they were quiet for too long, it felt like some incredibly eerie entity was calling out to them.
Of course, buying a BUFF could solve this problem, but everyone unanimously chose a more cost-effective method—
Playing Fight the Landlord, Golden Flower, Texas Hold’em.
Finally, after more than a dozen hours, while everyone was somewhat numbed by playing Fight the Landlord, Golden Flower, and Texas Hold’em, they simultaneously received a message in their minds.
[Mission “Unrest Beneath the Lightless Deep Sea (1/3)” completed, new mission “Find a Suitable Area to Establish a ‘Bonfire Sacrificial Ground'” issued, please check the mission panel for details.]
“Establish a ‘Bonfire Sacrificial Ground’?”
Colin’s eyebrows twitched, then he opened the mission panel and knew from the details of the mission that his speculation about the “Ascension Project” when he entered was confirmed!
[Trial Task – “Find a Suitable Area to Establish a ‘Bonfire Sacrificial Ground’ (2/3)”].
“Description”: The area has been identified as “World Code-4”, a special deep-water world. Due to certain reasons, information about this place has been lost, and you, as a special task force employee, will find a civilized place to establish a ‘Bonfire Sacrificial Ground’ and recover the knowledge of the old days.
“Requirement”: Gather a thousand initial believers or a hundred corpses of zealous ‘Bonfire Followers’ and establish a ‘Bonfire Sacrificial Site’ in a human settlement.
“Note”: When the conditions are met, it will be automatically established.
…
“‘World Code-4’.”
Seeing this text in the description, Dog Brother, Naming is Hard, Arsonist, and Surfing for Pigs all collectively fell silent for a moment—if nothing unexpected happened, this could, should, might, perhaps, possibly be…
Descent Project!
All the people present had participated in Colin’s “World Code-13” elective trial project, and even all acquired the Talent “Tyrant Body” after dying a hundred and eighty times or so, so they were not at all unfamiliar with this naming convention.
And it was at this moment that they suddenly remembered the familiar bell that had rung when they came in.
This is just…
Almost immediately, the four of them turned their gaze toward Colin in unison, with the last glimmer of hope lingering in their eyes.
If anyone had the right to speak about the “Descent Project,” it was undoubtedly Colin.
“It is indeed the Descent Project…”
Colin shattered everyone’s hope, causing the atmosphere inside the submarine to freeze.
“Why the hell do I have to do this kind of mission…” The Arsonist couldn’t help but howl in grief.
That “World Code-13” had cost him his life nearly forty times over, using over a hundred tons of various explosives, before he barely managed to complete it, and now he was actually taking part in the project!
This time there was only one life!
“We’re done for, this kind of mission, I have a feeling it’s not going to be a one-time thing, and if it turns into a permanent type, we’re really done for…” Naming is Hard couldn’t help the despair from showing in his eyes.
The high mortality rate of the “Descent Project” was such because if you didn’t die the first time, there’d be a second, and if not the second, then a third, until eventually you’d meet your end.
He really hadn’t expected that by doing a promotion mission, he wouldn’t run into an Out-of-Control Copy, but instead got tossed into the “Descent Project”!
“Wait, that’s not right. Among the twenty-something group instances for the D Level Promotion Mission, aside from the three Out-of-Control Copies, I haven’t heard about this one, what’s going on?” Naming is Hard looked utterly perplexed.
Seeing their expressions, Dog Brother managed a bitter smile: “That’s actually normal; promotion missions usually have two parts, the first one is a randomly assigned temporary mission, with uncertain content, but it typically has a sense of immediacy, then there’s a fixed instance assessment.
“What we’re doing now is one of those randomly assigned temporary ones.
“Those twenty-something group instances you mentioned should be in the next round after this mission ends.”
At this, they all thought back to the hardship when they participated in “World Code-13.” Even though they had completed it once, if they were to do that mission again now, they wouldn’t be sure they could make it through with their life intact.
The slap from the sky was still a nightmare for many, to the point where it would wake them from sleep, making them feel a heart-stopping hunger.
And now there was only one life…
If they didn’t encounter any trouble, that would be fine, but if something did happen, it was hard to say whether they could leave alive.
However, it was at this time, seeing that the atmosphere was turning gloomy and not conducive to teamwork, that Colin spoke up:
“Actually, there’s no need to worry. Even though it’s a ‘Descent Project,’ it’s not as difficult as you think during the first stage. From my experience, if we’re careful, the probability of survival is still quite high.”
The despondent people, upon hearing this, couldn’t help but question in their minds:
Not that difficult? Do you know what the “Descent Project” is? Do you understand the stakes of a mission with a ninety-nine percent mortality rate? Do you know how easy it is to die exploring unknown worlds? Who do you think you are?
They wanted to say this, but after thinking it over, oh, it seemed that the person in front of them was that one percent.
The one who had successfully carried out the “Descent Project” multiple times and cleared the Out-of-Control Copy, the hardcore badass.
Well, that settles it…
Everyone swallowed their words back down.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 286 - 286 284 With so much money hes bound to be
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 286: Chapter 284: With so much money, he’s bound to be tempted, right?_1 Chapter 286: Chapter 284: With so much money, he’s bound to be tempted, right?_1 “What should we do next? The mission requires us to establish a ‘Bonfire Sacrificial Site,’ but right now, let alone finding any believers, we can’t even see a single person…”
The Arsonist said helplessly about the current situation.
We’ve been running for so long, and while we’ve seen plenty of monsters, we haven’t spotted a single person…
‘Isn’t that unfortunate?’
Colin remembered the report from the Little Maid not long ago, which mentioned receiving a distress signal; all one could hope for was that the ones who sent the distress signal were still there after several hours had passed.
He did not conceal it and shared the intelligence with everyone.
Quickly, the group reached a consensus to check out the place first.
“Let’s head over there right now then, starting with a three-hour journey at the least. Discuss among yourselves who will use the ‘Book of Fate’ when the time comes.”
Excluding the Parchment that Dog Brother was using, everyone on the scene only had one each.
With a choice at hand, Colin did not plan on using the item first. It wasn’t that he was reluctant to use it but rather that he feared accidentally seeing something he shouldn’t.
Nowadays, the longer he stayed under the Deep Sea, the more he felt the Deep Sea Egg he had brought out from ‘The Seventh Box Garden World’ in his head seemed to be showing signs of wishing to hatch.
“Wait, Deep Sea, Deep Sea Egg; could it be that this mission is also influenced by this thing?”
Colin looked at the others and suddenly felt a bit guilty, as there was indeed a possibility.
The first phase of the mission involved gathering enough people and then loading into a group before randomly generating a suitable mission, unlike the second phase, which involved choosing a mission from a set of fixed instances, avoiding scenarios where a mission could be delayed for several years due to the lack of participants.
However, since they were already there, such an unhelpful conjecture wasn’t appropriate to express.
Colin thought for a moment and decided to ignore it.
After all, no one knew; there was no need to burden himself with blame.
“This egg… The ‘Father of the Deep Sea’ told me to find a suitable place for it to hatch, so is there a possibility that it has quietly interfered with something, leading us here on this mission?”
He remembered what that divinity-stripped entity had said—if he couldn’t find a suitable place, there was a certain probability that Colin himself would be directly absorbed by the egg.
However, since it entered his brain and had been inactive, Colin had temporarily forgotten about it.
Only now, with the Deep Sea Egg showing some activity, did he recall and begin to harbor a series of doubts.
“If there’s a chance to deal with this thing, it wouldn’t be a bad idea to hatch it right here.”
Colin had no objections to this, as whatever emerged from the egg, whether good or bad, wouldn’t matter as long as it was born outside of Earth.
As for what would become of the people from ‘World Code -4’—in such times, the Other World’s folks would just have to endure a bit more hardship.
“Although there’s a bit of a feeling, this thing doesn’t seem to have the intent to come out of my head, and I don’t know when it will emerge. I just hope its entrance isn’t too spectacular, not like an alien bursting out from inside me…”
Colin sighed, gathered his thoughts, and looked out the window at the flow of water parted by the advancing submarine, feeling somewhat relieved that he had a ‘Nano Intellectual Mechanism’ on him. Otherwise, they would probably have just been sitting in a scrapped submarine, waiting to die.
Without dwelling on it further, he gathered his resolve and quietly waited for the journey to end.
Meanwhile, in the vicinity of Colin, the unperceivable ‘Light Chaser’ sat in a corner, his gaze seemingly fixed on Colin from beneath the black hood.
Recently, there were several missions with substantial Points rewards, and for some reason, he always ended up grouped with the man before him.
Contrary to the previous occasions where things were unclear and hard to understand, today it seemed he could finally catch some words, though sporadic and mostly incomprehensible, possibly in another language—
Could it be that he indeed came from another world?
However, as he too possessed Parchment, was there a chance by bringing an item of sufficient level, combined with some Points, to complete an exchange?
The Bone Spur after all was the remains of a former Saint, which was stolen by some ‘Honest Knight’ who had, for reasons unknown, betrayed them, and it had been lost ever since.
Having finally found it, she was reluctant to give up so easily.
During this time, she had been frantically completing various tasks and, having already escaped the danger zone, she had saved up a considerable amount of points. If she offered all of it to exchange with the other party, he would probably agree to the trade, right?
The Light Chaser brought up the points he had painstakingly accumulated and took a glance.
201.5.
The substantial balance bolstered her confidence in the success of the transaction.
With so many points, he must be tempted, right?
…
“Report, Mr. Colin, I have pinpointed the location of the signal emitted by that submarine. They are roughly one hundred and forty-seven nautical miles in front of the submarine…”
“Very good.”
Upon receiving the report, Colin turned to look behind him, and then “It’s Hard to Pick a Name” stepped forward.
This time, it was his turn to use the “Book of Fate: Fragment”—
[About two hours later, you encounter the people who sent the distress signal. Their submarine is covered with various terrifying damages, as if they had just fled from some dangerous place, and the people onboard are full of despair.]
[After the initial conversation, you board their submarine and meet humans from this world for the first time. They have very robust muscles and pale skin, with exceptionally large pupils, but otherwise, they aren’t very different from humans.]
[It is only after your arrival that these people suddenly turn hostile and attack you, and only then do you realize it’s a trap.]
[However, Brother Shunzi seems to have been aware from the start and makes arrangements calmly. Although the enemies have some special methods, they fall short compared to you and are all easily subdued. Upon further understanding, you learn that these people are akin to pirates.]
[You don’t dwell on it too much and instead command them to lead you to the nearest human settlement from here.]
[Soon, you arrive at a human settlement, a special town mainly composed of underwater islands.]
[However, at this moment, something seems to be happening here.]
[Shortly after arriving on the island, your body is invaded, and your brain is overtaken in a short time.]
[You died.]
…
When the premonition ended, under the feedback from the “Book of Fate: Fragment,” “It’s Hard to Pick a Name” felt his brain writhing, and darkness fell upon him as if something truly was devouring his brain.
The brain was trembling!!!
This feeling was very unpleasant…
“‘Project Descent’ really is terrifying; so far, none who have used the ‘Book of Fate’ have survived…”
“It’s Hard to Pick a Name” lamented internally. For employees like them who advanced normally, using the “Book of Fate: Fragment” ten times wouldn’t necessarily result in a deadly outcome even once.
Yet, since coming here, both times he and “Miss Nell’s Dog” had used the item, they had died both times.
After a few seconds, once his brain’s thoughts stabilized and the discomfort faded away, he took a deep breath and began conveying the information he had gathered to the others.
“Heading to the nearest city, then being parasitized by something, and then dying?”
Leaning back in the captain’s chair, after hearing the report, Colin stroked his chin and immediately spoke, “Are you suggesting that the pirates are not an issue, but the issue lies with the nearest city we go to afterward?”
“Yes.”
“Then, let’s deal with that group of pirates first; don’t let them escape.”
…

chapters.title: Chapter 287 - 287 285
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 287: 285 Chapter 287: 285 “Boss! Quick, look, a big fat sheep has taken the bait! I’ve checked, it’s a nearly brand new T1 Civil Exploration Transport Submarine from Black Water Heavy Industry Plant No. 6, the Deep Sea Unicorn Whale!”
In the murky ink-green sea water, hidden within a submarine camouflaged by large floating debris, a pirate with pale skin excitedly reported to the “Little Dwarf” who had a small stature but thick limbs.
“Really?” The “Little Dwarf”‘s rough face showed an invigorating expression.
“Yes, I can confirm through the sonar image that it is indeed those black-haired guys’ Deep Sea Unicorn Whale, although the horn seems broken. As long as the engine of this model isn’t completely scrapped, just taking it apart could sell for at least three hundred and eighty thousand Marks!”
The pale-skinned pirate said excitedly.
“Good, good, good!”
Little Dwarf Peter became excited.
With this substantial sum, they could recruit many more people and grow stronger. The Sea Giant Pirate Group could become true giants, not just be mockingly called “Short Giants” like now!
At the thought, his blood surged, his head turned red, and his brain became somewhat muddled with excitement.
“You, come here, you’ll be my reward and help me cool down a bit!”
Little Dwarf pointed down his pants.
Thirty seconds later.
Little Dwarf Peter squinted, shuddering as his subordinate swallowed it all, feeling considerably calmer:
“Everyone hide well, don’t be discovered until I give the order. The Deep Sea Unicorn Whale has powerful and long-lasting propulsion. If we don’t catch it the first time, we won’t get another chance.
“If we succeed, you all will get a dose of physical enhancement drugs, and I’ll let you enjoy yourselves at Soul-Searing Bar for a day, no matter the drinks or the women, heh heh. I’ve got news that many of those women from the recently breached Station No. 7 have been sold there, and some are from noble families!
“But! If anyone scares them off, I swear, I’ll stuff a spotted electric eel up your ass and let it devour your insides!”
“Yes!”
All the pirates shouted in unison, their morale high.
…
Meanwhile, Colin and his companions arrived at their target location on their submarine, and as soon as they did, they saw a vessel much larger than theirs floating ahead.
It was severely damaged, and if it were on Earth, it would certainly have exploded.
But perhaps because the people of this world always lived under water, their submarine construction technology was outstanding, so that the vessel, despite looking heavily damaged, was not scrapped.
“Mr. Colin, within the nearby distance, there are nineteen submarines of various sizes approaching rapidly…”
“Let’s not pay attention to them for now, we’ll see when they get closer.”
Colin planned to follow the original script since the problem was with the city behind them and not the pirates they were facing now.
“Mr. Colin, that submarine is requesting communication, should we accept?”
“Let them through.”
Colin wanted to hear what they had to say, and soon, as the communication was established, he heard a moving female voice:
“This is Omor the Beast Deepwater Ship, I’m Captain Vina. Like you, we are people under Black Water Heavy Industry jurisdiction. Please, we need assistance. We hope you can take away the thirty or so crew members here. I promise to pay you three hundred thousand Marks as compensation!”
Black Water Heavy Industry? Marks?
Colin’s mind turned, guessing that Black Water Heavy Industry was probably a power in this world, and those Marks were likely the local currency.
However, having never encountered this, he didn’t have much concept of what the three hundred thousand Marks mentioned meant.
But this didn’t interfere with the conversation:
“Alright, I’m Captain Lin Ke. You guys wait; we’ll launch a rescue mission for you right away! Just make sure that the three hundred thousand Marks can be delivered!”“Of course!”
On the other end of the signal, the woman in the conversation revealed a cruel smile. She released the communication button: “This little man isn’t bad, just his voice alone is irresistible. After we grab them, he’s mine; I want to take good care of him!”
“Heh heh heh, maybe the boss will want him for himself, he also likes ones who cry out prettily…”
“I don’t care; I was here first!”
The woman had a cruel face, and the sound had prompted an impulse in her—no one could stop her!
Soon, when Colin’s submarine approached their vicinity, the “stranded” deep-sea ship suddenly lashed out. Dozens of chains shot out from its holes, instantly entangling the submarine worth millions of Marks like tentacles.
“What are you doing!” The little man’s angry voice came through the signal.
“Don’t worry, baby, we’ll be seeing each other very soon.”
The woman let out a cruel laugh.
At this distance, if the other party used torpedoes, they would also blow themselves up, so they were not worried at all.
Immediately after, more than a dozen small submarines, about ten to twenty meters in size, rushed in from all directions. Although they were much smaller, their speed was incredibly fast.
When they arrived outside Colin’s submarine, dozens of figures surged out of the various submarines like divers, rushing towards Colin’s side.
They carried all kinds of special tools in their hands and quickly opened several special hatches on the submarine, then swiftly climbed in to take control of various areas.
While they were in action, Colin’s Nano Intellectual Mechanism was also in motion, secretly approaching the power sources of those submarines to sabotage them and prevent the targets from escaping.
“Reporting to Mr. Colin, all Nano Intellectual Mechanisms are in position, assuring that we can corrode and destroy their submarine propellers at the first instance.”
“Very well, you may proceed to take them down.”
Colin sat in his chair without moving, and did not take action because these pirates were mediocre in strength.
Some pirates who had just invaded the submarine were stunned by its empty interior, which was unexpectedly undermanned, until they reached the command room at the front and saw five people there.
“You can’t run now! Hahaha, lads, go!”
Suddenly, a cruel smile appeared on the pirates’ faces, but it did not last long, as they saw that among the four people, aside from one guy sitting at the forefront without moving, three of them suddenly underwent a transformation, their muscles abnormally swelling, their body hair becoming thicker and longer…
Seconds later, these few individuals turned into a type of humanoid monster they had never seen before, covered in hair, with protruding faces and mouths like the wolf-fish of the icy seas.
Laughter moved from the pirates’ faces to those of the monsters…
Soon, a massacre feast began!
Aside from “Naming is Hard,” the other three simultaneously used their Talent “Tyrant Body,” swinging their claws to slaughter the pirates who had intruded here.
Amidst the shrill screams, pirate bodies were easily torn into pieces.
The ordinary firearms or blades the pirates wielded were incapable of breaking through the dense black hair, at most only able to cut a few strands.
“Retreat, retreat! Damn it! These people aren’t the prey—we are! Only the ship’s cannon can injure them!”
Some pirates fled the costly Deep Sea Unicorn Whale.
But what terrified them even more was that their proud deep-sea swimming skills were a complete joke in front of those three monsters; once the monsters gave chase, they swam five to six times faster than the pirates!
“Report, we have discovered a hidden submarine attempting to escape; it seems to be the head of these pirates. It is recommended to use Corpse Mountain to capture it.”
“Corpse Mountain? Can it swim too?”
Colin was surprised; he hadn’t expected the Little Maid to understand his cards better than he did, giving him an indescribably strange feeling.
However, considering that the Nano Intellectual Mechanism had been with Miss Bunny for a while, it may have been implanted with some information during that time.
As someone adept at listening to advice, Colin fished a Purple Name Card out of his pocket.
“Using all the corpses on the submarine as materials, activate this card’s effect to summon… ‘Smiling Mountain of Corpses’!”
Colin muttered with a good mood.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 288 - 288 286 Cultist Colin_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 288: Chapter 286 Cultist Colin_1 Chapter 288: Chapter 286 Cultist Colin_1 “Whoo!”
Little Fist Stone now appeared directly in the water, intending to let out a loud yell, but as soon as he opened his mouth, he swallowed a large gulp of sea water.
“Pfft!”
Spitting out the seawater, it swiftly made its way in a specific direction, its two enormous arms churning like propellers.
Eight hundred meters of water pressure hardly affected it at all.
In fact, its movements underwater were even more agile than on land.
Colin stood in the captain’s room, holding a thermos in his hand, while gazing out the window at the situation outside and making a rough judgment:
“The total number of enemies is around two to three hundred. Roughly four of us taking action, two hundred against four, the advantage is ours.”
Apart from Naming is Hard, the others could all transform directly into their beast forms, so the water pressure wasn’t much of an issue for them; and combined with some personal gear, they weren’t afraid of the submarines’ attacks. The whole process could be described as a unilateral crushing.
“The people from ‘World Code-4’ can hold their breath for an impressive amount of time, seven or eight minutes without any assistance. And their skin is really white… Is it due to the lack of light or some other reason? Is this place just the deep sea?”
Colin mused curiously for a moment. So far, their own experience has been such that whether they were ascending or descending, they could never see the seabed or the surface, always remaining at the “depth” of “eight hundred meters of water pressure” by Earth’s standards.
“Speaking of which, ‘World Code-13’ also features a rather unique astronomical phenomenon, with a clear distinction between day and night. Here, however, it can almost be said to be an endless stretch of water.”
“The company seems to have a say in ‘naming’ things, like ‘Box Garden World’, ‘Script City’ and such. I wonder if this ‘World Code’ has some other significance…”
“Tsk, but I don’t know about the rest. One thing I can be sure of is if there’s no hidden meaning, then judging by the sequence, there are at least thirteen ‘World Codes’…”
Colin pursed his lips, beginning to be curious about what the other worlds looked like and also how Earth was named within the company…
Besides, as far as he could tell, the company’s employees didn’t all necessarily come from Earth.
The Light Chaser who had joined their team this time was one example.
“No, not just whether they are from Earth, they might not even be human.”
Colin looked around the captain’s quarters and did not see The Light Chaser, but combining that with the report from the Nano Intellectual Mechanism that they were unable to find his physical body, it was highly probable he wasn’t human.
After all, since his appearance, the individual had been invisible. If it was the effect of a tool, it would have lasted too long.
The great likelihood was that it was a special trait of a non-human species…
“Speaking of which, why is such a strong employee still F Level to this date? Could it be true as he says, that he isn’t good at combat but only proficient in survival techniques and buffing? And so he is stuck?”
Colin thought about it carefully, it seemed apart from that time in Passionate Paradise where he used some unknown method to either lure or force the creature to leave, he really hadn’t seen The Light Chaser use any legitimate offensive methods.
Moreover, considering the honest and simple nature of the people from ‘World Code-13’ who never lie, it might actually be that he was telling the truth.
However, Colin didn’t continue to dwell on this issue, as the battle was about to end.
Smiling Mountain of Corpses went after the pirate leader’s submarine alone and brought back all the key targets.
At this moment, the water in Colin’s thermos was still warm.
Sometime later, as prisoner after prisoner was captured and brought onto the Deep Sea Unicorn Whale where Colin was, harsh shouts resonated within the cabin:
“Hands on your head, squat in the corner, don’t move!”
Dog Brother, with a somewhat androgynous voice, sharply scolded the prisoners in the cabin, causing rows of pirates to squat trembling in the corners of the submarine, not even daring to breathe too loudly…
Because these pirates knew all too well that the individuals behind them were exceptionally bloodthirsty and brutal; they looked like people, but they were definitely not human!
It was as if some kind of “sea wolf” monster covered in seaweed!
“Which one of you is the leader?”
Colin sat at the forefront of the captain’s cabin and asked.
As his words fell, there was no response. Colin frowned, pulled out his pistol, but it was at that moment that a man with short limbs but very muscular, much like a dwarf, seemed to finally not be able to stand the pressure and spoke with a trembling voice:
“I am…”
Thinking of the monster that had burst in earlier, he had none of his previous arrogance and did not dare to hide.
“Do you know where there is a human settlement?”
Colin spoke calmly, without too much emotion, flipping the gun in his hand.
Although he was in a different world, fortunately, a bullet could still make a pirate reform and start anew.
“I know, I know!”
The little dwarf Peter quickly said, “I know all the seaports in this sea area. I can take you to any seaport!”
“Which is the nearest seaport from here? How long will it take to get there?”
“About four hundred nautical miles, with your vessel, it would only take less than ten hours to arrive there. If you need, I can be your navigator and take you there…”
As long as you can spare me… Little Dwarf Peter hadn’t finished speaking when Colin interrupted him.
“Good, we won’t go to this closest one. How about the other one?”
Colin directly rejected that direction. Although he did not know exactly what was there, the “Book of Fate: Fragment” had confirmed there was an issue, so naturally, they couldn’t go there.
“Uh.” Little Dwarf Peter was taken aback but said no more and continued to introduce to Colin.
The second port was quite a bit farther, about a thousand nautical miles away, and it might take a day’s time to arrive.
And while speaking, he realized that these people seemed a bit odd.
It was as if they didn’t know much about this sea area, no, about the world in general, to ask whether “Water Island” was floating in the water and if it could drift away…
The question left him somewhat speechless; any sea person should know, almost all “Water Islands” never change position unless they are destroyed—a common sense fact.
Moreover, these people would ask about such obscure words as “sea surface” and “seabed”…
Those were terms only mentioned in some Church teachings, yet in this group’s mouths, they seemed to exist for real.
In any case, Little Dwarf Peter could not imagine what the world above the sea surface or below the sea bed was like because, in his view, the world was clearly composed entirely of an endless ocean!
Because of these questions, Pirate Peter had already categorized Colin and his group as part of some insane cult.
Most importantly, he had realized that this submarine, which typically required at least fifty crew, actually had only five people on board.
This indicated that there was a not small chance the submarine was commandeered by them…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 289 - 289 287 Peeking from the Deep Sea_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 289: Chapter 287 Peeking from the Deep Sea_1 Chapter 289: Chapter 287 Peeking from the Deep Sea_1 Of course, although that’s what he thought, Peter didn’t show it. He was afraid the other party would shoot him with that oddly shaped weapon that was unrecognizable as to which factory it came from.
“You mean to say that theoretically, if we proceed in any direction and keep going straight, we might eventually come back to this starting point?”
Colin asked curiously.
“Yes… This is the conclusion reached by the great pirate Soloros!” Little Dwarf Peter said somewhat proudly.
So, something that even forces couldn’t manage to do had been confirmed by them, the pirates.
“Hmm, that’s quite interesting.”
Could this world be akin to a Mobius strip, but as a sea world?
Little Dwarf Peter added, “However, if you want to try it, it’s very difficult to achieve because very few people possess the strength of Soloros to keep moving in one direction without stopping.
“After him, many others attempted the same, but very few succeeded.
“Speaking of which, the great pirate Soloros reportedly said before he died that at the end of this path, he buried a treasure…”
Why does this smell so strongly of ‘One Piece’…
Colin looked at the fellow in front of him, who seemed to be getting carried away, and couldn’t help but make a comment.
He even wondered if this might be a colleague too.
But he dismissed that thought because “Soloros” lived a hundred years ago, and the timelines for the joke didn’t match up.
However… To say it is absolutely impossible is not completely true.
As for now, Colin felt that the timing in worlds outside of Earth, or more precisely, in other worlds related to the company, were a bit off.
But he didn’t dwell on these meaningless thoughts any further.
“Bang!”
Colin fired a shot to interrupt Little Dwarf’s speech, “Alright, lead us to that second underwater island you mentioned.”
“Okay, okay, okay…”
Little Dwarf Peter promptly took out a nautical chart from his pocket and then a very special precision instrument that had grids like compasses on top along with many other counters that seemed to indicate changes in water pressure and so on.
Although the deviation in water pressure here was not significant, there was still a bias.
It seemed that the pirate was judging their current position by comparing the various numerical values on it.
Colin couldn’t quite understand it, but it didn’t matter, “Xiao Yin, try to crack this thing.”
They would need their own navigator…
Before long, having confirmed their direction, Colin and his group commenced their movements again.
This time, Colin’s team wasn’t just a lone “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale” anymore; it was joined by seven or eight pirate submarines, over a hundred living pirates, and the nutrients for over two hundred bodies from Corpse Mountain.
The hundred or so pirates couldn’t exactly be called good or bad, only that the evil deeds they committed were somewhat fewer.
Colin had given them a chance to mend their ways. Besides, there were some like the female first mate with a penchant for merciless killing, to whom, adhering to a people-first principle, he also gave a chance to start anew.
What surprised him was that besides his killing and, well, somewhat odd sexual orientation, this Little Dwarf Peter didn’t have that twisted, bloodthirsty penchant for cruelty…
Moreover, to establish his authority, this guy had killed more pirates than regular folks.
In a sense, one could say he was “saving the country by a curve.”
After everything ended, Colin would still grant the chance he promised to the other party.
Suddenly, the submarine halted momentarily. Just as Colin was feeling puzzled, the voice of the Nano Intellectual Mechanism appeared in his ear:
“Mr. Colin, several control rods in the submarine’s reactor have reached their usage limit. The estimated remaining usage time is twelve hours and fifty-seven minutes…”
“Control rods? Aren’t there backups on the submarine?”
Colin wasn’t very familiar with this, but normally, such things would have backups.
“There are, but the backup ‘control rods’ were already damaged and corroded, rendered unusable before we arrived here. The ones on the other pirates’ ships don’t match this submarine and are also unusable. Moreover, their submarines also need maintenance…”
“Alright, a dozen or so hours should be enough.”
Colin pondered for a moment, thinking that if nothing unexpected happened, reaching the second harbor should be no issue.
But what he didn’t expect was that upon arriving at the appropriate distance and time, they used the “Book of Fate: Fragment” again, only to find that something seemed off with this second harbor.
[…]
[Walking through this special town, you are sent to find control rods, only to quickly discover that this harbor doesn’t have the model you need. However, it’s not a big problem, because you plan to do your preaching here.]
[Just as you’re about to find a suitable place to “Pass the Flame” with your colleague, you feel something’s not right.]
[Suddenly, you see your colleague ‘Picking-a-name-is-tough’ walking unsteadily. As you’re about to ask what’s wrong, you feel dizzy, and there’s a sharp pain in your brain, as if something is gnawing at your mind.]
[In the midst of unspeakable agony, you see “Choosing a Name is So Hard” throat bulge, followed by several slimy red tendrils wriggling out…]
[It seems he has been infected, invaded by something.]
[Not far away, a battle suddenly erupts, and you see a massive blaze shooting into the sky. Brother Shunzi, bathed in flames, appears to be facing a formidable enemy, fighting against some terrifying entity.]
[But you no longer have the time to be shocked or to wonder what is happening, because at this moment, you know you are beyond salvation…]
[Many things are approaching you, and unwilling to accept such a simple death, you pull out your ultimate masterpiece that embodies all your efforts, theoretically equivalent to 500 TNTs, in the very last moment.]
[You don’t get to see the dazzling art that now reverberates around you.]
[You are dead.]
…
“Arsonist Tao Tie” rubs his temples while sharing the news he has received.
“Another gone cold?”
Colin watches the other rub his forehead and does the same.
He hadn’t expected that two nearby cities seemed to have been attacked by some kind of enemy.
‘In both instances recorded in the ‘Book of Fate,’ teammates died from being parasitized or infected. What thing is launching a major attack on the humans here? From what can be inferred from these two instances, that thing is not weak; even I must treat it as a serious threat.’
With several thoughts flashing through his mind, Colin waves his hand to signal the submarine, known to the pirates as the “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale,” to stop.
“How much longer can our submarine operate?”
“About six hours.”
“Six hours, huh.”
Colin looks at Little Dwarf Peter, who is tied up: “Besides this port, you mentioned another nearby one within a six-hour journey. Are there any other sea ports within that range?”
“Within six hours?” The little dwarf is puzzled, but still asks to have the ropes untied from his body. He takes out the sea chart for comparison, then checks again with precise instruments.
“There are none.”
“Click.”
Colin spins the cylinder of the revolver in his hand, alarming Peter, who suddenly remembers something:
“I remember now, not long ago, ‘Pirate City’ passed by here. If you don’t mind, that counts as a sea port too. Let’s measure the distance—you can get there in five hours, no need for six…”
“Passed by? Didn’t you say sea ports usually stay on immovable water islands?”
“No, I said most… there are a small number that are movable, ‘Refugees City’ is one of them. It has been transformed into a mobile place by a major pirate and is also called ‘Pirate’s Paradise City,’ where many pirates and Federation fugitives gather…”
Peter says anxiously, “If nothing unexpected happens, that ‘Pirate City’ will be there for the next few days to rest. If you’re planning to replace the ‘control rods,’ they have them too.”
“Then… let’s head to the ‘Pirate’s Paradise City’ you mentioned.”
After pondering for a moment, Colin makes his choice—not that there is much choice to begin with.
Whether or not they find any Believers there, they first need to repair the submarine. If it wasn’t for the second port lacking “control rods,” he might even be tempted to storm in, steal them, and flee.
However, since those bandits from “Pirate City” have them, it’s no problem to go there and snatch them.
This time, just three hours later, they detect the enormous outline of a water island on their radar—
“Refugees City.”
This time, Colin is unable to use the “Book of Fate: Fragment,” because although the users come from different subjects, it seems…
He has an inexplicable hunch that the third user might trigger some undesirable events.
It’s not about triggering “The Dice of Probability,” but something else…
Something is likely to follow some kind of guidance and lock onto them, launching a pursuit.
He feels this strongly.
Colin is keenly aware that while observing others through the “Book of Fate: Fragment,” there’s a certain probability of being observed by the enemy too.
Once, “0-9 ‘Hunger'” had directly attacked him following the “Book of Fate: Fragment.”
This time, having used it twice in relation to the same anomaly, it might have already caught the attention of something.
.
.
.
ps:
I recommend the book “Alighieri News Agency.”

chapters.title: Chapter 290 - 290 288 Seven Pirates_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 290: Chapter 288 Seven Pirates_1 Chapter 290: Chapter 288 Seven Pirates_1 “There’s a not-so-small chance that something has indeed discovered us, and the next time we use the parchment, we must ensure that it doesn’t make any contact with that thing, otherwise we’ll really be in trouble if we’re caught,”
Colin felt an unease in his heart, knowing he must be cautious and careful.
At this moment, they were still a little way from reaching “Refugees City”, and he looked towards his companions:
“The past few times we’ve used ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’, we have been invaded and eroded by something. I have some methods to counter this.
“Of course, one of the interference measures will require your cooperation.”
During their journey, he had learned from “Little Dwarf” Peter about the existence of an enemy with parasitic abilities, known locally as the “Crimson Abyss” cult.
They were the biggest cult around here, using spores or something of the sort to infest and control their enemies…
If things went as expected, those two cities had been invaded by them.
“How do we cooperate?” Dog Brother asked just in time.
“I’m going to implant roughly a pound of a special substance in your bodies. It won’t affect your movements, but it will ensure that when your true bodies are contaminated, you won’t immediately be left without any means of resistance.”
If there was anything that could combat those invaders of the human body, Colin’s first thought was “Nano Intellectual Mechanism”.
The total mass of the Nano Intellectual Mechanism he brought from “The Seventh Box Garden World” was about fifteen pounds.
He had secretly implanted less than ten grams into their bodies, but this was enough for Colin to control them or make them lie down and act as WIFI at a moment’s notice.
But to resist the invasion from this unknown enemy, ten grams was definitely not enough, he would need a significant amount to provide full-body protection.
Implanting ten grams might go undetected, but implanting a pound without being discovered was frankly impossible.
Even just now, when several of them were using “Tyrant Body”, Colin noticed they seemed to vaguely detect something, though they were not certain.
So, to avoid unnecessary emotions arising, Colin decided to inform them of his decision.
“I… accept,” Dog Brother looked around at the others and was the first to make a decision.
After speaking, Dog Brother felt like the way the others looked at him was a bit like they were looking at a — traitor.
“Stop being so suspicious. If I really wanted to harm you, would I need to go to all this trouble?”
Dog Brother pursed his lips; he trusted Brother Shunzi’s character and believed he wouldn’t do such a thing.
If the other party really had ideas, they could resolve them in an instant.
“Alright… I agree too,” the Arsonist relented, vaguely realizing that even if he disagreed, Colin would probably still force-feed it to him.
After all, what Colin gave them was merely the privilege of being informed, not the right to refuse…
Instead of getting to that level of force, it was better to agree now; at least they could save face.
After those two, the others gradually agreed…
They were very clear about one thing: if Colin really had ideas about them, he truly could take them down in an instant, thanks to that particular item—
“Time Stasis”.
This was the item they feared the most since entering, second only to that Revolver; however, after coming in, they found that what made Brother Shunzi strong was not just those items.
On him seemed to be a great number of special items beyond their understanding, which didn’t require a Golden Card to easily suppress them…
“Good, since no one objects, just relax your bodies, it will be over quickly.”
Colin secretly communicated with the Nano Intellectual Mechanism, instructing it to start.
After that, everyone could feel an inexplicable coolness in their body, as if something had entered and was spreading rapidly to every part.
This sensation made them somewhat apprehensive because if Colin hadn’t warned them in advance, they probably would only find out about these things after being invaded, and they still might not be certain, as the feedback was too subtle.
However, because of the passive effects of the Talent “Tyrant Body,” they could genuinely sense the presence of a threat.
‘What exactly is this thing?’
‘With such a strange item, why doesn’t Shunzi show it off like he does with the Golden Card? And why hasn’t he been showing off his gear recently!?’
‘…’
Thoughts flickered through their minds one after another.
“Right, didn’t you say that besides this, there were other methods we need to use?” The Arsonist said, suddenly remembering Colin had mentioned that it seemed they needed to use more than just one method.
“Yeah, it’s best to buy some BUFFs on the side.”
Colin’s lips curled into a slight smile, thinking that being the only one getting fleeced made him feel a bit out of balance.
Of course, with the enhancement of BUFFs, the resistance to pollution would indeed see a significant increase.
And just as these words were uttered, the seller of buffs appeared as if from nowhere.
“Usually have no idea where they hide, but mention buying buffs and they jump right out.”
Colin pursed his lips. Although this guy was indeed unscrupulous for profiteering during difficult times, it had to be said that the BUFF effects sold by “The Light Chaser” were indeed very powerful.
Even when facing some high-tier existences or boss-level creatures, they could have a very good effect.
Nonetheless, no matter what, Colin was determined to find this person if he got a chance and must teach him how to behave.
Otherwise, knowing only to profiteer, it’s just too outrageous!
On him alone, Colin had already spent more than twenty thousand points…
Without giving it too much thought, about half an hour away from that “Refugees City”, everyone’s faces were painted with a pained expression—
Five hundred points could almost buy an item, and just for one use of a BUFF, it was indeed a bit hard to accept.
They weren’t like Colin, earning several thousand points on a single mission. Typically, they would only earn around three to five hundred points per mission, not too much…
To them, it was like spending a hundred bucks on a single clove of garlic.
But thinking of the content of the two “Book of Fate: Fragment,” they eventually bit the bullet and purchased a six-hour BUFF effect for five hundred points.
After all, life is precious, and no one could be sure what “Refugees City” would be like.
Another ten or so minutes passed.
Colin could now see that there were many dilapidated submarines of various models coming and going in this vicinity. Some of them, like the previous Peter, cast covetous glances at their submarine.
But in the end, all those pirates chose to back off…
“This is the territory of Omar, the second most recognized among the seven great pirates. So, these people just look and dare not approach. Unless Omar personally takes action, no one ignorant would come bother us. But even if Omar were to make a move, it wouldn’t be here, so we’re most likely safe,” said the tightly bound “Little Dwarf” Peter to Colin.
“Tch, you guys still have rules?” Colin snorted in derision.
“It’s not us that have rules, we must abide by Olma’s rules,” Peter didn’t find anything wrong with this.
Outside of this place, it might be another story. But here, even the number one pirate among them would have to give face to this number two.
Merely the “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale” was not enough to tempt this great pirate to break his own rules.
And “Free Roaming Pirates’ City” was home not just to fugitives and pirates but also various undercover agents, even members of the Alliance and cultists—people of all sorts, accepting everyone, thus considered the most liberated underwater city.
So they weren’t worried about Colin and these cultists getting into trouble upon arriving…
And precisely as he spoke, Colin and the others finally saw the moving underwater island city.
A city wrapped in an incredibly large bubble, floating in the murky green sea water, shaped like a gigantic top.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 291 - 291 289 I cant take it anymore I want to blow
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 291: Chapter 289 I can’t take it anymore! I want to blow her head off!_1 Chapter 291: Chapter 289 I can’t take it anymore! I want to blow her head off!_1 An hour later, the “Deep Sea Unicorn” stopped at the harbor, and Colin walked down with two people.
One was the pirate leader “Little Dwarf” Peter, and the other was an arsonist.
As for the rest, they were all left to guard the submarine lest someone steal such a big vessel upon their return…
“The arsonist’s main method involves concocting various explosives and then using item effects to evade the explosions. In this way, if team members are nearby and don’t have something like a ‘Time Stop’ artifact, they’re likely to end up dead or severely maimed; but as long as he’s with me, there should be no problem.”
“‘Surfing for Pigs’ tends to trigger extra events, so I’ll just lock it up at home to prevent it from causing any additional incidents. I doubt it can surprise me with any more tricks.”
Reassured by this thought, Colin glanced around; the port was not small, hosting a variety of submarines moored there, though these vessels had some peculiar designs.
Some were encrusted with barnacle-covered bones, resembling a submarine made entirely of bones…
Others were severely damaged; instead of repairing the breaches properly, wooden boards were used as a makeshift fix, and the subs were covered in graffiti…
And then, there were those submarines adorned with various dazzling lights, twinkling nonstop…
…
Seeing these diverse submarines, only one phrase came to mind for Colin—
“Ghostfire Boys.”
“If that ‘Funeral of Love’ family member from the company were here, he’d probably find quite a few common interests with them.”
Colin couldn’t help but scoff, then he diverted his gaze and walked onto the streets of the island port, which was enveloped by a huge bubble.
Before long, amidst the strong fishy stench, cries from vendors filled the air.
“Fresh Titan Squid Tentacles just off the boat, ten Marks a pound!”
“Selling a second-hand Sardine Submarine Fleet, thirty-seven subs in total, interested parties can contact me…”
“‘Delicacy Egg Injection’! It can give you a heavenly pleasure!”
“Top-grade Federation Lady, gents, come take a look, experience a prime Federation beauty for just a hundred Marks!”
“Just caught ‘Sea Siren’ slaves, come and see if you need one…”
…
A plethora of individuals of varying identities were peddling their goods.
Food, weapons, medicine, slaves—the whole street was bustling with activity…
However, seeing some people locked up and waiting to be sold like products, Colin couldn’t help frowning. Although he had seen quite a bit in his time, such a scene still inevitably evoked a sense of compassion.
The light of flames flickered in his pupils…
Unfortunately, Colin was well aware that even if he took action then and there to offer help, the result would most likely be counterproductive.
“Unless I could take down this big pirate named Olma, even if I managed to rescue these people, they would still be on the path to death, because I simply can’t take them with me.”
Colin silently shook his head, temporarily shifting his gaze away from them.
Then, he turned his eyes to where the spectators were the most numerous, the strikingly stunning “Sea Sirens.”
“Aren’t these mermaids?”
Colin observed from a distance, spotting a dozen or so Sea Sirens with the upper body of a human and the lower half of a fish amidst the onlookers.
They were easily a size larger than the average human, but at this moment, they were all locked in irons on the land, their beautiful faces filled with a look of despair…
Colin sniffed the air, detecting a hint of fishiness.
It was somewhat reminiscent of the Fishmen he saw in “The Seventh Box Garden World,” but not quite the same…
Those Fishmen had turned into such due to contamination from the leaking Divine essence of the “Father of the Sea,” all of them males, whereas these here seemed to be some sort of native species.
Just as Colin’s gaze fell upon them, a round, burly female pirate with a face full of scars and many test tubes in her clothes bought all the “Sea Sirens” for a total sum of three hundred thousand Marks.
“Hey, hey, what a pity, it had to be the mad witch Livina who bought them. You see, experiencing these ‘Sea Sirens’ would be… Mmm, I heard this from a friend, yes, they say as long as the ‘Sea Sirens’ keep their mouths shut, the whole experience is very comfortable, but in her hands, I bet they’ll all be wasted.”
“Little Dwarf” Peter clicked his tongue twice beside Colin, subconsciously trying to show off, but remembering that this group seemed to have higher moral standards than the Federation folk, he hurriedly corrected himself.
“Ruined? What do you mean?”
Colin asked as they walked along a pathway in a larger market area, planning to look for reactor control rods they could use.
“Uh, if someone else got their hands on these ‘Sea Sirens,’ they’d definitely… experience them, but that crazy old hag is different. She buys them just to kill for their blood and some organ parts, using them to concoct special potions. Isn’t that a waste? And this lunatic also enjoys torturing them…”
“Kills them for their blood and organs?”
Colin raised an eyebrow and looked back.
When he heard Peter mention that these mermaid-like creatures were being killed, he felt a tremor in his mind from the “Deep Sea Egg,” as if it was startled…
“Could it be that the ‘Deep Sea Egg’ is from the same species? Why else would it be frightened?”
Colin had a hunch. If there was indeed a connection between the two, maybe he could figure out a way to retrieve the egg.
At that moment, Peter seemed to have thought of something and spoke up, “Come to think of it, that crazy lady seems to be very close to the ‘Crimson Abyss’ cultists. Many people say she is a believer.”
“‘Crimson Abyss’?”
Upon hearing that name, Colin felt a heavy feeling inside.
It appeared that the other two human ports had already been contaminated by the “Crimson Abyss,” and now there were more related incidents emerging. He doubted it was a coincidence.
Regardless, whether he wanted to save the mermaid, get information about the “Sea’s Egg,” or something else, he needed to obtain the reactor control rods first.
Ten minutes later, Colin and the others entered the massive dock.
…
Meanwhile, at the port location, Livina, covered in various vials and with a face scarred, returned to her submarine decorated with skeletons, carrying a cage of “Sea Sirens.”
In the nearby “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale,” “Naming is Hard,” who was playing cards with the others, threw down his cards in frustration, about to sigh about his bad luck—damn, losing two more points—when he inadvertently caught sight of a scene outside the window…
“Holy shit, mermaids!” Naming is Hard exclaimed, quickly pressing his face against the window.
“Mermaids what? Don’t you cheat me, I’ve recorded the points, remember to pay up when we go out—holy shit, mermaids!”
Dog Brother muttered and turned his head, his eyes suddenly brightening.
The “mermaid” locked in chains appeared pitiful, stirring some thoughts in him—the currently temporarily dysfunctional old employee—as if some unique kinks were activated.
Another one, “Surfing for Pigs,” also turned his head: “Six!”
Several old gentlemen together admired those beauties, but before long, their faces changed, and their expressions froze.
They saw a burly, feral-looking obese woman approach one of the mermaids, tie an iron spike to the end of its tail, and take out an iron hook attached to a rope from her pocket. With practiced ease, she pinched the mermaid’s neck and pierced its chin with the hook.
The pirates behind her suddenly pulled the rope hard, and the exceptionally beautiful mermaid was hoisted up.
Then, before the mermaid could struggle, the obese woman took out an iron spike and jabbed it violently into its spine…
Immediately, the mermaid stopped moving.
The obese woman didn’t stop there. She quickly made an incision at the tail, and blood gushed out, flowing into a bucket prepared in advance through the iron spike.
Next, she scooped up a handful of bloody water and took a sip, then stood up with a cruel smile and slit open the delicate white belly with a knife.
The entire process was swift. By the time the others realized what was happening, they saw…
A massive amount of intestines and organs, still wriggling and steaming, spilled out from the mermaid’s wound, the fresh red intestines hanging from its waist like a skirt…
“Ugh…” someone retched.
“Motherfucker! I can’t watch this! I’m going to blow her head off!”
The usually silent “Surfing for Pigs,” suspected of being mute, stood up furiously cursing and grabbed a longbow from the Storage Room, aiming directly at the hideous-looking obese woman.
…
…
…

chapters.title: Chapter 292 - 292 290 Great Pirate Omar_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 292: Chapter 290: Great Pirate Omar_1 Chapter 292: Chapter 290: Great Pirate Omar_1 “Whoosh!”
A pure flame arrow detached from the longbow.
This arrow, made entirely of flame, flew through the thick glass in a way incomprehensible to ordinary people and sped towards the person dozens of meters away.
“Wha…”
The bulky female pirate had just sensed something amiss when her innate sense of danger made her react instantly, rolling forward, but even so, the arrow still pierced her shoulder.
Boom!
A surging flame erupted on her body.
“Aaargh!”
A scream came out from her mouth.
Seeing this at the port, everyone was in shock, not expecting someone to take action here.
“Who? Who dares to lay a hand on this madwoman! This one has some troublesome moves!”
“Tsk tsk, looks like there’s a show to watch. It’s probably an enemy from her past seeking revenge.”
“Seeking revenge? I think they’re crazy. This is Omar’s territory. Who dares to make a move here, wanting a death wish?”
“…”
The crowd speculated about the reasons.
Meanwhile, it was only then that Dog Brother realized what had happened and gritted his teeth: “You just went ahead and did it?!”
He had initially been so shocked by the sight of that fat woman brutally killing a lovely young lady on the spot that he had been stunned for a moment and didn’t stop the man in time.
Though he also disapproved of that behavior, he knew very clearly that making a move here would likely cause no small amount of trouble.
“Sorry, I just couldn’t stand to watch that happen.” “Surfing for Pigs” put away his longbow and headed towards the submarine’s watertight exit, seemingly planning to go out.
“You…”
Dog Brother paused mid-sentence, but did not continue with any phrases like “Do you know how much trouble you’re bringing us by doing this?”
After all, the deed was done, and they had to figure out a way to solve it.
He now had a concrete appreciation for just how true it was that the other person “100% caused additional incidents.”
“Don’t worry, I’ll take responsibility for my own actions… Watch out!”
“Surfing for Pigs,” about to leave, suddenly felt a mysterious sense of danger approaching. Although his “Tyrant Body” lacked the limited-edition “Deadly Insight,”
he still felt that some danger seemed to be looming…
Just at that moment, through a crack in the submarine, a creepy scarecrow crawled in.
“So it was you who ambushed me.”
As soon as these words were spoken, the eerie scarecrow exploded violently like a balloon stretched to its limits, and countless tiny crimson spores spread out…
The three inside the submarine held their breath, feeling a tingling on their scalps, but they didn’t dare to slow down their actions, each pulling out their own counters.
Dog Brother deftly stabbed his dagger into the scarred palm of his left hand, followed by his body being immediately covered in an abnormal shadow that also protected “Naming is Hard” by his side…
“Surfing for Pigs” flicked his bow, and a curtain of fire immediately engulfed those tiny, invisible dust spores.
Despite their quick reactions, some spores still imperceptibly invaded their vicinity, attempting to infiltrate their bodies.
At that moment, a layer of silver light shimmered on their skin, blocking all the spores.
“That was close…”
Dog Brother took a breath of relief, but before he could breathe again, he found that his nostrils seemed to be blocked as well.
At the same time, information from the Nano Intellectual Mechanism surfaced on the retinas of the three of them.
“Please refrain from breathing temporarily to avoid inhaling dangerous spore dust.”
Although it was their first encounter with this device, they all knew that this was a contingency plan left by Brother Shunzi, and they held their breath accordingly.
With their physical condition, holding on for a while was definitely not a problem.
However, unlike them, the pirate hostages inside the submarine weren’t so lucky.
After the attack, their eyeballs rolled around like chameleons, emitting strange and delighted laughter as something wriggled beneath their skin.
The three could see that under their skin, something was growing rapidly, and then infecting and overrunning their bodies.
Clearly, it would probably not take long for all the pirate hostages here to die.
“Let’s get out of here first.”
Dog Brother didn’t delay, leading the three through the submarine’s wall, directly arriving above the port.
At this moment, they saw the woman who had just been shot through the shoulder with skin bulging continuously, as one after another burning scarecrow burrowed out of her skin.
With each scarecrow that appeared, the flames on her body diminished rapidly, and even the burn wounds were transferred.
Suddenly, she raised her head and looked at the group who had already arrived above the port…
“No matter who you are, you’re dead for sure!” Pirate Livina spoke with resentment filling her voice.
