And just as she spoke, she quickly took out several glass vials resembling test tubes from her body and squeezed them forcefully with her right hand, shattering them and letting various colored liquids seep into her palm.
Then, she lifted her hand, aiming at the few individuals who had launched an attack on her…
“Die!”
As the word fell, her right palm exploded violently, from which dozens of tendrils lashed out towards the people a dozen meters away.
At that same moment, several Four-Armed Citizens brandishing sharp claws stood in front of Dog Brother, cutting off the incoming tendrils.
“Move, kill them fast!”
Without hesitation, Dog Brother commanded the Four-Armed Citizens while also taking out an ancient-looking round fan, and with a forceful wave, he sent dozens of sharp wind blades flying rapidly, shredding the tendrils to pieces.
While he was fending off the enemy upfront, “Surfing for Pigs” didn’t delay either, speedily drawing his longbow and successively shooting fire arrow after fire arrow.
However, this time, with the enemy prepared, the arrows were not so easily hitting their mark.
But at the same moment, Livina’s pirates also took action; a pirate swam stealthily to near “Surfing for Pigs” amidst the clash and suddenly leaped out of the water, swinging a rusted saber filled with corrosive force.
“Heh heh.” “Surfing for Pigs” spun around, using the bow as a club, and delivered a heavy blow to the opponent’s head. With a loud thud, the pirate’s upper body instantly exploded.
The eyeballs flying in mid-air still seemed to carry an expression of disbelief.
“Haven’t you heard that an archer who can’t fight up close is not a good warrior?”
“Surfing for Pigs” mocked.
The tremendous strength made Dog Brother and a bunch of onlookers gape in amazement…
Dog Brother quickly spoke up, “See if you can perform a beheading. I’ll hold off the pawns.”
“Okay!”
“Surfing for Pigs” grabbed a handful of beans, stuffed them into his mouth, and stealthily pulled out a round metal object from the Storage Room weighing at least 300 pounds and casually tossed it out before charging directly at the enemy.
“Clang—”
Naming is Hard suddenly pulled open the collar of his shirt, revealing his chest, and immediately after, three rusty chains shot out from a “gate” on his chest.
They wrapped around the opponents, and during this process, some eerie tendrils tried to block them.
But as soon as they touched the chains, they lost their strength and went limp.
This was an abnormal “Binding Chain” that had fused with his body; it somehow entered and went dormant inside of him when dealing with an anomaly, and then he gained the power of this thing.
“Damn it!” Livina’s eyes flashed with malice, not expecting these guys to be such a tough fight.
Seeing the man with the ridiculous mask charging at her, her throat pulsed, seeming like she was about to spit something out…
But it was at that moment…
Clang.
A heavy lead ball fell from the sky, smashing straight onto her head, caving in her skull, and almost knocking her eyes out of their sockets…
“Since when…” She was stunned, writhing all over her body, her wounds seeming to be shifting.
“You’ve never seen it, have you? A lead ball falling from the sky.”
Not giving the old witch a chance to heal her wounds, “Surfing for Pigs” seized the opportunity, swung the longbow, which was taller than a man, and smashed it onto her body. Blood and flesh exploded, and her organs turned to mush.
The beheading was complete!
At the same time, the pirates watching the scene were all in shock—
Had the notoriously infamous Evil Witch Pirate Group just been wiped out?
The whole encounter had not even lasted two minutes before it came to an abrupt end?
Remembering the old witch’s fearsome reputation, many of them felt it was somewhat unreal…
After winning the battle, “Surfing for Pigs” didn’t pay attention to them; he intended to approach those Fishmen, who looked quite large, to rescue them, but he noticed that they were staring back at him with terror, their eyes filled with fright.
“Don’t be afraid, I’m a good guy.”
“Surfing for Pigs” wiped the sticky blood off his face and said so.
However, before he could continue to calm the scared mermaids, he suddenly heard a commotion among the surrounding pirates and then, as if having seen some terrifying thing, they panicked and fled in all directions.
At the same time, a sense of deadly danger washed over him.
“They’re not afraid of me, but of something behind me!”
“Surfing for Pigs” quickly realized something, turned around, and saw a three-meter-tall figure in a black robe standing behind him.
From that figure, an unbearable, oppressive force emanated.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 293 - 293 291 He who stabs others will always be
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 293: Chapter 291: He who stabs others will always be stabbed._1 Chapter 293: Chapter 291: He who stabs others will always be stabbed._1 “Not bad, your strength isn’t bad, but do you all know what it means to make a move on my Olma’s territory?”
A cold voice emanated from beneath the black cloak.
As soon as the words ended, a large number of sinister and sticky crimson tentacles shot out from below the cloak, lashing around and creating thunderous explosion-like sounds.
The surrounding pirates who hadn’t had the chance to run far were unaware of the attack and were directly blown apart.
“Ah…” Dog Brother suddenly let out a scream; the few Four-Armed Citizens who tried to ambush their opponent had just approached when they were smashed to pieces by those tentacles.
“Heh, don’t worry, I’m here, and none of you will get away. I’ll smash you into pulp to feed my Freedom City,”
The pirate Olma chuckled, but he didn’t hurry to attack the man, instead continuing to look at the one with the bow.
“Let’s start with you! Your disgusting flame!”
The next second, Wave Rider’s expression turned serious as he saw a blood-red tentacle fiercely lashing toward him.
He instantly activated his “Tyrant Body,” and drew out his longbow to block.
A fiery shield enveloped him just before the attack.
With a loud bang,
The fiery shield instantly exploded, and he was flung away by the immense force wrapped in the tentacle, rolling several times on the ground before coming to a stop, feeling his internal organs boiling.
The pirate didn’t stop his attack but swung another tentacle directly at Wave Rider.
“I’m going all out!”
Wave Rider took a deep breath; he hadn’t expected the enemy that appeared this time to be so strong.
He did his best to place the longbow in front of him, set up a wall of fire, and drew the bow, thinking that even if he were to die, he would shoot his last strike.
Almost mockingly, the huge crimson tentacle slowed down its speed until he shot his attack, and then fiercely accelerated its strike.
Pop.
The tentacle shattered the flames, and then stabbed directly toward him; its thick black shadow already reflected on his face.
“Can’t dodge it.”
Wave Rider’s eyes narrowed as he channeled all his spirit into the longbow, intending to explode the weapon.
Even in death, he wanted to take a bite out of his opponent!
And then create a slight chance for his comrades, who were stuck in a deadlock because of his impulsiveness, to escape…
However, at that very moment, a figure shot into the scene like a bullet, and with a flash of silver light, the giant tentacle coming straight at him was suddenly cut in two.
And, at that moment, a familiar silhouette appeared before him.
“Brother Shunzi?”
Wave Rider was taken aback.
‘You really do stir up trouble; I was just stepping out for a bit…’
Colin looked at him with a complex expression and didn’t respond; as he was coming, he had been informed of the situation here through the Little Maid.
The reason they weren’t locked down was purely because they had been discovered the moment they attacked, and if they had been locked in, they would most likely have been killed…
Now that things had happened, Colin didn’t think too much about it, reined in his thoughts, and looked calmly at the tall figure:
“We hope you’ll give us some face, and stop this matter here, how about that?”
As he spoke, Colin’s right hand slowly drew a revolver out of his pocket, while pure, more crimson flames than the longbow burned on him throughout this process.
In the roaring heat waves, all the oppressive atmosphere was devoured.
Simultaneously, a layer of silver “mist” floated around Colin’s body, and a silver substance began to adhere to his surface, making him look as if he were cast in silver.
It was at that moment that the pirate Olmar ceased his attack, his hidden face under the hood seemed to reveal a hint of seriousness.
Clearly, the sudden entrance of Colin also made him feel a slight threat.
Many pirates who had run even further away were looking at Colin with astonishment, wondering who this person was to make the second of the seven great pirates, who dominated the Deep Sea, cease his attack.
In the standoff, Dog Brother looked at the figure and let out a sigh of relief. In his view, as long as Brother Shunzi showed enough power, the conflict would probably end there.
After all, it was clear that the other party also held Brother Shunzi in awe…
There was no need for everyone to fight to the death over a dead underling.
But at that moment, he suddenly heard Brother Shunzi’s voice, “You guys… find a way to break through with Tao Tie, I’ll hold them off here.”
He paused, then added, “Oh, and take those Fishmen with you.”
Feeling the killing intent hidden in the shadows, Colin couldn’t help but sigh to himself, ‘Alas, it seems I can’t resolve trouble with just a few words like those anime characters.’
No sooner had he spoken than a mass of tendrils extended out from beneath that gigantic black robe.
These writhing tendrils grew longer and longer, akin to a mountain flood that destroys everything in its path…
“I might let someone else go, but since it’s you lot who dare to spy on my Master, don’t think you can escape!”
Olma’s cold voice arrived alongside the tendrils that seemed to press down like a Dark Cloud engulfing the city.
“Spy on your Master? Why would I peep on yours for no reason? Even if I had such a hobby, why would I look at you instead of pretty girls?… Huh? Wait a minute”.
In his confusion, Colin suddenly had an epiphany, vaguely realising whom the other party referred to by spying.
But there was no time to ponder; seeing the enemy initiating an attack, he didn’t dare slack off. Flames erupted from his body like a volcano, and with his will, the fierce fire surged towards the oncoming flood of writhing tendrils.
In his estimation, the Pirate’s strength was probably at the Eighth Level by official rankings, and on the higher end of that scale.
Even he couldn’t easily take him down…
Sizzling~
When the two sides met, there was no collision, just the sound of the tendrils sizzling as they were scorched by the flames.
“Not sure if these tendrils count as the main body…”
Colin pondered as he drew his revolver, aiming it directly at those grotesque, enlarged tendrils.
If there was a connection to the main body, then firing thirty-three bullets would cause this great Pirate Olma, if not death, then significant injury.
However, just as he raised his revolver to aim, “Deadly Insight” suddenly triggered—
A blood-red tendril pierced out from the ground behind him and burrowed into his head.
…
“Another one who likes backstabbing.”
Colin’s action of raising his revolver didn’t change, but his left hand touched a golden card. In an instant, the sound of an invisible engine roared, and a force pulled everything around it into frozen time.
Outside the effect’s influence, Olma’s body stiffened, feeling as if the scene in front of him had frozen, and all his limbs that extended into it lost control.
Meanwhile, within the frozen space, Colin turned around to see a blood-colored tendril just breaking through the ground like a bamboo shoot…
“You like playing dirty with backstabs, huh!”
Colin thought to use a Bone Spur in response, but having another idea, he instead pulled out the “Emblem of the Humility Knight”, took a deep breath, and then released the Time Stop Effect.
“Where is he?”
Omar’s body had just disappeared, and as he was about to continue the fight, he found that the person who dared to spy on his Master had vanished.
His combat instincts told him the other hadn’t left, but before he could figure out how to find him, a terrifying, unbearable pain suddenly spread from his lower back in all directions…
“Aaah!!”
Olma let out an extremely painful scream, feeling as if some foul water was spreading inside his body from the point of agony.
Struggling to turn his head, he noticed that somehow, that guy had gotten behind him and had thrust a bone spur, full of black cracks, into his back…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 294 - 294 292 Thrilling Duo Act_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 294: Chapter 292: Thrilling Duo Act_1 Chapter 294: Chapter 292: Thrilling Duo Act_1 “You… ah!!”
Upon seeing that guy, Omar very much wanted to tear the other apart, yet before he could make a move, Colin forcefully stirred with his hand holding the Bone Spur, promptly shutting the other’s mouth, leaving him only capable of letting out a painful scream.
That piercing scream spread, causing pirates in the distance to feel their hearts tremble…
“What has he encountered?”
They couldn’t imagine what exactly the man behind this had done to make Omar scream so loudly.
You should know, this was a top-ranked sea pirate, placed second, who would not necessarily make a sound even if he really couldn’t win and was killed, but now he was wailing like a child, horribly embarrassing.
The dozens of sturdy tentacles extending from under him were all taut and stiff, and continuously swelling.
It seemed as if some sort of bizarre liquid was being rapidly forced into his body…
“Good, he’s screaming loudly, very spirited!”
Seeing the effect still outstanding, a slight smile crossed Colin’s lips. Currently, unless it was against a Level 1 Containment Subject or any entity above that standard of the Bonfire Company, the Bone Spur could achieve very good results.
And the thing in front of him, Colin estimated to have a fighting power close to an Eighth Level Personnel’s, and such personnel did not yet have the immunity to such items; once truly stabbed, they would be left either dead or disabled.
However, just as he was prepared to thrust the Bone Spur deeper, a vision suddenly appeared in his mind:
Under the wide robes of the formidable sea pirate in front of him, hundreds of tentacle tips, like arrows, burst out, his body directly perforated into a honeycomb by these eerie attacks…
In the face of such assault, he still wasn’t dead, but from those piercing tips, murky black liquid surged forth.
Suddenly…
The solo screaming turned into a terrifying duet, back and forth, a relentless chorus…
“You think you can drag me down too? Fat chance!”
With the passive Talent, “Deadly Insight,” any head-on attack, unless two came one after the other at the same time, wouldn’t catch Colin off guard.
Any single sneak attack with an interval of more than three seconds didn’t mean much to him…
After acquiring the deadly information, Colin immediately ceased his attack, stepped on the pirate’s back, forcefully pulled out the Bone Spur, and quickly left the scene.
And at that moment, a multitude of blood-red spikes burst outwards through the black robe as though a hedgehog exploded into shooting spines.
Massive amounts of foul-smelling black pus were ejected from those tentacles, seemingly in an effort to expel the toxins from the body…
“Some quality stuff here, the physique is almost like that of the ‘Deep Sea Messenger’.”
Colin was amazed; the last one who had not died after being jabbed was the “Deep Sea Messenger” from the Seventh Box Garden World, though that one had only been nicked slightly.
This time, it had been thrust halfway in; Colin judged by the feeling in his hand that it probably reached the kidneys.
Unexpectedly, under such circumstances, this guy could still avoid death, even attempting to expel the toxins and return to normal by his unique physiological structure.
“Worthy of being the undisputed number two pirate of the Deep Sea, indeed you have some stuff. But I’m not just going to sit here and let you recover.”
As his thought flashed, Colin raised his hand with the palm facing the other, his five fingers suddenly clenched tightly.
Boom!
Surging flames erupted once again, directly engulfing the formidable sea pirate within.
Then, he pulled out his pistol again and aimed at the pirate’s real body, pulling the trigger.
Under the effect of the “Rapid Fire” gun, in just one second, seventeen bullets were fired out, passing straight through the flames to strike the true body of that sea pirate.
Omar, tumbling and screaming in the flames, didn’t even notice these bullets.
Compared to the indescribable terrible pain on his body, the damage from these bullets was nothing more than a tickle…
However, when thirty-three bullets hit him, the situation was likely to be very different.
The Bone Spur, combined with the “Lethal” effect, really could cause instant death.
“One more volley should do it.”
Colin stood aside, quickly reloading the bullets. He had not been thoroughly ruthless before, but now that all pretenses were dropped, he would not just stand by.
But, just when the salvo of sixteen bullets was about to hit the target, his heart suddenly skipped a beat.
An invisible surge of air burst forth in front of that figure…
The bullets flying in mid-air all fell to the ground.
Even the flames were directly scattered by some terrifying aura.
And at the center of everything, Omar lay limp on the ground, his body twitching occasionally and continuously oozing black pus, looking like a broken toy…
His breath was rapidly fading, yet a majestic will was reviving within him.
“Damn it, exploiting cheats and calling in a substitute player, you’ve got a Second Order phase, haven’t you?”
Feeling the ever-increasing oppression, Colin realized that this might indeed be the power of the “Master” from the “Crimson Abyss” descending upon him, as the other had mentioned.
It was that strange creature they had become aware of simply because they used the “Book of Fate: Fragment,” without even having actual contact with it.
With his rich experience of breaking into various dangerous realms during this period, Colin immediately discerned that the danger level of this “Master” would not be lower than a “Level 1 Containment Subject.”
That level was equivalent to the “Formless Mother,” at the very least the “Father of the Deep Sea” stripped of divinity.
“Gotta bail!”
Colin took a deep breath, faced reality, and without a second thought, turned around and raced away.
The risk of disrupting the descent ceremony seemed considerable, and he even faintly felt it might be a trap; there was no need to take this risk anymore…
By his estimation, in a quick scenario, it would take ten minutes, or half an hour at most, until that thing arrived. If they were still on the scene by then, they wouldn’t be far from complete annihilation.
So, they had to escape this damned place before all this happened, lest they get stuck in the mire and be unable to get away when the time came.
At this moment, the harbor area was littered with corpses killed by an unknown AOE attack, most of them meeting a ghastly end.
From a distance, some pirates saw Colin leaving, somewhat perplexed.
In their view, Colin had eliminated Omar, effectively promoting himself to the second, no, even the chance to contend for the first amongst the seven great pirates.
Yet in such circumstances, he was giving up the spoils of battle and trying to leave?
Is he out of his mind?
Some pirates eyed the gigantic “corpse” of Omar amidst the numerous other bodies, a greedy glint appearing in their eyes. Hesitating for a moment, they swooped down towards the dead to scavenge the spoils of war, embarking on a spree of “free scavenging.”
All kinds of shoving, cursing, and bloody fights for loot ensued after Colin left…
They weren’t strong enough to sense the entity descending behind the scenes.
Another group of pirates looked at the limp body on the ground and seemed to realize something, quickly starting to flee.
They too sensed something was amiss, but they didn’t believe that after killing Omar, he would leave in such a hurry unless something was about to happen!
Instead of picking up some trash, it’s better to escape and avoid the risks!
Meanwhile, Colin quickly caught up with “Surfing for Pigs” and others. Upon his arrival, he saw these employees had already met up with the Arsonist and others but were being attacked by strong fighters from the major pirates’ crew.
The most eerie among them was a gigantic strawman covered in bloodstains, wielding a scythe.
The strawman’s head was empty, with several leech-like flesh tubes wriggling…
Every time it swung its scythe, the group was forced to retreat, fearing any contact with it, and even the pirates nearby didn’t want to get too close to the strawman…
Because in addition to killing enemies, it could also flip open an ally’s skull and directly suck out their brain matter.
Even if it didn’t drink an ally’s brains, just getting too close could lead to cursed contamination, resulting in troublesome ailments.
When Colin arrived, the giant strawman immediately shifted its target, its hollow eye sockets fixing directly on him, and it charged at him, scythe swinging.
“Careful! If you get touched by this thing, you’ll be afflicted with diseases and such!” Dog Brother shouted a warning upon seeing this.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 295 - 295 293 100 Little Tricks to Summon a Subspace
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 295: Chapter 293 “100 Little Tricks to Summon a Subspace Demon” _1 Chapter 295: Chapter 293 “100 Little Tricks to Summon a Subspace Demon” _1 However, Colin, upon hearing the words, did not stop but continued to face the oncoming threat head-on. But just as they were about to collide, an extremely terrifying repulsion force suddenly exploded!
The straw man wielding the scythe exploded right where he stood, his eerie straw body torn apart in mid-air.
With the Force of the Gold Card, tearing apart an enemy of this caliber was no different from ripping a piece of paper.
Colin did not pause, but continued through the flying straw, charging towards the “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale” docked not far away.
Seeing him easily shred the straw man, the other pirates who wanted to block his path immediately stepped aside, halting their advance, not daring to obstruct him any further!
They could also hear Omar’s screams from afar, but, being at a considerable distance, they were uncertain of the situation.
However, at this moment, with Colin’s arrival and their own leader nowhere to be seen, the situation was clear enough…
“Good that you know better.”
Colin snorted, quickly making his way through the crowd without wasting time to kill them.
For he felt that the impending arrival of that thing was becoming a reality, and they had to make every second count to get away.
His gaze shifted toward the Arsonist and others; everyone was now here. Although they had sustained some injuries and showed signs of battle, the situation wasn’t too grave.
“We need to leave, now,” Colin said gravely, heading straight for the “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale”.
But then, he suddenly thought of something, and realized that the “Sea Siren,” who were quite beautiful, had all vanished:
“Where are the mermaids?”
“The situation was urgent just now, there were too many people, so I broke their chains and let them escape into the water…”
“Alright.”
Colin had wanted to see if he could get some information about the “Sea’s Egg” from those “Sea Sirens.”
Given the current situation, that was no longer an option…
“By the way, Brother Shunzi, something invaded the submarine,” Dog Brother stepped forward to remind him.
The mutated pirates were still inside the submarine, and they were uncertain about the situation within…
“I know, but it has been resolved now.”
Colin moved on without stopping; he had just been informed through the “Nano Intellectual Mechanism” that everything inside the ship had been taken care of by the Little Maid.
These ordinary parasites weren’t that strong to begin with…
The real issue was the spores they released.
“About that strange straw man, he might not be dead. That creature seems particularly hard to kill.”
“Surfing for Pigs” added.
That woman was smashed into a pulp, and they thought she was definitely gone, but as soon as they turned around, a giant straw man crawled out from the corpse on the ground.
“If he’s not dead, we’ll kill him again. It’s not a big problem.”
Colin wasn’t concerned. In his view, the most troublesome thing about the straw man was a weird curse of contamination.
But coincidentally…
The buffs they bought from “The Light Chaser” were heaven-sent counters to those things, to the extent that they hadn’t even noticed that Livina, embodied as the straw man, was also puzzled when she attacked them, wondering why her illusions weren’t effective.
Soon, when they returned to the submarine, all the anomalies had already been cleared by the Little Maid.
Aside from what happened on the dock, their luck wasn’t bad at all, as they had just entered the more upscale trading area and found a reactor control rod they could use.
It was second-hand, but that was not a problem. As long as it worked, it was fine.
Under the operation of the Little Maid, it didn’t take long to replace the nuclear reactor control rod, and the “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale’s” engine room was quickly preheated, ready to start.
Seeing this, Colin turned to Peter, the “Little Dwarf” who had followed them all the way without daring to say much:
“Apart from the ones we knew about earlier, are there any other human islands a bit farther away? Nothing nearby, and nothing affiliated with the Alliance…”
If things were to go as expected, something bizarre might be brewing in the vicinity.
That “Refugees City” was also within the range of influence, and there was even a considerable chance that it was the mastermind behind the scenes.
“In about three days’ journey, there’s an island controlled by ‘Separatism’…”
“Little Dwarf” Peter didn’t know the situation, but seeing Colin’s serious face, he didn’t dare to delay.
At this moment, he had already fully witnessed Colin’s strength and knew that this was not someone he could afford to provoke…
“Separatism?”
Colin had heard about it from Peter before; it was a radical force completely opposed to the “Alliance,” whose core ideology was to overthrow the alliance and then… whatever those guys wanted to do next didn’t matter much.
They just needed any place to preach…
“Then let’s head over there.”
Once the direction was decided, the submarine powered at full speed toward the target.
Within less than ten minutes, they had left that “Refugees City” several nautical miles behind, with no shadow of the city visible anymore.
However, Colin still felt somewhat uneasy and then looked at the “Arsonist Tao Tie”: “Besides the ready-made explosives you have, try your best to prepare another explosive with enough power.”
“Haven’t we already escaped?” The Arsonist was puzzled.
The city was now out of sight; was there still a need for such vigilance…
To his confusion, Colin simply shook his head: “Hard to say, anyway, everything on the submarine that doesn’t affect its operation, and you think can be used, go ahead and use it.”
“Alright then…”
The Arsonist didn’t delay, first donning a pair of black-framed glasses. This device could help him quickly understand the properties of various materials for proper chemical component matching.
Then, he took out various bottles and jars.
Some contained minerals, others unidentified liquids, and some unknown biological organs, all without labels, but he remembered them clearly.
At this moment, in addition to Earth’s resources, he had begun to try combining some extraordinary items for an explosion.
The results he had achieved so far were quite satisfactory…
Seeing him getting to work, Colin was not idle either. After pondering for a moment, he opened the “small-sized” storage room with a hundred-liter capacity, rummaged through it, and found a small piece of flesh attached with black blood.
This was a piece remaining from the “Demon” he had blown up last time in “The Seventh Box Garden World.”
If used properly, it might serve an important purpose…
“Sorry…” “Wave Rider Seek Pig” came over at this time.
If it weren’t for Colin’s timely arrival, their group would have likely been entirely wiped out…
The various troubles in the “Descent Project” were indeed not in the same league as ordinary missions.
“I don’t mind your desire to save people or anything, but some things… let’s not talk about it for now.”
Without looking up, Colin toyed with the demon flesh and pulled out “The Hundred Tricks to Summon Subspace Demons,” given to him by the “Father of the Sea,” to consult it.
A few minutes later, he had roughly prepared a sacrificial summoning document.
“Good, this content should be enough to reliably summon another demon of the same type with a certain connection to the previous one.”
Colin was quite pleased with the document he had composed.
However, it was also at this moment that he suddenly shuddered internally, as a vision flashed through his mind—
The steel ceiling of the submarine seemed to come alive, extending a large mouth that bit off his head.
With a splat, his headless corpse fell from the ceiling.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 296 - 296 294 Speak of Cao Cao and Cao Cao Arrives_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 296: Chapter 294: Speak of Cao Cao and Cao Cao Arrives_1 Chapter 296: Chapter 294: Speak of Cao Cao and Cao Cao Arrives_1 “A big mouth grew out of the submarine’s ceiling? What’s going on?”
As Colin’s thoughts flickered, he didn’t dare to slow his movements. Flames erupted from his body, launching an assault toward the submarine ceiling barely two and a half meters above him.
At the same time, he retreated, slightly tilting his chin to look upward while warning the others.
It was in this moment that he saw the metal wall soften like skin, then split open to reveal a dark, gaping maw.
The surging flames poured into it, forcing the mouth to close again…
But what really made Colin’s heart skip a beat was the fact that the submarine had come to life!
“Material activation… Could this ‘Crimson Abyss’ actually be related to Red Moon?”
Colin had his suspicions, but they were unconfirmed, and he shouldn’t associate the two simply because of the color red—
That would truly be seeing a bow in a cup and fearing it a snake, an overreaction.
Yet now, the eerie vitality that had inexplicably emerged on the submarine forced him to consider the connection.
‘The power feels similar, but the essence seems different; at least this one is not as high-level as Red Moon.’
As he pondered, Colin heard Little Maid’s voice in his ear: “There are some residual ultra-micro spores inside the submarine. They previously played dead to escape detection but have now been activated for unknown reasons.
“To eradicate them, we need to stop moving forward and spend about an hour.”
“Spore parasitism causing activation? It seems it’s not Red Moon indeed. Red Moon’s power truly brought the submarine to life, making machinery grow flesh or fuse with mutations…”
Having confirmed this, Colin let out a sigh of relief. His previous experiences with the activation and betrayal of his organs still haunted him.
Even now, he wanted no further contact with it…
However, these spores from the so-called ‘Crimson Abyss’…
“What the hell kind of spores can even corrode a steel body?”
Colin also found it absurd. Although Little Maid indicated she could handle the corrosion, just then, as the submarine slowed down, something caught up and slammed hard into the side of the “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale.”
With a bang, one side of the submarine dented in.
Through the shattered glass windows, they saw a pirate submarine with eerie anemone-like appendages growing on its exterior, and numerous tentacles tightly gripping the “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale.”
They could also clearly see a significant number of parasites attempting to breach into their vessel from the pirate submarine…
“Is this an attempt for a boarding battle?”
Dog Brother was shocked, maneuvering the Four-Armed Citizens through the submarine to confront them, swinging his specialized claws to cut several gaps in the pirate submarine as easily as if slicing tofu.
He thought this would directly kill the pirates aboard and end the trouble…
However, after emitting a strange scream, the cut-open submarine released countless deeply parasitized pirates like a burst cockroach egg pod.
Ratatat…
Amidst the skin-crawling sounds, dozens, if not hundreds, of infected climbed up the outer hull of the “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale.”
They roared and howled, swarming like a tide, trying to destroy the submarine.
Even more alarming was the sight of additional corroded and activated submarines rushing toward them.
Even if they managed to shatter the attacking activated submarines, a whole bunch of parasitized pirates would then burst out from inside.
They were like cockroaches under the sea, densely covering the submarine’s hull, wreaking havoc from all sides, aiming to invade.
“What do we do now?” Arsonist looked to Colin, then glanced at certain areas inside.
Not just the outside, the interior of the submarine also occasionally twitched and convulsed oddly. Colin didn’t have time to explain, leaving everyone unaware of the specifics, only sensing that the submarine seemed to have come to life.
They didn’t feel as though they were inside a cold submarine but rather in the stomach of some creature.
“You keep working on your explosives, don’t worry about anything else for now.”
Colin bathed in the flame, looked around, and not seeing “The Light Chaser,” he gave up seeking help from that direction. After retracting his gaze, he glanced at various parts of the submarine that kept trembling intermittently.
Inside the submarine, the blood-red spores and Little Maid were clashing at a microscopic level, making the submarine look like a twitching fish stalled in the water…
Completely driving out these things would probably take an hour.
But feeling the incessant arrival of submarines outside, Colin felt a wave of weariness.
“Hold out for an hour if possible, otherwise, we will all die in this sea. Take these, use one if you feel exhausted,” he said.
As he spoke, Colin tossed several “Colorless Crystals” to everyone.
These were originally intended for Li Ming and the others to use for overtime work, but now, given the emergency, there was no time to hold back.
Underwater combat had far too many restrictions compared to on land; one misstep and the submarine would be doomed, leaving them, even if alive, struggling to leave this place and find a proper location to complete their mission.
And if they failed to complete the mission, there was a high probability they would really end up trapped to death here…
After giving Colorless Crystals to his companions, Colin didn’t stop his movements and took out the Corpse Mountain Card.
Without any nonsense, he directly fused a Colorless Crystal into it…
This card had no strict requirements for corpses; any bodies, as long as there were enough of them, could be summoned directly through it.
Soon, the Little Fist Stones appeared outside the submarine, frantically hunting the parasitized infectees.
The unique traits of Little Fist Stones made it very difficult for them to be parasitized in return.
“Good, no problem.”
Colin observed for a moment and, confirming that Little Fist Stones wouldn’t get infected by consuming the infectees, he took out another “Colorless Crystal” to strengthen them. He then released his hold on them, letting them act freely.
Afterward, he brought out the “Yukionna” ring and ordered her to quickly deal with the anomalies outside.
For some reason, whether it was rest or sleep, Yukionna was forcibly aroused by Colin and was a bit angry. Despite her anger, she obediently carried out his orders.
Her body was special, like a ghost’s, capable of entering and exiting the submarine at will.
Finally, with Colin releasing his combat forces, the otherwise passive situation started to improve significantly…
“As long as that thing doesn’t chase us, holding out for an hour should be possible,” he said.
Colin glanced at the summoning contract in his hand. Although he felt that the summoning would definitely be successful based on its contents, unless absolutely necessary, he still didn’t want to use that method.
Because if that thing came, the likelihood was high that the submarine would be done for…
However, just as he was silently rejoicing, Colin’s brow suddenly jerked with a jump, feeling a terrifying sense of oppression spreading from somewhere in the murky waters.
That overwhelming presence arrived like Dark Cloud bearing down.
“Really, speak of the Devil, and he shall appear…”
Colin sighed quietly, then heard an array of cold voices echoing inside the submarine:
“You don’t think you can escape, do you?”
Unsurprisingly, this voice was emitted through the throat of the great pirate Omar, but whether it was still him was another question…
The unceasing vibrations of the voice transmitted only this far, causing the crew to suffer from throbbing pain and grogginess.
Colin reached out, flames once more howled through the submarine, severing the voice that carried a measure of psychic attack.
Then, without any hesitation, he activated the prepared Demon Summoning Altar.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 297 - 297 295 This Generation of Firebearers Is So
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 297: Chapter 295 This Generation of “Firebearers” Is So Rude!_1 Chapter 297: Chapter 295 This Generation of “Firebearers” Is So Rude!_1 A rudimentary altar was set up at the front of the submarine…
On the altar lay some flesh and blood from the last summoned Great Demon.
Although the setup was extremely simple, the most important aspect of summoning a demon was the intent. As long as that intent was conveyed, it could turn sincerity into a key that unlocks stone, calling the other party forth.
With a whoosh.
The contract written in Omar’s blood that Colin held burst into flames.
The summoning was over, and all that remained was to wait for a response.
However…
It was at this moment that a heavy sense of oppression struck again. Colin turned his head and could already make out Omar arriving, looking like a chaotic ball of yarn composed of numerous blood-red tentacles.
Today, the Great Pirate’s displayed form was almost entirely inhuman.
The only human part left on his massive, over ten meters long aggregate of tentacles was a head on top of the “yarn ball.”
“So it’s really all tentacles below the neck.”
Colin took a deep breath, glanced at the Arsonist who was still hurriedly making explosives, knowing the explosives weren’t ready yet, so without delay, he had the “Yukionna” remerge into him.
Then, without a second thought, he popped three “Colorless Crystals” and charged out of the submarine.
The fight had to be taken far, it couldn’t break out nearby…
Otherwise, the submarine would definitely not survive the collateral damage.
With the Yukionna’s ghost-like phasing effect in play, the sea was like nothing to Colin, who moved unimpeded through it.
The only trouble was that the Firebearer’s power was greatly restricted in the water and was almost unusable.
But just when he thought that thing would prioritize chasing after him, he realized it was still locked onto the “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale,” almost as if to say, “If you don’t block me, I’ll just tear apart your crystal.”
“Dammit, a sneak attack on me failed, so you turn to sneak attack my sub?”
Colin cursed under his breath, no longer attempting to lead it away, he charged directly toward the creature.
At this moment, Omar’s enormously large body bore a power that was clearly even more terrifying than his own.
However, it seemed it was still his own will controlling his body…
“Only granted power, but not entering the fray yourself? Or watching from the shadows for some other reason?”
Colin had a hunch, but seeing the massive “yarn ball” coming at him like a meteor, trailing countless tentacles, he couldn’t afford to be careless and drew “Force – Repulsive Force.”
Even as the other was not yet truly upon him, Colin could feel the undercurrents swelling around him in the sea.
Compared to that behemoth, his own body seemed as minute as a sesame seed in front of a watermelon.
And when the other was within a hundred meters of him.
Colin, holding the card, took a deep breath and then forcefully swung it forward.
All his spirit poured into the card at once!
In that instant, appalling Repulsion erupted from this spot, the force driving the water forward and even creating an underwater cavity for dozens of meters around, while the water pushed forward by that terrifying force turned into a shockwave surging ahead.
Omar didn’t evade or parry, his countless tentacles flailed, speeding up as he collided head-on with the shockwave.
As he himself moved rapidly forward, he likewise propelled the massive shockwave.
“Boom!”
A huge explosion sounded where the two forces collided, and some submarines that were closer to the site instantly exploded.
Numerous contaminated individuals burst into smithereens like fireworks in the water.
Even the crew inside the “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale,” further away, distinctly felt the violent vibration.
“Cough cough cough…”
Colin drifted in the water, unable to help but feel a churning inside himself until he vomited a mouthful of fresh blood, which finally brought some relief.
Because of the overuse of the “Force – Repulsive Force” card, his internal organs had begun to sustain damage.
However, on the bright side, that full-force strike managed to hold Omar back and it seemed he wasn’t faring well either. His numerous tentacles snapped, writhing in the water.
“I’m going to kill… you!”
Omar glared at Colin, his eyes filled with hatred. However, upon seeing Colin pull a Bone Spur out of his body, Omar seemed to recall some unpleasant memories, causing his voice to waver and pause.
But then he remembered he was blessed with the power of a great being, and his confidence surged once more.
“Sigh… Without the divine blessing, that strike could have severely wounded him. And where are the demons? Save me, why haven’t they come yet?”
Feeling the demons had not yet arrived, Colin let out a silent sigh.
In his mind, the ideal scenario was to intercept them himself, drag things out until the demons arrived, then pit the two sides against each other, muddying the waters so that he could escape in the chaos.
As for dealing with Omar, who was possessed by a Level 1 Containment Subject, he had not even considered it, despite it being only a fraction of its full strength.
Still, holding off for a little while was doable, since it was only a fraction of the strength.
Yet, the demons still had not responded…
“Could it be, I really have to release my true self?”
Colin felt the “Beast Transformation Syndrome” pathogen that was lying dormant in his body, influenced by various forces, along with a small part of “0-9 ‘Hunger'” that had deeply integrated with it. His expression grew serious.
With his increasingly skillful use of the Firebearer’s power, he vaguely felt that he might have a chance to use this power.
However, it was like walking a tightrope over a cliff—extremely prone to disaster.
But if it came down to a last resort, even if it was prone to disaster, a choice had to be made.
…
Meanwhile, in a special world, countless distorted smoke clouds writhed in the sky, and a terrifying figure roared incessantly upon the land, its force enough to tear open rifts in the earth.
“Damn it all! This is too much! Those cursed Firebearers killed my father, and now they dare provoke me. I’m going to kill them Aaaargh!”
A Lesser Bloodthirsty Demon Lord bellowed in rage.
At this moment, by his ear, he could faintly hear some blood-boiling words…
“See that, you filthy ****, here lies your father’s corpse ***….”
“You foolish ****, you ********, waiting for you in the deep sea, I’m going to tear you to shreds, use your **** to ****** you, you piece of ****, come and fight if you dare, if not, just *****…”
“You coward **, this time I’m not setting any rules, I just want to beat you the **** up.”
“Remember, my name remains unchanged, I am the Deep Sea King, the great pirate, Omar!”
“Watch how I’m going to ****** you….”
“*****”
The text was full of insults, unbearable even for a demon.
“What do we do? The Lord’s blood is boiling over, he’s entered a state of absolute fury…” a tiny demon sighed at the side.
If it weren’t for the chains holding him back at this moment, this Lesser Bloodthirsty Demon Lord would have likely charged already.
“Hold him back, wait for a Demon Duke to arrive. The Firebearers of this ‘Bonfire Campsite’ are really too disrespectful!”
A demon agreed.
Hundreds of years ago, the Bloodthirsty Demons nearly went extinct because of these people; they have been listed as a protected species. So much time had passed and they had just begun to recover a little, only to be exploited again for their wool.
That’s too much!
They were already fools; why did it have to go this far!
The most crucial point was, the reason these brainless demons were being reared was that they had some very important uses!
“We have to hold on! The great Lady Lilith instructed us, if we want to tear open a crack and truly return to the real universe, to break the seals set by the three giants of ‘Bonfire Campsite’ back then, we must rely on them. Only they are unaffected by any mental attacks, unswayed by any ‘fate’, able to break through one of the most crucial barriers…”
As this demon subordinate was speaking, he suddenly heard a “clang.”
They were startled to see the chains that bound the Lesser Demon Lord snap.
And the Bloodthirsty Demon, emphatically raised by the great Demon Duke Lady Lilith herself, answered the call and vanished into thin air…
…

chapters.title: Chapter 298 - 298 296 So Youre the Kid Named Colin Huh_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 298: Chapter 296: So You’re the Kid Named Colin, Huh!_1 Chapter 298: Chapter 296: So You’re the Kid Named Colin, Huh!_1 “Boom!”
Yet another colossal collision occurred, and Colin was sent flying by a tentacle from Omar, although the hit nearly shattered his skeleton. But Omar did not get off easy either.
For as Colin was being struck, he managed to simultaneously stab the other’s tentacle with a bone spur, making it howl in pain.
This time, however, bolstered by an unknown and terrifying power, he was not incapacitated by pain as before.
“Cough cough…”
After being flung backwards for more than ten meters in the water, Colin barely stabilized himself and then couldn’t help but vomit a mouthful of blood.
After using various artifacts in succession, his bodily functions had obviously sustained damage.
Suffering from the effects of numerous negative conditions, he felt time speed up and slow down unpredictably. His internal organs were being compressed by repulsion, and prolonged handling of the bone spur had resulted in uncomfortable edema…
If the standoff continued like this, he estimated that it wouldn’t be long before he died violently.
And the anticipated demon had yet to arrive…
“Sigh…”
Colin rubbed his stomach, feeling the discomfort of his organs being squeezed. Had his physique not been strong enough, his stomach might have exploded like fireworks…
But if the demon did not come, persisting further would be meaningless.
“It seems, I have to go all out.”
Colin spat out another mouthful of blood, took off his ring, and threw it forcefully behind him. After issuing a “”flee”” command to “Yukionna”, he closed his eyes.
Omar, watching with a suspicious look, did not dare to approach rashly, instead opting to attack from a distance as a precaution.
Unfortunately for Omar, such tentative attacks were of little significance to Colin…
“What’s the matter with this person?”
Omar could sense that the enemy before him was undergoing some kind of change, with a mysterious entity seemingly reviving rapidly within.
Seconds later, Colin’s gaze abruptly opened, his eyes instantly transforming into vertical pupils. A violent and tyrannical mood spread, yet more horrifying to Omar than this tyrannical aura was the strangeness hidden within it.
Though faint, the scent alone stirred an indescribable sense of hunger within him…
“‘Hunger’…”
Suddenly, a voice echoed in his mind—the voice of the great entity from the “Crimson Abyss”!
In a sense, he had received a “divine prophecy”!
However, what unsettled Omar was the hint of fear shaking within this “prophecy,” the cause of this trembling—
Impossible! How could the grand being of the “Crimson Abyss” feel fear!
Omar couldn’t believe it, unable to accept such a thing. But at this moment, as he saw Colin raise his hand, he felt an alarming premonition.
If this battle continued, even the grand being that dwelled in the “Crimson Abyss” might not be able to save him!
However, just as he entertained the idea of retreating and became distracted, he suddenly realized that Colin had disappeared.
The extremely terrifying presence had vanished along with him…
“Gone, what’s going on?”
Omar’s large mass with a head on top showed a bewildered look, but then, seemingly coming to some realization, countless tentacles grew from his body, wrapping layer upon layer over the “back” position.
Some tentacles underwent a change similar to petrification, to prevent being stabbed directly into the body later on…
However, the expected attack from behind didn’t come; instead, a suffocating pressure suddenly assailed him from the front.
In the blink of an eye, Omar saw a creature towering before him, with skin red as blood, bat-like wings on its back, and a giant battle ax in hand, breaking through the waves and charging.
“So you’re Colin, huh! You dare try to deceive me into thinking you’re Omar? Do you think I’m that easy to fool?!”
The Lesser Bloodthirsty Demon Lord angrily cleaved through the tentacles in front, slashing into the massive fleshy orb, severing countless tendrils and carving out a massive wound on its body, causing an explosion of blood and spores to splatter everywhere.
But these things didn’t affect the demon too greatly; its wings flapped behind it, and it continued to hack wildly at the “Colin” in front of it.
Omar couldn’t understand a thing that this bizarre creature, which bore a hint of divinity in its essence, was shouting. He took it for yet another helper summoned by the intruder, and so he flailed his many tentacles and fought tooth and nail against it.
…
“At least they’ve started fighting.”
Colin felt the ebb and flow of the battle behind him and let out a sigh of relief. At the critical moment, his sincerity had finally reached the demon in the subspace.
This time, the contract he summoned was written with some of Omar’s blood that had stained him before.
This way, unless the newcomer was of the intelligent type, it would probably rush into battle with Omar head-on upon arrival.
Now, the situation was indeed as he had expected—the demon appeared and immediately charged towards its target…
“Although I used the original to blow up one last time… its combat power is indeed strong. As soon as it appeared, it could fight head-on against the great pirate, who was empowered with a part of the power from a higher-tier containment subject, without falling behind. And with a demon’s extraordinarily strong life force, Omar is quite fortunate.”
Feeling the aftershocks of the fight behind him, Colin reflected internally. The moment the demon’s presence emerged, he promptly suppressed the fury within him, then held his breath and turned invisible.
Then, within seconds, the demon arrived on the battlefield, playing out a surprising rescue.
At this moment, while the two sides were engaged in combat, Colin retrieved the “Yukionna” ring and slipped it back onto his middle finger.
A cool, icy breath radiated from the ring, and the information it contained caused Colin’s expression to stiffen:
“If you can’t talk, then keep quiet! What do you mean you thought I was done for, already pondering who to cling to next, talking like you’re a widow…
“Hurry up and float me back, I need to rest for a bit.”
As he spoke, he took out a “Colorless Crystal” to enhance his status while suppressing the “Hunger” within that had stirred from its slumber and was starting to get active.
Although the arrival of the “demon” meant he no longer had to fight desperately, he had briefly attempted to awaken that power.
Even if he hadn’t fully awakened it, it had stirred somewhat, so he had to suppress it…
After resting for quite a while, Colin managed to suppress the wave of hunger within him.
“Had I known this guy was coming, I would have held on a bit longer.”
Feeling the faint hunger still inside him, Colin sighed inwardly and mentally noted the demon’s tardiness in his mental notebook.
About ten minutes later, he returned to the submarine’s location.
Surveying the chaotic battlefield before him, Colin received both good and bad news.
The good news was that several company employees had survived until his return, and all the contaminating spores on the submarine had been dealt with. Now only some deeply parasitized and infected pirates remained.
The bad news was that “Little Dwarf” Peter was dead, his body covered with blood-red tentacles and chopped into several pieces. Furthermore, the front of the “Deep Sea Unicorn Whale” had been slashed open by the demon with a ten-meter-long gash, as if it had undergone a cesarean section—apparently, it wouldn’t be repairable for some time.
This also meant that the submarine’s speed was significantly reduced, and they couldn’t immediately escape.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 299 - 299 297 Escape from Death _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 299: Chapter 297: Escape from Death _1 Chapter 299: Chapter 297: Escape from Death _1 “Corpse Mountain seemed to have just been in the way of that Demon Lord, getting chopped in half right away,”
Colin had a rough sense of how his summoned creature died.
He knew the unfortunate Little Fist Stone happened to be in its path and was cleaved into two, returning directly to the Card Graveyard.
Now, when he appeared here and Dog Brother and the others saw him, they immediately got excited:
“Brother Shunzi is back!”
With Brother Shunzi back, everything would turn out alright!
“The battle over there will probably end soon. No matter who wins, it doesn’t seem to bode well for me. The Demon has a time limit, while the pirate doesn’t, but he might not chase too far. All things considered, it’s best to get away from here for now.”
Colin had made some decisions and then commanded ‘Yukionna’ to use her power.
In an instant, bone-chilling cold erupted, instantly freezing many of the infected within the seawater. A substantial area seemed to have plunged to absolute zero…
‘Yukionna,’ after consuming the ‘Colorless Crystal,’ was not to be underestimated either.
Seeing this, the others couldn’t help but breathe a sigh of relief.
“If it weren’t for her slightly nasty personality, liking to freeze living things into ice sculptures, I would probably have destroyed this ring and let her out a long time ago.”
In the blink of an eye, Colin moved onto the ‘Deep Sea Unicorn Whale’, which had a big hole torn in it, and with a ghost-like presence, he passed through the submarine’s shell to the still dry rear section.
There was an emergency chamber there, not large, but enough to fit a few of them.
The others followed him, entering the chamber as well.
Colin looked at them, just about to speak, but couldn’t help coughing up blood again.
“You…”
“It’s nothing. My issue isn’t that serious, cough cough…”
His voice hoarse, Colin waved his hand, signaling there was nothing to worry about.
Due to the ‘Repulsion’ within his body, he guessed some blood vessels had burst, but it wasn’t in a critical area, so it wasn’t too big of a deal.
“Right, I’ve finished making my bomb.”
The Arsonist suddenly spoke up, pointing to an object one meter tall and saying, “If we’re lucky, the power here is equivalent to at least one to several tons of TNT, which is my personal limit…”
Hearing his words, everyone present took in a sharp breath.
Most of them had experience with firearms and explosives, so they knew what over a ton of TNT meant. If thrown onto an ordinary aircraft carrier and hitting the right spot, it could even sink the carrier.
If it exploded here and their reaction was a bit slow, everyone present would be done for.
‘To make something so powerful so casually, you’d be seriously dangerous if you weren’t locked up in prison…’
Colin scanned the Arsonist from top to bottom, giving the latter the creeps.
“Cough cough, although I possess some special knowledge, making these things isn’t as easy as you think. Of course, I haven’t done anything particularly bad either.”
The Arsonist explained, and then quickly handed a remote control to Colin while introducing the item:
“I added some special powder to the inside, discovered during an incident, a special material that can suppress the supernatural. So, compared to ordinary bombs, it might even kill ghostly entities…”
“This here is the remote detonation switch. Underwater, the remote control distance is around a kilometer. If we’re not careful, we’re likely to get blown up badly ourselves.
“For the password, entering 399054 will detonate it immediately, while entering 427111 sets it to explode after ten minutes. If you need anything else, I can make adjustments… You decide how to use it.”
Brother Shunzi had only asked him to make it powerful enough, and he was curious to see how the other guy would use it.
Because of the added powder, if the detonation distance was too close, they’d all likely be in big trouble…
“Good, but we don’t need it for now. Keep it.”
Colin took the remote control, examined it, and then picked it up with one hand.
The Arsonist was startled by this action; although the explosive device didn’t seem large, it weighed several hundred pounds. Brother Shunzi was able to lift it single-handedly without using any supernatural means, just pure physical strength.
Seeing this, the rest felt reassured by Brother Shunzi’s formidable constitution, also relieved that it likely meant he was indeed alright.
“So, what do we do next?” Dog Brother asked.
“Escape.”
Colin was succinct, not waiting for their questions and continued, “All you need to do shortly is to sit tight. The submarine might deform and leak water.”
The Little Maid informed him that although the submarine was severely damaged in battle, the power source was mostly fine.
The only issue was that if they wanted to get away immediately, they needed a thrust…
Colin decided he would be that thrust.
‘Peter is dead, so it might be a bit tricky to find our way, but with his instruments and the sea charts, the Little Maid should almost be able to decipher it.’
With that thought, Colin no longer hesitated and quickly moved outside the submarine, dragging the tail of the submarine with one hand and sticking “The False Powerhouse” onto his body, then he popped a “Colorless Crystal.”
“Even if I am in the deep sea, needing one hand to drag the submarine, I can still manage to escape…”
After grumbling to himself, Colin took a deep breath, allowing the Nano Intellectual Mechanism to reinforce the submarine at full strength, and then used frost to increase the contact area between himself and the submarine.
Finally, before the fierce battle at the rear concluded, Colin activated the “Force – Repulsive Force” effect.
This time he used the card for a sustained effect instead of a single burst, significantly enhancing the submarine’s speed for a short duration to a terrifying level.
Even for a submarine produced by a major deep-sea factory, it now trembled as if it were about to disintegrate.
Crack…
Just as Colin had said, the immense water pressure from the super-fast speed exceeded the submarine’s load-bearing capacity, and many areas not reinforced by the Nano Intellectual Mechanism showed cracks immediately.
Massive amounts of seawater flooded in instantly, and the crew inside clung together, getting battered beyond recognition by the wash, so much so that they had to use “Tyrant Body” to withstand the onrush.
At last, after enduring nearly three minutes of intense water pressure, the submarine began to slow down.
“Cough cough cough…”
Colin walked into the submarine staggeringly, his face deathly pale, blood continuously spilling from the corner of his mouth.
Using the power continuously for three minutes had pushed his body to the brink, and if it weren’t for “The False Powerhouse” making him insist on keeping up appearances, Colin guessed he would probably be writhing on the floor, howling in misery…
Nevertheless, even so, after staggering in, he found a spot to sit down at random.
“Your status is detected to be extremely critical, repairs are needed to halt further damage, do you agree?” the voice of the Little Maid rang in his ear.
“Do I look like the type of weakling who needs healing?”
Colin intended to reject haughtily, but a gush of blood forced him to suppress his “instinct” and nod his head.
Instantly, a surge of “Nano Intellectual Mechanism” flooded into his body, starting to mend his internally displaced organs.
That’s when a glowing hand placed itself on his shoulder.
A powerful blessing effect was bestowed upon him.
The frightening injuries inside him were quickly being suppressed…
Colin turned his head to take a look and was slightly startled. “The Light Chaser,” who seemed to have appeared out of nowhere, was casting buffs on him.
“Directly eliminating the negative effects for me? With such strong effects, he’s not going to drain all my points later, is he?”
Colin was alarmed, fearing for his finances.
But then he thought, buff payments had to be approved by him, and since the option didn’t arise, he could only assume that the other party was offering the buff free of charge.
While Colin was lost in his wild thoughts, “The Light Chaser,” upon seeing his condition stabilize, withdrew her hand.
She still wasn’t entirely sure what had happened.
In her vision, everything around was quite blurred, with only a vague perception of several employees scurrying about, their vitality fluctuating between strong and weak, seemingly under attack.
And just now, the one she was more concerned about, his life force had dropped to a critical point, verging on severe injury and shock.
Without waiting for the Parchment to propose any tasks of bestowing a 5-point blessing, she immediately intervened to stabilize Colin’s condition.
Leaving aside her own attitude towards life, just the fact that the Holy Relic was in Colin’s hands, she couldn’t let him die here.
Fortunately, the problem wasn’t too serious.
After forcefully erasing the negative effects from Colin’s body, he recovered almost instantly.
But this action made her avatar noticeably dimmer, and it probably wouldn’t last much longer before disappearing, potentially costing her several dozen points…
This caused her some distress.
“Thank you.”
Colin said with gratitude, then stood up, intending to ask the other party whether this buff, which forcefully erased the negative effects of items, was for sale or not, but he noticed she suddenly turned her head towards a certain direction.
Following her gaze and sensing for a moment, he was startled…
Because from there, the power of another terrifying existence was pursuing them!
“The Crimson Abyss’s aura… wasn’t Omar trapped? No, that’s not Omar; it’s support from other cities!”
Colin suddenly realized that the human cities nearby must have already fallen under the encroachment of “The Crimson Abyss,” and while he was engaged with the sea pirates, those fallen cities probably already dispatched reinforcements!
And with their current strength, they had no way to face another blessed being like Omar!
“In the end, do we still have to fight with all we’ve got?”
Colin sighed deeply.
However, it was at this moment that he suddenly noticed a large group of gorgeous “Sea Sirens” swimming towards their battered submarine.

chapters.title: Chapter 300 - 300 298 Sea Siren Queen_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 300: Chapter 298 “Sea Siren” Queen!_1 Chapter 300: Chapter 298 “Sea Siren” Queen!_1 “These are… the mermaids from before? *cough cough*…”
Colin was astonished, finding it incredible to see such a large group of mermaids, some of whom looked quite familiar.
If he wasn’t mistaken, these had to be the same mermaids they had rescued before…
Only, aside from the dozen or so that had escaped, there were also several dozen others, equally beautiful but dressed in blue scale armor resembling dresses, their gaze towards them filled with hostility.
Unlike those they had saved, the animosity they exuded was almost tangible.
Following Colin’s gaze, Dog Brother and the others also noticed the mermaids and were immediately surprised.
In their view, these Fishmen had fled before and would most likely have gone far away, never to be seen again, but unexpectedly, they had come looking for them…
The Arsonist glanced back at “Surfing for Pigs”:
“Have they come to return the favor?”
“Hard to say, but rather than gratitude, I feel like vengeance might be more likely,” Dog Brother was the first to speak.
He noticed that a significant portion of the mermaids looked at them unfavorably, giving off the sense that they could lash out and tear them to pieces at any moment.
However, recalling what they had seen in Pirate City, and considering how most people treated them.
Everyone thought such an attitude was completely normal…
But, though the timing and the place seemed somewhat inappropriate, as the exceptionally beautiful group of mermaids drew near, they couldn’t help but let their eyes sweep over their bare abdomens…
At the same time, they couldn’t suppress a thought:”Why do so many things underwater grow unrestricted, but all these Fishmen are top tier in appearance?”
Aside from being one size larger in stature, standing up with their fish tails might make them two heads taller than Yao Ming, but there were no significant flaws.
It was then, under their watchful eyes, that the mermaids stopped as a group a short distance away from the submarine.
Colin took a deep breath and stood up, taking the foremost position to make eye contact with them.
Leading the mermaids was a larger one holding a Scepter topped with a diamond-shaped jewel. Her eyes were not black but a pale gold, and her tail was very long—more a serpent tail like the “Deep Sea Messenger” Colin had seen before, rather than a fish tail.
And from her, it was possible to distinctly feel an air of nobility that comes with long-held power.
“She might be even more powerful than a single ‘Deep Sea Messenger’, and that scepter gives me a dangerous feeling; it must be a rather powerful artifact,”
Colin rapidly assessed the situation, then activated the “Combat Power Observation” that came with his “Gene Panel”.
[Name]: ???
[Race]: Approximately human.
[Strength]: 10.1.
[Constitution]: 9.7.
[Agility]: 11.4.
[Description]: An exceptionally beautiful “human”-like creature, with an elegant and noble aura that seems to suggest she’s a leader of some kind?
[Note]: The data above does not represent final combat power; please refer to actual encounters for a precise assessment…
…
“Indeed, the overall quality is very impressive, but what’s with this ‘approximately human’ thing? Does this mean that a ‘Sea Siren,’ when you take away the lower half, rounds up to approximately human?”
Colin muttered to himself, and just then, the mermaid leader who had been making eye contact with him for about a dozen seconds nodded her head as if she wanted to say something, but a sudden terrifying pressure arrived, causing her expression to change.
She then turned to look at the crowd of mermaids, and after seemingly saying something, several Fishmen suddenly swam out of the group and approached the submarine.
These Fishmen were the ones they had saved before.
Now, after swimming closer, they seemed a bit nervous as they made some hand gestures towards Colin and his companions—
To be honest, I couldn’t quite understand it, but I could comprehend their voices when they spoke.
“A very powerful individual is coming this way, and I’m going to take you all to run,” one said. “Do you understand me? I will help you all escape, thank you for saving us.”
A few Fishmen seemed anxious that the humans might not comprehend, explaining with urgency until Colin spoke up:
“Okay, sure, thank you.”
“Ah?”
The delicate faces of the Fishmen showed a hint of dumbfounded surprise, “You can speak our language?!”
This was odd, as it was typically very difficult for humans to learn their language, right?
Only a few rare linguistic masters among humans could barely make sense of it…
‘Of course I can’t, it’s all thanks to the company’s powerful translation capabilities…’ Colin pursed his lips but didn’t say this out loud; instead, he just nodded.
The Fishmen were taken aback for a moment, then one of them said with excitement, “That’s great! Let’s run together!”
Without further delay, they all flapped their tails and came forward, each taking a person and holding them in their arms like a doll, and then they started running towards the exit.
“Cough, cough, cough…” Colin couldn’t help coughing out a few congealed chunks that looked akin to pieces of internal organs.
“Oh! Are you alright?”
The mermaid holding Colin blinked her pale golden eyes, looking somewhat helpless and a bit innocent.
By now, she had realized that it was the arrival of this very person who directly confronted that terrifying monster, allowing them to escape so smoothly; otherwise, they might have ended up like the unfortunate Ramu, slaughtered by humans and turned into a fish soup.
“It’s fine, just choked a bit by accident, please continue,” Colin said somewhat awkwardly. His negative status effects had just been unreasonably wiped clean by “The Light Chaser,” and then the Little Maid had helped him reconnect and heal his wounds, so he was now, more or less, “unscathed.”
But no matter how “unscathed” he was, the fact that the mermaid had hurriedly held him so tightly to her chest had been a bit too much, causing him to accidentally choke…
However, what would it matter if it happened again?
Colin, like a Little Cat being picked up, popped his head out from the chest of the mermaid. He saw the others being held in the same way, each having a different degree of embarrassment on their faces.
“Tina! What are you doing? We need to get moving!” the regal “Sea Siren” spoke out, her voice ethereal like an elf’s, carrying a commanding presence.
“Okay, …Your Majesty the Queen!” The mermaid holding Colin quickly replied and hurried to follow.
Once they entered the water, the queen wielded her Scepter adorned with an exquisite diamond-shaped blue gem, creating several bubbles to envelop Colin and the others, sparing them the trouble of breathing.
Then, the “Sea Sirens,” led by the queen, swam swiftly in a certain direction.
“Charge! Charge!”
With the “Sea Siren” queen holding her Scepter at the forefront, the entire school of fish followed her like a flock of geese in the sky or a charging legion, their speed increasing by the moment.
The unfortunate sea creatures in their path were pulverized upon mere contact.
Furthermore, a blue light emanated from that special Scepter, and under its influence, all the “Sea Sirens” seemed to evolve as their fish tails elongated, resembling serpent tails.
The mermaids’ appearances also became even more enchantingly beautiful at that moment.
After about fifteen minutes of movement, the fish school’s swimming speed had reached a terrifying level.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 301 - 301 299 There Are Two Types of People I Colin
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 301: Chapter 299: There Are Two Types of People I, Colin, Hate the Most in My Life!_1 Chapter 301: Chapter 299: There Are Two Types of People I, Colin, Hate the Most in My Life!_1 “It’s almost as fast as the speed I achieve by pushing the submarine with my own strength single-handedly, impressive, impressive…”
In Tina’s embrace, Colin lamented. He had nearly collapsed maintaining that speed for just a few minutes, yet these fishmen seemed to be speeding up even after ten-plus minutes.
However, no matter how intense the water currents, they seemed to have no effect on him.
That unique bubble seemed to possess the capability for oxygen exchange; he had been breathing for so long without feeling any stuffiness.
Colin comfortably leaned his head back… Hiss!
At that moment, he realized that the pursuer with the aura of the “Crimson Abyss” seemed to be catching up again, determined not to give up until they did.
“Was it just a minor conflict and then I used a few ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’ and accidentally saw something? Do they really need to chase like this? They’re really not giving up…”
Colin sighed inwardly, feeling there might be some other purpose for that thing chasing them.
After all, many high-level life forms in these “Other Worlds” were quite familiar with “Bonfire Company,” and most of them were not particularly friendly upon encountering “Bonfire Company.”
The likely reason was that they had all been oppressed by the company before, and now they wanted revenge.
But what did those problems of the past have to do with him? Colin for one was not willing to take the blame for that.
The queen of the “Sea Siren,” wielding her magic wand as the spearhead, seemed to have noticed something too. The gemstone on the wand flickered with radiant light, and they increased their swimming speed once more.
After thinking it over, Colin also decided to lend a hand and reached into the Storage Room.
When the conditions felt just about right, he let one of the Arsonist’s bombs fall out.
The extremely tiny Nano Intellectual Mechanism attached to the electronic components could detonate the bomb that was imbued with both science and mysticism without the need for pressing a button.
Although such a thing was definitely not fatal to a high-level life form.
It could certainly disrupt their chasing speed for a moment…
And once their chase was disrupted, the likelihood of them catching up again would be slim.
Afterward, Colin contemplated and had the Little Maid inside him notify the Arsonist to throw out whatever explosive things he had in his pocket.
Despite being underwater and at high speed, the “Nano Intellectual Mechanism” was somewhat inconvenient to operate.
But before, Colin had injected each person with a pound of Nano Intellectual Mechanism, so communication wasn’t an issue.
Soon, the Arsonist received the message. He wanted to say that in this situation, it was unrealistic to throw any bombs—like a land mine would detonate immediately due to the water pressure upon being taken out.
It’s uncertain whether the enemy would be affected, but it was likely that he himself would end up battered and bruised.
However, at that moment, an idea struck him, and he let loose several mine-like triggered bombs from the Storage Room, each the size of a thumbnail and smooth on the surface.
These devices were originally set to be smashed on the ground and then, after a dozen or so seconds, to explode upon contact.
In their current high-speed flow, there was no need to worry about hitting the ground; just releasing them into the current would suffice. However, due to their small size, they only contained about a hundred grams of explosives each.
About the same as a standard grenade, enough for humans, but not quite for monsters.
But Brother Shunzi only asked him to use them to hinder something for a while, so scattering thirty of them should be of some use.
“It’s a pity, that little amount is probably useless.”
Colin’s thoughts were the opposite of the Arsonist’s. Having faced something comparable in strength to a “Level 1 Containment Subject,” he knew these devices were not so effective, amounting to no more than leaves blown against their pursuer.
However, he also knew the capability of the Arsonist required preparation; in such sudden situations, they were powerless, but with preparation, he could convert many things into explosives.
Given the right conditions and enough time, Colin had no doubt the other could create a super “Starfish” capable of destroying a city in the shortest possible time.
“I just don’t know what this person actually does in real life, his knowledge is exceptionally solid and vast, and he has a strong Talent for making explosives. If I could find his real identity, and if he’s not officially employed, maybe I could bring him over to the Tongliao Dragon Farm to learn a thing or two. If he’s an official, then see if I can get him transferred to my side.”
A flurry of thoughts passed by in an instant.
But Colin didn’t have much time to think further, as a surge suddenly came from behind—the bomb with at least 1T of TNT equivalent had been detonated!
“The breath of the Crimson Abyss also broke off at this moment, left behind.”
“Looks like we shook them off this time, after all, it’s all about racing with props,” Colin said.
Colin let out a slight sigh of relief. If they were caught, the mermaids here would probably suffer heavy casualties, and he guessed his own group would likely be wiped out as well.
Finally, after advancing for almost an hour with the followers in pursuit, the team began to slow down.
Apart from the queen, the tails of the other ‘Sea Sirens’ started to shrink and appeared more like those of ordinary mermaids.
It seemed that this state was not permanent for them.
Through the murky dark green seawater ahead, Colin and his companions could see a small floating island with a structure resembling a honeycomb, swarming with many ‘Sea Sirens’.
Upon reaching Water Island, the ‘Sea Siren’ queen glanced at Colin, then turned to Tina, “Come find me after you’ve finished your business.”
Afterward, the queen left with the other mermaids.
Only eleven mermaids rescued by Colin and his people remained.
“We’re here,” Tina said as she gently placed Colin down, pointing ahead. Then with eyes gleaming with a golden light, she looked at Colin, “This is one of our homes.”
She paused for a moment, her eyes seemingly filled with a kind of yearning, “I’ll take you to find a place to stay, you can settle down there for now.”
‘A home? It seems there must be more than one, which makes sense,’ Colin thought.
Given their hostile attitude towards other humans, and how humans regarded them, it would be unrealistic to bring them silently to their main base without a word.
At this moment, facing an invitation from Tina, Colin prepared to shake his head in refusal.
He needed to find a place to spread his faith…
But just then, Colin suddenly noticed that the number of “initial believers” on his mission list had jumped by one hundred and ten.
Not one more, not one less.
“Could it be…?” Colin looked up, a realization dawning on him as he met the gaze of the large mermaid in front of him and noticed that her look seemed a bit off.
No, it seemed likely that all eleven ‘Sea Sirens’ had some intention of becoming believers.
If it was indeed as he suspected, then…
Why go anywhere else?
Where else would preaching not be preaching? Besides, each believer here is worth ten!
