“That’s right, my thinking was rigid. There is no requirement that believers must be human, and even if there were, mermaids are also people. How could I assume mermaids aren’t human? I can’t indulge in racial discrimination or exclusivism!” Colin thought.
The two kinds of people Colin hated most in his life were racists and __ people.
However, speaking of which, he wondered how the Bonfire Company calculated “believers.” Tina and her mermaids clearly weren’t believers, yet they were still classified as such.
To say they were “believers” was perhaps more to do with the fact that they had a profound connection with them because he had saved them.
Shaking his head without overthinking it, Colin accepted Tina’s invitation—
Whether or not they’re believers, if the company says they are, then they must be.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 302 - 302 300 My Geiger Counter Went Off_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 302: Chapter 300 My Geiger Counter Went Off!_1 Chapter 302: Chapter 300 My Geiger Counter Went Off!_1 Under Tina’s guidance, Colin and others entered the beehive-like Water Island, adorned with glowing gems. After several twists and turns, they were settled into a very spacious cave.
The cave turned out to be surprisingly dry and cool, and it was very bright due to a pile of glowing Crystal Stones…
“Okay, guys, wait here for a while, I’ll come back later and bring you some food… Oh, do you eat giant squid?”
As Tina swished her fish tail, she asked curiously.
Uh, although it didn’t have much to do with the “Father of the Sea,” the preference was similar…
If another Fishman claimed to eat squid, Colin felt he was about to form a stereotype. Looking at Tina’s expectant expression, he answered, “Under normal circumstances… if nothing unexpected happens, it’s not like we can’t eat it.”
Although their bodies after the descent resembled their original selves, strictly speaking, it seemed it was not the original selves who came, so eating should be fine.
Of course, if conditions permit, it would still be best not to eat.
But now the conditions did not permit…
“Good, I’ll bring it to you in a bit.”
After speaking, Tina swished her fish tail and leapt into a pool beside her, quickly leaving the place.
Colin turned to his colleagues and cut straight to the point without any small talk:
“You should have noticed the mission requirements, and for those who haven’t, you can take them out now and see. These merfolk are also considered ‘Believers,’ and one could count for ten.”
It was only after Colin spoke that his companions suddenly realized why Colin had agreed to stay here.
However, before they had a chance to speak, everyone suddenly heard a series of rapid “click, click, click, click” sounds.
“What’s that noise?”
Following the noise, Colin and the others saw that the source of the sound was “Arsonist Tao Tie.”
At that moment, they could see him holding a yellow device, which was making noise continuously…
“Uh… it seems, my Geiger Counter is going off.”
Arsonist Tao Tie, holding the detector in his hands, looked up at the dazzling Crystal Stones above: “There seems to be a bit of a radiation spike here. Let me check again…”
“Ah, this.”
Upon hearing this, Colin and the others suddenly fell silent, each feeling a bit uneasy—after all, they had grown up hearing just how dangerous radiation could be, and to be sitting in such an environment all of a sudden
As everyone watched, the Geiger Counter in the hands of Arsonist Tao Tie abruptly stopped its rapid “clicking” sounds.
Dog Brother couldn’t help but ask, “What’s happening now? Was it a calculation error earlier and it stopped beeping after an adjustment?”
“It’s not that…” Arsonist Tao Tie fiddled with the counter in his hand, a weird expression on his face: “It’s not, it seems that the metal wire inside might have burned, ah, you could also think of it as a fuse…”
No sooner had he finished than everybody went quiet, their faces looking a bit uneasy.
They hadn’t expected to be treated to this kind of “radiant aura” just after coming in.
“So why are we sitting here not running?” “Picking a Name Is So Hard” couldn’t help but speak up.
“There’s no rush. We’ve been sitting here for a while, and if there was really a problem, it would be too late to run now.”
Arsonist Tao Tie explained, “Looking at it now, the problem shouldn’t be big since this is used to measure some special scenarios, and the threshold is not high. It could burn even if you undergo a CT scan, so burning doesn’t mean there’s a problem…
“Moreover, we’re uncertain about what kind of radiation source it is…
“Since the mermaids have been using it without any issues, it means that this type of radiation probably isn’t very harmful.”
“Let me take a look…”
Colin interrupted him, reached into his “Storage Bag” with his right hand, and pulled out a lens. He held it between his fingers, positioning it in front of his left eye, looking towards the glowing Crystal Stones.
Ever since he had accidentally made Direct Gaze at “Hunger” and nearly fell prey to it last time, he has been extra cautious every time he uses it.
And here, there shouldn’t be a risk of coming across anything one isn’t supposed to see.
Soon, after the spiritual infusion, lines of interpretive text began to emerge.
[You may not be clear about the origins of those radiations, but intuitively, you believe that based on your physical condition, the impact on you isn’t significant, falling within a range that is completely unaffected.]
[You can enjoy these radiations to your heart’s content…]
“It should be fine,”
Colin put away the lens and explained, after which everyone breathed a sigh of relief.
On the side, the Arsonist saw Colin’s lens and couldn’t help but say, “Could I borrow that lens? I can pay a fee of 100 points…”
He was familiar with the item, as he had seen others use it in earlier team missions and felt it was quite good.
However, that person disappeared soon after reaching F Level, and later on, their equipment showed up in the auction house, presumably because they had been killed.
Unfortunately, at that time he was in dire need of points and thought to buy it later, but didn’t expect that Brother Shunzi got it first.
‘A hundred points, what a joke…’
Colin pursed his lips and casually tossed the item over: “I hope you make good use of it.”
The more knowledge one had, the more comfortably they could use this tool. If giving it to the Arsonist could lead to something big, it would be worth more to him than a mere 100 points…
After that, Colin looked at the others: “Since there’s no issue, let’s continue our previous discussion.”
“Yeah,”
Dog Brother nodded: “Since the Fishmen are also people, the remaining question is how we should go about preaching. But I have a question… We haven’t preached before, right? Was it Brother Shunzi who made a move earlier?”
As he spoke, besides the Arsonist who had gone to study the glowing crystal stones nearby, everyone else turned their gaze to Colin.
“No.”
Colin shook his head and explained about the company’s criteria for determining Believers. In his view, most likely, as long as they had enough contact with the local humans, they could be considered “Believers”.
Or to put it another way, as long as these people showed a certain level of recognition towards them, it should suffice.
Meeting the conditions shouldn’t be difficult; maybe they could just help the locals with some chores, fully demonstrating their goodwill, and get these folks to acknowledge them, which could also stand a good chance of completing their mission.
“I have observed before that there are three to five hundred merpeople here; we don’t need everyone’s recognition, just one third will do.”
“However, we must be cautious with these matters to avoid arousing their suspicion.”
…
Just as everyone was nearing the end of their discussion, Tina finished her conversation with her mother, and then immediately brought over a dozen “Sea Sirens” to them.
They carried a few large squid tentacles that had been killed, sliced into pieces, very pale and tender, with some seaweed as garnish.
Besides that, there were also some small squids wriggling on the plates.
“Hi!”
Tina called out from the edge of the water pool, prompting Colin and his companions to immediately end their discussion, walking over with trademark smiles on their faces, but glancing at the live squid, he was about to suggest perhaps cooking them.
Then, they watched as Tina grabbed a squid that was about the size of their heads and started eating it, her mouth full of ink:
“It tastes better this way.”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 303 - 303 301 Where are the Fishmen Where is my big
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 303: Chapter 301 Where are the Fishmen? Where is my big group of Fishmen?_1 Chapter 303: Chapter 301 Where are the Fishmen? Where is my big group of Fishmen?_1 “Uh.”
It wasn’t that eating raw squid had much of an impact on them; rather, it was just now that they noticed the pointy teeth in the mouths of these mermaids, which contrasted sharply with their beautiful appearance…
‘No wonder Brother Shunzi said before that mermaids are all good, as long as they don’t open their mouths.’
Colin blinked his eyes, relieved that their teeth seemed to be retractable and didn’t usually affect their beauty.
However, the squid still had to be roasted to eat.
It was when Colin was controlling the fire to grill that he realized the mermaids present were staring at him, their eyes seemingly shining, and they crowded around him one by one like sea caterpillars.
This scene resembled someone who has finally found a spark in a frozen wasteland…
His mind whirring, Colin had an idea, “Do you like this flame?”
He found these mermaids seemed to have simple minds, not very complicated—at least, it might just be that he happened to meet a group of simple-minded mermaids.
Others, like Her Majesty the Queen, were very mysterious and extremely cautious.
“Mhm mhm.”
Upon hearing Colin’s words, the “Sea Sirens” looked at each other then nodded in unison.
Seeing this, a wave of joy surged through Colin’s heart.
‘Found the breakthrough, it must be the power of the “Firebearer” that attracted them…’
Yet at this moment, Colin also suddenly remembered that during “World Code-13,” what the Believers anticipated the most seemed to be the “Holy Fire Mass” he conducted every week upon his arrival.
Not long after quickly satisfying their hunger, Tina shyly looked at Colin:
“Sir Bonfire, could you, show us that again? That big flame.”
“Sir Bonfire” was the title they had previously told them to use.
“Sure!” A bright orange and red flame sprouted from Colin’s hand, emitting a comforting warmth.
“Yes, that’s it!” Tina’s eyes sparkled with excitement as she playfully swished her plump fishtail.
“You all step back a bit.”
Colin instructed the fishmen to step back; he then pointed towards the dome and, with a flick of his fingers, a spurt of flame shot out and swiftly expanded into a three-meter diameter fireball resembling a little sun.
Colin, standing under the light of the fire, was framed as if he truly were a Flame Dominator.
“Using this prop so smoothly… It seems like Shunzi has somehow managed to fully master it,” Dog Brother remarked, recalling how they had used this thing back in “Passionate Paradise.”
Back then, his thought was—who the hell made this stupid prop?
However, once it was fully harnessed, the effect it demonstrated was indeed very powerful…
Under the warm light of the fire, not just the Fishmen, even Dog Brother and the others felt much more comfortable.
Thud…
Tina couldn’t help but flop onto the ground, like a lazy seal on the beach, basking in the hard-found light and warmth on her body.
After her collapse, the other mermaids also fell one by one, opening their bodies to absorb as much light and warmth as possible…
“Wait, what’s that smell…”
Colin sniffed the air, catching the faint aroma similar to grilled fish, and then he noticed Tina and the others, a few meters away, were steaming much like mackerel on a grill.
The scene almost made him lose his composure—
“At least flip over, otherwise you’ll really be cooked…”
Thinking it over, Colin made a gesture of closing his fingers.
Whoosh.
The grand flames went out on cue.
The cave’s atmosphere once again grew dim.
Tina and the other Fishmen, who were enjoying the warmth, opened their eyes as it disappeared and sat up from the ground, looking at Colin with a perplexed expression as if to say, we were just getting comfortable, why did it stop all of a sudden?
“I need to recover a bit and make some preparations, though…”
“Though what, Sir Bonfire?” Tina asked curiously.
“I might start charging if you keep mooching off the fire…” Colin muttered under his breath before speaking in a tempting tone, “Such a big fire doesn’t seem quite right for just a few people, does it? Shouldn’t we share it with more?”
“Share with others?”
Tina was taken aback. The other Fishmen still harbored no small amount of hostility toward them, but then it dawned on her that now was the perfect time to resolve the conflict between them.
She didn’t find her act of “aiding the enemy” the slightest bit improper.
After all, Her Majesty the Queen had confirmed with the “Deep Blue Soul” gem that these people bore no ill will, which meant they truly were good people.
And somehow, an indescribable affinity made them feel Colin was one of their own.
The only difference was that he lacked a fish tail.
“Sure, the other Fishmen are all bathing in the Hall of Holy Fire.”
After some thought, Tina decided to take everyone there. Once Mr. Bonfire brought out the flames at that time, no one would have anything to say!
Quickly, they took the group in their embrace, swimming through the honeycomb-like islands, arriving at a vast area.
At that moment, a large irregular chunk of white crystal was burning, sending up a flame five meters high.
The Fishmen lay about in twos and threes, lazily enjoying the glow of the fire…
“You’re really… roasting fish here, aren’t you?”
Colin pursed his lips, his gaze traveling over the Fishmen to the giant white crystal at the center, and he quickly surmised that it was probably something similar to combustible methane hydrate.
He then quickly counted the merpeople present…
“61…”
Colin scanned quickly, then turned to the petite mermaid, “Shouldn’t we call the others over, too?”
“Except for the eighteen on patrol, everyone else is here,” Tina said honestly.
“What?”
Colin’s eyes bulged, and he counted again, indeed only seventy-one—
‘Where are my Fishmen? Where’s my big group of Fishmen?’
They hadn’t all been roasted, had they?
“Where did they go?”
“The queen had to deal with some urgent matters and has already gone back, taking many people with her,” Tina blinked her eyes.
“Well, alright then…”
Colin didn’t insist. Sixty-one plus the eleven with Tina here, plus the eighteen outside on patrol, that made ninety in total. After dealing with these, the remaining ten wouldn’t be hard to handle.
The mission didn’t have a time limit anyway, so it wasn’t a big problem.
Just then, three ‘Sea Sirens’ clad in scale skirts came slithering over on patrol:
“Tina! What are you doing? How could you bring outsiders here!”
The scolding here suddenly startled many of the beautiful Fishmen, who jumped away toward the distance.
Some of the faint-hearted even plopped into the water and fled…
“Mr. Bonfire and the others are not bad people!”
Tina said and turned to Colin, “Quickly show them that thing…”
Once the light ignited, everyone would understand her!
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 304 - 304 302 Firebearers Contingency (Extra
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 304: Chapter 302: Firebearer’s Contingency (Extra chapter for monthly votes)._1 Chapter 304: Chapter 302: Firebearer’s Contingency (Extra chapter for monthly votes)._1 Colin didn’t delay; he secretly consumed a “Colorless Crystal” and, standing more than ten meters away, reached out shakily to point at the bonfire.
“What are you doing to the Holy Fire!” A patrolling “Sea Siren” exclaimed in shock, hastily raising a magic wand in her hand that was embedded with a round gemstone, with ice cones beginning to condense in the air.
However, before she could act, a huge spherical fireball with a diameter exceeding five meters rose from the bonfire.
From the orange-red and bright light cast by the fireball, there emanated a warmth they had never experienced before, but which was exceptionally comforting. Under this light, even the faint whispers from the deep sea that occasionally reached their ears slowly dissipated.
She felt as if her humanity had been stabilized.
“So… comfortable.”
The patrolling “Sea Siren” squinted her eyes, basking in the warmth radiated from the firelight.
Although she still harbored considerable malice towards Colin and those “non-human” beings, it was true…
The flame was indeed very comfortable.
More of the startled mermaids who had fled earlier now quietly popped their heads out from the water, basking in the flame and couldn’t help but squint their eyes in comfort—
Although mentally they still greatly rejected Colin and the other outsiders, their bodies honestly climbed onto the shore and opened up their postures widely.
Bang.
It was unclear who started it, but one by one, the fishmen all lay back down again, positioning themselves comfortably like lumps of mud, with lazy and satisfied expressions on their faces.
Meanwhile, Dog Brother, the arsonist and others noticed that the task list was rapidly growing.
“Believer” +10.
“Believer” +10.
…
“How can you, how are you able to guide the Holy Fire?”
The patrolling “Sea Siren” suppressed the comfort spreading throughout her body, struggling not to moan, as she tried to get an answer from Colin.
The “Holy Fire” was not subject to any abnormal manipulation. It could be destroyed but would not be controlled, not even by godlike beings. That was their basic understanding.
Yet, the man before her had shattered this age-old belief!
Colin didn’t answer her but, with a certain doubt, walked towards it.
He also noticed that the “Holy Fire” the mermaids mentioned seemed off, not like a normal flame…
And seeing this, the patrolling “Sea Siren,” though her reason told her she should stop him, some instinct made her halt in her tracks.
Soon, when he reached the bonfire and saw the irregular crystals beneath, there was also a clay pot containing something like grease, which when burning, faintly emitted a sensation similar to that of the power of a Firebearer.
This power was merging into the surrounding flames.
“No way…”
Colin sniffed and immediately understood—the flame originated from a Firebearer!
It was no wonder he had felt that the flame was easier to control than he had expected, almost like the fire at Bonfire Sacrificial Ground of the “World Code-13.”
However…
His eyes fixed on the grease in the clay pot within the bonfire…
“Damn, don’t tell me some Firebearer got caught by the ‘Sea Siren’ and is now hung up as a human torch?
Colin suddenly had some not-so-good associations about his own situation.
Swallowing, he stealthily glanced around and noticed that all the mermaids were lying on the ground, accepting the roasting. So, while maintaining the five-meter-diameter fireball in the sky, he surreptitiously took out the “Analytical Chip” to make a final determination.
He had retrieved the lens from the arsonist before he left.
[A can of grease extracted from various marine creature’s bodies. However, after a sniff, you’ve picked up on a distinct scent that doesn’t seem like fish, but rather like fat from a person.]
[You’re not sure, so you sniff again, and ultimately you’re fairly certain it matches what you were suspecting…]
…
“Shit, it really is the Firebearer’s grease!”
Colin felt a shock surge through him, suddenly remembering that Tina mentioned the queen seemed to have some business to go back for—could it be that she was going to shake down people and then come to capture him to make oil?
‘Hiss, the Firebearers I’ve encountered are incredibly dominant; even if I possess a variety of powerful items, I can almost be sure they are not my match. If a real Firebearer actually fell into these Fishmen’s hands, though I don’t know by what means, I definitely couldn’t deal with it.’
‘After all, if this company’s trump cards can’t win against them, a Reservist like me stands no chance at all!’
With his heart palpitations, a rush of thoughts crossed his mind at breakneck speed, and Colin couldn’t help but think about running away.
But soon, he realized there was a flaw in his logic.
If the queen truly wanted to shake people down, there was absolutely no need for her to go back, because as the highest combatant, she should stay here watching him to prevent him from escaping or any other accidents.
Someone else could handle the shaking down, or it could be done by communication.
“The situation shouldn’t be too bad, so there’s no need to panic. Even if it was, panicking wouldn’t help. Right now, there’s no escape; the only option is to complete the task and leave this world.”
“But now that I think about it… why do all these Firebearers end up in such tragic states?”
So far, none of the Firebearers he’d seen had met a good end.
Either they turn themselves into kindling, or someone else does.
This made Colin, who had already merged with part of their essence, feel as if he’d been coaxed by Lady Bunny onto a doomed pirate ship.
But…on second thought, if he hadn’t boarded this pirate ship,
He would most likely already be dead from Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), without even a chance…
“Sigh, is this what they call a blessing in disguise?”
Colin sighed, preparing to put away the mirror in his hand, finish the task at hand as quickly as possible, and then leave this place—
As for that Firebearer who might be currently used to make oil, whatever their situation may be and whether he could save them or not, it really wasn’t out of modesty, but these matters were better left to someone more capable from the company.
Given past experiences, the fact that he’d seen this meant the company was likely aware of the situation here as well.
So, if there was a similar mission above, Colin hoped they would send the “Corps,” not C Level or lower employees like him—poor, helpless, and weak at the bottom of the corporate hierarchy.
However, it was just then, Colin’s hand, which was pulling back the mirror, uncontrollably stiffened.
Immediately after, he saw a line of text emerge uncontrollably on the mirror—
[In the faint light of the burning grease, you seem to hear a whispering murmur: ‘Your appearance means that my mission in this ‘World Code’ has failed. However, successor, I’ve left a trick up my sleeve; here you may find what you wish to know.’]
…
“Hiss!”
Colin’s pupils shrunk when he saw these words, feeling the item he’d bought for several hundred points was so hot he wanted to throw it away. But before he could do so, the content on the mirror faded away.
Everything seemed like an illusion.
But he knew for sure—it was no illusion!
.
.
.
PS: It seems there have been monthly tickets these past few days; I’ll add an extra update to see if you all still have them.

chapters.title: Chapter 305 - 305 303 The Wandering Minstrel - Rosen_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 305: Chapter 303 The Wandering Minstrel – Rosen_1 Chapter 305: Chapter 303 The Wandering Minstrel – Rosen_1 “Is this… a message from the ‘Firebearer’?”
He swallowed hard, silent for a few seconds, before Colin seemed to snap back to reality, realizing almost immediately that this must be a message from the “Firebearer.”
These guys…
“I haven’t used this thing in a while, and just my luck it brings bad news?”
Colin pinched his forehead, realizing that powerful beings seemed to have a good chance of detecting him once he established a certain connection with them. He couldn’t figure out how they managed to do it…
He guessed that not only using the “Analytical Lens,” but also the “Book of Fate: Fragment” would probably cause a similar effect.
When you become aware of their existence, they too can sense yours.
“Probably only after gaining higher clearance at the company will I be immune to these things.”
Colin took a deep breath, recalling the message he had just received that purported to contain information he’d want to know—
‘I don’t, I’m not, don’t talk nonsense, I have no curiosity whatsoever about backups and information.’
What a joke, a big shot much stronger than him was hanging up there like a dripping oil lamp, why would he go there for no reason, to deliver himself to doom?
What relieved him a bit now was that the company had not generated any additional branching tasks requiring him to go there.
Accordingly, Colin himself certainly wasn’t planning on it.
Reining in his thoughts, Colin did not dwell further on the matter; instead, he opened the task panel to have a look.
“There are now 820 believers, divided by 10, that means there are 82 here who have already been subdued. It seems the flames have indeed conquered them.”
“If Little Tina is right, there are eight more Fishmen patrol teams that haven’t arrived yet, but that’s not a big problem—they can be called over in a bit.”
“What remains is just the last ten ‘Believers’ whose whereabouts are unknown.”
During his contemplation, Colin looked around the scene, where the scent of fish invaded his nostrils, and many a mermaid’s face showed an indefinable expression of contentment.
This felt as if cats had been thrown into catnip, so stimulated that they were almost rolling their eyes back.
Even the patrol squad that had just barred him from approaching the Bonfire now lay flat on the ground with eyes closed, opting to enjoy the moment first.
“The power of the ‘Bonfire’ seems to be about more than just comfort for them; I always feel that under the fire, their mental status becomes significantly more stable, more purified, as though many things have been purged from their bodies amidst the burning.”
Colin vaguely realized the reason the “Sea Sirens” yearned for the “Bonfire” was probably to maintain their own spiritual stability.
Then, he looked over at Dog Brother and the others and could see that, although their status clearly improved under the Bonfire and they felt comfortable, their reactions were not as exaggerated as those of the Sea Sirens.
It seemed that for normal people, the “Bonfire” only gave a sense of cleanliness without much of a burning sensation.
“The Firebearer’s flame has quite a few tricks up its sleeve.”
Colin exhaled deeply and then noticed that the neatly lying Sea Sirens, each one steaming and skin reddening, looked as though they were about to be seasoned for a meal with a sprinkle of cumin.
He had no choice but to remind the Fishmen present to turn over, lest they get burned and spoil everything.
But speaking of which, watching this group of mermaids made Colin wonder if the proud Sea Siren Queen would exhibit a similar expression?
If possible, he somewhat looked forward to it.
While Colin maintained the flame, in a small corner of the bright hall, Shana, executing her task as a Light Avatar, sat on a small rock, propping up her chin with her hand, tranquilly watching the flame that still seemed bright in her blurred vision.
The body in “World Code -13” was almost in sync with what the avatar saw.
“The master of the ‘Bonfire,’ huh?”
The body focused more attention and watched quietly for a while, possibly pondering something, then took out parchment and from her small ten-liter bag, extracted a creased book.
The book was filled with square, unfamiliar script, accompanied by a line of ancient Holy Light text:
“The Adventures of Rosen.”
This was a casually-penned notebook passed down from an ancient era, seemingly the account of a famous wandering bard’s various experiences throughout his life, not necessarily factual, but quite interesting.
The book always looked back on those times from a perspective many years later.
She opened the first page, which contained some descriptions of “Firebearers” from the “future.”
The main text was still in that square, unknown script, but beneath this script, there was translated content left by the predecessors from the “Light” doctrine:
“Legends of the ancient eras tell of such a group, holding flames in their hands, calling themselves Firebearers, traversing Star Domains, invincible wherever they went; where they arrived, all people worshipped.”
“They knew neither whence they came nor whither they were bound, but in each place, they would suppress all calamities, bringing dawn.”
“Upon departure, they left part of their power to suppress terror, making countless disasters tremble; whenever they were mentioned, all beings could only describe them with awe.”
“In their era, within the ‘Solar System,’ all anomalies had been quelled, and from this point, they looked out over the entire Galaxy, gazing into the universe and even the multiverse.”
“Even among the most ancient and unknowable, many had been expelled by them after overcoming countless hardships.”
“Later, for reasons unknown, they were about to depart, but there’s no need to worry, it’s only temporary…”
“When The Night comes, the Bonfire will reappear, shining through the eternal night.”
….
“Could the records in this ancient book be true?”
Shana raised her head to look at the flames flickering in the vague distance and couldn’t help murmuring to herself. She didn’t use to believe, treating it merely as a story since in some sense, this notebook was a collection of both true and false tales.
It also mentioned something about a holy mountain in the mists, holding a Holy Relic that dispelled all evil, akin to a Brave One obtaining a dragon-slaying sword.
She once believed it to be true and genuinely sought it for a while, only to find nothing there and wasting a lot of time, leading to quite an injury…
If not for those injuries, she might have been able to save even more people this time.
But now, feeling the faintly discernible special power in the flames…
Perhaps, this story could also be possible?
After all, not everything in it was false…
“Bang.”
Shana closed the book, her gaze lingering on a line of text below the cover.
This script seemed shielded by some unfathomable power, rendered indecipherable to this day; she could barely make out it was a signature, with only the words “Rosen” recognizable.
“Perhaps, when the time comes, I can ask him to take a look at it?”
The Saintess seemed to have some ideas; her strong Spiritual Intuition made her feel that there was a high likelihood he knew the content above.
If it weren’t for the fact that she couldn’t converse with him or make actual contact during mission execution apart from applying Status, she would want to discuss the contents of the book with Colin right now.
But that’s alright, it won’t be long now.
However, if Colin saw this book, he would indeed immediately recognize the text as a very formal corporate seal:
“‘Bonfire Campsite’s’ Special Resident Executive – Rosen.”
Then, for the content therein, he would most likely ridicule it, commenting that Rosen had no idea which online novel he copied this exquisitely fairy-tale-like section into his notes.
Because the fairy tale essence is just too potent…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 306 - 306 304 Will You Hatch the Egg with Me_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 306: Chapter 304 Will You Hatch the Egg with Me?_1 Chapter 306: Chapter 304 Will You Hatch the Egg with Me?_1 After the massive fireball had been approaching for close to an hour, seeing that the situation was about right, Colin retracted his control of the flame.
Although with the effect of that special grease, he could continue to burn for another two or three hours, it wasn’t necessary because all the Fishmen present had already transformed into believers.
“If there’s a chance, I should see if I can collect some of this Good Brother’s grease. Not to discuss his fate, but the grease on his body does burn well.”
If he could collect more to use in battle, Colin felt that his control over flames would likely see a significant improvement.
Having left the center of the Bonfire, the mermaid on patrol on the ground immediately noticed him and awkwardly got up, “Hmph,” she insisted, saying:
“Hmph! Don’t think this means you’re not at all suspicious!”
‘If it weren’t for my status showing that all the ‘Sea Sirens’ present had become ‘believers,’ I might actually believe that you are truly as hostile toward me as you claim to be.’
Colin glanced at her, didn’t say much, knowing she was probably just being stubborn while soft-hearted, trying to say something for the sake of appearances—
It had a bit of a tsundere feel to it.
However, tsundere was kind of out of fashion these days…
By the time he left, these Fishmen would probably search the entire Deep Sea and still not find flames as comfortable as these.
And at that very moment, as Colin left the Bonfire, the gigantic fireball with a diameter of several meters slowly faded away.
One by one, the mermaids, who had been comfortably roasting, opened their eyes, groggily propped up their upper bodies, searched around, and looked towards Colin as if to say: burn, why did you stop burning?
Even though the Bonfire was still there, after experiencing Colin’s hot and large flames, they were no longer satisfied with this “little flame.”
“Cough cough…”
Colin coughed twice, showing a hint of weakness on his face: “I’m not feeling very well, let me rest a bit before we talk.”
After saying that, he saw the look in many a stunning Fishwoman’s eyes, those big watery eyes expressing a flicker of disappointment, longing, and dissatisfaction.
Some of them blinked, making a gesture like they were about to pounce.
“They aren’t really planning to hang me up there to burn, are they?”
Colin’s heart skipped a beat.
But at this moment, Tina suddenly rushed out, hugging him like a rag doll, and faced the crowd of Fishwomen, big and small, huffing:
“‘Sir Bonfire’ needs to rest now!”
Having said that, without waiting for the other mermaids to respond, she hugged Colin and plunged into the water with him, like a child worried her toy would be snatched away.
After they left, the mermaids directed their gaze towards Dog Brother and the others, their eyes flickering with an almost tangible sense of anticipation.
For the first time, Dog Brother and his companions understood what it meant for “eyes to speak.”
Unfortunately, they couldn’t satisfy these Fishwomen.
“Er, we don’t know how to play with fire…” The group explained awkwardly, then a few Fishwomen approached, one Fishwoman for each, and carried them away from there.
However, upon returning to the great hall, they didn’t find Colin’s figure.
“Where did the boss go?” Dog Brother asked curiously.
…
In another room, on Honeycomb Island, adorned with various sparkling gems, the much larger Tina laid him on a soft sponge bed.
Apparently specially treated, the sponge bed was relatively dry.
“Sir Bonfire, this is my room, my room is pretty big, if you’re tired, you can rest here. Would you like something to eat?” Tina blinked her eyes.
Why does that line sound so familiar… Colin sat on the sponge bed, looked up at Tina who was much taller than him, thanked her, and declined the offer of food.
“By the way, when will other ‘Sea Sirens’ come to this island?”
Colin decided to create a breakthrough from Tina.
He could tell that Tina probably considered him a good friend, which was perfect for initiating the breakthrough.
However, no sooner had he finished speaking than Tina, as if something secret had been discovered, her face turned a bit red, “No, it shouldn’t be so soon that others will come by, it’ll be several days.”
Several days? But no big deal, given the current situation, by the time people come by to warm themselves by the fire, he should be able to take them down immediately…
Colin’s mind raced quickly, and after the reactions of the fishmen in the “Hall of Holy Fire,” he was fairly confident in his flames.
Meanwhile, Tina, staring at Colin with gold in her eyes and a touch of bashful shyness, suddenly asked, “Sir Bonfire, can I, can I ask you a question?”
“What question? Go ahead.”
Huh? Colin had just finished speaking when he suddenly realized that the atmosphere seemed a bit off.
It’s just a question, why turn so red?
“Can you, can you help me hatch a baby?” Tina asked awkwardly.
“???”
Colin’s eyes widened, he sucked in a breath of cold air, his usually nimble mind momentarily stalled as he stared at her. He sensed something amiss, considered many possibilities, but this was the one possibility he hadn’t thought of—
Goodness, I thought you saw me as a good friend, and here you want me to father your children?
And besides, setting aside the issues of size differences, shouldn’t we think about reproductive isolation?
‘I am a ruthless preaching machine, not a seeding machine.’
Colin’s mind whipped up a storm of thoughts, trying to figure out how to explain himself to avoid the “love turns to hatred” scenario often found in legends, when he saw Tina turn around and lift a basketball-sized spherical object towards him.
“This is, Sister Lana’s baby, but she died before she had time to hatch it, and I’ve taken over. I, I don’t have much experience, can you help me with it? I feel that if I do it with you, with that flame, the baby might turn out to be very strong…”
After all, hatching an egg is a rather complex and private matter, and she felt somewhat embarrassed.
“Oh, you mean you want me to help with incubating the egg? I thought…”
Colin let out a sigh of relief, his mood suddenly easing, but thinking about what he had been assuming made him feel extremely awkward.
“You thought what?”
Tina blinked, looking a bit puzzled, but the next second, it seemed like she realized something and began to speak timidly, “After we’re done with this one, it’s not that…”
As she was speaking, a splash of water suddenly interrupted her.
Both turned their heads to look, and saw a mermaid suddenly leaping out nearby, warning with a voice weak from exhaustion:
“Princess Tina, escape quickly, humans have attacked the Holy City, they’re coming this way…”
A strong scent of blood wafted over, and Colin noted the numerous wounds on the mermaid’s body.
“The Holy City has been attacked?”
Tina was taken aback, then asked with worry and tension, “Mother… Is Her Majesty the Queen okay?!”

chapters.title: Chapter 307 - 307 305 Has Brother Shunzi been taken away and
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 307: Chapter 305 Has Brother Shunzi been taken away and become angry at being a star?_1 Chapter 307: Chapter 305 Has Brother Shunzi been taken away and become angry at being a star?_1 “Her Majesty the Queen… is leaving, you must escape with me first, your other seventeen sisters have already set off, they will go to other Holy Cities…”
The blood-covered mermaid Queen’s Guard said with difficulty.
“What exactly happened?” Tina’s eyes widened.
She recognized this guard as an elite alongside her mother, who under normal circumstances, would never leave her side!
Yet now she was here…
But noticing the severe wounds on the Queen’s Guard, Tina quickly cast a healing spell.
“No need, I’ve been contaminated, and without Pure Holy Fire level power, I can’t recover…”
The Queen’s Guard said, attempting to urge Princess Tina to flee, when suddenly, a bright, comforting light shone upon them.
Under the light, she could clearly feel her condition rapidly improving.
It wasn’t until then that she noticed the pseudo-human who had been saved earlier was in Princess Tina’s room!
“This is Sir Bonfire! He can control the Holy Fire!” Tina promptly introduced.
But he was still a pseudo-human!
Although the Queen’s Guard wanted to say this, the Holy Fire leaping in his palm was unmistakably real.
Moreover, they had previously rescued some of their people captured by pirates…
“It’s a bit troublesome to remove these things from you, and the fire can’t stop the final outcome.”
Colin approached the Queen’s Guard to inspect her and could almost confirm that she was infected with the spores of the “Crimson Abyss” cultists.
However, these non-targeted spores seemed to spread slowly.
‘Considering the situation of the past two “Book of Fate: Fragment” users who were quickly parasitized in a short time, it’s likely that after we emerged, we were already being closely monitored. Strange, the second time is understandable, but the first time was targeted that quickly?’
Colin thought to himself, it was only speculation, but perhaps they were discovered as soon as they used it, which is why such a fate unfolded.
Indeed, using this thing during dangerous events is like digging one’s own grave.
Hearing his words, the Queen’s Guard seemed resigned and nodded, “I know, I can’t live much longer, and to prevent those things on me from spreading, I will find a suitable place to end myself as soon as I finish explaining…”
“Actually, that’s not necessary, I mean you can still be saved, but we’ll need to use some special methods, and it’s going to hurt a bit, you’ll need to bear with it.”
Colin kindly warned her that a spore infection was indeed troublesome, but he had the Little Maid, and as long as she wasn’t completely parasitized, her brain devoured by the spores, she could still be saved.
“Pain? How could I possibly be afraid… AAAHHHH!!!”
The Queen’s Guard, feeling indignant, was about to say that as a noble Queen’s Guard, she did not fear even death, so how could she be afraid of pain?
Before she could finish her sentence, she felt an excruciating pain tearing through her body as an intense agony seemed to emanate from every cell, making her scream uncontrollably.
Thankfully, the Little Maid was swift in her actions; the pain lasted for less than three seconds before disappearing.
Dirty blood seeped from beneath her scales, with the remaining spores quickly neutralized by the radiating light of the fire…
Although the first time was painful, she immediately felt a sense of relief and comfort afterward.
‘So that’s a +10 believers? The company’s ‘believer’ label really is casual, it feels like it should be changed to, anyone who establishes a certain connection with them qualifies.’
Noting the change in mission progress, Colin mused internally and then, seeing her condition stabilize, he directly asked:
“Can you tell me now exactly what happened?”
Hearing Colin’s words, she hesitated for a moment, then took another look at Tina before choosing to speak, recounting the events that had transpired.
In essence, not long ago, the Mermaid Queen received a message from the Holy City, their merfolk stronghold, mentioning a significant matter and urging a swift return. But no sooner had they returned than they encountered multiple assaults from the Activated Fleet.
It was only then that they became aware of the situation within the Holy City. Following this, the Queen commanded a portion of her Guards to break through the siege and inform her children to flee to other clan territories, ensuring the continuation of their lineage…
She, on the other hand, communicated with the remaining forces inside the Holy City, intending to enter and retrieve the “Holy Fire Relic,” or destroy it if necessary. In any case, they could not let it fall into the hands of the “Crimson Abyss.”
The whole incident was not too complicated.
‘This “Holy Fire Relic” of yours wouldn’t happen to be that “Firebearer” old-timer hung up and drained of grease, would it?’ Colin couldn’t help but wonder inwardly. To his surprise, the Mermaid Queen actually had over ten daughters, with Tina here being just one of them. It didn’t show, but she sure was prolific.
But then, thinking of Tina’s eggs, bearing a bunch at once seemed pretty normal.
At this moment, the Queen’s Guard struggled to rise to her feet, “Those bastards have traced my trail, and I estimate that it will take only a few hours for them to catch up. We must leave…”
“If we’re lucky, we’ll reach our destination within ten days.”
Ten days… Colin raised his hand to interrupt her, “How many of you successfully broke through?”
“Four, and there are some more holding off the enemies…”
“Then, are there any of those enemies I encountered before?” Colin gestured, inquiring if there were any adversaries similar to the God Descend Vessels like Omar present.
If not, he planned to swoop in to see if he could rescue a few people.
This was much better than traveling for a dozen days to another region.
Soon after, the Queen’s Guard confirmed to Colin that apart from within the Holy City, no such enemies were present in other areas.
Colin immediately decided to undertake a rescue mission right away.
The Queen’s Guard had initially doubted his strength, but after Colin exhibited just a hint of his big and hot flame, she no longer had any reservations.
In her view, with such power, even if he couldn’t win, escaping should be no problem.
“I’ll have the engineers move Bubble City. If all goes well, the entire city should be activated within thirty-one hours, and then we’ll arrive at the outskirts of the Holy City,” the Queen’s Guard informed Colin of the current situation.
‘Thirty-one hours, just over a day…’ Colin nodded, “Then I’ll go get ready too.”
Without hesitation, he had Tina take him back to where his companions were.
Meanwhile, back in the room where they had settled, Dog Brother and the others grew restless as Colin was yet to return.
“Those Fishmen wouldn’t have caused Brother Shunzi to kneel down and forced him to become a star of wrath in the mermaid clan, right?” “Hard to pick a name” blurted out with a hint of envy.
They had all clearly noticed that the underwater beings were giving Colin some rather odd looks earlier.
Just as he finished speaking and the others were about to say something, they suddenly fell silent.
“Why the silence? Don’t tell me you all are thinking the same thing as me? Sigh, I’m envious. So many beautiful mermaids, a bit mature, but that feeling when held, those smooth and toned abs, that soft…” “Hard to pick a name” trailed off, shaking his head as he spoke.
But then, a voice chimed in from behind him, instantly causing his body to stiffen.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 308 - 308 306 Fear of Insufficient Firepower_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 308: Chapter 306: Fear of Insufficient Firepower_1 Chapter 308: Chapter 306: Fear of Insufficient Firepower_1 “Do you want me to play matchmaker for you?”
“Coming up with a name is so difficult.” He shuddered as he recalled the terrifying moments during his student days when he’d turn his head and find the class teacher standing right behind him, which brought an awkward smile to his face.
Colin shook his head, not saying much, instead he turned his attention to the Arsonist, “If all goes well, soon we’ll be sailing to the Sea Siren’s holy land aboard this island, which is currently under attack.
“Of course, our only goal is to rescue a few people and complete our mission.
“But we should be prepared. If I asked you to create an explosive with as much power as possible within a day, could you tell me any ideas you might have?”
According to the Queen’s Guard, we’d face a substantial number of enemies when the time comes, so we’ll need something explosive to clear the way.
As a child reared in a five-thousand-year-old ancient country, Colin felt a powerful need for more firepower.
The Arsonist pondered the question and asked, “Big enough, without considering issues of propulsion or delivery?”
“Right,” Colin confirmed with certainty.
As long as he could produce it, he had at least nine ways to deliver it, though the aim might not be precise. But with sufficient power, accuracy wouldn’t be a problem.
At that moment, the Arsonist’s mind flashed with collected intelligence, and looking around, he said, “A day and a half is tight, but if all goes well, it’s not impossible to do. However, I need your full cooperation…”
“Just say what you need help with.”
“I require Dog Brother’s summoned creature for cutting, high-temperature and ultra-low-temperature methods, and the Sea Siren’s electrical generating techniques, as well as the preparation of some devices… I’ll need them all…”
“That can be arranged, but don’t you need to prepare any materials or the like?”
Colin noticed the Arsonist didn’t mention gathering materials.
“Materials? Ha, Brother Shunzi, you might not have noticed, but I have—the largest material repository here is this very ocean!”
“I had already spotted this, the seawater here contains rich amounts of certain chemical elements, as well as those luminous crystal stones. It’s a pity, though, I haven’t fully understood the elements in the crystal stones, it’s a little risky to use them rashly, but it’s no big issue…”
He grew more excited as he spoke, his thought processes coming to life.
‘Sss, a true talent never complains about their surroundings.’
Colin had worried about finding the right materials for creating firepower, but he didn’t expect that in the Arsonist’s eyes, the world was truly a treasure trove everywhere.
“By the way, does anyone here have a Decree Book?” The Arsonist inquired.
“I have three… What do you need them for? Aren’t they generally used to establish rules that are advantageous for us?”
Dog Brother spoke up. From the previous “Passionate Paradise” mission, he had made a fortune, not only updating his equipment but also extravagantly purchasing several six-hundred-point “Decree Book·Fragment.”
But he hadn’t used them much since then.
“It’s not just advantageous rules, this item can also change the environment to some extent, like altering air pressure, for instance. Normally in the open, others wouldn’t notice, but it can create a very suitable processing environment…”
“Are three enough? If not, I have a few more.” Colin interrupted the others.
“Should be about right, of course, the more the better!” The Arsonist said excitedly, having a lot of ideas about utilizing the company’s various tools, but limited by funding, he hadn’t been able to realize them.
But now, he finally had the chance for unrestrained action!
Without further ado, Colin immediately arranged for members of the Sea Sirens proficient in thunder and frost to come, and then ordered the Nano Intellectual Mechanism to assist.
The production process went rather smoothly, the Arsonist successfully extracted the materials he wanted from the sea and the air, initially confirming some of his own theories…
However, unexpectedly, they thought they would encounter enemies only nearing the outskirts of the “Holy City,” but to their surprise, they soon ran into a fleeing contingent of the Sea Sirens.
Standing atop Hive Island, Colin peered into the distance over the sea, where he saw several animated submarines covered in tentacles chasing behind the Sirens.
These submarines differed from any they encountered before, instantly giving off a militaristic vibe.
Moreover, neither their performance nor any other aspect was inferior in the slightest.
“Are these the submarines from that ‘Alliance’?”
Colin seemed to sense something, then after confirming there were no enemies like Omar, he decisively plunged into the water to take action.
He moved through the Fishmen at an extremely fast pace, swimming in the opposite direction from them.
Several activated submarines sensed Colin, but sadly, the torpedoes carried by the submarines themselves were hardly effective against such an enemy.
And when Colin approached the submarines, they released a terrifying electric current in an attempt to kill him, but to no avail. Not only that, but the tentacles and such growing from the submarines had no effect on him either.
Without high-ranking combat power to check him, Colin was virtually in a realm of no opposition.
Soon, with a terrifying Repulsion Burst, several nearby submarines exploded instantaneously under the suddenly increased water pressure.
Some of the infected surged out of the submarines, but as soon as they appeared, they were immediately killed by the Nano Intellectual Mechanism that Colin dispersed into their bodies.
After several military-grade submarines were destroyed in succession, this rather ordinary encounter came to an end.
Colin returned to the hive-like Bubble Island, and soon in the hall, he saw Tina soothing the mermaids who had just been rescued.
He stood to one side, silently counting, making sure there were about thirty or so.
This time the number was not only enough, but there was quite a surplus.
However, the “Sea Siren” queen was not among them.
‘It figures, if it was her, the chase wouldn’t have been by these minions.’
A thought flashed through Colin’s mind as he walked towards them, and seeing the “Pseudo-Human” Colin approach, the Fishmen immediately tried to flee in shock.
“It’s okay, Sir Bonfire is a good person!” Tina and the already-subdued Fishmen quickly reassured them.
And Colin also raised the flame in his hand in time, as its warm radiation calmed the faces still marked with fear.
But a few minutes later, a message appeared in the minds of several employees, including Colin.
[“Task condition has been met, please find a suitable location and light the Bonfire in front of all the Believers.”]
[“Recommended fire-starter for this task: ‘Unnamed123456’.”]
…
“Tina, call everyone over, I’ve got something great to show you.”
In the spacious hall, Colin reminded Tina.
Before long, all the mermaids had gathered there, and a few colleagues, apart from the Arsonist who was still working overtime, had been called over.
Standing in front of everyone, Colin looked down at the crowded faces below, scanning their curious expressions, then slowly raised his right hand and snapped his fingers with a “pop”.
In an instant, a huge, clear, bright flame burst forth, bringing an even more “authentic” warmth!
“Wow!”
The “Sea Sirens” all let out exclamations, their mouths forming “o” shapes.
While they were still in shock, Colin too felt that something was forming a connection with this place, regardless of spatial distance and time.
And this signified the true advent of the “Bonfire Company’s” presence!
[“Trial Task – ‘Find a suitable area to establish a Bonfire Sacrificial Ground’ (2/3)” has been completed.”]
With the completion of this phase of the task, the content of the third phase also appeared in everyone’s minds.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 309 - 309 307 Attempt to Initiate the Bonfire
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 309: Chapter 307: Attempt to Initiate the “Bonfire Protocol”._1 Chapter 309: Chapter 307: Attempt to Initiate the “Bonfire Protocol”._1 [Trial Task – “Relic Recovery (3/3)”]
“Description”: Investigations have confirmed the presence of important intelligence left by a former employee within this area, which is related to whether the company will take further actions on the “World Code”.
“Requirement”: Follow the guidance to approach the location of the object and obtain as much information from the remnants as possible.
“Note”: Upon completion of this task, you may return to reality and settle the reward.
…
When everyone opened this task, they all felt an instinctive pull from a certain direction in the deep sea, as if some eerie entity was exerting a strong attraction towards them.
“Great, it’s almost over! Just find that thing, and we can go back!”
Dog Brother and the others were exhilarated, wanting to spend not a moment longer in this accursed deep sea!
Even if there were eye-pleasing beautiful mermaids, every additional second they stayed, they felt an overwhelming, breath-stealing pressure growing heavier.
This feeling was especially pronounced while sleeping, with some of them already starting to have the same distressing nightmare repeatedly.
In the dream, they floated alone in a lightless sea, cold, oppressive, dark, with something constantly calling out to them. Their lungs gradually filled with seawater until they woke up gasping for air.
And the calling entity, besides calling, never replied; when they uncontrollably tried to respond in their dreams, they found that the caller would never answer back as if its sole purpose was to haunt their dreams.
Dog Brother and his companions were furious but helpless.
As a result, everyone’s mental status, except for Colin’s, had inevitably begun to deteriorate.
The only way to soothe their spirits was to kindle a flame.
Meanwhile, Colin couldn’t help but sigh:
“I knew it, the company, after obtaining that ‘Firebearer’s’ information, would definitely not let go of further investigation. I actually thought the absence of a side mission meant it was over, sigh, how naïve I was.”
From this direction, he could almost confirm that the target must be within the Sea Siren’s Holy City.
This risk had to be taken, it was utterly unavoidable…
Moreover, this guidance felt both special and familiar. The last time it appeared, Colin ended up finding the severed head of a former colleague, as well as the equipment “Contrarian Revolver” that burst from him.
“This time feels similar. Unless something unexpected happens, there’s either a ‘Firebearer’ being drawn out and drained of grease ahead, or some kind of limb left behind. Tsk, if it’s the latter, that would be interesting.”
Colin rubbed his forehead, feeling that the Extraordinary Ones on the path of the ‘Firebearer’ were truly like born kindling.
Whether it was for his own use or for others to burn, it was a five-star rating.
However, now with a broader perspective, Colin suddenly realized that the ‘Firebearer’s’ leftover intelligence might be worth much more than he initially thought.
The rewards given to him at the beginning seemed excessively low.
“I remember it was only a thousand or so Points, which seemed fine at the time. But thinking about it now, I was recovering a head; even tens of thousands would feel insufficient, let alone just a thousand or so.”
Colin couldn’t help but complain, feeling he had been cheated.
Of course, speaking of the task’s difficulty, due to “Luck”, apart from the corpse in the small chapel, he had almost encountered no enemies throughout the mission, making the task not particularly challenging.
So the small reward could indeed be understood…
The only challenging aspect of the earlier task was rolling the dice, with the inability to roll ‘Luck’ leading to a switch of players, and success initiating the real task.
However, he didn’t dwell on the matter and was about to continue with his preparations for heading to the Holy City.
It was confirmed that there was at least one entity similar to Omar, and dealing with adversaries of such caliber would be very troublesome. He had no basis for confidence, so he had to be well-prepared.
Just then, a piece of information suddenly popped into his mind.
[“World Code-4” Event One: “Attempt to activate the ‘The Hunger’ within after obtaining the ‘Sea Siren’ Holy Fire Relic and apply to Bonfire Company to initiate ‘Bonfire Protocol’.”]
“Is this… an additional task given to me by Lady Bunny?”
With a sense of realization, Colin saw the part about “activate the ‘The Hunger’ within” and could basically confirm that it must be an individual task.
Because among all the people present, only he had such an unlucky thing inside him.
“Wait a minute, does this mean that after getting that Holy Fire Relic, I could even use the power of ‘The Hunger’?”
Colin’s face lit up with joy; if he could use “The Hunger”, even just a part of it, he was confident in facing those things from the Crimson Abyss.
However, he had never carried out the initiation of the “Bonfire Protocol” and had no idea how to do it.
He didn’t even have a clear understanding of what the “Bonfire Protocol” really was.
“The issue shouldn’t be too big, as long as I can get to the Holy Fire Relic first. With the company’s uniqueness, I should be able to figure it out on my own by then. The only problem right now is how to break through and enter.”
Taking a deep breath, Colin turned and called Dog Brother and the others to start preparing for battle.
And those mermaids, after the Bonfire was lit, revered Colin to an unprecedented degree, showing no hesitation in any of his needs and arrangements.
As Bubble Island continued to move forward, Colin also saved many Fishmen teams, and the team continued to grow.
“There are over two hundred Fishmen now. If I use ‘The False Powerhouse’ at this time, I can instantly elevate my physical condition to the Half-step Perfection. Combined with other items, I can take on those creatures…”
“After all, things from the Crimson Abyss probably can only act through some descendant containers and can’t do it personally.”
Standing in front of the Bonfire Sacrificial Ground, Colin overlooked the sea ahead, his mind flashing with thoughts.
At that moment, the Queen’s Guard approached, and seeing Colin turn his head, she spoke solemnly,
“We’re not far from the Holy City. We will arrive in three hours. Are you ready?”
“No problem.”
Gathering his thoughts from his mind, Colin nodded affirmatively.
At this moment, he could also sense the sound of explosions ahead and the presence of multiple terrifying presences, similar to Omar’s kind. There were at least two near the Holy City!
The good news was that from the aftereffects of their constant attacks, it seemed they had not yet breached the Sea Siren’s Holy City.
Thinking this, Colin’s gaze inadvertently passed over the Queen’s Guard and saw the scene behind her, causing the corner of his eye to twitch involuntarily.
He saw Tina and a group of Fishmen, in order to better deal with some of the Crimson Spores on the Sea Siren, had tied them up to a stick with ropes and propped it next to the Bonfire.
Then, like roasting a suckling pig, they slowly turned them to allow the firelight to radiate more evenly.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 310 - 310 308 Do Not Direct Gaze at Me_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 310: Chapter 308: Do Not Direct Gaze at Me!_1 Chapter 310: Chapter 308: Do Not Direct Gaze at Me!_1 “…If I didn’t know they were being detoxified, I’d think we were grilling fish.”
Muttering to himself, Colin stepped forward, “Give them another half an hour. If they don’t recover by then, knock them out and carry them.”
“Understood.” Tina nodded and signaled the others to take down the Sea Sirens from the grill.
As the final moments approached, Colin noticed that the monsters nearby were getting more and more outrageous. Many monsters had bizarre appearances and huge bodies, with extremely deadly means of attack. Even just with their bodies charging, one could feel breathless.
Fortunately, apart from their size, the majority of them were all talk and no action. Colin didn’t need to lift a finger; they had already been dealt with by swarms of “Sea Sirens.”
Suddenly, Colin narrowed his eyes, his pupils instantly changing and turning vertical, barely able to glimpse an enormous circular island in the dark green deep waters.
Its diameter was an astonishing ten kilometers.
Without hesitation, he affixed a badge to himself.
“Everyone get ready. Follow me, and let’s break into enemy lines!”
…
Meanwhile, within the Holy City, the Sea Siren Queen stood outside the Sanctum of Holy Fire, holding the Scepter adorned with a delicate sapphire, her chin lifted as she stared at the chaotic battlefield overhead—
Countless bizarre creatures tirelessly and fearlessly assaulted this holy place. Among them were Pseudo-Humans, as well as many other unknown creatures and schools of fish, and so forth.
However, before they could get close, they were thwarted by a gigantic blue barrier that enveloped the Holy City like an eggshell.
Boom!
A terrifying tentacled creature slammed fiercely against the blue barrier.
Although it had yet to break through, the dreadful force within made the sanctum vibrate.
The Queen raised her Scepter, and strings of data-like symbols flashed in her pale golden eyes.
The next second, many metal spires established within the Holy City began to operate, and about a thousand of them released frost from their tops, lowering the temperature of the sea water.
Having dealt with these things frequently, she was well aware that in cold environments, their activity would be greatly reduced, making them much easier to handle.
Indeed, all creatures contaminated by the Crimson Spores slowed in their movements.
Seeing this, the Queen waved her Scepter again, causing some spires to discharge lightning that pierced through the barrier straight into the sea.
In an instant, a large number of infected creatures turned belly up…
And those entities blessed with divinity were forced to avoid this area.
Another charge had been repelled.
Seeing the situation temporarily stable, the Queen’s Guards hurried to her side, applying magic to help the Queen regain her energy.
“These monsters used to avoid the Holy Fire before. Why are they charging straight at us this time?” a Queen’s Guard asked in complete bewilderment.
“I don’t know. It feels like they’re rushing for some reason,” the Queen replied, also puzzled, but she could sense a feeling of urgency from those infected creatures.
That’s when a voice suddenly came from above.
“Yield this place, and my Master promises that you will be allowed to leave safely and receive the blessing to resist the Deep Sea Call. You will even be permitted to receive Fire Radiation at intervals. Give up; there is no point in stubbornly defending this place.”
The Queen looked up following the voice and saw a strange creature made up of a mass of tentacles, but in response to the other’s words, her expression remained unchanged as she replied with just one word:
“Scram!”The mermaids of the Sea Sirens depended on the Holy Fire for survival. Without it, they would rapidly lose their reason in the near future, becoming empty, wandering, irrational beings.
Only the Flame could preserve their humanity.
So, no matter what, they could not possibly give up this holy relic.
As for what the enemy had said about still allowing them to use it—they certainly didn’t believe that after handing it over, the enemy would still permit them to use it. If they really did that, they would truly become meat on the cutting board, completely at the mercy of others.
And so, just as the brief dialogue ended, another round of battle erupted.
This time, the intensity of the fight suddenly escalated, the blue barrier nearly breached multiple times.
Despite largely remaining stable, numerous enemies managed to break through.
The “Sea Siren,” already prepared, met them and engaged in close combat.
After several exchanges, blood suddenly seeped from under the scales on the queen’s body. Without waiting for her guards to speak up, she, as if unfazed by pain, kept her mind connected to the Holy City’s defense system, and calmly said,
“Pour all the fuel into the furnace, operate the Holy City at maximum capacity; I want to activate the ‘Eternal Domain’!”
“Eternal Domain”?!
The guards nearby were taken aback by her command. If executed, not only would the enemy be frozen, but they, including the Holy City itself, would also be frozen within a short time, and then die.
Moreover, a large area of the surrounding sea would become icebound, inaccessible.
“I have received a message through the ‘Soul of the Ocean’ Scepter; Queen Calydos will not be able to provide support until at least one hundred thirty-seven hours from now. Apart from using the ‘Eternal Domain,’ we will not last that long.”
The queen said in an even tone.
Queen Calydos was another “Sea Siren” queen, the most powerful one, who had allied with the humans and possessed an Emperor Level Deepwater Battleship.
That thing was enough to deal with the current situation, but they couldn’t hold out until then.
So the only solution was to freeze the battlefield until that moment…
Several guards fell silent, ready to execute the order, but just then, the queen’s expression suddenly changed:
“Wait, who is that? Tina?”
Above the dome, connected to the Holy City’s defense system, the queen “saw” a moving Bubble Island approaching, and on it was one of her daughters who had fled—Tina!
“Damn it, it’s so dangerous here; has she lost her mind?!”
The queen was somewhat frantic.
Out of her eighteen daughters, it had to be Tina, the least intelligent!
But at that moment, the three divine beings that had been attacking the barrier suddenly changed direction, abandoning their assault on them and instead started to attack the Bubble Island.
“Damn!”
The queen cursed under her breath, wanting to stop them but powerless to do so.
In her eyes, the simultaneous strike from the three divine beings was enough to obliterate Bubble Island.
However, to her surprise, just before the attack reached them, a massive flame suddenly erupted on Bubble Island. The fire, filled with a terrifying inner power, even made the three divine beings halt, as if facing a formidable enemy.
“Is this the sacred object? No, it’s not…”
The queen was stunned; if it weren’t for the fact that the “Holy Relic” was indeed inside the sanctum, she would have thought it had been taken away.
But it was only then that she noticed, amidst the bonfire, there stood a human, a human who controlled the flame, arms crossed and looking down in contempt at the three divine beings!
“Is this the same man from before? How is this possible, he can… control fire? How could the Holy Fire possibly be controlled by a person?”
The queen was puzzled, but there was no time to ponder. She suddenly heard the brazen human speak up during the standoff with the three divine beings, using a tone that sounded incredibly provoking:
“Who gave you permission to come near me?
“And who allowed you to gaze directly at me?”

chapters.title: Chapter 311 - 311 309 Blade in Hand Follow Me and Kill_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 311: Chapter 309: Blade in Hand, Follow Me and Kill!_1 Chapter 311: Chapter 309: Blade in Hand, Follow Me and Kill!_1 Three attacks, each wrapped in the terrifying strength of the deep sea current, came from three directions, almost sealing off all of Colin’s retreats, as if no method could evade them.
On the island, Tina and her little mermaid companions stood in front of the Bonfire, holding their breath, their beautiful faces turning pale from shock.
On the other side, Dog Brother and the others were also holding their breath, feeling the terrifying energy that seemed to shift nature itself, their brains sending crazy warnings, with visions of themselves being torn apart by the water already flashing before their eyes.
The only thing that gave them a bit of comfort was that Colin stood in front of the Bonfire, unflinching and without a hint of panic.
In fact, he indeed had no intention of dodging.
“Ignorant runt, so eager to rush to your death!”
In a sigh of resignation, Colin suddenly raised his hand when the attack was close enough and extended a finger towards the enemy.
In that instant, a terrifying repulsion force burst forth from the tip of his finger.
The effect of the repulsion force he unleashed in a flash even surpassed that of explosives, creating a formidable current that collided with the three attacks.
Boom!
A massive roar erupted at the point of collision, and as the shockwave spread, each activated submarine and each infected creature was instantly vaporized into a mist of blood in the water.
While some stronger individuals survived, they also floated in the sea like tattered sacks, losing all activity.
At the collision’s center, dark currents surged as the sea seemed to be ripped in half, revealing a colossal “crack,” akin to the sea being parted.
The parties involved in the attack were also slightly pushed back thousands of meters by the vibration…
“Hiss, a clash of Conqueror’s Haki? Brother Shunzi’s true strength is terrifying indeed!”
The Arsonist and the others shook their heads, looking at Brother Shunzi standing firm in front, still looking down at several divine beings, feeling an intense shock within.
Just now, they truly felt the power of nature, facing the helplessness of a hundred-meter tsunami.
Although they knew Brother Shunzi should be able to handle it, before he actually did, they couldn’t help but feel a sense of dread for him; if he couldn’t block it, they might all die together.
Fortunately, Brother Shunzi was indeed strong and managed to stop it with force.
However, in reality, Colin wasn’t as relaxed as they thought.
“Gulp.”
Colin’s Adam’s apple moved as he swallowed the blood that was almost vomited out with stomach acid—this strike was the strongest one he had delivered since he acquired the “Force – Repulsive Force” card.
If it had happened before, his stomach might have burst with fireworks, and his internal organs might have exploded out and still might not have been able to block the strike.
But this time Colin had learned his lesson; he first had the Little Maid merge into his body to protect his organs, then he fused with the “Yukionna,” and then he activated half of his “Beast Transformation Syndrome.” On top of that, he employed the “Power of the Bonfire,” activated his rarely used Talent, overlaid it with “The Light Chaser’s” BUFF, gobbled up a “Colorless Crystal,” layered on “The False Powerhouse,” and so on…
In short, after a series of actions, his physical strength reached a terrifying level, allowing him to make full use of the repulsion card.
For a short time, he could withstand the negative effects of using this card.
At this moment, after the initial clash without delay, as the Vibration in the Deep Sea began to subside slightly, three weird tentacle creatures similar to Omar arrived once again.
Behind them, a whole host of bizarre deep-sea lifeforms followed.
“Hmph, courting death.”
After saying that, Colin glanced sideways at Dog Brother, who immediately understood, promptly gobbled a Crystal, then took out a dagger and stabbed it straight into his own thigh.
Instantly, an indescribable sensation of pleasure surged from his leg.
A rich shadow burst forth from Dog Brother, and in an instant, covered all his colleagues, the “Sea Siren,” and the entire Bonfire Sacrificial Ground, temporarily placing them beyond reality.
Upon seeing this, the three “Containers” paused, unclear about what the guy from the Bonfire Camp planned to do.
But just then, a voice slowly started to spread…
“What now? Have you realized my greatness, recognized your own insignificance, and begun to fear death?”
Colin spoke calmly, his arrogant tone laced with a hint of disappointment.
After speaking, he shook his head, “Indeed, if your Master doesn’t dare face me directly at this moment, let alone you.”
While Colin didn’t understand why the entity inside the “Crimson Abyss” was reluctant to come out on its own, instead sending underlings, it did not prevent him from using it as a taunt.
For a Cultist, curse his whole family and he might not care; kill his son, steal his wife, turn his parents’ bones to ash, and he still might not respond, possibly even seeing it as bearing a burden in silence.
But if you speak ill of his “Master,” that’s a completely different story…
Indeed, upon hearing this, the three “Containers” erupted with a terrifying aura, suddenly picking up speed to charge again.
It wasn’t just them; several colleagues also felt a somewhat inexplicable impulse.
The Arsonist took a deep breath and then turned to Dog Brother, “Speaking of which, why has Brother Shunzi’s personality changed so drastically?”
When it came to understanding Colin, Dog Brother, who had previously teamed up with him, was undoubtedly the most knowledgeable.
Unfortunately, Dog Brother could only shake his head, “I’m not sure, it must be the influence of some item, but it’s rare for an item to have such a significant impact.”
The Bonfire Company did have items that could influence a person’s personality, but their effects were usually minor.
At “Passionate Paradise,” Brother Shunzi did not seem to have used such a thing, so he was also unclear about it.
The reason not to use it back then was either the absence of such items or because that mission had a rule that prohibited the use of personality-influencing items.
After all, Brother Shunzi had said that using the corresponding items could easily lead to being trapped to death by the “Script Book”…
However, before they could discuss further, a sudden “snap” sound came from ahead.
Colin snapped his fingers.
“It’s our turn!”
Hearing the sound, the Arsonist quickly proceeded as planned, taking out a simple detonator and connecting it to the metal wires already laid out on the ground.
A Beautiful Mermaid on standby immediately stepped forward and used her scepter to create a bolt of lightning, striking it.
As the electric current traveled along the fuse, the flammable and explosive substances filling the island underwent a violent chemical reaction at that moment.
In the next instant, a shocking explosion burst furiously.
The three Divine creatures, driving a multitude of sea animals toward them, directly faced this horrifying detonation…
Boom!
Within the suddenly flashing firelight, a frightening shock wave erupted once more, and the sea in the area instantly roiled.
“Damn it!”
A “Container” cursed under his breath; all their attention had been focused on Colin, and they hadn’t anticipated the very ground beneath their feet—the island itself—contained a deadly move.
They prepared themselves as quickly as possible.
As for the dependent creatures, they could no longer be cared for; it was time to trust in their own instincts…
Meanwhile, Colin and his companions, shrouded in shadows, also felt some vibration, but the impact was not significant, much like experiencing an ordinary third or fourth-level earthquake.
However, the waterborne floating island they were on, which had been quite substantial, now consisted only of the thin layer they stood upon.
Only the great Bonfire leaped behind them…
‘It’s about time; those spores can’t invade the shadow realm for a while, no worries about parasitism, and with the minions cleared out, we can start the assault,’ Colin thought. He intended to say just that, but when he spoke, it came out as:
“Heh, the annoying noises of those mongrels are gone, so can I finally take pleasure in this properly now?”
As he spoke, he reached back with his hand, and the Bonfire, like a stream of red light, surged toward him and cloaked his body like a cape.
Not waiting for the enemies to react, he charged out, leading with Bone Spur and revolver in hand.
“With the blade in hand, follow me to kill!”
A large group of Sea Sirens, ready in position, adopted their familiar stances and followed the fiery figure ahead, breaking out towards the Holy City in the opposite direction.
Several colleagues, “inconvenienced” in the water as before, sat uselessly, each ensconced in the embrace of a Beautiful Mermaid.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 312 - 312 310 Come Here Let Me Devour You_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 312: Chapter 310: Come Here, Let Me Devour You!_1 Chapter 312: Chapter 310: Come Here, Let Me Devour You!_1 “Charge! Charge! Charge!”
Her Majesty’s Guard led the formation of the team, initiating a mass charge at a grand scale.
At this moment, the charging troop consisting of hundreds of people was like a sharp blade cutting through the stream, forcibly carving out a path through the murky, deep red waters ahead.
Monsters that had survived the two charges but were in their path were torn to shreds.
Three “Crimson Abyss” Containers granted with divinity appeared once again.
In the sudden explosion, they sustained some injuries, but not many, and not severe.
‘Indeed, with a bit of “Divinity”, they are too hard to kill, whether it’s control over otherworldly abilities or vitality, one can feel some kind of qualitative leap.’
