[Feature 2 “Herald”: In any area of the “Deep Sea (World Code -4)”, when every three believers pray together, a portion of the Bonfire can be summoned to descend.]
[Feature 3 “Bonfire Messenger”: From among the believers, the chosen one, after passing judgment, will receive the “Bonfire Blessing”. The maximum number of people is 3, current number 0.]

chapters.title: Chapter 322 - 322 320 Is the Company No Longer Able to
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 322: Chapter 320 Is the Company No Longer Able to Compete?_1 Chapter 322: Chapter 320 Is the Company No Longer Able to Compete?_1 “This is… Lady Bunny upgraded it directly to the fifth level?”
Colin came to his senses and remembered the signature at the end of the paper he had seen before, knowing that things should be more or less as they appeared.
He just wasn’t clear on how the other party could upgrade the flame directly through a piece of paper.
He remembered that to upgrade this thing, shouldn’t one need to submit a bunch of containment subjects, as well as points and the like?
‘However, with Lady Bunny handling the upgrade, that does save me a heap of points and resources.’
Colin pursed his lips, then took a closer look at this “Bonfire Sacrificial Site” and quickly became disappointed to find that this bonfire seemed not to produce “eggs”, that is, it wouldn’t yield things like “Colorless Crystals”.
Not only that, it lacked functions such as enchantment and had only some characteristics that didn’t mean much to him…
“‘Will of the Cinder King’, feels like some sort of defensive self-preservation method, the strength of this will is probably enough to confront the ‘Crimson Abyss’ head-on, but… it’s not very useful to me, ‘Herald’ is also not very meaningful, ‘Bonfire Messenger’ too has limitations, not of much significance…”
After scanning it once more, Colin couldn’t help but sigh with resignation; all the features listed had geographical restrictions.
They weren’t very meaningful to him…
Unless he was planning to spend his life in World Code-4 with the mermaids, they indeed weren’t of much use.
But when he turned around and saw the excited expressions on the faces of the “Sea Sirens”, slightly flushed with beauty, he felt an indescribable sense of accomplishment.
‘Maybe this is the psychological satisfaction that comes from the joy of helping others?’
With that thought in mind, Colin explained to the group of mermaids how the “Bonfire Sacrificial Site” worked and informed them how it should be used now.
The “Sea Siren” queen was dazzled by his words—this was much more useful than the holy relic they had before!
After explaining all that, Colin finally spoke about his own matter:
“We’ll probably leave here temporarily in a few minutes…”
“Ah? Sir Bonfire, are you all leaving in a few minutes?”
Tina couldn’t help but interrupt Colin nervously, then seeing Colin nod, her eyes filled with a thick sense of reluctance, “I still want to take you to some places to have fun. There are some really fun and delicious things in the Holy City, can you stay a little longer…?”
“Tina!” the queen suddenly spoke up: “Do not disturb Sir Bonfire’s regular mission!”
Colin waved his hand: “It’s okay… Whether I can stay longer isn’t under my control, there’s nothing I can do.”
“Then, will you come back?”
Hearing this, Colin thought for a moment, then continued, “Well, there’s a high probability. And it won’t be too long before we might come over again…”
Listening to Colin’s words, Tina’s eyes lit up, but the others, like Dog Brother, their expressions changed—
It was only then, when they thought they had breathed a sigh of relief, that they remembered something; the most tricky aspect of “Descent Projects” was that they were not a one-time thing!
Dog Brother and the rest hurriedly got up from the steps, crowded around Brother Shunzi, then whispered:
“We are not really going to come back again, are we?”
“Not sure, we’ll probably find out once we leave, but it’s a very likely thing.”
According to Colin’s own understanding, the task here was completed in phases, but overall, it wasn’t considered complete. It was just the beginning, and he estimated it would have follow-up arrangements like “World Code-13”.
But what those arrangements would be was far from clear…
‘Now I have an ongoing task in “World Code-13”, and if they schedule a weekly routine here as well, then… I’d need 21 days in a week, right?’ Colin complained inwardly.
Then, seeing how scared the others looked, he couldn’t help but laugh, “What? I heard you guys talking in private earlier about wanting to find a mermaid wife, saying how pretty and considerate they are, and all this talk about ‘Star Rage’ or whatever. Weren’t your thoughts quite fanciful?”
“This…”
Hearing his teasing, one by one, they were a bit at a loss for words.
“Don’t worry, even if there are follow-up tasks, this place should be relatively safe, and stabilizing the ‘Descent Project’ is a low-risk, high-reward good task,” Colin assured them offhand.
It’s just like some companies sending people overseas on assignments…
You’re strong enough to be fine, of course… they complained internally.
“True, with Brother Shunzi here, there probably won’t be a big problem…”
“Yes, yes…”
With that thought, their mood lifted slightly, but upon hearing Colin’s next words, their spirits deflated once again.
“That’s not a certainty, I already have a long-term ‘Descent Project,’ so I may not be dispatched here again.”
At those words, everyone was shocked, remembering that Brother Shunzi initially made a name for himself because of the “Descent Project.” It seemed indeed possible to avoid this side of things.
However, before they could say anything more, a distant chime suddenly rang in their ears.
Accompanied by a sudden sense of disorientation…
All they saw was a surging gray fog enclosing them.
When they opened their eyes again, they were back in reality.
The inexplicable oppressive feeling of the deep sea was gradually fading away at that moment…
…
“Back…”
Colin shook his head, opened his eyes, stared at the ceiling, took a deep breath, and slowly sat up.
After sitting for a few minutes and acclimating, he subconsciously glanced at the digital wall clock.
“December 11th, Monday, three in the afternoon… Huh? December 11th, Monday at three in the afternoon?”
Colin was startled; he remembered entering the instance on Friday, and he hadn’t expected that over a week in the instance would be only around three days in reality—
Wait a minute!
He hastily checked the parchment and found that this Monday’s “World Code-13” mission had been skipped.
The next entry time had shifted to twelve o’clock the following Monday.
“This…”
Colin frowned. He recalled there were some troubles looming over his territory…
Skipping once meant that the next entry time would be a week later.
“The ‘Catastrophe of the Magic Fog’ was said to only possibly come, but not necessarily, so there shouldn’t be an issue, and besides, the people in my territory should be able to hold on for a while.”
Colin comforted himself before noticing that “World Code-13” now had an additional “Descent Optional Location”—”World Code-4.”
“The ‘Descent Project’ won’t stop, but I can choose where to go. However, next week I’ll definitely go to ‘World Code-13’ to resolve the troubles there.”
Afterward, Colin closed the mission and looked towards the flickering “Promotion Mission,” choosing to confirm completion.
[In this event, your rating is: A.]
[You have completed this event with an outstanding performance.]
[Below are your rewards from this event’s settlement—”Bonfire Points*37000,” “Gold Mission Voucher*6,” “Silver Task Certificate*5,” “Advanced Talent Lottery Ticket*1,” “Advanced Talent Fusion Ticket*1.”]
[All items have been transferred to the “Storage Room,” please check.]
…
“Quite a lot of points, decent mission vouchers, solid base rewards, though this time it seems I didn’t get an item lottery ticket…”
Colin frowned, wondering if his luck was too good, always drawing gold, and the company couldn’t afford it anymore, so they stopped issuing them?
However, although there was no item lottery, they did add something new this time—
a Talent Fusion Ticket.
Upon checking the details, fusing two Green Talents would reliably produce a Purple-colored Talent?
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 323 - 323 321 Task The Disordered Ghost Train_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 323: Chapter 321 Task: “The Disordered Ghost Train”_1 Chapter 323: Chapter 321 Task: “The Disordered Ghost Train”_1 “Just as well I don’t have Purple-colored Talent, that’s still manageable. Green Talent isn’t that hard to fuse; it’s the purple that is difficult…
Colin pursed his lips, planning to spend a few thousand Points later to first fuse a Green Talent and hope to get a Talent that he could actually use.
Setting that aside for the moment, before the next task was assigned, Colin decided to change his company ID name.
Wondering if he could change the streak of getting troublesome assignments…
Soon, the name change was complete, becoming: “654321”.
Though it was still Shunzi, flipped upside down, it also gave a sense of reversing fortunes—Colin felt quite satisfied with his interpretation and then accepted the next stage of the D Level Promotion Mission.
“Please, please let it not be any task from ‘Script City’, and it’d be best to avoid any Out-of-Control Copy, and of course, no incompetent teammates!!”
Colin prayed silently to himself, honestly speaking, with both “Sleeping Dragon and Young Phoenix” in their team this time, one handling explosions and the other accidents, it would be really hard to say if he was a bit weaker.
After quietly praying, he opened his eyes.
[Promotion Trial Task·Team—”The Disordered Ghost Train” has been dispatched to the “Task Bar”.]
“Ghost Train… the name of this mission seems kind of familiar.”
Colin felt like he had seen the name before, but didn’t think much of it and opened the task bar to check directly.
[“The Disordered Ghost Train”]
“Description”: In one catastrophic mission incident, a train carrying employees on a retreat operation unexpectedly went missing without a trace. This major accident quickly caught the attention of the company’s upper echelons, and after a series of investigations, they finally located the train half a year later.Unfortunately, the twelve small teams, totaling seventy-one D Level staff and one Level C Employee, had all perished, and their lives had undergone an abnormal transformation.
“Requirements”: Enter the copy on December 20th, suppress at least three train cars and three small teams of abnormal employees (failure in this task will not result in death, but after three failed attempts, the D Level Promotion Mission will be reset).
“Remarks”: The more suppression, the higher the mission rating upon completion. Upon defeating half the personnel, the top three contributors may choose the defeated employees’ hand-held items as their own rewards, in order of merit.
“Current task participants”: Form your own 5-member small team, current number waiting to form a team (34). If you fail to form a team before time runs out, five people will be randomly selected for entry.
…
“Damn it, seventy-one D Level employees gone, plus a C Level… The casualties are that massive?”
Colin was shocked by what he read in the description. You need to know that there aren’t necessarily seventy-one D Level employees in the company now, and here more than seventy had died…
In these circumstances, is it really appropriate to use it for their promotion task?
“It seems to be different from immediate tasks like ‘Sea of Lightless’. Is it like ‘Self-Selected Task Events’, depicting past incidents as a ‘copy’? Does that mean this happened in the past?”
“To speak or not to speak, it feels a bit immoral, to make a copy out of dead employees’ experiences. I wonder if their families would accept this…”
“However, since it’s been made into a copy, the content inside must have been altered. Otherwise, with such difficulty, not to mention a mere Employee Level E like me, even if you pulled in a truckload of D Level employees, they might not make it.”
Thinking this, Colin let out a sigh of relief and then took a serious look at the task again.
“A team per train car, just need to fight three out of the twelve teams, the requirement doesn’t seem that high…”
“But on average, it looks like a team has about five or six people, and these people were all D Level staff before their deaths, and we would need to contend with fifteen such individuals…”
“Tsk, overall, this task is quite difficult among the regular tasks. If we fail, we’ll have to start over.”
Colin pursed his lips again, without using some kind of edge, he didn’t feel too confident about taking these people down.
A couple of them could still be handled…
With the crowd growing, he also couldn’t really handle it.
After all, they were all D Level employees, who knew what strange and bizarre items they had on them.
However, fighting with former colleagues was still quite interesting.
“Currently, every D Level employee in the company holds at least one piece of Purple Gear, a few might have Orange Gear, and as for Gold, I don’t know if there are any, but those D Levels who died shouldn’t be much different.”
Colin thought for a moment, then casually opened the dedicated chatroom for forming teams.
“The Company’s Number One Handsome Fella”: Powerful team short two people, need support and someone who can tank, contact me directly if you have…
“Storm Warrior Gay Lot”: Speedrun team needs someone who can give BUFFs, or heal…
“Son of Sadomasochism”: @Storm Warrior Gay Lot, what kind of speedrun are you talking about, if you were truly speedrunning you wouldn’t be shouting here? Besides, my team is the strong one, we nearly finished two carriages without a healer, need someone with healing or BUFF capabilities…
“Gentleman Nangong Hate”: Got 34 people, the number waiting for a team seems to have increased by two, looks like Brother Shunzi just finished a mission?
“God? Start!”: One “654321,” one “Card Dealer Your Mom Is Gone,” doesn’t seem like they’re related to Brother Shunzi’s team, no point, they appear to have started some other Second Order promotion copy.
“I Am the Cutest”: Four missing one, need someone with strong offensive capabilities, five Level Cs to charge in…
…
“Ah, this… seems like we’re lacking people with support abilities?”
Colin looked at the people and the conversation in the chatroom, no wonder it was familiar, since that “Son of Sadomasochism” was always in the “Interaction Hall” looking for someone who could play support.
He briefly flipped through the browsing history, from their conversation, this ring mission seemed quite difficult.
A team needed a reasonable distribution of roles.
And there was a high demand for someone skilled in healing tactics…
Because the interval between battles was short, they needed rapid recovery of status, and the enemies apparently had ways to disrupt mental states, so it was necessary to have some capable of applying specific effect BUFFs.
“Lots of Cs but short on healers.”
Colin muttered to himself and didn’t rush to join a team. After all, there was still quite some time until December 20th.
He decided to watch for a while longer before deciding…
Then, as if it was his habit to light a cigarette at his bedside after finishing every task, he closed that content and opened the “Chat Hall” for a glance.
At this moment, everyone inside was exclaiming about the “Wave Rider Seek Pig” and “Arsonist Tao Tie,” the Sleeping Dragon and Young Phoenix teaming up and still coming back safe and sound, or it was still “Brother Shunzi taking all the heat” and such.
Colin scanned these matters and didn’t pay much attention.
It was just that seeing one of the guys trapped below the eighteenth floor of the hospital tagging him, he couldn’t help but lament:
“This guy really knows how to hang in there, I have no idea how he does it…”
Now he was starting to doubt whether this guy was still normal.
However, apart from that, after watching for a while, he noticed something strange on the chat forum that piqued Colin’s curiosity…
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 324 - 324 322 The Emperor of Labor Virus Incident _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 324: Chapter 322 “The Emperor of Labor Virus Incident” _1 Chapter 324: Chapter 322 “The Emperor of Labor Virus Incident” _1 “Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦”: What’s going on, why don’t I have a daily task this week? It’s been two weeks!!! A whole two weeks without a task, and I’m just one bronze Mission Voucher away from starting the E level Promotion Quest…
“Loafing Immortal”: I do have tasks, but it seems like the difficulty level has suddenly increased…
“Unnamed 114514”: @Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦, I know, I know, but because it involves some secrets, I can only tell you privately…
“Partner of Justice”: No, to be precise, it’s the tasks in regions like C, US, UK, RUS, EU, and so on that have been reduced. If you go to some more remote areas, there are still a lot of tasks.
“Zhan Wangdao”: Don’t feel anything special, I still have two to three weekly routine tasks, so many that I don’t even feel like doing them.
“Professor Cute Cuddle”: @Zhan Wangdao, you better do the tasks while you can. The truth is, the company recently hired a bunch of people and the tasks have been spread out. F Level is the first to be hit, E Level is next, D Level will probably be unaffected for the time being…
“O God? Start up!”: Damn, how did things start to get so competitive? Could there be a problem with these people?
…
“Is this… the content collaboration with Lady Bunny officially taking effect?”
Colin glanced around and quickly realized the underlying reason. Most likely, as Lady Bunny had mentioned, general tasks are now being prioritized for official personnel.
This also leads to some people starting to miss out on tasks.
However, what he didn’t expect was that this situation existed not only nationally but internationally as well…
“The internal chat channel has indeed become super active all of a sudden, how many people did they hire this batch?”
Colin originally thought it might just be one or two hundred people domestically, but he didn’t expect that there had been international recruitment as well.
Now, estimating roughly, he felt that there might be thousands in this batch, almost doubling the number of people…
And as he continued to scroll through the chat, he noticed that some of the old employees began to suspect that these newcomers were some kind of new invaders who specialized in snatching tasks and hindering their development…
Some even called it the “Emperor of Labor Virus Incident”.
“Tsk, people complained when there were too many tasks, and now they complain when there are too few. Really should round them all up and take them to build the Other World with me.”
Colin pursed his lips. There might be more people here, but his “World Code-13” was still short-staffed!
Even if he brought this whole crowd over, there would be a use for them—after all, the Points are distributed by the company, not by him. The more people, the better.
‘I wonder when I’ll have the chance to talk to Lady Bunny again…see if there’s a way to fulfill the employees’ wishes and give them more job positions. Nowadays, everyone’s talking about how great it is abroad, wanting to flee. The difference between fleeing abroad and to another world isn’t big, it’s all about fleeing in the end.’
The thought flashed through his mind, and Colin couldn’t help but laugh a little.
He knew that if such an opportunity really came, the employees would probably cry like imps.
Just like the Arsonist and the others, he could see from the chat that their “Descent Project” was not over. Starting from next Monday, they had to make a trip to “World Code-4” every week.
The only difference between Colin and them was that he could choose whether to go to “13” or “4”.
“That’s not bad, at least… their mermaid wives might have a chance, and the salary is high too.”
Seeing others involved in the “Descent Project” like himself, Colin felt rather relieved.
In terms of benefits, the offer was actually quite generous. He earned more than 30,000 Points, while Dog Brother and the others each got between ten and fifteen thousand, which was more than they had earned in several years with the company…
Though the subsequent rewards definitely wouldn’t be that much, at least a thousand or two could still be expected, which was already a decent treatment.
The only little flaw was the high likelihood of encountering a wide variety of unlimited unexpected events, which made it slightly more prone to, well, kicking the bucket…
But no big deal, if he accidentally kicked it, cremation and buying a box could even afford one with diamonds, slightly more noble than others.
With each whimsical thought passing by, Colin put away the Parchment, then reached to the bedside and found the always-charging phone, swiped the screen, and was momentarily puzzled by a message from an unfamiliar beautiful girl avatar.
Not until he saw the note “Old Master Wu” did he remember who it was.
“Kikyo from Inuyasha? Keeping a young mindset.”
Colin pursed his lips, opened the avatar, and saw the reply—
Regarding the previous experience of sudden relief.
“Recently, there has been a noticeable increase in abnormalities in some regions, and the ‘Barrier’ has been somewhat impacted. This situation is not unusual, it’s like ‘showers’ that appear occasionally, hence causing some fluctuations. But I have a premonition that there seem to be other things hidden in it, just that at the moment, there isn’t much to go on…”
…
“Just ‘showers’?”
Colin furrowed his brow, feeling something was off, but couldn’t quite put his finger on where exactly.
Then he collected his thoughts and continued reading the following content sent by Old Master Wu, which spoke about the tasks.
“Bonfire Company far exceeds us in detecting anomalies, uncovering many hidden elements in various regions and resolving a large number of potential dangers before they could erupt. In this regard, I, on behalf of myself and the entire Global Supernatural Alliance, want to express our gratitude to you. Of course, the corresponding rewards will be sent to Base No. 5 in due time. As for the content, I guess you might be interested…”
Finally, we started more formal cooperation huh…
Reading this, Colin felt a bitter-sweet sensation, realizing now he had to burden old employees. Also, he wondered what the mentioned rewards could be…
And in the third part behind it, it was mentioned that the official side had already preliminarily prepared a list of Containment Subjects to trade with the company, with items continuously arriving at Base No. 5, asking him when the trade would take place.
“Lady Bunny didn’t reply, and I don’t know either…”
Just as Colin was about to respond that he wasn’t certain, a message suddenly popped into his head.
[The task event “December 15th train trade” has been issued.]
“December 15th, that’s in four days.”
Colin nodded, opened the task to check it, and saw no mention of how the train would come, nor the specific location, just that he should be there when it happens.
Without thinking much, he sent a message back.
Then he looked at the next item of content, which was about various anomalies within the company.
But after seeing just one, his expression became slightly strange.
“If possible, find out who ‘Unnamed123456’ is. I have some guesses, but I’m not sure.”
‘There are no outsiders here, your guess couldn’t possibly be about me, could it?’
Colin was somewhat amused, but had no intention of responding to that, as some things are understood by those who know, and can’t be discussed further with others due to matters of interest. He trusted the old man would figure it out himself.
Then there were inquiries about various anomalies within Bonfire Company.
After Colin read that, his smile faded, and his brow slightly furrowed:
“You really aren’t afraid of dying, are you…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 325 - 325 323 The Companys First Strange Tale Stupid
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 325: Chapter 323 The Company’s First Strange Tale: “Stupid Robot”!_1 Chapter 325: Chapter 323 The Company’s First Strange Tale: “Stupid Robot”!_1 “Actually went and tried to make contact with the company’s number one taboo, ‘the unnamed stupid robot’?”
To be honest, Colin couldn’t quite understand it, but he was greatly shaken.
From the feedback provided by Old Wu, it was evident that during his “sleep,” some attempts had been made to uncover what it actually was.
However, the outcome was that the employee who released the address disappeared on the spot, but that wasn’t all: one of the two Level Seven Personnel protecting him died on the spot, and the other disappeared, and an Eighth Level Personnel went mad on the spot.
In addition, a whole bunch of related experimental personnel died violently or disappeared on the spot…
Besides the new employee, none could be considered to have made direct contact; they were only trying to provide aid during the experiment.
The most crucial point was that, despite such massive casualties, they had almost nothing to show for it.
They didn’t even have a clear understanding of how their own people had died…
The exceedingly serious consequences of this incident almost shocked the entire supernatural circle of the world.
“Didn’t I say during our previous conversation that there are some company taboos that must never be touched? Why so stubborn?”
Colin furrowed his brow—he had mentioned it before, but he didn’t expect that the officials would actually dare to probe further.
The only consolation was that this was a research initiative launched by other forces within the “Global Supernatural Alliance,” and apart from a Level Seven Personnel who perished on the spot, everyone else was from abroad.
The catastrophic results were distributed, making the impact on any one region not too severe.
As for these outcomes, Colin wasn’t surprised at all; while the robots in the chat channel might seem silly, anyone who truly dared to touch the forbidden would definitely have no good end…
Things that the company cannot resolve, other forces should not even seek to understand.
Keep in mind, even “Lady Bunny” was exceedingly wary of that thing back then.
‘Stubborn, these people died, let’s just hope they don’t bring forth something else.’
Colin silently prayed, then after a thought, responded to Old Master Wu, “I’m not clear on this matter, but I surmise that it most likely involves a ‘Level 0’ Containment Subject as defined by the company…”
“Now that the situation is stable, the best course of action for you would be to forbid related research to avoid really summoning something.”
During “World Code-13,” even the source of the “Beast Transformation Syndrome” at its worst could match a Level 1 Containment Subject; yet, it had barely shown itself for long before being devoured by “Hunger.”
Though Colin had made a slight contribution at the time, keep in mind that back then, that “0-9 ‘Hunger'” was in an extremely fragmented state, with only a couple of percent intact…
From this one could glimpse just how terrifying a creature of this level could be.
Although the company and official definitions of a disaster might differ, comparing them both, Colin believed Old Master Wu would understand the horror of this thing.
Beyond that, he also reminded him of some other matters.
“Robots that don’t change their names in the group,” “Out-of-Control Copies,” and several high-level officials who disappeared without a trace, along with the elusive Manufacturing and Evaluation Departments, the War Department, as well as the mysterious protocols endowed with special powers, and so on…
These things are best left unstudied—truly untouchable entities.
“Speaking of which, officials once sent a team to track down the Red Moon Cultists, eventually entering ‘Script City.’ This kind of matter also should not be delved into deeply…”
Colin recalled this matter and immediately issued a stern warning—
If they kept probing and “Script City” merged with reality, bringing countless sealed “scripted realities” into existence, it would definitely be a world-ending disaster.
Not to mention anything else, just take the “NPCs”; if they still retained a human form that was fine, but once they lost their humanity, then any named entity, each at the very least, would be a terrifying creature as strong as or stronger than a “Level 6” Personnel, created through modification.
And this was just the case in the low-level Script City, “Passionate Paradise.”
Somehow, even higher-level “Terror Zones” were unthinkable, leaving one to dread what might be confined within…
However, after the message was broadcast, Colin realized something—it was practically an admission that he had entered “Passionate Paradise,” and there were only a few people who had recently entered that Copy…
But before he could retract the message, he saw Old Master Wu had sent information.
“Well, thank you for the reminder. We have already forbidden further attempts in that regard, and we apologize for our rash trial…”
Your reply is timely…, Colin thought, his lips pursing as he was at a loss for words.
At that moment, Old Master Wu continued to send messages:
“The first batch of containment subject names has been confirmed, about fifty of them. We will transfer them to Base No. 5 by December 15, according to the methods you mentioned.”
“No problem,” Colin responded.
“Next, there are two other things, both concerning you. First, soon, a group of people is likely to seek you out. They are from a different faction, under the guise of task exchange. I can’t really stop them…”
“It’s not a big deal,” Colin was about to say, but then he saw the next message from Old Master Wu.
“One thing, though, these people have some temper issues and sometimes they speak without thinking. I don’t know if they’ll have a brain short-circuit this time. Normal exchanges are fine, but if things go south… heh, as long as no one dies, I’ve got your back.”
Are they coming to cause trouble for me? Why does it feel like there’s a baiting element to it?
As Colin pondered, he sent the message he had already typed—”It’s not a big deal”—and then inquired about the second matter.
“The second thing is about your own destiny, which may not be very peaceful. I can’t give you details, as I’m not clear myself, but it feels like you’re constantly in some sort of large net. Be cautious in this regard…”
Old Master Wu told Colin that the situation might not have originated because of him, but it was as if he had stepped into a tranquil lake, creating ripples. Those ripples wouldn’t just disappear after spreading out; they would bounce back after reaching the shore…
“Hiss, just look at what you’re saying. Can you even understand that? Speak some human language!”
As Colin struggled to understand, he couldn’t help but interrupt.
“It means you’ve been lucky, reaped many benefits, but also unlucky, because something might come looking for you. Overall, it’s not so good; just be careful…”
“…”
Colin took a deep breath. Although he still didn’t fully grasp the concept, he became a bit more vigilant—after all, this was a warning from a Level 9 Personnel.
And thinking carefully about the most likely troublesome event recently, it had to be “The Disordered Ghost Train.”
‘It seems that although it’s not an Out-of-Control Copy, without teammates like Sleeping Dragon and Young Phoenix, nor is it a descending project, I can’t be careless because it’s a common event. I must prepare well.’
With a heightened sense of caution, the conversation with Old Master Wu concluded.
Colin glanced at other messages from Qin Chuan—trivial matters like reminding him that it was time to go to work—so he didn’t pay much attention.
“Go to work my ass; I’ve just worked so many days in a row, it’s time to enjoy some leisure…”
He closed his phone and took out the parchment to begin the Talent synthesis.
Before long, after spending approximately four thousand points, he obtained a Green Talent.
Then Colin spent points to dismantle his own “Physical Outburst” Talent, placing both into the “Advanced Fusion Ticket…”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 326 - 326 324 This Fist of 20 Years Cultivation_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 326: Chapter 324: This Fist of 20 Years’ Cultivation!_1 Chapter 326: Chapter 324: This Fist of 20 Years’ Cultivation!_1 “Crack crack…”
The sound of smashing arose, followed by a mechanical whirring that sped up progressively until it nearly sounded overloaded…
Amidst the buzzing noise, Colin’s heart gradually lifted, an unbidden memory surfacing in his mind, fearing that his two talents would snap and shatter into a pile of colorful little crystals.
Fortunately, what he imagined didn’t happen.
Accompanied by a crisp “clang.”
Colin’s purple-colored talent was ready.
A cluster of diamond-shaped transparent crystal, emanating a misty fog, floated in mid-air.
From the center of that transparent crystal, one could feel a diagram containing some unique energy, and information about it was being generated…
“What the hell, who made this thing, and where did they copy these sound effects from!”
Colin couldn’t help but complain.
He was certain that this series of “animation” effects must have been copied!
Then, he looked up at his purple-colored talent—
[“Energy Eruption (Basic)”]
“Effect Description”: Burns one’s potential, bringing the body’s functions into an outburst state, enhancing vitality, mentality, strength, agility, and endurance in all aspects, lasting up to half an hour, with a cooldown of ten minutes.
“Note”: When the effect ends, based on one’s status, it will be determined whether to enter a weakened state, so, avoid using it when severely injured as much as possible.
Moreover, during the use of this effect, please try to eat some high-energy foods.
“Remark”: The energy I’ve been holding back is already bursting at the seams!
[Expend 6000 points + 3 Silver Task Certificates to activate “Talent Exclusive Skill”.]
…
“Why does the description look almost the same as my previous ‘Physical Outburst’… just changed two characters in the name.”
At first glance, Colin thought he’d drawn a dud.
But upon closer examination, he discovered that this time there was no need to burn anything like energy, as long as there was energy in the body, it could be used directly. If you had nothing, it would likely consume one’s own fat and then muscles, and so on…
“This thing is a blessing for the overweight, just use it once a day, and you can easily slim down.”
Muttering to himself, Colin looked at the note at the end and almost without thinking, chose to upgrade.
For him now, what’s the difference between 6000 points and three Silver Task Certificates and getting something for free without spending any money?
“Ah, I’m short of Gold Mission Vouchers, and have too many points to spend.”
Colin sighed, and as points were poured into his talent mercilessly, a new exclusive skill emerged—
“Talent Exclusive Skill ‘Heavy Strike•Matchless Strike’: Harnesses full body strength into one strike for an extremely powerful energy-charged attack.”
“Remark”: Can you withstand this punch of twenty years’ worth of strength?
“Note”: Once the attack takes effect, the “Potential Burst” state will immediately enter cooldown time.
…
“This time, it seems pretty good.”
When Colin held the diamond-shaped crystal in his hand, he sensed that he could conceal its activation effect. In other words, he could make a punch that looked ordinary, like a plain A-strike, but actually contained all his body’s power.
If the enemy wasn’t paying attention, they could be instantly blown away by one punch.
The key was that as long as his own status was in good shape, there would be no negative consequences for using it.
“Combined with ‘Presence Diminished’ or Time Stop, plus Bone Spur, and adding this one, tsk, this combo, most enemies just can’t withstand it, worthy of a purple-colored talent, not bad…”
With a slight curl of his lips, Colin felt he had gained another killer move.
Then, he clenched the diamond-shaped crystal in his hand and with a “crack,” crushed it.
The special energy within quickly fused into his body, or more precisely, into the “Talent Grid” that the company had opened for him.
And just after tidying up those things, Colin didn’t think any further, nor did he care about the time. He neatly put everything away and immediately flopped onto his bed and fell into a deep slumber.
After so many days of exhaustion, his body wasn’t tired, but he just wanted to have a good sleep first.
This was also the first thing he did after coming back from each “Descent Project.”
Laying down his mental burdens, he slept incredibly sweetly—
At least for the first half of the night.
When an unknown amount of time had passed, Colin suddenly felt that within the deep dream, there seemed to emerge some other vague landscapes.
A cold and vast land, with thin air, covered in red sand and gravel, full of pits and fissures, completely silent.
The consciousness in the dream was unclear, as Colin looked around in confusion, feeling that there was absolutely no sign of life here, even more desolate than the emptiest desert.
“Where… is… this?”
In a daze, he looked up and saw endless darkness that somehow felt inexplicably cold and bloated, and seemed to be slowly writhing with many points of light within…
It was at that moment that Colin suddenly had a realization, and slightly turned his head to see a faint point of light in the boundless darkness, an intuition telling him that this little point seemed to be connected to his existence somehow.
“Is this… the universe?”
Colin vaguely had some guesses.
However, before he could think further, he abruptly noticed that there were countless black threads, far too many to count, emerging from beneath the land covered in red sand and gravel. They were eerily writhing, entwining like strands of hair…
Colin’s breath hitched as he felt an indescribable sense of oppression approaching.
But at the same time, a hazy and illusive sound of dice rolling suddenly reached his ears, as if someone had cast a die.
Soon, the sound ceased, and the outcome remained unknown.
However, a destructive blaze suddenly erupted, and the entire desert of sand and gravel melted in an instant; some parts that came into contact with the flame directly vaporized.
Similarly, those bizarre and abnormal threads were all burnt to nothingness…
And consumed by the fire was also Colin, who was in the midst of it all.
“Whoosh!!”
Colin abruptly sat up in bed, his eyes wide open, gasping for air. It took him a moment to stabilize his emotions before he leaned back against the headrest, his face full of confusion.
If he were still an ordinary person, he would most likely have dismissed it as a wretchedly strange nightmare.
But now, he no longer thought this way…
While pondering, he looked at the time. It was now nine in the morning on the following day, and he had slept for about ten hours.
If not for the nightmare in the latter half, it would have been perfect.
“Do I feel like something is trying to reach out to me?”
Colin wasn’t quite sure, but he could recall what had just happened.
And with the clarity of consciousness he had at this very moment, he quickly thought of numerous things.
“That perspective seemed a lot like what I understand space to be… Did I dream of myself appearing on some planet outside of space? The small light looked like Earth, and those threads…”
He wasn’t too unfamiliar with these things.
Because as long as one was a Level 7 “Fate Propeller” among the Extraordinary Ones, they would more or less have some of these threads emerging from their bodies. The most severe case was Old Master Wu at Level 9—his entire back was covered, densely packed like the canopy of a tree…
Previously, he wasn’t quite sure where these things were connected, but at this moment, he had some guesses.
“The extraordinary path of ‘Propelling Fate’ is based on the ‘Book of Fate,’ so… if nothing unexpected happens, could the thing I ‘dreamed’ of be the ‘Book of Fate’ itself, or the place where it originally resides?”
Frowning and thinking for a while, Colin felt there was a high probability because he had indeed joined the officials to investigate this thing.
But he had not expected that it seemed he had been discovered by the other party first?
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 327 - 327 325 The Eight Planets of the Solar
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 327: Chapter 325: The Eight Planets of the Solar System_1 Chapter 327: Chapter 325: The Eight Planets of the Solar System_1 “No, it shouldn’t have been that we were discovered, but rather that something was sensed, but what was the situation in the end, and who was it that rolled the dice? Old Master Wu? And what about the fire, it seemed to have the scent of a ‘Firebearer,’ but it was even more violent, more savage…”
His brain swirling in a brainstorm, Colin picked up his phone, planning to send a message to Old Master Wu to see if he knew anything about this.
Soon, he had composed the related content and sent it off…
Just as he was waiting for a reply, a red exclamation mark appeared next to his message.
“‘Message sending failed’?”
Colin frowned, checked his signal, and sent the message again, only to get the same result—he could no longer send messages…
After several failed attempts.
He was about to try using another device, but then had an inkling and re-edited the content to ‘Are you there?’ and sent it.
This time, it was sent successfully…
And even, Old Master Wu almost instantly replied, “What’s up?”
“Nothing much.”
Thinking it over, Colin didn’t continue to attempt that topic. He had a premonition that it would surely fail.
Countless accidents would lead such a communication to failure.
Although still very curious, as an employee with quite some experience, he knew that satisfying his curiosity by forcefully pursuing it would ultimately lead to his own hurt…
“However, it’s pretty certain that the dice in the dream surely wasn’t rolled by Old Wu. Recently, I haven’t even used the ‘Book of Fate’ directly, so it shouldn’t be ‘The Dice of Probability’ either. But then, who could it be? Eighth Level wouldn’t be capable of this, and there’s only one Ninth Level Fate Propeller…”
His mind whirled with thoughts, but ultimately, Colin had to suppress his unease and sigh, “I’ll wait until I don’t know when to chat with ‘Lady Bunny’ again and see if I can get some information from her.
“For the rest, maybe I can start by getting in touch with some astronomers.”
Afterward, gathering his thoughts, Colin rose from the bed, barefooted, and took a few steps into the bathroom for a hot shower. He changed his clothes and then stood in front of the mirror in his room, taking a glance at himself before lowering his head.
“Almost 130 pounds now, my weight is gradually recovering.”
Colin’s gaze moved away from the scale.
Since the onset of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, combined with his generally low food intake, his weight had plummeted. It was only recently that he was adjusting and starting to gain back some weight.
Nevertheless, weight has an impact on his combat capabilities, but not a significant one, the more significant effect is that it might not make his physique look very appealing.
“Upcoming important matters include the extraordinary item trade on the 15th, the ‘Descent Project’ on Monday the 17th, and ‘The Disordered Ghost Train’ on the 20th.”
Having somewhat organized what he needed to do, Colin sent a message to Qin Chuan.
Of course, it wasn’t about going to work, but rather to have him help get in touch with some scholars knowledgeable in astronomy…
“There are some things I can’t convey outwardly, or that I’m not supposed to know. It seems that no matter what, I won’t possibly know, at least not within the next 24 hours, but what I can figure out, I can try to understand a bit more about…”
Colin remembered the feeling as if he was in the universe.
He intended to contact the relevant scholars to see if he could obtain some information.
And quickly, in less than an hour, as if always attentive to Colin, Qin Chuan and the others rushed into a university at his request, randomly grabbing a lucky astronomer to bring over.
“Knock knock…”
Opening the door, Colin saw Qin Chuan, Xia Liufang, Hu Zheng, and the bewildered astronomer Sun Liancheng by their side.
After inviting them in, Colin asked his question, describing what he had seen.
Although the scholar felt that being summoned for an inquiry due to a dream seemed neurotic, considering that he was reminded by the VIP upstairs, a heavyweight, he didn’t dare to take it lightly.
“…Uh, assuming the small bright dot you saw in your dream was Earth, then, according to my speculation, it might be a view observed from one of Jupiter’s moons…”
The astronomer pondered and said, “Did you see a much larger Jupiter? Or maybe…”
He added some knowledge.
“No.”
Colin shook his head, indicating the other’s description didn’t quite match what he had seen: “I can be sure that there shouldn’t be any other celestial bodies around; um, can you tell me more about our planetary situation? I want to see if there’s any other possibility…”
“Oh, okay…”
The middle-aged scholar pulled out a crumpled map: “This is our ‘Solar System’, with a total of eight major planets, Mercury, Venus, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto…”
“Eh…” Qin Chuan pointed at Venus: “Isn’t this one closer?”
“I was just about to say… according to Mr. Colin’s description, it should not be Venus, because due to the high temperature, there is a thick layer of fog, and Earth cannot be seen.”
“All right.” Qin Chuan waved his hand.
“Could it be some kind of meteorite?”
“It’s possible, but not very likely, because…”
“…”
While they were discussing, Colin stared at the map for a while and eventually just shook his head, ending the related discussion, and sent away the bewildered scholar who had come with a puzzled face.
However, although the matter had not been resolved, he had a premonition that this was not the end of it.
‘I guess when I get enough merit to become a Level 6 Personnel, maybe I’ll be able to get further answers, but, ‘Book of Fate’, the oppressing feeling it gives is also not to be underestimated…’
Colin inwardly sighed, feeling that Lady Bunny’s investigative task was a huge pitfall.
Shaking his head to clear his thoughts, he was about to head home and lie down, maybe launch a couple of video games, but before he could turn around, he saw Qin Chuan and the others looking at him, with an indefinable expectation in their eyes.
“Okay, I’ll work for one day today.”
Colin reluctantly agreed to their request, heading to his workplace while casually inquiring about the content of the work for the day.
“There are a few events nearby that need resolving, and also, all the talents sent by Old Master Wu have arrived…”
Listening to him, Colin gradually understood the current situation, which was nothing serious, but when he saw the dozen or so people in his spacious office ten minutes later, his expression changed:
“Talent? You call these talents?”
There, in the office, were a multitude of Level 1 or 2 “Fate Propeller” members, men and women both, mostly around the age of 20, totaling nineteen.
This scene reminded Colin of a game called Pokémon, which has a learning device. This situation seemed quite similar.
Except that it’s usually just one-on-one at most, and here it almost amounted to one-on-nineteen.
“Do you guys really trust me that much?”
Colin was now beginning to doubt whether the reason for his nightmare the previous night could possibly have been the passive ability of “Deadly Insight”, giving him a premonition about this bunch of extras?
And hearing Colin’s somewhat sarcastic lament, Hu Zheng gave a wry smile: “This, well, I…”
He was a bit at a loss for words, even he felt there were a bit too many slackers.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 328 - 328 326 Progressive Anomaly_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 328: Chapter 326 Progressive Anomaly_1 Chapter 328: Chapter 326 Progressive Anomaly_1 “Ugh, whatever, send me today’s tasks. I’ll see which one to start with.”
Colin waved his hand dismissively and took his seat without giving it much thought.
Hu Zheng, on the other hand, hurriedly delivered the report that had been prepared a few days earlier.
After casually accepting it, Colin leaned back in his boss chair, casually placing his feet on the desk, browsing through the contents in his hands as if reclining in a deck chair.
In the rustling sounds…
Colin roughly understood the nearby situation and also got a clear picture of these people.
Among the dozen or so Fate Propellers, there were two or three who had joined the company not long ago, and the matters to be dealt with this time were mainly their assignments.
“…according to higher-ups, someone else would handle it even if I didn’t go, so why bother? Oh, I forgot, I still need to accumulate merits. Just pick an easy one, give it a shot, and that should do…”
Colin pursed his lips, flipping through the pages one by one.
He wasn’t afraid of doing tasks; he was wary of accidentally triggering something that could complicate the situation significantly.
After all, he had once fallen victim to an incident.
As he flipped through the pages, a group of male and female Fate Propellers couldn’t help but size up Colin.
“Is this really…the status and demeanor expected of someone of that rank?”
One female Fate Propeller whispered, not with malice but out of sheer bewilderment.
They had heard roughly upon arrival that the person they were supposed to, well, follow, was a powerful expert with at least a Seventh Level strength.
They had imagined it would be either a Divine Strike with a stiff countenance and unpredictable emotions or a Fate Propeller who looked around thirty but quite elderly…
To their surprise, it was a somewhat slim-looking young man.
From him, there was none of that indescribable eeriness that usually radiated from such important figures…
If it weren’t for Qin Chuan and others’ attitudes, they might have only considered him a good-looking guy who was just an average Joe.
“It shouldn’t be a problem…look at Brother Hu, he was at my level just a while ago, and now he’s jumped straight to Fourth Level. Plus, it seems like he’ll move up again soon. Once he reaches Fifth Level, he’ll start handling things on his own.”
“Insider gossip says that this guy might be even beyond Seventh Level…”
“Seventh Level? Are you joking? A relative of mine’s boss said that in a previous mishap, this guy single-handedly repelled a highly dangerous Deep Sea God and held off tens of thousands from Different Races, forcing them to retreat back into the sea.”
“At least Level Nine!”
“Are your sources reliable?”
“…Kid, don’t worry about if it’s true or not, just tell me if you believe it or not.”
…
“Deep Sea God? Talking about the ‘Father of the Sea’? When have I ever done something like that? They retreated on their own, not because of me…”
Colin heard all the whispered conversations around him, but he wasn’t particularly concerned about these things; he just internally scoffed a bit.
And then, after going through the dozen or so documents, he picked one out.
The title of the document was “An Anomaly in a Murder Mystery Game Room.”
An F-Level routine Sunday task required him to resolve the anomaly within, and that would be considered completion.
Compared to other freelance workers at a typical company, the biggest advantage of official personnel was that they didn’t work alone; they could mobilize far more resources than he could back in the day.
As for the murder mystery game room, someone had already entered to investigate. Besides needing to follow some rules…
Actually, the problem wasn’t too big.
Basically, one could say that when those people actually started to act, they could easily clear the stage.
‘The officials really value their employees joining in, huh? The protection is much stricter than I imagined, aside from that stupid experiment. Overall, they haven’t really let them take many risks.’
‘But that makes sense, the officials are still waiting for them to earn points so they can buy more Gene Compensation Medicine…’
Colin’s thoughts whirled as he flipped through a few more documents, finally deciding to start with the scripted murder game.
“Let’s just do this one first, arrange it, and start acting immediately.”
“Got it.” Qin Chuan quickly took over, rushing out to arrange for a vehicle and so on.
While he was busy, Colin also sat up straight, began to discreetly check his own equipment, and made full preparations to avoid an accident—
Giving his personal experience, accidents were rather easy to come by.
If there were no surprises, he might actually feel a bit unaccustomed right now.
Another ten minutes or so passed, and Colin and others arrived at the site of the anomaly, a factory located on the outskirts of the town.
These factories had been abandoned, but with the rise of scripted murder games and the like, they had been rented out at low prices to be renovated into venues specifically for scripted murder game players.
“Just realized the word ‘scripted’… I hope it’s not related to that thing, hope it’s just me being paranoid.”
Colin’s gaze swept across, noticing some of the scene setups, recognizing that this crew had put in some effort.
However, at this moment, due to the abnormal event, a security cordon had already been set up.
Colin looked beyond them, and, led by his intuition, his eyes were drawn to the second floor of one of the factories, then his nostrils twitched, smelling some restive scents.
The report mentioned that the owner of this folklore-horror themed murder game copy had, for a high price, purchased some odd statues such as ox-headed and horse-faced night-roaming deities, originally intended to add to the atmosphere.
It turned out that those things were the “real deal.”
This resulted in several employees being controlled into servants, continuously using the internet to lure people into trying…
“Abnormalities have really kept up with the times,” Colin couldn’t help but remark to himself. It was then that Qin Chuan approached, accompanied by another man in his thirties.
This man had a certain unique rigidity on his face, and through this feature, Colin could basically confirm he was a “Divine Strike”…
However, because he was only Fifth Level, the effect on him was not severe.
“Mr. Lin, here are some of the taboos of this place. Please take a look. Currently, as long as we act according to the rules listed here, even if we enter and move around, we will not be too affected…” the man handed over a document.
Colin nodded, took it, and glanced at it:
“Great Temple Museum rules: 1. Do not make direct gaze into the eyes of the statues; if you notice they are looking at you, you must divert your gaze. 2. The exhibits are just exhibits, there’s nothing weird here, no need to worry. If you find something wrong, please contact the Administrator…”
About a dozen such rules seemed somewhat interesting.
Moreover, compared to other incidents that easily resulted in death, the anomaly here was actually somewhat “friendly.” Other than the members of the scripted game crew, other players who came here were not harmed.
Only after playing and going back, they generally exhibited signs of mental exhaustion over the next two or three days, some even falling seriously ill and being hospitalized, staying in the ICU for a few days.
But overall, these were all minor injuries.
…
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 329 - 329 327 Anomaly in the Ancient World_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 329: Chapter 327: Anomaly in the Ancient World_1 Chapter 329: Chapter 327: Anomaly in the Ancient World_1 “Half a year ago, there was actually a problem here, it’s just that the people who went back then only had minor colds and such, it wasn’t until now that the situation became serious, which drew some attention.”
“Anyway, being involved in an anomaly and surviving, they can say their luck is not bad…”
After reading, Colin looked ahead again to double-check.
Overall, it should be about the standard for an F Level Sunday event, within the completion probability of ordinary people.
At that moment, Qin Chuan asked, “What should we do next?”
“Have all the people inside been rescued?”
Hearing Colin’s words, Qin Chuan glanced at his former superior, who promptly spoke, “Yes, the people have been rescued, but if we’re going to act, I suggest following the rules of the anomaly, for those unaffected to delve deeper inside…”
“Find a suitable position, our current problem is not being able to touch the source, from neither outside nor inside, but with your arrival, perhaps you might find some opportunities…”
The experienced Level 5 Personnel man was sharing his thoughts, but before he could finish, Colin waved him off with a gesture.
“There’s no need for all that trouble.”
Colin waved his hand nonchalantly, “Go on, call in a… rocket launcher or something, the kind that can do a sweeping strike, a single sweep should finish it.”
“Ah?”
The Level 5 Personnel thought Colin had some profound insight, but he didn’t expect this.
“Ordinary firepower, without the enhancement of ‘Talisman Art,’ is unlikely to be very effective, and we have few such Extraordinary Ones on our side…” he hinted gently.
To say “few” was already a compliment, it should be that there were none at all…
However, this time, Qin Chuan and the others didn’t wait for Colin to speak and started following his orders, beginning to request military intervention through the phone.
“This…”
“Don’t worry.”
Colin pursed his lips, hands in his pockets, looking ahead with a calm face and offered a brief explanation:
“For such low-level stuff, it should be following my rules, not me adhering to whatever rules it has.”
Truth be told, if it weren’t for the fact that “murder mystery” shared two characters with “Script Book” and he was worried it was a trick, he would have gone in and dealt with the thing inside long ago.
If everything was indeed as it appeared at present, the whole process might not even take a minute.
After all, he was now a genuine employee, halfway into D Level territory!
“Right, right, Old Liao, just watch, my bro Colin’s judgments are almost never wrong, you just lie down and relax.” Hu Zheng also spoke up.
Old Liao looked at Hu Zheng with a somewhat bemused smile, “Tch, impressive, with the increase in power level, even the way you address me has changed, it used to be Director Liao.”
“From the perspective of strength, I also think it should be the anomaly that adheres to our rules, not us to its.”
The usually quiet Xia Liufang spoke up as well.
“Alright, alright, I hope it’s as you all say,” Old Liao didn’t say more.
He could sense that Colin’s presence had indeed given a great deal of confidence to his subordinates from two different regions…
Ten minutes later, an armored vehicle arrived, and more than a dozen armed personnel quickly disembarked.
Soon, after setting up the artillery, with a command given, the first round of volley fire shot out. The shells hit the target at a speed that Colin didn’t consider fast.
However, amidst a roar of explosions, the target building didn’t budge.
Seeing this scene, Colin reached into his pocket, pulled out a yellowed piece of paper, and threw it out. As soon as it left his hand, it eerily self-ignited without any flame.
At the same time, Colin also declared:
“By my command, mystical and extraordinary effects here are diminished, and real-world forces are amplified.”
As his words ended, everyone’s faces changed, feeling like they had been rendered ordinary by a cut, their Extraordinary Power within becoming so faint it was almost unusable.
Meanwhile, the second round of artillery fire was launched.
Without exception this time, the seemingly sturdy reinforced concrete building crumbled like foam under the barrage of shells, utterly torn to shreds.
Strangely though, when the dust settled, a statue about two meters tall with a threatening pose stood defiantly amidst the debris.
From it, there emanated an unsettling aura.
At that moment, the statue’s head turned, looking towards Colin and the others, while at the same time, the stones around it began to levitate one by one.
But before it could take any further action, Colin suddenly stepped forward and stamped his foot onto the ground.
In an instant, a torrent of surging orange-red flames erupted, rushing forward and engulfing the statue in the blazing light in a flash.
It was at that moment that the ancient statue’s originally ferocious face transformed into one of horror, letting out a piercing scream:
“Fire Master? No, you… Huo Zheng?!”
“Huo Zheng?”
Colin, who had been ready to increase his efforts, paused at these words, but before he could ask any questions, he saw that the statue—whether it was a god of the night or something else—crumbled into pieces in an instant.
At the same time, a transparent vortex appeared and swept away all the abnormal sources present.
“That’s… that’s it? I didn’t even try that hard!”
Colin scratched the back of his head, doubting whether the statue was some kind of clone.
Because it felt just too fragile upon contact…
However, when the employee’s parchment showed the task as completed shortly afterward, Colin confirmed that the mission was indeed finished, completed just like that!
“Damn it, this is what an F Level Employee’s task should be like!”
Colin almost couldn’t help but tear up. When he compared it, what kind of monstrous tasks had he been taking on at F Level?
Now, he finally had a “childhood” experience and completed a proper F Level task.
Although it wasn’t actually his task…
“If I had known it had nothing to do with the ‘Script Book’, I wouldn’t have used the ‘Decree Book’ fragment, wasting my six hundred points. Really, all these rules and regulations, flashy and overcomplicated.”
Colin shook his head in resignation and then, without delay, continued on to his next task.
This time, perhaps really due to good luck, Colin didn’t run into a single mishap all day. With ease, he led everyone to quickly resolve three or four tasks within a short time.
At this moment, Colin finally had a clear understanding of the daily missions for an F Level Employee.
“The normal tasks for F Level, the strongest among the sources of anomalies, may also just come close to but not reach the standard of a nearly Stage 3 ‘Beast Transformation Syndrome,’ but I’m not sure if it’s because of local characteristics, that the things here carry a bit of supernatural color…”
At home, Colin sat on his bed, reviewing his experiences of the day.
Was there a sense that ancient mysteries were reviving?
Most anomalies were housed within ancient objects, with some being statues, some rusted swords, and others strange and bizarre corpses…
Then, half-squinting his eyes, he remembered how every time he dealt with a source of anomalies, they would be shocked at the sight of his flame and exclaim—
“Huo Zheng!”
“Upon investigation, it appears to be an ancient official in charge of managing fire—could it be the archaic name for ‘Firebearer’?”
Colin pondered, but wasn’t it said that anomalies are a modern phenomenon?
Looking at it this way, it didn’t quite make sense…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 330 - 330 328 Mysterious Pseudo-Humans_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 330: Chapter 328 Mysterious Pseudo-Humans_1 Chapter 330: Chapter 328 Mysterious Pseudo-Humans_1 “‘Huo Zheng’… if it truly is an ancient ‘Firebearer,’ then perhaps, mystical things have existed since ancient times, but for some reason, they all vanished, only to reappear in modern times?”
Stroking his chin, Colin felt that this possibility seemed fairly plausible.
Because many of the anomalies’ appearances are quite archaic…
For instance, the eighteen-armed, cyan-black “0-9 ‘Hunger'” Stone Buddha figure certainly wasn’t its original form, but rather the result of something; it was either possessed by or confined in the stone statue, causing it to appear that way.
“From the situation and experiences in ‘Script City,’ it’s clear that some executives within the company are keen on transforming anomalies into ‘humans.’ ‘Yukionna’ is a classic example of such a transformation…”
“Yukionna’s humanity has suppressed her instincts, and is gradually taking over that part of her. If one day she fully masters her own strength and doesn’t lose control easily, her base level of power is probably around Seventh or Eighth Level…”
“If such methods have existed since ancient times, then ‘Gluttonous Buddha’ is likely another attempt, but it seems that ‘Gluttonous Buddha’ has failed…”
Colin was curious; if today’s methods were learned from ancient times, then the ancient mysteries were there, but why did they suddenly disappear?
And why have they reappeared in modern times…
However, Colin remembered that there was no certain explanation for this in the whole world, so he didn’t think too much about it.
As for that “Huo Zheng,” besides what he could find online, he also had Qin Chuan look for it. If he could find it, great; if not, it didn’t matter…
“It seems like it’s not that important after all, finding it would probably just satisfy my curiosity.”
Shaking his head, Colin prepared to sleep, then get up to play some games for fun.
He had a premonition that he might not have a chance to relax like this in the future.
But just as he lay down and was about to close his eyes, his expression subtly changed, and he reached out to take out a Small Parchment that held a notification of a task assignment:
[Weekly Task: “Download a special software and join it to observe the members within.”]
“The timing of this Small Parchment’s weekly routine task is really spot-on.”
Colin sat up reluctantly and proceeded to open the “Task Bar” to check the details.
The task requirements were almost effortless, just like the task title said: find a special software, join and infiltrate within, monitor and observe the members inside, probably checking it once a day for a week…
If circumstances permit, try to make contact with the members inside.
All the methods to find the software were already specified; what Colin had to do was just follow the instructions.
Soon, he had completed the installation and successfully logged in.
“I wonder how the company acquired this account, but is this software imitating a penguin?”
Seeing the software that looked almost identical to a penguin but was called Emperor Penguin, Colin couldn’t help but laugh out loud.
There were no friends in the account, but there was one group that was messaging @everyone.
There seemed to be about three hundred people in the group, apparently in the midst of a class.
At the sight of the course content, Colin almost lost his composure—”How to laugh correctly like a human?”
An Administrator with a middle-parted Little Chicken avatar was constantly posting messages:
“…How to produce a healthy laugh that won’t be detected has always been a problem for many of our classmates. In formal occasions when everyone around us is laughing, it would be inappropriate for us not to, but due to lack of skill, some classmates end up making hideous laughing sounds like ‘huff-huff’ or ‘quack-quack’, which raises suspicions…”
“Today’s lesson is about teaching you all how to laugh like a human, politely yet elegantly, with a clear, crisp sound…”
“First and foremost, the essence of laughing is the use of air. Generally, there are two laughing modes, let’s start with the easier one, the jet-style laugh…”
…
“Huh? What’s all this?”
Colin clutched his phone, unable to comprehend but deeply shocked by what he saw.
After briefly observing, he could almost certainly conclude that the group members were not human, but a special species hidden within human society…
Currently, it seemed they were trying to find ways to blend into human society better.
And today’s lesson was about “laughter.”
A bunch of individuals under the guidance of the center-parted Little Chicken Administrator eagerly tried out loud in the voice chat, uttering various crazy and chaotic frightening laughs, which were unsettling just to listen to.
A vague and indescribable expression appeared involuntarily on Colin’s face.
It was clear that those flagged by the company surveillance, whose species was unknown, were indeed trying hard.
Afterwards, he browsed through previous files in the group, coming across titles like “How to Cry Like a Human,” “Decoding Puzzling Human Behavior,” “108 Small Tricks to Become Human,” “How to Find a Human Mate,” “How to Find a Suitable Job?,” “Computer C Language: From Beginner to Earning Money,” “How to Evade Official Hunters,” and a ton of other files…
“Tsk… the more I look, the more amusing it seems…”
After investigating for a while, Colin felt more and more ambivalent, first at the unexpected infiltration of so many things into human society, and second at the abnormal style of these creatures.
If the file names had been “How to Cook and Eat Humans,” “108 Clever Tips for Consuming Humans,” “How to Dispose of Fresh Humans Without Being Discovered,” etc., they would probably have been more on-brand…
“Just from this first contact, these creatures don’t seem very harmful.”
Colin made a rough judgment and then continued to lurk in the group, eavesdropping on their activities.
Finally, after about an hour, the day’s lesson came to an end.
Then everything moved into a free discussion phase…
Many were summarizing the difficulties they encountered while practicing “laughter.” Colin glanced through and felt there were no substantial contents, so he prepared to end his observation and go back to sleep, without disturbing these anomalies.
But just at that moment, an odd one in the studying crowd suddenly blurted out:
“Help! I’ve been abducted into a scam den, can someone come rescue me?”
“@Mister Weirdo: Huh, weren’t you running your script murder store quite well? How did you get mixed up with scams, what happened?”
The group’s center-parted Little Chicken Administrator asked curiously.
Meanwhile, Colin, who was watching from behind the screen, also noticed the words “script murder store.”
“You’ve got to be kidding…”
Colin also remembered something at this point; it seemed that the owner of the script murder store hadn’t been caught yet today…
The person had said they had urgent matters to attend to back home two days before the incident and ended up going who knows where.
Initially, it was assumed to be a coincidence, but now it appeared to be a deliberate escape…
“@Mister Kun, the recent batch of merchandise that absorbs psychic energy has run into issues; I was discovered and hurriedly fled, planning to hide out in Southeast Asia. But as soon as I arrived, I fell for it. They initially just wanted me to participate in scams, but because my blood happened to match someone’s, they now want to harvest my kidney, what should I do…”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 331 - 331 329 I Will Take Care of Your Wife Do Not
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 331: Chapter 329: I Will Take Care of Your Wife, Do Not Worry_1 Chapter 331: Chapter 329: I Will Take Care of Your Wife, Do Not Worry_1 This person, who asked to be called “Mister Weirdo,” didn’t have complete language skills, but the general meaning of what he said was pretty clear.
“So it really is a follow-up to today’s events…”
Colin wasn’t surprised, but what surprised him was… this was an anomaly!
He had been through a lot, encountered all kinds of things, right?
Anomalies fleeing because they’d been exposed weren’t common, but not inconceivable. However, he’d never encountered one that had fled into a bandit’s den and was about to be chopped in half…
“Are all the people in this group really anomalies?”
Colin suddenly felt doubtful, it seemed a bit unreal.
And at this point, after hearing his description, others uniformly responded: no rescue possible, you can wait to restart after death.
“But I have a pretty good physique, and I have a wife, if I die, what will she do…” Mister Weirdo was getting anxious, his language skills going haywire, clearly not willing to give up just yet.
The other members of the group offered little comfort, typing things like “Thy wife, I shall care for, fret not,” “Give up this body and start over,” and “Try harder on your own,” indicating their helplessness to intervene.
The few who wanted to help, after seeing his description, were not willing to take the risk.
“Now is a time of trouble, the pressure from the officials is too intense, they’re telling us not to act rashly…” They also had their reasons.
…
“Tsk, still worried about his wife? Interesting. But these kinsmen seem pretty cold-blooded. Maybe it’s because their race has means of rebirth, so they’re not afraid?”
After thinking for a moment, Colin took the initiative to ask for his location: “Give me the exact path you’ve taken, I’ll see if I can find a way to help you, create a chance for you to escape…”
The company’s mission had said, if possible, they could try to make contact with them.
Colin also felt the need to truly understand what was going on with these guys.
“Okay, okay, @Mr. Digital, I will message you privately…”
Mister Weirdo, seeing someone willing to save him, was immediately overjoyed.
Before long, Colin received the complete action path from him. After encountering problems in the role-play group, he hastily fled, first taking a plane to the border, then leaving by bus through a local fixer.
Everything had gone smoothly until he realized the bus was headed to Bei Mian, not Bangkok.
“These humans really have no respect for rules!”
Mister Weirdo complained to Colin. If he hadn’t hidden a few mobile phones in his belly, he wouldn’t have been able to send any messages this time.
“That’s really unlucky…”
Colin hadn’t expected such a strange turn of events.
“‘Mr. Digital,’ you must save me. In at most a week or two, they’re going to… There’s r coming, I can’t tell you anymore.” Mister Weirdo was in such a hurry that he made several typing errors.
“Okay, okay, don’t worry…”
Colin sent a message back, but got no response.
However, just at that moment, another person sent him a message, “Mister Kun.”
“While I know your intentions are good, be cautious. Recently, for some reason, the pressure from the officials is great. ‘Mr. C’ has ordered that even in death, we must not reveal our identities or use those powers…”
The increased pressure from the officials must have something to do with the “world barriers” being under attack, right? But who is Mr. C? He seems to have a lot of influence in this race… Colin was curious, but still replied:
“Okay, don’t worry, I have my ways.”He ended the conversation and put down his phone.
Colin looked thoughtful, and after a few seconds, couldn’t help but remark, “The diversity of the human species has become richer,” before calling Qin Chuan, planning to have them handle the matter.
In his current position, he didn’t need to personally undertake such tasks.
At the moment, Qin Chuan was puzzled, yet did not delay. Even late at night, he dutifully submitted the issue to his superiors.
By the next day, Xia Liufang and Hu Zheng were the ones running around instead of Qin Chuan.
“They move fast…”
Colin muttered, knowing roughly that this guy had headed out early in the morning with a few officials, taking a plane to their destination.
In the following days, besides clearing various tasks, there were no other incidents.
The only issue was on Qin Chuan’s side—they had thought it would be a quick job to find the person, but unexpectedly, Mister Weirdo had been tied up and put on a plane to South America the same night he finished talking to Colin…
Having no other choice, Qin Chuan led his team to follow suite.
Besides that, no other incidents occurred…
Colin enjoyed the rare quiet moment.
Not until after December 15th did he return to Base No. 5.
This time, the security along the way was much more relaxed towards him.
After walking a distance, Colin encountered Fate Propeller, Xu Duojin, an Eighth Level employee under Old Master Wu who looked middle-aged, but was actually only in his thirties.
Knowing Colin’s straightforward nature, Xu Duojin did not beat around the bush, instead saying simply and directly: “Everything is prepared. They are all locked up in a large containment chamber; we’re just waiting for you.”
“Alright.”
Colin nodded, then followed Xu Duojin to the large containment chamber he spoke of.
Fifty white containers of varying sizes were imprisoned there—these were anomalies the officials had selected as not overly dangerous, but with complex mechanisms, very troublesome and hard to destroy.
‘It seems the officials are still wary of the company, not daring to trade those of the highest threat level right away.’
Colin’s gaze swept over a few of them, most of which he did not consider to be very threatening, and he had heard that the officials contained some horrors that were “not to be heard, spoken of, or looked upon.”
But those were not on the current trade list.
Without giving it much thought, Colin pulled back his mind and turned to Xu Duojin:
“Now, have everyone withdraw, I’ll be fine on my own here.”
“And those… special items, if they go out of control, they might act immediately…”
Xu Duojin glanced at a special containment unit sealed with transparent glass. Inside was a constantly changing painting with someone sitting in front of it—
This object required constant supervision; otherwise, within a minute, creatures resembling, but not, dogs, would crawl out of it…
Moreover, people had to be switched out every hour on the hour; any longer, and the person would disappear.
Apart from that, there were many other items that required constant suppression…
“No problem.”
As he spoke, Colin flicked a glass bottle from his right hand and, before it landed, raised his right hand to his side, flicking his thumb across his middle finger.
With a “pop,” a burst of flames erupted from the bottle.
A fiery ball akin to a Little Sun rose in the hall.
The intense heat radiated across the large containment chamber, striking all anomalous entities…
“With me here, they won’t dare lose control today.”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 332 - 332 330 The Bunny Logistics Troop on the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 332: Chapter 330: The “Bunny” Logistics Troop on the Train._1 Chapter 332: Chapter 330: The “Bunny” Logistics Troop on the Train._1 A fireball several meters in diameter hovered in midair, radiating a glow that was not scorching to those around it.
But under the radiance of this warmth-inducing light, the originally “noisy” large containment room fell silent, and all signs of anomalies retracted like frightened ostriches…
Colin stood beneath the enormous fireball, as trickles of flame fell from above, clinging to his body, making him resemble a divine being.
‘The grease from that hand, even if diluted tenfold for use with oil, is still very effective…’
Colin looked up at the flames, thinking that if it had been before, maintaining a fireball with a diameter of five meters would be like an ordinary person carrying a weight of several kilograms—not too strenuous, but definitely not too relaxed either…
But with a little added ingredient, controlling such flames almost felt like no pressure at all.
And with this addition, his effective control range over the flames had climbed another large step.
Behind him, Xu Duojin and several senior guards stationed at Base No. 5 watched this scene unfold, inevitably feeling astonished.
Even though the containment subjects present were not of a high level, they were also not to be considered low.
Unexpectedly, merely by releasing his special abilities, he was able to suppress them all…
