If it were them, they might have a chance to resolve the situation, but not to suppress it.
However, for some reason, Xu Duojin and the others showed no intention of leaving…
Colin turned to look at them and at this moment, a senior guard from Base No. 5 who was following Xu Duojin stepped forward:
“Mr. Colin, may we have one person stay behind?”
According to the rules, such a situation must be supervised, to prevent Colin from going mad and triggering some other accident.
Although he personally felt the likelihood was not high, a rule was a rule.
Colin didn’t speak immediately, but opened his task to check; it said to work alone as much as possible, but the request was not mandatory.
After pondering for a moment, Colin said, “That’s fine, but if anything unexpected arises, I’m not responsible.”
“No problem…” the senior guard agreed immediately.
“Chang Wei, you stay here. The rest of us will leave now, so as not to disturb Mr. Colin.”
Xu Duojin waved his hand and spoke before the others behind him could, “One person staying is enough, if there are any further issues, I’ll take responsibility.”
These cooperations were essentially negotiated by Old Master Wu; compared to others, he had to care more.
Soon after, with Xu Duojin’s directive, everyone on site exited orderly.
Then, seeing that the situation was suitable, Colin scanned the surroundings and stomped on the ground. Subsequently, a ring of flame spread out from beneath his feet, like ripples in water, quickly expanding in a short time.
“Don’t use any special abilities, and it won’t harm you,”
Colin reminded the person beside him.
Afterward, under the watchful eye of the senior guard, the entire large containment room was completely enveloped by flames.
In that instant, a feeling of isolation from the rest of the world emerged.
To his surprise, although the flames were unmistakably fire, they defied all logic by not causing any harm to ordinary objects, the first time he had seen such “tame” anomalies…
But wasn’t there supposed to be a trade? What was the purpose of sealing this place?
While he pondered this, Colin suddenly sensed something and spoke out, “It seems to be coming.”
The key to this trade was to create an enclosed spatial anomaly, which would fulfill one of the conditions for the “Infinite Train” to arrive.
As for the rest, it was up to the company’s people to operate.
Soon after his words had faded, a monotonous and hollow flute sound abruptly arose.
In the scene, a faint layer of grey mist began to emerge; at the end of the mist, a hint of tungsten filament light shone through…
At the same time, time itself became vaguely disjointed.
It was when they saw that light that both Colin and the senior guard Chang Wei simultaneously “spaced out” for a moment.
Then, as if time had been cut short, when they came to their senses, a series of ancient trains marred with various scars slowly came to a halt.
As the train stopped, Colin noticed behind the flickering dim windows sat figures, tall and still, with long ears…
“Seems familiar… could it be the Corps?”
With some sort of barrier present, Colin couldn’t make out the details, but the indescribable pressure he felt almost confirmed it.
It was at this moment that the train finally stopped with a “click” sound.
The carriage door in front of Colin opened.
Accompanied by heavy footsteps, many people wearing full-cover exoskeleton armor jumped down from the carriage.
The person in the lead glanced at Colin, nodded to acknowledge him, then stretched out his hand, pointing towards the various containment units.
More than a dozen similarly equipped people immediately sprung into action behind him.
Colin’s gaze swept over these individuals; compared to the armor from the incident he encountered, these armors appeared significantly lighter and more flexible.
“Might they be from some kind of logistics team? But, how are they going to transport everything here? The train doesn’t seem big enough to fit it all, does it?”
As Colin wondered how they intended to move all these big and small objects,
he suddenly saw that this group wasn’t moving the containment units at all. Instead, they took out a kind of metal sphere and threw it at the restrained anomalies. Immediately after, the spheres opened up, chains shot out, ensnaring the targets, and pulled them into the spheres…
Colin’s eyelids twitched, and he couldn’t help clicking his tongue, “I almost forgot the company had these ‘Elf Balls’.”
He had used these things once during his F Level promotion mission and hadn’t really been in touch with them since.
To his surprise, the company had brought them out again…
In less than ten minutes, all fifty containment subjects were packed into the spheres, and the transaction was essentially complete.
The man who seemed like the logistics team leader approached Colin, handed him a yellowed piece of paper, and also passed over a pen.
Colin took it and saw that it was essentially the final confirmation of a trade list.
There was a place for a signature at the bottom…
“Party A: ‘First Corps ‘Bunny’ Logistics Seventh Squadron Thirty-first Team Second Group’…”
Colin silently read the information, glanced at a “Bunny” stamp, confirmed there was nothing wrong with the paper, and then signed his own name before handing it back.
With that, the transaction ended.
All the logistics teams returned to the carriage silently and swiftly.
However, just when Colin thought everything was about to wrap up, he suddenly noticed that one of the formerly silent logistics team members looked back at him while boarding the train.
Then, as he turned away and continued boarding, his body shuddered as if he suddenly realized something and sharply turned his head, staring straight at Colin.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 333 - 333 331 Transaction Successful_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 333: Chapter 331 Transaction Successful_1 Chapter 333: Chapter 331 Transaction Successful_1 “What’s wrong?” Colin was a bit puzzled.
As he spoke, a member of the logistics team, with a flashing red light under his helmet, trembled as he stretched out his hand, pointing at him with a quivering finger as if he wanted to say something, but no sound came out.
It was clear that his emotions were very agitated at the moment.
However, Colin wasn’t sure if it was just an illusion, but he faintly felt that these emotions were complex, including a sense of grievance, anger, and sorrow.
“Speak up. Is there a problem?”
Colin didn’t understand the reason for the other’s resentment.
But at that moment, a fist stretched out from the train and heavily struck the back of the head of the logistics member.
With a “bang.”
The logistics team leader dragged him back into the train and then, towards Colin, gestured with his hands as if to apologize.
“Click.”
The train doors closed, and amidst a chiming bell, it slowly moved away into the distance.
The surrounding mist gradually dissipated…
Colin also extinguished the flame.
But he was still puzzled about the distressed emotions of that member.
He couldn’t understand how someone could harbor such resentment towards him, especially since he always acted kindly and didn’t make enemies with anyone.
Especially someone from the Corps…
As he pondered, he suddenly realized something, and turned to look at the high-ranking guard named Chang Wei, “Did you offend someone from a company?”
After speaking, Colin frowned as he saw the guy behind him stare blankly ahead, clenched his lips tightly, as if enduring something…
It wasn’t until Colin turned around that he remembered what had just been said, but before he could speak…
“Vomiting”…
He suddenly bent over and vomited a “rainbow,” the sour smell of viscous stomach acid mixed with fermented food wafting through the air.
Colin stepped back unchanged, letting the flame cloak his body to avoid getting splattered by the vomit.
“Was this due to a direct gaze at the train or something that caused the status to become chaotic?”
With a quick glance, Colin could guess the reason, and he estimated that the other party had been enduring it during the business transaction, which is why there had been no movement until now.
And now, as he had lifted the containment of flame, people outside seemed to have sensed something and reopened the door…
As soon as they came in, Xu Duojin and others saw Chang Wei lying on the ground vomiting incessantly, as if trying to bring up last year’s New Year’s Eve dinner.
However, everyone present could determine that his problem wasn’t serious.
Xu Duojin looked around and noticed that the various containment units hadn’t disappeared, but everything inside them was gone…
“Mr. Colin, regarding the transaction…”
“The transaction went smoothly,” Colin waved his hand. “As for when the items produced will be returned, I’m not sure. If it’s fast, maybe one or two weeks, if it’s slow, it might take over a month.”
The “Humility Knight” legacy had taken about half a month to arrive previously.
Upon hearing this, Xu Duojin’s face showed a hint of a smile, “That’s fine, that’s fine… As for the items, there’s no rush.”
To them, the “items” were nice to have, but it was no big deal if they didn’t have them…
Leveraging the company to deal with problems that were difficult to resolve was the real core of their business deal.
‘How come it feels like they’re slacking off? With this attitude, how can I urge the company to speed up production…’ Colin pondered, pursing his lips; he was eager to get a hold of some good deals and profits.
After thinking it over, he reminded them, “You all can start preparing the equipment list for the next phase of the transaction. If there’s nothing else, I should be going. Also, if you aren’t satisfied with the progress of the item crafting, you can give me feedback.”
He slightly slowed down his speech for the last part.
“Okay, okay…” Xu Duojin nodded his head and said no more.
‘Why do I feel uneasy about this?’
Shaking his head, Colin didn’t continue to remind him and, accompanied by a staff member, he turned and left the place.
Outside, Hu Zheng and the others had been waiting for a long time.
Previously, the transactions made inside were all at least of the Sixth Level, so they didn’t have the credentials to enter and could only wait outside.
Colin didn’t say much and led them towards the exit, but halfway through, he suddenly paused, sniffed the air, and frowned.
“What’s wrong?” Hu Zheng asked from one side.
“I thought I smelled something, but I must be overthinking it.”
Colin pondered the moment prior, feeling like he had detected a scent but then again it seemed like nothing.
After thinking it over, he asked Hu Zheng to remind Xu Duojin and the others to check inside later on, and then without further delay, he turned and continued to leave…
This time, after leaving the trade site, Colin didn’t choose to go directly home, but instead went to the New Blue Sky Welfare Institute, a place he hadn’t visited in a long time.
Two hours later, a helicopter gently landed on the helipad atop a large building.
Colin walked down from it and then left the building, casually purchasing some gifts before taking a car for another fifteen minutes and arriving at the newly renovated New Blue Sky Welfare Institute.
“It’s been a while since I’ve been back…”
Even with all his experiences, Colin couldn’t help but feel a surge of nervous emotions as he stood at the entrance.
Taking a deep breath, he walked in.
Perhaps it was the timing, but the children were in classes inside the institute, so he didn’t see anyone.
However, after walking a bit further, Colin saw a familiar old man, looking robust but, in reality, in his eighties and nearing ninety—an authentically old man, unlike the cases of “Old Master Wu.”
At that moment, the old man sat in a grandmaster’s chair, engrossed in something on his phone.
A nameless emotion welled up inside him…
“Grandpa Chen.”
Colin called out, but the old man did not respond.
After a moment of silence, he didn’t continue speaking and instead walked up to the old man to find him watching a piano tutorial video, absorbed in learning…
The piano teacher’s instrument was grand and white, captivating the old man completely.
After quite a while, the video finally ended, and the old man smacked his lips as if wanting to savor the experience. However, he abruptly noticed someone by his side and was so startled that he sat up straight in his grandmaster’s chair.
“Holy moly, who’s that? You gave me a start… Wait, Colin? Little Colin?”
The old man held his phone, squinting and looking uncertain.
“Yes, it’s me.” Colin smiled and nodded, setting down the milk and other items he had bought.
“Tsk tsk, a rare visitor indeed. It’s been so long, I thought you’d only come back after I’d died,” the old man said in jest, unceremoniously accepting the gifts.
Speaking of which, who would pass first was really uncertain… Colin didn’t explain his condition of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, and simply smiled as he said:
“I just happened to have some free time, so I thought I’d come back and have a look.”
“All right, all right. First, go and visit your parents at the cemetery in the back hill. There’s beer in the fridge; bring one with you.”
“Okay.”
Colin nodded, took a bottle of beer, and after passing through the institute, he went out the back door into the hills. After a while, he arrived at a very well-maintained graveyard.
Walking a few steps among the graves, he then found his parents’ tombstones.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 334 - 334 332 Whimsical Goodbye_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 334: Chapter 332 Whimsical Goodbye_1 Chapter 334: Chapter 332 Whimsical Goodbye_1 “Martyr…”
Colin stood before the black marble tombstone, his eyes squinted slightly, his mind filled with an indescribable emptiness.
His impressions of his father weren’t deep. No, it would be more accurate to say, besides a few photos, he had almost no memory of him, and even memories of his mother had become very vague.
Sometimes, even when he tried to remember, he couldn’t quite recall their faces.
After quietly observing for a while, Colin flicked his thumb, prying off the beer cap with his fingernail, and poured it in front of the grave.
At this moment, just like the times he had come before to sweep the tomb, he didn’t know what to say.
Every time he came here, he would just stand for a moment and pour out a bottle of beer before leaving straight away.
However, this time, after he had poured out the beer from the large green bottle,
Colin slowly crouched down, sitting cross-legged in front of the grave, suddenly feeling a desire to say something.
“By normal reckoning, I should be busy sending out resumes everywhere, about to graduate and ready to enter the workforce. However, because of ‘Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis,’ my fate took an unexpected turn.”
“When I was first chosen by the Bonfire Company, I wondered if I had some special identity, like maybe you were also an employee of the company or something…”
“But later experiences and understanding made it clear that our family really has been law-abiding citizens for generations, nothing special…”
“You aren’t special, I’m not special either…”
“And, inside the Bonfire Company, it doesn’t seem like there’s any tradition of following in one’s father’s footsteps.”
“So I really just got lucky, was chosen, successfully rolled the dice, and, fortunately, completed that task.”
“Though now, you put out fires, and I set them… I don’t know what you’ll do if you ever find out about this, whether you’ll give me a good beating or not.”
Colin couldn’t help but laugh softly, then he composed himself and sat quietly for a while.
In this “conversation,” he simply recounted his own experiences and didn’t mention the fire incident from back then.
At this point, he also had no thoughts of revenge, because he had long heard that the man who escaped the fire, due to nearly thirty percent severe burns, had lived a life so painful that he wished for death.
That person had kicked the bucket back when Colin was still in elementary school…
As for whether that man had any descendants or anything, Colin didn’t really care, nor did he have any thoughts of revenge.
After speaking, he suddenly felt much more relaxed.
Perhaps because he felt so light physically and mentally, it even seemed that his understanding of the bonfire had deepened considerably…
Colin raised his hand, and a flame flickered and danced between his fingers.
“Without using ‘Revolver Contrarian,’ the flames I can control seem to have grown stronger, about the same range as when I first had the ‘Ring of Flame Dominance.’
Having a chat can actually have this effect?
Colin pursed his lips, unsure of what to say. His return this time had indeed been just a simple visit.
Just like those people striving in big cities, who also sometimes think of home.
Worried that he might suddenly kick the bucket without having another chance to come back.
He took a deep breath, slowly exhaled, and after fulfilling his wish to “visit home before a sudden death,” Colin didn’t dwell too much on these matters and didn’t stay much longer in this cemetery adjacent to the orphanage.
“Goodbye, your son is off to save the world again.”
After leaving those words, Colin retraced his steps and climbed over the wall to depart from this place.
Before long, he was back at the familiar orphanage.
“Huh, one hour, forty-six minutes, fourteen seconds, this time you stayed longer than all the times when you were a kid put together, what made you suddenly wise up?” Old Man Chen teased, as soon as he saw Colin’s figure reappear.
Colin waved his hand dismissively: “I was just ignorant before.”
After a pause, he looked up at the ceiling, listening to the sound of teaching coming from the third floor: “Are they still in class?”
“Yeah, want me to call them down? There are a few kids who really miss you.”
“Never mind,” Colin shook his head, feeling that with all the mess he was currently in, it wasn’t too appropriate to have too much contact with the kids.
“Okay, by the way, you’re not getting any younger. When are you going to bring a girlfriend back to visit?”
‘A girlfriend? A girlfriend would only get in the way of my missions, not even dogs would bother.’
Colin grumbled in his heart and was about to speak when he saw a man with a slicked-back hairstyle, dressed in a suit, carrying a briefcase under his arm, walking out.
At that moment, upon seeing Colin, the man was startled, then immediately smiled, “When did you come back? Why didn’t you say anything?”
“Brother Chuan? Doing pretty well, aren’t you…”
Colin sized up Chen Chuan, who looked like a successful person.
If he remembered correctly, last time Old Man Chen mentioned that Brother Chuan suddenly received a surprising investment and their factory’s sales skyrocketed.
Colin guessed that it was probably overtures from some official, so he didn’t take much notice.
“Just so-so…”
Chen Chuan smiled, flicking his right hand and inconspicuously showing off a very expensive-looking green watch.
“Tsk… impressive, impressive, now you’re sporting such an expensive watch,” Colin remarked after seeing it, offering a timely joke.
Brother Chuan immediately beamed at the comment, but then, he seemed to remember something:
“Right, you lad have a driver’s license, but you don’t have a car yet, do you?
“Come, take this one to drive for now. We’ll transfer it to your name later.”
As he spoke, he handed over an Accord car key.
Colin was familiar with that car, knowing it was Brother Chuan’s ride from five years ago, but he didn’t expect Brother Chuan to be so generous. He hastily waved his hands:
“No need, no need.”
“How can that be? How can a man get a girlfriend without a car? You don’t want my dad to pass away without seeing a daughter-in-law, do you? Don’t worry, I’ll subsidize the gas money.”
‘Brother Chuan is still as filially dutiful as ever…’ Colin mumbled to himself.
What’s more speechless is that Old Man Chen gave his own son a stern look, and then turned to Colin, “Alright, just take it. This guy has made it now; I’ll have him buy you a house later too.”
“No problem, if the daughter-in-law comes, then I’ll cover that room,” Brother Chuan said magnanimously, waiving his hand and taking that responsibility too.
Clearly, he hadn’t earned a small fortune during this time…
Seeing the two’s demeanor, Colin was somewhat torn between laughter and tears, just about to say something.
But right at this moment, a figure suddenly entered, and upon seeing this person, Brother Chuan’s eyes widened, and his breathing seemed to come to a halt.
Colin turned his head to look at the newcomer, “Xia Liufang?”
“Yeah.”
Dressed in a simple and elegant floral sundress, with a bright and delicate appearance, Xia Liufang nodded.
“Ah, sorry, I have something and probably…”
Colin nodded at them and then quickly stepped forward, heading out, following Xia Liufang to a sedan parked outside.
Behind him, Brother Chuan took in the scene and couldn’t help but gasp,
“Damn, that car is luxurious. Has Colin been taken under the wing of a wealthy woman or something? No wonder he looked down on my old Accord.”
“A wealthy woman taking care of him?” Old Man Chen frowned, “It better not be that what… ‘Wealthy Woman’s Delight Whip’, ‘Wealthy Woman’s Joy Balls’ or something, right? That won’t do! How can he get involved in such things?!”
“Shh, Dad, keep your voice down, they haven’t gone far yet. And where did you get the idea to look at those strange things? I never should’ve let you use the internet…”
Brother Chuan was filled with regret, but still comforted him, “Don’t worry, it doesn’t look like it…”
Having said that, recalling the look of that woman, he couldn’t resist muttering to himself, if it were such a beautiful woman, even a steel wool might be acceptable…
Seeing the other party’s attitude, little Colin must be onto some good fortune.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 335 - 335 333 Apologize or Die. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 335: Chapter 333: Apologize or Die. _1 Chapter 335: Chapter 333: Apologize or Die. _1 “Didn’t you have something going on at home? Why did you come over again?”
After getting into the car, Colin curiously asked a question.
Previously, before the trade between the two parties took place, Xia Liufang seemed to have something to attend to at home. He had thought she might need to take a few days off, but unexpectedly, there she was again in the afternoon.
Moreover, it seemed like she had come over deliberately…
At the moment, having heard Colin’s words, Xia Liufang, who was sitting in the driver’s seat, hesitated before saying, “It’s like this, a relative came through our family, and they wanted to get in touch with you through me…”
“Get in touch with me?”
Colin was taken aback for a moment, then quickly remembered that Old Master Wu had mentioned that someone would be looking for him.
He hadn’t expected them to come so quickly.
However, he had thought it would be under the guise of a mission exchange, as Old Master Wu had mentioned, not a private discussion…
Seeing that Colin didn’t say anything, Xia Liufang carefully added, “If you don’t want to go, you don’t have to pay any attention to it…”
“It’s fine, I’ve settled most things recently anyway, so taking a look shouldn’t be a big issue.”
Colin said, “I’m also curious what these people want from me.”
Old Master Wu only told him that these people were here to talk business and might even look for trouble, but he did not elaborate on the specifics.
“Okay, shall we head there now?”
Seeing that Colin didn’t seem too concerned about the matter, Xia Liufang let out a small sigh of relief.
“Go there? Let them come over themselves.”
Colin gestured with his hand and directed Xia Liufang to drive to the hotel where he had just alighted from the helicopter, then found the best room and began waiting for visitors to arrive.
“Boss Colin, the people coming to visit this time are probably these…”
In the room, Hu Zheng brought over a file with a list of names for the upcoming visitors.
“‘Ghost-faced’ Tang Qinghu, Eighth Level, tsk, seems like we have some high-caliber visitors this time…”
Colin briefly checked and felt that the matter they were going to discuss was not ordinary.
Otherwise, they wouldn’t have sent someone of that level personally, and there was a name “Hu Xiaoyuan” on the list that caught his attention, which made Colin think of some embarrassing past events.
It was about an hour later…
The squad led by the “Divine Strike” Eighth Level arrived, and from afar, Colin could sense a faint oppressive aura spreading from outside the room.
Soon after, as the door opened, a man who was both fat and robust walked in.
His face bore the stiffness characteristic of the Extraordinary Ones, and at the moment, he seemed to be in a bad mood, emitting a somber aura that normal people couldn’t sense.
‘This must be that Tang Qinghu…’
Colin nodded in acknowledgment, then shifted his gaze to the person following behind him.
It was a woman who stood close to one meter ninety, well-proportioned but imposing in appearance—Hu Xiaoyuan.
For this particularly tall woman, Colin had a rather vivid memory…
Besides her, there was another person with a familiar scent but an unfamiliar face.
‘Fifth Level Personnel, probably also involved in the incident at the time, but it seems we didn’t directly interact? Still, it looks like those from the first promotion mission have come looking for me…’
Colin pursed his lips, having seen Hu Xiaoyuan’s name on the list and suspected it, now it was confirmed.
Yet, compared to him, Hu Xiaoyuan did not seem particularly certain when she saw Colin.
Because her memories related to him had become very, very vague.
‘Thank goodness, it looks like she doesn’t recognize me for sure, otherwise if she remembered all those weird things I said back then, I’d really have to endure social death…’
As the thought flashed through his mind, Colin gestured toward the sofa, indicating they should sit.
However, the corpulent Tang Qinghu did not take a seat and instead looked down at Colin sitting on the sofa: “Heh, meeting you is not an easy task…”
While speaking, Colin felt an indistinct and invisible mental force approaching.
This psychic power wasn’t lethal, but being enveloped by it certainly felt like being stripped naked.
‘So he really did come here to pick a fight?’
Colin’s brow furrowed, and without almost any hesitation, a burst of flames erupted from his body, like a mountain river’s torrential flood, vehemently crashing against that wave of psychic energy…
“Hiss, ah!”
A sudden sensation of being burned spread through, and Tang Qinghu couldn’t help but cry out in pain.
After that, he couldn’t help but feel a surge of anger within him. He had only meant to test the waters, yet the other party had responded so ruthlessly!
Veins popped on his face, twisting like earthworms, as if another fierce and strange face was about to emerge from beneath his own…
Before Tang Qinghu could further explode into anger, however, the Colin in front of him suddenly vanished.
Immediately after, something sharp and piercing pressed against his back, and a terrifying sense of fatality flowed through the sharp object and into his body.
All over his body, an inexplicable sense of swelling and discomfort arose…
Simultaneously, Colin’s cold voice suddenly rang out from behind him:
“I’m now giving you two choices.
“First, apologize to me and then sit down, let’s talk properly.
“Second, die.”
Colin’s tone was calm and concise, with no discernible emotion.
However, it did make Tang Qinghu realize that if he really chose to continue the struggle, he could very well drop dead on the spot in an instant.
‘Damn it, how on earth did he manage to do that…’ Tang Qinghu was inwardly shocked. He didn’t even know when exactly Colin had made his move, nor how he had done it.
Everything seemed as though time had stopped!
After a stalemate lasting two or three seconds, feeling the other party’s growing impatience, he finally spoke:
“I apologize, Mr. Colin, I have offended you.”
Fighting to the death over such a matter with someone of equally formidable strength clearly wasn’t wise.
Meanwhile, Hu Xiaoyuan and her supervisor Luo Wenhao, who had come with him, were inwardly startled, having not expected Colin to make Tang Qinghu back down so quickly.
This man, in their circles, was a true hot-head, the kind who would rather die than lose face…
“Hmm.”
Colin withdrew the Bone Spur, stepped past him, and returned to his seat:
“So, what exactly brings you here? Don’t tell me you’ve come all this way just to pick a fight.”
Upon hearing Colin’s somewhat sarcastic words, Tang Qinghu’s face twitched, but he took a deep breath and said:
“Have you heard of the ‘Spark’ project?”
“The Spark project? I’ve heard of it, what about it?”
Colin nodded, knowing that the official plan was, if exceptional events escalated to an unmanageable level, to transport humanity to several identified locations for escape as far as possible.
He wasn’t sure of the specifics, but rather than that, Colin was curious about what this project had to do with him?
“Yes, we’ve come for this project… More precisely, we’re here because of a special anomaly, hoping to inquire for information about it.”
As Tang Qinghu spoke, he took out a document and placed it on the table.
From it, Colin saw a familiar codename—
“The Infinite Train”.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 336 - 336 334 Boat Tickets at the End of the World
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 336: Chapter 334: “Boat Tickets” at the End of the World. _1 Chapter 336: Chapter 334: “Boat Tickets” at the End of the World. _1 “Infinite Train?”
Colin’s expression was odd, and for a moment, he wasn’t sure what to make of it. After all, there were quite a few anomalies related to trains.
He picked up a document from the table and looked it over.
“Also known as ‘Death Herald Train,’ ‘Mist Train,’ ‘Strange Train,’ its characteristics are that it is currently observed only in areas where anomalies have manifested…”
“When it appears, grey fog will materialize around it, followed by an abnormal ‘fast-forward’ in time. Moreover, some researchers believe it is not a speeding up of time but rather a reduction of ‘processes.'”
“To this day, no one of any power has ever seen its locomotive or its caboose. People will hear a whistle sound typical of last-century trains, followed by the observation of a yellow light, and then the train gradually coming to a stop…”
“In an accidental experiment, a member who entered tried to find the locomotive, but after walking through over a hundred carriages, they finally gave up. At present, it is believed that the number of carriages of this train could be infinite…”
“So far, no means have succeeded in reaching the locomotive…”
…
“So it really is an ‘Infinite Train’…”
Colin, who had read halfway, was sure it was the one he was familiar with, and he realized that the official understanding of this train seemed rather extensive.
Unfortunately, it was all rather superficial research.
They knew some taboos, but not why they were taboos.
On the whole, it seemed to be a bit more than he knew, but not by much.
After quickly finishing the briefing on the “Infinite Train,” Colin casually placed it on the desk.
“I do have some understanding of this anomaly, so, what exactly do you want to know?” he asked, crossing his right leg over his left and tipping his toes up, leaning back in his chair.
Upon hearing this, Tang Qinghu hardly hesitated before asking directly:
“I heard that you seem to have a way to control the train’s arrival and then use it to go wherever you want?”
In the information they had obtained, Qin Chuan and Colin had ultimately escaped using the train in the last incident…
And from the current intelligence, it seemed that members of the Bonfire Company had, more or less, all come into contact with that Strange Train.
This was enough to indicate that the Bonfire Company had the capability to use that train.
‘Control the train’s coming? Are you perhaps overestimating me…’ Colin pursed his lips. He did know that “Lady Bunny” probably had a certain authority to mobilize that train, but he had never heard of a regular employee having this ability.
Everyone got on the train as part of a mission and then disembarked as required by the mission.
Beyond that, he hadn’t heard of any employee who could actively adjust their landing spot…
After some thought, Colin spoke up, “If you think I can control the train, you’re probably going to be disappointed. I’m like the other employees; I can only use the train passively as dictated by missions.”
Hearing this, Tang Qinghu and the others frowned. Clearly, this was not the answer they had been hoping for.
At that moment, they heard Colin continue to ask:
“I may not have the means to control the train, but I am curious, where do you want to go through it?”
If you don’t have it, then why bother asking… Tang Qinghu couldn’t help but complain internally. He felt that Colin did have a way but was too selfish and self-centered, lacking the spirit of sacrifice to share the information.
That’s also why he had tried to use some minor tactics before, so as to lead the conversation into his own rhythm…
Of course, this was also his usual style of conversation—first intimidate, then soften the tone a bit during the dialogue, before “delegating a major task,” often yielding good results.
Unfortunately, Colin’s methods were far more mysterious than the intelligence he had received…
Even now, Tang Qinghu couldn’t understand how he had been taken down in an instant by Colin.
Shaking his head to clear his thoughts, he continued:
“Through this train, we’ve discovered several unique extraterrestrial regions. If something were to happen, we might be able to carry out a mass evacuation.”
“No, given this train’s properties, if it could truly be used, it would certainly save countless lives.”
As he spoke, he looked towards Colin, and a sincere expression appeared on his face, lined with many horizontal folds: “If you can do it, you will surely be granted…”
“Stop, stop, stop, don’t start with that.”
Colin raised his hand to interrupt the other person, “I can’t do what you’re asking, but if I get a chance, I’ll look into it.”
“Of course, of course, I believe that with your character, you would certainly do so…”
Tang Qinghu’s rigid face cracked into a smile, then as if he remembered something, he said, “Of course, apart from this way, we have some other preparations. Rest assured, whether things succeed or not, you and a portion of the people you choose will be able to board it.”
While speaking, he handed over a black and gold card.
“What’s this?”
Colin’s gaze fell, and he didn’t take it.
“This is a highest-level ‘ship ticket.’ As long as you enter your or your friend’s information, in the event of an emergency, their safety and evacuation will be assured in no time, with someone specially assigned to escort them…”
“It’s also simple to use. You can start entering information on any smartphone with NFC capability…”
“Heh, we are currently recording the first batch of staff. Only after us will it be others’ turn. Just one of these spots is sought after to no end outside, but this card allows for many more registrations!”
Tang Qinghu briefly introduced the card’s function with a smile in his eyes.
“Ship ticket”…
Colin still didn’t take it, but the thought led him to consider more, suspecting that the situation inside might not be as calm as he thought.
“To be honest, rather than calling it the ‘Spark’ plan, I prefer the ‘Expedition’ plan. Like the explorers of the seas from centuries ago, we will venture into unknown territories that humanity has never reached before.”
“We will blaze new trails for humanity, reaching boundaries that our current civilization has not touched…”
“…”
Listening to Tang Qinghu’s words, Colin showed no reaction, while Hu Zheng and others beside him couldn’t help but curl their lips.
They had no objections to the “Spark” plan, but this level of self-aggrandizement and self-congratulation was a bit irksome.
However, seeing that Tang Qinghu seemed quite carried away by his own rhetoric, Colin didn’t hesitate to interrupt, “Okay, ‘Spark’ or ‘Expedition,’ it doesn’t particularly interest me right now…”
“If there’s nothing else besides this, then let’s end our discussion here.”
He had already visited several “Other Worlds,” and could only say that the world out there might not be as wonderful as the other party thought. Even if you went, if you were lucky, you might just barely survive.
“Alright then, sorry for the intrusion…”
A stiff smile appeared on Tang Qinghu’s face as he stood up, about to leave, but then he seemed to think of something and added:
“Oh, there’s one more thing. Our plan also needs more talent, and you, believe me, we are very sincere about recruiting someone like you. Perhaps when you want to know more, I could introduce you to Mr. Gao…”
Even though their current knowledge of Colin’s specific circumstances within the company was still unclear due to Old Master Wu’s interference.
They could clearly sense that this person seemed to have some other identity within the company, so if the opportunity arose, they would definitely want to try to recruit him.
Despite a small conflict between them earlier, that was not a major issue.
If they succeeded in recruiting him, that would be a great accomplishment!
But before Tang Qinghu could finish, Hu Zheng on the side suddenly coughed twice—
It’s one thing to talk about all those other matters, but openly poaching right in front of someone is a bit too much!
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 337 - 337 335 Complex and Chaotic Internal
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 337: Chapter 335 Complex and Chaotic Internal Struggle_1 Chapter 337: Chapter 335 Complex and Chaotic Internal Struggle_1 “Let’s not talk about introductions for now.”
Colin waved his hand dismissively as well, his mind cluttered with a slew of troubles. He had no interest in social niceties and even less in getting involved in the mess here.
As for Mr. Gao mentioned by the other party, Colin had never met him but had heard of him. He seemed to be another Ninth Level Personnel within the country.
A master of both the Divine Strike and Bonfire paths…
However, from bits and pieces of gossip, it appeared that his status wasn’t any good either.
Thoughts whirled in his head for a few seconds before Colin blinked, reeling his wandering mind back in.
Then, Tang Qinghu and the others didn’t continue the conversation and left.
No sooner had they left the building than a swirl of black mist surged around him, enveloping him and a few others, creating another “secret chamber.”
“Can you be certain? Is it the one you encountered before?” he asked in a low voice, turning to Hu Xiaoyuan and Luo Wenhao behind him.
Upon hearing this, the two exchanged glances and shook their heads simultaneously.
“It’s slightly similar, maybe it is, maybe it isn’t, but we can’t be sure…” said Hu Xiaoyuan.
“Forget it, this matter isn’t that important,” Tang Qinghu stated expressionlessly.
Afterward, they boarded an eight-seater van, getting ready to head to the airport…
Only, halfway there, Tang Qinghu, seated at the back, suddenly tensed up inside, then realized something. As he tried to rise from his seat, he saw a dump truck loaded with gravel barreling toward them from outside the window.
His pupils shrank, and as he tried to muster his powers, he found he had “stumbled” due to the urgency of the moment.
And in that brief window of time…
The out-of-control dump truck crashed fiercely into the rear of their vehicle.
Perhaps due to a quality issue, the van’s front end was fine, but the rear section, “conveniently” where Tang Qinghu was sitting, detached from the body and was sent flying away.
The immense force hit him right where he had gathered his strength, scattering the breath he had struggled to hold.
In the end, after a series of lightning-fast flips and sparks, he ended up in a construction site toilet filled with waste…
Ten seconds later, Tang Qinghu emerged from the public restroom, bedraggled and reeking, and looked expressionlessly toward a large tree not far away:
“Xu Duojin.”
After speaking, he turned and walked away without uttering another word.
He was well aware that the opponent, who was also Eighth Level, wouldn’t be able to prevent him from resisting the whole time.
So, not leaving now would only lead to more humiliation shortly…
This was, after all, not their turf.
…
Meanwhile, Colin was already on the helicopter headed back, and as the rotors spun, he thought back to the conversation they’d just had and couldn’t help but narrow his eyes slightly.
‘The situation inside seems not as calm as I thought.’
Colin generally knew about the various factions within, holding different philosophies, which could be roughly divided into two parts.
One was those planning to leave, the so-called “Spark,” “Expedition,” “Ark,” or whatever they were called. The names varied, but the meanings were similar.
The other was those who believed in humanity’s victory and chose to stay… some were referred to as the “Water Control” faction.
One side fleeing, the other staying, they seemed unconnected and capable of coexistence.
But in reality, whether they chose to leave or stay, they both needed resources, and currently, both sides were striving to secure as many resources as possible for the future.
“Looking at this, the ‘World Barrier’ might not have been affected as lightly as Old Master Wu mentioned, or rather, something else has happened that’s got these people acting up?”
Colin stroked his chin, making some rough guesses.
On the matter itself, he held no particular prejudice against those inclined to flee…
After all, external activities were indeed challenging, facing countless unknown threats, and carving out a haven from these threats was no easy task.
Besides, it wasn’t fair to generalize about those who chose to leave…
He seemed to have also heard about something referred to as “big run” and “little run” – the “big run” naturally involved taking as many people as possible to seek new paths, while the “little run” entailed a small group of elites taking a large amount of resources and leaving…
Or even more despicable, some, under the guise of the “big run,” gathered investment when in fact, they were planning a “little run”…
The situation in this regard was pretty complicated.
However, that didn’t mean those who chose to stay were any better or more committed.
That’s because when Colin read the Red Moon adherents’ profiles, he was shocked to find that a considerable portion of them could be classified within the faction opting to stay.
Of course, they were the most extreme of the lot.
“He believed that once humanity left Earth, they would cease to be human and that this place must be protected at all costs.”
“Yet, humans themselves lack the ability to guard this place and to survive the final day; they must rely on the help of the Outer Gods.”
“Besides that, there are some who believe that humanity is destined to triumph no matter what.”
“However…”
“Speaking of which, it feels like whether we run or stay, we can’t escape ‘2044’…”
Colin remembered that in other worlds, there was also news about this thing.
If simply running away would suffice, then there would be no need for the senior members of Bonfire Company, as well as those in the anomalous realms, to keep mentioning it.
Unfortunately, up to this point, Colin still hadn’t figured out what exactly would happen in 2044.
But he felt that whether it was the company or those truly great beings, many things seemed to revolve around this event.
“Forget it, maybe when I have high enough clearance, I’ll understand all this. As for now, it’s more pragmatic to think about the ‘Descent Project’ the day after tomorrow than these things.”
Colin took a deep breath, momentarily emptied his mind, and began to consider what to bring with him next time.
…
Meanwhile, thousands of miles away, Qin Chuan and his companions got off the plane at a small airport in South America and soon met with a few international colleagues stationed abroad.
Shortly thereafter, they appeared at a manor that claimed to sell fruit but in reality dealt in “flour.”
The master of the manor received them in the hall.
At that moment, Qin Chuan, looking at the weapons surrounding them, couldn’t help but feel a tingling on his scalp.
As an Extraordinary One who had just been promoted to level 3, such a scene was still quite shocking to him.
His promotion from level two to three had been through the backdoor help of Colin, from whom he had obtained further resources.
However, he wasn’t particularly scared since there were several bigwigs among those who came this time…
Colin’s orders were usually given high priority by the higher-ups.
After all…
It was all part of the plan.
Even though Qin Chuan didn’t know what the plan entailed.
“I wonder what brings you here?” asked the manor’s master in fluent English.
At his words, Qin Chuan felt someone nudge him, and then he took a step forward, pulling out a photo and handing it over, saying in the same foreign language:
“According to our investigation, this person was taken by you. We hope you can hand him over.”
The master of the manor glanced at the photo and then shook his head with a smile, “Sorry, I don’t know this person.”
To admit would be to concede to outright kidnapping; if the news spread, it would be a headache for him, and the real supplier would kill him to avoid scandal…
Hearing this, Qin Chuan frowned. They had come here with complete confidence.
But…
It was at this moment that an international colleague, wearing a cowboy hat, suddenly spoke:
“If you’re not willing to hand over the person, then come with me.”
“Sorry, you have no evidence, so according to the law, I don’t need to…”
The manor’s master was speaking when he suddenly saw the other person violently pull out a handgun from his waist and aim at him, causing him to lose focus for a moment.
Simultaneously, a rustling sound filled the air as his men immediately raised their guns and aimed at Qin Chuan’s group.
Just one command or a slight movement, and they would turn these few individuals into a hornet’s nest.
This gave the manor’s master an added sense of security.
However, just then, his eyes narrowed as he saw all his men deflate like punctured balloons, collapsing to the ground…
And on the floor, streams of fresh blood flowed toward the Asian man in the cowboy hat.
He reveled in the pleasure brought by this blood as he spoke,
“Sorry, when we act, we only need a name, not evidence.
“From now on, I give you ten seconds to agree.
“Otherwise, including you and your family, I will hunt down and kill every last one of them.
“Remember, your so-called backers mean nothing to us.”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 338 - 338 336
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 338: 336 Chapter 338: 336 ‘Fuck, are the people from the external operations department in this area always this ruthless?’
Qin Chuan couldn’t help but feel shocked by the scene before him.
Listeing to the words of the old brother beside him, he felt that his own side seemed more like a big owl, not the guy on the opposite side who was scared as if he had lost the ability to think.
At this moment, the owner of the manor saw the eerie scene around him and was startled. But at the same time, he recognized them from an inconspicuous sign on their bodies—
A group of people who possessed mysterious powers, truly lawless!
“Global Supernatural Alliance” agents!
Though in reality, there were a multitude of different forces within the alliance and it wasn’t a monolith, for those who had never entered this circle but had heard of their deeds from some sources, it was a terrifying behemoth!
If it was these people…
Indeed, even the guy he was helping couldn’t guarantee his safety!
In an instant, the manor owner made a decision after just two or three seconds, “I am willing to cooperate…”
However, facing his words, the man in the cowboy hat showed a snow-white grin as he laughingly said:
“Sorry, too late.”
As his words fell, several gunshots rang out, and the manor owner’s body was riddled with bullet holes.
“But you clearly said, ten seconds…” He widened his eyes, trying to speak, but blood gushed from his lungs due to the bullets, and all he could do was cough.
In the end, he fell down with eyes wide open, full of unwillingness.
“And to think you dare talk to me about the law, considering what you are,” the man in the cowboy hat said with disdain as he spat.
He had wanted to settle the score with these guys for some time, but unfortunately, there had been no good excuse.
But this time, with the opportunity at hand, he definitely wouldn’t go easy.
On the other side, Qin Chuan and the others couldn’t help but frown. He didn’t care about the life of this manor owner, but if this man was killed, then what about the mission he came for?
But before they could speak up, the man in the cowboy hat turned around, revealing a bright white-toothed smile and said cheerfully, “Don’t worry, don’t worry, the intelligence we needed to get won’t be missing at all.
“The person that high-ranking individual is looking for, we’ll definitely be able to find them.”
As he spoke, a palm-sized blob of viscous blood seeped out of his skin and shot toward the body on the ground with its eyes wide open at an incredibly fast speed.
Before long, the manor owner stood up once more, showing Qin Chuan and the others a set of snow-white teeth:
“Sorry, sorry, let me think, um, I have some good news and some bad news…
“The bad news is, one-half of that person’s kidney has been removed and is now implanted in a rich man’s illegitimate child.
“The good news is, since there were concerns about the surgery going wrong and damaging the kidney, that person is still alive, living with their remaining one.
“How’s that? What are we going to do next?”
Hearing the “manor owner’s” words, Qin Chuan thought for a moment and then made a call to Colin.
Soon after, the call connected, and there was a sound like “whoosh whoosh whoosh” from the other side, as if someone was in a helicopter.
He immediately reported the situation on the scene…
Hearing Qin Chuan’s words, Colin was somewhat amused yet exasperated, feeling that this “Pseudo-Human” was quite unlucky.
He had just become “human” not long ago, and already he had experienced a series of accidents.
He now has one less “kidney”…
Of course, such a situation is not fatal for them.
After lurking in the “Pseudo-Humans” group for so many days, Colin had more or less figured out that these guys seemed to specifically target those who had died due to various accidents for replacement.
For example, the original owner of this kidney-less fellow seemed to have driven drunk a few months ago, crashed through a guardrail on a mountain road, and tumbled down a steep slope of more than ten meters…
According to the investigation Colin had people conduct, the impacts inside the car made it clear that the person was definitely dead.
However, in reality, that person had miraculously survived and was eventually rescued.
Then they took the place of the original person, continuing to live in human society, from initially stiff expressions and inarticulate speech to now laughing with ease—so much so that the original’s wife and daughter hardly suspected anything, attributing it all to the shock from the car accident…
In the group, this individual was even considered a “top student” for quickly learning various human living details.
‘As it stands, the only unusual thing about these guys after they replace someone is that they find ways to provoke people’s emotions and then collect them, though the purpose of this collection remains unclear…’
‘However, I can’t shake the feeling that they seem to thoroughly enjoy human experiences, constantly sharing their own experiences with their peers and then looking for better opportunities…’
‘The latest development is that, after some of them got involved with online forums and the like, they plan to act crazy and play the fool to become internet celebrities, believing this will help them collect emotions more effectively…’
Thinking about his surveillance over the past few days, Colin couldn’t help feeling that they naturally carried a dichotomy of both indifference and jubilant optimism; indifferent and cold-blooded towards life, yet joyful and carefree about living…
Besides collecting emotions, they were also eager to experience all sorts of things in human society and even followed social rules more closely than the average human, making Colin feel like they were playing a kind of “human simulator.”
Overall, they didn’t seem very harmful.
Of course, this was just for the time being.
After all, those stupid robots in the company chat groups were virtually harmless until they blew their cover.
Until these guys reveal their ultimate intentions, many things truly remain uncertain.
To understand whether they posed a threat or not, it was necessary to find out where they came from, what the source was, and what they intended to do with the collected emotions before making a conclusion.
Then, Colin shook his head, reining in his thoughts, and had Qin Chuan create a vacancy to let that “Pseudo-Human” brother escape on his own, which would settle things.
If he deliberately captured him, it wouldn’t be so good…
These guys were still very careful in protecting certain sensitive information about themselves.
Therefore, he needed to save this guy, so he could help Colin better blend into the group afterwards.
After conveying his intentions, Colin shut his phone off without paying attention to the situation on the other end, and then let Hu Zheng and others deliver the materials he needed; he was preparing for the trip to “World Code-13” tomorrow.
…
After hanging up the phone, Qin Chuan closed his mobile, and explained the situation to the member of the overseas operations team.
“I think I understand, so, about that rich kid who had surgery and was reborn…” said the man in the cowboy hat.
Remembering Colin’s instructions, Qin Chuan said directly, “Don’t worry about him, just give me the opportunity to let him go, and remember, during this process, no extraordinary measures are to be shown!”
“No problem!” The man in the cowboy hat showed a sparkling white smile.
Once the final target was set, and with no one in the way the whole time, they quickly found the man who was locked up in a forest village not too far away…
It was then that the sound of heavy gunfire and even artillery broke out in this quaint little village.
..
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 339 - 339 337 Mr. Lin Ke Asks Me to Say Hello to
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 339: Chapter 337 Mr. Lin Ke Asks Me to Say Hello to You!_1 Chapter 339: Chapter 337 Mr. Lin Ke Asks Me to Say Hello to You!_1 “What’s the situation, a gang shootout?”
The brother whose kidney had been removed clutched the throbbing seam of his surgery on his back and took a deep breath. As he inhaled, he could smell the primitive scent of gunpowder in the air and felt the presence of something pure, a “nourishment,” drifting around.
Although the “spiritual nourishment” was tempting, now was an obvious chance to escape. It was a pity that a chain locked around his neck made it impossible for him to run away.
Before he could think further, a figure suddenly entered the room.
“Am I… in the end, going to die?”
The “pseudo-human” brother looked distressed. He’d finally gotten a good start, only for it to end like this.
However, just as he was bracing for death, he realized that the other person had shot his chains apart.
“You…” While he was surprised, the obviously Asian man said to him:
“Run straight to the right when you exit the door, and after a while, you’ll reach a small town.
“I am a mercenary who came specifically for this.”
Hearing this, the brother didn’t quite believe it and stood still, not moving.
After thinking it over, Qin Chuan spoke up:
“Mr. Lin Ke sends his regards.”
“Is it Mr. Lin Ke? He really saved me!” The brother was immediately moved to tears, touched that among his compatriots there was someone who kept their word and had mixed in so well!
Without any further hesitation, he clutched the cut on his back and bolted outside.
After he left, the battle here also suddenly picked up speed, and within less than ten minutes, everything was over.
Inhaling the mix of gunpowder and blood in the air, Qin Chuan couldn’t help but breathe a sigh of relief—Mr. Colin’s task was finally completed.
After this run, he could almost have circled the Earth.
“Alright, we will arrange for someone to keep an eye on that man, so rest assured,” said the man with the cowboy hat as he walked out of the smoke, revealing his white teeth and a hearty smile. “I also have some matters to deal with on my end, so I won’t be escorting you any further.”
“Hmm, there’s nothing much left to do anyway,” Qin Chuan nodded, and followed by the few team members who came with him, left directly.
Watching them depart, the man with the cowboy hat slightly lowered the brim and quickly headed in another direction.
As a man of his word, he always kept his promises.
If he said he’d help the manor owner’s family reunite, then he’d make sure the family reunited!
A few hours later, he found a random phone booth and dialed a number: “It’s taken care of.”
Upon hearing this, a relieved sigh came from the other end of the phone.
“Remember my payment, the ‘True Ancestor’s Blood,'” the man reminded.
But just after he finished speaking, a gentle old voice came through the phone: “This incident obviously didn’t go as I expected, so perhaps we need to discuss the allocation again…”
He now knew that this sudden investigation wasn’t targeted at him at all, so paying with something so precious was too much of a loss.
“Hey, that’s not my problem, although the incident is over, there could still be surprises,” the man with the cowboy hat chuckled. “Besides that big shot, there might be quite a few other people interested in some of your affairs.”
After he spoke, there was silence on the phone for a while, but in the end, the deal was agreed upon.
Then the old man’s voice continued: “There’s one more thing: could you find out who actually gave the order this time?”
Although the intelligence suggested that it was just an accident, he still wasn’t reassured and wanted to get to the bottom of it.
He felt that making such a big fuss over merely fishing out a person seemed a bit unrealistic.
Moreover, it was a particularly troublesome time due to the recent family migration.
“It’s difficult. As far as I know, the assistance order came from an almost top-secret, really big figure. Trying to find out is nearly impossible, even though I’ve been partners with you guys for over a decade…”
The man wearing the cowboy hat shared what he knew, making the old man on the other end of the phone feel the incident was extraordinary, especially after hearing about the difficulty of the investigation—his heart sank deeper…
However, just as his breathing began to grow heavier,
the man wearing the cowboy hat suddenly changed the subject, “It’s going to cost more.”
“Hmm?” The old man was taken aback.
“I have a way to find out what’s behind this, but this time, I want the ‘True Ancestor’s Blood’!”
Hearing his demand, the person on the other side of the phone fell silent again, and ultimately, with difficulty, said, “Fine.”
When the call ended, the man wearing the cowboy hat narrowed his eyes but didn’t hurry to leave.
He took an encrypted phone out of his pocket: “Old Master Wu, they seem to have agreed on their end. I’ll have a chance to get in touch with their core personnel.”
“Excellent! Continue with the operation. As long as there’s contact, we’ll be able to confirm whether they are ‘Red Moon’ cult followers, and identify the real criminals behind that tragic massacre. Then, none of these guys trying to migrate here will get away!”
Listening to him, the man in the cowboy hat couldn’t help but remember the large-scale bloodbath caused by “Red Moon” cultists operating within the country.
What was supposed to be a day of New Year’s celebration turned into a nightmare as over a dozen villages evaporated overnight, leaving no living relatives except for him, who was studying abroad at the time.
After years of jumping from place to place, from domestic pursuit to international, he knew who the enemy was but was unable to act. After all, those guys were legitimate powers within the circle; he couldn’t act as freely as he could today.
It wasn’t until recently that a major figure from within the country suddenly sought people, found that estate owner, and the people of this family, as if scared, promised many things to let him take care of the hidden dangers.
That’s when he found the breakthrough.
“I look forward to that day.” The man in the cowboy hat said.
Putting aside personal grievances, he was well aware that the higher-ups were so concerned about these people because the “World Barriers” had been under threat lately, leaving the island that once ruled over most of the world looking grim.
A number of foreign artifacts that had been plundered in the past were now slowly spiraling out of control. The more places they had looted, the more types of strangeness they possessed, making it the place with the richest array of anomalies in the world today…
Many of the local ancient powers were preparing to flee and migrate.
This group was no exception; it’s just that the direction of their migration posed a threat that the country felt uneasy about—
East India.
And without a proper reason, taking action against them would easily lead to a major dispute.
At this moment, Colin could probably not imagine that what was meant to be a routine mission had now caused so many people sleepless nights, willing to pay a huge price just to confirm who he really was, thus stirring up a massive incident.
…
December 17th, noon.
The endless, ancient tolling of the clock slowly faded in his ears…
Colin found himself once again in “World Code-13”.
But as soon as he had arrived and taken in the scene before him, he couldn’t help but feel his heart skip a beat.
Before the bonfire, numerous old people and children were kneeling down to pray, trembling with fear, constantly chanting the name Colin had left behind in this world…
Outside the church, heavy footsteps could be heard from terrifying creatures moving around.

chapters.title: Chapter 340 - 340 338 The Catastrophe of the Magic Fog
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 340: Chapter 338: The Catastrophe of the Magic Fog Strikes!_1 Chapter 340: Chapter 338: The Catastrophe of the Magic Fog Strikes!_1 “So, something did go wrong…”
Colin’s eyebrows knitted together as he observed the scene within the church, his mind quickly filling with conjectures.
He hadn’t been able to enter as usual last week because of the task for “World Code -4,”…
So this time he arrived seven days later, instead of the usual next day.
At the same time, Li Ming and others, who had just descended and were ready to pop some pills to work overtime, also stopped their movements and stared for a few seconds upon seeing the scene before them, then immediately spoke up:
“What happened? What’s going on?”
With the sound of his voice, the Bonfire Followers, who had been praying continuously in the church, finally opened their eyes and noticed their arrival.
Suddenly, as if they had found their backbone, they began to call out.
The situation became a bit chaotic for a moment.
“Quiet down, tell us what happened first…”
Colin raised his hand to calm them and chose one of the believers, who seemed relatively calm, to come forward and recount what had occurred.
“Archbishop, during the time you returned to the ‘God Kingdom,’ it was the ‘Catastrophe of the Magic Fog,’ the terrifying creatures from the ‘Catastrophe of the Magic Fog’ attacked over here!”
The elderly believer tearfully narrated the hardships of the past few days.
The monsters of the “Catastrophe of the Magic Fog” appeared nearby roughly four days ago.
Perhaps it was Luck, the creatures, usually sensitive to the living, did not launch an attack here, as if they were unaware of it.
But three days ago, things suddenly changed.
The lingering monsters suddenly arrived, launching an attack here…
At that time, there were tens of thousands of people on the estate; clearly, not everyone could escape, nor was everybody able to move.
Thus, those who couldn’t leave could only seek shelter inside the church.
Everyone thought they would perish alongside the church, but it was at that moment when they noticed that all the monsters were avoiding this church.
Many of the old, weak, sick, and disabled thus narrowly escaped tragedy…
‘So these are those so-called monsters?’
Colin lifted his head, and through the front door, sensed the situation outside.
He could feel there were still some people outside the church, mostly the elderly and frail, along with some especially faithful Believers who were sworn to live or die with the church.
And a little further away, at a distance of about fifty meters, creatures of various sizes and distorted shapes lurked around.
From them, one could sense a twisted hostility towards the living.
But perhaps it was due to a wariness of the Bonfire, or some other reason, they dared not venture within a fifty-meter direct distance of the Bonfire.
However, due to the arrival of these creatures, the buildings around had all been knocked down and destroyed, looking like ruins.
‘The strength of the monsters nearby isn’t very high, they can be dealt with. It’s just that their numbers are a bit large; there are a few hundred, but that’s not too big a problem…’
Colin took a deep breath and further analyzed the information in the scents.
After understanding the general situation, suddenly a message appeared upon his retina…
[Event One: Rescue the disaster victims who have come for the Bonfire as much as possible.]
“Note”: Higher mission evaluations will be awarded.
…
As this task appeared, Colin immediately felt, approximately at the nine o’clock direction, several “guidances.”
Although he couldn’t sense specifics, he could vaguely determine there were quite a few survivors.
“Close call, not everyone died.”
Colin let out a silent breath of relief. For him, the greatest significance of this mission was that he could accurately locate the people who had once come before the bonfire…
Although he could slowly find them by their scent, it was definitely not as fast as this method.
This time, if they all died because of this incident, he could not accept it.
This was the territory he had established with so much effort!
From nothing to something, it had developed little by little into the territory it was now.
After that, Colin looked around the church and was about to leave when he suddenly realized an important person was missing…
“Where’s ‘Red’?” Colin asked.
If she were here, she would probably have rushed over as soon as he arrived.
But he had not seen her up till now…
And inside the church, there was none of her scent at all, while the faint scents that lingered seemed to be several days old.
This gave him a bad premonition.
Just as he finished speaking, several children with red-rimmed eyes emerged, “Archbishop, sister, she suddenly left after the monsters arrived, leading away some beasts, and we have no idea where she is now…”
“She left on her own?” Colin frowned deeply.
He knew there was something special about Little Red, but that specialty was unlikely to handle the current situation.
However, seeing several children crying, Colin said, “Don’t worry, I’ll find her and bring her back.”
After comforting them, he looked at Li Ming and the other two, “You guys take charge and manage the disaster-affected people for now. I’ve brought you some help this time, you can find out how to use them for yourselves…”
Colin raised his hand and three silver mists flew out towards them.
The Nano Intellectual Mechanism contained in each was about five jin, enough for the trio to cope with the current situation, and even form a layer of nano-armor on their skin.
Having done all this, Colin quickly pushed open the door, took a distant look at the swarm of monsters ahead, then with a powerful leap, he plunged into the midst of the beasts amidst the gazes and cries of astonishment from thousands of believers, like a cannonball.
Crack!
A monster, coincidentally at the landing spot, was crushed on the spot by Colin.
He looked around quickly, scanning the scene and saw a large number of creatures with twisted shapes, the smallest of which were the size of a small car, covered in the area, with gray-white chitin claws or hammer-like appendages.
It was then that Colin felt a chaotic and strange wave of spiritual energy washing over him…
At the same time, after initial surprise, all the monsters immediately began attacking him.
“A group spiritual attack? Seems like it has strong polluting effects too?”
While pondering, Colin quickly took out a 300 milliliters test tube from his pocket—
Pure Firebearer essence grease, no additives, free of any extraneous substances!
He had just received it yesterday from the company and hadn’t yet had the chance to dilute it with water.
Moreover, considering the emergency, Colin had no intention of holding back. He squeezed forcefully, breaking the test tube, and flames ignited.
Boom!
A tremendous fireball erupted from within the group of monsters.
The scorching light rose like a mushroom cloud before exploding outwards like a tidal wave, engulfing all the nearby magical creatures.
Under the intense heat, many of the weaker monsters were instantly charred and killed on the spot.
Even the slightly stronger ones lasted no more than a dozen seconds in the flames before they too howled in agony and died.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 341 - 341 339 The Might of the Firebearer_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 341: Chapter 339: The Might of the Firebearer!_1 Chapter 341: Chapter 339: The Might of the Firebearer!_1 “You’re very lucky. In normal times, I definitely wouldn’t have been willing to use this thing like that.”
Colin muttered to himself, watching as the corpses evaporated like ice cubes in the sun, turning into mist and disappearing without a trace.
Some intuition told him that these things hadn’t died; they had only returned to something.
Of course, if he had put in a bit more effort and contained that mist as well, they would surely have been completely killed…
Or, if he had used the “Little Fist Stone” to devour them before the bodies vanished, it would have probably resulted in their complete demise too.
However, he didn’t have time for such precise operations.
After all, the monsters near the church were not the main concern.
Without much thought, Colin controlled his body to float up, stretching his hands to either side and crushing two more “Colorless Crystal Blocks”.
Instantly, torrents of flames erupted from him as if they were a flash flood under his command, sweeping in all directions. Countless tongues of fire, dozens of meters long, lashed and consumed the demonic beings, reducing them to charcoal, vaporizing them…
Some of the stronger individuals who weren’t killed on the spot were finished off by the “Flying Blades” formed from Nano Intellectual Mechanisms.
At this moment, the might of a “Firebearer” was beyond any doubt!
“The effect of pure grease is indeed much stronger, both in strength and range… It’s incredibly handy,”
He couldn’t help but take a deep breath after feeling the flames, inhaling some of the lingering fires into his nostrils…
Suddenly, he experienced a refreshing sensation, his mind feeling clear and unobstructed.
If it were fire made from ordinary materials, maintaining an effective range of thirty meters would have been a strenuous task, let alone being able to “enjoy” it like now.
“It’s the ‘Agent of the Bonfire’!”
Only at this moment did the people nearby the church realize that the person who had just charged out was their own Bishop!
“Indeed, the ‘Bonfire Church’ would not abandon us!” someone cried with joy.
“Please save us, Envoy of the ‘Bonfire’, my father left this place… I beg you…”
“With the arrival of the great Envoy, everyone will be saved!”
“…”
The atmosphere, which had been filled with despair and fear, was cleansed by the blazing light ignited by Colin!
After initially dealing with the monsters on the scene, Colin, following the sense of his mission in his brain, floated to a height of about a dozen meters. After determining his direction, he suddenly shot out with a thunderous roar.
In the eyes of the onlookers, he was like a meteor wrapped in flames, rapidly departing…
…
Meanwhile, over a hundred kilometers away from the church, within a rugged and uneven forest, a group of approximately a thousand people were struggling to flee deeper into the dense woods.
Days of relentless flight had left them in terrible condition, with many walking with flesh so torn their feet were a bloody muddle.
Countless pebbles were deeply embedded in their flesh…
Even among them, those with exceptional physical strength were not in a much better state.
In fact, some were even worse off due to occasional direct encounters with demonic beings.
In the middle rear of the large group, within a small squad of about a dozen people, a man with a gaunt face suggested to someone wearing soft armor and armed with a broken sword: “Yeger Lan, give up these people. If we keep going like this, we won’t be able to escape either…”
Whoosh!
A cold light sliced through the air.
Yeager cut through the thorny vines ahead: “No need to persuade me. If you want to leave, you don’t have to follow me. I will continue to carry out the mission given to us from above.”
Hearing this, one of the people couldn’t help but respond: “I don’t understand. Our mission was just to monitor that territory per the instructions, investigate the church, at most to show a certain goodwill. We’ve been helping these people for so many days; we’ve already reached our limit.”
“Our goodwill has already been given enough… Leaving now, the Knight Commander won’t hold us accountable.”
As he finished speaking, others chimed in: “That’s right, we have no need to take risks here. The Knight has already promised that once this mission is completed, we’ll be the first to become first-order ‘Virtue Knights’ for the next ten years…”
“Yeah, yeah…”
“People sent from other churches have all fled by now, we have done more than enough.”
“…”
Listening to their comments, Yeager fiercely swung his sword, cutting through a clump of thorns in front of them.
Seeing this, everyone fell silent.
Yeager turned around, his face gaunt from days of relentless campaigning, yet it bore an indescribable resolve:
“I have said many times, you can leave on your own, there’s no need to follow me.”
This time, the same words carried a hint of warning.
‘Leave? How can we leave? You are the Knight Commander’s prized protege, and what are we? Leaving like this, what difference is there from being dead?’
The members of the squad couldn’t help but complain to each other, exchanging glances, then one of them spoke up, “Yeager, you… you’re not just doing this for the mission from above, right?”
Hearing his words, Yeager didn’t answer directly, “What do you think a knight’s duty is?”
“To offer loyalty to the king, to guard every inch of the king’s territory, to protect every one of the king’s subjects…”
Yeager cut them off at the third clause, “So, all I’m doing is protecting the king’s subjects.”
Upon hearing this, everyone couldn’t help but share the same thought: Those refugees are considered the king’s subjects?
Although they had always known that Yeager was a bit “unreliable,” they never expected him to actually harbor such thoughts—
Had he been brainwashed by the Bonfire Church?
Only those people would waste their effort on the unworthy.
Or perhaps, had he been brainwashed by that oddball “Saintess,” whose unrealistic and incomprehensible ideas filled her head?
The former possibility seemed most likely, but the latter was not far behind.
After all, they had heard rumors that the Light Church’s Saintess might be coming this way.
Moreover, many normal people had inexplicably changed their personalities after interacting with the “Saintess” and developed unnecessary compassion.
As if he saw through their thoughts, Yeager spoke, “The Bonfire Church has been acknowledged as an orthodox faith by all the churches, and those accepted by the Bonfire Church are naturally the king’s subjects as well.”
The others fell silent for a few seconds before someone spoke up, “To be precise, although they are subjects, they are in fact the Bonfire Church’s people. It should be them saving these people, not us…
“Yeager, what you are doing isn’t just ‘protecting the king’s subjects,’ is it?
“You haven’t… betrayed us, have you?”
“I have always followed the teachings and have not betrayed anyone.”
Having said that, Yeager took a deep breath, sidestepping the issue and instead said:
“Do you know, they truly save the weak, provide healing, food, and even impart knowledge and literacy…”
“We do the same…”
Yeager cut off his comrade’s words, “It’s not the same, the direction is different…”
Thinking back to what Colin and the others had done, he didn’t know how to describe it, he could only feel; those people weren’t doing it because of doctrine, not out of charity… they seemed to truly want to change this place.
What struck him most was the scene of Colin, as the Envoy of God, the representative of the divine on earth, a personage of unparalleled dignity… actually willing to sit down on the ground among a crowd of filthy, reeking poor, and speak with them—
Like… like equals in conversation?
This nearly impossible thing had actually happened…
Yeager found it hard to articulate that sense of absurdity; since that day, he had been repeatedly shaken by that image.
And before this, he had always felt that something was wrong with the Knight Kingdom, no, with the world…
But he couldn’t pinpoint what exactly was wrong.
He wanted to ask that “Saintess,” who seemed a little off to most nobles and higher-ups, but he never had the chance.
Until recently, when he was assigned a surveillance mission and saw that scene, he began to vaguely grasp something.
It was this realization that had driven him to act in a way that seemed utterly irrational in the eyes of his colleagues.
However, before he could say more,
a series of monstrous roars came from behind, causing Yeager and everyone else to abruptly change their expressions.
.
.
.
