﻿Chapter 342: Chapter 340 Warden Calder (Extra chapter for monthly votes)_1 Chapter 342: Chapter 340 Warden Calder (Extra chapter for monthly votes)_1 “Speed up and escape!”
Yeager roared, his originally thin body suddenly swelled up, with muscles piling upon muscles, transforming him into a small giant over two meters tall, with a bronze skin tone and even taller than Warden Calder had been.
The other members of the squad were unable to pay attention to anything else, all entering a state of combat readiness.
It was at this moment that a dozen or so strangely shaped figures moved swiftly in the back, catching up to them in no time.
These creatures all had gray-white chitinous claws…
Though they were small in size, their speed was incredibly fast.
And for some reason, they were filled with a certain hatred for the living, swinging their sharp claws and attacking the crowd as soon as they arrived.
A 25-year-old soldier had just fended off one attack and hadn’t retracted his weapon when another gray-white figure suddenly pounced on him.
Whoosh.
The chitinous claw swept past.
His body was directly sliced in two, blood splattering everywhere, and his innards instantly spilled out…
Stimulated by the pungent smell of blood.
Many of the surrounding monsters suddenly abandoned their current targets, pouncing on the bisected 25-year-old, ferociously drawing his blood and flesh.
Taking advantage of this moment, Yeager swung his sword with force, killing several of the gray-white demons.
“Hold on! Reinforcements will arrive soon!”
As he bellowed, he prepared to pull back and retreat.
However, a terrifying Mental Shock suddenly surged from behind…
Swept up by this mental tide, countless people on-site turned blank, some even fainting on the spot.
“Damn it!”
Yeager despaired internally, looking up in the direction from which the mental tide had come, and saw, high in the sky at an unknown distance away.
A giant creature over several dozen meters tall with sinister, blood-colored wings flapping, continuously emitting roars that vibrated the heavens and the earth.
From afar, its upper body resembled some kind of fallen angel polluted in hell, while its lower half was like mangrove roots dangling tentacles…
The mental waves produced by its screeches were enough to immobilize them all.
It was as if witnessing the advent of the end of time.
“It looks like we can’t escape after all…”
Everyone present despaired.
If they weren’t mistaken, this was definitely a demon of a caliber comparable to a third-tier Virtue Knight or higher!
But just then, everyone suddenly felt a rumbling vibration in the air…
The waves of mental contamination assaulting them in succession also weakened as a result…
While they were puzzled, they suddenly saw a “meteor” falling from the sky, directly smashing onto the horrifying creature that had driven them to utmost despair.
With just one blow, he saw that half of the terrifying creature’s body was blasted away.
Everyone present was stunned, then quickly realized something.
“Is it… the Divine Envoy from the ‘Bonfire’? Has it returned from the ‘God Kingdom’?” an incredulous 25-year-old soldier exclaimed.
At first, they had all hoped that the Divine Envoy would appear and save them, but after some days passed without sign, they lost hope.
They had not expected to see the Divine Envoy at this critical moment.
At this moment, as the large demon was struck, numerous lesser demons quickly moved to defend the large one.
Seeing this, the escapees near the area breathed a sigh of relief.
The voices erupting from this large demonic entity targeted a very vast area…
Fortunately, the Envoy of God had finally arrived…
However, Yeager was just about to sit down and rest when he noticed, in the dense woods not far away, several figures rapidly moving away, apparently chasing after something…
“These people…”
Yeager remembered, back when they were in the territory, he seemed to have noticed them there as well.
In fact, he suspected that the outbreak of this minor Catastrophe of the Magic Fog was also related to these people…
Without hesitation, he immediately followed them.
As one of the promising Squire Knights regarded highly by the Knight Commander, he was also no stranger to tracking.
“This aura, could it be… the Cultists from the Gluttonous Feast? What are they doing here?” Yeager puzzled internally. He had heard of these cultists, who came from nowhere, with an abnormally huge appetite, consuming anything edible, as if never satisfied.
Once, these cultists devoured all the food in a city.
Then, unsatisfied, they ate all the plants…
And in the end, they devoured everything that could be swallowed.
About half a month ago, during the “God War” in the vicinity, the Knight Legion and the Church had organized a siege against them, and he had participated, which is why he remembered the aura.
Not long after he started moving, he arrived deep within the forest.
Just as he wondered what was happening…
he suddenly saw the group quicken their pace toward a dense forest, followed swiftly by the sound of clashing weapons.
“Are there still people here? Wait a minute, is that… Warden Calder?”
Yeager had just caught up when he saw a man, as tall as a little giant at three meters high, his body shrouded in a thin light of Glory, fiercely battling these cultists.
He was familiar with this man who had recently survived the “Catastrophe of the Magic Fog” and become the “Virtue Knight—Glory”.
Not far behind Warden Calder lay a man who, with the exception of his right hand, had all his limbs amputated, the stumps simply wrapped in bandages, and a huge wound in his chest.
Yeager remembered that this seemed to be the Warden’s nephew who had previously led a group of people in an escape.
He had not expected the nephew’s current situation to be so dire.
And in the middle of this group, a little girl was encircled…
“Is this… Little Red?”
Yeager almost immediately recognized this girl as the one who often followed by the Envoy of God’s side.
“Who exactly are you? Some of your habits and reflexes don’t seem typical of cultists. What is your purpose, and why would you lay hands on a little girl…”
Warden Calder waved his greatsword as he attempted to gather information.
Unfortunately, the enemy did not respond and instead more figures launched attacks on him from other directions…
Even as a first-tier Virtue Knight, it was very difficult for him to face a dozen “cultists” alone.
Suddenly, Warden Calder’s heart chilled as he saw several figures pass by his side, initiating an attack on the little girl behind him, and the others were also busy dealing with enemies, unable to protect her.
But just as they were about to succeed, Yeager’s figure appeared in front of Little Red, blocking these attacks.
“Who’s this?”
Calder was taken aback, feeling that the figure was familiar but unrecognizable, but he could tell from the “Knight’s Six Techniques” high-speed movement that this was probably a fairly capable squire.
The stalemate between them instantly deepened once again.
But overall, the situation was still not optimistic.
However, perhaps sensing something, a figure in a dark blue-black robe walked out from the woods, looked toward Calder and the others, and said with a hoarse voice:
“Hand over the girl to our ‘Gluttonous Feast’, or everyone here will die!”
Now he seemed more impatient than before, sensing perhaps that an unexpected turn was coming.
“Hey, I thought you guys were like mutes, destined to never speak…”
Warden Calder swung his greatsword to deflect his enemies, about to say something more, when his face suddenly took on a bizarre expression and he swiftly found an opening to jump backward.
Seeing this, the dark blue-black robed figure thought they were finally giving in.
But at that moment, he suddenly heard the Warden speak:
“To be honest, if I were you, I would start running now.”
“What do you mean…”
The voice of the dark blue-black robed figure abruptly stopped, and then he seemed to swallow hard, as his gaze slowly drifted downward to the right.
Unnoticed, a hand ablaze with fire had come to rest on his own shoulder.
Looking back along the fiery hand, he saw a man slowly burning, staring back at him impassively.
When did he get there, and how was he so fast? The figure in the blue-black robe was shocked, breaking out in a cold sweat.
He knew that Colin had once again descended upon this land, but he had not anticipated the other party would appear so quickly!
The surrounding space became viscous at that moment, with countless orange-red glows surging, and the terrible oppression felt like suffocating magma.
“It seems you hold a particular interest in Little Red?”
Colin stated coldly, looking at the man.
Having said that, he was ready to take action, to completely subdue these fellows and understand the situation…
But at that moment, the man’s life force disappeared rapidly, his body decayed quickly, the skin melted, bones disintegrated, and large chunks of flesh fell from his robe, turning into a putrid red liquid…
Not just him, but all the assailants at the scene experienced an incomprehensible decay.
“It’s a vicious curse; they have committed suicide due to mission failure. It seems that person doesn’t want us to track them down…” Calder’s voice came from up ahead.
When Colin looked at him, Calder’s figure was shrinking back into the somewhat portly middle-aged appearance.
“I know, I can tell…”
After Colin spoke, he shifted his gaze from the pile of rotten flesh on the ground and nodded to the first person he had met when he arrived in the Other World:
“Long time no see.”
.
.
.
ps: If I stay up late to burst my liver and add another chapter, can you still keep your monthly tickets in hand?

chapters.title: Chapter 343 - 343 341 The Construction Site Needs Talents
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 343: Chapter 341: The Construction Site Needs Talents Like You!_1 Chapter 343: Chapter 341: The Construction Site Needs Talents Like You!_1 Virtue Knight…
Colin’s gaze lingered on the dawn light flowing over Calder’s body.
He felt an aura similar to that of the “Emblem of the Humility Knight.”
However, the aura was similar, but the abilities were vastly different…
The kind emanating from Warden Calder’s body seemed more suited for combat, allowing that dawn light to bless his body, turning it into something akin to armor.
And compared to before, the opponent’s physical condition had clearly improved by a notch.
Of course, after comparing, Colin felt that there was a slight discrepancy compared to his own progress.
He should still be a bit stronger than the other party.
‘It seems the reward that Helena promised him has been delivered…’ Colin muttered to himself.
As he pondered, he lifted his right palm, gathering a ball of flame which he then gently tugged upward, sending it flying into the air.
The fist-sized flame rapidly expanded as it rose.
In no time, a warm sensation radiating strong warmth enveloped everyone present, quickly healing their spiritual trauma.
“Ah, long time no see.”
Warden Calder, somewhat overweight, looked up at the flame in midair, then stared at Colin with an odd expression, as if he had something to say but didn’t know how to start.
“Do you have any questions?” Colin asked curiously, taking the initiative.
After a moment of thought, Warden Calder ultimately shook his head: “No, forget it, it’s nothing…”
Being versed in the art of slacking, he knew well that sometimes, knowing too much could only complicate matters.
However, even without asking, Colin could roughly guess—
When he had arrived, he used the “Emblem of the Humility Knight” to conceal himself, so the other party was probably curious about the Virtue Knight-like power on him.
Seeing that Calder did not pursue the matter further, Colin didn’t dwell on it either.
“By the way, that large monster that made the noise just now…”
“I’ve taken care of it.”
Colin recalled the scene at that moment; he rushed forward and delivered a “Matchless Strike,” instantly blasting apart more than half of the enemy’s head, then used the “Revolver Contrarian” to finish it off completely.
Though it looked big, its strength wasn’t very great—it was over in a few blows…
However, he had heard that the true horror of the “Catastrophe of the Magic Fog” lay in their numbers. If one truly entered the Mist Disaster’s direct range, creatures of such level would probably be more numerous than mosquitoes by the river.
By then, even if he dispatched them one punch at a time with the “Matchless Strike,” he would not be able to cope.
And hearing Colin’s words, Warden Calder visibly breathed a sigh of relief: “That’s good then, if it had escaped and then grown stronger, it would have been troublesome. Once it reaches a certain stage, it would release ‘Magic Fog’ and trigger a new round of disaster.”
“Yeah, so I didn’t give it a chance to escape,” Colin nodded in agreement.
Having been in this world for so long, he had also heard numerous legends and knowledge about these entities…
And at this moment, seeing the conversation between the two had ended, Little Red finally plunged towards Colin.
Her tiny body quivered as she clung tightly to him, not crying, but the fear in her was palpable.
“It’s alright, no need to be afraid now.”
Colin said, smiling as he stroked her little head.
“I’m not afraid, I… I just thought you weren’t coming back,” Little Red said with a hint of a sob and some grievance.
“Don’t worry, I won’t,” Colin reassured.
While speaking, he glanced over at Warden Calder’s nephew not far away, alive indeed, but apart from having a left hand, he was almost reduced to a human pig.
“If I had been a bit slower in coming to support, this guy would probably have been dismembered by now.”
Warden Calder likewise turned to look at the child of his old comrade. Thinking about what had happened earlier, he couldn’t help but give his unconscious nephew a light kick on the ground.
“Let’s take him back for now. This time he was injured while helping out with matters in the territory; we’ll provide treatment.”
Colin first had a portion of the “Nano Intellectual Machines” drift towards the other person, seeping into his body to repair the damage.
“I’m sorry, it’s my fault, I led them here, it’s me who got everyone killed…” Little Red said, lowering her head in self-blame. Underneath her somewhat disheveled hair, her eyes began to redden slightly.
At that moment, Colin could feel that her words were also filled with a certain fear as if she was worried about being driven away because of this.
But before she could finish, Colin placed his hand on Little Red’s slender shoulders.
“Don’t think too much for now. Do you know who those people were?” Colin took the opportunity to ask.
“I… I don’t know. I’ve always had people looking for me as far as I can remember, but a few years ago, they disappeared. I thought… they would never show up again.”
As she spoke, it seemed as if she had made some kind of decision, “But… I guess they…”
“No, wait, don’t say anything. If it’s a major secret, you can tell us after we get back. Don’t mention it here…” Warden Calder abruptly cut her off.
Instinctively, Warden Calder could sense this was definitely a huge problem.
So, without a second thought, he decided not to listen at all…
As long as he didn’t know, even if the “Loyalty-Virtue Knight” arrived, he wouldn’t worry about knowing some shocking secret that might get him killed to keep it silent.
“However, I can tell you one thing, those people probably aren’t cultists, at least not proper cultists, as there are traces of formal knight training in their bodies…” Warden Calder added.
Cultists can be proper or not proper… Colin mumbled in his heart, then spoke,
“Alright, thanks for the warning, let’s head back.”
Having said that, he sensed his surroundings, “Get ready. I’ll take you away from here now. There are still many roaming creatures nearby…”
While speaking, his gaze landed on a young man with a fairly familiar face standing behind.
“You did well, you’re Yeager, right?”
If it hadn’t been for this young man stepping forward just now, Little Red would probably have been injured, or worse, her eyes might have lost control…
“Yes… ‘Bonfire’ Agent, sir.” Yeager nodded, feeling that his identity was already seen through at this moment.
Of course, they didn’t know that from the moment they entered the territory, Colin had already seen through them…
Otherwise, he wouldn’t have assigned them specifically to clear the land for farming.
You must understand, such fields are so tough that not even bulls can easily plow them, and with ordinary people, the efficiency is terribly low. Only these guys, who have something about them, could handle the kind of work even cattle and horses wouldn’t want to do.
“What are your plans moving forward?” Colin asked.
“I want to continue staying in the territory…” Yeager said, “I want to learn some things more deeply…”
He wanted to delve into those thoughts that seemed somewhat out of place in this world.
“Hmm.”
Colin nodded and reached out to pat him on the shoulder,
“Work hard. The fields need people like you who can handle the tough work.”
After speaking, everyone did not delay further, each carrying the wounded and rushing towards the territory…
However, Colin did not follow them, but instead initiated rescues for several other people still under attack by the creatures, aiming to clear all the threats within this large area as much as possible.
.
.
.
Chapter two coming later.

chapters.title: Chapter 344 - 344 342 Holy Beast Smiling Mountain of
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 344: Chapter 342 Holy Beast “Smiling Mountain of Corpses”_1 Chapter 344: Chapter 342 Holy Beast “Smiling Mountain of Corpses”_1 Boom!
High in the sky, hundreds of meters above, a gigantic fireball soared, dazzling like a miniature sun.
Bright flames radiated light in all directions…
Even from a considerable distance, one could feel the heat emanating from that fiery glow.
And it was at this moment.
The people who were still persevering in their escape from the monsters finally realized that their great Divine Envoy had returned!
For the monsters still lingering nearby, Colin struck with heavy blows.
From the church, he sliced his way through hundreds of miles, then chopped his way back, his hand rising and falling without even blinking…
“┗|｀O′|┛ Wow~!”
As a mass of corpses dissolved upon the earth, a thunderous roar suddenly erupted.
The dark “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” propped itself up with its hands on the ground, facing a large group of monsters, issuing a soul-striking psychic attack that deterred them, and then rushed forward, not leaving a single one alive, before unapologetically swallowing them all.
With a combination of moves, all the lesser creatures present were cleared out by it.
And behind the Corpse Mountain, amongst a group of refugees, many showed faces of terror at the sight of the giant black beast, while others showed completely opposite expressions of excitement:
“It’s the ‘Bonfire’ Church’s Holy Beast of the Divine Envoy!”
On his territory, Colin would sometimes deal with some badly behaved refugees and not waste the residual value hidden in their bodies.
He would usually summon the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses.”
Then he ordered the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” to join him on tasks like digging pits and farming…
So quite a few refugees were familiar with it.
Although the “Holy Beast” had some quirks, like sometimes stealing what the Divine Envoy called “potatoes” they had planted, or occasionally liking to hold them in its mouth and suck for fun…
But at this moment, seeing it, the crowd could not help but be moved to tears, getting up and following it.
And with Colin proactively and swiftly intercepting the monsters, the dangers nearby were finally beginning to be announced as over…
Even though there were some smaller individuals still roaming, they no longer posed much of a threat.
One group of refugees after another set out once again on the road back to the “Sanctuary.”
“Speaking of which, I feel like we need to leave some weapons or something behind. Otherwise, if there’s another delay, this place could suffer again…”
While maintaining the huge fireball in the sky, Colin couldn’t help but rub his forehead.
But for the moment, he couldn’t think of what kind of weapons would be better for guarding this place…
The items he carried weren’t quite suitable…
And as for firearms, it might have been difficult to get them before, but with the Little Maid, the nano intellectual mechanism, it shouldn’t be a problem.
However, once the items were made, there was another problem.
There was no suitable gunpowder or anything here; they would have to carry it, but there was not enough space to bring a large amount…
“Troublesome, might have to wait until after reaching D Level…”
Shaking his head to dispel the thought, Colin sighed with resignation and, after providing some assistance to the refugees, proceeded ahead, returning to his territory before nightfall.
By that time, a large number of people had once again gathered on his land.
However, the vast majority were wounded, and all plowing and development plans had been put on hold due to this…
The immediate priority was clearly to heal the people first.
As more and more people returned to the territory, Colin himself had to join in the effort to save people, dealing with injuries he could manage.
For almost three days and three nights, he stayed busy until the situation with most of the injured on the territory was finally somewhat stabilized.
“God forbid I find out who’s the mastermind behind this, or else I’ll have their ancestors’ graves blown to the wind…”
Colin sat at the entrance of the Church, listening to the sporadic sounds of pain around him, feeling somewhat angry in his heart.
He could now roughly confirm that there was something fishy about this monster attack—
For instance, creatures that arose from the “Catastrophe of the Magic Fog” usually wouldn’t stray from the fog’s range, but this time, they had anomalously appeared, clearly being led by something or someone.
Adding to that was the attack on Little Red, which all but confirmed…
The adversary intended to lure people away from the territory with these monsters and then take the opportunity to target Little Red.
However, as the group of people had resolutely committed suicide last time, Colin, for the moment, had no way of dealing with this mastermind…
As for Little Red’s secret…
Colin felt it wasn’t much; her eyes seemed rather special and attracted certain people’s covetousness.
Since she was very young, she’d always been able to sense danger in advance and avoid it, but this time, for some reason, she was found by them again…
However, this time, because Colin protected her, those people didn’t dare to approach normally.
As for who exactly those people were, even Little Red herself didn’t know.
At that moment, a thunderous roar came from nearby, interrupting Colin’s thoughts.
He took a deep breath, stood up, and looked towards the direction of the sound.
He saw the two-headed “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” dragging a heap of bizarre things, swiftly crawling this way.
Atop its heads, the hazy figure of “Yukionna” looked like a triumphant knightess, happily surveying the territory.
When Colin and others were treating the common folk earlier, they incidentally released “Yukionna” to send Corpse Mountain out on a hunt and carry out relief operations for the refugees.
Clearly, their outing this time had been rather successful.
“Not bad, should be enough to upgrade the Bonfire here to Third Level.”
Colin looked at the prey dragged by “Little Fist Stone,” called out to the two creatures, and turned to walk into the small Church.
Soon, after investing “10,000 Points” along with the spoil of over three hundred creatures with the strength comparable to D Level Beast Transformation Syndrome, the Bonfire was upgraded to Third Level.
The gentle glow of the Flame penetrated the Church, eliciting bursts of exclaims from outside…
[“Bonfire Sacrificial Site”: Level 3.]
[Remaining burnable time: 65 days 23 hours 57 minutes.]
[“Level 3 Enchantment”: Can use special methods to apply temporary or permanent enchantment effects to items.]
[“Level 3 Fusion”: Can fuse suitable items together (with certain risks, possibly leading to items being less effective than before)…]
[“Flame Guard”: When a creature posing an extreme threat enters within a 300-meter range, authorized employees or a certain number of Bonfire Followers, through praying at the Bonfire, can summon a Bonfire Exorcist.]
[Notes: The Bonfire yearns for more Kindling…]
[——Sacrifice one Containment Subject assessed at Level 4 threat (Reference: Stage 5 “Beast Transformation Syndrome”) +3,000 Points to upgrade the Bonfire Level and gain additional features.]
[——Produces one “Pure Energy Crystal” every 60 minutes.]
…
“Finally got some means of defense.”
Colin looked for a while; although this “Flame Guard” wasn’t as strong as “World Code-4″‘s “Incarnation of the Cinder King,” once summoned, it was still pretty powerful.
He estimated it could match him in a back-and-forth fight without using a Golden Card and greasing up with the “Firebearer.”
Afterward, just as he was about to check out the “Enchantment” and “Fusion” features to see if he had anything that could combine, he suddenly felt a presence, turned his head, and saw a faintly glowing figure appearing suddenly from a corner of the Church…
Even without an introduction, Colin recognized the figure.
“The Light Chaser?”

chapters.title: Chapter 345 - 345 343 Divine Its a very pure Divine_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 345: Chapter 343 Divine! It’s a very pure Divine!_1 Chapter 345: Chapter 343 Divine! It’s a very pure Divine!_1 “He shouldn’t be here to sell buffs this time, right?”
Upon seeing that indistinct light and shadow figure whose gender was unclear, Colin almost subconsciously checked his retina first.
He always felt that any second now, an advertisement would pop up on his retina.
“‘Light of XXX,’ five hundred points per day, buy for the whole day with a buy-six-get-one-free deal for only three thousand.”
But fortunately, that didn’t happen this time.
The person in front of him, “The Light Chaser,” was not here on a mission dispatch…
Instead, he had come to visit in a non-working, private capacity.
‘Although I’ve had my suspicions before, it should be fairly certain by now that “The Light Chaser” is very likely a member of the Church of Light, possibly the Saintess, possibly the Pope, or some other high-ranking church member…’
Colin narrowed down the possibilities to a few high-ranking members of the Church of Light.
And this was logical…
As the Saintess who had ventured alone deep into the “Catastrophe of the Magic Fog” long ago was about to be free, it would not be strange for a high-ranking member of the “Church of Light” to come nearby to welcome her, and meanwhile, meet with him as well…
As for how they found him, Colin felt that although he was a mystery to most local people,
he probably wouldn’t seem so to “The Light Chaser,” a fellow employee.
At the same time, he could also roughly guess the other’s purpose.
If all went as expected, he should be here to fulfill the promise conveyed by Helena and exchange the Bone Spur in his possession.
On his body, that was probably the only thing that could draw the attention of the Church of Light’s high-ranking members.
However, perhaps thinking of something, Colin curiously used the “Combat Power Observation” feature of the “Gene Compensation Panel.”
He was very curious about the actual strength of “The Light Chaser”…
[Name]: ??? (Not the true body).
[Strength]: ???.
[Constitution]: ???.
[Agility]: ???.
[Description]: ???.
[Overall Evaluation]: Divine! It’s divinity! There is a streak of very pure divinity blocking my observation!
[Note]: The above data does not represent final combat power, please base judgement on actual contact…
…
“Useless…”
Having seen the result, Colin could not help but inwardly criticize; the observation turned out to be devoid of any useful information.
Oh, but that’s not exactly right; it’s not completely devoid of useful information.
At the very least, it was known that the one coming this time, like before, was not the true body…
And although it wasn’t the true body, just feeling it a bit, Colin realized there was a good chance that he might not even be able to defeat this incarnation.
This made him abandon the initial idea he had had of confronting the figure upon meeting, and straight up grabbing and hoisting by the neck.
‘Well, it’s not the real person, there’s no need.’
Colin’s thoughts quickly shifted, and he decided to settle the score when he encountered the real body.
This guy never dared to show his true face from the beginning, perhaps the real body isn’t that strong!
Such cases were not unheard of in the company…
Dog Brother was pretty much in the same boat—his “Four-Armed Citizens” were strong, but his real body was average.
Maybe this was a “Light and Shadow Folk”, just a more advanced version of the “Four-Armed Citizens”?
While he was observing the other party, “The Light Chaser” was also observing him.
Even though she had already carried out many missions with Colin, this was the first time she had actually seen what he looked like.
A simple, pure, and clean soul…
From this soul emanated numerous flickering flames, providing a comforting warmth that settled the heart.
Beyond that, she also sensed the surrounding people’s devout and pure faith…
This faith coalesced into an unfathomable bonfire.
“It seems that indeed they are not… cultists with ulterior motives.”
Shana felt a sigh of relief at this realization.
Although a deeper look into the soul revealed something worryingly dangerous lurking within, it did not affect the person directly.
What a pity…
If it had been a cultist who harbored disaster, retrieving that thing would have been much easier, perhaps even profitable, without needing to offer anything in exchange…
Undertaking a normal exchange, I have no idea how much I would have to offer to get the holy relic back.
My hard-earned savings of over 500 points, amassed through helping the people, are likely doomed…
As she was pondering, Colin suddenly spoke:
“Are you here to exchange for that item?”
As he spoke, he beckoned beside him, and the level 3 bonfire draped over him like a cloak.
It could have been an illusion, but Colin felt as if the other party was slowly stripping him bare, and if they kept staring each other down, he was afraid that every single pore on his body would be known to the other.
This instinctively made him pull the “bonfire” closer to shield his body, lest he really was stripped bare…
Upon hearing Colin’s words, The Light Chaser nodded and hummed in affirmation.
Whoosh.
Colin reached out for the Bone Spur, twirling it in his hand, and indeed saw the other’s gaze, from under the light and shadow, fixated on the object in his hand. But in the next second, the Bone Spur disappeared from Colin’s grasp.
“The item can certainly be exchanged, but… since you’ve come to trade with me, shouldn’t you show me what you’ve got?”
Enshrouded in flames, Colin casually observed the indistinct figure of light and shadow.
In his heart, the terrible effect of this item was worthy of an orange or even a gold-tier offensive artifact.
Its shortcoming lay in being a close-range weapon, but the advantage was that if it struck the enemy, they would instantly suffer a lethal effect similar to the thirty-three bullets of ‘Revolver Contrarian’.
Even now, it was one of Colin’s important means of defeating or containing powerful foes…
Of course, if the other party had something better, he certainly wouldn’t mind making an exchange.
If they didn’t have anything…
Then the discussion would have to wait for another day.
At this moment, Colin wasn’t worried that the other party would attempt to steal it; after all, they were in front of a bonfire. He felt he couldn’t beat the other, but if he played his trump card, he wouldn’t necessarily lose—an even fight at fifty-fifty should be possible…
However, the other’s demeanor suggested that they hadn’t come to steal, which piqued his curiosity about what this colleague had prepared to exchange with him.
“I… apologize, I don’t have an offensive type artifact of the same caliber as a holy relic…”
‘Then why the hell did you say anything?’
Colin’s eyebrow twitched but he didn’t voice his thoughts. Instead, he had already decided to refuse the trade in his mind.
Without this item, his main means of dealing with enemies would be significantly reduced.
But it was then that he saw The Light Chaser reach into thin air and pull out an old-looking triangular shield emblem, about the size of an adult’s palm, that clearly was no ordinary item.
What was more important was…
Colin caught site of the item’s name—gold!
[Shield of Fairness Adjudication]
Without more permissions being granted by the other party, Colin was only able to make out a faint golden name.
But that alone was enough to set his heart racing.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 346 - 346 344 The Golden Artifact Shield Badge of
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 346: Chapter 344: The Golden Artifact “Shield Badge of Fairness and Justice”!_1 Chapter 346: Chapter 344: The Golden Artifact “Shield Badge of Fairness and Justice”!_1 ‘Indeed, not only do I possess a Golden Artifact, but others also have them in their hands. However, it seems that in the eyes of “The Light Chaser,” he also thinks the Bone Spur is at least on par with golden items, right?’
Colin kept a calm exterior, but inside, he couldn’t help feeling a sense of camaraderie among heroes.
In front of him, “The Light Chaser” silently observed him, but unfortunately, ever since she used that flame to block, she hadn’t been able to discern any useful information.
At the same time, Colin spoke up, “Although the item isn’t exactly to my liking, considering the sincerity you’ve shown, I’m not unwilling to discuss it…”
Hearing his words, “The Light Chaser” breathed a sigh of relief. Being able to retrieve the item was good news. She nodded in agreement with Colin’s words.
Colin continued, “I believe you understand the value of Bone Spur as well.”
“Yes,” the blurry figure nodded earnestly.
Bone Spur came from a previous, now-deceased Saintess, and for the Church of Light, its significance, whether symbolic or otherwise, was indisputably of utmost importance.
‘This reaction… she seems not to be adept at negotiating,’ Colin’s eyes narrowed slightly. A normal person would try to minimize the value of Bone Spur at this point, throwing in something like how they don’t absolutely have to make the exchange…
But the other party simply nodded without saying anything else.
After thinking for a moment, Colin smoothly said, “Although the item is not bad, I still don’t know the specific effects. May I take a look at the detailed information on it first?”
Upon hearing this, the blurry figure cocked her head, seeming to ponder for a second or two, before handing the item over.
Such high-level items come with binding, and Colin couldn’t just snatch it away, as it wouldn’t fit into the Storage Room, and he wouldn’t even be able to use it without at least a verbal permission.
It was like if he were to drop a Golden Card on the ground, other employees who picked it up couldn’t use it either.
For items of this level, the company’s security measures are far more extensive than what they provide their employees.
There are only two ways to take it: trade or death.
However, Colin is an honorable man and never indulges in murder for gain.
Upon receiving the triangular Shield Emblem, he was eager inside, but he still put on a look of disdain—
The Shield Emblem depicted a clearly outlined scale with a sword as its fulcrum, feeling slightly heavy in hand, with a touch reminiscent of gold…
[Shield Badge of Fairness and Justice]
[Quality: Extremely Rare.]
[Status: Excellent (77% Integrity).]
[Energy Level: Class A.]
[Effect “Arena of Honor”: When you possess this Shield Emblem, you can choose any target within a kilometer radius that you can directly observe and drag them into the colosseum to launch a sacred duel!]
[How to Use: You can activate it by declaring to the target, for instance, “Under the witness of the ‘Shield Badge of Fairness and Justice,’ I hereby launch a fair and just duel.”]
[Basic Rules: The Shield Bearer can set three rules that comply with common sense and are fair and just, which both duelists must follow.]
[The effect can be used three times every 24 hours, with each battle lasting up to 7 hours. If the Shield Bearer survives until the end, the bearer will be deemed the victor.]
[The following are the specific effects of this artifact.]
[“Arena of Honor・Victor”: When the duelist emerges victorious, the enemy will be shackled automatically, becoming a slave whom you completely control.]
[“Arena of Honor・Vanquished”: When the Shield Bearer is defeated in battle, they will enter an Autistic Shutdown State and the Shield Badge cannot be activated for a period of seven days.]
[“Arena of Honor・Draw”: The Shield Bearer can end the duel (can only be used once every 24 hours).]
[Attention: When used in “World Code-13,” it can only be used once every 24 hours. Activating it more than once requires final confirmation, and overtime usage will summon an unpredictable, high-level contaminated being.]
[In such a case, according to the Bonfire Item Use Regulations, “Bonfire Camp” has the right to reclaim and process the artifact before the crisis ensues, and to a secondary extent rescue the user, followed by assessing accountability for impacts.]
[Note: Fight! Fight! A true man must fight!]
[Message from the creator “Mister Huang He”: I’ve never seen such a devious feature in my life, but great, now it’s mine…]
…
“Dragging someone into the colosseum to start a duel? This… is it just mediocre?”
Colin raised an eyebrow; the description was flamboyant, but it seemed of little significance.
To be honest, did such an item really deserve to be called golden?
Especially after seeing that last name, Colin’s expression involuntarily shifted—
“Mister Huang He”?
Isn’t that the name of a top social death expert at the company?
“A Purple Gear ‘The False Powerhouse’ almost brings on social death, so what if it’s golden? That’d be even worse, right?”
For a while, Colin suddenly didn’t want that crappy artifact anymore, even if it was golden.
He really had a psychological shadow over that “Mister Huang He”…
Never mind whether his creations were easy to use, the negative effects were ridiculously huge.
So far, Colin still had some trouble handling “The False Powerhouse”.
Compared to that, another creator “Kattu’s” card-based golden artifacts seemed much better—lesser negative effects, straightforward and brutally effective.
“Sorry, but this thing… I feel its effects might not be very satisfying. Do you have anything else?”
Colin handed the item back.
“Huh?” Shana, who had been preparing to see Colin nod and then planned to increase the points for bargaining depending on his reaction, was taken aback.
In her view, it was highly likely that he would choose this item, although there might be some hesitation because it wasn’t an offensive type of artifact, he would definitely act on it.
Then, she would gradually throw in points as bargaining chips, a hundred points, two hundred points, three hundred points…
In the end, she would add up to five hundred points at most. A similar high-quality item plus a large amount of Bonfire Points, and Colin would surely agree!
But unexpectedly, the negotiation failed at the very first step?
And now, the only item she had that could rival a Holy Relic was this one…
If she didn’t have this item as a foundation, then the points would be meaningless too, unless she could come up with a number that would make it impossible for him to refuse, like ten thousand points!
But that was obviously not going to happen…
She wouldn’t have that much if she added up all the points she had earned over the years…
Somehow at a loss, Shana didn’t know what to say as she took back the artifact.
“Seems like you only have this one item?”
As he spoke, Colin took out a bottle of alcohol and squeezed some onto his hands for disinfection—
Having touched an item made by that guy, he felt somewhat unlucky and needed to be cautious.
Lest he get afflicted with some bizarre negative effect.
“I…” The vague silhouette hesitated in his speech.
Seeing his hesitance, Colin pursed his lips, feeling like the trade was likely off the table.
However, just then, Shana suddenly thought of something.
‘Is he dissatisfied with the introduction, so he refuses to trade?’
The Saintess had a flash of spiritual intuition; she could see the information on the artifact too, but what it was, she couldn’t fully understand, because it was all in some unfamiliar script.
And this script could shield against any mystical method to crack it…
However, through her own spiritual intuition, she could guess it was some sort of introduction to the item.
Just now, having noticed that he could understand it, she hadn’t introduced the artifact.
“May I demonstrate its effect once, and then you can decide?”
Hearing the persistent request from the vague figure, Colin thought for a moment and nodded, “Alright, go ahead and try.”
Although the description wasn’t promising, he was curious about how exactly the golden artifact operated.
And since the user was her this time, he didn’t have to worry about being affected by any weird negative effects that could lead to his social death…
No sooner had he spoken, he saw “The Light Chaser” raise the artifact and aim it at him.
The next second, Colin’s heart suddenly skipped a beat.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 347 - 347 345 Am I Really Going to Become a Slave_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 347: Chapter 345 Am I Really Going to Become a Slave?_1 Chapter 347: Chapter 345 Am I Really Going to Become a Slave?_1 “I don’t think I’m quite ready…”
Colin’s pupils constricted, realizing in that moment that he was seemingly about to foolishly attempt to withstand an artifact of the Golden Level!
But before he could call for a pause, the surrounding scene began to change abruptly…
And the blurred figure of light before him issued a declaration of battle:
“Under the witness of the ‘Shield of Fairness Adjudication,’ I hereby initiate a sacred duel with the person before me!”
This sentence was not short.
However, as soon as the voice began the word “I,” Colin felt everything around him stretching away, and by the time the last word dropped, they were already in what seemed like a boundless and massive spatial domain.
And that blur of light was now around thirty meters from him…
Intuition told Colin that if he didn’t defeat this figure, even with two Golden Cards in hand, he would not be able to force an exit.
The feeling of being violently stripped from the real world and thrust into the colosseum stirred an intense unease within him…
Thinking this, he turned his gaze toward the vague silhouette nearby, his eyes narrowing, flames surging about him as he charged up, contemplating whether to take this person down right now.
Otherwise, if he really allowed the opponent to establish three rules, even if those were truly fair and just, he’d be finished if he couldn’t win.
Colin hadn’t forgotten what was written on that artifact…
For someone like him, a non-artifact holder, losing meant becoming a slave!
Then he would be at the mercy of the other, unable to resist however he might be tormented…
Yet, though he harbored these thoughts, he didn’t dare to make a move; his instincts warned him that acting might bring some inexplicable consequences…
They wouldn’t be fatal, but very troublesome.
At this moment, the blurry figure of light thirty meters ahead seemed to see right through his thoughts.
“You may try to attack me now with a standard assault…”
There couldn’t be a trap, could there?
Hearing these words, Colin couldn’t help but ponder for a few seconds but decided to give it a try. Pulling out the “Revolver Contrarian,” he aimed at the shadow’s chest and pulled the trigger.
Bang!
The flash of flame in an instant, a bullet wrapped in fire shot out.
Logically, at a distance of thirty meters, it would take very little time to hit the target.
Yet, halfway there, the bullet mysteriously vanished into thin air.
And at the same time…
“Snap!”
A sound of a whip cracking echoed from behind Colin.
His whole body shuddered, a searing pain like broken bones swept through him, even feeling his attributes decrease.
This temporary decrease might have reached twenty percent!
‘Damn, that’s a steep price. Even if I broke a pinky, my level wouldn’t drop by that much…’
Colin thought in shock.
“Next time, it will be three lashes!”
A ghostly whisper crept into Colin’s ears, as if cautioning him of the consequences of another mistake.
‘One lash costing me twenty percent of my strength, three lashes would be unbearable…’
Colin drew a deep breath, resisting the urge to panic.
Especially wicked was the power at play—if one didn’t know and was rather hotheaded or skeptical, they’d likely end up in a really bad spot.
Meanwhile, a voice came from ahead:
“Before the duel rules are set and officially commenced, any form of attack is not allowed. Even if one bears Divine status, such attacks cannot be ignored. Once warnings exceed three times, the ‘Death Judgment’ will be enacted, and even if it’s not fatal, a substantial price will be paid.
“At least within the Domain of the Demigods, no one can break out of the colosseum through brute force.”
Shana seriously introduced the value of the item to the other party, hoping to make them change their mind.
After all, the Holy Relic was indeed very important to her as well as to the Church.
“Instructive.”
Colin nodded slightly, while becoming increasingly worried that “The Light Chaser” might seize the opportunity to strike.
If he really got captured as a slave, it wouldn’t be a laughing matter.
“The remaining rules that seem more troublesome are those three, right? If they all require both parties to confirm ‘fairness and justice,’ then it shouldn’t be much of a problem…”
However, before he could continue to ponder, Colin saw the other party continuing to speak.
“In this sacred duel, I swear that we will adhere to three completely fair rules…”
“First, I promise that in this battle, I will forgo the use of any ‘items’ with mystical effects. In the interest of fairness, my opponent will also be unable to use any ‘items’.”
Upon hearing the first rule, Colin’s face involuntarily changed—
Not use “items”?
Without “items,” facing “The Light Chaser,” a strong opponent blessed with Divine Status, he would have no chance of resisting, and even if the opponent wasn’t actually adept at combat, they could easily mount him and lay their hands on him.
Clearly, in Colin’s view, this didn’t count as “fairness and justice” at all.
Yet, some vague response echoed in the area, and the rule was set.
“Damn it, what kind of fairness and justice is this?”
When Colin read the description before, he thought this kind of “fairness and justice” required agreement from both parties.
He never anticipated that it was one-sided!
The bland description in the brief and his previous prejudice against “Boss Huang He” gave him a less than favorable impression of the item.
But only at this moment did he realize what this so-called “fairness” really meant…
Just as Colin’s thoughts boiled over, the “The Light Chaser” in front of him didn’t pause either, continuing to state the subsequent rules.
“Second, I promise that in this battle, I will not use ranged attacks as my primary mode of combat. In the interest of fairness, my opponent also cannot use ranged attacks as their main method of attack.”
“Third, I promise that in this battle, I will not retreat more than three times to avoid combat. In the interest of fairness, my opponent also cannot engage in the act of retreating more than three times.”
…
“Damn… I’ve never seen such a despicable ability in my life.”
Colin couldn’t help but express a sentiment similar to “Boss Huang He’s” initial one.
The more he listened to the rules, the more he felt a tingling in his heart, wondering whether he should acknowledge that this thing indeed came from the machinations of “Boss Huang He”—the item’s effect was undoubtedly unquestionable.
With these three “fair and just” rules out, he felt as if he had been completely paralyzed.
But soon…
Colin suddenly noticed something, the first rule seemed not to have taken full effect?
Looking at the “Revolver Contrarian” in his hand that was still emitting flames.
He was certain that although the Bone Spur and his items below the purple level seemed no longer usable, the two Golden Cards and the “Revolver Contrarian,” an orange-tier item, as well as purple items, were still usable?
On the other side, “The Light Chaser” also noticed this, seeing that the weapon in the man’s hand across from him was still emitting flames, indicating that it was likely still in a usable state.
But the opponent hadn’t received any punishment, which seemed to conflict with the first rule, right?
Yet…
Shana checked her status and found that among her items, it seemed that aside from those issued by Parchment, all other unexplained items sourced from different means were now unusable.
However, soon, through her connection with the item, she received an “Inspiration” from the will within the “Shield of Fairness Adjudication,” understanding the reason for this situation.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 348 - 348 346 Attempting a Counter-kill_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 348: Chapter 346: Attempting a Counter-kill!_1 Chapter 348: Chapter 346: Attempting a Counter-kill!_1 “Unable to fully restrict the items from ‘Bonfire Campsite,’ only a few can be specified for restriction, and even then, those of higher quality than that orange named weapon can at best be limited, not prohibited? Is the current situation due to default restrictions on some lower-level items, since none was specified up front?”
Shana quickly dismantled “Inspiration,” roughly grasping the situation.
This was indeed her first encounter with such circumstances, as it was also her first battle with a parchment holder.
“It seems it can’t fully control the artifacts from ‘Bonfire Campsite’…”
She didn’t hide the information she had obtained.
“So that’s how it is, huh…”
Colin could only marvel internally at whether it was impressive or the company behind it even more so…
Of course, even if the “Shield of Fairness and Justice” was at a disadvantage with internal artifacts, its effect was undeniably powerful.
“But now that the introduction to this item is complete, why hasn’t it been lifted?”
Colin couldn’t help but worry.
Looking at the blurred silhouette of light ahead, he began to fret, what if…
What if the opponent doesn’t release the ‘Arena of Honor’?
Thinking from the perspective of ‘The Light Chaser,’ it would make more sense to simply steal rather than exchange a Bone Spur at a tremendous cost.
Even though Colin habitually suspected the worst of human nature…
But putting himself in their shoes, Colin felt that even his own sterling morality was tempted, not to mention the other party—
“If it really comes down to it, losing the Bone Spur isn’t the end of the world, but now… what if they actually take me as a slave?”
He would have been reluctant to give up the Bone Spur before, but now, not only might he lose the Bone Spur, but he could even be captured and enslaved, so losing just the Bone Spur seemed acceptable.
It was at this moment he heard the blurred figure of light speak again, “‘Bonfire’ Agent Sir, this is the first time I’ve encountered another holder of ‘parchment.’ May I make a small request?”
“What request?”
Colin asked tensely.
“Would you like to try fighting a battle? Of course, rest assured, regardless of the outcome, I will release the ‘Arena of Honor,’ and moreover, I will use matching strength in combat,” Shana invited the man in front of her.
She was very curious about the strength of another chosen by the “parchment.”
As she spoke, Colin saw the divine aura dissipate from the blurred figure like evaporating vapor.
While still strong, it was now at a level where a counterkill was possible!
Seeing this, Colin’s confidence returned once more: “Alright, alright! Bring on the fight!”
The opponent had overwhelmed him with superior power before, making him unwilling to accept it, but now they were on equal footing.
Then, don’t blame him for not holding back!
On equal terms, Colin had never been afraid of anyone; he felt he could already write victory across his face!
He was determined to teach that oblivious fool a lesson!
“My fighting style might be a bit brutal, and I could accidentally hurt you,” Colin reminded, maintaining the martial spirit.
“No problem, you go ahead with all your techniques, don’t hold back on me…”
Quickly, as his voice fell, blinding pale light and terrifyingly intense heat burst forth simultaneously within the ‘Arena of Honor’!
Horrific vibrations occurred in the arena, one after another.
Presence diminished, “Firebearer” grease, “Time Stop,” repulsion, “Beastial Power”…
Colin threw everything he had at the enemy with a charge.
Finally…
After three minutes.
The ‘Arena of Honor’s’ effect was lifted.
It was a stalemate.
The surroundings returned to their original state.
“Phew, that was close…”
Colin looked seemingly unscathed as he stood in place, taking a glance around and let out a sigh of relief.
This “Light Chaser” had actually managed to make good on his word; regardless of the outcome, he had granted a draw.
Moreover, the radiance of the “Light Chaser” dimmed a bit, becoming somewhat transparent.
“Can we consider it now?” the blurred silhouette asked, holding the triangular shield emblem and directing the question at Colin.
“Indeed, it’s not bad.”
Colin nodded, acknowledging its effect, and showed an intention to acquire it for himself.
“But…”
“Ah?” The sudden shift caught the “Light Chaser” off guard.
“I have a task coming up for which I might really need this Bone Spur, so perhaps we can postpone the transaction for a period of time.”
Colin thought for a moment and realized this “Light Chaser” seemed much more agreeable than he had expected, giving off an unexpectedly honest impression.
Inside here…
There was room for bluffing, no, for maneuvering!
Without waiting for the other party to speak, Colin continued, “Also, although I’ve experienced this item once, it’s hard to say how well it works in various situations.
“So, if it’s possible, I’d like to borrow it for a few days in advance to try it out…
“Let’s be reasonable, you wouldn’t want me to accidentally die in an anomaly just because I suddenly switched my main weapon, would you?”
Hearing this, the blurred silhouette pondered for a moment, found the point fairly reasonable, and nodded. If suddenly taking away the holy relic led to an accident for the other party, that was something she didn’t wish to see:
“It seems… that makes sense…”
Seizing the moment, Colin struck while the iron was hot, “But don’t worry, I won’t freeload off you. I’ll offer some points as compensation.”
Points as compensation?
Shana couldn’t help but feel amused, as she had intended to say that she actually didn’t need points.
She had saved quite a sum of points for this very transaction!
But then, she quickly heard…
“How about this, we’ll go with your normal rate from before, three thousand points for one week. I’ll test it for a week.”
“Three, three thousand points?!” Shana was stunned, wondering if she had misheard.
Too little?
When Colin heard her reaction, he subconsciously felt that she must think it was too little.
After all, this was a golden artifact; even though a few thousand points was just for a few days’ rent, the effect was completely worth it!
“Then, let’s say five thousand points. I have a task coming up and I’ll give it a real trial. If it’s really good, we can discuss it then,” Colin proposed sincerely.
“Five… thousand points?” Shana was utterly dazed.
The amount of points made her feel somewhat unreal, suspecting that he was just throwing out numbers as a joke.
She was about to suggest letting him have it for fifty points.
But before she could speak, a message popped up on her retina.
[Special Task: Lend the “Shield of Fairness and Justice” as a temporary item to “654321” for seven days.]
“Notice”: “654321” has agreed and paid the full amount of points, awaiting your final confirmation.
“Remark”: After seven days, the item will be automatically retrieved.
…
Upon seeing the message, Shana, who was sitting on the ground on the other side, gnawing at her stiff and sour black bread with a “crack” sound, couldn’t help but jump up on the spot. Holding the black bread like a hamster, her eyes bulged in shock —
Five thousand points! This was actually for real?!
…

chapters.title: Chapter 349 - 349 347 The Saintess is Greatly Shocked_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 349: Chapter 347 The Saintess is Greatly Shocked_1 Chapter 349: Chapter 347 The Saintess is Greatly Shocked_1 “Really, truly just bringing the five thousand points, just, just, just to exchange for its seven days of usage rights?”
Shana stood up straight, her lips slightly parted, her eyes wide open, her ice-blue pure eyes filled with an undeniable shock.
According to the task “hint,” the other party had already given out the points!
Shana looked over the content of the task again to confirm it wasn’t fifty or five hundred but five thousand!
This…
This simply made no sense!
And both the task and her intuition were telling her that as long as she agreed, she could immediately get her hands on this massive sum of money that she had never seen before in her lifetime!
“Not even the legacy left by the previous Saint Heir and Saintess amounted to that much.”
The Saintess murmured to herself, her face still somewhat distant.
She remembered, when she first got the parchment, it still had some of the predecessors’ legacy on it.
These were the various tasks the predecessors completed, saving up as much as possible to leave for those who came after them.
But all together, it was barely under three thousand…
It was only about half of what this seemingly ordinary and completely safe task offered.
Even for herself, after striving for ten or eight years and adding up all that she had used, it barely amounted to just over ten thousand, yet this very ordinary task was equal to half of her entire Saint career’s efforts…
This stark, blunt comparison caused her usually swift thinking to come to a halt.
Snap.
The sour and stiff black bread involuntarily fell to the ground.
Shaking her head, Shana came back to her senses from the shock, bent down gently, picked up the black bread, wiped off the dust on it with a piece of clean cloth, then stored it in the Storage Room before looking at the parchment task again.
“There couldn’t be… something wrong with it, right?”
Shana wore a doubtful expression.
The payment for this task was completely disproportionate to what was being offered.
In the past, the largest income she received from a task was two years ago when she entered an unknown world and hunted a part of a special intangible rule-based Ancient God creature.
In that battle, she had to face attacks from multiple mythical creatures and fight with the main enemy.
She eventually succeeded, but she also sustained severe injuries, nearly spending a month lying in bed resting.
And the income from that was…
800 points.
Shana remembered coughing up blood every day but still being very happy because it nearly caught up to what she could earn in a year.
And this time, merely lending something out for seven days could earn her such an amount.
To her, it was simply incomprehensible.
However, with the guarantee of the parchment, she knew this was very likely real…
But after confirming that both the parchment and her own judgment were correct, Shana began to wonder if the “Bonfire” agent’s brain and sanity might have issues?
‘If he made such a decision due to some temporary problem with his brain, wouldn’t it be… somewhat unethical for me to take advantage of it?’
What if this was all he managed to save over a lifetime, and in a moment of irrationality, he traded it away, might he suffer a mental breakdown after “sobering up”?
Shana gradually calmed down.
This act of taking advantage of someone whose wisdom might be momentarily weaker than normal didn’t seem quite right…
But… from that first glance observation earlier, his mind seemed to be functioning normally, didn’t it?
Could it be that during the battle just now, she accidentally hit too hard and caused his brain to malfunction?
While she thought this, the large sum of points still greatly tempted her.
If she could get her hands on this fortune, she would have the chance to save even more people.
At this moment, as Shana hesitated, a voice came from the side:
“Your Highness, what’s the matter?”
Shana turned to look back and saw a woman with blue short hair dressed in female armor.
This was her current First Knight, Helena’s sister, Dianas.
“I’m fine…”
Shana said, then seemed to think of something. She patted a stone beside her, signaling for the other to come sit and began,
“Dianas, would you… If you met a friendly but irrational person, who had something you wanted, would you try to take advantage of their irrational state to acquire that necessary item?”
What kind of bizarre question was this? It was almost as strange as the previous one about whether to save many or save few with a single slap…
Unable to help it, Dianas murmured in her heart. She detested these kinds of brain teasers the most.
While pondering, Dianas glanced at Shana.
On the surface, Shana undoubtedly appeared saintly and beautiful, clad in simple yet elegant white with golden edges. Her pale golden hair was coiled behind her head, surrounded by a holy light, her demeanor gentle. Just sitting there, she seemed like a beautiful painting crafted by a divine hand.
However, upon closer inspection, beneath this superficial gleam, lay an extremely gaunt girl who was still beautiful, but with scarcely any flesh on her face, and pale skin that seemed stretched over bones—
If she were any thinner, she could be described as a skeleton blessed by the holy light.
Dianas remembered that ever since Shana had entered the disaster area over half a year ago, she had scarcely eaten anything.
To the point that, at this moment, the saint herself looked so emaciated that it was disconcerting.
No matter how frail and weak her body was, her eyes shone as bright as ever, flickering with the same pure and kind aura that had made people involuntarily revere her at first sight.
It was only now, nearly able to leave this hazardous area and seeing that there was surplus, that the saint began to eat a bit.
Yet, for some unknown reason, she saw the saintess’s light flicker, standing there confused, even forgetting to maintain her facade, seemingly witnessing something incredibly shocking.
Worried, Dianas approached.
“Dianas?” Seeing her silent, Shana spoke up.
“Ah… Regarding your question…”
Dianas tried her best to exercise her mind, aiming to provide a sensible explanation.
After a while, Colin, who was far on the other side, finally received a response.
“Decide whether to agree to the trade after three days if nothing changes?”
Colin watched ‘The Light Chaser’ fade away, his ‘Shield of Fairness Adjudication’ taken by another, confused in his heart.
He felt that ‘The Light Chaser’ must have agreed, but the agreement wasn’t very decisive.
There might be variables.
However, the other party didn’t mention the Bone Spur this time…
‘Could it be that the points offered were too low?’ Colin wondered if it was possible. The right to use a powerful Golden Artifact could be employed to take the enemy’s head in a multitude of armies. And his next promotion task involved those former D Level employees from the ‘Ghost Train.’
If unlucky, he might even encounter that C Level.
With this item, perhaps he could overcome each one and avoid a lot of trouble…
So, to say 5000 points— even 10000 points wouldn’t be unacceptable.
Initially, Colin started with 3000 points, merely wanting to leave room for bargaining, but unexpectedly, just as the negotiation reached half the psychological expectation, the “seller” suddenly went “offline” due to a network interruption.
They waited quite some time to reconnect, only to say that the trade would proceed after three days.
Colin raised his hand, looking at the bonfire burning beside him, stroked his chin, “Does this imply that the points I’m offering now are too low and he’s not satisfied? Suggesting I should figure it out?”
Of course, Colin, who was considering how to appropriately raise his offer, couldn’t possibly imagine at that moment; his upfront offering of five thousand points had dramatically shocked ‘The Light Chaser’, who was now suspecting him of being a fool…
So much so that he needed to leave three days open to properly calm down.
.
.
.
Chapter two will be posted later.

chapters.title: Chapter 350 - 350 348 High Handling Fees. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 350: Chapter 348: High Handling Fees. _1 Chapter 350: Chapter 348: High Handling Fees. _1 Three days slowly passed…
During these days, Colin busied himself, following the Bonfire’s instructions, re-accepting scattered refugees around and finally managed to stabilize the situation once more…
The only thing that gave him headaches was that sometimes, when he rested, he would dream of a fist hammering down.
Directly waking him from his dreams.
Anxiety started to form a shadow in his heart…
However, once the three days had passed, and the time for the trade came once again.
Colin casually stuffed a creamy white rabbit candy and a copy of One Lesson Three Practices into Little Red’s hand, sending her off to play by herself before secretly entering the church to meet with “The Light Chaser”.
Not long after, as that blurry shadow appeared once again, the suspended transaction resumed.
Just as Colin was about to open his mouth to raise the offer from five thousand points to seven thousand, and then consider raising it to ten thousand depending on the conversation,
once Shana confirmed that Colin wasn’t just being whimsical, and that there was nothing wrong with his mind, she agreed to the deal first.
“No increase in price? You’re really being generous this time?”
Inside, Colin was astounded. At that moment, he suddenly realized that perhaps he was the one with impure thoughts.
“The Light Chaser”, like himself, was not short on points. The three days’ delay was certainly not about driving up the price as he had thought.
As two slightly different notifications appeared on each of their retinas, Colin and “The Light Chaser”, having acquired from each other what they needed, both couldn’t help but breathe out in relief.
…
“I really got it, five thousand points…”
Shana bit her lip, widened her eyes, and checked her savings, seeing that 5013.68 – an amount she wouldn’t have dared to even dream of before – made her heart race uncontrollably.
But soon, she noticed something was off…
“5013.68 points?”
Shana counted quietly to herself, and normally, she should have 5513.68 points.
Why was there five hundred less?
In confusion, she opened her mission log and quickly found the issue.
[You have received “Bonfire Points 5000”, which has been transferred to your “Storage Room (10% transaction fee deducted)”.]
“…So, just like that, five hundred are gone?”
Shana opened her mouth in shock, feeling a deep sense of loss.
She thought she would get the full five thousand points! She hadn’t expected to lose a whopping five hundred points to the parchment before she even got them in her hands…
However, it was only after her first transaction that she learned that the parchment would deduct fees like this.
“But I wonder if it deducts for regular missions too…”
It seemed like the parchment would indicate if it was skimming something off the top to let her know…
So… maybe it didn’t?
After pondering for a moment, Shana wasn’t entirely sure, but if normal missions also took a tax of only ten percent, it seemed acceptable to her.
The eighty points she got from the last aid mission, after doing the math, were just eight…
Although it also seemed a lot to her, it was nothing compared to the sting of losing five hundred.
But then, she remembered something the “Agent of the Bonfire” might have said before, about using her regular rate?
What was her regular rate…?
Just as this thought barely surfaced, before she could delve further, a mission notification appeared.
[The mission “Save More Sufferers” has been issued!]
This mission reminded her of her original intent.
“No, no Shana, you can’t get hung up on this any longer. I’m not after points for their own sake; they’re just a means to an end. Now, with five thousand points in hand, that’s plenty, and it’s time to focus on the important things. There are still many people in despair, waiting for rescue…”
Taking a deep breath, Shana collected her emotions.
Having over five thousand points meant she could now return to the depths of the Catastrophe of the Magic Fog and lead out another large group of people!
The main reason she had only saved so many people to date was that her points couldn’t support it; she couldn’t afford enough food and had to make the hard choice to abandon some places.
But now…
Shana clenched her fists——she wanted them all!
…
“Finally got it.”
Clutching the triangular shield emblem in his hand, Colin also breathed a sigh of relief, which meant he had another important trump card for his upcoming mission.
As for the five thousand points spent, it was almost painless to him, hardly stirring any emotion.
Even for many company employees, it was not an amount they couldn’t scrounge up if they gritted their teeth.
And for someone like “The Light Chaser” who only did support missions, entering without doing anything and just selling BUFF effects to earn over ten thousand, in Colin’s view, they must lead a plain, unadorned, and dull life similar to his own, not lacking points.
It could be said that, in his opinion, those five thousand points were probably not the decisive factor for the transaction’s success.
It was just a small bonus…
More importantly, it was his sincerity that had moved the other party and facilitated the success of the trade.
Otherwise, lending out such an item for five thousand points was practically no different from charity.
For Colin himself, putting himself in their shoes, if someone said they would exchange seven days of usage rights for his Golden Card for five thousand points, he would definitely be unwilling, would reject the offer without even thinking about it.
Who knows what kind of incredible missions might pop up during those seven days.
“From this perspective, although ‘The Light Chaser’ is a bit greedy for money, he’s still a decent person, not one of those with an insatiable greed.”
Colin glanced down at a golden ornament that had arrived along with the “Shield of Fairness Adjudication” in his hand.
A pure gold ornament, weighed probably a bit over one hundred grams.
This was a gift just now from “The Light Chaser,” said to be a one-use item that, once activated, could grant a very powerful BUFF effect.
Even without using it, simply possessing it would confer some blessings…
For instance, Colin now felt that his brain was operating with unprecedented clarity and swiftness.
It was as if an i3 processor had suddenly been updated to an i5.
A 1060 graphics card had become a 2060.
…
His whole body felt rejuvenated.
And this was one of the effects “The Light Chaser” had mentioned to him, his brain would receive targeted enhancement…
Colin was very satisfied with the effect.
It’s just that he didn’t know whether he was overthinking, but he always felt that when the other person left, their look, tone, and demeanor seemed a bit strange, a bit complex, hard to describe—
But if he had to say, it seemed to have a touch of “caring for the intellectually challenged”?
“Forget it, I’m probably overthinking it.”
Colin pursed his lips, this transaction had changed his view of “The Light Chaser” quite a bit, feeling that, if he encounters The Light Chaser’s real body, he might consider not hitting his face when it comes “time for revenge.”
“So far, this ‘Descent Project’ has landed smoothly, not encountering any problems; the only possible disaster lies a few days ahead with the ‘Promotion Mission’…”
Colin thought for a moment, once tomorrow’s time arrived, he would be able to go back to participate in the promotion mission.
Currently, during this period, after interacting with some company colleagues, he was pretty confident that, given his circumstances, he most likely wouldn’t be assigned any ordinary tasks…
Just like a company hiring or emphasizing the training of an employee with an ultra-high salary, they are certainly not doing so for the employee to slack off and mop floors.
A stronger employee would be given tasks that are a bit more complex than others.
Even if a seemingly ordinary task comes their way, if it can be speedrun normally, the company would most likely pull some tricks, letting him experience the “protagonist’s fate”…
But overall, except for those out-of-control types, one is generally not sent to do completely uninspiring tasks.
“Mr. Colin, are you leaving again?” Little Red’s voice suddenly came.
“Yeah.”
Colin habitually ruffled her hair: “Did you finish your homework?”
“Finished, so… will you come the day after tomorrow?” Little Red asked softly.
Seeing her reluctantly parting, Colin smiled and shook his head: “Don’t worry, nothing should come up this time. Alright, now that your homework is finished, let’s go out and take a turn, there’s quite a lot happening outside…”
“Okay.” Little Red blinked.
He had prepared quite a lot for his territory this time; even if something unexpected happened, it would be enough to deal with disasters similar to last time’s catastrophe with magical creatures.
As the “Descent Return Time” finished its last second.
The ancient and distant sound of a bell rang out.
Colin and the others returned to reality once more…
Then, regaining his senses, he quickly discovered that a group of people on parchment were constantly @’ing him.

chapters.title: Chapter 351 - 351 349 Boiling Inside the Company_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 351: Chapter 349 Boiling Inside the Company_1 Chapter 351: Chapter 349 Boiling Inside the Company_1 “Arsonist, Seek Pig, Dog Brother?”
Colin glanced at the IDs of these people and realized they were from the last batch of the mission.
He quickly skimmed through their messages and grasped the reason why this group had @ him.
It’s related to “World Code -4″…
“This time the time seems to have been corrected, the same as me—entered at noon and returned to the real world at three o’clock. There was no situation like last time… Has the timeline been corrected?”
Sitting on the bed, Colin stroked his chin.
For this situation, he wasn’t very surprised. At present, it seems that the times in each “World Code” should be equivalent.
However, this group didn’t run into any setbacks in the Deep Sea World this time; they just carried out some scattered regular exploration tasks…
With the assistance of the local species, “Sea Siren,” there wasn’t much of a problem.
As for those more powerful beings, they probably won’t come up to make trouble again in the short term…
After all, the previous time Colin went there, those beings reacted because they were worried that he’d come up and directly press the “nuclear button”…
Now the misunderstanding can’t be said to be resolved, but as long as he doesn’t destroy the world, the higher beings probably won’t continue to kick up a fuss.
Although everyone still doesn’t get along with each other, if they can just get by without interfering with one another, life can go on.
“I didn’t expect that an Evil God would also have a day to protect the world…”
Having thoroughly sorted through the logic, Colin still felt somewhat peculiar in his heart.
“The matter with ‘Corps’ seems to be unresolved still, and I have no idea what those people were doing by entering ‘World Code -4.’ Could it be they want to use it as a stepping stone to enter the first three worlds?”
Colin had some speculations; after all, it seems that the company still places much importance on the matter with the former employee, Rosen.
And within “World Code,” there had been a death of a big shot from Bonfire Company.
Apparently, the former employee died while carrying out the task to recover his leftover affairs; however, the specific details of the task were not disclosed.
“Just don’t know what level a company member crowned as a big shot by ‘Bonfire Company’ could be at.”
He felt it should be an existence capable of going head-to-head with a complete Level Zero lifeform.
As for whether this kind of “big shot” is human or not, it’s hard to say…
Shaking his head, he looked again and noticed, besides these matters, this group kept asking when he would next go to “World Code -4.” Although they hadn’t faced any crises this trip, Tina tormented them so much that they were all a bit neurotic.
That little “Sea Siren” appeared from the most unexpected places almost every minute.
Asking the Arsonist and others incessantly when he would come…
Not just her, many mermaids would ask, only Tina was the most fanatical.
“Going to ‘World Code -4,’ huh…”
Colin tilted his head and pondered for a moment, feeling he likely didn’t have any time for the short term.
Then, without further thought, he checked the mission settlement…
Counting the guaranteed one thousand points from “Lady Bunny,” the total settlement was just a plain seven thousand-plus points.
However, Colin wasn’t interested in points.
“Two Gold Mission Vouchers, not bad. I now have nine Gold Mission Vouchers, and to buy one dose of D Level Gene Compensation Medicine, it only takes 3 vouchers plus 1800 points…”
Touching his chin, Colin pondered and calculated his future plans.
Currently, he already had one dose of D Level Gene Compensation Medicine from a previous mission.
That is to say, as long as the next mission goes smoothly, he could become a Late Stage D Level by doing nothing and using the medicine at home every week…
And then, getting seven more Gold Mission Vouchers, plus the remaining three, to exchange for ten “Freely Discretionary Points” from the Gene Compensation Panel would make him a D Level at full circle!
After that, it would be C Level…
“This, ‘Lady Bunny’ had said before, if I successfully investigate the ‘Book of Fate’s’ status and complete the ‘undercover’ mission smoothly, I would get her personal assistance. Judging by her tone, it doesn’t seem difficult?”
Colin sat cross-legged on the bed, touching his chin.
Although his current “undercover” life was a little bit different from what he had thought.
It felt like everyone in the world seemed to know he was undercover…
But it wasn’t a big issue, the company usually cares about the result and isn’t too concerned about whether or not he’s been discovered.
“Putting that aside, even if I could hide well, it wouldn’t matter.”
After roughly sorting out the current situation, Colin again opened the chat channel inside the Parchment to take a look.
It wasn’t much different from when he checked before entering in the morning…
