Those asking for help were still asking, the ones doing science popularization were still at it, those selling equipment kept selling, those asking offline daily reality were still seeking that, and with the influx of a bunch of newcomers, the inner chat was still a scene full of vibrant and burgeoning life.
“It’s just that the conflict between new and former employees seems to have intensified a bit…”
Colin lurked quietly, his gaze sweeping across the stream of messages.
Because there were too many people working, task distribution was uneven, and many former employees averaged 0.5 tasks in the last two weeks, with monthly points income not exceeding 300, further widening the wealth gap.
Without points, they couldn’t buy the things they wanted.
Their promotion speed had slowed significantly…
So much so that many former employees had to leave their homes, they had stayed in for over a hundred and eighty years, to go to other smaller cities or even directly to some remote countries to look for tasks, and then bitterly criticized the new employees for lacking martial ethics, turning the situation too competitive and so forth.
The previously niche “Emperor of Labor Invasion” incidents or “King Virus” sayings are now aired openly…
“Who exactly is doing these tasks?”
“Three weeks, it’s been three whole weeks, and I haven’t gotten a new task, I can’t even get a regular task…”
“Now, who is really doing the tasks?”
“How come so many people pop up all of a sudden, what’s going on?”
“These people, one, don’t bubble up, two, don’t show off equipment, three, don’t share mission experiences, what kind of people are these?”
“Every day, just snatching tasks…”
“In the past, when you were idle, you could still apply for extra tasks on your own. Now all the orders have been snatched, what are these newly arrived doing, just doing tasks all day?”
“It was fine that there were fewer regular tasks, but even the tasks on the ‘Task Board’ for voluntary application have been snatched…”
“Are these tasks something you newbies can complete?”
“Not only did they complete them, they completed them so quickly it’s alarming. Are they still newbies? What’s the situation? Not even robots can work like these guys…”
“It’s like this now, won’t the company take care of it? If we can’t grow up, who’s going to be responsible when the world is destroyed?”
“Company, company, come out and say something!”
“…”
.
.
.
Update first, cover later. Wait for the second chapter.

chapters.title: Chapter 352 - 352 350 Information on the Ghost Train._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 352: Chapter 350 Information on the “Ghost Train”._1 Chapter 352: Chapter 350 Information on the “Ghost Train”._1 ‘This move must be the official intervention to spin private workers to death, right?’
Seeing the old employees’ breakdown quotes, Colin couldn’t help but laugh and cry inside, not knowing whether to say it was very interesting or what.
It was apparent that this wave had a significant impact on the employees who used to slack off at work.
Colin remembered that before the official intervention, when there were three routine tasks in a week, they complained; now with one task every three weeks, they still complained…
However, currently, although the “spin” was still mainly concentrated at F Level, those at E Level and even D Level had started to take action.
They were no longer like what Colin saw when he first joined: idling around all day either bragging or trash-talking.
Now, everyone was afraid that this group of “spin virus” kings would finish spinning up F Level and then move up, leaving no tasks for the rest.
“All the world’s officials stepping in to rectify the bad work habits of slacking off?”
Colin found it amusing, but it was indeed somewhat unfair…
Officials took the addition of new company employees very seriously; often, even F Level newbies could get protection from Level 5 and Level 6 powerhouses.
Some with special circumstances could even get direct help from Level 7 or even higher-level official personnel.
General employees simply couldn’t compete with them head-on…
“If I remember correctly, for most of the F Level tasks, bringing in a Level 6 could already wreak havoc. At E Level, another one or two Level 6s could solve most situations. If that doesn’t work, they’d pull in higher-ups. With basically unlimited human resources, geez, it does look like they’re spinning out of control. With this number of tasks, I guess it won’t take long for E Level to get busy too…”
However, even though the company atmosphere had changed, Colin wasn’t worried at all.
The pile of random events he was dealing with was headache-inducing enough…
Then, his gaze swept over those messages calling for the “company” to step in, he could only say they probably didn’t understand the situation.
This wave was obviously beneficial for the company—they’d be a ghost to take a stand…
Of course, not everyone was worrying about something; some people hoped for fiercer competition…
For instance, “The Unyielding” was quite looking forward to these “spin kings” advancing to F Level tasks so that they might rescue him from a neverending stay in the hospital.
Shaking his head, Colin decided not to keep looking and opened the internal chat group for the E Level Promotion Quest.
Perhaps influenced by the “spin kings”, a good number of people stopped slacking off and resolutely started their Charge towards D Level…
There were seven or eight more people in the group.
However, the teams looking for members were still mainly the same few…
And what they were missing was still “healers”, that is, those skilled in support and healing measures.
Naturally, if someone had a purple-named item with healing effects, they would be recruited without hesitation.
“The people moving up now mostly come from individual tasks; how many of them could have mastered healing methods?”
Colin pursed his lips, but it wasn’t a major issue; he happened to have some mastery.
The “Gluttony Power Mark”, although only green-named, could still be of some use.
Plus, with the help of things like “Nano Intellectual Mechanism” in healing…
Colin suddenly realized he wasn’t bad at “healing and saving lives” and could consider joining a reliable team as a “healer”.
“The task is the day after tomorrow; now is the time to find a team.”
His eyes lingered on several continuously recruiting taglines, and after scouting around for a while, he chose a familiar ID, “Son of Sadomasochism”.
This person had been recruiting non-stop since Colin joined the company last month…
I heard he succeeded once or twice, but it seems it hadn’t worked out.
However, among the few teams, “Son of Sadomasochism” had gotten the farthest; they had succeeded in reaching the third phase of the task and defeated two D Level compartments.
Unfortunately, they still ended up losing in the third car due to not being able to keep up with healing.
Then, “Son of Sadomasochism” booted the unqualified healer trash out of the team…
It was heartless, but it also showed that they were determined to clear the level.
[Your application to join the group has been accepted. You have formed an assault team with “Son of Sadomasochism,” “Emperor Sun,” “No.7 Little Chicken,” and “Fuer Mushroom.”]
[Note: You cannot leave the team until this mission fails.]
As soon as Colin joined the group, he saw a message from the team leader, “Son of Sadomasochism”:
“Welcome, welcome. I saw in your introduction that you’re good at treating external injuries and also have the means to recover others’ items?”
“Yes, but some methods aren’t item-related; they’re powers I’ve gained myself and can’t be demonstrated.”
After Colin replied, he directly sent information on the [Gluttony Power Mark].
“Yeah, yeah, yeah, that item is not bad, though its recovery speed is a bit slow, not very suitable. But if you do have that fast healing ability you mentioned, then there should be no problem,”
“Son of Sadomasochism” responded to Colin’s message in the group channel almost instantly.
In truth, anyone who had teamed up with Colin before could almost immediately realize his true identity upon seeing this item.
Unfortunately, this time, those people were assigned to other promotion instances…
“By the way, can I ask why you kicked out the last ‘healer’?” Colin curiously asked.
At this moment, before “Son of Sadomasochism” could respond, a team member with the slightly abstract ID “Emperor Sun” jumped in:
“Don’t even mention it, was that a healer? That guy’s healing effect required going head-to-head with enemies and getting bloody to recover. It was almost useless; that should be called a berserker…”
“Exactly! Damn it, that healer walked in, planted his weapon on the ground, and completely baffled us all,” another team member complained.
Uh… Colin pursed his lips and sidestepped this topic, trying to find out more about the situation on the train.
At this point, the team members were rather open…
“The car is very spacious, and those are all very strong, unknown D Level staff. They are difficult to beat head-on; the only method is to stall until after fifteen minutes when their strength starts to decline. The counterattack opportunity comes after thirty minutes.”
“Son of Sadomasochism” continued to inform Colin that after thirty minutes, the D Level Personnel would generally stop using items…
Only then would they stand a chance to win.
The reason being that when D Level employees were first confronted, their status was normal, but as time went on, they would slowly lose their sanity and turn into non-human monsters, abandoning their strongest methods, “items.”
After defeating them, there would be some time to rest before the next battle began.
‘Why does it feel like we’re just wearing down some old guy…’ Colin thought to himself, pursing his lips.
Though the method was a bit unsporting, after all, it was fighting above one’s level, and brute force was simply a death wish.
“With each subsequent car, those people get a bit stronger, but it’s only their items that are stronger, not themselves. So as long as we endure, we can still fight.”
“Of course, when you make it to the third car, you’ll need to endure until they weaken after thirty minutes…”
“At least 45 minutes before we can counterattack. From what I’ve heard from those who’ve moved up before, if you can endure the third car for sixty minutes, it seems you can win directly, reason unknown…”
“Son of Sadomasochism” made sure to share all the information he knew with Colin, the “newbie.”
Then, after explaining the general situation with the train, he began assigning tasks among the group members.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 353 - 353 351 Is Brother Shunzi That Amazing_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 353: Chapter 351 Is Brother Shunzi That Amazing?_1 Chapter 353: Chapter 351 Is Brother Shunzi That Amazing?_1 “First, let’s confirm the basic method of play, ‘Emperor Sun’ and I will use our own techniques to drag out the situation at the start. We’ll take the front, while ‘No.7 Little Chicken’ and ‘Fuer Mushroom’ protect ‘654321’.”
“In the early stages, ‘654321’ should avoid revealing his identity as much as possible, because the enemy usually has someone fast and with special means like an assassin.”
“He will try to assassinate you, and @No.7 Little Chicken, @Fuer Mushroom, you two aren’t new to this, so you should know how to deal with it.”
“During the first wave, just drag it out like this, and after holding on for 15 minutes, we’ll start looking for opportunities to counterattack…”
“Remember, without my command, don’t even think about counterattacking.”
“Those D Level teams, whether it’s teamwork or individual strength, are all far above us; there’s no way we can beat them under normal circumstances.”
“So even if they show an opening, don’t get greedy for an extra hit.”
“Speaking of which, let me confirm one more time, @654321, you’re not gonna walk through the door and just stick your weapon into the ground, are you?”
…
“@Son of Sadomasochism, rest assured, I won’t, I’m a professional support, I won’t hold you back…”
Colin responded with a somewhat ironic smile.
From the recent conversation, he could roughly tell that the person from the last round’s gear was a special big club; jab it into the ground upon entering, and within a certain range, everyone attacking the enemy can gain some energy and healing feedback.
But the problem is…
Unless one could absorb the enemy’s blood, the healing amount was pitifully small, and, setting that aside, the enemy wouldn’t even give the chance for close contact.
Even if they managed to delay the time, those guys would transform into monsters with a rich combat instinct, and would not be foolhardy.
So in the last round, they just struggled to drag a redundant sauce bottle into the third round.
“But talking about this, the strategy is really simple, huh? Just the secret of ‘dragging’.”
Colin pursed his lips as he read the content above.
This wasn’t something unique to their team, other teams were more or less the same.
They would all drag out the time, wait for the D Level team members to turn chaotic and out of control, then they would try to counterattack, instead of directly brawling while the enemy still retained considerable intelligence…
And for some teams that had been assigned to this task in the past and eventually cleared it.
They generally adopted the same tactics…
Or more precisely, if those who cleared it weren’t lying, then based on the current known situation, this was the only known way to clear it. Only by dragging it out could one continue fighting, without dragging, there was no game to be played.
At present, there is not a single team or individual who has cleared the challenge by defeating the enemy face-to-face.
“Generally speaking, they’re ten times stronger when they’re chaotic, seven times weaker when cleansed, only here it’s the other way around…”
Colin couldn’t help but mutter a complaint under his breath.
However, regarding “Son of Sadomasochism”‘s combat arrangement, he didn’t have any objections.
After all, they were about to face a group of well-trained D Level staff.
Even if they were on the same level, there was no guarantee of victory, let alone when the opponent was a level higher, with perfectly matched double Talents and very strong Gear that complemented each other.
“Right now, has any team managed to get through five carriages?” Colin curiously asked the members in the group.
After all, after passing five carriages one could choose equipment, and most likely get Purple Gear, which was the most urgently needed healing gear…
And these people didn’t discuss it at all?
“Hey, it’s only you newcomers who would think about getting through the fifth carriage. The requirements, well, are definitely not achievable for average people. In the past two years, I’ve only heard of the team formed by ‘Lifecoach Kawaii-many’ that succeeded; there were others who tried and died, but none of them made it.”
No.7 Little Chicken” answered Colin’s query, and it was apparent that he was an old fail-er who knew quite a bit of “insider information.”
Lifecoach also had such glorious moments? Colin was somewhat surprised at the bottom of his heart; he thought the other party was just a science popularizer and probably not that strong in combat, but it seemed that he was quite formidable after all.
At that moment, “Son of Sadomasochism” also complained, “I was such an idiot when I first came up here last year. After clearing it with great difficulty once, I got greedy and wanted to try for the fifth carriage, but not only did I fail, the team fell apart after a couple of members died on other missions within the following few days of restarting the copy. Otherwise, I would have risen a long time ago.”
Quite unlucky, Colin objectively assessed. Actually, compared to what he initially thought, the company’s fatality rate wasn’t that high—usually only ten or so out of a hundred people would die in a year.
“Ah, what a pity. If Brother Shunzi had been promoted and placed in our team, we might have had a chance at the dream of clearing the fifth carriage. Now, forget it, we should just focus on figuring out how to get through the third round.”
“Emperor Sun” gave some insights.
“Is Brother Shunzi really that incredible?” Colin asked curiously.
“Of course, yeah, ‘The Ascension Project,’ ‘The Out-of-Control Copy,’ it’s said he even once carried a bunch of useless employees through a new ‘Ascension Project.’ Think about it, aren’t those tasks much harder than this one? Those are difficulties with no upper limit! He still managed to return after completing them. Fighting a normal copy, even if it’s a bit tougher, would still be easy as pie for him.”
Well, that’s not something you can just say, kid, don’t jinx it here…
Colin thought about the mission description, over seventy D Levels and a C Level just died without explanation, and although the company had made it safe and turned into a copy event, who knew if something was hidden in there.
After all, right now, clearing three carriages was considered passing, and no one knew any more than that.
Anyway, from his experience with the tasks since he joined the company, even if there were no problems with this mission, something would probably go wrong once he was involved.
“Yeah, that guy is unbelievably strong, stronger than if he were overpowered. If he really joined our squad, we probably wouldn’t need any healers, just lie flat and don’t bother the boss.”
“At this point, it looks like Brother Shunzi is probably the strongest in the company, bar none.”
“…”
The group members, seeing what “Emperor Sun” said, couldn’t help but join in with their contemplations, almost resenting the fact that he was not a member of their team.
“Isn’t that a bit exaggerated?” Colin couldn’t help responding.
As he sent the message, he couldn’t help but think of that ridiculously strong ‘The Light Chaser,’ who was still at F Level, and then he remembered the recent battle—
That guy fighting felt like he genuinely had hacks on!
Even when using Time Stop, it couldn’t contain him.
Every time Colin had just a thought, the other party would instantly react and escape beyond a thirty meter radius.
And it was precisely at the instant he activated it that the other party escaped.
Causing him to waste a usage in vain…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 354 - 354 352 Mysterious Person on the Train_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 354: Chapter 352 Mysterious Person on the Train_1 Chapter 354: Chapter 352 Mysterious Person on the Train_1 Colin was facing such a difficult enemy for the first time, the only consolation was that the other party had no malice…
After that battle, his slightly inflated ego had been hammered down, and sometimes even when he slept and dreamt, he could feel a fist smashing towards him, sending him flying ten meters away.
Of course, although the battle was a bit tough, luckily, the outcome was a draw.
However, most company members, except for a very few, didn’t know about “The Light Chaser”, so they were surprised when they heard Colin speak up.
“I’m telling you, no exaggeration, let’s not talk about anything else, but you’ve always done the ‘World Code-13′ self-selected mission, right? You know the difficulty of that, how many of us didn’t die ten or eight times to get through, and someone else cleared it on the first try…”
“Yeah, yeah, if I get the chance, I’d go kneel and carry a sedan chair to bring them over…”
“Me too…”
Watching this group of people start to boast, Colin shook his head, he also had no immediate desire to reveal his identity.
It wasn’t because he wanted to hide his strength, but given the current situation, once he revealed his identity, these people would probably really become “bystanders”, which would not be conducive for their future growth.
Since the team already had a mature approach, he might as well give it a try…
If he could get through it, then great, if not, then he would deal with it.
“I’ve already changed my name, so my luck shouldn’t be that bad.”
Colin closed the group chat and then looked for “Lifecoach Kawaii-many”, hoping to get some more information from him, since in the past two years, only this group had definitely reached the fifth stage.
He wasn’t sure about the others, but he only knew this one.
He glanced at his remaining number of messages and drafted a message to send over.
Unlike those employees who could speak freely, for some reason, when his number of messages exceeded a certain amount, he felt very endangered…
The only one who probably knew why was “Lady Bunny”.
It was also her who had told him about the message restrictions…
Meanwhile, “Lifecoach Kawaii-many”, who seemed to always be lurking in the company’s internal chat feature, replied in less than a minute.
“Eh, who are you? Wait, are you Brother Shunzi? Did you finally change your name? No wonder I haven’t seen you lately.”
Lifecoach was initially surprised at having a friend with an unfamiliar ID, but he quickly identified the person through some records.
He just didn’t expect that Brother Shunzi, who hadn’t changed his name in ages, had actually done so, he thought he would use that name for a lifetime.
But he didn’t dwell on it too much.
He read the message and then immediately recalled the experiences on “The Disordered Ghost Train”.
“This mission as a whole, belongs to the higher difficulty among D Level missions, of course, this is in comparison to the average employee, but for you, it shouldn’t be a big problem, at least clearing three parts should be doable…”
“Besides, each time the mission starts, the enemies are random, even if you’re lucky to encounter the same group as before, it’s useless because their props and equipment are most likely different from the last time.”
“This also leads to different combat tactics from the enemy, using the experience from last time might just make your defeat look slightly less terrible.”
“I reckon this is the company’s way to train us to adapt to varying situations.”
“However, there are still some clues, there’s a fixed strategy which is to drag it out, and then consider adapting to the randomness. Honestly, if it weren’t for the ability to drag them out until they lose their minds, I guess even if our D Level team went back, even just to fight a random team, it would be difficult to win…”
“The D Level on the train is a bit different from us, their combat experience is frighteningly rich. They can utilize their tools very proficiently, frankly speaking, we’re like flowers in a greenhouse in comparison.”
“Then there’s the matter with the fifth car, there’s something a bit different from what everyone thinks…”
“Almost our entire team was wiped out, we didn’t really clear it in the true sense.”
“…”
Not really clearing it in the true sense… Colin was taken aback, what did that mean?
He sent a “?” over.
“Back then, our team’s props by chance were quite restraining to them, which allowed us to drag on without injury. So we started by dragging it out for thirty minutes, which let us clear it relatively easily, to the point of being overly optimistic.”
“But after clearing the third car, the difficulty spiked suddenly. We barely managed to get through the fourth and were about to give up when the mission alert said that only after clearing sections 3, 5, 9, and 12 would the mission be settled.”
“Oh right, there’s one thing, starting from the third car if any props get damaged, they are really damaged, so you’ve got to be careful.”
“At that time, we had no choice but to continue fighting. Just as we got to the fifth level, we didn’t last long before those guys smashed our protective equipment, and we couldn’t even counterattack because the enemies’ aggression was no weaker. One of our members attempted to strike, only to be torn to shreds…”
“In the end, we endured. After staggering for over an hour… I vaguely remember something coming from another car to assist us, which barely counted as clearing it.”
Reflecting on the past, “Lifecoach Kawaii-many” still felt a tremor in his heart.
After that battle, almost all the tools in their hands were nearly wrecked…
Not to mention the others, even he had several pieces of green gear torn apart, and his purple gear went from being 90% intact to just twenty-something percent, it had only been repaired to 60% so far, and its overall performance was down by more than ten percent from the start.
…
‘Assistance from something else…’
Colin focused on this sentence, feeling that his bad premonition was somewhat coming true; there really was something hidden within.
He immediately inquired about that thing, but unfortunately, “Lifecoach Kawaii-many” said he didn’t know, as they were all in a bad condition at the time and couldn’t figure out what it was.
They didn’t even know from where this powerful supporter came.
A mysterious altruistic supporter?
Muttering quietly, Colin seemed to remember something, “Wait a second… When he assisted you, did he ask you to pay him points or something like that?”
“No.”
Then it wasn’t “The Light Chaser” after all.
If it were him, these people would have lost more than just their equipment; they would probably have to pay with everything they owned.
‘But thinking back on it, they most likely couldn’t have afforded his exorbitant fees anyway, oh, but maybe…’
Colin remembered that guy’s fees could also be put on a tab, you could first rack up a massive debt and slowly pay it off later.
And while he was pondering, he suddenly thought of something—
Despite knowing so much, why had no one mentioned the only “C” level person on that train?
Weren’t the train’s staff supposed to rotate among the dozen or so cars?
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 355 - 355 353 The Islands Invitation_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 355: Chapter 353: The Island’s Invitation_1 Chapter 355: Chapter 353: The Island’s Invitation_1 Since every member on the train was randomly selected for rotation, why haven’t I heard anyone mention…
…encountering the Level C Employee?
Colin curiously sent out his question.
If it was truly random, over the years there must have been a lucky one (or an unlucky one) who would have encountered them at least once.
However, discussions about that person were not entirely nonexistent, yet they were scarce.
“This… well, it’s not very clear because we can’t remember what they look like. But based on some characteristics and the effects of their items, we conjecture that of the more than seventy D Level personnel, only about two-thirds have shown up. The ‘randomness’ most people refer to typically includes just this portion.”
“There’s also another third, who you probably meet as you fight your way to the back carriages…”
“As for whether the C Level is among that two-thirds, it’s assumed probably not, but it’s hard to say. And one more thing, rather than that C Level, what we’re usually more concerned about is the number of enemies because the team sizes vary on each train carriage.”
“Sometimes you encounter five, sometimes six, and in the most extreme cases you could face up to nine…”
“The more there are, the harder it is to fight. It’s not like a game where if there are more players it gets balanced by lowering the level; however strong those you were matched with before were, that’s how strong they will be this time…”
“And no matter how the numbers change, their teamwork is top-notch, even Brother Shunzi should be careful, especially if you want to clear the fifth checkpoint.”
“…”
As he spoke, Lifecoach Kawaii-many recalled more memories and sent them one by one.
At the same time, he couldn’t help but marvel at which team was fortunate enough to team up with Brother Shunzi.
Based on the information received from employees who had teamed up with Brother Shunzi before, as long as no mistakes were made, people who teamed up with him could easily complete the mission without lifting a finger.
“No, that’s not necessarily true…” Lifecoach Kawaii-many suddenly remembered that Brother Shunzi seemed to attract mishaps on missions, and if nothing went wrong, then something definitely would…
‘Tsk,’ they could only hope for those people to fend for themselves.
…
“So only two-thirds have been seen, huh.”
Colin slightly shook his head, expressed his thanks, and did not continue to inquire.
Compared to Son of Sadomasochism, Lifecoach Kawaii-many knew more information about the checkpoints, but core details, such as those about the Level C Personnel Colin was most concerned about, were limited.
“Handling D Level should be doable for me if nothing unexpected happens. I just need to watch out for their gear a bit. The trouble is with the C Level…”
Colin knew his own matters best, and for others, considering an unseen Level C would not be necessary.
But for him, it might be different…
Even, it was possible that the reason he was assigned this mission was specifically to target that Level C Employee.
Although it seems that there’s only a difference of one level between D and C, no one knows what additional capabilities the C Level possesses.
Colin pondered for a moment and then shook his head, deciding not to dwell on these thoughts any longer.
The information available was not sufficient to support further consideration…
Recollecting his thoughts, Colin then browsed the chat channel, wishing to see if there were any good pieces of gear available. However, after a while, he realized that the prices for gear had recently surged.
An item like “Analytical Lens” was now breaking a thousand points…
Many common items were being purchased by the company’s newcomers.
“Are they attempting to crack the company’s item manufacturing technology?”
Colin murmured to himself, feeling that the possibility was unlikely. He might not have noticed before, but now he could almost be certain that the creation of “items” involved certain protocols…
Just this alone was enough to deter those trying to crack it.
Of course, he didn’t tell Old Master Wu to stop researching and waste time, since there was still a chance something might be uncovered by accident.
“Speaking of which, I haven’t seen a single piece of Purple Gear for sale on the trading floor since I joined the company. It’s hard to even find a few green-tagged items… sigh, these employees are not efficient. They cling to Purple Gear like heirlooms as if it wasn’t a common thing…”
After scrolling for a while and not finding anything useful, Colin closed the internal chat in disappointment.
Then, he ordered a pig trotter rice from the takeaway app downstairs and checked the messages. Apart from Qin Chuan, who just returned from abroad, and some urging him to go to work to handle some anomalies, there was nothing else.
Except for a lengthy message from Xu Duojin sent two hours earlier that was worth his attention.
“Mr. Colin, here’s the situation: the ‘Global Supernatural Alliance’ has recently asked for international assistance from us. They hope we can dispatch some personnel to help with ‘Da Bu… Island,’ to assist in containing some historical artifacts that have been lost from our country. Among them, there’s one, and they are especially hoping that you can join them… around the 19th…”
Is this a sign they’re really struggling?
Colin was surprised, then quickly skimmed through the rest of the message sent by Xu Duojin—
It detailed a request for their help in dealing with some artifacts related to their country. Many of these artifacts, because of regional and cultural reasons, require specific containment measures that often vary greatly and have a certain legacy.
In situations where this legacy knowledge was available, the control of artifacts that had become unstable was usually more manageable.
They often just needed to patch things up, not full containment. Many horror stories in films about haunted places could be resolved by finding a certain object or person in the vicinity, which, although not entirely accurate, was somewhat linked to these underlying reasons.
But…
This approach wasn’t quite suitable for Great Britain.
‘Tsk, that place due to historical reasons has a “small land with a rich collection” of artifacts, or rather, ill-gotten gains, that are undoubtedly diverse. The problem is the lack of legacy… tsk tsk, it really is a situation unique to my Great Britain now…’
Colin finished reading what Xu Duojin had sent, and though he felt it was somewhat inappropriate, he couldn’t help but laugh.
Of course, the invitation didn’t expect them to resolve all anomalies, but only the portion belonging to their own country. In return, they promised many benefits, returning historical artifacts being only the most basic one…
However, regretfully, Colin checked the dates.
Leaving on the 19th…
It clashed with the second stage of his promotion mission.
Without a second thought, Colin directed Xu Duojin to decline the invitation for him.
After all, it seemed there were plenty of others going; one more or one less wouldn’t make much difference, and the event even involved Ninth Level personnel, the highest echelon…
His presence or absence wouldn’t have much impact. There was no need to put himself in such danger.
“Understood,” Xu Duojin responded quickly.
In fact, Xu himself had his own grievances about that request.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 356 - 356 354 The Disordered Ghost Train Begins._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 356: Chapter 354 “The Disordered Ghost Train” Begins._1 Chapter 356: Chapter 354 “The Disordered Ghost Train” Begins._1 About seven or eight years ago, many people within the circle had already anticipated these events, urging those on the island to transfer everything as quickly as possible, even if not returning it…
But that group wouldn’t listen, insisting that everything was normal and nothing had happened.
They also stated that, as a historical great power, they had the ability to solve their own internal problems.
Afterward, the anomalies from that island spread to their neighbors in Europa Continent and even across the ocean to the Grand East Coast.
They still claimed there were some issues but nothing major.
Eventually, when they detected regional weakening of the “world barrier”, multiple countries voted and decisively sent a joint team to investigate, only to find that the problems were far worse than they had said.
The current situation over there is like an Okamoto 0.01 stretched to its limit, a few more shakes and it might explode.
Even so, those people were still arrogantly protesting this and that…
It wasn’t until this year, when two Eighth Level Personnel from the island ran away with a bunch of people in tow, that they couldn’t cover it up any longer and finally asked for help.
Thinking of this made Xu Duojin somewhat angry.
Colin didn’t know what was going through Xu Duojin’s mind on the other side of the phone. After ending the conversation, he looked at the messages sent by the other party and did have some thoughts:
“Speaking of which, if the anomaly suppression fails, I guess it’s going to be another grand vanishing act, right?”
Colin blinked his eyes.
Although he wasn’t too concerned about that place, he couldn’t help but consider the global impact if problems arose there.
First of all, should that happen…
A hit to the “world barrier” was completely foreseeable.
This invisible, intangible barrier, once breached, would cause anomalies around the globe to erupt at a rate that would make one’s scalp tingle.
One could say that the current chaos on Earth entirely depends on the condition of the “world barrier”.
So it was clear, no matter what Colin’s impression of that place was, if it spiraled out of control, it would definitely be bad news for everyone.
Which is why, despite the situation there being at its worst, countries around the globe were still willing to offer assistance.
If it had been some unknown small country experiencing this…
The big five, if they were willing to send someone to save even a rat, could be praised as a “benevolent force”, and more likely would simply erase them from the world altogether, along with their land…
“If real trouble arises, company employees probably won’t ever have to worry about lacking missions again.”
Colin pursed his lips, made an ironic comment in his mind, and then shifted his focus back to the present.
“Because I saved that old brother in ‘Pseudo-Humans’, he has been singing my praises every day, granting me a bit of a status boost. While it’s not like the company’s ‘call and they come’, at least when I send out messages, people no longer ignore them. There’s still some time before a breakthrough development. For now, I just need to keep observing and grant a few small favors as requested by the mission.”
“Today is the 17th, and there are a few days left until the 20th, these days are rather leisurely, so I can spend some time mentoring those soy-sauce disciples…”
Thinking of those nineteen clamoring soy-sauces, Colin felt a mixture of laughter and tears.
In recent times, he has been dragging them around, and a group of low-level Fate Propellers generally advanced a level, going from the initial 1-2 to now 2-3 Level.
Honestly, the way they upgraded was quite magical to Colin.
Not to mention, they didn’t need to gain the next set of characteristics like other paths.
As long as they had opportunities to mix in, they really did advance in levels…
According to what he understood, if the situation allowed and the conditions were right, this group of soy-sauces could keep mixing their way up to Eighth Level, becoming one of the strongest among the Extraordinary Ones on Earth.
It was only because Ninth Level was rumored to have a sort of “uniqueness”, limited to one individual.
He didn’t doubt in the least that this group of people could carry on blending in.
“No wonder it has the most participants through the official channels, just don’t know what the logic behind the promotion is…”
Colin pursed his lips, feeling relieved that he hadn’t encountered any troublesome matters with the official-type of abnormal tasks.
Thus, he wasn’t overly resistant to tagging along for a ride.
The problematic missions that were occurring now were basically all handed down by the company.
If he weren’t aware of some underlying logic in the assignment of tasks, Colin might have believed he had enemies within the company.
“Once the D Level Promotion Mission is complete, I should be able to free up some time, quickly elevate my internal official rank from 5 to 6, investigate the ‘Book of Fate’, and then secure Lady Bunny’s promise.”
“After becoming a C Level, I should be able to understand more things, like the situation with senior employees, something like that 2044…”
“Then, if there truly is some sort of grand, apocalyptic disaster, I’d have some means of self-preservation.”
Although the overall global situation was stable, aside from that Sunset Island, he still felt that something far more dangerous was slowly happening—
Something unstoppable brewing beyond the islands.
Colin wasn’t certain if his instincts and premonitions were right, but he hoped, before that day arrived,
He would have the strength to protect himself, everyone at the welfare institute, as well as nearby friends and so on…
One thought after another floated through his mind.
It wasn’t until Zhu Jiaofan’s knock on the door that he was brought back from his reverie.
After dinner, as was routine, he slept until about two or three in the morning; then, with nothing better to do, Colin woke up Qin Chuan and the others who had just lay down, had him bring out all the tagalongs, and started executing missions in the dead of the night.
To clear up the outstanding nearby tasks that had piled up recently…
Just as Colin had thought, non-company missions mostly caused no ripples.
Many of the anomalies within the incidents seemed troublesome to Qin Chuan, to Qin Chuan’s former boss, to the boss of Qin Chuan’s former boss, to the boss of the boss of Qin Chuan’s former boss, but they weren’t much of an issue for Colin.
Leading a whole bunch of tagalongs hither and thither, this exemplary worker’s life went on for several days, until number 20 arrived a few days later.
Colin sent all the tagalongs away, and at ten minutes to eleven, he skillfully lay down on the bed.
Soon after, accompanied by the sound of a flute close to his ear,
a surging dense fog rolled in, smearing everything around into obscurity…
Colin couldn’t help but feel a moment of trance.
When he came to his senses, he found himself in a familiar train carriage.
Beneath the yellowish, cozy light, the carriage, exuding a steampunk style, clattered along with the train’s movement, while outside the window, a haze of grey fog hung in the air.
He shook his head vigorously to dispel the haziness.
“No bell sounds, seems it’s not a Descent Type, but the train indeed is that Infinite Train…”
In a flash of thought, Colin sat upright in his seat and looked around the carriage, quickly noticing that apart from him, there were four other figures, each seated in different parts of the carriage.

chapters.title: Chapter 357 - 357 355 Your Life is Assured by Me_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 357: Chapter 355 Your Life is Assured by Me!_1 Chapter 357: Chapter 355 Your Life is Assured by Me!_1 “It’s the other employees…”
Through the IDs above their heads, Colin quickly confirmed this.
As for the enemy, it seemed none were in sight for now.
Everything on this train car was normal…
However, it was at this moment that a series of messages began to emerge in his mind.
[Incident One: ‘Infinity Train-3000-1’ is expected to merge with the detached accident train in thirty minutes. Please prepare as required and investigate at least three carriages of the detached and uncontrolled train.]
“Note: The task is considered complete after the investigation of the three detached and uncontrolled carriages is finished.”
“Attention: You may choose whether to conduct a deeper investigation.”
…
“Thirty minutes, they even gave us some time to rest and get ready, not starting with a full-blown attack… It’s really…”
Colin gathered his thoughts and sat up straight.
Seeing the subtle reactions of the others, it appeared they too had received the mission requirements.
However, the few who had been on multiple missions didn’t scrutinize the content in detail and closed it. They stood up together and walked through the swaying carriages to Colin’s vicinity.
After exchanging looks, “Son of Sadomasochism” took out a pack of cigarettes from his pocket, lit one, and offered it between two fingers.
“No, thank you,” Colin declined.
“Oh, oh,”
“Son of Sadomasochism” did not insist, and as he placed the cigarette on his ear, he said, “We don’t need to introduce ourselves with the IDs showing. So, buddy, can you now confirm that the stuff you mentioned is real?”
So far, this “654321” had only shown off the Mark of Gluttony; the rest hadn’t been displayed…
But based on his excellent evaluation, they had still let him join.
“Sure.”
Colin nodded and without hesitation took out the “Gluttony Power Mark” and tossed it to them, verbally transferring some authority for them to use it themselves.
“What is this…”
Seeing Colin’s move, the group was somewhat taken aback. Generally, props were not shared so casually.
Because not knowing was one thing, but after seeing it, there was often an unavoidable temptation.
However, after understanding the “negative effects” of the item, they seemed to grasp why “654321” did not want to use it himself…
“Not bad, the negative effects are tolerable, but the recovery isn’t quick enough…”
“Emperor Sun” experimented and objectively evaluated it. He estimated it could have decent effects for the follow-up recovery from hemorrhoids, appendectomy, dental root extraction, or extensive burns.
But before high-intensity combat, it was somewhat insufficient.
“However, little brother, no offense, but the way you’re just handing over props for others to borrow, it’s very likely to attract covetous eyes. In these immortal mission types, it’s fine, but in real missions, if there were a crook among us, you’d probably be in trouble. It’d be easy to get robbed,” “Emperor Sun” said as he handed the prop back.
Are you telling me this with your ID on, as if introducing yourself… Colin took back the Gluttony Power and nodded, thankful for the advice, then said:
“Who among you will give themselves a cut? I’ll demonstrate my other methods.”
Following that, “No.7 Little Chicken” stood up, took out a seemingly sharp knife, and with some difficulty made a small incision on the back of his hand…
Upon seeing this, Colin secretly instructed his Nano Intellectual Mechanism to repair it.
Soon, the group saw the cut, as though pulled by some force, quickly close up, leaving almost no trace of the wound.
“Combined with the ‘Gluttony Power’, this ability could greatly reduce the recovery time. Under normal conditions, for internal injuries, broken bones, and the like, as long as you’re not instantly killed, I can handle it,” he said.
As he spoke, Colin’s eyelids drooped slightly, and he shifted the conversation, “However, in order to make better use of it in a moment, I may need to apply my abilities to enhance you guys.”
Everyone was attached to about half a pound of Nano Intellectual Mechanism, so if there were any accidents, he could intervene as soon as possible.
It’s just that this time he didn’t choose to forcefully become the team leader, so doing this might bring about the rejection of this group of people.
However, what Colin didn’t expect was…
Upon hearing his words, the people present not only didn’t show any suspicion but actually looked pleased.
Especially the “Son of Sadomasochism,” who couldn’t help but laugh and say, “Great, great, great! Finally, there’s a decent support; hurry up, dude, give me a BUFF!”
“And me, and me…”
“Same here!”
“…”
They didn’t harbor any doubts at all, could their demands be so low? And here I thought there would be a long period of cunning and plotting…
Colin fell silent for a moment, then infused each person with the power of intelligence.
Unlike the situation with the Arsonist in the last mission, this time when he did this, they even had to say thank you.
“Dude, thanks, awooo!”
The “Son of Sadomasochism” and the others felt that kind of “aura” flowing into their bodies, all functions were indeed enhanced!
At last, after nearly half a year, a proper “healer” had arrived!
“You two remember, you must protect this dude’s life as much as possible!”
The team leader “Son of Sadomasochism” turned to “No.7 Little Chicken” and “Fuer Mushroom” to give the reminder once again.
Seeing the few who looked as if they had found treasure, Colin felt inexplicably guilty for some reason, “By the way, I also have some special enhancement methods…”
While he was speaking, he took out a palm-sized Energy Crystal and controlled that force to fly towards the four of them.
As the energy flooded in, they felt their bodies enter a full and perfect state.
“Holy shit, there’s even a BUFF on top!”
“6!”
The group was overjoyed; this “healer” could actually add more than two buffs!
Luckily, this time there was truly hope for clearing the level!
“Big bro, don’t worry! Your life is safe with me and Little Chicken! Even if the team leader dies, you can’t die!”
“Fuer Mushroom” guaranteed seriously.
Colin nodded his head, thought for a moment, tried to reach out his hand, and drew on the power of a Golden Mark he carried on his person: “When necessary, I can also provide some of this effect.”
As he spoke, a faint, but unignorable, pure white radiance appeared in the palm of his hand.
At this moment, everyone who gazed directly at this radiance felt an inner peace, a clear and active brain, and a certain degree of strength enhancement in their bodies!
“Holy shit, big bro—no, Righteous Father! From now on, you are my Righteous Father!”
“Rest assured! Unless I die, those enemies won’t even touch a hair on you!”
“Righteous Father above, if you do not abandon me, I will be your frontline fighter from now on! If there are any missions that can be quit midway, you can call on me!”
When that radiance appeared, they were all instantly convinced; this was a real healer!
What the hell were those previous recruits? Some freaking demons and ghosts?!
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 358 - 358 356 Fighting like this nobody will die_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 358: Chapter 356: Fighting like this, nobody will die!_1 Chapter 358: Chapter 356: Fighting like this, nobody will die!_1 “Slap, slap!”
“Son of Sadomasochism” patted his chest, offering a guarantee:
“Don’t worry, as long as we’re not dead, we won’t let you suffer even the slightest harm!”
“Speaking of which, do you have a ‘Tyrant Body’? If you don’t, when we level up later, we’ll help you farm one…”
“Right, right, don’t worry, we’ll cover all the Points for you!” No.7 Little Chicken nodded eagerly like a pecking chicken.
The upcoming mission might not have a guaranteed success rate, and in case of failure, it’d be good to foster relationships for teaming up again.
Plus, even if they succeeded at the first attempt, such a great support character with specialized aids was a rare commodity within the company. There was a chance they’d be useful in other missions, so it was wise to maintain good relationships—an extra righteous father never hurt anyone!
‘Tyrant Body’? Why would I want that trashy Talent…’
Colin couldn’t help but smile wryly as he dealt with the enthusiastic offers, informing them that this was all the support he had.
No one seemed to mind this revelation, expressing that his contributions were more than enough.
“We’ve got seven minutes left, the battle is about to start, everyone get ready…”
“Son of Sadomasochism” glanced at the time and reminded everyone, then suddenly turned to Colin, “By the way, do you have any other self-defense measures?”
“I have a few…”
Colin showed off his combat style, with Nano Intellectual Mechanism attached to his body, Analytical Lens, and a temporarily purchased imitation oversized and thickened Han Sword from the trading market, the effects being “Perfect Grip” + “90% Weight Reduction.”
The great sword, originally weighing over thirty pounds, felt like just a few pounds in his hands…
“…That’s decent, I guess. You don’t have to worry about fighting, just find a way to protect yourself.”
“Son of Sadomasochism” didn’t say much more, glancing at Colin’s stature, his thin arms and legs, which, while not an indicator of combat power, certainly made him look frail.
If those D Level Personnel got a chance to land a punch, even with the silver aura for protection, he’d likely get seriously injured.
They needed to take care to protect him well!
After a serious word of caution to everyone once more, shortly thereafter:
“Click.”
A slight vibration suddenly emanated from the front of the train carriage where the group was, as if they had collided with something while moving.
At the same time, a message appeared in their minds.
[Connection Complete.]
Immediately following, a larger set of double doors covered the original connecting door.
Behind the doors, there was an incredibly thick fog.
Rustling voices of conversation emanated from beyond the fog, and one could faintly hear people talking…
From these noises, it seemed that the people inside were unaware of their presence.
Colin listened for a few seconds, sadly unable to discern any useful information. Seeing the others preparing to enter, he couldn’t contain his curiosity and asked:
“Shouldn’t we check with the ‘Book of Fate’ first…?”
Before he could finish, the people around him all simultaneously exclaimed in horror, “Don’t use it for heaven’s sake!”
“What’s wrong? Don’t worry, I haven’t used it yet.” Colin was curious.
Seeing that Colin hadn’t used it yet, everyone breathed a sigh of relief. Then, “Son of Sadomasochism” explained:
“We forgot to tell you, these D Level staff seem to have special anti-surveillance measures. The moment you use it, they’ll definitely notice. And it’s not just about being discovered.”
“If you’re unlucky and encounter a few special staff members, they might even be able to alter the content you get from the ‘Book of Fate’ fragments.”
“They could trick you into crying.”
This was a lesson many employees within the company had learned the hard way.
“Altered? It can go that far?”
Colin was taken aback; he had been discovered a few times before, but this was the first time he’d heard of someone directly altering the content.
It seemed that even “0-09 ‘Hunger'” couldn’t achieve this.
“Let’s go, we can’t stand here for too long.”
The team leader, “Son of Sadomasochism,” did not elaborate further. He reached out, felt his way into the Mist Gate, and slowly walked forward.
Colin and the others followed closely behind.
Soon after taking a few steps forward, the intermittent chatter from behind the Mist Gate abruptly ceased.
However, the voices didn’t stop; instead, they switched to a different channel, appearing directly in their minds.
“…Something’s infiltrating. You two, prioritize protecting the injured, move them to the rear, and notify the other carriages as soon as possible, informing them of the situation here. Humanoid, strength unknown, purpose unknown…”
“Yes!”
“Others… follow me,… block…”
“…”
Bits of dialogue concerning arrangements filtered through their minds.
Colin was not surprised by this since he knew before entering that during combat, they seemed to be able to tap into the enemy’s internal communication channels, allowing direct insight into their actions.
It was as these voices appeared that the grey mist before their eyes dissipated, revealing an extremely expansive carriage interior space.
Though still a carriage, this compartment alone spanned at least a thousand kilometers in area!
Within it, Colin saw several D Level Personnel wearing brown Hunter’s Coats. It was the instant the two groups made contact that any superfluous exchanges were absent.
A D Level Employee clad in a brown Hunter’s Coat suddenly took a large step forward.
In the next instant, his figure flashed overhead, holding a sword hilt and making a chopping motion towards the group. During this motion, a large flaming sword gradually materialized from the hilt.
“Son of Sadomasochism,” unflinchingly at the front, pushed outwards with both hands.
Dozens of radiant beams of light burst forth…
“Boom!”
The great sword sliced through the beams of light and exploded, igniting a vast array of flames.
The blast erupted at the point of collision…
In the aftermath of the initial clash, the D Level Personnel in the brown Hunter’s Coat showed signs of exhaustion, as if the strike had drained much of his strength, to the point where he barely lifted his sword.
However, “Son of Sadomasochism” didn’t take the bait; he made no move to attack but instead danced, spun, and leaped as though performing street dance.
Breathtaking brilliance emanated from him, forming a dense protective membrane around them, enveloping Colin and the others within…
Meanwhile, in Colin’s mind, enemy communications akin to neural transmissions resurfaced.
“…No pursuit? It looks like their captain can’t use ‘Strike Second for Advantage’ then, they seem quite cautious…”
“Doesn’t matter…”
“…According to Combat Power Observation, these people aren’t strong…”
“Don’t be complacent, ‘Fate’ tells me there’s something off about these enemies…”
“Never mind the problems, let’s see how it goes. Kill the one giving the BUFF, I’ll tear an opening, and you guys charge in…”
“…”
As these communications surfaced, the squad leader clashing with “Son of Sadomasochism” suddenly shed his exhausted demeanor. First, he popped a fiery red Energy Crystal into his mouth, then gripping his sword with both hands, he delivered swift and continuous strikes toward the dazzling protective membrane formed by the light.
His speed was so fast that, on the retinas of the onlookers, he left a trail of afterimages…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 359 - 359 357
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 359: 357 Chapter 359: 357 “Boom boom boom!”
Gigantic explosions kept ringing out.
Even the “Son of Sadomasochism’s” complexion suddenly changed, sensing the strain, but his hands never ceased moving. Facing the storm-like onslaught of slashes, he still maintained his “dance,” only now it moved as if on fast-forward.
“Tch, not playing by the rules and unleashing colorless skills, huh?”
Seeing this, Colin didn’t hesitate and directly tossed a “Colorless Crystal Block” at the “Son of Sadomasochism.”
However, although the battle situation was tense, watching the two fight as if they were competing in a dance battle at the village edge…
Colin couldn’t help but let his thoughts wander a bit and felt like saying, “Stop it, you can’t kill anyone fighting like this… Huh?”
Why was he distracted?
“Detected a subtle mental influence, please be alert!” the Little Maid’s voice sounded in his ear.
Upon hearing this, Colin immediately alerted everyone.
“Eh, they responded so quickly, noticing the effects of ‘Mental Interference: Attention Loss’?”
“…That’s kind of impressive…”
“No big deal, get ready, I can break his defense in one second… and take out that blessing-added one… so annoying…”
“…”
The very next second, the D Level Squad Leader suddenly swung his sword with force, tearing a hole through the dazzling light shield.
At the same time, an image suddenly popped into Colin’s mind: a shadow loomed above, and a rope, emerging from nowhere within the darkness, dropped down, snaring his neck in less than 0.1 seconds…
And then, it pulled with force.
Amidst a snapping sound,
Colin was hoisted up into the air.
“This prop effect, why does it feel somewhat familiar…”
As thoughts flashed by, Colin didn’t dwell on it; he was about to shout a warning and prepare to dodge when he heard “Fuer Mushroom” next to him speak first, “Righteous Father is in danger, get down!”
As he spoke, Fuer Mushroom swung his fist upward with force, sending a shockwave that dispersed the shadow overhead.
With the disappearance of the shadow, the rope vanished as well.
However, that attack seemed to be just a feint. While he was distracted, multiple illusory figures emerged from thin air, rushing towards Colin and continuously expanding.
“Warning! High-energy incoming!” Little Maid’s voice transmitted, inquiring whether to counterattack.
In this critical moment, “No.7 Little Chicken” on the other side suddenly shifted form, transforming into an upright werewolf, with a large string of prayer beads around its neck.
The beads, with a pale golden glow, adorned and reinforced its body, giving it the appearance of a golden werewolf.
Then, it threw itself on top of Colin, using its flesh and blood to block the explosion.
“Boom!”
After the explosion, “No.7 Little Chicken” got up with its back a mangled mess of blood and flesh. Despite the damage, it swung its golden claws, forcing an illusory figure from the air and tearing it apart before it could explode.
…
“Mutation-type blessings, suspected to be the aura of a Level 5 Ancient God Type. Moreover, from their reactions just now, one of them seems to have some form of death premonition…”
“… Continue probing. Starting now, reduce the frequency of fatal attacks from once every two seconds to understand the interval of this death premonition before arranging assassinations…”
“Having taken a few ‘Illusory Body Bursts,’ that werewolf-like creature shouldn’t last much longer. The Ancient God’s Aura is the biggest variable; it could attract ‘God Descent’: he should be dealt with as a priority…”
“Alright, let’s kill him first…”
“The way they are acting, it’s like they are intentionally dragging out the time? I have a bad feeling. We need to wrap this up quickly. Captain, how much longer before their shield is completely destroyed?”
“It’s a bit troublesome, but I can shatter that ability of his within ten minutes!”
“It’s weird, I always feel like they can predict our moves. No matter how many flaws we sell, they don’t bite. But I didn’t notice the ‘Fate’ being peeked at. What’s going on?”
“…Get me the ‘Book of Fate’ and see if they have any precognitive counter-surveillance measures…”
“What about the other carriages? Why haven’t they responded yet? Has someone cut us off?”
“Something’s not right; it seems like something’s going to happen in ten minutes. There’s a problem, and I can’t probe into anything…”
“If there’s still no response from the other carriages in five minutes, abandon all the seriously injured personnel, take the members that are still valuable, initiate an evacuation protocol, and jump into the grey mist. I’ll cover the rear, and you guys evacuate. Don’t worry, these people aren’t strong, I can hold them down on my own, they can’t kill me, and unless something unexpected happens, I’ll catch up.”
“Got it!”
“…”
“These people are quick observers…”
Colin was internally surprised; this group not only quickly figured out their abilities, they also immediately made arrangements, and from beginning to end, everything was orderly and decisive.
Mistakes were occasional, but the speed of their corrections was very fast.
With their coordination, even maintaining a stalemate was difficult, let alone a counterattack.
And there was a critical point, all the “counterattack” opportunities that were currently visible were all deliberately exposed by the adversaries.
However, with time passing by, after a few minutes, the brainwave transmissions within the team became less frequent, gradually turning into chaos and noise, with incomprehensible roars starting to dominate…
It was at this moment, a D Level personnel suddenly dropped the tool in his hand.
His eyes bloodshot in an instant, he charged our way with a half-crawling, half-running gait, his face ferocious like a deranged monster…
Simultaneously, the flame of the greatsword wielded by the man vanished.
Though he still held the tool, it no longer triggered any explosive effects with the flames; his attacks could now be said to be without any technique, simply holding the sword and swinging it wildly.
The pressure on everyone began to greatly lessen!
Finally, as the transmissions within the team came to a complete halt, the “Son of Sadomasochism” stopped “dancing”, and on his skin, one after another, bizarre purple tattoos emerged, with two new pairs of arms stretching out from under his armpits…
“Kill!”
As his voice fell, he dropped his protection, and everyone armed with tools and weapons counterattacked these deranged beasts in human skin!
Though the beasts were still fearsome, it was like armed hunters facing wild beasts.
The battle didn’t bring much suspense…
Just ten minutes later, they had successfully killed the enemy one by one.
[Prepare to rejoin the second detached carriage in one hour.]
As this message appeared, everyone collapsed on the ground, exhausted.
The investigation of the first carriage was thus completed.
Colin looked over the people present, deployed the Nano Intellectual Mechanism, and began to heal the group.
In this battle, they indeed honored their promise; he fell into “traps” multiple times yet the enemy never managed to touch him directly…
And the most severely injured “Little Chicken” took several blasts to protect him, with one sword qi puncturing his hand clean off—
If Colin hadn’t kicked him at the crucial moment, it would have been his head flying off.
To be honest, he was quite moved.
However, as he helped everyone recover from their injuries, Colin turned to look at the corpses of the D Level personnel scattered everywhere, eyes unblinkingly dead, and inexplicably felt a wave of sorrow…
These people truly died too pitifully.
.
.
.
