“Are you a member of the ‘Bonfire Outstanding Talent Nurturing’ program?”
“Hmm? You’ve guessed this identity of mine?” Colin asked, astonished.
The Fire Tree’s smaller manifestation stiffened as if struck by some shock upon hearing Colin’s response.
“What’s the matter, is there a problem?”
“Not at all! I just never expected that I, an old tree, no, that I would have the honor to serve such a distinguished and bright figure of the future! I will go through fire and water for you, unhesitatingly facing death!” the Fire Tree persona hurriedly said with determination.
But for some reason, Colin felt as if the other had cried while saying this.
However, after a friendly exchange, they had verbally confirmed a voluntary and equal partnership.
There was no need for Colin to linger since his goal had been achieved.
And watching Colin depart, the human face on the Fire Tree’s body first breathed a sigh of relief.
Then, its face crinkled up like a chrysanthemum…
“It’s all over, he really is a member of the ‘Bonfire Outstanding Talent Nurturing’ program! How is that possible at D Level? That’s against the company owners’ ancient teachings, isn’t it?”

chapters.title: Chapter 422 - 422 383 The Ancient God Hit List (6.2K)_4
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 422: Chapter 383 “The Ancient God Hit List”! (6.2K)_4 Chapter 422: Chapter 383 “The Ancient God Hit List”! (6.2K)_4 “Who the hell did this, so unscrupulous!”
“Don’t they know that joining the plan before reaching C Level will incur divine punishment?!”
Fire Tree muttered to itself, its face filled with shock and horror. What did it mean to be a member of the “Bonfire Talent Cultivation Plan”?
It meant a walking disaster trigger!
It was called the “Bonfire Talent Cultivation Plan,” but Fire Tree remembered, before it was contained, this list had another name among their circles—
“Ancient God Hunting List”!
This was a list of eradication targets designated by the Ancient Gods themselves!
In that era, once the members of the list were discovered, and their seeds began to scatter, it almost certainly provoked the appearance of great entities!
They did it to eradicate the targets before they succeeded…
However, after being captured by the company, they were forbidden to refer to those high entities as “Great Gods,” “Ancient Gods,” or “Supreme Wills.”
Instead, they could only use “Level One Containment Subject,” or “Super First Class Containment Subject,” and the likes for reference.
Otherwise, they would undergo extremely pitiful and painful torture.
Fire Tree vaguely remembered a Clan that chose death over compliance, until their “Great Entity” was caught too and then placed before them to be brutally tortured and dismembered.
The Clan members had no choice but to tearfully opt for “voluntary” compromise, let down their psychological defenses, and were severely injected with humanizing substances, undergoing deep physical, mental, and even soul-level transformations, ultimately falling into humanity…
Of course, the Gods they worshipped did not escape this fate either, vaguely recalling that they were locked in the “City of Scripts” for a more advanced transformation…
This was also a reason why some great… Level One Containment Subjects would personally intervene.
The conflict between both sides was beyond the simple life-and-death struggle…
“I’m just a small, insignificant Third Level containment subject, how did I get involved in such a huge vortex?”
Fire Tree felt, associating with such entities, its future was surely destined to be bleak.
And most importantly, this one was only D Level, not yet at a stage where it could stand alone, nor had it received further protection. Going out was like a torch in the darkness, very eye-catching…
Plus, there were some company upheavals it faintly sensed but wasn’t certain about.
Perhaps, even at C Level, effective protection might not be guaranteed these days, not to mention D Level. Who knows when an avenging higher entity might seek them out for annihilation!
“No, I must escape! I have to take flight! Oh, seems like I’ve lost the bucket, but still, I need to run!”
Fire Tree clung to its novel video game and snacks, and while muttering to itself, thought of some methods used by its seniors in the containment circle…
It had to find an opportunity to lower its containment level. The lower the containment level, the less attention it drew, and the more likely it would get a chance to escape with poor quality gear.
Fire Tree faintly remembered an elder who had successfully fled using this tactic.
It even spitefully stole a space bucket from the company on its way out.
Its grand deed became a legend in the Third Containment world!
Of course, such actions came at a great cost, and it hesitated whether it should really flee…
Escaping was not merely about running; if it were caught and brought back, the consequences would be very, very dire.
…
“2 a.m., still okay, not too late…”
After coming out, Colin checked the time, then thought about tomorrow’s actions, so he took out his phone to contact Qin Chuan, ignoring some routine reports and asking him to work a little overtime.
He could handle tomorrow’s mission by himself, but two hundred kilometers was outside his jurisdiction. To avoid unexpected situations and conflicts, it was better to coordinate the handover.
If possible, he could also try to perform another one against nineteen, accumulating some merits.
To quickly become an official Sixth Level Personnel to investigate the “Book of Fate”…
Meanwhile, after sending the message to Qin Chuan, Colin then reached out to Old Master Wu, wanting to understand the capabilities related to “Fate Propeller” adepts.
After all, the “Reset” method of those like the “Fate Propeller” D Level Personnel on the train was quite troublesome.
It was hard enough to kill someone, then just a “Reset” would bring them back to full health.
Luckily, the ones encountered before were not powerful D Level Personnel. If more formidable C Level “Fate Propeller” company renegades were encountered, then it would most likely be an unwinnable fight…
However, after sending the message, there was no response.
Colin didn’t think much of it, pulled up the blanket, closed his eyes, and left the hustle to Qin Chuan and the others.
.
.
.
PS: Asking for monthly tickets at the beginning of the month!

chapters.title: Chapter 423 - 423 384 The Perfect Girl from the Starry
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 423: Chapter 384 The “Perfect Girl” from the Starry Skies_1 Chapter 423: Chapter 384 The “Perfect Girl” from the Starry Skies_1 The next day, 8 AM.
Colin had woken up after just five hours of sleep.
After a routine shower, which included brushing his teeth and washing his face, he slowly made his way downstairs and found a street food stall to have breakfast.
Even though he had a task coming up, he was not the same person he was a few months ago.
He wouldn’t get so nervous about a mission that he couldn’t eat; however, as he ate, Colin realized he was eating a bit too much…
Early in the morning, he had consumed five servings of steamed rice noodle rolls, attracting some odd looks from people at the other stalls.
One by one, they seemed surprised that someone who didn’t look particularly overweight could eat so much…
‘I must have been inadvertently influenced by “Hunger”; I need to control my appetite.’
Colin shook his head, took a deep breath, and suppressed the subtle desire to eat that bubbled up in his heart.
For him, eating a lot wasn’t a problem in itself; the problem with the act of “eating” was that it was liable to trigger some undesirable reactions in his body…
“With this thing inside, if I want to gain weight or something, I’ll probably have to be force-fed like a duck, with food pumped directly into my stomach, right?”
Colin murmured to himself, then got up to pay and leave.
Outside the food stall, Qin Chuan and others had been waiting for a while. Seeing him approach, they hurriedly opened the car door…
“Where did you learn that kind of service?”
Colin chuckled, not bothering with formalities and got straight into the car. Once everyone was on board, he continued:
“Any response from the neighboring district?”
Upon hearing Colin’s question, Qin Chuan shook his head, “No, they agreed to our intervention from outside the area, but they’re curious about how we knew about the anomaly there. They’ll probably have some questions when we meet.”
“Let them ask, as long as they’ve agreed to outside intervention, that’s all that matters.”
Colin didn’t much care and leaned back in his seat.
At that moment, seeing that the conversation between the two had ended, Hu Zheng spoke up, “Boss, are we bringing along those ‘Destiny Propeller’ personnel for this mission…”
“I’ll decide once I get there and assess how difficult the mission is.”
If the mission wasn’t from Bonfire Company but a general type of official mission, Colin wouldn’t mind bringing along the uninitiated, as official missions lacked the element of surprise and vexing hidden agendas typical of company tasks.
But for missions from the company, careful preparation was necessary.
“Alright.” Hu Zheng didn’t object, after all, with more bystanders, his “experience” would lessen…
Currently, their work consisted of missions within their jurisdiction and those assigned to Colin personally.
Under normal circumstances, missions assigned to Colin himself had the highest priority.
Jurisdictional missions were like weekly cleaning chores; when the time came, Colin would lead the team to sweep through them.
Looking at Colin pretending to nap with his eyes closed, Hu Zheng couldn’t help but inwardly shake his head in awe. Since following Mr. Colin, those difficult and often deadly missions that were but a common occurrence when they followed Fourth or Fifth Level Personnel seemed like a thing of the past…
With them, all they had to do was gain experience by training together, without the need to worry about any dangers.
About two hours later, the car exited the highway and drove into a secluded office building.
Soon, Colin found himself in a conference room, sitting across from the person responsible for the area—a man in his thirties, who looked somewhat unhealthy and pale…
His identity was that of a Fifth Level Official Personnel.
Besides him, there were two other Fifth Level Personnel in the office, though their specific ranks were slightly lower.
Once Colin was seated, the pale-faced man began, “We won’t waste words. Let’s get straight to the point, Mr. Colin. I want to know how you found out there would be a cultist ritual happening nearby?”
He had only received some intelligence the night before, and before they could prepare an operation, the people from the neighboring city had already called them.
This made him feel somewhat strange…
When questioned, Colin thought for a moment and replied, “Confidential.”
“Uh…” The Fifth Level Official Personnel did not expect to be stymied by the first question.
After thinking for a bit, he continued to inquire about how and when Colin received the information, including the source of the intelligence.
However, Colin answered every question with a calm and straightforward “confidential.”
He even seemed to have no intention of disclosing the mission personnel to them…
“This isn’t very conducive to cooperation, is it?” One of the deputies frowned and spoke up.
“Oh?”
Colin was taken aback, then said, “Oh, my apologies. I’m not here to seek cooperation; I’m here to do a job. If possible, give me someone familiar with the local situation, and I can start the mission.”
As he said this, he glanced at Qin Chuan, figuring this guy probably hadn’t explained the situation properly.
As for these people not recognizing him, Colin wasn’t surprised. His identity was only known to a very few inside the organization, and others who had interacted with him, even if they had seen his abilities, seemed to have had their memories handled afterward…
It could be said that Old Master Wu’s approach to him was to assist him as much as possible without interfering too much with him personally.
“That’s a group of extremely vicious cultists, comrade; aren’t you being a bit too casual?” The other deputy spoke out sternly.
‘Ah, well, I’m being serious enough, aren’t I? For an F Level mission, I even went to the trouble of repairing a few pieces of my usual equipment…’
Colin muttered in his mind without getting annoyed and casually reached into his pocket.

chapters.title: Chapter 424 - 424 384 The Perfect Girl from the Starry
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 424: Chapter 384 The “Perfect Girl” from the Starry Skies_2 Chapter 424: Chapter 384 The “Perfect Girl” from the Starry Skies_2 A document was tossed onto the desk…
Several Fifth Level Personnel who were about to speak were momentarily stunned, then one of them picked it up and looked at it. His pupils contracted when he saw the signature, which contained only a few lines, roughly indicating that any decision and arrangement made by Colin must be fully supported…
At the bottom of the document, there were as many as seven or eight official stamps.
Stamps from “The Great Wall No. 1 Office,” “Fate Hub Office,” “First Level Agents Joint Office,” and so on were all there…
All from the highest level of certification stamps of the internal departments!
In the signature column, there was a name equally well-known, a big shot from the “Fate Propeller” pathway: Xu Duojin!
“It can’t be fake, can it?” The Fifth Level Official Personnel felt a tingling in his scalp as he gazed at it.
Each stamp could make a small area tremble if taken out alone, not to mention that this document nearly included them all.
Soon, from the unique aura of the stamps, he confirmed that the document was indeed genuine!
However, to avoid any accidents, he still made a call in front of Colin…
A few seconds later, the call ended…
“It is indeed genuine, but who on Earth can get hold of such a document?!”
He couldn’t help but raise his head and take another look at Colin but saw nothing more than an ordinary person. However, the more ordinary he seemed, the more enigmatic Colin appeared at this moment…
Shaking his head, he stood up and carefully handed the document back.
“I understand, what should we do?”
If only you were this cooperative earlier, Colin grumbled internally, then glanced at a clock in the meeting room: “Just find someone familiar with the local geography to accompany me.”
This mission was time-sensitive.
But the requirement was not to act as quickly as possible, but to disrupt the ritual at a critical moment during the ceremony.
Not too early, nor too late…
Of course, the mission briefing mentioned that, if possible, it would be best to wait until the ritual was successful and then kill the entity summoned by the ritual.
Doing so would increase the mission rewards…
But Colin felt this was too risky, prone to mishaps, and he had no intention of taking such a gamble.
“Then I’ll accompany you…” the Fifth Level Official in charge thought for a moment and stood up.
Upon hearing this, Colin gave him a look and then nodded.
“However, to prevent any accidents, you won’t be coming this time,” Colin said, turning to Hu Zheng.
“Alright…”
The latter scratched his head feeling a bit disappointed, but didn’t say anything and showed obedience to the arrangement.
“Mr. Colin, when do we start the action?” the Fifth Level Official Personnel asked.
Although Colin was ostensibly of the same level as him, in a relationship of equals, he understood after seeing the document.
The other’s equality seemed to be a bit more equal than his…
He just didn’t understand why such a person was still at the Fifth Level within the internal hierarchy.
“No rush, we’ll act after the afternoon; first, I’ll review your intelligence,” Colin said.
This time, the Fifth Level Personnel was quite cooperative…
They had learned a few days ago from a mole who had infiltrated the “Dawn Star” cult, that the cultists would perform a summoning ceremony today, but the exact location was still unclear.
The mole took a risk infiltrating their ranks, and now there was no word from him. He had only managed to send out some codes before losing contact.
From these, they could roughly determine the direction should be within a certain body of water…
“So far, we have requested several battleships and aerial units for a firepower deployment, also we’ve sought assistance from a Seventh Level high-ranking official within the province, just waiting for the scouting team we sent out to find the location…”
“No need to search anymore, I’ve got a rough idea of the direction, it’s just the environment I’m not familiar with,” Colin interrupted.
Hearing Colin’s words, the Level 5 Personnel had a strange expression, feeling as though the person from the neighboring city knew more about the situation than he did.
Ignoring the other’s gaze, Colin continued, “Tell me what you know about this ‘Dawn Star’ cult…”
He remembered that in a previous fight, he seemed to have heard of this power…
But he wasn’t very certain.
At the time, he had too many enemies—so many that if all the heretic cultists who wanted to chop him down were to send representatives, they’d have to queue up for half an hour. He really couldn’t remember some who performed poorly…
Soon, Colin got the intelligence on this cult from the official personnel.
This was a cult that worshipped the stars and believed in the “Lady of Dawn’s Starlight.” Most of the members were adept at attacking their enemies through means such as painting, singing, and the like.
“They refer to the ‘Lady of Dawn’s Starlight’ as the most perfect girl or lady from the universe, and they have an obsession with her that’s distinct from other cults. Rumor has it that all who have heard her voice or seen her image will be mesmerized, falling deeply into infatuation, both physically and psychologically…”
“In addition, they are one of the few cults capable of teleportation, making them hard to capture…”
“Their presence can be found all over the world, though their size is not as large as that of ‘Red Moon’…”
The Fifth Level Personnel introduced the intelligence to Colin bit by bit.
‘Psychological and physiological infatuation? That is indeed special. I wonder just how perfect the most perfect girl is…’
‘But then, is the reason our mission requires such critical timing due to their propensity to flee, hence the need for such precise timing?’
Reflecting deeply, Colin was about to ask some more questions when he heard a burst of hurried footsteps coming from outside the meeting room.
“Mr. Lu Yang, it’s terrible, an investigation team has gone missing!”
A staff member rushed in, speaking anxiously to everyone in the meeting hall.
“What? Which direction did they go?” The Fifth Level in charge, Lu Yang, immediately stood up.
“It’s the C31 Zone Waters, the last message came ten minutes ago…”
“So they were hiding there? No wonder we couldn’t find them no matter how hard we searched. They’ve changed locations, we…”
The Fifth Level in charge turned his head toward his nine o’clock direction, wanting to get someone to take action immediately, but after taking a deep breath to steady his emotions, he instead turned to Mr. Colin, who was holding top-level documents.
“I was originally planning to go tonight, but since people are trapped, let’s start now. You just lead the way.”
“Okay, thank you for this.”
Lu Yang immediately got up and led Colin towards the target location.
However, they had only walked a few steps and just reached the edge of a sandy beach by the coast, not yet boarding the helicopter, when Colin, who was following behind, stopped him: “Are you sure it’s that direction?”
Colin sensed something; that place was almost the opposite direction from where his mission indicated.
“Yes… In the C19 Waters, dozens of nautical miles away, there is a small archipelago. If the cultists are truly nearby, they should be operating there…” Lu Yang explained to Colin.
Hearing this, Colin did not respond immediately, but instead looked at the opposite area.
He was certain that the direction specified by the mission and the one the other party intended to go were completely different.
‘There’s something wrong with the direction. Under these circumstances, there are two possibilities. Either they encountered a different incident, or there’s something happening over there, a feint to distract attention…’
As the thoughts flickered through his mind, Colin decisively issued an order: “You have others head to the C19 Waters. You come with me this way. If we’re lucky, we should be able to find that search team over here…”
“This Area B… Alright then.” The Fifth Level official hesitated for a moment, but then nodded.
He also remembered that the last signal from the undercover agent who had lost contact was pointing in the very direction that Colin had indicated.
However, this time Colin did not choose to go by helicopter.
“Helicopters and regular boats make too much noise; let’s use this instead…”
As Colin spoke, some silver haze drifted from him, condensing over the sea surface into a large surfboard. He didn’t delay any further and directly stepped onto the surfboard created by the Nano Intellectual Mechanism…
Behind him, the Fifth Level Personnel hesitated briefly before stepping on as well.
Once the two were standing firm, a surge of force came from beneath the surfboard, propelling it quickly in a certain direction.
Its noise was almost nonexistent compared to a regular motorboat or helicopter.
But its speed was not inferior in the slightest…
About fifteen minutes later, Colin suddenly had a feeling and had the Little Maid stop their advance. He then grabbed the Fifth Level official with one hand and took out the “Emblem of the Humility Knight” with the other, holding his breath.
In an instant, a Secret Force enveloped them, rapidly diminishing their presence…
And just a few seconds later, several lines of sight passed by from under the sea surface.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 425 - 425 385 The Bizarre Dawn Star Church._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 425: Chapter 385 The Bizarre “Dawn Star” Church._1 Chapter 425: Chapter 385 The Bizarre “Dawn Star” Church._1 Deep beneath the sea, a few figures clung to sharks, observing from below…
“There seemed to have been some disturbance earlier…”
“You must have seen it wrong, that was probably just the movement of sea birds, I didn’t feel anything…”
“…Probably… continue to patrol…”
The faint whispers emerged from beneath the water, and Colin stood just above them in the waters, the linear distance not exceeding thirty meters. Under the influence of the “Emblem of the Humility Knight,” even though their gazes swept over their heads several times, it was as if they saw nothing and consistently missed them.
And their conversation could just be vaguely heard by Colin, whose senses were different from ordinary people.
As for the Fifth Level Official Personnel he had caught, he didn’t hear anything at all, only noticing that Colin suddenly became alert and put his finger to his lips to shush, thereby realizing there might be something around.
After a while, the cultists patrolling on sharks departed…
Colin then retracted his hand.
Seeing that the situation seemed stable, the Fifth Level Personnel made a hand signal. Colin didn’t quite understand it, but he roughly got the meaning: Are they gone?
“They’re gone for now.”
Colin nodded and, before the other could say more, asked, “Is there anywhere nearby where we can land?”
Now, as they drew nearer to their destination, the guidance became somewhat vague, as if it were harder to discern the true nature of their surroundings in the midst of it…
‘Why do I feel like the mission guidance is less clear here on Earth than it was in the Other World…’
A thought flashed through his mind.Meanwhile, the Fifth Level Personnel, intending to ask something upon hearing Colin’s words, pondered for a moment, surveyed the surroundings—especially pausing at several sea buoys—and then quickly pointed in a few directions:
“If you go about a dozen nautical miles in this direction, you’ll soon see a sandy island. Over there, a few nautical miles away, there is a patch of reefs…”
After pointing out six or seven places in succession, he said, “If this group of cultists is in this sea area, then these few places all have a significant chance of their presence. Of course, there’s also a fair chance that they are at some other secret location…”
“Hmm… Let’s first take a look at the reef.”
Colin spoke up, the direction significantly different from the patrolling figures, but his intuition made him feel there might be something there.
Afterward, without waiting to see if the other person objected, Colin told the Little Maid to get moving again.
Their pace slowed down once more, the progress even more secretive…
A few minutes later, Colin caught sight of the reefs mentioned by the other person—an assortment of hard rocks covered in a variety of shellfish, with a peculiar scent wafting vaguely from beneath them.
“If they’re here, they must have used some method to carve out a cave or something similar under the water. These ‘Dawn Star’ cultists are indeed adept at such things…” the Fifth Level Official whispered.
As he spoke, he looked at Colin as if to suggest that in such a situation, it would be advisable to return and invite some specialized extraordinary personnel to come over.
Otherwise, it would be rather difficult to locate the entrance to the reef…
Moreover, if they were not specialized personnel, they might locate the spot only to have the group of cultists slip away.
Before he could finish speaking, he saw Colin take him to leap above the sea surface where the surfboard transformed into a field of silver mist and sank into the water.
“These people are quite cunning. There’s no surveillance at the target site. If we followed their patrol members, we would likely be led to somewhere entirely different…”
Colin remembered, occasionally sensing some underwater cultist figures.
None of these figures came close to this area; instead, they all headed for different regions…
The search wasn’t quick as, to avoid accidents, the Little Maid moved cautiously, taking more than an hour. Sitting on a rock, scorched by the fierce sun, Colin finally received new feedback from the Little Maid.
“Found it, 1.7 kilometers away, two hundred meters beneath the water, there’s an underwater cave that fits the bill, with signs of life and not weak ones.”
Colin looked up at the western-tilting sun and slowly stood up from the rock.
“Have we confirmed the location?” The Fifth Level Personnel, upon hearing this, was elated and also stood up.
Once the direction was determined, they could begin to plan and request higher-level officials to come…
“It’s pretty much confirmed…”
Colin, following the direction provided by the Little Maid, was almost certain the location was accurate.
Next was to infiltrate…
Seeing Colin’s movement, the Fifth Level Personnel realized he seemed prepared to take further action himself and was momentarily stunned, “If that is indeed an enemy’s nest over there, I suggest we better return now and proceed with a covert operation, to avoid alarming the enemy…
“Moreover, this will also be safer for us…
“Otherwise, if there’s an accident…”
Pausing, he glanced at Colin—how could someone of such a “modest” status take responsibility if anything happened here?
But he didn’t finish his thought and shifted his tone: “I have already requested the presence of a Level 7 expert. As long as he can come over, everything will be resolved…”
“Level 7? I’m afraid Level 7 might not be quite capable of dealing with this situation…”
Colin received feedback from the Little Maid, feeling fairly certain that this mission went far beyond F Level.
It would be more prudent if D Level Personnel were to carry it out…
Colin wasn’t surprised by this development; after all, from what he understood so far, Bonfire Company not only considered an employee’s rank but also their actual combat power when assigning missions.

chapters.title: Chapter 426 - 426 385
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 426: 385 Chapter 426: 385 That is to say, as long as the employees can endure hardship, there will always be endless hardship to endure…
But what it controls rather well is ensuring that the employees aren’t overwhelmed by hardship all at once; rather, it achieves sustainable suffering.
At the same time, upon hearing Colin’s words, the Fifth Level Personnel was startled.
“Level Seven Members can’t handle the situation here?”
He instinctively found it hard to believe, because Level Seven indicates domestic senior management, capable enough to solve most problems. If even they couldn’t handle it, then the situation here was somewhat beyond his imagination.
But considering this man’s uniqueness, he realized that, perhaps, what the other party said was true…
In an instant, his breathing became slightly restrained, “Then…”
He wanted to suggest calling for Eighth Level Personnel to intervene, but since the disappearance of Liping from this region for unknown reasons, the upper levels simply couldn’t spare more Eighth Level Personnel to take charge. They had always been jointly managed by three Level Seven Personnel!
Of course, to say there were no Eighth Level Personnel wouldn’t be correct, as there was one inside Base Number Five.
Only, the one from Base Number Five was impossible to pry away from the base…
The local governmental forces also didn’t have the authority to mobilize much of Base Number Five’s power, whose influence only obeyed orders from the central upper echelons…
As for transferring people from other regions, it wasn’t impossible either, but who knows how long it would take for them to arrive with all that procedure.
Wrong!
The Fifth Level Personnel looked at Colin, remembering the document in his hand.
This man, with a document of almost the highest clearance, akin to those who bore imperial mandates in ancient times, symbolically also represented the will of the central hub. If he were to step forward, maybe he could request that top-tier force from within Base Number Five…
However, as a myriad of thoughts flashed through his mind, he had just formed an idea when he heard the other party say, “What are you still standing there for? Let’s go.”
“Ah?” The Fifth Level Personnel was taken aback, watching Colin’s figure moving forward:
“Wait, are you saying we’re going to solve it?”
“What else?” Colin said as a matter of course, as he set the Nano Intellectual Mechanism to expand into a small diving apparatus.
Diving tens of thousands of meters into the deep sea was impossible, but a few hundred meters was not a big problem.
Even if an explosion occurred a few hundred meters deep, with his physical condition, he wouldn’t have to worry about being torn apart by the seawater…
“You said that even Level Seven Personnel are fundamentally unable to resolve the situation here, right?” The Fifth Level Personnel still didn’t understand.
He still couldn’t discern Colin’s strength and could only guess that the other might be carrying some special items, but no matter what, his capabilities, at best, would reach Sixth or Seventh Level…
“So, that’s why I’m here, isn’t it?”
“You’re here?” The Fifth Level Personnel hadn’t quite caught on yet.
Colin had no idea that so many thoughts had just raced through the other’s mind.
Seeing that the other hadn’t moved yet, he reached out with his left hand, grabbed his shoulder, and then leapt into the diving apparatus transformed from the Little Maid.
Afterward, he took a deep breath and held it.
In the blink of an eye, a Secret Force was bestowed upon him, rapidly reducing the presence of all things related to him.
Moreover, during this period, any noise he made would also have an extremely low presence.
In his current Status, as long as he didn’t engage in vigorous movements, he could easily hold his breath until the maximum use time of this tool, which was thirty minutes…
However, it was not even five minutes later when the two of them encountered a fissure beneath a dark reef.
Following the fissure down, they entered through a very narrow passage; after about a dozen meters, like reflecting from the bottom, they passed a bend and a tunnel leading upwards appeared…
Although the above was utterly dark, Colin could already sense the presence of some people.
“It’s not easy for these Cultists, managing to find such a secluded area in a place like this to secretly conduct their rituals,” Colin murmured to himself, then commanded the Little Maid to continue upwards.
About ten seconds later, they surfaced from the water and saw the entrance to a cavern.
It was at this moment that the Fifth Level Personnel felt a chill run down his scalp because he saw three brown-haired foreigners, Cultists, positioned at different spots at the cave entrance…
They had appeared directly in front of the enemy!
However, the next second, to his surprise, the item in the hands of the employee carrying the “all-powerful” document still worked wonders; they stood right in front of these people, yet it was as if they were never seen…
The others kept discussing some intriguing objects.
“Ah, the ritual is about to begin… I’m so excited, looking forward to the ‘Dawn Star’s’ favor, longing for her tentacles to harshly lash against my body…”
“Too gentle, too gentle, only a recent convert like you would enjoy such unexciting things. Unlike me, I hope she uses that thing of hers to tear my mouth open and pour relentlessly into it…”
“I want to stretch out my tongue and lick her portrait…”
“…I’ve washed every corner of my body clean and tidy…”
…
“Ah, heavy taste, it’s got to be Western…”
Although he already knew from intelligence reports that the ‘Dawn Star’ Cultists were a bit strange compared to other cults, hearing these words still nearly made Colin burst out laughing…
He felt as if he hadn’t come to a den of Cultists but to a certain… adult establishment.
“And who exactly is this so-called most beautiful girl, ‘Dawn Star’?… The name sounds quite normal, certainly better than Followers of the ‘Red Moon’, but why are their actions and behaviors even more outrageous than those of the Followers of the ‘Red Moon’?”
Colin’s gaze swept over a Cultist and could smell the heavy scent of blood on him.

chapters.title: Chapter 427 - 427 385 The Bizarre Dawn Star Church. _3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 427: Chapter 385: The Bizarre “Dawn Star” Church. _3 Chapter 427: Chapter 385: The Bizarre “Dawn Star” Church. _3 And he could see, beneath the clothes, those self-inflicted wounds…
However, after only a brief pause, he continued to hold onto the Fifth Level Personnel, crossed several guards, and arrived at the entrance of a tunnel with multiple branches. He sniffed the air and then moved deeper into it.
The marks he would leave behind were all cleaned up by some Nano Intellectual Mechanisms…
Even the bubbles he left in the water when he surfaced were completely eliminated.
While holding his breath, these footprints would go unnoticed, but as soon as he released the effect, everything would return to normal.
“Unless I actively attack, it would probably take a Level Seven Official to sense anything. Well, this isn’t accurate either…”
“If it’s an Extraordinary One with special sensitivity like the ‘Destiny Propeller,’ perhaps a Sixth Level or even a Fifth Level might notice.”
“I still need to be careful…”
As thoughts flickered through his mind, Colin’s left hand held onto the shoulder of the Fifth Level Personnel, while his right hand’s ring transformed into a revolver, the barrel tucked into his pocket, ready for a quick “American Iaido” if necessary.
At this moment, walking through the complex tunnels, Colin couldn’t help but think: “If it weren’t for the possible involvement of some higher entity, would it not be perfect to use a ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’ right now?”
Unfortunately, using one now would almost be like telling the higher entity behind the scenes—
I’m coming to raid your place.“Probably only a higher entity from the ‘Destiny Propeller’ Path could observe without harm; others can only crudely borrow this power, and using it might be as good as seeking death…”
Colin sighed silently and suddenly caught a whiff of a bloody scent distinct from that of the cultists.
After thinking for a moment, he adjusted his footsteps and headed in that direction.
Soon after, a series of feeble screams could be heard from the front of the tunnel…
At that time, something dawned on the Fifth Level Personnel, and he seemed to realize something.
“Shh.”
Colin put a finger to his lips.
From the other’s reaction, he could roughly guess that the one screaming must be the undercover agent sent into the Church.
Before long, in a man-made cave, the two of them saw the undercover agent.
Right now, he was clearly caught because he adventured too deep, and now he was tied to a stone column with iron wires full of thorns; his appearance was miserable.
Starting from the scalp, his head was sliced open in three parts like a banana…
Above the grotesque mass of blood and flesh, a salty seawater, thick with salt, dripped down from the top of his head.
Falling upon a skull now lacking the protection of skin and tissue…
“Ah!!!”
The bound undercover agent screamed in agony.
Seeing this, the Fifth Level Personnel’s eyes split with rage, involuntarily wanting to rescue him but restrained by Colin.
‘In order not to let him die, they’ve done some blood-stopping treatment, and now he’s in a semi-comatose state, which turns out to be a good thing… and this wound, though scary-looking, is actually treatable…’
Colin slightly narrowed his eyes, retracting his gaze from the man and looking towards other areas of the cave.
He discovered many other tortured individuals besides the undercover agent, totaling over a dozen…
Surprisingly, there were followers of “Red Moon” among them!
“Aaagh! You filthy masochists! Have the guts to kill me! Else, you will regret it sooner or later! My Master will purify this land, will exorcise you heretics, leaving none behind!”
At this moment, this nearly skinless “Red Moon” follower screamed and roared in rage.
Just as Colin was reflecting on the followers of “Red Moon” for their cockroach-like resilience…
Footsteps suddenly arose from outside the cave.
Someone was coming…
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 428 - 428 386 The Missing True God Container _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 428: Chapter 386 The Missing “True God Container” _1 Chapter 428: Chapter 386 The Missing “True God Container” _1 “Crack.”
Before the sound of approaching footsteps could be heard, an invisible limb arrived first, striking the head of a “Red Moon” follower. His neck broke with a sound, hanging limply over his shoulder as if dead.
The swearing also ceased in that instant…
However, not even two seconds later, the muscles in the “Red Moon” follower’s neck began to twitch…
His previously dilated and unfocused pupils rapidly regained their usual sharpness during the process.
“Damn sadists…”
The cursing voice returned.
“The life force of the ‘Red Moon’ followers is indeed tenacious to not die from that.”
Colin watched from the side, clicking his tongue in amazement. It was his first encounter with these people, and with Bone Spur in his possession, a tool that could ensure a hit for each attempt, he had thought they were all fragile weaklings.
But it was only after he stopped using Bone Spur that he realized how astonishingly robust their vitality was.
Common types of injuries hardly caused them any lethal damage.
“These ‘Red Moon’ bastards are truly disgusting, not dying like that…”
“If it weren’t for the fact that their vitality is needed for the action later, I wouldn’t want to see them at all…”
“Indeed, just like cockroaches. Anyway, let’s move quickly. Evening will be upon us soon…”
“This is the best spot to observe the ‘Dawn Star,’ except that it’s not on the surface; everything else is perfect…”
A few members of the “Dawn Star” organization walked by, their faces filled with disgust as they spoke, passing by Colin without noticing the presence of others around them.
Colin’s gaze swept over these individuals. They were all wearing dull hooded robes, and although their skin seemed normal, it was marred with numerous wounds, whether from enemies or self-inflicted was unknown.
Quickly, under the covert observation of the two, they moved all the punished personnel out of the area…
Only at this moment did Colin realize that the individuals these people were looking for, aside from that undercover spy, seemed to be strange characters from other forces.
Afterward, they locked the group in a cart and left the cave.
Colin didn’t immediately follow them. Instead, after making sure that there was no one else around, he took out an oxygen mask with a small built-in breathing canister, took a breath, and only then did he follow the faint scent in the air.
About ten minutes later, Colin and his companion arrived in a spacious cave hall filled with pleasurable shouts and sounds of whipping echoing throughout.
A large number of people were inflicting wounds on themselves using various methods.
And those who had been brought here earlier were piled up within a ritual array.
Apart from the dozen or so punished individuals Colin had seen before, there were many other captured individuals he hadn’t seen, totaling over a hundred.
Next to Colin, a Fifth Level official member, sensing the strength of some of the “Dawn Star” higher-ups inside, involuntarily held his breath, realizing that Colin’s earlier words were no exaggeration; ordinary Level Seven Personnel would mostly be unable to resolve the issue here…
Because all the wanted high-ups of this organization were now basically concentrated here!
‘Indeed a small organization, overall very weak…’
After briefly sensing the area, Colin did not feel the presence of any being with “Divinity.”If he were truly F Level, it might be a bit difficult…
But he was not jumping in and killing indiscriminately right now simply because the time was not right.
‘With this level of strength, I’m starting to doubt what kind of power the entity that “Dawn Star” has brought in from behind is.’
Colin muttered to himself, his gaze turning to the center, where a peculiar stone lay…
An exceptionally beautiful, pitch-black and translucent mineral crystal studded with many reflective points, it looked like a star chart when viewed from above.
However, he didn’t ponder over it too much. They had been waiting for a long time, occasionally leaving the place to get some fresh air, and after almost two hours, the ritual finally began…
Countless followers of the “Dawn Star” were shouting a certain name while whipping themselves with spiked whips.
Stimulated by the pain, their spirits became increasingly exuberant, and the spiritual energy that overflowed from them began to gather on the mineral crystal…
Soon, the crystal stones became even darker, and the points of light within twinkled like stars. After a moment, all the starlight dimmed except for one crystal point that became extremely bright.
If at this moment, Colin were looking up at the starry sky from the sea’s surface, he would feel that one normally imperceptible starlight was now dazzlingly bright.
It seemed that some entity was about to arrive from an unknown and distant place…
Colin felt a sense of crisis welling up within him, and the spiritual feedback in his mind already vaguely provided an image of a voluptuous female figure cloaked in starlight.
The proportions of her body invoked an involuntary sense of “perfection.”
The starlight in the black mineral crystal, at this moment, was slowly descending into this space, aided by the spiritual power of the “Dawn Star” believers…
‘I’m not sure what the “Dawn Star” behind the scenes looks like, but the one coming here is at most an avatar with a certain “Divinity.” It’s not particularly strong, and if captured successfully, that would settle the tuition fees for the “Light Chaser.” Otherwise, relying solely on the meager savings from the “Firebrand Tree,” I could at best craft some equipment. The key still depends on me…’
‘However, my instincts tell me this thing runs very fast, which is a bit troublesome…’
‘Right, I must find a way to capture it in one go…’
Colin’s gaze flickered. He hadn’t intended to take such a risk, but after sensing its strength, he immediately came up with quite a few ideas about the “Star Maiden,” planning to forcefully take her away in full view of these people…

chapters.title: Chapter 429 - 429 386 The Missing True God Container _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 429: Chapter 386 The Missing “True God Container” _2 Chapter 429: Chapter 386 The Missing “True God Container” _2 Make a killing for the company by racking up points!
While Colin was contemplating how to make his move without letting the other party escape, the Fifth Level Official Personnel he was grabbing by the shoulder felt an increasing pressure there and a chilling aura in the air, harbouring an entirely different set of thoughts.
At this very moment, he felt that every second spent in this cursed place could lead to sudden death…
The existence that followed the starlight brought a tremendous sense of oppression to his heart.
With a slight shift of his gaze, the Fifth Level Personnel who saw Colin’s expression growing ever more “grave,” immediately realized that the situation was dire.
This person, who had always appeared so carefree…
Now seemed so serious, which was enough to indicate one thing—the situation was extremely bad!
‘No, if we’re really discovered, I must find a way to ensure his safe departure; otherwise…’
The thought of such a high-ranking member dying within his domain made the Fifth Level Personnel feel as though the sky were collapsing.
Even though, in his view, the whole predicament was entirely due to Colin’s reckless intrusion…
No matter what, he must not let him die here.
And it was at this time, he was thinking of persuading Colin to leave this place quietly before they were discovered…
But just then, as if what one fears most is bound to happen, a sudden change occurred.
“Who’s there?! Show yourself!”
Were we discovered?!
The Fifth Level Official Personnel felt a shock, and as he was preparing to urge Colin to flee while he covered for him with his life, he felt a force pressing down on his shoulder, silencing all his words.
Simultaneously, the entire cave tremored as the walls seemed to become animated.
The cold cavern writhed like the intestines of a beast…
Under Colin’s gaze, lumps of flesh, like polyps, grew from the undulating cave walls, then fell off like hemorrhoids cut loose, taking the form of figures in blood-red robes!
Followers of the “Red Moon”!
Colin was not particularly surprised by this; he had sensed the presence of some followers of the “Red Moon” lurking nearby earlier on.
At this moment, dozens of followers of the “Red Moon” had just arrived and launched an assault.
“Damned Outer Gods, we shall never allow you to descend upon this land, to taint this beautiful soil!”
“Expel these nefarious Outer Gods with ulterior motives! Victory belongs to the ‘Red Moon,’ long live the ‘Red Moon!'”
“Earth Forbidden Zone, Outer Gods be halted!”
“As long as I am not dead, the Outer Gods shall not lay a finger on our beautiful homeland!”
“Kill them all!”
“…”
A horde of “Red Moon” followers, their bodies sprouted with tentacles, chanted various slogans while brandishing their weapons, attacking…
In the crimson glow, the air around them took on a bizarre activity.
Countless things reacted with animation.
A member of the “Dawn Star” who couldn’t dodge in time was struck in the head by a “Red Moon” follower wielding a unique scepter, and instantly, their body disintegrated on the spot, every organ transforming into an independent entity, growing limbs, and joining the embrace of the “Red Moon”…
“Tsk, somewhat interesting, these lines, if someone else were shouting them, I bet they would stir up quite a bit of passion…”
Colin watched the chaos unfold without any urgency to intervene.
He was surprised but not shocked by the “Red Moon” followers’ actions because he had already read in some documents that these followers were extremely sensitive to the worship of “Outer Gods”…
Most of the time, the official personnel hadn’t even entered the scene before these guys have already detected and intervened.
Even in some particular cases, official personnel from some places occasionally received tip-off letters from “Red Moon” followers about malevolent groups…
Or when confronting certain evil groups and the official personnel were in despair, they would witness “Red Moon” followers rushing to the scene to turn the tides wildly.
Of course, they wouldn’t rescue anyone after arriving but would kill everyone or convert them into their own kind…
Apart from the “Red Moon” followers, adherents of other Outer Gods did similar things.
If you were to summarize the official standpoint…
This group of Outer God followers could accept the failure of their own deity’s descent, but not the successful arrival of another’s belief, which was more unbearable than death to them.
Between each other, they existed in a state of mutual distrust and sabotage.
What sets them apart from the followers of the “Red Moon” is…
Besides reporting, they sometimes even engage in deeper cooperation with the officials to strike against the actions of the “Red Moon” followers.
“The followers of the ‘Red Moon’ have become the hated existence to everyone, and it’s not without reason.”
Although Colin had seen a fair amount of documents after joining the officials, this was his first time seeing it with his own eyes.
In the chaotic battlefield, the “Dawn Star” members were not particularly surprised by the arrival of this group, as every faction was aware of their bad reputation.
They had long been prepared to take action against them!
“Your dog noses are still as sensitive as ever, but it’s of little significance!”
A member of the “Dawn Star” was invigorated, his face flushed with excitement at the thought of contributing to the cause of the girl of his dreams.
For their current operation, they had set up a multitude of false locations all over the globe.
These false locations took on a great deal of the firepower meant for this operation…
Thus, by the time the officials or other forces arrived, the “Perfect Lady” was already able to descend to this place.
By virtue of her special status, the moment she arrived, she could immediately break free and lie dormant atop the Earth.
With the “Star Maiden” as their spiritual totem leading them, the “Dawn Star” would soon become a first-rate power and wouldn’t have to resort to sneaking around for everything like now!
Once the “Star Maiden” adapted to this land, she could become a True God container, embodying the Great Will of the “Dawn Star.”
At that time, they would turn their fortunes around and rise as a dark horse from the countless shadowy forces.
They would become the first force on this land to summon the master’s arrival!
The future looked incredibly promising!
Just as his words ended, the followers of the “Red Moon” became even more intense in their movements.
Some “Red Moon” followers even chose to attempt a breakthrough by self-detonation…
Unfortunately, since the main force had not yet arrived, they failed to break through here, and on the altar above, strange lights flickered frequently as a door slowly began to form…
The figure of the “Star Maiden,” perfect in proportions but unclear in detail to everyone’s eyes, slowly reached out her hand.
“Hahaha, it’s already too late! The emissary of my Lord’s God has arrived! ‘Dawn’s Light’ will become the first existence to return to this land!”
A Grand Elder of the “Dawn Star” turned around, looking towards The Gate of Starlight, preparing to kneel and welcome the other.
However, with a “thud,” his knee had just touched the ground.
When they saw that the figure of the girl, which had just emerged into reality and had not had the chance to unleash her aura, disappeared abruptly…
This situation made everyone present stunned for a moment.
To the point that the fierce battle came to a halt.
At this point, some individuals with higher inspiration could vaguely hear faint sounds emerging in the empty space…
“In… the presence of witnesses, I… fair and just… duel…”
“First, I promise… not to use… and the opponent… cannot use either…”
“…Second… not to use… as a matter of fairness…”
“Third… among the mysterious items… I will only use the props made by… company… as my… for fairness, the enemy must also use only… company props, as my…”
“…”
In the intermittent voice, everyone was dazed, not understanding what was happening.
“What’s going on?! What have you done!”
The “Dawn Star” members looked displeased; they could sense that the “Perfect Lady” sent by the Great Will to lead them was still here, but looking all around for a clue, they found nothing at all.
…
Meanwhile, in the colosseum, Colin smiled as he looked at the exceptionally perfect form before him while slowly drawing out his immensely hungry greatsword:
“I’ve been poor lately, can’t afford bullets, so I’ll settle this with my sword…”
The Dueling Arena effect of the “Shield of Fair Judgment,” besides allowing for one tie in the first fight each day, meant that at other times, one party must surrender and bear the terrifying instant-death curse, becoming a slave with little chance of resistance, or they would be beaten to death…
Colin had no expectation that this external force would surrender.
Since they wouldn’t surrender…
Then they would just have to be beaten to death.

chapters.title: Chapter 430 - 430 387 Subduing the Starlight Maiden_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 430: Chapter 387 Subduing the “Starlight Maiden”_1 Chapter 430: Chapter 387 Subduing the “Starlight Maiden”_1 ‘The three rules of the Arena of Glory perfectly took effect without encountering any resistance…’
‘This confirms that it can be suppressed by the Shield Badge of Fairness and Justice, which means it is far from reaching levels similar to those of a Demigod, Sub-God, or Ancient God as mentioned by “The Light Chaser.” It’s not able to fight me while under the effect of the Shield Badge of Fairness and Justice…’
‘Based on the items and my own feelings, I can almost be certain that it’s not that strong…’
In the midst of these thoughts, Colin held a Golden Card in his left hand and a greatsword in his right, his body covered in flames that surged along his arms into the blade.
At the same time, he was also observing the opponent…
Compared to the fleeting glance in the cave, now that both were in the same space, it was much clearer to see.
This entity lacked a sense of substantiality; it was very tall, over two meters, yet perfectly proportioned, draped in a dark long robe covered in twinkling starlight. Every twinkle sent ripples of light cascading out…
Beneath that dark robe adorned with starlight, there was the outline of a transparent female figure, only perceivable through intuition.
At this moment, feeling the threat from Colin, it rapidly became ethereal after the fight started, scattering into countless lights shooting outward as if trying to escape.
It was difficult to stop this process; Colin’s flames instinctively covered it, but they mostly missed.
If it weren’t for the effect of the “Colosseum,” just that move might have allowed the enemy to escape from this place…
Unfortunately, the act of “running away” violated the rules of the arena.
With a crisp “snap.”
As though an invisible whip had struck something, the scattered starlight instantly reversed, and the figure reemerged.
The tall and perfect form wavered a bit, seemingly quite injured.
Its aura also became noticeably weaker at that moment…
Seeing this, Colin, who was preparing to charge forward, stopped instead, looking at the opponent with a strange expression.
‘How can it be so weak?’
After all, it was a foreign creature summoned by the followers of the “Dawn Star” with great effort. Its aura wasn’t strong, but it seemed of a high order. Yet, a single violation of the rules left it nearly unable to stand as if whipped.
‘It shouldn’t be this weak; is it a trick?’
Colin suspected the opponent was feigning weakness, which made him hesitant to approach immediately.
Of course, if he knew more information, if he knew that this was a creature summoned by the followers of the “Dawn Star” to serve as something like a coordinate or a container, he would have a better understanding of the situation.
While Colin remained cautious, the “Starlight Maiden” adopted a defensive stance.
The dark robe sprinkled with stars twinkled in a unique pattern, sending out layers of radiance, enveloping it like an egg.
At this moment, it was not trying to escape nor to attack…
‘Regardless, it probably doesn’t have information on my ‘Time Stop’ or Bone Spur. I should go up and test its strength with a poke; otherwise, this standoff isn’t getting us anywhere…’
With that thought, Colin no longer hesitated, rapidly closing the distance between them.
During this process, the greatsword in his hand shifted to a Bone Spur.
Then…
Once he was sure the opponent was in effective range, Colin decisively activated the effect of the Time Stop Gold Card, and instantly, the sound of an invisible engine roared in his ears, pulling everything around him into stasis.
‘There is definitely something off…’
Colin, observing the “Starlight Maiden,” could see that the starry points on the dark robe she wore still shone brightly, and even seemed to faintly twitch.
Until now, this was the second entity he had seen, aside from “Red Moon,” that wasn’t fully controlled by “Time Stop.”
Of course, compared with “Red Moon,” it was still far inferior…
But the fact that it wasn’t completely affected was enough to show that the power graded in terms of purity on the opponent was extremely high.
Before seven seconds were up, Colin augmented himself with flames and tore through the outer defense like tearing off a garment, brutally ripping it apart.
Then, in front of the opponent, he stabbed directly down at the invisible figure beneath the dark robe…
The Bone Spur seemed to pass through nothing more than a slightly “sticky” patch of air; he felt nothing else.
But intuition told Colin that he had hit the target.
Thereupon, he no longer lingered; he quickly recoiled to a distance he considered safe.
It was at this moment.
‘Tick-tock, tick-tock…’
The sound of an invisible clock hand ticking arose…
‘Ahh!!!’
A scream of non-human agony came from ahead. This was not a human cry but a special sound, translated by Bonfire Company’s passive translation.
‘The timbre is nice; it seems the effect was quite effective. Could this creature really be so weak?’
Colin, akin to a snake that had bitten its prey and was stealthily observing the reaction, watched the opponent’s response.
At present, the “Starlight Maiden,” upon being stabbed, clutched her abdomen, shaking violently as the dark starry robe flashed more frequently and occasionally drops of black pus fell from underneath…
‘It seems to be unsuited for combat?’
Seeing this, Colin realized the opponent was not laying a trap; it truly was weak.
With this realization, he struck with full force, stepping forward with his right foot and drawing that greatsword again, intending to instantly kill it with a “Matchless Strike”…
After all, the task from Bonfire Company required its body and uniqueness; its soul didn’t matter.

chapters.title: Chapter 431 - 431 387 Subduing the Starlight Maiden_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 431: Chapter 387 Subduing the “Starlight Maiden”_2 Chapter 431: Chapter 387 Subduing the “Starlight Maiden”_2 “Boom!”
The surging flames erupted with a roaring sound…
However, just then, a formless, eerie whisper reached Colin’s ears…
The voice came from the “Shield of Fairness Adjudication.”
Through the passive translation provided by the company, he quickly grasped the gist of the message.
“‘Dawn Starlight’s Shadow’… choose to surrender?”
Colin’s flames stilled for a moment, and he hesitated, giving the tall, seemingly perfect figure in front of him a puzzled look.
Now, the “Shield of Fairness Adjudication” was waiting for his response.
To execute the captive on the spot, or to take him as a prisoner…
If he wished, he could decide the other party’s fate with a mere thought.
Of course, turning the other party into his slave was also an option…
Compared to the motionless former, the latter clearly offered the potential to unlock many more positions.
“‘Dawn Starlight’s Shadow’, doesn’t this name seem more fitting for its identity? But wait, isn’t it some sort of Divine Envoy or something? Is it really okay to surrender like this? Aren’t you afraid of retaliation from the ‘God’ behind you?”
At this thought, Colin’s vigilance rose anew. He still didn’t understand why the Followers of the “Dawn’s Light” went to great lengths to summon such a being.
If it wasn’t for battle, what was it for?
Colin suddenly remembered the priest who wore the robe of flesh and blood and worshipped “Hunger” in the “World Code-13” when he first descended the great cathedral.
Back then, it seemed that the arrival of the “Beast Transformation Syndrome” was caused by being devoured by “Hunger” after one bite of the other.
This one might well choose to commit suicide immediately after being freed.
And then resurrect through some special means from another place…
Or perhaps, after its death, some kind of plague would break out from here and trigger the apocalypse prematurely.
“No, it must be killed!”
Colin’s gaze hardened once more as he looked at the perfectly silhouetted young woman.
And he had to do it himself!
First, use “Matchless Strike” to severely wound and kill her, then use the curse of the “Shield of Fairness Adjudication” to kill her once more…
Sensing his murderous intent, the ‘Dawn Starlight’s Shadow’ trembled slightly.
But just as Colin was ready to reduce her to ashes, a message suddenly appeared on his retina.
[Subsidiary Event One: Capture the living ‘Dawn Starlight’s Shadow’ and hand it over at the end of the mission for additional rewards.]
“Remark”: Try to kill all the Followers of the ‘Dawn Star’ on the scene.
“Hint”: Be wary of other imminent troubles…
…
“Does the company prefer it alive? But what’s this so-called other trouble? More Followers of the ‘Red Moon’ coming?”
Although still puzzled, Colin stopped his hand and refrained from taking further action.
He then acknowledged the other’s status as a “slave.”
The “Arena of Honor” disappeared at that moment.
The entire battle lasted less than three minutes…
But in those three minutes, the cavern hall was littered with corpses everywhere.
“It’s the ‘Starlight Maiden’!”
A Follower of the ‘Dawn’s Light’ exclaimed with a gasp, tears welling in their eyes before they were instantly killed by another sneak-attacking Follower of the ‘Red Moon’ for being distracted in battle.
But with the arrival of the ‘Divine Envoy’, the previously despondent believers became overwhelmingly excited!
So much so that nobody noticed the ‘Starlight Maiden’s’ body, continuously trembling as if still subjected to some intense sensory stimulus, remaining motionless yet with a hard-to-detect murky stench of black water dripping from under the robe.
However, they didn’t stay happy for long as both the Followers of the ‘Red Moon’ and the ‘Dawn Star’ could feel the temperature in the slightly dim cavern dramatically increase.
A wave of flame accompanied by a strong oppressive force was surging towards them.
The next second, everyone’s eyes focused and turned to see a fiery figure emerging at the entrance unknowingly.
“The official bastards are here! At least above eight levels, damn!”
One of the Followers of the ‘Red Moon’ with a Hong Kong accent immediately alerted everyone, prompting a rapid retreat.
But before they could all get moving, Colin’s flames erupted with a boom.
Like a giant mouth of fire, it swallowed the group whole…
“Just keeping an eye on you. Others may run, but don’t think any of you can escape.”
Colin muttered, his eyes shifting towards the Followers of the ‘Dawn Star’ at the center of the cave.
The next second, a blazing light surged forth as well.
Indiscriminately cleansing the area of all heretic beliefs.
“Divine Envoy ‘Starlight Maiden’! We will cover your retreat, fight to the death for you!”
“Get out of here now!”
Believers roared in anger, and around them, points of light appeared, intertwining and sparkling, forming a unique defensive network…
However, this feeble defense probably wouldn’t last a minute before it would be pierced straight through by that person’s flames.
But…
Having successfully summoned the “Divine Envoy” and brought forth the “Dawn Star’s” container.
They already had no regrets in their hearts…
As those who made great sacrifices for the return of the Great Will, when humanity under the Power of the Starlight would see a new dawn, their names would be immortalized.
Forever engraved on a great stone, bestowed with the name like that of a holy protector, worshiped by future generations.
At this moment, the only regret was that they would never again experience the “Starlight Maiden’s” tentacles offering them rewards, deprived of that indescribable delight…
Just then, a believer struggling against the flames suddenly realized something was wrong.
He noticed that the Envoy of God was still standing there, bowing slightly, looking towards that official strip…
Not showing any sign of leaving.
Unbeknownst to them, the starlight they so yearned for had become a prisoner under someone else’s step.
“Divine Envoy, why… Why aren’t you leaving…”
He voiced his confusion with difficulty, fully aware that the “Divine Envoy” had no combat power at the moment, and might not even be able to contend with the Grand Elder…
Only once she truly took root in this world, becoming the “Dawn Star’s” anchor here…
Would everything undergo earth-shattering change.
Feeling the “Power of the Starlight” on the barrier rapidly being eroded by the flames, he grew anxious, “My lord, leave quickly, we can’t hold on much…”
His voice suddenly came to an abrupt halt.
The believer’s eyes widened as he watched a transparent tendril from beneath the “Starlight Maiden’s” dark robe pierce his forehead like a spear: “…why… why…”
There was no answer.
With his death, a breach appeared in the starlight barrier, and the raging flames burst in like a breached dam.
“What’s going on, why…”
“‘Divine Envoy’, why have you betrayed us…”
“…Tell me, no, it can’t be, I don’t believe it, it’s the enemy’s illusion, don’t be fooled, the ‘Divine Envoy’ couldn’t possibly betray us…”
“It’s all fake, all an illusion, damn official strip, don’t think you can deceive me! I will tear off your faces!”
“…”
One by one, believers were penetrated by the “Starlight Maiden’s” invisible tendrils, then crumbled emotionally, either unable to believe or descending into madness, or with a vacant gaze…
The chaos did not last long.
Amidst the howling sound.
Everything was swallowed by the scorching flames.
All followers of the heresy turned to char and ash.
In another corner, the Fifth Level Official Personnel, whom Colin had earlier granted temporary access to use the “Emblem of the Humility Knight,” looked at the absurd scene unfolding before him, equally in disbelief.
“Damn, I must be, I’ve been holding my breath for too long, are these hallucinations I’m seeing?”
After holding his breath for several minutes, the Fifth Level Official Personnel’s face reddened, feeling as if his brain might have been damaged from the lack of air.
Otherwise, how could he be witnessing such a scene.
Just then, he saw the figure of the “Starlight Maiden” flicker slightly.
Then she instantaneously appeared in front of Colin.
“Be careful!”
He was about to speak, but before the words came out, he saw an even more shocking and absurd scene.
This very tall, but seemingly loftily perfect “Starlight Maiden” appeared in front of Colin, bowed, and slowly lowered her head…
It seemed like an act of submission.
Seeing this, the Fifth Level Official Personnel no longer doubted; his head must indeed be broken.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 432 - 432 388 The Paranoiac Who Clings to Humanity
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 432: Chapter 388 The Paranoiac Who Clings to Humanity! _1 Chapter 432: Chapter 388 The Paranoiac Who Clings to Humanity! _1 “What on earth, what exactly has happened?”
The Fifth Level Personnel, with a puzzled face, stared at the scene before him, his brain becoming increasingly unable to make sense of it.
The terrifying entities that those evil enemies had summoned with great effort not only spared their adversaries, but even turned on their own people…
What was even more bizarre was that now, inexplicably, they were bowing down to Colin?
No, what was the deal with Colin who was outwardly “equal” to him?
Looking at the flame on Colin’s body, the Fifth Level Personnel felt a deep unease; he had seen with his own eyes that the other party had hardly moved throughout the process, simply allowing the flame to spread and thereby resolving all opposition.
Despite it feeling not hot, as if it couldn’t even ignite cotton, that flame scorched all the evil enemies into charcoal…
This…
“It’s not a charm, not ‘Destiny Propeller,’ nor does it resemble ‘Divine Strike,’ what kind of power is this?”
The Fifth Level Personnel suddenly remembered some rumors.
It was rumored that the organization had recently recruited a rather large number of outsiders…
Was he one of them?
But what was the situation with the “Starlight Maiden”?
Why would such an entity bow down to him?
The Fifth Level Personnel especially could not understand, for this simply could not be explained by sheer strength alone.
Even Old Master Wu, who had the ability to adjust the fate and arrange others’ destiny, might not be able to achieve this step.
However, as for his confusion, let alone him, even Colin himself was not very clear.
‘I always feel like there’s some kind of hidden transaction going on that I don’t know about…’
Colin glanced at the “Starlight Maiden,” who was bowing her head in submission, suspecting that there had been transactions behind the scenes; otherwise, the company wouldn’t have been able to find this place with such precision.
This time, he was sent, probably to ensure the final execution of the mission.
If he had not come, the “Starlight Maiden” might have fled or failed to show up. His presence stopped her, of course, and probably only he would have waited for the “Starlight Maiden” to descend…
Anyone else would have probably stopped everything from happening before it could begin.
Only he would take a risk for the sake of points.
Of course, this was just Colin’s speculation. Upon closer examination, there were many loopholes and no evidence.
But there was one thing Colin was sure of, there was definitely a hidden transaction.
As thoughts flickered, his gaze passed over the “Starlight Maiden” and looked at the followers who had turned into charcoal…
These guys were quite pitiful.
They might have been sold out right from the beginning…
“Looking at it this way, the existence that they worshipped and their followers often cannot be regarded the same.”
Colin collected his thoughts and turned his eyes back to the “Starlight Maiden” in front of him.
Aside from her body occasionally trembling in some aftereffect, she had mostly recovered from the effects of the Bone Spur.
Among the enemies that were attacked, she was one of the quickest to recover.
Without giving it much thought, he accessed the mission in his mind, chose to complete it, and then prepared to hand over the “Starlight Maiden” in exchange for points.
Although he didn’t know what the company was going to do with this creature…
But for him, this thing, apart from being pleasing to the eye, certainly wasn’t as valuable as points.
However, at this very moment, Colin’s heart suddenly chilled.
He instantly felt that something capable of causing fatal danger was about to happen, but no image appeared in his mind…
“No image… The target isn’t me? Damn it!”
A scream came from the side, and Colin quickly realized something, immediately turning around, his gaze shifting to the still suffocating Fifth Level Official Personnel.
At this moment, from the ground beside that person, hordes of unusual entities that emitted “squeak squeak” sounds emerged; their exact shapes were unseen, only their shadows were visible.
“The Rat?”
As Colin’s thoughts flashed, he saw the Fifth Level Official Personnel’s calf gnawed clean in less than a second!
At this rate, it would take only a few seconds before the creature would be completely devoured.
He might not make it in time to save him…
With that thought, he decisively activated “Time Freeze.”
In the roar of freezing engines, everything came to a halt…
Colin extended his hand towards that direction, the flame surged forth, incinerating all the shadowy, entity-less rats completely…
But even after rescuing his colleague, the alarm in Colin’s heart did not subside.
Suddenly, a faint cry reached his ears.
“Save… save…”
Amidst the fluctuations of non-human thoughts, Colin’s pupils constricted, and turning his head, he saw that beside the “Starlight Maiden,” a large group of rats glowing with a blood-red light was pouncing on her…
There were thousands, countless in number. Although similar to the “rats” that attacked the Fifth Level Official Personnel, they seemed to have been blessed personally by some hidden entity, endowed with writhing red light.
So much so that they could act almost unhindered in the midst of “Time Freeze”!
At this point, because the “Starlight Maiden’s” body was much stronger than the Fifth Level Personnel’s.
They couldn’t devour her, but surged forth, biting her, dragging her in a certain direction…
At this moment, the frozen time that Colin had used to immobilize the enemy had ironically become a shackle for the “Starlight Maiden.”
“Damn it! This is the real target of the enemy!”
As thoughts whirled, Colin spun around swiftly, rushed to the “Starlight Maiden’s” side, and grabbed her by the shoulder.
Even within the frozen space, he could feel a titanic force wrestling with him.
Immediately, Colin lifted the effect of “Time Freeze.”
“Tick tock tick tock…”
The sound of the ticking of a clock came through.
Time Stop ended…
Then, an even more terrifying force emerged, and the strange cries of the “rat” swarm rose from all around.

chapters.title: Chapter 433 - 433 388 The Paranoiac Obsessed with Human
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 433: Chapter 388: The Paranoiac Obsessed with Human Nature!_2 Chapter 433: Chapter 388: The Paranoiac Obsessed with Human Nature!_2 “Without Time Stop, their power is even stronger than before.”
Colin clenched his teeth, his fingers white-knuckled against his skin, veins pulsing at his temples.
He knew that if he let go now, his points gift package would be stolen by those damned “rats”, so he activated all his strength and let the flames devour them in the dragging process.
However, in addition to the group of rats glowing red as if one, many ordinary “rats” charged forward.
They fell one after another, wave upon wave, throwing themselves fearlessly in front of the flames.
Even when they let out strange, horrid screams as they burned, they desperately blocked the way of the red-glowing rats…
Their terrifying numbers actually succeeded in holding back the flames for a moment!
As for the “Starlight Maiden” caught in the middle, she tried several times to break free, but the rat’s teeth that bit into her were like special nails, preventing her from doing so.
“No good, if this keeps up, I’ll run out of strength soon.”
Colin steeled his heart and directly activated “Potential Burst”, triggering his Talent’s exclusive skill, “Matchless Strike!”
With the sudden burst of power, there came a ripping sound of “whoosh”.
The “Starlight Maiden” let out a scream.
Part of her dark star-covered robe was torn, as if it was part of her very flesh.
Colin felt a sudden lightness in his hands.
The once tall “Starlight Maiden” was now reduced by a third!
As for the group of “rats” emitting red light, they fled into the unknown with a part of the “Starlight Maiden”, disappearing from the spot with extreme speed.
“Are these the other enemies mentioned in the mission?”
Colin furrowed his brow, looked at the “Starlight Maiden” in his hands, light as a piece of clothing, and straight away confirmed the mission handover option with the company.
When the invisible transparent vortex appeared, he did not care about her ongoing screams from the tearing, and directly threw her into it…
At the same time, the mission settlement began, Colin glanced at the results, and his expression turned sour in an instant.
“Rating B minus, only gave me over eight thousand points, it should have been at least fifteen thousand and up…”
Muttering to himself, Colin put aside his complaints, thought of those rats from before, and realized that those things seemed to appear in the “Disordered Ghost Train” operation as well.
Not only that, he had a hunch that these creatures were most likely related to his experiences in “The Seventh Box Garden World”.
Those things lurking behind the scenes, it seemed, were about to make their move…
…
At the same time, in a huge and gloomy hall, the single incandescent light was casting shadows of many large and small rats.
Some were eating, some fighting, some playing cards, some playing mahjong, some playing with airplanes, some watching the playing with airplanes, the scene was chaotic and lively…
But if someone were to enter the hall, they would find “nothing at all”.
In the middle of the hall, on a finely crafted chair, a significantly larger “rat” seemed to be in deep slumber.
From the shadow alone, it was nearly the size of a ten-year-old child…
All the passing “rat” shadows lowered their voices to avoid disturbing it.
However, at that moment, the “rat” on the chair seemed to open its eyes.
An invisible presence swept through the hall…
All the “rats” stopped what they were doing and bowed down in front of the large “rat” on the chair.
At that moment, from a corner, a group of rats glowing with red light emerged…
They hurried to the grand “rat”, some with swollen bellies, opened their mouths, and spat out some dark fragments dotted with stars…
“Very good, very good, another type of raw material!”
The large “rat” uttered a satisfied sound, extending a small paw that moved slightly.
Then, out of thin air, it dragged out a peculiar crucible…
In the pot, countless twisted colors were intertwined like a unique paint.
It threw the dark star-covered robe fragments in and took out a pestle, with a group of rats immediately crowding over to grind the newly obtained material to mix it in.
Just as it was about to reward the group of rats, another crack in the corner set loose a large group of rat shadows…
However, compared to the others, the shadowy figures known as “The Rats” were significantly more fragmented.
They, too, ran to the side of the “Big Rat,” their guts churning as they vomited bizarre mineral crystal formations filled with twisted colors…
“Not bad, not bad, yet another raw material obtained. It seems the situation over there has concluded?”
“Big Rat” grabbed a smaller “Rat,” tossed it into his mouth, and chewed it to extract the information within.
Soon he understood that the battle in the “Lost Fragments World” had ended…
“On the battlefield, the corpses of C Level Personnel and all else had been taken away by the company, while the body of the ‘Ancient God’ that was dragged down by that C Level Personnel was resurrected and reclaimed by the ‘Red Moon’ Mother…”
