But just when he thought it was the end for him, the eerie and terrifying atmosphere suddenly shattered…
“What’s happened?” The Sixth Level Personnel and several official members were puzzled.
They could feel something was coming; its presence had yet to arrive, but its momentum had already dissipated the lethal dark atmosphere from before…
Without further thought, they suddenly saw the ceiling above the containment unit turn red and melt.
In less than a second, a torrent of flame poured in from the opening.
A figure shrouded in flames plummeted down directly onto the out-of-control Level Seven Personnel.
And just like that…
They saw their leader instantly carbonized into ash.
“Is this… is this support? Who’s this? Which Eighth Level Personnel has come…”
Everyone’s spirits lifted; this level of power was something only an Eighth Level Personnel could achieve!
Yet before they could continue pondering, Colin looked around, raised his chin slightly, and looked at the Sixth Level Personnel, “What’s happened here?”
Hearing the question, the Sixth Level Personnel began to respond but suddenly felt a chill run down his spine and shouted to Colin, “Watch out! It’s absorbed too much blood and entered the Second Order!”
Just then, the grey cabbage stone statue, now covered in flames, saw all its wings suddenly come to life, numerous wings wrapping around Colin as if trying to engulf him within…
Although this creature’s threat level was considered moderate, its terror rating was not to be underestimated.

chapters.title: Chapter 459 - 459 397 The Tragic Scene on the Periphery of
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 459: Chapter 397: The Tragic Scene on the Periphery of “Base Number Five”._3 Chapter 459: Chapter 397: The Tragic Scene on the Periphery of “Base Number Five”._3 Many even higher threat entities would be suppressed by it!
Even if eighth level personnel got involved…
However, the next second, he witnessed an even more astonishing scene…
That “eighth level personnel” faced the deadly assault with just a nonchalant glance and then, quite ordinarily, raised a fist, directly aiming at the countless wings that enveloped him…
There were no flashy abilities; it was only a simple and pure punch thrown out.
The image of Colin with his arm a bloody mess had already flashed through their minds.
Yet…
“Boom!”
In the deafening explosion, countless wings burst, sending feathers flying.
The statue’s main body seemed to be dragged by an enormous force, brutally embedding itself more than three inches into the steel wall.
Vibrations echoed non-stop throughout the entire containment unit…
“Try looking at me one more time.”
Colin looked at the statue, stared at the eyeball at the center of its tongue, spoke calmly, and raised his fist again.
As soon as the words were out, the writhing tongue, studded with eyeballs, retracted into the statue…
“Hiss.”
At that moment, everyone present couldn’t help but inhale sharply.
This was the first time they had seen such a rudimentary and brutal sealing method.
“Now, tell me what happened here,” Colin turned his head, looking at the sixth level personnel.
Quite quickly, from the mouth of this sixth level personnel, he roughly understood the situation…
About one hour ago, inside the base, some transported Containment Subjects suddenly broke their seals, and then the chaos started, they weren’t clear about what had happened inside, only that this loss of control was likely not an accident.
Because it seemed like they saw alarms for unauthorized intruders going off…
And most crucially, the internal eighth level personnel hadn’t shown up, unaware of what had happened.
At present, the interior of Base Number Five remained unclear, but a substantial part of the exterior, especially the area they were in, G Area, could almost be described as overran, with at least one high level personnel confirmed dead…
‘The effective intelligence isn’t very much…’
Colin nodded and said, “Just stay here, other help will arrive soon.”
Having said that, he didn’t wait for a response and quickly walked further in…
Flame erupted in all directions from his body, like a walking wildfire, but the humans enveloped by this flame weren’t only unaffected but also received a certain degree of protection.
Other many lower-level anomalies either vanished or returned to their containment sealed state.
Using the Flame Perception he had just learned…
Colin quickly found the spot where problems likely originated.
Seconds later, he entered a place that looked like a slaughterhouse, where all the guard personnel were dead, limbs torn and scattered, covering the entire area.
“Not a single one alive…”
Colin walked unhurriedly along the corridor, strewn with blood with barely any place to step, while examining the corpses with their ghastly deaths.
The direction they were facing when they died was forward, as if they had been fighting something.
But sadly, due to the significant gap in strength, the outcome wasn’t very nice…
Colin refrained from undue interference by cremating them and after walking some more, stopped in front of an opening.
The pitch-black opening was about the height of a person, resembling a large rat hole, sloping downward, leading to an unknown destination.
A chilling aura faintly emanated from within…
At the sight of this opening, Colin fell silent momentarily because he was no stranger to it.
In The Hague Shelter of The Seventh ‘Box Garden World,’ he had seen a similar “rat hole”—
Indeed, was it related to the thing that had escaped from there?
“Ah, still a step too late…”
A sigh rang in Colin’s ears.
Colin turned his head and saw Xu Duojin’s silhouette appearing not far from him.
“What’s the situation with the eighth level personnel from Base Number Five?” Colin asked, as he hadn’t entered the core area of Base No. 5 because he sensed no issues there…
“Trapped, but should be fine,” Xu Duojin glanced around, looking at the corpses with a flash of anger in his eyes.
Although this assault had not penetrated into the core area, for the external personnel, the losses were severe.
After a deep breath, Xu Duojin suppressed the anger in his heart: “I’ll review what happened here and see what these people’s goal was…”
As he spoke, he waved his hand, and a mass of pitch-black threads drifted out from his body.
Then, these dark threads sketched out several figures, replaying the incident here like a movie.
“…”

chapters.title: Chapter 460 - 460 398 Second Self·Death Immunity_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 460: Chapter 398 “Second Self·Death Immunity”_1 Chapter 460: Chapter 398 “Second Self·Death Immunity”_1 The figures outlined in the lines were a bit rough, with no facial details, but Colin could generally make out that they were likely the official guards stationed here…
At this moment, their frantic movements made it clear that the loss of control was not a first at this location.
Soon after, a wall collapsed, revealing a hole from which a dozen figures burst out and launched an attack on the other personnel present.
The personnel on the scene were shocked for a moment and then began to retaliate…
Unfortunately, faced with this group that had come prepared for a sneak assault, the guards suffered heavy casualties in an instant.
Even though there were a few stronger guards among them, they still couldn’t hold on.
The battle did not last long before it was over…
After taking control of the area with almost no significant cost, Colin and the others saw them disperse as if they had planned ahead, continuing to infiltrate the outskirts of Base Number Five.
Regrettably, at this point, the line-like appearances could hardly be maintained.
Beyond knowing that the entire process from their appearance to departure took no more than ten minutes, everything else remained unclear.
It was impossible to ascertain their purpose for the attack…
“They have specific countermeasures on them, too indistinct to see clearly, and they even deliberately erased their own presence…”
Next to Colin, Xu Duojin sighed and stretched out his hand, summoning back those black lines.
“Indeed…”
Colin, recalling what he had just seen, curiously asked, “Do you know about the ‘Awakeners’?”
As Old Master Wu’s liaison officer, Xu Duojin was obviously aware of the matter and nodded immediately:
“Are you suggesting that this whole group are those individuals?”
“Yes, I’m not very sure, because there are so few traces left by these people’s actions. But it’s precisely because of the scarcity that I think they are like those ‘Awakeners,'” Colin explained his thoughts briefly.
“According to current intelligence, ‘Awakeners’ usually appear alone, and their numbers are scarce, like some sort of special cases that occur randomly. We have not yet seen them act together, nor have there been any with power exceeding Fifth Level Personnel…”
“However, hearing what you’ve said, I too think there’s a possibility,” Xu Duojin conceded.
“If that is indeed the case, then the situation will be complicated…”
Xu Duojin’s tone became even more grave. He looked around again, at the corpses strewn everywhere, he thought of the interference at the moment of the reenactment, and of a group of high-level “Awakeners” who seemingly teamed up…
In a vague sense, it was as though one could glimpse an invisible, disruptive force trying to throw everything into chaos.
Colin followed his gaze and also took a look around, then said, “I feel that more than this incident, it’s time for a purge within your ranks.”
The hidden orchestrator of this attack had an exceptionally high understanding of the situation here.
They even managed to reassign their higher combat forces, creating a gap for infiltration…
Frankly, Colin didn’t believe that there hadn’t been some sort of information leak from the inside.
Hearing his words, Xu Duojin had no objections.
Inside… It was indeed time for a major cleanup.
But before they could say more, they simultaneously sensed something and turned their necks to look in a specific direction.
There, the wall contorted, and a stout, short figure emerged, his body covered in long charms with yellow backgrounds and red lettering. After arriving, he silently glanced at the scene and then, from his weird belly, a voice said:
“Sorry, I must ensure internal security…”“Right, there are no problems in the internal area, correct?” Xu Duojin asked.
“None.”
“That’s good.”
Xu Duojin looked at this special embodiment of Base Number Five, wanting to say something, but in the end, he shook his head and remained silent.
As the garrison of Base Number Five, on the surface, his performance could be considered quite poor.
His strength was definitely not as limited as it seemed…
But as a member of the higher echelons, Xu Duojin was well aware that, in a sense, this defense had been a success.
Because what he needed to ensure was the safety of the core area within Base Number Five, he could only intervene so much in the outer areas. Even if his main body came over and could quickly suppress these people, it wouldn’t really come…
With no blunders occurring in the core area, there was nothing to criticize about their entire response process.
After the conversation ended, silence fell upon the scene for a while.
Then, the stout man glanced at Colin and emotionlessly made a report via belly-talk, saying:
“I can sense that there are a few other uncontrolled anomalies roaming within the base. The threat level is not high, and several Level Three Armed Suppression Teams have been dispatched. There shouldn’t be any further problems…
“In addition, the enemy’s targets might be certain specific Containment Subjects, as I can feel that some of the subjects are missing…
“However, the specifics are still to be confirmed. If needed, I will inform you as soon as the results are out,” he added.
“Good,” Xu Duojin nodded.
After listening to their conversation for a while, Colin was the first to leave Base Number Five.
Although he was very interested in the specific purpose of the enemy, he was not too keen on staying here…
On the way back, he called on Qin Chuan and the others, asking them to gather everyone and report to his office.
Soon after, by the time Colin returned to the city and entered his office,
A group of “Experience Babies,” still unaware of the situation, brightened up, thinking that a new mission was about to begin…

chapters.title: Chapter 461 - 461 398 Second Self·Death Immunity_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 461: Chapter 398 “Second Self·Death Immunity”_2 Chapter 461: Chapter 398 “Second Self·Death Immunity”_2 The feeling of leveling up just by lying down was simply too comfortable!
However, Colin just did a check to make sure that the group of people around him were all right, then dismissed everyone present, leaving only Hu Zheng with his cane, Qin Chuan wrapped in bandages, and Xia Liufang.
“Mr. Colin, are you going to ask about this morning’s incident?” Xia Liufang asked, curious about the reason for Colin’s meeting.
“No, if it was that, I would have asked over the phone.”
Colin waved his hand and continued, “From now on, any unusual tasks you encounter, whether you can solve them or not, try to delay them as much as possible. Make a list in order of priority, and I will take care of them all together whenever I have some spare time.”
Although he was accustomed to seeing death, it usually referred to the death of enemies or unrelated parties.
Seeing the devastation around Base No. 5 today, he suddenly worried that one day, these Little Cats like Qin Chuan, Hu Zheng, and Xia Liufang might end up as corpses scattered on the ground…
After working together for so many days, he personally did not wish for such a thing to happen.
So…
Asking this of himself might be tiring, but it was okay to be a little tired.
Although there were also many dangerous things on Earth, as long as the tasks weren’t issued by the company, they weren’t a big issue.
The overall environment here tended to be stable, and the probability of encountering exceptionally high-standard external entities was very low.
After hearing his words, the others were stunned for a moment, but they all nodded without hesitation.
“Boss, is this related to the incident at Base No. 5 today?” Qin Chuan curiously asked.
“It’s somewhat related, but the specifics are classified. If the higher-ups decide to inform you, you should receive the information in the next couple of days.” Colin did not provide too much explanation.
After making sure there was nothing wrong with his subordinates, he went straight home.
The night passed without incident, until the following day.
Colin took his usual crew to resolve the local issues, and at the end visited the market, bought some seafood, returned home, and instructed the Little Maid to prepare dinner…
Normally, he didn’t eat seafood, but in the past, his abstinence wasn’t due to any reason other than lack of money.
However, considering that a catastrophic event could happen soon…
Colin decided to fill in some of the blanks in his life because there might not be anywhere to eat seafood later on.
Even when disaster hit and pollution spread, it might be the seafood coming ashore to eat him…
However, just as dinner was ready and he was about to start eating, Xu Duojin sent over some information.
Colin picked up a crab leg and opened the text message, which was about Base No. 5.
Old Master Wu had been consulted by Xu Duojin, and it was essentially confirmed that the enemy was indeed the “Awakeners”, a group capable of opposing Eighth Level Personnel, who were aware of internal intelligence and sticking together.
Furthermore, there was follow-up information about the stolen items…
However, Colin couldn’t help raising his eyebrows when he saw what was stolen, because there was a slight connection to him.
It was from an item left behind by the “Celestial Observation Society” at a school he was dealing with some time ago, some special oil paints with a peculiar activity.
“Just to steal these things, they risked exposing themselves? Could it be that I overlooked some crucial item at that time?”
Colin pondered. He remembered that the key unusual nature of that task seemed to have all been taken by the company.
What was left were supposed to be some trivial knick-knacks…
Could it have been a mistake?
He couldn’t help but send a message to ask, but Xu Duojin quickly responded, telling him that he originally thought the same thing because several Containment Subjects were missing. However, by using some exceptional means of “Fate Propelling”, they were certain it was those items.
Even in the end, Old Master Wu advised him to trust his judgment…
‘So, these people barged in and made a killing rampage, revealing themselves, all for some paint of little use?’
Colin pursed his lips, unable to understand the actions of this group.
But lacking the enemy’s information, he couldn’t guess anything useful about them…
After pondering for about fifteen minutes and coming up short, he gave up.
“Currently, it seems the authorities will probably focus on the ‘Awakeners’. I hope they catch these guys soon or get more information. This kind of power with nowhere to be used is really passive.”
Shaking his head, Colin took a deep breath, ready to continue eating.
But at that moment, an intuition suddenly rose inside him.
“What now? Can’t a person even enjoy their meal?”
Colin grumbled as he set down his rice bowl and pulled out the parchment, only to notice a new and unfamiliar task named “Item Return.”
However, the task was already completed as soon as he took it on.
“Is this… the containment subjects from the transaction half a month ago finally settled?”
Colin opened the “Storage Room” to check and found that his pockets were now eight items heavier, with two purple, three green, and three white ones.
According to the task prompt, he could choose one of these eight items as his reward.
“The first purple gear, ‘Yin Soldiers Passing Scroll,’ can unleash a large number of ‘Yin Soldiers’ as an attacking method. It’s a summoning type of thing, with a fairly long existence time, but it can summon hundreds of ‘Yin Soldiers’. They’re only a bit better than the physical quality of an F Level Staff not carrying anything…”
“But if used well, a few hundred Yin Soldiers, each strapped with a bag of explosives, should have a pretty good effect…”
“The second purple gear, ‘Second Self·Death Immunity,’ creates an overlapping avatar based on my body. This avatar can’t leave a ten-meter radius from me, and isn’t very strong, but that’s not the point. The key is that with this item, as long as I suffer any actual fatal attack, it can die in my place once…”
After a quick glance over the purple gear, Colin’s gaze shifted towards the green gear, feeling that the effect of one or two of the items was quite good.
For instance, there was an item that could promote rapid plant growth, a true godsend for farming.
If taken to “World Code-13,” it would be utterly game-changing.
Compared to the two pieces of purple gear, this seemed a bit more practical…
‘That’s right, equipment selection is about finding what fits best. For someone on the brink of death, a green gear that can stabilize their injuries and save their life is more precious than a golden artifact.’
‘So the key to choosing items is their suitability and utility…’
‘Rather than blindly pursuing a high rating, if you don’t choose wisely, even a high-grade item is useless…’
As these thoughts swirled in his mind, Colin seemed to gain a deeper understanding of equipment selection.
Subsequently, he chose a purple-named item.
[“Second Self·Death Immunity”]
[Quality: Excellent.]
[Status: Almost new (Integrity 89%).]
[Energy Level: None.]
[Effect “Death Immunity”: This item is a special type, which, once used, will always passively exist on the user. It can exempt the user from death once from any kind of deadly attack and restore all the user’s status (excluding items, etc.), and can also be used at any time, the specifics of which the user needs to discover for themselves.]
[Negative Effect: Once “Death Immunity” is activated, this item will be completely ineffective.]
[Note: Hehehe, what made you think you only had one life?]
…
“Avoiding death once is not bad, hm, as long as I’m alive, everything has meaning. If I were dead, no matter how fast the potatoes grow in ‘World Code 13,’ it would be meaningless.”
Colin nodded, taking out “Second Self·Death Immunity” to examine it.
It resembled a burning blue flame.
It looked somewhat grotesque and eerie…
After a few seconds, Colin no longer hesitated. His palm clenched suddenly with force, crushing the blue flame, and countless flames immediately seeped into his skin.
Afterwards, Colin noticed an indistinct shadow appeared under his feet, barely perceptible.
At the same time, he also gained a deeper understanding of the item…
“It feels like it’s wrapped around me. Well, calling it ‘Death Immunity’ isn’t quite accurate; it’s more like a special shield. Only by destroying it can my real body be revealed again…”
Colin’s eyes shifted as he thought pensively.
Then, he shifted his attention to a letter in the “Storage Room.”
On this letter was the signature of Lady Bunny.
.
.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 462 - 462 399 Civilization-Alternating Catastrophic
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 462: Chapter 399: Civilization-Alternating Catastrophic Event!_1 Chapter 462: Chapter 399: Civilization-Alternating Catastrophic Event!_1 “A letter this time?”
Colin was surprised, and then he opened the envelope and pulled out the paper inside.
It was written in familiar, graceful handwriting, conveying quite a bit of content—
“First off, congratulations on being successfully included in the ‘Bonfire Outstanding Talent Development Plan’. Joining it means you’ve officially become a reservist of the Firebearers…”
“The characteristics recovered from the ‘Ghost Train’ should have been handed over to you, but possessing them too early might not be a good thing…”
“So, for now, continue as before, focusing on integrating more essences.”
“When the time is ripe and the Bonfire reignites, it will come to you of its own accord. However, from the intelligence I’ve gathered so far, it seems this won’t happen unless you have at least Level C Clearance.”
“Otherwise, even if you meet the requirements ahead of time, it would be difficult to handle attacks by some ancient beings during this period.”
“Besides that, there are some things about the ‘Ghost Train’; it’s not that important, just some analysis…”
“As far as I know, this incident should have concluded a long time ago, and anything that needed to be recovered should have been recovered by then, but… it’s only recently that I discovered from some intelligence that the situation was different from what I expected.”
“Things that should have been recovered were hidden until now, almost ‘invisible in plain sight’.”
“It appears there wasn’t just one mission with such circumstances…”
“It’s a pity, these matters don’t concern me too much. Plus, they’ve been given a very high level of confidentiality, so I’m not very clear on the specifics…”
“Although, if I wanted to delve deeper, I could investigate, but it would come at a significant cost just to satisfy a bit of curiosity, so I’ve given up on the related investigation proposal.”
…
“…It’s still at least C Level for a ‘Flame Bearer’.”
Colin’s gaze swept over this point without much surprise.
After all, during his previous conversation with the C Level Elder Brother, he had roughly gathered information on this matter…
For the company at its peak, D Level Personnel barely reached the threshold of graduation, similar to university students starting to choose their career paths.
C Levels belonged to those who had achieved significant success…
“Judging from some of the conversations on the train, suppressing some kind of catastrophic disaster and receiving significant commendations are necessary for a nomination, tsk, really competitive…”
Colin muttered to himself. If the requirements were this high just short of C Level, then the B and A Levels likely wouldn’t suffice with just saving the world…
Shaking his head and without dwelling on it any further, Colin glanced at Lady Bunny’s messages regarding the ‘Ghost Train’.
From her words, it seemed there might be other intelligence hidden within?
However, seeing that even this person who seemed to be high up didn’t know, he didn’t speculate blindly either.
His gaze continued to move down…
The second part of the content was related to a conversation with an Eighth Level Personnel, namely, whether it was possible to seek the use of the ‘Unlimited Train’ from the company.
Lady Bunny gave a very clear response to this.
Not possible.
This thing could be borrowed temporarily through some means for short-term use, but not for regular usage…
Although she indeed had the ability to summon it, at present it was not feasible to cooperate with the official agencies of Earth.
The only theoretically possible way for Earth’s official personnel to use it would be to have someone like Old Master Wu, a Ninth Level ‘Fate Propeller’, predict the fates of the upcoming passengers…
With such a forceful solution, at best only the stop regions for the next five stations could be deciphered.
Regardless of what the officials thought, one of the basic prerequisites for borrowing this thing temporarily was having Level C Clearance of the company.
“Tsk, if the official personnel see this, they’re probably going to start investing resources to train C Levels.”
Colin thought while sucking on the grilled matsuba crab leg handed to him by the Little Maid.
The ‘Unlimited Train’ seemed to be quite a high priority inside the official circles…
Many regarded it as an extremely important escape route if doomsday were to come, planning to transfer a large number of people through it when a great disaster hits.
After all, with today’s forces, if disaster truly struck, it would clearly be impossible to save everyone.
Under these circumstances, this train, which seemed to have infinite carrying capacity and could leave this world, became particularly significant…
Nevertheless, the requirement for Level C Company Clearance was somewhat high.
Even pooling the efforts of the entire world, it’s uncertain if enough can be accumulated…
However, the company would presumably be happy to see their efforts, after all, they’re all high-quality labor, huh?”
Colin suddenly remembered something. Currently, the most capable person approaching C Level on Earth was probably him…
If there were to be a major push for development, he was likely to make it onto the support list.
“Regarding this matter… I should fight for it.”
Colin made a mental note, then looked further down the letter, his expression becoming a bit more serious.
He saw that the third part mentioned something related to ‘Awakeners’.
“…It can be confirmed that a highly threatening individual has returned through ‘The Seventh Box Garden World’. I once tried to capture it, but the results were not ideal.”
“And for some reasons, it has successfully hidden within the company’s mechanisms, preventing further attempts on my part.”
“Therefore, in this respect, I can only provide some intelligence. First of all, it’s certain that it’s a rather troublesome entity. It’s adept at creating significant chaos with a variety of true and false information, inciting upheaval, and then obtaining the outcomes it desires…”

chapters.title: Chapter 463 - 463 399 Civilization-Alternating Catastrophic
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 463: Chapter 399: Civilization-Alternating Catastrophic Event!_2 Chapter 463: Chapter 399: Civilization-Alternating Catastrophic Event!_2 “Because it is also very good at hiding itself, it’s extremely difficult to catch it,”
“At least, until its goal is achieved, it’s highly unlikely to expose itself. Plus, it has a considerable understanding of some internal mechanisms of the company and knows quite a bit about what’s going on, so there probably won’t even be an opportunity to act against it…”
“The only way is to wait for it to show itself.”
“However, there is one thing, based on feedback from some intelligence reports, that can be confirmed: its true form is currently on Earth, and for some reasons, it cannot and dare not leave Earth, not even a single step…”
“As for the internal reasons, perhaps only Boss Huang He, who was initially responsible for handling it, knows…”
“But at present, it should have already achieved the basic conditions it needs.”
“And due to its extremely elusive nature, it’s difficult for me to provide any effective advice…”
“What I can offer are only two pieces of intelligence where it might appear.”
“One is that you become a ‘Flame Bearer’ or obtain B Level Authority before it succeeds. Once you do, you’ll immediately be able to use some methods to lock it down. Given its current state, probably any D Level Personnel could have a chance to hunt it down.”
“So it won’t just sit around and wait; it will use all its means to obstruct you.”
“This will also cause immense chaos, so you must prepare in advance.”
“The second is that it believes the time is right and decides to incite rebellion. At that time, at the very least, a disaster of planetary civilization replacement level will be triggered, and at that moment, it will certainly expose itself to achieve the desired outcome.”
“As for the timing, it may be related to the ‘Book of Fate’ and its temporary users.”
“Aside from these two, the likelihood of encountering it by other means adds up to less than five percent of these two possibilities…”
“And, regarding the events happening over there, I cannot intervene without bypassing some things.”
“…”
“An expert in hiding, a troublemaker whose actions are alarming only when it chooses to act?”
Looking at the information provided above, Colin felt the situation seemed more troublesome than he thought.
Because, from both of Lady Bunny’s hypotheses, whether it’s the first or the second, they both indicated that disaster was about to erupt…
The only difference lay in whether it was a moderate disaster, a major disaster, or an extreme disaster.
“Sigh, what a headache.”
Colin sighed helplessly. If it had been right after he joined the company, he would probably just grumble that if the sky fell, there would be someone tall to bear it, and then he would continue doing whatever he had been doing.
But the tough part was…
Now he was the tall one.
Furthermore, judging by this person’s hostility towards the “Flame Bearer,” it seemed that whether the opponent succeeded or not, he would be targeted and hunted…
So this enemy was highly likely unavoidable.
“Forget it, I chose this path myself. All I can do now is to advance as quickly as possible. To look on the bright side, Old Master Wu should still have a good half a year to live. With my promotion speed, maybe by then I’ll already be A Level…”
Colin continued reading the contents of the envelope, but after mentioning that hidden “The Rat,” there wasn’t much left.
It only mentioned that there might soon be a task that would require him to wear the guise of “Dawn Star” to receive responses from followers of “Dawn Star” on Earth…
“Not wearing the guise of ‘Starlight Maiden’ but ‘Dawn Star’? Tsk, no wonder ‘Starlight Maiden’ rebelled, was it initiated by a certain high being?”
Colin conjectured a bit based on what he knew and then continued reading.
Unfortunately, that was the end of the letter.
A short blessing.
His gaze went over the letter again, and Colin felt like something was omitted in the response. Soon, he remembered the information about the 2044 disaster, and it seemed that once again, no further response was provided.
“Not a single mention, is it because my Authority Level is still not sufficient?”
Furrowing his brows in thought, Colin guessed it probably had to do with the fact that he hadn’t reached the required Authority Level.
Information about this aspect might only be disclosed once he reached C Level or even became a “Flame Bearer.”
And it seemed to confirm that he had finished reading and memorized the content of the letter.
The sheet of paper in Colin’s hand spontaneously combusted without flame, along with the envelope, instantly turning into nothingness without leaving any ash…
Just thinking about the content made him suffer from a bit of a headache.
He was just a diligent little employee doing tasks, seemingly having made no enemies, but now it looked like every time he stepped out, nine out of ten people he met wanted his life, and the tenth was on the way with a knife…
Even raising his head to look at the starry sky, every thread of starlight seemed filled with malice.
“One after another, the powerful ones don’t dare to bully but prey on us underdogs who haven’t grown up yet.”
“You like being unreasonable, huh! Well, just wait for me. I may not be powerful now, but that will change when I am!”
Colin clenched his fist; he did not like this feeling of being shrouded in crisis at all times.
Whenever I get the chance, I’ll definitely have a serious talk with those guys!
But no sooner had he finished speaking than he suddenly felt something, and then he saw a prompt appear.
[Your chosen trial instance “Nightmare Origin of a Dying Ancient God” is now on the market~]
“Huh? That was quick this time?”
Colin was taken aback at the sight, recalling that it almost took a month for the last instance to hit the market.
Just as the question popped into his head, an inspiration emerged…
All matters involving members of the Excellent Talent Program are, according to regulations, entitled to a fast-track review.
And…
This time, the instance allocation ratio had changed.
It was still a seventy-thirty split…
But this time, he got 7, and the company got 3.
“That’s not bad, aside from the pay-to-play items, I’m finally seeing some other benefits…”
Colin nodded, then opened the “Chosen Trial Instance.”
Compared to the last time he’d opened it, there seemed to be a few more instances inside; obviously, the experiences of others, after who knows how many months of review, had finally gone live…
However, he wasn’t very interested in those.
After searching for a while, Colin spotted the second instance he had put on the market.
“The content isn’t much, just the part where I went up the mountain and fought with C Level Personnel, and like last time, it’s a rewarding instance, with recognition for clearing and even a special passive Talent upon success?”
“This time there’s a bit of a change in the mechanism, with two modes: one is a team mode costing 20 points per person for one try with one life, the other is a solo mode costing 79 points per person for five lives, with no consumption of item durability during combat…”
“Wait, what the hell, I’m the provider of the instance experience, so why do I have to pay to experience my own life events?”
Colin felt odd, like his home had been transformed into a tourist spot, and he was being charged an entrance fee to return home.
But according to the split, it would actually only cost him 24 points to go in once…
Without giving it much thought, he paid the fee to initiate the event before any other tasks arrived, intending to test the results of his secret training with “The Light Chaser” over the past several days.
Following that, as his vision blurred for a moment, Colin once again arrived at the mid-mountain position.
In the vast open space ahead, countless Divine beings stood motionless, heads bowed low, silently erect in the presence of a figure seated on the cliff’s edge.
However, unlike the last time when Colin approached and the figure awakened,
this time, as soon as he appeared, it was as if he could hear a powerful gust of air explode beside his ear…
Then, Colin heard the whisper filled with a sense of power:
“You, are you the one wrapping up this event?”
“Yes.”
Upon hearing this, Colin responded flatly and unhesitatingly drew a revolver.
“‘Containment Protocol’ Item Liberation request! ‘Revolver Contrarian’ liberate five percent of the item!”
Before the sound faded, a terrifying Flame burst forth like a volcanic eruption, almost fully illuminating the area.
The next second, combat erupted instantaneously.
…
And just as Colin entered the instance, inside the company’s internal forum, a large number of employees quickly took notice of this newly launched instance…
“Brother Shunzi has released a new task! It seems to be related to the ‘Ghost Train’ event before…”
“The task is to fight a half out-of-control C Level Personnel? So, that’s what Brother Shunzi was up to when he was escorted up the mountain, I thought he was doing something else; with Brother Shunzi’s strength, that C Level Personnel probably got beaten badly…”
“Holy shit, look, clearing this task gives you a chance to acquire a powerful Green Talent or Purple Talent!”
“Charge, charge, charge! The task seems simple, just defeat one C Level Personnel, guys, watch me solo mode and annihilate him!”
“79 points, why are Brother Shunzi’s instance prices getting more expensive…”
“But this is a rewarding instance, 79 points is actually reasonable.”
“Right +1, where is 79 points considered expensive, Brother Shunzi’s instances are always of high quality, instead of complaining about the cost, sometimes it’s worth looking at oneself and thinking about the years spent with the company…”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 464 - 464 400 The C Level Personnel Who Was So Angry
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 464: Chapter 400: The C Level Personnel Who Was So Angry He Lost Control._1 Chapter 464: Chapter 400: The C Level Personnel Who Was So Angry He Lost Control._1 “Are you the one wrapping up this incident?”
A deep voice echoed from ahead, “Life Mentor Adorable” didn’t answer immediately but curiously glanced around at the motionless figures.
He could feel that each figure here possessed tremendous power.
“At the very least, they are ‘Chosen of God’ or something of that sort…
“Life Mentor Adorable” estimated quietly.
Normally, encountering these guys would require at least four or five Level D employees setting an ambush to have a chance at repelling them.
But now, they all lay motionless, submissive to the figure in front of them…
Submissive to the man sitting on the pale blue plastic chair of a shabby roadside food stall.
No, more accurately, it seemed all figures had fallen into some kind of trap and couldn’t break free.
It wasn’t that they truly wanted to submit…
“The strength of a Level C Employee is this formidable?”
He wondered incredulously, but it was right then when the figure in front didn’t get an answer for a few seconds and asked the same question again.
According to standard procedure, the answer should be yes, and then the fight begins.
Before coming in, he saw some other employees who had already failed and left, and they seemed to have said something similar…
However, just as “Life Mentor Adorable” was about to reply, he suddenly had an idea – what if he said no now?
What would happen if he said no?
Curiosity got the better of him, and he decided to try…
“No.”
He had barely spoken the word when a strong sense of impending doom surged through “Life Mentor Adorable’s” heart.
The whole place seemed to darken at that moment…
Before he could react, the man from the plastic chair disappeared and appeared before him like Flash.
Then…
Then there was no then.
A plain punch, moving seemingly slow yet impossibly fast, smashed brutally onto his head.
In an instant, his head exploded like a watermelon falling to the ground.
Bone, flesh, brain, eyes, all turned into a bloody mist under the immense force.
As for his body, it still stood defensively as if it hadn’t caught up with what happened.
But with the head exploding, the rest of the body “belatedly” also suffered some attack and kept exploding until only a pair of legs stood on the barren ground.
…
“Holy shit, that was ruthless.”
“Life Mentor Adorable” suddenly exclaimed, then paused, finding himself appearing again in the middle of the arena.
A life…
Just gone like that?
What on earth had just happened?
However, before he could continue to ponder, the man on the roadside food stall chair slowly got up.
And once again uttered the same sentence…
This time, he didn’t dare to delay, fearing that any hesitation would get him killed with a punch.
And right after saying “Yes,”
“Life Mentor Adorable” suddenly saw a ten-minute countdown timer start ticking in front of him.
‘Survive for ten minutes to pass?’
As this thought flashed by, he saw the guy charging at him again, raising a fist that was almost as big as his head.
But this time…
“There’s room to react.”
Without thinking, “Life Mentor Adorable” threw out a scroll and unfurled it around himself.
A majestic mountain leaped off the paper.
A heavy aura enveloped the surroundings.
This item could absorb most types of attacks and then bounce them back…
This was one of the key items that helped them reach the fifth checkpoint of “Ghost Train,” and although there was a limit to how much it could absorb, it should last a few minutes at least…
“Since it’s about stalling for time, don’t blame me for using some tricks. First, I’ll get my hands on that Talent…”
He dragged out a modified rocket launcher from “Storage Room,” aimed at the enemy, and prepared to shoot.
But the next second, he saw several fist-sized dents punched into his scroll.
“Are you kidding me?!”
“Life Mentor Adorable’s” eyes bulged, and he hurriedly pulled the rocket launcher trigger.
However, the opponent didn’t dodge and exploded the incoming rocket with a punch, seemingly unscathed…
“Damn, that’s exaggerated! Is that even human?” he inwardly exclaimed in shock.
It was then that the majestic mountain in the scroll started cracking and then shattered.
In barely ten seconds…
The whole scroll became ineffective and fell to the ground!
“An excellent defensive item and this is how you use it? You release it and just stand behind it, daydreaming?”
A disappointed murmur rang in his ears.
“Life Mentor Adorable” was breathless from keeping up, unable to respond, and relying on some combat instincts, he felt the opponent seemed to leave a bit of space with each attack.

chapters.title: Chapter 465 - 465 400 The C Level Personnel Who Was So Angry
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 465: Chapter 400: The C Level Personnel Who Was So Angry He Lost Control._2 Chapter 465: Chapter 400: The C Level Personnel Who Was So Angry He Lost Control._2 If I had seized the opportunity, I might have held on for a few more seconds…
But…
Such opportunities were too fleeting, too hard to grasp.
Thus, I was left unable to care for myself, constantly being beaten, feeling intense pain all over my body along with the sound of bones breaking.
As I was being pummeled, time seemed to stretch on forever. Then I glanced at the countdown on my retina.
“How has only less than two minutes passed…”
In desperation, I realized that this C Level Personnel, who had started out “guiding” me, was becoming more and more irritable, more and more dissatisfied…
“Too weak! Too weak! Too weak! You are just too weak!”
“Who is your instructor!?”
“Let them come over. Rather than suffering a contaminated life worse than death due to weakness in the future, it’s better to die together now!!!”
The C Level Personnel’s fury intensified, veins in his eyes branching out as if his emotions were getting out of control.
What he despised the most was employees whose “deeds (items) did not match their positions.”
So many more capable members were struggling on the dangerous front lines, needing items that matched their own capabilities. Yet, with such unequal distribution, some still occupied spots without producing results…
It was unforgivable!
The rising rage led to the onset of a loss of control within him, suppressing rational thought, taking over more dominantly…
Several seconds later.
He lost control.
Bang!
In the final ten seconds before reaching three minutes, “Life Mentor Adorable,” who was being beaten, suddenly found that everything seemed to have reset to the beginning.
He still had three lives left.
However, more saddening than this discovery was the fact that he didn’t even know how he had just been killed.
Meanwhile, not only him but all employees except those on Colin’s battlefield were currently enduring the most straightforward and unadorned beatings.
Whether they were solo or in a team, hardly anyone could last three minutes.
In less than ten minutes, a large number of employees, full of fighting spirit, were forcibly ejected from the mission by a pair of iron fists.
“What kind of monster is this? How can a C Level Personnel be this monstrously strong? It’s not scientific…”
“Exactly, F Level can take on D Level with a chance, but D Level going up against C Level, there’s just no hope. The gap is even bigger than that between me and the dog downstairs from my house…”
“It’s not impossible, I can feel that he’s training us, constantly giving us chances, or else we wouldn’t be able to last even ten seconds. By the way, what about the Elder Brother who wanted to solo it earlier, did he make it through?”
“Indeed, he asked me if I were the closer, and I just told him ‘I am your grandpa’, and then I was done for…”
“Damn, look at the mission details, someone’s made it! First kill!”
“Who?”
“It’s Brother Shunzi…”
“…”
In the midst of numerous complaints and wailing from the company, Colin exited “The Nightmare Source of a Dying Ancient God” and couldn’t help but take a sharp intake of breath, feeling aches all over his body.
“Hss… I can hold out for ten minutes, but that’s just it.”
Colin rubbed his body, as if he could feel an indescribable phantom pain.
Compared to last time, this time he was much better off due to item upgrades and his own enhancements, and it was not a one-sided beating.
Of course, “The Light Chaser’s” private training also had a significant effect.
Otherwise, even if his hardware had caught up, without the right software, he might not have cleared it on the first try…
And indeed, he even forced his opponent to use a weapon, pulling out the rust-covered longsword from the ground. After that, his first life was lost…
Colin could only recall how his opponent seemed to flash into eighteen silhouettes, each silhouette drawing a space-cleaving slash.
He was struck dead on the spot, reduced to a pile of broken flesh.
“That C Level Elder Brother’s sword seems to be an orange-grade equipment too. The D Level employee who was a Fate Propeller didn’t even bother to share this crucial information with me, leaving me completely unprepared for the assault…”
“Compared to the ‘Heavenly Lightfall’ move, this eighteen-flash move combined with an orange-grade sword is the real killer move.”
“An instant eighteen fatal strikes, ‘Deadly Insight’ is useless to even see, at most, you just know how you’re going to die…”
Colin felt a lingering fear, as even when he had used Time Stop, he was still attacked by the opponent.
Even within the Time Stop, that thing completely enveloped him without any dead angle, leaving him no chance to escape.
The only way to dodge was to use another Golden Card “Force – Repulsive Force” at the same time, and within the effective range, repel all the attacks…
But, the C Level Elder Brother reacted quickly too, and after discovering it once, would change to forcing him to use either “Force Repulsion” or “Time Freeze” with each strike…
As for the performance of another Golden Artifact “Shield of Fairness Adjudication,” it was somewhat less than ideal.
Because the opponent was too well-rounded, Colin couldn’t find any really good points of restriction.
“This reminds me, to use the ‘Shield of Fairness Adjudication,’ I have to find a point where I’m clearly superior to the opponent, otherwise, I’m afraid I’d be the one turned into a slave.”
“However, this feeling of fighting with all my might is truly comfortable, and my next goal is to force the opponent to initiate ‘Item Liberation’.”
“Oh right, speaking of which, why wasn’t this orange gear in the selection list?”
Colin couldn’t help but grumble.
If there had been a choice of orange gear, he wouldn’t have chosen something like a lousy Fire Tree Mark.
Now, as he worked on fully restoring “Revolver Reverser” and was recasting the glory of orange gear items, he knew just how powerful items of that level were.
He would never again think of them as chicken ribs that were a pity to discard.
‘Sometimes, I really should look at my own issues, whether I have been seriously developing the full potential of items, whether I have been diligently reviewing missions…’
He scoffed inwardly,
and then, refocusing his thoughts, Colin opened the “Storage Room” to check out the Green Talent he had obtained from clearing the stage.[“Return to the Fundamentals” effect: In a battle before using a ‘signature move,’ you will receive a 10% to 1% improvement based on your own quality and strength. The stronger you are, the weaker the effect.]
“Note”: Currently can improve by 5.1%.
“Signature Move Determination”: “Matchless Strike,” “Heavenly Lightfall”…
…
“An improvement of five-point-one percent, this effect is actually quite okay.”
Colin nodded and then equipped it in another Talent Grid slot that had been freed up since he reached D Level.
“There’s no good choice for ‘Skills’ yet, but I can learn them stealthily, see if there’s a chance to steal one from ‘The Light Chaser’ or C Level Personnel…”
With this in mind, Colin reopened the task from the C Level Elder Brother and started training.
For the next day, he nearly soaked himself in the “Self-selected Trial Event,” constantly trying to improve himself.
This employee with extremely high combat experience would always swiftly detect his weaknesses and then launch an attack targeted at them.
And Colin would patch up his vulnerabilities quickly…
His previously floating strength gradually began to settle and solidify in the course of battles.
Unfortunately, it was still quite difficult to force the C Level Elder Brother into “Item Liberation.”
However, compared to his now “enjoyment” of the battle, other employees, after being beaten up, would even cry out in their sleep not to hit them anymore, no longer maintaining their previously optimistic attitude after one experience…
After all, those punches coming down were quite painful.
But even so, most employees still chose to continue paying money to enter the instance.
It wasn’t because they enjoyed getting hit, but because they realized that following what the C Level Elder Brother had said…
Their strength had indeed improved significantly.
Some employees even felt that their abilities had started to catch up little by little with the D Level elites they encountered on the ‘Chaotic Phantom Train’…
“It’s a pity, ‘Chaotic Phantom Train’ is gone, or else if we went as a team now to face them head-on, maybe we would have a chance to win.” A D Level Personnel couldn’t help but regret.
Many other D Level Personnel who had risen from that instance echoed the sentiment…
Another half-day went by, and just as Colin exited the instance, he saw a new mission appear.
“Take the place of ‘Dawn Star’ to respond to the follower’s call…”
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 466 - 466 401 A Bit Too Urbanized. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 466: Chapter 401: A Bit Too Urbanized. _1 Chapter 466: Chapter 401: A Bit Too Urbanized. _1 “The task requires, at 1 AM tomorrow morning, no, at 1 AM the day after tomorrow, to enter the hidden sanctuary of the ‘Dawn Star’ followers via projection, to use them as much as possible for intelligence gathering on other anomalous forces…”
“Then, gather them together and neutralize them harmlessly as a whole.”
“The time limit is half a month…”
After briefly reviewing the task, Colin could only sigh that the “Starlight Maiden” had defected thoroughly.
The entire ‘Dawn Star’ follower organization was probably sold out completely.
It wouldn’t be long before they were eradicated from this world.
“The only difficulty of the task is not to blow the cover, at least, before all the members of this organization return to their hidden sanctuary, you can’t just blow your cover….”
“With some assistance from the ‘Starlight Maiden’, the problem isn’t very serious.”
“And if the cover is blown after they return… just deal with it promptly, as long as no one finds out, I am still perfectly infiltrated.”
Upon briefly reviewing, Colin roughly understood the tricky part of this task.
When it came to coaxing people as a “Divine Envoy”, he was pretty much “in his element”, so there was no need to worry about stage fright or the like.
However, the believers of “Dawn Star” were somewhat abstract; he wondered if he could impersonate them well…
With a slight shake of his head, Colin looked up again at the wall clock; it was around five in the afternoon, with plenty of time left.
Then, he opened the parchment of the Trial Task to take a look.
The current usage was about 1,700 times, with team entries accounting for over 1,400, and solo ones less than 300…
“Calculating roughly, 20 points per team entry, 1,200 or so entries, rounded to 1,400, minus the company’s cut, I would get 14 points each, totaling over 19,000; rounding to 300 for solo entries, that’s about 23,000…”
“Not bad, with the task being open for not very long, I’ve earned more than 40,000 points, almost equal to what I’d get from a single relatively troublesome large task that I would do desperately.”
“With these points, I can consider repairing advanced items, but now, the clearance rate seems to have slowed down a lot…”
Colin murmured, then quickly determined the specific reasons after observing the internal group chat for about ten minutes.
Initially, the majority of those who experienced it were F Level Employees…
It’s just that, while this mission offers rewards, its more significant purpose is to improve one’s foundation.
And for F Level Staff, after entering the mission, even if a C Level Elder Brother is lenient and wants to guide, it’s easy to kill them unintentionally.
After all, they are in a semi-uncontrolled status, not a normal one.
So after experiencing being killed off once or twice, they lost their curiosity—in their view, the “World Code-13” task was difficult, but there was a chance to muddle through, and with good luck, they might be carried through…
This one requires real strength; no chance to muddle through means no way forward.
One after another, they cried out in desperation with statements like, “D Level Personnel can’t last three minutes, E level Personnel can’t withstand a minute, F Level Staff can’t hold for three seconds… against such a powerful individual, who else in the company could resist, what else in the company could resist?”
Then came the E level Personnel, some of whom were relatively capable and could barely learn something while taking a beating…
However, not many of them could learn something.
They were somewhat better than the F Level Staff but not by much…
To be frank, this mission was best suited for the current group of somewhat resigned D Level Personnel.
And they also contributed the vast majority of solo entry purchases.
“I guess once everyone’s strength improves, this task can truly make money. For now, although it’s not bad, it’s slightly lacking somehow. Hmm, the official double-duty employees seem to be saving a lot, hardly any of them participating, miserly thieves.”
Not too concerned about this, Colin ordered some takeout and, as usual, took his daily look at the group of “Pseudo-Humans.”
During this time, he had managed to stand his ground in the group and secure some say.
But…
Having a say didn’t seem to be of much use.
So far, Colin had hardly seen any useful information about this race in the group.
All these creatures talked about the whole day was how to imitate humans and the like, not doing any real work at all…
“No discussions about plotting to replace humanity, no display of extraordinary methods other than usurping human corpses, no signs of worshiping any being…”
“Tch, there seem to be some who believe in Buddha or Dao, or some Christ, but they are purely imitating to believe in something…”
“Why do they all have an attitude like they’re just playing games? It’s weird, these creatures, always out experiencing this and that, imitating humans relentlessly, what exactly do they want to do?”
Colin couldn’t help shaking his head.
Having observed for so long, if there were any gains, it wouldn’t have been like now, without any payoff at all.
Currently, all he knew was that they would replace some humans who were about to die, attach themselves like possession, taking over their original daily life, with a steadily increasing number, roughly one person per day…
The first question of each “Pseudo-Human” that joined the group was almost always about various minor everyday troubles.
Colin could clearly feel that they seemed genuinely eager to become human, but he didn’t know what prompted them to have such a desire…
Next, the only thing they were afraid of was “Supernatural Cops”, fearing that if they were discovered one day, they’d be captured and sliced up…

chapters.title: Chapter 467 - 467 401 A Bit Too Urbanized. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 467: Chapter 401: A Bit Too Urbanized. _2 Chapter 467: Chapter 401: A Bit Too Urbanized. _2 “It must be some sort of joke from that so-called ‘Mr. C’ that he found on some website, to scare these guys…”
His gaze swept over each piece of information, and Colin’s mind grew more perplexed.
He had come to learn a bit about this revered ‘Mr. C’ among the “Pseudo-Humans” in recent days.
It seemed he was the first of their kind to arrive in the human world.
An equivalent of a pioneer among them, he had taught many “Pseudo-Humans” the essentials of living…
But that was about it.
“Forget it, just keep observing. If there’s really an issue, the company should issue a corresponding task.”
After finishing his daily observations, Colin withdrew his attention.
Then, seeing that he still had some time, he started a few rounds in the “self-selected trials.”
It was not until late into the night that Colin lay back down by the window, waiting for the event to begin.
“The moon is so bright tonight…”
The pale moonlight poured in from outside the window. As Colin turned his head to look, he couldn’t help but exclaim, realizing it was a full moon tonight.
The crisp light seemed to drape the world in a hazy veil…
And that moon suspended in the sky…
Colin frowned suddenly, feeling somewhat… uncomfortable at the sight?
However, before he could ponder further, the time for the task arrived, and a transparent vortex appeared in the room, and from it trickled starlight that shone upon him.
It was at this moment…
Many kilometers away, in an independent spatial city accessible only at specific times and specific places,
Thousands of “Dawn Star” followers knelt on the ancient altar, lashing themselves with spiked whips. After each prayer, they would flog themselves, their bodies blurred with blood and flesh…
The smell of blood spread throughout the town.
However, despite how bizarre this method seemed, it only unified their resolve even more.
And this was their penance for losing the “Starlight Maiden.”
“Great ‘Dawn Star,’ I beseech you, grant us one more chance, a chance for redemption; for that, we are willing to offer everything…” a Priest said, trembling with fear.
The recent ritual had been a complete failure, with not only many high-ranking members within their organization dying but also the most important divine container, the “Starlight Maiden,” going missing.
Afterward, the Master’s response was completely cut off not long after the disappearance of the “Starlight Maiden.”
Had it not been for the ability to still use some associated blessings…
They almost believed they had been abandoned by the “Dawn Star.”
No, perhaps they had already been abandoned.
The power they now possessed was probably just something the great being couldn’t be bothered to reclaim…
The thought that he might never again experience the delight of being fiercely filled by those invisible tendrils drove the believer into despair.
If that was the case, what was the point of living?
However, just then, the despairing “Dawn Star” followers suddenly saw a glimmer of hope as countless stars fell from the dark canopy above…
Soon, within the altar, an indistinct shadow of starlight formed.
“It’s the aura of the ‘Master’!”
“Thank goodness! I knew it, I just knew that we wouldn’t be abandoned…”
“Praise the Great Will, praise the Divine Envoy!”
“…”
One after another, the “Dawn Star” followers, with reddened eyes and trembling lips, witnessed this.
And while they were moved, Colin also took the opportunity to cast his gaze upon this place, this bizarre space hidden from reality.
The space was not very large, probably totaling no more than 150,000 square meters, with pitch darkness beyond its edges.
Within this limited land, there were various modern buildings everywhere.
“If this place were a castle or something, the atmosphere might be full, but as it is, it lacks a sense of mystery…”
Colin judged in his mind, feeling it was a bit too urbanized.
Then, without giving it much more thought, he saw a High Priest approach, his upper body drenched in blood, surrounded by starry lights, emitting a faint divine aura.
“I am High Priest Ramir. May I ask, are you the new ‘Divine Envoy’, sir?” the High Priest asked tremblingly.
‘Not very strong, if I take this seriously, I could probably kill him within a few minutes. If I use the Golden Card, instantly taking him down wouldn’t be a problem either. But he seems to be willingly assigning me an identity? Good, saves me the trouble of making excuses…’
Colin, in his state of Starlight projection, looked at him and slowly nodded, uttering a simple “Yes.”
Upon hearing this, the thousands of believers burst into tears…
“Praise the Great Master, thank you for not abandoning us!” One follower, elated, grabbed a handful of leaves similar to those of nettles, and furiously rubbed them on his festering scalp.
“We request the great ‘Divine Envoy’ to lash us harshly…”
Aside from that, other followers also began performing various incomprehensible acts as if they had lost their minds…
‘I was prepared for this, but seeing it now still feels strange…’
Colin couldn’t help but criticize inwardly, these people stood out even among the various Heretic Forces.
Of course, what stood out was their peculiar behavior…
However, this time, Colin noticed that as these bizarre demons tormented themselves, their spiritual strength kept rising…
In the end, the spiritual power of a large group of people converged and connected with the “Light” on his body.
But after the frenzy went on for over a minute, when they saw that the “Divine Envoy” remained silent and did not torment them like the “Starlight Maiden” with invisible tentacles…
One by one, as if doused with a bucket of cold water, they all quieted down.
” ‘Master’s’ Angel Envoy, may I ask, what should we do?” the High Priest who had spoken earlier asked cautiously.
They had no doubts about Colin’s identity, for the power emanating from him was the genuine, unmistakable force of the “Dawn Star.”
If one wanted to impersonate such a thing, it would imply that the great being they worshiped was dead, otherwise it wouldn’t be possible.
But how could that be?
How could the “Dawn Star” possibly die!
Everyone knows that the great beings are eternal and immortal!
Therefore, a “Divine Envoy” graced with the power of the “Dawn Star” couldn’t possibly be a fake!
“I’ve come here to do three things…”
Colin looked at him and said calmly, “First, gather as much information about other Heretic Cults as possible. The last operation faced setbacks because the intelligence work wasn’t sufficient…
“Second, once we’ve gathered enough information, summon all believers here.”
“Third, when everything is ready, our Master will descend upon this world soon after!
“Everyone here will have the chance of spiritual ascension, to return to the ‘Master’s’ side, and bask in eternal glory!”
Hearing these words, the followers in the crowd were stunned for a moment, then burst into cheers again.
“We will definitely fulfill your entrustment! Within seven days, we must obtain all the information we can on the Heretic Forces…” the Priest hurriedly promised.
After speaking, he seemed to recall something and asked in a slightly lowered voice:
“Honorable Divine Envoy, how fares the holy ‘Starlight Maiden’, if I may inquire…”
He lost the bet, likely living more comfortably than you by now… With a thought fleeting through his mind, Colin’s expression remained unchanged as he spoke indifferently, “That is not your concern…”
As he spoke, a wave of pressure spread out from him.
Sensing the power within, the follower instantly felt a chill in his heart and quickly bowed his head in prayer for forgiveness.
However, at that moment, he heard the “Divine Envoy” reply in an indifferent tone:
“If all goes well, the ‘Master’ might return from its journey…”
Upon hearing this, he was overjoyed and promptly praised while promising, “Three days, just three days, and we will have fulfilled all that you have commanded!”
They had heard that the “Starlight Maiden” had disappeared, and with “Red Moon” followers involved, he had assumed that she may have been captured by the “Red Moon,” possibly tormented severely…
But now, going by the Divine Envoy’s words…
It seemed the tables had turned, and the danger had passed without incident!
A new era belonging to them was dawning!
Feeling the devout faith emanating from this Priest, Colin suddenly thought that merely using them to gather some information and then neutralizing them without harm felt like too small a gain.
After pondering for a moment, he opened his mouth and added a few minor requests of his own to the Priest.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 468 - 468 402
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 468: 402 Chapter 468: 402 “Spread the news of my ‘Master’s’ imminent arrival far and wide, in secret if possible…”
Colin finished speaking simply and saw the followers nearby lift their heads abruptly.
One by one, their faces betrayed shock and confusion, wondering if they had heard wrong to receive such an odd request.
If it weren’t for the fact that the speaker was the “Divine Envoy,” and it wasn’t for his arrival powered by the “Dawn Star,” the people present might have rushed forward to check if there was something wrong with his brain.
Once the news spread, a massive battle would surely erupt, and even this secret site might not remain hidden…
“Honorable Envoy of God… I, I don’t understand,”
Suppressing the shock Colin’s words had brought to his heart, the High Priest, bowing his head as with a hint of remonstration, said:
“If we do as you say, countless enemies will come, those damned followers of evil existences are likely to seek us out…
“There’s a certain chance against… of course, I don’t mean to question you, I am…”
He had meant to say that it might threaten the smooth arrival of the “Dawn Star.”
But before he could finish, he suddenly realized that to say so was to question the authority of the Great Will…
“It doesn’t matter.”
If they don’t come, I wouldn’t do this anyway… Colin muttered to himself, then spoke through the projection of starlight:
“The return of the ‘Master’ is a certainty, no force can stop it. When the time comes, their blood will be the first flames of fury proclaiming the return of the Great Will…”
As he spoke, Colin’s power of starlight spread, a powerful aura burst forth, silencing everyone present.
Contained within this radiance was indubitable power.
“Praise the ‘Dawn Star’!” Followers of the “Dawn Star,” a bit further away, though unaware of what had happened, nevertheless showed fervent expressions and offered devout prayers.
“I am guilty, I have committed the sin of doubting the God…” Feeling the killing intent within the starlight, the High Priest knelt before Colin, confessing devotedly.
How could he dare to question the decisions of God?
Truly deserving of death!
“Go and do as I have commanded.”
Colin nodded slightly; what he needed were mindless heretic personnel, not those capable of thought.
If this man dared to say another word, Colin wouldn’t mind neutralizing him first…
After all, is it you who are the “Divine Envoy,” or is it I?
Do my decisions, made on behalf of the “Master’s” will, require the questioning by a priest?
After pausing and seeing that the other party had the sense to ask no further questions, Colin continued to add some related details—such as summoning all followers of the “Dawn Star” to converge here.
Furthermore, he spread the message that the “Starlight Maiden” had almost succeeded and that the “Dawn Star” would descend to this world in twelve days.
At that moment, no one said anything further.
In the eyes of the vast majority of “Dawn Star” followers, just as Colin had said, the descent of the “Master” would drink the blood of countless enemies.
Moreover, after being bullied by that bunch of various evil beings for so long, they were more than eager to retaliate.
‘It seems that quite a few organizations are aware of the “Starlight Maiden”‘s information from the previous actions, yet no one knows the follow-up situation, after all, I’ve slaughtered everyone who came on the scene…’
‘Inside the ‘Red Moon’, there might be some who know the situation, but those orphans will hardly cooperate with others. Even if they take the initiative to speak, it’s not certain others would believe them, so there’s no need to worry too much about a leak of the true information.’
‘They should also know what it means if the “Starlight Maiden” successfully becomes the Container for the God; therefore, quite a number of high-ranking heretics will certainly come knocking…’
‘Tsk tsk tsk…’
Colin couldn’t help but sneer inside; by that time, there was no doubt this place would be bustling with activity.
To say they’d fight until the sky turns dark would be an understatement…
And those aberrant forces would have to come, even knowing it’s a trap, given the lack of key information—that the “Starlight Maiden” had betrayed.
In front of them lay only two options: one is to confirm the truth by losing a few high-ranking individuals, and the other is to watch the “Starlight Maiden” usher in the power of the God and return to reality…
As unacceptable as option one might be, compared to two, it wasn’t quite so unbearable.
Most of the Heretic Cults know what choice they should make.
‘This plan, one, will help defuse urbanization and reduce the anomaly index…’
‘Two, it will strike against a number of Heretic Cults, maintaining the stability of reality…’
‘Three, the rewards for the task should overturn quite a bit.’
Colin felt it was a case of killing three birds with one stone…
And then, after roughly outlining the situation, upon the altar in the secret Heretic City hidden in a special manner, Colin’s projection of starlight gradually faded…
Watching his figure disappear, the followers remained unmoved for a long while.
It was only after a considerable time that the High Priest slowly got up, a trace of confusion in his eyes. To tell the truth, as the current highest authority, he had sensed something slightly amiss about this “Envoy of God”…
Yet the power of that starlight was genuine…
If this all was a deception, he couldn’t bear to think further.
“To doubt further would be an unforgivable sin.”
Minutes later, he ultimately decided to act as the Envoy of God had required.
…
“Just relying on their power to disseminate the news might not be enough; I need to mobilize some official power, getting them to play along. With the credibility of officials as a guarantor, the scale of the event should be greater.”

chapters.title: Chapter 469 - 469 402
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 469: 402 Chapter 469: 402 Colin sat at the dining table, his fingers stroking his chin, a thoughtful expression flashing in his eyes.
Since it had to be done, it naturally had to be done thoroughly.
Not just officially, but if given the chance, he should also see if more assistance could be obtained from the company.
“For the company, clearing out heretic forces is also part of the routine, so it shouldn’t be a problem. Moreover, even if I can’t get help, my power is more than enough to disguise as a ‘Divine Envoy’ even if it can’t conceal the ‘Dawn Star’…”
As these thoughts flickered through his mind, Colin’s plan began to take shape.
After another ten minutes or so of checking for omissions, his brain finally ceased pondering…
“Ah, working with the company for so long, my heart has also started to turn a bit dark…”
With a sigh, Colin took out his cellphone and notified Xu Duojin to hurry over, then resumed eating the seafood feast that he had barely started due to various interruptions.
A stack of freshly prepared delicacies was brought over by the little maid.
Colin, while suppressing the “Hunger” within his heart, stuffed various foods into his mouth.
Through eating over the past half month, his weight had recovered rapidly and was almost back to that of a normal person.
At least when he went out, people would no longer think he was suffering from Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis or anything of the sort.
Almost three hours later, after eating continuously, there was a knock on the door.
“Come in.”
As Colin spoke, in walked Xu Duojin, dressed in a black suit and tie, carrying a briefcase. Without waiting for Colin to say much, he pulled a chair over to the table and sat down.
“I just finished eating. If you had come a bit earlier, you could have had a crab leg,” said Colin, picking his teeth with a toothpick fashioned from a part of the little maid, while looking at the other man.
Meanwhile, the little maid began to clear the mess on the table without any complaints.
Xu Duojin glanced at the “Nano-smart Machinery” that made scientists around the world exclaim as impossible and then sat up straight, facing Colin:
“Sorry for being late. Is there something you needed?”
Colin had not specified the details over the phone, and Xu Duojin, through his spiritual intuition, felt the matter was important but not particularly urgent, so he hadn’t left the important meeting he was attending about the “Awakener” matter…
“Let’s start with this…”
Colin took out one item after another that the company had sent down and pushed them across the table.
“This is…”
Xu Duojin took the items handed to him by Colin, inspected them closely, and quickly recognized that they were likely items with some special effects.
Moreover, the faint aura emanating from these items felt somewhat familiar.
He then realized these were the difficult-to-handle items that might not have very high World Codes but were extremely troublesome.
“They’ve been turned into items?”
Looking up at Colin with surprise, Xu Duojin held an item resembling a cabbage.
“Yes, have a look at them.”
“Okay.”
Xu Duojin nodded and examined each item. Although he already knew that the “Bonfire Company” had the ability to completely digest and process anomalies, actually seeing them still gave him a small shock.
The batch of anomalies he personally verified before were all things that even with great cost, were difficult to handle and even impossible to destroy on their side.
They could suppress and seal, but somehow they still couldn’t destroy them.
He hadn’t imagined that in such a short time, they would have changed into this form.
“Inside each item, there is more than one abnormal aura, but these abnormalities seem to only possess a small part of their original selves, having been disassembled and then recombined. The form is changed, and it’s hard to imagine how it’s done…”
After assessing each one, Xu Duojin finally shook his head.
At this moment, he faintly understood that sense of absurdity scientists felt when faced with the little maid.
It was as if the other party had broken common sense by telling him 1+1=3 and, damn it, it was correct.
However, since he wasn’t an employee of the company, even though the items were currently ownerless, he couldn’t see the detailed descriptions of the items.
It was unclear what effects these items had, what negative effects they might possess… Even before being verbally granted temporary authority, he wasn’t even qualified to use them…
But that was of no consequence, as among the officials, there were quite a few who were employees of the company.
“Alright, there are a total of eight items in this trade. I’ve taken one, and the rest are all yours,” Colin said, not accustomed to lying about such matters, as he handed over the other artifacts.
“No problem.”
Xu Duojin nodded, tactfully refraining from asking whether there really were only eight items or anything of that sort, as that would have been somewhat impolite to pursue.
Moreover, his, or rather the officials’ main purpose, was simply to resolve these difficult anomalies, and any other benefits that arose from them could be considered a bonus.
After a pause, Xu Duojin took the initiative to ask, “Mr. Colin, do you have any suggestions on how to use these items?”
Oh?
Hearing this, Colin, who was ready to turn the page and move on to the next matter, was momentarily taken aback, then quickly grasped the other party’s intention.
“Among these, there are two with healing effects, as well as one that can make plants grow rapidly, which might be very suitable for employees executing the ‘God Descent Project.'”
Colin provided his “suggestions.”
“I see.” Xu Duojin nodded and then looked at Colin, indicating the next matter.
Colin didn’t dawdle and directly shared some thoughts about the “Dawn Star,” informing the other party of his plans.
A few minutes later, Xu Duojin, a middle-aged man dressed in a suit but looking somewhat younger, nodded:
“No problem, I will mobilize the relevant forces shortly and assist you as much as possible…”Under the pretext of a divine descent, he would mobilize international forces to spread the news…
If it were up to Xu Duojin alone, it would be feasible to mobilize resources domestically, but it would be problematic abroad. However, making the request from Colin was another matter entirely.
In some sense, although Colin was not widely known within the organization, if he wanted to do something, even the world’s top Ninth Level Personnel could not ignore his requests. His influence was frighteningly high…
And since this matter was clearly beneficial for the officials, they had no reason not to cooperate.
However, the specifics of how to conduct the operation would depend on how Old Master Wu would respond after he received the intelligence.
“I expect the scene will be quite grand…”
Xu Duojin thought to himself and could vaguely foresee some indistinct inspiration.
Based on his understanding of those individuals, he could already envision the kind of spectacle it would instigate.
It was after discussing this matter, concluding the topic, that Xu Duojin picked up his briefcase, holding a bunch of artifacts, and was about to leave when he seemed to recall something and sat back down.
“Is there something else?” Colin leaned back in his chair, crossed his legs, and raised an eyebrow.
“This is the list of anomalous objects for the next trade…”
Xu Duojin opened his briefcase, pulled out a thick folder, and handed it entire to Colin.
Ordinarily, if they were still unable to confirm the company’s exact capabilities, they would likely have only given the first half of the folder. But now…
Having confirmed that the company truly had the ability to dismantle anomalies and turn them into artifacts, achieving a kind of “harmlessness” in another sense, he presented the complete list.
Xu Duojin felt that many of these artifacts were composed of multiple anomalies, suggesting perhaps that the company was showing off its skills.
