After all, according to his observations, most artifacts were not normally “stitched together” like these.
“Okay.”
Colin took the folder and glanced at it. The first few pages were fine, but the latter half listed many high-level anomalous beings that were challenging for the officials to deal with, including some marked as “ultra-high risk”…
‘According to the company’s metrics, this should be close to the standard for Level 2 Containment Subjects.’
Estimating in his mind, Colin thought that this time he should select an appropriate one from here to be used as an upgrade material for the “World Code-13” Bonfire…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 470 - 470 403 The Parchment with Anomalies. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 470: Chapter 403: The Parchment with Anomalies. _1 Chapter 470: Chapter 403: The Parchment with Anomalies. _1 “The Level 2 Containment Subjects that can meet the company’s standard, intuitively, there should be four of them, just not sure if they can fit into the ‘Storage Room’. I’ll have to find time to try it after the upcoming task is complete…”
Colin silently estimated as his gaze swept over the list of high-level anomalies.
If you compare it to the strength level of that great pirate in ‘World Code-4’, a Level 2 Containment Subject should be several times stronger, though I’m not exactly clear on how much stronger,” Colin mused.
Nevertheless, even for him now, facing such a level of creatures,
a careless mistake could potentially lead to an accident.
After all, in some of the more backward areas of certain worlds, they’ve already earned the right to be called ‘God’.
“Mr. Colin, do you have a time for the next trade?” Xu Duojin, who was next to Colin, asked after seeing him finish reviewing the containment subject list.
‘We haven’t been given a mission yet, so I’m not too sure.’ Colin murmured inwardly, but outwardly, he said without a trace of difference, “Come back and ask in a few days.”
He guessed that once he returned successfully from this task, the trade time would be announced.
Hearing this, Xu Duojin nodded without further inquiry or questioning the reasons, changed the topic, asked about other matters, and upon realizing there was nothing more, he stood up to take his leave.
“By the way, take the trash out with you.”
Colin reminded him.
With a shake of his head and a wry smile, Xu Duojin didn’t say much, picking up the black trash bags the Little Maid had packed.
With a bang, the door closed, and one less person was present in the room.
Colin withdrew his gaze, glanced over the containment subject list again, and finally put it back into the “Storage Room.”
Then, after looking at the task for the day after next, he couldn’t help but sigh:
“It’s almost January 1 of the new year, others have started their holidays, and only I am still working overtime, not knowing to what unknown place I’ll have to travel on business…”
In recent times, in addition to various company or official matters, people like the Dean had also been in touch with him…
Especially, the Dean had recently implied in his questions whether he had a sugar daddy of some sort, suggesting that he bring his girlfriend over for a meal during the holidays.
Facing this situation, Colin reminded Xu Duojin and arranged for those people to be kept busy.
For instance, arranging all sorts of honorary activities for the old man, the subsidies that used to take half a year to be approved were now arriving every day, leaving no extra free time…
As for his son, Brother Chuan, Colin’s childhood friend, that was simpler: just add a bunch of new orders to his factory.
Being busier meant fewer issues to deal with.
“If I really need to get in touch, it seems I’ll have to wait until the end of days…”
Shaking his head, Colin stopped his wandering thoughts, looked at the requirements of the task, and glanced at his current few cubic meters of space, starting to contemplate how to prepare for this task.
“The only useful information I have is that this task is related to a Golden Card, but unfortunately, I don’t know which one it is, so I can’t prepare specifically for it. It looks like I’ll have to start with stocking up on supplies…”
With experience in ‘pioneering’ multiple times, although Colin wasn’t clear about the specifics of the destination, he wouldn’t hesitate about what to bring.
“Food doesn’t have to be delicious; prioritize what’s necessary for survival. Considering my current physical condition, eating just a little something could probably sustain me for a month or two, or even if push came to shove, relying on ‘Hunger’ to eat some stones would keep me alive for quite some time…”
“However, I should still bring some along. As for other items, functional ones like the Little Maid and various company tools are basically interchangeable, so I just need to prepare a set of emergency gear…”
“Then there’s all sorts of bullets and the like. Tch, speaking of which, I’d almost forgotten that my revolver can now fire 155mm caliber bullets…”
Pursing his lips, Colin was reminded that apart from ‘Item Liberation,’ the intrinsic property of the “Revolver Reverser” had also kept up to date…
He took out the revolver, looked it over twice, and then made a call to Qin Chuan.
To arrange for some large-caliber bullets…
“Okay, Mr. Colin, I’ll get right on it… Huh? Wait a minute…” Qin Chuan’s somewhat muffled voice came through from the other end of the phone, as if he had just woken up from sleep.
As one of Colin’s subordinates, he had grown accustomed to sudden late-night calls, being asked to arrange all sorts of matters.
This time, however, after he came to his senses, he noticed what the request was for—155mm caliber ‘bullets.’
Is that even a bullet? Shouldn’t that be called a shell!?
“What’s wrong?” Since there was a few seconds pause on the other side, Colin asked.
Thinking of Mr. Colin’s experiences and knowing he might not have undergone proper military training or had many related military hobbies, Qin Chuan considerately reminded him:
“Mr. Colin, the 155 caliber isn’t a bullet anymore; it’s a shell. One shell of this kind usually starts at about forty to fifty kilograms…”
“Yup, that’s the kind of bullet I need.”
While holding the phone between his neck and shoulder, Colin glanced again at the description of the “Revolver Reverser.”
From a few millimeters to one hundred fifty-five millimeters, the revolver could adapt to any of these bullet sizes…
Honestly, when he first leveled up, the description surprised him as well.
He had wondered how the small gun could shoot such large ammunition…
But now, considering the gun itself came with a separate chamber space, it seemed less impossible to Colin…
One day, when it’s complete at “100%,” he wouldn’t be surprised if it could shoot nuclear warheads.

chapters.title: Chapter 471 - 471 403 The Parchment with Anomalies. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 471: Chapter 403: The Parchment with Anomalies. _2 Chapter 471: Chapter 403: The Parchment with Anomalies. _2 ‘Speaking of which, for personnel above C Level, even B Level staff, a 155mm caliber shell might really not be too different from a normal bullet…’
Colin remembered the body of the C Level Elder Brother.
He estimated that if a shell with added special effects hit him, it would most likely not leave much of a mark.
At least, Colin made a rough comparison and thought that if he were in a fully stimulated “Hunger” state, he wouldn’t be afraid of such a shell. In fact, he could swallow it and digest the kinetic energy it carried along with it…
And the C Level Elder Brother had said before that if he hadn’t been in poor condition, he might have wanted to fight with that little part of “Hunger” in him.
Obviously, even if he couldn’t win, he wouldn’t be off by much.
He naturally had no fear of ordinary conventional weapons.
However, this thing, when dealing with some stronger but not too strong individuals, would be a bit more convenient than taking action himself.
“It’s a cannon, forget it, Mr. Colin, do you have any requirements for the performance of the bullets? And approximately how many do you need?” Qin Chuan seemed to realize that for his boss, these might really be at the level of standard bullets…
So he didn’t dwell on it any longer.
“The more armor-piercing capabilities, the better. Prepare around one cubic meter’s quantity of that. Besides, prepare some bullets of other types too, altogether making up about a cubic meter as well. Also, I hear there are some special, extraordinary bullets?” Colin spoke up.
“Yeah, some bullets can make the enemy’s luck turn bad after hitting them, as well as special explosives and some special grenades…”
“Get a variety of those then, and deliver them to my office tomorrow. I’ll take care of the receiving…”
Colin said this unapologetically, without a hint of concern that he might be refused.
Afterwards, he made some other requests and ended the call.
“‘Revolver Reverser’ itself has an independent one cubic meter space magazine. With another one or two cubic meters of space to carry these things, the bullets should be enough. If not, there’s always ‘Air Bullet’…”
He put away the revolver, stood up, and returned to his bed to check the status of his other items, making sure there wouldn’t be any hiccups for his upcoming assignments.
He went through each item in his possession…
“Time Freeze,” “Force Repulsion,” “Revolver Reverser,” “False Mighty One,” “Mountain of Smiling Corpses,” “Fire Tree Mark,” “Gluttony Power Mark,” “Widow Yukionna,” “Analytical Lens,” and Bone Spur related to the Church of Light…
“Aside from ‘Double’ existing in a special passive form, it seems like these are the main items for now. However, ‘Analytical Lens’ and ‘Mark of Gluttony’ are starting to fall behind like money-grubbing slaves…”
Colin sat cross-legged on the bed, contemplating that if something had to be phased out next, it should be these two.
Of course, while he couldn’t make much use of these two items, he hadn’t thought about selling them…
He could hand them over for his subordinates to use.
“To tell the truth, ‘Mountain of Smiling Corpses’ is also having trouble keeping up on the battlefield. But that thing is tough. Summoning it at a critical moment can help block some curses and supermodel attacks or serve as a one-time meat shield…”
“If I had the same raw materials, maybe I could upgrade it a bit, but similar materials are a bit hard to find…”
The best material, of course, would be “Human Patchwork Monster.”
But unfortunately, although there seemed to be many copies of this thing, it appeared to be a rare monster.
Since he killed one before, it had completely vanished without a trace. He hadn’t seen a second one, and he had no idea where it might be hiding now…
Ensuring there were no issues with his equipment, he put everything away and Colin breathed out a long sigh.
He casually checked the parchment again, didn’t notice anything new, and was ready to go back to sleep…
But at that moment, he suddenly remembered something.
“Li Ming and the other two seem to have reached F Level, right?”
Colin thought for a moment, then closed his eyes, his consciousness swiftly sinking down.
Soon, when he “opened his eyes” again, he was already in a familiar place…
Streams of orange-red light rained down from above. Looking up, one could see a massive fireball resembling an abnormal celestial body continuously spewing out vast flames suspended high in the sky.
Under its radiant firelight, the entire world seemed to warp and wriggle like melting magma.
Directly below it, in a hall filled with the traces of war and rust, Colin sat at the end of a ruined gray stone long table…
He looked up, glancing at the object in the sky.
When he first opened this office, Colin had always thought the thing above was a special effect. But as time passed and his rank increased, he realized…
This was indeed a special effect, but this effect might not be imaginary.
Perhaps there really is such a special place within the company.
“Bonfire,” huh…
However, not giving it much thought, Colin’s eyes moved, glancing toward a particular seat on the side of the gray stone long table, With a thought, a flame moved with his will, igniting on the seat and quickly condensing into a humanoid shape—
This was his arrangement for his own “Brother Shunzi” nesting dolls.
Next, Colin was about to pull the trio in for a meeting, but suddenly noticed that there seemed to be 29 more faintly visible points of light on the table in front of him…
“Are these the 29 people I recruited before?”
Colin sensed these glimmers of light, and an inspiration flashed through his mind.
Only, these points of light were currently a bit dim, and the connection wasn’t as clear as with the trio, making it difficult to pull people in.
He estimated that after one or two more rounds of tasks, the lights would be clearer, and then he would be able to recruit people…
“It seems there aren’t enough seats, looks like I’ll have to change the format of the place, make it look like a big auditorium, and then at the back of the auditorium at the highest point set up a seat that’s elevated…”
“Heh, that being said, when I really pull this bunch in, they will probably get quite a shock, and some employees might even think of me as an ‘invader’ or something, they might even report me…”
Colin made a self-deprecating remark, but his intuition told him.
Once he pulled people in, he wouldn’t have to worry about being reported anymore…
Afterwards, with a thought, three stars fixed on the seats spontaneously combusted, shaping into familiar figures like a “vest.”
Li Ming and the other two were notified and immediately submerged into this place.
“Mr. Bonfire Agent, greetings…” the trio greeted Colin, who was seated at the end of the table.
“Mm.”
Only after that mysterious and powerful figure, shrouded in gun smoke, gave a nod indicating they could sit down, did the three sit once again and then turned their heads to look at the leader who appeared to have been waiting for some time.
In fact, in “World Code-13,” the leader also walked as a “Bonfire Agent.”
But in this “Hall of the Gods,” only the person at the end of the long table could be the agent.
As for who “Bonfire” is…
Li Ming couldn’t help but sneak a glance at the great fireball above, feeling along with the other two that it… seemed alive.
Without lingering on the view, the leader’s voice came through.
“You’ve reached F Level now?” Colin looked over the trio, quickly getting a rough grasp of their status.
“Yes,” the three nodded in unison.
“What are your names? Let me see if I can add you, so we can contact each other directly through parchment in the future,” Colin inquired.
Having parchment would make future contacts more convenient. As for this place, each opening seemed to consume a bit of energy.
Better to save it for occasional meetings, which could retain more of a sense of mystery.
“We can, but, I’m only at F Level, seems like I can’t add people, nor can I speak…” Li Ming scratched the back of his head.
Hearing this, before Colin could speak, Tang Ken and Lin Yilan looked at each other and said simultaneously:
“We… also seem unable to speak.”
“What do you mean?” Colin raised an eyebrow, not quite understanding what they meant.
But soon, after hearing their explanation, his brows furrowed deeply.
There seemed to be some problems with the parchment function of these three people.
For example…
Their “Interactive Hall” was sealed and restricted to some extent.
How could this situation arise?
Amidst his confusion, an insight sparked in his mind, and Colin suddenly realized something…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 472 - 472 404 Signals from the Depths of Space_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 472: Chapter 404: Signals from the Depths of Space_1 Chapter 472: Chapter 404: Signals from the Depths of Space_1 ‘Interaction Hall’ speaking ability locked, can watch but cannot speak, seems like it’s not just us who have this issue…’
‘I seem to have the same problem, too. Once you exceed a certain number of times, it feels like you’re going to die.’
‘But I remember, when I first joined the company, there wasn’t this restriction…’
Frowning, pieces of information in Colin’s mind connected at this moment—
When he finished the first loop of the mission and returned to Earth, in the first few days after he joined the company, he sent quite a few messages without any mention of restrictions.
The appearance of this restriction happened after he returned from the second loop of the mission.
At that time, he saw a door, entered it, and then arrived at Lady Bunny’s office…
And then the restriction appeared.
Though he felt something was off at the time, he didn’t think too much about it, no, to be more precise, under some indistinct guidance, he had subconsciously avoided thinking about related matters until now when his power increased, and he began to ponder some questions.
Thinking of this, Colin glanced at the trio who were clearly confused.
Then deep inside, he was certain of one thing…
“The reason for the restriction must be related to Lady Bunny…”
The way these three joined the company, officially he selected them, but in reality, it can be said that they were personally brought in through “Lady Rabbit”.
If the company’s recruitment is through some unknown selection to draw specific people, then she quite simply specified them.
Apart from Lady Bunny, he hadn’t seen a second person who could achieve this.
Originally, Colin thought, they should have entered through the company’s normal process.
But thinking about it now, it likely wasn’t so certain…
If it was truly a legitimate entrance, then there wouldn’t be any restrictions.
Of course, just these alone Colin didn’t find too concerning, but there was one more thing on top of these.
“During the period I was in contact with ‘Lady Rabbit’, it seems that an ‘Expel the Invaders’ mission was added, this… item, I remember is still on my taskbar…”
Colin instinctively thought to raise his hand and pinch his forehead, but considering the others, he refrained from making any excess movements.
However, under these circumstances, if he still hadn’t noticed that “Lady Rabbit” might probably perhaps have some issues…
Without the meddling of a mysterious force, he might as well be blind.
The company they entered might not be the same one he was in…
There’s a certain probability they entered Lady Bunny’s branch company.
“Also, speaking of which, I’ve never seen ‘The Light Chaser’ speak in the company, could it also be for this reason?”
“Did she join through a branch company route as well, so she’s like the trio, only able to watch but not talk?”
“Sss… thinking about it, it seems quite reasonable, feels about right.”
Behind the smoke that concealed his form and features, Colin pursed his lips, his mood relaxing slightly.
For someone of Lady Bunny’s caliber to have her own branch company was not incomprehensible.
Then, the reason for the restriction may be related to the interface between the main company and the branch company, and there might be some slight conflicts between the two?
In thought,
Colin sensed the well-known mission called “Unyielding Guardians” in his mind—
The creepy red font, million points, ultra-rare item, B Level…
If Lady Bunny really was associated with this, then judging from these rewards, the relationship between the two might be slightly more intense than the “minor conflict” he had imagined?
However, it was at this moment that he felt an almost imperceptible sensation of trepidation envelop his surroundings.
“Sss…”
Colin suddenly realized that what he was thinking about now seemed a little bit dangerous.
He took a deep breath in secret, suppressing his emotions.
“Forget it, it’s a big problem but panicking won’t help, I should just focus on what needs to be done for now…”
Colin muttered to himself, his current understanding of the company itself was still too limited, thinking wildly in this direction hardly yielded meaningful information and might instead trigger some dangerous mechanism…
It would be better to wait until he leveled up and naturally understood what needed to be understood.
Moreover, if it wasn’t for Lady Bunny, it’s not very realistic for him to want to grow so quickly….
Without definitive evidence, it was inappropriate to make such wild guesses about the other party.
Afterward, reining in his thoughts, Colin decided not to ponder further, and turned his attention to the trio, asking them about the status of the parchment.
“Besides the ‘Interaction Hall’ restriction, there are also missing ‘Expel the Invaders’, ‘Unyielding Guardians’, and other special nationwide tasks from the task bar…”
“Then recently, during the ‘Ghost Train Incident’, all idle personnel went, but they didn’t…”
“However, aside from these minor issues, everything else is fine, internal market, item trades can all be conducted.”
Colin roughly understood the situation with the trio under his command.
At this moment, Li Ming, who had been asked for a while, spoke up, “Boss, is our situation abnormal?”
“No, it’s very normal, there’s nothing wrong, just some small BUGs,” Colin reassured
After speaking, Colin casually added, “It should be fine after a while.”
As for when that would be, that was anyone’s guess.
“Wow, then that’s alright,” Li Ming and the others breathed a sigh of relief.
At first, they thought something was wrong when Shunzi kept asking questions, but it turns out it was just a minor BUG.
At this time, Xia Liufang raised her hand, waiting for Colin to gesture before speaking, she asked curiously:
“By the way, our mission type, is it that ‘Descent Project’ with nine deaths out of ten as mentioned by Kě’ài duō (Cute Duo)?”
In the past two days while browsing the company’s internal communication channels, not only had she seen many former colleagues, but she had also noticed this.

chapters.title: Chapter 473 - 473 404 The Signal from the Depths of Space_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 473: Chapter 404: The Signal from the Depths of Space_2 Chapter 473: Chapter 404: The Signal from the Depths of Space_2 Colin gave a clear and affirmative reply.
“Is that so…” Xia Liufang nodded without showing much concern.
Under the boss’s leadership, except for the first day, they didn’t find anything too difficult in “World Code-13,” which had largely stabilized by now.
Moreover, she didn’t go there on the first day for some reasons.
After she finished asking, Tang Ken also spoke up, “What should we do next? Should we buy the ‘F Level Compensation Medicine’ first, or should we get some tools instead?”
Hearing his words, the other two also pricked up their ears.
Frequently undertaking Descent Protocols, they undoubtedly had more points than their peers.
However, the excess was relatively limited…
They had to choose either the medicine or one or two props, as they couldn’t have the best of both worlds.
“Let’s buy the medicine first. We can think about authority promotion later for the props, and I can lend you some when the time comes…”
Colin briefly helped to plan their direction.
Afterwards, following a brief exchange, Colin concluded this temporary discussion.
Lying in bed and looking at the familiar ceiling, Colin deftly closed his eyes, hugged the pillow, and fell swiftly into a deep sleep.
Directly clearing his mind…
As time went by, the time for the mission arrived quickly.
January 1st, Sunday, twelve o’clock noon.
An ancient and distant sound of a clock chimed punctually by his ear, followed swiftly by a surging fog blanketing everything.
This time, however, when Colin woke up, he was slightly stunned…
In front of him was still the unending, surging grey mist…
“What’s going on?”
Colin stood firm in the swirling mist, arching an eyebrow. As an experienced traveller through the Descent Protocol, he could sense that he should still be within the “Protocol.”
And it was at that moment when some kind of guidance emerged within him…
“Left side, eleven o’clock direction…”
Following the guidance, Colin turned and walked towards that direction without hesitation.
His feet sinking into the writhing fog as if trudging through snow, he left deep footprints behind with every step…
Soon, a thread of starlight appeared in front of him.
Colin squinted his eyes, flames arose around him, attempting to sense his surroundings, but unfortunately, even the Bonfire couldn’t illuminate far in this enigmatic grey mist.
But detecting no danger, he took a deep breath and continued his action.
Another roughly fifteen minutes later…
Colin saw a door, an arched door standing amidst the grey mist.
The main body of the door was two grey stone pillars, and sandwiched between them was a dark, profound, special transparent black curtain, covered with twinkling stars that flickered incessantly…
After a brief glance, Colin looked bemused as he realized…
The door seemed to be made from something familiar.
“Starlight Maiden?”
Colin clicked his tongue, noticing that the “Starlight Maiden,” who had been captured not long ago, now had her dark robe brutally torn open in the middle, then stretched out and nailed firmly onto two stone pillars with dozens of nails, forming a three-meter-tall gate.
Even so, she was still alive; Colin could faintly feel the “door” trembling softly.
Uttering quiet, non-human murmurs…
However, this wasn’t important. An instinct told him that he had to walk through this “door” to reach his destination.
“Quite a brutal way to utilize it.”
Colin didn’t hesitate, flames wrapped around him, forming a layer of protection as he walked towards it.
Soon, when he reached the door, he slowly extended his hand and entered the body of the “Starlight Maiden,” not sensing any danger or abnormality, and then he stepped forward, walking into it…
The next instant, countless stars streaked past behind him, a multitude of almost intangible messages coming from those lights.
Many indescribable presences seemed to notice him but couldn’t keep up with him.
However, all this was unknown to Colin, who was in a state of trance.
When he came back to his senses, he suddenly felt weightless, as if floating, unable to touch anything beneath his feet, with no directional sense of up, down, left, or right, and the dazzling starlight before his eyes fading away into darkness all around…
An indescribable sense of suffocation and loneliness swept over him.
Clearly, he had come alone to another unknown region.
“What the hell is this place? Hiss, no good, my body feels so awful…”
Colin felt his body seemed to be collapsing from the inside out, as if it was about to explode.
With some initial protective force fading away, the extreme discomfort rapidly intensified.
However, when a burst of flame suddenly erupted,
the indescribable pain gradually vanished.
But unlike in a normal world, where flames rise “upward” like a lit candle, this time it seemed a bit chaotic, clinging to his body and dispersing in all directions…
Nevertheless, with the power of Bonfire, Colin also figured out where he was.
“Crap, what’s the deal? Turns out it’s freaking outer space.”
Colin looked around and couldn’t help but curse under his breath. Though he had never left the Earth’s atmosphere, he was not entirely clueless about these things and quickly realized the situation based on some basic concepts.
Then, looking at the pitch-black surroundings.
Colin skillfully tossed out a can of grease, and the flame erupted. Under his will, it gathered just above the back of his head, forming a huge fireball about five meters in diameter, slowly rotating inward…
By the light radiated from this fireball, Colin saw that he was in the midst of a dense field of asteroids of various sizes.
Numerous rocks of different sizes drifted slowly in the dark…
“No wonder it’s a solo type of mission. If it were any other employee and they weren’t prepared, they’d probably just arrive at the destination, be exposed to this kind of space, and immediately explode on the spot.”
Muttering to himself, Colin applied BUFFs to himself while curiously observing his surroundings.
Although unexpected, he wasn’t surprised to be in such a place.
He just didn’t know what he was supposed to do here.
At that moment, as if remembering something, Colin silently thought, “Bonfire Camp Special Item Containment Company.”
The flickering signal connection began to solidify a lot.
Immediately after, a new event began to emerge from his mind…
[Event One: Target area has been largely confirmed. Please proceed to the destination as soon as possible for further investigative actions.]
…
Seeing the mission, Colin subconsciously sensed the direction through it.
Then, the corner of his mouth twitched…
In the distance, there was a vague glimpse of a gigantic celestial body. That seemed to be his target destination.
But…
“This has got to be a joke, the landing location this time is a bit too far off, isn’t it?”
Colin couldn’t help but take a sharp breath. Just the distance felt like it could almost circle the entire Earth!
At this moment, comparing horizontally with the Descent projects he had performed in the past, he realized that deviations like “World Code-13” could now be described as precise.
A few dozen kilometers, a few hundred kilometers, on this scale, were nothing at all.
However, since he was already here…
Colin collected his emotions and pulled out the “Yukionna” ring from the Storage Room. After confirming that it was not affected here, he released it to create an ice cone “battleship.”
He then had the “Nano-smart Machinery” attach to it, enhancing the ship.
Finally, Colin turned into a thruster, propelling the battleship towards the target direction…
Soon, he discovered that moving in this almost frictionless environment, his speed was much faster than he had imagined.
And it was still accelerating…
If he accidentally hit something, even for him, it would be a troublesome affair.
But fortunately, the “dense” asteroid belt, while seeming dense, actually had frighteningly large gaps between them, enough to fit several celestial bodies without any problem…
Along with various sensory enhancements, Colin was not at all worried that he would die from colliding with something.
And, there were no anomalies or enemies emerging in the vicinity.
The journey was tedious and dull…
Sometime later, the Little Maid’s cat-eared head suddenly emerged from the ice cone battleship.
Its delicate face looked at Colin, and immediately text appeared on his retinas:
“Mr. Colin, I’ve received some unknown signal frequencies…”
“Hmm? Signal frequencies?”
Colin expressed surprise and then grew curious, responding in his mind, “Did it say what it’s about?”
“Unknown, but, it seems to be sending out a distress signal…”

chapters.title: Chapter 474 - 474 405 Do Not Approach Do Not Approach Do
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 474: Chapter 405: Do Not Approach, Do Not Approach, Do Not…_1 Chapter 474: Chapter 405: Do Not Approach, Do Not Approach, Do Not…_1 “A distress signal? Are there still living people in this damned place?”
Surprise showed on Colin’s face, but after a moment of thought, it didn’t seem too strange, so he continued to ask:
“Where is the distress signal coming from? Can you hear the specifics?”
“It might contain the meaning of ‘help’ and seems to be mechanically sent on repeat, not by a living person. Beyond that, the rest is unknown, as the signal is very weak when it reaches here. The location, it seems, is just ahead…”
“Ahead, then that must be where the target is.”
Colin pondered. He was a bit curious about what could be emitting this signal…
It could be humans, or an anomaly, or perhaps one of the xenomorphic races.
Anyway, the possibilities were numerous…
But no matter which it was, he now had to be careful not to capsize in the gutter all at once.
With this in mind, Colin slowed down a bit to prepare for any sudden situations, but he didn’t reduce the range of the flame’s illumination. On the contrary, he expanded it further…
Even though this increased the likelihood of being discovered by something bizarre.
But it also increased the likelihood of detecting anomalies.
Then, after several more boring but cautious hours, Colin, shooting forward like a comet, suddenly saw the space ahead open up into a vast and immense void of darkness.
Then he squinted, his pupils contracting, and looked ahead through the diffused light of the flame, his breath catching slightly.
A celestial object of immense size occupied most of the view ahead and conveyed an intangible oppressive force to Colin, who gazed directly at it.
After steadying his emotions, Colin focused his attention and surveyed the celestial body before him.
It drifted at the center of the open space, and further around it, one could vaguely make out strange asteroid belts…
Overall, it looked quite like a moonscape archetype.
The encircled celestial body was shrouded in a dark mist, looking as if it were covered in black mold from afar.
An indescribably eerie aura slowly emanated from it…
“From this angle, it looks a bit like the Earth viewed from the Moon on TV, though the distance isn’t quite that far…”
Colin opened his mouth to mutter silently.
Then he collected his thoughts, his gaze moving to several gigantic man-made objects around the perimeter of the spheroid misty celestial body—
Three massive and severely damaged rings.
Their presence made the sphere resemble a special kind of gyroscope.
And it was at that moment that the Little Maid reappeared, bringing a line of translated text onto Colin’s retina.
“Mr. Colin, I have received a recognizable signal frequency. After translation, it’s confirmed to be a distress message, roughly meaning: ‘Alert… Star… calling’ severe damage, urgently requesting assistance…”
“Recognizable… message?”
Upon hearing this, Colin immediately realized that the object on the celestial body was likely related to Bonfire Company.
Otherwise, decoding alone would not know how long it would take…
However, for some reason, a spiritual instinct made Colin feel that the information given by the Little Maid might not be quite right.
“Can you send me the original content of the signal to take a look?”
Colin inquired, and after receiving an affirmative nod from the Little Maid, he quickly obtained the signals.
Then…
He discovered that they seemed to be some sort of coded language, completely incomprehensible, but after just two or three seconds, Colin suddenly grasped another layer of information.
This information, compared to what the Little Maid provided, was completely contradictory…
“Do not approach, do not approach, do not…”
“Anyone who enters… will be trapped…”
“All things approaching this place…”
“…please be careful…”
“…”
Because the signals were incomplete, the obtained information was not entirely clear, but it was evident that the content differed significantly from a so-called “distress” message.
It was then that a flash of insight struck Colin’s mind, realizing the reason for this discrepancy.
‘It requires a true human interpretation to obtain the real message, while other life forms only receive a false message…’
‘So this means, that distress signal is like fishing bait? If Different Races heard it, knowing a company force is calling for help, they would likely move in to kick it and then… there would be no after…’
After deciphering the message, Colin found it a bit amusing.
It was consistent with the style of the previous generation of Bonfire Company employees, who were generally harsh and had the kind of character to bite back even while on the brink of death or leave a trap.
It’s very likely a trap that was laid when this place fell… one of them, at least.
Their treatment of all non-human entities and heretics was really without mercy.
“But, my mission this time is to come here. If I don’t approach, then wouldn’t my trip be in vain?”
Colin murmured to himself.
Then his gaze returned to that thing shrouded in black mist, which had been referred to as something Alert, something Star, something number, and started to wonder what had occurred here.
The true signal indicated that entering would surely result in entrapment.
But it didn’t mention why one would get trapped…
“Is it this black mist? Next, shall I enter the moldy celestial body to investigate?”
Colin paused briefly, and without too much hesitation, continued moving forward.
At this moment, he became even more cautious, referencing the full name of Bonfire Company each time he moved a distance, to ensure the connection didn’t break.
‘If the signal is lost here, it’s going to be big trouble.’
As thoughts flashed through his mind, Colin drew ever closer to the gyroscope-like celestial body with the three rings, at its moldy heart…

chapters.title: Chapter 475 - 475 405 Dont Approach Dont Approach Dont..._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 475: Chapter 405 Don’t Approach, Don’t Approach, Don’t…_2 Chapter 475: Chapter 405 Don’t Approach, Don’t Approach, Don’t…_2 And as the distance closed, he saw the outermost ring refracting a chilling metallic luster through the flames.
It was vastly more spacious and huge than what he had seen from the outside, perhaps with the width of the ring alone stretching for tens to hundreds of kilometers…
On it were lined up a multitude of indistinct devices, whose specific functions were unclear, but all emanating a profound sense of technology.
“The ring didn’t trigger any so-called defense mechanisms, could it be scrapped? No, all the black fog is confined within the ring, this must not be a coincidence…”
“So, ‘cannot enter’ means, one can’t enter within the outer ring?”
“However, if we talk about it, if a few super energy cannons were added on top, it would be simply perfect…”
Colin couldn’t help but speculate that the outermost ring might be weapon-related, it’s just a pity he seemed not to have seen parts that could be called weapons.
He saw none of those planetary orbit cannons described in sci-fi works…
Or perhaps, some of those incomprehensible devices might be lethal weapons.
He just couldn’t recognize them.
But before Colin could think much about it, he suddenly received a notification.
[“Event One” has been completed.]
[“Event Two”: Ignite a special type of temporary ‘Bonfire’ within any area of the Alert Starship Number’s third ring, summoning five employees…]
“Note”: Under normal circumstances, this task will not result in the actual death of employees before 21:34:59.
[“Event Three”: Ignite a special type of temporary ‘Bonfire’ within any area of the Alert Starship Number’s second ring, summoning five employees…]
“Note 1”: Under normal circumstances, this task will not result in the actual death of employees before 21:34:59.
“Note 2”: Event Two must be completed as a prerequisite.
[“Event Four”:….]
“…”
“A countdown of twenty-one hours, I haven’t seen a task with a countdown in a long time. I also don’t know what will happen when the countdown is over, but boy, this is asking me to build a Signal Tower from scratch, isn’t it?”
The moment Colin saw the task, he immediately realized its true nature.
It was to look for more signal transmitting devices…
No, to be precise, it felt more like it should be called a Signal Tower.
However, given he was prepared, he didn’t have to worry about the employees coming here, dying from exposure to the space environment.
Just that…
“Assuming the task can be declined, the employees who can come to a place like this are probably not easy to find, are they?”
Colin raised his hand and scratched his head.
Those who would come here, especially the ones to these outer rings, unless they were D Level personnel or E Level employees with special constitutional talents, other low-level company staff would hardly be able to endure the space environment even with his help…
Yet such old slickers would basically not be willing to carry out such tasks.
“This should also be part of the ‘Descent Project’, but not the permanent type. Whatever, since the mission is issued, let’s give it a try first.”
Colin didn’t think too much and quickly flew towards the third ring.
In no time, he landed on the third ring, and as his feet touched it, the long-lost “gravity” returned.
Even sound could be heard once again…
But should he leave the ground, everything would revert to just like space.
“It’s quite magical…”
Colin forcefully stamped his feet twice on the third ring, which shimmered with a dark metallic luster, then looked around to ensure there were still no dangers before finding a spot and opening “Event Two.”
[Destination reached, would you like to deploy ‘Bonfire’ materials?]
“Yes.”
As he spoke, Colin saw a transparent vortex emerge, and from it, a metal sphere was cast out.
It landed with a snap and opened by itself.
Immediately after, a pitch-black lump resembling a huge eyeball, akin to a piece of coal, was tossed out.
Colin glanced at it and roughly determined it must have been some sort of Demon brand coal in its previous life, but without much thought, he extended his hand, with flames covering it.
Soon, a hundred-meter high Flame burned and rose, enveloping the surrounding area.
“This flame is indeed a bit special, it feels like as long as one is within it, they can be assured of survival…”
Colin sensed for a bit and roughly assessed the situation.
The rest…
He had summoned the employees here.
This was also done automatically; however, Colin was rather pessimistic about whether it could find employees willing to come here, especially those crafty D Level staff…
To his surprise, merely a few seconds later, the light of the fire squirmed, and five figures were outlined from the flames.
“Damn, suddenly I feel uncomfortable…”
“What’s going on…”
“What kind of godforsaken place is this?!”
“…”
They had just appeared when they began to feel significantly unwell; however, protected by the flames, they weren’t going to die on the spot. Following that, they instinctively activated the Talent effect of “Body of Tyranny.”
In an instant, they took on the appearance of were-wolves, and their status stabilized.
“Next, divide these among yourselves; if you feel like you can’t handle it, pop one…”
Colin pulled out fifteen “Colorless Crystals” and tossed them over.
It was at this moment that they noticed Colin’s figure.
“Brother Shunzi?” One of them asked curiously while catching the crystals.
“Yep.”
Colin nodded, then curiously asked, “How did you guys wind up here?”
Usually, these guys were quite sly—this prompt arrival was a bit against the norm.
But soon after a brief exchange, Colin understood the reason.
The task description stated they were to assist employee number “654321” in carrying out a certain task, and provide a certain level of help.
The reward was a guaranteed 2,000 points…
Upon seeing this, the thought of carrying out what seemed like a harmless investigation task with Brother Shunzi, and earning what seemed like easy points, prompted them all to agree.
By the time they realized something was amiss during the transport, it was too late.
“I’m such an idiot… Sigh, oh well, this wouldn’t happen to be a ‘Descent Project,’ would it?” A D Level Personnel said with trepidation.
“It’s an external assignment, but whether it’s a Descent or not, I can’t say until after we carry it out…”
Hearing Brother Shunzi’s words rendered them tearful without tears; they felt they had been short-changed just for the greedy pursuit of a few points.
Although the task included about twenty-something hours of “immortality,” there was no mention of when they could return.
“Just stay here according to the task’s requirements and make sure the bonfire doesn’t go out. From what I’ve discovered so far, this place should be quite safe, unless something unexpected happens…”
Colin waved his hand dismissively, not waiting for the employees to respond, and rushed towards the second ring.
The distance between the two rings wasn’t too great.
From a bit further away, they could almost be described as “seamless.”
In less than half an hour, Colin, moving at full speed, landed on the second ring and did the same thing, summoning a second batch of D Level staff.
Following this, these employees looked around just like the previous ones, all with downcast faces.
However, at the bonfire point on the third ring, sensing new colleagues had arrived and seeing the exclusive communication for the task progress in their minds, the five D Level Personnel all revealed smiles on their faces.
“Gentlemen, that’s no way to look. Don’t worry; as soon as I collect the stuff, I’ll leave…”
Colin shook his head. This time, without further conversation, he rushed towards the first ring.
There were a total of four “Signal Towers” required for the bonfires according to the task, one on each ring, with the fourth needing to be established on the surface of this so-called Alert Starship Number…
This time, as he approached the Starship itself, some strange black fog drifted over. Within the fog, it seemed as if invisible life was wriggling…
It gave off a very strong sense of uneasiness.
But without waiting to get too close, the light from the flame by Colin’s side dissolved it.
“I’ve now entered the black fog area, but the feeling of not being able to leave hasn’t occurred.”
Colin’s brow furrowed, but he didn’t overthink it and continued with the summoning.
“Just stay here and don’t stray from the bonfire; once I collect the target, we can leave.”
After saying this offhandedly and tossing down the “Colorless Crystals,” without waiting for a response, Colin looked towards the surface wrapped in thick black fog and charged in…
His instinct told him, the longer he stayed in this ghastly place, the more likely something would go wrong.
He had to finish the task as quickly as possible.
As for the five employees who had just arrived, they quickly understood the situation through the internal team communication channel in their minds.

chapters.title: Chapter 476 - 476 406 The Mothership Enshrouded by Death_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 476: Chapter 406 The Mothership Enshrouded by Death_1 Chapter 476: Chapter 406 The Mothership Enshrouded by Death_1 “Boom!”
Flames erupted violently…
After setting up the three “Signal Towers,” Colin, without a word, dove straight towards the planet’s surface.
And as he delved deeper, the black fog became even denser.
Above the atmosphere of this world, there began to appear a large number of mangled corpses.
Some were human, but many more were of never-before-seen non-human remnants…
“The battle here must have been quite fierce in the past.”
His gaze swept over a colossal, fragmented corpse resembling a mountain, and Colin couldn’t help but feel a shock in his heart.
He felt that this must be a part of some terrifying First Level Containment Subject…
Fortunately, it seemed to have died quite cleanly, with no divine activity remaining beyond organic and inorganic material.
“It probably won’t suddenly come back to life and throw a punch at me.”
Pushing down the shock in his heart, Colin withdrew his gaze and continued to plunge into the world below.
But it was at this time…
He suddenly stiffened, realizing that the death state of that body seemed familiar.
“Wait, this way of dying, isn’t this the same as those creatures near the small church on ‘World Code-13’? ”
Colin carefully observed the surrounding corpses, and he could basically confirm that their death was similar to that near the small church on “World Code-13”.
“Another mission related to some ‘World Code’? But this power effect, the complete erasure of vitality, spirit, and divinity, utter extinction of all things… The existence that triggered this effect back then, could it be in this place?”
Thinking this, Colin grew wary.
Until now, he had not figured out why such bizarre deaths had occurred near the small chapel.
Bacteria, animals, plants, and so forth…
All living things had completely succumbed to death.
“I hope whatever caused this effect isn’t here.”
Quietly praying, Colin withdrew his gaze and continued on his mission.
Given his current speed, in a few minutes, he would likely reach the surface of this peculiar celestial body that was called a starship, but was not small in scale.
Meanwhile, as Colin made his silent journey, one by one, the D Level staff in his mind gradually calmed their minds, standing curiously around the Bonfire and looking around.
“What kind of godforsaken place is this, feels a bit like outer space?” A first ring employee inquired curiously.
“Drop the feels; it is outer space. From this angle, I think I can even see the stars…”
“Tsk, Brother Shunzi is no longer content with conquering backward Other Worlds; now he’s begun conquering the stars, embarking on a galactic war.”
“Our goal is the starry sea!”
“What are we doing here, reclaiming this weird world?”
“What Brother Shunzi does, I’m not sure, but as for us, ever used WIFI? Our role is similar to that…”
“…”
“The old hands among the D Level Personnel sure know a lot.”
Colin controlled his descent while looking at the information in his mind.
After these guys arrived, he clearly felt that the oppressively dead atmosphere was considerably diluted.
After a while, Colin suddenly saw the black fog thinning, and soon after, the contour of a vast expanse of land appeared before his eyes.
“Aside from the black fog being a bit strange, it’s almost a completely dead zone.”
Colin continued to use Flame Perception to sense his surroundings, but did not feel any particular threat.
Having left the layer of black fog, he looked back and saw the sky almost completely obscured by the writhing black fog…
Below the fog was a dark world devoid of any light.
However, without giving it much thought, Colin landed on an expanse of pale, broken stone ground.
“Crack, crack…”
His body landed, and a large number of crisp snapping sounds emanated from underfoot.
“Are these things, bones?”
Colin looked down in surprise at the white “stones” the size of his fingernails, realizing that they were actually bones.
And, by seeping the Flame into the bones, he could confirm that this layer of bones was dozens of meters high, and that the area he could sense so far was covered by them…
“So many bones… What are they all from?” Colin sniffed the air, trying to distinguish them.
Unfortunately, the state of weathering was too complete, and he couldn’t make out any scent; he needed to deploy more advanced equipment for that.
Immediately, Colin turned his gaze towards the Little Maid.
“Mr. Colin, most of these… seem to be from humans, a small part is of unknown composition, belonging to unknown species outside my data bank,” the Little Maid quickly concluded.
“Humans, huh? How many people does that make…”
Upon hearing this, Colin subconsciously looked down at the bones dozens of meters deep under his feet, feeling a chill in his heart.
Among the glow of the Flame, wisps of black smoke were rising from underneath the bones.
He simply couldn’t imagine what had happened here to result in such a scale of death…
Nevertheless, without dwelling on that subject, Colin continued the mission, summoning the fourth “Bonfire,” and calling forth the fourth batch of D Level Personnel.
This time, nine people arrived.
“Damn it, I’ve been had, got assigned to a scam type of mission; just looking at this place you can tell it’s dangerous!”
“Shit, all these below are human bones…”
“Huh, who are you? Wait, Brother Shunzi?”
“Steady…”
“…”
After a moment of chaos, all D Level Personnel got into a defensive posture, vigilantly looking around.
Then, they saw a familiar figure emitting flames standing not far away.
“I need four people to come with me and delve deeper into this place. You won’t need to do much, but the level of danger is likely to be slightly higher than staying here…”

chapters.title: Chapter 477 - 477 406 The Mothership Enshrouded by Death_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 477: Chapter 406 The Mothership Enshrouded by Death_2 Chapter 477: Chapter 406 The Mothership Enshrouded by Death_2 “Choose someone among yourselves; we’re leaving in ten minutes.”
Colin didn’t waste any words. After this group came out, his next mission also emerged.
Take four people to continue further into the investigation.
Of course, the best scenario would be to capture a certain number of abnormal entities, hand them over to the company, and then start the next subsidiary event…
‘It seems that the company must have gotten information about the Golden Card being here but hasn’t locked down the exact location.’
Colin pursed his lips and had some guesses about the current progress of the mission.
But before he could think further, a shout came from the Bonfire.
“Brother Shunzi, we’ve made our selection.”
“That fast? You’ve chosen already?”
Colin was surprised; he thought these people would have all sorts of excuses because of the danger associated with the mission and would eventually have to resort to flipping a coin or playing rock-paper-scissors to select team members.
But to his surprise, it had taken less than three minutes to make their choice.
However, seeing the names of the four who stepped forward, Colin wasn’t surprised after all.
“Life Mentor Adorable,” “Son of Cruelty,” “Fool’s Mushroom,” “No.7 Little Chicken”…’
Previously unnoticed, Colin hadn’t expected this familiar group to show up.
“We said before on the train that if you, Brother Shunzi, needed anything, as long as the mission wasn’t too crappy, we’d definitely come!”
“We saw the mission and came over right away…”
“Son of Cruelty” slapped his own chest, while the other two nodded in agreement.
“Yeah, yeah! We didn’t expect you guys to be here too. It’s like our group of five is all here, except for Sun Huang. I don’t know if he didn’t get the mission, or if he refused, or what.”
No.7 Little Chicken looked around and couldn’t help saying.
But before he could finish, “Fool’s Mushroom” patted his shoulder:
“Think positively, he might just be dead.”
Touched, next time I really can’t find a D Level staff member, I’ll just pick one of you three… Colin felt a warm current passing through his heart.
He hadn’t roped in these acquaintances before because their value wasn’t very high.
He needed employees with some real skills…
But this time, just for their attitude, they deserved a “Other World Seven-Day Adventure” gift package.
“Life Mentor Adorable” on the other side glanced at their little circle and didn’t say anything. His reason for being here this time was simple: he came for Brother Shunzi’s name.
Plus, he wasn’t worried about “The Descent Project” now.
As far as he knew, once a location was confirmed for “The Descent Project,” it generally wouldn’t be replaced by other similar missions, so as long as he could get back, he didn’t need to worry about being forced to return.
“Alright, now that we have our team, let’s get ready to move.”
“As for the rest of you, if you find something wrong, immediately communicate with me through the mental channel. Report any abnormalities.”
Colin warned the others not to be complacent and then moved out with the four employees.
“By the way, what is this place? Why are there so many bones?” No.7 Little Chicken, seeing the scenery here, couldn’t help but ask.
“I’m not sure either. I only know it’s a starship. These bones are probably the bones of enemies or something…”
Colin casually explained the information he had gathered thus far.
This celestial object called a “Starship” was probably much larger than the Moon.
Hearing his words, everyone clicked their tongues, unable to imagine how this place was constructed.
“The company used to be so glorious that they even… made a starship.” To express his astonishment, “Life Mentor Adorable” swore, which he rarely did.
Many of the company’s strange items could be explained away by anomalies, but these things couldn’t be created without some serious firepower.
He thought the “Ghost Train” event was already a big deal, but if the battleground was set in space, their previous “big scene” felt a bit like a village brawl from ancient times…
“Who the hell runs this company, the more you know, the more outrageous it seems…” Another D Level staff member couldn’t help but join in with the sentiment, sending a message through the squad’s mental channel.
Unfortunately, no one here could provide an answer to that question.
During the exchange between the few individuals, Colin didn’t interject. He followed the mission guidance while observing the employees, noticing that their movements were much more “standardized” than when he had met them before.
It seemed as if they were always in a state ready for an immediate counterattack.
And this state, while not previously absent, wasn’t as “efficient” as it was now.
‘It looks like the guidance from the C Level Elder Brother is pretty effective; in such a short time, they’ve improved by a significant margin… I just wonder how many times one or two of them had to die to get this proficient.’
Colin muttered to himself, then refocused his thoughts.
Shortly after leaving the campsite, about fifteen minutes later, they found a raised hill of bones in the direction provided by the mission’s investigative guide.
Through Flame Perception, Colin could ascertain that there was an unknown facility beneath the hill.
After some thought, Colin pointed his finger towards the heap of bones, and a burst of flame surged down from his fingertip, incinerating all the bones obstructing the view to reveal a cylindrical metal structure emerging from the ground.
Its diameter was about ten meters or so, resembling a gigantic chimney with an extremely smooth surface.
At the same time, an inspiration emerged from the mission.
Colin cocked his head, continued to stride forward, and reached out to touch the metallic wall of this chimney-like structure.
A cold, icy sensation of hard metal came through…
However, after about a dozen seconds, it seemed as if nothing happened?
Just as Colin conceived this thought, he saw a light beginning to shine where his palm touched.
Ripples of light spread out like waves…
[Verification… passed…]
A choppy mechanical female voice echoed beside his ear.
Following that, the part of the black metal that had felt extremely hard to the touch and had been barely affected by the bonfire began to move, then it indented, revealing a passage leading downward.
“I had thought that this place had completely fallen, but it seems that it still retains some operational capabilities…”
Colin didn’t enter immediately, but with a thought, he let the flames flow into it.
Soon, he had a rough idea of the situation inside: spiral stairs leading downward, a dense and complex network of metallic corridors, and the presence of numerous indistinct non-human life forms…
“The situation inside seems rather complicated, but overall, it’s still manageable,” Colin noted, then withdrew the flame and stepped inside.
Seeing this, the few D Level staff behind him didn’t waste any words and followed just as decisively…
Having teamed up through various events, they had not a shred of doubt about Brother Shunzi’s judgment.
And just as Colin had anticipated, after they completed the descent of the spiral staircase, they arrived at a junction.
The junction had six passages, arranged in the shape of the character for “rice,” each extending straight in different directions. Each passage was relatively spacious, about seven to eight meters wide, with a layer of bone ash on the ground.
The thick metallic walls were lined with rows of guide lights radiating green light, stretching out into the far distance.
Unfortunately, one couldn’t see very far as everything was obscured by black fog.
“Brother Shunzi, which way do we go? Or are we splitting up to explore?” The Son of Sadomasochism looked around curiously, asked, then rubbed his throat, hawking up some phlegm.
The bone dust was so pervasive that it made his throat uncomfortable.
But luckily, the bone ash itself wasn’t dangerous, and as long as they were careful to avoid inhaling more, it would be fine…
“Don’t split up,” Colin said as he looked left and right before choosing a direction at random.
After descending, the mission guide disappeared, probably allowing him to take the initiative.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 478 - 478 407 The Terrifying Golden Out-of-Control
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 478: Chapter 407: The Terrifying Golden Out-of-Control Artifact!_1 Chapter 478: Chapter 407: The Terrifying Golden Out-of-Control Artifact!_1 ‘It’s strange, the air is filled with an unusual aura, as if monsters are everywhere, but other than the black fog, no living creatures can be seen, not even anomalies. Could it be that everything has already died?’
‘Without a clear investigation target, this is pretty annoying…’
Colin’s brow slightly furrowed as he observed his surroundings while moving forward. Fortunately, since his investigative mission only required him to delve deep enough, there was no need to rush.
Afterward, approximately every thousand meters, another “T” shaped intersection would appear in the corridor.
Besides that, no other entities were encountered.
This place was like an extremely special, large labyrinth.
“Clang clang.”
Colin stamped forcefully on the ground twice, flames attached to his body, trying to directly melt a downward path.
Regrettably, the metal material here was unknown, and even when he intensified his efforts, it only glowed red hot.
To think he could burn through it was somewhat of a fool’s dream.
However, it was at this time a series of rapid footsteps suddenly came from behind.
It seemed something had finally appeared.
“Alert!”
Colin flicked his hand, and the ring on his ring finger immediately transformed, becoming a delicate revolver that he grasped, then watched vigilantly in that direction, not daring to be the slightest bit careless…
Just now, they had traversed that same road without seeing anything.
Yet suddenly there were footsteps…
It seemed as if something had appeared in an incomprehensible way!
No sooner had everyone assumed a defensive posture than a group of bizarre-looking, leather-clad humanoid creatures rushed out from a thousand meters away at the bend in the road.
Despite seeing them for the first time, Colin recognized their essence from the unique energy emanating from them.
“Demons or some such creatures? There sure are a lot of them…”
Colin muttered to himself.
However, the black fog here seemed to have little to do with them…
In other words, these demons were likely responding to a “distress signal,” intending to come here for revenge, but ended up as one of the victims caught in an ambush.
At this moment, their original target did not seem to be Colin and the others but rather something else in a different location.
Yet upon noticing them, their eyes lit up…
“Such a weak aura, are they solitary administrative personnel?!”
“Perfect, kill them!”
“Top up our blood food, then leave this damned place and die to return!”
“Hurry up, or those things below will catch up!”
The various oddly shaped demons quickly made a decision after a brief exchange and set upon Colin and his companions.
One particularly ferocious Heretic Demon, wielding a longsword that radiated a green light, moved very fast, speeding toward them like a cheetah. The distance of over a thousand meters could be covered in just a few seconds…
It was at this moment that the demon realized those guys seemed to have just reacted, hastily making defensive preparations.
This speed, compared to the legion members they had previously encountered, was not in the same league—
And indeed, it was the level of non-combat personnel!
More amusing was that the man in the middle actually aimed at him with what looked like an antique revolver from some bygone era.
The bullets from such a weapon could hardly outpace its speed!
If it were a standard gauss weapon, it might choose to back off, but for just a small handgun…
“Too weak! Let me show you what speed as power means!”
The Lightsaber-wielding demon roared, doubling its speed once again and completely surpassing the speed of sound!
However, just as it was about to reach them, a voice from other demons echoed in its mind.
“Damn it, be careful, there’s something off about this guy, watch out for that handgun!”
“Not… right?”
The thought had just arisen in the Lightsaber-bearing demon’s mind when it abruptly felt a strong sense of crisis. Following this, as it moved at high speed, it suddenly noticed that the other party had already pulled the trigger, and from the muzzle flashing with firelight, a seemingly normal bullet was fired out.
Upon its exit, the bullet rapidly enlarged, cloaked in a layer of frightening flames, and sped toward it even faster…
Bang!
A mass of red gore exploded ahead.
A large number of intestines scattered like dropped spaghetti on the ground…
“That scared me, it’s just this?”
Colin pursed his lips, having just seen the other party charge at them with such momentum, he thought it was some powerful enemy. Instead, it turned out to be the kind that dies after one shot.
Meanwhile, more than a dozen demons were shocked.
“Damn it! That guy was still too young, he didn’t know this is a ‘skin’ weapon, it’s unbeatable!”
“Split up!”
Compared to that young demon, some of the older demons, upon seeing the revolver in Colin’s hand and the flames on his body, almost didn’t need to think due to a fear deep in their bones. They didn’t mourn for a moment and turned tail to run.
“Since you’re here, don’t think of leaving.”
Colin’s flames surged as he finally found someone who could give him information about this place. How could he let them go so easily?
Lucky for him, there was only one of that type capable of breaking the sound barrier.
Soon, Colin effortlessly captured all the demons he could catch and locked them together. As for those he didn’t catch, they were turned into a spread of tomato sauce on the ground.
Just as he was preparing to start interrogating them for information about the place, a mission prompt appeared.
“Next step in the mission already? I haven’t even started questioning yet…”
Colin murmured, unfazed, as he summoned the specific details of the mission in his mind while contemplating how to extract information from the group of demon creatures…

chapters.title: Chapter 479 - 479 407 The Terrifying Golden Uncontrollable
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 479: Chapter 407: The Terrifying Golden Uncontrollable Artifact!_2 Chapter 479: Chapter 407: The Terrifying Golden Uncontrollable Artifact!_2 He was curious about how this group of guys had initially appeared and what they were avoiding.
However, just at this moment…
…
“Brother Shunzi, which way should we go? Or should we split up to explore?” “Son of Cruelty” looked around, curiously asked a question, then rubbed his nose…
“No splitting up.”
Colin looked to either side and casually chose a direction.
After descending, the task guidance disappeared, probably allowing him to improvise.
‘However, there are strange auras all over the place, as if it’s crowded with people, yet there is no sign of any living thing besides the black fog, could it be that everything is dead?’
‘Strange, I keep feeling that something is off, very off…’
Colin and his companions observed as they moved forward and quickly realized that this place was like a huge maze.
Every thousand meters, there would be a crossroad shaped like the character “米.”
The whole thing was like an exceptionally special large maze.
Then, Colin glanced at the ground and shifted his gaze towards the distance.
This metal was too unique; even with the enhancement from the Power of the Bonfire, he couldn’t leave a mark on it. Forcing a path open would definitely come at a significant cost.
But no sooner had his gaze shifted, Colin suddenly froze—
He hadn’t tried it, so how would he know that even with the Power of the Bonfire he couldn’t breach it?
But before he had the chance to think further…
A series of hurried footsteps suddenly approached.
“Stay alert!”
Colin flicked his palm, and a ring on his ring finger transformed into a revolver.
At the same time, a group of extremely unfamiliar yet oddly familiar demons charged out…
“Such weak auras, are they lone clerical staff?”
“Perfect, kill them!”
“Replenish our blood-food, then leave this cursed place and suicide to return!”
“Hurry, otherwise those things below will catch up!”
“…”
What’s catching up?
In his confusion, Colin saw a demon racing towards him at high speed, and without thinking, he fired a shot directly.
A 155mm shell blasted out from the muzzle…
Without any suspense, the demon instantly exploded into a rain of flesh under the heavily augmented shell.
‘Odd, I keep feeling… that something is very strange…’
While Colin was puzzled inside, the other employees didn’t seem to notice anything amiss.
Furthermore, when their companion died, the group of demons behind fled without hesitation, giving him no time to think further as he immediately gave chase.
Soon, all the demons were captured.
But Colin didn’t rush to interrogate them, feeling as though something might happen at this moment?
Suddenly, an inspiration flashed within him, he opened the task panel, and immediately a new task appeared.
[Special Event: Kill any demon, recover it, and immediately use the effect of “The Sealed Right Hand” to strengthen yourself…]
“Hint”: Act quickly.
“Just need to kill one? You should have said that earlier, wasting my time… wait, when did a new task appear…”
Colin was puzzled, but he didn’t hesitate and immediately prepared to do as requested.
He reached his hand into the “Storage Room.”
…
“Brother Shunzi, we…” “Son of Cruelty” began to speak.
But before he could finish, Colin interrupted, “Don’t scatter, this way…”
“Uh.” “Son of Cruelty” was stunned, he hadn’t finished speaking yet, how did Brother Shunzi know what he wanted to ask?
At the same time, Colin was also momentarily startled, looking around, feeling very familiar with the surroundings.
But he didn’t dwell on it and quickly headed in the chosen direction…
The others felt something off about Brother Shunzi but still followed closely behind him, moving rapidly.
In a short while, footsteps could be heard from behind…
“Stay alert!”
As Colin drew his gun, the thought subconsciously appeared in his mind: ‘Here they come again, wait, why would I say again?’
And at that moment, a group of demons that seemed familiar appeared.
The same dialogue followed…
Yet another demon burst forth.
A loud “bang” sounded.
The demon instantly exploded, with the others scattering in frenzy.
Colin was about to give chase but suddenly remembered something and opened the task panel.
“This task…”
At that moment, Colin vaguely understood some things. Instead of chasing after the group of demons, he approached the pile of “Italian bolognese” that seemed familiar. He confirmed the task was to upload these items.
At the same time, he pulled out an orange card named “The Sealed Right Hand” from his pocket.
“Isn’t this thing supposed to be used only during ‘Item Liberation’?”
Harboring doubts, Colin infused a large amount of spiritual energy into the card and immediately felt a more refined familiarity with “Time Freeze.”
If he continued to stimulate it, he might be able to use “Time Freeze” with slightly greater strength.
But to maintain its effect through a huge exertion of strength for just a bit more proficiency was clearly not worth it.
Even Colin couldn’t use it for an extended period…
‘However, what is the reason the task requires me to do this?’
Colin had a feeling of semi-understanding.
But before he could figure anything out, an anomaly suddenly occurred.
“What’s happening with that group of demons?” “Life Mentor Adorable” looked ahead in surprise.
They saw the demons, which had originally scattered in retreat, comically reverse back through the corridors from all directions, the whole process resembling a film being played in reverse…
They seemed to regroup at the crossroads and then step by step retreat back to their original spots.
However, the “Speed Equals Strength” that had been reclaimed was gone forever.
Even time reversal could not make the company regurgitate what it had consumed.
Meanwhile, as he watched this unfold, some memories surfaced in Colin’s mind…
“Damn it! No wonder everything feels so familiar…”
Colin sensed the memories in his brain, then quickly made a strange face, as these memories also included the process of reversal.
And then…
He saw the “Son of Cruelty” spit that phlegm twice in succession…
“Hiss…”
Colin shook his head, throwing the disgusting image out of his mind. Seeing the “Son of Cruelty,” who was completely oblivious to everything, he hesitated for half a second but decided not to tell him about this for now…
Afterward, looking at the demons being reversed by an unknown power…
Colin realized which Golden Card was involved in this incident.
“Time Reversal.”
Besides this card, Colin couldn’t think of any other effect that could trigger such a similar result at the moment.
Looking at the orange card in his hand, he couldn’t help shaking his head…
‘No wonder the company sent me here, probably no one else would be quite right for the job besides me, at least not with a high cost-effectiveness.’
‘But usually, a Golden Card’s effect only extends a few tens of meters, and I didn’t notice it nearby, tsk…’
‘This card isn’t in some kind of imminent uncontrollable state, is it? A Golden Artifact on the brink of being out of control, and they send me to do the retrieval work, is that really appropriate…’
With these thoughts flickering through his mind, Colin couldn’t help but exhale deeply.
And it was at this moment that he felt the power that caused time to reverse in this place disappear.
He immediately deactivated “The Sealed Right Hand” effect, then showed a trace of weariness in his eyes…
This thing really drains one’s energy severely.
At the same time, a new sub-mission event appeared.
[Event Six: For unknown reasons, the location of “Time Reversal” still cannot be locked. Please proceed to the negative second floor of the mothership or below, and try to recover as many remnants of the Heretic Races creatures as possible to gather further intelligence.]
…
“Can’t sense it, eh? That’s very much like me. When I was stimulating the right hand, I felt like this card was here, omnipresent yet seemingly nowhere…”
Colin recalled his previous feelings and then shook his head, gathering his thoughts.
At this moment, “Life Mentor Adorable” saw him come out of his contemplative state and inquired about the situation.
“It’s somewhat related to what we’re here to recover, but let’s talk while we’re on the move…”
Saying this, Colin followed the mission guide, looking in a certain direction and started explaining the situation as they moved forward.
“Hiss, another Golden Card…” Several D Level Personnel couldn’t help but exchange glances.
Brother Shunzi said it’s about retrieving for the company, but they all felt that this card would probably end up in Brother Shunzi’s hands…
If that happened, he would likely be the only person in the company to hold two Golden Artifacts!
Ignoring what these people were thinking, Colin earnestly led the team forward. Along the way, he encountered the “Time Reversal” phenomenon several times and faced a few waves of enemies that appeared out of nowhere…
There were demons, as well as other cultists and oddities.
But being prepared this time, he killed and reclaimed them almost instantly upon encountering them.
“It seems like they’ve been trapped in different temporal loops, possibly being triggered when I get close and thus reappearing out of thin air. Is this what the signal warning meant by saying you can’t leave once you enter?”
“But is this really the true power of a Golden Card? It’s terrifying…”
Colin pondered thoughtfully.
After about fifteen minutes, they came upon a spiral staircase leading downward.
.
.
.
PS: Humbly asking for your monthly ticket…
