chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 480: Chapter 408: The Repeat of Yesterday (6K for subscription and monthly ticket)_1 Chapter 480: Chapter 408: The Repeat of Yesterday (6K for subscription and monthly ticket)_1 In the glow of the bonfire, wisps of eerie black fog slowly rose from the downward spiral of the staircase ahead…
“So, the thing those demons were afraid of is down there? But it seems I can’t feel it…”
As he pondered, Colin manipulated the flames like a stream, cascading down the stairs layer by layer, pouring into the second sub-level area.
Through his flame perception, Colin “saw” that the layout of the second sub-level seemed similar to that of the first, with “M”-shaped intersections and the same cold metal constructs…
The difference, though, was the presence of some bodies below, as well as a denser black fog.
Overall, however, the problem didn’t seem too serious.
Having reassured himself of this, Colin led his four companions downstairs.
As soon as they descended, it seemed they triggered something; not far away, some abnormal creatures suddenly appeared out of nowhere.
They had a very peculiar form, manifesting in a gaseous state, with faint glimmers within the mist, resembling bizarre little nebulas.
At that moment, they rushed toward the staircase corner, seemingly trying to escape this place.
But sensing Colin and the others, they paused momentarily, then thunder and lightning roared out from within the clouds.
Streaks of lightning flashed and struck…
“Another life trapped in the ‘counterflow’ of time…”
As the thought crossed Colin’s mind, the flames he had prepared earlier burst forth, dispersing the lightning.
He didn’t wait for those things to decide whether to flee or stay, but crouched slightly and then pounced toward them like a cheetah.
In the process, he lifted his revolver and pulled the trigger over and over.
Bang, bang, bang—!
The sound of gunfire was almost continuous.
Bullets that carried flames but were otherwise ordinary solid projectiles passed through their mist-like bodies without appearing to inflict harm; however, the flames on the bullets ignited them directly.
One by one, they exploded into flame as if they were catkins that had encountered fire.
“Clang, clang, clang~”
A mass of colorful crystals, containing strange energies, fell from midair.
“Tsk, bursting gold coins.”
Colin’s gaze wandered among those dozens of crystal stones, and then he noticed among them some small metallic objects the size of a thumb, densely engraved with something.
He reached out his hand, flames swirling, and took those thumb-sized things into his hand, then a quick scan informed him of the situation with the abnormal creatures they had just encountered.
“Containment Subject label, number 6-978341, containment level, level 6 and below, low threat, low intelligence, specialized silicon-based life, experiment report, each ‘6-978341’ can produce about seventy-four kwh of electricity per hour, can survive for three years with continuous power supply, after death their crystals can absorb stellar thermal energy, most can regenerate within three months to a year in appropriate conditions, with a medium third level difficulty of hatching…”
“The energy department of the starship rates it as having low development value, not as good as demons…”
“Tsk, seventy-four degrees of electricity an hour and that’s considered low?”
Colin’s eyes lit up, the company might not value this, but he found it quite impressive, seventy-four kwh an hour meant that a single one could power a large building…
Crucially, it seemed to have no pollution, a high-efficiency clean energy source.
The method to stimulate its power generation and its limitations were all detailed on the metal plates of the containment tags.
He could easily make use of it after a bit of work…
As for hatching methods, besides naturally splitting through unknown means, they could also be artificially forced into a crystalline state and then divided into a certain amount; after some exposure to the sun, they could turn into two…
The process reminded him somewhat of a potato, though the results were somewhat unstable.
“Let’s call it ‘Plasma Potato,’ this thing the company doesn’t care for because it doesn’t have a high limit, but it’s just perfect for us.” Colin nodded, the company at its peak might have disdained it, but he didn’t. Without any rush to hand it over, he collected some of the crystals.
This wasn’t a creature that died from being drained of energy; its revival time was much faster, likely just a few days before it could come back to life and continue to contribute to human energy.
In Colin’s view, this was definitely a strategic energy source…
As someone who enjoyed sharing and never hogged good things to himself, Colin picked up over a dozen before remembering to share with his teammates, selecting two “Plasma Potatoes” and handed them to the four people around him.
“Each of you take half of these two.” Colin instructed.
“What’s this thing?” Fuer Mushroom didn’t refuse, but was curious.
The other three felt the same, all turning their eyes to Colin, waiting for an explanation.
“Have a look for yourselves.” Colin handed them the containment number tags.
Then…
“Sheesh, damn, I think I just saw the future of new energy sources beyond nuclear power…”
“Life Mentor Adorable” looked at the crystal stone in their hand, their face showing astonishment.
Although the label mentioned something about having lower value than demons, the extraction of demon energy was far more difficult, not as easy and suitable as this one.
Of course, the only limitation was that there was a cap on how many times they could divide; it seemed like beyond a certain number, their efficiency would decrease, the difficulty of division would increase, and the results would become unstable and so on…
Even so, it was still seen as highly valuable in everyone’s eyes.
“It’s no wonder that it comes from a starship capable of interstellar travel; even the little things that slip through seem like they could solve the biggest problems plaguing our world…” Little Chicken mused while pocketing the items, planning to research how to use them back home.
If they could find the technology to make them hatch naturally, they’d truly be entering a new era.
Fuer Mushroom, hearing the comment, couldn’t help but make a joke, “You know, if this thing spreads, there probably won’t be ‘oil in the backyard, life couldn’t be sweeter,’ right?”

chapters.title: Chapter 481 - 481 408 The Repeat of Yesterday (6K for
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 481: Chapter 408: The Repeat of Yesterday (6K for subscription and monthly ticket)_2 Chapter 481: Chapter 408: The Repeat of Yesterday (6K for subscription and monthly ticket)_2 “It’s hard to say for sure; we’ll have to be more careful when planting potatoes in the future…” “Son of Cruelty” pursed his lips.
“Alright, let’s continue with the investigation below and see if we can find anything else of value.”
Colin waved his hand, handed over a “Plasma Potato” to the company, and then continued to lead them with the “The Sealed Right Hand” card in his hand.
Not many anomalies trapped in “Time Reversal” were found on sub-level two…
However, they were significantly stronger than those on sub-level one, otherwise, they wouldn’t have made it this far; unfortunately, although they encountered other escaped containment subjects twice during the period, they weren’t of much value.
Or rather, they weren’t of much value to them at the moment.
Besides, Colin and the others also came across a few bodies, some of different races and some belonging to starship crew members.
“Strange, as far as we can tell, if not recovered by the company, once someone dies or moves beyond a certain range, they would be forced into time reversal and usually not leave a corpse behind. So how did these bodies remain?”
In one corridor, Colin and his team looked at the corpse of a man in a faded brown coat, puzzled.
The corpse was like a mummified body in the desert, long dead…
And the cause of death seemed to be the loss of half his head and several clean-through holes in his chest.
Even in death, his hands were still tightly gripping several chains, at the other ends of which were the bodies of several grotesque creatures…
They probably died together, taking each other down.
“Can’t make out the creatures, probably unknown species, and everything about it has been erased. He died thoroughly, to the extent that even his power level while alive can’t be discerned. But my gut feeling is that they wouldn’t have been C Level…”
Colin withdrew his gaze and didn’t dwell on the unsolved mysteries.
He tried to recover the body through the mission…
However, there was no response from the mission; it seemed the company currently had no plans to retrieve this employee and bury him.
“Sorry, mate, I can’t take you with me for now, looks like you’ll have to lie here a while longer.”
After muttering to himself, Colin stepped past the area and headed towards the stairs further down the road.
Only after making sure with Flame Perception that there wouldn’t be any unpleasant surprises did he lead his four mobile eyes to the third sub-level…
Compared to above, the fog here was thicker and the atmosphere more oppressive.
Even the metal walls that had always been free of scratches now had some permanent marks on them.
“The strength of the monsters here must be quite high, after all, according to my estimation, at least a Third Level Containment Subject would be needed to make marks on these special metal walls…”
“And those monsters caught in ‘Time Reversal’ are honestly quite troublesome. They’re only triggered when you get close; normally, you can’t detect them through Bonfire, and you have to activate ‘The Sealed Right Hand’ to notice them…”
“But to constantly activate this thing is too draining on my energy; it’s not possible to maintain it all the time… Let’s just take it one step at a time, then.”
Shaking his head and gathering his thoughts, Colin continued to move forward as the mission required, searching for the staircase that led to the next level according to the mission’s directions.
However, as they approached the staircase leading down from the third sub-level, Colin and his team noticed that there were more bodies not caught in “Time Reversal.”
Sometimes in one corridor, there were only bodies in various states of death, indicating a high intensity of combat.
Even stranger, in some places, Colin could hear sounds without going there, whether it was a roar or heavy footsteps; the overall atmosphere was incredibly chaotic…
Yet, out of curiosity, they walked over to see if they could investigate anything. Still, they found nothing, triggered nothing, and saw nothing.
But after leaving, they could faintly hear whispers and see the silhouettes of unknown figures…
This place was no longer “quiet” like the first and second sub-levels.
“It’s almost like it’s haunted…”
Even with Brother Shunzi’s flames enhancing them, “Life Mentor Adorable” couldn’t help but touch his own arm, feeling a chill down his spine.
He wasn’t afraid of the monsters that could be seen, but these invisible oddities made him somewhat uneasy.
“Prepare your defenses.”
Colin cautioned, then controlled a fireball to float behind his head and continued leading the team forward.
The mission directive was to keep investigating downward, but it didn’t specify how far down they had to go to complete it.
Even if they felt something was off, they had no choice but to proceed.
Another ten minutes later, after Colin had dealt with a creature caught in “Time Reversal,” he couldn’t help but hiss sharply as he passed a crossroads corner…
There, for a considerable distance in the corridor beyond the bend, were carcasses wrapped in brown clothing.
They filled every corner, leaving hardly any room to set foot.
“They’re all human, and most likely starship employees. What happened here…”
Colin looked ahead, his pupils turning vertical and flickering with light. He vaguely made out a staircase a kilometer away leading to the next level, and on the road to this staircase, he saw countless carcasses.
And they were all uniformly employees of the company…
Gloomy, eerie, but… strangely, not frightening.
“All are facing away from the staircase, roughly judging, they must have been dealing with something? But it seems that there are no creatures other than humans, why is that? Are they incorporeal types, or were these people taken out in one fell swoop?”

chapters.title: Chapter 482 - 482 408 The Repeat of Yesterday (6K for
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 482: Chapter 408: The Repeat of Yesterday (6K for subscription and monthly ticket)_3 Chapter 482: Chapter 408: The Repeat of Yesterday (6K for subscription and monthly ticket)_3 “Forget it, just like before, don’t think too much about it.”
Colin glanced at the stairs ahead, then took another look at the bodies on the ground. Although he held respect for these employees, to avoid any accidents,
he still manipulated the flames, incinerating the corpses on the ground to ash…
“Occasional ones before were fine, but this time there are too many. If something goes wrong, there really might be no way to handle it.”
Looking at the “refreshed” corridor, Colin gathered his thoughts, then, with three cards pinched in his left hand and a revolver in his right, he continued to move forward.
However, it was at the midway point that the sudden change violently occurred!
“Die!”
Accompanied by a roar, a female figure charged from ahead, her features blurry, short-haired, wearing a brown coat, dragging a long knife from which a large amount of flame spewed out.
When she appeared, the entire corridor vibrated, and the temperature seemed to be rising sharply.
“Life Mentor Adorable” and others felt their scalps tense, as the figure felt like the front of a train, and they quickly braced for defense…
‘A Bonfire’s scent? Is this one of ours?’
Colin was ready to draw his gun and shoot, but upon sensing a familiar strength, he stopped, his own flames rising, trying to use this to verify the other’s identity.
However, despite his actions, the other did not stop.
“Didn’t recognize me, or already lost rationality? Nevertheless, the strength is quite strong, definitely not a C Level, most likely D Level…”
As thoughts flickered, Colin kept his eyes fixed on the other, ready to subdue her when she reached the “Time Stop” or “Repulsion” areas.
But just when he thought they were about to collide…
The next second, the figure stopped halfway and violently swung her surging flame-spraying knife.
“Boom!”
The knife seemed to have hit something.
An ethereal figure wrapped in bandages was forced out of thin air and severed by a slash…
However, before its demise, it also dealt a fatal blow to the female wielding the flame knife, slicing off nearly a third of her head on the left side.
“That seems to be a ‘Bonfire Hunter’? She’s not targeting us, wait, is this a historical image reappearing because of ‘Time Reversal’?”
With his understanding of “time-related” matters, Colin immediately realized the root of everything.
Meanwhile, he saw that, after the woman’s head was cut, her figure wavered, and she used some ability to make a pale hand emerge from the ground, pick up the other half of her head, and hand it to her.
“These not-quite-human, not-quite-ghost things are such a hassle!” She pressed her head back into place.
“Damn, what vitality…” Several employees jumped at the sight.
However, “Life Mentor Adorable” glanced at the three of them and spoke:
“Don’t underestimate yourselves. After the D Level enhancement, along with your Talent or artifacts, getting your heads chopped off, you could achieve a similar effect.”
Upon hearing this, the few of them made an “Eh” sound.
But before more could be said, a large number of anomalies surged into the area.
New enemies had arrived…
“At least the strength of a Level 2 Containment Subject.” Colin sensed their aura and made a quick judgement.
At this point, some faint figures appeared beside the female member.
“…Commander, you can’t continue to fight… hurry and leave… this defensive line… won’t hold much longer… you need to retreat…”
“Leave this to us…”
“… we will give our all… to hold them back…”
Compared to this powerful woman, those figures were very blurry, their features indecipherable, their words somewhat distorted.
They were only faintly visible when beside her, otherwise existing in a weak state that could be sensed but not seen or heard.
“Retreat?! There are still a great number of suffering people below who haven’t been moved! The breeding grounds are also in the process of transfer; what about those people if we retreat? Do you have the power to hold back?”
She spoke disdainfully, with no intention of retreating, and after speaking, she used Flame Perception to scan the scene: “Ten minutes! Hold the 17th Defensive Line! At all costs!”
“You’ve already been nominated for C Level, you have a great chance… cannot… end up like us… dying here for nothing…”
“To hell with C Level, if we can’t hold a position, what’s the point of promotion? Nothing here can afford to fail! My gut tells me that if this place falls, the entire battlefront might be affected, and I definitely don’t want to become a sinner of humanity!”
As her words ended, a new round of battle erupted.
Colin watched her swing the long knife, and in this “prolonged” ten minutes, she repelled many enemies with her blade.
Even the Level 2 Containment Subjects were forced to retreat under her relentless Charge…
Although he knew she was not alone, in Colin’s eyes, she was almost fighting by herself.
Most of the other members only materialized in her presence.
“Report! The front line is in crisis… the enemies are breaking through…”
“It’s… Dreadfiends… Level 2 threat, some with the will of First Level threats… conventional means are inadequate…”
“Hahaha, the will of First Level Threat Creatures? Seems I’m indeed at a crucial point that can affect the battlefront, or else these fellows wouldn’t be coming!”
The female member wielding the power of Bonfire laughed, her battered and bleeding face showing Direct Gaze ahead, facing the impending arrival of power once known as “God” without an ounce of fear, only hatred.
“Three minutes and twenty-one seconds more, brothers of the Expedition Army, the time has come to sacrifice for the fate of humanity!”

chapters.title: Chapter 483 - 483 408 The Repeat of Yesterday (6K for
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 483: Chapter 408: The Repeat of Yesterday (6K for subscription and monthly ticket)_4 Chapter 483: Chapter 408: The Repeat of Yesterday (6K for subscription and monthly ticket)_4 “I’m staking your lives and mine! All personnel, activate the ‘Bonfire Furnace Device’! Within three minutes! I won’t allow any enemy to breach this line! The 17th Defensive Line will not become a gap!”
She flung her longsword aside, her right hand driving into her chest, forcefully tearing out a burning heart and lifting it above her head:
“Accept the power of ‘Bonfire,’ I will fight shoulder to shoulder with you all!”
In an instant, searing flames spread from the burning heart.
It was at this very moment that Colin’s pupils contracted, witnessing the once spacious corridor now filled with tens of thousands of figures.
“Bonfire’s” power had been bestowed upon them, converging at the region of their hearts…
“Charge!”
Member after member of the Expedition Army collided with the indistinct enemies, like a blazing torrent of flames.
The line that was about to be breached held firm once more…
However, it wasn’t long before an even more terrifying force descended upon them.
A vast number of members fell to the ground, dead.
“Time Reversal” came to a halt, the tunnel once filled with flames returned to darkness, leaving only countless corpses on the ground…
“What…?!”
Observing the reappearing skeletons, Colin’s breathing halted for a moment, but he soon calmed down.
“There’s no scent of contamination; they probably won’t turn into zombies or anything, but, was that the First Level Containment Subject itself descending just now?”
Colin pondered, realizing that the entity was probably not trapped here.
Otherwise, it would have appeared within the “Time Counterflow.”
Instead, it seemed like he was clashing with the air a moment ago…
Shaking his head, Colin reined in his thoughts and looked at the plethora of bodies on the ground so dense there was hardly space to step. He did not choose to incinerate them again but extended his foot and nudged an open spot through the pile of bones to continue forward.
The few behind him initially intended to step where Colin had found footing, following like chicks behind a hen but thought better of it and chose to maintain their formation, continuing to advance together.
Before long, Colin passed through the area where the female employee had fallen, glancing there subconsciously, yet her body was nowhere to be found…
Conversely, at her last position, there was an uncommon “empty spot.”
After all, she wasn’t a ‘Flame Bearer,’ and might not even have been a Reservist. Forcibly borrowing power, igniting herself, the outcome could only be complete disintegration without leaving any remains…
Nonetheless, although she had completely burned herself up, some remnants still lingered.
A shattered longsword lay quietly in an inconspicuous corner of the corridor.
After some thought, Colin took out a hundred-dollar bill and summoned a “Money Slave” to pick up the item.
Once he deemed it safe, he took it into his hands and opened its panel.
[A completely ruined longsword: It once seemed to be an item of excellent quality, but now it is utterly beyond use. Its special qualities are erased, beyond any hope of repair…]
“Ah, what a pity… However, given that, she really was probably just D Level Personnel, just one of the elite type.”
Thinking this, Colin subconsciously glanced at the few people beside him and then couldn’t help but shake his head.
All D Level members, but why such a huge disparity?
‘That said, this employee only had, what, one piece of Purple Gear? Including that somewhat special heart, at most two, and apart from the heart, even if this sword were fixed up, judging by the way it just performed, the effect likely wouldn’t be anything special…’
‘Among Purple Gear, it’s not the worst, but it’s hardly a fine piece. If tossed into the company group now, it might even be scorned…’
Suddenly, Colin understood why sometimes, when fighting with that C Level Elder Brother, he would often get criticized for their gear, feeling that excellent Purple Items were completely wasted in their hands…
If this woman had an Orange Item in her possession, or if that heart had been a genuine ‘Flame Bearer’ heart,
Perhaps the tide of this battle could have turned.
Or at the very least, had the sword been switched for a slightly better Purple Gear, maybe things here wouldn’t have been so tragic…
Noticing Colin’s glance just now, the D Level staff looked at each other, some baffled…
They felt somewhat looked down upon, although they weren’t entirely sure.
.
.
.
ps: Humbly asking for monthly tickets…

chapters.title: Chapter 484 - 484 409 Pre-war Honors a One-way Trip. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 484: Chapter 409: Pre-war Honors, a One-way Trip. _1 Chapter 484: Chapter 409: Pre-war Honors, a One-way Trip. _1 The events happening in the spacious corridor went largely unnoticed by the four employees.
All they could see were glowing figures fighting in the area, the speech indistinct, everything quite ambiguous, but from the pressure that seemed to seep through the years, they could roughly infer that the scale of the battle was quite significant.
And Brother Shunzi probably heard something that made him look at them like that…
They weren’t surprised by this, after all, dogs can often see things invisible to human eyes, oh, that’s not right, it’s Brother Shunzi who always sees things that others can’t.
It had been the same on the “Ghost Train”; nothing to be curious about…
“Did something strange just happen?” “Life Mentor Adorable” asked curiously.
However, Colin shook his head and said no more.
At this moment, looking at the scrapped prop in his hand, he remembered her last words.
A contemplative expression crossed his face…
‘The power of the Bonfire’s Succession… I didn’t pay much attention to it before, but now that I think about it, her method of using this power is a bit like the way heretical forces call upon God Descent, no, in general, it’s more alike to ‘Divine Strike’…’
Colin stood still, thoughtfully fiddling with the remnants of the prop in his hand.
She was not a “Flame Bearer,” nor did she possess the related items, yet she was able to use the power to a certain extent.
This way was very reminiscent of one of the three official paths known as “Divine Strike.”
However, she did not have that rigid, self-losing sensation; overall, she seemed very “complete.”
‘I’m not sure, but if it’s really like that, it’s quite strange… Of the three paths, two are related to the company. ‘Destiny Propeller’ goes without saying, as the whole path originated from the company’s release of the ‘Book of Fate.’ If this item were lost, the path would probably collapse on the spot…’
‘And regarding ‘Divine Strike,’ I remember chatting with Xu Duojin earlier and learning that this thing is not really related to the ‘Divine Strike’ from folklore…’
‘It’s purely because the methods are somewhat similar and coincidentally share the same name, that it was adopted by the officials.’
‘I don’t seem to have researched its specific origins much. I’ll ask about it when I return; it might in the end be related to the company. Yes, not only that, but charms might be as well.’
As thoughts flickered in his mind, Colin realized that most of the pathways to extraordinary powers seemed to have some association with the company.
Even another related to talisman charms…
Within the company, it seemed they also used such items, like the man on the train playing with talismans, throwing out a handful of talisman papers, each releasing a machine gun…
Colin’s initial impression of that was quite strong.
“Not only domestically but also internationally I shall search, if all sources of power can be found within the company, then the situation seems quite strange…”
Taking a deep breath, Colin suppressed the various thoughts in his mind.
Then, he handed the remains of the long sword to Money Slave and instructed him to pick them up and put them back where they came from.
Those that left behind corpses were always somewhat peculiar.
It was better not to get involved if it could be avoided.
Afterward, Colin resumed walking, stepping over bones, heading toward the stairwell at the far end.
It was evident that this place had ultimately been breached.
It was just uncertain if it had withstood the ten minutes…
Seeing Colin move, the few employees didn’t think much and promptly followed.
Minutes later, Colin arrived at the fourth sub-level, and after descending, it was no longer the unchanging “米” shaped crossroads resembling a maze; some rooms began to appear…
Past a large door, Colin looked up at the marking on top of the door: “Which number is this, Breeding Hall?”
Then, his gaze entered the space, and in a hall of tens of thousands of square meters, he saw an array of cultivation chambers that looked like incubators.
Inside, there were vaguely discernible shapes the size of a palm, similar to undeveloped embryos.
If he was not mistaken, they were likely humans…
Perhaps influenced by “Time Reversal,” he seemed to hear the sound of babies crying.
“Are these the devices that can produce tens of millions of people at a time?”
Colin focused on the dried embryos, wondering if a cultivation chamber of about ten cubic meters could contain several dozen people.
The capacity was quite significant; it was just uncertain how often a batch of people was produced…
“Hiss, it sounds like there are baby cries, so many, it’s a bit unnerving… Is this a cloning device?” Little Chicken couldn’t help but wrap his arms around himself and speak out.
“If nothing goes wrong, it indeed is…”
“Life Mentor Adorable,” walking beside Colin, nodded in affirmation.
Hearing his words, “Son of Cruelty” asked curiously, “Speaking of which, how does the company usually deal with these special humans in terms of human relationships? Aren’t they criticized by some power groups?”
Life Mentor glanced at Brother Shunzi, saw that he had no intention of answering, and then spoke:
“Not clear, but there should be a set of human rights logic inside, right? As for criticism… as long as no one inside their company objects, even if other forces know that they are doing ‘morally degenerate’ things, they can only say a word about respecting local customs…”
‘That does make sense…’
Colin, listening on the side, nodded silently as he led the group forward, and according to his understanding of the company.
With its massive size…
Merely relying on traditional methods of natural reproduction, the population growth could hardly keep up.
Shaking his head, he didn’t think too much of it. Colin was drawn by some barely audible sounds ahead, his gaze passing over the hallway to see an area up front that looked like a temporary hospital.

chapters.title: Chapter 485 - 485 409
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 485: 409 Chapter 485: 409 The battle at the beginning obviously had no agreement that prevented attacks on the injured.
Humanity and the Heretic Forces were completely engaged in a war of survival, intent on each other’s utter destruction, so this place was severely attacked as well.
In the air, occasional old and blurry images and sounds flashed by.
Unfortunately, due to the lack of clarity in sounds and such, there wasn’t much of value to be found.
“However, it’s worth mentioning that the monsters trapped in the ‘Time Reversal’ on this floor are basically gone, and most are just historical images…”
“Those trapped mostly congregate from the minus first to the minus third floor, and moreover, they are all of intermediate strength… This seems pretty normal as the more powerful ones can usually detect traps and wouldn’t easily enter.”
“It’s just unclear who the ‘Demons’ fear from ‘them’ specifically.”
So far, Colin had encountered many enemies escaping from the “Time Reversal” in their first status, and they seemed to be fleeing.
It seemed that they were all afraid of something…
However, having descended to the minus fourth floor, they still hadn’t seen anything that could cause such creatures to be afraid.
After nearly half an hour of progress, Colin and the others entered a special room of about a thousand square feet.
The layout inside was somewhat like that of a hotel lobby…
Then, following the guide, they closed the door and placed their hands on it.
Subsequently, a line of seemingly writhing three-dimensional information appeared in the air…
[You are currently attempting to enter the “living quarters.” However, according to the information feedback, the area still contains highly contaminated objects. Please confirm whether to continue with this command?]
The minus fourth floor had such complete living facilities yet it was not considered a living area?
But was this room actually a facility like an elevator?
Colin was surprised for a moment and then requested to continue the access, following the mission’s guidance for further confirmation.
He had become accustomed to the mechanical facilities still functioning in this place.
“Click.”
The entire thousand square foot room vibrated for a moment.
Then, everyone felt a sense of weightlessness as it seemed to start descending rapidly…
‘The commotion is so big, riding this elevator feels almost like taking off and landing in an airplane…’
Colin couldn’t help but make a comment as he tensed his leg muscles slightly and adjusted his stance to stand firmer.
Five minutes later…
The elevator seemed not to have reached the bottom yet.
By Colin’s side, “Son of Cruelty” couldn’t help but speak:
“Where are we descending to? It’s not like we’re going to fly to the center of the earth, right?”
“This…”
As Colin was about to speak, a sudden change occurred.
From behind them, seemingly from the center of the room, a terrifying aura spread out violently.
This power had not even exploded, its mere presence made everyone feel tight-chested.
Almost simultaneously, flames erupted from Colin’s body as he swiftly turned around and saw six extremely solid figures appear in the center of the room, their formidable presences emanating from them.
“Don’t be nervous, they seem to be just historical images…”
Upon realizing their nature, Colin immediately relaxed.
These historical figures were sitting in the center, seemingly in conversation, but the sofas they were originally sitting on were long broken and out of place due to the battle, causing some of them to be sitting in mid-air, while others seemed to be half-sunk into the couches…
However, that was not the point.
Upon the appearance of these formidable historical images, Colin walked straight toward them, routinely snooping – no, gathering information.
‘With such a fluctuation of aura, they all feel like C-level characters at the least, tsk! Similar elevator rooms, I remember there’s more than this one, yet the mission’s guidance led us here, there seems to be some arrangement…’
This level of individuals, even just chit-chatting, would reveal information of immense value!
Perhaps there was a chance to understand what happened on this starship.
The four members of the mobile unit by his side also kept silent and hurriedly followed.
However, only taking a few steps closer to them, Colin stopped abruptly as he suddenly felt a “thud” at the bottom of his heart.
“I feel like… there are eyes other than ours… focused here.”
One of the six high-level members suddenly spoke.
As their words fell, the other five individuals simultaneously unleashed an incredibly terrifying aura, causing the entire elevator room to shake uncontrollably and, at that moment, come to a complete stop.
The frightening fluctuation of aura made everyone present, including Colin, catch their breath, as if reminded of that man.
But, a few seconds later…
“Where’s the person?” One of the C-level personnel said in confusion.
“Calm down, sit down. I was just saying. I’m not entirely sure either, and even if there really was someone, it likely wouldn’t be a bad thing…”
As that high-ranking member was soothing everyone, Colin also took a closer look at him and noticed a large number of fine black lines emanating from his body.
These fine lines trembled subtly in the air…
‘A ‘Fate Principle’ member who has reached the C-level.’
Colin was inwardly shocked, seeing him after an unknown stretch of years?
It’s a bit exaggerated…
At that moment, another serious C-level member said, “How can you be sure it’s definitely not bad?”
“It has a certain connection to the ‘Flame Bearer,’ more than that I can’t describe…”
Hearing this, the heavy atmosphere at the scene eased, and everyone sat back down, while a C-level individual, whose position wasn’t aligned correctly, spoke:

chapters.title: Chapter 486 - 486 409
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 486: 409 Chapter 486: 409 “Could it have something to do with the ‘Flame Bearer’ superior who’s about to join our starship fleet?”
Upon hearing this, a C-level ‘Fate Propeller’ pondered for a few seconds before replying, “It might be, it might not be…”
“Your answer is as good as saying nothing. You guys who draw power from the ‘Book of Fate’ really… love to speak in riddles and enjoy giving everyone a startle… It’s no wonder you’ve been voted the number one group most people want to smack with a club each year.”
“Don’t sweat the details, it’s all good.” He waved his hand dismissively, revealing his teeth beneath his upper and lower lips, forming a smile that begged for a punch.
“Whatever…”
A high-ranking official, sitting mid-air, shook his head, then leaned back, stretching while speaking:
“After transferring so many ‘World Code’ personnel, I was hoping to get some rest after the mission, but now it seems that’s not going to happen…”
“Indeed.”
A C-level who hadn’t sat down, holding a thermos and wearing glasses, nodded in agreement:
“A pre-war reward, all D-levels get a minor rank promotion, and even from my perspective as someone who enjoys C-level benefits, it’s practically a one-way ticket…”
“But for all C-levels to get a major promotion, being shortlisted for B-level authority directly, it’s simply unheard of.”
“Plus, there’s going to be a ‘Flame Bearer’ superior parachuting in here later, no idea what for exactly…”
Hearing this, a ‘Fate Propeller’ of C-level spoke up: “If not for the pre-war reward, based on this setup, I’d guess it’s to deal with a Super First Class Life. But with the reward being so substantial… it’s hard to predict.”
Pre-war reward, a trip with no return.
The more generous the reward, the less likely to return alive…
Yet, even dealing with a Super First Class Life doesn’t justify such a cost.
Even they don’t know what’s going to happen next.
“Stop guessing; we’ll find out what we’re supposed to do once he arrives.”
A C-level who had been silent up till now interrupted everyone’s speculations, then frustratingly ran his fingers through his hair:
“Anyway, my task is to ensure, at any cost, that our starship can consistently produce a military force of ten million people, with immediate replenishment, no matter the losses. Who wants to volunteer for the Breeding Hall and give me a hand…”
“I can’t handle breeding duties, you’re on your own.”
The high-ranking official next to him moved his buttocks without hesitation and, before his colleague could reach out, switched to the other side of the couch.
“There are five days until the ‘Flame Bearer’ arrives. Let’s talk about something else… Hey, I managed to secure a ‘Protagonist’ life experience on the Mother Star for my daughter. Initially, I wanted her to experience what it’s like to have both parents as ‘Protagonists,’ but now it looks like we’ll all just have to follow the trend…”
“Ha-ha…”
“You’ve done well; a Mother Star Experience Card doesn’t come cheap. But it seems like there are quite a few people doing the same thing. With so many, won’t we end up with a world where ‘Protagonists’ are everywhere?”
…
“Looking at this situation, it seems the battle hasn’t started yet. I guess it’s still the historical imagery before the invasion. But this pre-war reward and the mention of a ‘Flame Bearer’ having been here before…”
Listening to their conversation, Colin muttered the key words to himself, faintly realizing that “Time Reversal” might stem from the “approaching” “Flame Bearer.”
Unfortunately, the group didn’t delve further into these topics, choosing instead to chat about other things.
And as time went by…
The elevator car, which had been moving for thirty minutes, seemed to finally reach its destination, the historical imagery on the couch growing dim.
Even Colin could no longer hear their voices clearly.
…
…
…
PS: Making up for yesterday, tonight’s update will be late. I’ll be writing all day for the national holiday, humbly asking for double-month tickets.

chapters.title: Chapter 487 - 487 410 Do I Need to Retrieve an Organ Again
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 487: Chapter 410: Do I Need to Retrieve an Organ Again? (Compensation)_1 Chapter 487: Chapter 410: Do I Need to Retrieve an Organ Again? (Compensation)_1 “A ‘Firebearer’ who is about to arrive here, the ‘Firebearer’…”
As he recalled their conversation, Colin glanced at the slowly halting elevator car and raised an eyebrow—
Putting aside everything else, would this recovery mission include not only “Time Reversal” but also some body part of this ‘Firebearer’?
It was uncertain, but the possibility was indeed not small.
“If that card ‘plays another hand’ or, say, requires the retrieval of some organ, I feel like I’m really becoming an organ trafficker…”
Muttering to himself, Colin slightly refocused his thoughts.
As troublesome as it might be, it had to be said that in missions involving ‘Firebearers,’ securing the key items usually meant nearly securing the battle situation.
Like the heart of a ‘Firebearer’ in a seaside watchtower, or the “hand” from ‘World Code-4,’ or that heart…
They were strong enough that, even in death, they could exert enough power to suppress the aftermath.
“However, the premise is securing the key items, and besides, ‘Firebearers’ seem to only play in high-stakes scenarios, so the battlefields they head to are bound to be among the most dangerous places. Therefore, before getting appropriate protection, caution is still needed…”
“It’s just unfortunate that, so far, I have yet to truly see a living ‘Firebearer.’
“I wonder just how strong such a formidable fighter actually is when he gets serious…”
Colin rubbed his forehead, slightly regretful as he surmised that this one here was most likely dead too.
These days, the stronger the ‘Firebearer,’ the more thoroughly they seemed to die, the cleaner their death, and exceptions were almost nonexistent.
If a ‘Firebearer’ didn’t die cleanly, it probably meant they weren’t strong enough.
Take the ‘Ghost Train’ incident’s C-Level Elder Brother; he claimed to be a ‘Firebearer,’ but wasn’t quite one…
That’s why there was an opportunity to meet him and even exchange a few words…
The truly formidable ones now were typically left with only ashes, or even less than that.
“That’s not right, why do I always feel like this thought has the air of a hellish joke… According to this logic, my future prospects don’t seem too bright.”
Flexing his fingers, Colin murmured in his heart, and then thought of the six C-Level Personnel from before.
Recalling their explosive aura…
‘The aura of a typical Level C Personnel is about the same as a Level 9 official power, which means the entire Earth might not be able to gather two hands’ worth of Level 9 Personnel, yet this room alone could gather enough for a table of mahjong, and still have two left over for chess…’
Colin secretly marvelled, understanding that on Earth, Level 9 wouldn’t be so abundant to have five of the Four Heavenly Kings.
The actual number would only be fewer…
Moreover, apart from Old Master Wu, most Level 9s mostly remained in a semi-dormant state, preferring not to act unless necessary,
lest the problem remains unsolved and they become the problem themselves.
Furthermore, whether domestically or internationally, if a fighter of this caliber were to be active, the scene would be equipped with as many high-level Fate Propellers as possible, constantly adjusting their ‘Lifeline of Fate’…
To minimize the chances of losing control.
“Without ‘Gene Compensation Medicine’ the cost of using extraordinary powers is still too great.”
“But speaking of which, if those six Level C Employees faced off against that half-step ‘Firebearer’ or C-Level Elder Brother, they would probably still lose.”
“After all, the Elder Brother might be in the ‘Firebearer’ Reservist, but if he could safely return, he’d likely be Bonfire embodied.”
Thinking this, Colin could not help but shake his head and quietly lament the pity.
But not dwelling on it for long, the descent of the elevator car jolted slightly, as if it had reached the destination floor.
At the same time, a completion notification for the investigation mission popped up in the minds of Colin and the four people behind him, along with a new mission event.
[Event Seven: Attempt to locate the remaining personnel on this level, and obtain further information about this place.]
“Note”: If the remaining personnel cannot be found within one hour, this mission will be automatically cancelled.
…
“There are still remaining personnel?”
Colin was somewhat surprised.
Given the current view of the Starship Expeditionary Force members, who were mostly sacrificed, he had thought they were utterly annihilated.
But through this mission, it could be determined that not all of them were dead.
‘So it seems, there may soon be an additional mission to take away survivors from this place, that is, in addition to retrieving the card and human organs, there might be a rescue mission as well?’
Based on past experience, Colin felt reassured.
He wasn’t afraid of having more things to do, but of not knowing what exactly to do…
At this time, Son of Sadomasochism spoke up, “Speaking of which, this note says that if the remaining personnel are not found, the mission will be automatically canceled. And if they really aren’t found, what happens after it’s canceled?”
After being tricked once by the mission description of the “Ghost Train”, he now carefully reads the mission details several times.
Fearing that he might miss something…
And the current event only mentioned cancellation, but not whether a new one would be issued afterwards.
This made him somewhat anxious.
If there won’t be an update following the mission, wouldn’t that mean they’re trapped again?
If it’s about fighting some formidable creature, Son of Sadomasochism felt that with their strength as a team with Brother Shunzi, they could handle even the strongest of enemies…
But when it comes to the uncertainty of searching for people, plus with a time constraint, it’s not looking too good.
Hearing his words, Colin shook his head, “I don’t know, I’ve never failed a mission, so I’m not clear on what exactly happens afterward.”
Hearing this, the others couldn’t help but curl their lips.
If it were anyone else claiming they had completed all their missions, they wouldn’t believe it.
But coming from Brother Shunzi, it seemed much more reasonable.
“Generally speaking, even if there are no immediate tasks, as long as you continue to stay here, new missions will eventually come,” Lifecoach Kawaii-many pondered for a moment before giving a straightforward answer.
Assured by the words of this authoritative D Level veteran, the group felt somewhat relieved.
“Alright, there’s not much time. Let’s get moving, prepare yourselves. If there are no problems, I’ll open the door…”
Colin waved his hand to end the conversation, giving everyone a minute.
Then, seeing no further questions, he reached out and placed his hand on the grand door.
[A large number of abnormalities exist on this floor; after opening, there is a significant risk that this elevator will stall. Please confirm whether to open…]
“Yes.”
Colin made his choice decisively.
With a “clack,”
the doors of the elevator slid open, and as they did, a thick black fog squeezed in through the crevices…
However, under the glow of the firelight, they dissipated and dissolved.
And as the gap in the door widened further…
The scene of the starship’s “Living Layer” was revealed to everyone—
At first glance, one could see a vast space containing a city, and above it in the kilometer-high sky, a celestial body emitting a dim yellow light like the sun…
In a trance, Colin thought of the term “Arcadia.”
If it weren’t for the city being flattened, and the strange howling coming from everywhere, along with the thick black fog drifting in most parts of the sky…
This place could indeed be considered an “Arcadia.”
“This light, it’s somewhat like the halo above the ‘Twilight Angel’s’ head; they both have a weariness debuff…”
Feeling the power within, Colin recalled that First Level Containment Subject with only the upper half of its body.
However, he didn’t dwell too much on remembering that thing. As he prepared to look away from the imitation sun’s glowing object and to enter this place to search for the so-called “survivors”.
Suddenly, his heart “thudded.”
Then he saw a crack open up in the center of that dim, artificial sun.
The crack spread to both sides…
A giant eye looked towards him.
.
.
.
Just adding one more

chapters.title: Chapter 488 - 488 411 Life Will Find a Way_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 488: Chapter 411 Life Will Find a Way_1 Chapter 488: Chapter 411 Life Will Find a Way_1 Emptiness, fatigue, as if his body had been hollowed out in an instant…
Under the gaze of that enormous eye.
A sense of extreme desolation rose in everyone’s heart.
“So tired, so sleepy, don’t want to move at all…”
“Living is so hard…”
“Wuwuwu, I barely advanced to D Level in less than three months, it took me three years, I’m trash, I am…”
“…”
Several employees thought in unison about sitting down right here, giving up, never to take action again.
However, deep inside, a strong will to survive emerged.
It barely allowed them to regain some semblance of rationality.
Before the crowd could use their own methods to counter this cunning force, a burst of orange-red firelight exploded in front of them, dispelling most of the weariness and helplessness.
“Indeed, it’s a power similar to the ‘Twilight Angel’…”
Colin took a deep breath.
Compared to that Twilight Angel thousands of kilometers high, this one was much smaller in scale.
And, more fortunately…
It seemed to only have one eye there, with no other body parts.
Colin then took a step forward, walking out of the elevator room, triggering the eruption of his own Bonfire to block and neutralize the sleepy, dull yellow light.
At the same time, on the ruined land ahead, numerous deformed entities filled with hateful spiritual fluctuations seeped out from both expected and unexpected places, swarming everywhere. Then, like a tide, they surged towards this location from all directions.
The ground shook incessantly as a result…
“Hiss, what the hell are these things… So many of them!?”
Lifecoach Kawaii-many, Son of Sadomasochism, and others gasped in shock upon seeing this scene.
As if they had seen a glimpse of the world’s end a step ahead.
At the same time, looking at these entities, Colin couldn’t help but think of a term he had heard from historical records.
“Flood Devil.”
Innumerable, like a flood, the name was not wrong at all.
However, Colin didn’t feel too panicked because of this. His right hand reached into the Storage Room and he calmly dragged out three objects that looked like high-explosive grenades but were much larger, comparable to a general bucket. He hurled them forward.
The next second, these special grenades exploded.
Their explosive power wasn’t strong, but they sprayed a large amount of grease in every direction.
Seeing this, Colin raised his right hand and snapped his fingers. A snapping sound echoed, and the next second, all grease ignited explosively, making a thunderous roar.
Terrifying flames erupted instantly from this place, rolling up like a mushroom cloud…
“Go!”
As he spoke, Colin held his Revolver and fired a shot at the heretic wave surging towards him like a blanket. The exploding flame, as if following an order, tilted down like an avalanche, colliding with those terrifying creatures known as “Flood Devils.”
Serpentine flames, dozens of meters in length, twirled like grotesque tongues licking the earth, scorching all incoming enemies…
For a moment, the monster wave that had made their scalps numb was somehow halted in its tracks.
“What kind of grenade is this, so fierce? What’s it filled with that feels like a chemical plant exploded.”
Lifecoach Kawaii-many felt the hot wave coming from ahead and was astounded.
He had not seen any company’s mark on those grenades; they were clearly made by another unknown force.
And hearing his words, Son of Sadomasochism, who knew some inside information, shook his head and explained loudly over the howling flames:
“It’s not the grenades that are powerful, it seems to be that grease, but this time it doesn’t look like they used soda bottles…”
Brother Shunzi had used this stuff before, but back then, it was bottled in 1.25-liter Sprite bottles, not these things.
Clearly, Brother Shunzi’s craft had been upgraded…
Hearing this, Lifecoach Kawaii-many wanted to ask more questions, but suddenly felt an intense wave of fatigue attack him again.
Overhead, that giant bizarre eye seemed unwilling to let them off the hook so easily.
“Can’t let you off without a cleanup, can I?”
Colin lifted his head, his eyebrows arching as he looked at the eye. He casually pulled out three more “grease grenades” and flung them into the sky.
In mid-air, the grenades exploded, a large amount of grease spreading instantly before it was ignited.
A massive flame covered the sky.
Then, without waiting for the flames to fall from the sky, Colin held a Golden Card in one hand and pointed to the heavens with the other.
In an instant, a great fireball slowly rose.
Guided by “Repulsion” and Colin’s own will, it charged directly at that “eye.”
If it had been before, Colin might have had to think about how to respond, but during this time, under Shana’s special training, they had studied numerous ways to use artifacts, as well as simulated many battle scenarios…
So there was not a hint of panic.
While Colin couldn’t control the fireball, which had a diameter over a hundred meters, very well, the situation was different when combined with “Repulsion.”
The rising flames melted away all the invisible abnormal attacks en route.
And that staring “eye,” seeing the flames growing ever closer, finally chose to close again.
At this moment, the light of the fire replaced the twilight.
“There seems to be no one within the range covered by the flames. I’ll need to go deeper. I’ve never encountered monsters like these before,” Colin thought.
“However, the Saintess simulated a similar scenario for me. If all goes as expected, the key is not to get swept up by those ‘Flood Devils’. I need to stay as close to them as possible, otherwise things will get troublesome,” he surmised.
Quickly making his judgment and realizing the key points, Colin prepared to act.
But before taking formal action, he made some other preparations, taking out another Golden Artifact from his pocket.
A seemingly ordinary Shield Emblem…
Using the passive effect of this artifact, he quickly found the weak spot in the flow of the Flood Devils.
Of course, if the situation became really dire, he could designate an employee behind him for a one-on-one attack, adjusting his status and recovering himself in the process…
As for which employee to choose, that would depend on their fate.
After all, according to the prompt, dying before the countdown ends wouldn’t result in true death.
As for what came after…that was left to “Life will find a way.”
After identifying the weak spot in the wave of Flood Devils, Colin continued to rummage in his pocket and pulled out an ordinary-looking sticker to apply to himself.
“The False Powerhouse.”
This thing’s boost to him was starting to diminish, and to be truly effective, it required a massive number of people.
Now there were just a few misshapen figures on the scene, not making much of a difference in enhancement.
But what Colin needed now was the “effective recognition” layer of effect…
That is, as soon as someone perceived him to be strong, he could instantly follow that “gaze” to determine the precise location of the target.
This way, if someone was hiding in the shadows, unseen by the Bonfire,
But as long as they harbored the corresponding thought,
He could avoid oversights, serving as a double insurance.
‘The only pity is that the maximum distance of the effect is just one kilometer. In a sense, it seems that I also have somewhat a trait similar to those of certain powerful creatures – “where there is knowledge, there must be detection”…’
‘It’s just a bit of a pauper’s version…’
Shaking his head inwardly, Colin gathered his thoughts and, without looking back, said to the others, “Hurry up and come out, don’t just stand there spacing out.”
With that, the group finally came to their senses and walked out of the elevator.
As soon as everyone was out, the elevator door slammed shut with a “bang.”
[Thank you for riding with us this time, we look forward to your next ride.]
Subtitles floated in the air.
But a second later, rumbling noises came from behind the door, as it seemed eager to leave this place.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 489 - 489 412 Special Level 2 Containment Subject
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 489: Chapter 412 Special Level 2 Containment Subject “Flood Devil”._1 Chapter 489: Chapter 412 Special Level 2 Containment Subject “Flood Devil”._1 “Quick on the draw, huh? Is this artificial intelligence?”
Colin found himself speechless but didn’t dwell on it. Taking a deep breath, he distinguished some smells and roughly chose a direction based on his instincts, advising a “Follow me” before plunging ahead.
He had barely started moving when he saw even more Flood Devils, flowing like liquid, racing towards them.
But the vast majority were reduced to thorough charcoals beneath the flames.
And as they broke through, getting closer to these creatures, Colin and his team got a clearer look at them.
They were a kind of special amorphous liquid creature, composed of dense paint-like substance, with their surfaces covered in a large number of seemingly underdeveloped hands, feet, eyes, noses, and various organs of other creatures…
Every Flood Devil had an exceptionally fierce appearance.
However, what truly unsettled Colin and the others was not these external features.
It was on these creatures that…
He smelled the scent of humans.
Moreover, when the bonfire consumed them, the screams emanating from those mouths sounded eerily similar to human voices.
‘Could it be that these monsters were humans who lost control? No, on the whole, it seems more like some anomaly fused with humans…’
While firing and killing those individuals that couldn’t be immediately taken down by the “Air Bullets’ AOE, Colin thought.
But regardless, since the company mission didn’t indicate completion, meaning they were not shown to be humans,
Then they were not human…
…
Meanwhile, in another vast space, a large group of people fully covered in lightweight black armor were walking under the dusk, holding distinctive weapons and exterminating substances resembling black tar on the ground and walls.
After every “Reversal,” in addition to the appearance of more anomalies, a large number of Flood Devils would seep out from the deepest “Core Layer” of the starship.
They had to be cleared out quickly, otherwise, if they accumulated too much, the next “Reversal” would become an incredibly troublesome disaster.
Moreover, only by dealing with these creatures could they further address the troubles seeping out from the “Core Layer.”
“Move carefully, don’t let your biomatter leak, to avoid activating… huh?”
A commanding officer, with a knife at his waist, was speaking when he suddenly felt something was off.
The Flood Devils in the crevices on the ground were subtly wriggling about.
It looked as if they were rapidly reviving…
“Damn it, who let out their biomatter scent… Everyone pull out!” the commanding officer exclaimed in shock, immediately decided to retreat from the area.
They simply didn’t have the capability to suppress them with just their troop.
And upon his command, without any hesitation, everyone began to evacuate as practiced, leaving their tasks behind.
But just at that moment…
A squad member, ensnared by the anomalies that were slowly coming to life, tripped and fell to the ground.
He had already been entangled by one of the Flood Devils that had revived earlier.
But upon seeing their comrade fall, no one moved to assist. After falling, the ensnared soldier didn’t struggle or call for help…
According to the regulations, he had ten seconds to attempt to free himself.
Unfortunately…
The ten seconds quickly passed.
He took out a sharp kinetic dagger and tried several times to cut through the Flood Devil’s limbs but failed to achieve any success.
The short dagger simply couldn’t cut through the wrappings of the Flood Devil.
When time was up, without any hesitation, he activated a special device on his armor.
In an instant, a cold mist erupted, freezing him and the Flood Devil together, silently returning to death.
These abnormal beings are extremely sensitive to the breath of life…
If one doesn’t end themselves in time and the armor is breached, all creatures within a nearly ten-kilometer radius will be revived.
By then, no one on site will be able to return.
What he didn’t expect was that after he chose to perish together, all the “Flood Devils” in the field began to revive at an unimaginable speed.
The entire field seemed to be boiling over…
“Damn it, everyone’s armor is still intact, who the hell revived them?”
The commander cursed under his breath. Normally, these creatures would choose to hibernate after one or two days of activity if they didn’t sense any active life force. During hibernation, with special armor to avoid detection of their life breath, one could easily dispose of them.
But now, for some unknown reason, they were all awakening.
In the face of such a potentially catastrophic situation, he was not thinking about his own safety or that of his teammates, nor was he interested in pursuing whose fault it was. Instead, he was preoccupied with another matter:
If the Flood Devils in this spatial region revived bizarrely and completely came back to life, and if this intelligence was not relayed back, the entire rear team could suffer an attack.
Even more alarmingly, the entire defense might collapse.
Because these creatures, though classified as Level 2 Containment Subjects, actually carried traits of First Level Containment Subjects. If they escaped, it meant that humanity’s enemies from the “core zone” would once again extend their claws toward the outside world behind them…
This was absolutely not allowed!
Yet, at this very moment, they were deep in trouble, who could break through the black fog and safely bring back the information?
“Everyone, break through to Area 112 with me; there is a Signal Tower there…”
After brief contemplation, the commander issued his instruction.
In a certain period afterward, due to the presence of a special anomalous life form, they had abandoned the original communication systems and only used face-to-face interactions among personnel on the ground.
And now, they were uncharacteristically using this device to send the information back.
Regardless of whether the information was intercepted or altered.
Others would understand that there definitely was something wrong with this area.
Thereupon, without any hesitation, they decisively turned direction, not contemplating whether anyone could survive the return, but instead charged toward a possible Signal Tower in this area.
At the same time, a great number of “Flood Devils” woke up from their slumber.
And then they launched an attack on them directly…
Brandishing their Power Swords and utilizing their armor, they continuously drew the black mist from the air, controlling it to counter the enemies.
Finally, after about fifteen minutes, at the cost of one-third of their comrades falling in battle,
The commander saw the Signal Tower within the ruins of the city, collapsed yet with its main structure still preserved.
“The main part is still there, if only we can manage to repair it in time…”
Just as the commander started to harbor this thought, his pupils suddenly contracted as he saw a “Flood Devil” individual with a diameter surpassing one hundred meters falling from the sky.
With a thunderous crash, dust and smoke soared to the sky, the terrifying shockwave causing everyone to stagger.
In an instant, it had smashed his last sliver of “hope” to pieces.
However, more horrifying to him than this was that an unfamiliar voice abruptly sounded in his ear…
The language was very strange.
Yet inexplicably, it seemed comprehensible…
“I’ve been searching for a long time, finally, I see a living person.”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 490 - 490 413 We Cannot Become Sinners._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 490: Chapter 413 We Cannot Become Sinners._1 Chapter 490: Chapter 413 We Cannot Become Sinners._1 When?!
The squad commander of the Silent Legion turned his head and saw a figure engulfed in flames, who had appeared beside him without notice.
Following him, they looked at the gigantic “Flood Demon” that had been slain in front of them.
At this moment, as if noticing his gaze, the powerful man withdrew his eyes, turned his head toward him, and raised the corners of his mouth slightly, revealing eight teeth in what he thought to be a mild smile:
“Hello.”
Whoosh whoosh whoosh…
The rest of the squad reacted extremely fast, aiming their weapons at the stranger who had appeared suddenly.
However, before they could retaliate, the squad commander raised his hand to stop them.
He did not feel any obvious malice from these people.
And it seemed they were not traitors to humanity, those Heretic Followers…
“Who are you?” the squad commander asked.
Upon hearing the electronic synthesized voice that was neither male nor female, Colin didn’t beat around the bush and replied straightforwardly, “We’re sent by the company to execute a special item retrieval mission.”
While speaking, he took a glance at the “survivors”…
It could be seen that these people were clad in a special armor that was impenetrable to air, all of them towering at a uniform height of two meters. Except for the insignia on their shoulders, it was hard to tell who was who.
Hearing Colin’s words, the squad commander was puzzled for a moment: “Company?”
Didn’t recognize us? Could it be they are not from the company?
Colin raised his eyebrows but quickly noticed the insignia on the chest plates of their armor, which should be the Expedition Army symbol he had seen before, so it must be right…
Moreover, there was a certain “aura” about these people that only company employees would have.
And of course, the most crucial point was…
The moment he set eyes on these people, the mission refreshed.
[Event Eight: Communicate with them, obtain as much intelligence as possible, and use their help to infiltrate ‘Core Zone B’ at the appropriate time, locate and retrieve the item…]
“Remark”: The time is approximately within three hours, please understand the specific details on your own.
…
With the mission “guarantee,” it was basically certain they were one of us.
After a moment of thought, he changed his statement and then said, “The full name is ‘Bonfire Camp Special Item Containment Company’…”
Upon hearing this, the squad commander hesitated for a moment, then as if coming to a realization, his body trembled, “You… are the personnel sent by the company? The company still exists?”
The other members of the squad heard this and seemed to show signs of shock, becoming unsteady in holding their weapons.
If it weren’t for the fact that they were all wearing full-body armor, Colin felt their expressions underneath would be quite amusing.
‘It seems like they hadn’t thought of it because the company’s presence had been absent here for too long?’ he thought to himself.
With that thought, Colin nodded.
“It’s… truly… such a relief, that outside, our company’s people are still around, that our persistence has not been meaningless…”
The squad commander murmured in confusion, his hands trembling before clenched into fists, then after what seemed like an internal struggle, he finally let out a sigh of relief as if a great burden had been lifted, releasing his fists.
As the other party recited the name, they could confirm through some implanted items in their brains.
These people… were colleagues!
‘Why such a big emotional swing, isn’t it too much?’ Feeling the emotional changes, Colin had a sensation that the guy in front of him could pass away “with a smile” at any moment.
“May I ask, what item are you here to retrieve?” The squad commander seemed to have let go of all doubts and asked.
“An item related to time, it causes a regional reversal of time in certain areas, making affected people possibly repeat the process over and over…”
Colin feared they might not understand “Time Reversal,” so he simply explained some of its effects.
“Related to time…” The squad commander immediately realized what Colin was talking about.
After all, the infamous “Reversal” within the entire starship occurred because of this thing.
All anomalies seeking to leave were trapped here forever, repeating the same events countless times, unbeknownst to them, because of its power.
But before he could say anything,
Boom boom…
The ground trembled slightly.
Looking up, they saw a massive wave of twisted, mutated flesh surging towards them.
Seeing this, the squad commander’s face under the armored helmet changed color as he spoke urgently, handing something on his chest to Colin while directing him, “It’s a massive ‘Flood Disaster’! You escape first, take this badge and move in that direction…”
“And you?” Colin asked instinctively, taking what was handed to him.
“We’ll try to lure these things away. According to their habits, they’ll prioritize chasing the largest group. Head in that direction, and you’ll soon meet the main task force. You’ll be safe then. Just tell them you’ve encountered 999178534220121511…”
While speaking, the squad commander placed her hands on her helmet and removed the black helmet to reveal the face of a woman with short gray hair, lovely features, but slightly asymmetrical…
As if a realistic oil painting had been scorched by the flames, somewhat distorted.
At the same time, the other squad members removed their helmets as well.
“Hiss…” Seeing their faces clearly, Colin and the four mobile eyes behind him were taken aback.
It wasn’t that these people were extraordinarily striking in appearance.
It was because, regardless of gender, their features were too similar, as if cast from the same mold.
The only discordant thing was that their faces were somewhat distorted…
However, not dwelling too much on this, Colin shook his head: “I thought you had some other mission to attend to. If it’s just this, then follow me.”

chapters.title: Chapter 491 - 491 413 We Cannot Become Sinners._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 491: Chapter 413 We Cannot Become Sinners._2 Chapter 491: Chapter 413 We Cannot Become Sinners._2 These twisted beings, if they continued to engage him in unrelenting combat for ten days or half a month, could indeed exhaust him to death.
But as long as he found the direction…
Colin spread his hands, chuckling and shaking his head, “These little things can’t really pose any threat to me, with my strength, I can ensure the safety of everyone present.”
“Don’t be careless, this is a large regional… com…” the squad leader named by a long string of numbers was trying to say something.
The next second, a massive column of fire fell from the sky, enveloping everyone within it.
And it was at this moment that she seemed to realize something, noticing that the brightness here seemed much higher than usual…
Slowly lifting her head, she saw an enormous “sun” overhead, with a diameter stretching hundreds of meters.
The flames that fell from it made them feel a warmth they had never experienced since birth.
“Just follow with confidence, my ‘Brother Shunzi’ has never had a death on a mission,” “Little Chicken No. 7” assured them, seeing their hesitation.
Then, Colin didn’t continue to linger and charged ahead leading the way.
The others exchanged glances and eventually followed Colin, trailing behind.
It wasn’t that they weren’t afraid of death…
But given a choice, they wouldn’t deliberately seek to sacrifice themselves.
The squad leader looked ahead at the man advancing unstoppably, as if entering an uninhabited territory, and couldn’t help feeling internally moved:
“Worthy of being a direct member of the company, indeed, just as strong as the historical records say,” he thought.
From a distant era, generation after generation had stood firm to this day; they were no longer the earliest of people.
Nor had they inherited too much of the legacy from that time…
When faced with numerous dangers, all they could offer in return were their lives and sacrifices.
About ten minutes later, Colin suddenly heard a vibration in his ear, followed by the sight of hundreds of armored vehicles of various models, each outfitted with multi-barreled cannons, emerging from the continuous ruins of the town.
Each shell fired could annihilate a group of Flood Devils.
Amidst the vibrating roar of the cannons, there were also drones buzzing like swarms of bees, firing searing rays and plasma, suppressing the wave-like enemy.
The grand war scene before him made Colin think of a term.
Steel tide.
“The weaponry is quite advanced; some even I can feel the threat from…”
Colin was surprised internally, he had thought the people here were weak.
But with these equipments being pulled out now, the strength was still up to standard.
‘Also, if they were too weak, they couldn’t have lasted so long, but compared to the regular ‘Zoo’ Corps, the strength is quite a lot lower,’ Colin silently compared.
At that moment, it seemed the enormous steel tide had noticed Colin; they began adjusting the bombardment location, and a large number of drones, about the size of dogs, flew towards him…
“Attention! Please follow the green lights to proceed.”
“Attention! Please follow the purple lights to retreat.”
“Attention! Please follow the yellow lights….”
The mechanical calls repeated over and over, coming from those drones ahead.
Colin, with a fist in his left hand, shattered an aberration, and his right hand revolver transformed into an eight-feet-long sword, holding his breath, he unleashed a flame-boosted power air slash, forcibly tearing a path through the non-human tide.
Afterward, he looked at those things in mid-air, frowning.
“It’s fine, because of certain things, our signal transmission might get distorted, but the issue is only here, just follow its movements…”
The squad leader, with a beautiful face but an exceedingly long name, explained while running.
The man in front of them was unexpectedly fast; they had thought about providing some side assistance.
As a result, merely keeping up with their speed had already required his full effort.
Upon hearing that, Colin didn’t say much and directly followed the group of drones that were verbally unreliable but physically very honest.
Shortly after, he led everyone through the dense barrage of bullets and arrived before a massive convoy of war vehicles. He stretched out his hand, causing the fireballs in the sky to shrink continuously until they became an orange-red glowing ball, only the size of a basketball, floating beside him.
Many eyes at the scene turned towards him, curious about his power, but they only took an extra glance and did not approach.
Within the entire massive procession of steel, other than the sounds of machinery operating, there were no superfluous noises.
Just as Colin stepped into the advancing torrent of steel, a tactical squad immediately came to meet him and moved them to a relatively safe place before taking the gray-haired squad leader away…
“Sorry, you’ll need to wait here for a while, and those things outside, leave them to us to handle,” said a soldier dressed in full covering armor.
Colin nodded, indicating it was not a problem, and casually tore off the “False Mighty One” from his body.
Though after gaining strength, the negative effects were much smaller than what had been described.
But…
He was about to interact with others, and no matter what, it wasn’t quite appropriate to keep it on.
The people at the scene did not make them wait for too long. Ten minutes later, someone came over and quickly took them away from the place. After zigzagging through the advancing multitude of war vehicles, they arrived in front of a dilapidated moving base vehicle.
At this moment, several people who had been waiting there for a long time stood up from their seats.
They sized up Colin and his companions up and down for a while, their emotions seeming to fluctuate greatly, but after a while, one of them sitting in the middle spoke:
“We don’t have any specific names, only identifiers, but you may call me ‘Night Owl.’ Maybe that will make our conversation more convenient. Also, thank you. Your arrival lets us know that our existence is not without meaning.”
He paused briefly, not waiting for Colin to say anything, the Expedition Army officer who called himself “Night Owl” directly went to the point:
“Is your objective to recover that special time artifact?”
“Yes,” Colin nodded.
“That thing… it’s currently located at ‘Core Layer B Zone 3441 Area 301 Street,’ and furthermore, it only appears at certain times, causing ‘Reversal’ every time it materializes…
While speaking, he took out a paper document and handed it to Colin.
Looking through the contents, Colin understood the meaning of “Reversal”, that is, at certain times, all time within the starship would experience some level of chaos…
Enemies of the past could take advantage of this moment to return.
Sometimes they would leave something behind, sometimes not.
The duty of those garrisoned here was to eliminate these remnants to prevent the true return of heretics.
“Do you have anything that can negate the effects of time? If you don’t have the necessary items, then it’s impossible for us to succeed in entering that place,” Night Owl asked.
“We do,” Colin nodded.
“Alright, then according to intelligence, the best time to move is two hours from now. At that time, we will do our best to assist you in entering and recovering that thing.”
The time matched the mission briefing, so there should be no mistake. It was just that, after only confirming their identities, they offered help without asking for compensation. Colin looked at them:
“Thank you. If all goes well, I think I should be able to take some people with me as a continuation and future for this civilization…”
‘I should apply to take some people away; it’s the least I can do,’ Colin added silently to himself.
However, what he did not expect was, upon hearing his words, Night Owl shook his head.
“The war here is not over; we will not leave, and we have been heavily marked. The departure of any one person could potentially lead to catastrophic consequences…”
“We cannot become sinners.”
“If one day the bell that signifies humanity’s victory truly rings, and they still need us, we will return, rebuild houses, rebuild homes, one by one…”
“But, we haven’t heard that prophesied bell toll yet, everything is still unfinished, the war continues, and no matter how many homes are rebuilt, they will be destroyed.”
“So… we will not leave.”
“In our eyes, colleague, you are the future.”

chapters.title: Chapter 492 - 492 414 The Victory Bell in Ancient
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 492: Chapter 414 “The Victory Bell” in Ancient Prophecies._1 Chapter 492: Chapter 414 “The Victory Bell” in Ancient Prophecies._1 ‘It seems I was too narrow-minded…’
Looking at the people in front of him who were willing to continue their stand here, Colin fell silent for two seconds, unexpectedly they had refused.
However, he didn’t ponder on this…
He had noticed a key term in their words—
‘The bell in the prophecy’?
‘You just said… prophecy, right?’
Colin was unsure if this was a “machine translation” error by the company, so he spoke up, emphasizing it again.
At first, when he heard ‘victory bell,’ he thought it was just some kind of descriptive expression.
But it’s somewhat different if you add the word ‘prophecy’ in front of it…
This indicated that the so-called ‘victory bell’ might very well be something that actually exists, rather than a simple description.
‘Yes, the ‘victory bell’ mentioned in the prophecy…’
Night Owl confirmed, then looked at Colin and the few people beside him with a hint of curiosity:
‘You, you don’t know about this?’
‘Really didn’t know, seems like apart from 2044, I haven’t come into contact with any other prophecies…’
Colin shook his head, then glanced at the people next to him to see them shaking their heads as well.
‘Can you tell us what the situation is?’ he asked.
