At this moment, a few seconds after drinking the medicine, some information suddenly emerged on the parchment.
[Your rank has been detected as improved. In accordance with the “Bonfire Outstanding Talent Training Program”, your current authority will be updated…]
Upon seeing this message, Colin quickly learned about the change of authority through some sort of sensation.
“An extra three cubic meters of spatial expansion, now making it five cubic meters of extra space…”
“Personnel transfer limit increased from 30 to 50 people, can find an additional 12 F Level, 6 E Level, 2 D Level employees, oh ho, another batch of employees are going to enjoy the benefits…”
“These two seem to be the main changes in authority; the rest, like the ‘Extermination Order’, still can only be watched from the sidelines, no chance to intervene…”
“Though, who knows when a high-up will issue an ‘Extermination Order’ for me to observe and broaden my horizons…”
Curiosity filled Colin’s thoughts.
After that stunt earlier, he roughly knew about the execution method of the “Extermination Order”.
But the specific effects… still unknown to him.
Then, he shook his head, opened the group chat within the parchment, and planned to look for some new candidates for “The Descent Project”.
Nowadays, under his suggestion, the previous batch that entered “World Code-13”.
Has started to “whitewash” “The Descent Project”…
…
“Mooncake with Five Kinds of Nuts tastes so good”: It’s frustrating, I’m just a few hundred points short to buy the third F Level potion, but I haven’t seen a mission for two weeks, and applying for one gets me nowhere, so competitive…
“Life Mentor Adorable”: @Mooncake with Five Kinds of Nuts tastes so good, go apply for the “Descent Project” of “World Code-13”. I always say one thing, Brother Shunzi managed to get promoted to D Level in less than three months through the ‘Descent Project’… So for us, joining this mission and getting promoted to D Level in half a year is not a problem…
“Confused Cutie①Sob Sob⑦”: Isn’t the “Descent Project” too dangerous?
“Life Mentor Adorable”: Not to mention other things, “World Code-13” has Brother Shunzi there, what difficulty could there be? Sometimes, when you want to get promoted without putting in the effort, you need to look for issues within yourself, after all these years…
“Anonymous 007”: Wow, the recent experience with the “Descent Project” was just too comfy, working only three hours a week following Brother Shunzi nets me thousands of points. If all goes well, I’ll get promoted to D Level this week, easily surpassing my peers by a wide margin…
“Arsonist Tao Tie”: Wow, really? I want to get stronger, take me with you, where can I apply?
“Wandering Speedy Lad”: You guys are faking it, right? If it weren’t for the anonymity, I’d believe you. How strange, why have there been so many people luring others to the ‘Descent Project’ recently? Has there been an intrusion?
…
“Tsk, you guys are trying to recruit people by playing good cop, bad cop, and cross-dressing…”
Colin couldn’t help but be amused seeing many familiar faces actively posting above; he didn’t know what to say for a moment.
Without joining their discussion, he was preparing to find “Life Mentor Adorable” to discover employees with various technical knowledge and offer them a luxurious other-world travel package.
To help them realize their dream of promotion.
However, just then, a mission notification suddenly popped up.
[Event: “Use any Item Extraction Ticket on January 5th” has been issued, please check the mission bar for details.]
.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 518 - 518 423 Book of Fates Gift._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 518: Chapter 423 “Book of Fate’s” Gift._1 Chapter 518: Chapter 423 “Book of Fate’s” Gift._1 “Any time after January 5th, use an ‘Item Extraction Ticket’ with no upper limit on grade?”
Colin opened the parchment, looked at the task, but the details seemed even less than the name of the task itself.
However…
After a moment of initial confusion, he soon realized that at the appointed time, there was a high chance of drawing a Golden Artifact…
Even with the most inferior ticket, with only a one in a billion chance of drawing a Golden Artifact.
He could become that one in a billion…
That is…
‘Doing so, won’t that give off a sense of being chosen?’
Colin’s expression was peculiar, as he always felt that doing this seemed a bit like self-deception.
It might be better to just directly hand it to him.
“But, the Golden Card was initially in a semi-uncontrolled state. It has only been a week since it was recovered. Can it really be returned and repaired so quickly?”
After thinking it over, Colin felt that it might not necessarily be the Golden Card.
There was also a certain chance that it was the special moldy giant scepter he had taken, no, picked up before.
“That thing’s grade is at least Purple, with an upper limit of Orange, and even if it’s Purple, it’s a very powerful Purple Item. But as for its actual abilities, that remains to be seen.”
Colin remembered feeling a very difficult to describe sense of decay from that scepter.
That level of threat, it was only a bit less than Bone Spur…
He didn’t fuss over it too much. After all, whether it was the Golden Card or the scepter, he was guaranteed to get a powerful equipment.
“Speaking of which, ‘Bone Spur’, it seems the company has never brought up the idea of ‘Itemizing’ it… What a pity.”
Colin pursed his lips, but this time, even without any inspiration as a reminder,
He had a rough idea of why this was happening…
‘Bone Spur’ is, strictly speaking, not unclaimed property. The Church of Light, where the Saintess is, has a strong claim to it, and the Church of Light seems to be in a friendly relationship, or at least not considered a hostile force.
So the company, which cares about various regulations, most likely is unable to do that…
Unless the Saintess, like Earth’s officials, formally proposed negotiations,
To transfer the ownership of this item to the company in an official manner…
“Such a pity,” Colin sighed deeply.
If it were ‘Itemized’, guaranteeing an Orange grade, using it for ‘Item Liberation’ would probably be terrifying.
He felt that Bone Spur must have quite the history…
It’s just that he was worried that if he kept talking about it, the Saintess might ‘change her mind’ and take the item back.
So he never queried the matter with her.
“But thankfully, last time we agreed to wait until her body was done with disaster relief before starting recovery. That could take quite some time, and if there’s a chance this time, I can inquire about it… Right, the pressing matter at hand is something else.”
Colin rubbed his forehead, finding it a bit troublesome that he currently didn’t have an extraction ticket on hand…
This thing is quite hard to come by for regular employees…
Because you need high scores to have a chance of getting it.
And the scores, which aren’t greatly tied to how smoothly employees clear their tasks, hinge upon whether the items they recover are valuable enough.
Usually, the missions that Colin sees as easy to overcome by throwing a Yukionna into, without getting involved himself, represent a low chance to recover anything valuable…
Getting two or three tickets in a good year would be considered incredibly lucky.
But…
For Colin, it’s not that difficult, though he might not get them every time, doing one or two more tasks usually yields some.
“Plus, there might be mysterious forces behind the scenes, and it’s possible the day after tomorrow when I get back from ‘World Code-13’, I’ll have one waiting for me. Of course, when I go there, I’ll have to find some work to do.”
Colin massaged his forehead again.
The tasks over there are usually more routine now and don’t assign any proactively.
Even if there are any, you have to trigger them yourself…
‘Speaking of which, there’s supposed to be a shard of ‘Hunger’ over there, and some Church related to a Feast of Gluttony or something like that, but those people are as hard to find as The Rat…’
Some time ago, Colin had inquired about related information there but unfortunately hadn’t made any significant headway.
Then, gathering his thoughts, he was about to close the task.
But at that moment, another task popped up…
[Event: “At noon on January 4th, conduct a transaction inside Base No. 5…”]
“Remark”: As stated.
…
“There’s a message delivery type of task, is this… the second trade?”
Colin opened it to see, it was issued by Lady Bunny, about the second official trade between the company and the Church.
This time, the scale was much larger than the last…
A total of nearly one hundred and eighty containment subjects were being traded, including three Level 2 Containment Subjects. Oh, it’s two Level 2 Containment Subjects, as one had been lost to the fire.
Possibly, its remains might be found in one of the bonfires in ‘World Code-13’…
“Level 2 Containment Subjects, though I have the capacity to deal with them alone, they usually inhabit extremely dangerous environments, so there’s no need to take unnecessary risks, a little profit is enough…”
Finding a Level 2 Containment Subject isn’t too hard, but locating a solitary one is more challenging.
“Just right, I’ll call Xu Duojin or Old Master Wu later, to discuss the source of ‘Divine Strike,’ and I can mention this matter to them.”
Thinking of this, he took another glance at the message delivery task.
Then he couldn’t help but shake his head: “Poor company task system, manipulated and played with by senior employees at their whim…”
Nowadays, using so many backdoors, if one day the one above decides to crack down on corruption within the company, could he also be swept up in the checks?

chapters.title: Chapter 519 - 519 423 Book of Fates Gift._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 519: Chapter 423 “Book of Fate’s” Gift._2 Chapter 519: Chapter 423 “Book of Fate’s” Gift._2 As Colin learned more and more about the internal information, he increasingly felt that what the “company” and the “company executives” were thinking,
might not be the same…
Just like the “Starlight Maiden” who, as the “Container” of the “Dawn Star,” to some extent, could represent its will, wasn’t exactly in agreement with those believers…
Or, in reality, those who call you family every day might not truly consider you family. They might just want you to buy counterfeit liquor.
“It feels like there is some chaos within the company. I wonder if it’s related to those invaders.”
Colin stroked his chin as he pondered, but couldn’t figure anything out.
Shaking his head, he stopped pondering and glanced at the time, confirming it was only eight or nine in the evening before taking out his cell phone to contact Old Master Wu.
As before, there was no response.
He probably was on some high-difficulty special mission again…
“Old Master Wu only missed by a step, otherwise, if he joined the company, he would be a model worker.”
Colin muttered to himself and then started to contact “Xu Duojin.”
This person must have been sitting right next to his phone; Colin had just sent an “Are you there?” and immediately got a reply:
“Yes, is there something??”
“There is something I want to ask about, it’s not very convenient over the phone. Can you come over?” Colin’s fingers flew as he typed the message quickly.
Meanwhile, in a certain dimly-lit semi-enclosed space, Xu Duojin, dressed in a tidy suit with not a hair out of place, stood at the top of a large tree.
On a middle-aged face, one eye watched the cell phone while the other gazed ahead at the battlefield, chameleon-like, each eye focusing on its own task.
However, upon seeing the message from Colin about something inconvenient to discuss, his eyebrows suddenly raised.
A feeling of impending doom rose within him…
It felt as if he suddenly couldn’t breathe, as though submerged in water.
The sensation was quick to come and go, almost like an illusion, but he knew it was not an illusion. It was the special perception of “Fate Propeller”—
‘Hiss, what issue could make me feel as if I am about to die…’
After a moment’s hesitation, he took a glance at the situation ahead, confirmed it was in the final phase with no major problems likely, and then sent a query.
“I can come, but may I ask, what is the issue?”
“Oh, it’s not a big issue, just something about the origin of ‘Divine Strike’…”
This wasn’t a big issue?
Xu Duojin wiped the cold sweat from his forehead, instinctively not wanting to respond to the questions or go there, but given that Old Master Wu had requested him to cooperate, and considering he was capable of answering…
Well, speaking of which, Xu Duojin suddenly realized something.
Last night, Mr. Wu had suddenly and inexplicably “kindly” reminded him to remember to charge his phone today…
‘So you don’t want to answer yourself and want me to step in…’
Xu Duojin was speechless; without the other’s reminder, he might have instinctively “forgotten” to charge his phone…
Then avoid the matter—not that he could hide forever, but as long as he could.
Of course, it wasn’t that he wanted to avoid anything, but rather, it was a somewhat mystical property of “Fate Propeller.”
Too bad Old Wu… Mr. Wu had awakened him from his “dream.”
There was no escaping…
Xu Duojin sent a message to Mr. Wu, but his pretty-girl avatar was grayed out with no response, likely because he forgot to charge his phone…
Shaking his head, he then opened Colin’s chat window, sent a message saying he would arrive in an hour, and pocketed his phone.
Not in a hurry to get on the road, he looked up and gazed into the distance, toward an old village in the mountains. Deep within, he could sense several Sixth Level Personnel were dealing with an awakening Ancient Evil Sacrificial Creature…
It was presently subdued, in the final phases of enclosure.
However, to accelerate the process, more than a dozen transparent, boneless-looking invisible hands extended from Xu Duojin’s body, grabbing various threads in the air that ordinary people could not perceive.
Adjusting, manipulating, arranging.
Immediately, the evil being desperately fighting on the battleground started committing multiple errors and was ultimately subdued completely.
Under normal circumstances, he wouldn’t have been so eager to take action, since each use incurred a price—his body would corrode—so if it could be avoided, it was avoided.
But to save time and ensure surety, he took action anyway.
Now, seeing that the evil creature had been subdued, Xu Duojin withdrew his gaze, turned around, and prepared to leave for Colin’s room.
But before he could move, he sensed something and saw several of the latest combat planes flying overhead…
They appeared to be on some mission, coincidentally passing the area he was headed toward.
“…Mr. Wu’s arrangements are quite seamless.”
Xu Duojin sighed with a wry smile, knowing this was likely the other’s doing.
…
An hour later, after playing a few rounds of 1V1 with a C Level Elder Brother, Colin first heard a rumbling in the sky, as if a row of fighter jets was passing over…
Then a few minutes later, there was a knock at his door.
“The door is not locked, come in…”
No sooner had he spoken than Colin saw Xu Duojin push the door open and enter.
He pointed to the sofa nearby and waited for the well-dressed “middle-aged” man with an air of a charlatan to sit down. Without any pleasantries, Colin immediately began to inquire:
“Regarding the origin of ‘Divine Strike’, is there any special explanation?”
During their previous contact over the phone, Colin felt as if Xu Duojin was quite cautious about this topic.

chapters.title: Chapter 520 - 520 423 Book of Fates Gift._3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 520: Chapter 423 “Book of Fate’s” Gift._3 Chapter 520: Chapter 423 “Book of Fate’s” Gift._3 However, since he was able to come and answer, the problem shouldn’t be too big…
Of course, sitting opposite Colin, Xu Duojin, although he had no expression on his face, couldn’t help but inwardly gasp for breath.
Discussing such a big matter right after arriving…
After pondering for a few seconds, Xu Duojin seemed to have finished his thoughts and then spoke:
“‘Divine Strike’s origins are actually rather taboo, but such taboos aren’t particularly dangerous. The main reason is that there are some loopholes within them. If they become known, individuals at the Sixth Level and below would be in considerable danger…
“However… this isn’t much of a problem for us, and my intuition tells me that what you want to understand isn’t about this matter…
“As for other matters…”
His speech hesitated slightly, knowing that the topics to follow were rather life-threatening.
Colin might not necessarily be affected, but he might not be as safe, for he knew more.
Then, Colin saw that Xu Duojin, as if his mouth was scorched, hissed for quite a while before he hesitantly said bit by bit:
“‘Divine Strike’ and the emergence of another system, in a certain sense, are the ‘Fate Principle’s arrangement…”
“‘Book of Fate’s arrangement?” Colin asked curiously.
“That, um, yes…” Xu Duojin wanted to remind the other party not to speak so directly about this thing’s name.
But then, considering the other person’s identity, a likely former owner of the ‘Book of Fate’, a special employee with backing…
So he didn’t continue on and instead said:
“When anomalies first appeared, the sources of people’s Extraordinary Powers were very chaotic, lacking any systematic approach. At that time, becoming an ‘Extraordinary One’ to deal with other troubles was like dousing oneself in oil, setting a Flame ablaze, and then desperately chasing away other anomaly threats…
“Usually, one would inherit powers today, and within a day or two, at most a week, they’d lose control…”
“Although firearms could be effective, many anomalies had to be covered with heavy firepower, which was too costly…
“Some Level 5 Anomaly Threats, at that time, were already considered extremely difficult to resolve.”
Level 5 Anomaly Threats, roughly equivalent to Third Level weaker Containment Subjects on company standards; however, your system over here has me doing my own conversions every day…
Colin couldn’t help but internally criticize.
Then, Xu Duojin continued: “However, after the end of the second year, the situation changed,
“In an incident where someone made a desperate wish, subsequently, some powerful, but more ‘friendly’ compared to general dangers, entities appeared.
“Among them was that one…”
As Xu Duojin spoke, he suddenly stopped. Colin, puzzled, felt a sudden twitch in his eyelid. He saw that Xu Duojin’s shadow on the ground uncontrollably began to expand and pulse.
Threads on his body swayed continuously like seaweed…
“Boom.”
Colin snapped his fingers, and a ball of flame erupted, engulfing the area.
The invisible entities seemed to vanish utterly in the heat…
Xu Duojin’s shadow returned to normal; he raised a hand to wipe the cold sweat from his brow, looked at the special flame, and let out a wry smile.
“Can’t talk about it; shall we leave it unsaid?” Colin suggested.
Xu Duojin running into problems was one thing, but he was worried it might cause both of them to go up in flames.
“No matter, I was mainly reminded of something else, which doesn’t relate to this conversation.”
Xu Duojin pursed his lips, several invisible hands extended from behind him, manipulating the “black strings” on his body, as he continued:
“Anyway, that book also emerged… ‘Destiny Propeller’ appeared along with it, and then under… arrangement, two other formed paths were also ‘luckily’ found.
“Thus, the three major systems were established, and chaos came to an end…
“Then, thanks to the efforts of the previous generation, the imminent disaster was forcibly suppressed.”
Although he didn’t specify, Colin realized that the official power now could be considered a boon from the ‘Book of Fate’…
And one of the ‘Fate Propeller’s core tenets is:
“Every gift of fate is already marked with a price in darkness.”
It’s just that, at present, no one knows what that price is.

chapters.title: Chapter 521 - 521 424 Second Mothers Book of Fate._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 521: Chapter 424 Second Mother’s “Book of Fate”._1 Chapter 521: Chapter 424 Second Mother’s “Book of Fate”._1 ‘This, to put it more bluntly, is hardly an exaggeration to say that the ‘Book of Fate’ has put an end to all sorts of anomalies…’
Listening to the other party’s words, Colin felt this particularly keenly.
If it weren’t for this thing, it is very likely that the world would have drastically changed even a few years before he was born.
It might have entered an era of disaster that was no better than the “Seventh Box Garden” world, or even “World Code-13.”
After all, without extraordinary methods, many high-level anomalies would have been solved only with conventional missiles.
Even reaching the standard of a “Level 2 Containment Subject.”
Colin estimated that without resorting to originals, it would be difficult to resolve.
‘Moreover, the more a region is aware of anomalies, the more anomalies there will be… It’s simply hopeless.’
Colin felt his heart palpitate in silence.
“Hehe, are you thinking that if it hadn’t been for that… we would have been doomed?”
Xu Duojin seemed to see through Colin’s thoughts and said with a chuckle, his smile appearing to hint at something.
“Right.”
Colin didn’t deny it because, considering the situation, they really couldn’t have fought it off.
However, looking at the other person’s smile, he seemed to realize something, “It seems not quite right, the main body of the ‘Book of Fate’ is within the country and doesn’t interfere much internationally, but has there been similar development abroad during this time?”
“Not during this period, to be precise, it was almost synchronous.”
Xu Duojin recalled the information, his smile fading as he slowly furrowed his brow: “As if by agreement, various paths sprouted like bamboo shoots after a rain, and even the initial abilities bore some resemblance…
“The earliest to appear were ‘Fate Propeller,’ ‘Prophet,’ ‘Sage’ and the like. Here we have the… Book, and there are similar ones abroad, which then under some guidance obtained others.
“Just like copy and paste…”
“Does that mean… during that period, something that transcends the ‘Book of Fate’ might have taken action?”
Colin also furrowed his brow.
In his understanding, the “Book of Fate” was likely on par with “Hunger”, and at that time, it seemed not only was the “Book of Fate” present, but also similarly grand things…
Anyone capable of arranging these affairs…
The first thing that came to Colin’s mind was the Bonfire Company.
But on second thought, it seemed not quite right since at that time all the artifacts were in a ‘lost’ state.
Even now, the ownership does not belong to the company.
After all, they are currently held by the authorities, and the company seems to have no intention of reclaiming them.
“Stop thinking about it. The only one who knows everything about who’s pulling the strings behind the scenes is probably only Mr. Wu, who knows a little. Nobody else has any clue, but he obviously can’t tell you more.”
Xu Duojin waved his hand, interrupting Colin’s musings.
“Only Mr. Wu? Why?” Colin was surprised.
“I don’t know, it’s just a gut feeling…”
Xu Duojin pushed his sunglasses, “If you want to know, we’ll have to wait until either I or some Eighth Level Candidate is promoted to Ninth Level ‘Fate Propeller’ to understand the reasons…”
At his words, Colin nodded and asked no further.
From the current perspective, it was certain that someone or something had intervened back then; otherwise, everyone wouldn’t have obtained various extraordinary powers so neatly…
But exactly who had intervened remains unknown…
And whether their ultimate intention was good or bad was also unclear.
At that moment, Xu Duojin suddenly shook his head: “Actually, it’s clear to any discerning person that something took action, but even though we knew it, under the circumstances of that time, we couldn’t afford to refuse.”
He paused for a moment and added: “And whatever the person behind all that wanted to obtain, let’s not discuss that for now, but the so-called gifts from the book genuinely require a price to be paid afterward…”
“What?”
Seeing Colin’s expression, Xu Duojin gave a wry smile and then explained the matter.
Once one reaches Fourth Level, all ‘Fate Propeller’ individuals start to feel as though they owe the ‘Book of Fate’ something, and the stronger they are, the stronger this feeling gets.
So, it’s clear to some extent that, at a certain point in time,
They will need to pay the price for the ‘gifts’ of these years.
Of course, Xu Duojin didn’t know exactly what would be required as payment, but he was sure that Old Master Wu knew, yet the latter simply didn’t speak of it…
In such a case, guessing was unlikely to be possible.
Using extraordinary methods was equally impossible…
To put it bluntly, the ‘Book of Fate’ could be considered the forerunner of all such things, with scarcely anyone able to uncover its unwillingly disclosed affairs under its unwilling gaze.
At least on Earth, this is the case…
‘Actually, it should be called ‘Mother,’ not ‘Father’…’
Hearing what he said, and quite unexpectedly, Colin remembered his experience in “Passionate Paradise” and the way “Yukionna” referred to it—
Second Mommy.
At this point, Xu Duojin shook his head again:
“Honestly, I used to think it wasn’t too bad to pay a little price for power as long as there was a chance of survival, but…
“We once thought that in our generation, we had been very fortunate because, on the whole, we could ensure that extraordinary power remained within us. As long as it wasn’t used frequently, it wouldn’t go out of control—compared to the early chaos, the price was minimal…
“But your arrival has let us know what a small price means…”
As he spoke, he turned to Colin, his eyes behind the sunglasses carrying an inexplicable sense of resentment.
No, to be precise, it should be no need for a price at all!
Generally, the limits of lower-level Divine Strike range from one to three hours; exceeding that, a person’s emotions quickly get supplanted by the entity they borrow power from, becoming abstract and rigid…

chapters.title: Chapter 522 - 522 424 Second Mothers Book of Fate. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 522: Chapter 424 Second Mother’s “Book of Fate”. _2 Chapter 522: Chapter 424 Second Mother’s “Book of Fate”. _2 For example, borrowing the power of a Martial Saint would begin to gravitate towards that particular personality.
This certainly doesn’t mean getting close to the historical figure, but rather the one perceived by the public, which is not unified and can lead to increasing insanity…
However, there was once a double agent at level six, “Divine Strike,” who, after being injected with “Gene Compensation Medicine,” could even manage to sleep while operating “Divine Strike”!
He could maintain it for an entire day. Aside from mental exhaustion leading to collapse, there was no risk of becoming rigid.
Even the super-genius who used to wield “Divine Strike” could only operate it for three hours at most, not reaching this level.
In other words, what used to be their limit wasn’t even the new group’s minimum.
“Fate Propeller” double agents can now do something similar; as long as they don’t collapse from exhaustion, they can use “prediction” at will.
The key is, they also don’t feel that unease of being in debt to the “Book of Fate.”
“This isn’t even borrowing anymore; it’s seizing…” Xu Duojin couldn’t help but conclude.
Had they been able to use the “Gene Compensation Medicine” alongside earlier, they feel like there would have been far fewer problems.
‘Seizing? That’s about right, fits the company’s usual style.’
Colin nodded, making no comment on this, since although he was a member of the company, he’d never been involved in seizing other people’s things, so there was no need for him to take the blame.
Later, after having some questions answered, Colin brought up the matter of trading.
“Is it starting again?” Xu Duojin became interested at once.
The previous mission’s haul of equipment had questionable durability to say the least, but the stability was simply goddamn phenomenal.
He, along with some other senior personnel, had attempted to destroy one of the poorer pieces of equipment to induce item malfunction and breakage.
The result was that the item indeed got wrecked by their tampering.
But even when it broke, the anomaly contained within didn’t go out of control.
Instead, it dissipated along with the item’s destruction…
It was a pity indeed. Although many distinctly unique structures could be seen inside, they couldn’t learn anything valuable from them.
Putting it bluntly, they didn’t understand a thing.
Even if they wanted to copy them, they couldn’t…
“Yep, the trade time is January 4th at noon, here are the items, you guys can check the accounts,” Colin said as he passed the list over. “As for how many items we’ll ultimately obtain, that’s hard to say, it depends on what we end up securing.”
“No problem.”
Xu Duojin took the list and glanced over it.
“Four Level 2 Containment Subjects, nine Third Level Containment Subjects, and… a total of one hundred and ninety-one?”
The official standard for Level 2 Containment Subjects consisted of very weak low-level items; the higher the level, the higher the danger. However, since they were trading with the company, they naturally used the company’s standards, so Xu Duojin was unlikely to make a mistake.
Estimating it, he roughly understood the other party’s needs…
“That’s correct.”
Colin nodded without changing his expression.
Although there were some discrepancies between the listed numbers and the actual items, during the trade and transportation, it’s possible that there could be some wear and tear, and they might be short a piece or two.
So it was understandable to report a higher count.
“No problem.”
Xu Duojin nodded. While his instincts told him there might be a slight issue with the list…
It was that same instinct telling him that being blissfully ignorant was sometimes a part of life.
Knowing too much wasn’t necessarily a good thing…
He carefully filed the list away in his suit’s inner pocket, then, with a smile on his face, tried to broach a new topic: “Speaking of which, is there any possibility of discussing technology related to item creation?”
Had he set his sights on the company’s item creation?
Colin shook his head: “In this regard, there’s almost no possibility…”
Even if the company didn’t mind about such matters, giving the actual technology would be challenging for these people to replicate, since the company’s item creation tied into some mysterious and specific agreements.
However, considering the company’s understanding of anomalies, providing some conceptual advice might be feasible.
Going any further, however, would be difficult.
Xu Duojin wasn’t surprised by his response; the gap between them was immense, and the more he understood, the more he felt it.
The Bonfire Company, though called a company, could just as well be considered a type of advanced civilization.
“By the way, what’s the situation now with the followers of ‘Dawn Star’?” Colin changed the subject.
He had the officials watch these people long ago, even hinting at them to spread their message as widely as possible.
Now, several days later, he was curious about the developments.
“It seems they’re saying… a powerful entity might return through a container that arrived not long ago. The rumor has gone wild outside…”
Xu Duojin’s expression was odd when mentioning this because the container in question had “descended” and escaped within their territory.
Some within the Alliance criticized their mishandling of the situation…
But Xu Duojin, who knew more about the incident, was well aware that it was this man in front of him who had resolved it.
Not a single Heretic from the scene got away; all were killed.
Yet within a few days, there were rumors that the escape was successful and that the summoning of some Great Will to Earth was imminent…
Considering what Colin had instructed before…
Even if Xu Duojin thought with his feet, he could sense that the guy in front of him likely played a “not so honorable” role in the whole affair, and did it convincingly.
Otherwise, the specialized Heretic-fighting Churches would have noticed.
“Lately, not just us but every global official organization has received quite a lot of reports of evil forces. Does that have much to do with you, um, there’s no need to be too explicit…”

chapters.title: Chapter 523 - 523 424 Second Mothers Book of Fate. _3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 523: Chapter 424: Second Mother’s “Book of Fate”. _3 Chapter 523: Chapter 424: Second Mother’s “Book of Fate”. _3 Xu Duojin asked a question carefully and ended with a reminder.
This matter has attracted too much attention from various powers, and if there truly is any scheming involved, then it must not be spoken of carelessly.
Otherwise, it might be a bit like the legend of talking behind someone’s back and causing them to sneeze…
In reality, it’s a coincidence.
But in the extraordinary world within, there definitely exists the possibility that some especially sensitive beings could sense something.
The probability is not high, but it’s not nonexistent.
Understanding his gaze, Colin said knowingly, “There’s a bit of a connection, I have a friend who plans to take this opportunity to clean up some trash, of course, I suggest you also send some strong enough people to help.”
While speaking, he made a “7” hand gesture, hinting that the rank should not be lower than this.
Although he didn’t understand how Colin got mixed up with those vile forces,
Xu Duojin didn’t dwell on it: “I understand, as for the location…”
“Let them search slowly, I reckon with their abilities, it won’t be very difficult to find. Sometimes, allowing them to struggle and uncover the information themselves makes it easier for them to believe.”
“Of course, if they really can’t find it, then I’ll take the initiative to reveal the location.”
Listening to Colin’s plan, Xu Duojin figured that this time it might really give those heretics a harsh blow.
To completely eliminate them is highly unlikely, but causing significant harm is inevitable.
With this in mind, he couldn’t help but sigh, the fact was that many heretics are remnants from the earliest days of chaos, when in the face of anomalies, all methods were desperately conceived…
But once the major extraordinary paths were established, those excessively bloody powers, of course, should have been abolished.
Unfortunately, it was a little late by then.
Many people were misled and could no longer turn back, forced to defect and become lingering toxins—
The key issue with these toxins is that they jeopardized the hard-earned stability of the world while believing they were saving it.
It’s very… abstract.
…
Meanwhile, as Colin and the others were engaged in their “encrypted call,” over a certain stretch of the ocean, inside an unimaginably large and ancient wooden ghost ship, a group of Heretic Followers were also plotting in secret.
“We’ve almost found the headquarters of that group of masochists, this time, we must not let them succeed…”
An authoritative old man dressed in a naval uniform said, his gaze sweeping over the round table where people wearing various garments were seated along the edge.
These were members of the “Deep Blue Guardians” mingled among humanity.
Although they performed rituals that involved sacrificing people to the entities beneath the Deep Sea to gain power; although they used human brain wetware to create special mystical engines; and although a large number of people died or were injured because of their actions…
They knew they were the good guys.
All was but a necessary sacrifice.
“The existence of the stars above threatens to destroy our habitats, only with the coming of The Deep Sea Era, the arrival of the Great Will, will our civilization continue. Even though today, a small portion of people might view us differently, I believe, in the future, they will understand…”
“But, before that, we must do everything we can to protect this place.”
The old man repeated the “lines” he had said countless times before.
After nearly ten minutes, he finally turned his sharp gaze to one member who had received the “Deep Sea’s” blessing:
“But you don’t need to worry, ‘Dawn Star’s’ sanctuary will soon be found…”
“By then, ‘Wavebreaker’, you’ll infiltrate the ‘Dawn Star’ sanctuary amidst the chaos and sabotage their God Descent ritual, killing their God Descend Vessel!”
“Ah? Me?”
The person being looked at widened his eyes and pointed at himself.
…

chapters.title: Chapter 524 - 524 425 Bonfire Temple_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 524: Chapter 425 “Bonfire Temple”!_1 Chapter 524: Chapter 425 “Bonfire Temple”!_1 At two o’clock in the middle of the night, after having sent Xu Duojin away following the discussion, Colin lay back on the sofa.
After the conversation, Colin had a more detailed understanding of the various human heretics and couldn’t help but marvel at the diversity and number of these heretics; there were indeed many.
There were no less than a hundred that needed close attention.
Each one of them, if not carefully monitored, could bring a big “surprise” to humanity.
“It’s not easy for the officials to deal with anomalies while keeping them in check, but there is also serious internal strife among these heretic organizations. They report each other, use each other, and engage in cutthroat competition.”
Colin muttered to himself, thankful that these guys were not united, or they might have been able to accomplish some significant feat.
And the reason for their lack of unity was complex, but the fundamental reason was that the entities they worshipped behind the scenes, did not trust one another…
“Many higher beings seem to be trapped because of ‘Bonfire Company,’ worried that once the others escape, they would immediately block the path and monopolize the benefits…”
Touching his chin, Colin considered this to probably be one of the main reasons.
Besides, there might be something like the Book of Fate interfering with them.
“Feels like a shit-stirrer…”
Colin shook his head, contemplated for a while longer, then took out a parchment.
He opened the mission related to “Dawn Star.”
Then, his consciousness sank into it, his eyes narrowing slightly…
The next second, above the central altar in the “City at the Lake’s Bottom,” an overly urbanized, high-literacy independent spatial area, strands of starlight cascaded down…
Colin observed the situation here through these strands of starlight.
In the time that followed, at his request, the entirety of the “City at the Lake’s Bottom,” both inside and out, was filled with var54ious traps.
Should people from the outside break through and come to prevent his “God Descent,” they would receive a big surprise.
“Great Envoy…” a priest who sensed Colin’s arrival fell to his knees in submission.
However, before they could finish speaking, Colin remotely controlled this avatar made of starlight to inquire about the current situation.
“Everything is within Your foresight, Great Envoy. If those despicable sinners have normal brains, they should discover this place within this week or the next. Then, all invaders would become the sacrificial offerings for Your return…”
The priest reported all the recent developments in detail.
Although the “City at the Lake’s Bottom,” their ultimate stronghold, would be exposed to countless eyes when that day came,
By then, there wouldn’t be anything to fear anymore.
The magnificent “Dawn Star” would descend with Its myriad starlight blessings upon this place, providing every believer who worshipped It with the blessings It brings…
And the endless pleasure It imparts.
Thinking of this, he couldn’t help but tremble with excitement.
‘I always feel like this guy is thinking about something not very classy.’
A thought flashed through Colin’s mind as he saw the other party looking at him expectantly, seemingly praying for some “reward.”
But after a shiver ran down his spine, he chose to disperse the avatar.
After his consciousness withdrew, Colin looked at the mission and pondered over the feeling he had just experienced…
While wielding this power, he once again felt the presence of the “Starlight Maiden,” who seemed still caught in a fog, her body torn asunder, trembling as it hung on a door, maintaining the same posture as when he last saw her.
“Still being used as a portal. This thing seems indeed to have a special teleportation function.”
Colin remembered that finding the starship before was thanks to it.
It felt… like a great material for making props.
After ensuring that there were no problems here, he routinely opened the information about the “Pseudo-Humans.”
He found that, as always, these beings were “slacking off…”
The “God Descent” event, which drew the attention of all evil powers on Earth, caused not even a ripple here.
All movements seemed unrelated to them.
They were still discussing how to avoid “cops,” imitating humans, and the like.
“Are these guys really good anomalies?”
Colin said skeptically, as all the things he currently encountered, regardless of the surface appearance, had some sort of agenda or intended to make a big move…
And here they were discussing where to play, travel, eat…
In the group, the words he saw most often were food names like snail rice noodles, lychee roast goose, sweet and sour pork, big plate chicken, and they even argued for days and nights over more than a thousand messages about whether to add sugar to fried tomatoes and scrambled eggs for flavor enhancement and whether to eat sweet or savory tofu pudding.
And they were still arguing…
Is this even an anomaly?
What genuine anomaly discusses these things?
As Colin looked through the dull chat records, he wondered if they concealed some kind of riddle.
Unfortunately, it seemed not…
At least, after having the Little Maid scan and check multiple times, he was confident there probably wasn’t a problem.
“They genuinely argued over these trivial matters for so long.”
Colin shook his head, glanced twice more at the new messages, and felt they really had too much free time.
“But honestly, who eats salty tofu pudding? Eating five-nut mooncakes makes more sense than that thing…”
Muttering to himself, Colin closed the app and glanced at the current time.
It’s not even three o’clock in the morning…
Quite early.
He took out his phone and called Qin Chuan, instructing him to prepare various food supplies.
This time, increase the food allocation, reduce the medical supplies, and then, expand the items to 4.5 cubic meters.

chapters.title: Chapter 525 - 525 425 Bonfire Temple_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 525: Chapter 425 “Bonfire Temple”!_2 Chapter 525: Chapter 425 “Bonfire Temple”!_2 “The large-caliber bullets from before haven’t been used up yet… But there’s no need for such things in ‘World Code-13’…”
Colin piled all the ammunition in the living room to make space for supplies.
If someone were to come check this sight, they’d probably be scared enough to call the police on the spot…
But, with Xu Duojin’s “arrangements.”
The chances of that happening were extremely slim…
After roughly finishing these tasks, Colin didn’t idle but instead took a look at the parchment.
He was going to continue to search for candidates for the “interdimensional gift package,” but he saw a message from “Arsonist Tao Tie” and company…
They were all asking when he could make a trip to “World Code-4.”
“Can’t go, I have to attend tutoring classes.”
Colin skimmed their messages with a glance.
They had developed a certain fear of “World Code-4,” not because of some strange tasks there, but because of that “one thousand jin.”
The other party kept asking when he’d come; although she wasn’t tired of asking, the others listening were almost stressed out.
Even when they returned home and opened the refrigerator or cracked an egg, it seemed as though a head would pop out and ask Sir Bonfire when he would come…
It was driving them crazy.
“This… after so long, the feelings haven’t faded yet?”
Colin felt inexplicably guilty; he hadn’t expected that doing just that little bit would leave such a lasting impression on the other party.
However, no matter what, going there was definitely out of the question.
He simply couldn’t miss his weekly “extra lessons” with the Saintess…
After a series of exchanges, Colin felt like he was about to steal Learn her skill similar to “Flash.”
It would probably happen this week or the next…
So, there was definitely no way he could go to “World Code-4.”
But as a compromise, maybe he would upgrade the Bonfire of World No. 13, and there might be a chance for interworld communication.
“Other places’ Bonfires have never had the ability to communicate like this, does it mean ‘World Code-4’ or ‘World Code-13’ are actually not very far from each other?”
Colin thought for a moment but eventually shook his head. To the company, it might not be far.
But if he foolishly tried to breach the atmosphere, to cross the distance on his own, he probably couldn’t reach the destination even if he flew until his death.
Putting away his lingering guilt and conscience, Colin thought for a moment, stood up, and returned to his bed, ready to enter his “office” and inform the trio about something.
Consciousness sank, as if passing through something…
Before long, when Colin opened his eyes again, he saw his extravagantly decorated “office.”
A terrifyingly huge fireball hung high above at an unknown height, like a heart, spewing out a massive amount of flames, illuminating the entire world with its light.
Below the fireball, everywhere was shrouded in smoke.
Except for the hall beneath Colin’s feet, filled with the traces of war and looking exceptionally ruined.
As his authority increased, Colin felt the “background” here seemed to be becoming more realistic.
It felt like…
One day when looking up, the gigantic fireball above might become real.
Taking a deep breath and putting away the strange thoughts, Colin walked briskly to the long table in the hall, sat down on a high-backed chair he commonly used, and was about to summon someone when he noticed the previously vague 29 points of light had become bright.
“Can I pull them over now?”
Colin was startled, soon realizing this point.
And whether by coincidence or not, through the lights, he could tell that they were currently free from assignments.
“Should I pull these guys over here?”
Colin sat in the high-backed chair, pondered for a moment, and then tapped his hand on the table.
“Dong dong.”
Amidst the crisp sound,
All the points of light scattered, each finding a seat at the table, then stretched, expanded, and gradually coalesced into a series of blurred figures.
…
At the same time,
In a small room, “Life Mentor Adorable,” who had just conned a few coworkers into applying for “The Descent Project,” was lying on a couch, eyes closed, ready to nap.
But at that moment, he abruptly felt a strong sense of weightlessness.
His body jerked, and he immediately opened his eyes.
Then…
“Hiss, where is this?”
“Life Mentor Adorable” gasped, seeing that he had somehow appeared in a mysterious and eerie hall, sitting at a long table in the center of it.
Bright and warm light cascaded down from above…
He subconsciously raised his head and saw, as if on the infinitely high ceiling above, there was an immensely huge fireball. It seemed like a star, yet very active, continuously spewing flames that seemed to set the entire dome ablaze…
Almost simultaneously, he wanted to activate his “Tyrant Body·Limited Edition” Talent, as well as the “High-Speed Movement”.
However, he found that everything inside him was suppressed by an unknown rule…
An intangible intuition told him that if he wanted to move, he had to submit an application and obtain an approval response.
“Damn, my mom!”
“Mama Mia!”
“What is this place?!”
“…”
A string of expletives came from nearby, making the place noisy.
Only then did he notice that besides himself, there were quite a few figures who had come here. These figures were shrouded in a very thin layer of smoke and their specific appearances were unclear.
However, from the IDs above their heads, Kě’ài duō still recognized that these were all colleagues from the company.
And they were all…
“World Code-13” members of “The Descent Project”!
“Thump thump.”
A knocking sound came from not too far away.
Although the sound was not loud, it clearly entered everyone’s ears, calming the place down.
They almost simultaneously and uniformly turned toward the sound and saw, sitting at the main seat of a long table, a figure with flames burning all over his body, silently staring at them.
Having recognized the familiar presence with just one glance, they knew who it was.
Brother Shunzi.
Some were just about to ask something when they suddenly saw three people stand up, facing the other direction of the ancient and majestic hall, which seemed like a temple, to pay their respect.
Following their gaze, everyone slowly raised their heads and saw, at the end of a sequence of steps behind the hall, a huge stone chair upon which sat an awe-inspiring figure shrouded in smoke, emanating a mysterious presence.
From this angle, the terrifying fireball on the dome looked just like a halo behind its head.
The aura emanating from it made everyone feel a chilling terror, instinctively averting their eyes and not daring to look directly.
“Whoosh.”
He also quickly stood up to express his respect.
After he stood up, the other colleagues, although unsure of the circumstances, belatedly stood up and paid homage to that unknown presence.
‘Paying respect to myself feels a bit strange, but it seems the effect of intimidation has been achieved.’
Colin mumbled to himself, then with a thought, a large amount of smoke flowed over the street, shrouding the towering figure on the steps from view.
It was at the moment when that being disappeared that the group of three sat back down.
“Is it over?”
The rest, not knowing what to do, sat down following the lead of the trio.
With the watchful presence gone, they felt a certain ease in their hearts, and immediately after, they couldn’t help but speculate about the identity of the mysterious figure…
Without a doubt, aside from possessing great power, they could also feel that the authority of the figure was above theirs.
This…
Could this be the elusive high-level executive of “Bonfire Company” about whom there were legends?
So far, the only high-level executive from the company that they had contact with was that C Level Personnel who was privately called the “Iron Fist Instructor.”
But that person had long since passed away, leaving behind only a few tasks.
Unlike this one, who was very much alive!
In thought, everyone couldn’t help but turn their gaze to the man sitting at the main seat of the long table.
Even though he hadn’t spoken yet, they all realized.
“Brother Shunzi surely has someone backing him…”
Although they had speculated about this before, the confirmation still shocked them.
Indeed, how could the “Descent Project” be completed without someone’s support? How could they breach the “Out-of-Control Copy”?
Everything pointed to the fact that Brother Shunzi’s background was not simple!
“Cough cough…”
Feeling the stares, Colin couldn’t help but cough twice.
He always felt that these people seemed to have misunderstood something.
.
.
.
ps: Revision made after updating.

chapters.title: Chapter 526 - 526 426 Bonfire Companys Recruitment
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 526: Chapter 426 “Bonfire Company’s” Recruitment Standards. _1 Chapter 526: Chapter 426 “Bonfire Company’s” Recruitment Standards. _1 “This place is just for conversation and exchange; there’s no need to be nervous.”
Colin said, easing the tension among the crowd.
Hearing his words, people breathed a sigh of relief, though they were still somewhat ill at ease.
At that moment, another D Level employee besides Lifecoach Kawaii-many spoke up, “What are we discussing here this time?”
“Basically, it’s about the preparation for the project arriving tomorrow, and then confirming if there are any personnel changes; of course, if time permits, we can touch on some other topics,” Colin replied succinctly.
Without waiting for the others to ask, he continued, “If everything goes as planned, we will have a similar meeting before every ‘arrival project’ to exchange information.”
After all, the employee death rate at the company is not high, but not low either.
You never know which of those present might suddenly disappear while on a task…
It’s better to confirm things with a meeting beforehand.
Compared to the others who were still somewhat restrained, the trio was not as concerned; they had been through many meetings already.
“Brother… Boss, do we have any new recruits this week?” Li Ming asked instinctively.
They were now F Level, and their parchment had been integrated into the large “System,” and in the internal forum, they had a very clear understanding of their boss’s current status.
Knowing that his combat power was definitely the best within the company…
All sorts of tasks that regular employees couldn’t handle, he had completed them all.
Last time, they thought that the other D Level employees were more or less at the boss’s level, but once they got inside, they realized that all the D Level personnel combined were not necessarily a match for the boss.
He was the only one who could make “nuclear bombs” with his bare hands in a short period of time.
At this moment, after he made the inquiry, everyone’s attention turned towards them.
Whether new recruits had arrived was quite important to them.
“Yes,” Colin nodded.
“Oh okay then, so next week have we got… Huh? Wait, there really are new recruits?” Li Ming was already prepared for a negative response, since it had always been like that in the past, and almost subconsciously assumed there were none.
But he was halfway through speaking when he realized there were!
“About twenty or so, I’d say. It depends on the situation. After all, it’s voluntary, and I can’t really force anyone.”
“Twenty people, huh? Yeah, that’s not bad,” they nodded.
Having some is better than none…
It was not just the three of them; all the others exchanged glances, a strange smile flickering at the corners of their mouths.
Of course, they weren’t thinking about how to torment the newcomers.
They really needed the manpower…
While they were over there, they didn’t have to worry about danger too much, thanks to Brother Shunzi’s presence.
But obviously, there is no such thing as a free lunch in this world.
Everything has a cost.
When there was no danger, Brother Shunzi was the danger!
They had experienced firsthand what it meant for even the Extraordinary Ones to be worked to death.
“Life Mentor Adorable” was moving bricks at night, while white-haired individuals operated the “Body of Tyranny” to till the fields—the ground was so hard there that without being one of the Extraordinary Ones, you’d have to resort to large specialized machinery.
Unfortunately, they obviously didn’t have such things there.
So they had to rely on the Extraordinary Ones, along with all sorts of explosive packs.
After seven consecutive days,
even the D Level Personnel could hardly bear it.
Those with the “Body of Tyranny” Talent felt an inexplicable threat of death in the latter days and initially didn’t know what was going on.
Late, they realized that it was a signal that their bodies couldn’t hold up anymore.
So, one more person meant one more beast, no, one more laborer to share the joy of work.
Seeing everyone’s expressions, Colin shook his head privately.
The number of refugees over there was increasing at an incredibly fast rate.
Even if all twenty people showed up, the tasks they needed to do probably wouldn’t decrease, but they definitely wouldn’t be any less.
‘Too bad I don’t have the authority to recruit directly; otherwise, I’d use my authority to bring in a thousand people and solve most of the problems at once,’ Colin lamented.
Now, after the official research on the company had begun, they roughly knew the company’s recruitment standards.
It was said to be random recruitment, and it was indeed random…
But it wasn’t entirely random.
Colin initially thought the company preferred to recruit people who were on the brink of death because such people might be more willing to compromise, but after official systematic research and a huge amount of samples, it was discovered…
That approach was wrong.
The company actually preferred those who were “optimistic” and “unyielding,” and who held to some line of good moral standards.
Simply put, if a person in severe pain could still laugh, find joy in suffering, know they were headed toward inevitable death, yet refuse to give up easily, and at the core of their being wasn’t entirely bad, that person could be considered a target for recruitment.
In addition, such people are not rare…
But the reason why those close to death are recruited more is that these individuals have usually “proven” themselves in the real battle against their illness and pain.
That’s why they are sought after for recruitment.
And the diseases they carry, in the eyes of the company, fall into the category of “nice to have but not necessary.”
A few shots of “Gene Compensation Medicine” would cure the majority completely…
Beyond that, abilities, insight, and so on are also considered by the company, but usually are not the absolute criteria.
Or to put it another way, most of the time, these things are not essential, as the company has the capacity to artificially cram all sorts of knowledge into their brains.

chapters.title: Chapter 527 - 527 426 Bonfire Companys Recruitment
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 527: Chapter 426 “Bonfire Company’s” Recruitment Standards. _2 Chapter 527: Chapter 426 “Bonfire Company’s” Recruitment Standards. _2 ‘It seems that for those who are severely disabled on their first mission, they are typically assigned tasks similar to The Descent but not exactly that, like obtaining a random body at a certain location on Earth…’
Thoughts flickered through Colin’s mind.
Though these aren’t necessarily one hundred percent accurate…
They likely come close to the truth, at least in one aspect: Company employees rarely suffer emotional breakdowns.
In any case, Colin himself had hardly ever witnessed such an event.
Furthermore, due to a pervasive “never give up” attitude among the staff, their favorite thing to do was to slack off overtly while secretly being a hard worker.
Meanwhile, after initially broaching the topic, those present also began to exchange information.
At this moment, someone spoke up:
“By the way, speaking of which, has anyone here joined the official forces?”
Hearing this, Colin turned to glance at him, pondered for a moment, and could confirm that the speaker was not an official member.
“Yes, I have. Why do you ask?” An employee at the “double” F Level from Bonfire Company spoke up.
Caught by surprise at his response, some people paused, then began regarding him with a hint of wariness.
“Just wondering how the treatment is once you join the official forces…”
As he spoke, this wild Employee Level E glanced at Colin, then looked away, continuing, “I’ve seen all sorts of claims and I don’t fully believe them, but here, with witnesses, I’m curious to learn more…”
“Actually, it’s not much, just some travel restrictions, the occasional cooperation with interrogations and blood tests. The perks are, your tasks will have a specialized team to assist, they give you all sorts of life-saving items, and then the pay really is high, all sorts of subsidies, basically never short on money…”
“Of course, this is all within reason; you can definitely get a few tens to hundreds of thousands a year. If that’s not enough, you can exchange Points for money at a higher rate than within the company—several times higher.”
“As for status, currently, anyone who sees you will show respect; you’ll often see those people you never could reach before come to offer their condolences…”
“Simply put, by joining the official forces, even as the lowest F-Level Company employee, you essentially transcend your original class.”
“…”
Hearing this, the rest of the Bonfire Company staff couldn’t help but be somewhat tempted.
After encountering the supernatural, they weren’t too concerned about class distinctions.
But they were quite drawn to the idea of receiving assistance from various official powers, knowing from some who had interacted with official forces before how vast and mysterious their scale is, full of capable individuals.
If they could get the protection of these forces, their mortality rates would significantly decrease.
And there was another point…
The company, for some reason, currently showed particular favoritism towards employees involved with the officials.
As a result, other employees were left with no missions to take on.
If they really couldn’t compete with these “Emperors of Labor”… they had no choice but to join in.
Otherwise, given a choice, most wouldn’t opt to take on Brother Shunzi’s “The Descent Project” with its potentially limitless dangers.
At this point, a D Level Personnel, other than Kě’ài duō, spoke up, throwing cold water on everyone’s enthusiasm:
“Aren’t you worried about exposing your location and getting eliminated by those robots?”But before he could continue, “Life Mentor Adorable” took the initiative to speak:
“Actually, about those internal chat bots, reporting someone else’s information to them doesn’t really do anything; it only matters if you personally, in your own belief, reveal your location.
“Otherwise, even if you accidentally let slip your own position, at most it might attract other people, not those ‘robots.’
“So you don’t have to worry too much.”
“What if the other person reports their location and tries to drag you into it?” the D Level Personnel continued to inquire.
“Just close your eyes and don’t listen,” replied Kě’ài duō. “To my knowledge, as long as you don’t interact with them, nothing will happen to you. Based on this, they can’t ambush you using this method because if you don’t know, you won’t be harmed the entire time. There was an experiment like this before…”
‘Huh… this Kě’ài duō, even if not an official, must have quite a few connections at home,’ Colin couldn’t help but click his tongue inwardly.
He could pretty much confirm that the experiment mentioned was the recent incident orchestrated by the “Global Supernatural Alliance.”
Many had died then, including several high-ranking individuals.
Yet, surprisingly, many ordinary people had managed to survive.
This information was relatively secret, and the fact that “Life Mentor Adorable” knew of it suggested he probably held no low status in the real world.
At this moment, Colin felt someone’s gaze on him. Looking up, it was the other D Level Personnel.
Obviously, he was uncertain about Kě’ài duō’s words, seeking some kind of confirmation from Colin…
“It’s roughly correct.”
Colin made no habit of being cryptic and nodded straightforwardly.
“In that case, there shouldn’t be any major problems,” the D Level Personnel thought, probably harboring certain ideas.
Then, Li Ming, who was sitting to one side, couldn’t help but sigh, “I just wonder when someone will solve this thing. Every time I ask something up there, they always follow up with mentions of me, it seemed silly at first, but it’s somewhat unsettling after a while.”
“You don’t have to think too much about that,” Colin said offhandedly.

chapters.title: Chapter 528 - 528 426 Recruitment Standards of Bonfire
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 528: Chapter 426 Recruitment Standards of “Bonfire Company”_3 Chapter 528: Chapter 426 Recruitment Standards of “Bonfire Company”_3 “Why?” someone asked, instinctively curious.
“How would I know why… Every time Colin was about to reach the limit on the parchment, he felt a vague sense of some terrifying gaze,”
and the owner of that gaze had a not insignificant probability of being related to the “robot.”
So, his intuition told him that the thing must be extremely troublesome, and unless someone truly high-level beyond C Level got involved, it probably couldn’t be resolved.
As for why it wasn’t dealt with, he guessed it had something to do with the unusual situation among the higher-ups…
‘Although Lady Bunny seems to have not a low level of authority, I always feel like she’s avoiding something. Even meeting with me is a hassle. She simply can’t spare the effort to deal with those things,’ Colin couldn’t help but think.
However, at this moment, “Life Mentor Adorable” from the side said, “Actually, I think what Brother Shunzi meant was, there’s no need to meddle with it…”
Huh? Colin was startled, this wasn’t what he meant.
But seeing the look in Kě’ài duō’s eyes, he suddenly thought of something and didn’t speak up; he just nodded to indicate for them to continue.
The one who was the first to reveal the “robot” to the public.
Maybe he really knew something.
“I have a feeling that there’s a very good chance this guy is intentionally contained there. After all, from what we can tell so far, it’s obviously a very powerful anomalous being and is clearly hostile to us.”
“But, in such a situation, it wants to move against us but has so many restrictions.”
“I’m afraid it’s not that it doesn’t want to, but it can’t.”
“I guess that’s why Brother Shunzi said not to think too much on it,” “Life Mentor Adorable” slowly voiced his speculation.
Intentionally contained there? Colin paused, pondered a bit, and felt it was indeed possible.
It was just that, upon hearing the other’s last statement, his expression post-nitroglycerin couldn’t help but be a bit odd—
So that’s what he was thinking?
‘If I say now that I also don’t know, would that somehow spoil the mood?’ he wondered internally.
Colin equivocated with a comment, “Not a bad idea.”
Not confirming, nor denying.
What the other person imagined from this was anyone’s guess.
In that moment, Colin inexplicably understood why some leaders, after hearing opinions, do not express their views publicly; chances are, they’re not sure what to think and don’t want to lose face.
The others, according to their understanding, all showed an expression of sudden enlightenment.
They instantly understood why no one had dealt with this issue.
Thankfully, the topic didn’t go too deep into the “asking any more would be impolite” territory.
Colin figured that in all likelihood, he wouldn’t be encountering this thing so soon anyway.
No need to take it too much to heart…
Next, the discussion turned to matters of resources. This time, Colin had them prepare as much food as possible, etc., and generally other weapons that were not items were not needed.
After all, with him there, that was the biggest security guarantee—
That is, of course, if he couldn’t handle it.
The “Saintess” was just there, one of the peak forces of “World Code-13,” and according to Colin’s estimation, her real body’s strength, feared to be much stronger than many at C Level.
Having such a woman behind him, backing him up, gave him a lot of extra confidence.
The only downside was that this “confidence” tended to drain… his wallet.
‘I’ve heard that besides the Saintess, there are also other strong ones, like The Kingdom of Knights’ King. It seems the overall strength of “World Code-13” is quite impressive…’
‘But it also seems normal, as that Rosen guy relocated personnel from other ‘World Codes’ here back in the day.’
‘With so many legacies, it’s probably hard to be weak even if you wanted to.’
As these thoughts flashed through his mind, Colin interacted with the group for a while and then dismissed the meeting.
He opened his eyes and glanced at the time.
In a few hours, he’d enter “World Code-13.”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 529 - 529 427 Bisect Saintess Shana._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 529: Chapter 427: Bisect “Saintess” Shana._1 Chapter 529: Chapter 427: Bisect “Saintess” Shana._1 “Nightmare Lantern,” within the hazy dreamscape.
“Time, halt!”
Whirr!
An invisible engine noise roared beside his ears, flames surged over Colin’s body as he watched ahead with a grave expression.
Six or seven incandescent light shadows, unable to move within the frozen time.
The reason he sensed six or seven, rather than an exact number, was that these clones from the “Light Chaser” were some visible, and some invisible.
However, Colin hesitated not, his revolver firing ceaselessly.
One shot each, he shattered all the light shadows, including the invisible one…
Yet, the dreamscape did not dissolve.
“It seems I haven’t successfully pinned down the main body, tough fight,” Colin sighed, and at that moment, he heard a ticking countdown nearby.
When the stasis of time ended, he saw, outside the range of the effect, a large group of Saintesses quietly observing him, simply impossible to kill.
This sight made Colin’s scalp tingle slightly.
Not long before, upon entering “World Code-13” and quickly settling some planned events, he met the “Light Chaser” whose true identity was the “Church of Light” Saintess Shana, already waiting in the small chapel.
Then, the tense battle training started once again.
The Saintess, as always, tested him first, examining his current combat situation.
Only then would she train him against various abnormalities—it was unclear where she got so many anomalies from, but to this day, Colin continued to encounter an ever-enriching variety without repeating any.
“Not bad, the intensity of your power is higher than before,” a disembodied voice lingered by his ear.
It seemed to acknowledge the improvements he had made over time.
Definitely, it was the kind of sound produced by the vibration of air…
Not some kind of mental message transmission.
However, Colin clearly didn’t see any of the thirty-odd blurry light shadows before him move their lips to speak.
“Are they all fake?” Colin couldn’t help but grumble to himself. One of the Saintess’s abilities was a multitude of light shadow clones, indistinguishable between real and fake.
You could deliver a blow to decapitate her, and only a regular clone would die…
But when she punches you, it’s a solid, real punch.
Even now, Colin still found it extremely difficult to discern which were real and which were fake.
“Heh.”
Colin took a deep breath; flames on his body spread like a carpet being unfurled, or like waves rising due to the wind, surging outwards in an attempt to entrap all the light shadows.
At this moment, he saw the clones around him starting to “flash.”
With each “flash,” they would move to another location in an incomprehensible manner…
‘This is it.’
Colin narrowed his eyes; the skill he wanted to covertly learn was “Flash.”
After he had mentioned it to the Saintess, she had not concealed her technique, demonstrating this ability to him in subsequent battles…
Letting him begin to deepen his understanding of this trick.
Focusing on it…
Colin suddenly felt an itch in his “Skill Grid,” a new skill was emerging!
A sensation appeared, and information surfaced in his mind.
[…Do you wish to spend One Thousand Points to learn it?]
“Yes.”
Without much thought, Colin made his decision promptly; then, a sudden surge sapped his mental energy.
[You have comprehended the skill “Flame Leap.”]
[“Flame Leap”: Allows you to “leap” to any flame point within a hundred-meter radius, up to seven consecutive times per hour. Each use requires one hour to recover.]
‘Finally, I have a teleportation ability too!’
‘It feels similar to Big C Teacher’s teleportation, doesn’t it?’
‘Too bad it’s not the “Holy Woman’s” unconditional teleportation, as it requires fire as a prerequisite, slightly lacking, yes, but still pretty good.’
Colin’s thoughts raced within.
Actually, many in the company had the “Flash” skill, but he did not, forcing him to rely solely on physical charges, sometimes feeling like he was the only “mythical beast” that couldn’t fly.
Just then, a faint sense of crisis suddenly rose…
“It seems like you might have learned something,” the ethereal androgynous voice sounded near his ear.
The Saintess, pausing momentously for him to “comprehend,” once again set into motion.
The next instant, Colin’s pupils constricted as he saw a light shadow, like a haunting specter, suddenly appearing before him.
A blindingly intense light burst forth from the shadow in an instant.
Even with his eyes closed, he felt the glaring light piercing through his eyelids, causing his eyes to ache.
All over his skin, areas directly hit by the light passed a severe burning sensation.
Colin felt as if he had been thrown into an oven.
He reached out, drawing in a great amount of flames back to his body for protection, which made things much more bearable.
It was then that the subtle sense of crisis suddenly became particularly intense.
Yet, due to a certain trait, even though there might be “death replay” in his mind, he had no energy to check it.
In a brief moment, he had no time to ponder, drawing his revolver and firing blindly behind him.
A shadow with a light-forged lance, aiming to impale him, could not evade in time and was killed outright.
But Colin was well aware that under such intense light, he would eventually be ground down to death.
Just like in the last training session…
“It’s just a shame I’m no longer the person I was half a month (actually seven days) ago,” Colin recalled the starship encounter and that enigmatic “Flame Bearer” who seemed to arrive yet not arrive, indescribable as being there or not, only describable with the term “as if present.”

chapters.title: Chapter 530 - 530 427 Cutting Saintess Shana in Half. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 530: Chapter 427: Cutting “Saintess” Shana in Half. _2 Chapter 530: Chapter 427: Cutting “Saintess” Shana in Half. _2 Invisible, he maneuvered his flames, repelling the “Night.”
These days, after many deep reflections and under the teachings of “Big C Teacher,” he had figured out a bit more.
“Yukionna, take good control of my body…,”
Colin instructed, pouring all his energy into the flames around him.
Then, he took out an ordinary-looking container subject, resembling a spoon, from the “Storage Room.”
This was one of the things he had obtained from the officials.
At that moment, while holding it in his left hand, Colin channeled flames into it, igniting and burning the anomaly to generate new heat energy.
Simultaneously, he controlled every wisp of flame and heat, coaxing them to roll inward, compressing the fire further and further, reaching an extreme high-pressure status, locking in every trace of thermal energy from escaping…
This operation wasn’t particularly difficult, but it was incredibly draining.
So much so that he couldn’t maintain control of his body properly, entrusting it to “Yukionna” to prevent accidents.
Afterward, once the flames had taken shape, Colin immediately invoked “Force Repulsion,” splitting them into over thirty segments, shooting them out simultaneously.
In almost an instant, dozens of fiery sparks pierced through all the clones he could sense.
And at the very moment these light shadows shattered…
Colin suddenly felt as if someone was above his head.
It was the original!
Without a second thought, dragging his somewhat exhausted body, he moved his left hand, invoking “Time Stop,” as the revolver in his right hand rapidly transformed into a long sword.
Then his figure flashed, emerging from a cluster of flames mid-air, appearing directly above.
He swept his gaze and saw an embodiment more refined than the other clones.
Of course, to Colin…
This could already be considered the original!
At this moment, now aware that this figure was the Saintess, he could faintly make out a slight feminine contour on her form, but due to its vagueness, not much could be discerned.
However, he didn’t dwell on this.
With a smirk on his face, before “Time Stop” ended, Colin swung at the nebulous glow beneath the “delicate” neck of his opponent.
Tormented by her for days, he could already imagine the head of the Saintess flying off!
Just the thought was pleasurable!
“Clang!”
The crisp sound traveled up the sword, which wasn’t caught in stasis, to his ears.
The sword, transformed from the revolver, was surprisingly blocked by some “light” surrounding her.
“So hard!”
Colin raised an eyebrow, realizing he had reached his limit; those fireballs were exhausting.
If he failed this time…
Thoughts flashing like lightning, he didn’t hesitate and immediately resorted to his ultimate move in combat.
“Matchless Strike!”
Flames erupted once more from the sword.
Empowered by the terrifying force, Colin broke through the protective light and brought the sword down fiercely.
Whoosh.
The head flew off.
The battle was finally over!
However, before he could celebrate, Colin sensed something was off.
Mainly, the sensation didn’t feel quite right.
Having decapitated so many heads these past days, his experience told him that the sensation just now didn’t feel like cutting a head but rather something else…
At that moment, a chill in his heart, Colin’s fiery eyes saw an “invisible” figure, the Saintess’s left half, from elbow to belly button to hip bone, cleanly sliced in half.
“Indeed, I thought it didn’t feel quite right,”
A thought surfaced deep within Colin.
As for her, a mere bisecting was nothing to worry about; as long as the neck remained intact, it was merely a minor injury…
The next second, Colin’s pupils shrank suddenly.
He saw the Saintess’s lower half that had been cut off, now splitting into over a dozen blurry shadows.
From those shadows, numerous chains formed from light shot towards him.
…
Opening his eyes, he found the familiar Bonfire.
Colin shook his head, looking at the flame, barely audible from within its Fourth Level burn of a “Level 2 Containment Subject,” was a chant as if coming from the Deep Sea.
“Take a rest for now, your energy seems to be lagging,” a voice filled with an indescribable sense of ethereal purity came from aside.
Without caring for appearances, Colin collapsed into a wooden chair beside the Bonfire, took a deep breath, turned his head, and saw a blurry figure of light slowly approaching from the side.
Nodding, he didn’t say anything.
Fighting non-stop for an entire day at high intensity and frequent exchanges, he was indeed very tired.
But compared to before, when he had to rest after only half a day, his stamina had now more than doubled.
“Your ability with flames is quite impressive, to perform more intricate operations with fire, concentrating the power—it sounds simple but isn’t easy to execute… It seems you’ve had a remarkable experience, and your power level has significantly improved,” the Saintess commented as she sat down on another wooden chair beside him.
“Indeed it is…”
Colin nodded. While he lost the battle, his mood was still good.
After all, he had at least learned the much-desired “Flash” ability.
“Congratulations, but from now on, we will develop and train specifically in this area to further familiarize yourself with its use. I can feel that using it just once is not your limit…”
The Saintess’s controlled vague figure of light, looking at the disheveled Colin sprawled in the chair, spoke with a tone of blessing.
Watching this guy, she felt as if he was her own student, transforming from a mere “brute” with strength to someone with increasingly skilled movements, giving her an indescribable sense of accomplishment.

chapters.title: Chapter 531 - 531 427 Cutting Saintess Shana in Half._3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 531: Chapter 427: Cutting “Saintess” Shana in Half._3 Chapter 531: Chapter 427: Cutting “Saintess” Shana in Half._3 As they spoke, she glanced outside.
