Through the nearby light, she could see the refugees in the area being managed in an orderly fashion by the others, which caused some turmoil in her heart…
Shana felt that her own ability to manage common people was as “pale” as the skills the Agent of the Bonfire demonstrated in his strength.
She really wanted to ask the other how to effectively manage the refugees without resorting to measures like temporary enforced brainwashing.
However, thinking about the exorbitant “tuition fee” Colin had asked for just to give her some instruction, she found herself unable to open her mouth.
She couldn’t afford such high points and could only secretly observe the situation outside while fighting, trying to learn on her own. Sadly, there was still so much she didn’t understand…
Colin, however, had no idea about the Saintess’s thoughts. After discussing training methods,
he curiously brought up the question of the Bone Spur, “About that White Bone Spur, the Holy Relic… can we talk about it?”
“That ‘Holy Relic’?” The Saintess was surprised he brought it up.
“Yeah, if it’s inconvenient, we don’t have to discuss it.”
“Actually, it’s not taboo… It’s essentially about a Saint from hundreds of years ago who appeared during an event known as the ‘Rain of Filth.’ In order to stop a disaster, he absorbed the source of the disaster into his own body…”
The Saintess spoke slowly, with vague inherited images surfacing in her mind.
She seemed to see, through the depths of history, a luminous figure standing before an indescribably horrific disaster, using “Chains of Light” to drag the aberration into his own body.
And then…
Her beautiful brown hair rapidly fell out, her fair skin swelled and darkened, and her pores oozed foul-smelling filth. In extreme agony, she let the “Chains of Light” wind around her, layer by layer.
After completing the sealing of the source, she fell into a lake formed by the polluted rainwater, where her body lay decaying for an unknowable amount of time…
Until many years later, when the pollution from the ‘Rain of Filth’ had receded, some people luckily found her.
By then, the Saint, once called the most holy and beautiful of all, had decayed into nothing but scattered bones on the dried-up lakebed.
Within those remains, one of the bones in the right hand was the vessel for the ‘Rain of Filth.’
Later on, some people polished it and turned it into a certain artifact…
As it became famous, some members of the Church of Light realized it belonged to the remains of a Saint.
Thus, they recovered it.
But, about a hundred years ago, it was stolen from the storehouse by a ‘Honest Knight’ who had defected from the Kingdom of Knights, and once again, it was lost.
“The Honest Knight?” Colin looked puzzled, as if he had realized something.
“Yes, an Honest Knight who upheld ‘Humility,’ ‘Glory,’ and ‘Honesty,’ with ‘Honesty’ as his main Virtue. His reasons for defection are unknown, as is his reason for specifically stealing the Bone Spur. After all, the records are too few and I am not a witness. However, since the Bone Spur ended up in your hands, it means he’s dead. When he stole the Holy Relic, he was already around one hundred and seventy or eighty years old. By now, he’d be around three hundred, and one with the Three Virtues does not live that long…”
‘Not necessarily dead…’
Upon hearing this, Colin subconsciously retorted in his mind.
If nothing unexpected had happened, they might have indirectly met a few months ago.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 532 - 532 428 Trading Life for the Continuation of
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 532: Chapter 428: Trading Life for the Continuation of Civilization_1 Chapter 532: Chapter 428: Trading Life for the Continuation of Civilization_1 ‘If that guy really is the ‘Honest Knight’, then… who bewitched it to find Earth and then use all sorts of dirty tricks to keep drawing people over?’
‘Based on the cognition of the people here, they generally have a concept of ‘other worlds’, but it seems they are other World Codes.’
‘And their knowledge of Earth is basically zero, so the chances of that guy finding Earth on his own are very small…’
As Colin conversed with Shana, he mulled over it, and thoughts flickered through his mind.
However, he couldn’t be certain of that guy’s identity; the “Human Patchwork Monster” might not be the “Honest Knight.”
Given that thing’s characteristics…
It might simply be one of its many disguises.
To figure out who it really is, with all the twists and turns, you’ll probably only know for sure by catching him in person.
‘Do you know of a special life form…’ Colin looked at Shana, mentioning the “Human Patchwork Monster.”
An abnormal presence lurking behind the scenes.
If left unresolved, it would always be a hidden threat.
Of course, if caught, he could also settle the upgrade of the “Fusion Card: Smiling Corpse Mountain.”
Colin vaguely felt that this thing’s limit should be at least to grow three heads.
‘No…’ The Saintess thought for a few seconds, and her brain swiftly ‘scanned’ through all the abnormalities she had heard of or seen since the age of three, finally shaking her head.
If she had really come across such a special form of creature, she would definitely have some recognition of it.
Pausing, without waiting for Colin to speak, she added, ‘But one thing, if it’s extremely cautious and has many identities, then it must be aware of me and be guarded because nobody can hide in front of me in this world…’
As she spoke, she unconsciously glanced at Colin.
Since the time of Helena, besides some information given through parchment, she had also glimpsed some things with her own ability, like… a vague, emaciated, pure, and friendly soul.
Back then, this soul’s figure seemed to be troubled by something, so weak it could hardly stand, but now…
It seemed to have grown much fatter and stronger?
‘Well then.’
Colin sighed in regret, but the corners of his mouth curled slightly, as if he had thought of something else, ‘By the way, isn’t one of the twenty-three Bishops of your ‘Light’ Church supposed to arrive today? Want to meet him?’
‘Gordon? I think I can sense that he is approaching this area, but I’d rather not meet him…’
Perhaps because they had grown quite familiar with each other, the Saintess said, ‘Although there’s no conflict with the ‘Light’ Church… the relationship isn’t that good either, especially those Bishops, Elders, and core members higher up. They probably wouldn’t be happy to see me.’
‘Eh?’ Colin was taken aback, immediately thinking of some internal factional strife.
It’s just… does it feel like the Saintess is including all factions in her description?
Shana gave him a look as if observing something, causing Colin to have the sensation that his ‘true self’ had been glimpsed.
But before he could reflect on this meaning, he heard her say, ‘Let me tell you a secret that’s not really a secret, Mr. Colin, do you know about the Holy Light Court?’
‘I know…’
If Colin remembered correctly, this was the predecessor to the “Light” Church, but for some reason, it fell apart.
‘The Holy Light Court, in some sense, was overthrown by the ‘Light’s Saint… well, my predecessors, of course, some others were involved too, but the main force was us…’
‘Eh?’ A phrase popped into Colin’s mind: The prince staging a coup?
‘Originally, the ‘Holy Light Court’ strayed from the right path in the name of ‘Light’, attempted to rid humanity of desire, causing the Pale Catastrophe, among other things. As a result, the Third Generation Holy One emerged consecutively, dismantled the main body of the ‘Holy Light Court’ and caused it to split apart, so not only the ‘Light’ Church, most powers arising from the split of the ‘Holy Light Court’ don’t care much for me…’
‘Ah?’ Colin was startled, but quickly realized something: ‘Consecutively emerged? Isn’t the Saint chosen by themselves?’
‘That’s not the case…’ The Saintess provided an unexpected answer.
She didn’t leave Colin hanging and simply explained this aspect: ”Light’ is quite special, it’s not passed down from generation to generation. It only happens when there’s something going on, some time, someone becomes… it’s hard to explain.’
She left out some details… for instance, it was she who chose the “Light,” not the “Light” choosing her.
Meanwhile, as he listened to her, Colin felt that a more appropriate phrase was ‘born for the times.’
The “Light” Saint, or more accurately, the Saint of “Light,” emerges with a certain natural mission to do something, maybe to avert disasters or something else…
But among the most famous is the Saint who overthrew the misguided ‘Holy Light Court.’
This…
Colin roughly understood why all the believers of the “Light” were not too keen on her.
Not because there was a conflict between them, but because once the Saint appears, all forces related to the “Light” faith become quite awkward…
Who knows if any of them have strayed from the right path again?
No? How did the “Saint” emerge without any straying?
‘It seems you’ve understood,’ came the Saintess’s voice from the side.
‘It is indeed quite awkward,’ Colin nodded.
No wonder in the information gathered, this Saint was often associated with words like ‘alone’ and ‘solitary.’

chapters.title: Chapter 533 - 533 428 Trading Life for the Continuation of
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 533: Chapter 428: Trading Life for the Continuation of Civilization_2 Chapter 533: Chapter 428: Trading Life for the Continuation of Civilization_2 ‘I don’t know why this would happen, but this does confirm what we already knew: the Church moves with the power of faith, but that doesn’t mean they are truly of one mind…’ Colin nodded to himself in the dark.
At that moment, he suddenly felt that the Saintess glanced at him. Was it an illusion? Even though the light was too dim to see any details, he felt like she had smiled a bit?
“According to some information left inside ancient Holy Relics in the secrets of the great cathedrals, when you fought alongside the ‘Holy Light Court,’ there were those from your side who took part as well…”
“Ah, I see.” Colin suddenly understood why the Saintess seemed relatively friendly.
Then, when he noticed the word “Holy Relic,” his expression became a bit odd: “Your Holy Relics… are they all made from some sort of body tissue?”
“Hm? This…” The Saintess paused, as she hadn’t really paid attention to this before, but now that she thought about it…
It seemed they mostly were…
“‘Holy Thorn,’ ‘Finger Ring,’ Skull Holy Grail…”
She murmured to herself, then nodded and asked with curiosity, “How do you know about this?”
“I… feel it’s a bit difficult to explain.”
Colin’s expression was subtle – having a connection with a “Flame Bearer,” so the “Light” Church used parts of their own bodies as artifacts, which resulted in a “transmission from person to person” phenomenon, huh?
Truly comrades who could fight shoulder to shoulder.
And there were still many relics left; why did it feel like the fates of the Saints from generation to generation weren’t so great?
Otherwise, why were there so many skeletal “Holy Relics”…
‘Speaking of which, the ‘Holy Relics’ here all seem to be skeletal, while the relics left by ‘Flame Bearers’ from outside this world are mostly various hearts… So, did my colleague, the confused ‘Flame Bearer’ Rosen, conform to local customs and leave a skull instead of a heart?’
Colin couldn’t help but think of a hellish joke.
He shook his head inwardly, and then, looking at the light and shadow before him, he asked curiously, “Do the records mention where those people went?”
“No, there aren’t any. They didn’t stay here for too long. After finishing their business, they just vanished all of a sudden. I’ve searched before but found no records. However, I did meet you, and it seems you’re also looking for them?” the Saintess said.
It seemed likely that they had headed to “World Code” 321 and never returned… While thinking this, Colin replied, “Yes, I roughly know that they went to some dangerous places, but I don’t know where.”
‘But I do know that one’s head for some reason came back… and it seems to be continuously sending distress signals to the ‘Bonfire Company’… resulting in a special ‘Descent Project’…’
Colin added silently to himself.
He felt that many things in this world were interconnected, like the “Human Patchwork Monster” definitely didn’t target Earth for no reason – it was most likely related to what the company employees left behind…
Unfortunately, it didn’t seem that these related things were easy to find.
After chatting for a while longer, Little Red entered with a cup of water steeped in concentrated nutrients, first greeting the glowing figure, then handing a cup to her big brother, in anticipation of his praise…
“Did you finish the exercises?” Colin affectionately touched the overly emotional girl whose eyes would turn red.
“I finished them.” Little Red blinked and looked expectantly at Colin, hoping he would go out and play with her.
However…
“Alright alright, I’ve brought you another new gift. Are you excited?”
“Excited.”
Then, amidst the little girl’s anticipation, Colin took out a new, one-inch-thick “One Lesson Three Practices.”
Little Red’s face visibly deflated with joy…
But still, she didn’t reject her big brother and slowly left with her new textbook.
“Mr. Colin, are you teaching them how to read?” Shana inquired.
She found it quite miraculous that among these refugees… about five percent had actually begun to grasp the basics of writing during this period. Of course, this script was not the script of this world, but from another world.
The two groups didn’t share a language, but strangely, they had started using the same script, and the meanings of the words appeared to be more or less unchanged.
Which meant that, one day, if people from Colin’s world came over, even without some power to translate, they could still communicate using different languages with similar script—…
If it weren’t for the “Flame Bearer,” she might call the “Tribunal of Judgment” over.
After all, if the other party was an invader… that… would not be good at all.
Colin didn’t think too much about it and nodded: “Only by learning to read can they accomplish some tasks better.”
There was an important reason for being able to replace local text with Earth’s language without any loss…
Those refugees, the vast majority, had no previous knowledge of script.
Since they were a blank slate, teaching them was naturally much easier than one would imagine.
Of course, a lot of official knowledge aid was working in the background, setting up plenty of things for him.
Beyond that, the refugees needed to use all kinds of mystical tools to help their brains to learn the language.
Otherwise, they might not be able to understand…
At the very least, they wouldn’t be able to grasp the meaning of written words quickly, especially not a group of people who struggled to speak clearly.
Shana gazed directly at him and nodded lightly: “I see…”
After exchanging a few more words, the training resumed.
…
At the same time, batches of employees were returning from the outside. After a day and half of time, they had finally brought back the entire group of twenty-one people.

chapters.title: Chapter 534 - 534 428 Trading Life for the Continuation of
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 534: Chapter 428: Trading Life for the Continuation of Civilization_3 Chapter 534: Chapter 428: Trading Life for the Continuation of Civilization_3 “Has our domain caught fire…?” a new employee wondered as he gazed at the massive flames shooting up into the sky over the land.
It was the first time he had ever seen a fire that burned over a hundred meters in height…
“Guess what our company is called?”
“Bonfire Shelter…”
“So a bonfire is pretty normal then.”
Lifecoach Kawaii-many’s inexpensively acquired disciple, Professor Cute Cuddle, rolled her eyes: “Hurry back to register, or next time you come it will be random again…”
As she spoke, she glanced at the others in the group, some riding horses, trailing slowly behind.
Hundreds of people.
It’s said that they were the second batch of envoys from other churches, and in terms of strength, they were much greater than the previous ones…
Moreover, there were knight legions, various churches, all gathered together.
And just now, in searching for people, they encountered each other, and then the other party actively offered help, expressing some goodwill, so they proceeded together.
“That’s it over there.” She reminded those people.
“Thank you for guiding us, miss…” said an elderly man in armor with a nod of his head.
Afterward, his gaze fell upon that cluster of bonfires, feeling deeply shocked. However, noticing the small church beneath the bonfire, and on the church, the sun symbol composed of a circle and various lengths of lines surrounding the circle, his face revealed a hint of strangeness…
He glanced aside to the church officials who were dressed in plain white edged with gold, walking alongside.
“Tsk… If I’m not mistaken, Bishop, isn’t this the ‘Church of Light’? Are you here for this? To take it back?” he said tauntingly.
However, upon hearing his words, the old bishop acted as if he hadn’t seen anything and didn’t say a word.
Of course, they were not here for this thing but wanted to find out the “Bonfire” Church’s attitude.
He had heard that the “Saintess” might have already made contact with these people.
He wanted to clarify their stance—surely they weren’t about to perform another purge of the godly side?
After all, typically a saint would just occasionally exercise their authority, getting them to cooperate with some tasks, but they normally do their own things, without contacting other powers. The only exception would be when the “Holy Light Court” was on the wrong path, and they would contact others.
So… hearing that the “Saintess” might have made contact with “Bonfire,” they couldn’t help but ponder deeply if they had once again strayed from the right path…
But thinking it over, it seemed they had not.
The saint of this generation seemed to be destined to resolve various natural disasters and provide aid to the displaced, rather than sorting out their issues.
Nevertheless, even if the “Light” Church’s bishop knew that it was probably not their fault, he couldn’t help but personally come to understand the situation, seeking peace of mind.
Of course, if there was indeed a mistake that could be corrected, there was no need for confrontational approaches right off the bat…
What issue couldn’t be resolved through proper communication?
The current “Church of Light” was much more open-minded than the former “Holy Light Court.”
They wouldn’t continue down the wrong path even when knowing their mistake.
‘Oh saints…’ he couldn’t help feeling emotional in his heart.
He admired these people from the bottom of his heart because they were indeed some pure and idealistic individuals.
Moreover…
So far, each saint that appeared over hundreds of years had not had a good end, and almost without exception eventually died a shattered death due to their mission.
This generation…
He feared that one day they too would fall amidst some great catastrophe, sacrificing their lives to prolong the world.
Then, only after several or even many years later, when the natural disasters finally subsided, might someone find their already decayed and only slightly intact skeleton from the scene of the disaster.
These bones would then be collected and stored in the holy mountain of the “Light” faith, serving as a kind of kindling.
And when some catastrophe erupted in the future, shedding the dust, they would emit their final radiance…
While contemplating, he sighed deeply, gazing at the domain, dismounted, and walked towards it, leading the horse by the reins.
…
Above the domain, a “Bonfire People’s Supply and Marketing Cooperative” had opened.
Yeager, who had just moved bricks for half the day and then taken half the day off, stood with many others outside the door, casting curious glances at this supermarket set up by prominent figures.
It was said to be a sort of shop where one could purchase goods to enrich their lives.
After hesitating for a moment, he stepped inside, where various flavors of instant noodles were on display, along with many other items he had seen and some he had not…
“A pack of instant noodles only costs 0.02 Points?”
Yeager stopped in front of a shelf stacked with green-packaged instant noodles—
Nowadays, a person could typically earn about 0.04 Points worth of… wages each day.
Yeager still found this term somewhat new; giving money to the displaced was something he had never seen before.
That is to say, aside from their three meals a day, could they still earn enough for an additional day’s meal?
This… was a level of welfare that the slaves had never even imagined.
After looking around, Yeager stopped in front of a pack of chocolate sweets, which he recognized.
In previous brick-moving competitions, whomever achieved first place would receive three pieces as a reward.
They had a strong scent, were sweet, and tasted very good.
Perhaps even nobles may not have had the chance to taste them.
Yeager clearly wanted to buy them, but after looking at the price, he hesitated.
It was the most expensive item in the coop, valued at 0.5 Points!
“0.5 Points could buy more than thirty packs of instant noodles, and it’s almost a third of my recent commendation income.”
Yeager silently calculated his finances and considered giving up, but thinking of his family soon to arrive, he decided against it…
However, at that moment, an employee approached with a certain smile:
“Actually, I think you might consider an installment payment plan.”
“Installment?”
“Yes, that is, you don’t have to pay all the money at once. For example, for this box of Fédel chocolate, you only need to pay every seven days, and each time you only need to give 0.1 Points. Continue for six weeks, and in this way, when you make the purchase, you won’t have to worry about any burden…”
The employee spoke with a smile beaming across his face.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 535 - 535 429 Praise the Great Sir Bonfire._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 535: Chapter 429 Praise the Great “Sir Bonfire”._1 Chapter 535: Chapter 429 Praise the Great “Sir Bonfire”._1 ‘Every time 0.1 points, given in six installments, that makes a total of 0.6 points, but every week, an ordinary person can earn about 0.25~0.28 points, and I need a bit more, can reach 0.5…’
‘So if I’m only giving 0.1 each time, it seems like the pressure isn’t really that great?’
As one of the 0.001 percent intellectuals among the 99.99 percent illiteracy rate in the territory,
Yeager’s mind raced and he quickly worked out the account.
Overall…
It seemed not too bad.
At least it was much better compared to some City Lords he had served before, who would double or even triple the loan for various reasons… Yeager had seen with his own eyes, a family borrowing just a handful of seeds, a few hammers, ended up…
Somehow, inexplicably, the whole family turned into personal slaves of the lord.
With this in mind, he tensed up and asked, “If, I mean if, I can’t pay it back…”
“Don’t worry, don’t worry, there definitely won’t be any strange tricks, erm, I mean, like making it impossible to find someone to enforce, there won’t be any additional conditions, and it won’t involve others…’
“If for some reason you really can’t pay back in the end, then I’ll just consider myself unlucky.”
‘After all, doing business is all about sincerity.’
This company employee said earnestly, producing a handwritten contract.
He wasn’t worried about this person being unable to pay back because this man was considered a representative of the local populace.
No matter what, there was no reason to make such a mistake…
Of course, for him, whether the other party could pay back was irrelevant; what mattered was that signing this “contract” would trigger a special artifact he had made from the skin of a hellish being, the “Demon Contract.”
This type of “unfair trade” could enable him to use this artifact better…
Whether the other could pay back or not and whether he could earn those points was unimportant to him, but the act of “unfair trade” itself was very important to him.
Of course, if he could earn something, he wouldn’t mind making a bit more.
Listening to his explanation, Yeager was somewhat tempted, and the quantity of that pile of chocolate sweets was not small…
There must have been more than thirty pieces, right?
The key thing was, soon his family would be sent to the territory, and he wanted to give his newly arrived family members a surprise.
A weekly repayment of 0.1 didn’t pose much pressure for him.
Even if he bought them, he could roughly ensure that his family could live a “decent” life, meaning eat three meals a day —
In the local populace, having three meals a day was currently considered a symbol of “wealth.”
Generally, the Administrator only provided two meals a day.
The meal, a small piece of biscuit that was very hard but became very large once soaked, along with a cup of nutrient liquid.
That was the basic. If you did well, you could get more, even a share of meat…
In the end, he chose to sign the contract and bought a large pack of chocolate sweets on credit.
Behind him, an E level Personnel who had just completed a transaction wore a smile on his face, but the smile didn’t last long before he suddenly felt himself being violently restrained by something.
“Shadow!” He saw a shadow on the ground, coming from nowhere, connecting to his feet, forming an unknown special control.
Thinking of fighting back, but following the shadow, he saw a D level Personnel with an unfriendly look on his face:
“Son of a bitch, I’ve heard that someone has been lending money with steep interest, compounding debts, and I’ve finally caught you, come with me…”
“What a pain…”
…
“Little brother!”
Just steps away from exiting the supply store, Yeager heard someone calling him, a familiar voice that made him pause, then he saw his brown-haired sister and parents not far away.
But the next second, noticing the people behind them, he couldn’t help but hold his breath.
They were all important figures one wouldn’t usually see in churches!
At that moment, the invisible force of the old rigid hierarchy made it difficult for him to breathe, and his knees involuntarily knelt down.
However, just then.
“Snap.”
Someone patted his shoulder.
Yeager turned his head and saw a man wearing special glasses. If he remembered correctly, this man seemed to be a powerful individual brought by “Sir Bonfire” the Agent, with a strange name… Kě’ài duō.
“Do you know these people?” the man asked.
“Yeah.”
“Then go and meet them, don’t just stand there.”
“Thank… thank you…”
Yeager nodded, watching several “Bonfire” Church’s powerhouses move past him toward the group made up of various Knight Legions and churches, and suddenly felt a surge of courage, quickly calling his family over.
As a 25 recruit initially deployed here, he knew very well that the Knight Legion’s personnel bringing his family intact, rather than just delivering their heads, was to a great extent a gesture of goodwill towards the “Bonfire” forces.
With this in mind, he couldn’t help but silently chant to himself:
“Praise the great ‘Sir Bonfire’ the Agent.”
And as his family stood together neatly, on the other side, the Kingdom Knight Order personnel, regarding this traitor, simply nodded their heads and didn’t say anything else.
This time, their visit was almost the same as that of the Church of Light’s Bishop; they were here to formally visit and understand attitudes.
To expand or to choose this location as their church ground, what were their targets, doctrines, philosophies, personnel strengths, and so on…

chapters.title: Chapter 536 - 536 429 Praise the Great Sir Bonfire._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 536: Chapter 429 Praise the Great “Sir Bonfire”._2 Chapter 536: Chapter 429 Praise the Great “Sir Bonfire”._2 All of these matters are of great importance.
As for the rest, such things as refugees, slaves fleeing here, are actually matters of little consequence.
Though I don’t know why the “Bonfire” Church values lowborns so highly, even treating them better than the Church of Light, it doesn’t matter.
They’re just inferiors after all…
If they’re given something, then so be it.
In this world, what is noble consists only of those extraordinary forces in possession of certain means and the nobility, not some insignificant underlings.
What could more commoners do, anyway?
Certainly, these commoners couldn’t overthrow them, could they?
It’s simply impossible.
Just like now, some refugees see them and do not humbly kneel aside, but rather some even dare to boldly stare at them, clearly not taking them seriously. Normally, they should have been whipped.
However, because of the “Bonfire” Church, they didn’t say anything.
This isn’t cowardice, but rather… when in a foreign land, one must always respect local customs.
For now, the members of the “Bonfire” Church seem very mysterious; whether they have extraordinary powers or not is mostly invisible, and one can’t discern their true strength.
And as for divination methods…
A member of the “Earth and Nature Rebirth” Church couldn’t help but recall an experience from a few days ago.
A venerated “Earth Sage” had performed a divination for them, and on the crystal, the number “3” appeared.
At that time, the situation was unclear…
They proceeded with the next step of the divination.
Then appeared the number “2”…
Still unclear, the final number became “1”.
Following that, a bolt of lightning from nowhere struck fiercely.
At the point of impact, a fire instantly ignited, sweeping away everything in the divination ritual site—yes, this flame was strange; it didn’t burn things, but like a robber, it took away most of the valuable items.
Fortunately, aside from falling into a special emotional chaos, most people had no other problems.
You have to understand, that was a sacred land of the forest, yet the adversary could come and go as they pleased…
This time, they had come to find out if there was any further blame from this side.
But all along the way here, it seemed there had been no targeting.
This made them wonder if there was a possibility of redeeming the stolen items…
“┗|｀O′|┛ Wow~~”
A strange roar came from afar. Some people turned their heads to look and, with their superhuman vision, saw on a barren piece of land in the distance, a flesh ball with two large heads wildly swinging its power, pounding on the slightly stiff ground with punch after punch, causing dust to fly…
It seemed to be… loosening the soil?
“It’s the ‘Holy Beast’ of the ‘Bonfire’ Church,” a knight explained softly.
Hearing this, people nodded. They had already gotten a rough understanding of this black, two-headed monster from earlier intelligence…
But aside from these things, what surprised them even more was that giant mechanical life form that intermittently emitted a deafening noise. This being was somewhat beyond their understanding.
In this territory, it seemed there were noticeable changes every week.
There were also a few people whispering that this thing resembled the creations of an evil church that worshiped the “God of the Shattered Gear”, an entity that had been expunged by all the churches a long time ago.
But recalling the city ruins that remained in a “hollow” state to this day, they were convinced.
The “Bonfire” Church was certainly not an evil church…
At the least, they hadn’t shown this aspect, and they had successfully prevented the descent of an Evil God. How could such a force possibly be evil?
Meanwhile, seeing several individuals who appeared to be members of the “Bonfire” Church approaching, they quickly put on smiles.
“We are here to visit Mr. Bonfire’s Agent…”
…
On the sixth day, Colin emerged from the small chapel with a somewhat haggard face, concluding his training.
“My combat power and skills have become much more proficient, and not as crude as when I first advanced to D Level. That flame, which burns my own essence and requires intense concentration, can now be released quickly…”
“Oh, and I learned a ‘Flash’ skill. Combined with ‘Time Stop’, it’s basically instant kill…”
Taking a deep breath, Colin quietly sensed his own condition.
He felt that the “tuition fee” he paid was well worth it, for under normal circumstances, it wouldn’t be easy to find someone like her willing to teach things meticulously.
Especially that “Nightmare Lantern,” which made each of his battles a life-and-death struggle.
Although each death brought a strong sense of palpitation,
it wasn’t a big problem…
Compared to the Saintess, the style of C Level Elder Brother shifted entirely, providing scornful remarks on weaknesses, giving a certain direction, while striking with heavy punches, targeting specifically…
But he wouldn’t discuss more detailed things.
His original self in that “Ghost Train” had a good impression, but this copy… was a bit stiff.
Although there were no issues with his strength…
Sometimes Colin still felt like the other party was snickering like a girly ghost, uttering taunts like “Is that all? Is that all?”
Of course, this also related to the fact that the other’s essence belonged to a certain kind of AI simulation.
As his thoughts dispersed, Colin touched his pocket and took out a golden Sun Mark.
When he acquired it…
His brain’s operational speed increased.
This time, the Saintess custom-made this one for that flame technique of his, which required tremendous energy to control. It was designed to enhance his mental capacity fully, preventing him from falling into energy exhaustion…
“With the tuition fees paid, I’ve got two Golden Marks already. This one certainly earns back its cost, and then there’s Bone Spur and the Shield Badge of Fairness and Justice, plus the teaching. It feels like I’m getting all this from her for free…”

chapters.title: Chapter 537 - 537 429 Praise the Great Sir Bonfire._3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 537: Chapter 429 Praise the Great “Sir Bonfire”._3 Chapter 537: Chapter 429 Praise the Great “Sir Bonfire”._3 Thinking of this, Colin surprisingly found that his dwindling conscience was actually aching.
So, he quickly recalled the exorbitant fees charged by “The Light Chaser” at the beginning, which were akin to robbery…
He felt much better instantly.
However, upon further reflection, he always felt that “The Light Chaser” indeed craved points, but it seemed… the intensity of this desire was not that high.
No, to be precise, the points he’s been asking for so far all seemed quite reasonable, even on the low side.
Instead of the usual demands of tens of thousands in “entrance fees” and various “BUFF fees” for missions…
A whole set would usually flush out directly twenty or thirty thousand points.
‘Hmm… where exactly is the problem?’
Colin stood in front of the small church, stroking his chin, feeling that something was not quite right.
His character setup seemed… too fragmented?
At this moment, a rumbling hunger surged, after battling against the Saintess for six consecutive days, his stomach was indeed a bit hungry…
Well, better take care of my hunger first.
Hunger was usually no big deal, but if one were hungry for too long, things might go awry.
Colin had to make sure that he was usually in a state of being neither hungry nor full.
Putting his thoughts aside, he summoned everyone and started a bonfire banquet, getting some dry steak and lamb legs from other employees, preparing to treat himself.
Meanwhile, he would meet with the clergymen from various churches who had mentioned they would visit him.
But before their arrival, Colin eagerly bit into a freshly roasted tender lamb chop…
“Ptui, who grilled this? Can’t eat without salt…”
…
Meanwhile, in a small castle shrouded by the Magic Fog, Shana had also finished the personnel transfer work for the area and was preparing to rest for a while to adjust her status.
She sat on a broken stone chair, glancing into her pocket…
Three thousand points more.
Oh, after deducting the handling fee, there were still two thousand seven hundred points left.
Although she had no intention of exchanging points this time, the parchment mission appeared anyway, and she ended up with so many stuffed into it.
“‘Sir Bonfire’ agent… Points, indeed, seem plenty…”
Shana took out the hardened food she hadn’t finished eating days before and stuffed it in her mouth like she was chewing on a rock.
However, more than this, her thoughts were mostly on the agent’s points…
Not because she coveted them, but she realized that both the agent and his subordinates seemed to have plenty of points in general.
Even an ordinary citizen doing some very routine work could usually earn 0.04 to 0.01 points as a reward, likely doling out tens of points a day.
And those tasks…
She could split herself into dozens of replicas, and in just a day, or even half a day, she would have finished the work it would take a thousand people seven days to complete, and then…
She hadn’t done the exact calculation, but the total of seven days’ points for over a thousand people was definitely several hundred.
That amount of points, if distributed from the parchment, would be close to engaging in combat with an Ancient God…
For a moment, Shana fell into silence.
She took out the parchment, and those ice blue eyes, transparent as gemstones, gazed at it with a kind of perplexity for a while…
After several seconds, she pursed her lips and said nothing.
Never mind…
She opened the parchment’s store and spent one point, rewarding herself with a rye bread that wasn’t sour, wasn’t smelly or hard, and could exchange for three instead of thirty for one point.
No “crack” sound, as if breaking a stone, occurred.
Shana chewed for a bit, blinked her eyes, and looked at the somewhat coarse rye bread.
Soft, tasty.
It had far more nutritional content than the other type, and she could feel some energy as soon as it entered her mouth…
If it weren’t for Mr. Agent who kept shoving thousands of points her way, in times like these, she personally wouldn’t want to indulge in such an expensive luxury as rye bread.
According to inherited memories…
The previous Saints, it seemed, never had the chance to eat this kind of food in their lifetimes.
Of course, each generation could exchange for different things on the parchment, so it might not necessarily have been bread.
But then again, it’s rare to fight such a well-off battle for the first time in life.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 538 - 538 430 0-09 Hunger News. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 538: Chapter 430 “0-09 Hunger” News. _1 Chapter 538: Chapter 430 “0-09 Hunger” News. _1 “Next, there are still some people in five areas within three kingdoms that have a chance to relocate…”
Shana ate bread while studying the special planar map before her.
The map floated in midair, woven from countless pure white radiance emanating from her body, forming a three-dimensional model that clearly depicted the region’s situation and marked her current position.
The base of this thing was composed of “Light” churches or other “Light” faith church buildings, believers’ faith, and so on.
She had been moving through the Magic Fog, of course, not wandering about like window shopping, she had to follow the map.
Otherwise, even she would have a high probability of being exhausted to death by endless disasters.
“The distance is not very far, within this period, everyone should be able to relocate successfully, and then… be sent to the ‘Bonfire’ Agent…”
Shana pondered the plan for their arrangement.
After all, rescuing people wasn’t the end of it; they also needed to be settled. In the past, she might have had to lead people from place to place, looking for cities and villages willing to accept some—
—a little arrangement…
Otherwise, a fair number of nobles would not treat the majority of the people she rescued as humans, they wouldn’t even grant them the status of refugees.
But now, Mr. Colin was kindhearted…
He told her he was willing to accept those she saved.
This spared her many distressing bothers.
And from what she could see, not long ago Helena’s sister had taken a large group of refugees over, and they had indeed been well calmed and settled, blending into the larger community.
Even her doppelgänger, who had always been there for practice, clearly saw that this was not their limit in management.
That newly-formed territory seemed to have been prepared to accommodate even more people.
“Managing the lives of tens of thousands of refugees, just by confirming some general directions, the whole can be roughly operated well… Mr. Colin really is capable and kind.”
Shana couldn’t help but feel a bit moved.
In this period, she hadn’t mentioned the Holy Relic recovery, and also the meticulously crafted “Light” marks that were given as gifts at the end, partly because she felt a bit guilty in this regard.
However, what she didn’t know was that Colin’s management method was much simpler than she thought—
Adhering to the principle of using what works to exhaustion, he toughed it out with capable employees; as long as they could work, they had endless tasks, with plenty of spirit-refreshing artifacts and physical replenishments.
“Once this matter here is over, after going out, I’ll help him look for that ‘Feast of Devouring’ guy…” Shana’s thoughts flashed.
Actually, before entering the “Disaster of Magic Fog,” she was also tracking these terrible entities.
And had made some gains…
However, it was because of this suddenly erupted mega-disaster that she had to rush here for support.
Another few dozen seconds passed, Shana put the remaining half of the bread she couldn’t bear to eat in one go into her pocket, then stood up, ready to move.
Resting for five minutes was already enough for her.
On the map, people disappeared every second.
Moreover, within the Catastrophe of the Magic Fog, the stronger one’s power, and staying in one place for too long, the easier it was to unknowingly fall into trouble.
Certain Ancient God Types with some intelligence might set ambushes for her.
These things, although called “types,” were not Ancient Gods in essence, but just as troublesome.
Shana lifted her head, with white light dancing in her eyes, she could see all details within dozens of kilometers, the thick, writhing grey-black Magic Fog broadcasting dreadful threats from almost every direction, every piece of the sky, and every inch of the earth…
Looking around here, she couldn’t help but get slightly distracted.
The Magic Fog had been raging for a long time, countless people died within it, and sadly, as of now.
She still couldn’t find the root of these phenomena…
Without finding the root, there was no way to solve it completely.
However, a vague and indistinct intuition kept giving her the subtle feeling that the solution wasn’t far from her, but unfortunately, not finding it means not finding it.
“Better focus on rescuing people first, the next step, there are two directions, and one seems a bit dangerous…”
Shana was considering which way to go when.
At that moment, something unexpected happened violently.
A sudden, intense sense of crisis welled up inside her.
“I seem to have made eye contact with something that should not be faced…”
The next instant, outside this small castle, an immensely huge and terrifyingly oppressive “giant hand” crashed down from the sky.
Boom…
The earth trembled, and a terrifying shock wave and dust spread like a sandstorm.
The small castle and a large part of the city were directly reduced to dust under the immense pressure.
All anomalies were also obliterated within it…
The “giant hand” might have been a hand or it might not; visually, it indeed looked like an enormous hand, but through the third sense derived from “Light,” it was just an indescribable ball of “Chaos,” capable of immense destruction.
However, whatever it was, Shana had no intention of entangling with it.
An imperceptible streak of white light, like a comet, dashed toward the next area waiting for rescue.
…
“Crackle…”
Sparks flew within the bonfire, the aroma of roasting meat wafting all around.
In the evening of the sixth day, Colin sat beside a bonfire, with Little Red, Xiao Bing (Yukionna), and others being noisy around him, he stared at the meat in his hand, pondering some limited information he knew from Shana about the “Flame Bearers” who had once come to this place.

chapters.title: Chapter 539 - 539 430 0-09 Hunger News._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 539: Chapter 430 “0-09 ‘Hunger'” News._2 Chapter 539: Chapter 430 “0-09 ‘Hunger'” News._2 The “Firebearer” who came here that year must have been Rosen…
To Colin’s surprise, these “Fiery Brothers,” who would often turn their enemies to cinders, didn’t seem to have taken much action at that time.
Instead, they provided another type of aid to the three Saints who had been advancing in succession.
“The Weapon of Critique.”
They mainly provided various ideological support beyond the use of force, which shattered the teachings of the “God of Holy Light” and destroyed its mystique.
In essence, it was akin to issuing a “Human Declaration” to the “Holy Light Court,” which at that time was comparable to the “Land-based God Kingdom,” and laid the foundation for secular liberation in theology.
“Who would have thought, these guys, aside from getting their hands dirty, would also use their brains…”
Colin was rather taken aback.
In his mind, the “Firebearers,” as a combat unit, would only talk physics, but unexpectedly, they also dealt with reason, which was staggering…
It’s just a pity that it’s unclear why these guys disappeared so thoroughly after their collaboration with “Light,” leaving hardly any traces behind.
Of course, according to what Shana said, when these people disappeared…
The so-called “God of Holy Light” also vanished.
I wonder if they were caught by the “Firebearers” to make soup.
Colin scratched his head, feeling unable to comprehend the logic—like how Saints are chosen by “Light,” and the “Light” that the “Holy Light Court” used to worship was the “God of Holy Light.”
So… Did He choose Saints to be His very own antithesis?
No, that’s not right…
Thinking of these people’s circumstances, Colin had some thoughts—
“The God of Holy Light” might be related to “Light” but might not be “Light.”
“Forget it, I won’t think about this anymore. It seems that even if I could understand it, I wouldn’t be able to figure out where these people went, what they did, and why they ended up in such a plight.”
While his thoughts flickered, he turned and looked at his little chapel, which writes “Church of Light” but reads “Bonfire” Church…
He had previously asked the Saintess about the chapel.
She didn’t know either, stating it was beyond her knowledge.
Every “Church” was registered, with something akin to an identity card, but this one had none. The reason might be related to the Bonfire or simply because there wasn’t one.
Then, Shana told him that he could ask the members of the “Virtue Knight Order.”
Because according to her, a “Humility Knight” had died here, and even the disappearance of a single “Virtue Knight” bound to just one vow was supposed to be recorded.
Unfortunately, communication with the “Virtue Knights” who came here revealed they were also unaware of this.
The death of a “Virtue Knight” was definitely a significant event.
However, recently, and over the years, aside from the God Descent not long ago, there were hardly any battles here. Though there were deaths, none were of “Humility Knights”…
So there were plans to check back later, and speak on the matter the next time he came.
Similarly, they had no knowledge of any “Bonfire” Church in the past.
“These people, they left cleanly, without leaving much information…”
Colin shook his head; he cared quite a bit about this matter.
However, aside from these loose ends, another matter had made some progress.
It was about the situation with the heretical force, the “Feast of Gluttony”…
It could be confirmed that it was indeed highly likely associated with “Hunger.”
Or, to be more precise, it was a fragment of “Hunger,” and it was estimated that the main body’s fragment was not small.
Shana told him not to worry, as she had a way to find these guys.
“I wonder if I can face them directly, ah, that seems difficult. If their revival is too advanced, like if they’re completely satiated, I’m afraid that neither the Saintess nor I would be enough to fight. Though what the Saintess truly looks like is still unclear…”
“Anyway, fighting ‘Hunger,’ as long as we can find it, would work as a human transmitter, allowing Lady Bunny to summon the legions through the agreement…”
Colin mumbled to himself, not too worried about this.
If it were any other “Level 0,” he might have been scared.
But “Hunger” was highly controlled by the company, so there really wasn’t much to fear.
If the fight went south, just call for back-up…
At that moment, footsteps approached, and Colin gathered his thoughts to see “Life Mentor Adorable” and others arriving.
Apart from two slightly better-off D Level Personnel, the rest had an air of effortless grace.
With “Colorless Crystal” + “Bonfire” + “Tree of Flame?” They would say they’re tired and indeed their bodies could take it, but they felt listless nevertheless…
“We’ve come to report on the main intelligence of the domain…” a D Level Personnel began, and seeing Colin nod, he signaled everyone to sit down. So, without further ado, they sat down.
By the bonfire, a small meeting commenced.
Soon, through their reports, Colin came to understand the situation here.
No warfare in the territory…
Aside from a bit of chaos due to accommodating new arrivals, there was basically nothing else amiss.
All work steadily progressed over these few days, and with the addition of the “Base Vehicle,” efficiency in all tasks greatly increased.
This thing was too versatile, once deployed, it had various labs, all sorts of data detection equipment, high-temperature furnaces, as well as medical facilities, food supply, command center, and so on…
It was almost like a construction site’s main engine.
Except for the fact that it hadn’t considered where they would sleep, lacking dormitories and leaving everyone to find their own spot to roll out sleeping mats, everything else was fine.
In terms of construction capabilities, it could be said to be on par with Purple Gear, rivaling the prowess of Orange Gear.
——It was just that one matter making Colin feel somewhat uneasy: they had recently caught an employee who had been stealthily offering usurious loans with compounding interest.
No, to say he was offering usurious loans wasn’t quite right, for in a certain sense, his actions resembled charity.
Because the purpose was to accumulate the effects of a certain item he had.
And upon hearing the specifics of this item, Colin’s expression remained unchanged, but he couldn’t help but feel speechless inside.
‘It seems like many people have similar ‘demon’ items; I wonder how much they’ve contributed to the company over the years.’
He felt that the company’s development likely owed an indelible contribution to these “demons.”
“This… What should the punishment be?” “Life Mentor Adorable” pulled Colin out of his contemplations with her question.
What punishment…
Colin couldn’t help but fall silent for a moment, as this could be considered the company’s first employee “crime;” although, calling it a “crime” wasn’t exactly accurate, since everything was established by common consent and there were no explicit rules as such.
The person hadn’t caused any serious consequences…
Yet to not impose some form of action seemed improper as well.
After pondering for a few seconds, Colin finally spoke, “You handle it, and don’t be too harsh. But one thing, some rules do need to be established; discuss it among yourselves and show me the results when you’ve reached a decision…”
“Alright.” Everyone nodded, indicating no objections.
One could foresee that as more people obtained the “Other World Crossing Gift Pack,” there would invariably be all kinds of issues.
Therefore, some internal regulations for our own needed to be set down…
To avoid disputes that might arise and be irresolvable later on.
Before long, the mini-meeting concluded, and everyone dispersed.
Rarely did they get a half-day off in the evening, and they certainly weren’t keen to keep working nonstop.
Some went off to stretch their legs, while others grabbed a bundle of straw, spread it out, and went straight to sleep.
Time passed little by little…
When the twelfth hour arrived, the thick darkness beyond the flames abruptly brightened, as if someone had hit a light switch, making the hazy glow appear from nowhere, illuminating the world.
“Could ‘World Code’ possibly be something like a ‘Starship’ too?”
Even after witnessing such scenes many times, he still found it amazing.
The Night was distinctly divided between darkness and the bonfire’s light…
From black night to dawn, there was no intermediate transition, it simply changed.
By daylight, everything was dimly lit, but no light source could be seen.
However, before he could ponder too deeply, he heard the Little Maid’s voice by his ear.
“Sir… I have received some unknown signals in the form of large, special brainwave patterns emanating from deep within the ground…”
“Received unknown signals?” Colin was startled, “You just said, from where?”
“From underground…” The Little Maid said calmly.
Hearing this, Colin vaguely recalled something, “Is it possible to play it?”
“Yes, shall I start playing it now?”
“Yes.”
As his words fell, the Little Maid simulated the sound, which came through disjointed, like a kind of lament.
Hearing this voice, though distorted yet with a somewhat familiar tone and style, Colin’s expression began to turn strange and contemplative.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 540 - 540 431 First Level Containment Subject King
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 540: Chapter 431 First Level Containment Subject “King of Savage Sound”!_1 Chapter 540: Chapter 431 First Level Containment Subject “King of Savage Sound”!_1 “Let me out, let me out…”
“I already know my mistakes…”
“Great Rosen, please, I beg you, let me out, I sincerely pray here…”
“I am willing to become human and struggle for the rise of mankind, and take up this just cause without hesitation…”
“…”
The slightly distorted, yet still clear words were emitted by the Little Maid.
Colin only listened briefly before immediately recalling a short but quite memorable encounter from before.
“This tone… is it that guy from the depths of the Underground Labyrinth?”
Colin’s expression was slightly odd.
In thought, memories surged forward, and indeed it was through this being that he first learned of the name Rosen.
In that encounter, the other thought he was Rosen and so kept praying.
But…
“Once this guy recognizes me, the probability of him turning hostile was pretty high, wasn’t it?”
Colin muttered quietly, however, he was still quite interested in this alleged relic from a past era, a First Level Containment Subject.
After all, it was a high-level containment subject, and perhaps he could get something interesting out of it.
With that in mind, he looked at the Little Maid and asked, “Can we make contact with it?”
If they were to communicate with it from here, that would be relatively safe.
“I can try, but I suggest not to do it at this place.”
‘Not here?’
Colin was initially startled, then realized that regardless of whether they could make contact, if they did, this place would likely be exposed to the other’s view.
Being watched by a First Level Containment Subject was not good news.
He nodded, stood up immediately, instructed others about some matters, and then left the territory, choosing a direction at random and flying for nearly half an hour before stopping.
Thereafter, Colin set up some “Flame Bearer” Grease cans.
The Little Maid didn’t dawdle, part of her intelligent mechanical body seeped into the ground, seemingly making contact with the other party.
Unfortunately…
Several minutes later, the Little Maid looked back at Colin: “I can confirm that my message has been sent. Theoretically, it should have been received, but for some reason, it did not reveal a status of having received the information.”
“Also, its voice is starting to weaken now.”
“Is that so? It seems the ‘Containment God Kingdom’ is holding it quite strictly.”
Colin hesitated about whether to go to the underground area: “Right, this call for help, has it happened in the past as well, or is it just today?”
“I’m not sure, it should only be able to send signals during the transition from ‘night’ to ‘day.’ I might have received it before as well, but I’m usually in a dispersed state at that time, with not enough power, so I didn’t receive it…”
The Little Maid pulled up her previous work reports and guessed it was likely that the calls had been going on, but due to work, she hadn’t noticed…
“Is that so.”
Colin nodded, then looking in the direction of the Underground Great Labyrinth with a certain perception.
Flames flickered within his gaze…
‘Although it’s a First Level Containment Subject, it’s in a forced state, so given my current strength, it should be okay to talk to it from a certain distance.’
As thoughts turned, Colin had more or less made a decision.
As an enemy of the company in the past, this thing definitely had a lot of understanding of the company.
For example, the upper management structure, the 2044 disaster, the Red Moon, or the whereabouts of “0-09 ‘Hunger'”…
For the sake of this knowledge, the risk was worth taking.
Having decided, Colin did not hesitate; he once again soared into the sky and dived towards the target direction.
About several hours later, he arrived again at the edge of the Underground Giant Great Labyrinth.
Not far ahead lay a ground fissure.
Traveling down the fissure for a bit, he would find the labyrinth.
The last time he went to retrieve those misfortunate “Heroes,” Colin followed this route.
Nowadays, those “Heroes” had already awoken some time ago and joined the construction here, but generally, they were not much help.
After all, to this world, the only thing of value they had was the knowledge in their heads.
But in this respect, the employees handpicked by Colin knew even more.
And what made it even more awkward was that since they came here through non-company channels and got mixed up with some inexplicable stuff.
So…
They couldn’t return to the other side through the company’s channels.
“Though thanks to having those special organs implanted, their physical fitness is quite sharp now.”
Shaking his head, Colin withdrew his gaze from the crack, not rushing in. He took out various items: “Flame Bearer” Grease, Energy Crystal Blocks, a Revolver, and so on, roughly reinforcing himself.
Afterward, Colin jumped into one of the ground fissures and continued onwards, guided by his memory.
Soon, he came across yet another entrance to the chaotic underground labyrinth.
After making sure he was fully prepared, his figure flickered, leaping inside.
It was at that very moment, as his foot touched the floor…
Colin clearly “heard” over and over again the pleading voice in his ear.
The content wasn’t much different from what the Little Maid translated…
However, it was right after he “heard” the sound here that the pleading voice suddenly stopped, followed by a presence laden with intense oppression that seemed to sweep over him.
The next instant, a tumult of savage, grating noise erupted around him…
Colin felt the entire area around him vibrating incessantly.
The air, the ground, everything seemed to be stirred by something.

chapters.title: Chapter 541 - 541 431 First Level Containment Subject King
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 541: Chapter 431 First Level Containment Subject “King of Savage Sound”!_2 Chapter 541: Chapter 431 First Level Containment Subject “King of Savage Sound”!_2 “It’s you… Hahaha, you actually came again!”
“Let’s make a deal!”
“Release me to a certain extent, lift some of my restraints, and I will allow some of your curiosity to be satisfied, and bestow upon you some powers originating from myself…”
“Otherwise…”
“…”
“Otherwise what?”
Colin’s expression suddenly darkened, flames ignited on his body, ready for combat.
His instincts told him that, in this place,
It wouldn’t be difficult to deal with a First Level Containment Subject that was forcefully controlled.
At the same time, judging from the tone of this creature’s speech, Colin couldn’t decide at the moment whether to describe it as a bully that’s afraid of toughness or rich in humanity…
However, by the latter’s standards, it means the modification was indeed very successful.
It’s just…
Damn it, it’s really true that nature is hard to change…
Colin shook his head inwardly.
“Otherwise, hehehe… this time, I will make you understand…”
In the midst of the weird noises, some terrifying thing surged from all around the corridor.
As the voice faded, Colin immediately saw a strange creature, invisible to the naked eye, seemingly composed of some kind of vibration and with a hint of human form, rushing out from the depths of the maze.
It was like a mass of unruly, ear-piercing noise, just hearing the sound was enough to cause inner turmoil.
Moreover, Colin was certain, it wasn’t its true body, but the emanating might was by no means weak.
In just a moment, it had traveled an unknowable distance from deep within the maze to right before Colin.
And then…
“…I will let you know… should you not renounce… I… am willing to serve you… praying to be part of your command.”
Following the abrupt pause in the violent, noisy speech, it seemed to finally sense the essence of the flames and softened.
Its figure, resembling a sliding kneel, slid to a halt not far from him.
“Ah, what…”
Colin, who had been prepared for battle, was momentarily taken aback, then felt his mood a bit weird.
Truth be told, this thing is a First Level Containment Subject, its true strength absolutely surpasses his current level, and a fight would require a do-or-die effort with ‘Hunger,’ but now, what it’s showing…
Isn’t that too abstract?
But might it somehow be consistent with its true nature of being a bully that fears the strong?
‘What it fears is my heavy identity, not my true strength, but, my high regard for a High Order Containment Subject has certainly been utterly destroyed by this creature.’
Colin shook his head inwardly.
There’s no doubt that this level of Containment Subject is incredibly powerful.
It possesses a might in the eyes of the common man akin to that of a god, and it’s exceptionally indifferent and arrogant…
But… due to the existence of this “disgrace of a First Level Containment Subject,”
Everything has been ruined.
‘Your name “King of Mad Sounds” has absolutely nothing to do with your behavior.’
Colin felt his mood was very complicated, subtle.
It was like a feeling of having his childhood destroyed.
In fact, the special life form made of savage noise never anticipated that in just the blink of an eye, the one who was almost negligible as an ant, had already started leaning toward becoming a “Flame Bearer.”
And indeed, had truly inherited that revolver weapon often used by Rosen, and if nothing went wrong…
Then there would be no surprises at all.
Looking at the revolver in the other’s hands, it once again recalled the fear of being dominated.
For a moment, the air was filled with an awkward atmosphere.
Neither side opened their mouths.
Several seconds later, Colin was the first to break the silence, looking at the other party and speaking, “Let’s talk about whether to join your ranks later. I’m here to ask some questions.”
“Rest assured, as long as I know and can answer, I will certainly tell you, just hope you can accept my devout self…” Words composed of vibrations spread through the air.
Hearing this, Colin pondered what he wanted to know: “Start by telling me your information.”
After speaking, he felt that the other party had sent a special informational entity composed of information and inspiration.
Given the credibility of this thing, Colin did not listen himself but let the Little Maid do the job.
“‘King of Mad Sounds,’ Middle-Lower Tier First Level Containment Subject, its essence is a constantly agitated composition of vibrational frequencies, authority related to vibration, specific frequencies, has been injected with special Gene Compensation Medicine…”
Related information was slowly spoken by the Little Maid.
“First Level Middle-Lower Tier Containment Subject? There’s such a distinction… Moreover, this thing can be injected with ‘Gene Compensation Medicine’? And the name ‘King of Mad Sounds’…”
Colin thought of the “Child of Voice”: “Do you know ‘Child of Voice’?”
“‘Child of Voice’? I know Them, no, it, we have both wanted to devour each other, but there was never a right opportunity…”
“King of Madness” caused vibrations all around and, speaking with caution, asked, “May I inquire, what has happened to it?”
In response, it couldn’t help but feel uneasy…
Assuming someone else might had become a pawn of the corporation behind his back, that guy wouldn’t want to dismantle him to repair himself this time, would he?
Thankfully, just as he was preparing to say something to himself,
Colin waved his hand and spoke, “No, it’s just that it got killed sometime back, and I was asking casually.”
Hearing this, the tumultuous frequencies that composed the “King of Madness” paused noticeably, and a second later, an extremely excited laughter erupted, “Good riddance, good riddance… Did the corporation recover it?”
At this, his train of thoughts began to stir.
If the corporation did recover it, by making a good impression and earning merits, he could not only have a chance to reclaim some of the authority stolen by one of his old adversaries, the “Child of Voice,” but perhaps even directly devour all of the “Child of Voice’s” authority.
Then his strength would surge, becoming a powerful Middle-Upper Tier First Level Containment Subject!
Of course, even though this would mean more restrictions, when compared to the benefits, it was hardly worth mentioning.
Unfortunately…
“I don’t know.”
Colin shook his head. He only knew from the envelope given by Lady Bunny previously that during the “Ghost Train” incident,
several high-level beings had fallen…
One of them was the “Child of Voice.”
Then, not waiting for the other party to inquire further, Colin waved his hand:
“Alright, to the point, do you know where Rosen ended up?”
As for this person’s end whereabouts, all his intelligence was speculative, without any solid conclusion, so he was quite curious about the actual situation.
“Rosen…”
After fearfully uttering this name, the “King of Madness” felt a throb as it “looked” at the revolver in the other party’s hand.
Then, adjusting its emotions, it said, “He, he should have taken his team and entered ‘World Code -1’, and the reason for entering, from what I’ve learned from other containment subjects, is related to the death of a titan at the Bonfire Camp. This titan seemed to have ventured ‘Beyond the Known’ into the ‘Unknown Region,’ in search of something…
Ultimately, there was a problem, and he died, but he sent out his coordinates…
Rosen’s goal was to recover that thing, that is, it seems some unknown situations arose, I’m not clear on the details, but it probably didn’t end well, because his signature weapon is now in your hands…”
Beyond the Known, into the Unknown Region, a corporate titan’s fall, Rosen rushing off to recover…
It seems to match the information I had before.
Colin stroked his chin, thought for two seconds, then continued to ask, “Do you know what the recovered item is?”
“There’s no way for me to know, but I estimate it should be related to the ‘Ultimate of Everything’…”
“Ultimate of Everything?”
Colin muttered to himself, puzzled at first, then an idea sparked like a lightning bolt, connecting this unfamiliar term to something else.
“2044…”
An indescribable and sudden fear emerged.
Colin took a deep breath and then continued,
“2044, or rather, ‘Ultimate of Everything,’ what exactly is it?”

chapters.title: Chapter 542 - 542 432 The Conservative Faction thinks the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 542: Chapter 432: The Conservative Faction thinks the extremists are still too conservative…_1 Chapter 542: Chapter 432: The Conservative Faction thinks the extremists are still too conservative…_1 “It’s something you know exists, but can’t understand…”
“What it actually is, when it will arrive, there’s no precise consensus…”
“In this regard, I don’t know much, because only a very, very small subset of beings can observe it and prepare for it, and I am not included among them…”
“King of Madness” seemed to know a little, but not much.
‘A First Level Containment Subject that doesn’t know about the entity? Although it’s a middle-lower tier among First Level Containment Subjects, it is, after all, considered equivalent to an Ancient God.’
Colin frowned, feeling somewhat perplexed.
At that moment, it seemed he realized that Colin was not very satisfied with this answer.
“King of Madness” added:
“The company should know a bit more. If you want to understand, I suggest that after you go out, you ask some of the bonfire higher-ups above Level B. With your current Level C and as part of the talent program… you should be able to get an answer.”
Ah, this…
Colin’s expression remained unchanged, but he felt a strange mix of emotions: The other party had deduced his status as a “Flame Bearer” Reservist, but had not detected his actual level of authority at the moment?
After thinking it over, he still decided not to reveal his true identity.
After all, given the character the entity currently showed, who knows what other thoughts might arise after the revelation.
Of course, the most crucial reason was that he had already obtained the useful information he needed.
‘2044, it seems, isn’t particularly secretive within the company; one can learn about it once reaching a certain level.’
‘However, one needs to inquire starting from Level B…’
‘The only concern is whether there are any bona fide high-level B Level employees in the company right now.’
Colin stroked his chin, pondering for a few seconds.
“Lady Rabbit,” he always thought her level should be enough.
It’s just…
Although there’s no direct and exact evidence, Colin always felt her identity was somewhat sensitive.
He mentally shook his head, dismissing the thought, and looked at the other party: “Is this all you know about the matter?”
“Yes…”
Unfortunately, this information might as well be nonexistent… Colin asked the next question: “What do you know about Rosen?”
“Eh?” Hearing this question, the frequency of vibrations on “King of Madness” changed as if it had a puzzled expression, as if to say… you’re asking me about someone from the company?
“For some reasons, I don’t know much about him, so I need to learn from you.”
Colin casually remarked.
Are you someone who had been promoted from the outside and hadn’t gained much knowledge yet?
“King of Madness” thought for a moment. After being captured, he hadn’t known much about the outside world, so he wasn’t clear about the current company’s status. He only felt something was off, but a starving camel is still bigger than a horse after all…
He was completely unaware that these people were now incapable of even appointing a “Flame Bearer.”
He then spoke without giving it much more thought and told Colin all he knew about Rosen.
This was one of the high-level “Flame Bearers” that had once made countless lives and heretical civilizations tremble in fear.
His exact ranking was not clear to “King of Madness,” but he surmised it was at least at the B+ level, or possibly he could also obtain A Level when needed, although it seemed he was not a permanent resident…
Yet even so, Rosen was one of the few within the company who stood just below the “Big Three,” excessively powerful and with control over the fearsome “Primordial Fire” Corps…
He was also the primary frontline executor for a company giant of uncertain identity.
‘Sss… a B+ Level identity of a ‘Flame Bearer’.’
Colin was shook inwardly, thinking back to the death of the plain head in the small church—why did it feel off?
Compared to the dominating presence the other “Flame Bearers” left behind, this one was not as impressive…
‘Wait, the key with ‘Flame Bearers’ should be the heart; perhaps the brain was not that important. This means that even if this cunning fellow lost a ‘non-essential part,’ there was still considerable power.’
Colin felt a secret chill, suspecting that perhaps even that head was a ‘backup.’
Given their propensity for “holding back,” maybe they had many backups of their own body parts in their pockets.
If the head happened to fall off, they could just pick up a new one, and keep the old one for parts…
As long as the heart was intact, it was all good.
But decoding the information, he gained a vague understanding of the corporate upper echelon’s structure.
‘Non-permanent A level status. There’s a distinction in frequency for this tier? That means, the Big Three at the company’s summit are likely these permanent A Level employees or possibly even a higher S Level?’
‘But it seems the company’s ratings, evaluations of items, and various affairs all use A Level as the highest standard, with no S, SS, SSS, or SSSR rankings.’
‘So, A Level might be the highest internal rank within the company.’
Thought after thought flashed through Colin’s mind; he surmised that the so-called Big Three were indeed those permanent A Level individuals.
Of course, “King of Madness” didn’t have a very accurate understanding of the absolute high-level ranks either.
Information about these upper-tier authority levels, even if not classified, wouldn’t be something a captive about to be infused with humanity and forcibly transformed would know.
Colin then asked about other names, but unfortunately, most of the ones “King of Madness” mentioned were unknown to him, and the list didn’t include “Lady Rabbit,” the one he was most curious about.

chapters.title: Chapter 543 - 543 432 The Conservative Faction thinks the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 543: Chapter 432: The Conservative Faction thinks the extremists are still too conservative…_2 Chapter 543: Chapter 432: The Conservative Faction thinks the extremists are still too conservative…_2 Shaking his head, Colin asked about another matter of interest:
“‘Primordial Fire’ Corps?”
This was the second Corps name he had heard.
“Uh… It’s a Corps organized by a part of the ‘Flame Bearers,’ and although it’s not considered a large military legion, its reputation is by no means weak. It congregates a large number of ‘Flame Bearers’ from the entire company, exceeding a three-digit figure, as well as many company elites.”
Exceeding a three-digit figure, one hundred is also a three-digit figure, six or seven hundred is also a three-digit figure, and a large number must be at least a third or half of that…
So, theoretically speaking, there are at least two to three hundred ‘Flame Bearers,’ or even over a thousand?
If there were just three hundred, would that be too few?
No… it doesn’t seem too few, as each one of them is a master who can dominate an entire area of anomalies on their own.
At this moment, Colin, who was deep in thought, suddenly heard the “King of Savage Sound” cautiously say:
“I notice you seem to have not joined a Corps yet? If you don’t mind, I can offer you a little advice on the choice of Corps.”
Out of curiosity, Colin asked, “What advice?”
“If you’re going to join… I suggest, don’t join this one.”
“Hmm?” Colin uttered a puzzled hum.
“It’s a bit too dangerous. The people in this legion are very frightening ‘Conservatives.’ They are rather extreme in their actions, which has resulted in them having the most enemies. While they are powerful, they often enter the most dangerous areas to face upper-level entities and are a prime target for attacks, without equal…”
You must be mistaken, right? How can ‘Conservatives’ who take extremely drastic measures be ‘Conservatives’?
No, seeing the fear expressed by the body of the “King of Savage Sound,” Colin started to doubt…
This ‘Conservative Faction’ might not be the conventional conservative type.
Moreover, according to what he knew, Rosen seemed to have issued the ‘Extermination Order’ more than once during his mission.
‘Ah, it’s that kind of Conservative Faction that thinks the radicals are too conservative…’ Colin couldn’t help but criticize internally.
Of course, from a non-human standpoint, Rosen’s actions might seem excessive, but from a human perspective, it’s a different story…
Humans had suffered a great deal before their initial rise and had come close to extinction several times.
Is it a problem to be a little too harsh in one’s actions?
However, regarding the suggestion, Colin waved his hand, interrupting the other party’s subsequent speech, “Are you teaching me how to conduct my business?”
“No, no…”
“Alright, which Corps I join is not for you to know. Tell me the names of the other Corps.”
As for joining the ‘Primordial Fire’ Corps, Colin didn’t have any particular thoughts on it, given his limited understanding and not having received any invitation or such.
Soon after, he learned of several other Corps names from the “King of Savage Sound.”
“Primordial Fire,” “Zoo,” “Radiant Angel,” “God Kingdom”…
Colin said in surprise, “Only four?”
“Not just… But in each sector of the galaxy, there are specific Corps stationed. I only know the ones in this sector, and the ones I have actually come into contact with are only the ‘Radiant Angel’ and ‘Primordial Fire’ Corps…”
As he spoke, the “King of Savage Sound” seemed to recall his past: “Back when I was active in this galaxy, then the ‘World Code’ arrived, I had clashed with the ‘Radiant Angel’ Corps stationed here, and then I retreated without a clear victory… ”
“Later on, when I heard that the ‘Bonfire Company’ had undergone major changes, filled with sinful thoughts, I descended upon ‘World Code-334’ to take one of the authorities that I could integrate.”
Saying this, his entire “person” displayed a sense of horror, as if he had seen some great terror.
And influenced by his emotions, the region began to vibrate uncontrollably, as though on the brink of collapse and an impending earthquake.
You freaking… Colin raised his eyebrows, snapped his fingers, and a burst of flame erupted with a “pop.”
The “King of Savage Sound” calmed down.
“What’s going on?” Colin asked.
He then learned that this creature, along with several of his kind, had just penetrated the defenses of the “World Code” and secured the item, which hadn’t even warmed up in their grasp, when they encountered Rosen, who had just begun his retrieval mission.
No, to be more precise, he had encountered a formidable team led by Rosen, and supplemented by five “Flame Bearers.”
Then, as expected, there were no further surprises.
Upon hearing this, Colin could only silently lament that this guy’s luck was indeed terrible.
At that time, it had been held captive, thrown into the “Containment Divine Kingdom” specially prepared by Rosen.
And the condition for its release was…
After completing a series of transformations, it must acknowledge itself as human and voluntarily sign the special Level One recruitment contract offered by Rosen under fair and friendly conditions.
After Colin asked around, the general information he got was…
The content of the contract included an obligation to work without rest or sleep, provided only with room and board, and no salary, for a duration of three thousand years.
Besides that, there were generally assessments every six months on human values, cognition, and so on…
And if it committed any offenses during the period of labor, there would be severe punishment.
