Once the contract was signed, it would be bound by some “agreements”; regret would not be an option afterward.
Of course, if it accidentally died during the work period, its characteristics would be forcibly reclaimed, made into an item, and it would continue to work.
Upon completion of the sentence, oh no, upon successful completion of the work period, there was a certain probability that some leftover countermeasures would be used to reconstruct its consciousness.
This method seemed to involve keeping a part of the “consciousness” in advance and making another body if the original was lost…
Theoretically speaking, Colin thought it resembled cloning but was much more complicated.
But if it died too thoroughly, and even that part of the “brain” was destroyed, then all was lost—the company would thank it for voluntarily donating its exceptional characteristics to create a new item.
“‘Father of the Ocean’s’ eight hundred-year contract is nothing compared to this, huh? Is this the difference between a war prisoner and actively recruiting?” Colin mused, clicking his tongue in awe. However, regretfully, his spiritual intuition told him that with his current D Level status, he had no authority to sign that thing on behalf of the company, even if he had, the risks would be huge…
Otherwise, he would have snagged a super enforcer directly.
Afterward, Colin curiously freeloaded some other miscellaneous knowledge.
For instance, what were the deciding factors for a high-level containment subject.
“Level 2 Containment Subjects aren’t finely categorized. The strong ones are very powerful, capable of changing the landscape of an ordinary planet, while the weak ones are very weak, probably not much better than me.”
“And, according to the company’s classification, a First Level Containment Subject generally refers to an entity with the minimum capability to inflict a devastating blow to an ordinary planet (taking Earth as the benchmark) and its civilization. There are detailed subcategories like lower, low-mid, mid, mid-upper, and upper…”
“Of course, this is assuming that there’s no one to restrain them.”
“Each subcategory marks a significant difference in strength. Among them, the Upper-Level First-Class Containment Entities stand out from the rest by a lot and are sometimes called Super First Class. They’re the intermediary level between ‘0’ and ‘1’, albeit in very small numbers.”
“Level ‘0’ Containment Subjects, besides being extremely powerful, often possess certain rule-based traits. Even the company finds it difficult to properly assess these entities. Some special forms of Level 0 entities allow anyone who understands and is lucky enough to follow the rules, even a common person or a child, to easily survive under their influence. Conversely, even a B Level or stronger ‘Flame Bearer’ might face mortal danger…”
“So, to deal with this level, you typically need to follow the rules.”
Colin now had a clearer understanding of these entities in his mind and then continued:
“By the way, do you know about ‘Hunger’?”
Hearing this, the “King of Madness” seemed to shudder: “I do, I was consumed by it along with the entire ‘World Code-334’, then contained. That thing is legendary in the ‘Containment Realm’ because it’s said to have initially not been highly ranked, but under the company’s control, it kept integrating and eventually became Level ‘0’.”
A man-made Level “0” creature? But consuming an entire world, that’s formidable… Colin was startled, not expecting this entity to be so fearsome in the hands of the actual boss, Rosen.
“Can you sense it now?”
“I can’t, nor dare to; it will devour your ‘premonitions’ and then find its way here. You should be fine, though, because you’re under the implicit protection of the ‘Bonfire Company’; even if you initiate contact, you just have to disconnect in time. But for me, even if it’s just a fragment or theoretically weaker than me, it can consume my current state.”
The “King of Madness” seemed to realize what the person in front of him was thinking and quickly explained.
However, pondering on something, he paused and added: “Of course, if you’re willing to release me and remove the control…”

chapters.title: Chapter 544 - 544 433 It Awakens in My Brain. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 544: Chapter 433 “It” Awakens in My Brain. _1 Chapter 544: Chapter 433 “It” Awakens in My Brain. _1 Let you out? My, my, we’re getting to the point where true intentions come to light, aren’t we?
Colin suddenly became alert.
At that moment, he heard the other party continue speaking.
“In my sufficiently intact status, there would be a chance to contend with ‘Hunger’ in its incomplete status. Otherwise, even separated by the ‘Containment God Kingdom,’ there is a probability that I would be devoured by it for my certain traits.”
“The rules of a Level ‘0’ Containment Subject, at times, can disregard many things.”
“Last time, I sensed that an entity had fallen from a First Level Containment Subject to a lower tier and was devoured by ‘Hunger.’ Not long after, the power of the ‘Bonfire’ descended, and everything was resolved…”
…
‘A lower-tier First Level Containment Subject?’
Colin heard this description and quickly recalled what the other was referring to.
“Tyrant.”
That huge creature with the body of a wolf covered in blood-red fur.
Its size was abnormally massive, and its strength equally terrifying. Merely by walking, it could cause mountains to shake and the ground to tremble, then it gave “0-09 ‘Hunger'” a full meal.
At first, Colin had thought “Hunger” was probably on par with “Rage.”
Because his strength observation at that time…
Both appeared to be high-ranking existences whose peaks were hard to see.
But now that he understood enough, he could only say that no matter how much “Tyrant” struggled, even without his interference, the outcome wouldn’t have changed much. It was just a matter of dying sooner or later.
However, dying later might have led a whole bunch of people to die with it.
Thankfully, Colin managed to cut his losses in time, breaking off the fingers that clung to the cliff’s edge, sending the entity on its way.
Avoiding more personnel perishing alongside it…
And incidentally sharing many Gold Coins (Tyrannical Talent, etc.) that burst forth from it with company employees.
‘But, seeing the attitude of this “King of Mad Sounds,” does he think it was me who contained “Hunger”? Looking back now, the “Hunger” from back then must have reached beyond First Level Containment Subject…’
‘If I had the power to deal with it alone, I wouldn’t be here wasting words with you.’
Colin muttered to himself, then heard the “King of Mad Sounds” cautiously say:
“If you could let me out, then the next time you find a fragment of Hunger, let me assist you, and I am certain your reclamation of it will be even more successful…”
Not waiting for the “King of Mad Sounds” to finish, Colin waved his hand: “Let’s skip that part, move on to the next question.”
“Alright, you ask…” The “King of Mad Sounds,” though disappointed, dared not show it.
Curious, Colin spoke up: “What exactly is this ‘Containment God Kingdom’? What’s inside?”
“This… This is a unique and independent spatial dimension constructed by Rosen and others through their own power. It’s specifically designed to contain entities of certain value or those that cannot be killed quickly… Inside, time is twisted, space is segmented, chaos reigns, and the ‘fate’ of all things is controlled. Once captured inside, it’s basically impossible to escape on your own…”
As he spoke, the “King of Mad Sounds” seemed to realize something and hurriedly added: “I… I only have this minor chance to communicate with the outside world because I earnestly wish to become human and atone for the wrongs I’ve done. In my heart, there’s only the Bonfire Company as my sun…”
“And besides, it might seem like I can talk to you, but in reality… The most I can do is talk to you. I can’t sense other lives unless they are powerful enough, like that time with the lower-tier entity.”
After finishing speaking and noticing that the company employee enshrouded in flames had no intention of pursuing further, he breathed a sigh of relief.
“As for other entities inside… I’m not very familiar with them, because within ‘Containment God Kingdom,’ everything is both unified and isolated, with each Containment Subject remaining unseen by the others…”
Listening to his explanation, Colin roughly understood what this thing was.
But how exactly it was achieved, that remained unclear.
Having briefly grasped the concept, Colin thought for a while and continued to inquire: “Do you know what caused the ‘Plague of Magic Fog’?”
“The ‘Plague of Magic Fog’?”
The unique frequency changes composing the “King of Mad Sounds” seemed to express confusion.
Almost forgot, that seems like a local term, Colin thought for a moment and sent a related “Inspiration” across.
“This thing…”
After interpreting the “Inspiration,” the “King of Mad Sounds” for the first time showed uncertainty in his speech:
“Its cause is a bit complex, like pus leaking out from a pile of high-ranking bodies after they have rotted together…”
“Pus leaking from a pile of high-ranking bodies after they’ve rotted together?”
Colin was stunned by this explanation.
Before now, he had thought this thing might have been an invasion by some kind of high-dimensional being.
But to hear the “King of Mad Sounds” tell it, it seemed to be just pus from somewhere’s pile of rotting corpses?
“Do you have more specifics?” Colin pressed further.
Regrettably, the “King of Mad Sounds” shook his head, offering an unclear response.
“Of course, if you could release me…”
That again? Don’t even think about it.
Colin decisively waved his hand: “It’s not time for you to be let out yet.”
He didn’t reply with something like “the knowledge you’ve given isn’t enough” as tempting the entity with what could be enough wouldn’t be wise.
Better to cut off his expectations now to avoid too much hopefulness.
However, he couldn’t cut it off too completely, as that might provoke some retaliation.
After a pause and before a sense of disappointment arose from the other party, Colin added:
“I know you’re anxious, but don’t rush; let me finish speaking… If you cooperate well with the company’s work and stand out in your performance, there’s still a chance for you to come out…”

chapters.title: Chapter 545 - 545 433 It Awakens in My Brain. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 545: Chapter 433 “It” Awakens in My Brain. _2 Chapter 545: Chapter 433 “It” Awakens in My Brain. _2 “Of course, of course, as long as you need it, I will definitely cooperate!”
“Then that’s settled, I will come over again in a few days.”
Colin felt that after proving his strength, these anomalies, they were quite communicative.
Of course, he knew that if he wasn’t strong enough,
this guy would definitely have a different attitude.
After saying this, Colin indicated he would come again after some time and hinted to the other party that as long as he worked hard and did well, there was definitely a bright future ahead…
The company wouldn’t mistreat any loyal employee.
Then, Colin asked about the whereabouts of the “Human Patchwork Monster” that had once stayed here, thinking about how to capture it.
His “Fusion Card: Smiling Mountain of Corpses” was still eagerly awaiting an upgrade.
But upon hearing this, “King of Savage Sound” shook his head, indicating either that creature had some unique way to stay hidden, or it was too weak…
Most likely not even at the “Sub-Subordinate Level One Containment Subject” rank.
At most Level 2.
So, there was no way to sense it.
Of course, he slyly suggested that if he could be released…
then, given some time to restore his peak status, he could quickly observe the world’s vibrations and sounds through his authority and then ferret out that “Human Patchwork Monster.”
‘Wishful thinking…’
Colin ignored him, pitying inwardly, hands clasped behind his back, slowly heading toward the underground labyrinth’s exit.
“King of Madness” followed behind, wanting to stop him but instinctively fearing the flames.
“By the way, one last question, what do you know about ‘Red Moon’?”
Before leaving, Colin planned to scrounge one last bit of information.
“‘Red Moon’?” “King of Madness” couldn’t quite recall what that was at first.
“Yes, ‘Red Moon’ Mother.” Colin added a bit more information and threw in some memory inspirations.
“Crimson Mother!?”
“King of Madness” shrieked an unfamiliar name, the frequency of its vibrations nearly exploding on the spot, appearing as if it wanted to shrink back into the “Containment Divine Kingdom” to hide.
Was his reaction this big… Colin shook his head to himself.
After a while, “King of Madness” said timidly:
“She, from the moment of her birth, was an exceedingly exalted and terrifying entity. To call her ‘God above Gods’ would not be too much, for she originates from… Ah!!”
“Get out, throw it out, this memory inspiration wants to awaken in my mind, ah ah!!”
“I don’t want to remember Her ah ah ah ah ah——”
The scream stopped abruptly.
The vibrations that constituted “King of Madness” exploded on the spot.
The terrifying vibration swept across all directions, causing the entire underground area to shake nonstop, as if it could collapse at any moment…
Colin was taken aback, initially thinking the creature intended to sneak attack.
Flames erupted violently on his body, entering a state of combat readiness…
At this moment, Colin’s eyes narrowed, noticing amidst the shaking surroundings, strands of crimson emerging.
He reached out, and the intense flames rushed forward, completely consuming them.
Seconds later, the vibration ceased abruptly, and “King of Madness” reappeared, looking much weaker.
He had been careless, focusing only on “Crimson Mother” and forgetting to guard against another, nearly getting invaded and affected. However, fortunately, there was no serious issue now.
After a pause, he continued to speak:
“I’m sorry, can we not talk about Her? With my current state, rashly delving deep in discussing Her could likely draw Her attention. This time, She probably hasn’t noticed this place, but next time…”
Simply discussing Her in depth could potentially attract Her?
This is the level of a “Level 0”?
Hearing this, Colin fell silent for a few seconds, then eventually waved his hand, indicating the end of the current topic.
At the same time, he also consciously put away any further inquiries in his mind.
This… was knowledge he was not meant to have.
Shortly after completely leaving the tunnel, Colin breathed a sigh of relief and suddenly realized why some in the “company” were so eager to embed “humanity” into anomalies.
Because with “humanity,” they were indeed easy to coax.
Colin recalled that if what he had encountered was a primitive First Level Containment Subject, it probably would not have been possible to converse at all.
It would have been a bloody conflict right from the start.
“It’s like the feeling of pulling an enemy into a familiar domain and then crushing them in reduced dimensions…”
With that thought, Colin looked back and saw the human miniature created by “King of Madness,” which was still standing motionless.
‘This guy probably didn’t expect that with my current authority, I couldn’t lift the restrictions anyway.’
Colin murmured to himself inside.
On his way, he hadn’t sensed any company clearance that could be triggered.
That either meant there was none, or his current clearance wasn’t high enough.
Or it required going to the edge of the “Containment Divine Kingdom.”
He’d be crazy to do something so dangerous.
If the other party saw his real rank, it would probably lead to another round of troubles.
“It feels great to plunder knowledge and then leave.”
Without lingering, Colin used the domain bonfire as a coordinate, sprung forth, and flew away from this place.
And “King of Madness,” who watched Colin leave, didn’t retreat right away but rather pondered with some curiosity.
He always felt this Level C Employee seemed to know suspiciously little?
Something wasn’t quite right…
…
While hurrying on his way, Colin also quickly digested the knowledge he had just acquired.
“Overall, the knowledge is about the high-level structure; it doesn’t seem very applicable at the moment, and I can clearly sense that while this guy claims to cooperate, he definitely held a lot back.”

chapters.title: Chapter 546 - 546 433 It Awakens in My Brain. _3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 546: Chapter 433 “It” Awakens in My Brain. _3 Chapter 546: Chapter 433 “It” Awakens in My Brain. _3 As the thought flickered, Colin couldn’t help feeling that his own fist wasn’t big enough.
Otherwise, he would have made this guy spit out everything he should have said!
Another two hours later, after ensuring he wasn’t marked, Colin returned to his territory.
At this moment, various tasks within the territory were still being carried out in an orderly manner by the employees; however, after seven days of continuous work, a hint of fatigue surfaced on their faces, each one looking as if they had smeared the same kind of mystical patterns found on pillars, surrounded by an aura of mysticism.
Seeing this, Colin’s kindness overflowed, and he declared that the status of the work positions was not urgent.
With the last three hours of the countdown approaching, they could lay down their work and take a three-hour break.
Upon hearing this, the employees’ enthusiasm for work surged once again.
Standing at the top of the small chapel, bathed in the light of the bonfire, Colin scanned the territory several times over to ensure that nothing out of the ordinary had crept in during his absence, and only then did he allow himself to relax.
“Big brother, want something to eat? I just roasted this…” Little Red approached him with a freshly roasted mouse.
“Thank you.” Colin didn’t refuse and reached out to pat her on the head.
Seeing that Big Brother had accepted the food she offered, Little Red smiled, and then the two of them sat at the door of the small chapel, with her chattering incessantly about her own observations during the days Colin was catching up on lessons.
Colin gnawed on the mouse while listening, everything peaceful and indifferent.
Yet, more than the things she talked about, when Colin occasionally looked at Little Red, he observed her eyes more intently.
‘Now that her emotions have stabilized, they don’t turn red as much.’
Colin inexplicably breathed a sigh of relief.
From the very first encounter, he knew that this little girl possessed something special.
But what was strange was that even now, Colin still couldn’t quite comprehend what exactly it was.
Even the Saintess couldn’t notice the problem with Little Red when her emotions were not agitated.
‘According to the Saintess, Little Red might have some special recessive bloodline; her difficult growth environment is probably causing some loss of control. Paying a little more attention should suffice.’
‘As for more details, we’ll have to wait for her rescue operation to finish before going and searching the archives in the ‘Light’ Holy Land.’
As the thought turned, Colin also remembered that he once asked Little Red’s friends and learned that when she was in grave danger and extremely agitated, some kind of tainted power would erupt from her.
But after the eruption, those who had offended her seemed to perish instantly.
And turn into a pile of dust…
Or, the things she stared at intently would also inexplicably die from organ failure.
Little Red seemed aware of this, which is why she blinked frequently.
She wouldn’t stare at him often…
However, in truth, Little Red’s concern was entirely unnecessary, as Colin, after observation, was fairly certain that merely making direct gaze contact had little effect on him.
‘Though the eye color has a sense of déjà vu, it probably has no relation to the ‘Red Moon’; the form this power takes is completely different.’
Colin ruled out the scariest option, “related to the Red Moon.”
If it had really been related to the “Red Moon,” those people wouldn’t just drop dead or turn into a pile of dust.
Instead, there would be a massive uprising of internal organs, scattering all over the sky.
Thinking this, Colin felt somewhat relieved.
.
.
.
ps: Will catch up with the updates after the immortal update.

chapters.title: Chapter 547 - 547 434 The Points Required to Repair the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 547: Chapter 434 The Points Required to Repair the Golden Card_1 Chapter 547: Chapter 434 The Points Required to Repair the Golden Card_1 “Dong dong dong~”
The distant and ancient chime of the clock faded away with the dense fog surrounding me…
Colin opened his eyes and saw the familiar ceiling.
He took a deep breath, slowly sat up, shook his head, and looked around. Everything inside was bright.
It was three o’clock in the afternoon now.
As usual, he had spent seven days in “World Code-13.”
But on this side, it was merely three hours.
Colin didn’t rush to take any action, but waited a while longer for that sense of daze in his mind to fully dissipate before skillfully taking out the parchment from the side and glanced at it twice…
Then, his brows furrowed slightly.
“Troublesome, just a few thousand Points, no Item Extraction Ticket.”
Looking at the task reward, Colin couldn’t help but sigh.
However, he wasn’t too surprised by this situation since it seemed he really didn’t do much this time entering.
Of course, for Colin himself, his gains were actually not small.
For example, with Shana’s assistance, he had a preliminary grasp on further applications of “Bonfire.”
Next, he also found the human, oh, the disgrace of a First Level Containment Subject, the “King of Savage Sound,” and from it, learned a lot of past secrets, which in other respects, gave him a deeper understanding of the company.
But… these gains were not highly valued by the company.
“Well then, over six thousand Points, plus three Silver Task Certificates, barely enough to scrape by and better than nothing.”
“It seems like getting any rewards from ‘World Code-13’ next time won’t be easy either; I’ll have to either solve the ‘Plague of Magic Fog’ or find the remaining unknown fragments of ‘Hunger’.”
“With the Saintess unable to resolve the ‘Plague of Magic Fog,’ I don’t even want to think about it. Too difficult.”
“As for the fragments of ‘Hunger’…”
Colin raised his hand and rubbed his chin. Based on his previous interaction with Shana, it seemed she had some methods?
But since she didn’t explicitly say it, he also didn’t know the exact situation.
Without further guessing about this matter, Colin, sitting cross-legged on the bed, first asked the Little Maid to prepare some food, then casually released the restless “Yukionna” to move about freely, but not to leave the room. After that, he continued to browse the inner hall’s parchment.
“Get on with whatever needs to be done, it doesn’t seem like anything important has happened…”
Colin stared for a while.
Except for seeing that people praising “World Code-13” had increased, making many suspect that a new “virus” had invaded, he found nothing else unusual.
He browsed through the company’s internal group chat for a while, seeing it as a way to lighten the mood, and then shut it down. After that, he checked his current internal company progress.
“Wait another week, I can inject the third dose of Gene Compensation Medicine, and apparently, a regular event task cycle will open up. After completing it, I can proceed to D+, then embark on the D Level promotion trials…”
The usual way is to wait for a C Level position to open up after obtaining the qualification.
From C Level upwards, positions are limited; only when they become available will there be room…
Even if one has all the necessary elements and the strength to match, one must wait earnestly for the opportunity.
“However, it seems this isn’t a big problem for me. When my official level is promoted from Level 5 to Level 6, and after figuring out the situation with the ‘Book of Fate,’ ‘Lady Rabbit’ will help me solve it…”
Thinking this, Colin couldn’t help but feel how comfortable it is to have connections at the top of the company.
A small show of power.
Can solve quite a lot of problems.
Of course, calling it a backdoor isn’t quite accurate, after all, these are opportunities exchanged for risking one’s life.
If one’s foundation isn’t strong enough, even with the opportunity to act capriciously, it wouldn’t be one’s turn.
At that moment, Colin smelled the aroma of food coming from the kitchen and put away the parchment. He got out of bed and started pondering his official level situation.
Compared to his progress in the company, his promotion speed in the official ranking was undoubtedly quite slow.
According to Old Master Wu, this was because many of his achievements couldn’t be credited to him as they didn’t fit his “true identity” as a Level 5 Personnel.
After all, which Level 5 personnel in the world could directly confront a “Chosen of God” or similar individuals?
How could that still be considered Level 5?
Forcibly attributing the corresponding events to his record could provoke some trouble from the “Book of Fate.”
Colin didn’t know the details, but since it involved a terrifying object, he felt it was better to avoid trouble if possible.
So he had to slowly accrue customary merits by dealing with various anomalies around him and steadily climb the ranks.
However, Xu Duojin and the others had mentioned during a late-night talk that if he managed the ‘God Descent’ event involving the ‘Starlight Maiden’ as a catalyst well, as the provider of the “information,”
Colin could take this opportunity to be promoted to Level 6 official personnel and gain access to the “Book of Fate.”
Then he could complete the task “Lady Rabbit” had entrusted to him early on.
Of course, he also needed to do some “routine peripheral clean-up” tasks from time to time.
“Damn, I’ve only ever heard of laundering money, never that merit needs to be laundered too.”
Colin sat at the dining table, eating the meal prepared by the Little Maid while muttering to himself.
About an hour later, Colin leisurely finished his meal and drink.
While the Little Maid was clearing up, he looked up at the time and planned to play a couple of rounds with “C Level Elder Brother” to consolidate his learning outcomes, then sleep a bit to rejuvenate—mixing work with relaxation…

chapters.title: Chapter 548 - 548 434 The Points Required to Repair the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 548: Chapter 434 The Points Required to Repair the Golden Card_2 Chapter 548: Chapter 434 The Points Required to Repair the Golden Card_2 But at that moment, he suddenly had an inkling and pulled out his phone from his pocket.
It was a message from Xu Duojin.
“I just finished eating and here comes your message… nicely timed.”
Colin pursed his lips, opened the message to read it, and found nothing special. It essentially said that the transaction for tomorrow, January 4th, was almost ready.
By tomorrow morning, someone would come to pick him up, and then he could proceed with the execution.
“The location is still Base No. 5, but security will probably be much tighter after the last breach. After all, there will be hundreds of containment subjects on offer this time, and one slip-up could lead to a regional disaster.”
Colin nodded, not too worried about this.
Given the “Rat”‘s usual MO, it was unlikely it would dare to face him head-on right now.
Because it wasn’t just the officials who were watching it.
From the content of the letters “Lady Rabbit” had given him before, Colin estimated that if it really came down to a confrontation, “Lady Rabbit,” who seemed constrained or perhaps had some reservations, was quite likely to take direct action.
“But these guys are as tricky as snakes to pin down.”
Just as Colin was digesting this information, he saw Xu Duojin had sent some other things.
It was about those “Awakeners.”
The other party was asking him if he had any further information on these people, as they’d found the number of such individuals appeared to be rising steadily…
At present, they had already caught nearly a hundred.
But they were far from done.
Every few days, they’d come across several more, more numerous than leeks.
Xu Duojin’s message read, “About these people, one miraculous thing they all seem to share is a personality difference but an essentially strong egocentric trait. Then, under fixations of ‘revenge’ or ‘becoming stronger,’ they’d go do various things… In other words, they might feel like the protagonists of the world due to some kind of guidance or influence.”
“Of course, that’s not the key point. The key is that as they grow stronger, their mental state becomes more and more unstable, often lashing out violently over trivial issues.
“And then they themselves end up losing control and turn into monsters…”
Ah, this…
The previous batch of “protagonists” are still toiling in the Other World for reformation…
Seeing Xu Duojin’s description, Colin was reminded of those several “Heroes” who were enthusiastically set on changing the world.
“That’s too much, why target these people for bullying?”
“However, I only know that their abilities seem to be linked to the company, beyond that, I don’t have much more information.”
“As for the mental instability, that’s not surprising. After all, the company’s products are meant to be used together, and these people having talents and whatnot crammed into their bodies to forcefully symbiose would be abnormal if they were mentally stable.”
Talents, skills, company tools… if ordinary people could just casually use these things,
then why would they tirelessly do missions, strive for performance, and drink Gene Compensation Medicine?
Besides, the nature of the employees is also an important factor.
After pondering for a moment, Colin edited some of the information he currently knew and informed Xu Duojin, then after making sure that this guy had nothing else, he took the initiative to inquire about the movements of those heretic forces.
“At the moment, it seems that because they are under the protection of the ‘company,’ many heretic forces are unable to see the details of this ‘God Descent’ through prophecies, divinations and the like, leading them to believe that something is indeed likely to descend this time.”
“As a result, almost all mobile heretic forces have started exploring the ‘City at the Lake’s Bottom,’ swearing to protect human territory from the contamination of wicked Outer Gods…”
“Just from what we currently definitely know, there are as many as fifty organizations from around the world of all sorts that have now mostly banded together.”
Seeing Xu Duojin’s words, Colin couldn’t help but tear up, moved by the determination of these people to defend the world.
Moved to the point where he couldn’t help but slightly curl the corners of his mouth…
“It seems this wave is destined to be a bountiful harvest. Many of these heretic forces aren’t very strong, but the status of the items in their hands isn’t low. If we pick them up, we’ll probably make a tidy sum…”
“This way, my Golden Card repair plan can also be put on the agenda…”
Based on the points required to repair the orange equipment “Revolver Reverser.”
Colin estimated that the Golden Card would likely need several hundred thousand points, which made him feel a suffocation in his chest…
It was like when he was working part-time earning a salary of five thousand yuan, yet faced with the shock of a three million yuan house price.
But the difference is…
This time, there was actually a chance of getting the Golden Card repaired.
It’s just a bit life-threatening.
Of course, even if he could repair them, he could only choose one of them and couldn’t repair all at the same time.
Both “Force Repulsion” and “Time Freeze” were very useful.
He couldn’t decide which one to choose for half a day.
“Forget it, I’ll wait until the points are in hand and then make a decision based on the situation,” he concluded.
Colin ended his daydream and checked his phone again, confirming that aside from Qin Chuan asking him when he would go to work to lead everyone to clean up the nearby anomalies, there was nothing else, so he lay back down on the bed.
He began the sparring session with the C Level Elder Brother.
…
“What?!”
The C Level Elder Brother, fabricated by the copy, spun around quickly, dodging a fatal blow aimed at his vitals.
Still, he could feel a charred hole, reeking of barbecued meat, burned right beneath his right chest rib.
Inside, his large and small intestines writhed—if his reflexes hadn’t been quick, if he hadn’t used his strength to contain it…
They would have probably burst forth…
“Damn it, I finally breached this guy’s defenses!”
From a distance, Colin’s eyes lit up, having fought normally for so long.
This was the first time!
This way of using flames was indeed correct!
With his vitality, he controlled every thread of flame, achieving precise operations, while also forcibly infusing the “Bonfire” with spirit and making it swirl inward…
The resultant destructive effect was quite powerful.
As long as it hit, even the C Level Elder Brother, who specialized in his own foundational abilities, couldn’t handle it.
However, even wounded so severely, the C Level Elder Brother’s movements did not stop. He kept his eyes on Colin, who was enhanced by the orange-red firelight, reached out, and pulled a 1.9-meter-long blade from the air.
Then, he took a step forward, and his figure disappeared on the spot.
Almost at the moment he vanished, dozens of blades that seemed to tear through space flew at him from all directions.
Seeing this, Colin, already somewhat exhausted, braced himself and used various methods to forcibly block most of them.
Unfortunately…
Due to the continuous fighting, his strength and vitality were rapidly depleting.
In a moment of carelessness, he was still cut by what seemed like a hair-like space slash.
The next instant, countless fine cracks appeared all over Colin’s body. Although he tried to control various powers to stitch them back up and continue the fight…
Unfortunately, starting from his navel, his upper and lower body began to separate.
He turned into 2.5 Colin, collapsing onto the ground.
Blood and a mass of steaming organs spilled out from the break in his upper body.
However, even with such an injury…
If there was no follow-up cut, he could stuff his organs back in and have the Little Maid or “Fire Tree” help with stitching, and after a while, he could revive himself and continue fighting.
Regrettably…
The C Level Elder Brother, now in a “frenzied” state, didn’t seem to have any intentions of letting him hang on.
A barrage of attacks followed immediately…
Colin’s body, lying on the ground, exploded further into countless pieces of flesh, thoroughly ending this self-selected trial copy.
…
“F*ck… did he really go so damn hard this time?”
As soon as Colin opened his eyes, he felt as if his entire body was aching unbearably.
.
.
.
Will update and then revise

chapters.title: Chapter 549 - 549 435 Only the Containment Subject is
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 549: Chapter 435 Only the “Containment Subject” is Unhappy with the Trade…_1 Chapter 549: Chapter 435 Only the “Containment Subject” is Unhappy with the Trade…_1 “Huff…”
A clouded white breath slowly exhaled.
As the pain on his body quickly subsided,
Colin finally felt much better.
In the past, when he fought with C Level Elder Brothers, his head was either explosively bashed by a punch or chopped off by a blade; his usual deaths were quite straightforward – no pain, certainly not as wretched as this time…
“This time I’ve reached a new height–I can break through his defense with my own methods now.”
“If I’m lucky, after breaking through his defense and combining various tools, a needle stabbed into a weak spot could mean that I, during a normal outburst, also have the chance to defeat him…”
“Unfortunately, the characters in the copy are nevertheless just characters in a copy, although the imitation has been very successful, there’s still something missing; it seems as though every aspect is slightly deficient.”
Colin couldn’t help but sigh; he figured that once he became a little more familiar with his powers and techniques,
he should be able to break through this copy…
Although beating the opponent would require using a lot of equipment, and comparably speaking, there was a sense it was somewhat an unfair victory over a C Level Elder Brother, but it was also the C Level Elder Brother who had said,
the use and mastery of tools is also a part of one’s own strength…
No one would be foolish enough, when confronting a tiger or a lion face to face, to throw away the gun in their hands and compare something like “physical strength” with the opponent…
Such people in the company, if not on the front line, would be fine.
But if they’re on the front line, most likely they wouldn’t survive three missions before dying a violent death…
After sitting for a while longer, Colin took a shower, dried off, then returned to his room and fell asleep.
Though his body wasn’t particularly tired, there was still a slight mental fatigue.
The night quickly passed…
The next morning, right after Colin finished a bowl of braised Large Intestine with roast goose Shahe fen, he saw Qin Chuan and others’ car parked on the side.
“Sigh…”
He drank down the soup, wiped his mouth with a tissue, and stood up to walk over.
“Speaking of which, with my current identity, continuing to live in a densely populated district doesn’t seem quite appropriate; I need to find a new place. Ah, to experience what it’s like to live in Big Haus? The only issue with moving is that I wouldn’t be able to eat this kind of breakfast anymore…”
Colin looked at Fuji Pork Knuckle Rice Restaurant, which had been open for many years offering breakfast, lunch, and dinner, with considerable reluctance.
Though with his abilities, it would be no problem to take them along and provide for them as they moved.
But, that unspoken feeling seemed a bit too much.
“Today we’re heading to… Base No. 5?” Qin Chuan bought the bill and then came over to ask.
“Right.”
Colin nodded and, while walking towards the car parked on the roadside, he said,
“It shouldn’t take too long; if nothing else comes up these next few days, I’m fairly free until at least the 10th and can take you guys to clear out the surrounding area.”
Qin Chuan’s eyes lit up as he quickly replied, “Great, no problem.”
Although, with Colin there, clearing the surrounding anomalies, if he didn’t deliberately preserve them, the whole process was like going for a stroll, with little participation, but correspondingly, their lives were virtually worry-free…
And most crucially, even though they might be not working too hard, the rewards were indeed going to be issued.
At this moment, he couldn’t help but look at Hu Zheng lying in the car, feeling a bit of regret.
How good it would have been to choose “Fate Propeller” back then…
With “Fate Propeller,” he could be working towards Level 5 right now, instead of just creeping from Level 3 towards 4.
Colin, walking in front, was unaware of their thoughts. He opened the car door, got in, and they had a smooth ride. About an hour later, the vehicle left the city and stopped in a secluded area.
Colin alighted alone and, after a few simple checks, boarded a helicopter.
Qin Chuan and the others waited there…
Shortly after, when Colin arrived at the periphery of Base Number Five, he immediately felt that the atmosphere was much more severe.
A large number of fully armed soldiers with some extraordinary power enhancements patrolled everywhere.
“The forces guarding this time have increased a lot compared to before,”
Standing below, Colin sensed around and couldn’t help but narrow his eyes.
Compared to before, he could actually sense the presence of four Eighth Level Personnel in this area.
“Heh, to ensure the smooth progress of the transaction, we’ve pulled two high-level combat personnel from nearby provinces to protect this place,” a familiar voice that was somewhat aged came from the side.
Colin turned to look and saw Xu Duojin appearing out of nowhere, like a ghost.
However, Colin was not unfamiliar with this ability of the other party: “It’s evident you’ve taken this very seriously this time.”
Although, with his strength, Eighth Level Personnel… weren’t really a significant help anymore.
But having them is always better than not.
“Of course, otherwise if we have a repeat of the last incident, we really can’t afford it; after all, what we’re bringing out this time includes many mechanism creatures that are very troublesome to deal with; if they escape, they’re hard to recover. Haha, at the necessary moment, Old Master Wu’s gaze will be upon us,”
Xu Duojin laughed and then made a gesture, indicating to follow.
Old Master Wu, huh… Colin thought, and walked over.
Meanwhile, he couldn’t help but sense the aura of the Eighth Level Personnel discreetly and, based on what he knew, he re-compared the strength of official Eighth Level Personnel and the company’s personnel—
It was certain that these people were stronger than most of the company’s D Level Personnel listed on paper, but they were clearly a big step weaker than C Level Personnel.
Even the few C Level Personnel who seemed to be in “civilian” roles in the starship elevator at that time were much stronger than them.
After some quick calculations…

chapters.title: Chapter 550 - 550 435 Only the Containment Subject is
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 550: Chapter 435 Only the “Containment Subject” is Unhappy with the Trade…_2 Chapter 550: Chapter 435 Only the “Containment Subject” is Unhappy with the Trade…_2 ‘Almost on par with some Elite D Level,’
Colin pondered for a moment before roughly drawing this crude comparison.
Nowadays, the company’s D Level staff, on the whole, were almost on a par with Level 7 Official Personnel; some were weaker while others stronger, with specific variations depending on the individual…
However, recently, due to “Item Liberation” and the “Iron Fist Instructor,” among other things, their overall strength had risen again. Among them, some of the stronger individuals could probably catch up with Level 8 Personnel.
Of course, not many people reached this D Level standard.
But one interesting point was…
According to Colin’s estimate, these D Level employees might find it very difficult to defeat Level 8 Official Personnel.
However, if they were to fight to the death, the company’s D Level staff would most likely be the ones to survive.
As for the Level 8 Personnel…
Most would have gone mad during the battle.
‘It’s just like with those D Level Personnel in the “Ghost Train” incident; they went insane before showing their full strength…’
Colin sighed inwardly, no wonder the officials valued “double-duty” personnel so highly.
They were willing to pour massive resources into F Level to nurture them…
Most likely, they were trying to cultivate a group of high-ranking individuals who could freely use extraordinary power, filling the gaps and voids in the upper echelons of official power.
Nevertheless, without giving it much more thought, Colin was led into a vast hall.
Inside, there were more than a hundred anomalies contained.
Even though they were in containment status.
Colin still felt a slight tightness in his chest, sensing the intangible pressure emanating from them inadvertently…
‘Is it the same as last time?’ Xu Duojin inquired from the side.
This time there were more transactions than before, and the space was larger. He wondered whether the other side could handle it.
After all, some anomalies needed people to maintain their containment…
Once the people leave and there’s no suppression, containment breaches could easily occur.
If it were just one or two, it might be manageable, but here it wasn’t a matter of just one or two.
However, as the thought had just surfaced, Xu Duojin’s eyelids twitched violently when he saw Colin raise a finger, from which a flame burst forth, turning into a large fireball.
Then, the fireball suddenly boiled, brightening as if infused with oxygen…
It was as if a small sun had risen in this place.
Heat waves flooded every inch of the air.
The next second, the anomalies that had been somewhat restless all quieted down.
‘He’s gotten so much stronger…’ Xu Duojin felt a bit numb inside.
Every time he didn’t see the other party for a few days, their strength seemed to shoot up like an elevator. What was even more astonishing was that the other party had reached this level of power in just a few months.
On the other side, Colin tilted his chin upward slightly and surveyed the area: ‘It seems there’s not much of a problem.’
‘I’m relieved then. However, if there are any issues, call out at any time, we’ll be right outside,’ Xu Duojin repressed his emotions, nodded, gestured to the other employees to release their suppression, and orderly retreated from the area…
Once everyone had exited the hall.
Colin allowed the flames around him to spread further, encompassing the entire space.
Next, he didn’t rush to trigger the transaction task, but went to a few high-level containment subjects with terrifying auras. After observing them for a while, he touched one of them, transferring it into the “Storage Room.”
Only then did he trigger the transaction task…
Before long, a pale single-toned flute sound traveled from afar.
Hearing this sound, Colin couldn’t help but blink, and then he noticed that, in the hall, a layer of mist had formed, seemingly slowly undulating.
Deep within the mist, there appeared to be something enormous rapidly approaching.
In another blink of an eye, the dim yellow light shone through from the depths of the mist.
The shadow of a train was faintly visible.
Colin’s pupils glowed with fire as he stared in that direction, wanting to see what the front of the train looked like. As he gazed, he suddenly realized he had somehow lost focus.
By the time he regained his senses, the train, marked with the scars of war and seemingly having traveled through various perilous locales, was gradually coming to a stop.
‘This train… it’s really eerie…’
Colin mused internally, then saw the train doors go ‘clack’ as they opened.
A figure clad in silver full-body armor stepped out…
He first locked eyes with Colin, a red light flickering in the helmet’s facial area as if signaling. After Colin nodded, the figure waved to those behind him.
In an instant…
More than a dozen figures in silver lightweight full-covering armor poured out…
Upon descending, they didn’t interact with Colin, nor did they make any unnecessary movements. They walked briskly toward various containment subjects and began extracting them into “Elf Balls” along with the containment measures.
‘These lightweight armors seem much more advanced than those left by the starship crew.’
Colin stood by, observing.
From their basic speed and movements, their strength appeared to be around the average D Level, but it seemed, rather than relying on brute strength, they were more inclined towards logistics…
‘The real combat personnel of the Corps would be the ones in the thick armor.’
Colin didn’t think too much about it and quietly maintained the flame, waiting for the transaction to be completed.
Meanwhile, some logistics personnel, with hands on hips and not uttering a sound, had lights frequently flickering on their sci-fi helmets, seemingly engaged in some kind of secret communication…
“Damn it, who the fuck came up with this containment procedure, XXX and XXX together, aren’t they scared it’ll explode…”
“Fuck, using this thing to hold a Level 2 Containment Subject is like using paper to wrap nuclear waste; what genius thought of this containment procedure, I really want to twist his head off…”
“Holy mother, come over and give me a hand, need to redo this thing…”
“…”
The company’s passive translation allowed Colin to vaguely “see” the messages those light flickers were conveying.
Although the details weren’t very precise, the general idea was definitely there.
It seemed…
Their attitudes weren’t very friendly.
‘Are logistics always this irritable?’
Colin muttered to himself and looked away as if he knew nothing since the complaints were not about him.
However…
Looking at the lights flickering on their faces.
He suddenly remembered something.
‘Speaking of which, during the last transaction, there seemed to be a guy pointing at me non-stop; I wonder what that was all about.’
Colin suddenly recalled that at the end of the last transaction, someone was pointing at him with a very excited demeanor.
He didn’t know what it was about…
With that thought, Colin curiously scanned the surroundings, looking at the company’s logistics personnel who were busy with secondary containment.
Unfortunately, he didn’t see the person.
Either they hadn’t come, or they had bad luck and were “gotten”…
‘It shouldn’t be a big problem; if there really was an issue, ‘Lady Bunny’ would have told me.’
Colin wasn’t overly concerned.
He shifted his gaze away from the group of workers and locked eyes with the little squad leader standing at the train door, seemingly supervising everyone. After about half an hour, the containment work was finally completed.
All the executing personnel, holding a bunch of metal elf balls, lined up to return to the train…
After the squad leader had counted all the metal balls, he took out a list as usual and handed it over.
Colin glanced at it, saw no issues, and signed his name.
Just as he made the final stroke of his signature,
An inspiration emerged at the same time.
“Transaction mission completed.”
However, just when Colin thought the group would leave directly,
The little squad leader didn’t leave right away but took out a small box about the size of a laptop bag and handed it to him.
“Is this from ‘Lady Rabbit’?”
Colin accepted the small box and saw that there was a stamp often used by Lady Bunny on it.
However, the other party didn’t respond to his question but turned and boarded the train.
Without any fuss, he thought for a moment and decided to place the small box in the “Storage Room” first, planning to check it when he got home.
But at that moment, a gaze filled with resentment was cast upon him.
Colin sensed it and looked in the direction of the feeling, seeing that inside the train carriage, a logistics employee was gripping a metal containment ball, continuously holding the train’s handrail and staring at him fixedly, radiating an indescribable mix of complex emotions…
Was it that guy from last time?
He hadn’t seen them earlier and thought they might have died.
Turns out they were busy with other tasks on the train.
‘What’s the deal, I haven’t provoked you, why do you seem to have such a big problem with me?’
Colin, holding the small box, scratched the back of his head, puzzled.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 551 - 551 436 Request from Lady Bunny_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 551: Chapter 436 Request from “Lady Bunny”_1 Chapter 551: Chapter 436 Request from “Lady Bunny”_1 “Clank, clank,” the train sounds gradually faded away…
Colin didn’t pay too much attention to this.
After all, it seemed like the problem wasn’t too big; otherwise, the logistics staff would have said something to him.
If they didn’t say anything, then there should be no problem.
Afterward, as the train went off into the distance and the grey fog dissipated, Colin completed this small task involving the transaction.
Then, he happily received one thousand points + a gold mission voucher.
“Not too bad…”
For a simple intermediary task that was handsomely rewarding, in which he hadn’t done much except ensure that some transactions went through, the compensation was quite decent.
Unfortunately, it didn’t include the item extraction ticket that Colin needed most.
“Looks like, barring any accidents, I can only get it from that task in a few days. Fortunately, this lottery is after January fifth. Anytime’s fine, not just that one day.”
Colin collected his thoughts, waved his hand, and immediately, the flames vanished as he thought it.
It was when the flames disappeared…
Some sort of enclosed status was broken, and on one side of the hall, a door was slowly opened after emitting three “bangs.”
Xu Duojin and others who had already been waiting for some time peeked inside when they saw all the abnormal items had vanished, and Colin stood still. They immediately had a rough guess about the outcome of the transaction process.
If everything had gone as expected, there shouldn’t have been any accidents.
Thinking this, Xu Duojin saw a look of confusion on Colin’s face. Thinking there might have been an accident, he quickly approached and asked,
“How did it go?”
While speaking, he was afraid of hearing Colin say that, by some accident, a few had run off.
That would be a bit of a headache…
These things, although not very high in level and not particularly destructive—at worst, they could kill a family in one go—but dealing with them was extremely troublesome, like a ticking time bomb, always potentially on the loose.
“It went pretty smoothly.”
Colin added, “The next ‘item’ feedback should be in about a month. Of course, exactly how long is uncertain…”
Hearing that everything went smoothly, Xu Duojin breathed a sigh of relief, “No problem, there’s no rush.”
These “time bombs” were the kind that they’d prefer to get rid of, even if it meant paying someone to take them off their hands.
Of course, if there were any gains, they wouldn’t refuse them either.
After speaking, a woman dressed like a secretary beside Xu Duojin sent out an invitation to Colin, seemingly wanting to invite him to a celebration party…
However, Colin wasn’t too interested and directly declined, saying he had things to do and needed to leave.
He roughly understood that it was probably the personnel from the neighboring area who wanted to discuss something with him or show good faith—a kind of social favor…
But Colin had no need to waste his energy on social exchanges.
“Compared to this, I’d better go back and see what kind of good stuff ‘Lady Bunny’ has brought me this time.”
Thinking this, when Colin boarded the helicopter to return home, he first communicated over the phone and let Qin Chuan and the others leave without waiting for him. After reaching his destination, he had Xiao Yin transform into a wheelchair and immediately sat on it.
…
“Swoosh.”
A breeze blew by…
A man walking his dog by the road was completely baffled. He wondered if it was an illusion, but did he just see a glowing wheelchair zoom past at a speed barely visible to the naked eye?
“What’s wrong?” asked a woman who appeared to be his partner.
“Nothing, just thought my eyes were playing tricks on me…”
After all, even if there had really been a wheelchair that zipped by at speeds over 120 kilometers per hour, it wouldn’t be possible for it to not slow down on turns and be silent, would it?
That would defy science.
With this in mind, the staunch materialist continued to walk his dog.
Approximately two hours after leaving the perimeter of Base No. 5, Colin returned home. He pocketed the “Emblem of the Humility Knight” and stepped off the silver wheelchair.
In the process, the “wheelchair” gathered itself and shrunk into a metallic ball, floating and following behind him.
Considerately helping Colin with the door and shutting it behind him.
“Wonder what she’s brought this time.”
Colin sat down on the living room sofa, took out the small suitcase, and opened it.
It contained many items, but on top were several sealed brown leather envelopes.
With curiosity, he opened the topmost envelope and found a black arrow without feathers inside…
It emitted a kind of disturbing aura that made one’s heart uneasy.
“What is this…?”
Colin raised an eyebrow, feeling a sense of familiarity with the aura. After thinking for a bit, he quickly remembered that this aura was similar to that of the special scepter he had obtained before.
Only, this time it lacked that decayed, rotting sensation…
As the remarks related to it emerged, he learned what it was.
An orange consumable.
[“Thorn Punishment”: Originates from the malice of a higher life form. Once the target is locked and this item is used to throw at them, it can immediately fix them in place, effective on many first-level containment subjects…]
[Exclusive Feature “Unswerving”: Once this attack is locked and used, it cannot be retracted, is very hard to defend against, and very hard to escape…]
[Note: One-time use.]
…
“So this is the leftover thing from that scepter?”
Colin examined the arrow in his hand, tuning in carefully, and he was certain it was the right one.
Back on the starship, if he had been hit with the scepter imbued with this thing, he probably would have been fixed in place and killed on the spot…

chapters.title: Chapter 552 - 552 436 Request from Lady Bunny_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 552: Chapter 436 Request from “Lady Bunny”_2 Chapter 552: Chapter 436 Request from “Lady Bunny”_2 After all, if it worked on a First Level Containment Subject, it was even less of a challenge for him.
“Higher Life Form, is this referring to an Upper-Level First-Class Containment Entity? Indeed, that’s impressive, it’s just a shame it can only be used once…”
Gripping the arrow tightly in his hand and confirming how to use it, Colin slipped the item into his pocket.
Then, he turned his attention to the next object, also contained in a brown leather mailbag—
A dark robe adorned with countless tiny points of light, translucent.
“…’Starlight Maiden’?”
Was this creature fated to be turned into an artifact after all?
But no, on closer examination, Colin realized this was only part of it, not the entirety of the ‘Starlight Maiden.’
It was at this moment that the relevant details emerged.
Upon reading them, Colin’s expression twitched, suddenly becoming quite animated.
[‘Skirt of Myriad Starlight’: A temporary item fabricated from materials taken from a special containment subject, which, when worn, can perfectly imitate the appearance of the ‘Starlight Maiden’ for three hours…]
[Exclusive Feature ‘Dawn’s Light’: Can simulate a fake but incredibly realistic ‘God Descent’ ceremony.]
[Note: Perhaps it should be paired with a pair of black stockings?]
…
“The skirt…”
Colin held the beautiful clothing in his right hand, his left hand covering his mouth, silent for a moment.
However, the good news was…
Through this garment, it was clear that ‘Lady Rabbit’ was supportive of his overall grand plan.
Otherwise, she wouldn’t have stripped the ‘Starlight Maiden’ of her clothing to dress him in it, no, more precisely, it wasn’t clothing but a garment fashioned from the materials of her body…
“Why couldn’t it have been a robe or something?”
Colin had no intention of trying it on immediately and disregarded the teasing note, stowing it straight into the ‘Storage Room.’
He then picked up the next item.
This time, the object was not encased in parchment but in a clear plastic shell.
Inside the plastic case were two size D batteries.
The batteries were transparent from the vertical midpoint, and through this clarity, Colin saw that each battery contained a creature resembling a starfish.
Upon a glance, he recognized these as the energy-generating creatures he had captured when boarding the starship.
They seemed to be called something like a Sixth Level Containment Subject with the code 6-978341.
“I almost forgot about this thing…”
Colin pursed his lips, recalling that this device could produce several dozen kilowatts of electricity in an hour…
Although for ‘Bonfire Company,’ it was deemed low in maximum output and poor in stability and thus not highly valued.
But for Earth, it was a different story; a single battery could produce several dozen kilowatts of electricity in an hour, enough to overcharge a car if simply attached to one found on the streets…
However, the company didn’t just give him two batteries.
Beyond the batteries, there was also a manual about the thickness of a fist, detailing the intricacies of this object.
“This containment subject’s battery will not cause instability in ‘reality,’ and its manufacturing process is not complex; below are the detailed manufacturing procedures…”
Colin followed the manual and saw first the metals needed for creating the special container to hold the anomaly, the manufacturing process, and so on…
The densely packed, dazzling formulas made Colin feel as though he were under a mental attack just by glancing at them.
His rationality kept taking hit after hit…
And the section purely about the manufacturing materials spanned dozens of pages.
It went on to cover the cultivation of the creatures, the purification and conversion of electricity, how to avoid explosions, etc…
Moreover, to ensure comprehension by the people of Earth, all formulas and manufacturing processes used were applicable on Earth and contained no unnecessary unknown content.
Still, even so, to Colin…
This object was essentially a ‘book from heaven.’
“Hiss, I’d rather face an Ancient God than deal with this thing.”
Colin took a deep breath; his brain worked incredibly fast, but being fast didn’t mean he understood, and understanding didn’t guarantee he could apply the knowledge.
Some things, if you don’t know, you just don’t know.
Of course, if he set his mind to learning, it felt possible to get to grips with it entirely.
But for him, it didn’t seem to carry too much significance.
“I just need to know a rough idea. The rest, let the officials worry about. If this works out well, who knows, the so-called energy crisis in the world might get solved in a short time…”
“However, once this thing can be mass-produced, those who sell resources might be in for some bad luck…”
Colin thought with a sense of schadenfreude.
The emergence of such super “biological batteries” would undoubtedly be a good thing for humanity as a whole.
But for a small group of interest groups that made a living from this, not so much…
Colin figured that if it weren’t for his special status, the moment he took out this “battery,” he might be found dead at home the next day with seventeen bullet wounds in his back from an apparent suicide.
But now…
As some dangerous ideas began to surface in people’s minds,
they might not even require his intervention; those people could just vanish into thin air without a trace.
Picking up his phone, he informed Xu Duojin to come collect the items the next day, then Colin stored the object temporarily and noticed a letter at the very bottom of the briefcase…
After opening it, inside was a message that was not particularly long.
The content was brief, basically two points.
The first point was about cooperation with the “Infinite Train”; such collaboration was not out of the question, but the specifics of cooperation were quite different from what the officials had in mind…
The authorities mainly sought to intervene in various incidents as early as possible through the special properties of the “Infinite Train”.
But “Lady Rabbit’s” message indicated she could not do this. The reason was not explained, but what she could do was provide a retreat for humanity in the event of a future catastrophic crisis.
To massively transfer afflicted individuals from around the world to a safe area and wait for the future…
Similarly, she required a formal transit authorization document from all over Earth, which needed to be effective with at least ninety percent of the sovereign nations’ approval.
“Playing it so official, huh?”
Colin clicked his tongue, but if it were just that, he reckoned places around the world would probably compromise.
Or rather, after The Five Wicked agreed, there was no room for others to disagree.
If there were voices of dissent and those dissenting people disappeared, then there would be no dissenting voices left.
It was one of the things they were best at doing.
If a doomsday disaster were to erupt in the future,
ensuring one in ten people survived would already be considered incredibly lucky. Now, having the chance to have an additional way out, they would almost certainly agree…
However, the second request that followed was likely to cause some controversy.
“Lady Rabbit,” aside from the aforementioned demands, also wanted them to grant a portion of the core permissions for “world barriers” for better execution of her operations here…
As for which specific items she needed and how they would be used, that was not specified.
“This… might be contentious.”
Not just the officials, even Colin himself couldn’t help but feel a sense of unease, as though a plot was about to be uncovered.
It was foreseeable that the first point would probably pass.
The second point… was not so definite.
“But if ‘Lady Rabbit’ really has some sort of plan for this place, what exactly is she after? And the ‘world barriers,’ they don’t seem all that powerful for the company. Do they really need authorization…”
Colin pondered for a moment. It seemed like Earth wasn’t exactly rich; it lacked high technology and high-end power. As for some irreplaceable anomaly…
Seemingly not?
Of course, it could also be limited by his own understanding, Colin simply couldn’t guess the reason.
Sweeping aside that thought, Colin decided to continue to leave this issue for the leaders above to worry about, then looked toward the second matter at hand.
“Next week heading to ‘World Code-4’? Is everything settled over there?”
The first thing Colin remembered was that formidable mixed task force composed of many elites.
That team had gone there for some unknown reason…
Now it seemed they must have completed the mission, and he might have to go on behalf of the company to finalize things.
The letter mentioned it would just involve signing some agreements or similar things, normally without any danger.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 553 - 553 437 Yukionnas Reward. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 553: Chapter 437 “Yukionna’s” Reward. _1 Chapter 553: Chapter 437 “Yukionna’s” Reward. _1 “‘Danger level none or low’… why do I feel like I can’t really trust that?”
“Regardless of the danger, let’s consider another point. Those mixed team members, whether they have C Level authority or not, their combat abilities are probably not far off from C Level, right?”
“With their strength, couldn’t they represent the company to handle this task?”
Leaning back in his chair, Colin suddenly had an epiphany amid his doubts and realized the key issue at hand.
What was needed here was most likely not his strength, but his identity—the special identity of a “Flamebearer” reservist.
This status seemed to bear quite a few privileges within the company.
“Hmm, that makes sense, it should be like this. Otherwise, there’s no need to insist on my involvement. After all, in terms of combat ability, even if I go all out, I might not be able to beat that elite squad.”
Colin figured that the real motives behind the task were most likely as he suspected.
At the same time, he also found it strange.
“Flamebearers” might be absent these days, but surely he wasn’t the only “Flamebearer” Reservist, was he?
Or was it that he just happened to be the most available at the moment?
Colin couldn’t help but wonder if there were others besides him but soon, he couldn’t afford to be concerned with that anymore…
There was one last point on the letter.
Colin quickly scanned through it, his face revealing a cautious but odd expression as he focused on that part of the information.
“…Before completing the observation of the ‘Book of Fate’, make as many preparations as possible because it’s certain that at that time, on this side, there will be some extremely dangerous conflicts…”
Muttering softly to himself, Colin’s brows gradually furrowed. “Lady Rabbit” claimed it was safe, which could mean it was potentially safe, or it could result in significant troubles.
Or to say, her so-called safety was theoretical—as long as nothing got triggered.
However, it was often hard to achieve such ideal circumstances when executing tasks in reality.
Unexpected things tended to happen…
So Colin, who had been involved in many missions related to her, was very clear that the safety she promised needed to be viewed dialectically. When on a mission, one had to act according to the specific situation, not go in with the mindset that nothing would go wrong.
Otherwise, a lapse in caution could lead to sudden death.
And that was when she had claimed it was safe, or relatively safe…
When “Lady Rabbit” said it was unsafe, or even extremely dangerous—that meant the situation would definitely be terrible at that time.
“If it’s like this when it’s safe, how bad will it be if it’s extremely dangerous?”
Colin muttered to himself, looking at the content on the parchment. It seemed like a disaster was inevitable, regardless of what happened, right?
Then… would it be possible to avoid looking at the “Book of Fate”?
Before receiving an answer from above, Colin shook his head in silence, knowing that something had already been fermenting in the shadows…
The observational result might just be one of the larger variables.
In fact, whether he observed it or not, it would be hard to change these events…
“To my current knowledge, the sources of potentially troubling disasters are about three. The first is ‘Red Moon’. It seems omnipresent and the level of its influence is terrifying. If a disaster breaks out, that thing will definitely be part of the cause…”
Colin hadn’t really accounted for the Followers of the ‘Red Moon’.
Their displayed power, as of now, was neither strong nor weak…
There weren’t many actual achievements, but their ability to cause chaos was off the charts.
“Besides this, the second is The Rat aiming for the destruction of ‘The Seventh Box Garden World’, seizing the divine authority of ‘Father of the Ocean’, but ever since escaping after doing something and then hiding away with no clear movements…”
After pondering for a moment, Colin thought that the entity itself seemed very weak, possibly dying from a random encounter with a D Level.
But that did not mean it was incapable…
In fact, it indicated how cunning and troublesome it was, otherwise, it wouldn’t have managed to kill “Father of the Ocean”.
“That Rat seems to have certain ties with ‘Red Moon’, and I’ve also heard it shouting slogans for ‘Red Moon’, but I always feel that its relationship with ‘Red Moon’ doesn’t seem like the extreme faith seen in the lives of the ‘Red Moon’ followers. It seems more like some sort of cooperation…”
Colin raised his hand to rub his forehead. Ever since the attack incident at Base No. 5, the creature seemed to have disappeared.
Who knows what it was plotting…
“Aside from these two, there are various followers of the Outer Gods. Each one taken on their own is fewer in number and weaker than those of ‘Red Moon’, but when they band together, they become a real nuisance…”
The relationships among these individuals were incredibly complex, with both cooperation and conflicts, but overall they could be summarized in one sentence—
As long as you don’t bring about a God Descent, we can still be good partners.
“Although they are holding each other back, preventing any of them from succeeding and appearing somewhat comical, it has to be said that many of them really do have powerful entities standing behind them. One misstep, and a major calamity could ensue, just like what happened with ‘Starlight Maiden’ this time…”
If he didn’t know the full story and were to see it from another perspective, Colin figured that if he were aware of the imminent arrival of an Evil God, he’d probably be losing sleep over it.
And this sort of situation could potentially occur at any time with countless Heretic Forces in any of the numerous groups.
“Troublesome indeed; it’s a pity that even with this cleanup, we can’t kill them all off, at most we’ll break each one’s leg…”
Colin sighed resignedly.
Even more realistically, even if he had the chance to kill them all, he most likely wouldn’t really go through with it.

chapters.title: Chapter 554 - 554 437 Yukionnas Reward. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 554: Chapter 437 “Yukionna’s” Reward. _2 Chapter 554: Chapter 437 “Yukionna’s” Reward. _2 Because besides these dangers, this world also harbors many abnormal things that are constantly resurfacing. They mostly lack any semblance of reason and indiscriminately contaminate their surroundings upon emergence, like natural disasters, triggering catastrophes, and are extremely difficult to deal with…
When looking at some high-level official documents, Colin often saw that the first to arrive at the scene and begin the suppression were about twenty percent from various Heretic Forces…
Even because they valued their lives less than ordinary people did.
Their processing speed might be faster than that of official forces.
Of course, there’s nothing to be grateful for because these people act regardless of the cost.
If comparing it to a surgery for a tumor, their way of doing things is roughly like cutting open the flesh and digging directly at the tumor, pulling it out and calling it done…
Sometimes they even take the “tumor” back to turn into weapons.
And many times, survivors who could have been saved end up buried alongside…
It’s hard to say which causes more harm, the revival of anomalies or their actions.
“But when you think about it, besides a few Heretic Forces, doesn’t it seem like everyone else, both official and private entities, seem to uphold the stability of the ‘world barriers’ to some extent?”
Colin stroked his chin, puzzled, and for a moment he couldn’t think of the reason.
Logically, the collapse of the world would give those behind them a greater chance to escape from those unknown shackles, right?
So why does everything seem to be the opposite?
Officials uphold “world barriers” for world peace, that can be understood.
But what about Heretic Forces upholding “world barriers”?
It can’t possibly also be for world peace, can it?
“There must be some reasons I’m not quite aware of.”
Thinking for a moment and finding no answers, Colin shook his head, summarized the intelligence he knew, and then felt like he was getting an alarming revelation upon calculating the risks.
Earth may seem calm on the surface, but actually, there are undercurrents surging, with more than three sources of terrifying apocalyptic crises alone, any one of which could explode with just a trigger…
And that trigger might just be the observation of the Book of Fate.
It could be a little later, but not much.
“This is troublesome…”
Colin inexplicably felt like he was personally triggering the end of the world.
Looking at the letter again, a vague and intense anxiety grew stronger in his heart.
The key point is…
He felt he truly lacked the ability to stop all this.
Taking a deep breath, Colin calmed himself, folded the letter, and after ensuring there was nothing else inside or outside the briefcase, he returned to the bed and slowly closed his eyes…
At this point, he might as well get some sleep before thinking about it.
…
The night quickly passed, and near noon the next day, Colin, though sleeping on the bed and tense from the anxiety of the previous night, suddenly felt a blast of cold air approaching.
He subconsciously prepared to ignite flames to protect himself.
But the next second, he quickly realized…
Opening his eyes, he saw “Yukionna” with her ice-blue translucent body floating nearby, holding a few icicles and giggling as she stared at him…
On seeing him awake, she handed one over to him.
“Eh? You made this yourself and want me to try it?”
Colin shook his head sharply, obviously stunned for a moment, and reached out to take it.
“Yukionna” nodded, then with a pair of beguiling eyes, she watched him, seemingly anticipating his taste.
Seeing this, Colin glanced at the ice stick in his hand that seemed to be milk-flavored and for some reason, he was suddenly filled with a comforting feeling, as if a low-functioning daughter finally knew how to return a favor to her caring father…
The previous tightly-strung anxiety immediately eased a bit.
After tasting it…
The flavor was surprisingly good, though a tad too sweet.
“If it weren’t for the fact that my body was silently healing everywhere, I feel like this sweetness alone could make my back teeth hurt so much I’d ascend to heaven…”
Colin pursed his lips, making an objective assessment in his mind, but he still offered “Yukionna” words of encouragement.
As of now, her “human” traits seemed to be growing stronger.
It was a good trend…
‘It’s just a shame she still can’t talk. If she were a bit smarter, maybe she could start learning and doing homework, right?’
Colin’s mind wandered for a while, then he shook his head and gathered his thoughts.
He then got up, brushed his teeth out of habit, had “breakfast,” and was ready to take “Yukionna” out for a walk. But at that moment, he felt something and turned to look out the window, catching a glimpse of Xu Duojin among the crowd.
“The spot used for pigeons is now yours, huh?”
Colin muttered, glancing at the faint traces of pigeon droppings on the windowsill.
Ever since joining the officials, he hadn’t seen that pigeon for quite a few days, and wondered if it had been captured for soup…
Or perhaps, it bore a grudge after he ate one of its eggs last time.
But if nothing unexpected happened, that pigeon probably wouldn’t return again…
“Dong dong…”
There was a knock at the door, and when Colin said that it wasn’t locked, Xu Duojin walked in.
“New stuff, you guys might want to study this…”
Colin didn’t beat around the bush. Sitting on the living room sofa, he waited for the other person to sit down before tossing the “Anomaly Bioorganic Battery” and related materials over.
He had also had the Nano Intellectual Maid record these things, so if he needed to in the future, he could attempt to replicate them himself.
But for now, it was good to let the officials test the waters first, so he could easily navigate their regulations later on…
“This…”
Xu Duojin examined it and appeared surprised. He then looked carefully at the documents, his eyes lighting up.
A single battery could reliably output at least ten degrees of electricity per hour…
He had no idea how it was achieved.
He flipped further back, glanced at the technical principles, nodded, and then looked away.
He didn’t understand…
As a former surgeon, his knowledge of physics wasn’t bad, but to completely understand these documents from such different fields was a bit too challenging.
Still, he recognized the value of this invention.
He knew it was groundbreaking and could bring enormous benefits.
The key was everything was ready to use right off the shelf!
Xu Duojin carefully placed the battery into a small box for safekeeping, then began to speak, “If it becomes widespread, its value could very well exceed that of so-called Purple Gear, even Orange Gear. No, society might witness another major technological leap…”
Although there seemed to be certain risks, they were entirely within a controllable range.
“I think so too…”
Colin nodded and then pulled out a backup letter to discuss another matter, about the “Infinite Train.”
“Is there really a chance?”
Xu Duojin was visibly startled; during this time infiltrating the company, they had learned a lot.
Everyone suspected that borrowing it was unlikely.
Because even Bonfire Company seemed to be unable to perfectly control every journey it made.
But unexpectedly, Colin was providing the opposite answer.
However, before he got his hopes up, after hearing Colin’s description, Xu Duojin crossed his hands, pondered for a while, and soon furrowed his brows.
Like Colin, he also felt that the first condition, the request for world traversal documents, was probably not a problem.
There might be some obstructions, but nothing too significant…
