However, the second condition was suddenly much more difficult.
“The ‘world barriers’ aren’t just for suppressing the Anomaly Index, to avoid external threats; they’re involved in a lot of things. In fact, the mental status of many Extraordinary Ones is also connected to it…”
Xu Duojin explained solemnly, “The issue is, this requirement seems to involve core, fundamental logic. Once we make this decision, it’s almost as if we’re entrusting a large part of our security to others, so… the controversy will be significant.”
He paused, seemingly adding, “Very significant.”
Now, although many powers coveted the Gene Compensation Medicine inside Bonfire Company…
It didn’t mean they had completely let down their guard against the company.
Having said this, he looked up, his gaze toward Colin seeming to inquire if there was any room for negotiation.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 555 - 555 438 How on Earth is this Earth about to be
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 555: Chapter 438: How on Earth is this Earth about to be gone?_1 Chapter 555: Chapter 438: How on Earth is this Earth about to be gone?_1 “Hard to say,”
Colin understood Xu Duojin’s meaning, waved his hand, unable to make any promises.
After all, current conjectures subconsciously assumed that the company might have some kind of conspiracy, but in reality, it was also possible that without those authorities, Lady Bunny truly couldn’t come in…
Colin was well aware that this possibility was equally not small.
Because, strictly speaking, it was probably not that “Lady Bunny” needed these authorities, but the “Bonfire Company” with all its bizarre, powerful yet incredibly rigid “protocols” needed these authorities…
If these things were not restricted…
Given Lady Bunny’s habit of exploiting loopholes in missions, she would likely not hesitate at all and would bring the Corps over to suppress the unrest directly.
“Some rules in the ‘Bonfire Company’ are quite strict, and without meeting the conditions, you can’t take action,”
Colin added another sentence.
“Alright,” Xu Duojin nodded his head, not pursuing the matter further.
Then, without waiting for him to continue speaking, Colin asked something he had been curious about before:
“Why do a considerable number of heretic forces not only refrain from destroying the ‘world barriers,’ but also seem to have an intention to maintain them?”
Hearing Colin’s question, Xu Duojin pondered for a moment, thought for a few seconds, then opened his mouth:
“The question is actually not so complicated… Tell me, who do you think would be the first to appear if the barriers were destroyed?”
“Red Moon?” Colin immediately thought of this name.
According to current intelligence, this figure seemed to be the closest to a state of return…
But no sooner had he finished speaking than Colin’s brows raised: “That seems not quite right, Followers of the ‘Red Moon’ also maintain the ‘world barriers’ to some extent…”
At that moment, Xu Duojin spoke: “Theoretically, ‘Red Moon’ is the closest one, but in fact, once the ‘world barriers’ are completely destroyed, perhaps… some other higher external beings will cast their eyes here…”
Higher external beings? Colin was stunned for a moment, quickly realizing that not only was there turmoil within the nation, shrouded in stormy weather, but also a host of covetous gazes cast from beyond their cognition.
Seeing Colin realize this, Xu Duojin didn’t delve too deeply into the matter of the “Outsiders,” but instead said:
“However, to be honest, the Followers of the ‘Red Moon’ will not always maintain the ‘world barriers.’ They, too, are destroyers, but of the gradual kind, seeking a methodical erosion…
“And every time they erode a bit, they strive to let their ‘Mother’ occupy the void created, to ensure that their mother’s power dominates.
“If not for that, they might even reinforce the barrier as much as possible in their own way.
“The reason this situation arises seems to be because their mother’s revival is gradual, like a person waking up and opening their eyes, there’s a process to it…
“The Followers of the ‘Red Moon,’ by and large, act according to the degree of ‘Red Moon’s’ awakening over time.”
Ah, this…
Hearing this, Colin couldn’t help thinking that the “world barriers” had become a protective shell for the other side, and from Xu Duojin’s intonation, the officials seemed to have no real solution for the “Red Moon’s” awakening.
He asked about this and received an affirmative response from Xu Duojin.
“Over time, their mother will gradually awaken; indeed, there’s not much that can be done to force her back…”
“The only good news for now is that the extent is not large, typically less than a percentage point a year. At this rate, we do have a few decades…”
“And that’s why, when the ‘world barriers’ damage suddenly increased by several percentage points last time, causing the entire community to grow tense, everyone suspected the ‘Red Moon’ was about to emerge.”
“But fortunately, everything has stabilized for the time being.”
As Xu Duojin reached his last statement, a self-mocking expression flitted across his face.
However, regarding this, Colin had little firsthand experience; it seemed that he had only recently joined the officials and was doing various missions, with not much contact with this side of reality.
Of course, Colin could guess the hidden reason behind the “world barriers” being shaken.
It must have been The Rat’s doing…
The “stabilization” Xu Duojin spoke of was probably only because after lurking, this thing was preparing to make a big move.
Clearly, from the tone, Xu Duojin knew this as well.
Unfortunately…
Neither Colin nor his companions had a very good way to deal with that adeptly hiding creature.
‘Currently, it seems that when it comes out to make trouble next time, there will be two likely moments: one is when I observe the ‘Book of Fate,’ and the other is when Old Master Wu, the Ninth Level ‘Fate Propeller,’ reaches the end of his life…’
‘Both possibilities are not small… troublesome.’
As thoughts flashed in his mind, Colin felt a bit overwhelmed, and thinking of the covetous foreign gazes beyond his home, he felt an even bigger headache:
“Why are some external gazes focused on this little place?”
“That… you might have to ask the ‘Bonfire Company’ about,” said Xu Duojin, shaking his head and chuckling.
“Oh…”
Colin had almost forgotten that a fair number of these “Outsiders.”
Were probably coming for the “Bonfire Company”…
Xu Duojin seemed to see through Colin’s thinking and continued to say:
“Actually, according to some of Mr. Wu’s views he shared with us, many higher life forms, especially some truly ‘Outer Gods,’ do not have the concept of ‘resentment.’ What drives them here is because something of great importance to them exists here.”

chapters.title: Chapter 556 - 556 438 How on Earth is this Earth about to be
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 556: Chapter 438: How on Earth is this Earth about to be gone?_2 Chapter 556: Chapter 438: How on Earth is this Earth about to be gone?_2 “As for what it is, it probably has something to do with the ‘corporation’.”
Listening to his words, Colin thought about it, feeling that there were quite a few possibilities.
Some probably had been screwed over by the corporation and wanted to come over and nail its coffin as tightly as possible, reinforcing it to prevent the corporation from emerging again.
Then there were those who were probably just there to watch the excitement unfold.
Of course, if there was an opportunity to profit, these high-level beings would most likely not mind taking advantage of it.
Especially those golden artifacts…
Not only were the employees of the corporation covetous, but some higher beings were probably equally envious.
Afterward, Colin didn’t continue on this topic but went on to ask Xu Duojin about the developments regarding “2044” from the official side.
Unfortunately, Xu Duojin shook his head, “I can’t see anything, not a thing. I have no idea what it is…”
“Is that so…”
“Yes, before we, along with the international department, decided to make certain sacrifices, risking the lives of high-level personnel to peek into what might happen on that day, but nothing happened. It seemed like just a regular day.”
Xu Duojin gave a wry smile.
There was no sighting of indescribable entities resulting in observers dying because they couldn’t bear it.
Aside from the corrosive cost paid for using extraordinary abilities…
They had paid nothing extra.
But they had also gained nothing.
However, the lack of results was the biggest problem itself.
Contrary to this conclusion are some powerful beings who clearly have some indescribable concerns about a certain point in the future.
Not to mention just looking at the “Red Moon.”
By estimates, this being will likely fully awaken sometime before that future date arrives.
In such a scenario, how could everything be normal?
While discussing this, Xu Duojin couldn’t help but glance at Colin. In his view, the corporation definitely knew what was going on with the event of 2044.
After all, from many aspects, it was apparent that the corporation was making some kind of arrangements for it.
But unfortunately, this young man who seemed to have a significant ‘background,’ apparently due to insufficient permissions, was not yet privy to this knowledge.
He could only silently wait for the other to move up first…
Xu Duojin silently shook his head. If it weren’t for Old Master Wu’s instructions, asking him to engage in conversation with Colin while trying as much as possible not to actively inquire about Colin himself or about the corporation, Xu would have liked to ask when the other was going to move up…
After finishing the conversation about this topic, the two did not continue communicating.
Xu Duojin gathered his thoughts and left the room with the “Anomaly Bioorganic Battery”.
He needed to deliver this thing as quickly as possible.
Once this thing became widespread, how good the effect would be, he hardly dared to imagine.
After his figure had left, Colin sat on the sofa, lost in thought for quite a while, not knowing what to think.
If this were any other world, with the situation as it was, he would have relaxed and thought the problem was not big.
But now a disaster was truly about to befall him.
This mentality was a whole different matter…
The Earth, seemingly normal now, gave off a feeling as if it might be gone in an instant, didn’t it?
“Forget it, there must be a way out when we get to the mountain. No use worrying… What the f*ck, ‘Yukionna’, what are you up to?”
Colin shook his head, collected his thoughts, and then suddenly saw.
All around the room…
The temperature had plummeted significantly at some point, with ice frost crystals everywhere, and “Yukionna” was spewing cold mist all over the room like an ice mist machine, seemingly determined to transform it into a large refrigerator.
Taking a deep breath, Colin stretched lazily, stood up, called “Yukionna” back, and burned her “masterpiece” with a burst of fire.
Then, while heading out the door, he dialed Qin Chuan’s phone.
He planned to find a few lucky anomalies in the vicinity to get in some exercise.
Before long, Qin Chuan and others arrived by car, and before getting on, Colin glanced back not far behind the car at four Toyota vans—
It seems like there was more soy sauce.
Colin was speechless. Others had all kinds of precise combinations on hand, with milk, meat, and DPS, but all he had was soy sauce and nothing else.
Apart from shouting “666”, they were good for nothing else.
No, not exactly nothing else, having this group with him was like having “auto-loot” on…
Every time they dealt with an anomaly, they would comb the scene and find various suspicious items, improving the drop rate significantly.
Nevertheless, he didn’t pay much attention to this.
One more or one less bottle of soy sauce didn’t make a big difference.
Colin glanced over the report file handed to him by Qin Chuan.
While he was reviewing it, Qin Chuan also said on the side, “Currently, the anomalies within our own jurisdiction have basically been wiped out, everything is still stable…”
Generally, the average number of incidents in a district managed by a Fifth Level Personnel was less than ten a month.
And with Colin’s efficiency…
These anomalies were not even enough for one punch from him.
So now, with Colin taking the initiative to work and wanting to deal with anomalies, they would have to go to the surrounding cities.
“Arrange a route for me, let’s see how many we can clear today…” Colin gestured, not particularly concerned.
Tasks not “carefully selected” by the corporation for him, he carried out with hardly any effort, as many anomaly sources didn’t even meet the standard of Third-Level Containment Subjects.
For Colin, it was pretty much one punch per anomaly.
Although it felt a bit like bullying the weak, he quite enjoyed it…
Soon enough, the convoy of vehicles stopped outside a supermarket building that had already been cordoned off.
“Who are you…” A special police officer came up, stopping them.

chapters.title: Chapter 557 - 557 438 How on Earth is this Earth about to be
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 557: Chapter 438: How on Earth is this Earth about to be gone?_3 Chapter 557: Chapter 438: How on Earth is this Earth about to be gone?_3 “Support personnel,” Qin Zheng said as he took out a document.
After the other party verified it, they allowed passage.
“The situation here is, it seems there are some special anomalies within the entire building. Once you enter and move around, you’ll find it impossible to leave. When night falls, you can see shadows moving inside, singing and dancing and such. The Fifth Level Personnel who were originally managing this area have been trapped for two days now, and there has been no news so far…” Qin Chuan quickly explained the situation to Colin.
“Singing and dancing?”
Colin had a strange expression on his face as he looked towards the shopping mall building that appeared fairly new. He sniffed, detecting a hint of rot and an eerie smell.
It seemed the first encounter today had a bit of substance to it…
However…
“Problem’s not big…”
Colin said briefly before leading the people towards the building.
Over twenty individuals followed behind him, looking like bystanders…
If one ignored that they were all “Fate Propellers,” the scene was quite impressive.
Soon after entering the first floor of the supermarket within the mall, Colin glanced inside. There were a dozen individuals, seemingly official personnel, busy making arrangements, with a lot of yellow charms posted everywhere…
“Charm symbols?”
Colin withdrew his gaze, ready to continue leading his group towards the stairs to check the upper floors.
But at that moment…
“It’s very dangerous above. We’ve just suppressed the first floor. Who are you?” the group of official personnel seemed to finally react, quickly stepping forward to stop them.
“We’re reinforcements,” Qin Chuan negotiated with them.
“We’ve already taken over the situation here, and moreover, we’re about to resolve it…” a man dressed in a leather jacket, presumably the team leader of the Sixth Level Official Personnel, emerged from the back, eying the newcomers with hostility.
It’s clear at times like this that fresh reinforcements might look like they’re trying to steal credit…
While such occurrences aren’t too common, they’re not unheard of – quite simply put, they’re very annoying.
However, just as he was about to send this group away to prevent his credit from being taken, he suddenly heard the opposition say…
“I feel like you guys are pretty lucky. If it weren’t for me, you’d all be dead here.”
Colin suddenly spoke up, but his gaze wasn’t on the group.
Instead, he kept staring at the supermarket floor…
As if seeing through the floor, he locked onto the root of the anomaly within the supermarket.
And as if sensing his scrutiny, the calmness within the supermarket shifted. The red lettering on the yellow charms started to fade and fall off…
Even the central array, a large cluster of main charm symbols, wilted and dropped.
“How is this possible?! What a joke!”
The Sixth Level personnel were terrified; his set of charms seemed to have had no effect at all before vanishing?
How could this be…
“Hiss, what’s going on…” Qin Chuan was stunned for a moment, taking out several charm symbols and sticking them to himself.
Within their ranks, some preferred playing with arrays, others liked affixing charms to themselves.
And he was one of the latter…
Though not an expert in the field of arrays, he still had a basic understanding and knew that the charm symbols here were of a not-so-low standard. Yet, they were mysteriously erased of their effects.
This alone indicated that the crisis here was extraordinary…
As the charm symbols fell off, a bizarre and absurd song began to resonate throughout the place.
At the same time, a strong sense of inspiration surged in Colin’s mind, evoking a vivid image of a particular area deep underground, apparently venerating a special statue at its center.
The statue was peculiar, depicted as a figure clad in yellow robes without a sculpted distinct face – a special humanoid existence. The worn and tattered yellow robe had patterns resembling tendrils at its base.
Beside it, a name was inscribed…
“Golden Spectacular Mysteriously Yellow something something… Fortune Sovereign?”
Colin murmured to himself, but he cut off halfway, alertly skipping the middle part, not voicing it entirely.
From the surrounding arrangements, it seemed to be a shrine, and it bore some resemblance to an ancient stage. Colin couldn’t quite understand most of the terms associated with its name, but he comprehended the word “Fortune.”
‘Hiss, these days, people will worship just about anything.’
Colin couldn’t help but ponder the situation:
“6.”
And it was at that moment, the inexplicable songs of praise grew increasingly eerie.
.
.
.
ps: Update first, revise later.
Also, I’m shamelessly asking for a monthly ticket…

chapters.title: Chapter 558 - 558 439 Yellow Garment Hermit Society_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 558: Chapter 439 “Yellow Garment Hermit Society”_1 Chapter 558: Chapter 439 “Yellow Garment Hermit Society”_1 “Ahhhh…”
Eerie, hollow voices echoed around their ears, causing everyone but Colin to suffer from dizziness and blurred vision upon hearing the strange, singing-like yet praise-like sounds.
It was as if they had stood up too quickly after squatting for a long time, their brains momentarily deprived of blood, vision darkening.
When the darkness before their eyes faded, and they could see clearly again, everyone couldn’t help but catch their breath.
They saw that, in the middle of the area, a large group of figures wrapped in what seemed to be gray cloth had appeared out of nowhere.
The strange, eerie chanting that resonated throughout the empty mall originated from them.
At first listen, the figures seemed to be emitting sounds akin to singing or praising, but upon closer listening, it was faintly discernible that they resembled people arguing with each other, cursing, as noisy as a marketplace.
“What’s going on here…” An Official Level Six person shook his head forcefully, a bunch of charm-like imprints surfaced on his body, suppressing some indescribable influence, and then he noticed.
Those extra figures did not seem to be targeting them.
Instead, they were scattered all over, arguing with one another, rather than with them…
Or perhaps, it was as if they didn’t see the people dealing with the incident at the scene at all.
It was as if…
They were engaged in some kind of special script performance?
At this moment, the Level Six felt the influence he had suppressed within him suddenly grow stronger.
He suddenly harbored a desire to join the quarrel among those people.
“No…!”
The Level Six bit his tongue, a sharp pain stimulating clarity, and his mind sobered up significantly.
Only a few seconds had passed since the anomaly appeared, but when he came to his senses, he found that several of his subordinates had already been enveloped in a faint black mist, inexplicably arguing and loudly cursing at each other…
“I told you! I don’t eat cilantro! Why do you always insist on adding it when we go out to eat?!”
“Damn it, damn it…”
“You all deserve to die! Everyone who eats cilantro deserves to die!”
“…”
A usually mild-mannered subordinate, his eyes filled with bloodshot veins, was arguing with others, neck stiff and tendons bulging, his face even redder due to congestion.
By the looks of it, he was even showing signs of violence at a word of disagreement!
“You’re crazy! When the hell did you ever tell me you eat cilantro?! And usually, you don’t even mention your dislike for cilantro. How are we supposed to know that?! Huh? You don’t eat it but don’t say it, and now you blow up?!”
Another subordinate, stronger and a Fourth Level, was seemingly more rational than the mild one, but not by much…
It seemed they were both oblivious to the absurdness of their argument.
“You guys can even fight over such a petty thing, you… No, that’s not right!”
The Level Six’s eyes flickered, realizing something, he immediately exerted his power to maintain his status, not to be contaminated by the bizarre emotions, thus becoming one of the participants in this chaotic play.
‘The source of danger does not seem to have any concealment; it can be sensed directly below.’
He could clearly feel a strange danger emanating from the lower ground floor of the mall, which appeared to be the location of a lifestyle supermarket.
It was just uncertain whether this situation might be a trap.
Compared to Colin, who could accurately reproduce a certain scene, he could only have a rough intuition.
Sensing the increasingly deepening Domain around him and that inexplicable atmosphere, like that of a stage play.
He realized he must resolve it quickly before the crisis erupted…
“We need people to come with us…”
While thinking, he saw that all his subordinates seemed to have succumbed, but quickly, he noticed that the new team that had come over and was thought to be trying to steal the limelight, seemed to be largely unaffected?
This…
All are combat forces above Fourth Level?
If that’s the case, everything is under control!
“I need five Fourth Level and above personnel skilled in breaking through and assaulting, preferably of the ‘Divine Strike’ type, and one Fourth Level ‘Destiny Propeller’…”
After speaking quickly, the Level Six waited for people to volunteer, ready to rush down.
However, as his words fell, no one responded. Instead, everyone’s gaze turned toward the leader of the newcomer team, who is said to be the captain of the Fifth Level personnel.
He frowned, was about to say something, then paused noticeably.
It was only then that he spotted something off about their team…
“Fuck, what the hell is with your team?”
The Level Six was shocked.
He discerned from the faint “black lines” on these people that this group of more than twenty individuals were all “Fate Propellers”—
Is this the sort of team that a person with a healthy mind would assemble?
All “Fate Propellers,” and all low-level at that; would this be fielded in current times if the casualty rate wasn’t high enough?
…
If it were normal times, he would surely have realized that the one leading such a team would be no ordinary person.
But with the urgency and some interference now, he hadn’t thought of that.
“Damn it!”
The Level Six then turned to look at Qin Chuan, Hu Zheng, and Xia Liufang, but his gaze eventually moved to the captain of this oddball team with a contribution that amounted to over four-fifths of uselessness.
The others were somewhat affected, only this slim captain appeared completely unaffected.
Even seemed, like himself, to have pinpointed the anomaly source.
Obviously, even if the slender captain’s strength wasn’t equal to his, he likely wouldn’t be far behind.
Or perhaps he carried with him some powerful item…
Either way, he could assist and coordinate with him to rush down and deal with the trouble.

chapters.title: Chapter 559 - 559 439 Yellow Garment Hermit Society_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 559: Chapter 439 “Yellow Garment Hermit Society”_2 Chapter 559: Chapter 439 “Yellow Garment Hermit Society”_2 Bearing a certain desire to argue and join the fray as if wishing to become part of the “curse play,” the Sixth Level Personnel spoke:
“It seems you too have confirmed the anomaly’s location. Now, let’s go down together and destroy that dangerous source…”
Upon hearing his direct question, Colin did not immediately reply.
Instead, he squinted his eyes, perceiving the images in his mind, and spent a few more seconds deciding whether to run or to fight, before shifting his gaze back to the Sixth Level Personnel standing about seven or eight meters away:
“Go down for what?”
“To resolve the crisis at its source. As it stands, we appear to have been dragged into some domain. To leave, we must deal with the source. Otherwise, trying to flee now would make us easy targets…”
The Sixth Level Personnel quickly explained, but, halfway through his sentence, he suddenly realized something and furrowed his brow: “You haven’t… failed to detect the anomaly, have you?”
If Colin hadn’t detected it, the man would have to seriously consider whether Colin genuinely possessed the strength to be compared with him.
At this moment, he also realized that he couldn’t gauge the strength emanating from Colin at all.
“Locked on to? Yes…”
Colin said casually, taking a high-explosive grenade out of his pocket:
“But I didn’t plan on going down. I was thinking of just dropping a bomb from up here, blowing up an entrance. If we were to descend normally, we might step on some specially arranged traps, which would be risky.”
Although Colin felt the anomaly’s intensity wasn’t high, he still sensed an inexplicable threat from that sculpture.
So if he could solve it remotely, he certainly wasn’t going to approach it up close.
But upon hearing this, the Sixth Level Personnel was stunned, momentarily doubting whether he had heard wrong…
Blow a hole?
What was he talking about?
The mall’s floor was quite thick. Even if they did want to blow it up, they’d need to place specialized directional explosives, and they did… indeed have remote-controlled directional bombs with them.
However, those explosives might suffice for blowing up walls, but not so much for floors.
What’s more…
Looking at the grenade Colin pulled out, he wondered if the other man had been contaminated to the extreme to be acting so “rationally” and foolishly.
After all, “madness” isn’t just about shouting and not distinguishing between friends and foes…
Colin’s behavior seemed rather in line with that.
However, as the high-explosion styled grenade was thrown out, followed by the clang of it hitting the ground and its subsequent detonation.
Errorwhat burst forth wasn’t a shockwave, but a fog-like substance…
“Boom!”
A swath of orange-red light suddenly erupted in front of them, almost illuminating the area…
Immediately afterward, the expanding burst of flame, as if controlled by something, surged towards the ground.
The seemingly impenetrable floor melted as if it were foam being preheated…
A spacious hole was instantly scorched open by the flames.
“What kind of fire is that, so exaggerated?” the Sixth Level Personnel was dumbstruck.
By feel alone, he hadn’t even sensed any heat, yet the floor was completely melted; it was truly against the grain—
Even though “Extraordinary Ones” were a thing in this world.
But there were certain things that still had to follow the basic laws, they wouldn’t overturn too drastically.
At the very least, a Fifth Level Personnel definitely couldn’t accomplish this!
“Is this really what an ordinary Fifth Level Extraordinary Being could cause?”
He looked at the rapidly melting hole in the ground, his heart shaking with shock.
Which family’s Fifth Level could do this on their own?
He would believe it if it were Eighth Level!
At this very moment, he sharply realized that there might indeed be a gap in strength between them, only that the disparity could be the other way around.
But, he couldn’t linger on that thought…
As the flames swiftly melted the ground, burning out a passageway about five or six meters in diameter, he finally saw below, an ancient stage built of redwood that was completely out of place with modern things.
The stage was adorned with many lanterns, exuding an ancient charm.
Behind the stage, a statue donned in a yellow robe was placed, impassively watching some figures arguing on stage…
“This is the source of the anomaly!”
The Sixth Level Official Personnel immediately confirmed this.
He threw out a handful of charms which burned in the air, then turned into streaks of lightning, hurtling towards that direction.
But, halfway there, the lightning vanished.
And, at the moment when he launched his attack with a Direct Gaze at the yellow-robed statue, he suddenly felt his eyes bulge, his vision blur, and a wave of nausea surged up from his stomach…
In that instant, the statue appeared eerily lifelike, and the tendrils-like patterns engraved at the bottom of its yellow robe began to wriggle…
The “arguing” figures around it all stopped their bickering, twisted their necks, and looked their way, their gazes heavy and oppressive, making it difficult to breathe.
The next moment, as if driven by some will, they all charged towards them!
“Why do you have to put cilantro in the food! Why the cilantro!”
“Die! Monster! It’s all because of you that my daughter became a vegetable…”
“Why do you talk so loud?!”
“…”
Amid the roar-like cursing, over a hundred figures attacked, and the Sixth Level Personnel even spotted some Fifth Level Personnel and their subordinates with Extraordinary abilities who had been garrisoned here.
Behind these people, there seemed to be a sinister thread connecting them to the statue in the yellow robe.
“Have they been turned into blood puppets?”
He wanted to strike back hard but also worried that this might kill these people.
At the same time, he glanced sideways, eager to see how that abnormally strong “Fifth Level Personnel” planned to act.

chapters.title: Chapter 560 - 560 439 Yellow Garment Hermit Society_3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 560: Chapter 439 “Yellow Garment Hermit Society”_3 Chapter 560: Chapter 439 “Yellow Garment Hermit Society”_3 Then he saw the other party fumble in his pocket, pulling out a transparent, flame-red object resembling an eyeball, pinching the top and bottom, and bringing it to the socket of his left eye with a forceful push.
“Pop.”
The Sixth Level Personnel twitched at the corner of his eye and saw a bunch of burning flames emerging from the other’s left eye socket.
The entire left eye seemed to have been ignited.
At that moment, Colin was unaware of what the Sixth Level Personnel was thinking. He quietly rotated his eyeball, ignoring the various puppets being controlled that were attacking him, and looked directly at the statue. Then, with a slight opening of his mouth, he silently muttered:
“General.”
“Boom!”
In an instant,
despite the considerable distance, the statue on the stage exploded like a gas cylinder.
Weird screams echoed from all directions immediately.
It was at this moment that Colin saw the statue seemingly trying to sustain itself by controlling the puppet strings to absorb the life force of others, or perhaps activate Second Order.
But, unfortunately for it…
It was nothing more than a statue with a high status but with actual capabilities that did not reach the strength of a Third Level Containment Subject.
Colin burned it down to the last trace of blood.
Then, with a raise of his hand, he fired a 155-caliber Enchanted Bullet.
With a “bang,” the statue burst apart, shattering into the sky as burned fragments.
Everything here started to return to normal.
And the “puppets” that had been controlled fell to the ground, their fates unknown, as the statue was destroyed.
“That’s it? It’s resolved?” The Sixth Level Personnel found it hard to believe, feeling it was surreal.
This… he recalled his previous thoughts.
Suddenly, he felt vaguely guilty…
Colin lifted his hand and snapped his fingers crisply. In the next moment, flames began to burn on the bodies of all the people who had fallen around them.
Without waiting for a question, he directly said:
“These flames will last about thirty minutes. They will slowly burn off the contamination in their bodies while also minimally sustaining their status.
“After the flames go out, it’s best to administer immediate help to avoid unnecessary deaths afterward.”
“I understand…” The Sixth Level Personnel nodded hastily.
“Also, what do you know about this anomaly?”
Colin asked, his tone somewhat somber, reminded of what he had glimpsed when he killed the statue in an instant.
For a moment, he sensed through the statue, across infinite distances, a tremendously terrifying lifeform seemingly gazing this way…
And around it, there were various horrifying shadows densely scattered throughout the vast cosmos, terror-inducing to anyone who saw them.
Each one was incredibly powerful…
Just a brief observation gave him an inexplicable sense of near-death.
Fortunately, Colin decisively severed all connections with the heart, not daring to take another glance…
Otherwise, that feeling of near-death might have become a reality.
‘Damn it, what kinds of things has ‘Bonfire Company’ provoked?’
Colin suspected that these might be the “Outsiders” Xu Duojin talked about.
Upon hearing his words, the Sixth Level Official Personnel shook his head to indicate he didn’t know, this being his first encounter.
However, Xia Liufang suddenly approached and said, “If it’s not unexpected, that thing just now was a member of the Yellow Garment Hermit Society. They are… quite mysterious, worshipping a very dangerous entity, but I don’t know the specifics. I’ve only heard my family mention them, and I don’t have the clearance to understand more.”
“Yellow Garment Hermit Society?”
Colin nodded slightly, taking note of the name, intending to ask Xu Duojin or Old Master Wu about it later.
Afterward, he didn’t linger much longer in this place.
Leading his team, they did a round in the vicinity. Once certain there was nothing else to see, they decided not to stay any longer.
This incident, from entry to resolution, took less than ten minutes.
Basically, a straightforward push through…
After that, they left as if nothing had happened, ready to move on to the next fight.
.
.
.
ps: Post first, edit later…
Also, asking for some early-month votes.

chapters.title: Chapter 561 - 561 440 Trying on the Skirt of Myriad
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 561: Chapter 440 Trying on the “Skirt of Myriad Starlight”._1 Chapter 561: Chapter 440 Trying on the “Skirt of Myriad Starlight”._1 In the flickering heat of the firelight, not a bit surprised, another source of anomaly was burnt into charcoal…
“The intensity of these eyes… indeed is formidable. Typically, just a glance is enough to strike down enemies within a certain range through the air; and the flame they wield is that compacted kind of fire…”
Colin nodded, granting his approval to the “Favor of the Flamebearer,” which was, in fact, not all that kind a tool.
Unfortunately, though powerful, it was somewhat taxing on the mind…
Every use felt like being forced to solve a dozen complex Olympiad math problems at once, leaving one’s brain feeling as if it had been pummeled, somewhat fatigued.
And with consecutive use, this negative effect would multiply.
Colin even suspected that using it several times in quick succession might smooth out the surface of his cerebral cortex.
Then his smile became one of pure innocence…
Perhaps, there was a chance to compete for the Summit of Innocence…
“My laughter could also be deemed pure.”
Colin muttered to himself.
Of course, upon further contemplation, he felt as though he couldn’t possibly compete. The phrase mmsd represented an insurmountable pinnacle of awe he dared not surpass.
However, although there were some side effects, with sensible usage—say, setting off a blast every fifteen minutes or so.
The problem wasn’t that significant…
Furthermore, Colin had yet to use “Direct Gaze – First Flame Summon,” but the indirect contact had given him a sense of its power.
Based on his own assessment, combined with the single-use orange artifact “Thorn Punishment” and his various other methods.
Colin was confident he could resolve all but a few special types of Level 2 Containment Subjects and, given the right conditions, even had the power to kill lower-ranking Ancient Gods.
That is to say, First Level Containment Subjects recognized by the company!
It should be known that killing and inflicting heavy damage, forcing a retreat, are not the same concept…
“Next time I encounter those things, I won’t be so powerless…”
As he pondered, Colin tested his skills against the anomalies he encountered, while leading the soy sauce brigade to the next location of anomaly.
…
Meanwhile, at the same time, in a desolate desert area where the temperature was extremely low and a bright moon hung high in the night sky, a group shrouded in yellow bandages, from a distance appearing as though clad in yellow cloaks, moved forward in silence.
They were one of the teams from the Yellow Garment Hermit Society sent to seek out the hiding place of “Dawn Star”…
However, suddenly, one of them leaped into the air and fell back, stiff as a board.
Then, after a while, began to roll frantically on the ground.
“Ah!! It’s so hot! Put it out! Hurry up and put out the fire! Quickly put it out! Ah!!!”
The screams suddenly pierced the night in that area.
The other dozen or so members looked at their comrade rolling on the ground in puzzlement, wondering what was wrong with him.
There was clearly no fire on his body…
The group was somewhat at a loss, using their own methods in attempts to wake their fellow member.
Yet, it seemed to be of little use…
This colleague, cursed by some unknown spell, seemed to be ceaselessly scorched by nonexistent flames.
Eventually, as his heart-wrenching screams continued, a senior officer couldn’t bear it any longer, stepped forward to hold him down, extended a palm that was twice as long as that of an ordinary man, and squeezed the neck, pulling out the head along with the spine.
Instantly, the howling stopped…
“What, what is this?” a member of the Yellow Garment Hermit Society asked, confused.
“If I remember correctly, he was once bound to an altar sculpture. Perhaps, someone traced back through that object and attacked him,” said the senior officer in a gentle tone, appearing rather scholarly—if one ignored the corpse at his feet and the head in his hand.
“To kill a person who is who knows how far away through a sculpture?” the other cultists exclaimed in shock.
“Yes, it’s likely that a very powerful individual has noticed him.”
The senior officer roughly understood the cause and felt some trepidation.
They had specifically induced the altar concealed in the shopping mall base to create chaos, allowing them to escape successfully. Otherwise, they might have been captured by official Extraordinary Ones…
But unexpectedly, a subordinate who had been only minimally bound to the sculpture was then remotely attacked.
This…
If one were to make a real-world analogy, it was almost like killing someone through an internet connection.
Colin himself probably didn’t know that the flames he inadvertently intensified while blocking the gaze of the Outer God could accidentally kill someone en route…
“However, I have received a faint revelation. This attack only reached him. For now, just handle the body,” the senior officer said, soothing the team while extending a hand to control the yellow cloth wrapping and processing the subordinate’s corpse.
This desert region might look barren as if not a soul could be seen.
But in reality, a large group of people had already converged here.
If the body wasn’t disposed of quickly, it would attract the followers of “Red Moon”…
The sensitivity of those creatures to fresh, unconscious flesh rivals that of flies to feces.
A slight misstep could bring in a swarm…
And once a fight breaks out, it would draw all manner of malevolent forces.
Even with the great enemy “Dawn Star” ahead of them, those wretches would still not pass up an opportunity for a cheap shot, devoid of any semblance of a bigger picture!
Soon, as the yellow cloth completed enveloping the subordinate’s body, a secret force emerged, causing the body to age rapidly and wither until it became dry and brittle bones.
To the followers of “Red Moon.”
Even turned to skeletons, they wouldn’t pass up the chance to reclaim them if the opportunity arose.

chapters.title: Chapter 562 - 562 440 Trying on the Skirt of Myriad
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 562: Chapter 440 Trying on the “Skirt of Myriad Starlight”._2 Chapter 562: Chapter 440 Trying on the “Skirt of Myriad Starlight”._2 But their perception will be greatly reduced, so there’s no need to worry for the time being…
After completing these tasks, the senior executives breathed a sigh of relief.
At that moment, a member of the “Yellow Garment Hermit Society” approached and whispered, “A team from another area just sent word that the exploration here is finished, and it’s highly unlikely that the ‘City at the Lake’s Bottom’ is located here. They’ve advised us to check another area…”
“Understood, rest here for an hour then we’ll set out…” the senior executive nodded.
Although the desert temperatures at night were just a few degrees, it didn’t affect them much.
Those who were dispatched to prevent the descent of an evil god…
Were all top-notch elites, blessed by the Great Will, with bodies that feared not the common weather’s chill.
“These damned ‘Dawn Star’ Heretic Believers, choosing a name like ‘City at the Lake’s Bottom’ made us search most of the lakes around the world, only to find out later that this so-called ‘City at the Lake’s Bottom’ is actually in the world’s largest desert…”
A member of the “Twilight Hermitage” couldn’t help but complain.
They only knew it was in the desert, but had no clue where exactly the enemy could be.
This made them extremely anxious, fearing that a second’s delay would allow the enemy to complete the ‘God Descent’ and then turn around to blockade this world.
“Damn heretic forces, always so devious,” cursed a Heretic Believer who didn’t consider themselves a heretic.
After he spoke, a voice suddenly agreed, “Yes, indeed.”
In the next instant, everyone’s hair stood on end as they rose to their feet, looking toward a direction outside the crowd, “Who’s there!”
“Relax, relax, I mean no harm, one of your own…”
An Asian man wearing a cowboy hat sauntered out, his eyes blood-red, face wearing a polite smile, responding in fluent foreign language:
“I am a member of the ‘Silver Moon Mutual Aid Society’ skilled in vampiric arts, here for the same reason as you, to prevent the ‘Dawn Star,’ this evil god’s descent…
“Perhaps, I think we might work together?”
A few other men with blood-red eyes stood by his side.
“‘Silver Moon Mutual Aid Society’…”
The senior executive clearly had heard of this organization reputedly affiliated with vampires and murmured the name, but did not respond immediately.
The man in the cowboy hat did not rush them, just watched smilingly, seemingly indifferent to the outcome—
After all, their mission was to “unite” all Heretic Forces in solidarity wherever possible.
And not necessarily make them join together.
After a good while of thinking, the senior executive of the “Yellow Garment Hermit Society” finally spoke up, “What can you offer?”
“Some temporary friendships with around thirty other forces, after all, with the ‘Dawn Star’ imminent, it’s better that we join forces rather than confront each other…”
“Otherwise, if that evil god succeeds, there’s no need for me to elaborate on the outcome…”
“Besides, I’ll also share with you our current intelligence, for instance, the potential location of the ‘City at the Lake’s Bottom’ as well as some necessary information. Without unusual measures, you probably won’t even find them before ‘Dawn Star’ descends.”
“That place, when completely sealed, is impossible to enter with conventional means, let alone to glimpse into…”
“By joining us, we can share intelligence and methods to locate the place faster and forcibly open it.”
“To be honest, I highly regard your methods that can twist reality to a certain extent.”
“Moreover, joining us can avert any potential mutual suppression and accidental harm later on…”
The man in the cowboy hat spoke quickly yet clearly, expressing his intent.
In the end, he paused for a few seconds and added,
“Friend, in our homeland, there’s an old saying ‘A wise man submits to circumstances…’
“You wouldn’t want various reasons to lead to our ultimate failure in stopping them, would you?”
Listening to his earnest words, the senior executive remained silent for a while, and after inquiring with a higher-up, he asked again to confirm that the united team didn’t include any “Red Moon” followers, then nodded his head, choosing to join this temporary alliance.
After all, as the other had said, if the forces clashed, it could give the evil god an opportunity.
The result of that would be something no one wanted to witness.
Of course, all could unite, with the exception of the “Red Moon” followers.
Among the various heretic forces, they had all received, in one form or another, revelations from the Great Will they worshiped.
In a time of need, one can join hands with any “enemy.”
But never with “Red Moon” followers.
They’d rather have a meteor smash Earth and be forever trapped, than cooperate with these beings.
If a meteor smashed Earth, the Great Will could still survive.
But if “Red Moon” fully revived, it would target all forms of life—
And it indeed had the power to do so!
So, given the option, he’d rather choose to side with “Bonfire Company” instead of following those “Red Moon.”
Soon, the Asian man wearing a cowboy hat led them into a large camp.
At this moment, a whole bunch of heretic forces were gathered together.
Though the atmosphere was somewhat tense, all the parties were striving for the same goal at the moment, putting aside disputes for the sake of humanity’s future, so no fighting had broken out.
After preliminarily entering the circle, one of the massive joint teams began their operation.
…
Meanwhile, in the desert within the “City at the Lake’s Bottom,” priests, through special means, observed the situation of the outside world, and one after another, couldn’t help but feel a bit panicky—
The heretic forces returning this time were too many!
Every group from around the world that could send people had done so, including official personnel, some private but legal powers, some illegal heretic forces, and a group deemed “The Rat” by everyone (Red Moon) that stubbornly squeezed through…
Nearly a fifth of the world’s top powers were gathered here!
“Hiss, we might be seeing as many as fifteen to twenty Eighth Level Personnel, perhaps even Level 9 Personnel who usually remain out of sight may have secretly followed.”
A “Dawn Star” believer’s heart trembled.
Originally, they thought the heretics would come scattered into countless groups on their own…
That way, they would be easily killed.
But now, influenced by some damned fellows, each one had chosen to band together, seeking common ground while reserving differences.
Should they really let them enter this place when the time comes?
After all, there is a significant difference between loose sand and a united force.
“It’s fine, these wicked heretic forces, as soon as the ‘Dawn Star’ descends, we will be able to clean them up all at once, restoring peace to the world…”
The High Priest said viciously.
“But…”
“Do you not have faith?”
“Of course I do!”
“Don’t worry, the Master has already conveyed His will not long ago, assuring us there is nothing to worry about, and I have received a promise that when the time comes, the great ‘Dawn Star’ will grant us ecstasy akin to ascending to heaven, we just need to arrange this place according to the words of the Envoy of God…”
Upon hearing his words, all believers felt relieved. It was good to know the Great Will was aware of the situation here.
They worried that the Master’s envoy might not be fully aware of the situation, leading to an accident.
But clearly, everything was still under control.
Then, without pondering much further, one by one, they looked forward to experiencing what the ecstasy of “ascending to heaven” really felt like.
They had not enjoyed the torment of the “Starlight Maiden” for many days.
They felt unbearably uncomfortable all over…
They definitely wanted to indulge in a great celebration when the time came.
As for the truthfulness of these words, they did not doubt at all; after all, would that great existence deceive them?
…
Time flew, and a few days later, on January 10th.
Over the past few days, Colin had been leading a gang of onlookers, clearing all matters within the nearby cities. Having secured his home front against battles, he then shifted his entire focus onto the affairs of the “City at the Lake’s Bottom.”
“This time, almost everyone is here.”
Colin, receiving intelligence from the “City at the Lake’s Bottom,” couldn’t help but click his tongue.
Currently, under his secret orchestration, these forces were banding together in search groups and had nearly found the entrance to the “City at the Lake’s Bottom” several times.
But they were always just a bit short…
“We can’t drag this out for too long, in a couple of days I need to make another trip to ‘World Code 4’, I also need to prepare well.”
Colin nodded. Many high-level powers with all sorts of mysterious methods had gathered here.
Even he couldn’t afford to be careless.
However, just as Colin took out the “Skirt of Myriad Starlight,” looking troubled and hesitant about whether to try it on first,
a prayer from the “City at the Lake’s Bottom” reached his ears through a special channel…
“Envoy of God, it seems they have found us…”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 563 - 563 441 Victory Will Belong to Humanity_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 563: Chapter 441 Victory Will Belong to Humanity!_1 Chapter 563: Chapter 441 Victory Will Belong to Humanity!_1 “We’ve found it?”
Colin was slightly taken aback, but not surprised; after all, the general location had already been pinpointed, and with a plethora of extraordinary search methods at their disposal, it would indeed have been problematic had they not found it.
As he pondered, words of sincere prayer continued to emerge.
“The discovery here was made by a joint team numbering around five hundred, among them are three individuals whose strength meets the official standard of Level 7…”
“There’s one who is suspected to be Level 8…”
“Overall, their strength is formidable and they have sent out signals, drawing most of the search personnel closer. By estimates, they could all arrive here by three o’clock tomorrow morning, possibly bringing the number to over five thousand…”
“Currently, they are still engaged in preliminary exploration, dispatching only a small number of people to investigate and test…”
“According to some hidden lookouts and spies we have infiltrated among them, we received information that these people are likely to begin a large-scale forceful breakthrough at four o’clock sharp in the morning. Even with an optimistic estimate, we can hold at most until just after four thirty in the morning.”
“Please forgive our incompetence, but the enemy is simply too numerous, and all are extremely elite individuals, also carrying a large amount of powerful artifacts….”
“Moreover, the magical barrier protecting this independent space will exhibit certain breaches every day between four and five o’clock.”
“Respected Envoy of God, what should we…”
How should we respond?
Colin shook his head slightly and pondered for a moment.
“These guys only start breaking through the formation at four o’clock tomorrow morning? That’s a bit slow. And I estimate that with their strength, if no expense is spared, they might be able to tear open an entrance before two o’clock.”
“Rather than waiting until four o’clock when the formation naturally reveals vulnerabilities due to changes over time.”
Colin recalled the mission brief related to the “City at the Lake’s Bottom” that he had previously projected into.
This independent space is like some special isolated island; before the tide recedes, the only way to cross is by taking a ship, braving great risks.
But after the tide ebbs, there will be a land passage that people can cross…
Although the duration of this passage is not long, it is still enough for the Heretic Forces to use.
If we let these people come in like this.
The casualties of the Heretic Forces would be minimized.
“It seems that these people must have acquired some knowledge about the ‘City at the Lake’s Bottom’ and chose to enter in large numbers only after waiting until four o’clock. This is understandable; after all, with so many heretic forces, there are always some who possess unique methods and can deduce certain things…”
“Some higher entities have even personally entered the fray in response.”
“But to stop the ‘Evil God’ from descending and still play tricks like this?”
“How could you do it without a fearless, do-or-die spirit?”
Colin chuckled, planning to give these fellows a proper challenge at the appointed time.
He had to force them into making an entrance with maximum casualties.
The best outcome would be one where every inch is soaked in blood…
The more brutal the fight, the more amusement Colin derived from it.
In the midst of these thoughts and decisions, he used the special channel provided through the company’s mission to send a response to the follower of “Dawn Star”:
“Be prepared for high-intensity large-scale warfare after midnight.”
The lofty, distant, and magnificent voice, like an irresistible surge, entered the ears of the high priest of “Dawn Star,” the one able to communicate with “God,” causing him to freeze for a moment.
‘After midnight?’
As the high priest, he was well aware, just like Colin, that some patterns of the “City at the Lake’s Bottom” might have been deciphered by the enemy, hence the deliberate choice of that specific time.
Yet the Divine Envoy suggested being ready for intense battle at midnight.
This was the time when the Power of the Starlight within the “City at the Lake’s Bottom” was most robust, far stronger than at ordinary times.
Why would the enemy foolishly risk so much at that point in time…
No, that’s not it—after a brief hesitation, he immediately realized the reason: the Divine Envoy said so because there must be a reason for those heretic forces to be forced to attack at that time…
And that reason, the high priest only had to ponder for a moment before he sharply drew his breath, his pupils constricting, realizing the reason—
“Master” would descend at that time in an unstoppable manner.
So these people would have to struggle desperately at that moment!
Realizing this, the high priest nearly smiled, straining not to laugh out loud, after striving for so many years, they were finally about to succeed!
“We will follow your will in all things!”
Having said this, the sense of being watched from afar vanished.
“Hahaha, in just a few more hours, everything here will change completely!!”
…
“Nine fifty-seven, there’s still a little time left.”
After ending the conversation, Colin glanced at the electronic clock on the wall and then withdrew his gaze, looking at the special garment in his hands. He hesitated for a moment, and finally put it on.
As it draped over him, Colin felt as if something had changed.
But… it seemed as if nothing had changed at all?
He felt himself, and it seemed just like he was wearing a normal raincoat?
In his bewilderment, Colin suddenly had an epiphany, his gaze shifting.
There, reflected in an old-fashioned wardrobe with a mirror, his appearance had undergone a drastic transformation, becoming a figure shrouded in a dark robe, over two meters tall with a familiar female form.

chapters.title: Chapter 564 - 564 441 Victory will belong to Humanity_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 564: Chapter 441 Victory will belong to Humanity!_2 Chapter 564: Chapter 441 Victory will belong to Humanity!_2 With just a glance, Colin recognized the original owner of this figure—the “Starlight Maiden”.
“Hiss…”
Colin looked down at himself only to realize that he seemed to be himself without any changes.
The changes had occurred only in appearance…
Or to be more precise, in the perspectives of others observing him.
“Well, that’s fine. If my appearance had changed into that of a woman as well, that would indeed be somewhat unacceptable,” he muttered, feeling somewhat relieved.
Then he withdrew his gaze, took out his cellphone to compose a message and was about to send it to Old Master Wu…
But before he could send it, he suddenly noticed a new message from the other side.
“Beautiful lady, who are you? Where is he?”
‘Eh? Has he noticed something is amiss, but doesn’t understand the situation?’ thought Colin, surprised.
Perhaps in Old Master Wu’s “view,” he could only perceive that the person he was talking to had changed into the “Starlight Maiden” and did not realize it was Colin who had transformed.
‘Looking at this, the company’s methods are still reliable. Even Old Master Wu, a Ninth Level “Fate Propeller” who always seems so mysterious and knowledgeable, couldn’t detect the issue…’
‘However, on second thought, Old Master Wu is also quite sensitive. If I hadn’t been almost certain that there might be some hidden observers around without actual surveillance, I might have thought he was monitoring me all the time.’
Considering the text on his phone, Colin thought for a moment and chose not to explain this point, but instead sent the message he had just composed.
“Begin to act according to Plan A, meet in the ‘City at the Lake’s Bottom’.”
It was only a few minutes after the message was sent that he received a reply, “OK, I will arrange for Xu Duojin to go.”
Seeing this, Colin put away his phone and began to absorb the knowledge from the “Skirt of Myriad Starlight”.
First, he temporarily inherited some abilities of the “Starlight Maiden”.
Second, there were the “Starlight Maiden’s” personality traits and preferences…
Soon, Colin acquired some peculiar knowledge, such as why the “Starlight Maiden” would lash her believers?
It wasn’t really because of any sadistic tendencies, but rather because, in the “Starlight Maiden’s” eyes, those “believers” looked like succulent, roasted two-legged sheep, exuding an aroma of “humanity” all over.
She couldn’t help but draw out humanity using her own methods.
‘To be specific, it’s more like licking an ice cream? Ugh, that seems even more disgusting. But, the “Starlight Maiden” actively absorbing some humanity? It seems she might have caught a human affliction, and quite a severe one at that…’
Colin stroked his chin, his face showing a thoughtful expression.
Of course, after continuously drawing out these people’s “humanity”, the “Starlight Maiden’s” own character in this human aspect, also began to morph.
Soon, in another place, located in the world’s largest desert, at the central altar of the “City at the Lake’s Bottom”, myriads of starlight converged, and the beautiful and haughty form of the “Starlight Maiden,” with a seemingly perfect sense of proportion, descended.
It was the moment his figure appeared.
The entire “City at the Lake’s Bottom” erupted into anarchy.
“Praise the Highest Being, praise the will of the ‘Dawn Star’!”
“We will follow Your figure, unto death without rest…”
“Please whip me hard! Before I die, I want to feel Your punishing tentacles once more…”
“…”
A mix of praises and mad ravings arrived.
Colin paid no attention to them, but through this location, he sensed some external situations, extended his hand, and bright radiance began to coalesce there.
The next instant, the terrifying presence of the “Dawn Star” made its arrival felt…
Authority from a higher entity spread out like a tsunami…
Meanwhile, outside the “City at the Lake’s Bottom”, in a special Rift Valley, myriads of dense water vapors converged below. Standing at the edge of the chasm looking forward, it seemed as though one could see a “lake” formed by the dense mists.
Occasional flashes within the “lake” subtly refracted the illusion of a city…
“…After all this, even the ‘lake’ in ‘City at the Lake’s Bottom’ is fake,” griped a member of the Heretic Church after realizing this fact.
Clearly, many were deeply deceived by the name.
“The pattern here has already been divined; as soon as the time comes, we’ll charge in and catch them off guard…”
Another member of the heretic forces skilled in divination said.
He was wearing a robe strikingly similar to those of the “Dawn Star” believers, but the constellations painted on his robe did not include the “Dawn Star” but rather other sources of starlight.
Hearing his words, no one objected, as all of these people belonged to the same overarching category of “the cosmos.”
Obviously, to know more details…
In fact, their success in finding the exact location was largely due to the knowledge of these very people.
However, just at this moment, from within the dense fog below the canyon, a terrifying and startling aura suddenly trembled forth.
The moment everyone felt this aura, they involuntarily shivered, and a word flashed across their minds—
“True God”!
Even though everyone’s beliefs differed, the fear of such a high-order being was deep in their bones.
“How is this possible?! According to our understanding, He, He shouldn’t be appearing at this time!” a member of the heretic forces wrapped in a starry robe exclaimed.
“This is just the aura spreading, not the actual arrival, we can’t wait any longer!”
Someone shouted, and immediately, a person made a move, sending out several special chains that pierced into the mist, accurately hitting a twinkling “light.”
Trying to use it to open a path to the inside.
Seeing this, some people hesitated for a moment but also used their own abilities to forcibly push apart the starlight.
A path faintly revealed itself.
“Charge! Follow me to stop the false god’s descent!”
Several dozen heretic believers leaped in without hesitation, and almost the instant they entered, their bodies were crushed and exploded by the invisible power of the starlight, blood and bone scattering…
It was a sight to make one recoil in horror.
However, at that moment, some corrosive force within the blood surfaced, forming a bright red gate amidst the starlight, laying out a path.
“The Red Passage has been established, charge with me!”
A person cried out and leaped forward.
“Kill! For the sake of our Earth’s tomorrow, not to fall into evil hands!”
“To maintain Earth’s purity, our duty is undeniable.”
“…”
Under someone’s rallying cry, thousands of linked members of the heretic forces started to mobilize.
Even though the Red Passage had been established, it did not mean safety.
Upon entering, they immediately encountered various ambushes and attacks, and right from the start, heretic believers equivalent to Level Seven Personnel were severely injured, on the brink of death.
Meanwhile, a group of “Dawn Star” followers also charged out: “For the ‘Master’s’ arrival, everyone, charge with me, destroy this place!”
They were surrounded by countless twinkling stars, secret forces surging, erasing the mysterious power above the Red Passage…
The Red Passage, bolstered by various forces, also showed signs of beginning to collapse.
At this moment, a dying Level Seven cultist suddenly supported the passage, sacrificing all his blood to stabilize the somewhat shaky path!
“Knock down one of me, and more will come! You can’t stop us, victory will belong to humanity!!!”
His already desiccated, skeletal body hadn’t finished speaking when a streak of starlight swept across, cutting him into countless pieces.
It was at this moment that more allied heretic believers trampled over the path solidified by his blood and charged in.
A heretic believer of immense power waved his hand, and dozens of lightning bolts flashed, instantly striking down the enemies in the front.
Then, as they charged fearlessly one after another, the passage was finally completely opened!
After 27 minutes and 06 seconds, they succeeded in breaking through the portal to the “City at the Lake’s Bottom”!
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 565 - 565 442 The Evil God Guards the National Gate
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 565: Chapter 442: The Evil God Guards the National Gate, Heretic Dies for the Altar of the State_1 Chapter 565: Chapter 442: The Evil God Guards the National Gate, Heretic Dies for the Altar of the State_1 When they forced their way through the passage, what appeared before everyone was an unexpectedly modern city, resembling a downtown area rather than an evil church headquarters.
“Over there!”
A member of the heretic forces pointed in a certain direction, and soon, in the sky above what seemed to be the city center, they saw a sphere of light emitting a blinding brilliance.
The extremely high-lumen light almost illuminated the entire urban space.
For a moment, everyone was almost unable to open their eyes.
Moreover, they directly faced the terrifying pressure coming from a superior being within this brilliance.
Despite long since having lost their fear of death…
Yet…
The fear in everyone’s heart could not help but emerge, and they all froze in their tracks.
However, it was at this moment that some severely wounded people stepped forward…
“Quick! It has not truly arrived yet! It’s still in the process of entering this place! If we rush forward now, there might still be a chance to stop it!”
“Those of us who are seriously injured can’t survive much longer, we’ll go first!”
“The future is in your hands!”
With those words, dozens of heretics with severe injuries charged forward, once again rallying the morale of the crowd.
The massive coalition of heretic forces advanced once more.
At the same time, the High Priest of the “Dawn Star” also arrived:
“Block these heretical evils for me, behind us lies the hope of the world, we have no escape! Kill! We must not let them destroy our only hope!”
Countless believers, hidden by the light of the “Dawn Star,” launched their attacks on the invaders.
On first contact, they immediately killed a large number of the vanguard.
The battle saw an extremely high death toll the instant the two sides met.
Above the altar, Colin, watching his own followers of the “Dawn Star” fighting desperately before him, as well as the heretic organizations’ coalition forces surging in with the same fearless spirit, felt so moved that he was almost splitting with laughter.
‘Good, good, good, that’s it, kill even more fiercely, are there still some at the back?’
‘What are you waiting for, the “Dawn Star” is about to descend, go on! Let me see your determination!’
‘I want to see rivers of blood!’
Using the effect of his robe, Colin simulated the arrival of the “Dawn Star”…
The effect was so realistic he initially thought he might actually summon that entity.
But on second thought, the item was given for a company mission, and it had a seal.
So even if he really did summon this being…
It might not necessarily be an enemy, but a colleague instead.
Of course, given the current situation, it should only be a sufficiently realistic special effect; the “Dawn Star” was unlikely to come.
‘When it comes to playing with “special effects,” the company is indeed a master.’
Colin couldn’t help but sigh once more.
….
Outside “City at the Lake’s Bottom,” by the edge of the canyon, many who sensed the situation almost without any hesitation leaped down, joining the great holy war to prevent the arrival of the evil god.
Yet, there were still some who watched vigilantly and did not take action immediately.
They always felt something was off but couldn’t put their finger on it.
However, it was at this moment that everyone suddenly felt a chill in their hearts and looked in a certain direction.
They saw mounds of earth bulging on the ground a distance away, and a large, sinister red coffin burst from the soil, surrounded by rows of hands, hundreds in total, all tightly gripping the coffin to prevent the lid from falling off.
Above the coffin, one could also see a blood-drenched ‘7’ symbol.
A chilling and inexplicable sensation spread throughout the area the instant the coffin appeared…
At this moment, after emerging from the ground, all these hands let go.
With a “bang,” the two-meter-wide and three-meter-tall coffin lid fell to the ground.
Dark grey mist swirled inside.
Within seconds, vague human silhouettes could be seen stepping out.
“The ‘Coffin of the Styx’… It’s the officials; they’ve come too…” a high-ranking member of the heretic organizations recognized this artifact, knowing it to be a well-known transportation tool from the Global Supernatural Alliance.
It had one main coffin and seven auxiliary coffins interconnected; opening it in the past would summon countless evil spirits…
However, after being constrained, it had become a usable tool.
Though its use was strict and came with a significant price, possibly leading to seals weakening and a resurgence of evil spirits, in a state of emergency, no one cared about that.
At that moment, an official with an imposing aura, certainly at the Eighth Level, emerged from the coffin.
Following behind were a large group of people, each with a strength of at least the Fifth Level.
They first looked disdainfully at the evil heretic believers, then, suppressing the urge to fight, turned their gazes down to the canyon.
Although they knew that a passage had already been established, they did not head towards it.
And it seemed they were preparing to build their own official path.
At this time, an official holding a paintbrush stepped out, and after a glance at the scene below, brought out a little stool.
Meanwhile, someone brought over a picture frame and a specially made camera.
After first snapping a picture of the scene below, they placed the photo in the frame, and the official immediately picked up the brush to perform secondary adjustments on this photo…
In less than two minutes, he had drawn an entrance.
When the final stroke was made…
An entrance nearly identical to the one on the canvas appeared in the area below.
“‘Reality Distortion Paint’… to bring such a precious thing here.”

chapters.title: Chapter 566 - 566 442 The Evil God Guards the National Gate
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 566: Chapter 442: The Evil God Guards the National Gate, Heretic Dies for the Altar of the State_2 Chapter 566: Chapter 442: The Evil God Guards the National Gate, Heretic Dies for the Altar of the State_2 The high-ranking members of the heretic organization who were observing from the sidelines were taken aback and also realized that this time the “Evil God” might really be descending!
“Boom!”
A terrifying blast resounded suddenly from within the tunnel.
Almost everyone present changed color, feeling an even stronger presence of divine power descending!
“Damn it! Is that thing about to succeed?”
The high-level heretic believer who sensed this aura was starting to get restless.
Although his spiritual intuition kept him skeptical of problems, what if it were true?
He took out a sail emitting a strong contaminated aura from his hand, glanced once more at the official personnel who had also stormed in, and ultimately made a decision, opening his mouth to speak…
…
“We can’t wait any longer!”
In a hidden cave, an “old man” with a face full of wrinkles and dyed black hair used his right index finger as a pen to swiftly write these words in the air.
Then, without hesitating, he rapidly wrote other content.
“Although some people had noticed something off, feeling that the events were too abrupt, forced, and highly unreasonable, they didn’t delve too deeply into it at this critical moment because the ‘Dawn Star’ was about to descend…”
“Whether or not it’s a trap, action must now be taken.”
“For once the opponent truly descends, everything will be irreversible, and the real Ancient God will seize all ‘exits’ at the first opportunity, cutting off other wills, and taking this place entirely into its possession…”
“For the sake of humanity’s future, even if there’s a trap ahead, we must jump into it.”
“Otherwise, we will become the sinners of mankind, the sinners of history…”
“…”
After a series of texts appeared, everything advanced in a certain predetermined direction.
Old Master Wu was not only writing with his right hand, but behind him, hundreds of “invisible hands” were also constantly interfering with some things through similar means…
To steer this battle towards its destined direction.
As a vital Level 9 Personnel, he should not be here.
Not because of the danger, but once he left some critical locations, those forcibly suppressed heretic entities would immediately strike back, attempting to break free from the seals…
But this time, Old Master Wu had a premonition that this incident might be the precursor to a major turn of fate.
He did not have much confidence in leaving it to Xu Duojin…
Furthermore, with Xu Duojin’s ability, he simply could not handle leading and guiding a battle of this scale…
After all, the heretic forces had truly been tricked this time.
A force that could match a Level 9 Personnel might arrive.
So, although he told Colin he would send Xu Duojin, in reality, it was the other way around.
Xu Duojin pretended to be him, still guarding the key areas.
While he himself took a secret path alone to the very frontline of this battle…
“I can be certain that they won’t detect my absence for at least half an hour,” Old Master Wu murmured to himself.
However, no sooner had he spoken than an inexplicable sense of awe arrived…
It seemed as if some terrifying presence had cast its gaze this way…
“Hmmph, like to watch.”
He did not panic, continuing his actions uninterrupted, but his left hand suddenly lifted slightly, palm up, as if holding a non-existent book.
In an instant, all the scrutinizing sensations were diverted…
Old Master Wu “huffed” and continued with the work at hand.
…
Inside the “City at the Lake’s Bottom,” what was once a modern town had now become a vast ruin through intense high-intensity battles, with massive bloodstains and body parts scattered everywhere, rivers of blood flowing, and the smell of blood pervading the area.
The highest priest of the Followers of the ‘Dawn Star,’ panting heavily with blood occasionally spilling from the corner of his mouth, bore terrifying crimson patterns spreading across his body. Having been seriously injured and cursed in clashes with some high-level powerhouses, he looked anxiously towards the ceaselessly advancing battlefront—
“The Master” seemed to still need some time.And they were almost at their limit.
Under the glaring light, it was clear that the battlefront was divided into two directions…
On one side were the well-trained and not-so-weak official personnel; on the other were numerous heretic forces’ upper echelons.
As for the heretic forces, they could still be somewhat suppressed, after all, this was the “Dawn Star”‘s home field. Any force that wasn’t the “Dawn Star” would ultimately be subdued. In the chaotic street battles, they could still hold their ground…
The official forces, on the other hand, had a lot of trouble.
All sorts of heavy weaponry, even small guided missiles, combined with extraordinary methods, kept moving forward.
They didn’t care about street battles; they encountered people, they blew them up; they encountered buildings, they blew them up…
They fought with great difficulty.
Frankly, if it weren’t for the power that spilled out during the “Dawn Star”‘s arrival, they would likely have lasted less than fifteen minutes after these guys entered, and would have been wiped out directly…
However, apart from the unfavorable current battle situation, what he was especially worried about at this moment was.
…
“Where have the Followers of the ‘Red Moon’ gone?”
Amid the dense starlight, Colin voiced the same confusion and concern as the High Priest.
Up till now, there had been no involvement of the “Red Moon” followers in the battle.
‘It shouldn’t be like this. We had received intelligence confirming the presence of Followers of the ‘Red Moon’ in this area, so why has none of them joined the fight yet?’
‘In similar situations before, they rushed in so eagerly; even for a pile of shit, they would fight for a fresh bite.’
‘This time… it’s as if they’ve collectively vanished?’
Colin couldn’t help but suspect that these guys might have other plans.
Or perhaps…
Had his plans been seen through?
Thinking this, Colin suddenly felt it was not impossible, considering that these guys were backed by a high-ranking entity of at least “0”.
Compared to those heretic churches that had only First Level Containment Subjects, or even Level 2 ones, it wasn’t close…
‘Ah, if that’s the case, it’s a bit of a shame.’
Colin sighed softly to himself.
At this moment, he was releasing the power of the “Dawn Star” like a hen laying eggs, squeezing it out bit by bit.
Everyone could see, as if through the cloaca, the egg being extruded little by little…
While making them desperate enough to charge in and fight, it also gave them the illusion that if someone just poked it, the egg would be pushed back in.
Overall, Colin was quite satisfied with the current intensity of the war.
There were more than a dozen Eighth Level fighters, not counting the officials, nearly half of all known high-end combat power of the heretic organizations!
Even among them was a Level 9 fighter…
But what he was dissatisfied with was that he had not yet seen the Followers of the “Red Moon”.
However, it was at this time that Colin suddenly had a premonition, his gaze shifting toward the direction next to the heretic forces.
Over there, suddenly, a surge of exclamations erupted.
A swath of churning crimson fog appeared out of nowhere, and whatever it touched or stained, regardless of what it was, rapidly began to animate…
Shattered limbs and blood recombined, forming stitch-together beings with horrifying strength.
Battered buildings grew veins, organs, and tentacles, writhing on the ground; even the air around the crimson fog seemed to come alive, twisting…
…
“Damn it! Followers of the ‘Red Moon’…”
The High Priest watched the immense wave of red cloud surging toward them, his heart racing with dread.
These damned people had finally shown up!
It was at that moment that, from the rolling waves of red mist, a clump of dense fog shot out, transforming into a sticky, barbed, blood-red tentacle spear in mid-flight, targeting the sphere of light hanging in the sky behind him.
Seeing this, the High Priest, not minding the wounds on his body, prepared to meet it head-on.
But before he could do so…
The curse on him suddenly erupted, and he fell from the sky once again.
Besides him, other followers charged forward, trying to defend, but as soon as they touched it, their bodies exploded into a sky full of organs, following in the wake of the tentacle…
..
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 567 - 567 443
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 567: 443 Chapter 567: 443 “Damn it!”
The high priest cursed under his breath because the curse had been detonated secretly just now.
Now it was too late to stop it, he could only watch helplessly as the tentacle shot towards the orb of light. Despite the light have some defensive properties, could it…
…withstand something so huge?
Moreover, from that blood-colored spear-like tentacle…
…there emanated an extremely terrifying divine power as well.
“It’s over…”
