With this in mind, Colin glanced at the group of local power representatives around him, unsure if they were aware of the critical information.
‘No, if they didn’t have the relevant information, they probably couldn’t come up with so much…’
‘After all, the so-called mobilization of over seventy percent of the water resources, even if they saw it, they would mostly think that it’s for use inside the ‘Dark Sea World,’ and wouldn’t imagine it being sent to other worlds…’
‘Tsk…’
Colin’s expression was slightly strange.
Ordinary locals might not guess the reason, but those containment subjects that had been affected surely could…
Yet, they still agreed and did not prevent it.
Colin thought that aside from the fact that the team from “Bonfire Company” was really persuasive, it might also be because they truly didn’t care that much.
“Water abundance or lack thereof might not be so significant for them.”
Colin sighed inwardly, then reviewed the contract clauses again, becoming more certain of his conjecture.
The entire document, as thick as a fist, essentially hinged on the key point of “water diversion”; everything else was probably a cover, the true intent obscured.
Of course, this was all predicated on the accuracy of his speculation.
After reading the contract several times and being certain there was nothing in it detrimental to himself, no worry of facing treatment like a corporate person after signing, Colin put down his signature…
“Sssss…”
As the last stroke of his name was completed, the contract suddenly flared up.
And in a very brief moment, it disappeared completely.
Vaguely, Colin felt that he now had a deeper…understanding of this world.
It was as if he had suddenly become its master.
Unfortunately, it seemed his authority fell short, preventing him from utilizing the terms he had just agreed to.
“Maybe when my level is higher, I won’t need ‘Lady Rabbit’; I could directly be nature’s mover myself.”
Colin looked up at the surrounding power representatives, each showing a pained expression.
Clearly, they too had sensed some form of covenant being established.
If they breached it, the consequences were unquestionably unacceptable to them.
However, regarding the water extraction, they didn’t care too much – after all, how much could be extracted from the vast waters of the “Dark Sea”?
Certainly, they couldn’t drain an entire world of its water, could they?
This thought never even crossed their minds.
What they were troubled with was that in addition to coordinating with “Bonfire Company’s” efforts and granting more authority…
They also had to improve the living conditions of ordinary humans under their control and more…
And they could not sacrifice them at will.
Without sacrifices, what was the point in keeping so many people around?
These parasites would only drive up the cost of fish and rice in the Dark Sea if left alone.
But, they didn’t dare disobey these commands.
Some forces had completely turned over their upper echelons, while some received responses directly from the “Gods…”
No matter the circumstance, it indicated they had to follow the higher-ups’ directives.
At this moment, while they were inwardly full of complaints, they had to show a pleased expression on their faces, gathering around Colin, congratulating the successful implementation of the treaties…
‘Good, no fools jumping out to be slapped in the face.’
Colin’s gaze moved away from them to check the content of the “World Code-4” mission in his mind…
The task of signing the contract had been completed, and there seemed to be nothing additional left over.

chapters.title: Chapter 579 - 579 448 Lady Bunnys Mad Plan._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 579: Chapter 448 “Lady Bunny’s” Mad Plan._2 Chapter 579: Chapter 448 “Lady Bunny’s” Mad Plan._2 “Could it be that the tasks here have come to an end?”
Based on past situations, by this time, there should’ve been new tasks handed down, at the very least, there would be some basic building task or some long-term task as a foundation…
But now, does it seem like everything has ended?
Colin then glanced at the four employees beside him, “Have you received any new tasks?”
“There was a previous ‘garrison’ task, nothing else…” Wave Rider Shunzi shook his head.
Actually having no tasks to follow up… Colin stroked his chin but didn’t dwell on it more.
There are still six days left…
Maybe at some point, new arrangements will come down?
But what Colin didn’t expect was that four or five days passed with no new content appearing, to the extent that every day, out of boredom, all he could do was eat and drink with Tina and the others, indulging in pleasure, watching the mermaids dance, slurping up giant squid…
“Sir Bonfire, are you troubled by something?”
Tina’s youthful voice rang out beside him while she was holding a roasted crab half the size of an ordinary person—
They don’t particularly like to eat these sea creatures, but since Sir Bonfire likes them, she went to catch one.
“No…”
Colin shook his head; he surely couldn’t say that he was being silly, constantly thinking why this task hadn’t sprung any surprises, right?
Taking the crab Tina handed him, Colin, observing the mermaids who had all stopped dancing to watch, waved his hand:
“Carry on playing the music, carry on dancing…”Hearing this, the mermaids started hopping and jumping in front of the Level 5 Bonfire Hall once again.
This dance wasn’t specifically for him; it was more like the kind of square dance that elderly men and women do. However, because the mermaids looked so delicate, it was quite pleasing to the eye, and so it became one of the must-watch items for Colin and the others every day…
“No idea how these mermaids grow, each and every one is so beautiful,” Arsonist Tao Tie said from the side.
There are almost no ugly mermaids; each one could match the word “gorgeous.”
The only differences were things like their personalities…
“Yeah, yeah, if it wasn’t for the mermaids being generally twice the size of an ordinary person, I’d have thought about finding one as a partner…”
One employee lamented. Although their popularity wasn’t quite up to Brother Shunzi’s level, they were quite well-liked here.
Too bad they were afraid of being willing but unable…
The only Talent that could compensate for the size difference, “Body of Tyranny,” would completely eliminate this weakness when transformed, turning it into an “absurd notion.”
Colin didn’t interject in their conversation and temporarily had no thoughts on the matter.
The absence of additional tasks these few days gave him a sense of pleasure like being on a paid vacation.
“If only every task could be this easy.”
Colin sighed internally.
But just at that moment, his expression suddenly changed, he turned around and looked behind him at the roaring bonfire.
He could faintly hear some elusive voices coming through…
“This is bad… this…”
“Save…”
“Save Save… Shunzi… there’s a disaster…”
“Here…”
“…”
The intermittent voices kept coming, and although Colin couldn’t quite make out the words, he could sense from the tone that something not so good had happened.
“Damn…” Colin felt a headache coming on, instantly stood up, and quickly walked towards the bonfire.
“What happened?”
“What’s going on?”
The few employees had also heard the intermittent voices and could sense something might be wrong.
“Not sure…”
Colin walked into the bonfire, trying to listen more clearly and attempting to communicate.
“It’s… a disaster…”
“Save save…”
“Plague of Magic Fog…”
But unfortunately…
Colin found that they seemed to generally understand his side, but from his end, he could only receive broken pieces of voices, and most of the time, it was a familiar but uncertain female voice speaking.
Listening to it was frustrating; he almost wanted to smash the “phone.”
Such a feeling of helplessness was too unpleasant…
“Was Tina conversing with me under these conditions before? It’s remarkable she managed to communicate…”
Colin felt some sympathy for Tina.
Then, taking a deep breath, suppressing some emotions, he carefully analyzed the situation.
From some of the terms…
“‘Plague of Magic Fog’ broke out again? Damn, why does it always happen when I’m not there?”
“Is it that if I don’t leave, it doesn’t break out? Don’t make me angry, I really will release ‘King of Mad Sounds’ to keep watch…”
As a First Level Containment Subject, although it might not necessarily solve the “Disaster of Magic Fog,” it would surely be no problem to guard the home.
However…
Colin knew that it probably wasn’t feasible right now.
He suppressed his emotions, then began to soothe the other side, indicating he would come over in a couple of days to take care of the Magic Fog.
“There’s a Fourth Level Bonfire over there now, with a large group of employees, no matter what, they should be able to hold out for a while; according to this timeline, by the time I enter next, only two days would have passed over there…”
After ending the conversation with the other side, Colin couldn’t concern himself with whether to keep playing the music or dancing.
“Brother Shunzi, what happened?” The employees on the side looked over with concern.
“There’s some trouble in World Code 13.”
Colin gave a brief explanation.
He hadn’t expected that the place he had visited would remain untroubled while trouble arose in a place he hadn’t visited.
The unexpected happened, albeit late.
And the most difficult aspect was that being in a different world, he didn’t really have a way to help.
“Gotta get the flame there up to Level 5 as soon as possible, see if there’s a chance to open a passage, to prevent similar situations from happening…”
Colin’s thoughts flashed through his mind, then he looked at Tina and the others, who were watching worriedly from afar, and reminded his companions, “Let’s not mention any of this to Tina and the others.”

chapters.title: Chapter 580 - 580 448 Lady Bunnys Mad Plan._3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 580: Chapter 448 “Lady Bunny’s” Mad Plan._3 Chapter 580: Chapter 448 “Lady Bunny’s” Mad Plan._3 “Don’t worry.” Several people nodded.
Taking a deep breath, Colin composed his emotions and walked out again with a smile.
In a certain uneasy atmosphere, the last bit of time quickly passed.
…
“Dong—— Dong—— Dong——”
As the clock chimes slowly faded away…
Colin immediately sat up, then shook his head to rid himself of the inexplicable daze and took out the parchment, ready to inquire about the situation from his subordinates.
However, halfway through, he stopped and thought about it, put down the parchment, and laid back down.
Then, his consciousness rapidly sank…
After passing through a surreal doorway, Colin opened his eyes and saw his own office, which was styled with slight exaggeration.
In a flash of thought…
Several figures were dragged into the expansive hall.
“Life Mentor Adorable” and a few other key D Level Personnel appeared.
“What exactly happened?”
Seeing their solid figures, Colin didn’t bother with pleasantries and directly asked about the situation there.
The few exchanged glances, then “Life Mentor Adorable” moved forward slightly and spoke, “The territory is actually fine, there are no problems…”
“Hm?” Colin was puzzled, seeing their expressions, it seemed like there really was no issue?
Then… what was with all the sobbing and wailing when “Bonfire” transmitted their message?
Soon, as he listened to their explanations, Colin finally understood the situation.
One piece of good news, and one piece of bad news.
The good news was… the territory had indeed encountered some roaming Magic Fog and heretic believers as threats in recent days, but they were all resolved by a hunting team formed by a D Level Personnel…
Overall, the territory was unharmed.
The bad news was…
It seemed like the “Saintess” was in trouble!
Colin’s heart skipped a beat and said, “The one from the ‘Light’ cult, the living saint from legends?”
As he spoke, he remembered that the voice he heard at the time seemed to be Nun Vanessa’s.
“Yes.”
“Life Mentor Adorable” was unclear about his boss’s private relationship with that saintess and found it odd that Brother Shunzi seemed especially concerned, but without dwelling on it further, said, “Vanessa said she hasn’t been able to sense their saintess these past few days. And according to some information, the saintess, while saving people during the ‘Disaster of Magic Fog,’ seems to have stepped into a trap specifically aimed at her…”
Regarding this widely respected saint, he actually had some understanding, knowing she should be someone who sympathizes with the common people, treating mortals as equals, a person worthy of respect.
Put simply, she was somewhat like the “Holy Mother,” a true, exemplary “Holy Mother” who practices what she preaches.
“Later, a female knight came by and said that the situation for the saintess is not optimistic. She had many injuries on her own, and after being ambushed, her condition might not be too good. She wanted to request our help…”
“However, I specifically investigated the possibility of providing aid on site. Apart from the saintess’s strength and whether she is still alive, we do not have the capability to reach her with our strength; we can barely hold up even at the periphery of the disaster…”
“Just stepping a bit into the periphery, we encountered several attacks from Magic Fog Spawned Creatures close to Fourth, Fifth Level, and even Third Level Containment Subject strength, nearly resulting in casualties before we had to retreat…”
“We can confirm that the ‘Plague of Magic Fog’ is not something we can deal with.”
“Life Mentor Adorable” outlined the situation they knew so far, with a hint of lingering fear in his voice. After pausing for a few seconds, he added:
“So, are we going to head out and rescue her?”
Frankly, after sensing the terror of the “Disaster of Magic Fog,” he felt that the chances for the saint were slim.
Even if they went, it might already be too late, and they would have to pay a significant price.
But, the final decision still depended on Brother Shunzi…
And from what they knew of Brother Shunzi, with such high risks, it would be no surprise if he decided not to take action.
After all, with no personal connection to the saintess, suddenly making a significant sacrifice to look for someone, with no guarantee of finding her, seemed like a losing trade.
Of course, there was also a chance that he might act if the “Light” cult promised some significant compensation.
However, to their surprise…
“Save her.”
Brother Shunzi made his decision almost without hesitation, adding solemnly:
“We must save her!”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 581 - 581 449 Saving Saintess Shana._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 581: Chapter 449: Saving Saintess Shana._1 Chapter 581: Chapter 449: Saving Saintess Shana._1 “Ah?”
Everyone was taken aback, looking at Brother Shunzi with some surprise, not understanding why he had made a decision so quickly.
Everyone present had more or less worked with him on certain matters before and knew that, according to Brother Shunzi’s usual practice, even if he eventually agreed, he would likely discuss for quite a while, considering all possibilities before making a choice.
It was rare for him to make a decision so directly…
Could it be that there was some inside story they didn’t understand?
Facing the employees’ confusion, Colin pondered for a moment before saying, “The ‘Holy Woman’ is actually one of our more steadfast and important allies. No matter what, if she can be saved, we must try everything possible to rescue her.”
“Ah??”
The employees were stunned again. Allies?
Since when?
Up until now, their knowledge of the “Light” Church’s Saint had only come through the nun who wouldn’t leave their territory and some descriptions from refugees…
The key point was that among these people, apart from a blue-haired lady knight who had arrived not long before with considerable strength,
almost no one had really come into close contact with that Saint…
But looking at Brother Shunzi’s attitude, it seemed as if he knew the Saintess personally?
What was going on?
However, facing these subsequent doubts, Colin did not explain much more, simply inquiring about some details. After confirming that the current whereabouts of the Saintess were unknown but she had not been confirmed dead or captured, he shifted the topic.
“What about the ambushing enemies?”
Colin asked.
“There are many. We are not clear about those deeply hidden, but… during those days, we could see many heretic believers begin to move, entering the Magic Fog, seemingly trying to find her to strike at her, but most are not certain of their specific identities. The only one we could confirm was the ‘Feast of Devouring,’ which we had been paying closer attention to…”
“The ‘Feast of Devouring’?”
Colin nodded, remembering that this should be the part of the believers who worshiped the “Hunger” Fragment.
At that moment, “Life Mentor Adorable” continued, “In terms of reinforcements, there were some, like the Virtue Knight Order and some other noble knight legions from different nations, Mage Corps, and some Church Alliance Forces, as well as ‘Light’ Church personnel, but it’s just…”
He hesitated as he spoke.
“Speak your mind.”
Colin said.
“It always feels like the people from the other forces, apart from a part of the ‘Light’ Church’s power, just seem to be dragging their feet, not showing much concern, and even failing to dispatch persons of sufficient weight…”
“Life Mentor Adorable” recalled the attitudes of some of the noble members he saw during the investigation.
There was a sense that although they did not wish for the Saint to die, there was an attitude of ‘if she can be saved, we’ll save her; if not, then what happens, happens.’
There was a lack of a firm resolve to save her at all costs.
The various assembled teams looked impressive in size, but none of them had any capable fighters.
The strongest Virtue Knight among them, who possessed five Virtues, used the excuse of needing to protect the local safety so couldn’t make a move…
Moreover, although the general middle and lower ranks had high praise for the Saintess.
The upper echelons, on the other hand, were different. They were not hostile, but not particularly friendly either, and their attitude was much more indifferent compared to the apparent adoration from those below…
“Life Mentor Adorable” initially thought it might be a case of “the tall poppy syndrome.”
But later realized it seemed not entirely the case…
After all, in this world, all great powers belonged to the extraordinary, not to the people as was the case on Earth.
Therefore, the high-ranking individuals who wielded extraordinary paths indeed did not particularly care about the reputation of the Saints…
On the other hand, Colin, remembering what he had learned in recent times from his exchanges with Shana during their sparring sessions, was not very surprised by this situation.
He knew that it wasn’t that they had any objections to Shana herself, but more so that there were some unspoken objections to all Saints that emerged from the “Light” Church.
‘No wonder every Saint doesn’t end well. With this kind of attitude of being surrounded by onlookers when in trouble, I guess the previous Saints went down with quite a bit of frustration.’
Colin shook his head internally and then dismissed the temporary meeting.
Looking at the employees as they disappeared one by one in the hall, he did not rush to leave. Instead, he extended his finger and gently tapped on the mottled stone table, pondering how to deal with the situation when the time came…
To be fair, during the time he had been sparring with the Saintess, he had come to understand how formidable this Saint was.
In fact, when she was fully unleashed, her strength might not be far off from a bona fide “Flame Bearer”…
In this situation, for her to be ambushed and badly injured, then to disappear, the enemy’s strength must not be taken lightly…
“Plus, with the ‘Plague of Magic Fog’ causing dire circumstances, if I go there, I might have to fight with all I’ve got.”
Colin raised his hand to rub his forehead.
His trump card was to rely on the temporary surge of power when his body was fully BUFFed, manipulating the “Hunger” Fragment within him…
Now, this method even allowed him to face a First Level Containment Subject with confidence.
But, managing the “Hunger” for a while was fine, but indefinitely was a bit challenging…
It was like blasting a hole in a dike – easy to let the water flow through, but not so simple to patch it up again.
However, no matter what, the person definitely had to be saved.
“Prepare well and do the best we can… Yeah, and see if ‘Lady Bunny’ can offer any help, or perhaps some assistance from the officials.”

chapters.title: Chapter 582 - 582 449 Saving Saintess Shana._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 582: Chapter 449: Saving Saintess Shana._2 Chapter 582: Chapter 449: Saving Saintess Shana._2 He took a deep breath, Colin ended his contemplations, and left the office.
Glancing at the time, it was only a little past four, he then took out his phone, tapped on Old Master Wu’s anime girl avatar, and began composing a message.
“Based on some recent experiences, I’ve gained some new intelligence, which confirms that constructing a series of underwater buildings, as well as shipbuilding, is necessary…”
“Because ‘The Deep Sea Era’ has been confirmed to be inevitable, seizing this opportunity and ensuring one’s own survival in such an environment is of great importance.”
While writing, Colin couldn’t help but think of a science fiction story that was essentially about two advanced civilizations at a higher dimension going to war.
Neither side could gain the upper hand, and if the stalemate continued, they might both be destroyed…
But it was at this moment that one of the civilizations discovered their ability to exist in two dimensions, unlike their enemy, and so they launched a wide-scale strike in two dimensions…
Dragging both themselves and the enemy into the two-dimensional plane, they successfully defeated their formidable foe.
At present, the “Lady Rabbit” plan seemed much smaller in scale compared to that story but appeared to be based on a similar principle.
Soon after sending the relevant message, Colin continued to edit another one.
“Due to certain reasons, I might need some special items to assist me, so that I could find the person I’m looking for in dangerous scenarios, or rather, acquire means of continued self-enhancement…”
Colin briefly explained his needs in the message.
He knew that the authorities would definitely cooperate fully with his requests.
So without much courtesy, he stated that the item’s level of power should be as high as possible, of course, the negative effects had to be within his ability to endure…
Colin was well aware that the authorities themselves had various items, but their quality was mixed.
Moreover, they generally had very significant negative effects…
However, with the upcoming battle so perilous, having an extra resource was better.
After sending this message, the gray anime girl avatar lit up, and Old Master Wu sent an “OK” emoji and responded:
“I will promote the relevant measures as much as possible. Regarding the items, if you urgently need them, I can have Xu Duojin bring one to you right now. If it’s not that urgent, wait the day after tomorrow, I will finish processing a special item and then hand it to you…”
“Good.”
After replying with a single word, Colin began to wait.
Time flew, and it wasn’t until almost noon on the third day that he saw Xu Duojin at his door. At this moment, the middle-aged, leaning towards old, robust man, aside from wearing his usual sunglasses, was also carrying a box that was sealed by all manner of chains and enchantments.
Colin’s gaze subconsciously focused on it, but he did not see the “Item Information” emerge.
However, he could be sure that this item was no trivial matter.
The air around the box seemed to be boiling, squirming around it.
“A new item created using some ideas from the company as well as the residual knowledge from that world…”
“The raw material used is the root idol of the ‘Divine Strike’ faith, but after some modifications, its rough effect is to summon a ‘Fire God Embodiment’ based on your own basic appearance…”
“We haven’t released it yet, but the initial intention of creating this thing was to give a Level 9 ‘Divine Strike’ an extra trump card, its power won’t be weak…”
Xu Duojin explained bit by bit to Colin.
“‘Fire God Embodiment’?” Colin raised his eyebrows in question.
“Yes, I’m not certain about the specifics, because I wasn’t the one who collected it, but from what I’ve heard, it may come from a ‘Zhu Rong’ stone statue from some temple. Don’t worry, it’s generally a positive divine being, so there shouldn’t be any major issues…”
“Zhu Rong?”
Colin clicked his tongue; the ‘Divine Strike’ was no longer satisfied with just divine possession but started researching how to directly bind the “God” for utilitarian purposes…
It seems that after such long contact with the company, the authorities had indeed learned a thing or two.
Of course, he knew that this “Zhu Rong” was definitely not the historical figure, but rather an avatar imagined into existence by some special methods.
Normally, it would be hidden away somewhere, reserved for those following the path of the ‘Divine Strike’ to borrow power from.
This time it was also a loan, except that the “entity” itself was being borrowed as well.
“So what are the negative effects?” Colin inquired.
“There might be a powerful mental shock, which could disturb your reasoning, and then it might instinctively replace you. After that, it’s time to borrow fire, which will probably be very painful, like being burned all over your body. Of course, this pain can be alleviated. What you really need to watch out for is ‘assimilation’, but with your ability, you should be able to hold on for an hour or two, or maybe even longer?”
“Yeah, that’s roughly it. I’m not too sure about the other details…”
“After you’re done, if you can recover it, do so; if not, just let it go. We’ve taken some precautions to ensure that you can always drive it out of your body.”
Geez, the whole explanation was either ‘should’ or ‘probably’, hardly a definitive word. You’re treating me like a guinea pig, aren’t you?
Colin couldn’t help but grumble inwardly.
However, he also knew that the thing was indeed quite valuable.
According to Colin’s understanding of the officials, there are only six or seven ‘idols’ that the high-level “Divine Strike” users can borrow from within the whole “Divine Strike” path, and the “Fire God” is one of them…
In other words, taking one away means that the high-ranking sequence in the “Divine Strike” is effectively crippled.
In dealing with certain anomalies, they could’ve used this method to suppress them directly, but without it, the situation might become more complicated and riskier.
The impact on the situation is indeed significant…
“Don’t worry, I feel like I should be able to handle this thing, and unless something unexpected happens, I shouldn’t lose it.”
Moreover, if this were lost, the people from “World Code-13” would probably have trouble sleeping, as they’d suddenly have an evil god to deal with… Colin added in his mind, then reached out to pick up the briefcase and took the opportunity to sense the situation inside of it.
It was indeed different from the flame of the “Flame Bearer”.
The flame inside the briefcase was filled with a violent desire to destroy everything, as if it wanted to incinerate all…
Nonetheless, for the most part, Colin felt that he could still control it.
After thanking the officials for their assistance and sending Xu Duojin away, he packed away the items, glanced at the time, and then directly purchased and used a third Gene Compensation Medicine from his pocket…
It was like drinking a sip of water, bland and tasteless.
His strength didn’t seem to have increased, but he distinctly felt that his spiritual aspect was becoming “complete”.
“After absorbing it completely in seven days, I can start the C Level Sprint.”
Colin looked down, clenched his fists, and sensed his own condition.
Then he closed his eyes, sorted out his thoughts, and organized the various preparations he had to make.
As he waited, time arrived at the last day.
Rather than the usual reluctance to go over there, this was one of the rare times he actively wanted to make the trip.
“It’s a pity, ‘Lady Rabbit’ doesn’t seem to have responded in the last two days; I don’t know if she hasn’t received my message or if she thinks there’s no need to intervene.”
Colin exhaled, but there was one thing: unexpectedly, this week had been without the “weekly task”; it had been uneventful, with rare leisure time.
For the first time, he experienced the benefits of “flexible working hours”…
Of course, since he needed to rescue Shana, even if there were tasks, Colin reckoned he would probably reject them and not execute them.
“Come to think of it, I don’t think I’ve ever refused a task before.”
Colin lay on the bed, staring at the time on the wall not too far away, as he pondered.
In just a few hours, “The Descent Project” would begin…
Based on his previous experience, at most only one day would have passed there by now; he hoped not to hear any bad news after entering.
Praying quietly, time quickly passed by.
Before long, Colin heard the distant and ancient chimes ringing beside his ear.
Mists rolled in from everywhere.
“The mission to save Saintess Shana begins!”

chapters.title: Chapter 583 - 583 450 Arriving at the Battlefield_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 583: Chapter 450: Arriving at the Battlefield_1 Chapter 583: Chapter 450: Arriving at the Battlefield_1 “Ding—Ding—Ding—”
The distant, ancient bell sounds slowly receded into the distance.
Opening his eyes, Colin saw the familiar chapel and then, subconsciously, he looked towards a corner of the church.
Unfortunately, the hazy light and shadow did not appear…
He gathered his thoughts, and first thing, he took out the Golden Mark given to him by Shana from his pocket and immersed his consciousness into it—
There was no response…
And, compared to before, there was a distinct feeling of communication being completely severed, like a stone sunk deep into the ocean.
‘Indeed, there seems to be a problem…’
Colin put away the mark, and at the same time, grey ashes spewed from the bonfire, these ashes quickly transformed midair into solid figures of employees.
“Brother Shunzi? You’ve finally come!!” Some showed delighted expressions upon seeing this, then immediately began reporting the prior situation.
However, only half of it was said before Colin waved his hand, interrupting the rest of their words.
“I already know.”
Having said so, Colin did not elaborate further, instead, he sensed the area outside.
He could feel that outside the small chapel, Nun Vanessa was already waiting.
He strode forward, stepping out to see Vanessa in her stance of meditation, hands crossed over her chest, head bowed with a worried expression on her face.
Little Red and several children were beside her…
Beyond them, there stood a woman over one meter eighty-five tall, with blue hair, at Vanessa’s side.
Her appearance was beautiful, and seemed very familiar…
‘This hair color, what does it have to do with Helena?’
Colin’s gaze swept over her, recalling the noble Helena he had met some months before.
This one looked very much like Helena, only taller, like an enlarged version of her, and her eyes were very sharp, her presence overwhelming, and her strength on another level.
“Sister Vanessa, big brother is here…” Little Red saw Colin and her eyes immediately lit up, and then she gently tugged at Vanessa’s robe.
Upon hearing this, Vanessa immediately opened her eyes: “‘Bonfire’ agent sir…”
“No need for more words, I’ve decided to commence the rescue. Just tell me, do you have any news about the current whereabouts of the Saint?”
As he spoke, Colin looked towards the blue-haired lady knight.
According to “Life Mentor Adorable,” this one nearly followed the Saintess all the way through the disaster’s epicenter and knew a lot.
And seeing Colin’s gaze, the blue-haired lady knight did not hesitate and spoke decisively:
“Based on the intelligence I have, it’s very likely that the Saintess encountered an ambush in the Golden City of Black Rock Kingdom because when we left, I heard that place seemed to be a trap…”
“A trap and yet you went?” Colin frowned.
Upon hearing this, the blue-haired lady knight was silent for a few seconds, then nodded:
“Yes, that’s just the kind of person she is…”
She paused, not waiting for Colin to speak, she continued: “In fact, during the ‘Disaster of Magic Fog’ relief efforts, the Saintess has also encountered many ambushes, but most of those plots were crushed by her, this time…”
It could be negligence, or some other reason.
The blue-haired lady knight did not continue.
‘This is really… If we manage to rescue her, she certainly needs to be thoroughly lectured, having strength doesn’t mean being reckless!’
As for now, continuing the inquiry seemed pointless, Colin directly asked: “Do you have a map?”
“Yes.”
“Mark out the potential areas and safe routes.”
Before long, with the map in hand, Colin swiftly set off, but the first destination was not towards the direction of the Mist Disaster but another area.
The Underground Great Labyrinth.
This First Level Containment Subject, though trapped, definitely knew more about the “Disaster of Magic Fog” than it had claimed last time.
‘This time, if it doesn’t yield something actually useful, then for wasting nearly a half-hour of my time, this creature can forget about ever coming out, or if it does come out, I’ll have to ensure it appears in the form of an item.’
Colin muttered to himself.
Ten more minutes passed, and he arrived once more at the Underground Labyrinth.
This time, because Colin did not conceal his presence during the journey, “King of Savage Sound” seemed to have already sensed it.
Just as he reached the entrance, a figure composed of a unique frequency spectrum appeared.
“Respected pre… No, ‘Flame Bearer’ your excellency, congratulations, your strength seems to have advanced further.”
“King of Madness” paused halfway through his speech, recalling some of the humanizing knowledge infused—
Generally speaking, if the other person is a deputy something but such a meeting should still directly address with the proper title; it makes the other feel slightly better and also conveys preemptive congratulations.
This “Flame Bearer” C Level was somewhat lacking in the intensity of flame.
But… among the reserves, should be considered among the best.
It was time to pop the champagne… Wait, what is “champagne”?
“King of Madness” briefly puzzled internally, but before making sense of it, heard the other speak:
“Tell me as much as you can about your understanding of the ‘Disaster of Magic Fog’.”
“This…” “King of Madness” hesitated.
“If the information is accurate and useful, when the opportunity arises, I will give you priority consideration.”
Colin casually painted a picture.
However, “King of Madness” immediately perked up upon hearing this: “Of course, of course, I’ll tell you what I know.”
Although there was no definite reply, this was the first time there was an indication of letting it out.
Good things come to those who wait…
With more performances in the future, there might really be a chance to get out!
Thinking this, “King of Madness” did not hesitate to transmit a special “Inspiration” and, combining with words: “This ‘Magic Fog’, I haven’t really been in contact with it, but I can generally sense that it’s probably a fusion of consciousness from some High Order Containment Subjects, originating from some specific Containment Space…”

chapters.title: Chapter 584 - 584 450 Arriving at the Battlefield_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 584: Chapter 450: Arriving at the Battlefield_2 Chapter 584: Chapter 450: Arriving at the Battlefield_2 Its words, coupled with the “inspiration” in Colin’s knowledge, allowed him to quickly understand the greatest probability of the “Magic Fog.”
“World Code-13” is much larger than a typical World Code, and the reason for its size is due to Rosen merging some other useful World Codes into this one in the past.
Among them, it is possible that the Containment Subject of a certain World Code was not completely resolved.
Then there might have been some interference…
The abnormal aura that overflowed from within, to the “King of Savage Sound”, if made analogous, would be equivalent to the pus oozing out of rotting human corpses.
And it’s not just from one person…
‘Looking at it this way, the “King of Mad Sounds” didn’t lie to me when it said it’s like the pus from a stack of high-grade corpses rotting together.’
Colin nodded and continued to inquire, “So, is there anything in particular we should be cautious about in dealing with it?”
“Ordinary life forms need to be wary of many things, especially the ‘Magic Fog’ itself. It has an extremely strong corruption quality, posing a threat to both Second Level and Third Level Containment Subjects… However, for you, it’s not a problem…”
“Why?”
“Because of its life experience, that kind of fog will instinctively fear the power of ‘Primordial Fire.’ With the ‘Primordial Fire’ upon you, even an ordinary person need not be afraid. So, the only thing you need to be careful of are the corrupt creatures that have derived from the ‘Magic Fog’…”
As he said this, “King of Madness” carefully made a sound:
“However, if you are willing to release me, then… although my strength has diminished, I can still fend off those ignorant, feeble beings for you…”
Tch… Colin didn’t speak, merely looking at it with an indifferent expression, causing its voice to gradually fade away, without continuing.
Clearly, releasing it now is not an option.
However, after a pause, “King of Madness” seemed to have thought of something, “Right, I have a small question. I gather from your words that you intend to enter that area to look for something?”
“Right.”
Colin nodded, “Do you have something to say?”
“If you have an exact location, perhaps I could offer some minor assistance in that regard.”
“Oh? Continue.”
Colin was taken aback, listening to this; could the “King of Madness,” a disgrace among First Level Containment Subjects, offer not only knowledge but also some method of teleportation or positioning?
If true, that would be an unexpected gain.
“If you need, I can find a way to quickly teleport you to a labyrinth in the nearby area. These labyrinths cover the vast majority of this world, and I can use my powers to move within them and send you there…”
Labyrinths covering the vast majority of the world? Is this damned place that big?
Colin was surprised in his heart, but for the moment, he did not agree.
Because he was not quite certain whether this creature would secretly play dirty tricks…
From a few encounters with this entity, Colin had come to a basic understanding of its nature.
At this moment, seemingly sensing Colin’s hesitation, “King of Madness” assured, “If you are concerned, I am willing to make a commitment under the witness of the ‘Bonfire Company’, swearing not to have any ulterior motives…”
If it’s with the “Bonfire Company” as a witness, then indeed he could feel at ease.
Only…
‘Weird, why do I feel like it’s being especially proactive this time around?’
Colin looked at the other party with a hint of suspicion.
If it were any other time, he wouldn’t accept help from the other party, no matter how proactive, just to avoid risks.
But this time, in an urgent situation, it might be worth a try…
Even if it doesn’t work out, he should be able to withdraw in time.
“Then swear it,” Colin nodded.
Hearing this, “King of Madness” didn’t delay, and in a solemn tone, it declared, “Under the witness of the ‘Bonfire Camp Special Item Containment Company’, I promise, this assistance will bear no malice…”
As the full name of the company was spoken, Colin could clearly sense some indescribable entity, centering on himself, turning its gaze upon this place.
“King of Madness” shivered noticeably when it felt this presence.
If it were still the being it once was, then even upon sensing the company, it would merely back away driven by instincts of seeking benefit and avoiding harm. But now, it had begun to exhibit feelings of fear.
However, in the end, under a certain pressure, it fulfilled the promise…
“Very well.”
Although it was still unclear why this First Level Containment Subject suddenly became so compliant, once Colin was certain the promise had taken effect, he did not refuse its help any longer and took out the map he had just obtained.
“Can you take me to this place called the Golden City?”
Colin pointed to a spot on the map.
If he were to go there normally, even he would probably need a day or two. And with the threat of the Magic Fog, it could take three or four days.
By then, he might not be able to make it in time.
However, upon hearing Colin’s words, the “King of Mad Sounds” shook its head, indicating it was not clear:
“These creatures make too little noise; even if they blew up a mountain, it would be hard to sense. However…”
Seeing that the “Flame Bearer” looked somewhat indifferent, it changed its words, “Before I was sealed in the past, I had observed this world and knew roughly where this is—if I remember correctly, nearby, not long ago, there were some fluctuations, seemingly from a battle, and one of the parties seemed to be connected to the company…”
This was also why it had previously been able to guess that Colin’s question about the “Disaster of Magic Fog” might be related to looking for something.
A battle? The Saintess?
Without thinking much, Colin’s instinct told him he was probably right, and he decisively chose: “Then take me to the vicinity of the place where you said the battle took place, the closer the better.”
“Okay.” The shadow formed by the “King of Mad Sounds” at a special frequency nodded and, after confirming the location, said cautiously:
“Now…I need you to remove the flames on your body, as well as some of your defenses.”
Upon hearing this, Colin frowned, but with the promise made earlier, he chose to comply.
The next second, the shadow of the “King of Mad Sounds” suddenly spread out, eagerly pouncing like a starving wolf, and enveloped him into its body…
It was at this moment that Colin felt a certain shape transformation occurring.
His entire being became a set of special frequencies…
Then, he traveled at an incredibly fast speed, weaving through the undergound labyrinth.
‘These First Level Containment Subjects, each with their methods and so-called ‘powers,’ truly are bizarre. No wonder Big C Teacher fell victim before he forcibly became a “Flame Bearer”…’
Experiencing the methods of a First Level Containment Subject’s powers up close for the first time, Colin couldn’t help but feel a bit shocked.
Just a few minutes later…
In a corridor similar to the underground maze, Colin’s figure emerged from the special state.
“We’ve arrived. If you go out through this cave, you’ll reach your destination…” the “King of Mad Sounds” said on the side.
After a pause, he added, “If you need help again, please feel free to call on me.”
“Mhm.”
Colin nodded, not dwelling on it any further. His body’s flames blazed fiercely as he leaped forward into the cave.
From his senses…
Outside, there truly was an aura left by the Saintess!
And behind him, the “King of Mad Sounds” did not leave but made a gesture as if staring at his back, seemingly pondering something.
The reason it had helped him so proactively this time was that it faintly sensed something unique…
Its opportunities to leave were becoming scarcer…
Although it did not excel much in divination and such arts, its essence was that of an “Ancient God,” a being not to be underestimated in spiritual perception.
A strong intuition told it that in a few months, there might be a major change.
This period was its last chance to strive to leave…
If it did not seize this opportunity, then it might…
End up as one of the rotting corpses in the “Disaster of Magic Fog.”
…

chapters.title: Chapter 585 - 585 451 The World Within the Demon Disaster_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 585: Chapter 451 The World Within the Demon Disaster_1 Chapter 585: Chapter 451 The World Within the Demon Disaster_1 A dark grey dense fog shrouded the land, with strange gusts all around, and from time to time came distant roars that drove one mad…
At this moment, the clearing suddenly convulsed and twisted, letting out a “scream.”
But it didn’t scream for long before it began to melt away and burn…
Following that, a flame burst forth from beneath the center of the melting.
“Is this the world deep within the disaster?”
Colin hovered in midair, flames flickering from his left eye, his whole body radiating a strong aura.
To avoid any accidents, he had already stacked all the BUFF Effects except for the short-term ones while flying up…
Now, he looked around.
Within a few kilometers, the land was ripped apart, and bizarre howls echoed all day.
An endless grey-black fog dispersed all around…
Warnings of spiritual presence came from all directions…
And an oppressive feeling like a tidal wave suffocated him.
Even though he had yet to encounter anything, Colin already felt a deep crisis.
It was as if enemies were about to attack from all around at any moment.
But fortunately, just as the “King of Mad Sounds” had said, the Magic Fog itself had a natural fear of flames; just a thumb-sized light could carve out a “safe zone” with a diameter of more than ten meters.
And his flames now kept the Magic Fog turned back for several kilometers, not daring to cross the line.
“This information should be correct, that ‘King of Mad Sounds,’ although I don’t know why it’s being so cooperative this time, its ultimate goal is inseparable from wanting to break free from the ‘Containment God Kingdom.’ In other words, before it escapes, it doesn’t want anything to happen to me…”
Colin thought it over and took another careful look around, noticing many signs of battle.
If things were as expected, this must be an area where Shana had once fought…
Then, following his intuition, he picked a direction and transformed into a streak of light and fire, quickly weaving through the traces all around.
Along the way, large amounts of Magic Fog dispersed.
And Colin encountered many remnants of horribly twisted creatures that had been killed.
These beings were not completely dead, continuously emitting random, distorted Mental Shocks, and the flesh at their fractured wounds writhed, as if attempting to heal again…
Or perhaps, mouths grew on the chunks of flesh, breathing in, trying to absorb the surrounding Magic Fog to recover and replenish themselves.
Unfortunately for them, there was a thin layer of white Light on the surface of the chunks.
This light not only kept the Magic Fog at bay but also prevented the pieces of flesh from healing back together.
“This technique, it can be confirmed as Shana’s…”
“Not seeing any Heretic Forces corpses indicates that the Magic Fog Spawned Creatures left in retreat, but these remnants look like they’ve been sliced up like in Fruit Ninja…”
Colin didn’t linger or take a closer look, continuing swiftly on his way.
Apart from the remains of the powerful creatures scattered everywhere, he also encountered the attacks of numerous Magic Fog Derivatives.
These creatures weren’t very strong; compared, they were probably about the same as The Rat, Little Cat, or small dogs—not fatal, but a nuisance. You would have to wave your hand a few times, which greatly impeded progress.
Even if being bitten by them wasn’t harmful, accumulating too many bites was another story.
But apart from that bit of bad news, there was some good news: he hadn’t encountered any Magic Fog Spawned Creatures with a strength of Third Level or above…
About ten minutes later, he saw a massive walled city and couldn’t help but be inwardly startled, taking a sharp breath.
A corner of the city, which covered dozens of square kilometers, looked as though it had been shattered by a formidable force.
In the center, a web-like ground fissure spread outwards in all directions.
Many bodies of Heretics in Cult Robes lay dead across the ground, some in pieces, some pulped, others charred black, and some seemingly intact but deader than the mangled flesh…
Moreover, among them lay a grey-black hand covered with mouths and eyes.
Even now, Colin could feel a brutally oppressive aura lingering here…
The air sometimes filled with strange whispers, a mist of blood, oddly flowing shadows, spiraling tornadoes, or bursts of intense white light flashing.
“Sheesh, part of a super-strong Level 2 Containment Subject? That was quite the fierce battle.”
Colin clicked his tongue and controlled himself to land in the midst of the town.
His gaze swept over the almost utterly destroyed city, faintly sensing that there must have been at least five parties involved here at one point.
However, from certain traces, it appeared that Shana neither died nor was captured here at that time.
This slightly relieved Colin.
“Unfortunately, I still haven’t triggered the mission, so I can’t locate her exactly.”
Colin rubbed his forehead and decided to look for any survivors, as he had sensed some signs of life when he first arrived.
But he wasn’t sure whether it was the scent of living beings from the undestroyed flesh of Extraordinary Ones, or if there were actually survivors.
Because in the city, there were many special creatures that seemed both dead and alive, their bodies melding together like mud, moving and writhing like giant banyan trees, emitting screams.
These creatures looked even more blasphemous than a Human Patchwork Monster.
And yet they exuded the scent of humans…
Colin refrained from exterminating them and quickly investigated the area, hoping to gather more useful information.
But just as he began, Colin’s scalp tingled, feeling as if he had been targeted.
Turning around, he saw from a fissure in the street that a meatball with a diameter of over five meters had flown out.
It had wings of flesh over ten feet long, its entire body a sanguine red, resembling skinless flesh—but on this chunk of flesh was a closed mouth full of serrated teeth…

chapters.title: Chapter 586 - 586 451 The World Within the Demon Disaster_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 586: Chapter 451 The World Within the Demon Disaster_2 Chapter 586: Chapter 451 The World Within the Demon Disaster_2 Combined with the Magic Fog aura swirling around it,
it was almost certain that it was a special monster contaminated by it.
“Bang! Bang! Bang!”
Colin raised his hand and fired three 155mm bullets augmented with flame.
However, to his surprise, just as the bullets were about to hit the strange meatball, they were suddenly “clang” deflected.
“There’s even a Positional Shield?”
Colin was astonished, noticing that around the large meatball, there appeared a layer of grey protective barrier.
Its diamond-like patterns looked just like those of a Positional Shield.
And it was at that moment, the meatball with fluttering wings opened its mouth and spat out an eyeball almost the size of a person.
In an instant, a strong Mental Shock surged towards him.
Colin felt his head swell slightly…
The meatball harboring the eyeball in its mouth saw that Colin didn’t dodge and thought it had succeeded in controlling him; countless grey mists condensed on its eyeball, seemingly about to shoot out a grey-black laser.
But before the laser could be shot out…
“Boom” went the noise.
The entire meatball suddenly burst into flames as if it had been filled with gasoline and set on fire, burning in mid-air.
“Didn’t anyone teach you not to stare at people for no reason?”
Colin blinked his eyes.
This meatball’s strength wasn’t very high, not even comparable to a Third Level Containment Subject, just a creature that could be killed with a glance.
However, to his surprise, when the meatball exploded,
a scream suddenly came from a corner of the ruins of the city.
A human scream.
“Oh? An unexpected catch?”
Colin sensed that this meatball monster seemed to be controlled by someone?
In the next second, his figure flashed, appearing on top of a pile of ruins that seemed empty.
Then, he took a half-second to charge back and kicked fiercely.
With just one kick, he sent the ruins of a three-story building flying away.
At that moment, the scene beneath the ruins was also exposed to the air…
Inside was a small space, and within the space, there were three… or rather, one person?
Three bodies with normal upper halves, but the lower halves were grotesquely fused together like melted wax, appearing somewhat monstrous.
At that time, one of the bodies, dressed in the garb of the Heretic Forces, was holding its head and wailing incessantly.
It was clear that the creature had been under his control…
But when Colin arrived, his cries gradually stopped, and he was clearly not going to live much longer.
Luckily, the other two bodies fused with him were not dead.
“I’ve heard before coming here that some people worship the Magic Fog and even gain some power from it, it must be you then.”
Colin spoke as he approached this fused human.
The remaining two bodies looked like Heretic Believers, but they didn’t share the same creed.
“No, don’t kill me! He was the one who acted! It has nothing to do with me! Don’t…” one of the central position Heretic Believers screamed in panic, his emotions seemingly out of control as he sobbed and pleaded.
“Shut up.”
Colin scolded, waiting for them to quiet down before asking, “Have you seen the Light Church’s Saintess?”
“The Light Church… The Saintess… It’s her! Ahhh! It was her who made us like this! Oh, why couldn’t she just willingly sacrifice herself to fulfill us, why did she prefer to save those lowlifes and not us important people, it’s all her…”
The Heretic Believer on the left, dressed in a blue robe, shouted as if triggered.
But before he could finish, a flame flashed by.
This “important person” was instantly turned to char and died…
“I don’t want to die!” Seeing this, the central position Heretic Believer screamed out in terror, also feeling intense pain.
“Tell me, what is her situation now!”
Flames expanded around Colin, radiating a powerful presence.
“She… After she forcibly rescued those lowlifes, she encountered an ambush. Many powerful forces joined hands, but, she left, she left, she got away…”
The central Heretic Believer, somewhat delirious, spoke in a trembling voice.
Hearing this, Colin let out a sigh of relief.
Although he had presumed that she had probably escaped,
he was still anxious until he got confirmation.
“How long ago did she leave?” Colin continued to ask.
“It seems like a long time, a few days, a few months? Or years… I can’t remember clearly… I…”
“Next question, in which direction did she escape?”
In the Magic Fog, even with the enhanced sense of smell from “Beast Transformation Syndrome,” Colin couldn’t detect any useful scent.
Here, it seemed only the original source of “Beast Transformation Syndrome” itself might be able to pick up the trail.
“She…”
The Heretic Believer at the center hadn’t finished speaking when a terrifying power suddenly surged from the distance.
With it came the shaking of the earth and the sound of heavy footsteps from afar, still oppressively heavy despite the distance.
‘At least a Level 2 Containment Subject’s strength…’
Colin furrowed his brow, sensing that the creature was coming for him.
The Sound Blast emitted as it walked vibrated his eardrums…
In the darkness, it had already locked on to him.
‘When Kě’ài duō investigated the outer areas, it took nearly two days to encounter an entity of this level. Yet here, I’ve only shown up for twenty minutes, and a big one is already on me…’
The risks within the core area were indeed higher than he had anticipated.
However, judging that it would take some time for it to arrive, Colin continued to focus his attention on the Heretic Believer before him.
But this time, the terrifying pressure seemed to have restored the man’s reasoning, and he suddenly had a thought: “No, if I tell you, you have to take me away, you have to save me! Otherwise, I won’t talk! You must save me…”
“So much nonsense, speak or not!”
Colin punched him directly, bursting his chest.
“Why…”
The Heretic Believer’s eyes widened, looking at the flaming hole in his chest in disbelief: “Weren’t you… wanting to know…”
‘The moment the mission came up, you lost your value.’
Colin snapped his fingers, following the teachings of Big C Teacher, allowing the flames to consume the monsters before him, and finished them off.
At this moment, a mission notification popped up on his retina.
[Mission Event: “Assist ‘Saint Sana’ in escaping danger…”]
Note: Please follow the guidance to proceed and rescue Saint Sana…
…
Colin squinted his eyes, sensing briefly, certain of one thing:
“Without the ‘Lady Rabbit’s’ stamp and it appearing before my eyes instead of in my mind, it seems the mission is from a branch office…”
If it was a mission dispatched officially by the company, it would have appeared directly in his mind.
Not on his retina…
However, under the current circumstances, whether he could immediately act on this mission was still not a decision easily made.
Because it could possibly be a trap mission…
If he was led into dangerous territory, even Colin would not have an easy time.
‘The Rat isn’t here, so it’s likely not a trap mission, which is somewhat reassuring.’
‘Yeah, and based on what is currently known, The Rat, now under close watch by ‘Lady Rabbit,’ wouldn’t dare to make any significant moves, so he should be hiding.’
On Earth, ‘Lady Rabbit’s’ influence was slightly weaker, but not necessarily here, so The Rat wouldn’t dare take risks.’
After some thought, Colin believed there should be no issue and began to sense the details of the mission.
First…
He vaguely felt that this mission annoyingly seemed to have no reward.
The kind without a single point!
“Damn…”
Colin cursed under his breath, though he didn’t care too much.
After all, points were extraneous to him, 100,000 points wouldn’t trade for The Light Chaser’s life.
If she were harmed, the loss would be too great.
Not to mention the emotional aspect, but just in practical terms, it would mean Colin would be missing an essential card in his hand.
Furthermore, through this mission, Colin could barely sense the position of the Saintess, but could only ascertain a general direction, failing to perceive more specific details or her exact condition…
“The tracking methods of the branch office seem to be many levels inferior to those of the main company…”
Colin was somewhat displeased.
But, although the sensing wasn’t very clear, he could still determine the approximate location and distance. With luck, he might find the area within ten hours. If unlucky, it could take more than a day…
Overall, however, this was much better than his initial plan.
Based on his original thoughts upon arrival, he feared he might not see anyone for the whole week, or even find the vicinity of the other person…
In that case, by then it’s unknown whether he would find a person or a corpse.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 587 - 587 452 Success Doesnt Have to Be Me_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 587: 452 Chapter Success Doesn’t Have to Be Me!_1 Chapter 587: 452 Chapter Success Doesn’t Have to Be Me!_1 Having confirmed the direction, Colin was about to move when his body suddenly sank…
He was locked in from all sides.
At the same time, within the dense grey-black fog above his head.
A dark shadow plummeted with a whistling sound tearing through the air.
The arrival of it caused the air across the entire area to tremble.
And just as Colin’s gaze fell upon it, a grey foot at least three hundred square meters in size descended.
It seemed poised to squash him into a pulp.
“What a stinky foot,” Colin frowned, unfazed by his immobilized body.
As the giant foot descended within a few dozen meters of him, he activated the “Force – Repulsive Force” effect…
A horrific blast erupted immediately.
The entire large foot was struck by a strong force, crumbling into the Magic Fog like a sandcastle hit by a wave, then evaporated under the flash of firelight.
“Ugh!”
A strange, mournful cry came from the gloom, but no subsequent attack arrived.
“With the strength of a Level 2 Containment Subject and the boost from the ‘Plague of Magic Fog,’ it’s quite hard to kill. If you dare, wait until I’ve finished my business, then try chasing me onto my territory…”
Colin glanced at a corner of the dense fog, vaguely perceiving something without a definite shape.
Knowing it’d be a waste of time to try and kill this thing, he didn’t look further.
He turned, confirmed the direction once again, and quickly left the area, speeding towards his intended target.
After all, finding Shana was crucial, not wasting time on a monster in this thick and heavy drama.
…
At this time, in the path ahead of where Colin was heading, a terrible creature as massive as a mountain suddenly emitted countless rays of light. Then, in the next second, a shadow flitted by in a flash and disappeared into the distance…
The beast that had just swallowed her was rapidly disintegrated, turning into a sky full of shattered, incomplete bodies.
“Damn it, she got away again.”
Six figures holding lanterns and dressed in black cloaks arrived to find nothing but fragmented pieces on the ground that could no longer be put together…
“Who could have imagined that she would hide an important piece of her body inside the stomach of an ‘Ancient God Type’ creature?”
Another member of the Heretic Church, also carrying a lantern but with numerous dark, mysterious patterns on his face, sighed in resignation.
Half an hour earlier, they had successfully assassinated another of the Saintess’ bodies and had locked down all of her avatars. They thought that this time they had her, almost assuredly captured.
But what they hadn’t expected was to witness a sky filled with fragmented brilliance after the killing strike…
The adversary still had a hidden avatar capable of replacing the original!
After divination, they arrived here only to realize that she had hidden an “original body” within the body of an ‘Ancient God Type’ Magic Fog creature…
This effectively shielded their God-level divination. Who the hell would have guessed that this Saint would be so bold?
After all, such a feat was very likely to accidentally lead to her own demise…
But this generation’s Saint didn’t just dare to do it, she actually succeeded, thereby escaping a situation that was intended to be a surefire deathtrap for her.
Even more so, she managed to counter-kill numerous beings that could be termed ‘Servants of God’ in an instant!
“Could this shadow also be a ruse? Could there be other avatars hidden in the ‘Plague of Magic Fog’?”
Some began to doubt as the chase over time had really started to make them question themselves.
This generation’s Saint possessed an incredibly powerful ability unlike any before.
Her avatars, if they reached a certain threshold, would almost become identical to the original, with the ability to switch places at any time, and memories and experiences were fully shared among them…
That is to say, her “original body” could be transferred at any time, making it extremely difficult to kill.
These pieces of information had been obtained through trial and error during their encirclement, at the cost of a great number of lives…
“It’s impossible now. Earlier, in order to forcibly rescue people under the wrath of God, she recalled most of her strength. To have such a transferable avatar, this one is already at its limit,” said a tall Heretic Believer with tree branch-like black tattoos on his body.
“How can you be so sure of this?” someone asked, puzzled.
“On the way here, I sought counsel from the Revelation Tree. The Revelation it gave…” the tall Heretic Believer spoke with devout sincerity.
And upon mentioning that name, everyone showed reverence on their faces.
“So… do we continue to pursue her immediately? If we corner her this time, might it lead to a situation where our own powerful individuals are dragged into a mutual downfall, thereby allowing others to take advantage of the chaos?”
This time, it wasn’t just them; many other forces were involved.
Given the character of the Saint, it was foreseeable that if she were pushed into a corner, she would definitely sacrifice herself, taking many others with her.
Just as she had done several times before…
And crucially, no one had been able to wipe her out directly, disrupting her fatal abilities before they were unleashed.
Even the mightiest of beings found it almost impossible to do so.
Unless several powerful wills embodied in person…
However, if they could do that, they wouldn’t need to move against the Saintess to begin with.
After all, their objective was to obtain a certain permission to bypass the restrictions of God from her!
Hearing this, everyone fell into a moment of silence.
But in the end, the leader of the Heretic believers said, “What we seek is not much, just her eyes. Our demand is not great, the rest belongs to them. If anyone intends to usurp it, ‘Revelation Tree’ will make sure they understand the consequences…
“As for sacrifices, someone always has to be sacrificed. Without initiative, everyone else just watches, and that will only allow her to escape.”

chapters.title: Chapter 588 - 588 452 Success Doesnt Have to Be Mine_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 588: Chapter 452: Success Doesn’t Have to Be Mine!_2 Chapter 588: Chapter 452: Success Doesn’t Have to Be Mine!_2 “After this, it will be even harder to come by such an opportunity.”
Originally, the Saintess had not gone to the Golden City, and they all thought that the ambush had completely failed.
All those lying in wait would gradually die off under the erosion of the Magic Fog…
After all, not everyone had the ability to be active in the Magic Fog for a long time.
But unexpectedly, this Saint, who was said to be leaving, somehow turned back and stepped into their ambush, which gave them a hard-won opportunity.
“Yes, if we miss this time, there will be no chance in the future,” someone nodded.
“The Saintess repelled an Outer Evil God three years ago, entered disaster zones multiple times, and finally wandered in the Magic Fog for a very long time…”
“During that time, she was injured repeatedly, and even though she was born strong, she couldn’t withstand it.”
“Now she has reached her limit!”
“Even if we die, history will remember this day, recall our experience of martyrdom for the future.”
“We may not need to be present for the success, but our participation will surely be on the path to it!”
The Heretic Force Squad Leader, inspiring those around him, reignited their fighting spirit.
However, just then, the squad leader’s speech abruptly halted as he grabbed his throat, his face revealing extreme agony.
His stomach swelled as if something inside was twitching and writhing.
“How…” the tall man sensed something was amiss.
At the same time, his words faltered as he felt something crawl up into his throat from his stomach, and a tremendous pain as if being torn apart spread throughout his body.
At that moment, he caught sight from the corner of his eye that everyone in attendance seemed to be struck down at the same time.
“What is that…thing?”
In his confusion, he suddenly felt a chill in his heart as he saw a pale hand with splotches like those on a corpse stretch out from a companion’s mouth.
One hand, two hands, three hands…
More and more hands emerged from his companion’s mouth, squeezing out along with the blood.
And by the time there were four, his body had been blown apart, the sight gruesomely bloody and ghastly.
However, he couldn’t afford to look further as he saw several pale, splotchy fingers extending from his own mouth…
During this process, his Extraordinary Power felt as if it were bound, unusable.
So all he could do was watch himself die.
“The Saintess? No, she wouldn’t employ such an inefficient method of killing… what on earth is it?”
With his brain flashing through his last memories, he fell completely into darkness amid intense unwillingness.
After they died, the hands that crawled out of their bodies dragged them together, connecting them with some special power.
Before long, a Human Patchwork Monster made up of a great deal of flesh, limbs, and heads appeared at the site.
Its appearance was utterly blasphemous, enveloped by black mist.
Its head was huge, like a tumor, with countless arms dangling down, and its body was covered in faces filled with pain on stretched out skin, while many disordered feet supported it…
“Hehehe, well said, well said, your participation will indeed be part of the success…”
The Human Patchwork Monster, seemingly pleased with the high-quality flesh it had amalgamated from many humans, enjoyed the sensation.
If Colin were here at this moment, he would undoubtedly recognize this as the “Human Patchwork Monster” that had haunted his dreams!
“It seems almost certain that this is her last body. Once I take it down, I can truly leave this place, search for the sun… search for that true Sun!”
“I want to question Him! Why leave this place! Why abandon us!”
“No, no, no, I submit to Him with reverence, expressing everlasting subjugation, hoping He will not forsake us again…”
“Whimper, whimper, why have you abandoned us…”
“Why won’t you save us…”
“Hehehehehe…”
“…”
The “Human Patchwork Monster” spoke while crying and laughing, its numerous mouths uttering strange and varying rants.
This world was like a cage from which no life could escape; the apocalypse was inevitable.
Hope did not lie here…
Only where the true Sun resided was there real hope.
However, everything was now in place, but to leave, there was one essential condition…
To acquire a certain authority, without which departure was impossible.
The only known person in this world with this kind of authority was the Saint of the “Light” Church, no, to be precise, the known one from whom it could be obtained was the Saintess.
Others, he had peered into those outsiders from beyond…
Although they also possessed this ability, some experiments had clearly determined it was unusable.
The “Human Patchwork Monster” had secretly hunted in the shadows, but its authority would directly expire the moment it died…
It was downright unusable, and moreover, a strong premonition told him.
Even if successful, what appeared might not be the sun, but some other horrific, dangerous entity.
Therefore, the only method involved the Saint…
At least, at least by obtaining one fifth of her flesh or more significant limbs, hands, feet, preferably the head…
Only by merging with her body could he possess the ability to leave this place and venture into a greater world.
The thought of seeing the sun in his heart upon success made his emotions somewhat uncontrollable; he could already fantasize about basking in the sunlight…
Several seconds later, his emotions stabilized and his body suddenly burst into six chunks of flesh.
These pieces of flesh reassembled into six followers of the “Shadow Treant Mother,” who then summoned other believers of the same faith to this place to besiege the Saintess…
“We must act quickly; if we delay until the ‘Magic Fog’s’ master arrives, that would be bad,” he whispered in the communication.
Once that terrifying entity, which even gods shunned, arrived,
All efforts might be reduced to naught.
After finishing the conversation with others, the “Human Patchwork Monster” was about to take action when he suddenly felt a wave of invisible horror approaching.
He had a premonition, looking toward a certain direction…
There, a group of strange people wearing red veils stared at him.
The group was shielded by blue-black mist, protecting them from the influence of the “Magic Fog”… In fact, they actively consumed the Magic Fog drifting around them!
“Gurgle gurgle…”
Under their gaze, his stomach growled, a strong sense of hunger surging within.
However, it seemed they were not targeting him; after merely licking their lips at him and showing a hint of regret, they swiftly left toward…
The direction where the Saintess was?
“These people… are they the ‘Feast of Devouring’?”
The brain of the “Human Patchwork Monster,” formed from countless memories, conjured information about them and recalled the scene where they consumed the Magic Fog, with shock resonating in his heart.
What kind of monsters were they, after all?
But before he could think further, he felt a distant, invisible tremor.
It seemed… the fight had already begun up ahead!
Without hesitation, controlling hundreds of branch nodes, including the six bodies here, he moved forward.
If he were too late and the Saintess was killed, he could forget about grabbing an important limb, not to mention one fifth of flesh and organs…
Especially with the involvement of that “Feast of Devouring”!
…
Elsewhere.
Within a vast spatial expanse, most things appeared frozen like insects trapped in amber.
“Cough cough…”
Shana, clad in the white and gold-edged Church garb, coughed twice, blood seeping out, but it turned into radiance and was reabsorbed.
At this very moment, she could clearly sense that an upper-level power had blockaded the area.
Yet before she could unleash a bright light to dissolve this mighty force,
Shana suddenly felt a sharp pain in her left eye, followed by copious bleeding at the corner of the eye, and a black crack emerged, rapidly spreading to her other skin…
As if intending to envelop her entire being from this point.
“The curse of the Shadow Tree Mother…”
In the flash of a thought, a light emerged from behind Shana, like a cicada shedding its shell.
Hardly had it left…
When she saw her own “body” rapidly consumed by darkness, transforming into a strange tree. This tree, like a writhing shadow, sprouted branches with eyes budding as “fruit.”
Before Shana could make her next move, all the “Shadow Tree’s” eyes focused on her.
The next second, shadows for kilometers around came to life, surging towards her in a massive, overwhelming wave…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 589 - 589 453 0-09 Hunger and Light._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 589: Chapter 453 “0-09 ‘Hunger'” and “Light”._1 Chapter 589: Chapter 453 “0-09 ‘Hunger'” and “Light”._1 Countless shadows nearly enveloped all vision around him…
Shana, who had experience fighting it, knew very well that once she was covered by it, her body would likely be controlled…
As for its purpose, Shana was not completely in the dark.
After all, the thing wanted to take her eyes, or to be more precise, to obtain the aggregate concepts of her “sight,” “observation,” “watching,” and so on…
Its corresponding physical reality was simply “eyes.”
Of course, there was one more thing she was not quite certain about, but she guessed it was probably also related to some of the powers she held.
But now was not the time to think deeply about these things…
In the flicker of a thought, Shana also took action. Around her, hundreds of multi-faceted irregular diamond-shaped crystal stones emerged, spinning rapidly and condensing and scattering pale light.
Beams of extremely white light, like lasers, sliced through the shadows wherever they passed.
Even the ground around her melted from the heat.
The large-scale offensive created by the “Shadow Trees” was directly segmented…
She seized the gap, and her figure turned into a streak of light and appeared thousands of meters away in an instant, directly escaping the attack range.
However, she had just broken free, paused briefly, ready to continue fleeing, when…
Several roof-sized bolts of lightning, like divine warhammers, struck Shana with a posture destined to destroy everything.
Although at the critical moment, they were blocked by the shield of light around her, they successfully halted her.
“Cough cough…”
Shana pursed her lips, which were turning pale, coughed twice, then swallowed the blood that had surged to her throat.
That strike had shattered many bones inside her body and damaged some of her organs.
Moreover, there was no time to catch one’s breath…
Dozens of arrows, accompanied by wild winds and lightning, shot towards her.
The speed was extreme…
Beyond that, a bronze gate embellished with mysterious patterns was also taking shape not far away.
Some terrifying entity was gazing at her through the gate…
“Thunder Hunter and Abyssal Gate…”
Shana tilted her head, and a delicate gold earring on her right earlobe suddenly evaporated, then burst into fierce white light…
“Be careful, don’t observe…” someone exclaimed from afar.
But before the voice fell, a strong white light instantly enveloped all the surrounding areas…
The light lasted for less than a second.
But all the ambushers shooting arrows, whether they had closed their eyes or not, all underwent the Purification effect of the pale light, which cleansed both their souls and the vitality of their flesh, leaving no trace behind…
Consequently, they all collapsed limply, completely dead.
In addition, the arrows they had shot out, apparently because of the extraordinary blessings they carried, were erased by the white light and turned into ordinary arrows, falling to the ground.
At the same time, the bronze gate that was about to form was also directly scrapped, exploding into fireworks in the air.
As for these situations, Shana didn’t take much notice, she simply used the flash of bright light as a chance to rapidly break out toward the distance.
If she were to be trapped by these people, more and more enemies would arrive.
Under such heavy encirclement, escape would be impossible.
Moreover, what was most concerning to her was that there was a group of key individuals lurking in the shadows, not making a move yet.
These individuals were like predators tracking injured prey, driving her on, waiting for her to exhaust herself before they would strike…
Compared to those who had already acted openly, they were the part that troubled Shana the most.
“I must make them come out; this situation cannot be sustained,” she thought.
Within the flow of light, Shana suddenly changed direction, no longer trying to escape to the outside world but instead heading deeper into the “Disaster of Magic Fog.”
Within the depths of the disaster, there resided entities known as dominators of the “Disaster of Magic Fog”…
Even the so-called great beings did not wish to provoke those things because they had a natural restraint against the Gods, apart from some churches like the Church of Light…
So, if they saw her attempting to escape deeper into the midst of those catastrophes, determined to die rather than let these entities succeed,
then the enemies hiding in the shadows would inevitably become restless…
Indeed…
Not long after she made this choice, some individuals seemed to notice something wrong with the direction of her movement.
Some lives began to act restlessly.
Beneath a certain area, a massive number of monsters with limbs stitched together and countless faces upon their bodies opened all the mouths on their faces all at once.
Instantly…
As she continued her journey, Shana felt a terrifying surge of soul energy that swept over her in a flash.
Under its influence, the extraordinary power within her body became briefly unstable. Although this instability did not cause her much harm, it forced her to exit her simplified state of light and stop her movement.
Seeing this, the “Human Patchwork Monster” did not immediately approach to attack but quickly concealed itself again.
He was well aware that it was not yet time for this powerful prey to be exhausted…
