It was right when Shana had heightened her vigilance to the utmost that she stared at the arriving high-ranking lifeform, her eyes widening in a stunned expression.
There, the humanoid figure that the “King of Savage Sound” had become, lunged forward towards Mr. Colin in a sliding, kneeling posture.
“Great ‘Fire Bearer’ sir, please forgive my inability to appear immediately, but there is a reason for this…”
“Just now, as soon as those Corps forces of the ‘Radiant Angels’ rushed forward, they started attacking me, this external vessel, without any discrimination…”
“I tried to explain several times that I am here to assist you, Mr. ‘Flame Bearer,’ but they wouldn’t listen and instead escalated their efforts to forcibly seal me…”
“Mr. ‘Flame Bearer,’ it’s not a big deal that they attacked me, but they did not show the slightest respect for you and the great beings behind you…”
The “King of Madness” seemed to cry out in grief, employing all his life’s learning to convey his sense of injustice.
Meanwhile, Colin finally remembered something embarrassing. Right after Shana sent the report letter, amongst the feedback, indeed the name of the “King of Savage Sound” was also submitted.
Ah, this…
The situation seemed to have become somewhat awkward.
Colin hadn’t initially thought that the “King of Savage Sound,” hiding from so far away, would also be forcefully thrashed.
Because of his negligence, he hadn’t mentioned this to Shana…
And Shana, standing beside Colin and witnessing this scene, had her mouth slightly open, still not quite grasping the situation—
This…
Was this really a terror existing on par with the gods?!
Though her lifetime was not long, she had encountered many high-ranking lifeforms.
But this was the first time seeing this kind of… indescribable entity.
In her simple understanding, such “great existences,” “noble wills,” can generally be described as:
Their power is unspeakable, unpredictable; their actions are unspeakable, unpredictable; their methods are unspeakable, unpredictable, and so on…
Everything elusive, mysterious, and overwhelmingly powerful.
Yet today, this perception was shattered.
This did not seem like the language that could be uttered by a high-ranking existence…
Shana took a deep breath, feeling an absurd sense that her cognitive filter had been shattered.
“Alright, alright, I get it, it’s just a small misunderstanding.”
Colin waved his hand, “The situation is urgent right now, I need you to help us escape from here, back to the outside world.”
Now that the misunderstanding had been cleared up, there was no time to dwell on it.
Seeing that Colin appeared to have no intention of “deciding for him,” the “King of Madness” also changed his expression:
“Of course, it would be my honor to serve you.”
Although for the moment he had only obtained the authorization to converse…
It was enough.
“Sound” was part of the influence of his authority, and he could now exert his power through this medium.
Moreover, different from his previous method of digging a hole and seeping power through, this time he had been given proper authorization, and the power he could use was a bit more substantial…
However, to be safe, before acting, Colin made him promise again not to harm Shana.
The “King of Madness” had no objections and subtly explained a few things, indicating that he didn’t have much regard for that Saint, his heart harboring only one sun—the “Flame Bearer”—
The fundamental reason was that the entities targeting Shana were contained in a different place from this one.
The “Containment Divine Kingdom” was an arrangement belonging to Rosen…
Even if Shana herself wanted to release him proactively, the help she could provide was minimal—not none, but only a trivial amount, at best a mere embellishment.
Only the special authorization of the “Flame Bearer” or direct documents from the headquarters could play a decisive role…
This was also why, although he had been able to exert some power,
For hundreds of years, he never harbored thoughts against any Saint, nor did he recruit a Heretic Church to vie for power.
Otherwise, those besieging Shana today might have included followers of the “King of Madness” or the like…
The “Containment Divine Kingdom” was akin to the highest-level VIP dungeon.
Unless it was that group of people, or a seal of sufficient significance, anyone else would hardly be effective.
So, there was no longer any desire to struggle.
‘The use of various privileges within the company is still so complicated…’
Colin was secretly astounded.
After ensuring there was no other trouble, Colin grabbed Shana and allowed the power of the “King of Madness” to envelop them both.
The very next second, the two of them felt themselves traversing beneath the earth in a special form…
However, not long after they had set off, small, illusory green specks of light suddenly seeped into the Underground Great Labyrinth, releasing specific messages and seemingly trying to communicate.
Shortly thereafter, series of vibrations wafted out, forming a vague human silhouette in the air.
He looked at the seeping green light and expressed his thoughts very bluntly, “Defecting? You say I’m defecting? I will expel every single one of you vile evil gods!”
The evil God “King of Madness” responded as such.
This time, the “Radiant Angel” had left behind defensive forces that sealed away a large batch of “old acquaintances,” but there were also some that slipped through the net.
This one, clearly, was among those that slipped through.
It came seeking to persuade him to hand over the Saint, promising that once they were released, they would come to aid his escape.
Such words would not be believed by anyone with a bit of sense!
Moreover, he had finally established a good relationship with a “Flame Bearer”; why would he take that risk?
“Get out of here quickly, I would never stoop to your level and collude with you.”
No sooner had he spoken than he saw that the other party had not yet left and even showed signs of taking action, with the green light spreading.
He did not bother with courtesy a second time and responded with violent vibrations.
The fearful vibration swept across, reducing even gravel and dirt to dust, dismantling their fundamental material structures thoroughly into “dust.”
“Don’t try to get familiar with me; what you did in the past is unforgivable, you can only be locked away for life, waiting to be completely erased of all instincts and, when the time comes, thrown into the ‘Primordial Fire’ to burn.”
“I, on the other hand, am different. I have behaved well and have a chance to leave. If Rosen hadn’t died in some unknown way, I might have already obtained my freedom by now!”
“I’m about to have the opportunity to get out, and you think you can drag me into taking risks? Don’t even think about it!”
“Whoever dares to obstruct my embrace of freedom, the breathing of sweet air, I will kill them!”
As the “King of Madness” gnashed his teeth in anger, he couldn’t help feeling somewhat relieved that, back in those days, he had not yet managed to do anything before encountering the “Radiant Angel” Corps.
He had fled after a hard-fought battle.
Then, he had regained his strength, and just as he had left his lair to opportunistically attack the World Code, he faced the squad of the Primordial Fire Corps…
The good news was, the squad was fewer than thirty people.
The bad news was, in that small squad, there were six “Flame Bearers,” one of whom was amongst the highest-ranking leaders.
After a hard battle with them, he was captured and tried under the Bonfire Protocol. Finding that he had not really done anything, he was locked within the Containment Divine Kingdom, forged from multiple protocol authorities and various forces.
During his imprisonment, he had the chance to leave early…
But back then, he was too proud and ignorant to agree.
But now, if he did not agree, there might come a time…
When even the chance to agree would be gone.
The “King of Madness” was increasingly certain that there had been earth-shattering changes in the outside world, which he was unaware of.
Staying within the “Containment Divine Kingdom” was certainly a road to death.
Only by trying every possible means to escape, could he attain freedom…
Of course, before enjoying freedom, he had the obligation to work for Bonfire Company for about three thousand years.
However, for a high-level being, that span was not particularly long, unlike within the “Containment Divine Kingdom” where even a second could be twisted to feel like a hundred thousand years, coupled with various tortures…
This so-called three thousand years of work was almost inconsequential.
Of course, although he had heard that the job had a somewhat high mortality rate.
But it still offered a glimmer of hope, unlike here, where the mortality rate was a definite one hundred percent.
.
.
.
Post now, edit later.

chapters.title: Chapter 603 - 603 459 0-9 Hunger Buffet. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 603: Chapter 459: “0-9 Hunger” Buffet. _1 Chapter 603: Chapter 459: “0-9 Hunger” Buffet. _1 Shuttling through the almost endlessly vast underground labyrinth…
“Dear ‘Flame Bearer’ sir, some heretics had just tried to bewitch me, but I sternly refused them and then unceremoniously expelled them…”
“King of Madness” turned his head and sold out a few “Ancient Gods”, with no inkling of the consciousness of being a lowly creature.
Of course, the differences between “Ancient Gods” as well as some cognitions are even greater than that between humans and ants, plus “Bonfire Company” had been secretly causing trouble back in the day; they never truly united, so he did not feel as though he had betrayed anyone…
“Very well, I’m gratified by your loyalty,”
Colin nodded in agreement, offering verbal encouragement but made no mention of any concrete reward.
Shana, who was observing this higher life form acting so humbly, felt her worldview continually being shaken. If she had a certain amount of knowledge about Earth, she would undoubtedly have uttered one word—
Abstract.
At that moment, “King of Madness” hesitantly responded:
” ‘Flame Bearer’ sir, during my contact with those heretical factions, I discovered some things; I’m not sure if I should mention them. They may be related to that ‘0-09’ Hunger.”
Hmm? Colin became interested at once and asked, “Tell me, what did you find?”
“I sensed that the gods, oh, I mean, the heretical factions that came here, most of them seem to be somewhat related to ‘Hunger’. It appears they might be collaborating?”
A collaboration? Colin thought back to the previous battlefield.
The factions were mixed together in combat, and there were indications of collaboration among the containment subjects, but he had not seen “Hunger” collaborating with anyone.
“Hunger’s” status in this world is probably not much better than that of “Red Moon” adherents on Earth.
“I’m not too clear either, but from what I gather, ‘Hunger’ seems to want to open the cage that imprisons them and let them out…”
“King of Madness” remembered some tidbits from previous gossip and added:
“Normally, these creatures shouldn’t be able to release such vast amounts of power. There must be something assisting them. Otherwise, they wouldn’t be able to interfere with the outside world for such a prolonged period today.”
Having learned from experience, as a part of “Bonfire Company,” “King of Madness,” while not clear about the situations in other containment areas,
did not let this stop him from making some approximations based on his own experiences.
As a result, the power they released was nearly fifty percent more than expected!
This was highly abnormal; there had to be some external force helping them.
Furthermore, based on what was heard today, it seemed that the “fate” of some individuals was entangled with “Hunger”…
Therefore, everything must definitely be related to “Hunger.”
“Let them out? Since when is ‘Hunger’ so benevolent?”
Colin raised an eyebrow, knowing this was almost impossible.
But quickly, he had some speculation…
“Is ‘Hunger’ intending to consume those existences?”
If there was some reason compelling this higher existence to do something so against common sense,
then all Colin could think of was this one point.
“Hunger” wanted to open the cage to have a buffet…
And the First Level Containment Subjects, having been locked up for so long, wanted to take the opportunity to flee. Once the gate was opened, and if all First Level Containment Subjects moved at once, “Hunger” wouldn’t possibly be able to consume them all in one go.
In that case, the thrilling fight for survival would come down to luck…
As for why there was “collaboration” between the two sides, but without any apparent mercy during the fray moments ago,
this was not hard to understand.
Whoever captured Shana would have the upper hand. If “Hunger” took Shana and got the authority, the consequences would truly become a matter of “Hunger” flipping the box open and having a buffet.
Fortunately, as it stood, neither party had succeeded.
And just by themselves, they couldn’t open the containment restrictions.
Reminded of this, Colin felt somewhat relieved. If they allowed “Hunger” to gorge,
swallowing several First Level Containment Subjects at once and maxing out its combat strength,
then in the end, except for the intervention of the giants, no one else would likely make much of a difference.
“King of Madness” also thought of this, but it wasn’t overly worried because, to its knowledge, there were many restrictions on “Hunger,” which would directly fragment once it surpassed a certain threshold.
The fragmented entities would then consume each other.
Ultimately, the crisis would not exceed a certain critical value.
This piece of knowledge it did not reveal.
After all, the “Flamebearer” Reserves sir himself harbored a remnant of the “0-09 Hunger”…
Being one of the carriers of “Hunger,” how could he not understand this basic knowledge?
As the flow of logic cleared up, Colin also chose not to continue on this topic.
At this point, due to her lack of relevant knowledge, Shana, who had been quiet throughout, asked:
“What’s the origin of this maze here?”
This labyrinth was known to many, but those who entered it only knew that it harbored many strange creatures and potential fortune, yet it was more often fraught with danger.
About its specific origins, they couldn’t explain clearly or know why it was built by whom.
Hearing this, “King of Madness” observed Colin, knowing that this Saint knew not too much, and “Flame Bearer” sir seemingly hadn’t disclosed relevant information; it did not feel it appropriate to explain directly.
Soon, seeing Colin nod for him to go on, “King of Madness” then gave his explanation.
“This is a special, abnormal containment site born from the merging of many ‘World Codes’, I heard its original name was something like ‘Script City·Underground Labyrinth of Twenty Thousand Leagues’…”

chapters.title: Chapter 604 - 604 459 0-9 Hunger Buffet. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 604: Chapter 459: “0-9 ‘Hunger'” Buffet. _2 Chapter 604: Chapter 459: “0-9 ‘Hunger'” Buffet. _2 Hiss, City of Scripts? This underground labyrinth is actually part of the “City of Scripts”?
Upon hearing this name, Colin felt a tingle on his scalp and couldn’t help but take a slight gasp of air.
There was an indescribable feeling…
“King of Savage Sound” was unaware of his thoughts and continued to explain, “I’m not clear on what was initially contained here, but I know that now it has been thoroughly neutralized…”
For them, being thoroughly neutralized was much like an ordinary person turning to ashes.
If only ordinary means were used, there was basically no chance of rescue.
Only the “Red Moon” or a “miracle” of equal authority can possibly recover it.
But…
Theoretically, if asked, the “Red Moon” would most likely extend a helping hand.
It’s just that the result might not be acceptable to everyone.
“Is that so…”
Shana nodded, then asked a few more questions, digesting information such as “World Code.”
Although there were many “new terms,” her recognition of the world she lived in was not slight; with a bit of parsing, she could quickly grasp some things.
Thereafter, she gained a clearer understanding of the place she was in.
Several hours passed by unknowingly…
Early the next day, on the second day of the mission, Colin arrived at the entrance to an underground labyrinth not too far from his territory.
Shana also sensed this…
This speed was much faster than what they had initially planned.
“By the way, Mr. Colin, about that matter…” “King of Madness” hinted subtly.
Although not explicitly stated, Colin knew what he was alluding to.
‘This guy seems to be getting slicker…’ he thought.
In a flash of thought, Colin spoke:
“Rest assured, your performance during this period has all been seen by the organization. When I return, I’ll write a report and submit a formal application to the superiors.”
Pausing, he continued to add, “You can go back now and wait for the notice.”
“Good, good.”
“King of Madness,” who had hardly come into actual contact with human society, did not have much doubt.
Just thinking about finally having the chance to come out…
He was somewhat excited.
Meanwhile, Shana, following Colin and witnessing this scene, although it wasn’t the first time, still felt an eye-opening sharpness as if a small knife was poking her rear.
Soon, the two left the underground labyrinth.
Upon emerging from the rift, Shana stood on the barren ground, gazing around with an expansive view, and couldn’t help but feel a moment of absence.
After all the turmoil within the “Disaster of Magic Fog,” she’d almost forgotten.
The world was originally so vast…
Spreading her arms, tilting her head back as if to embrace the sky and earth, she took a deep breath, which seemed to relax her quite a bit.
“There’s just a little way left, let me lead the way, we need to speed up.”
“Can your body handle it?”
“Of course, there’s no problem.”
At that, Colin did not refuse, knowing that Shana had recovered quite a bit of her status over this period.
At least he need not worry too much about hurrying on the road…
As his voice fell, Shana’s body was enveloped in layers upon layers of radiance, shrouding both of them at once.
Then, enveloping each other, they turned into a stream of light, darting towards the distance with an exceptionally fast speed…
In the “Disaster of Magic Fog,” fast movement was impossible due to the Magic Fog obscuring the propagation of light, but in the outside world, her speed could surpass the “King of Madness”!
From here to the territory, even if Colin were unobstructed, it would take a good half an hour.
But she could make it in less than a minute.
For the thrill of “running it out,” Shana took a slightly longer route on purpose, only reaching the vicinity of Colin’s territory after a few minutes.
“This feeling, watching it, kind of reminds me of the ‘Father of the Ocean’ when it was liberated…”
Colin thought of that person from the past, vaguely remembering that they had wished for something to be burned for them after death.
He had forgotten what exactly it was, but it didn’t seem important, so he didn’t dwell on it.
At this moment, seeing the towering bonfire from afar, Shana couldn’t help but feel a sense of security, even though it was her first time truly being here, it felt just like coming home.
However, just as she was about to enter her domain, Shana stopped in her tracks.
The two of them transitioned back from their luminescent state, landing on the ground…
Colin had thought that Shana wanted to walk the rest of the way, but seeing no indication she wished to do so, his puzzlement turned into sudden realization, and he kept quiet.
Before long, a group of people arrived one after another.
“Her Saintess, I am Amido, a Cardinal Archbishop from the ‘Radiant Assembly.’ We were en route to rescue you, but upon sensing your escape and arrival here, seeing you safe and sound is truly wonderful…”
A church member adorned in white with blue edged vestments approached, his face showing respect.
‘Radiant Assembly’ was a faction that had split from the ‘Holy Light Court,’ and although Shana was ostensibly just a ‘Light’ Saint…
In reality, she was a saint of all ‘Light’ faiths, not just the ‘Light’ Church, so the correct attitude must be displayed.
However, he was abruptly interrupted before he could finish his inquiry.
“Ahem, thank you, Your Excellency Amido, my health is very good, ahem, I appreciate your help, I am doing well now, ahem ahem ahem, being a Saint, I am touched…”
As she spoke, Shana’s face showed gratitude, she covered her mouth, coughed lightly twice, and when she removed her hand, there was some fresh blood in her palm.
The crimson quickly transformed into light and was reabsorbed.
Nevertheless, this left Amido somewhat embarrassed, feeling that he was deliberately made uncomfortable…
After all, everyone knew what kind of help they had actually provided…
At the same time, Colin, standing by Shana’s side, was also surprised.
From their previous interactions, he hadn’t noticed that Shana, usually carefree and humorous, also had a slightly manipulative streak.
Then, more individuals with not insignificant strength, who seemed to Colin to be at least official Seventh or Eighth Levels from Earth, and who held high positions, approached boldly to express their “respect” for the Saint—
No matter what they really thought or how they acted, the Saint’s status was there for all to see.
Afterward, Colin stood silently behind her, somewhat dumbfounded, witnessing how Shana ‘dominated’…
“Thank you,…Knight Commander, Your displayed bravery, sacrifice, humility, and fairness leave me in no doubt, you are an extraordinary and admirable Virtue Knight…”
“…Count, thank you for your gift, your character does not pale in comparison to that of the Knight Commander, I am very fortunate to have been able to save you and your family from that disaster…”
“Mr. Calinsis, your army is the most valiant I have ever seen. I heard that when the disaster broke out, they transferred their living forces as much as possible, so that now they can fight bravely outside the outskirts of the ‘Plague of Magic Fog,’ protecting the people before them…”
“So happy to see you, Lady Archbishop Ovinya of the ‘Light’ Church, if not for your assistance, I might not have been able to return, I am truly grateful…”
Shana, emanating a holy light, faced everyone who had come with a naturally pure smile, extending a sincere ceremonial greeting.
Even for her own ‘Light’ Church members, she graciously did not neglect the appropriate manners.
All who were greeted stood somewhat nervously excited.
“Alright, alright, I’ve received everyone’s sincerity, but I am sorry, forgive me for being a bit impolite, I do not like overly complicated ceremonies; currently, there are some matters I need to attend to, and I cannot continue to accompany you all here.”
Usually, hearing such dismissive words, those present would become angry.
But now, they all breathed a sigh of relief, tactfully indicating they wouldn’t bother the Saint any further and left one by one.
During this time, it wasn’t that they hadn’t thought about talking back…
But saying such things could provoke an attack from any of the others standing there.
What’s more, they would face further questioning upon their return…
After all, apart from the favors they owed the Saint, just the fact that she truly held various authorities made it impossible for them to retort.
In front of Shana, they could avoid doing things, but they couldn’t afford to make big mistakes.
As everyone left one after another, Colin finally closed his slightly agape mouth.
Today, he had witnessed another side of the Saintess.
A bit manipulative, with full-on assertiveness, a stronger side.
Colin had no doubt that if there were a keyboard present, her fingers could fly across it like playing a piano.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 605 - 605 460 The Adventures of Rosen_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 605: Chapter 460 The Adventures of Rosen_1 Chapter 605: Chapter 460 The Adventures of Rosen_1 “Finally gone.”
Shana hummed softly, a rare display of her emotions.
She couldn’t possibly be completely unbothered by these people slacking off.
But, that’s probably as far as she’d pursue it…
Then she turned around, holding a bunch of gifts given by the others, and looked at Colin:
“Is there anything here you need?”
“Uh…”
Colin touched his nose, still immersed in the atmosphere of Shana “slaughtering all directions”—
For some reason, he found Shana like this somewhat cute.
Now, hearing her words, Colin came back to his senses and looked over the received gifts without much politeness.
The vast majority were mystical items emitting various auras, complete with instruction manuals.
Besides those, there were also some exquisitely packaged medicines, gold, and so on.
Colin glanced briefly and then shook his head. The items mostly inclined towards defense or offense, not very functional, and not very powerful, so he wasn’t very interested…
Of course, a key reason was that the company’s items had spoiled his tastes.
He had no interest whatsoever in things that were mediocre and came with considerable side effects.
‘Feels like the craft on Earth was even better.’
Colin muttered to himself, then saw Shana putting away the gifts while saying, “If you need anything, feel free to tell me…”
After this incident, the relationship between the two had become much closer than before.
Afterward, the two of them walked back to the edge of their territory together.
When some of the people tilling the fields at the edge of the territory saw Brother Shunzi, they were first startled, then somewhat relieved—
After the “Disaster of Magic Fog” began, Brother Shunzi hadn’t replied, making them a bit nervous.
You see, whether the “The Descent Project” was safe or not often depended on whether Brother Shunzi was around.
If he was around, even if the sky fell, Brother Shunzi would hold it up.
They would only have to deal with trifles at most.
If he wasn’t, then the level of danger could be limitless.
They weren’t up to handling too high-end of situations.
“I haven’t checked your messages yet. Has anything happened in the territory?”
Colin looked at “Life Mentor Adorable.”
Just earlier, Adorable was exploiting the “Body of Tyranny” status ruthlessly on a wasteland around the perimeter of the territory, wantonly expending his power to cultivate the land…
“Everything’s quite normal,” Adorable said, glancing at the woman wearing white clothes with gold trim, standing beside Brother Shunzi.
“This is ‘Light’ religion’s Saintess Shana,” Colin briefly introduced her.
“Welcome, welcome…” Adorable and a few employees hurriedly expressed their welcome.
They were full of curiosity about this so-called angel walking upon the earth, a living saint among humans.
Curious glances abounded, but unfortunately, they weren’t sure what method the Saint had used; she seemed hazy.
Her aura was filled with an indescribable sense of sanctity…
Staring at her a bit longer, one felt peace within, and all feelings of fatigue seemed to be relieved and erased.
“By the way, Brother Shunzi, the 3rd experimental field is doing great. I estimate the first batch of tomatoes and potatoes can be harvested in a few days,” Adorable suddenly remembered to mention.
“The potatoes are ready for harvest? It’s only been a bit over twenty days, right? That’s so quick?” Colin was surprised.
They had several experimental fields specifically using particular extraordinary items to induce growth, trying out the final effects of these crops.
Listening to “Life Mentor Adorable”…
Overall, it wasn’t bad. Theoretically, as long as one was willing to continually use “Colorless Crystal” to output the item’s effect,
and keep up with fertilizing…
then a crop of rice could possibly be ready half a month per cycle, or even faster.
As they talked, they naturally arrived at the neighboring 3rd experimental field. In the field stood a special sunflower about five meters tall, smiling…
It was a company product known as “Smiling Sunflower,” a green functional item.
The light emanating from it could effectively promote the growth of the crops in the field, or more precisely, all plants within its range of effect.
“A miraculous item,” Shana said as she followed Colin, looking at that thing from a distance.
The sunflower also turned its head, smiling at them.
Colin bent down to look at the plump, red tomatoes on the ground, then dug around and found irregularly shaped potatoes underneath the tomato plants.
This batch of potatoes was grafted onto tomato plants, all expertly done by “Little Maid.”
The survival rate was high, and, as far as could be seen, the fruiting rate was also pleasing.
Colin grabbed a potato, broke off the roots, and weighed it in his hand.
“Is there any water?” Colin asked.
“Yes, there is.”
“Wash it, I want to taste it.”
After Colin asked for the potato to be washed, an employee cleaned it and brought it back. Colin’s hand emitted flames, quickly roasting the potato. He took a bite to taste it.
“Edible,” Colin gave a fair assessment.
It certainly had nutrients; it was just that the flavor left something to be desired…
However, with some seasoning, it could be palatable; besides, people in this world weren’t too picky about food.
“Can I also try it?” Shana asked.
“No problem,” Colin said as he prepared to dig up another potato, but Shana took the one he’d bitten from, broke off a piece from another side, and tasted it.
“Tastes better than black bread,” Shana gave an evaluation that wasn’t the worst.
“Yes,” Colin nodded and stood up.
After a brief tour of several experimental fields, he reckoned that everything would be stable.

chapters.title: Chapter 606 - 606 460 The Adventures of Rosen_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 606: Chapter 460 The Adventures of Rosen_2 Chapter 606: Chapter 460 The Adventures of Rosen_2 The shortage of food in the territory would soon be greatly alleviated.
Later, when Colin returned to the territory with Shana, Nun Vanessa came over, looking at Shana with surprise, and then prayed to her right there.
She had heard Shana’s voice many times before, but this was the first time she saw her in person.
“Thank you for speaking up for me…” Shana raised her hand and touched the nun’s head with her wheat-colored skin.
Pure radiance flowed down from her palm, infusing into Vanessa’s head, and brought her a boost.
Then, Shana seemed to sense something, turned her gaze, and saw a little girl with red eyes curiously staring at her from afar…
‘That somewhat special little girl?’ An idea flashed through Shana’s mind.
But before she could think further, a blue-haired female knight approached, pulling back Shana’s attention.
The female knight then knelt on one knee in front of Shana:
“Thank you for the War God’s blessing, you have finally returned.”
Compared to others, Shana’s attitude was much better toward this deputy who had been with her during the disaster.
It’s just that hearing the other party utter praises about the War God…
She made a strange expression, then finally said, “Alright, get up, there’s no need for these elaborate rituals between you and me.”
Helena’s sister nodded, got to her feet, looked at Colin, and was about to say something when she paused abruptly.
Seeing Colin standing shoulder to shoulder with the Saintess, it seemed… their relationship appeared…
Somehow, even closer than hers?
Even though she knew the Saintess better, she had the feeling of an outsider…
There was an inexplicable taste to it.
However, she didn’t think too much, thanked Colin and mentioned that her family would definitely show their gratitude in a big way.
Truthfully, she did not expect that Colin could bring people back in just one day.
This showed that the “Bonfire” Divine Envoy was indeed powerful, master of incomprehensible methods, as well as formidable strength…
…
Aside from there, in a more distant place, some employees were looking over, casting curious glances like “Life Mentor Adorable” had done before.
But alas, they could only perceive a sense of holiness, purity, and a vague sense of ethereal beauty.
They couldn’t make out the details anyway…
Some tried to focus their eyes in order to take a closer look, only to have their pupils stung by the brightness.
“Hahaha…” other employees showed schadenfreude smiles.
Yet, without paying too much attention to them, Colin led Shana into the “former ‘Light’ Church, now Bonfire Church,” where Shana could recuperate in peace.
Standing before the kindled bonfire, she felt the warmth of the flames above.
Shana squinted comfortably.
This was not the first time she had seen the flame, but only by being near it could she understand its true specialty.
“Right, those more than ten thousand disaster victims on the periphery of the ‘Plague of Magic Fog,’ I plan to form a team with my people and that female knight to bring them out. What do you think?”
Colin said while pulling over two chairs and asking Shana.
The fields were now mostly ready…
Other matters were generally stable; it was time for them to go out and try more work.
Maybe they could trigger a mission and earn some more points.
“They… Can they manage?” Shana accepted the chair, sat down with her legs together, placing her hands on her thighs, and while basking in the warmth of the fire, she was somewhat apprehensive.
The abilities of these people did not seem very high…
“Don’t worry, they can’t get to the core area, but they can manage a trip around the periphery.”
Colin wasn’t too worried; judging by the location given by Shana, that position was fairly peripheral and quite safe.
It shouldn’t lead to any further accidents…
“Okay then, I’ll give them some blessings and things at that time, oh, and also them…”
Shana said halfway, seemingly recalling something, as ripples of light surged in her ice-blue eyes like stones being cast into the center of a calm lake.
At the same time, Colin saw a door made of light appear in a certain part of the church.
As the door was gradually opened, Colin saw a spatial area inside with thousands of disaster victims lying peacefully in their sleep.
Thin streams of light flowed from Shana’s body, dragging each person out like tentacles.
Seeing this, Colin called some employees from outside, bringing out all the sleeping people from the church like a truck being unloaded.
Otherwise, given the scale of the church, it would be difficult to accommodate so many people.
“They should start waking up one after another in about an hour,” Shana explained.
After dealing with these people, which took about fifteen minutes, thin streams of light pulled out hundreds of irregular orbs wrapped in a substantial amount of white light.
“Do you still need this?” Shana asked, as the layered light dissipated from her eyes.
The door of light vanished, and the light wrapping the irregular orbs dissipated as well, revealing the enclosed creatures—
Chunks of grotesque flesh of various sizes.
What the heck?
Colin felt a sense of déjà vu but couldn’t remember at first. He flared his nostrils, took a whiff of the air, and then his expression changed.
“‘Human Patchwork Monster’? So many of them?!”
“Yeah, I heard you talking about them before and seemed to be looking for them, so during the previous fight, I intercepted some and preserved their bodies for collection.”
“Great, great, great!”
Colin was moved; “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” was about to be upgraded again!
At the same time, a task popped up before his eyes.
[Event Three: Toss the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” and the corresponding materials into the bonfire, and spend a certain amount of points to improve the item’s effect level.]
…
Seeing this, Colin didn’t hesitate and went about doing what the instructions specified.
A confirmation message quickly popped up in the bonfire.
[This upgrade will consume all materials and require 5,000 Bonfire Points. Do you confirm the upgrade?]
“Only five thousand?”
Without giving it much thought, Colin immediately chose to confirm.
Soon enough, following a burst of special sound effects, the new “Fusion Card: Smiling Mountain of Corpses” was ready!
Colin eagerly picked it up to check it out.
It was still a Purple Item and hadn’t broken through to orange, but the purple text was richer.
As for the description page…
Originally, twelve bodies were needed to use this item.
But now, only three were required, and the scale of release had increased significantly. A single Corpse Mountain could exceed ten meters in diameter, truly making it a mountain of corpses!
As for other skill aspects, two new ones were added.
One was “Adaptive Evolution,” which allowed it to evolve physiques that adapt to various extreme environments by devouring corpses.
Or evolve suitable limbs to perform tasks.
The second was a long-distance transport skill that worked across tens of kilometers!
“If it eats enough bodies, its upper limit can reach the strength of a Second Order Containment Subject, not bad, not bad…”
Colin nodded, noting that up to now, many pieces of equipment had become unnecessary.
For instance, “Money Slave” was now basically for his subordinates’ use, and “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” was one of them.
But after a boost, it could be useful once again!
“Very nice.” Colin thanked Shana.
“As long as you like it.”
Shana raised her hand, swept her hair back, smiled, then reached into the Storage Room and pulled out a hardcover notebook: “Want to take a look at this?”
Colin’s gaze shifted, and he was taken aback when he saw that the cover was inscribed with five big, formal characters.
“The Adventures of Rosen?”
That guy, who liked to hold back, actually left behind adventures?
“Did he write this himself, or…” Colin asked curiously.
“I’m not sure, this book is something left over from before. Take a look and if possible, tell me what it says.”
“Alright.”
Colin took the notebook from her hands.
Then…
When he flipped open the first page and read part of the content, Colin’s face scrunched up.
He wore the expressions of an old man befuddled by subway trains and smartphones.
The notebook had loads of phrases like “ancient times,” “worshipped by all,” and “dictatorial for eternity”…
If there weren’t some actual content, Colin would have suspected he was reading a cultivation novel.
‘Unless it’s some mistake, the intelligence behind the ‘Fire Tree Mark’ must have come from this guy.’
Colin couldn’t help but mutter to himself.
“What’s up? Anything strange?” asked Shana.
“It’s nothing, just a bit strong-tasting…”
Colin waved his hand to indicate it was nothing and then continued reading somewhat speechlessly.
However, when he came across some important information, his brows furrowed a little more…
There was indeed a lot of intelligence in there.
But much of it was somewhat outdated for him, like something about the top three World Codes, who’s legacy to reclaim, and so on…
What caught his interest was that Colin actually saw a description of “Lady Bunny” in there!
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 607 - 607 461 Rosen I Dont Eat Beef _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 607: Chapter 461 Rosen: I Don’t Eat Beef! _1 Chapter 607: Chapter 461 Rosen: I Don’t Eat Beef! _1 “… ‘Lady Rabbit’s’ reputation within the company seems… not very good either?”
Colin’s gaze swept over some content on his notebook.
It mentioned that Rosen, while executing a certain task, encountered an employee who complained about a series of tasks assigned by ‘Lady Rabbit’…
And Rosen offered comfort in response.
“… As a rule, no matter the level of employee, they usually dislike tasks assigned by ‘Lady Rabbit,’ because she always gives out tasks that push the edge of an individual’s abilities, in order to maximize benefits”…”
“Under her arrangement, employees often feel like they are walking on a tightrope or about to capsize at any moment. During the execution of these tasks, many choices once made incorrectly can lead to major problems, but even after receiving numerous reports and complaints, she still tirelessly continues to let people try to complete tasks that are theoretically possible, leveraging as much benefit as possible with the smallest sacrifice…”
“As a result, employees don’t rate her very highly, but… the tasks she assigns usually bring in benefits that match one’s own, resulting in highly polarized evaluations…”
Looking at the description above, Colin’s expression appeared somewhat peculiar.
This was his first time seeing a description of ‘Lady Rabbit’ elsewhere.
Though the content was not extensive…
One thing was certain, ‘Lady Rabbit’ and those like Rosen were from the same batch and not later additions.
Of course, this was all predicated on the fact that an account is non-inheritable and can be permanently retained.
Otherwise, today’s ‘Lady Rabbit’ might be someone else’s successor.
“Assuming what’s said above and the one now are the same person, then ‘Lady Rabbit’ really is considered a senior member, and Rosen’s tone when describing her here seems relatively egalitarian…”
It’s quite a pity…
Colin shook his head slightly as he looked at the content in the notebook.
There was no mention of ‘Lady Rabbit’s’ specific position or Authority Level; one can only roughly guess that her status within the company was not low and that what she mainly managed had to do with tasks.
However, the related description…
Was actually quite accurate.
Colin recalled his tasks, which did indeed often give the feeling of being on the verge of catastrophe.
Initially thinking it was his own issue, it turned out to be a problem with ‘Lady Rabbit.’
“It seems that tasks frequently going awry was ‘Lady Rabbit’s’ fault, not mine…”
Colin murmured and continued reading.
The subsequent mentions of ‘Lady Rabbit’ came to an end, with more about some people and events encountered while recovering the ‘Light’ remnants along the path…
It also mentioned the ‘King of Savage Sound,’ infamous for being as slippery as an eel, snatching things and then trying to flee.
But eventually, it was still caught on the spot by Rosen, wielding the complete ‘0-09 ‘Hunger’,’ and after consuming half of it, tossed it into a special containment chamber for remodeling…
“So it appears, the ‘King of Savage Sound’ is very good at fleeing, eh? If it really can be released in the future, we have to be careful in case it escapes.”
Colin turned to the next page, examining the handwriting chronicling past events.
“Day 731, recovered the core, evacuated the civilians, and set off fireworks in the rampaging World Code-366…”
“Day 829, set off fireworks in the rampaging World Code-211…”
“Day 837, set off fireworks in the rampaging World Code-97…”
“Day 839, Rosen oh Rosen, you can’t keep bombing like this. Mister Huang He demands we recover as many useful worlds as possible, so it looks like we need to relax the review criteria, and leave some leeway…”
“Day 863, these damned Heretic Races! I gave them a chance, yet instead they took it as a sign the company was showing weakness! Daring to ambush our refugee ships! Indeed, compared to higher lifeforms, these non-human Heretic Races are far more vile!”
“Using humans as brood for breeding filthy beings and so on…”
“The entire race’s hatred and evil towards humanity can no longer be reversed. And it is rooted in their very nature, not manipulation by higher beings, and they have no value for reformation nor any possibility of coexistence!”
“Our human blood is more precious than that of every Heretic Race! I will make them remember the respect they should show when encountering humanity!”
“Day 897, set off fireworks in the rampaging World Code-77…”
“Day 897, set off fireworks in the rampaging World Code-59…”
…
“Ah, this…”
Colin opened his mouth wide, looking at this old chap who had been setting off fireworks all along, not knowing how many worlds he destroyed in the process.
Besides “World Codes,” he bombarded people’s mother stars, or threw some high-level Containment Subjects into their lairs, completely eradicating all manner of Heretic and Xenomorphic races, causing many to become utterly extinct…
Now, he was understanding more why some higher lifeforms stationed in “World Code-4” became so agitated when they sensed the company’s approach.
It was all because of the Master who “didn’t eat beef.”
Of course, such assertiveness was external. Internally, Rosen was quite amiable.
“But from the look of these things, such retaliation doesn’t seem to be a problem at all.”
Colin was beginning to feel that wanton destruction wasn’t quite right.
But upon seeing what the Xenomorphic races had been doing, mere destruction seemed insufficient.
Nevertheless, he didn’t dwell on it; an entry in the diary caught Colin’s attention.
In the second half of Rosen’s mission, the upper echelons issued a very special task: recall all the ‘Flame Bearers’ that could be recalled, as it seemed a major mission was about to be launched.

chapters.title: Chapter 608 - 608 461 Rosen I Dont Eat Beef _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 608: Chapter 461 Rosen: I Don’t Eat Beef! _2 Chapter 608: Chapter 461 Rosen: I Don’t Eat Beef! _2 And this recall directive,
seemed to be related to the completion of the manufacturing of a certain prop within the company…
In the description of this prop, Rosen used terms such as “super-specification,” “theoretical transcendence,” and “beyond cognition,” claiming that with it, human nature would truly become the subject…
Unfortunately, because of the mission at hand, Rosen didn’t go back and didn’t know much.
“For the love of god, at least tell me what this so-called ‘super-specification prop’ is used for, specifically what it does? At the very least give me a specific name…”
Colin scratched his head in frustration.
He realized that this matter might very well be related to the current status of the world.
The birth of a super-specification prop…
The recall of most Firebearers…
Combining the current situation, Colin wondered if the timeline had been reversed?
This possibility was not low because some high-level props were clearly manufactured a long time ago, yet some of the notes and memo-like things on them were from more recent times.
Not to mention that the “Za Warudo” thing shouldn’t have existed a few hundred years ago.
“Could it be that the world today has already been through a time reversal, once or even multiple times?”
Holding the notebook, Colin thought about it and felt it was possible, but not entirely so.
Because if it was just time reversal, why do things like “World Code” still exist without having been reversed as well?
There were many complexities…
After a bout of brainstorming, Colin shook his head and stopped thinking further.
When his own authority increases later, and he has the chance to meet “Lady Bunny,” he’ll ask her directly.
Then, Colin continued to look through the notebook, but there were no significant updates afterward. The notebook stopped at “World Code-13,” without even a mention of “World Code-4,” let alone the last three.
“What a pity.”
Colin initially guessed that this notebook was probably given as a gift to someone here by the other party.
Beside him, a palm propping up a cheek, ice-blue eyes quietly watched Colin until he flipped through the pages and closed the notebook, then Shana finally asked with a hint of curiosity:
“Can you tell me, what stories are in there?”
Upon hearing this, Colin didn’t hold back and shared what he knew with her.
This notebook, in a sense, was indeed like an adventure log as the name implied, except within this adventure log, there were many hidden things, a bit like in a diary.
More than the secrets, what interested Shana more were the scenes of different worlds described within.
“Mr. Colin, does your world really have a sun?” Shana asked curiously.
In the various legends of “World Code-13,” the sun was something that hung in the sky, selflessly bestowing warmth and heat…
And it seemed to have actually existed.
But now, hardly anyone knows what it really looks like anymore.
“There is one, but it’s not that magical a thing…”
Having seen it from childhood, Colin found it hard to yearn to see the sun.
It’s just a star after all, you see them everywhere you look…
But… this thought seemed a bit too insensitive?
To know that here, some extreme entities, like “Human Patchwork Monster,” have a pathological adoration for the “sun.”
If given the chance to escape to Earth, Colin estimated it would give anything.
“How nice that would be.”
Shana sighed softly, a glint of hope flashing in her eyes.
After explaining more about the contents of the “adventure log” and teaching Shana some of the written words, Colin handed the notebook back to her.
“Oh, and this thing for you, the coordinates before ‘Hunger.’
Shana seemed to be thinking of something, extended her hand, and light gathered in her palm, coalescing into a sphere of light with mysterious patterns flowing within it, which seemed to store a lot of information.
However, just as Colin was about to reach out and take it, he saw the mission completion regarding “Hunger’s” positioning on his retina display.
Then he was asked if he wished to submit it…
“Yes.”
Making his choice, Colin then saw an invisible vortex appear, sweeping away the sphere of light.
Then a new mission followed in his mind.
[Proceed to the designated area of the “Black Mountains,” light a temporary bonfire, and release coordinates…]
Note: This mission will start the next time you enter “World Code-13,” and the duration will be seven days.
…
“Ten or so days, is ‘Lady Rabbit’ getting ready to take action against another ‘Hunger’?”
Colin pondered thoughtfully, faintly sensing that the mission pointed towards a not-so-near address.
He asked Shana about the “Black Mountains.”
Learning that the place was not too far, theoretically, it could be a few thousand kilometers away…
After some thought, Colin figured this mission could be outsourced to “Life Mentor Adorable” and others, allowing them to reach the vicinity through the “King of Madness.”
“Anyway, it’s just a mission to anchor coordinates and plant a flag, there shouldn’t be any big problems.”
Colin took another look at the mission details, recalling how employees had complained that despite his impressive D Level status, why was it that since coming here, he had been relegated to farming and dealing with people’s excretory issues every day?
Now, he decided to give his subordinates something more challenging to do…
After all, most of them had chances of revival.
It was after this discussion ended that Shana suddenly spoke up, “Mr. Colin, could you watch over my body here for me?”
“Watch over your body?” Colin was taken aback, wondering how he was supposed to do that.
“Yes, I would like to sleep for a bit, and it might be quite a deep sleep…” Shana said, a bit embarrassed.
“Sleep? And here I was thinking it was something serious. Go ahead and sleep, I’ll keep watch.”
Colin waved his hand, indicating it was no big deal, and found her a small room in the church where Little Red usually slept.
Logically speaking, a Saintess at her level could count as resting as long as she wasn’t fighting.
Since she was going to sleep, it probably wasn’t ordinary sleep.
“Thank you…”
Shana showed her gratitude.
Then, she closed the wooden door, and a gentle glow appeared around her, sealing the room and starting some personal protection measures, ensuring that if an accident occurred, she could instantly detonate her overlaid clones and force herself to wake up…
Shana entered “sleep.”
Her consciousness kept sinking, and before long, the pitch-black dreamscape was filled with clouds emitting a soft white light.
Traversing through these clouds, Shana “saw” a circular archway.
It was just before reaching the archway that a slightly melancholic song and melody reached her ears.
In the past, she couldn’t understand it, but now she was beginning to grasp its meaning…
“There’s a voice coming from the most beautiful faraway place, bearing dew at dawn. The brilliant prospects are captivating, and I’m overjoyed and jubilant, just like in my childhood…”
Humming the tune, Shana strolled along the clouds, continuing forward.
Time passed by…
In the clouds, she followed the guidance and passed through many doors, eventually reaching an area filled with numerous large and small white orbs.
These orbs were covered with mysterious and ornate patterns, surrounded by fairy-like points of light.
Shana looked intently and information related to them surfaced in her mind.
Within the legacy of the Saints, they were referred to as “Angel’s Horns,” each orb representing a “Horn.”
“When the ‘Heaven’s Melody’ plays, white light shall fall upon the earth, enveloping all things, the stars will tremble for it, the earth will quake, all voices will be silenced, everything will return to its most essential state, all will fade away…”
These words, almost prophetic, flashed through Shana’s mind.
This was the description of what would happen when the “Angel’s Horns” were played—
Why did the Gods hold them in such esteem?
Because of this thing.
Each generation of Saints had the power to wield it, their ultimate trump card.
And the cost of using it once was not small; so far, there hadn’t been many accounts of someone surviving the ordeal.
Everyone who used it disappeared without a trace afterward, along with the enemy, shrouded in mystery…
Moreover, its power wasn’t as exaggerated as stated, activating it once wouldn’t resolve all enemies; otherwise, there wouldn’t have been a need for the sacrifice of three generations of Saints to finally defeat that “Great Will” cultivated by the “Holy Light Court.”
In thought, Shana noticed that the orb she could use this time seemed to have grown larger.
She walked step by step until she stopped in front of a ten-meter-tall large orb.
At the base of this orb, filled with various mystical patterns, she saw a string of numbers and characters…
“1000000000t.tnt”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 609 - 609 462 Analyzing the Hidden Knowledge Behind
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 609: Chapter 462: Analyzing the Hidden Knowledge Behind the “Saint”._1 Chapter 609: Chapter 462: Analyzing the Hidden Knowledge Behind the “Saint”._1 “1000000000t.tnt…”
“‘Radiant Angel’ Sixth ‘Power Angel’ Construction Corps, Fourteenth Brigade, Production Number…”
“Warning, this item can have a significant impact on the surface topography. Please submit an application for approval before use…”
“Unauthorized deployment will result in the user being sent to the ‘Light Domain Tribunal’ for a ‘Seed of Light’ trial…”
Shana, using the knowledge she had just learned from Colin, deciphered a few lines of small text and suddenly discovered something—
This doesn’t seem to be meant for use as a weapon?
“The Saints’ inherited memories, could they be inaccurate? Could this actually not be the ‘Angel’s Horn’?”
If the knowledge Mr. Colin imparted to her was correct.
Then…this explanation doesn’t seem relevant to the “Angel’s Horn” at all…
Upon further understanding, it appears to be an ordinary item that is not particularly special?
But she gave it some thought.
Although misunderstood, it could still be used as a weapon. Although she didn’t grasp the specifics, she knew the larger the number, the greater the potential power, vaguely foreseeing the kind of impact it could cause.
The destruction it caused, it would definitely qualify as a weapon.
However, its use came with many restrictions; it could only be used under certain conditions.
It wasn’t something you could just throw anytime…
And its effects would not be particularly satisfying.
Like this trap operation, Shana hadn’t even considered using it.
Compared to the “Angel’s Horn”, the “Angel of Wisdom” was more suitable and targeted when facing higher life forms…
As thoughts flickered, Shana lifted her chin, her gaze sweeping past several light orbs of varying sizes, dozens or even hundreds of meters in diameter.
Unfortunately, she didn’t have clearance to activate those light orbs; she couldn’t see how many “0s” there were.
And thus couldn’t discern their power…
Afterward, she redirected her gaze toward the ten-digit light orb in front of her, a trace of confusion in her eyes.
“Based on perception, this thing has a wide range of destruction and sufficient strength, but it’s unlikely to have much effect on an Ancient God…”
Shana doubted.
This thing didn’t seem to possess any extraordinary power, so against most higher life forms, to say it could kill them was tough, let alone inflict a wound…
Because those high-dimensional life forms in possession of various “Authorities” have too many ways to avoid injury from such non-targeted area attacks.
For example, the “King of Madness”, although Shana was encountering it for the first time, she had some initial understanding of his Authority. She could infer that this entity, when facing such bombings, could directly become a part of the explosive shockwaves…
Thus achieving an “unharmed” effect.
And if the opponent was determined, they could even spread the impact to the entire world, causing global collapse.
Furthermore, if Saints enter a “Mythical Life Form” state and prepare themselves before deploying it,
There doesn’t seem to be a risk of death, given that in that state they are immune to a great deal of physical impact…
Then… why would there be a “mutual destruction” scenario?
This conflicts greatly with the inherited memories which assume it can only be used once.
Logically, it likely isn’t restricted to a single use.
But soon, she seemed to realize something, shifting her gaze to the last section of the large light orb’s text:
“Unauthorized deployment will result in being sent to the ‘Light Domain Tribunal’ to face a ‘Seed of Light’ trial…”
An intuition told her that perhaps what truly takes effect is this sentence.
Not the inherent power of the large light orb.
“‘Light Domain Tribunal’…”
A name she had never known before…
However, Shana noticed something; the inherited memories depicted the Saints using this weapon as perishing together in mutual destruction, but upon closer thought, it seemed more akin to a mysterious disappearance, whereabouts unknown.
Especially since using this thing, there wouldn’t be any Holy Relics left behind, no Explode Equipment.
This was quite abnormal…
But, what if they hadn’t died but were transferred to whatever this “Light Domain Tribunal” was?
Then indeed there wouldn’t be any Holy Relics left behind.
“So looking at it this way, perhaps they might still be alive?”
Shana thought for a moment and felt she had unraveled another mystery, yet, at the same time, had encountered a new one.
But what is the “Light Domain Tribunal”?
In the past, the illiterate Saints misinterpreted this term as going to “Heaven”, returning to bask in the embrace of “Light”, with the word tribunal being read as passing judgment on the enemy…
This time, she has retrieved more of the “true scriptures” from Colin, understanding more knowledge, and combining context, it seems that even if Heaven exists and the Saints are taken there, it’s probably not for pleasure.
After all, according to the above, the Saints are the violators, so no matter how you look at it, they shouldn’t all be going to enjoy any kind of blessing.
The judgment is likely to pass on both parties, leading to a “mutual destruction” effect…
Nevertheless, Shana didn’t dwell too much on it.
She hadn’t come here to look at these light orbs.
After some fruitless contemplation, she turned her gaze towards the clouds further back, took a step forward, and continued onward, venturing deeper into the world of glowing clouds.
After a walk that felt “endless”, Shana saw a broken bridge.
The wide bridge was made with dazzling nine-color lights, and there was no road beyond the broken edge.
Beyond the endless white-glowing clouds obscured everything…
Shana paused for a moment to look, then continued on, her polished ankles stepping on the clouds, moving towards the broken bridge, eventually arriving at the fracture point of the bridge.

chapters.title: Chapter 610 - 610 462 Analyzing the Hidden Knowledge Behind
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 610: Chapter 462: Analyzing the Hidden Knowledge Behind the “Saint”._2 Chapter 610: Chapter 462: Analyzing the Hidden Knowledge Behind the “Saint”._2 Then, she closed her eyes, and her body began to flicker with pure white brilliance.
Before long, she had transformed her life form.
She became a conscious cluster of white light, the light taking on a vague humanoid shape, but much taller.
And it was imbued with a holy, pure aura throughout.
It was in this form that one pair, two pairs, three pairs, up to five pairs of wide, white Wings of Light, slowly unfolded behind the human figure.
Next, some luminous limbs extended from the sphere of light.
The limbs tugged at the air, and, after a moment, pulled out a piece of parchment.
Upon appearing, the yellowed parchment emitted a multitude of pale blue lights, which wove into mysterious symbols that spread deep into the cloud layer, endlessly parting the clouds like the sea of some mythological story…
In the distant expanse, a massive gate built upon the clouds, reaching all the way to heaven and earth, appeared.
The gate, constructed from pure white light, was so remote that its actual height was impossible to discern.
And in front of the gate, standing at least a thousand meters tall, was a giant humanoid figure made of light.
However, Shana knew that this was probably not its final size…
For once one stared at it, they would find that it rapidly grew in the viewer’s eyes.
This growth seemed limitless, potentially surpassing celestial bodies…
In the end, anyone trying to gauge its size would come to one conclusion—it was nearly infinite.
And if one recklessly kept staring, it could even burst their brain—Shana, initially filled with curiosity, had “died” one of her avatars this way when she first came here.
At this moment, this colossal humanoid figure of light, like a gatekeeper, stood with its back to the gate, holding a Lightsaber with its point facing down and bowing slightly, unknowing of how many years it had stood like this…
However, as Shana’s gaze landed upon it, the giant humanoid figure of light suddenly moved.
Its posture unchanged, the figure slowly lifted the Lightsaber, pointing it towards the onlooker…
When the sword’s tip was directed at the other party.
Thousands of pale streams of light sliced through the world, rushing towards Shana, enveloping her and making her appear as if encased in a cocoon of light.
These streams penetrated her body, baptizing her.
How much time had passed…
The sixth pair of wings grew slowly out from behind Shana.
‘The sixth pair of wings…’
This meant she had surpassed most of the Saints following the “Holy Light Court” and could now stand shoulder to shoulder with the best among them.
However.
Though her strength had increased, this additional pair of wings…
Didn’t have much actual utility; at most, it looked a bit nicer, or rather, it was like a pass, a display of one’s status to gain access in this world of light and clouds.
In essence, it was like a knight’s badge, more a symbol than of practical significance.
Paying no great attention to the wings, Shana’s thoughts turned.
Ahead, a myriad of brilliance intertwined, forming a tree-like diagram, and on the edges of the diagram were pale points of light…
Shana focused on this diagram for a while, flapped her wings, and some light points flew onto the branches of the tree-like diagram she was focusing on, causing new branches to light up and extend.
With the extension of new “branches,” she understood some new abilities and received specialized enhancements.
After all this, the cocoon of light surrounding her dissipated.
Shana was momentarily bewildered; when she came back to her senses and looked forward again, she found that the giant figure of light had returned to its previous stance, back to how it was, as if it had never moved.
“Those things…”
Now strengthened, Shana suddenly noticed, beneath the white cloud layer in front of the figure of light, there were a great many broken objects, resembling remains. They looked like the remains of some substantial entities…
Some of these remains were like bones, some metallic, others were strange constructions, and even remnants of unusual celestial bodies…
She didn’t know what these remnants once were, but she could sense that they were by no means weak.
Many could be compared to Ancient Gods…
But at this moment, all were quietly interred within the sea-like layer of white clouds, filling onlookers with an indescribable sense of awe.
However, the most notable among them was a grand, ancient, yet dilapidated complex of ancient hall structures…
“Is that the ‘Holy Light Cathedral’? So after it disappeared, it ended up here? It’s also unclear what happened here to leave behind so many things.”
A glint of curiosity flashed in Shana’s eyes, but she shook her head, not dwelling on it further.
Yet, just as she was about to withdraw her gaze, she felt a sudden intuition, turned her eyes beneath the doorway behind the figure of light, and saw a small cluster of flames burning away…
Under the light of the huge door and the giant of light and shadow, this flame seemed as inconspicuous as dust.
It was only after her promotion and once her strength had reached a certain level that she barely noticed it.
“‘Bonfire’?”
Shana felt a power similar to that of Mr. Colin emanating from this flame, yet compared to him, this small flame seemed even more “intense”…
But…
How could there be a “Bonfire” here?
Shana instinctively focused her gaze and discovered that the burning object appeared to be a severed hand?
What was happening?
It was during her moment of confusion while “blinking” that she suddenly saw the severed hand under the door appear before her, floating in mid-air.
She immediately became alert, but fortunately, the hand made no further moves.
It just floated quietly…
It looked somewhat shriveled, like dried cured meat, and there was a tightly closed mouth at the palm of the severed hand.
“Crack, crunch…”
Chewing and swallowing sounds arose beside her ear.
The mouth in the palm seemed to be moving, but upon closer inspection, it appeared to be an illusion.
“Not detecting any aggressiveness, does it want me to take it away from here?”
After pondering for a while, Shana glanced at the guardian in front of the distant door, then withdrew her gaze and looked at the severed hand before her.
After considering, many writhing lines of light flew out from her sphere of light…
Halfway through their flight, they turned into chains with a strong sealing effect, wrapping around the hand in coils.
In the end, Shana dragged it into her private spatial domain.
After completing all this, a silent vibration suddenly echoed within this “dream world”…
The divided sea of clouds boiled and closed together.
Burying the giant light door, the towering giant of light and shadow, as well as the Holy Light Court and a large amount of rubble once again.
In front of her, the light blue light radiating from the parchment also faded and disappeared.
Shana took it into her private space, knowing the task she had entered to do was now concluded.
The enormous light sphere flapped its six pairs of wings on her back…
She flew back along the path she had taken, bit by bit.
Inside this light cloud world, the actual passage of time was completely different from her own perception.
After an unknown amount of time, Shana finally returned to the first archway she had entered; after passing through it, she felt the connection with her body once again, and then with a shift of thought, she returned to reality.
When she opened her eyes, the room was still the same, although she did not know how much time had passed.
Shana shook her head to dispel the sense of haziness.
She withdrew the clone set upon her body, got out of bed, and pushed open the door.
Drifts of strange meaty aroma entered her nostrils…
Not far away, that “Bonfire” Divine Envoy was grilling meat with a little girl in front of a “Bonfire.”
In a regular church, using the Holy Fire to grill meat…
It was no longer a question of blasphemy; one might not even need a trial before being condemned to burn at the stake—
Oh, but if the one grilling is a Divine Envoy, then it’s alright.
“Hey, you’re awake?”
Seeing her, Colin gestured and said, “We’re just having some midnight snacks, come on over.”
“Oh… oh…” Shana muttered in a daze, instinctively agreeing as she walked over, but only halfway there did she suddenly notice something was off…
She realized, aside from Colin, there was not a single person from the “Bonfire” Church left on the territory.
Shana sensed something and frowned:
“How long have I slept?”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 611 - 611 463 The Immoral Firebearer and Branch
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 611: Chapter 463 The Immoral “Firebearer” and “Branch Office”._1 Chapter 611: Chapter 463 The Immoral “Firebearer” and “Branch Office”._1 “Five days or so, almost six days…”
Colin said casually as he picked up a large skewer of freshly grilled meat and handed it to Shana.
The meat was a recent gift from other churches, and although he didn’t know exactly what kind of meat it was, it seemed to be fine to eat—it was quite fragrant, at least judging from the employees who ate it first without incident…
Little Red was sitting on a bench nearby, blinking and feeling a bit wronged. She had grilled the meat for her big brother.
And it had been given away just like that.
“Thank you…” Shana accepted with her right hand, took the back of her robe with her left, and sat down on an empty chair.
“Then, the church members…” she began, but she wasn’t quite sure.
“They went back earlier today, but I was a little worried because you hadn’t woken up, so I didn’t follow them back,” Colin explained nonchalantly.
Currently, once “The Descent Project” exceeded seven days, one could choose to stay or return. If one chose to return, one would re-enter after seven days, just like before.
But if one chose not to go back, there would be a risk period of one day.
During that day, Colin wouldn’t be able to sense anything from the main company on Earth, feeling a sort of discomfort as if he had been left behind here.
Fortunately, once this one day passed and the countdown restarted, everything would be reconnected, and the employees would arrive again…
By the time Colin went back to Earth next time, seven days would have passed there.
Moreover, this forced-stay approach could only be enacted twice. On the third time, if one continued to stay, it was likely that one wouldn’t be able to go back at all, and the corresponding authority seemed to disappear directly.
It would be very difficult to restart the process…
‘I’m afraid by that time, I would have to wait for Earth to become a part of “The Descent Project” to return, just like with Shana before,’ Colin muttered to himself.
“So…” Shana opened her mouth but ended up only saying thank you. She knew that Colin staying meant taking risks.
After all, in a sense, she was also a frequent guest of many unusual, one-off “Descent Projects.”
With this in mind, Shana felt a bit guilty and wanted to offer compensation, but upon reflection, she seemed to have nothing of value to give.
Not only could she not offer any compensation, but she also owed more and more…
He had helped refugees, alleviated her worries about safety, given a large number of points, made saving people possible again, kept her company in chats, and even served as a punching bag, err, for training purposes.
While it might be called mutual benefit, she felt she had received much more help.
And then, of course, there was the fact that he had come to her rescue from thousands of miles away when she fell into a trap…
This…
Shana could offer only points and some blessing methods, the former of which he didn’t need and the latter, well, they weren’t really impressive…
Beyond that, Mr. Colin was only interested in Holy Relics.
However, essentially, these relics were the remains of sages. Taking them as gifts for outsiders and making decisions against ancestors’ wishes…
Shana thought that the past Saints might actually come back to life and strike her down.
‘Ugh, my head is still a bit muddled…’
Shana shook her head gently. She was still adapting to her body after leveling up, causing her thoughts to be somewhat scattered.
At that moment, Colin’s voice interrupted her: “Do you have any places you need to go to next?”
As far as he knew, this Saint was constantly fighting fires or climbing mountains of blades, never stopping for a moment. He wondered if she had to leave soon…
“Not for now,” Shana shook her head.
All known disasters were already under control, and she had no place she needed to go to at the moment.
As for returning to the Royal City…
Even though she had saved many people, those same people, even if they threw a celebration banquet for her, wouldn’t want to see her.
Of course, in the past, she definitely would have attended the banquet to receive money and resources to settle the refugees. The dignitaries would have to give her face, no matter how much they didn’t want to deal with her.
But the past is the past, and now is now…
Now that Colin had dealt with these matters, she didn’t need to go anymore.
‘That’s good to hear…’
As Colin pulled a skewer of meat from the fire, chewing on it and reveling in the burst of fatty juices in his mouth, he said:
“There’s plenty of space here. If you don’t mind, you can stay for a while to recuperate…”
If he could entice the Saintess to stay, security would be guaranteed!
This place was particularly turbulent right now, and Colin didn’t want to come back one day to find his domain empty.
This place had significant value. First, it provided a steady stream of points for employees to improve their strength. Second, the output of the “Colorless Crystals” from the Bonfire was an especially important combat resource…
When running out of stamina, just using one could revive one’s vitality.
Plus, it had strategic value. If something did happen in the future, this would be one of the escapes.
So Colin was quite concerned about this place.
Of course, “World Code-4” was important, too, but it seemed “Lady Rabbit” had other plans there.
“Oh, okay.” Shana didn’t refuse.
In her somewhat distracted mind, she was still pondering whether past Saints would be angry enough to come back to life.
However, it was precisely at that moment… Relics?
Shana remembered something, suddenly gathering all her scattered thoughts, and mentioned an item.
“Right, there’s something I may need to show you.”
As she spoke, circles of light began to spread from her ice-blue eyes as she summoned a gate of light, and from behind it, she brought out an object wrapped in white light.
“Sniff sniff…”
Colin’s nose twitched subconsciously—it smelled great.

chapters.title: Chapter 612 - 612 463 The Morally Depraved Firebearer and
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 612: Chapter 463 The Morally Depraved “Firebearer” and the “Branch Office”._2 Chapter 612: Chapter 463 The Morally Depraved “Firebearer” and the “Branch Office”._2 The fragrance reached his taste buds, involuntarily prompting saliva to form… Ingredients? No, ordinary things don’t have such a tantalizing smell, and this scent is somewhat familiar, someone I know?
He faintly had some guesses, but wasn’t very sure.
Not until the covering light slowly dissipated did Colin’s gaze suddenly become complex.
What was revealed beneath the white light was unmistakably a familiar severed hand.
Although it was much more shriveled than the one he had seen before, its style was exactly the same, even the same hand…
Looking at the mouth in the center of the palm.
Colin could guess where it came from without even thinking.
“There wouldn’t be an ‘Extermination Order’ button here again, would there?”
With mixed feelings, Colin held the severed hand and realized he couldn’t sense anything.
Other than that it was very fragrant.
However, that changed as Shana began to undo all the seals on the severed hand.
As the Chains of Light were undone.
“Whoosh…”
A rich bonfire blazed upon the severed hand.
Colin suddenly felt that some things penetrated deep into his mind.
It was a sequence of images, where an immense and majestic figure made of light loomed to the skies, its movements of the ludicrously serious lightsaber cut down, but then, eighteen dark blue arms stretched out, holding it firmly in place…
At that moment, a grain of light, like a rice grain, flashed by, hitting the colossus’s head forged of light.
Immediately afterward, the colossus of light crumbled, scattering into pieces.
A man stepped out, his body draped in a tattered brown coat stained with a lot of fresh blood, his right hand holding a revolver still smoking from the barrel.
The eighteen dark blue arms, seemingly capable of engulfing the heavens and earth, also retracted back into his body.
He advanced step by step towards a closed door behind the giant, and when he arrived at the door, he lifted his foot unexpectedly.
“Boom!”
An unimaginably large door was kicked open a crack.
The man stood in the doorway, looking for quite a while before raising his left hand, grabbing his left wrist with his right, and yanked hard.
The left hand detached on cue, left lying before the door.
“I will go ‘Beyond the Known’, uncertain if I can return, but for our future, I will do my utmost to accomplish the mission and bring back this important asset that can deal with the ultimate crisis.”
Silent words flashed across Colin’s mind, and in the next image, the man entered through the door with the few people remaining.
The images ended there.
“Heading ‘Beyond the Known’…”
Colin was curious as to what the man saw on the other side of the door after looking for so long.
It’s just a pity that the “CG” didn’t show it.
At the same time, apart from those memories, he felt that there seemed to be a mass of “information” inside the severed hand that he couldn’t decipher.
It could be that his permissions are lacking or that it is meant to be brought back to the company.
But judging from the images above, this should be the last phase of Rosen’s mission.
“Recovering the ‘ultimate’ legacy, are they talking about 2044? What exactly will we be facing?”
Colin thought for a while but couldn’t come up with an answer.
Now what is known is that many things seem to be preparing for that one moment…
But as for what exactly will happen, even “King of Madness,” a higher being, is unaware.
“However, speaking of which, these images, this opening CG scene vibe, it has a first-person perspective and a third-person perspective, and all sorts of cool shots; it feels like it was deliberately retained…”
If it was anyone else, Colin would probably think who would be so bored as to do these things.
But, for a “Flame Bearer,” who is exuberant, loves to call out his moves, and pursues “ceremony,” it’s not incomprehensible for such a thing to happen.
Afterwards, having said a word to Shana, Colin stored the severed hand in the “Storage Room.”
Unless something unexpected happens, this hand will likely be reclaimed by the company on his next return, by which time he may be able to understand the information within…
Of course, it’s not a big issue even if it isn’t reclaimed.
During fights, having the hand on him also acts as a power-up item.
While holding it, Colin could feel that some of the “Flame Bearer” characteristics within him became more active.
Manipulating them became noticeably easier…
“By the way, in the experiences before, I also saw some things…” Shana seemed to recall something and shared the information she had got from the great sphere.
