The “Yukionna,” who Colin had carelessly summoned, blew a cold mist onto his face, and then let out a “hehehe,” a somewhat hollow, chilling laugh as she floated away like a wraith…
“I’m really envious of you, going everywhere like a carefree, happy-go-lucky soul without the need to ‘adjust to the time difference.’
Colin shook his head, feeling much more recovered.
HIs surroundings no longer held that feeling of both unfamiliarity and familiarity that made him uncomfortable.
After taking a deep breath, he first reached for the parchment.
When he spread it out, the words “Mission Completed” appeared.
[In this event, your evaluation grade is: A.]
[You have completed this event with an exceptionally outstanding performance.]
[The following is the settlement you have received after this event mission—”81,000 points,” “Special Grade Talent Draw Ticket*1,” “Special Grease Ticket*1,” “Gold Mission Voucher*9″…]
[All items have been transferred to the “Storage Room,” please check.]
…
“Eighty thousand points, the Company really did make a huge profit this time,” Colin remarked, seeing the rewards not with joy for himself but realizing that the “Bonfire Company” must have made a significant gain as well.
Otherwise, given the company’s policy, aside from the fixed base points, it’s nearly impossible to get them to give out anything extra.
It’s only when they’ve had their fill of meat and soup that the employees get to wash the bowl and chew on the bones.
“As for the points, bringing ‘Time Stop’ up to nine seconds shouldn’t be a problem, and for Shana, it seems splitting the points in half might not be enough for her upgrade. If not split in half, it should be around twenty-five thousand points, right?”
“I wonder if she’ll think that’s too little…”
Colin, holding the parchment in one hand and stroking his chin with the other, thought he’d see how many points were left over at the time.
The pile of points he’d just acquired was planned out in an instant.
Then his gaze shifted back to the mission vouchers. There were neither too many nor too few of them, but they should be enough to exchange for a good number of points on the Gene Compensation Panel…
“What the hell is a ‘Special Grease Ticket’?”
Colin examined the item description in his hands: With this ticket, you can collect ten liters of “Flame Bearer’s Grease” every week…
This… he scanned the “Storage Room.”
As expected, the severed hand was handed over.
Along with the hand, the letter with the coordinates for “Containment Divine Kingdom” was also submitted.
“Feels like I got the short end of the stick with this trade…”
Colin scratched his head; the grease he used to get weekly was just about enough, and now there was an extra ten liters.
It wasn’t unwelcome, just that the cost-effectiveness didn’t seem quite right.
Afterward, he took another look at the “Special Grade Talent Draw Ticket.” It said that he could get a talent of at least purple description.
“This is actually quite good…”
Colin had given up on the idea of synthesizing his own talent.
The Talent fusion with the company was either problematic or for some reason always ended up being a huge trap.
“Hope I get a decent purple… Eh?”
As he was talking, Colin casually used the ticket and noticed an orange font emerge.
[“Mad Flame·Wildfire Affliction”]
“Effect Description”: When stabilizing one’s mentality with “Flame Bearing,” one can summon “Wildfire” to enhance oneself, manifesting a huge and ferocious flaming avatar whose strength depends on the user’s current condition…
Current Status: The maximal theoretical height of the flame entity is approximately 324.5 meters with a width of around 76.9 meters, and it can last for about 6 hours (this information is for reference only, please take the actual situation as the standard).
“Effect Activation Prerequisite”: Enter “Flame Bearer” state.
“Negative Effect”: Within a day’s time, continuous use of around three hours will progressively lead to an extreme state; the maximum controllable time is about 6 hours, please exercise control…
“Remark”: Blessed with the supreme Wildfire, incinerate and ignite all life…
“Remark 2”: This is a bit too extreme.
…

chapters.title: Chapter 626 - 626 469 The Special Module of the Subsidiary
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 626: Chapter 469 “The ‘Special Module’ of the Subsidiary.” _1 Chapter 626: Chapter 469 “The ‘Special Module’ of the Subsidiary.” _1 “Ah, this… this, isn’t this…”
Colin blinked, if he wasn’t mistaken, the effect of this ability and everything…
Why does it look so familiar?
Wait, isn’t this “Descent of the Fire God”?
Previously, when saving Shana, it was difficult to control, so Colin tossed it to cover their retreat. Later, when Shana summoned the Angel of Wisdom, he didn’t know if it was sealed or it had run away.
Anyway, Colin hadn’t seen it appear again.
Unexpectedly, it had been quietly captured by the company and transformed into an artifact…
“But, the question is… why was the artifact made so quickly this time?”
Colin looked at the glass orb-like “Talent” in his hand, clearly feeling that the flame inside was familiar.
It was filled with that sense of frenzy…
He was probably right, it’s just that he didn’t know why the artifact was created so quickly this time.
“Forget it, no matter how it happened, an orange Talent, I’ll see how strong it is before deciding…”
His current Talents were one purple and one green, the purple one being “Potential Burst,” while he spent a point to dismantle the green Talent and throw it into the “Storage Room.” He then tried to affix “Mad Flame·Mad Flame Possession.”
[Once this “Talent” is installed, it will bind to the host and be difficult to remove, posing certain risks.]
[Please confirm your choice once more.]
“Do I really need to confirm it again? Is it that formal?”
Colin was surprised for a moment, but he wasn’t overly concerned.
After all, the strength of this Talent wasn’t low…
The stronger he became, the stronger it became as well, so there was no need to worry too much about being left behind by the times.
Whether orange Talents are more powerful than Golden Artifacts is debatable, but their rarity is definitely not any less than that of Golden Artifacts.
Plus, it was an artifact adapted for “Flame Bearers.”
Colin chose to ignore the risk and continued with the installation.
The next second, the glass orb melted, and strands of frenzied flame burrowed into his body.
Colin clearly felt a type of flame essence, similar to that of the “Flame Bearer,” but far more volatile and chaotic, surge into his body, leaving a special kind of slow brand like blood vessels between his limbs and body.
“If the ‘Flame Bearer’s’ flame projection can stabilize and strengthen the relatively positive aspects of ‘humanity’ to some extent…”
“Then this flame, I’m afraid, might ignite humanity, scorch reason, and is extremely violent in nature…”
“But fortunately, it seems to be at a lower level, so it can be controlled by ‘Flame Bearers.'”
As many thoughts flashed through his mind, Colin closed his eyes, his thoughts whirling as flames began to burn on the surface of his body.
Then, another wave of intensely burning Wildfire coiled around his hand.
Meanwhile, during this process, his pupils dilated to two-thirds their size, and within this dilation, a swirl of red flames spun, and around it, some small vortexes also slowly rotated…
Underneath his skin, some mysterious patterns emerged along with his blood vessels.
These were the outward expressions when using this power.
At this moment, Colin felt that if he wished, these flames could rapidly expand and coalesce into an avatar similar to the former “Descent of the Fire God.”
Only, unlike that uncontrollable avatar, this one could be manipulated.
“When it comes to making various artifacts, in the hands of the company, your boss is still your boss.”
The “Descent of the Fire God,” once highly unstable and disposable after one use in official hands, was quickly re-engineered by the company and became available for use whenever desired.
Colin murmured and then squinted slightly, sensing some of the special things it contained.
Gradually…
A dream-like vision appeared in his mind.
A bundle of frenzied flames was held in the mouth of a somewhat shriveled hand with a mouth.
When he attempted to use the corresponding power…
The mouth began to absorb the flames, then, in an unknown way, transmitted them to him.
“Ah, is it that crude and simple…”
Colin’s expression was strange, but after a while, he suddenly had an inspiration, understanding why this thing had fallen into the company’s hands.
To be precise, after Colin had used it to cover their retreat on the spot, it had been swallowed by “Hunger.”
Later, “Hunger” was successfully contained and, along with it, became the spoils of the company.
Then quite naturally, it flowed into his hands.
All in all, it sort of resembled the saying, ‘When the snipe and the clam grapple, it is the fisherman who profits.’
He just didn’t know what other valuable things the company had managed to salvage from the belly of that “Hunger.”
“Phew…”
Taking a deep breath, Colin put away his “Divine Skills,” and everything returned to normal.
“With this orange Talent, in my normal state, I guess I could take on ordinary Ninth Level Personnel without a similar background, right? As for C Level, I’m not sure, I haven’t had a direct fight so I don’t know clear…”
Colin recalled the ordinary C Level Personnel he had seen on the “Starship,” coming back from history.
He didn’t know what kind of ace they held, but usually it was even odds…
Perhaps he might be even slightly stronger.
“It’s just… I feel like I’m turning into some kind of discount warrior…”
Colin thought about some of the artifacts in his hands, “Flame Bearer’s Goodwill (Eyeball),” “Flame Bearer’s Grease,” “The Sealed Right Hand,” the combination of Wildfire and the severed left hand, plus the heart and severed hand he might get later…
It all seemed a bit abstract to him.
When he first joined the company, Colin thought that human body parts’ “hot-swapping” and “plug-and-play” were specialties of the “Human Patchwork Monster,” but now he realized that his perspective had been too narrow, the one playing it smoothest was the “Flame Bearer” after all…

chapters.title: Chapter 627 - 627 469 The Special Module of the Subsidiary
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 627: Chapter 469 “The ‘Special Module’ of the Subsidiary.” _2 Chapter 627: Chapter 469 “The ‘Special Module’ of the Subsidiary.” _2 No matter the strength or the usage, there was more than a little difference between the two.
“Forget it, having combat power is enough. Who cares if it’s abstract or not, later I’ll have Big C Teacher check my results. Unfortunately, the instance’s Big C doesn’t have the ‘Flame Bearer’s’ power, and its limit has been reached. I guess I should be able to win easily this time.”
Colin inwardly sighed with regret.
Originally, he had thought that the Big C of the instance would have been able to use the “Flame Bearer” power.
But after so much time in contact, it seems that there wasn’t any; on the whole, there exists a limit unless the company is willing to modify and strengthen the instance, adding higher difficulty, patching it with the “Flame Bearer”…
It’s just that feeling around, it seems unlikely.
Colin then opened the internal company parchment to see what had happened during his absence these past few days.
“Professor Cute Cuddle”: Brothers, I just randomly participated in a mission and made 3,221 points in three hours, plus got a green item. Now “World Code-13” is continuously recruiting…
“Burial Lotus King”: 5,993 points, “Physics Holy Staff (Purple)”, seems like I made more.
“Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦”: Fake, they’re all fake. You’re trying to trick me into working in the Other World!
“Loafing Immortal”: @654321, Brother Shunzi please take me with you, I also want to go to the Other World, casually earning more than a thousand points in three hours is so tempting…
“The Unyielding”: @654321, I’m begging you, big brother, to rescue me. As long as you can get me out of here, I’ll do anything for you, even if I get a chance, I will let you have an orange item!
“Two-Faced”: Damn it! I knew I shouldn’t open the internal group on Monday afternoon, otherwise, I’m bound to see this bunch of seals showing off their rewards on time!
…
About ten minutes later, he shifted his gaze away from the message.
Overall, nothing special happened; the employees were doing what they had been doing before.
“A chance at an orange item? Forget it, I’m not so blessed. The old guy is quite energetic, from the moment I joined the company, he’s been asking for help until now, still asking for help. If he were abroad, he’d surely be crowned a ‘Rescue Immortal’.”
Colin murmured.
He didn’t know how this guy was surviving, managing to hold on in an environment that was theoretically incredibly perilous.
According to what he said, because of rolling “Misfortune” on the dice, he “accidentally” entered that instance and then desperately held on until the effect wore off and the mission was over, ultimately only managing to eke out a meager existence in a safe zone inside.
For now, Colin had his doubts about how safe this so-called “safe zone” really was…
“It seems someone asked about his current situation, but it’s always ‘I don’t know.’ He only says that he hides and dodges from some inscrutable things every day, but when it comes to specifics, he can’t provide any details. Only mentions that he’s surviving by a fluke because of some internal rule conflict…”
Colin suspected that this person might have undergone some inhuman transformation.
And that the person himself might not even be aware of it…
Of course, according to some who had teamed up with him, his strength was there.
But whether that strength could sustain him for so long was another matter.
You should know, there were attempts by D Level Personnel at rescue missions. They could only get down to about the eighth or ninth floors before it became too difficult to proceed. The situation inside was special, with various conflicting rules that had to be followed, as well as extremely powerful Heretic entities.
This guy has been holding out on the eighteenth floor, sending out distress signals every day; without some real capability, he definitely couldn’t do it.
“However, even with relevant missions, it’s better to decline if possible.”
Colin remembered “Life Mentor Adorable” once privately told him, this company’s trivia expert.
Even the “Robots” in the company would ignore “The Unyielding’s” words…
This meant that even the “Robots” despised his situation, thinking it was impossible to take him away, thereby no longer responding to him.
After slightly shaking his head, pushing that guy’s information out of his mind, Colin looked at the parchment again.
He noticed one thing; this time there didn’t seem to be many employees complaining about the missions.
And the reason for that…
Perhaps it was related to the previous “City at the Lake’s Bottom” operation.
A great number of top-tier Heretic Forces were wiped out in one fell swoop, resulting in a “vacuum” in many regions where the anomalies were suppressed, and thereby missions naturally increased.
“Ah, this…”
Colin’s expression turned slightly odd.
Had the Heretics truly failed to guard their gates?
But overall, it didn’t seem like a big problem, as this “vacuum” was filled by the starving employees.
Then, seeing there wasn’t much information, he went on to the marketplace and purchased the third bottle of “D Level Gene Compensation Medicine,” the drinkable kind.
The taste was the same as before, almost like mineral water, but with a faint sweetness upon closer taste.
“One step closer to the C Level path…”
Colin squinted his eyes as he felt it for a moment, sensing his body’s mechanisms trending towards “completeness.”
This “completeness” isn’t just about how strong the body is, how many armor-piercing rounds it can withstand, but a perfection and change in the physical mechanisms themselves…
Under this change, the adaptability of the body to extraordinary things had increased again.
“It should be digested completely in a week.”
Colin nodded and then took out his phone to take a look.
Xu Duojin’s daily routine report on the situation of “City at the Lake’s Bottom” was stable. Most heretic members had been dealt with, and our side’s losses were minimal. In addition, in the subsequent part of the battle, many promising individuals from our side began to emerge.
Next was the success report of the technology from “The Seventh Box Garden World.”
With official high priority, various mechanisms and a significant portion of technology like special medicines, surgeries, and organ modifications had already been successfully replicated.
If things go well, it’s possible that the official authorities could create a medicine that can turn an ordinary person into a super muscle hulk with just one injection.
Besides that, the unsuccessful point was with “Nano-smart Machinery.”
The progress in related areas is still virtually zero.
Although the formulas and principles are all laid out there.
But…
If you can’t understand it, you can’t understand it.
That meant, other than the Little Maid stacking supplies, researching on her own, at least for the next ten years, no one else would be able to figure out what exactly it was, unable to utilize even a bit of it.
Even this was the result after many Extraordinary Ones intervened using various methods.
“Is the technological gap really that big?”
Colin clicked his tongue and glanced again at the Little Maid cooking in the kitchen.
Such an amazing thing, being used for chores all day long.
Isn’t that a bit too wasteful?
Shaking his head, his thumb scrolled down, and there were photos of the list of items for trade…
“The officials are getting bolder, with higher levels, and…”
Colin “tsk”ed.
He noticed that many of the names on the list began to lean towards foreign styles.
This time, the participating forces were not limited to the internal ones.
As a result, the quantity was several times more than the total amount of previous trades combined.
It seems that the containment pressure here is quite significant…
After briefly looking through Xu Duojin’s message, Colin looked at other people’s messages, similarly nothing major, at most, they were asking when he was going to work and what arrangements he had…
Colin briefly replied and then didn’t respond extensively.
“Let’s see what this ‘module’ is for.”
He lay back on his bed, his consciousness sinking into his special office. Sitting at the end of the grand long table, Colin took out the envelope containing the “module” that he had obtained from the branch office.
With a “hiss,” he tore open the envelope.
Colin saw an intangible, massless thing float out…
It was like an “information clump” with activity.
If he wanted, it seemed he could shape it into any functional accessory he desired?
“But… what should I turn it into?”
Colin stared at the object for a while and couldn’t seem to think of what to do with it momentarily.
Intuition told him that it could be combined with some items to make maps, health bar readers, or other trinkets like combat support calibration instruments.
But, they probably wouldn’t be very accurate.
And these small functions didn’t mean much to Colin.
However, it wasn’t quite right to say the object was useless…
“Perhaps make a clone to sit here, responsible for handling some trivial matters for other employees in the future?”
Colin thought it seemed that this thing could, in fact, be combined with the Little Maid—
That way, it would probably become more intelligent and be able to wield some of his authority within his office.
.
.
.
ps: Post first, cover later—Also, I might take a day off tomorrow for some business and to sort out the outline for what’s coming next.

chapters.title: Chapter 628 - 628 470 The First 15 Events for D Level
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 628: Chapter 470 “The First 15 Events for D Level Promotion Qualification!_1 Chapter 628: Chapter 470 “The First 15 Events for D Level Promotion Qualification!_1 “Indeed, it can be combined with the Little Maid to create something akin to a ‘System’…”
Colin had a strange expression on his face, as if he could recruit people himself.
No, that’s not right, I almost forgot.
Although the office is said to be his, he doesn’t have the authority to pull in people, not even company employees at will. He has to wait for them to agree to “descend for a mission” or become his subordinates…
“However, the authority to actively recruit people may become available once I advance a little further,”
“With my status as part of the special talent program, I should have greater authority than the average person…”
“By that time, I could set things up like this…”
Colin leaned back, with his feet propped up on the desk, casually pondering.
If he set up his own “System,” it seemed quite interesting, maybe do something like “the chosen child” or whatever…
Of course, he would need to access some company permissions for that.
For one thing, he would need to be able to issue tasks using company resources, otherwise even if he recruited people, it would be meaningless.
Also, this little module probably wouldn’t be enough…
“Come to think of it, if I get everything sorted out, it feels like setting up a branch office,”
Colin muttered, looking at the “information cluster” on his desk and ultimately deciding not to touch it for the time being.
If he started now, he could only create something insignificant.
Better to use it later when he had more resources, for now, he would keep it as an ace up his sleeve.
Of course, that’s in a figurative sense, not literally keeping an ace up his sleeve.
With this thought in mind, Colin repacked it into the envelope, stored it in the “Storage Room,” and left the office.
A whiff of the scent of a meal wafted into his nose…
On the dining table, the Little Maid had already prepared four or five home-cooked dishes and was still working on a stir-fried large intestine.
Colin was in no rush to start eating.
“First, I’ll upgrade my equipment, then open the ‘Promotion Trial Preliminary Task’ to take a look…”
He pursed his lips, opening his own “Storage Room.”
After some deliberation, he chose to repair the “Time Freeze.”
With a series of ‘ding ding dong dong’ effect sounds, tens of thousands of points evaporated, but Colin obtained the result he wanted.
“Not bad, the effect range of Time Stop has expanded from 30 meters to 100 meters, and I can adjust it infinitely, meaning I can control the diameter of the range to minimize energy consumption…”
“And the duration has been extended from 7 seconds to 9 seconds, that’s certainly a super enhancement.”
“Accordingly, some of my combo moves and usage plans must also change, two seconds more is enough for me to execute an additional killer move.”
“Repair progress has reached 49%…”
“This, by estimation, would the full state last for twenty or thirty seconds, and cover a kilometer or even a greater range?”
Colin measured the Time Stop Gold Card between his fingers.
After the repair… it looked no different from before on the outside, except for some changes in the description and the color being a bit more eye-catching.
“I wonder what kind of entity made this item. Based on its current strength, could it be an Upper-Level First-Class Containment Entity?”
Colin murmured, combining it with the other two time cards.
Not to mention, how exactly did the company contain a monster capable of reversing time in an area, freezing time, speeding up time, and turn it into an item?
Or perhaps, it’s not a containment subject, but some kind of technological creation refashioned into an “Item”?
Not every “Item” seems to be a containment subject.
Colin remembered that his own Base Vehicle was a combination of some basic technologies within the company, later modified into an “Item.”
“Guess I’ll find out when I get a chance to ‘liberate’ it in the future.”
Retaining his composure, Colin hopped off the bed, pushed open the partially ajar door with bare feet, and saw the Little Maid had finished preparing all the dishes, standing motionless beside the table.
“Mr. Colin, dinner is served,” said the Little Maid expressionlessly.
“Mhmm,”
As Colin sat down, he thought about what had come before and asked her, “How’s the progress on your replication going?”
“The initial semi-finished product is nearing completion, will start subsequent templating, and preparations are underway to iterate the next generation…”
“Semi-finished product? What kind?”
Colin asked curiously. Long ago, he had the company provide a place and then during non-urgent tasks, allowed the Little Maid to split off a large part to start self-replicating.
For nearly half a month, there had been no feedback, the company had always declared, “Don’t understand, we really can’t make heads or tails of it.”
He had thought there was no progress at all.
Who would have expected that an initial semi-finished product was already made?
“Yes.”
The Little Maid nodded, then her body morphed into a roughly two-meter diameter irregular sphere floating in mid-air, “It’s roughly like this, currently, aside from floating and delayed execution of commands, it has no practical functionality…”
“Is that so?”
Colin slurped up some large intestine and asked, “What did you tell the researchers in the manufacturing plant?”
No sooner than he finished speaking, the Little Maid sent out a portion of “Nano-smart Machinery”, projecting a three-dimensional hologram of the scene.
“Holy moly, how did you make this, and it’s floating too? Where’s the energy coming from, no visible electrical components either…”
“It’s not floating via magnetic levitation, could it be anti-gravity? What energy is it using to float? And where’s it receiving signals from? It’s just a shell, but I don’t see the necessary configuration…”
“Indeed, isn’t this just a steel shell made of alloy? It was just a pile of scrap metal a moment ago, how did it start operating, magic, superpowers? But that’s not right, there’s no fluctuation in the anomaly index…”

chapters.title: Chapter 629 - 629 470 The First 15 Events for D Level
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 629: Chapter 470 “The First 15 Events for D Level Promotion Qualification!”_2 Chapter 629: Chapter 470 “The First 15 Events for D Level Promotion Qualification!”_2 “Well, indeed it’s not an extraordinary method, for I am one of the Extraordinary Ones. Whether there’s extraordinary power involved, I’ll know with just a touch.”
“Ms. Silver, may I ask how is this achieved?”
“I don’t know, I just do it when I feel like it.”
“Don’t understand, I really don’t understand…”
“Impossible, there’s no reason for this, it violates all existing knowledge. Wait, the surface is so smooth. Could we take a slice to look at under a microscope?”
“Sure.”
“…”
Watching the bewildered expressions on the faces of the on-site projection staff, Colin couldn’t help but click his tongue in awe.
Although the Little Maid said this gadget was of no real use, it still brought a small dose of “nanotechnology” shock to the personnel on-site.
Even as the Little Maid made it in front of them, observed with all sorts of instruments.
The final conclusion still was incomprehension.
In this process, the Little Maid first gathered a pile of materials, mixed them, then melted… Up to this point, everything seemed understandable.
The difficulty, in people’s eyes, was no harder than 1+1.
But the next second, the Little Maid merged herself into the still-hot metal.
And then everything became incomprehensible.
Approximately two hours passed.
The product mysteriously materialized, astonishing everyone present.
“Looking at this, in the short term, it’s indeed unlikely that the officials will make any breakthrough progress.”
One can only say, no wonder this is something that stumped a bunch of shelters in “The Seventh Box Garden World,” there are indeed many unfathomable elements to it.
Afterwards, having dealt with dinner, Colin looked at his upcoming tasks.
Apart from the next trade of props and “The Descent Project” next Monday, there didn’t seem to be anything else…
“No, it seems there’s still something to do.”
Colin sat cross-legged on the bed, perusing the parchment, and noticed that shortly after the third Gene Compensation injection, details about the “D Level Promotion Qualification Task” appeared on the parchment.
After completing this, the “D Level Promotion Qualification Trial” would begin.
“The first round of D Level promotion is a random task, the second round is the fixed Joyful Farmstead, but there’s still too little information about this farmstead…”
Colin shook his head and then hesitated slightly about whether to embark on the preparatory task for the promotion.
If he accepted it, then there would not be a moment’s rest to come…
As “the seniors” have said, the preparatory task involves quickly completing ten slightly less difficult regular tasks.
So far, there hasn’t been any fatality rate, and the risk level isn’t high.
The only difficulty lies in “speed.”
The time requirement is very tight, such that even seasoned employees might not be able to finish on time.
Of course, that’s just the case for the average employee. When it comes to himself, Colin suspected that not only would “speed” be important, but the difficulty might also rise a notch…
After all, the company has great “flexibility” in arranging individual tasks.
“Oh, the problem must come from ‘Lady Rabbit’…”
Colin recalled the descriptions of this entity in Rosen’s handwritten notes.
Then, considering the potential disasters that might arise in the future, he sighed deeply.
“It’s a life of hard work.”
As he finished speaking, Colin pressed his thumb to the parchment, initiating the preparatory task.
[Task “Fifteen Events within the Specified Time” has been issued, please open the task bar for details.]
“Ah? Fifteen? ”
Colin was startled; this didn’t quite match what “the seniors” had told him.
Weren’t they supposed to have only ten rounds?
This isn’t human.
Colin grumbled to himself and opened the task bar to check—
[“Fifteen Events within the Specified Time”]
“Description”: Starting from this moment, three consecutive tasks will be issued every week, please complete them within the specified time. If you fail, please pay Points again and return after a day.
If you fail three times in a row, this task will be postponed and restarted after fifteen days.
“Current Completion”: 0/15.
“This Week’s Task 1”:
“Description”: Please enter the target area (roughly an abandoned underground mine) before 9:30 pm as per the mission guidelines, wait for and board the “Fog Train,” and disembark at the fourth station to receive new action content…
“Remarks”: Please complete the task as soon as possible and continue to trigger subsequent events.
…
“Ah, this… People get two a week, and you schedule three for me, huh? Would it kill you to allocate two weeks of spare time…”
Colin was somewhat lost for words, only hoping that the difficulty of the mission wouldn’t be too high.
If it were like the previous missions he undertook, finishing three in a week would be virtually impossible.
Let alone three, sometimes one complex mission couldn’t be completed in a week.
However, according to the mission guidelines, he roughly sensed that the indicated location seemed quite far…
It might even be beyond the province where he resided.
“The current time is, a little past six in the evening…”
To cover the distance, he had two choices, one was to fly into the sky, masquerade as a shooting star, and hurry on his way, clearly exposing himself.
Yet, exposure wasn’t the most important thing, Colin knew that doing so…
would set off a bunch of authoritative experts to debunk saying it looked like “this and that.”
Just like when a mission would cause a sky-rending tumult and buildings to fall askew, and after an investigation, it’d be attributed to a gas canister explosion; as long as there was an intent to explain, it could be easily explained…
If it really couldn’t be explained, they’d press it down, push out some celebrity big news, take the chance to delete records, track down through connections, and wipe memories clean, dragging it out.
So exposure wasn’t the focus, the focus was that such prolonged travel would prevent him from maintaining a good condition.
And the second option was to turn to the officials when in doubt…
“I need to make a long trip later, I need some help, lend me the fastest aircraft possible.”
Colin composed a message and sent it to Xu Duojin.
After a pause, he added another message: “Parking nearby, I can operate it myself.”
Currently, all vehicles, the Little Maid could operate—
Even more so, the more advanced and precise the intelligent machinery, the smoother she handled them.
It didn’t take more than about ten seconds after sending the message for Xu Duojin to give a clear reply and inform him where to go.
Colin glanced at the leftover food on the table not far away, sent a message to Qin Chuan, Hu Zheng, and Xia Liufang to come over for dinner at his place, and then immediately set into action.
Somewhat later, on a private airfield not open to the public, after the roar of an engine, Colin boarded a fighter jet, flying straight towards the target location…
“Hiss…”
The pilot in the cockpit looked up and saw the young man sitting on the glass above his head, fastened as if welded there, unaffected by the powerful airflow blowing over him, and couldn’t help but take a sharp breath.
But ignoring the gazes of others, Colin remotely directed the fighter jet towards his intended direction.
In the meantime due to the long flight path, Colin switched to another fighter jet that met up with him mid-air.
Later, around 8:50 pm, he arrived above the target location.
Facing the howling wind and clouds, Colin spread his arms, flames ignited on his body, closed his eyes, leaned back, and executed a leap of faith…
“Boom!”
It wasn’t long before Colin fell to the earth like a meteor, kicking up a cloud of dust.
In the woods, he looked around and quickly found an abandoned mine.
Inside, it was dark and grim, with a faint unclean smell.
“Considering the ‘Fog Train’s’ characteristics, there’s probably something in this mine shaft, but it shouldn’t be too big of a problem…”
Colin stepped on the uneven stones and moved to the entrance of the mine shaft, lifted his foot, and kicked open the not-so-sturdy iron gate, then strode inside.
Inside the mine, many charms and unknown mechanical devices could be seen.
“The officials seem to have dealt with this place, but it’s likely a seal rather than a complete containment and resolution.”
Colin observed while advancing deeper as per the mission requirements.
Eventually, in an underground cavern that was spacious and much warmer than the surface, he stopped moving.
“It’s past nine, the train should be coming soon, huh?”
Colin checked the time on his phone, then suddenly narrowed his eyes, feeling an invisible terror spreading from all directions of the mine’s caverns, the atmosphere heavy and oppressive, with foul whispers echoing in his ears.
However, with a “whoosh,” flames churned and burned.
The intangible terror receded like a tide…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 630 - 630 471 The Colossal Buddha Statue in the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 630: Chapter 471 The “Colossal Buddha Statue” in the Darkness_1 Chapter 630: Chapter 471 The “Colossal Buddha Statue” in the Darkness_1 “Retreating proactively? Knowing fear indicates it has certain instincts as an anomaly.”
Colin glanced over there.
Many anomalies lack any instinct, reacting naturally, as if impelled to clash head-on even when sensing the power of “Primordial Fire”…
Clearly, this one did not belong to that brainless category.
“I came here to take the train and didn’t burn you, which was a show of respect on my part. I hope you won’t be ungrateful.”
Colin withdrew his gaze and continued to wait with his phone in hand.
He didn’t specifically check what was inside the mine, but he could generally tell there was a tomb-like structure below, with the source right in the middle. As for the threat level, it wasn’t even Third Level…
No, to be more accurate, it might be on the cusp of a Fifth or Sixth Level Containment Subject as per the company’s standards.
At Fifth Level, it might barely withstand a punch and half a kick from him.
Sixth Level… Normally, the heat waves from the flames he set off by merely passing by could directly incinerate it…
If it wasn’t for his concern that dealing with it might stop the train from coming,
Colin could have resolved this problem in less than a minute with a wave of his hand.
As he waited, twenty-some minutes passed quickly…
Unnoticed, a hazy grey mist began to envelop the surroundings, and vibrations emanated from within.
The mist grew denser…
And then, accompanied by the monotonous, pale sound of a flute.
“Clang clang clang~”
The sound of the train grinding on the rails reached him.
Colin distinctly felt a moment of trance, and by the time he came to his senses, he saw a train, marked with various traces, gradually slowing down in front of him…
As before, neither the head nor the tail could be seen.
It seemed that every time it stopped, one could only see the middle section that was about to halt.
“At my current level, I still can’t discern the specifications of this train?”
Colin was secretly astonished.
He now felt that his consciousness was becoming much faster at combating that sense of haziness.
But still, what couldn’t be seen remained out of sight.
“Click~”
The crisp sound of a door opening interrupted Colin’s thoughts.
He composed himself, stepped forward, and was about to board when he suddenly saw three people at the door of the train, with faces full of surprise and doubt looking back at him.
Colin frowned at first, but quickly through some perception confirmed they should be employees.
By their physical condition, they seemed to be roughly at E Level; he wasn’t quite sure, but… that wasn’t something to fuss over.
To avoid accidentally missing the train as it was about to leave, Colin headed into the train first. The moment he stepped in, the intangible trance faded away.
The three people preparing to disembark stared at this fiery figure with hesitation, unsure if they should pass by him.
‘All that big talk in the company chat group, acting as if they’re the center of the universe, yet in person, they become this ‘nervous’…’
Colin shook his head, displaying his white teeth, and his lips curved into a friendly smile:
“Go ahead, or the train might leave without you.”
As he spoke, he casually took out two cylindrical metal objects from his pocket and tossed them over.
An employee, not sensing any danger, caught them as if they were cigarettes being passed along. When he realized what they were, a chill ran down his spine—these were two grenades!
Thankfully, the grenades were not armed.
“Consider it a small token of assistance from an ordinary D Level senior…”
Colin smiled: “If you encounter the anomaly itself, or a particularly dangerous situation, you can just detonate these close by. If all goes well, you might either eliminate the anomaly or ensure your survival.”
These grenades weren’t of much significance to him now.
But for them, they could be quite effective. Although a regular person might not control the flames upon detonation, after all, they contained a bit of “Flame Bearer’s Grease.”
So, should they run into trouble, even a Third Level Containment Subject might have to steer clear.
“Thank you…” The three exchanged glances, expressed their thanks, and quickly disembarked—not that they didn’t want to ask “Why are you helping us?” or something like that.
But they had no time to linger, or they wouldn’t be able to leave.
The train only paused for a few minutes before resuming its journey; there was simply no time for lengthy exchanges.
As for those grenades…
Unsure if they harbored any hidden traps, they resolved to try them out in a dire situation if they had no other choice.
‘Good, with this, their chances of handling the anomaly should be maxed out. As long as they don’t mess up with the controls, they should not lose.’
Colin’s gaze left the group of people.
Regarding anomalies on Earth, he was indifferent if he didn’t see them, but once he did, he generally wouldn’t mind casually dealing with them, lest they spawn something odd and troublesome.
Of course, it was also a bit of goodwill for the employees’ growth.
Such encounters could also be considered a form of fate.
Then, Colin moved towards the interior of the carriage, keeping his flames alight as he surveyed the surroundings.
He could clearly sense that on some seats, there existed some kind of unseen “people.”
Usually, as long as one didn’t interact with them for too long, they posed no harm.
At most, they just made one’s skin crawl a little…
Now, although Colin had the power to deal with these “people,” he refrained from wasting too much time on these endless entities.
Because even if he killed them, more would just come from the front cars after a while.
Who knows if dealing with them excessively might cause other troubles.

chapters.title: Chapter 631 - 631 471 The Colossal Buddha Statue in the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 631: Chapter 471 The “Colossal Buddha Statue” in the Darkness_2 Chapter 631: Chapter 471 The “Colossal Buddha Statue” in the Darkness_2 There’s no need to make oneself uncomfortable.
After looking around, Colin found a seat without a “person” and sat down.
Because of the flame he carried, the “people” on the train wouldn’t come near him, even if they changed seats. In fact, it was likely that the “people” nearby would soon move away to other places.
Before long…
“Ding, ding, ding—”
A series of urgent bell rings followed, the train doors closed, and it slowly started to move.
Watching the fog gradually thicken outside the window.
“Getting off at the fourth station, wonder how long it will take…”
Colin withdrew his gaze, spent several hundred dollars to summon a few “Money Slaves,” then took out a candle made of “Flame Bearer’s Grease,” lit it, handed it to a “Money Slave,” and told it to carry it to the train door, drip a few drops of the melted wax on the floor, then press the candle onto it before it solidified.
After that, he ordered the “Money Slave” to come back and sit around him, adding some “human atmosphere” to the lone carriage while also readying them to take any blows for him. He then closed his eyes and began to doze off.
He aimed to be in the best condition possible.
During the journey, two hours quickly passed.
Only when he felt the train start to slow did Colin open his eyes.
The first station was about to be reached.
“Hope it’s not some bizarre place.”
Colin saw that outside the fog-covered window, some scenery began to appear.
The first station was a desolate land with dense wild grass, seeming empty at first glance…
But on closer inspection, there was still nothing.
At most, one might feel it a bit eerie.
“This place must harbour great terror.”
Colin adjusted his sitting position and glanced at the candle at the train door, noting the slight flicker of its flame.
This indicated that things here were definitely not as calm as they appeared on the surface.
But what exactly was present would likely require stepping off the train to know the details.
However, only someone with a problem in their head would think of getting off.
After a few minutes of waiting, the train sounded a series of urgent bell rings again and then resumed moving.
This time, the train didn’t travel for very long.
In less than an hour, it began to slow down and stopped in a woodland basking in daylight.
Nothing came aboard and nothing seemed to disembark…
The train, as if it were a routine procedure, stopped for a few minutes and then closed its doors.
“This time it seems much safer; although I saw some abnormal entities moving, the candle’s flame didn’t even flicker.”
After observing, Colin made a brief assessment.
The third station was a bit slower to approach, arriving after about three hours when the train began to decrease its speed again.
At that moment, Colin saw outside the train window what seemed to be dusk, entirely dark.
However, ordinary darkness could not obstruct his vision.
Clearly seen beneath the darkness was an ancient town desolate and silent, scattered with ruined buildings made of wood and stone, and a dirt city wall visible further away…
Suddenly, his heart chilled when he saw within the pitch-black, unpopulated town, there was a hill about a hundred meters tall.
Engraved in the hill was a Colossal Buddha Statue as tall as the hill itself.
The statue’s pose was one of dignified sitting, making the hill appear as its seat, and on its face was an expression of compassionate benevolence, a merciful demeanor towards the people of the world…
Except, in the tight and cold darkness, it exuded an indescribable aura of gloom and eeriness.
Especially those very expressive eyeballs.
“Is that thing staring at me?”
Colin’s expression turned serious as he felt an extremely intense sensation of being watched.
Though he wasn’t directly in front of it, there was an unmistakable feeling of being stared at…
And then, he faintly heard something like an auditory hallucination in his ear.
“No, it’s not a hallucination!”
Colin’s brows furrowed, the voice seemed to be saying…
‘…Do we… have a fate?’
And it was at that moment.
An almost imperceptible vibration appeared outside…
The Buddha Statue seated atop the hill began to vibrate, as if wanting to rise, but consequentially, innumerable chains that seemed to pull up from the ground clanked in metallic discontent as it tried to stand.
“There’s no damned fate! Get moving!”
Colin felt goosebumps all over his body.
He wasn’t afraid of ferocious monsters, but there was something indescribably eerie about this sort of thing that made his skin crawl.
“Ding Ding Ding~”
After a series of crisp bell sounds,
the train started up again…
The bleak and gloomy scene was left behind by the train.
But for some reason, Colin couldn’t breathe easy; he had a feeling, a real possibility, that he might meet that thing again and continue their “past connection.”
“Hiss, damn it, this damn train, where do you find so many abnormal areas?”
Colin pinched the bridge of his nose.
What was that thing just now?
It didn’t feel especially dangerous, just a very strange, mysterious, and inexplicable unease.
‘Under normal circumstances, the train wouldn’t leave Earth within three to five stations, which means that big Buddha statue is most likely on Earth. When I get back, I’ll see if the authorities have any related records…’
Colin planned to take the initiative to come over and smash or contain it if he had the chance.
That way, he could properly wrap up their connection.
Taking a deep breath, Colin suppressed the inexplicable trepidation in his heart, quietly waiting for the fourth station to arrive.
Once again, he didn’t have to wait long…
About another hour later, the train slowed down, preparing to stop.
The dissipating fog outside the train windows revealed an icy, snowy landscape – endless and desolate, void of people. Apart from the unusually clear stars in the night sky dome, nothing else was visible.
“What kind of godforsaken place is this?”
Colin looked around for a while, unable to guess the exact location.
Then, with a “click,”
the train doors opened.
He first let the Money Slave jump out to make sure there was no danger, and then followed it outside.
And right as his foot touched the ground, information surfaced in his mind.
[Mission requirement: Please proceed to the designated area, locate the rift under the iceberg and toss the “Special Token” into it to be considered as completing this round of tasks…]
“Note”: Complete this mission within a day.
…
‘Special Token.’
Colin opened his “Storage Room” to take a look and took out the “Special Token,” realizing it seemed to be a hand that looked freshly severed.
The related item description read:
[Through extracting the blood and flesh genes from certain creatures and cultivating a replica using a considerable amount of resources in a compliant manner, it carries a significant portion of the original’s properties.]
Ah, this…
“Some creature’s blood and flesh genes? This scent… man, they’re starting mass production now?”
Colin was somewhat speechless, wondering what the company was up to.
The requirement was to throw it into a certain area to be considered complete.
The method seemed crude. Would throwing it cause an explosion, or would it serve some sort of sealing purpose?
Shaking his head, Colin stowed the item away.
Then, sensing the direction through his mission, he transformed into a streak of flame, speeding across the snowfield.
Only three to five minutes later, Colin slowed down slightly, his nostrils flaring.
“The scent of living humans, as well as the stench of heretics, gunpowder, and other anomalies…”
All sorts of scents were present, suggesting a rather complicated situation ahead.
It felt like he was walking into a free-for-all brawl…
However, when Colin reached the first battlefield, he found that the battle seemed to have ended. There were no living people to be seen, just numerous bodies left behind.
No, more accurately, there were clothes with no flesh and blood inside, just bare skeletons.
And an abundance of various weapons…
Even including a wooden “Ghost Ship” frozen on the surface of the water, already half-broken.
“Looks like an official force, hundreds of them. But judging by the uniforms and skeletal remains, it’s not just domestic forces; it’s quite complex, including factions from different countries…”
“Even Followers of the Heretics. Tsk, seems like the officials are currently collaborating with them to fight against something else?”
“However, these scents are all less than half a month old; they can’t possibly have turned to skeletons so fast. And if there are skeletons, it means the Followers of the ‘Red Moon’ didn’t win because if they did, even the down jackets would be collected, let alone the skeletons.”
Colin’s figure paused for a moment before continuing deeper in the direction of the target.
Remnants of scents in the air told him there might still be living people in this forsaken place…
Indeed, after moving forward a bit more, he suddenly heard distant, faint sounds of explosions from the air.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 632 - 632 472 The Sleepless One in the Eternal
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 632: Chapter 472 “The Sleepless One in the Eternal Chill.”_1 Chapter 632: Chapter 472 “The Sleepless One in the Eternal Chill.”_1 In the heart of the polar region, under gloomy skies, a continuous mountain range hummed with the storm, bringing snow as sharp as knife blades…
Within an area surrounded by some watchtowers on the bleak and oppressive land.
Shadows with a bloody red glow occasionally flitted and wandered…
“Creak~”
Inside a watchtower, a man coated in blood ice crystals and wearing thick clothes pushed open the door, holding a sickle caked with blood ice in his hand, and entered the tower’s top hall.
After entering, he scanned the room and ultimately his gaze settled on a muscular Caucasian man nearby.
The man’s complexion was gloomy, and his injuries were even more severe than his own.
However, severe as they were, they were not fatal.
On seeing someone enter, the pale-skinned employee first grabbed his weapon, but upon realizing it was an ally, he sighed in relief and spoke weakly,
“Have those heretics who worship the ‘Deep Sea’ been completely dealt with, Mr. Chang?”
“There was a group trying to retreat, but I just took care of them,” the man acknowledged with a nod, his visage firm and appearing to be in his thirties.
Though these heretics, who worshipped a terrifying entity deep in a certain strait and used an unknown Ghost Ship as their stronghold, provided certain assistance during this sudden incident,
But…
An enemy’s enemy is not necessarily a friend.
Even if it’s “cooperation,” coexistence is never possible. When it was time to strike back, one must do so.
After all, most heretics are far too extreme…
These people constantly created various bloody incidents leading to deaths in the name of unfathomable reasons like “for the future,” which were by no means fewer than those caused by anomalies.
“That’s good, that’s good,” the fair-skinned strongman nodded, pressing on his abdomen and breathing laboriously.
A transparent, pitch-black ice crystal stuck in his stomach, causing intense pain.
And from it, coldness spread continuously to other parts…
If the ice crystal could be pulled out, he might be able to slowly recover, but unfortunately, the curse had penetrated deep into the marrow, and pulling it out would kill him.
“Thank you,” Mr. Chang approached and took out a charm from his pocket and stuck it on; the chill from the ice crystal diminished significantly.
If it had not been for this colleague blocking a fatal strike earlier, he himself might be the one injured.
“Right, has the situation here been transmitted? Is there any response from the higher-ups? I am no longer able to evacuate, you, you might still have a chance to leave before those things launch another attack…”
However, before he finished speaking, Mr. Chang raised his hand to interrupt:
“The message has been sent out. But, I probably can’t leave either. This incident, it would require someone of real heavyweight to intervene, not to mention the myriad of cumbersome conditions for such a person to act…
“Even if they get here, it will likely take a week or more. By the time they arrive, we are most likely already doomed.”
“Therefore, I do not intend to waste time evacuating,” Mr. Chang said calmly. As an employee stationed in a high-level abnormal area, he had long been prepared to face death.
“As a member of The Great Wall, I will be forever cast here like a cornerstone, and I will preserve as much data as possible, so that the teams that come later can more effectively resolve the anomalies here…”
He sighed, helping his comrade press on the wound.
As for now, they would live for as long as they could…
“Is that so…” The strongman said despondently, his gaze hesitant for a moment before he spoke, “There’s something I suddenly want to tell you…”
“Go ahead.”
“You know, I’ve never had that kind of thought…”
“Hmm?” Mr. Chang suddenly sensed something oddly off in the atmosphere.
“But later, when I was assigned to work at the outpost, under your command, at first, I disdained it, couldn’t comprehend such arrangements, and opposed you at every turn, yet you tolerated me…”
“And later, I realized you truly had charm. You never swore, always kept calm, and though you seemed expressionless, you often thought of us…”
“I think, now, I might not be able to take my eyes off you…”
“Of course, I must clarify first that I’m not, I just can’t describe my feelings for you…”
Mr. Chang’s pupils shrank slightly as his always calm face twitched, showing a ripple of disruption.
“You say, if there is what you call the ‘next life,’ do we have a chance to work together again…”
Mr. Chang fell silent, silently withdrawing his hand.
Looking at that somewhat pale face and the eyes reflecting a return of light, filled with immense expectation, he suddenly felt an unconstrainable itch on his scalp, his facial muscles twitched uncontrollably, hardly able to hold together.
He felt it might have been better to have died at the hands of the heretics just now…
However, fortunately, at that moment, without the need to say anything, a thunderous roar of a storm suddenly came from outside the outpost.
A terrible pressure spread in all directions…
Mr. Chang stood up abruptly, looking through the thick glass towards the outside, witnessing an overwhelming fog accompanied by rumbling noise surge forward.
Within that massive dust-storm-like fog, a figure with a giant humanoid shape, horns on its head, and a contorted face resembling a human’s appeared ghostlike, flickering in and out of sight.
Its three eyes emanated a hate-filled bloody light, casting their gaze in this direction.
In an instant, several watchtowers about a hundred meters in height were engulfed by the blizzard it brought.
Although some sealing devices were operational at the moment, containing the anomaly within, the people in the outpost could not endure such a clash.

chapters.title: Chapter 633 - 633 472 The Sleepless in the Eternal Cold
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 633: Chapter 472 “The Sleepless in the Eternal Cold Wave”_2 Chapter 633: Chapter 472 “The Sleepless in the Eternal Cold Wave”_2 “Dying like this might be for the best.”
Mr. Chang closed his eyes and waited quietly for the storm to come, for the cold to descend and turn him into an ice sculpture.
However, the expected death did not arrive.
Even the vibrations outside the window, at this moment, ceased entirely.
In front of his eyelids, there seemed to be a bright light and a pleasant warmth spreading…
“Who’s there?”
As he opened his eyes, he saw the gigantic humanoid creature in the surging cold fog suddenly burst into flames inexplicably, let out a shrill and sharp scream, and fall to the ground.
The terrifying cold fog also dissipated at this moment.
“Oh, finally, a living person.” A voice suddenly echoed in the outpost.
Mr. Chang was startled, turned around, and saw a young man who had, at some unknown time, walked into the hall, flames flickering about him.
“Are you… someone from back home?” he asked uncertainly, responding in Mandarin.
“Yeah, one of our own.”
“One of our own?” Mr. Chang became alert.
The message sent out, according to expectations, the personnel who would first come to help would never be from within the country, the distance was simply too far…
Amid his confusion, he couldn’t help but take a closer look at the other person’s appearance…
Black hair, black eyes, brown long-sleeved undershirt, big slippers…
This attire… could only be said to match some people’s imagination of a “master.”
Of course, what made Mr. Chang most cautious was that he couldn’t make out the other person’s strength; if not for the presence of the flame, the other would appear almost indistinguishable from an ordinary person in his eyes.
“Just took care of some things, passed by here and thought I’d check in, incidentally resolve the issues here as well…”
Colin waved his hand, his gaze sweeping over his clothing: “How’s the situation here, are there any other survivors? You two, can either of you accompany me on a short trip later?”
The company’s mission guidance on Earth was hit or miss, which made pinning down a precise location a bit uncertain for him.
He needed someone to lead the way…
“I can, but can you prove your identity?”
“A way to prove my identity, huh? Hiss…”
Colin stroked his chin, suddenly realizing that he seemed to lack global travel documents…
And his slightly hesitant actions also made Mr. Chang nervous and alert. He surreptitiously made a hand gesture to notify his colleagues to prepare to commit suicide at any moment through a specific method.
To prevent heretics from obtaining information from their brains through evil means…
‘Ah, why do I feel like the reaction is quite intense.’
Colin wasn’t clear about the message conveyed by their subtle gestures, but he could generally detect from the two a sense of “fish die and the net breaks”…
After thinking for a while, he said:
“Will domestic work?”
“Yes, any official institution will do,” Mr. Chang nodded.
Upon hearing this, Colin didn’t dawdle; he searched the “Storage Room” and took out the pass document, displaying it before the other…
A paper contract photocopy? Mr. Chang became wary and thought it was fake the moment he saw its content.
Because it was simply too absurd!
On a small piece of paper, there were seven or eight stamps, all from the highest-level institutions’ hubs!
His experience told him this was nearly impossible!
Not only was there a “Fate Hub Office” but also the seal of his own “Great Wall” office …
If there was only one, he wouldn’t have doubted it, but a bunch of them together seemed a bit fake.
But… the aura from each stamp assured him that the document’s authenticity was beyond question…
Especially at the bottom of the document, the signature of a man named “Xu Duojin.”
This… this Mr. Xu was an actual big shot within “Fate Propeller,” one of the future five Ninth Level Candidates!
And “Fate Propeller” was very difficult to forge as well…
Because at their level, just the subjective act of writing their names would let them sense it and slightly interfere with this place, and they might even already be watching, so…
This document looked ridiculously fake, but it was indeed real.
“Your identity is confirmed, there’s no problem…”
Upon seeing so many high-level stamps all at once, Mr. Chang involuntarily spoke with some respect, curious about who the other person was while realizing…
The young man before him might appear to be younger than him…
But in reality, he could be in his eighties or nineties, or even over a hundred years old!
“Yeah.”
Colin nodded, unaware that Mr. Chang already saw him as an elder well over a hundred years old, and put away the document in his hands.
He had two documents that could prove his identity…
Aside from that, there was an identification for a “Fifth Level Personnel.”
However, presenting that proof might lead to even greater suspicion…
Following that, Colin looked at the Sixth Level Personnel and asked some other questions, “How is the situation here?”
Mr. Chang nodded and gave a brief and rapid introduction to the place.
There are still some survivors, but they are scattered across various outposts— not too many, possibly less than a hundred people, all sent by different forces to garrison the border.
After the recent charge, there might not even be a hundred left.
As for the situation here…
What appeared just now was a high-level lifeform known as the “Sleepless in the Eternal Cold Tide.”
It was first observed over a decade ago and was subsequently forcibly sealed by a coalition of parties.
It occasionally acted up from time to time, but never as intensely as during this period…
“Sleepless, huh? I’ll let it ‘sleep’ forever soon enough…”
Colin nodded, displaying tremendous confidence—the aura felt at most like a Level 2 Containment Subject, and although it was a bit troublesome, if necessary, he could kill it…
But…
A Level 2 Containment Subject, dangerous as it is, would not warrant the company sending him directly to deal with it.
And the request seemed somewhat biased towards sealing a certain area, rather than killing a creature.
Which suggested there might be something special inside.
“There must be some more troublesome things. Have you been to the deepest part?”
“Something more troublesome?” Mr. Chang was taken aback, but then, recalling some information, realized what the other might be saying could be true.
There had always been talk that the “Sleepless” in the cold tide seemed to be guarding something.
“I have been there, and if you need, I can show you the way…”
“That will do.”
Colin nodded and then glanced over the man standing behind him.
“I can hardly hold on any longer, you guys don’t have to bother, this ice spike isn’t easy to dissolve, even for Ninth Level Personnel…”
The pale-skinned muscular man responded in English, but before finishing, he saw a Tree of Flame appear next to the man who seemed to hail from the same country as his base commander, and its extensive roots enveloped him…
In less than a minute, the deadly wound he thought was sure to kill him was mostly healed.
“Just a minor flesh wound, no near-death about it.”
Colin shook his head, recalled the Fire Tree and threw out some healing items and a “Colorless Crystal”: “If you have time, you can help others around, I won’t be going.”
After a pause, Colin turned to the Sixth Level Official Personnel beside him: “Right, you seemed to have something to tell him? I’ll give you three minutes, I’ll wait for you outside…”
With that, he walked out.
It was after he left that the atmosphere became eerie all of a sudden.
Some things, previously thought to be death sentences, were already spoken.
Now…
If they all survive, the situation becomes somewhat awkward.
“You…”
“No need to say anything, I don’t quite understand your thinking, and I can’t give you any response.”
Mr. Chang pursed his lips and then, with a calm tone, shook his head and said:
“But damn it, I probably would never go to a sauna with you again, even if I were beaten to death.”
With that, he turned and left.
…
Half an hour later, Colin, leading the Sixth Level Official Personnel, passed through the dimly lit land of ice and snow to reach the depths of this secret area and saw a great number of mechanical towers standing tall…
Each connecting into a chain, resembling some sort of isolation wall, suppressing the mysterious forces of the site.
In addition, there were numerous shattered Ghost Ships destroyed there…
To suppress the anomalies, many personnel fell here, including an Eighth Level Personnel.
Yet, on the ground, at most, one could sense scattered, white skeletons devoid of any flesh or blood.
‘It’s a pity that unless the ‘Red Moon’ descends, there’s little chance of bringing them back to life,’ Colin thought to himself, shaking his head internally, and looked ahead.
There stood a towering black mountain range, covered in snow and ice…
From above, there was an indescribable sense of madness wafting down.
Accompanied by the eerie, wailing winds…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 634 - 634 473 Mist Train Stop 9. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 634: Chapter 473 “Mist Train” Stop 9. _1 Chapter 634: Chapter 473 “Mist Train” Stop 9. _1 “Were those flesh and blood extracted by this thing?”
Colin narrowed his eyes, faintly feeling that compared to that Level 2 Containment Subject, it was this stretch of Black Mountains, extending for thousands of miles, that was the true source of an intangible pressure.
“Further into the mountain range, there’s a crevice where the actual body of ‘The Eternal Sleeper’ rests inside. However, there seems to be some danger in approaching the high mountain. Even Ninth Level Personnel wouldn’t step into it lightly…” Mr. Chang began to explain.
The extreme climate was undoubtedly dangerous for most ordinary humans, and even to lower-tier Extraordinary Ones.
But for some high-tier Extraordinary Ones, it wasn’t much of a problem.
However, it was clear that the issue here was not simply a matter of extreme climate…
No sooner had he finished speaking than he suddenly paused, seeing the other party taking out a glass bead from his pocket which glittered with firelight like an eyeball.
Then, rubbing it on the clothing over his chest, he pinched the eyeball and inserted it into his left eye socket.
Bright orange-red firelight began to spill out from his left eye incessantly…
“Indeed, it’s a bit dangerous. Need to make some preparations.”
Colin blinked his left eyelid, rotating the eyeball several times. Once accustomed, he wrapped himself and the person beside him in flames and flew towards the intended direction.
“This mountain range definitely has problems.”
As he flew over the mountain, Colin’s sensation of this grew even stronger.
And looking at his companion, it seemed that he hadn’t noticed the issues with the mountain range…
“Officials above Eighth Level would have no reason to overlook this, but he seems unaware. Hmm, is it because knowing too much could instead lead to problems?”
Colin pondered thoughtfully.
But now, as there were no significant anomalies in the mountain range, there was no need to pay too much attention.
“Hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo~”
Within the dense fog, some eerie, twisted humanoid figures floated towards them, appearing like tattered sacks, yet possessing unsettling, red-glowing third eyes…
Compared to the large one they had encountered earlier, these creatures were numerous but smaller, only two to three meters in length.
Mr. Chang intended to warn this mysterious powerhouse to be cautious, as these groups of strange beings were very peculiar and sometimes harder to deal with than the larger ones.
But before he could speak, he found that the other party didn’t even glance at them and continued forward, while those eerie things, as soon as they came within a certain distance, would combust into ash…
Those terrifying beings, which were difficult for them to handle, seemed like a joke in the eyes of the other party.
“Feels more terrifying than a Ninth Level Powerhouse. When did the officials get such a formidable presence…”
Mr. Chang was secretly shocked.
About half an hour later, guided by the other person, Colin found the large fissure in the mountain range.
The crevice extended downward, its bottom unseen.
The final clue for the mission led to this place…
“Should be right here.”
Colin reached into his pocket and pulled out the “Token”.
And it was then that Mr. Chang on the side suddenly saw a massive figure emerge like a specter in midair, its head adorned with antlers resembling dead trees with numerous strange snowflakes circling around it.
At that moment, it swung a silver scythe, seemingly about to strike down at the “Ninth Level Personnel” beside him.
He was startled and just about to warn him.
But before he could speak, he suddenly saw a foot made of fiery flames with terrifying might descending from the sky.
“Whoo-whoo-whoo…” The figure started to emit a large amount of icy mist, as if it was trying to meet the fire-formed foot head-on.
However, the next second, it was ignited out of thin air and then stamped into the abyss.
“If it were the main body, it might be slightly troublesome, but a shadowy figure almost indistinguishable from an illusion trying to trip me up, they really underestimate me…”
Colin drew back his gaze, unconcerned.
Then, stretching out his hand, he casually tossed the “Token”, the copy of the severed hand, downwards.
A fierce wind blew up from below, as if trying to sweep it away.
But the severed hand burned in midair, unaffected, and continued to fall…
Then, not too long after, in less than three minutes, Mr. Chang, standing beside Colin, was suddenly struck by the sight of the dense clouds in the sky dissipating, and the blizzard quickly weakening until it vanished within a few seconds…
The invisible oppressive feeling that had enveloped this place for many years also suddenly disappeared.
“This… what on earth was that?”
Mr. Chang was taken aback, somewhat incredulous.
If he remembered correctly, it seemed to be a hand? But he was not entirely sure…
However, faced with his confusion, Colin responded irrelevantly, “Will you be able to get back later?”
“I can…”
“Then that’s fine.”
As soon as the words fell, Mr. Chang saw Colin throw a square crystal at him. He reached out to catch it but found the crystal merging directly into his body.
A surge of energy quickly filled his entire body, driving away hunger and fatigue.
Then, before he could ask what was happening, he suddenly realized that Colin had disappeared.
…
Inside the residential area’s living room, Colin returned home through the task mechanism.
“This mission, aside from encountering some bizarre things on the road, actually seemed to be safe…”
Colin sat on the living room sofa, somewhat surprised.
This task, if given to the average D Level staff, might not be very difficult, but wouldn’t be particularly easy; however, in his hands, it was like a straightforward push, just a matter of going through the motions without any real challenge…
It was hard to believe that this was a mission dispatched by the company.
If they all were like this from now on, Colin felt he could relax and not worry about not completing them.
“It’s only the first stage, celebrating too early.”
Colin muttered to himself, picking up the parchment to look at “Event 2.”
This time…
Did the task seem more or less the same as the previous round?
“This time I don’t have to ride the ‘Fog Train,’ but the requirement is, in three hours, to head to a certain area of international waters, dive into the deep sea to find a relic, then activate a certain door of the relic, and throw in the ‘Token’…”
“‘Token’…”
“Leaving something behind again.”
Colin sat up a bit straighter, looking much more serious.
It seemed that he was executing some kind of sealing ritual in both consecutive tasks; that did not seem like a coincidence.
This conjecture was confirmed the next day.
When Colin tossed the second severed hand into a mysterious door of a relic in a deep-sea cavern and returned, the third task appeared, this time also involving “leaving something behind,” as if to perform some kind of seal…
Three times in a row…
“This time, it’s definitely not a coincidence.”
Colin felt the company seemed to be making some sort of pre-emptive deployment.
The ten stages of tasks for other D Level staff were usually slightly tougher than regular random tasks on a Sunday, with a variety of types, not three consecutive ones like now, which required “leaving something behind.”
“Never mind the company or how many hands ‘Lady Bunny’ replicated…”
“This third task of the mission seems to be ramping up the difficulty.”
Colin set the “Token” aside and picked up the parchment to look at the requirements.
[Event Three: Take the “Mist Train,” and when it stops at the ninth station, tear open this “Envelope 1,” enter the special train carriage, and place the “Token” into the fuel room of that carriage…]
“Description”: Adhere as much as possible to the rules of conduct for the fifth section of the carriage and beyond.
…

chapters.title: Chapter 635 - 635 474 Ancient Gods Attitude. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 635: Chapter 474 “Ancient Gods'” Attitude. _1 Chapter 635: Chapter 474 “Ancient Gods'” Attitude. _1 “Note 1”: Avoid any form of contact with “shadows” as much as possible.
“Note 2”: Never allow oneself to be engulfed by darkness at any time…
“Note 3”: The mission execution time is at noon tomorrow. Proceed to a sealed space inside Base Number Five, create a curtain of fire to envelop the area, and wait.
“Note 4”: Prepare a sufficient number (over one hundred) of “Colorless Crystals,” as well as a Level 2 Anomaly Containment Subject in a fully contained state (with an effective restriction of 95%).
“Note 5”: At the fifth stop, two colleagues will join your team…
…
“So many notes? This Ninth Station doesn’t seem easy…”
Colin clicked his tongue, though he wasn’t particularly surprised; it was unclear whether the train had this many issues during the company’s peak years.
But these days, taking this thing meant facing a lot of risks…
After every few stops, the level of danger encountered would spike dramatically.
Not counting the experience with the “Ghost Train,” the furthest he had been on a train was the fourth stop.
“Speaking of which, looking carefully at the mission details, observing the carriage rules for the fifth section isn’t specified. I might only find out what they are when I get there. I hope they aren’t too outrageous…”
“Note one suggests reducing contact with ‘shadows,’ does this include the likes of eye contact? It’s a bit vague…”
“The second one is easy for me. ‘Bonfire’ can ensure I am always within the range of light, even glowing and giving off heat underwater. I just don’t know why contact with darkness is forbidden…”
“The third is the time and place of the action. Is this time on the same type of train used for goods exchange previously?”
“The fourth, a hundred isn’t a problem. I have several hundred on me right now. The difficult part is the fully contained Level 2 Anomaly Containment Subject. Injuring them is easy to say, but controlling them isn’t, I’ll have to ask the officials…”
“Someone’s getting on at the fifth stop? If I had a choice, I hope they send someone like ‘The Light Chaser’ with that level of power…”
Thought after thought, Colin made a simple assessment of the mission—
High risk.It was unclear if anything would go wrong during the journey.
But with all this information, it made one feel quite uneasy…
Colin couldn’t help but shake his head. He had just mentioned how the mission seemed a bit simple, but the turnaround came so quickly.
Gathering his thoughts, he took out his phone, found the contact with a pretty girl avatar, and quickly slid his fingers to edit and send some information…
The first question was about the whereabouts of the “Ancient City’s Giant Buddha.”
Colin knew it was not something he could handle, but he always had the lingering feeling that it was “peering” from behind, creating an indescribable unease.
He knew that many anomalies maintained a respectful distance from things stronger than themselves. Only this one was the exception.
If there was a chance, he wanted to resolve it as soon as possible.
‘Old Master Wu seems to be an expert in mystical arts. There might be a chance.’
After sending the message, Colin did not hesitate to ask if there was a fully contained Level 2 Containment Subject.
If it were just an ordinary containment subject, he could ask Xu Duojin.
But one that was 95% effectively contained was considered a key strategic asset by the officials.
To put it bluntly, they would rather lose a nuclear bomb than lose this thing.
So in this regard, without Old Wu’s approval, there was basically no possibility of getting one, and that’s why he didn’t approach Xu Duojin.
Not long after the message was sent, Old Master Wu responded.
“It’s a bit troublesome about the containment subject, I have to hold a meeting and vote on it, there are many procedures. However, for special matters, we need special actions. I will have it ready by 3 A.M. tomorrow morning and send it to Base Number Five. You can come to receive it then.”
As a Ninth Level “Fate Propeller,” even without knowing Colin’s purpose,
he vaguely sensed what he needed to do and went straight to preparing everything in the room.
‘Communicating with Fate Propellers is indeed smooth. Once you start, they know how to continue the conversation with you…’ Colin felt relieved in his heart.
Without asking Colin’s purpose, “Old” Master responded quickly to the next topic:
“As for the giant stone statue in the ancient city you mentioned, theoretically, I haven’t encountered it, but some guidance tells me that it seems to have had indirect contact with other forms of existence besides you…”
“I will organize the situation a bit and track it.”
“Unexpectedly, I will give you a response within the next few days.”
…
Alright, it seems there’s a chance to continue “past connections.”
Seeing this, Colin nodded and sent an “OK” back, then after thinking for a bit, he inquired about nuclear weapons…
He felt that with his current strength, he might already be qualified to try to understand these things.
Compared to casting a powerful spell by hand, these were much more efficient and convenient to use.
It’s just that there were numerous avoidance measures for certain anomalies…
“However, actually combining ‘Decree Book,’ weakening the mystical properties within an area, and then striking at physical anomalies, might yield some unexpected results…”
Colin felt the feasibility was not low, the only trouble was that it would not be very convenient for him to avoid using it himself.
One careless move could blow himself up as well.
But having some things is always better than not having them at all…
“Although I have the authority to throw a nuclear weapon at your place in some emergency situations caused by anomalies, but… I don’t have the authority to give them to others. However, I will speak to the relevant people about this matter, as it is quite sensitive and there might not be any results…”
Old Master Wu sent the message.
“Okay,” Colin replied simply.
