Although it’s not a guaranteed deal, there’s still a chance of getting it…
“It’s a pity, we don’t know the status of ‘The Seventh Box Garden World’ after we left. If we could get in touch, and if things are still alright there, we could take whatever we want with the nuclear stuff…”
Colin sighed quietly.
There were a couple of shelters there, each with a certain amount of nuclear material, and the permissions were quite lenient.
At least in the past, they would really give him whatever he wanted…
It’s just unknown what the situation is now.
If there’s a chance to visit “The Seventh Box Garden World” again…
Thinking of this, Colin paused mid-thought, estimating that he would probably be beaten to death the moment he appeared.
It seemed like “The Seventh Box Garden World” actually had First Level Containment Subjects in a state of semi or complete liberation, and not just one or two…
Back then, his strength was weak, and although he used the power of the “Bonfire,” he only used it and did not master much of it.
As a result, many beings did not really set their sights on him.
This time, if he went there with the official status of a “Firebearer” reservist.
Then, considering the hostility of higher beings, his fate was unlikely to be very pleasant.
“My current strength is not enough to turn high-level containment subjects from fighting to celebrating.” Colin sighed.
“Moreover, it seems that I can’t get there by ordinary means. The only one who knows how is The Rat… It’s not worth the risk for some weapons…”
He no longer wasted his thoughts on it.
Looking up at the clock on the wall, he saw it was not yet ten o’clock in the morning. With plenty of time left until noon the next day, he opened the parchment and found Big C Teacher’s copy, starting his daily practice.
In the afternoon, he called Qin Chuan, Hu Zheng, and a bunch of others to clear up the anomalies around them…
The day passed quickly.
The next day, approaching noon, Colin created a Bonfire isolation layer inside Base Number Five as required by the mission.
As the time reached twelve o’clock sharp, grey fog began to diffuse around the area.
Soon after, the long whistle of a train slowly approached…
.
.
.
.
Update first, revise later.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 636 - 636 475 The Mysterious Third Person. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 636: Chapter 475: The Mysterious Third Person. _1 Chapter 636: Chapter 475: The Mysterious Third Person. _1 The familiar feeling of trance appeared once again.
By the time Colin came to his senses, the train had already appeared a good length, and he could only see the body of it.
And it was slowly coming to a stop…
“It’s here…”
Without delay, Colin straightened his collar, adjusted the neckline, strode forward, and stepped into the train doorway, the indescribable sense of vagueness on him rapidly dissipating.
The warm yellow light inside the carriage was still the same.
However, the main style had changed a bit; it was no longer the common steampunk aesthetic, but had a slightly minimalist futuristic flair.
“The ‘Passenger’ remained unchanged.”
Flames gathered in Colin’s eyes as he scanned the surroundings, clearly seeing the pitch-black silhouettes on each seat.
Then, he glanced outside the door, withdrew the Bonfire that maintained the closed spatial area, and found himself a seat to sit down.
During this process, he kept his body enveloped in burning flames.
Just as he had anticipated…
Not two seconds after he sat down, the “shadows” within three rows of him stood up, changing seats or walking towards the rear carriages, silently increasing the distance between them.
“So averse to the ‘Bonfire,’ huh.”
Sitting by the window, Colin felt an indescribable repulsion.
“Dang dang dang—”
The urgent sound of the train’s bell rang out.
Colin shifted his gaze away from these objects and, after making some necessary preparations, took out the game console he had prepared and began capturing other creatures for his pet encyclopedia as a way to pass the time.
After all, once this train started moving, it could easily take several hours, and he couldn’t spend the whole time feigning sleep…
About two hours later, Colin, who was riding the train, felt the speed of the constantly moving train begin to slow down.
So he put away the game console.
The first stop was an unremarkable ordinary small city, concealed by special phenomena.
“What’s this place? And what are those people fighting?”
Colin, looking through the window, saw explosions from all directions, and in the center, a group of officials who were Extraordinary Ones were besieging a humanoid, somewhat strong, uncontrolled life form.
The officials, despite appearing dominant, were unable to take down their target and were sustaining numerous casualties instead.
Moreover, among the besieging officials, some were warily observing the train.
“Looks like a rogue element from the Heretic Forces, about as strong as that ‘Deep Sea Messenger’ I encountered before…”
Colin assessed briefly, estimating the strength of the creature.
It would not be easy for these people to subdue it,
especially since the highest-ranking person at the scene was a Level Seven Official, and to take this creature down, at least an Eighth Level Personnel would be needed for an easier battle…
Of course, given the current situation, victory seemed almost certain, though with high casualties.
After a moment’s thought and seeing that the train had just stopped and there was still plenty of time, Colin stood up and walked to the train door.
The onlookers, who were already wary, were shocked to see a stranger engulfed in flames at the entrance of the train, immediately suspecting intervention from the local Heretic Believers.
“Heh, don’t be tense, I, Colin, am not a brawler by nature, but I do enjoy resolving conflicts. I’m considering stepping in to mediate this dispute…”
Facing their gazes, Colin made a jesting remark.
And it was at that moment, while the outside crowd was still confused by his words, they suddenly saw him look beyond them towards the battlefield several hundred meters away, fire gathering in his hand, apparently preparing a powerful technique…
“Be careful!” shouted a protective official.
Everyone was concentrating on the Heretic Bishop, and any disturbance could lead to catastrophe!
However, to their surprise, the flames didn’t target their colleagues but the heretic element…
Colin flicked his hand, shooting out a jet of flame that twisted in midair into a rope, rushing straight toward the Heretic Bishop, ensnaring his neck and pulling him inside the train, where the creature could only emit a mournful howl before being neutralized and turned into a chunk of biological energy carbon.
“This…” The group of officials was stunned.
They had assumed the stranger was there to rescue someone, but it didn’t seem to be the case.
Otherwise, he wouldn’t have burned the victim straightaway.
But before they could understand what had happened, the train made a “dang dang dang” sound, the doors closed, and the eyes of all who were watching involuntarily flickered.
By the time they regained their focus, the stranger was already far away, like a passerby who did a good deed and left without a trace.
Just dealt with the anomaly and then departed.
But…
How could there be such a fortuitous incident in this world?
They were somewhat suspicious that there might be an unknown conspiracy hidden inside.
“Captain Rogue, what’s the situation…”
“I don’t know, but that train must be the S Level Anomaly ‘Death Herald Train’…”
“Hiss, S Level…”
Everyone gasped in shock, feeling a wave of relief as if they had survived a catastrophe.
In their minds, an encounter with something of that level usually spelled certain death…
“Although this train is S Level, it’s not that dangerous… But let’s not talk about it now, wait for me to report to the organization…”
After calming them, Captain Rogue started to make contact with higher-ups.
…
Meanwhile, inside the train, Colin stood by the door, not dwelling too much on the “good deed” he had casually performed.
To him, it was merely lending a hand while passing by…
It didn’t cost him anything, and who knows, it might even bring good karma.
At that moment, Colin’s gaze was on his spoils of war, a thought crossing his mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 637 - 637 475 The Mysterious Third Person. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 637: Chapter 475: The Mysterious Third Person. _2 Chapter 637: Chapter 475: The Mysterious Third Person. _2 “Swish…”
The carbon-based life form at the door burned fiercely under his command, eventually turning into a pile of ashes.
At the same time, Colin took out a piece of gold and, following the method taught by Shana, manipulated the flame obtained from the carbon to merge into the gold, creating a Golden Mark imbued with a certain bonfire power.
The flame on top, when necessary, could be thrown out, equivalent to his normal strike.
Thrown out at some critical moment, it should still be able to have some effect.
“Pretty good, just a bit wasteful of gold.”
Muttering, Colin put the mark into his pocket, then looked around to make sure nothing had sneaked onto the train, and sat back down, taking out his game to continue playing.
Some considerable time later, the train gradually came to a stop.
This time there were no surprises; the train stopped in the middle of a flat wasteland.
No one got off, no one got on, and when the time came, the train moved on.
“This train, I always feel like I’m slacking off…”
Colin touched his chin and watched the train start moving again.
The third station…
Similarly uneventful, nothing appeared to happen.
However.
Just as the doors closed at the third station and the train started moving, Colin suddenly realized that the entire train seemed to become a bit dilapidated…
The originally cozy lighting inside the carriage no longer felt so cozy.
Everything in front of him seemed unchanged, yet invisibly, it seemed as though something had changed.
Familiar things started to feel strange…
“Huh.”
Colin took a deep breath, sat back with one leg crossed over the other, took out his power bank, and charged his red and blue console while playing.
Based on past experience, now inside the train carriage itself, he wouldn’t encounter anything, the only thing to worry about was whether he would face any danger at the next stop.
The fourth stop, this time took a lot longer than all the previous ones combined.
After just over eight hours, Colin saw the train stop.
Outside was an endless, eerie forest…
“Feels like I’ve been here before.”
Colin looked around; this seemed to be the abnormal area where he had previously encountered the mass of heads forming a “Super Coconut Egg Tree.”
At that time, he was escaping from “The Seventh Box Garden World” after a close brush with death…
He still remembered that creature seemed to notice something on the train and gave a warning.
“This time, I didn’t see it, but if I had my current strength back then, I wouldn’t have let that rat sneak on board without a clue…”
Colin sighed, then turned his gaze away from the outside, waiting for the train to start again.
Just then, as if sensing something, he looked up sharply, his gaze sharpening, to see a “Coconut Egg Tree” comprised of hundreds of heads appear less than fifty meters from the train door!
The eyes on each of those heads stared uniformly at the train.
And it seemed to sense Colin’s gaze.
All the heads opened their mouths and spoke in unison, emitting a sound wave imbued with soul power.
“When the future… is in need… call upon us…”
“In times of need… the future… call upon us…”
“Call upon us… the future… when needed…”
“…”
The constant repetition of phrases kept coming; Colin squinted slightly, focusing on the thing outside. If he did not misunderstand, was this an expression of goodwill?
“When in need, what does that mean? Are they speaking to me, or through me, to ‘Lady Rabbit’? Or does it mean that it can predict the future, has seen something coming, and thinks I’ll need it, so it wants to establish some kind of contact?”
Colin puzzled internally.
But now that he thought about it, the first time he encountered this thing…
It didn’t seem to express any malice, did it?
‘My judgment back then seemed to be based on a D Level Personnel who boarded midway; in reality, it wasn’t clear whether it was good or bad.’
As thoughts flickered, the bell signaling the train’s departure rang.
Colin pressed down his jumbled thoughts, jotted down this incident to look into what “Lady Rabbit” would say when he got the chance.
Next, he would head to the fifth stop, which he had never taken before.
“The danger at the fifth stop isn’t too great, at least for me, that’s the case…”
Colin glanced around and could feel the almost indistinct sensation of being watched stealthily coming from all around, and those “passengers” seated everywhere became much clearer.
The intense feeling of disgust and loathing became very apparent…
“These things, it seems, are quite disdainful of, and uncomfortable with me,” he said.
Colin snorted.
If it weren’t for the mission’s request to avoid contact as much as possible, he would have burned these creatures into carbon for fuel by now.
However, he was starting to get a bit curious about the mission’s note number five, wondering who the two colleagues he would meet at the fifth stop would be…
Theoretically, they were likely to be people from Earth.
But, there was also a possibility they could be outsiders similar to “The Light Chaser.”
With anticipation, Colin changed the cassette and started a new game. In the game, he controlled a pink blob that could devour everything, swallowing various enemies and gaining their powers…
Until Colin had finished the game and collected all the achievements, the train had not stopped once.
“Fourteen hours, that’s a bit long…” he muttered.
Colin took a deep breath, grabbed some food and filled his stomach.
Two more hours passed…
The train finally showed signs of slowing down to stop again.
Soon, a lush green meadow appeared behind the window. Colin saw the flickering green lights amongst the tall grass and was momentarily stunned.
What’s going on? Twice today, he had entered scenes he had visited before…
This was a situation that had never occurred before when he took the train.
“Rumble rumble~”
“Whoosh whoosh~”Before he could think more about it, Colin saw a battle unfolding. Not far away, a swath of tall grass was scorched clear by the battle; the ground was littered with limbs and fragments.
Several figures stood at the spot where the train was about to stop, fighting a large group of pale-skinned humanoid creatures with sharp claws.
Cannon shots, lightning, blade winds, and other attacks followed in quick succession.
“Click.”
As the doors opened, the group inside released a wide-range attack in unison, dealing with the aliens and jumping into the train.
The following monsters did not pursue…
Seeing this, the refugees breathed sighs of relief.
Although the creatures seemed fragile, their massive numbers, coupled with their skill at ambushes, still made them quite a headache to deal with.
“Surprisingly, there’s someone familiar,” Colin said as he noticed two of them and could not help but feel astonished at the names floating above their heads.
One was “Master of the Fish Pond,” who had been converting various assets into points via parchment and owned a powerful set of Purple Gear, making him quite well-known.
Especially to Colin, who was very familiar with him since he had been the one begging to buy the Golden Card when they were first issued.
It wasn’t until later, when his true strength was showcased in front of the company, that he stopped mentioning selling the Golden Card.
At the same time, “Master of the Fish Pond” was also taken aback when he saw Colin, not expecting Brother Shunzi to be the assistance target mentioned in the mission.
‘Wait, what sort of difficulty would Brother Shunzi have that I could assist with?’ he thought, his heart skipping a beat.
The situation seemed a bit unsettling, but it was too late to refuse now…
Colin didn’t look at him any longer than necessary, slightly turned his head, and his gaze shifted toward another person, whose name read “It’s All Orange Cat’s Fault”…
To his surprise, this person appeared to be very powerful.
His body was covered with many mysterious and strange patterns that seemed to have something to do with airflow. A light breeze surrounded him, making a “whoosh” sound.
‘Is that a Talent, a real one for Extraordinary Ones?’ Colin wondered in amazement. Typically, an employee’s physical condition depended on their gear, Talent, and Skill.
But this one seemed to have merged with his Talent, becoming closer to an Extraordinary One like the official personnel.
However, as surprising as it was…
What puzzled Colin was, weren’t they expecting just two people?
Why were there three people who boarded?
His eyes moved to the third company colleague’s name above their head.
.
.
Update now, edit later.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 638 - 638 476 The Person Who Will Destroy the World
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 638: Chapter 476: The Person Who Will Destroy the World in the Prophecy, “Colin”._1 Chapter 638: Chapter 476: The Person Who Will Destroy the World in the Prophecy, “Colin”._1 “Night Eagle Laniweya.”
Above this third employee’s head floated such a string of words.
Colin noticed at a glance that this employee was no ordinary person—
First of all, the name didn’t seem to fit in.
It did not look like a name a serious Earth Company employee would have…
Moreover, Colin could feel that this person was very strong. Although some sort of shielding made it impossible to see specifics, there was just that feeling — possibly stronger than “Master of the Fish Pond” and Orange Cat combined.
He even boldly guessed that she could be stronger than some of the official Ninth Level Personnel…
If that was the case, Colin couldn’t possibly lack any awareness of her.
He probably knew all about the strongest batch of D Level from Kě’ài Duō (Cute Duo).
Definitely not the one in front of him now.
“Who is this?”
Colin looked toward Orange Cat to ask, then glanced over at the third person, a female figure faintly discernible under a complicated black robe, her pale hand gripping a black scythe.
Her appearance was hidden under a hood and seemed to be covered by a layer of shadow, making it unclear.
However, on her back, she was carrying a woman with brown hair who seemed to be injured and unconscious.
No ID showed above the head.
Hmm, probably not a company employee.
At this time, Laniweya became visibly alert upon noticing Colin’s gaze.
Her movements were slight, but not hidden from Bonfire’s observation.
“Just met this person at the station…” “Master of the Fish Pond” started talking, briefly explaining the situation.
He, following the mission requirements, first took the train, got off at the second station, met up with other employees, stood by for an hour, waiting for another train…
During this period, the three of them naturally ended up together. Oh, no, four people.
The one in the mysterious patterned black robe, Laniweya, also had a subordinate or something with her.
Only, at that time, this subordinate was accidentally attacked by the curse of a scarecrow at the tall grass station.
And then nearly died on the spot.
Hearing his words, Colin nodded and pointed to the seat next to him: “The train is about to start, sit down first and talk…”
“Okay.” The three didn’t stand on ceremony and came over respectively.
But Laniweya didn’t sit next to him; instead, she observed for a while and chose a seat not too far away.
After everyone sat down, the train bell rang, and it started moving again.
“Can you tell me about your mission?”
Colin asked after the bell stopped and quickly got an answer.
The ways the few of them came were theoretically much the same, each taking different trains to get there.
Then the requirement was to assist him to the stations ahead.
‘Is this mission so special that it’s not a joint operation from the start? Hmm, there seems to be some explanation…’
‘”Fifteenth Ring missions,” I’ve heard, are usually solo missions. There must be some specials, hence if they want assistance, they could only skirt around the rules with some tricks.’
‘So theoretically, am I still on a “solo mission” right now?’
Colin’s mind worked quickly, piecing together the logic with his own understanding.
If these few people all perished now, he would probably still be on record for a mission with zero casualties.
As for the so-called assistance…
It’s no more than adding a couple of antennas to a router. In a battle where Colin does not need to go all out, they probably can’t be of much help.
At this moment, all he could do was to marvel at mission assignments in the company, something “Lady Rabbit” had clearly mastered the art of bending to her will.
There’s always a way to get around some company mechanisms and loopholes for a favorable arrangement.
Of course, for those other than Colin, it might not be so friendly.
After all, their task was simply to assist an employee through four train stations and then finish.
In normal times, sitting for a few stations wouldn’t be a big deal.
But now the problem was, what they thought would be stations 1 to 4, turned out to be stations 6 to 9.
‘Tsk… This, this is downright fraud.’
As he heard them speak, Colin’s expression suddenly became lively.
If these two knew the situation, they’d probably cry on the spot…
But now that they were here, it was too late for regrets or refusal. Colin thought it over and decided not to be the bearer of bad news by not telling them too much of the truth.
After all, his reputation in related matters was a bit “stinky” now.
And rather than dwelling on such trivial matters, what was most important at the moment was the situation with this “third person.”
Colin looked toward “Laniweya”: “What about you? Are you the same as them?”
During their conversation, he could confirm that she indeed was the “third person,” and he also figured out why she seemed a bit off.
Because she was very similar to Shana. Though both were company employees, there seemed to be a difference.
‘If I’m not mistaken… This one is probably from another ‘Subsidiary’, different from the one Shana belongs to.’
Colin had a rough judgment.
Hearing Colin’s direct question, Laniweya was silent for a few seconds, then spoke: “I, I am here to assist you to the world beyond, assist you to the final station, to push the world stuck in stasis forward, to break the groundless fantasies of those stubborn dissenters…”
“What? What’s all this? Final station? Push the world forward? How come it seems mismatched?” Colin raised an eyebrow.
He was just going to station nine to refuel the train car and then head home, yet now he was supposed to be pushing the world forward, breaking groundless fantasies of stubborn dissenters?

chapters.title: Chapter 639 - 639 476 The Person Who Will Destroy the World
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 639: Chapter 476: The Person Who Will Destroy the World in the Prophecy, “Colin”._2 Chapter 639: Chapter 476: The Person Who Will Destroy the World in the Prophecy, “Colin”._2 Something seems off.
Colin raised his right hand to his chin, realizing the situation was much more complicated than the brief had suggested.
At the same time, the “Master of the Fish Pond” and the “It’s all Orange Cat’s fault” employees also exchanged glances, sensing that matters were far from simple.
Seeing the atmosphere, Raniweya silently gripped the scythe in her hands.
‘How does she know about pushing the world forward? Could it be that she knows what will happen after the eight or nine stations?’
Colin, who was quickly analyzing the information in the other party’s words, soon picked up on quite a few details.
If that was the case, he could further confirm that this person was from a “branch office.”
Because no one from the company on Earth could sit that far off yet…
Taking into account the strength and specialty of the person’s presence, he could almost certainly determine their origin.
‘But… even if she’s from further ahead, why so tense?’
Colin, observing the other party through the flame, noticed that although the person didn’t show it on the surface, some subtle body movements faintly revealed alertness and even hostility after those words were spoken?
Is that necessary?
After thinking it through, he was about to speak up and inquire, hoping to dispel any possible misunderstandings, but then he heard a pained groaning nearby.
In the adjacent seat, the subordinate who had been carried in on a back was now awake from pain, his face contorted in a grimace, as many pale lines appeared on his body, indicating a transformation of some kind…
‘Is he turning into one of those monsters from the tall grasses?’
Witnessing this scene, Colin thoughtfully considered.
On the other side, Raniweya’s eyes under the hood showed a hint of helplessness.
It seemed that her subordinate had still failed to withstand the curse.
Then, she pulled out a black precious metal dagger: “Vini, go to sleep peacefully; in the form of a human, your soul will be reborn in the eternal long night.”
“Ah?” Colin was stunned. Was she about to kill her?
“Wait, we can still save her.”
He waved his hands to halt Raniweya’s movement.
As he spoke, Colin watched the wounded woman’s skin turn increasingly pale, and said, “If you don’t mind, may I try to save her?”
Raniweya was silent for a few seconds, hearing her subordinate Vini groan in pain again before she responded, “Is it possible?”
“Yeah, but it might come at a certain cost…”
Colin stroked his chin as the flames around him spun, looking to see if there was a chance to gain something.
But to his surprise…
Hearing his words, Raniweya shook her head: “A significant cost, you say? Vini would understand our choice…”
“Ah?” Colin was taken aback.
Then, along with the two employees by his side, he watched her once again raise her hand to end her subordinate’s life.
“No no no, she can be saved, I’ll bear the cost, it’s not a big problem.”
Colin stopped her again, and couldn’t help but murmur to himself: how different the values of this branch office were from those of the Saintess.
If Shana were there, he might have been able to swindle a temporary right to use a Holy Relic.
But this “Night Eagle Raniweya,” upon hearing about the cost, immediately chose euthanasia…
“After all, it’s a life; if I hadn’t seen it, that would be one thing, but having seen it and there being a chance, I certainly can’t just not save her.”
Colin said offhandedly, stood up, reached out, and placed his hand on the unconscious woman’s forehead. Rolling flames traveled along his fingers, infiltrating the other’s body.
The strange curse within her was like bacteria in the twentieth century encountering penicillin for the first time, retreating defeated at every turn…
Soon, the twisted expression on her face began to relax.
‘The power of the “Flame Bearer” really has strong suppressive effects on all sorts of anomalies…’ Colin couldn’t help but marvel inwardly.
At his side, Raniweya seemed to be moved by the scene, a flicker of something indescribable in her eyes under the hood.
‘Is every life worth saving…?’ Raniweya felt somewhat lost in her thoughts, but then something seemed to reinforce her resolve, and she became cold and determined once more.
Shortly after…
A strong sense of crisis flashed through Colin’s mind, and instinctively, he raised his right hand and caught a sharp scythe tip with his thumb, index, and middle fingers.
A chilling, numb aura of death spread wildly from the scythe, attempting to infiltrate his body.
Colin looked up at the woman in the black robe: “Do you know what you’re doing?”
As he spoke, his heart was puzzled, not understanding why she had suddenly lashed out!
There was no response…
“Laniweya,” gripping the scythe, leapt backward. Her black robe seemed to come to life, turning into active shadows that enveloped her completely and spread out from under her feet in all directions.
The long-planned shadows engulfed the entire train carriage at that moment, plunging everything into darkness.
“Boom!”
Flames erupted suddenly from Colin.
His reaction was extremely fast, and the deep, thick darkness collided silently with the searing flames.
“Huff huff!”
The Orange Cat duo was a step slow. Normally, in just an instant, they would have been swallowed by the darkness, plunging them into a very passive situation.
But luckily, Colin held off the first wave of the explosion.
Mysterious patterns spread across Orange Cat’s body, transforming into blades as the wild wind swept towards the enemy.
“Damn it, are you insane?”
The Master of the Fish Pond cursed loudly as a pair of mechanical wings unfurled behind him, launching a barrage of laser beams in all directions.
Although they had always felt there was something off about this colleague, they never expected her to launch a sudden attack.
However, Laniweya didn’t respond to him either.
In the thick darkness, numerous black arms stretched out from all sides, reaching for them.
“Foreigners, considering you once saved Vini’s life, I’ll give you a chance to leave this place, to give up moving forward. Otherwise, I will consider your actions an invasion, an interference with our race’s great decisions and destiny.”
“And then, I will completely annihilate you here!”
In the pitch darkness, Laniweya’s indifferent voice echoed, but her figure was nowhere to be seen.
‘I knew it, this trip was never as simple as just refueling the train.’
Colin sighed inwardly, then said unflinchingly, “I refuse your request.”
As his words fell, a vision flashed through his mind: dozens of shadows emitting red light, like hounds emerging from the darkness, biting at every part of his body, tearing him limb from limb…
“A trifling trick.”
Colin “Humphed,” expertly pinching a Golden Card in his left hand.
“Force – Repulsion!”
In an instant, a terrifying repulsive force burst forth, carrying an unstoppable power that shattered the shadow hounds that had just poked their heads out.
And the entire Dark Domain began to tear, as if it was about to be broken open.
‘To not open in one go, this ‘Domain’ is something…’ Colin thought with surprise, while his hands kept moving, drawing a revolver.
In a flash, the power of the “Flame Bearer” was further unleashed.
The darkness in the train carriage quickly dimmed…
“What?”
Laniweya’s pupils tightened slightly. She had seen those who could break the Dark Domain before, but never as quickly as this!
What on earth was this flame?
However, as shocked as she was, her hands did not stop moving. She swung the “Blade of Death,” attempting to imbue the concept of “death” into the flames.
To extinguish this foreigner prophesied to bring apocalyptic disaster right here and now.
Despite the recently displayed good intentions, it was all merely a ruse by those demons!
For the fate of her homeland and her people!
She could not let them advance any further!
But at that moment, she abruptly noticed that the opponent’s figure had vanished…
And precisely at that moment of astonishment, a sharp pain surged from her lower back. Something sharp had penetrated her body, an indescribable filth being continuously injected into her.
“Found you.”
Colin’s hand exerted force, driving the Bone Spur completely into her body, while flames roiled on his body, turning into several tongues of flame, about to bind and subdue her.
But at that moment, he glimpsed a reverse hook of the scythe from within the blackness.
Laniweya decisively cut off her own head.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 640 - 640 Rule of the 5th stop 477._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 640: Rule of the 5th stop, 477._1 Chapter 640: Rule of the 5th stop, 477._1 “Outsiders, die right here!”
The next moment, his body exploded like an ink bottle sinking into a clear pool, with darkness so thick it caused hearts to palpitate surging forward.
“‘Containment Protocol’ Item Liberation request, ‘Revolver Contrarian’ item 5% liberation!”
In his mind, a thought flashed, and Colin dared not take any chances.
He went directly into a state of high eruption…
The next second, the bright orange-red bonfire and the profound, rich darkness chased each other away.
It lasted quite a while before everything finally came to an end.
The train cabin, which had been shrouded in darkness for a few minutes, became bright again…
“Hiss…”
Colin raised his hand to wipe the cold sweat from his forehead, recalling that intense dark power, and couldn’t help but think of a certain terrifying existence.
“What the hell is up with this guy?” The Fish Pond Master and Orange Cat looked around, still feeling the residual fear.
He had a premonition that if it weren’t for Brother Shunzi’s presence, they would’ve either died or ended up severely maimed during those few minutes.
“Did that person die?” Orange Cat asked, looking at Colin, whose body kept erupting in flames.
At this moment, only three people remained on the train; the original injured party and Raniweya’s figure had both disappeared.
Even those “passengers” had vanished during the brief clash.
Employees battled fiercely, and passengers died violently.
“Most likely ran away…”
While covering the train with flames to drive away all shadows, Colin shook his head.
The opponent had looked as though they intended mutual destruction…
But without surprise, that must have been some kind of skill or technique, at most paying a certain price, but certainly not dead.
Compared to this, what puzzled Colin even more was what the opponent’s words meant.
He could roughly guess that the opponent might have used some predictive method to foresee their arrival.
And then came in advance to block them, aiming to hold them back.
But…
“I’m just making a trip to the ninth station, how did that disrupt the grand destiny?” Colin scratched his head, utterly perplexed.
The essence of his mission was simply to refuel the train, but now the confrontation made it seem like he was there to carry out an “Extermination Order” or something similar.
Putting aside whether he was qualified to execute such an order, even if he was, he wasn’t Rosen; he wasn’t as extreme to randomly destroy the world.
At this point, Orange Cat spoke up, “Brother Shunzi, do you know anything about who that person might be? It feels like we’ve never really seen such a character in the company.”
From their brief encounter, he and the Fish Pond Master were sure that they were no match for that individual.
Surviving would be difficult enough.
To hold their ground, they would probably need two or three more people with specific equipment to barely manage a fight.
Such a strong opponent, and yet they didn’t recognize them…
It wasn’t impossible, but the odds were not very high.
“Background, huh… not sure, but they’re probably from a ‘branch company,'” Colin didn’t hide this fact.
“‘Branch company’?”
Both were startled when they heard this term.
However, they quickly understood what “branch company” meant through Brother Shunzi’s explanation, and were both enlightened.
They really hadn’t expected such a situation…
“Then why are we suddenly clashing with a ‘branch company’? Logically, shouldn’t they be our own people?” Orange Cat sighed while sitting in a chair.
“Could they be trying to seize power?” The Fish Pond Master suggested.
At that moment, recalling the current fragmented state of the company and combining it with the task Brother Shunzi was sent on to the “branch company” territory, both couldn’t help but wonder if their own Earth Company was playing a bigger game?
What if the founder had died, the corporate system and order had collapsed, branch companies were waging war against each other, foreign capital was looming, and everything was on the verge of bankruptcy, with internal and external troubles, and then… even if the company was already shattered, they were to become the majority shareholder to restructure the company and so on.
Colin wasn’t aware of the bizarre ideas in the minds of these two; he was currently feeling a bit of a headache, not knowing what to do if they encountered the opponent again.
Since it was confirmed that the opponent was from a “branch company”…
Then it was very likely that Colin would have to face the power of an entire “branch company.”
Although he was unclear about the state of this “branch company,” it must be known that not every “branch company” was like the one Shana belonged to, all of them orphans.
If the opponent had many people, and all with high power, that would be problematic.
One man against an entire “branch company”?
“It seems that only high-level employees can start a ‘branch office.’ That is to say, even C Level ‘Firebearers’ might not be able to do this,”
Colin was aware of his own strength and had not become overly inflated to think otherwise.
Moreover, even if he were lucky and this ‘branch office’ was like Shana, an orphan with only one person,
it would still be hard for Colin to defeat the opponent.
Because it was very likely that the opponent, like Shana, possessed the right to directly send ‘report letters’…
Once that defense mechanism was activated, it might be somewhat forced even for him to protect himself.
“The only good news is, that guy is quite a bit weaker than Shana, at best, on par with a non-core ordinary clone, and weaker than me,”
“But it’s also unclear how many people are currently in this ‘branch office,’ what means they have at their disposal, what corps may be stationed or left behind, and what their relationship with the ‘Firebearers’ is, and so on.”
Thinking of these matters, Colin felt overwhelmed and couldn’t help but curse silently to himself.
Wasn’t it agreed to just add some fuel?
“Brother Shunzi…”
At this moment, Orange Cat suddenly spoke up, interrupting his thoughts. When he looked over, the cat tilted its chin, signaling him to look in a certain direction…
Colin, with a puzzled look, turned his gaze in that direction, then his eyes slightly froze.
At the front of the train, a notice board had appeared at some point, and on it were some new rules.
“Welcome aboard this train, we are about to pass through a special area. For your safety, please adhere to the following rules while riding this train to avoid accidents…”
“1. Please coexist peacefully with the ‘passengers’ and avoid substantial contact with them.”
“2. After you have boarded the train at the fifth stop, please ensure that there is more than one ‘passenger’ in the carriage of this train.”
“3. If a ‘passenger’ comes to your seat, do not panic, as long as you promptly give up your seat.”
“…To be continued.”
“Attention! If you do not follow these rules when riding this train, you will be solely responsible for any consequences you encounter.”
“…”
Quickly taking in the content, Colin understood that the ‘passengers’ referred to were those black shadows that normal people couldn’t see, not them.
Afterwards, he subconsciously looked around and frowned—
The figures that had disappeared after the fight with “Raniweya” had not been replenished.
According to the pattern, those things would only come from the carriages ahead after the next stop…
And the core requirement above was that.
One must sit in a carriage where ‘passengers’ are present.
Previous task notes had mentioned that one should adhere to the rules as much as possible.
He didn’t know the consequences of not following them, nor did he want to find out…
“Follow me.”
As the thought passed through Colin’s mind, he decisively stood up and motioned for the two people to move toward the rear carriage.
However, just as they reached the connecting door, they found that this normally operable door was now completely stuck.
“Is it because there are no ‘passengers’?”
Thoughts flashed through Colin’s mind, but before he could think further, he suddenly heard the employees next to him gasp in panic.
Out of the corner of his eye, Colin clearly saw the two people’s faces turn pale, even showing fear.
‘Can D Level staff really be frightened to this extent?’
He frowned and followed their gaze, presumably to something outside the window?
“What is it?”
In his confusion, he suddenly saw a floating black shadow approaching through the surging gray mist, like a balloon…
Soon, the ghastly white face of a woman appeared in Colin’s eyes.
As soon as he saw this face, Colin froze, his mind unusually unable to comprehend.
This face was identical to the memory of his mother’s…
“Lin Lin, come out quickly, mommy misses you so much…”
His mother’s voice echoed in his ears.
Her head gently but repeatedly tapped against the train window, making a ‘thump thump’ sound.
.
.
.
Will update and edit later.

chapters.title: Chapter 641 - 641 478 The 6th Station Starry Sky Transfer
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 641: Chapter 478: The 6th Station: “Starry Sky Transfer Station”. _1 Chapter 641: Chapter 478: The 6th Station: “Starry Sky Transfer Station”. _1 The balloon-like head was knocking on the train window with its forehead, all the while uttering low, beguiling whispers…
And within the mist, even more “balloons” appeared one by one.
The old dean, Xiao Chuan…
And Colin even saw his father’s face, which he had only seen in photographs.
Like the others, it floated outside the train window, its forehead pressing against the glass. In the glow of the bonfire, his pale face was unsettling as it stared at him, lips wriggling, calling out:
“Daddy’s here, come over…”
“Didn’t you always ask where daddy was when you were little?”
“Quick, see what daddy has brought you…”
The knocking sounds were continuous, like raindrops, filled with an intangible eeriness.
At the same time, Colin saw that the two employees beside him were somewhat dazed, they seemed to want to look away, but their gazes were magnetically locked on the window, unable to move.
“Looking at this, they should be resisting, and shouldn’t have any issues for a while, but speaking of which, I’ve never seen my family so well-organized in my life…”
Colin watched the faces on the window and, under the protection of the bonfire, wasn’t much affected, his emotions didn’t fluctuate at all.
‘After the “passengers” inside the train are gone, these kinds of things emerge outside the window? No idea what the principle is…’
‘It’s quite eerie… but having been through numerous battles, there’s not much left to fear.’
‘However, after this rule is triggered, there’s bound to be more danger than just this…’
Colin looked at the faces, his mind racing with thoughts.
A rule that’s listed as a separate remark on the mission surely isn’t as simple as just a bunch of heads “shouting” a couple of words and knocking on the glass.
And it was at this moment, within the carriage, that the originally dim yellow light suddenly dimmed, and the whole train began to shake…
At the same time, the faces outside became even spookier.
Some sort of eerie entity seemed to be approaching.
Relying on his intuition, Colin vaguely realized that maybe by blocking the outside world’s prying into the inside,
It would be possible to avoid danger…
Colin took out a large bottle of grease from the “Storage Room,” ignited the flame, and allowed his own flame to envelop the entire train.
Then the flames on his body burned fiercely, emitting a bright light like a small sun for an instant.
“Ah!!!”
Screams resounded one after another.
All the faces on the “balloons” heads outside melted and twisted like wax candles under the flame, emitting sharp screams, and eventually exploded with a “pop.”
Various gazes thrown from the mist all disappeared.
The dim yellow light inside the carriage slowly regained its brightness, and the swaying sensation settled at this moment.
Obviously, even abnormalities couldn’t easily withstand the power of the bonfire!
“Fish Pond Master” shook his head vigorously, finally withdrawing his gaze, muttered cursing under his breath, “Damn, almost got taken in!”
Just after hearing someone calling him, his neck had snapped towards the window on its own accord, then he saw many reluctant faces, like friends and family, and others who had made a significant impression…
Although he came to his senses, it seemed to be a bit too late, as he was constantly pulling in a tug-of-war with the other party.
The Orange Cat beside him was slightly better off, but only by a little and couldn’t pay attention to much else.
It wasn’t until Brother Shunzi’s flames exploded outwards, completely covering the entire carriage with no blind spots, and “melting” all lines of sight, that they truly recovered.
“What’s going on now?”
The Orange Cat said anxiously, and took another look at the flames around, feeling as if they were in a crucible.
“It seems to be the consequence of violating the ‘rules’…”
Colin, while maintaining the flame’s envelope, said, “But things should be alright now.”
As he suspected, the key to stabilizing the carriage was to block the “gaze” from outside.
As long as the Firebearer’s flames continue to burn, there won’t be a big problem.
“I hope we get to the next stop soon, otherwise burning at such a high output for over ten hours will be a bit too much for me to handle.”
“But looking at it this way, did the original ‘passengers’ also serve to block the gaze?”
Colin’s thoughts shifted as he realized that the “passenger,” while being one of the crises within the train, also played a key role in its stability.
It’s just not known what is so special about it that it can actually block the line of sight.
‘Normally, when looking at these spectral figures, there doesn’t seem to be anything special. I didn’t expect them to have such an important function.’
Colin suddenly felt a bit of a shudder.
Because usually when riding the train, he would occasionally gaze curiously at the things, trying to figure out just what the heck they were.
He truly hadn’t expected that such behavior was as dangerous as playing with fire next to a gas canister.
But on the other hand, an anomaly that could prevent “peeping,” with a significant essence, was rendered seemingly harmless in the carriage as long as one didn’t touch it…
“Did you just see someone you recognize, like family members?” Colin asked the two about what they’d seen.
Then he quickly learned that, just like himself, they had witnessed the “family bucket”—both the dead and the living, anyone with a lasting impression, poking their heads out of the mist.
However, they didn’t dwell on this topic for too long.
Orange Cat spoke up, “Speaking of which, what’s with that ‘branch company’ woman? Are we… going to run into them directly next?”
“That person, I felt something off about her before I got on, and sure enough, there was a problem!” Fish Pond Master cursed under his breath.
“Let’s take it one step at a time; right now, we know absolutely nothing about the next station.”
Colin shook his head. With so little information, it was hard to make any sufficiently effective judgments.
Hearing his words, the two D Level employees could only sigh with worry.
Afterwards, Colin, whose flame had been maintained for nearly eight hours and was somewhat worn out, once again sensed that the train was slowing down…
The sixth station was about to arrive!
Soon, as the grey mist outside gradually cleared, a dimly colored scene appeared before everyone’s eyes.
Then, everyone was slightly taken aback.
They saw, beyond the window, a world with a deep black backdrop dotted with countless stars, and the area where the train was about to stop was on a desolate, dilapidated giant metal platform of a small asteroid.
It looked like a science fiction-themed space transportation hub.
And around the platform, they could also see a ring encircling the entire celestial body…
‘It does resemble a junior version of “Starship”…’
Upon seeing its general shape, Colin immediately recalled the starship from which they had recovered “Time Reversal.”
“Looking outside, Fish Pond Master spoke with some emotion, “I heard that after the fifth station, we might leave Earth directly. I thought people were just spouting nonsense, but it turns out to be true…”
Counting the previous aid they gave to Brother Shunzi, this was the first time he and Orange Cat had come to such a distant place, their eyes filled with a sense of novelty.
‘D Level employees from the company before have by now probably explored countless extraterrestrial worlds and participated in numerous incidents. Their level is indeed quite surpassed…’ Colin glanced at the two, who looked inexperienced, and couldn’t help but think.
At that moment, the train doors opened, and Colin, peering through the doors, looked out at the silent exterior—
He found it strange. Did the “Mist Train” stop because this was a station, or because there was an anomaly that caused them to stop the train?
‘It seems there’s nothing threatening, so it’s because it’s a station? But anyhow, once the train stops, I need to gather the flame first; otherwise, the ‘passengers’ won’t come over… Huh?’
Just as Colin was pondering this, he suddenly saw, with a focused gaze, a “plop” on the glass of a nearby window.
A blood handprint was slapped onto it.
However, outside, there was clearly no one to be seen!
But before he could think more, one blood handprint after another appeared, seemingly moving toward the train door.
“Are they… getting on?”
Colin’s brow furrowed. If it was an anomaly, it would be the first time he’d seen one trying to board the train. He immediately prepared for any possible charge.
Golden Card in his left hand, revolver in his right, ready for any potential threat.
Under the gaze of the three, it was almost fifteen seconds later when a pair of bloodied figures walked in from outside.
The strong smell of blood pervaded and hit them head-on…
Then, before Colin could act, they heard a “thump.”
Both figures collapsed to the ground, and blood from beneath them quickly spread across the floor…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 642 - 642 479 The Cruel Truth Thats Hard to Say_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 642: Chapter 479: The Cruel Truth That’s Hard to Say_1 Chapter 642: Chapter 479: The Cruel Truth That’s Hard to Say_1 “What’s going on? Was it those two people just now?”
Orange Cat’s steel wire twitched in hand, ready to coordinate an attack with the force of the hurricane raging within him.
But just as he prepared to make a move, he discovered that the one lying at the car door was the woman who had introduced herself as Akasha earlier and then, out of the blue, ambushed them.
“Yes, it’s the two of them, I’d recognize them even if they turned to ash.”
“Master of the Fish Pond” watched for a few seconds and also nodded. They had almost been erased; they remembered it clearly.
And it was at this moment that the woman called “Vinnie” struggled to raise her head and looked at the several people in the car, emitting a weak voice:
“Please… help us…”
“When you ambushed us just now, you didn’t sound quite like this.”
Orange Cat didn’t even budge upon hearing this.
If it hadn’t been for Brother Shunzi just now, the two of them might really have flipped over.
Now, not knowing what they had encountered, they had suffered severe injuries and were again seeking help from them, thinking they had no temper?
To not kick these two out of the train with one foot was already generous enough, let alone help them?
How could that be possible!
“Ambush?”
Vinnie looked stunned and suddenly realized something. Just as she was about to explain herself, she couldn’t help but cough due to the urgency, and with each cough, blood spurted out, leaving her unable to speak.
In her frantic coughing fits, blood gushing from her mouth and nose, she suddenly fainted away.
“Ah… what?” Both were momentarily stunned.
Then, they turned to look at Akasha, who they had brought into the car, lying aside with even more severe injuries, looking hardly human…
“Master of the Fish Pond” and Orange Cat simultaneously turned to look at Colin, unsure of how to proceed.
However, as they turned, they saw a virtual ancient tree appear next to Brother Shunzi, its many roots flying from the tree to pierce into the bodies of the two enemies.
The two instinctively thought they were going to be used as fertilizer, but then they noticed that after the roots took hold, the vital signs of the two women actually began to rise?
“Let’s revive them first, then ask some questions to see what’s going on.”
Hearing Brother Shunzi’s words, they nodded at once, feeling that they had indeed been affected by resentment, thinking of vengeance when they saw their enemies, rather than extracting information before killing, like Brother Shunzi.
But, what they didn’t know was…
The actual situation at hand was a bit different from what they were thinking; Colin gazed at the two lying on the ground and the employee IDs above their heads, his expression showing some confusion.
“Path of Progress·Akasha.”
“Path of Progress·Vinnie.”
“Wasn’t it something like Night whatever Raniweya? Why has it changed to this? Did they change their names? Or is there some kind of inside story? No, it shouldn’t be…”
Colin squinted his eyes slightly, recalling some things. In a previous conversation, the employee with the name “Night Eagle: Ravinia” above his head would sometimes refer to himself as “Akasha”…
In a flash of thoughts, he shifted his gaze and looked again at “Vinnie.”
This one didn’t have a name above her head just now, but now she suddenly appeared as an employee, and not even a newbie.
Connecting various dots, could this be a case of mistaking Li Gui for Li Kui?
‘That’s right, just now Raniweya has been acting somewhat evasive, several times she tried to approach me, was her intention from the start to kill me? Her murderous intent was well hidden, I didn’t even notice…’ Colin realized the reason.
However, at the same time, Colin noticed that neither Orange Cat nor Master of the Fish Pond seemed able to see the IDs above each other’s heads…
If they had noticed that, they would certainly have realized something was wrong, but they hadn’t mentioned it.
Obviously, they couldn’t see them…
As for Raniweya, if she knew he could see the original name atop her head, she probably wouldn’t have chosen to appear before them at all.
‘Interesting, the wounds on this person match the methods of that ‘Raniweya,’ so, the current situation is, she deliberately assaulted these two and then pretended to meet us?’
‘What for, to stop me from proceeding to subsequent stops?’
‘Then does this mean, these two, knowing that I would move on, deliberately sought me out, which led to their being attacked?’
‘What would they want from me?’
Colin looked at the two people who had passed out from their serious injuries, a trace of confusion flickering in his eyes.
But in the next second, it was as if a flash of lightning crossed his mind.
Some things suddenly became clear…
‘These two, couldn’t they be the people mentioned in the mission notes, the ones coming to assist me?’
Colin’s eyebrows raised, suddenly realizing that if this was the case.
Everything could be explained.
Perhaps the “Branch Office” people had received “Lady Rabbit’s” message and then came this way, but en route they were assaulted by opposing personnel from another “Branch Office,” resulting in the current mistaken identity scenario.
‘But then again, these two are a bit lacking in strength, aren’t they? Li Kui can’t even defeat Li Gui.’
Colin muttered to himself.
Then, his gaze turned to the other two employees who had followed from Earth…
If this explanation held, namely: the two coming from the “Branch Office” were the supporters, then the identity of these two on this mission got a bit awkward.
‘They didn’t just come here to act as a Signal Tower, did they?’
If so, it felt like the company didn’t take them seriously enough…
“Can you see the IDs above their heads?”
Colin didn’t keep his guess to himself, he instead asked outright.
“No…” Both shook their heads at the same time.
This further confirmed to Colin the specific identities of these newcomers.

chapters.title: Chapter 643 - 643 479 The Cruel Truth Thats Hard to Say_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 643: Chapter 479: The Cruel Truth That’s Hard to Say_2 Chapter 643: Chapter 479: The Cruel Truth That’s Hard to Say_2 Orange Cat asked Colin, with a face full of innocence, why he was asking such a question…
‘The truth is too cruel. Knowing too much isn’t very friendly to your mental health.’
Colin muttered to himself and brushed it off with a laugh.
After he spoke, he looked at the two people who were being healed by the “Fire Tree.” They were still unconscious, and he guessed it would be a while before they woke up.
Assured that they were not likely to die, he turned his gaze outside.
The empty space station platform was still deathly quiet, and he saw no immediate dangers…
Upon seeing this, Colin withdrew the flames covering the train. Less than ten seconds after withdrawing, some “passengers” emerged from the front carriage.
However, just two seconds after walking in, seemingly because they noticed Colin, who was like a giant fireball,
some of the figures unprecedentedly turned around to go back.
‘You think you can leave after just arriving?’
Colin ‘hmphed’ and, with a snap of his fingers, blocked the connecting doors at the front and back of the carriage with two firewalls.
The figures that couldn’t escape eventually resigned themselves to their fate and found seats.
‘Looking at it this way, the convenience of someone who can harness the power of the ‘Flame Bearer’ is great, but I don’t understand why this thing can ensure the train’s stable passage.’
Colin was puzzled, but unfortunately, his knowledge couldn’t explain this.
Once he made sure that there were passengers, Colin finally sat down to wait for the train to start and for the two aides to wake up.
‘With such severe injuries, can they really be saved?’
Orange Cat stared at one of their wounds and couldn’t help but murmur.
The vital signs of Vini, who said she could explain the situation, were somewhat stable.
But the other one had problems that went beyond internal injuries.
There wasn’t a single spot on her body that was unscathed; the crown of her skull was flipped open, revealing a red walnut-like brain pulsating inside, and half of her once beautiful face was torn off, leaving a ghastly and skeletal appearance.
In the torso area, from the abdomen to below the chest, a large chunk of flesh and skin was torn away, exposing guts that looked like noodles coated in tomato sauce or chili sauce, twitching inside. Slightly above, you could see a tomato-like heart weakly beating, along with organs not yet turned into lung soup gasping weakly…
The body had almost no intact bones, and it seemed the limbs were also broken in many places. Because there were no open wounds, the blood had accumulated, making them look like links of sausage.
As for the blood, many pools had already started to congeal on the ground.
Such a variety of injuries on a mere human would be enough to bleed out and die two or three times over, just from splitting the blood loss.
Only because of her strong powers could she last until now.
Overall, compared to the one beside her with an intact body, she was in slightly worse shape.
‘Tsk tsk, seems kinda dicey.’
The “Master of the Fish Pond” sat in a chair, smacking his lips as he observed those wounds.
He was still unaware of the real situation and wondered why they had ended up like this after such a short time he hadn’t seen them.
And these wounds… they probably weren’t caused by Brother Shunzi…
Otherwise, they would more likely be extensive burns, not this type of tearing.
However, just after he had spoken, the “Fire Tree” performing the healing didn’t seem pleased; as it was saving lives, these two good-for-nothings were doubting its skills?
Suddenly, a wizened face appeared from the tree trunk:
‘I used to be a senior doctor with Third Level A-class proficiency from the company! I am proficient in one thousand seven hundred and eighty types of human vitals, only a half step away from the specialist doctor’s license. How could I possibly fail with such superficial injuries! Young man! Are you looking down on me?!’
Upon hearing this, both the “Master of the Fish Pond” and Orange Cat were startled, then they drew in a breath of cold air and looked at the “Fire Tree” in horror.
‘…you can talk?!
‘Isn’t it normal for an old man to talk?’ The face on the “Fire Tree” looked disdainful.
Several branches were folded behind its back, hands clasped, as it adopted a pose with its back to the people, continuing to recite something akin to a defiant poem.
But just then…
‘Click.’
The sound of a revolver’s cylinder rotating, and the “Fire Tree” instantly became more alert.
‘How much longer before the people can be revived?’ Colin asked, casually holding the revolver, his tone amiable.
‘The one with worse injuries around two or three hours, the one with lighter injuries within half an hour…’
A tendril from the “Fire Tree” swept across the wizened forehead, miming a gesture of wiping sweat: ‘Of course, if you have a need, I can first repair the necessary areas to wake them up.’
“No need, base it on their physical condition,” Colin was not in a hurry.
“Okay…”
Having said that, “Fire Tree” continued to move its wooden lips without making a sound, as if hesitating.
“If you have something to say, just say it,” Colin spoke up.
“While healing, I found that their brains have suffered significant damage, and there might be some defects. Unless we have some old friends here to assist, or a high-level medical room, it’s not going to be easy to repair in a short time…”
“Fire Tree” said cautiously, afraid that the other party might get upset and deny him any chances of happiness.
“Let’s wake them up first.”
Colin nodded, not taking the difficulty to task.
After all, when Queen Akasha arrived here, even a walnut kernel might have been lost for a moment; a mere “Fire Tree” indeed might not be able to bring someone back in one piece.
After finishing, there was a moment of quiet in the area.
Colin looked outside uneasily; by now, the train had started moving.
After taking on “passengers,” there were no more “family bucket balloons” outside the window.
“Passengers” indeed seemed to provide effective protection from external threats.
“This thing, I wonder what’s so special about it.”
Colin shook his head, shifting his focus away and continued to wait.
About fifteen minutes later, the employee with the “Path of Progress·Vinnie” ID above her head, who had suffered lighter injuries, was the first to wake up.
She opened her eyes, first looking around in confusion, then quickly remembered, she had just shut her eyes for a brief nap before waking up again. It seemed like she might have been rescued?
That was when she suddenly noticed Queen Akasha next to her, severely wounded and wrapped in layers of branches, her eyes immediately reddened…
But before she could cry, a voice came from nearby.
“Now, tell us exactly what happened, why did you attack us before?”
Vinnie looked towards the voice, seeing a man surrounded by flames but not scorched examining her.
She quickly recalled some of the details before she fainted, watching the flames on Colin for a while, seemingly confirming something.
After about ten seconds, she began to explain the situation, bit by bit.
“Queen Akasha and I followed the Revelation to a special region where we found the broken train. Using it, we left The Eternal Land to seek help from someone destined to assist us, to save our people and to push our stagnant destiny forward…”
“But en route, Witch Laniweya from The Dusk Sect somehow discovered our plan and attacked us.”
“We were no match for the witch, and Queen Akasha was gravely injured protecting me. If it weren’t for her attempt to attack you and hastily disguising our identities to escape, perhaps, we wouldn’t have survived…”
“I am very sorry, our weakness has led to you being attacked…”
Vinnie’s back was filled with roots, making it hard for her to move, but she still did her best to bow her head in apology.
‘As I thought, it’s almost like I had speculated, we had been replaced…’ Colin nodded to himself, his brain operating at high efficiency to ponder several keywords in her story.
‘Revelation’, ‘The Eternal Land’, ‘saving’, ‘someone destined’, these on the face of it, have nothing to do with my mission, not even remotely related…
‘But why, when she mentions ‘someone destined’, does my spiritual intuition make me feel like she’s talking about me?’
‘Never mind, cleaning up messes is not something new to me…’
‘But the most crucial part is, could this ‘The Dusk Sect’ really be related to ‘The Night’?’
Colin was beginning to feel a headache coming on.
If he were to rank the enemies he least wished to encounter, “Night” would definitely be among the top.
After all, “Night” was at least as significant if not more significant than “Red Moon”. And fighting followers of “Red Moon” involved staking lives on the line, with participation being more important than success…
And all believers of “Night” he had encountered were incredibly powerful…
“This mission was clearly supposed to be a simple stop at the ninth station to fuel up, right?”
.
.
.
