After about three minutes, the turbulence gradually subsided…
“Hold on, I’m going to get something to prevent problems,” the “Lady of Thorns” said, and left the place. A few minutes later, Colin saw several black figures, bound by “Black Thorns,” being dragged into various train carriages.
After completing all this, the figure of the “Lady of Thorns” appeared again.
She actually knew that the figures could stabilize the train? Colin was astonished and asked curiously, “Speaking of which, I’ve always wondered, why are there figures inside the train?”
“You don’t know?” The “Lady of Thorns” looked at him in surprise, then remembered something: “Oh, I forgot, you’re not at C Level yet, but even C Level might not know this…”
“Let me put it simply, these shadows are actually related to ‘Night’…”
“Night?!” Colin’s pupils trembled slightly.
“Don’t be so scared; they’ve all been dealt with by a certain big shot, absolutely safe. One is placed in each train, and then, do you know what the windows of this train are made of?”
She paused for a moment, but before Colin could shake his head or say “no,” the “Lady of Thorns” continued to explain:
“Have you ever used crystals like ‘Analytical Lens’ or prognostication artifacts? Their effects are more or less the same. However, these have been modified, so only those who are non-company and harbor hostility can see through the windows…”
With that said, she didn’t need to explain further for Colin to understand the reason.
The moment a high existence peeks into something related to ‘Night’ through a “Analytical Lens” or the like,
then…
Colin couldn’t help but think back to a few months ago when he used an “Analytical Lens” to analyze the “Hunger” barrier, nearly ending up dead from being spotted.
“This design… is pretty clever,” Colin murmured, finally speaking out.
“But it’s not infallible. For example, if you stay on a few more stops and leave the protection range of that wall, despite the cost, there will be plenty of things willing to descend to erase your ‘bonfire’ seed.”
“Ah, that…”
Colin gained a deeper understanding of why the ‘Flame Bearer’ was so despised.
After that, he inquired about some knowledge above C Level…
“Is the company’s knowledge gap this severe now?” The “Lady of Thorns” glanced at him with surprise, as if shocked that he was ignorant of such basic knowledge that he had to ask her for information.
However, the “Thorn Lady” did give an explanation.
“As for Authority Levels above C, well, there’s nothing particularly special, it’s mainly about the positions assigned after C Level. If there haven’t been other reforms, then as far as I know, roughly… C Level allows for quite a large Spatial domain, plus there are some confidential projects. Give me a moment to sort this out; it’s really not easy to explain on the fly.”
The “Thorn Lady” thought for about ten seconds before she began to explain, using the method of “Inspiration”:
“First, the distribution of authority within the C Level depends on whether you’re part of the administrative or the Corps system, or something else. I’m not clear on the latter two because I’m in a clerical position. From a World Administrator as small as one world to as large as a planetary system, all theoretically fall within my Domain…”
Clerical? Colin was taken aback, this didn’t seem right.
“Oh, and you’re generally equipped with some celestial computers, ecological System Trees, and similar systems to assist with management. But mine were damaged during that special period, which is rather troublesome; I can’t even control the climate anymore.”
The “Thorn Lady” said, “That’s about all I understand for now, I’m not too clear on higher levels. I’m currently at C+ Level, so I only know the situation within C+…”
“C Level? You’re only at C Level?”
Colin’s eyes widened in disbelief. How could this be? That couldn’t be right.
“You’re at the strength of a legitimate First Level Containment Subject, how can you only be at C Level? The C Levels I’ve seen before seemed to be not much different from me?”
“C+! I’m at C+! What you must have encountered are C-, which are quite below me.”
The “Thorn Lady” emphatically reminded, with a snort:
“Moreover, you’re looking at this purely in terms of combat capability, but the range between levels is quite wide. Some externally hired employees in the Corps who are stronger than me are only at D+, at most they might have some temporary special authorization at C Level or higher, but officially speaking, they definitely don’t rank as high as me…
“Seeing me, they still have to politely call out ‘Leader, hello’.”
“Comparison should be within the same System. My area is about management scope and abilities and such. If we were to consider combat strength, maybe the Corps System would regard it more highly.”
“Oh wow…”
Colin scratched his head, which meant, if the “King of Madness” were to be released, it seemed he would be just a D Level staff?
That would indeed make him the ultimate D Level.
At least, that was the case on Earth for now.
‘So the competition for the limited positions was this intense back then, even a subject of the First Level Containment that surrendered could only be slotted into D Level initially, unable to receive a higher rank…’
Colin didn’t know whether to remark on how competitive the company was back then, or to marvel at the abundance of talent within the company.
“However, some special directly governed areas require a C+ who has temporary B Level work experience for management, and within a star system, there will be multiple C Level Administrators, not like me in the middle of nowhere, all alone.”
“Oh, not just me alone. I used to have two deputy Administrators under me mainly to handle affairs, but they were later transferred to the main company and they haven’t returned them to me.”
“Anyway, there’s a lot of intricacies to this whole thing…”
The “Thorn Lady” explained some special circumstances.
Colin felt somewhat baffled as he listened, but one thing seemed certain: C Level was the backbone of the management layer…
Someone like the “Thorn Lady” at C+ Level was indeed among the upper echelon.
As for combat capability, although the “Thorn Lady” said she was clerical and might not be good at fighting,
the base level was there, so no matter what, she wouldn’t be bad.
“If what’s managed by C Level is already so broad, how much more exaggerated are B and A Levels?” Colin clicked his tongue in wonder.
“Not sure, A Level, I’ve heard, is already manipulating various macroscopic conceptual stuff, that’s Level ‘0’ Territory. Anyway, it’s beyond my comprehension, but if you’re curious, I’ll look around when I head out to see if I can contact some people and tell you more in the future.”
The “Thorn Lady” said this while looking at him, swinging her fair feet.
.
.
.
More to come.

chapters.title: Chapter 679 - 679 500 Lady of Thorns Compensation Reward_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 679: Chapter 500 “Lady of Thorns” Compensation Reward!_1 Chapter 679: Chapter 500 “Lady of Thorns” Compensation Reward!_1 “A conceptual thing, huh?”
“First Level Containment Subjects tend to be special demonstrations of certain rules, and the higher they are, the more abstract they seem to become…” Colin thought pensively.
At that moment, Lady of Thorns suddenly thought of something, “Speaking of which, you always seem to use containment levels to measure combat capabilities and stuff, hahaha~”
Before she could finish, she couldn’t help covering her mouth with one hand and clutching her belly with the other, laughing out loud.
“Is there a problem?” Colin asked in surprise, looking at her.
It didn’t seem like there was anything particularly funny?
“It’s not very accurate, well, the key is not about being accurate or not. Let me give you an analogy: every time I hear you describe someone’s containment level… it sounds a bit like you’re saying ‘My strength is now as strong as a three-month-old pig in the pigpen, and I’m as strong as that old hen in the chicken coop,’ and when you just now said I’m genuinely at the strength of a First Level Containment Subject, it’s like saying I’m as strong as a pig that can bite a tiger to death, hahaha…”
Lady of Thorns didn’t seem to take offense, she just found it highly amusing, and laughed so hard that she was rocking back and forth, with her smooth feet shaking rapidly under her long robe.
“Ah, this…”
“But it’s normal to encounter this sort of thing.”
The Lady of Thorns gradually stopped laughing, and her feet stopped swinging:
“Our actual combat strength is calculated by stages. For example, I estimate your strength is around level ten, and I’m at sixteen or seventeen. As for those you were talking about, theoretically, they should have quite high power levels, but they act like a bunch of kids wielding knives and guns who don’t even know how to turn off the safety, so there’s no point in comparing…
“But… continue to use your own system for exchanges.”
Another evaluation system? Colin suddenly felt overwhelmed, but hearing the latter part got him curious, “Why?”
“Because the system that does the evaluation is probably gone now. Without a reference, it’s like a scale without weights; you can’t use that system to measure combat power anymore, so just keep evaluating in your way. At least there’s still a reference point, it’s just, hahahaha…”
Lady of Thorns couldn’t help but laugh again.
Nevertheless, after the brief diversion, Colin asked about other matters, like the status of Lady Bunny.
Both were in administrative roles, so perhaps she would know more?
“Her? I too find her quite mysterious. I can’t be certain about the rest, but it’s confirmed that she’s at least Authority Level B, higher than my former leadership level, and…”
Lady of Thorns said this, and then suddenly lifted her hand to stroke her chin as if hesitant to continue.
“And what?” Colin couldn’t help but ask.
“Well, it was quite nice of her to send someone to assist me, but I feel her main purpose in helping me is probably something else. As for what that something else is, I can’t say for sure right now—it might be to obtain the item that was placed in the ruins and later taken by you, or it could be something else, but I’m not certain, so I won’t give you any unfounded answers…”
“Alright then.”
Colin nodded, then felt as though there were still some things he hadn’t remembered.
Lady of Thorns, sitting in the seat opposite him, looked at him as if wanting to say something else.
But at this moment, Colin finally recalled what he hadn’t remembered:
“Speaking of which, you seemed to have promised me some sort of remuneration?”
When withstanding the pressure from The Night, this “beautiful girl” had mentioned several times that she would offer compensation.
“I’ve been chatting with you for so long, how do you still remember that? Why do you have such a good memory?” Lady of Thorns blinked.
“So, what is my reward?”
“Ahahaha…”
“You didn’t just say it at the time and have actually nothing prepared, did you?”
“Oh my, how could that be? Let me think, I just forgot for a second…”
Speaking of which, “Lady of Thorns” pretended to ponder for a moment.
Right then, Colin seemed to have thought of something. His gaze quickly swept over “Lady of Thorns,” not out of any interest in her appearance, but focusing on the thorns that adorned her body.
He remembered clearly that the flames that burned those were quite nice.
Very vigorous and big flames!
“Hisss…”
Feeling the burning desire for flame that Colin’s eyes conveyed, “Lady of Thorns” couldn’t help but shiver for no apparent reason.
“Don’t even think about it!”
“Lady of Thorns” raised her voice slightly, and her shaking little feet retracted immediately back into the robe:
“Not even a single toe of mine will you get to burn!”
It had been a special situation before, and giving some was fine, but using this as a reward now was impossible!
“But you did promise a reward before…”
“Alright, alright, I won’t go back on my word, you take this.”
“Lady of Thorns” sighed and then above her head, a dark halo-like thorn ring appeared, radiating a black light.
She reached out her right hand, and took off the darkly gleaming thorn ring.
“This is a device I made myself. I call it the ‘Crown of Suffering.’ Its main effect is that it can transfer the damage you’re currently suffering onto the ring. How much it can transfer depends on you. On average, it’s about ten times your own capacity. Besides, your body’s endurance should be able to double or even quintuple. I specifically mean you…”
“There’s also some resistance to mental damage and the like, though that’s not the main feature.”
“Furthermore, if you’re barefoot on the ground, it can transfer the physical damage you suffer to the ground. The stronger the ground you touch and the larger the area, the better the transfer effect…”
Is that why you walk around barefoot?
Upon hearing this, Colin subconsciously glanced at the part of her foot that protruded from her robe, revealing just a few toes.
And just when he thought she would give him the entire “Crown of Suffering,” he realized that “Lady of Thorns” was only emitting a certain amount of power from it, making the thorns grow and form a long strip.
She picked the long strip off, manually wove it into a ring, and handed it over.
“Forget about the one I’m wearing. It has some abilities that are exclusive to me. Also, it bears billions of ‘sufferings’ which I have to slowly grind away. If you were to put it on, I’m afraid that in the next second you’d be reduced to dust.”
“It’s that dangerous, huh.” Colin took the “Ring of Suffering” woven from the freshly sprouted branches.
Brand new, with no instructions…
He couldn’t be certain if “Lady of Thorns” was correct about its features.
But holding it in his hand, it seemed about right, and when he got back, perhaps “Lady Bunny” could help assess it for him.
“Of course, if you guys really can’t use it, you can always burn it as firewood.”
“Lady of Thorns” sounded utterly disdainful of such a practice.
….
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 680 - 680 501 Approaching Station No. 9_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 680: Chapter 501: Approaching Station No. 9!_1 Chapter 680: Chapter 501: Approaching Station No. 9!_1 ‘How could one tarnish a person’s innocence for no reason? Why would I burn it as firewood if there’s nothing wrong with it? It’s an artifact, after all…’
Colin grumbled in his heart, feeling that this “Lady of Thorns” had too much prejudice against the “Firebearers.”
Moreover, that was something those “Firebearers” did, which had nothing to do with him.
They were them, and he was himself, and the two shouldn’t be conflated.
And up until now, he hadn’t burned any artifacts at all.
Buying those things had cost real silver, and Colin felt he wasn’t quite that wasteful yet.
Then, he took another look at the “Ring of Suffering” that was full of short thorns and identical to the “Lady of Thorns'” own, and put it on his head as suggested.
The thorns pierced the skin immediately upon contact, causing a slight, sharp pain.
‘My scalp that could withstand a heavy truck just got pierced like that?’
Colin was surprised in his heart.
Then, with curiosity and amazement, he asked, “By the way, if I just wear it on my head like this, won’t it easily fall off?”
In high-intensity battles, it seemed like a situation that could easily occur.
“As long as you put it on and connect with it, generally speaking, it certainly won’t fall off. Not even if your head does,” the “Lady of Thorns” replied, sitting on the high chair, with her arms crossed over her chest, revealing a teasing smile at the corner of her mouth.
“Of course, if you’re really scared of it falling, you can also put it around your neck, and then I can give you a ‘Thorn Lock’ as well, and then it would be like leading a… haha…”
While speaking, she couldn’t help but laugh a few times joyfully, as if the thought conjured up an amusing image.
Colin ignored her teasing, letting the Little Maid reach out her hand towards the ring to see what would happen under the circumstance that he didn’t want it to fall…
Soon enough, he confirmed that the situation was indeed much as the “Lady of Thorns” had described.
Once he put it on, it was tightly connected to him; even if he didn’t wish it, an enemy might invert his skull and still not be able to remove it.
Additionally, Colin felt an indescribable lightness in his body the moment he put it on—
All the gravity his body was subjected to seemed to be transferred to the ground at that instant.
This was different from just standing on the ground.
Colin waved his hand. Normally, he would have felt a slight resistance from the air, but this time, although the impact on reality was still the same, that sense of resistance was gone…
Everything was transferred to the soles of his feet.
Watching the “Lady of Thorns'” little feet swing back and forth, Colin suddenly felt the urge to try stepping on the ground with slippers as well.
But after pondering for a moment, he still refrained from doing so.
“It’s a strange sensation…”
Colin couldn’t help murmuring. It was unclear to what grade this artifact would be assigned, but if nothing went wrong, it most likely hadn’t been restricted and was nearly in a state of “Item Liberation.”
The magnitude of its power was rather high.
And wearing this ring made his physical body and spirit, etc., become remarkably “solid” all at once.
It was like the loose filling of a dumpling being tightly sealed by the dumpling wrapper.
A bit of mental energy or anything wouldn’t easily dissipate…
After some simple testing, Colin confirmed that it truly was a good object. With “Deadly Insight,” he didn’t much fear taking the initiative, and with this object, even if someone took the initiative, it probably wouldn’t have much of an effect on him.
It suddenly made him very “sturdy.”
“I didn’t lie to you, did I? It’s a good thing,”
“Lady of Thorns” spoke with a bit of pride, confident in her own handiwork.
“Mm…”
Colin nodded as well, removing items and placing them in the “Storage Room” as he asked, “Then, does it have any side effects?”
“There are some,” came the reply. “For instance, the damage you carry doesn’t completely vanish. You’ll need to find time to gradually wear it away, simply put, if someone punches you, you can distribute the injury’s damage over several instances at different times.”
“Of course, you can also choose to let the ‘Ring of Suffering’ take the hit, but it wears down the item’s integrity, and if it hasn’t been modified by a master craftsperson, only I can repair it. But you can’t always find me when you need to…”
“So, it’s up to you whether you want to use it for a long time or just take on a single instance of damage…”
“Lady of Thorns” pondered as she spoke, “Right, this is a new sprout; some of its functions haven’t emerged yet. Later on, you can nurture it with some ‘Colorless Crystals’ or the like. It should gain some other abilities in the future, such as transferring someone else’s ‘suffering,’ ‘pain,’ and so on to oneself…”
‘I’d have to be out of my mind to transfer someone else’s injuries to myself.’
Colin spoke up, “What about transferring it to someone else?”
“That’s possible, but you can’t do that. Those are more advanced techniques. However, if you really want to learn, it’s not impossible…”
“Lady of Thorns” clasped her hands in front of her and rubbed them together, revealing a mischievous smile.
Even though Colin felt it wouldn’t be anything good, he couldn’t help but ask.
“It’s simple; give up the ‘Bonfire,’ become my successor. If you do succeed, those things inside of you can also be transferred out…”
“Forget it.”
Colin decisively interrupted, shaking his head.
In these chaotic times, he preferred to be more of a fighter, rather than one who takes hits.
Plus, “Firebearers” seemed to be getting stronger continuously in this era. Who the hell would choose a version from an ancient, outdated era?
“Such a pity, sister here had prepared a gift for you.”
“Lady of Thorns” twirled a strand of hair with her index finger, her face showing a hint of regret.
Colin had no interest in the “gift” proposed by this lady who liked to make empty promises. He didn’t look at her but shifted his gaze instead to the train window that was still obscured by thick fog:
Who knows how much longer this train will take to reach the ninth station…
After some thought, he inquired about “2044.”
“2044′? Hmm, are you referring to the ‘Ultimate Time’? That’s some of the knowledge that circulated within the company…”
“Lady of Thorns” paused, blinking before her tone changed:
“But for specifics, you should ask the one behind you when there’s time. She’ll let you know when you need to.”
“Alright.”
Colin shook his head in mild disappointment.
It was evident that “Lady of Thorns” knew something, but for some reason, she seemed reluctant to share.
Without dwelling too much on this, Colin took advantage of the following time to continue chatting with her.
To gain as much knowledge about the company, or various other enemies, as possible…
Time also passed bit by bit amidst the conversation.
After six or seven more hours, Colin and “Lady of Thorns” simultaneously sensed a slight change in the speed of the consistently steady-moving train.
This meant…
“The ninth station, we’re almost there.”
Colin looked out the window still shrouded in dense fog, muttering to himself.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 681 - 681 502 The Blockaded Railway Line._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 681: Chapter 502: The Blockaded Railway Line._1 Chapter 681: Chapter 502: The Blockaded Railway Line._1 With a “click,” the train door slowly opened under Colin’s tense gaze…
Beyond the door lay an expansive, vast world dark yet not completely black, thanks to the dazzling starry sky.
“Lady of Thorns” glanced casually outside, then withdrew her gaze and briefly explained:
“I’ve been here a few times before. If I remember correctly, there used to be a transfer station — well, it’s called a station, but it’s more like a small fortress world. But now it seems to have completely fallen…”
Hearing her words, Colin, who had been on alert, was taken aback as he looked at the empty expanse outside:
“There’s nothing left here. Can you still recognize it?”
“Look at the star map. Although there are some deviations from before, such deviations are not significant over just a few hundred years, so my guess should be correct. Why, can’t you read it?”
After “Lady of Thorns” finished speaking and saw him shaking his head, she couldn’t help but laugh and said, “It seems like another one who’s lost in the universe without a train, unable to find even the way home. Have her give you a copy of the star map model when you have time; otherwise, if the enemy tosses you out into space, you won’t even be able to find your way back.”
“Lady Rabbit” would need one too… Colin muttered in his heart.
Then “Lady of Thorns” continued, “Since it’s so clean here, either the entire region was dragged into the ‘Primordial Fire’ through an ‘Extermination Order’ issued by a ‘Flame Bearer,’ or it was something else…
“But for now, it seems to be safe.”
“You previously mentioned the target mission is at station nine. So, are you getting off?”
“No need; I’m going to enter the ‘fuel chamber’ right here on the train. I can complete it aboard…”
As Colin spoke, he pulled up the previous mission and double-checked it:
Ride the “Train in the Fog,” tear open this “Envelope 1” at the ninth stop, enter the special train compartment, and place the “Token” inside the compartment’s fuel chamber…
“I see…”
“Lady of Thorns,” seeing him take out a yellowed “envelope,” thought for a moment and then suddenly said:
“Wait a minute, make some preparations first to avoid any accidents. It’s not that I don’t trust the abilities of ‘Flame Bearers,’ but I also believe in their ability to find trouble.”
Clearly, she had heard quite a lot about the exploits of “Flame Bearers.”
In the midst of their conversation, “Lady of Thorns” waved her hand, and a secret force rippled out.
The next instant, countless thorns rapidly grew from inside the train, binding thousands of compartments in place. It seemed to not only stop the train but also to protect it, shielding it from the outside elements.
All former “Night” believers with thorns on their heads felt their eyelids grow heavy and heard a gentle whisper from “God” in their ears:
“Sleep well for now.”
Then, one by one, they fell into a deep slumber.
The “thorns” on their heads spread like spider webs throughout the train compartments, covering every inch of space…
After making the protective measures, “Lady of Thorns” then turned to Colin: “The train won’t move until you’re done with your business. Take your time preparing.”
“Thank you.”
Colin nodded. Although “Lady of Thorns” seemed to have some biases against “Flame Bearers,” in this aspect…
He agreed.
Tasks related to “Flame Bearers” usually involved all sorts of trouble.
Even if he wasn’t a “Flame Bearer” himself, but just a reservist, he couldn’t escape this fate either…
After learning that the train would stop for a while, Colin was no longer so urgent and began to prepare calmly.
First, he took out a “Colorless Crystal,” then various items, “Favor of the Flame Bearer,” grease, a revolver, and so on, and so forth…
All sorts of items were orderly re-attached by Colin.
“Tsk tsk tsk…”
“Lady of Thorns,” sitting to one side with one hand propped under her chin, clicked her tongue in wonder: “When I first felt you approaching, my first thought was that the old folks above had gone senile, sending a reservist over; I had no idea what they were thinking…”
“Then I realized something wasn’t quite right about this reservist. You could withstand a bit of the ‘Night’s’ will’s spread. At that time, I couldn’t show my face, and I didn’t know the situation. Now I find that your equipment is surprisingly abundant…”
“These things combined give you the appearance of a ‘Flame Bearer’s’ fighting ability.”
Although lacking compared to the real deal, inexplicably, by putting together a bit of this and that, a semblance of a “Flame Bearer” was created, like a patchwork warrior.
About ten minutes later, Colin made all the preparations, readying himself for explosive action at any moment.
With any anomaly, he could “ignite” at any time.
After one last check and finding no issues, Colin snapped two fingers, temporarily using his “Little Maid” substituted left hand to pinch the letter, and his right hand to take hold of the other side, tearing it open along the sealed edge…
“Huh?” To his surprise, there seemed to be nothing inside?
As Colin thought this, suddenly, a wispy, lively thread of gray smoke emerged, slowly drifting toward the middle section of the carriage and began to swirl.
Before long, it formed into a dense fog swirl about three meters in height.
Behind the swirl, a doorframe without a door appeared.
Through the door lay a wide, mist-filled corridor, roughly twenty to thirty meters long, with a spacious room faintly visible at the end.

chapters.title: Chapter 682 - 682 502 The Blockaded Railway Line._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 682: Chapter 502: The Blockaded Railway Line._2 Chapter 682: Chapter 502: The Blockaded Railway Line._2 It was just because of the fog that it was impossible to see clearly what lay beyond.
“This mist can block those who aren’t from the company, but for us, it’s not a big problem. We’ve come this far; I’ll walk with you,”
“Of course, I’ll need to protect my account from the outside and switch to a different one to go in with you.”
“Thorn Lady” said, as a shadow emerged beside her, almost identical to her in appearance.
‘Why does everyone seem to have this ability to create a duplicate…’ Colin watched with some envy.
Letting a “duplicate” face danger was obviously safer than doing it yourself.
Unfortunately, he had yet to find the right item or Talent Skill that could create a duplicate, so he could only watch.
However, after thanking her, Colin, with flames leaping around him, stepped through the gate.
The “Thorn Lady’s” “alternate account” followed behind.
Along the way, Colin walked cautiously, but other than poor visibility due to the fog, he encountered nothing else.
Behind him, “Thorn Lady” seemed much more relaxed, following silently with bare feet.
“Logically, since this mist hasn’t completely cleared, it means no one has broken through. So, inside, it should be safe unless something unexpected happens,”
“Thorn Lady” murmured while looking around casually.
But no sooner had she finished speaking than Colin suddenly stopped, and the fire around him flared brightly.
She followed Colin’s gaze and saw, in a corner of the burning room, about a dozen adults lying on the ground, both men and women, eyes closed, apparently asleep, unresponsive to the two newcomers.
“Dead.”
“Dead.”
Colin and the “Thorn Lady” spoke in unison.
Working it over for a couple of seconds, “Thorn Lady” shook her head and then added,
“They seem to have been dead for quite some time, probably preserved because of the uniqueness of this place.”
“Right.”
Colin nodded, assuring there was no danger, and crossed the threshold into the room.
But as his foot crossed, some kind of spatial balance within the “burning room” seemed to be disrupted, and the bodies of the dozen adults instantly turned to dust, crumbling into ash on the ground like sand castles hit by water.
Then, only about a dozen nameplates lay scattered on the floor.
Colin glanced at them, seeing only names.
But the “Thorn Lady” spoke up,
“Nine D Levels, four F Levels, and their silver outfits suggest they’re from some Corps’ style, just not sure which one.”
As she finished speaking, a mission popped into Colin’s mind.
The content was roughly: “Collect all nameplates and other remnants into the ‘Storage Room’ to be automatically handed over at the end of the mission.”
“I’ll collect their remains.”
Colin stepped forward, first bending down to pick up the “nameplates,” then using flames to sweep up all the “ashes,” dazzlingly combining them before putting them into the “Storage Room.”
At that moment, he noticed some unknown script written on the ground nearby.
The rough meaning was…
“Please take care of… the children on that train?”
Colin murmured softly to himself, then, puzzled, asked, “Which children?”
“Oh, that, it’s referring to the people currently on the train,”
“Thorn Lady” leaned over to take a look and explained, “When I did that mission, the invisible impact had already started, although it was in the early stages. The biggest people on the train were mostly kids around fifteen or sixteen, as well as some very young children in incubators…
“The rest of the employees, I heard, had gone out to meet the enemy.”
She briefly described the situation at that time, which also helped Colin understand why there was a disruption in the civilization of that group of people.
Afterward, “Thorn Lady” crossed her arms in front of her and suddenly remembered something:
“Come to think of it, I recall an old story. Long ago, I heard that someone within the company created something that could, supposedly, continue the lives of the fallen if their nameplates were successfully retrieved.”
“Eh?” Colin, just getting up, was stunned. “What’s that?”
“I’m not too clear on it. It seems to be related to someone associated with ‘fate’… I think?”
“Boss Huang He?” Colin mentioned a somewhat ominous name.
“Not sure, I just know there was such a saying. It does involve something quite famous, ‘Script City,’ I’m not sure if you’ve heard of it…”
Hiss, where have I heard of this before? I almost dedicated my life in there…
Colin did not explain, but nodded to show he knew about the unlucky device.
“I heard that the fates of the names borne by those nameplates might possibly be reshaped within, but whether that is true is not clear to me. I joined the company quite late, and it seemed like the company as a whole was on the decline…”
“According to the company… it’s a bit like what my former aide-de-camp said, something about joining the army in ’49, yes, it’s about joining at the wrong time… ”
“Then for the most part, I just stayed put on my own little patch, never really went out, so I’ve not seen the corresponding results.”
“Lady of Thorns” tilted her head and spoke while thinking.
‘Joined the country in ’49, in the army, right? Is this aide of yours a fellow countryman?’
Colin silently completed the other party’s sentence in his heart.
Then, from this topic, he suddenly thought of “Big C Teacher” Kong Shiping, who was currently in the copy.
If “Lady of Thorns” meant resurrection in this sense…
Then the significance wasn’t all that great.
Rather than resurrection, it was more like a virtual NPC created using some information.
“As far as I know, the only one who truly caused a ‘return from the dead’ kind of miracle…”
Colin paused and uttered the words “Red Moon”.
Even “Father of the Ocean” could be resurrected with a body so decomposed, a miraculous method like that, he had only seen with “Red Moon”.
But no sooner had he finished speaking than he saw “Lady of Thorns” with her arms crossed and a “what are you looking at” expression staring at him.
Colin touched his nose awkwardly, feeling it was indeed not quite right.
How could “Red Moon”, with that ghostly appearance, possibly desire to help them resurrect others?
“However…”
“Lady of Thorns” broke the awkward atmosphere, “If you can figure out the situation later, you must remember to tell me.”
After speaking, she blinked with some anticipation.
“Alright, I’ll ask around and let you know when I get a chance next time.”
Colin did not refuse the request.
It’s just that, I don’t know when the next meeting will be.
He turned around, glanced around, and saw a fuel delivery slot. He walked over, sized up the inside to confirm this was the place, and then took out the “Token” from the “Storage Room”—
A copy of Rosen’s severed hand.
“Lady of Thorns” showed some surprise upon seeing the hand that burst into flame as soon as it was brought out, then some data floated up on her retina, and she roughly guessed the nature of the other party’s task.
Colin did not hesitate to toss the “Token” into it.
After it fell into the fuel chamber, a “boom” roared out and flames spurted from the slot.
[Event completed, do you choose to return (forced return in 2 minutes and 58 seconds)?]
“It seems I’m about to go back.”
Colin did not return immediately, but turned to say goodbye to the little subordinate that “Lady of Thorns” brought along with her.
“Lady of Thorns” raised her hand and waved:
“Goodbye.”
As the words fell, Colin’s figure and the voices of all the other employees executing tasks on the train vanished without a trace in an instant.
“That was a clean disappearance…”
“Lady of Thorns” pursed her lips, shook her head, took back the little subordinate, and then sat on the high chair. She did not rush to disengage the device to leave, but instead pondered and shook her pure and unblemished feet in thought.
After a while, recalling the sensation of the hand bursting into flames, she mulled it over, and then looking at the dim world outside, she mused to herself:
“I originally thought it was a simple fight to regain control over this area’s railway tracks…”
“But… it seems not.”
“She seems to be completely blocking the passage to a certain direction?”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 683 - 683 503 Gene Compensation Panel Open Beta
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 683: Chapter 503 “Gene Compensation Panel” Open Beta Test!_1 Chapter 683: Chapter 503 “Gene Compensation Panel” Open Beta Test!_1 “The seal seems quite dead; no one can pass through by any means. It’s just unclear who it’s supposed to be warding off…”
“Thorn Lady” saw strings of information rapidly scrolling in her eyes, informing her that in this instant, while the surroundings appeared unchanged, in a certain sense, they had become a “dead end,” and the related “blockade” was still being layered on top.
It seemed to be cutting off all possibilities…
The myriad “gazes” that filled the universe and traveled with the starlight were also becoming increasingly blurred.
On this path, silent collisions occurred in dimensions beyond human perception.
As a result, the woman standing behind the “Flamebearer” reserves had temporarily gained the upper hand.
But such a blockade…
“Thorn Lady” wasn’t quite clear what it was for.
She had been on that planet far too long and was still uninformed about many things.
“Forget it, it seems to have little to do with me now…”
“Thorn Lady” stopped swinging her ankle, leapt down from the high chair, waved her hand, and all the thorny vines began to retract, as the train’s halted motion began to recover again.
She planned to visit a few places to try and find some old friends and take care of the train’s followers.
However, just as the train’s restrictions were lifted, the doors closed, and she was about to move,
an additional message suddenly appeared before her eyes.
[Alert! Unless unforeseen, this section of the train will connect with “Fog Train-4045-99” in 57 minutes and 32 seconds, switching tracks and adjusting the route. Please “employee number 9999999″…]
“Refuse.”
Just by glancing at that train code, “Thorn Lady” chose to refuse.
Even though that route might help her reach her destination more quickly, she had learned from Colin that the train seemed to have some strange issues now…
If it merged into the main system, many things would become passive.
Rather than that, she preferred to be in control.
“As an administrator and protector of all the disaster victims aboard this train, I request the temporary activation of ‘manual control’ rights for this train.”
“Thorn Lady”‘s gaze swept over datum after datum.
She began to manipulate some rights over this section of the train through her own authority and the “branch office.”
…
Meanwhile, Colin also returned to the real world in an instant.
Opening his eyes…
It was the familiar ceiling.
Colin’s expression was dazed for a few seconds before he vigorously shook his head and sat up quickly, first checking the calendar clock on the wall next to him.
“January 16th, just past 8:30 AM. Yeah, about three days have gone by, so this time the mission lasted roughly one-to-one. Hmm, in a couple of days, I’ll have to head to ‘World Code-13’ again…”
After letting his thoughts run for a moment, Colin took a deep breath, then sat still for a few minutes.
Then he took out the parchment.
At this moment, the fourth event popped up:
[Go to a solitary island in the southern part of Bengkulu Bay on January 20th. After the ritual of the “South Sea Bodhisattva” followers on the island begins, throw the “token” into the opened passage, and deal with all heretic believers…]
“Note”: Stay hidden, seize the opportunity when the passage opens to reappear.
…
“Huh? No mission settlement this time!”
Colin had been thinking about what rewards he might get, only to realize that the “Fifteenth Ring” major task had not yet been completed, so there was no settlement; it would all be resolved when everything was done.
After grumbling for a bit, Colin composed himself and looked at the new task.
“Oh heck, next week, I’m off to lend a hand again…”
He shook his head, not feeling surprised—
Pretty sure all the upcoming tasks will involve going to different places to leave a hand.
Until all fifteen tasks are completed.
No telling just how many “copies” that “copy” made.
However, Colin was certain without guessing that this kind of specialized task had something to do with “Lady Rabbit.”
But he had no idea why she was doing it…
Without her saying, it was very difficult to guess, and Colin didn’t waste much thought on it, instead manipulating the parchment with a wave of his hand, closing the task and opening the Storage Room.
“There are three portions of various branch office plant seeds. Sigh, seeing these things reminds me of the nine thousand points I laid out in advance. Oh, wait, these seeds…”
Colin casually picked up the seeds to have a look.
The quantity was the same as his previous purchase, and the content was the same, but the description was different—there were additional words and notes.
For example:
“‘Crazy Potato·Tuber·Cracked Version'”…
“Note”: This crop can produce seeds completely identical to the first generation (but it will consume significant energy, the amount of which the crop will disclose).
“Note 2”: Rapid growth; during special periods, it is possible to stimulate vitality through energy injection to hasten growth (taste may be compromised, but not the seed retention).
“…”
“There’s a cracked version of this thing?”
Colin looked astounded, recalling that once “Lady of Thorns” who was “Akasha” had said that if these things were planted, the seeds would decrease in quality over generations.
But upon returning, it seemed “Lady Rabbit” had resolved this issue.
Holding the “potato” seeds in hand and weighing them, Colin then took out his phone and sent Xu Duojin a message.
He asked him to come quickly to collect the agricultural gift package.
“If this thing could be widely disseminated, I fear that in the future, even if it were the end of the world, there wouldn’t be too much worry about food problems. Hmm, as long as there’s an employee present, seed retention can be carried out.”

chapters.title: Chapter 684 - 684 503
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 684: 503 Chapter 684: 503 Colin muttered to himself.
Of course, he also brought a set of seeds with him to “World Code-13”.
“Dealing with some anomalies, will arrive in the afternoon.” Xu Duojin’s message came back swiftly.
Colin glanced at it casually and then turned his attention back to the “Storage Room”. He found that this time the “Ring of Enduring Pain” had its item description updated.
The functional effect was quite similar to what the “Thorn Lady” had described, only now it was quantified with numbers to appear more precise.
“Seems like it hasn’t been graded, but by my estimate, it should also be one of the top items among the orange or purple ones.”
After reading it, Colin stored it away again.
Besides that, the nameplates and ashes in the “Storage Room”, as expected, were handed over.
As for the rest, there didn’t seem to be anything else worth noting.
He didn’t continue to look any further, but rather opened the Parchment Employee Exchange Hall as usual to secretly observe. He could see a bunch of people cursing about this and that, clearly very agitated…
“Damn it, this mission really sucks! They actually threw us in to get beaten to death by mobs of Mutated Bodies!”
“This is outrageous! Tens of millions of Mutated Bodies, and each of us has to fight hundreds or thousands, with just a damn hammer!”
“The key thing is, damn it, dying drops your rating, is this intentional by the company because they don’t want to give out good stuff?”
“Exactly, just over two thousand points, I feel like I could have made three thousand if I didn’t die!”
“Damn it, who was it that said they would break my hand before? I remember that voice. You better not let me catch you during a mission, or you’re going to regret it!”
“Hahaha, serves you right, who told you not to get on board earlier!”
“…”
“Ah, I really didn’t expect to actually come back through death in the end.”
Colin couldn’t help but laugh and cry at the same time.
Although he had guessed as much, actually seeing it still made him feel a bit overwhelmed.
However, looking around, it seemed that not everyone who remained had died and returned; some used the leftover terrain along with their items to barely scrape by and hang on until the end.
But such people were very few, less than five percent of those who undertook the mission at the time…
“They could be considered capable indeed.”
Colin felt that if there were to be dozens or even hundreds more missions like this, the people in the group could end up with experiences to rival those of the old employees from back then.
After watching for a while longer, he looked to see if there were any interesting items for sale.
Unfortunately, there didn’t appear to be anything worth buying…
“Next up is project number 18, ‘The Advent’, I need to give the Saintess a twenty-five thousand points cut for that, then there’s the courier mission on the 20th. Oh, and at the end of the month, there’s an official item trade mission.”
Muttering to himself, Colin didn’t feel like his schedule was particularly full, but neither was it empty.
He still wasn’t clear on the specifics of the courier mission…
It might be simple, or it might be difficult, but unlike the ‘Train Station Nine’ situation, the good thing about this mission was that it should be in the Earth world…
In that case, he could arrange for an aircraft carrier if needed.
Timing and location might be hard to say, but he ought to max out on cooperation.
Just as Colin was about to close the parchment, he suddenly saw a bold line of text pop up:
[Announcement! New function ‘Gene Compensation Panel’ is about to be updated and installed! All employees can unlock this function through ‘Character Profile’ by meeting respective requirements.]
….
“Huh? ‘Gene Compensation Panel’?”
Colin paused for a moment, then opened his “Character Profile”… his was already activated.
He had had this feature for quite some time, but since it required too many “Mission Vouchers”, even he found it difficult to fully satisfy the conditions for activation. Therefore, he had not really utilized it.
At most, he used its subsidiary function, which was for evaluating combat power.
He had previously used it on the “Thorn Lady”.
The results were visible during the early phases with “Akasha” and “Lavinia”, but later, when it came to the will-driven “Thorn Lady”, the results were all “?”
The reason might be that the opponent was too strong, or maybe they had some protection that prevented the inspection.
“I should leave this thing until the end to enhance. Right now, even if I max it out, it won’t make a huge difference.”
Colin took a quick glance and didn’t exhibit any emotional fluctuations.
However, compared to him, the chat channel was much more lively. After all, this was only the second time they had seen the company install a new function, and everyone was discussing it excitedly.
From their conversations, Colin roughly understood that their version seemed a bit different from his.
But the difference wasn’t particularly large…
For example, to initially open the panel, one had to spend fifteen hundred points and a Golden Mission Voucher. Then, the subsequent requirements for each upgrade were quite similar to his.
Both were on a level playing field.
The only difference might be the gap in personal ability.
If Colin wanted to accumulate enough to fill all the points in the “Gene Compensation Panel”, it wouldn’t be very difficult.
But for them… at least with their current progress, it would be a bit slower.
“Hope everything goes well for them.”
Colin grumbled, eyeing the chat messages. Many people spent a lot of money to unlock it, only to discover that the resources needed to upgrade were immense and that the improvements per upgrade were not very noticeable, which immediately frustrated them.
Of course, once the “Gene Panel” was unlocked, it meant an additional path, and overall, it did provide a decent enhancement.

chapters.title: Chapter 685 - 685 503 Gene Compensation Panel Open Beta
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 685: Chapter 503 “Gene Compensation Panel” Open Beta Test!_3 Chapter 685: Chapter 503 “Gene Compensation Panel” Open Beta Test!_3 It also motivated them more effectively.
However, this motivation had nothing to do with Colin.
After getting the general idea, he turned off the parchment, then began the feast that the little maid would prepare after each mission.
Day-to-day eating and drinking, filling the belly, excreting waste, he contacted Qin Chuan.
After asking around and making sure there was nothing amiss for the next two days, he sighed, “The environment is getting better and better,” then went back to observing those “pseudo-humans.”
Aside from their numbers seeming to have increased a bit, these anomalies hadn’t changed much during this period.
“It’s just that, I don’t know who brought it up, but they suggested trying out tieba, and one by one, they all ran off to mingle there…”
Colin felt the need to guide them, lest the “pseudo-humans” had their values corrupted by the abstract people.
Looking at it now, some people in the group were starting to talk in strange and off-putting ways.
It was time to step up the efforts to ban their accounts.
“A bunch of anomalies, led astray by humans…”
Colin shook his head, feeling it was still somewhat abstract.
Then, after confirming that there were no issues with the origins of these “pseudo-humans,” he ended the observation for the day.
He put away his phone, released “Yukionna,” opened the game, and began playing 7702.
It was just past midnight when the doorbell suddenly rang.
“Come in.”
As his words fell, Colin saw Xu Duojin, wearing dark sunglasses, walk in from outside. He pointed to a seat on the sofa across from him.
“May I ask what brings you here?” Xu Duojin asked after taking a seat.
“I’ve recently acquired some trinkets that, if all goes well, could bring a small impact to the world’s food supply,” Colin said.
As he spoke, Colin pointed to a drab-looking trinket on the table.
“Uh?”
Xu Duojin followed his gaze, paused, and at first glance, it looked like a potato. Unsure, he took another look. Yes, it seemed to indeed be a potato?
But since Colin said this thing could cause a global impact, he had to treat it seriously.
So, taking a third look, Xu Duojin lifted his sunglasses and squinted at it…
Well…
“Is this a potato?”
“Yes, you can also call it a ‘tater or a spud,” Colin nodded, and gave a simple explanation, then allowed the young-looking old man sitting opposite him to reflect in silence for a moment.
“I’m sorry, Mr. Colin, but I really can’t see what’s so magical about it, to do what you said, to bring an impact to the world.”
“Oh, I forgot you’re not from the company, you can’t see the information.”
Colin thought for a moment, took out a small piece of “Colorless Crystal” that hadn’t been used up, and directly injected it into the potato.
At this moment, Xu Duojin’s expression changed slightly, as he vaguely felt something.
Next, he watched as Colin took some water and poured it on the little potato piece: “Now it should be time to witness a miracle.”
No sooner had he spoken, than Xu Duojin’s eyebrows raised, and he saw purple-white sprouts emerging from the little potato.
Dozens of sprouts grew rapidly, like squid tentacles, writhing and stretching in all directions, seemingly searching for something…
However, this was merely a potato sprouting, at most a bit faster than usual. With some items, they could achieve this too; there was nothing strange about it.
What truly made Xu Duojin’s gaze freeze and him take a sharp breath was…
As those purple sprouts continued to extend and wiggle, he actually heard sinister whispers as if from an evil god, filled with a tyrannical tone—
“Soil! Soil! Soil!”
“Soil! I want soil!”
“Fuck, where the hell is the soil!?”
.
.
.
Seeking monthly votes…

chapters.title: Chapter 686 - 686 504 The statue of the Southern Bodhisattva
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 686: Chapter 504 The statue of the “Southern Bodhisattva” emitting a fishy smell. Chapter 686: Chapter 504 The statue of the “Southern Bodhisattva” emitting a fishy smell. Xu Duojin fell into silence.
He was unsure if this thing could cause an impact on the world, but sitting here, watching this potato exhibiting crazed, almost out-of-control behavior, he could clearly feel that it had definitely made a considerable impact on him.
At this moment, Colin stood up and walked to the balcony window, looked around, and then, with a motion of his hand, he summoned a succulent-filled flowerpot from the balcony of the neighbor to the left.
Afterward, holding the flowerpot, he turned around, preparing to pull out and discard the succulents inside.
But after a thought, he decided to burn them with fire into nourishment.
The potato’s frantic whispers also gradually ceased after the appearance of the little flowerpot.
Xu Duojin even saw that the potato didn’t require Colin to act; as soon as one of its sprouts touched the soil, it began to move in that direction on its own.
Its behavior resembled the soft and stranded squids on the beach or maybe starfish.
And during this process, some of the excess sprouts withered on their own before it began clamoring for fertilizer and water.
Colin had the Little Maid fly out and borrow some nutrient solution from the neighbors to water over its head.
Only then did the potato slowly stop its whispering and begin to grow contentedly…
Under the illumination of “Bonfire” and the irrigation of “Colorless Crystal” along with some basic fertilizers, it grew rapidly.
“How about it, in an emergency even three days, no, one day will be enough to see some yield!”
Colin pointed at the potato on the desk and said with a smile.
Hearing this, Xu Duojin looked down at the potato seedling humming softly under the glow of the firelight, then lifted his head, floated his sunglasses and looked at Colin, his voice tinged with skepticism:
“This… Is this really something to eat rather than to be contained?”
“Yeah, don’t judge it by its looks, but it is indeed edible,” Colin nodded.
“Right, right, I’m so clean, why can’t I be eaten?” the potato said as well.
Nurtured, its temper became much milder all of a sudden.
However, hearing the back-and-forth between the two, Xu Duojin again fell silent. He considered himself to be a major figure in the mysterious side of this world, having fought in battles north and south to achieve his status and seen many things. But today, he realized he might still be a bit ignorant.
Every time he stepped into this neighborhood and came into this room, Mr. Colin always managed to come up with something new.
“Sorry, I’m just…habitually cautious,” Xu Duojin thought hard for a while before he finally managed to squeak out a sentence under the watchful eyes of that man and that potato.
Otherwise, being constantly silent and reserved didn’t seem quite right.
“Don’t worry, my colleagues have already eaten it during a mission before,” Colin said, patting his shoulder, understanding Xu Duojin’s concerns.
After all, he too found it quite strange the first time he saw it.
But after seeing it often, he felt it was nothing special, and as far as he could tell, eating it shouldn’t pose any problems. His colleague seemed to be fine, as he had just seen him arguing with someone in the company’s internal group chat.
“If you’re not convinced, I can make it bear fruit rapidly now, cook you a plate of hot and sour potato strips to try a few bites,” Colin said, continuing as he noticed the hesitation on the other’s face.
Sometimes you need to have the experience before you can trust eating it.
“Yeah, yeah, I can grow you a small potato to taste right now,” the potato chimed in.
“Eh, no, no…”
Xu Duojin waved his hand, not waiting for the person and the potato to speak up, he quickly added: “If you don’t mind, may I take it back for everyone to study first?”
“That’s fine too,” Colin didn’t refuse.
After all, he was indeed planning to let others study it; it was just that the potato seedling seemed a bit reluctant…
“No way! I don’t want to leave Bonfire! Without Bonfire, I can’t produce delicious potatoes anymore ahhh!” the potato’s newly sprouted leaves trembled. If it had never seen Bonfire, it might have settled for fluorescent lights.
But now, it couldn’t endure being away, not even a little…
Seeing the potato’s slightly deranged state made Xu Duojin fall into silence once more, beginning to doubt.
If this thing were to spread, would it really be a good thing for this world?
No, what the hell does it actually produce, really potatoes?
Seeing the potato seedling somewhat frantic, Colin soothed it, assuring that it could bask in Bonfire for life, and that calmed it down.
The solution was simple, make a call for Qin Chuan to buy a couple of jin of gold and put it into the Bonfire.
“Don’t be fooled, this is just a form of intelligent reaction. Even if you take it away, it will be okay; it might complain a bit, but if it really doesn’t behave, just scold or threaten it, and it will calm down. At worst, it might be in a bad mood, affecting the taste slightly, but nutritionally, there’s absolutely no problem,” Colin said.
You think this is just a matter of taste and nutrition… Xu Duojin couldn’t help but ponder to himself.
However, he didn’t say much more, just nodded with difficulty, giving a superficial acknowledgment to Colin’s words.
Having agreed on the matters at hand, they moved onto other topics.
“About the matter of the big Buddha you mentioned, there have been some developments in the past few days; take a look if this is it,” Xu Duojin produced a photograph.
Colin took the photo and saw under the dim light, a Stone Buddha seated in the central area of an ancient town.
Only, in the photo, it seemed to be rising, as though preparing to stand up.
“Yes, that’s it, where is it?”
Colin nodded affirmatively, put down the photo, and looked at Xu Duojin, indicating he was ready to set out and “renew their past acquaintance.”

chapters.title: Chapter 687 - 687 504
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 687: 504 Chapter 687: 504 Back then, even separated by a train, that thing dared to look at himself and even provoked him, and Colin couldn’t bear to think what it would do next.
Seeing Colin about to set out, Xu Duojin waved his hand, signaling for him to remain calm, and then said:
“It’s okay, Mr. Wu took matters into his own hands and exiled it along with the small spatial area it was in… during your absence yesterday.”
“Old Master Wu, he exiled it?”
Colin raised an eyebrow, “Can it be brought back? I won’t feel at ease until this thing is burnt to ashes.”
“Uh, mainly because that thing is indeed a bit troublesome, and at one point it nearly invaded over, hard to deal with, so Mr. Wu exiled it…”
“But…” Colin still felt uneasy, it was too strange.
It wasn’t about how formidable it was but that inexplicable, spine-chilling feeling, similar to “fate”.
And from that one glance, he was aware that this wasn’t something that could be destroyed easily…
However, before he could speak further, Xu Duojin said, “Don’t rush, rest assured, Old Wu, oh, I misspoke, Mr. Wu has thrown it into a place from which it absolutely cannot escape, a place that can very tightly restrain it.”
The name “Old Master Wu”, others could address him that way, but those from “Fate Propeller” following suit…
With a few more mentions, their luck might take a slight turn for the worse.
As for why, nobody hinted at anyone specifically, surely only the knowledgeable understand.
“Which place?” Colin began to grow curious.
“Quite a while ago, we referred to it as the ‘chaotic unknown world of destiny,’ ‘world of the convergence of all things’ fate,’ and so on, but after the company appeared, we got a clearer and more accurate name… ‘City of Scripts’.”
Good heavens…
Colin was taken aback, they really restrained it thoroughly.
Playing with “fate,” “destiny”… “City of Scripts” might suppress it to the point of not being able to raise its head.
Even, perhaps after some time, “City of Scripts” might gain a beautiful girl sitting on a lotus dais, causing it to birth a new “human” self, thus achieving a harmless state like “Yukionna”, making it tameable…
It’s just unknown which of the script worlds of “City of Scripts” it was thrown into.
‘Hehe, if it ends up in “Script City: Horror Zone,” then those employees undergoing E-D Level promotion trials will be quite blessed.’
‘However, according to my knowledge, there’s a high probability it went to “Passionate Paradise”…’
Colin thought to himself, at the time he entered the incident, he had also seen heretic believers and some official personnel trapped within, with whom he had a certain level of cooperation.
Unfortunately, they weren’t in very good condition.
Without any accidents, the possibility of them still being alive now is quite low.
After all, back then, not just them, Colin and others nearly perished and failed to escape.
But more than that, Colin realized something from the conversation just now; the official investigation into “City of Scripts” seemed quite thorough, could Old Master Wu even utilize it to some extent?
This…
Colin pursed his lips, remembering he had once advised them to try not to have too deep of a contact with these things.
It seems Old Master Wu had listened, but only listened.
‘But then again, “Fate Propeller,” a pathway deeply tied to the “Book of Fate,” if it doesn’t have any interaction with “City of Scripts,” that would be odd…’
Taking a deep breath, Colin suppressed the thoughts flashing through his mind and directly asked:
“What do you guys know about this ‘City of Scripts’?”
“Asking me, you’re really asking the wrong person.”
Xu Duojin seemed to have anticipated this question, shaking his head while saying, “This is top-secret, in this world, the related investigation is personally conducted by Mr. Wu, besides him, we probably know less than you do.
“If you want to know, you could ask him, but most likely there won’t be an answer, as the matter is very dangerous, it entails the risk of contamination simply by knowing…”
“Alright.”
Colin didn’t continue to ask further, knowing he probably truly didn’t have the information.
As for Old Master Wu, he always found him mysterious, the only Level 9 “Fate Propeller” and the person closest to the suspected Level 0 entity that goes by the name of a book.
He seemed to, just like Lady Bunny, be arranging some unknown things through various events.
No one knew exactly what he was doing.
Even in a sense, they didn’t know whether it was good or bad.
Moreover, others couldn’t predict their actions at all, after all, something named “Book of Fate” was “standing” behind him; even the so-called ancient god’s descent couldn’t see through his thoughts.
“Speaking of which, after taking a walk outside, I realized that the most dangerous things seem to be here on Earth,”
Colin suddenly couldn’t help saying.
“Oh? The most dangerous things are here with us?”
Xu Duojin exclaimed in surprise. He had heard some company employees say that the “Descent Project” in other worlds was the most dangerous because the crises there had no upper limit.
From what he had heard, whether it was fighting aliens flashing red lights in outer space, constructing territories next to apocalyptic grey smog disasters, worlds made entirely of water, or gigantic starships, there were all sorts of weird worlds…
Listening to this, Xu Duojin felt it was magical, no, it was sci-fi.
If he didn’t know it was real, he would have thought it was fake.
But now, this “foremost authority on external exploration” suddenly said that Earth was the most dangerous after making the rounds, making Xu Duojin feel a bit panicked…
“Well…”
Colin thought aloud, “The thing is, the situations here haven’t blown up yet, but once they do, it’s hard to say.”
Here there’s “Red Moon,” and “Book of Fate,” unclear dealings with “City of Scripts,” and all the actions of Lady Bunny also seem to be arrangements made for this side.
Right, there’s also that “Rat” who smuggled in.
Even beyond Earth, there are many eyes casting their gaze through various means, attempting to come ashore.
So many miscellaneous things piled up together, and key is that none of them are minor; just picking one out could lead to an apocalyptic disaster…
“If it were to blow up, Earth, well, forget Earth, it’s hard to say whether the Solar System could withstand it,” Colin said without knowing why there was so much stuff accumulated here.
He guessed it probably had something to do with the company’s past people, but he was not quite sure.
However, if it was the company from that era, none of these issues would be problems, and even “Red Moon,” “Book of Fate,” and the like, which were unsolvable for them now, might probably have been just a game for the company back then.
End of the world or whatever…
If they dared to have such a notion, the company might turn them into a twin-tailed loli who can only say “meow” the next second…
But today is different from the past, the company staff disappeared in an instant, and fortune has taken a turn.
The unfortunate ones who can only say “meow meow meow” have become them.
“Don’t panic, everything is so stable now, as long as we’re careful, we should be able to maintain it for quite a while. When the company returns one day, all troubles will no longer be troubles…”
Colin simply comforted Xu Duojin and then shifted the subject:
“Right, have you gathered the information about that island in Bengkulu Bay and the corresponding situation?”
Before the other party arrived, he had inquired about the so-called Southern Bodhisattva information. With so much time passed, given Xu Duojin’s abilities, he should have been able to gather the intelligence.
“Yes.”
Xu Duojin did not disappoint, nodding his head and pulling out a strange statuette from his pocket:
“These heretic believers also appeared within our territory, but were expelled in the end. This is the entity they worshipped…”
Colin looked at the statuette, which had an octopus head, a human body, and was squatting on a square stone.
Holding the object in hand and examining it closely, there was a fishy smell of the sea.
It was somewhat sinister, but not much.
Then, he looked up at Xu Duojin, waiting for him to explain what exactly it was.
.
.
.
