chapters.title: Chapter 688 - 688 505 22000 Points_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 688: Chapter 505: 22,000 Points?!!!_1 Chapter 688: Chapter 505: 22,000 Points?!!!_1 “This is a rather widespread heretic force, with many branches of its existence. Most of them are located in coastal areas of various continents or on some islands…”
“Generally speaking, they are called ‘Sea Emperor’, ‘God of the Deep Blue Abyss’, ‘Doris from underwater’, ‘Savior of the Ocean’, ‘Southern Bodhisattva’, and so on. The specific nomenclature usually adapts to local customs and beliefs, but it’s essentially the same entity—at least current investigations indicate that the responses can be traced back to a single source…”
“However, just speaking of this ‘Southern Bodhisattva,’ we actually had one here too, but it has already been driven out by fire coverage.”
Xu Duojin pulled out a document and passed it to Colin, explaining as he looked it over.
“Yeah, the scale is quite large…”
Colin nodded, scanning the document in his hands—
It was a fascinating ancient existence with no specific physical form, nor an exact image. Essentially, it appeared as those who prayed to it conceived of it to be.
However, once the faithful gathered and unified their beliefs, their perceptions tended to merge.
The statue before him was the current manifestation of a subset of these people’s unified faith.
Colin just wasn’t sure why this group thought an octopus head looked imposing enough to sculpt their revered entity in such a pitiful, knee-hugging pose on a square stone.
After browsing the document, Colin set it aside and didn’t give it another glance.
Though he hadn’t made official contact yet…
Based on the faint traces of aura from the document, he couldn’t tell how powerful it was, but its seal seemed pretty tight.
“Are you suddenly investigating this because you have a mission?” Xu Duojin noticed Colin’s shifting attention from the document and asked, offering a tip:
“I was the one who drove them out initially. If you need anything, you can tell me directly.”“It’s nothing much, just a small matter.”
Colin waved his hand, indicating he didn’t need help—
Xu Duojin’s strength had not been revealed yet, but Colin estimated it to be about equivalent to three or five D Level operatives combined, certainly among the stronger ones like “Life Mentor Adorable” and “Master of the Fish Pond.”
Even so, if brought along and they encountered something, it would not be of much use beyond fighting minor foes.
And the official Extraordinary Ones…
Not to mention their strength, these people used their abilities at the cost of their lifespan.
Colin was genuinely concerned about bringing someone who looked about fifty but was actually only in their thirties and having them return looking more haggard than Old Master Wu.
Then, considering his current situation, only Ninth Level Personnel could provide effective assistance.
But with that ranking, they were strong…
Even with a favorable push, they might not make it back.
Just the act of maintaining sanity was enormously difficult for them.
However, after some thought, Colin said:
“It might be possible to dispatch some modern warships over there, I could use them when I need to later.”
While some anomalies could evade damage from conventional weaponry on their own, Colin could also use “Bonfire” to suppress the mystical attributes on them, revealing their bodies in reality and combining it with thermal weapons for efficient eradication.
Of course, this method could generally only be applied to anomalies with physical forms.
Some special anomalies have unique physical properties that are difficult to affect with such tactics, and there are even some that lack observable bodies altogether…
“Alright, I’ll think about it. Maybe we could conduct a peaceful exercise over there.” Xu Duojin nodded, not hesitating or finding it tough to agree to Colin’s idea of moving military power.
Perhaps over a decade ago, staging such a play would trigger all sorts of chain reactions.
But as the terror from anomalies grew worse, the status and influence of the Extraordinary Ones rapidly increased. Now, dealing with anomalies had become a top priority.
Under normal conditions, everything had to make way for the resolution of anomalies.
This event wasn’t geographically far and within their influence radius.
Even if there were objections, it didn’t matter if they couldn’t reach…
They just needed Old Master Wu to subtly hint that those making such requests would receive international assistance in clearing paths.
The technological value contained within the small box weighed tens of pounds was quite beneficial to everyone involved.
Add to that Colin’s special status within Bonfire Company…
To the extent that…
Although this young man hadn’t made many public appearances, there wasn’t a single power in the world benefitted by him that could afford not to give him face.
He could choose not to ask, but once he did, there had to be a response!
Xu Duojin had even heard that Old Master Wu was already assisting in obtaining personal authorization to use nuclear weaponry for Colin.
There was also a significant chance that it could truly materialize, making him the only individual with such authorization in the world.
But for now, there were still communications needed to reach a common consensus among nations to avoid a situation where Colin deploying a nuke leads to a reckless response that destroys the current ecological environment.
The necessary documents required thorough discussion, and only after this public notice period could any results come about.
Thinking of this, Xu Duojin looked at Colin and couldn’t help but inwardly marvel.
The gap between people really is wider than that between a person and a dog.
Not to speak of anything else, just the issue of nuclear warheads alone… if he had gone to Old Master Wu and mentioned he wanted to play with a couple himself, he’d probably get kicked so hard his brains would fly out.

chapters.title: Chapter 689 - 689 505 22000 Points_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 689: Chapter 505: 22,000 Points?!!!_2 Chapter 689: Chapter 505: 22,000 Points?!!!_2 Afterward, when that topic came to an end, Xu Duojin discussed the technological reproduction progress of various shelters.
“Currently, several critical areas have made clear progress, such as superconductors, some chip technologies, artificial intelligence, and aspects of mechanical involvement. There are also those flesh-grafting techniques and so forth…”
As Xu Duojin spoke, he thought of some human body-related technologies and couldn’t help shaking his head.
Many of these technologies required experimenting on humans, like the report he had seen which mentioned, “At the start of research, in a vast number of tests, less than ten percent of the cultivation hosts maintained vital signs after injection of the reagent, until the birth of new life with divine power factors…”
Cultivation hosts, specifically cloned through biotechnological means without intelligence, were used for various experiments.
In matters like these, Xu Duojin didn’t know whether to say these people valued life or disregarded it.
But no matter what…
The value of technology was still significant.
Having reported the corresponding information, Colin saw the Eighth Level Agent off.
Just as he turned to go upstairs, he could still hear the faint sounds of Little Potato from afar.
“Smelly old man, bring the bonfire closer!”
“Walk steadier, Old Deng; you’ve almost shaken off some of my roots!”
“I was planning on growing some big potatoes on this root when I got bigger, and now it’s broken! If I can’t grow potatoes, you can go drink the north wind!”
“…”
‘It feels like after “Lady Rabbit”‘s meddling, these crops are a lot livelier than in the world of “Lady of Thorns”.’
Colin couldn’t help but mutter, standing in the hallway and watching Xu Duojin leave dripping with sweat.
Afterward, he studied a bit more about the “South Sea Bodhisattva,” then casually set it aside and began to relax, rewarding himself with a few rounds of games.
Soon, two days passed, and it was the 18th.
Colin lay in bed, waiting in silence.
After a while, the distant and ancient sound of a bell slowly rang in his ears…
When he opened his eyes again, Colin saw that he had returned to the small but extremely bright chapel, illuminated by the bonfire.
Shortly after his arrival, dozens of ash-like figures burst from the great bonfire.
These particles of ash took human shape in mid-air, and upon touching the ground, each became an employee.
Colin glanced around, did not notice any reduction in staff, and nodded slightly.
“The main focus of this week’s task is still construction, no change from before, and here are the supplies for this week, you guys take and distribute them.”
“Additionally, those in charge of agriculture stay behind, I have some instructions for you.”
“Plant these seeds within the direct exposure range of the nearby bonfire…”
Colin handed the relevant seeds to the employees in charge.
“Is there anything special about these seeds?” asked a D Level staff member curiously as he took the plants from Colin.
The seeds looked ordinary, but upon close inspection, one could discover they actually came with item descriptions, and each seed had its own, suggesting they could talk?
Colin thought for a moment, ultimately deciding to let them discover for themselves: “Hard to say, try planting them first…”
After roughly setting the direction for their tasks, everyone left the small chapel and began their “willing” week of mule-like existence.
When everyone had left, Little Red, who had been poking her head around the chapel entrance, dashed into the chapel.
“Big brother~” Little Red threw herself onto Colin.
“Hmm.”
Colin patted her head and then retrieved her favorite One Lesson Three Practices from the Storage Room.
Seeing this, Little Red’s expression changed instantly.
“This is your homework for this week, hmm, you’re learning quite quickly, almost catching up with the first year’s content.”
“I’ve already memorized it, can I stop doing these homework assignments?” Little Red hesitatedly took One Lesson Three Practices, clutching at his hem, biting her lip as she spoke.
“No, you need to solidify your knowledge, and while at it, we’ll test how well you remember it.”
Colin kept a mischievous smile at bay, seriously speaking.
Leaving Little Red no choice but to accept her homework sullenly, she then began to inquire expectantly when he would teach her. Upon hearing that he would accompany her in learning all day tomorrow, Little Red’s face lit up with happiness.
Meanwhile, Saintess Shana also stepped out from the side.
“Mr. Colin, good day,” Shana said with a slight nod.
She was visibly better than before, no longer so thin and gaunt, no longer skin and bones, and her pale golden hair had left its previous dryness behind.
Now, her clear ice-blue eyes stared at Colin, emanating a sacred, hazy glow.
‘If she fully recovers, she will be very beautiful. If she dressed up a bit, she would be simply…’
Colin was momentarily stunned, then muttered to himself before nodding and saying, “Good day.”
Without further ado, he said, “The settlement from the ‘Hunger’ event has come through. It’s not much. After taking my share, there’s about twenty thousand left for you. Is that okay?”
“Yeah, no problem, twenty…”
Shana nodded subconsciously. The other party said it wasn’t much, so she assumed it would only be a few hundred, or maybe around a thousand?
Just about to say that any amount would be fine and that all amounts were good, she suddenly felt that something was wrong after hearing the rest of the sentence; the figures mentioned by the other party seemed a bit off.
Her lips, pale from blood loss after the fight, parted slightly.
After hesitating for a second, she uncertainly asked again,
“How, how much?”
She wondered if she had heard wrong.
“About twenty thousand…”
Colin, seeing the blank stare on her face, suddenly felt a twinge of guilt—
He had originally planned to give twenty-five thousand, but now, after spending most of his points, especially the nine thousand he had put up front for “Lady Rabbit,” he didn’t have much left, so he cut it down a bit.
So, he could only provide twenty thousand.
But judging by Shana’s expression, she seemed to think it was too little?
‘Well, after all, she baited out the ‘Hunger’ fragment with herself as the lure and took on the brunt of the gods’ wrath.’
Colin felt it was a bit less; forty or even fifty thousand would probably be more appropriate overall.
Just then, he heard Shana murmuring in a daze…
“Twenty, twenty thousand, this, this is…”
Shana blinked, wondering how many loaves of black bread that could buy?
Her brain, working at high speed, instantly came up with the number 660,000—a figure she couldn’t even dare to imagine in the past.
She thought that several generations of saints might never have seen such a large figure in their lifetimes.
While each generation of saints could earn a total of more than ten thousand points in their lifetimes, that was the sum total of a lifetime’s earnings.
To get so much at once was unheard of.
For just having done a somewhat dangerous task, this Agent of the Bonfire was going to give her twenty thousand points as a share?
Could there be any additional requirements?
Would the additional requirements be unreasonable?
Just as Colin was pondering how to explain why it was less, he heard Shana suddenly say, “So many points, Mr. Colin, are you sure they’re for me because of this event?”
“Huh?”
Colin was startled, looking at Shana’s innocent eyes, unable to discern if it was sarcasm.
In his understanding, this saintly girl with an exceptionally kind heart could earn twelve to twenty thousand points just by giving out buffs on missions, running along without doing anything.
But now, for luring “Hunger” and the hard-fought battle, she was only getting twenty thousand points.
In his opinion, it indeed seemed too little…
Shana mocking them was not out of the question.
But then again, she didn’t seem to be mocking…
Colin blinked, observing the girl whose every inch of skin seemed to shine like an angel; her face bore a naturally pure expression, devoid of even the slightest hint of sarcasm…
And when Shana had mocked those people the last time, her sarcasm had been quite strong.
It wasn’t like this…
Colin’s spiritual intuition regarding human nature also felt that she harbored no negative emotions…
Yet, it seemed the reality was contrary to his intuition…
So, was she satisfied or not?
‘I can’t tell, I just can’t tell!’ he thought, taking a deep breath inwardly. Eventually, he toughened up and nodded under her gaze.
Then, like waiting for a death sentence, he awaited her feedback…
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 690 - 690 506 Branch Going So Wild_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 690: Chapter 506 “Branch” Going So Wild?!_1 Chapter 690: Chapter 506 “Branch” Going So Wild?!_1 “This…”
Upon seeing Colin nod again, Shana knew he was telling the truth, just like last time…
Back then, she had carried over 400 “massive” points in her pocket and wanted to buy back the Bone Spur Tool made from the Saint’s Skeleton from him.
Thinking of this, Shana couldn’t help but feel secretly relieved that she hadn’t taken out her points, or she would have been terribly embarrassed.
Afterward, she didn’t retrieve her belongings, and instead, she gave away a Shield Emblem…
She was also shocked by Colin’s tendency to spend thousands of points at a time.
Of course, she also realized that the missions on her side seemed to be a bit lower than others’.
The reason for this situation was not very clear at the moment.
However, Shana had believed that a few thousand points were already an unimaginable amount in the past.
But the man before her had once again shattered her beliefs…
“If there is anything you are dissatisfied with, we can actually discuss it further…”
Colin, looking at Shana’s “expressionless” face, felt uncertain, but in this “standoff,” he suddenly remembered that every time he returned recently, she would give him various powerful Powerful Gold Imprint Personal BUFFs.
Then he thought about what he had done…
Originally with a total credit limit of eighty thousand points, only a small fraction of twenty-five thousand was given, and in the end, not only was nothing added, but five thousand were deducted.
Hmm, seems rather unsportsmanlike, doesn’t it?
He had just finished saying this when he saw Shana fall silent for a few seconds and then faintly nod her head:
“It is already a lot. I… I can’t even imagine that I could have so many points…”
‘Ah… isn’t this really mockery?’
Colin silently ‘hissed’ in his heart, but before he could say anything, a line of information popped up on his retinal screen.
[Special event: ‘Have you completed the event of giving 20,000 points to ‘The Light Chaser’?]
“Remarks”: There will be a certain amount of points deducted as a transaction fee.
…
‘The branch’s mission timing is quite prompt this time, but, are there really transaction fees?’
‘It seems that the exact proportion hasn’t been mentioned, but it should not be too high…’
Colin muttered to himself. It was a pity that employees couldn’t perform point transactions privately; otherwise, he definitely wouldn’t let the branch take advantage of free profits.
Then, looking at Shana again to confirm, he proceeded with the transaction and transferred the corresponding points.
At this moment, even though Shana did not pursue wealth too aggressively, she couldn’t help but glance at her pocket.
A number she had never dared to imagine lay there quietly.
While feeling overwhelmed by the enormous amount of points, she also felt a pang of regret for the transaction fee that had just been deducted.
“Hiss, two thousand points gone…”
Shana clenched her fists so subtly it was almost imperceptible and puffed her cheeks, as though losing two thousand points all at once.
This thing called a “transaction fee” was even more than what she had received from facing an Ancient God!
“What two thousand points?”
Colin, after overhearing her soft grumbling, asked curiously.
“Transaction fee?”
“A transaction fee of two thousand? That’s like ten percent!”
Colin was astonished; even the vampire banks wouldn’t charge more than five percent for withdrawals or transfers, and yet the fees here were so high?
But after thinking about it,
Perhaps cross-company transactions presented some difficulties, so charging a fee was somewhat understandable.
‘Later, I’ll ask ‘Lady Rabbit’ about it; are the transaction fees really this expensive here? I’ll see if there’s a way in the future to give Miss Shana her share directly and avoid the middleman’s cut…’
Colin’s thoughts flickered briefly.
Afterwards, seeing Shana’s expression of being slightly pained and a bit annoyed by the two thousand points loss, he could not help finding it somewhat amusing.
“Perhaps there’s some behind-the-scenes trouble causing this waste, hmm, the problem isn’t huge, I’ll make up for this transaction fee next time…”
Colin said with a smile, sensing from Shana’s expression that…
Her words just now did not seem to be mockery, but maybe.. joking?
After pondering, Colin felt that this was likely and reasonable.
Of course, during this brief moment, he also considered another possibility, which was that all of Shana’s expressions and words were genuine.
She truly thought over twenty thousand points was an enormous sum, which explained her shocked emotions.
But… how could that be possible?
Colin dismissed this erroneous notion right away.
After all, based on past situations, even without lifting a finger, she could easily get over ten thousand points. If she personally took action, the price would probably be in the six digits.
Under such circumstances, how could she find twenty thousand points satisfying?
However, speaking of which…
Miss Shana’s tasks, which could be deemed as profiting from others’ crises, indeed earned her quite a lot, though somewhat unscrupulous.
It felt like she might get her comeuppance one day.
Colin thought that he should find a time to talk to her about this.
While the company generally assigns tasks, employees do have a certain right to negotiate.
Then, upon hearing Colin offer to make up for the transaction fee, Shana immediately shook her head: “No, there’s no need, this is already sufficient, hmm…”
Very, very sufficient.
Looking at the sum in her pocket, Shana for a moment did not know how to spend it.
It certainly couldn’t all go towards dark bread.
But it could be a safety net.
Now, with Mr. Colin’s vast fields, as long as they were managed well—as Colin had said—they could sustain everyone. In the future, if there is a chance to prepare comestibles like a granary and others, they might even be able to stockpile next year’s food and ultimately achieve self-sufficiency—

chapters.title: Chapter 691 - 691 506
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 691: 506 Chapter 691: 506 A future she wouldn’t have dared to imagine just a few years ago.
That is…
With Bone Spur and that Shield Emblem, Shana felt it wouldn’t be easy to ask for them back.
“Really, these Points, I don’t know how to thank you enough,” Shana couldn’t help but whisper softly.
‘Is she happy because the money arrived just in time?’
Colin, sensing something, was moved by her emotions and couldn’t help but suggest, “How about a dance?”
Upon hearing this, Shana almost immediately shook her head, “That’s not possible, I can’t do that…”
She pursed her lips, not saying that dancing for others was also inappropriate.
After a pause, she tilted her head curiously and asked, “Is the amount of Points this time because of that ‘Hunger’ fragment?”
“Roughly speaking, yes.”
Colin nodded, sensing the desire for knowledge in Shana’s icy blue eyes, and said, “This task with ‘Hunger,’ it’s worth around fifty thousand Points…”
Out of eighty thousand Points, after deducting his own and Lady Bunny’s appearance fees and such, that was about the number.
But no sooner had he finished speaking than he felt something was amiss.
When really calculated, the “Hunger” fragment should be worth more than one hundred thousand Points. It’s hard to say exactly how much, but in terms of Points, that “Wildfire Affliction” could be seen to some extent as a partial compensation.
Or a significant compensation!
Hiss…
He hadn’t realized until he actually did the math, and then Colin felt even more apprehensive.
However, Shana didn’t notice this. Right now, upon hearing Colin mention the value of “Hunger,” her eyelids fluttered slightly and her pupils shone brightly—
It was so valuable!
This “Hunger” fragment was much more valuable than the Ancient God that had beaten her to the point of vomiting blood and lying in bed for half a month!
It’s just a pity that the “Hunger” she could feel seemed to have been reclaimed. No, there were three in total, two have been collected, and one she had come into contact with a long time ago was more like a concept than the other two, but then it disappeared…
Latter on, when she sensed that part again, it had already taken root inside Mr. Colin.
Thinking of this, Shana couldn’t help but glance at Colin, giving him an inexplicable shiver.
‘Feels a bit dangerous.’
Colin wondered if this might be a subtle warning from Shana?
But at that moment, he suddenly heard the increasingly beautiful lady in front of him saying:
“Mr. Colin, if I detect a ‘Hunger’ fragment, can I still work with you on it?”
She felt that if it was a task issued by her parchment, she wouldn’t be able to get more than fifty thousand Points, which according to her observations of late, might be several times less!
“Of course, that’s fine…”
Colin didn’t know if she was teasing or what, but he nodded anyway. After he spoke, however, he suddenly noticed something and said in surprise, “You know the whereabouts of other ‘Hunger’ fragments?”
“Not sure, but I’ve encountered some during descent missions in the past…”
Shana nodded, recounting an experience from about six or seven years ago.
Back then, the mission was, in some world, being summoned by a queen or something similar. She was asked to help in a war, emerge as the final victor, and claim a battle prize.
Other participants, akin to her, from different worlds, were summoned into this war.
One of those who descended held power similar to that of “Hunger”…
‘Good grief, they’re staging their own Holy Grail War, huh?’
Colin mumbled to himself and listened as Shana continued, “Among those I know, it seems you’re the only one who can wield ‘Hunger’s’ power. Was that person you?”
“No, it wasn’t me… I don’t even know them,” he shook his head.
Six or seven years ago? If nothing unexpected had occurred, he would have just been starting eleventh grade back then…
It was unexpected that, at that time, Shana had already started working for the company.
After thinking for a while, Colin asked for some more details and was basically able to confirm that person indeed held some power bestowed by a “Hunger” fragment…
But it was unclear whether the power was a gift from “Hunger” or harnessed through a method similar to “Bonfire.”
There was a significant difference between the two.
“Who ended up with that battle prize in the end?” Colin asked curiously.
“It should have been the person behind me. But after defeating the last one, my doppelganger reached its limit. Since it was my first one and I didn’t have good control, I returned, so I don’t know if she got the item or not,” Shana briefly shared the outcome and then shook her head, “Unfortunately, it seems impossible to find that person now.”
‘That’s true, unless he’s an employee of the company and then through internal means, sends a signal to ‘Lady Rabbit,’ just like Lady of Thorns did.’ Colin thought to himself.
‘Other than that, there was one other encounter in a chaotic, terrifying world, which does seem a bit possible.’
Shana took out her parchment, ‘I’ll look back and see if I can find more information about that place. If I do, I’ll let you know.’
‘Okay,’ Colin nodded.
As long as Shana provided the address, ‘Lady Rabbit’ would surely respond—
But looking at it, did ‘Lady Rabbit’ want to take over Shana’s ‘branch office’ because it still had control over multiple ‘Hunger’ fragment regions?
However, from what it had shown before, it probably wouldn’t be that easy.
But they didn’t continue to delve into this matter. After a brief chat, Shana began to examine whether Colin had grown stronger, and they both entered the ‘Nightmare Lantern’ and fought until the night before they finally rested.
After finishing daily training, Colin walked out of the small chapel, ready to also check whether his employees were slacking off late at night.
He also took a look at the harvest of the talking seeds…
Meanwhile, inside the small chapel, Shana split a part of her avatars to follow Colin, with her main body sitting in front of the Bonfire, continuing to heal and repair her various unhealed injuries.
Just as Colin left and she was focused on healing herself, she suddenly sensed something and pulled out a yellowing parchment from under the sleeve of her left wrist.
She then opened the ‘Marketplace’ feature, and was surprised to find that the shelf, which originally only had ‘black bread’ and ‘sour and hard black bread’ and items like drinking water, now had some other things.
[Multi-function Base Vehicle (Specially Optimized Version)]
‘Description’: A deployable mobile base vehicle with an unfolded area of about 50 square meters, which can be powered by injecting points, and has basic function templates such as ‘rest room’ and ‘medical room’.
‘Note’: Can be expanded in a limited capacity through the expenditure of points as well as the appropriate materials.
Price: 5000 Points.
…
‘This is…’
Shana looked at it, could it be the very useful ‘Base Vehicle’ that Mr. Colin brought?
But, it’s quite expensive, five thousand points for one…
Yet, if it’s similar, the usefulness would be great!
After thinking it over, she informed Colin through her avatar, who was strolling through the fields with her, to come over to her side to help advise on whether it was necessary to buy it.
But, just as Colin came over and saw the thing on the screen, he was shocked.
This damn thing…
‘I left the Base Vehicle here for two weeks without taking it back, and it went ahead and cracked it?’
Colin was completely stupefied.
What was most ridiculous was that they didn’t just mimic it and crack it, but they were damn selling it in front of him!
Selling it to him!
Colin almost laughed in exasperation.
Was the ‘branch office’s’ way of doing things a little too wild?
‘How about it, Mr. Colin? Is this thing worth buying?’ Shana asked, raising her arm to gently touch him.
‘It’s not worth it.’
Colin came back to his senses from his stupor, decisively shaking his head after seeing the so-called ‘Specially Optimized Version,’ which in reality was more like a cut-down castrated version, he couldn’t help but snicker.
‘500 points might be worth considering, 5000 points, the original version in the Heavy Industry World wasn’t even one thousand points, this price is a serious markup, they must be money-mad.’
‘Besides, the base vehicle we currently have in our territory is pretty much still sufficient, so there’s no need to fuss.’
Colin decisively offered advice against the purchase.
At the same time, he faintly felt that the ‘branch office’s’ nature reminded him of someone…
‘Oh, I see…’ Shana nodded thoughtfully.
But, it was at this moment that a line of a mission popped up on the parchment.
.
.
.
