chapters.title: Chapter 692 - 692 507 Subsidiary Mastering Special
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 692: Chapter 507 “Subsidiary” Mastering Special Technology._1 Chapter 692: Chapter 507 “Subsidiary” Mastering Special Technology._1 “Head to ruins marker number 796, recover a special site there, mission reward: ‘Base Vehicle’ price reduction, an Energy Crystal Stone, and 999 black breads?”
Colin, upon seeing the third item, showed a puzzled look, wondering what the heck these black breads were?
The first thing that came to his mind was not the black bread he had eaten before…
After all, having done missions for so long, it was the first time he had come across such an odd reward.
However, soon after he saw Shana pull out a black loaf from the “Storage Room,” his face changed immediately, “This… are you sure this can be considered a mission reward?”
“Yes.” Shana nodded, her gaze fixed on the mission requirements, seemingly a bit tempted.
The black bread offered for this mission wasn’t the sour and hard kind…
Which meant that just here, it was worth more than three hundred points, and then there’s the additional savings on the Base Vehicle.
That… actually seemed pretty good?
It was at least a lot better than before…
Of course, Shana also noticed that ever since Colin appeared, the rewards seemed to have increased.
“What do you think?” Shana, holding the parchment, turned to look at Colin next to her, seeking his opinion.
“I’m inclined to refuse.”
Colin shook his head and decisively offered his advice.
Using “black bread” as a mission reward, who are they kidding?
He had completed so many missions and this was the first time he had encountered such a bizarre one.
Pausing for a moment, Colin added an explanation, “The difficulty of this mission is unclear, but to compensate with black bread, I don’t even know how they have the nerve to offer that, and the price reduction isn’t guaranteed; who knows how much they’ll lower it…
“Unless they actually give us the production line, it’s meaningless.”
“Alright, let’s talk about the difficulty. What do you think, how difficult would this mission probably be?”
“Lady Rabbit” usually doesn’t disclose rewards in advance; only after seeing what was obtained do they finalize the amount, but most times, it’s taken for granted that there’s a minimum of a few thousand points as an appearance fee.
They would never compensate with “black bread”…
Revealing rewards beforehand could be seen as them already being aware of the whole task and therefore able to offer a reward upfront.
And through these rewards, you can somewhat guess the level of difficulty.
Of course, this is also some advanced knowledge on assessing mission difficulty distributed by “Life Mentor Adorable” within the employees.
Shana, looking at the reward content and resting her pointer finger on her chin, pondered, “Well… probably, there might be some interaction with remnants of Ancient God level entities, but no direct confrontation…”
“What?!”
Colin was taken aback, wondering if he had heard wrong. Could these rewards mean encountering at least peak Level 2 Containment Subject or even First Level Containment Subject grade Ancient Gods?
A ‘Base Vehicle’ of which the discount amount was unknown, and an Energy Crystal Stone with a use similar to a “Colorless Crystal”.
Plus a thousand black breads…
Are they expecting him to fight Ancient Gods with these items?
Well, not fight Ancient Gods but rather most likely encounter them…
Colin suddenly felt a pang of sympathy for this “Saint,” were all the missions he didn’t accept before like this?
‘Wait, before?’
He had a feeling that he was about to understand something, but logically, it didn’t connect, just like 1+1=2 missing the “+” sign.
The feeling was strange…
Meanwhile, Shana, noticing his look, said with some uncertainty:
“Probably will be…”
Although she didn’t know what Colin was thinking, she could tell that what might have seemed generous to her just a few months ago might not seem as appealing in Mr. Colin’s eyes.
Sure enough, after she finished speaking, Colin waved his hand, providing a response:
“Reject it, looking any further is a waste of time.”
“Okay, I understand…”
Shana nodded, currently having twenty thousand points in her pocket, she wasn’t in a rush, so there was no need to go out and take risks…
Following Colin’s advice, she unusually refused the mission.
“I’ll take care of the things above the territory, you don’t have to worry too much. After all, saving them is quite beneficial for me as well. You just need to understand the overall situation and if I can’t come over sometimes, help with maintenance.”
Colin briefly said, the “Colorless Crystal” spawned by believers now felt just like the meal before a fight.
If he didn’t take a few pieces, he felt like he lacked the energy to throw punches.
“Okay.” Shana nodded again, without objection.
“Of course, I’ll share some points with you for helping look after the territory.”
Before she could refuse, Colin continued, “Various things in the territory need points, and since there’s income from these tasks, it’s only fair if everyone working on it benefits, but it wouldn’t be right if I were the only one taking them.”
If he could rely on a small part of the basic mission points to have Shana stay here regularly.
He felt it would be quite worthwhile…
After a bit of persuasion, Shana did not refuse.
…
While Colin and Shana were patrolling the territory and discussing work, not far away, Warden Calder, who was interacting with a construction crew led by an Employee Level E, saw the two passing by and couldn’t help but reflect…
He suddenly realized that his perspective was still too narrow.
When the “Hunger” crisis broke out in the city, and Miss Helena, the noble’s daughter, followed Colin’s instructions throughout, he thought there might be some improper relationship between them.
After all, it’s true that some nobles play pretty wildly…
And about that Helena, to be honest, what was known about her character was not exactly commendable…

chapters.title: Chapter 693 - 693 507 Subsidiary Mastering Special
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 693: Chapter 507 “Subsidiary” Mastering Special Technology._2 Chapter 693: Chapter 507 “Subsidiary” Mastering Special Technology._2 It was indeed thought-provoking to see a real person actually listen to a prisoner with a mysterious identity.
But it was only now that he realized that it was because the other party had a good relationship with the Saintess.
They looked like friends…
And then there was Helena—the one he had also heard about, who seemed to remain willful during the disaster, and was completely transformed inside and out by the “Light” Saint Her Excellency.
Of course, this was also Helena’s luck, as she hadn’t really done anything terribly immoral or unjust.
Otherwise, the Saint would not hesitate to erase her completely.
In this respect, although the current Saint was a woman who appeared more gentle, no one doubted her resolve when it was time to act.
Helena’s family was somewhat dissatisfied with this, but they could only endure it.
After all, compared to Shana directly initiating “Judgment” against their entire family, this was just a minor issue.
Not to mention just erasing some bad morals…
Even if they had to clean up Helena and send her to the Saintess’ bed, they would do it.
“Calder, bro, you said earlier that we need to strengthen the third level of the underground prison, and that we must use alloy materials for the doors, even demanding some extraordinary means for reinforcement?” The Employee Level E nearby asked, puzzled:
“We’re building a refugee prison, not a containment facility…
“They are just ordinary refugees, let alone iron doors, even wooden doors would be hard to break through, is it really necessary?”
During this time, Calder had chosen to garrison here, taking the position of their Warden.
When Calder heard the employee’s words, he came back to his senses and, after listening, pursed his lips, pondered deeply for a moment, and recalled the scene deeply buried in his memory, where a giant beast with red fur had broken through the prison door and pinned him to the ground for a beating.
Then, Calder nodded vigorously with a large motion:
“There is, trust me, there definitely is.”
Although those incarcerated were all erring refugees, one couldn’t discount the occasional unexpected incident: a prison needs a sufficiently sturdy layer to truly make people feel secure.
In the event it’s not possible to keep the enemies confined, taking the opportunity to lock up allies for protection is also not a bad choice.
…
The dark and bright night soon passed away for the most part…
Approaching the time where day and night intersect, the Little Maid suddenly reported to Colin that she had received some special vibrational frequencies—
Without a doubt, they should be from the “King of Savage Sound.”
Although he was unclear about what was going on, Colin still flew over to see why the other wanted to seek him out.
About half an hour later, Colin entered the area of the underground labyrinth closest to his territory.
“Congratulations, your strength has advanced once more.” Just upon entering the place, Colin heard the compliment from the “King of Madness,” and then sensed through the “Flame” that the other was standing not far away.
“What is it?” Colin waved his hand.
“Well, can I ask about… my situation, has there been any response from above?” “King of Madness” asked quietly.
It seemed like there wasn’t any response from ‘Lady Rabbit,’ Colin muttered to himself internally, but outwardly he said without changing his expression:
“Rest assured, the organization sees all your efforts, keep working hard, and you’ll have a chance to come out and serve the company.”
“That’s great, that’s great, I can’t wait to start working!” the “King of Madness” stated immediately.
“Did you call me here just to ask about this?” Colin asked curiously.
In fact, even if the “King of Madness” didn’t seek him out, he still intended to find this person to ask some things.
“No, no, no, there’s actually something else…”
The “King of Madness” hesitated, seemingly weighing something difficult to say.
“What is it?” Colin raised an eyebrow.
“Well, before I say anything, I want to make it clear that I’m not plotting anything…”
Colin became intrigued and then heard the “King of Madness” say: “Actually, it’s because you often modify the ‘Logic Point Blockade’ feature, and there’s one that I wish you could remove, I can’t remember some important things, and I’d like to ask you to make some slight changes, probably to some of the blockade points from the day before…”
Because of this, he seemed unable to recall some critical tasks he needed to do.
It was very troubling…
But before he could finish speaking, Colin interrupted: “‘Logic Point Blockade’? What’s that?”
Seeing Colin’s expression, the “King of Madness” realized something was amiss: “…Wasn’t it modified by you?”
“No,” Colin shook his head, “you go first, what is this?”
Soon, from the Containment Subject’s mouth, he roughly learned what the so-called “Logic Point Blockade” was—
In general, it resembled a kind of mental firewall, usually employed to prevent the risk of knowledge contamination from certain dangerous entities that corrupt by mere awareness.
“In today’s world, not a single ‘God’s’ true name is known to mortals, all because of its existence. Only, compared to such an ultra-high-intensity cognitive cover-up, the current ‘Logic Point Blockade’ is much less formidable, but its effect still has…”
“King of Savage Sound” gave a simple example.
“You say, if it wasn’t me, then who could it be?” Colin suddenly realized a possible cause.
“Not sure, maybe some part of the company that garrisons this place? Of course, I’m not instigating; I mean, if you didn’t interfere with it, then it should be the company’s maintainers. Other things, even the arrival of some unimaginable entities, couldn’t manage it—they can destroy, but that’s all they can do. I can vaguely sense that it has been changing a bit too often lately…”
“King of Savage Sound” spoke cautiously.
In that period, he always felt like he couldn’t remember this, couldn’t remember that as if his brain was almost breaking…
Recently, huh… Colin nodded, confirming after inquiring about some details that “recently” referred to after his arrival.
“What is the ‘branch office’ covering up?”
“How can I counteract this influence?” Colin asked directly.
“This… This is related to your Authority Level and your position in the company to some extent, but I’m not entirely clear on the specifics. However, I can confirm that it has a range—you’ll be able to remember as soon as you leave this area…”
Concerning how some functions within the company actually operated, the “King of Savage Sound” didn’t know much, considering its status as a prisoner rather than an employee, so it could only offer its speculation as much as possible.
“But all in all, if you’re already aware of this, they definitely can’t affect you any longer, after all, you’re a candidate for ‘Flame Bearer’, a transcendent figure. Barely influencing cognition is already their limit. As for deeper interference, they can’t manipulate the memory layer of your brain…”
“King of Savage Sound” gave another example, saying:
“It’s like, there was once a bottle of cola in this room, if I hadn’t mentioned it, you probably wouldn’t even be aware of it…”
“But now that I’ve told you, you know about it.”
“Once you’re aware, even if they bury all traces, it doesn’t affect what you know.”
“…”
“Understood.” Colin nodded, indicating he roughly understood.
Apart from not knowing what the branch office was up to by modifying something, this feature was quite interesting—by blocking a logical point, it prevented people from piecing together the entire logic.
‘Come to think of it, it indeed seems like a technology the company would control, only it has been applied nefariously.’
However, it wasn’t a big problem. Colin felt he was very close to the truth.
As long as the other party couldn’t erase the messages he already knew, he should be able to figure out the reasons just by thinking about it when he got back…
“Besides, to resist such influence by sheer strength, one needs to be at least an Upper-Level First-Class Containment Entity,” “King of Savage Sound” added briefly.
Upper-level first-class? If I have that strength, it wouldn’t dare to show itself in front of me.
Colin couldn’t help but remember the night he exchanged Three Hundred Thousand Points.
Whenever he was in contact with the company, that thing wouldn’t dare to appear, afraid of being directly captured by “Lady Rabbit.”
It only dared to sneak around after everything was disconnected…
“Hmm, understood, not bad, the information you’ve provided this time is useful.” Colin nodded in approval; now it was voluntarily reporting the situation, which was much better than before.
He could consider offering it a non-stop 007 job…
Colin advised, “In the future, if there is any abnormality, you can also notify me, report at the earliest opportunity.”
“Of course, your future employee is ready to serve you at any time!”
“Hmm.”
Colin nodded, then was suddenly struck by a thought:
“Doesn’t this put you at risk of retaliation from them?”
So far, the “Lady of Thorns” branch office seemed to have many capable individuals, but this branch office he was at was the wildest he had ever seen…
There was no guarantee that following this “whistleblowing,” the “branch office” wouldn’t do something to his “Colin employee” reservist.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 694 - 694 508 Its an honor to be a bonfire dog
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 694: Chapter 508 It’s an honor to be a bonfire dog, unlike some wild dogs…_1 Chapter 694: Chapter 508 It’s an honor to be a bonfire dog, unlike some wild dogs…_1 “No, this is a ‘Containment Divine Kingdom,’ a special containment facility directly controlled by the sole conscious mind of Rosen. Not just anyone can influence it. At most, the local subsidiary company only has surveillance authority, along with some emergency intervention rights outside, but lacking the ability to deal with me any further…”
The tone of the “King of Madness” inexplicably rose a bit.
You’re locked up and you’re smug about it… Colin couldn’t help but sneer inwardly.
Sometimes, among containment subjects, inexplicable competitive spirits arise, baffling to anyone witnessing them.
Of course, this could also be considered an aspect of the “humanity” the other party displayed.
Then…
Noticing something in the other party’s words, Colin’s mind started whirring, realizing something intriguing…
‘If things are as usual, the ‘Subsidiary’ might be left by Rosen, but it actually can’t handle the containment subjects inside this so-called ‘Containment Divine Kingdom’?’ Colin thought contemplatively.
This subsidiary doesn’t have as much authority as I thought…
Following that, Colin inquired about the specific situation of the “Containment Divine Kingdom.”
“Generally speaking, those who are locked up here are considered of significant value to the company, which is why I was allowed inside…”
The “King of Madness” quietly boosted his own value.
Colin didn’t argue with this point; it was hard to say what the combat abilities of the “King of Madness” were, but its special authority, related to vibrations and such, did hold considerable research value.
He continued listening as the “King of Madness” went on:
“Besides Rosen himself, if others want to deal with me, all they can do is report upwards, wait for instructions, or in special circumstances, employ another ‘Flame Bearer’ for emergency handling. So, you need not worry about what impact it can have on me, it can’t even force me into labor dispatch.”Nowadays, with the “messenger” from above standing next to it, what’s there to fear from a mere local subsidiary?
That’s why it replied there was no need to worry.
Even if the subsidiary wanted to handle things themselves, their reports and applications wouldn’t go through. In its view, the higher-ups might be tied up with other matters at the moment, but once they were free, they could deal with the subsidiary in minutes.
“They can even dispatch for labor?” Colin stood on the spot, raising an eyebrow.
“Yes, some of the more cooperative containment subjects are sometimes dispatched through certain methods to handle troublesome tasks, and the uncooperative ones have their power transferred to machines in some way to be driven…”
“6.”
Colin opened his mouth, only to utter that one number.
“Isn’t that risky? Aren’t you afraid they’ll run away?” he couldn’t help but curiously ask.
“There is a risk, some containment subjects might not cooperate and cause destruction upon being sent out, but as for escaping, that’d be impossible.”
Although subtle, Colin still heard a hint of helplessness and resignation in the tone of the “King of Madness”:
“High-value containment subjects are the company’s important assets. I’m unaware of other star domains, but here, as long as the Containment Protocol still exists, any known method of escape is virtually nonexistent; the escape rate is currently at zero.”
Important assets…
Upon hearing this term, Colin couldn’t help but remember the incident involving “Time Reversal” when they were recycling starships.
They had captured a strange creature capable of generating electricity, and immediately afterwards, time began to reverse.
And then…
Even time reversal couldn’t make the company give up the catch and spit it out from their pockets.
Shaking his head, Colin didn’t dwell on it, and asked a few more questions, such as if the “King of Madness” knew “Thorn Lady” and so on, but unfortunately, the “King of Madness” didn’t know much in that regard.
After talking a bit more, Colin prepared to leave.
“Respected ‘Flame Bearer’ Sir, if you have any questions, you are always welcome to return. Within the range of my ability, even at the cost of my life, I shall fulfill it!”
‘Where did he learn these weirdly polite phrases? He seems to be getting smoother…’ Colin thought.
Colin waved his hand, turned around, and took step by step away from this place.
And as he watched his figure covered in flames walk away, the “King of Madness” started to feel a bit melancholic.
He couldn’t quite understand the current situation with the “Bonfire Company.” Why would a small regional subsidiary dare to confront a patrolling ambassador from above?
This…
Although the employee’s current status wasn’t quite right.
But as someone about to become a ‘Flame Bearer’ as a reservist, that level of authority was boundless, and even if he wasn’t a full-fledged ‘Flame Bearer’ yet, didn’t his authority peak, wouldn’t it be later?
However, there was also something the “King of Madness” always couldn’t quite understand…
Even though he knew the company might have had a minor issue, he thought there must still be a considerable amount of reserved force.
But why…
The important task of reclaiming what Rosen left behind, why would the company handle it so trivially, just taking small actions?
The corps and high-level employees they deployed were strong, but in terms of results, they were far less useful than having a proper ‘Flame Bearer.’
Not to mention combat power, just the “infinite emergency authority” they possess could have resolved the issues here by a large margin.
Everything could have been settled in less than three days.
Know that what the original inhabitants of the World Code think is insurmountable, all this Magic Fog disaster and whatnot, to him, was nothing more than a little leak in the roof.
Although if the leak becomes too severe, it could bury him in the room, it also demonstrates that the whole room is still quite solid.

chapters.title: Chapter 695 - 695 508
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 695: 508 Chapter 695: 508 Various subsidiary protocols were still operating normally.
Just by this alone, the “Flame Bearer” or a high-level employee, even if only their brain arrived, with a mere thought, without moving any other limbs, could solve all problems.
But now, there has been no sight of the able “Flame Bearer” or high-level employee coming over; instead, a reservist has been sent, slowly solving issues bit by bit.
With each growth, solving a bit more, with each growth, solving a bit more…
Is it to train newcomers?
Training newcomers “King of Madness” is understandable, but using this incident to train them, could it be a bit…
It pondered for a long time, and finally found a phrase from the “human nature” knowledge base— “using a sledgehammer to crack a nut”?
Or is it for some other reasons that it has to be this way?
What exactly is the situation outside?
“King of Madness” tried to look outside, but couldn’t see anything. Venturing even a bit of power beyond the labyrinth was difficult.
He could only receive some vibrational information passed down from above…
However, his action, without seeing anything, drew in some other entities.
Some strange whispers began to come from all directions again…
“Do you really believe their lies? Human words cannot be trusted, and in the past, you were nothing but a lowly mongrel…”
“Just a few centuries, and you have already resigned yourself to them?”
“I have glimpsed, the universe has already changed, Bonfire Company is about to step off the stage of history…”
“Chaos Divinity will descend once more…”
“Assist us, let the era of supreme divinity return, together with the noble will of divinity, transcend the ultimate moment…”
“…”
“Misfortune!”
“King of Madness” waved his hand in his ethereal form, and all the murmurs disappeared completely.
“It was listening to you lot that I took advantage of a disaster for personal gain, which led to my confinement to the present, you’ve completely ruined me; and those two, who agreed not to betray, turned long ago…”
“A few centuries is not a long time, but have you ever been confined to the ‘Containment God Kingdom’ to try it for yourself?”
“Here, the time I have suffered through the torment has already exceeded ten million years!”
“As long as I can get out, as long as I can get out, just as long as…”
“King of Madness” murmured agitatedly, then suddenly burst into laughter:
“A dog? To be a dog of the Bonfire is the greatest honor!
“Unlike some stray dogs, who, even after being imbued with ‘human nature’ and having some sense of honor and disgrace, still run around outside, not knowing who their master is…”
“Sooner or later I will get out, and you can only rot here forever, finally to be taken back by the ‘Primordial Fire’ as kindling!”
He mocked those sealed Containment Subjects.
…
After returning to his domain, Colin didn’t mention the branch office anymore. After all, with the shielding in place and logic disconnected, it’s no use thinking more about it. Anyway, the matter was already noted in his little book—there would be plenty of time to settle scores after his return…
The daily routine of accepting displaced refugees, cultivating land, building houses, general sanitation improvement, and preparing for educational initiatives, among many other tasks.
“It still feels like we don’t have enough staff,” Colin remarked, looking over his domain. The rough outline of the town had pretty much formed; there was an indescribable sense of farming achievement.
Yet it still felt like it wasn’t developing fast enough.
Given that here fifty employees, along with their multitude of tools, were already performing to their limits, Colin had done all he could by continuously providing “Colorless Crystal” for seven days and nights without rest to replenish their energy. Additionally, with the use of various tools including the “Mark of the Fire Tree,” he helped to occasionally soothe their spirits so that they could rest for ten minutes and work the entire day.
But even so, with more and more tasks to deal with, manpower still seemed inadequate…
On the other hand, the number of refugees arriving kept increasing. With that came more conflicts, and everything started to feel stretched thin. Previous management methods couldn’t keep up and needed updating…
“Sigh, it really does drain one’s energy.”
Although Colin sat in front of a hot pot, eating while watching the employees working below, without directly participating in the labor, his heart was always with the frontline workers.
So the fatigue was the same…
“In the end, it’s still due to a shortage of people.”
“Now that I’m at a D+ level, the ‘special talent’ privileges haven’t been updated yet. Once they are, I should be able to pull in another group. Before that, I need to figure out a way to have them exert more labor.”
Colin pondered for a moment, currently giving his employees one or two hours to eat each day—
Could that be a bit too extravagant?
Eating, after all, could also be done during work hours. With the physique of the Extraordinary Ones, a few bites should be enough to fill them up…
No need to waste too much time, especially in special circumstances.
‘After all, each of them is a Transcendent with extraordinary abilities. With great power comes great responsibility. Having been fortunate enough to possess power beyond ordinary people, they should make contributions beyond ordinary expectations…’
Colin thought about how to bring this up with the others in a way that wouldn’t get him strung up on a streetlamp—oh, in a way that they would accept it.
‘And to think,’ once the Descent Protocal concluded and we returned to Earth, it had only been three hours. So essentially, I’m just asking them to work continuously for three hours, which shouldn’t be too much to ask.’
With that in mind, Colin felt much better about the situation.
However, at that very moment, he couldn’t help but think about those protagonists in novels.
Those who alone could stir up the winds and waves in another world with just a bit of knowledge in their heads, moving the era forward…
Colin truly admired them, unlike him, with so much power supporting him from behind, and still, many things felt difficult to handle.
If he had a couple of ‘protagonists’ as subordinates, things would probably be a lot easier.
After shaking his head slightly, Colin dismissed the thought and started to prepare for the upcoming communication with his employees, starting with D Level. No, D Level was already swamped with work, naturally one of their own.
“We’ll have a meeting later and let them suggest some new time schedules.”
After having some simple ideas, Colin didn’t dwell on it any further.
Soon after, as the wails of some employees rose, the new arrangements began to take effect, and Colin, along with a few people, went out to hunt the horrifying creatures nearby.
As well as spending daily time with Little Red and training his skills with Shana.
Seven days flew by quickly.
In the last half-hour before departure, some employees looked at Colin expectantly—he had said that after they increased their work effort this time, there would be a small gold nugget that could unleash a BUFF as a reward.
They had gotten one of those before.
After using it during their abnormal events, it was like using a Level 30 indestructible BUFF in a Level 10 dungeon; they could steamroll through the whole thing, leaving a profound impression.
Seeing their gazes, Colin looked at Shana, exchanged a glance, and distributed the “BUFFs,” which were about the size of soybeans and had been prepared beforehand.
“Seeing how much everyone wants this thing, perhaps I could consider putting it up for sale at my auction house?” Colin mused aloud to Shana upon witnessing this scene.
“I could, but, I don’t have enough mysterious materials, and gold is still very precious…”
“No worries, I’ll cover this part. You contribute the effort, I’ll provide the materials.” Colin waved his hand, as the mystic value of gold hadn’t been much explored on Earth.
It wouldn’t be difficult for him to obtain it, he just wasn’t sure whether it would be usable over here.
“In that case, I have no problem with it.”
Shana nodded, no longer objecting.
Creating the “Golden Sun” mark specifically for Colin was quite time-consuming and labor-intensive…
But these little ones were much easier to make.
She could casually spare an hour or so a day and make dozens of them.
“Okay, I’ll scope it out when I get back, see what kind of price would be appropriate.”
After a brief exchange, Colin and his group returned through the “Descent Protocol,” amidst the reluctant gazes of the others.
…
Ding—Ding—Ding—
The distant and ancient bell sounds slowly faded from his ears…
Colin returned to reality, and before he even had the chance to pull out the parchment, he immediately started recalling some matters related to the “branch office” during this Descent Project.
.
.
.
First

chapters.title: Chapter 696 - 696 509 Moonlight Mutation_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 696: Chapter 509 “Moonlight” Mutation!_1 Chapter 696: Chapter 509 “Moonlight” Mutation!_1 “Every time it seems that when I think about reward benefits, there’s some disconnect; Shana’s rewards clearly appear scarce to me, yet she doesn’t seem to feel that way…”
“Moreover, since her missions often yield a hefty amount, the twenty thousand points shouldn’t even be a concern to her.”
“But her reaction this time was shock… no, it was always like this, she seems to care even about a mere few thousand points.”
Colin stroked his chin, realizing that this didn’t fit with Shana’s “rich lady” persona.
Logically, she shouldn’t really show any emotion over such a small amount of points…
That indicates that there’s a high probability she actually doesn’t get that many points normally.
“Right, some missions upon their descent, she always haggles over every little thing, a BUFF might cost hundreds to thousands of points each time, but when it comes to handing over things like the Golden Mark, she’s extremely generous…”
“She didn’t show any indication that she thought BUFFs could be sold for money, instead letting me freeload many times.”
“That miserly demeanor seems to only manifest during the descent of missions…”
“Maybe, the miserliness and greed aren’t Shana’s at all, but that of the mission? No, the person distributing the missions, or the ‘Subsidiary’?”
The train of thought in his brain connected at this moment, and Colin narrowed his eyes, feeling he must be right.
The Shana who came to execute the missions probably couldn’t receive the full amount of points she was due!
Just as “God” and His Believers don’t necessarily share the same thoughts, the relationship between Shana and the “Subsidiary” might also be similar?
“It seems every time I witness Shana’s situation firsthand and then remember her during a mission, feeling a sense of character dissonance, I always fail to ask her about her past mission rewards…”
“Hiss, is this ‘Logic Point Blockade’ blocking exactly these things? Truly disgusting.”
This damn thing, a corporate tool meant to prevent cognitive pollution from Ancient Gods, is actually being used by the ‘Subsidiary’ for their own selfish purposes, against their own people!
“That’s a bit excessive, are there no rules, no systems anymore!”
Colin was somewhat speechless, unclear on what the Subsidiary was thinking…
However, from this, he could guess that the Subsidiary probably didn’t want either him or Shana to know about the discrepancy in their wages.
He just didn’t know how much of the actual compensation was skimmed.
For the same event difficulty, he might get tens of thousands of points.
Shana might only get a couple thousand points.
Thinking of this, Colin shook his head: “To exploit my territory partner like this!”
Given the rogue traits displayed by the current “Subsidiary”, it seemed that when they did missions, and Shana came to assist, he paid tens of thousands of points while she might only get to pocket a couple thousand.
That really was a bit too much!
Colin noted this grievance in his mind and called out the Little Maid, instructing her to remind him next time he entered, to inquire about this matter.
If all went as expected, following the “King of Madness’ ” words,
next time he went in, the “Subsidiary’s” “Logic Point Blockade” would no longer be effective.
Unless it could erase the information in his own brain—
But unfortunately, even if it had the capability, it did not have the authority to act!
It couldn’t touch a regular D Level staff, let alone a “Flame Bearer” with all the privileges that come with various affiliations.
“Looking at it this way, the ‘Flame Bearer’ Reservist status might not mean much externally, but it sure works internally.”
Colin murmured softly.
“Of course, if ‘Lady Rabbit’ could intervene, maybe it would be better. I have to think about it and see if there’s a way to directly trade with Shana next time, to avoid the middleman skimming.”
A face-to-face transaction incurs a ten percent handling fee.
In Colin’s view, that was simply outrageous…
Unfortunately, it seems Shana doesn’t have access to the internal channels for staff on Earth, otherwise, a trade here could have her exchanging a few thousand points for food, which might feed her and her refugees until they were stuffed to the brim.
“I’ll jot down some feedback first and submit it to see if ‘Lady Rabbit’ has any solution; if not, we’ll see.”
Colin opened the Parchment, set aside the mission completion for the moment, and found an official post for submitting feedback within the internal communication channel on the Parchment.
Normally, feedback is basically ignored.
The complaints about “Stupid Robots” alone number in the tens of thousands here, but the BUG persists.
But his aim was to reach “Lady Rabbit”, so there still might be a chance for a response.
Response content, however, is generally similar to what has come before, returned via envelope rather than acknowledged on the Parchment.
After reporting the information about his territory partner being fleeced by the “Subsidiary,”
only then did Colin begin to check the settlement of the most recent “The Descent Project” mission.
“Some Silver Task Certificates and about six to seven thousand points?”
The reward content was disappointing.
Colin shook his head but then thought that this time “The Descent Project,” aside from accepting a few thousand refugees, indeed didn’t salvage anything of value.
He could only take a basic appearance fee, barely enough to be of any use.
“It looks like the big payoff can only come from the rewards of the Fifteenth Ring mission, accumulating fifteen missions. If there are more of those Mutated World missions against ‘The Night,’ at the end, the points alone could reach the mid-hundreds of thousands.”
Colin began to feel somewhat hopeful.
But until completion, he just had to do missions “on loan.”…
‘The officials seem to have made a tidy sum of points recently; if it really comes down to it, I’ll just borrow some to use.’

chapters.title: Chapter 697 - 697 509 The Anomaly of the Moonlight_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 697: Chapter 509 “The Anomaly of the Moonlight!”_2 Chapter 697: Chapter 509 “The Anomaly of the Moonlight!”_2 Colin pondered for a while and then looked towards the internal chat channel where his employees frequently huddled together.
They had been working on “The Descent Project” for seven days, with individual point earnings ranging from eight hundred to over two thousand, and unlike Colin’s mindset, they all seemed quite happy with these points.
“Sigh, all blame on ‘Lady Rabbit’, who initially offered too many points,” Colin lamented. “It caused me to lose any sense of excitement for a few thousand points. My threshold is too high, and I can’t get happy about it.”
After sighing, Colin didn’t dwell on it but reined in his thoughts.
He rarely sent some messages to inquire about their opinions on the “little golden beans” BUFF.
He asked how many points they would find acceptable for this thing.
Upon seeing Colin’s appearance, the employees were quite excited and shared their expectations.
Watching their ongoing flood of chat messages,
ultimately, after about an hour of discussion, Colin had an initial sense of the situation.
Currently, some people found ten to fifty points acceptable, with employees of higher ranks tending to cite the larger sums of points.
Naturally, those of lower ranks, with smaller point incomes, would quote lower amounts.
Weighing his decision, Colin planned to settle on a middle figure.
“Thirty points should be about right.”
Colin stroked his chin, considering the short-term, almost disposable nature of the low-tier BUFF; it couldn’t be sold too dearly.
This amount should be just about right…
And Shana, over the course of a week, could craft about three to five hundred manually, netting roughly ten thousand points.
That was fairly good.
‘It seems the ‘Light’ Church and other Bishops, less powerful than her, could also be considered to join the production workforce, to craft some to sell. Numbers matter.’
Sitting cross-legged on his bed, Colin stroked his chin while deep in thought.
Extracting points from a mega-church proved to be much more profitable than just from Shana alone.
Once this almost monopolistic trade was initiated, Colin couldn’t predict how much he would earn.
The only problem was not knowing how to compensate them.
Points, to the ‘Light’ Church, didn’t hold much significance.
On his side, he apparently couldn’t think of anything to trade in good time.
‘Later on, I’ll consult with the officials, too; there’s money to be made for everyone.’
Without dwelling on the matter and paying attention to the number of his messages to ensure it didn’t exceed the limit, Colin notified everyone that he was preparing to launch a batch of “golden beans” for sale, available for those interested to purchase.
Then, he opened the auction house and uploaded his items for auction.
Afterward, seeing “Book of Fate: Fragment” available, he promptly snatched up all six copies.
At two hundred points each, their effects were quite good.
Although they came with risks and one might see things they shouldn’t, Colin could have his companions use them to transfer the risk, so it wasn’t a big issue.
“Speaking of which, the officials are still diligently infiltrating the company with the ‘Book of Fate,'”
he muttered, looking at the newly acquired “Book of Fate: Fragment.”
The reason the “Book of Fate: Fragment” appeared in the “auction house” was because the officials were using it to continually infiltrate the company, creating a connection with the official side and thus better understanding…
In response to this, whether it was Lady Bunny or someone else’s decision, the company’s upper echelons had accepted it anyway.
After processing, they sold it again at a moderate price.
And the effect after processing was somewhat better than the original.
However, Colin couldn’t help but recall a conversation with Xu Duojin, who had confided that if employees made excessive use of these items, the probability of clashing with the company would increase.
It was like a magnet, and regardless of how much the company tried to cleanse it, its magnetic nature remained.
“In this regard, those old hands are quite vigilant.”
Colin thought of the seasoned D Level staff who knew all too well that the side effects of “Book of Fate: Fragment” went beyond what was stated on the parchment.
They were more cautious in its use; for example, the parchment instructions allowed for three uses a day as long as one didn’t use it consecutively…
But they usually limited themselves to no more than three times a week, with a day’s gap after each use to avoid continuous usage.
However, since the officials had already started to work with him for the company, they wouldn’t, as before, go out of their way to find employees who had not joined the officials—
If they wished to join the officials, they were welcomed; if not… it was fine as long as they weren’t discovered.
Xu Duojin had told Colin that if they were found, it wasn’t about forcibly recruiting them, but it was necessary to inquire about some situations and clear up misunderstandings.
They would definitely vie for what could be contended for.
Don’t look at the employees one or two at a time, especially D Level staff. They might be considered “inferior” compared to the company’s D Level in the past, but they are still quite valuable to the officials.
After all, their strength is equivalent to Sixth, Seventh, or even Eighth Level Personnel, and they can use their extraordinary abilities without any negative effects.
It’s quite impressive.
Then, Colin collected his somewhat scattered thoughts, preparing to put away the parchment.
But suddenly, a message popped up.
[…Detected promotion in your job rank. According to the “Talent Excellence Plan,” your current privileges will be updated…]
“Oh? The authority upgrade from D to D+ came through?”
Colin’s eyebrows rose as he sensed the specific changes to his privileges.
“The current 5 cubic meters of additional space has been changed again, increased to 10 cubic meters, doubled directly.”
“Staff transfer limit went from 50 to 100 people, also doubled. The recruitment requirements are pretty much the same…”
“And there’s one more, one thousand points plus a Gold Mission Voucher to buy a special color name, so in the future, in the internal chat group, my name can turn flame red, with a special effect display. However, one thousand points and a Mission Voucher only last for a month, ugh, what a waste, why not give something more practical…”
“The main changes are the first two; the rest don’t seem to have changed much.”
Having quickly assessed the situation, Colin felt it was not bad, the only useless thing that tempted him to complain was that purchase right for the special effect name.
Although one thousand points wasn’t a big problem for him, the Gold Mission Voucher was still quite precious.
Any sensible person would certainly not waste it on some trashy name effect.
“Ten cubic meters of space, feel like I could bring some larger vehicles now. Take them apart, stack them neatly, then pack them in. When I arrive, I’ll have the employees put them together. The oil and such are more troublesome, oh right, I can use those power-generating energy creatures. I’ll see if I could retrofit one.”
“Damn it, during the ‘Ghost Train’ incident, there were some battery-turned-monsters. I should’ve captured one of them back then.”
“That thing’s electrical output seemed quite a bit stronger than those smaller ones.”
Thoughts whirled in Colin’s mind, shaping up some ideas.
Then, he looked at the internal chat group, a slight smile appearing on his lips.
Another fifty lucky employees could be picked to go to the Other World.
However, just as he was starting the selection, Colin suddenly felt an intense sense of horror rise within him. Flames burst forth from his body, and at the same time, he turned his gaze to the window.
But even with his swift reaction, he could only see that everything seemed to have already ended.
The only thing observed…
“Was the moonlight color just now a bit off?”
Colin frowned, although looking at it now, it appeared bright and no different than before.
But he was sure that there had been a change just now.
And…
Although he hadn’t seen the extent of the color change, the word “red” inexplicably came to his mind.
After some thought, Colin felt an uncomfortable sense of unease. He put away the parchment, took out his phone, and was about to contact Xu Duojin to inquire about the situation—
For such mysterious and strange occurrences, the “Fate Propeller” Extraordinary Ones are much more sensitive than he is.
But before they could communicate, Qin Chuan’s call suddenly came in.
“What’s going on?” Colin answered without any pleasantries and went straight to the question.
Qin Chuan wouldn’t normally call directly, usually sending a text message instead.
“Mr. Colin, be careful, we just saw something rush into your room!”
“Hmm?”
Colin was surprised, then had a realization, lifted his foot, and kicked open the bedroom door. Outside, a figure dangled from a rope in midair.
As the door opened, the figure facing Colin flashed a pale face with a grotesque smile, the black corners of the lips twisted.
“Click.”
The next second, Colin felt something tighten around his neck as if caught by a rope and pulled upward. A terrifying force caused his neck bones to crack.
His entire spine seemed as though it was about to be pulled straight out.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 698 - 698 510 The World Fluctuation Brought by Red
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 698: Chapter 510 The World Fluctuation Brought by “Red Moon”…_1 Chapter 698: Chapter 510 The World Fluctuation Brought by “Red Moon”…_1 “Ka-ka-ka…”
A succession of brittle bone cracks emanated from within his body.
The brief and sudden attack lasted less than a tenth of a second, but Colin’s height had already been stretched by two or three centimeters…
Intense pain spread from his back as the enemy attempted to pull his spine out with immense force.
Colin did not panic. Although he felt nothing around his neck, through the fiercely burning bonfire, he still vaguely discerned the phantom image of a rope hanging from his neck, slowly dissipating in the flames.
“Strong, with extraordinary power for suppression as well as some other effects…”
Thoughts flashed through Colin’s mind. He raised his left hand, pressing down on his head to push his height back to normal, while his right hand flung out, the ring transforming into a revolver aimed at his opponent and fired.
However, facing his actions, the suspended figure still maintained a disturbing smile.
Even upon seeing him draw the gun, the smile only intensified.
“Bang bang bang!”
Amidst the flashing gunfire, three 7.62 bullets fired in response, hitting various parts of the hanged person’s body and blasting three palm-sized holes through him.
In Colin’s view, this entity wasn’t particularly strong; it just had a perverse nature.
But regardless, it was best to fire a few shots first.
It was precisely the moment the bullets hit the target that Colin also felt as if he’d been punched in three places on his body.
Followed closely by a dull pain…
“Cough, is this binding injury same as mine?”
Colin coughed dryly, almost immediately realizing the nature of the problem as he felt the same injuries as his opponent.
Quite bizarre…
At that moment, with the suspended figure shaking from the bullet’s impact, upon seeing Colin’s reaction, the strange figure’s mouth curled into an even deeper smile. First, he spat out a mouthful of blood, then he began to speak:
“Pain, right?! Is it painful?! Hahaha, attacking me is the same as attacking yourself! And it’s double the return! What I can bear is more than double yours! Now, the only way for you to survive is to join us, to become…”
Before he could finish, he suddenly saw an explosive eruption of flame on the man before him.
This blaze quickly engulfed him completely…
The almost instantaneous burning pain made his mind go blank for a moment, then he fell from midair, nearly losing consciousness.
“I didn’t kill you instantly, thinking you might have something to say with all your rambling. Turns out it’s just like a pyramid scheme, always recruiting people.”
Colin pursed his lips, slowly approached the man dangling in the living room, charred, and his seemingly unaffected demeanor shocked the charred man:
“How, how is this possible? How can you… How can you withstand it…”
If he was locked onto by him, the damage dealt by the other party would surely be returned in double. He was on the brink of death in an instant, yet the other man seemed unscathed?
Even, the binding had been directly melted!
Impossible! Absolutely impossible!
But in response to his incredulity, Colin simply smiled:
“The pain I can endure is beyond what you can imagine.”Unless it was a conceptual one-to-one exchange, his constitution far surpassed the other’s limits by several folds—an injury of a thousand points he could take it as it is, yet the other’s health cap was just three hundred, even if it was doubled, he would still end up in debt of a lifeline.
If Colin pulled out the “Ring of Enduring Pain” bestowed by “Lady of Thorns,” it would be overkill, but there was no need.
The only thing worthy of note about this guy was how, despite being quite weak, he had somehow managed to bind a life-and-death curse to him through some means, along with that noose-like object.
In an instant, Colin gathered his thoughts, step by step, he approached, and during this process, the flames wrapped and sealed off the entire room.
Finally, reaching the man, Colin lifted a foot and placed it on his throat, gently pressing down.
“Now, you still have one chance to live. Tell me, who sent you?”
Given that the man had just tried to recruit him, he probably wasn’t a heretic acting on a whim; he must have had a clear target to find him directly.
Otherwise, with all the disturbances in fate given by the “Fate Propellers”, with his strength, there would be no chance to enter this door.
Moreover, simply being an employee of “Bonfire Company” granted immunity to most divinations and surveillance.
Colin grew curious, how exactly had this fellow found him?
However, Colin didn’t hold out much hope that the man would answer his question, as these heretics, once connected with the Evil Gods, aside from burning, there weren’t many good solutions in a short time.
Unless the source was dealt with first, then he could trace down from the source to resolve it.
But to Colin’s surprise, in response to his words, the heretic actually responded.
“Who sent me? It is He, join us, return to His embrace. People connect with each other, no longer alone. Facing despair, we bond tightly, nurturing the birth of greatness. Maternity is He, mercy is He…” his voice was somewhat confused as he clamored.
“Enough, there’s no need to say more.”
Colin applied pressure with his right foot on his neck, his mouth pressed tight, expressionless as his gun pointed at the man’s head and he pulled the trigger.
After a few gunshots, the heretic’s body instantly relaxed.
But Colin didn’t let his guard down, flames swirled, poured down from his foot, and with a forceful stomp, the whole body crumbled like a brittle eggroll, leaving debris faintly glowing red.
The debris, further intensified by the flames, turned to ashes and then after a while even the ashes were gone.

chapters.title: Chapter 699 - 699 510 The World Fluctuation Brought by Red
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 699: Chapter 510 The World Fluctuation Brought by “Red Moon”…_2 Chapter 699: Chapter 510 The World Fluctuation Brought by “Red Moon”…_2 Even so, he still felt a bit uneasy.
“Strange, how did ‘Red Moon’s’ followers suddenly find me here?”
Colin glanced out the window, his brow deeply furrowed, sensing that this sudden incident was somewhat abnormal.
Especially the slight anomaly he sensed in the “moonlight” that appeared earlier, was making him inexplicably restless…
At that moment, Qin Chuan’s phone call came through again.
“Mr. Colin…” The voice sounded a bit hurried, as if he was running.
“It’s fine, I’ve already dealt with it. Who was that guy who just barged in? How did you know it was coming? And did anything else happen tonight?”
Colin rattled off several questions in one breath.
“Previously when we couldn’t reach you by phone, Hu Zheng said he felt something was wrong, so we came over together. We just happened to see something creeping in, and that’s also when the call went through. And, just a few minutes ago, in our city and the surrounding areas, several regions experienced a lot of sudden abnormalities…”
Accustomed to Colin’s personality, Qin Chuan spoke quickly about the situation in the surrounding area. And as he finished, Hu Zheng’s voice could be heard on the phone, “Mr. Colin, I have a vague feeling that this disturbance might be related to something reddish, you know that one, but I’m not very sure…”
“I understand, don’t speculate, just come over to my room first.”
Colin hung up the phone, took out his cellphone, and tried to contact Xu Duojin.
With such an obvious anomaly, this high-level contact of his must know something.
But there was no response yet?
“What’s the situation with ‘Red Moon’? Why has it suddenly started to move…” Colin muttered to himself, gazing at the faintly discernible bright moonlight outside the window.
…
At the same time, in a dark arena where flames were lit everywhere yet visibility was extremely low, almost to the point of not seeing one’s own hands, Old Master Wu stood quietly.
The silence in the darkness was as if nothing existed, while there seemed to be a ‘deafening’ turbulence stirring up.
From his left arm upward, he became countless black threads, and with his right hand raised, he looked as if he was holding an invisible book. His whole being stood steadfast in the darkness, like a rock amidst a maelstrom, unfazed by the onrushing inky tides.
In the waters before him, a city shrouded in gloom seemed to be trying to connect with this reality.
Yet, with countless indistinct black threads interfering, the proximity of the city remained endlessly slow.
Within the blurry darkness of the city, a faint red light flickered almost imperceptibly…
And through that red light, one could see the outline of a highly modernized city dominated by nightfall, the towering skyscrapers standing like silent, helpless giants beneath the darkness, the red light, and the ceaselessly writhing starlight.
Countless gazes emerged from the darkness…
And with its approach, even the slightest inch nearer could lead to an earthquake in this area.
Old Master Wu remained undisturbed, his gaze calm and indifferent, having made all necessary preparations.
He knew that enclosed within were entities beyond human comprehension, that once that dark world merged with reality, it would inevitably invade.
Then, a disaster of apocalyptic proportion, impossible for nearly anyone to stop, would erupt in an instant.
It was crucial to ensure, at all costs, that the fantastical and eerie city was kept far away!
At this moment, at some distance behind him, beside several unusual coffins and a number of one-way portals in ready posture—
If the situation turned dire, numerous Ninth Level Personnel would be resurrected from the coffins and members of the Supernatural Alliance from all over the world would rush to the scene, preparing for a desperate fight.
Even some well-performing heretics were allowed by Old Wu to come and support…
In the face of such a terrifying entity, humanity must marshal all available forces!
Fortunately, the most dangerous situation did not occur.
After about half an hour with Old Master Wu’s efforts, the modern city on the coast, mirage-like atop the ocean, began to disappear slowly under the influence of “Fate”…
The light from the fires around slowly became visible again.
“Thanks to the efforts of many, the city eager to descend upon reality once again sank into an invisible abyssal prison, unable to rise for a certain period of time…”
A narrative akin to a narrator echoed in everyone’s ears, putting an end to the incident.
“Hoo.”
Old Master Wu exhaled a long breath, waved his hand, and the various intent gazes that were anxiously watching receded slowly.
Then, his right hand still appeared to be holding an invisible book, but the myriad of threads that had transformed his left hand began to retract, turning back into a hand.
Looking at the scattered corpses on the ground, he touched his sweaty, bald head with his left hand:
“Sigh, I’ve died a few more times, burned through decades of lifespan.”
In this sentiment, numerous dark and elongated hands suddenly reached out from the shadows behind him, grasped at the white hairs running amok on the ground, and reinserted them into the pores of his smooth scalp.
And after almost everything was handled, the impact here had mostly diminished, and the light from the flames could now shine normally on the surroundings.
Old Master Wu lowered his right hand, took a deep breath, and absorbed the warmth coming from the light of the flames.
After facing the darkness, the flames seemed so precious, completely mesmerizing.

chapters.title: Chapter 700 - 700 510 The World Fluctuation Brought by Red
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 700: Chapter 510 The World Fluctuation Brought by “Red Moon”…_3 Chapter 700: Chapter 510 The World Fluctuation Brought by “Red Moon”…_3 At that moment, the sound of footsteps approached as several high-order “Fate Propeller” personnel walked over from farther back; these were all the high-order “Fate Propellers” that could be summoned.
Among them was Xu Duojin, who had always been handing over duties to Colin.
At this time, he stepped forward and said:
“Mr. Wu.”
“Similar to before, this time we managed pretty smoothly,” he said.
Looking at these people, Old Master Wu combed his hand through his hair as if it were a comb, and smiling, he started to speak.
He paused for a moment and without waiting for the crowd to speak, continued:
“However, the frequency of this thing’s appearance has indeed become more and more frequent. Initially, it used to pop up once or twice every couple of years, but in recent years, it’s been once or twice a year. This year, it has appeared three times already.”
Each time it appeared, even if they hurried back, it didn’t mean everything was over.
Although its influence was weak and fleeting, it nearly covered the entire world, causing anomalies to erupt everywhere.
“Next, Xiao Wei, organize a strong team to head out on an Expedition to assist those people; after all, every time it happens here, they do contribute somewhat, even if they are just going through the motions,” he said.
“Okay,” another rather ordinary but handsome middle-aged man nodded in agreement.
“Right, and while you’re at it, tell them, I’ll say it again, we’re not going to set foot on that tiny island. I don’t feel like there’s much hope, so if it has to be abandoned, so be it,” Old Master Wu casually remarked, and the latter continued to nod, indicating he would convey the message.
“Then, the rest of you, start taking care of things from now on. If nothing unexpected happens, there should be ‘weeds’ everywhere that need to be cleared to avoid affecting the big picture.”
Under his arrangements, the personnel present quickly departed, leaving only Xu Duojin alone.
“Duojin, I still have to observe for a couple of days. Afterwards, you go and check where the anomalies have erupted the most. The more they are, the more it means that it has turned its attention to that place. Determine its focal point as quickly as possible… Hmm,” he said.
At this, Old Master Wu seemed to remember something, “But while you search, you must still pay close attention to him. Don’t let anything unexpected happen to him. His missions are out of our hands, but in reality, there must not be any accidents…”
“Okay,” Xu Duojin nodded.
Although no name was mentioned, he knew that Old Master Wu was referring to Colin.
Old Master Wu had high hopes for him and had said more than once that Colin was a key factor in dealing with future catastrophes.
After receiving this assignment, silence suddenly fell over the area. Xu Duojin was preparing to leave when he suddenly heard Old Master Wu’s voice.
“Many years ago, the previous Ninth Level ‘Fate Propeller’ arrived here following the ‘Fate Principle’ and warded off the disaster. Even though he died as a result, he successfully and steadily passed the fate into my hands and entrusted me to ensure the safety of this place. As for me, my time is not much longer, as my ‘Lifespan’ is nearly exhausted…”
“When I die, the disaster will erupt with a severity far beyond the usual, and the others may not be able to withstand it. I’ve done a lot, but I haven’t found a way to stabilize everything, nor have I found a successor who can definitely take over.”
“At that time, because of my inability, the disaster will consume countless lives and destroy our homeland…”
“I…”
“By then, I will probably become an unforgivable sinner…”
His gaze drifted toward the pitch-black sea in the distance, his voice growing lower and more helpless.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 701 - 701 511 Indecent Behavior
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 701: Chapter 511 Indecent Behavior Chapter 701: Chapter 511 Indecent Behavior Standing a few meters behind Old Master Wu, Xu Duojin’s gaze was lowered, not daring to look past Mr. Wu to glimpse the things he saw…
The fact that the other could Direct Gaze and exile it did not mean he could do the same.
In the face of Mr. Wu’s words, Xu Duojin also fell silent, not knowing how to respond for a moment.
As an Extraordinary One, the lifespan of a “Fate Propeller” was actually very long. Not to mention the Ninth Level, just speaking of the Eighth Level, if he accounted for all the lifespan he had consumed, he could live for at least fifteen hundred years.
They could indeed live a very long life by choosing to remain in a corner, ignoring the chaos of the world.
But…
Choosing to come out of seclusion and fight against the tide meant that his lifespan would inevitably decrease with each use of Extraordinary Power.
So much so that he might live even shorter than ordinary people.
The conversion here is relatively complex. A “Fate Propeller” has a base lifespan, as well as additional lifespan gained by becoming a “Fate Propeller.”
The latter increases with strength, but even so, it is still not enough.
Once the added lifespan is used up, it starts to deduct from the “base,” which is their normal lifespan as humans.
This portion of “life” is relatively more valuable…
But no matter how valuable, if expenses exceed income, there will inevitably come a day of deficit.
The reason why people appear relatively aged is exactly because they have touched the “base,” otherwise, they would at most have some white hair, not looking old in their thirties.
And Old Master Wu, running around, has long been in deficit, both the “base” and the part beyond it.
That he is not dead now is purely because there is a “mandatory guarantee” of basic lifespan that allows him to stay alive.
Of course, if Old Master Wu wishes to survive now, there is still an opportunity…
That is during the “mandatory guarantee” phase, to grow as strong as possible and achieve some things, avoid using his power unnecessarily, so as to pay off the “debt” and thus obtain a glimmer of life.
However, it is quite clear that he did not choose so.
After reaching the Ninth Level, Old Master Wu’s strength was still growing, but the lifespan added by becoming stronger was not used by Old Master Wu to “pay the debt,” but continued to be spent in order to maintain the overall situation, to stabilize the stability of the Extraordinary world.
In a sense, prior to the Book of Fate, he could be considered a “debtor.”
Owing a bunch of “money,” and still indulging in “high consumption,” living the high life.
With this thought, a strong sense of unease and palpitations surged in the depths of Xu Duojin’s eyes…
Because, facing Mr. Wu’s debtor yet high-consuming behavior, the Book of Fate did not provide any negative response, even tacitly permitted such behavior to some extent, and never pursued the “debt”—
What, in the end, did it seek to gain?
It was not just Xu Duojin who occasionally thought of these matters and instinctively felt uneasy. All other high-order “Fate Propellers” felt the same.
The inherent nature of the Book of Fate is “balance”; it would not inherently allow such debt-accruing behavior against it…
The cost given by it would inevitably be reclaimed one day.
The lack of reclamation now is most likely because it believes the current debt is not yet sufficient to claim the “cost” it desires.
Apart from Old Wu, no one knew what they would eventually have to repay when the time came.
However, it was at this moment that Old Master Wu’s voice came once more:
“It’s a pity, there isn’t enough time, otherwise if they grew up, they should be able to take over the responsibilities securely.”Hearing these words, Xu Duojin’s chaotic thoughts snapped back to reality, and with an inexplicable shock, he realized he had almost been drawn into this dangerous topic. Then, he immediately followed Old Master Wu’s words and shifted the topic:
“Yes, the future lies with them, but it still needs a little time. When the time comes, we will do our best…”
That batch of “Extraordinary Ones” seedlings that joined the company, after the company’s methods, could “harmlessly” carry and utilize the power of the Book of Fate.
Even, some employees were said to be able to see their current “lifespan” in real-time.
So as to better wield this power…
This made them realize that inside the “Bonfire Company,” there likely existed a mature path for Extraordinary Ones related to the Book of Fate.
Therefore, “Fate Propellers” could perfectly trigger some additional things after joining.
‘If Mr. Wu had been nurtured entirely under that mature path of the company, he probably could have resisted for a few more decades without a problem,’ Xu Duojin couldn’t help thinking.
However, without giving him more time to ponder these matters, Old Master Wu spoke again:
“You should leave now, he must be looking for you.”
“Alright.”
After speaking, Xu Duojin did not hesitate and turned around to leave immediately.
…
Meanwhile, Colin, after ascending to Qin Chuan, upon hearing the report and learning of the multiple abnormal events around, decisively started to act, clearing the crises one by one.
Strange forests from which one couldn’t step out, corpses in morgues coming back to life, houses that moved, and buses that devoured people everywhere.
Piles and piles of aberrant events kept occurring.
Though none of the difficulties were considered high, usually, with a team of Qin Chuan, Xia Liuqian, and Hu Zheng, who were third and fourth-level operators, they could be resolved with some effort. Colin’s personal involvement made it even simpler: A fire to burn the forest, a fire to burn the corpses, a fire to burn the houses…
Wherever he went, he set it ablaze.
Yet, though mostly not too challenging, these events further assured Colin.
A certain event must have happened that night, and these incidents were likely related to the earlier “moonlight” abnormality.

chapters.title: Chapter 702 - 702 511 Not to be done. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 702: Chapter 511: Not to be done. _2 Chapter 702: Chapter 511: Not to be done. _2 Even related to the “Red Moon”…
“Speaking of which, apart from that one Follower of the ‘Red Moon’, I haven’t seen others; this seems a bit abnormal. Usually, these guys would emerge in swarms, but this time there’s only one? Coincidence?”
Colin beckoned with his hand, and flames erupted, turning a rogue bus that was rampaging through a secluded area and devouring anyone it saw into ashes.
During this process, he ensured that those who were still alive inside the bus continued to live.
It was after continuously resolving seven or eight abnormal incidents that Colin suddenly had a feeling and looked in a certain direction, where he saw Xu Duojin approaching from one side, and the companions like Qin Chuan beside him quietly walked away to tend to the injured on the scene, waiting for additional support.
“Let’s talk in the car,” Xu Duojin pointed to a business van parked not far away.
Colin nodded and followed him.
“Tonight’s events should be related to the ‘scarlet moon’…” Xu Duojin began directly as soon as Colin got in.
“Red Moon”… Colin nodded, knowing that Xu Duojin, under normal circumstances, would avoid saying “Red Moon” directly if he could.
“As for the specifics, I’ve forgotten a bit now, the place is such that once you leave, in some sense, it is ‘seen and then forgotten’, even I am not an exception. I can only roughly tell you that tonight’s events are related to this thing.”
After pausing, Xu Duojin added and continued, “Of course, you don’t need to be too nervous or worried, just continue what you should be doing. There are still people holding on, so don’t fret too much.”
‘So vague…’
Colin pursed his lips, feeling that the response was a bit perfunctory, but seeing that Xu Duojin indeed didn’t seem to know much.
Or perhaps, as he mentioned, it was a case of ‘seen and then forgotten’?
However, he also picked up on the key point in the other person’s words: “There are still people holding on? How much longer can they last…”
“About half a year,” Xu Duojin said.
Xu Duojin didn’t specify who it was, but there weren’t many candidates who could hold on, and through this timeframe, Colin could roughly guess who it was.
“This sort of event has happened before; it’s not anything particularly big. At most, there might be some abnormal incidents erupting, but for now, you don’t need to focus all your attention here. If it becomes troublesome, don’t bother with it too much, prioritize what you’re doing on your end,” Xu Duojin said.
“Okay.”
Colin nodded and did not continue to inquire further.
Afterward, they exchanged a few more words, discussed the end-of-month transactions, and Xu Duojin also obtained a copy of their action routes they had just taken and then left for the time being.
Old Master Wu had told him to keep an eye on Colin to prevent any mishaps, so now that he was back, he needed to quickly figure out the surrounding situation.
Understand if anyone had been plotting against Colin in secret during this time.
Of course, as Colin’s strength was rapidly increasing, Xu Duojin felt that helping the other conceal himself in the city was becoming increasingly difficult. When he first met Colin a couple of months ago, everything was still manageably well.
Back then, despite being strong, it seemed manageable because he didn’t possess too much extraordinary power.
But now, it seemed that Colin’s strength had already surpassed his own.
As he tried to help hide him, it was like a piece of paper trying to cover a fire; not being burned along with it was already a blessing; it simply couldn’t hide the flames…
The power that Colin possessed was naturally not meant to be hidden; it was very conspicuous.
Sometimes, when Xu Duojin was far away and closed his eyes, he could still vaguely sense a kind of flame igniting somewhere.
If the flame were big enough, it would be fine, but now, while indeed strong, it still somewhat lacked that final oomph to solve everything.
…
“About half a year’s time, huh?”
Colin raised his hand and touched his chin, wondering if there was enough time.
Theoretically, as long as he could step into C Level and become a “Firebearer,” things here wouldn’t be resolved entirely, but at least there shouldn’t be any problem keeping things stable, but…
Reaching C Level might be attainable, but becoming a “Firebearer” was uncertain.
The higher his strength rose, the more Colin felt that something was amiss with the current situation, like a heavy snowfall with no means of starting a fire to ignite that first spark.
Once the fire started, everything would be fine.
Once the flame ignited, any place could become kindling, and the fire could quickly grow fierce.
The fear was that it wouldn’t start…
Then all he could do was longingly sigh at the kindling.
“This is tough, I can only take it one step at a time,” he mused.
Colin shook his head without much fuss, glanced outside the vehicle, and saw that Qin Chuan and others were still dealing with the scene, with no issues, so he took out the parchment and looked it over.
Contrary to his expectations, the employees on the parchment seemed surprisingly happy.
“Confused Cutie ①Sob Sob⑦”: Damn, brothers, we’re open for business! A bunch of tasks came in today!
“Pissing Against the Wind”: Hurry up and do them! Otherwise, all these Emperor of Labors will snatch them away!
“Your pompadour is too big”: Damn it, I had to compete when I was just a regular person, and now as an Extraordinary One, I still have to hustle. I never got to experience those show-off, highlight moments, and instead, I’m stuck in this endless rat race every day!
“Little Building Breezed Last Night”: Actually, it’s not so bad; some tasks allow you to encounter regular people and flex a bit of muscle. My current boyfriend was someone I rescued myself…
“Miss Nell’s Dog”: @Little Building Breezed Last Night, 6.
“Professor Cute Cuddle”: Brothers, if you don’t want to compete, you can consider “The Descent Project”, “World Code-13”, Brother Shunzi is leading the team himself, no life-threatening risks involved, easy work, relaxed and comfortable, each task only requires three hours and you can easily pocket thousands of points…
“Pure Innocent Smile”: Three hours? I’ll believe that when pigs fly…
…
“Being clueless seems pretty nice too.”
Colin sighed. The majority of the employees were carefree like amoebae, unlike him— the more he knew, the more likely he was to have a lot on his mind and find it hard to be happy.
Then, he got in touch with “Life Mentor Adorable” and asked for a list.
This time, selecting people, he had his eye on the top ten percent of D Level Personnel.
He planned to pick five lucky individuals from among them.
As for those below D Level, although the official side was still not keen on letting him take people to join the adventure in the Other World, the issue wasn’t too big.
The company had a huge number of employees, so it would be enough to select some with specialized skills.
“This time, in addition to mastering land development technologies, we need to find some who can effectively manage the population and establish an effective administrative system…”
Colin muttered to himself. With the rapid expansion of his territory and the surge in population numbers, the original rudimentary management was no longer enough.
It was necessary to put together a more suitable and efficient framework, lest it become difficult to handle the crowds later…
In this regard, the officials were actually quite helpful, often mobilizing talents from all over the world to design various things, new ethnic concepts, spiritual outlooks, new values in life, and so on.
However, this kind of assistance was only like scratching an itch through a boot.
Specific employees needed to be found to carry out these tasks while the Little Maid handled supervisory and assistive management duties.
“Sigh, according to Xu Duojin, it seems some people from the official side have joined the company, but unfortunately, they seem to be cultivated by various factions as some sort of Spark and aren’t willing to be transferred to me.”
Colin felt it was a pity.
Not to say that there was a lack of talent outside of the officials, the company was full of all sorts of people, so finding the right talent shouldn’t be a problem, but the issue was, Colin didn’t have their personal details, making them hard to find.
However, the good thing was that after a long period of “desensitization” work,
Nowadays, people were less resistant to “The Descent Project.”
After all, of the initial fifty people, to this date, not one had died…
And the points they earned were indeed substantial.
So much so that Colin even saw people proactively inquiring about the situation and expressing their interest, and aside from a few who weren’t to his taste, they were all pretty good…
Afterward, having chosen some acceptable employee names and noting them in his notebook, Colin put away the parchment, planning to allocate tasks to them after he entered the event in some time.
“Next, there’s the delivery task on the 20th for ‘South Sea Bodhisattva’…”
Colin thought for a moment and decided to stake out the place tomorrow to ensure he arrived at the scene at the earliest opportunity.
Of course, before that, he had to clear all the anomalies near his home to prevent any new problems from cropping up in this area while he was carrying out the task.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 703 - 703 512 The Furious Fisherman._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 703: Chapter 512: The Furious “Fisherman”._1 Chapter 703: Chapter 512: The Furious “Fisherman”._1 That night, deep in the mountainous woods, darkness prevailed but there was no peace.
The constant explosions and firearms created a cacophony as a group of uniformed people wielded various weapons, besieging a dangerous creature in front of them that had four arms and resembled a mountain demon in shape, but was many times larger.
However, despite their numerical advantage, it was very difficult to take down the creature quickly.
Its strength and constitution were, in a sense, incomprehensible!
Every bullet from machine guns and cannons, though they caused injury and seemed as if they would blow the creature apart, tearing its flesh, seconds later it would regenerate to its original form.
At first, the Sixth Level Personnel were undaunted, attacking with firepower relentlessly under the belief, “I doubt your luck can last forever,” but now…
They had become believers of the curse.
What was worse, that damn monster seemed to trigger a Second Order transformation. If the flesh torn by artillery was not promptly dealt with, it would turn into smaller, yet similar mountain demon creatures.
And they moved extremely fast, attacking their enemies like zombies…
Since its initial appearance, the only thing the people had managed to do was lure it into the mountains to avoid it rushing towards civilians and causing greater casualties.
“Keep suppressing it at a distance of thirty to fifty meters as much as possible, waiting for higher-level assistance. Be extremely careful now, and don’t let it touch you; a touch would mean either death or injury,” warned a Sixth Level Official Personnel, vigilantly observing the situation and commanding his team through a microphone while throwing out various charms, forming killer moves that trapped the enemy.
However, as he was distracted by speaking, he saw the mountain demon dive at him aggressively.
