A chill went down his spine and he somersaulted in desperation, trying his best to evade, but was still hit.
The creature’s massive arm swept across…
With a loud boom, the rocks behind him were shattered into a large crater.
He too was unfortunately hit, but luckily, under his outer clothes, various charms activated, flashing with golden light that shielded him from the brunt of the blow…
“Phew, that was close,” the Sixth Level Official Personnel grunted in pain as he widened the distance between them.
Several team members immediately advanced to cover him, but to their surprise, the mutant mountain demon creature didn’t seize the opportunity to follow up with a lethal attack—this was against common sense!
It was then that the Sixth Level Personnel suddenly heard a scream through his headset, and he immediately realized something, looking towards the battlefield to find a person rushing at high speed towards the gigantic creature, seemingly intending to tackle it with a small handgun…
In his view, this was utterly unrealistic, surely a squad member had decided to sacrifice themselves to buy him time to escape!
“Damn it, come back!” he yelled, urging the person to retreat, not wanting to lose a member of his team.
At the same time, there was some admiration in his heart; he hadn’t expected…
However, the employee didn’t seem to listen. Covered by a hail of bullets, they approached the colossal being at a speed that was neither fast nor slow, raised their hand, and drew a revolver…
“Bang, bang,” two sharp sounds rang out as two flaming bullets pierced through the corrupted extraordinary creature’s chest and head.
Its massive body fell with a thud, not even managing to let out a scream…
“How is this possible?!” exclaimed the Sixth Level Personnel in shock.
How could he have someone like that under him?
No, was that the support?
No, that wasn’t right either; the Seventh Level “Fate Propeller” he had called for support didn’t use these methods…
But in the next second, that figure vanished into thin air…
While the Sixth Level Personnel was on high alert, he suddenly saw that person reappear right beside him, his eyes intense, holding several cards in his left hand and a flaming revolver in his right.
And what was particularly eerie was that he was wearing a casual outfit with slippers on his feet.
“You are…” he asked cautiously, on guard.
He had heard that sometimes Heretics would assist the authorities, but it had only been hearsay, until now.
However, in response to his question, the man before him didn’t say much, only giving him a few glances.
“It seems you haven’t suffered any serious injuries,” Colin’s gaze drifted from the sunken chest of the man before him, then he quickly left the scene without further interference.
Guided by some kind of Spiritual Intuition, he swiftly hunted down the anomalies that had emerged due to the “Red Moon” fluctuation.
Of course, more precisely, Colin just inexplicably felt…
There was something very ‘hot’ ahead, so he went over, which was not quite the same as his usual Spiritual Intuition.
“Speaking of which, a single fluctuation from ‘Red Moon’ seems to last no more than a second, yet affects almost half the world. What if it erupts? What then?” Colin wondered anxiously, feeling that if the Red Moon were to truly awaken, even a simple stretch would be enough to trigger an apocalyptic disaster in an instant.
‘Such a near-conceptual, high-dimensional existence, just by being, is incredibly dangerous…’ he sighed in his heart, suppressing his anxious thoughts. For now, other than trusting Xu Duojin’s assurance that this kind of disaster was currently under control, he had no other option.
His priority was to grow stronger quickly, strong enough to withstand anything…
Afterwards, he focused on clearing the various anomalies that had erupted that night, ensuring that he wouldn’t return from one trip to find his home no longer there.
The night passed swiftly…
By the next morning, after a busy night, Master Colin, following the mission schedule, set out a day early on the nineteenth to Bengkulu Bay and slowly approached the island where the Heretic was stationed, guided by his Spiritual Intuition.

chapters.title: Chapter 704 - 704 512 The Furious Fisherman._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 704: Chapter 512: The Furious “Fisherman”._2 Chapter 704: Chapter 512: The Furious “Fisherman”._2 To avoid startling the heretics, Colin didn’t rush on his way as he usually did with a great fanfare.
Instead, he meandered through the use of Little Maid’s and “Yukionna’s” powers…
Even leisurely standing on a seawater-corroded plank, fishing with a hook he had just bought at an auction while moving forward…
He had always heard that seafood caught straight from the sea was especially delicious, and today, having some free time, he decided to give it a try.
“Yukionna” floated beside him, batting her large eyes in curiosity at what he was doing.
“This is fishing.”
Colin explained his actions to “Yukionna” with a smile, taking the opportunity to temper her somewhat eager personality.
“With fishing, the most important thing is patience. If you have patience, sooner or later a fish will bite, just like now, there are fish following the bait, and when the time comes, I’ll let you try the freshly caught fish. It’s absolutely delicious,” Colin said like an experienced angler.
“Yukionna,” with the figure of a lady but the intelligence of a little girl, lay next to Colin by the edge of the plank, licking her lips with her tongue in half-understanding, curiously peering into the water, eagerly waiting for the fish to bite.
About ten minutes later, she looked up at him and exhaled a puff of cold air…
“Are you wondering why there hasn’t been a bite yet? It’ll happen soon, don’t rush, be as composed as I am.”
Colin nodded, indicating the need to wait a little longer, as rushing would only spoil the effort.
An hour later, “Yukionna” looked at him again.
Colin’s expression became more serious—
He could feel that many fish seemed interested in his hook, but they wouldn’t bite; instead, they followed along, nibbling at the bait…
“What the hell, following me and nibbling without biting, you’re just teasing me!” Colin grumbled under “Yukionna’s” watchful eye, as he cast his fishing rod and jumped into the water.
Dammit, you can’t let them get away with this!
Before long, Colin still managed to enjoy the fish he caught with “Yukionna,” despite some minor setbacks.
After a simple meal, he took out the seldom-used “Emblem of the Humility Knight,” reducing his presence before drifting toward his destination.
Of course, although he wasn’t moving at full speed, he was still much faster than most cars on the highway.
The vast sea showed no sign of stormy waves, and the scorching sun shone on the sea surface, reflecting off it like shiny scales…
“It sure is hot near the Equator.”
Colin grumbled to himself as he felt the warmth from the direct sunlight.
Almost two hours later, following the mission’s guidance, Colin finally saw a small island on the sea surface, as tiny as a grain of rice.
Unexpectedly, instead of being a deserted and secluded island covered with tropical rainforest, he found a small inhabited island with a miniature port.
“These heretics sure know how to pick a place…” Colin muttered, watching the small city built along the island and sending a picture to Xu Duojin with his phone.
Shortly after, Xu Duojin replied.
“We’ve checked, and it should be a midway supply point. It originated from the era of World War II powers, a bit off the beaten track but not too remote. Now it has been converted to a general merchant ship supply point. The island normally has a population of around thirty thousand. Besides that, there’s an abandoned Fungus Garrison Base from decades ago.”
“Thirty thousand?” Colin pinched his forehead, feeling a headache coming on.
The heretics were likely hiding in only a small part, but if any trouble arose, the majority would be affected, and with the numbers being high, civilians were likely to suffer casualties.
As for the background of the island, he was not too interested in learning more, since the mission did not require gathering such information.
At this moment, Xu Duojin continued to send messages.
“At present, under the guise of military… exercises, our naval forces should be able to reach the island within five hours. If needed, we can provide long-range strike capabilities or support a beach landing, etc…”
“If that’s not enough, other countries are currently conducting anti-pirate exercises under the name of joint…military…exercises in the Indo…cean. They’ll be slower, arriving in about nine hours for long-range strikes and other assistance. You can also call on their forces if required…”
“Alright, that’s sufficiently robust in military virtue…”
Colin floated in mid-air, looking at the information on his phone, then indicated that he didn’t need that right now.
However, should a fight break out, he would need people to evacuate the innocent.
After briefly mentioning his needs, Colin put away his phone and, after about fifteen minutes, stealthily came ashore on the edge of the island. Then, he entered the small port city…
After all, this mission involved infiltrating the enemy’s stronghold, so he had to be a bit cautious.
To avoid capsizing in a small ditch, as one might say.
As the island’s only bustling area, it was densely packed with people.
The locals mainly consisted of darker, smaller Southeast Asian types, as well as the occasional other nationalities resting at the port…
On the streets, there were also armed guards…
But whether it was guards or anyone else, no one noticed Colin as he walked among them.
However, after walking around for quite a while, he hadn’t seen any sign of the heretics.
“They are well hidden. If it wasn’t for the mission guidance, I probably wouldn’t know there was an issue here… but speaking of which, the lobsters and fish here are indeed really cheap…”

chapters.title: Chapter 705 - 705 512 The Furious Fisherman._3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 705: Chapter 512: The Furious “Fisherman”._3 Chapter 705: Chapter 512: The Furious “Fisherman”._3 Passing through a small market, Colin couldn’t help but click his tongue twice.
If this were back home, the prices would surely be several times higher…
But before he could take a closer look, he abruptly sensed something, his gaze shifting through the crowd until it finally settled on a middle-aged, plump woman with dark skin and a bald head, covered in large, odd tattoos of lightning, ocean storms, and other symbolic patterns.
Some stationed personnel, upon seeing her, betrayed a hint of fear in their eyes, then stepped aside, not daring to block her way.
It was as if they were avoiding something.
Colin also noticed that on this woman, there was a faint hint of an abnormal presence…
This presence was somewhat similar to that “squatting toilet, octopus head” statue he had seen not long ago.
Colin immediately restrained his thoughts, held his breath, and quietly followed her.
The woman, carrying a basket of groceries, walked towards the edge of the small city and directly into a wetland forest, where, despite being somewhat overweight, she moved through as swiftly as a catfish.
Shortly after, Colin saw some ruined military facilities.
And from this place, that statue-like aura spread faintly in the air…
He stopped his footsteps, didn’t continue tracking her, and then seemed to sense something, looking to the other side and quickly flew over.
Not far from here, there was a group of light-skinned armed personnel in tight outfits, about thirty-something people…
“Remember, at three o’clock in the afternoon, just rush in, destroy all the ceremonial arrangements, then retrieve the Containment Subject that sank nearby all those years ago and return, still several hours left…”
“Mike, you dress up a bit later, disguise yourself as a Believer, take this chance to go in as an investor, and get the lay of the land…”
The white commander was issuing orders to a yellow-skinned man beside him, but before he could finish, his body suddenly shuddered, feeling a weight on his shoulder as a hand laid upon him.
He turned immediately, and there was a man in casual clothing and flip-flops beside him, one hand on his shoulder.
What horrified him even more was that, despite his near-Eighth Level combatant strength, at this very moment, he was pinned down by some force, unable to move an inch…
Not just him, everyone present was under a strong suppression, immobilized.
“Although I don’t know what you plan to retrieve, for now, I hope you don’t disrupt my plans,”
Colin spoke softly to them, “Understand?”
The team leader attempted to struggle, showing an unyielding spirit, but recognizing the gap between him and Colin, he still nodded:
“Okay.”
In his eyes, this suddenly appearing man must be some powerful Heretic evildoer.
He might not be bloodthirsty, but he was definitely no good person!
“That’s good.”
Colin nodded, his gaze turning towards the abandoned military base overgrown with wild grass and painted with various strange patterns.
Among them, many Believers were worshipping a “Buddha Statue” dressed in a monk’s robe but with an octopus head.
This statue, unlike the ‘squatting toilet’ posture, had a similar aura.
It was almost certain that this was the destination…
And the mission required waiting for them to conduct the ritual and open the passage before acting; before that, not only could Colin not disrupt it, he even had to protect its successful progression, otherwise there was no way to keep an ace up his sleeve for that “South Sea Bodhisattva.”
Meanwhile, after seeing Colin “relax,” the white man quickly made some sort of spiritual contact with his superiors in his mind.
He briefly explained that he had encountered a powerful Heretic and requested support.
The light-skinned squad leader didn’t have much faith in the reinforcements, just wanting to get the message out to inform others of the situation here.
His submission was merely to convey the intelligence about this location, to avoid fatal errors in follow-up.
However, to his surprise, there was actually a response for support from the other end…
“Conveniently, we just learned that a very powerful agent of ours seems to have landed on the island. With his strength, as long as you make a call, in ten seconds, he can save you all.”
“Thank you!”
The white man glanced at the man beside him, took a deep breath, and, feeling that with his near-Eighth Level strength, he should be able to last ten seconds.
After receiving a set of special codes from the transmission, he immediately dialed using the most advanced tactical helmet with a brain wave interface, then braced for protection…
Ten seconds! All he needed was ten seconds!
He thought this, but suddenly realized that the “support” didn’t even seem to need ten seconds.
Because in the next second…
The phone in the right pocket of that strange man’s shorts buzzed with a vibration.
“Hello, who’s there?”
The man pulled out the phone and put it to his ear while keeping his eyes on the abandoned military facility.

chapters.title: Chapter 706 - 706 513 Keeping Ones Cards Close to the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 706: Chapter 513 Keeping One’s Cards Close to the Chest!_1 Chapter 706: Chapter 513 Keeping One’s Cards Close to the Chest!_1 “I need assistance…”
Clutching the cell phone in his hand, Colin heard not a human voice on the other end, but an electronic synthesized one.
He hadn’t used any shielding, so despite the very low volume of the sound coming from the phone…
the group behind him, all far more perceptive than ordinary people, could hear it clearly.
Especially the white squad leader, who upon hearing his own message, edited by consciousness, couldn’t stop his pupils from violently shaking.
He had reported upward, how could it be that the other party had answered the call?
For him, the situation was akin to encountering evil forces while stepping outside, secretly calling the police, only to have the phone of the robber ring.
What was left was just embarrassment…
Immediately, he couldn’t help but wonder if the incredibly strong ally had been killed?
But he quickly dismissed the thought.
He was one of the elite among Level Seven Officials, described as super-strong, perhaps close to Level Nine personnel; how could such a person be taken out silently and instantly?
So it was very likely a misunderstanding…
Fortunately, it seemed the other party did not know it was he who had made the call…
“What, you need assistance?”
As he was thinking this, the young man in front of him abruptly turned his head to look at him: “Assistance with what?”
Colin suddenly appeared beside him, hand resting on his shoulder; he also didn’t seem to detect anywhere in need of assistance, did he?
“There’s a certain probability that he has misunderstood your purpose.” The Little Maid’s reminder rang in his ears.
It was she who had intercepted the phone signal source and informed Colin that the person “needing assistance” was just behind them…
As the Little Maid’s voice faded, Colin indeed saw the white squad leader offering an awkward yet polite smile, his eyes filled with a flicker of panic as he tried to explain the situation.
They were still very afraid of this formidable presence who could appear unnoticed and suppress everyone in the vicinity…
Especially with higher-ranking personnel being notoriously volatile, it was entirely possible that because of such a small misunderstanding, they would all be killed.
If that were the case…
Great Britain would likely only have two reactions: one, to strongly condemn the other party for the use of terrifying weapons that caused their personnel’s deaths, and to declare the sending of higher-order Extraordinary Ones for punishment, demanding the place they represented pay the price; but this situation generally occurs if the man in question was only Level Seven or below.
Two, he would be honored for dying in battle against Heretic Believers, and all would be well with the other side, because they truly possessed terrifying weapons…
From the looks of it, the second possibility was very likely; the other side indeed had terrifying weapons!
Every person above Eighth Level, including those at Eighth Level, begins to possess a certain strategic value in this world.
And regardless of which of the above, he was doomed!
Thinking about this, he profoundly regretted making the call for assistance, as his speech became somewhat tremulous:
“I, I’m sorry…”
“All right, stop there, I understand.”
Colin waved his hand, not understanding why the man seemed inexplicably fearful; he wasn’t a bad person after all.
But, without paying much attention to that, he continued his observation.
At the small military base in the distance, those Heretic Followers appeared to be worshipping a Buddha-like, octopus-headed figure, shouting things like “May the winds be favorable and the rains timely.”
Some people around them were continuously smearing bright red blood all around, drawing strange and eerily complex Futharks, meaning they were likely setting up the ritual site; so much so that one could smell the blood even from far away…
“The Believers seem to have no real strength, all of them ordinary people, but a little deeper inside that bunker over there, there seem to be some individuals whose strength doesn’t exceed Official Level Six…”
Colin leapt onto the wetland forest canopy, secretly observing and gathering information.
If he wanted, he could simply throw a fireball over there and everyone present, including those Extraordinary Ones in the bunker, would be incinerated…
But, the mission required him to let them open the passageway and successfully conduct the ritual.
Otherwise, he wouldn’t be able to deliver the package…
That’s why, before this, upon seeing this white squad, he had to come prevent any accidents from occurring.
“Speaking of which, do you have other people here?”
Colin leapt down from the canopy, landing silently, and casually asked those beside him.
“Yes, apart from us, there are a few response teams, some armed boats, and also a submarine…”
“Wow, quite a lot of people.”
Colin was surprised, because in order to remain covert, he had shielded his light, which meant there were some things he wasn’t very clear about.
“Do you understand what’s going on here? Also, what are you here to do?” he continued to inquire. The man hesitated for a few seconds before finally explaining the situation.
They had been lurking in this place for over half a month, aiming to retrieve a key item from various war reparation artifacts received from a certain country during a war a hundred years ago…
At that time, a warship had sunk near an island.
With so many years having passed, they hadn’t considered recovering it, thinking that the ship, mainly filled with antiques, probably had rotted away.
But in recent years, with the resurgence of many strange phenomena.
An object up there caught their attention…
At this, the squad leader paused for a moment, looking at Colin with a touch of awe.
He wasn’t sure if it was just an illusion, but when mentioning the war reparation artifacts, he suddenly felt an overwhelming pressure, as if he was about to suffocate.
Thankfully, this sensation only lasted a moment, appearing to be merely an illusion.

chapters.title: Chapter 707 - 707 513 Keep a Trick up Your Sleeve _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 707: Chapter 513: Keep a Trick up Your Sleeve! _2 Chapter 707: Chapter 513: Keep a Trick up Your Sleeve! _2 But this made him weigh his words and tone even more carefully, no longer displaying the pride he had when he just mentioned that part of history.
What was once a glory, was now a death knell.
Times had changed…
“So what are you here to find?” Colin asked casually.
“Mainly, there’s a special intangible containment subject on our soil that we can’t contain, but a part of its cage is here. It was fished up and left here by those uncultured barbarians from North America, and we want to retrieve the cage to see if we can contain that thing…”
The squad leader revealed his mission this time.
“Oh.”
Colin glanced at these guys, unsure which country was responsible for that part of history, considering many had ground “My Great Qing” into the dust.
But now, it was possible to guess where this team came from…
If nothing surprising occurred, they were likely from that island where, nowadays, strange phenomena might outnumber people.
At this moment, the squad leader added, “Originally we had plenty of time, but for some reason, a few days ago, we were suddenly ordered to act within these two days and retrieve that item.”
Suddenly asked to hasten the pace? Was it because of me… Colin muttered to himself inwardly.
Nevertheless, he didn’t voice it out and just said,
“Considering this, we actually have no conflict. Wait until I finish my action tomorrow, then see for yourselves if you have a chance to retrieve that thing. Also… if you succeed in using that item to contain the subject, you should send, well, return it to us.”
“I’m not going to take advantage of you. In this case, I won’t charge you extra,”
“Consider it my payment for helping you this time.”
“This…” The squad leader was momentarily stunned; such matters were beyond his decision-making authority!
“May I communicate with the higher-ups?”
“Be my guest.”
Colin waved his hand indifferently, knowing that barring the unexpected, his request would be accepted.
Sure enough, about a minute later, the squad leader nodded his agreement.
As for any second thoughts they might have, Colin wasn’t particularly worried…
If they didn’t give it to him, he’d simply take it himself; it wasn’t much of an issue. Colin estimated his strength to be greater than that of some C Level corporate staff members and certainly surpassing over ninety-nine percent of Earth’s official Ninth Level Personnel.
In such circumstances, no one could refuse his reasonable demands.
Of course, if such an event did occur, Colin wouldn’t mind asking them, “Friend, what makes you disrespect me so?”
“Now we wait until I conclude my actions tomorrow…”
After giving his instructions, Colin’s figure vanished as he found another more suitable observation area to lie in wait alone.
Time passed quickly, and at 3 a.m. on the 20th, the atmosphere of the abandoned military base became unnaturally heavy and dense…
More and more Believers arrived from all directions to worship the “Buddha Statue,” with a figure in a dark blue robe, likely a Grand Elder or someone of a similar rank, standing at the forefront leading the worship.
“Southern Bodhisattva, bless us; Southern Bodhisattva, bless us…”
Amidst the echoing chants, the atmosphere finally peaked on the following morning at six.
The ocean, which should’ve been illuminated by the rising sun, was engulfed in absolute darkness under the Dark Cloud.
High above, the clouds grew dense, pressing lower with an oppressive feel.
“It’s coming, it’s coming! The entity is about to descend upon this world!”
The Archbishop’s voice thundered, dense mist emanating from him, streaked with flashes of lightning, and eerie tendrils sprouting across his skin.
And the next second, following his cry, thunder clapped.
Instantly, fierce winds rose and heavy rain fell in torrents!
Surrounding the island for hundreds of meters, kilometers, and even several kilometers out, waterspouts formed in great numbers, mirroring a dragon’s breath.
The sheer force of nature was on full display here, as if the apocalypse was unfolding…
Even Colin couldn’t help but stay on guard.
The Believers might be weak, but the entity they were attempting to summon was indeed powerful…
“At least First Level Containment Subject strength.”
Colin sighed inwardly, remembering official records. Threats of this level numbered a dozen or more on Earth, and that was just what was public knowledge; the hidden threats remained unknown.
Apart from “Level 0” entities, the number of high-level containment subjects here was higher than most other places he had visited.
The problem was that there were remnants of the “Flame Bearer’s” arrangements over there…
But not here.
However, he didn’t dwell on it and shook his head, refocusing his thoughts on the present situation—this could very well lead to a significant mishap.
“It’s coming! It’s coming! I am about to comprehend everything! The future, fate, everything in the world…”
The Grand Elder at the forefront, wearing the deep blue robe, shouted aloud.
His body, subject to some influence, began to distort, with numerous thick tendrils extending from beneath his clothes, wildly lashing the air around him with electric crackles.
“Should we really keep waiting? The end of the world is coming!” a squad member, holding onto a tree to avoid being blown away, sent an electronic communication to Colin.
If it hadn’t been confirmed several times that they were on the same side, he might have suspected a mole.
“If I don’t speak, we keep waiting.”
Colin stood with his hands behind his back, watching ahead.
And it was at that moment that he suddenly sensed something, looking up at the sky to see the thick Dark Cloud suddenly tearing open, as if the sky itself was being ripped apart…

chapters.title: Chapter 708 - 708 513
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 708: 513 Chapter 708: 513 He, feeling something was amiss, soared about a hundred meters into the air and then gazed toward a distant part of the sea near the island. There, he saw a vortex several kilometers in diameter slowly forming and rapidly expanding.
The passage was forming bit by bit!
“Hahaha, South Sea Bodhisattva…” on the altar, the Grand Elder shouted, and then his seven or eight eyes turned to a certain direction.
At the same time, Colin felt a heavy gaze upon him. Following the gaze, he saw that it was the Grand Elder, who seemed to have been parasitized by some force…
“Do you think you’ve been hiding well?! I’ve discovered you long ago! Now, it’s too late to come out!”
The Grand Elder, dressed in a deep blue cassock, said with a mad laughter, his voice piercing through the air.
Meanwhile, on the altar, those worshipping Southeast Asians with slightly dark skin began growing scales, undergoing a transformation of their life form.
“We shall receive the Bodhisattva’s mercy, escape the agony of flesh and blood, enter the sea, and enjoy eternal life!”
“You need not cling to us, and we will no longer come to land. From this day forth, we will head to the Eternal Deep Sea Great Mercy Palace, serve at the Bodhisattva’s side, and from you humans finish our karma, never to be entwined again…”
“Benefactor, please retreat.”
The Grand Elder’s countless tentacles assumed the position of prayer, looking toward Colin, his many eyes filled with dense blood vessels.
However, Colin did not respond. He pursed his lips, thinking that if it were really as the other party said, he might not be opposed to letting them go…
But Colin, who was all too familiar with many secrets, knew very well that the reality might be different from what they imagined.
Now the various Containment Subjects locked up by the “Bonfire Company,” who had gone mad, would say anything just to get out. Colin even suspected that, if possible, they wouldn’t mind claiming they were pregnant with “Flame Bearer” offspring…
Just look at the “King of Madness” to know…
Meanwhile, watching the people below gradually turning into Fishmen, changing their life form.
A thought flashed through his mind, is this considered an ascension of flesh and blood?
“Whatever kind of ascension it is, you dare to believe the blessings of these deities and spirits…”
Colin murmured, ignoring the “South Sea Bodhisattva” Grand Elder, and hovered high above, calmly staring at the huge vortex ahead amidst the stormy winds and torrential rain.
The passage was in the process of being opened and was not yet fully formed.
He temporarily refrained from invoking the Bonfire. Using the power of the “Flame Bearer” at this time would be like suddenly lighting a lamp in the dead of night.
It might easily lead to accidents…
Seeing himself being ignored by Colin, the Grand Elder’s dozens of eyes flashed with overt malice.
“Since the benefactor does not cooperate, refuses to heed advice, then I have no choice but to take action…” Having said that, his muscles and tentacles tensed as he shot towards Colin with explosive force.
Countless bolts of lightning burst from his body, making him resemble a spherical bolt of lightning.
However, just as he thought he was about to touch Colin, he suddenly found his consciousness empty.
With a bang.
By the time he regained his senses, he had already plummeted to the altar, his body surrounded by web-like spreading cracks.
“Just conduct your ritual properly and stop yapping.”
Colin muttered, retracted his foot, and did not pursue further. Below him, the white captain watched, his scalp tingling; that “spherical lightning” had been formidable…
Had it been him, he would probably have been killed instantly, but for Colin, it had been just a kick.
Yet, there was no time to dwell on it…
Between heaven and earth, a succession of heavy, frantic breaths suddenly filled the air.
“Huff.”
In that moment, Colin no longer hesitated. Taking a step in the sky above, he dove towards the vortex, pulling out a Severed Hand from his pocket that, once exposed to air, began burning intensely.
Preparing to throw it into the vortex…
At that moment, a huge and bizarre tentacle shot out from beneath the vortex at high speed. Colin was prepared; his left hand moved, activating “Time Reversal.”
The tentacle that was about to touch him began to “retract.”
And in that moment, Colin no longer hesitated to channel power into the Severed Hand, throwing it into the vortex.
“Rumble rumble~”
Countless bolts of lightning struck out from the vortex, falling upon the Rosen Severed Hand Replica.
But it had no effect on it…
As it entered the passage, a horrifying scream was heard, and in an instant, all the abnormal weather, lacking the support of mysterious attributes, dispersed completely.
“This trick is still useful.”
Seeing this, Colin couldn’t help but express his sentiments.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 709 - 709 514
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 709: 514 Chapter 709: 514 Without any surprise…
The so-called “South Sea Bodhisattva” beneath the Deep Sea was blocked and forced back, unable even to make a sound.
“Another great foe has been removed from the world.”
Colin nodded his head. After four consecutive attempts, he was fairly certain about the subsequent mission procedures.
The only difference, perhaps, was where to execute them.
“Ah!!!”
On the island, the Grand Elder screamed in despair, unwillingness, and so on.
He was actually unable to call upon the great existence he worshipped anymore!
The human face on the Grand Elder’s body, which was covered in tentacles, showed a twisted pain akin to a network disconnection at a critical moment.
However, although his scream didn’t summon the “Bodhisattva,” it successfully captured Colin’s attention.
“If you hadn’t howled just now, I really might not have noticed you, or any of you.”
Colin raised his right hand and stroked his thumb with his index fingernail, like one would strike a flint, and dozens of sparks scattered. In an instant, all the wails ceased completely.
It was as Colin was cleaning up the situation that all over the world, every Believer related to the “South Sea Bodhisattva” or any “Entity of the Deep Sea,” suddenly felt as though their connection to what they worshipped was being severed…
They screamed in terror incessantly, yet they were helpless.
At this moment, having practically solved the major issues, Colin took a final look around to check everything.
The heavy Dark Clouds dissipated rapidly, the dim Earth gradually brightened, and streaks of sunlight pierced the clouds, casting intense beams upon the surface of the sea.
“Nice weather.”
Taking a deep breath, Colin made a call for someone to come and “clean up.”
Then he directly returned to his neighborhood through the channel for completed assignments….
…
The familiar ceiling.
Colin opened his eyes for two seconds, then immediately rolled out of bed. The task had been so easy that it didn’t result in any peculiar sense of disorientation like “The Descent Project” had.
First, he checked the time. It was just before eleven o’clock on the 20th.
Dealing with those things had taken some time, but not much.
Afterward, Colin sat cross-legged on the boat, took out the Parchment, and spread it out. The task had ended, according to the update, but no reward was given. Instead, the next phase of the mission popped up.
“…At 9:37 tonight, at certain coordinates, not too fast nor too slow, ascend to an altitude of around three thousand kilometers and approach some space debris. Then, deploy a ‘Token’ within the debris to prevent further anomalies within the Containment Space contained within…”
“Huh? Three thousand kilometers? That’s beyond the atmosphere, wait, who the hell is tossing Containment Subjects into space…”
“This really is too much!”
Colin raised an eyebrow, unable to help but express his critique.
Although he knew that the Earth officials here had difficulty dealing with many Containment Subjects to the point of exasperation—so much so that sometimes they preferred to dump the Containment Subjects elsewhere rather than deal with them—
He had heard that many countries did this in the early days, until the Alliance was formed and things got a bit better.
But he hadn’t expected anyone to be throwing these things into space.
Moreover, based on the description, it seemed that an entire Containment Space was being thrown out there, along with a large number of Containment Subjects that might not have been dealt with very well, rather than just a single Containment Subject.
Colin pinched his forehead, somewhat speechless.
However, the difficulty of the mission didn’t seem too high overall.
From the looks of things, these deployment tasks happened three times a week, and the first two tasks of each week should not be too difficult, at most providing a thrill without danger, only the third task might be a bit more challenging.
Of course, even knowing the difficulty wasn’t high, Colin still made all possible preparations.
After all, something that had caught the attention of the company or “Lady Rabbit” was definitely not a trivial matter.
He sent the information to Xu Duojin, and soon he received the relevant details.
This time, the intelligence suggested that it wasn’t an individual tossing these things into outer space, but a collective decision by the Alliance…
“It was established quite early on, many things couldn’t be handled, and the strongest Extraordinary Ones were just barely reaching Eighth Level, hence many of the Containment Subjects were not dealt with properly, especially with limited understanding of some Containment Subjects…”
Xu Duojin provided a bit of explanation about the situation back then.
Ninth Level Personnel only became a possibility in the mid-period of anomaly emergence, and the first to reach it was the previous “Fate Propeller.” After that, many followed this path that broke free of constraints.
Only then did so many Ninth Level Personnel emerge.
In the process, people made numerous attempts to cope with various anomalies, and tossing them into space was one of those attempts.
“At least, what we can confirm for now is that we deployed… according to the data, twenty-six Containment Spaces, but we have since reclaimed nine of them…”
“The remaining seventeen, as far as we know, are all being monitored, and they have been quite stable in recent years…”
Stable? If they were truly stable, there would be no need for me…
After roughly going through the information on his phone, Xu Duojin paused before sending another message of inquiry:
“What is it, did you encounter some unexpected issue on your end?”
“Yes, there’s a task related to these things,” Colin simply informed him of the situation, the time, coordinates, and so on. Xu Duojin indicated he would need a quarter of an hour, and Colin was in no rush. After waiting a bit, right on time, he saw Xu’s next message.
It was indeed one of the seventeen…
And after a while, he sent a picture of what looked like an ordinary artificial Spatial Station.

chapters.title: Chapter 710 - 710 514 Followers of Red Moon Who Save the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 710: Chapter 514: Followers of “Red Moon” Who Save the World…_2 Chapter 710: Chapter 514: Followers of “Red Moon” Who Save the World…_2 According to Xu Duojin’s introduction, it was in a state of electronic malfunction.
However, all other satellite monitoring was fine, so no one bothered to deal with it at the moment…
If necessary, they could offer some help.
“Speaking of which, I remember there are roughly over a hundred containment subjects inside, all of which are the kind that’s hard to destroy. Also, there was an incident where followers of the ‘Red Moon’ attacked a site, leading to the loss and damage of some files, and this one just happened to be among them…” Xu Duojin’s message came again.
“That doesn’t seem like a coincidence anymore,” Colin replied.
“Yeah, we just don’t know much about it. At that time, Mr. Wu had just reached the Eighth Level, and I was merely at the Fifth Level. But if you need help, we can still provide some personnel to follow you…”
“I won’t need assistance with that…”
Colin expressed his refusal; the mission required ascending at a specific time and place, and arbitrarily altering that could lead to unexpected mishaps.
So he directly turned down the offer for help…
Of course, when the time came, the commotion caused by the ascent would still be handled by the officials.
After a brief exchange, Colin glanced at the time, inquired about the situation around Qin Chuan, and then covertly peeked at the groups established by the pseudo-humans. Finding nothing amiss, the afternoon had arrived.
After that, he idled away a bit more time…
Come evening, Colin arrived at the predetermined location and ascended into the sky as the mission required.
To ensure timely arrival at the target area, he did not do much to conceal himself.
While not as dramatic as a real rocket, the noise generated by his ascent was still significant, with thunderous explosions echoing through the surrounding area.
“Look, it’s a rocket!” exclaimed a child, pointing at the sky in amazement.
Many people, curious, followed the sound and lifted their heads, watching the “rocket” ascend.
As it soared swiftly into the sky with a long trail of flames…
But for some reason, at that moment, not a single person took out their phone to capture the sight, nor did the cameras and monitors that could have captured it inexplicably lost power.
Thus, the image of this “rocket” was destined to exist only in the memories of some people there at that time.
As time passed, the “rocket” had entered the high atmosphere, out of sight…
Three hours later.
Arriving at the designated location, Colin took a deep breath, looked around, and spotted the spatial containment space mentioned in the mission requirements, then his gaze slightly sharpened.
He saw faint red lights flickering above…
They were weak, but they were indeed there!
“The power of the ‘Red Moon’? Does that mean the containment subjects inside are influenced by the ‘Red Moon’? But then, how come the authorities haven’t noticed something so obvious? Or is it that it’s hard to spot unless from a specific angle? Or… do we have a traitor among us?”
Colin pursed his lips, thoughts flashing through his mind.
But he couldn’t afford to ponder much now, as he was on the same path as that thing, and would soon make contact. So he quickly took out the “letter” and headed towards it.
As he closed in, he could see through some transparent round windows the scene inside, which was different from the pictures Xu Duojin had shown him – inside, the various containment subjects were throwing a party…
Yes, that was the first thought that came to Colin’s mind when he saw the group of containment subjects hopping around inside.
Mask with long limbs, strange red refrigerator, twisted statue, human skin knife with a delicate long face, and so on were dancing wildly…
During the process, some containment subjects split like pregnancy, such as a mirror combining with a small knife to give birth to a glass knife…
Then they resumed hopping and jumping, and during this time, they merged again under the influence of some red entity’s power.
“Hiss, they’re really going all out,” Colin murmured with a frown, as each new generation of containment subjects seemed to enhance some kind of imprint.
And upon merging, it seemed that new abilities emerged due to the unique properties of both sides, and they continued to regenerate, recombine, and merge, with ethics not even coming into question…
If this continued, something serious would indeed emerge eventually.
Colin watched for a few seconds, almost sure that whatever was happening had something to do with a type of spatial portal.
Because a lot of things inside seemed to have spatial properties…
Or teleportation properties, etc.
As to how long it would take for that situation to arise, Colin was unsure, but he figured it would probably not happen immediately.
Yet there seemed to already be some risk inside…
He would have to be careful approaching it.
“Otherwise, there’s a good chance of being forcefully teleported away…”
As Colin pondered, he considered how to sneak in unnoticed and simply toss the “letter” inside to complete his task.
But it was at that very moment…
The faint red light on the surface of the spatial station flickered, and it seemed like all the anomalous entities within suddenly noticed him.
In an instant, all the containment subjects stopped their antics and, like people, turned around, pressing against the observation windows, staring intently at him!
Colin even thought he heard faint murmurs in his ears…
They seemed to indicate they didn’t welcome him, didn’t allow him to join the party, and so forth – vague, but that was the general feeling.

chapters.title: Chapter 711 - 711 514 Followers of Red Moon Who Save the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 711: Chapter 514: Followers of “Red Moon” Who Save the World…_3 Chapter 711: Chapter 514: Followers of “Red Moon” Who Save the World…_3 “Discovered? It seems there’s no other way then, I’ll have to get tough with you…”
Colin no longer hesitated, he harnessed the Flame as power and charged forward, then punched the glass mirror, shattering it.
However, it was in that moment that a kind of “Inspiration”-like voice appeared in his mind.
“Young man, I don’t know how you came to be here, but I tell you, this world is about to spiral out of control under the influence of the Rat, he has calculated everything, you stand no chance, only with us can you oppose him, you will regret it if you act against us…”
Sensing the mention of “the Rat” in the message, Colin’s heart sank.
But his actions didn’t stop, he directly threw the severed hand “Token” in: “A jackal of the same lair, taking care of you, then dealing with it, there’s no difference.”
After responding, it seemed another wave of Inspiration came through…
However, the radiant light from the burning severed hand obstructed it, all abnormalities were burnt to ashes.
Nevertheless, the “Token” severed hand didn’t stop after entering, but moved on its own, delving deeper into a hidden corner.
Through flame perception, Colin couldn’t help but gasp.
In that corner, everything was engulfed by sticky, scarlet flesh and tissue, at the very depth of the scarlet formation, there was a massive door made of flesh, and on the flesh, various blood vessels sketched out bizarre, magical patterns…
In the center of the flesh door, where countless blood vessels were connected, there was a huge eyeball.
It controlled a mass of fleshly tendrils, trying to stop the “Token” from approaching.
Regrettably, all efforts were in vain…
The severed hand directly penetrated the door, moving to its backside.
From that hole, a rich Red Light vaguely emerged, seemingly harboring something terrible…
But as the heatwave erupted, the Red Light faded, and the entire writhing door began to wither.
The massive eyeball shriveled up, losing its luster…
All the containment subjects sprawled inside also became still…
“Never thought there was such a big one hidden here.”
Colin was secretly alarmed, no wonder he had felt apprehensive as he approached; if the rich Red Light had actually nurtured it, a major event was bound to occur.
Fortunately, the mission had gone very smoothly this time…
Just as Colin was about to leave, a weakened voice came from inside.
“Young man approaching ‘Flame’, you will regret it, I have foreseen your terrible defeat at the hands of the Rat, and with the intervention of you fanatics, the world has once again embarked on an irreversible path to destruction…”
“Things that haven’t happened yet, and you think they’re wrong?”
Colin muttered, responding to the voice that was close to death.
Faced with these words, it seemed as though the other party had been broken through.
“Otherwise? If not for the path of ‘Bonfire’ already failing, how would the world have turned out like this? You think many disasters are blocked by people like you? In reality, if not for us ‘Red Moon’ Believers…”
“The entire world would have been destroyed long ago under the gaze of those higher-dimensional beings from beyond the cosmos.”
“It is the existence of ‘Mother’ that allows you to be here, to sleep in peace, eat, and enjoy the last pleasures before that day comes, amid countless crises.”
“It is our efforts that have saved this place, this Star Domain, this galaxy, this world…”
“However, what we got in return was betrayal.”
.
.
.
ps: Update first, revise later.
Having a bit of writer’s block..

chapters.title: Chapter 712 - 712 515 Tired lets destroy just destroy
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 712: Chapter 515: Tired, let’s destroy, just destroy everything. _1 Chapter 712: Chapter 515: Tired, let’s destroy, just destroy everything. _1 “Wait and see, you’ll eventually pay the price for your betrayal…”
The last weak voice came from a follower of the “Red Moon” that had transformed into a door of flesh and blood.
Colin didn’t interrupt, listening patiently to its words, eager to see if there was anything to gain.
He waited until it had finished speaking before he responded.
“The ‘Red Moon’ saving the world? Do you want to see the bullshit you’re spouting? Why the hell would this thing save the world, and what kind of despicable things have you done that you’re not mentioning? To put it rudely, how is that different from guarding food? And… Huh?”
Colin was almost amused by the nonsense this guy was spouting.
However, halfway through his speech, he abruptly realized that his opponent was already breathless by the time he started speaking.
Suddenly, he felt utterly disinterested.
He had finally encountered a talkative follower of the “Red Moon” and had been hoping to use a bit of reverse psychology to extract more information.
But damn it, the guy died just as he started talking, like throwing a punch into cotton.
It was like someone cursing at him, then crafting a lengthy reply only to find out he had been blocked by the other person – just disgusting.
“Damn it, aren’t your life forces strong? Resurrect and then talk big!”
Colin couldn’t help but say one more thing.
Unfortunately, having been directly attacked by the “Token,” it didn’t live long enough to say much before dying.
Colin took a deep breath of flame, then, seeing the mission completion content that popped up after the “Token” was deployed, he glanced at the situation inside and eventually decided it was better to leave well enough alone, choosing not to delve into it further.
He then used the mission pathway to return directly to his own neighborhood.
When he opened his eyes again and saw the ceiling above, Colin sat up, his mind whirring, pondering the words of his opponent just now.
“That Rat, has its threat level really become that severe…”
Colin rested his right hand on his chin, his expression serious.
Honestly, he didn’t give a second thought to any of the crap about saving the world that the other side had spouted.
He couldn’t deny that the “Red Moon” might indeed have played some role, deterring some extraterrestrial entities.
But… what the hell is the “Red Moon” thinking?
That’s the thing that wants to collect all biomass!
Not even a hair dropped on the road would be overlooked!
Even the fertilizer abandoned in the fields, with its possible organic microorganisms, wouldn’t escape…
These heretic believers, always on about saving the world or reviving humanity, but from start to finish, they haven’t done a single humane deed.
On the contrary, it seems that it is the “Flame Bearers” who are truly laying down their lives to block the enemy at the source.
Without the “Flame Bearers” and the Company’s efforts, the “Night” would have covered the universe by now; no need for the “Red Moon” to do anything…
So, now that he’s woken up, the pile of talk from the other side, in his view, only the part about “The Rat” held some value…
Heretic Believers are sometimes much keener on sensing heresy than the officials are.
Especially the Followers of the “Red Moon,” they are extremely sensitive to many entities they consider heretic, often making a dramatic entrance when some anomalies remain unsolved.
Which means, in the eyes of these beings, that Rat has become a threat to the world.
And they are currently unable to deal with it?
“This thing, you know, wasn’t this ‘Rat’ cooperating with the Followers of the ‘Red Moon’ before? And even shouted its belief in the ‘Red Moon,’ how did they fall out so quickly?”
Colin muttered to himself about how good that thing was at hiding.
According to “Lady Rabbit,” catching it before its next appearance would require him to level up to B Level, or have an entity of that level present, both of which are unreliable.
The most likely possibility was to become a “Flame Bearer”…
But that too was extremely difficult.
“Last time, ‘Lady Rabbit’s’ reply said that this ‘Rat’ had already completed its preparatory work and was now just waiting for Old Master Wu to bite the dust or for me to check the hidden conditions behind the ‘Book of Fate’…”
Colin felt an immense pressure.
He had no idea what moves it would pull when the time came or the kind of danger it would bring.
However, he didn’t take seriously the prophecy from the follower of the “Red Moon” about his failure at all. With the dual protection of the “Bonfire Company” and the “Primordial Fire,” it was unlikely anything could predict his future.
At most, it could sense his current location, but it couldn’t foretell anything…
“The fragmented ‘Book of Fate’ also only combines current information, mostly speculating future situations, and as soon as one gets to know a moment, it has already changed, far different from the kind of prophecy that’s nebulous and predestined, where no matter how much one struggles, they’ll eventually return to what’s foretold…”
“Hmm, if this guy wasn’t a Follower of the ‘Red Moon’ but the owner of the ‘Book of Fate,’ there would be some credibility.”
“After all, only something similarly suspected to be a Level ‘0’ Containment Subject and specializing in related concepts could give a prediction about me.”
As thoughts flickered through his mind, Colin took out his phone from his pocket and sent a message to Xu Duojin, inquiring about any progress with the Rat.
It wasn’t long after the message was sent, just under two minutes, that a reply came back.
“Since its last attack on Base No. 5, there have been no further moves, including the batch of ‘Extraordinary Ones’ it created, which also vanished overnight… Suddenly asking about it, has something come up?”

chapters.title: Chapter 713 - 713 515 Tired lets destroy just destroy
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 713: Chapter 515: Tired, let’s destroy, just destroy everything. _2 Chapter 713: Chapter 515: Tired, let’s destroy, just destroy everything. _2 “There’s no need for that. However, if possible, we should consider raising the danger level of this item.”
Colin added his reply.
“Alright, I will initiate that right away,” Xu Duojin continued with curiosity, “What’s the current situation with those space containment sites? Do we need to bring all the orbiting containment sites back to the ground?”
“No need, for now everything should be fine.”
Having thought it over, since “Lady Rabbit” only asked to keep one hand free and didn’t arrange for any follow-ups,
there was no need to do anything extra…
Sometimes, fixing one BUG might lead to more bugs surfacing.
This isn’t anything new in the realm of real-life mysteries.
After a brief exchange, Colin ended the conversation, then took out the parchment and saw that a new task had emerged…
Unsurprisingly, the task was still to place a “Token” somewhere.
But after looking at it for a while, he found himself surprised by the requirements listed.
“The requirement is to go to the coordinates… to light Bonfires at some key areas, and before that, to save some people listed above, then throw the ‘Token’ in to establish a Blockade. The specified location of these coordinates…”
Colin had a nagging sense of familiarity, and then he checked his phone to confirm.
Oh, was it actually that Isle of Anomaly across the Ocean?
“Figures, with such an abundance of anomalies there, it’s no wonder ‘Lady Rabbit’ would take notice, especially now with all this chaos. I’ve been treating it as a joke, but if left unmanaged, it might indeed merge into a huge problem,” Colin mused.
He looked at this new round of task events. Currently, it was the sixth round of the Fifteenth Ring, and also the last task of the week.
So, it probably wouldn’t be easy; he needed to prepare cautiously.
“However, compared to previously having to sit until the ninth stop on the train, this is much better. This task is just about skirting the perimeter, setting up Bonfire points, enclosing some of the worst-hit areas, finding an opportunity to pull some people out, then projecting the ‘Token’ in, and finally completing the Blockade,” he thought.
As he pondered, he continued to contact Xu Duojin to gather the necessary intelligence.
Learning that Colin intended to head there to execute the task, Xu Duojin was first surprised, then couldn’t help but send a voice message, “That place? It’s extremely dangerous, can you refuse?”
“The task is special, not suitable for refusal,” Colin replied simply.
Hearing this response, Xu Duojin didn’t say much else, just gradually provided the specific details about the place.
Then, Colin received dozens of relevant documents, one by one he opened them and was then shocked to discover that the situation was worse than he had expected…
“In just a few months, under the intervention of a host of powerful figures, the population has still declined by over one-fifth?”
Colin was astonished; one-fifth must be tens of millions of people, right? And there was no sign of it in the world, even as the data showed that many of the places where people checked in on the internet had become fallen zones.
But was it unknown to everyone?
Through the relevant documents, he found out why. This crisis not only utilized a large amount of resources from the Global Supernatural Alliance for comprehensive joint control, but also disseminated information about the island outward through some containment subjects and “intelligent” simulations.
All to minimize the impact of some information from there on the overall world situation…
“…Old Master Wu has repeatedly proposed to relocate the population to South America, Africa, Europa, and other regions, to enforce an island-wide Blockade and to carry out a sinking island blockade plan. Many countries agree with the first half, but a small but firm minority opposes the latter half, especially someone named Mr. Abrekect who strongly responded that Great Britain has been the homeland for generations, a symbol of human triumphalism, a historical treasure, and sinking it would be equivalent to surrendering to the anomalies…”
“Moreover, Britain has borne countless hardships for the world, so all countries have the duty to rescue them, expressing a willingness to return all cultural relics… Really, such nerve to speak thus, isn’t this just courting death? Ignoring past plunderings, the refusal to return later, and still blaming others?”
“Um, seeing so many countries scolding, I can relax now.”
Colin gnawed on his index finger, looking at a record of recent event discussions.
He was quite supportive of Old Master Wu’s plan addressed in those discussions; after all, that approach seemed much easier to execute…
As for homeland or not, as long as it didn’t contravene the “Bonfire Protocol,” everything was permissible for Colin.
Next, he opened up a comprehensive record of the island’s exceptional events…
Just from the introduction, even Colin, who was well-acquainted with a wide array of anomalies, couldn’t help but widen his eyes and his pupils shook with intense vibrations.
[The current count of anomalies is approximately 1,793,960 (as of January 12th data).]
“How many?”
Colin clutched his phone, his voice trembling, completely stunned. His expression was as vacant as Shana’s had been, murmuring as he counted the numbers displayed:
“One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, seven digits?!”
One million seven hundred seventy-nine thousand three hundred ninety-six devices in a semi-out-of-control or out-of-control state?
Colin took a deep breath. Many times before, when he had joked that this damn place had more anomalies than people, he was just kidding around.
But now, if it continued to spiral out of control, he feared that the joke would become reality…
After all, the number of anomalies was skyrocketing, while the human population was rapidly decreasing…
“With this number of anomalies, is there still any need to preserve this damned island?!”
Previously, he thought Old Master Wu’s suggestion to sink the island was a bit too extreme, but now, it seemed too mild—
Why hadn’t it been executed yet?
Colin swallowed hard and couldn’t help but ask if Xu Duojin’s source of information was reliable, but the reply he received was.
“Barely reliable, but Old Wu forbids us from going to the island, so all the information comes from the investigations of international teams. Yeah, I heard they estimated on the optimistic side, the real situation could be even more complex, because our people said that the anomalies have started to devour and merge with each other over there…”
“Optimistic estimates? Who’s being optimistic at a time like this?”
Colin hissed, feeling somewhat irrational, but could only say that these people were indeed quite optimistic in this regard.
In any case, even looking at the report estimated with optimism, he still couldn’t feel upbeat…
He continued to glance through the introductions of some anomalies but didn’t look too much and instead called out the Little Maid to rapidly process the information—
Otherwise, nearly two million anomalies, he wouldn’t be able to finish even if it were the end of the world!
A few seconds later, the Little Maid’s gaze flickered, and in front of Colin, she projected a set of three-dimensional data charts: “Information fully received, organizing in progress, do you want to convert to Bonfire Company standards?”
“Yes,” Colin nodded.
The official had their own system for defining anomalies, and this system varied between countries. It was easier to use the standards of Bonfire Company, which he was most familiar with.
The standards of Bonfire Company were unified across all the territories it influenced…
Even where there were differences, they were within his realm of understanding.
“Based on the current documents, we can estimate that there are approximately one million two hundred thousand containment subjects below Fifth Level, over three hundred thousand Fifth Level containment subjects, about two hundred ninety thousand Fourth Level containment subjects, about one thousand Third Level containment subjects, about forty Level 2 containment subjects, and one to three suspected Lower-Level First Level containment subjects, but they cannot be confirmed as of now…”
Listening to the Little Maid’s description, Colin felt somewhat numb, but he actually breathed a sigh of relief towards the end.
No mass quantity of First Level containment subjects… that’s somewhat relieving.
But…
“Why is everything ‘approximately’?”
“Based on the description of the related containment subjects for conversion. It’s impossible to confirm the accuracy of these descriptions, and while official estimates for some anomalies could be too high, others could be too low, or descriptions could be severely lacking. Unless we conduct an on-site investigation, we cannot acquire further information…”
“Is that so, well, under these circumstances, an on-site survey is no longer necessary.”
Looking at this information on anomalies, Colin felt as if he had opened a drawer to find it teeming with roaches.
Which ones are bigger and which ones are smaller didn’t seem to matter much anymore.
At this moment, all he could think was that it was no wonder this place was an old empire—it had some depth. This island’s mere existence now was nothing short of a miracle!
“Leaving First Level containment subjects aside, although I can deal with Third and Second Level containment subjects quite easily once I ramp up my output, with this number, getting hit all at once would still be troublesome…”
Listening to his words, the Little Maid spoke up: “Most of the anomalies are scattered throughout the island. As long as we avoid them wisely, we should still be able to get through relatively smoothly.”
“Let’s hope so.”
With a tone that carried a hint of “I’m tired, let it be destroyed,” Colin spoke.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 714 - 714 516 Haze Angel_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 714: Chapter 516 “Haze Angel”_1 Chapter 714: Chapter 516 “Haze Angel”_1 Colin didn’t pay much attention to what the Little Maid supposedly avoided.
After all…
Once he used the power of the Firebearer, it would be like a torch in the night, instantly attracting all abnormal attention—
Especially those suspected to be First Level Containment Subjects.
Even if it were just the Level 2 Containment Subjects, if they swarmed over upon seeing it.
He wouldn’t be able to handle it very well.
“If needed, we can bring out some powerful items and some strong figures to follow you and assist you with your mission…” Xu Duojin’s message came again.
“No need.”
Colin refused, feeling that while it was manageable to fight lower-level officials with higher-level officials in battle, confronting high-intensity warfare was truly a matter of life and death, and he felt he couldn’t live with himself using that approach.
Moreover, the fact that so many abnormalities hadn’t left the island yet indicated that the containment levels were still very high.
The officials must have used some quite powerful items for control…
“Alright, then I’ll bring a team to join you, to smooth over relationships, which can avoid many misunderstandings.”
Xu Duojin didn’t insist, but he still expressed his own thoughts.
Colin didn’t refuse this time.
The time for the action was quickly set for nine o’clock that evening, to get going as early as possible and resolve the issues as soon as possible.
Time passed quickly, and after Colin had quickly taken care of his belongings, under Xu Duojin’s arrangement, he boarded an ultra-high-speed combat aircraft.
However, unlike usual circumstances, they had standby tickets.
The operational authority was taken over by the Little Maid.
Flames from Colin enveloped the entire aircraft, further enhancing its performance and reducing resistance to some extent.
“Temporary enhancement is complete, we will arrive at the periphery of the target area in two hours at the fastest, three hours at the latest…” the Little Maid’s voice came to Colin’s ears.
He nodded his head and then looked over at Xu Duojin standing aside.
“Where’s your team?” Colin asked.
“They’re already stationed over there. We’ll meet up directly when the time comes. As per your request, it’s just a matter of communication, and then I’ll accompany you onto the island,” said Xu Duojin. “There are also some Alliance people moving on the island. I’ll help you communicate with them to avoid misunderstandings and accidents.”
“Okay,” Colin nodded his head.
With just one person accompanying, he was confident he could keep them safe.
Especially since this person was already capable of looking after himself…
During the conversation, the aircraft they were on docked at a moored aircraft carrier three hours later.
No sooner had they landed than a group of people gathered around. Xu Duojin jumped down first and began speaking with the greeters.
Colin followed, not immediately stepping down but standing on the back of the aircraft, feeling an inexplicable heaviness in his heart. Looking in the direction of that feeling, his pupils narrowed slightly. He could vaguely see a world teeming with all sorts of demons and monsters…
It could aptly be described as “demonic energy piercing the sky”!
“The fact that there are still people alive up there can only be attributed to luck,” Colin muttered to himself as he descended from the aircraft.
At this moment, many domestic officials who had come to maintain the situation approached with curiosity, and Colin even spotted the Eighth Level Divine Strike, who had tried to humble him before.
The man’s condition was even worse now; it was clear that he had exerted himself a lot in recent times, resulting in a numb expression…
However, despite this, he still managed to greet Colin briefly.
Colin nodded and then withdrew his gaze, looking towards Xu Duojin, who was currently negotiating with some people.
As Colin’s gaze shifted there, Xu Duojin just finished his conversation.
“What’s the situation here now?” Colin wasn’t shy and directly approached to inquire.
“It seems that some more abnormalities have popped up, but apart from a few areas that are relatively severe, the situation in other places is still manageable, almost matching the file we saw earlier…”
“Then that’s not too bad,” Colin sighed in relief, but he was heading to the most dangerous area.
He would need to ignite many temporary Bonfires to surround them…
As for firewood, the island was now littered with firewood; there was no need to arrange for more.
“Snap, snap.”
The sound of heavy claps echoed.
They carried a force strong enough to cause deafness in ordinary people upon hearing them.
It was an ill omen…
In the blink of an eye, Colin turned his gaze and saw people with white skin, black skin, and all kinds of complexions approaching. At the forefront was an unusually strong woman over two meters tall.
The thunderous clapping sound was coming from her hands.
Eighth Level standard, a bit temperamental… Colin’s eyes flickered with Bonfire light as he gauged her and then spoke:
“Is there a problem?”
He knew foreign languages but didn’t use them, after all, the company’s translation was good enough.
Upon seeing Colin’s gaze, she revealed a grin: “You’re the one going up? Not bad, you seem completely unaffected.”
She paused, then added, “I heard you cowards are finally going to take action, claiming there’s a chance to resolve the issues inside. I was somewhat looking forward to it, but it turns out such an ordinary person has come. I won’t mention what you intend to do up there… but such matters require strength.”
“Kid, you don’t look very powerful. Are you really qualified to have us assist you?” She spread her arms, which were crossed over her chest, shrugged, and shook her head, adopting a condescending attitude as she spoke with a mix of mockery and provocation.
As she spoke, a formidable presence emanated from her…

chapters.title: Chapter 715 - 715 516 Haze Angel_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 715: Chapter 516 “Haze Angel”_2 Chapter 715: Chapter 516 “Haze Angel”_2 Streams of electricity were flickering continuously on her body.
Regarding the refusal to help on the island led by Huafang, they had always had some opinions to a certain extent.
Especially since there were several times when, if only they had gone up to cover the retreat, they could have saved a lot of people, but they were utterly unwilling.
This had nearly cost her and many of her comrades their lives up there.
On one side, Xu Duojin frowned, tens of thousands of black threads wriggling behind him and numerous black long hands stretching out, as if wanting to speak, but suddenly sensing something, he did not continue speaking.
By this time, an Eighth Level “Divine Strike” on the side also edged closer.
Despite some past grievances, at times like this, they must direct the spearhead outwards.
And upon hearing the other party’s words, Colin was stunned, then his expression turned peculiar.
‘Has it been so long that a character who can make me eat my words is finally about to emerge?’
Colin thought about it and actually felt somewhat excited.
However…
He didn’t particularly like this thing, scratching the back of his head and saying, “Actually, I know that all of you high-rankers have some issues with your personalities to some extent, and I’ve always respected you, but…”
“What do you want to say…” The woman and some people around her were puzzled.
But the next second…
Blazing firelight exploded in front of their eyes, sinking everyone’s hearts, but before they could act,
a giant hand made of flame descended from the sky.
Five thick fingers staked into the ground, forming a cage-like enclosure, covering everyone within the palm.
Thump… Thump… Thump…
Under the terrifying and heavy pressure, even Eighth Level Personnel couldn’t stand upright, all kneeling on the ground, their extraordinary powers greatly suppressed.
The astounding power of the “Bonfire” dominated the scene, its transcendental authority covering the sky.
The massive aircraft carrier sank several meters below the ocean’s surface due to the sudden downward force, creating large waves.
Many prostrated on the ground, struggling to lift their heads to look at the young figure, who, unbeknownst to them, began to be enveloped in flames.
“Respect is mutual, madam.” Colin said, his hands in his pockets, looking down from above at the woman kneeling not far from his pair of large slippers, “Do you have any different thoughts about what I’ve said?”
Behind Colin, Xu Duojin and the others couldn’t help but take a deep breath upon seeing the giant hand that almost covered half of the aircraft carrier.
This, just this single action alone, his strength was comparable to, if not stronger than, many Ninth Level Personnel!
‘Wait, he’s tamed that thing?!’ Xu Duojin suddenly realized that this was the “one-time” item they had provided to Colin for support last time.
Now it seemed, he had directly tamed it?
This…
The other’s strength must have surpassed most of the Ninth Level Personnel already.
Only a minority similar to “Old Master Wu,” who could utilize certain things to a certain extent and possessed strong uniqueness as Ninth Level Personnel, could contend with it.
“I… don’t…” The Eighth Level woman on the ground shook her head with difficulty. After experiencing the minor shock of the Flame Bearer’s power, her eyes cleared up a lot compared to before.
This power was hard to describe, but there seemed to be some sort of natural suppression against her—
Not just a restraint, but an all-encompassing… advanced feeling.
It was like an automatic rifle to a Mosin–Nagant.
“That’s good, then.”
Colin waved his hand casually, and the flames covering the area instantly dissipated, but the brief conflict lasting less than two minutes had significantly clarified everyone’s view of him.
Some higher-rankers spectating from a distance had not faced the power of the “Bonfire.”
But they had certainly felt a bit of its might.
Seeing this, Colin nodded in satisfaction; it seemed that everyone could still speak reason after all.
Then, Colin immediately inquired about the real-time situation on the island…
“There are about twelve disaster zones you are looking to contain, to circle them, not… that won’t be easy.” She originally wanted to say impossible, but considering the other party’s power, she changed her wording to avoid being disrespectful.
Then she further detailed the situation.
Such as the status of survivors, and what others currently working on the island were doing.
“Currently on the island, there are sixty-one Level Seven Personnel, nine Eighth Level Personnel, and there is one Ninth Level Personnel active above, monitoring some high-order anomalies containment subjects that are still in a state of partial loss of control, as well as stabilizing the situation and transferring personnel off the island…”
“The number of Extraordinary Ones outside the island is about the same, but there are no Ninth Level Personnel in person, only some remote monitoring…”
Spectating? Does this count as one side having trouble and all sides watching in amusement?
Colin suddenly thought about it and, after hearing the other party’s words, felt much relieved.
Because the loss of control was not complete but a state of partial loss of control with sections of the area compromised, which was also the reason why they believed the island could still be salvaged and were unwilling to let it sink…
“For this, we have made a lot of efforts and sacrifices…”
“Heh, efforts? Sacrifices? If it weren’t for the cover-ups and delays here, waiting until the anomalies crossed the Ocean to us and other countries, and the early refusal of international support, would there have been so much trouble?” A brown-haired, blue-eyed individual suddenly appeared and interrupted with ridicule.
In his hand, he wore black gloves adorned with skull decorations.
Not just on his hands, but all over his body, there were various skull emblems.
“Hand of Reprimand”.
Colin recognized these items as symbolic decorations of a famous organization from across the Ocean.
It seems to signify the purity of mankind and the resolve to face death…
“Aren’t these two supposed to be as close as people of the same nationality?”
Colin turned and quietly asked Xu Duojin beside him, and after hearing his just as quiet response said, “Indeed, but they lost some people in the previous operations, so there are hard feelings.”
“Oh, understood…”
Colin nodded, but he wasn’t too interested in these matters or the ensuing pleasantries.
Nobody said much in response to his attitude; on the contrary, they were very friendly, expressing the hope to invite him for some event if the opportunity arises—
After displaying his power, everyone suddenly became amiable and friendly.
‘The internal hierarchy of the officials sure is strict, the stronger you are, the higher your status…’
Colin sensed this atmosphere but didn’t think much of it, simply refusing some other people’s requests for meetings and asked Xu Duojin to obtain the most current live situation map.
After further understanding the current situation, he communicated with the Ninth Level Personnel on the island, and then began taking action.
This time he didn’t use any airplanes or the like…
Colin, carrying Xu Duojin, rode on a large skateboard transformed by the Little Maid, flying directly to the island as though riding a sword.
Passing over various warships on the sea surface, after a while, Colin saw the haunted area of the island firsthand.
A port nearby had all its functions shut down and was enveloped in a dense fog of haze.
Within the haze, numerous eerie figures wandered and fought…
Roars, screams, explosions, and so on…
The noises were incessant.
“Quite a welcoming, a small area that’s partially lost control right from the start.”
Colin pursed his lips and, taking a moment to sense around, noticed that all abnormalities within all the ports were unable to leave and seemed to be imprisoned by the thick, murky haze…
Within the haze, countless fierce and emaciated human faces surged out like bubbles and then shattered.
These spectral entities seemed to be trying to break free from the haze but to no avail.
“The haze must be that strong conceptual tool from the officials, the ‘Haze Angel’… A pan-conceptual thing, the anomalies are sealed inside, hmm, there are two Level 2 Containment Subjects fighting inside, along with some Heretic Races, and a large number of weird containment objects releasing power, what is this, breeding grounds?”
After sensing briefly, Colin understood the situation.
Then, he shifted his gaze towards a frontline base not far from the port.
Some people inside looked at him curiously, but because he communicated his intent beforehand, they did not come up to challenge him…
Colin watched for two seconds before moving his gaze away, flames surging in his eyes as he slightly tilted his head, gazing towards the distant modern city completely obscured by mist.
He planned to start with the biggest trouble first—
The Mist City that had completely fallen and had to be sealed up with the “Haze Angel”.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 716 - 716 517 Containment Subjects of the World
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 716: Chapter 517 “Containment Subjects of the World, Unite!”_1 Chapter 716: Chapter 517 “Containment Subjects of the World, Unite!”_1 “Cough, cough, cough…”
Under the heavy smog, even the Extraordinary Ones, upon continuously inhaling the air filled with smoke and polluted particles, couldn’t help but cough violently, feeling an unbearable spicy sensation in their nose and throat.
