Afterward, Colin turned to look at Shana, noticing her calm demeanor that was mixed with a bit of dazedness, which in turn was very calm, ending with a somewhat inexplicable sense of aggrievement that couldn’t be put into words, he then spoke:
“I shouldn’t comment on the past, but from now on… from now on, let me handle matters concerning points. I will cover the point expenses for managing the realm and aiding refugees. Moreover, I’ll give you enough points as compensation.”
In the past, Colin would have thought to have Shana contribute some points, with everyone chipping in to manage the territory…
But after finding out she had been exploited to such an extent, Colin no longer had such thoughts.
If it weren’t for him, Shana wouldn’t be able to scrape together much money even if she were stripped clean.
Upon hearing this, Shana opened her mouth to instinctively say that she already had enough points now and that this was her responsibility; she needed no compensation.
Currently, she still had tens of thousands of points on her, which…
If she didn’t purchase that rip-off war chariot, as well as things like the “skins” in “Light’s Dreamland,” then she’d have more than enough points.
At least, according to her spending habits, she wouldn’t use much in a year.
And to be honest, personally she didn’t have a great desire for points.
However, Colin preempted her, saying, “Let’s just settle it this way, I will give you what you deserve. Otherwise, what difference would there be between me and ‘it’?”
As he spoke, Colin pointed to the detestable parchment that was practically bubbling with malice.
“Okay…”
Shana didn’t refuse again, but still added:
“But, but, the points you give me in the future, may I request to store them with you directly? If given to me, I feel, it still would continue taking that…’transaction fee’.”
“‘Transaction fees’ still haven’t been canceled, damn it, knows it’s wrong but still dares to do it next time?”
Colin couldn’t help but feel a mix of anger and amusement, then nodded his head:
“No problem, I’ll look after your points. Whenever you need to buy something or need them for anything, just tell me.”
Shana normally spent her points to buy a pile of black bread.
It was unappetizing but could sustain a person for a day’s consumption. In a way, it was a food technology miracle…
However, this kind of miracle technology was highly replaceable.
Colin could pull a vat of the official specially provided ultra-concentrated nutritional compound, which wouldn’t be much worse.
Moreover, it wouldn’t cost a penny, or rather, the officials currently still owed him a large sum, which was enough to feed the people here for the second half of their lives.
“Thank you…”
Shana said sincerely, blinking her eyes, not knowing how to express her gratitude towards Colin sufficiently. If it weren’t for him, things here might have been very difficult…
No, difficulty would be an understatement. The real issue was that this difficulty could lead to countless deaths.
What she could repay him with was to protect and manage this land she and Colin had opened up together.
Of course, there was also teaching Colin combat skills more heartedly, without holding back…
“By the way, I’ve now recovered about three clone avatars. If there’s anything needed in the territory, I can help at any time,” Shana said.
“Loosening soil, moving bricks, such tasks could currently use some help. As the population keeps growing, we are starting to fall behind in these areas. Other than that, it’s about bestowing blessings so people can learn some basic knowledge faster. Knowledge enlightenment is really important…” Colin immediately thought of numerous tasks Shana could help with.
Shana was not opposed to this…
After a bit more discussion, the topic drew to a close, and Shana sent out her “Light Avatar” to work.
Her main body stayed in the small chapel, preparing to guide Colin on matters of combat soon.
Before that, Colin took out the “Kindness of the Firebearer” and the document, ready to fuse some skills together.
“I hope to fuse something valuable.”
Colin prayed, then started to use the fusion function.
The bonfire madly swirled before his eyes, and amidst the cool special effects, it seemed as if some fearsome divine weapon was about to be born.
“Clang! Clang! Clang!”
Amidst the sounds of the hammer striking down,
there was a “crack.”
Fusion complete.
Colin eagerly took it out, only to find that the name of the equipment seemed to have changed…
From “Kindness of the Firebearer” to “Kindness of the Firebearer max,” and the description column had an addition that read “specially strengthened by the Haze Angel…”
“That’s quite a straightforward naming.”
Colin pursed his lips and continued to check the specific changes.
In the eyes that were like transparent fiery red crystals, a tiny figure made of haze moved about, and some kind of “inspiration” made Colin realize that this object could now directly connect to the “Haze Angels” that had been contained.
Furthermore, he could receive some sort of remote assistance from them…
“With this use, I can create an enormous haze domain filled with substances like sulfuric acid, covering a diameter of tens of kilometers. Those within it would be deprived of their sense of direction to a certain degree, and by controlling the concentration in the area, I can enhance this effect. Those anomalies in Britain, were they controlled like this? Not bad.”
“Second, whether you breathe or not, the respiratory tract will suffer corresponding corrosion damage; one must either endure it or use extraordinary abilities to offset it. It’s an assimilation of the era, to be blunt, it’s about making the world understand suffering together?”
“Besides, I can summon tens of thousands of ‘Mist City’ workers, orphans, and so on for my use. As long as I don’t die, neither will they. Moreover, every person who dies due to the ‘haze’ corrosion has a chance to become one of them, and while within it, I can take on the appearance of any of them…”
These were the three abilities specifically listed out for explanation.
It appears to be somewhat weakened, but not by much.
However, based on past experiences, there should still be some more detailed ways to use it, waiting for him and Shana to develop later.
At worst, a fire can be lit to maximize its utility…
“There are mainly three negative effects. The first is, the larger the range, the greater the consumption of energy, and if used continuously for three days, it would need a day to cool down.”
“The second is, within the domain’s coverage, there cannot be complete damage immunity for teammates like with a bonfire; there will always be some damage…”
“The third is, with the summons and such within it, one cannot exploit them too harshly, or it might lead to a major strike, resistance, and the like, or even possibly a fancy post on a lamppost? It would be best to give them reasonable assignments, huh? They’re all dead, why care about exploitation anyway…”
Colin raised an eyebrow, feeling the negative effects were acceptable, though he did not quite grasp the strike issue.
After thinking for a bit, he pinched the “max” bead between his fingers and brought it up to his left eye, inserting it into the socket.
As his thoughts turned, a very faint haze began to seep into the surroundings…
And from within the haze, countless people emerged: gaunt workers, maimed child laborers, sickly old folks, and tired women and children…
As these figures looked towards the flames around them, their faces revealed evident longing, basking in the enjoyment.
This gave Colin some ideas, realizing how he should command them.
Of course, as a conscientious person, Colin naturally wouldn’t say things like “If you want a bonfire, you must work,” “Work an hour, enjoy a minute by the fire,” or “No work today, become firewood tomorrow.”
After some thought, kind-hearted Grandpa Colin spoke in plain language:
“Cough cough, friends… I ask you all to join in building a new homeland, construct homes to live in, grow food to eat, strive for yourselves… Of course, all this is voluntary.”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 729 - 729 524
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 729: 524 Chapter 729: 524 Colin could have directly ordered the large group of ghosts, but he chose to drive them in a more reasonable way…
Thinking of this, Colin couldn’t help but be moved by his own conscience.
Unfortunately, as for what he called building their own houses, growing their own food, and striving for themselves, they seemed incapable of fully understanding, so there was no feedback whatsoever.
“Ahem…” Colin felt somewhat embarrassed, exchanging awkward glances with the crowd.
A moment later, under the Inspiration of the prop itself, he quickly understood the reason…
These people had already been exploited to death once; work had, in some sense, become instinctive.
And adding other things on top of that didn’t seem particularly meaningful.
‘Based on my understanding of the “Haze Angel,” it feels like even sparing it a few lashes counts as a blessing.’
Colin mumbled to himself, looking at the group of Mist City ghosts in front of him, impervious to reason, and after pondering for a moment, he could not think of any helpful words to say.
People who had died had no desire for lodgings or food.
It felt like being without desires but steadfast…
After thinking for a while, Colin suddenly realized something, took out a “Colorless Crystal” and held it in front of him; at this moment, a longing finally appeared in the people’s eyes.
Finally, I found a way… Colin tossed a “Colorless Crystal” out, which landed on a severely malnourished child about ten years old. The child’s missing limbs began to mend, quickly becoming a complete person!
Seeing this, Colin’s eyes brightened, and he was about to speak when he suddenly realized…
After the child’s limbs were fully restored, it began to dissolve and disappeared in an instant.
“Hmm? What’s happening?!”
Colin was stunned, then quickly, through the Inspiration from the prop itself, he learned the reason—
Due to its newfound wholeness and warmth it had never experienced before, it had ascended!
‘Thank you, warm-hearted big brother…’ A simple and childish voice of gratitude echoed in his ears.
This ghost, trapped and dead in a miserable historical past, had found release from suffering.
‘Hiss, you’ve ascended, but what about that huge chunk of ground I’ve got?’
Colin couldn’t help thinking this, but he also noticed that at this moment, in the gazes of all the ghosts looking at him, there was a longing…
A longing to be freed from historical suffering, just like that child.
In this way, redemption had its pros and cons; at least, it had stirred up some enthusiasm.
It’s just that once they became whole, they would ascend and vanish…
‘No, even though one person disappears, the “Haze Angel’s” completion seems to have slightly increased. But the number summoned has indeed decreased by one…’
‘Never mind, it doesn’t seem particularly important. Those who died under the erosion of the “Haze Angel” might get a chance to become a part of it.’
‘Which means the labor force lost can eventually be replenished.’
With his thoughts swirling, Colin looked thoughtfully at the people in front of him and said:
“From now on, as long as you complete each day’s tasks, the top five performers will each receive a Crystal as a reward…
“In addition, the top three hundred performers of the day will have the privilege of enjoying the direct radiance of the Bonfire up close…
“Now go and start striving for yourselves!”
The amount of Crystal needed varied from individual to individual; Colin estimated that for a child like that one crystal should suffice, but adults might need three to five. By proceeding slowly, though it meant that eventually everyone would be released…
But when all these tens of thousands of people are liberated at that moment, the remaining labor value should also be almost depleted.
…
Not long after, on the territory, after an initial short period of minor panic, the residents quickly accepted the existence of these ghosts.
For those who believed in the Bonfire, as long as you believed in the Bonfire, then we were brothers and sisters from different fathers and mothers.
This also let Colin breathe a sigh of relief, feeling that the Church really had something going for it.
But thinking about it, seeing that the Bonfire’s citizens even considered the “Smiling Mountain of Corpses” a Holy Beast, it seemed not so strange that they would accept some similarly tragic little ghosts.
Of course, compared to the citizens of the Bonfire Church, the employees’ reaction was a bit strange…
“Fuck, Brother Shunzi is really inhuman, dragging this little kid here to exploit for labor, and he’s got such a huge burn scar on his face! I feel my conscience squirming…” Someone watching the ten-year-old kid helping to loosen the soil couldn’t help but mutter under their breath.
“I came to work voluntarily…”
The little ghost nearby said in a somewhat husky, childish voice, while helping with some odd jobs on the farmland.
Though the work was a bit heavy, the thought of having a chance at liberation filled his tiny body with energy.
“Ah, this… this isn’t about volunteering or not…” A female employee, seeing the child’s sensible demeanor, felt a pang of pity.
“It’s just a prop, no big deal.”
There were also employees who knew about this “prop” from Colin, who explained the situation.
“They had died in misery under the persecution of unscrupulous capitalists, and after many years, under Brother Shunzi’s well-intentioned efforts, they have a chance to struggle for themselves after death, to realize their self-worth, and to be completely liberated. It’s moving…”
An employee who wished to remain anonymous, “Miss Nell’s Dog,” reached out to wipe away nonexistent tears from the corner of his eyes.
However, his words drew a round of scorn.
“So kind-hearted, why keep exploiting instead of just giving them a holiday to wait for liberation?” Someone spoke up.
Upon hearing this, “Miss Nell’s Dog” shook his head, “Malicious liberation is not advisable. First, we don’t have that many ‘Colorless Crystals’, and second, only liberation fought for by oneself is true liberation, which can realize the value of the self…”
“Is that what these principles are fucking for?”
“Big brother, big sister, please don’t fight. I really came to work voluntarily…” The child’s immature voice piped up, as he helped cut the ripe wheat.
Despite being just a child, his body was truly anomalous, and his strength was much greater than that of an ordinary person.
“Good boy, come here to sister, don’t stay over there, it’s dangerous with the dog.” The female employee waved her hand, calling the child over to her side.
“Using me to play the sympathy card and covertly exploiting labor, huh?”
Upon hearing “Miss Nell’s Dog’s” irksome words, the female employee nearly slapped him across the face.
“Don’t fucking think everyone’s like you!”
…
As the busy work days went by, with the addition of Shana, “Haze Angel”, and the new employees, the construction speed of the entire territory had increased substantially.
The once barren areas, through the spontaneous efforts of the people, had small buildings erected and acres of fertile land ploughed.
They had basically achieved a certain level of self-sufficiency.
The breath of life suddenly intensified.
On the last day of this Descent Project, Colin took time to visit the labyrinth of the “King of Savage Sound” and perfunctorily perform his duties by implying “the organization is placing more and more importance on you” before hurrying away.
With the activation of the “Descent Protocol”, this “Descent Event” was completed.

chapters.title: Chapter 730 - 730 525 Shanas Product._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 730: Chapter 525 Shana’s Product._1 Chapter 730: Chapter 525 Shana’s Product._1 “Another disappointing three thousand plus points,”
Colin shook his head and sighed as he reviewed the content of the task settlement.
Although it was more than what a regular employee would get, it wasn’t even close to enough for upgrading and repairing the Golden Card.
However, he hadn’t actually done much on this descent project, so it wasn’t likely to include anything like draw tickets.
Therefore, he didn’t dwell too much on the issue.
Colin glanced at the time, it was probably a few seconds past three o’clock on Monday afternoon…
“Next up is the official trade with the company the day after tomorrow,”
He got up from the bed and looked at the sunlight streaming through the window nearby. He stroked his chin with his hand, pondering for a moment.
It seemed the officials had quite a lot to trade with the company this time…
He would have to see if he could get a slice of the pie, or to be more precise, what kind of slice.
“I need to gather some backup stored energy anyway. Some of the higher-level anomalies don’t have unique traits and don’t seem particularly suitable for making into items. Those could be used as material for burning…”
From what Colin knew, anomalies with traits could drop useful equipment, just like elite monsters.
But the ordinary anomalies gave nothing when slain…
Except they were suitable as carbon material.
Of course, this usually only happened with First Level Containment Subjects and below. Once it reached First Level, it became an embodiment of some kind of power, and regardless of strength, it was unlikely to lack traits.
After some thought, Colin took out his phone and sent a message to Xu Duojin, but got no response.
“Huh? Speaking of that mission on Never-Setting Sun Island, seems like I didn’t bring him back with me last time?”
Colin just remembered something and wondered how Xu Duojin was doing now.
Since that day, aside from a brief follow-up call, there hadn’t been much news.
Just as Colin was considering whether to ask Old Master Wu for updates, Xu Duojin responded.
He didn’t mention the events of that day but instead addressed Colin’s request.
“The kind you’re describing is usually something we choose to completely eradicate. It’s one of the rare things we can solve completely. If you need them, we’ll be sure to keep them for you in the future…”
Xu Duojin sent a message back indicating it wouldn’t be a problem.
After having seen how Colin could quickly kill a Second-order Containment Subject, he wasn’t worried about anything going wrong if Colin handled these things.
‘Why do I feel like the officials are kind of happy about me taking a “kickback”?’ Colin wondered but soon pieced together the reason with a clearer understanding of the workings behind this world—
Compared to him, the officials were certainly more eager to annihilate high-level, unruly Containment Subjects.
But it was a difficult task for them to handle on their own.
While Level 2 Containment Subjects could be destroyed, how to do so wasn’t simple…
It wasn’t a matter of just finding a pit and detonating a nuclear bomb to solve the issue.
Doing that might let them escape instead…
Every execution had to be dealt with by high-ranking officials one by one, sacrificing their own status and life to destroy the other party.
Since Colin needed them, they were all too happy to oblige.
Afterward, they exchanged a few more messages and upon settling the details, Colin ended the conversation.
He then naturally checked the parchment as he usually would…
Only three hours had passed in reality, and there were no major changes; it was just as it was before, but now there was a whole bunch of bragging about “Mole” employees from “World Code-13.”
“Next major expansion, I guess I’ll have to wait until I’m C Level, huh?”
Colin mused that by then, the choices should expand significantly.
He just wondered what kind of tests he would face at C Level…
“Speaking of which, that ‘Joyful Seven Days Farm’ mission seems to never be settled. Where did all those employees who vanished after clearing it go? Could they have been drafted into the Corps?”
Colin found it rather strange that there was no news at all.
After browsing the forum for a while longer and not finding any useful information, he opened the auction house to look for items that could heal injuries.
Although he wasn’t in dire need of them now, if there were any available at a reasonable price, he would definitely buy them.
He might not need them, but his territory could use them, especially since medical resources were scarce.
Unfortunately, he found none after browsing through the listings.
“It must have been cleared out by the officials; I can’t compete. Also, since the officials got involved, even those ‘psychological stability’ props that regular employees normally wouldn’t buy are all gone…”
Colin observed the auction house, now considerably emptier, noting that these props were now scarce.
Those had been the most common type before…
The reason was simple: while employees didn’t fear contamination from anomalies thanks to various company measures like injections, it was different for the officials. A large number of them had extremely unstable psychological conditions, and it was probably these people who were the main buyers of those props.
“I should sell some stuff too…”
After checking and finding nothing he wanted, Colin opened his Storage Room and looked at the over four hundred tiny golden beans the size of rice grains. Each bean bore strange, twisted-looking but actually straight patterns of light—
These were the little buffs that Shana had created over seven consecutive days and nights, taking breaks from fighting him, assisting with the construction in the territory, and tirelessly handcrafting each one.

chapters.title: Chapter 731 - 731 525 Shanas Product._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 731: Chapter 525 Shana’s Product._2 Chapter 731: Chapter 525 Shana’s Product._2 A D Level Personnel under high-intensity use can last at least 3 hours, and under normal use, they’d start at half a day.
If they lie still, they might standby for a day or two.
Of course, the specific usage situation also depends on the user’s own quality.
The stronger they are, the faster it will consume…
“Actually, we could increase production of these ‘little golden beans’ by reducing costs and enhancing efficiency.”
Colin touched the batch of products that was about to hit the shelves. Shana had crafted them with great care, infusing a substantial amount of power into them.
If she had been less meticulous, there would have been at least seven hundred a week, nearly double the number.
However, unfortunately, Shana did not take up Colin’s suggestion to have his employees stick their necks out. Instead, she saw through everything and lightly tapped Colin on the shoulder with a flick of her finger, giving him a roll of the eyes.
Colin shook his head slightly, reining in his thoughts, and temporarily listed the items at a price of 20 Points each.
He then casually asked some employees to promote them and didn’t give the matter a second glance, having no doubts whether the items would sell.
…
“Take a look, powerful BUFF originally 30 Points, now on limited discount for 20 Points, use the same BUFF as Brother Shunzi…”
“A temporary blessing effect costs twenty points? That’s over ten thousand yuan in cash. Are you kidding me? That’s a rip-off!”
“How is it expensive? It’s not expensive at all, it’s something that saves your life! Sometimes, if you can’t afford it, it’s your own issue to consider…”
“Damn, who bought them all out? I just wanted to try one, are you playing a game of hungry marketing huh!”
“…”
…
As the employees were lamenting, Xu Duojin entered a meeting room. As he pushed the door open, the room was already full of officials of level seven and above.
Practically everyone from the province, whether they were stationed here or just passing through, had come.
When Xu Duojin entered, everyone stood up to greet him. He gestured for them to sit down and then turned his attention to something surrounded by people in the middle of the room.
Those shimmering golden beans were exactly the BUFFs Colin had listed for sale.
“You’re saying this thing is really that miraculous?”
Xu Duojin asked curiously.
He heard it could somewhat suppress the negative effects of purification in the body, which was indeed unheard of…
“Yes, we’ve tested it, and it’s definitely effective, working particularly well for Seventh and Eighth Level Personnel. It can significantly reduce the bodily pollution for at least one day and helps us use our powers more effectively…” a Sixth Level Personnel with a crutch said.
“What about the side effects?” Xu Duojin pursued.
“Extended use may result in a bit of emotional numbness, but it doesn’t affect thinking, and it seems reversible!”
“That’s it?”
“That’s it.”
“This… is virtually without side effects then.”
Xu Duojin adjusted his black framed glasses. They were almost driven mad by the torment of pollution; losing a bit of emotion was hardly an issue for them.
Without further ado, Xu Duojin picked up a golden bean, channeled his spirit into it, and called forth its power.
Soon, strands of pale light began to emanate…
Under the light’s illumination, he could distinctly feel the “buzzing” noise that had been persistent in his painfully aching brain starting to weaken…
The decrease was slight, but even that small degree of relief made him feel considerably more relaxed.
This sensation reminded him of being close to Colin and being exposed to the “Bonfire.”
Under the flame, he also felt more comfortable…
But the “Bonfire” seemed to rely on reinforcing one’s own humanity to resist, to achieve the desired effect, whereas this was a direct suppression and partial erasure of pollution.
If he could do both at the same time, the effects would be very noticeable.
“It’s indeed a good product, though it seems to suppress our Extraordinary Power to a certain extent. The suppressed part, however, is nearly offset by the enhancement effects it provides… Alright, I’ll take this one with me to test out its effects more, so no one else gets trapped.”
With a brief summation, Xu Duojin casually grabbed a few more golden beans into his pocket, causing other people’s eyes to twitch.
Without waiting for them to speak, Xu Duojin started, “So, where did this thing come from?”
“Only know it came from Bonfire Company…” said a Level Seven Personnel from out of town, shaking his head.
Xu Duojin’s eyebrows twitched, “Bonfire Company?”
“Yes, it’s said to be sold by a person called ‘654321,’ known as Brother Shunzi. This person is very famous, rumored to be the strongest company employee. You should also know him; there’s a record of him in the company. We’ve been trying to find out who he is, but so far, there’s no trace…”
The Level Seven Personnel paused before continuing, “We requested instructions from our superiors, and then received guidance from Mr. Wu, who said he didn’t have time and asked us to come to you. Perhaps you might have some knowledge?”
Brother Shunzi… Xu Duojin fell silent upon hearing the name.
Knowledge? It was more than just knowledge… he had to keep an eye on that side nearly twenty-four hours a day, even when carrying out certain events to avoid any incidents.
That these people were unaware didn’t surprise him.
The details of Colin’s case were top secret; within the Eighth Level, he was almost the only person who knew the complete truth. Even among the Ninth Level Personnel, besides Old Master Wu, not everyone was fully informed.
So, it was normal for the personnel on site to be unaware…
“Alright, I will try to find out more about the situation in a moment, but I may not get a response,” he said.
Xu Duojin quickly concluded the topic.
“Okay, this matter is very important. I’ll leave everything in your hands, Mr. Xu. We must prepare as many materials as possible for future use,” the out-of-town Level Seven Personnel said earnestly.
Now, with Old Master Wu’s “great birthday” approaching, the entire Earth was preparing for battle, allocating all resources to get through that period.
No one knew exactly what disasters would occur at that moment, nor how many demons and monsters would emerge.
But one thing was undeniable…
Even those who were not Extraordinary Ones with foresight or deductive powers could vaguely sense the imminent approach of something terrifying as time went on.
Xu Duojin nodded, indicating that he would take the matter seriously.
As soon as the meeting ended, he immediately called Colin to explain the situation…
“Ah, so it was you who bought it? I was wondering who was so extravagant to buy up everything within less than ten minutes,” Colin said while playing a game with one hand and holding the phone with the other.
He had been confident about selling the item, but to have it all sold out in about ten minutes was beyond his expectations…
However, from Xu Duojin’s description, Shana’s BUFF seemed to indeed have a significant effect on them.
“I wanted to inquire about a couple of things, one is whether it’s possible to trade with a currency other than Points, and two, how much of this thing there is and whether there are any more powerful items of this kind…”
All the golden beans gave off a sort of assembly line production feeling, leading Xu Duojin to intuitively figure out these were energy-produced items.
“Currency other than Points, huh? Let me think about it. You guys make a list of what you can offer, and I’ll take a look. As for the item, currently, we can only sell about five hundred per week at most, no more. As for stronger ones, there are, but we’ll have to see about that later…”
Colin pondered over the past few days’ events. Shana had already been contacting various “Light” branches or subordinate forces, trying to get everyone to work together to produce the item, but so far she hasn’t been able to pull out anything valuable to motivate everyone.
After all, Points were valuable only to her, not so much to others.
But the official miscellaneous goods were plentiful, and there had to be something that could be offered…
If a large-scale trade could be established…
The several Golden Cards he had might finally relieve his worries about Points!
‘It’s just a pity that I don’t have much space on me, and even with the space from my employees, it’s not that significant. It’s not easy to form large-scale trades. But come to think of it, working hard on missions may not earn as much as dealing in contraband…’
Colin couldn’t help but mutter to himself in a low voice.
Capital is truly detestable!
Fortunately, he was the one harvesting the leeks.
After exchanging some preliminary intentions, they didn’t continue the conversation.
Hanging up the phone, Colin continued to look at the screen in front of him.
“Dark Souls, launch!”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 732 - 732 526 Rosens Heart._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 732: Chapter 526 Rosen’s “Heart”._1 Chapter 732: Chapter 526 Rosen’s “Heart”._1 Wednesday, on the outskirts of Base Number Five, within an oversized spatial area.
Groups of official personnel were carefully dealing with various Containment Subjects to ensure the success of an imminent transaction.
Although the majority of objects here had gone through containment measures,
transporting them now and gathering them all in one place made it difficult to guarantee that nothing unexpected would happen.
After all, those that had been brought here were the types extremely difficult to handle, and the total number of these troublesome Containment Subjects had reached an astonishing five hundred!
This was a terrifying figure!
One misstep, and the entire Base Number Five could face a major incident!
“Be careful, be careful, don’t make a sound with your steps when you move away from it, be cautious…”
“When you pass this object, get down, keep your head low, don’t raise it above…”
“Damn it! Who just looked at it?”
An official cursed softly upon seeing countless faces suddenly sprouting on a mirror covered in charms, each face squeezing against the mirror, straining against his gaze as though wanting to break free from their restraints.
The glow from the writings on the charms managed to suppress them back into place…
However, a minor deviation triggered a series of chain reactions elsewhere.
A ghostly sailboat from the Yuanming Era sent a chilling breeze as a fishing line suddenly lashed out toward an employee…
Not far from it, several employees’ eyes were savagely scooped out by an unknown entity.
But that wasn’t the key issue; the real problem was that they had to keep their gaze fixed on a sculpture in front of them, or else it would begin to move and snap their necks…
Suddenly, as if undergoing rapid cell division, a meteorite sprouted eyes, shooting out lasers…
Just one small mistake, and within a matter of seconds, Zone C plunged into chaos.
At that moment, a garrisoned Level Seven Personnel promptly stood out to handle the emergency, unceremoniously unleashing three special pages:
“All seals here, increase in strength!”
As his words fell, the abnormalities began to diminish, letting him breathe a sigh of relief as he silently praised the effectiveness of the “Decree Book.”
“We only have ten minutes, quickly rescue the injured, maintain the seals…”
He was only halfway through speaking when the Level Seven Personnel suddenly became alert, blinked forcefully, and his pupils constricted.
He saw that the once stable scene had vanished, chaos ensued, with some people already being dragged towards the ghostly sailboat by the strange fishing lines, while others had their necks broken for not keeping their eyes on their target…
Despite the presence of professional teams, they were still struggling to cope with the situation.
What was more alarming for the Level Seven Personnel was realizing that what he had said was not “all seals increase in strength” but “all mystical effects increase in strength!”
Although it was just one incorrect word, the repercussions could be catastrophic!
“Damn, an anomaly just interfered with me!”
The Level Seven Personnel in charge of the area cursed softly, without hesitation he attempted to call for assistance.
And immediately, he pressed a button, enacting a full blockade of the Containment Zone C to prevent the danger from spreading.
As for their own safety, it was no longer a concern…
“We must not let this situation escalate any further!”
With this thought, the Level Seven Personnel sealed off the area, but just then, he saw a surge of flames melting the door and pouring in…
His pupils contracted, believing for a moment they were doomed, thinking the outside had also been breached.
But the next second, he realized the flames were not harming him, instead, they were flowing through him into the containment area of Zone C.
“Quite lively here, isn’t it…”
Colin entered with the flames.
Under the gaze of the Level Seven Personnel and everyone else, with each step he took, rings of terrifying flames erupted, engulfing the entire area.
Within the flames, all anomalies trying to break free shrank back…
Even seeming to shiver in terror!
Ignoring their stares, Colin glanced at the chunks of flesh scattered on the ground like a butcher’s display and then at the few bodies whose spines and skulls had been ripped out…
The brief chaos had resulted in a high rate of maiming.
“I apologize, my carelessness led to these deaths…”
“It has nothing to do with you, there was a little accident over in Area A,” Xu Duojin appeared and offered reassurances.
“A lot were injured, but nobody died.”
Colin’s voice came from one side as he looked at the meaty chunks on the ground, still alive and, more importantly, their brains were not damaged since not much time had passed, less than a few minutes, and there was no contamination.
Rescue was still a consideration…
Of course, what mattered most was that all the victims were Extraordinary Ones, whose physiques were far stronger than ordinary humans.
Plus, his “Bonfire” was providing “heat” to keep their vitality from dissipating…
The situation didn’t look too bad.
Colin casually threw a few “Colorless Crystals” to sustain their lives.
Roots from the “Mark of the Fire Tree” spread out, and along with the Little Maid, began the treatment, rapidly rejoining the chunks of flesh and restoring them to their original form.
They were still unconscious, but they were breathing again…
About fifteen minutes later, the roots of the “Fire Tree” converged, forming the figure of an old man who instructed the medical staff nearby:
“That should do it. These common injuries, when I step in, it’s nearly impossible for them to go wrong. And since they are merely physical traumas with no contamination or mutation, they’re rather easy to deal with. However, the maid can’t permanently bridge their wounds internally, so if you don’t want them to turn back into chunks of flesh on the ground, remember, you all need to handle them with care and take it slow…”

chapters.title: Chapter 733 - 733 526 Rosens Heart._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 733: Chapter 526 Rosen’s “Heart”._2 Chapter 733: Chapter 526 Rosen’s “Heart”._2 “Next, they will likely remain unconscious for ten days, but that’s not a big issue. Don’t wake them up early either, because they simply can’t handle it when we connect their sutured faces. So, just let them lie there.”
“The prophylactic recovery items can be used or not, but remember, it’s best to have them. It’s also fine without them. However, if used, they must be of a mild type…”
“Additionally, there might be some effect on their memories, but these will gradually recover, so there’s no need to worry…”
“Regarding the nutrition liquid configuration, pay attention…”
As he gave instructions to the medical team beside him, a Level Seven Personnel nearby stood there open-mouthed:
“This, they actually saved him…”
The body on the ground had not looked much better than pork laid out in a butcher’s shop…
Yet, in just about ten minutes, they managed to piece it back together and even bring it back to life!
Colin said with a smile, “Bonfire technology, kid.”
Another ten minutes or so passed, and once the situation at the site was completely resolved, all anomalies in the “Bonfire” became utterly still.
“Alright, everything is in our hands now, you can all pull out.”
Hearing Colin’s words, Xu Duojin and the others nodded, leading their group out of the vast space.
The thick partitions between each section were then gradually removed…
Colin, in turn, took control of the entire space.
And with the “Bonfire” sealing the area, he activated the transaction task. At once, a hazy fog appeared and quickly thickened “accidentally”.
“Wooo~”
From the depths of the gray fog, the monotonous sound of a flute and the sound of a train traveling along the tracks could be faintly heard.
In just a few blinks of an eye…
“Clack.”
The train doors opened, marked with various scratches as if they had just left a battlefield, and numerous employees clad in lightweight, full coverage exoskeleton armor descended…
Compared to previous times, there were more trade items, so more employees came down as well.
A total of almost forty employees.
It was just that work had not been long…
“Feels like everyone’s becoming more and more irritable…”
Colin blinked.
Visible flashes of light flickered frequently on the faces of the employees. Although unsure of what they were saying, if it followed the usual pattern, they seemed to be cursing a storm.
However, despite their cursing, their hands did not stop moving. They still handled the various Containment Subjects carefully and conscientiously before carrying them back to the train.
But Colin didn’t get a chance to watch them for long as an employee who seemed to be the commanding officer approached him. First, he saluted to show respect, then handed over a thick letter.
“‘Lady Rabbit’s’ letter? Why is it so thick this time?”
Colin, a bit puzzled, nodded back and accepted the envelope. He didn’t hurry to open it but placed it in the “Storage Room”, thinking whether he could communicate with this logistics employee.
He was quite curious about where this group of people came from…
“Could it be from some other ‘Subsidiary’?”
Colin thought to himself. He couldn’t tell before, but now he felt that these people seemed to be logistics personnel, but their level and quality were very high.
Of course, high compared to some of the company members here, but nowhere near him.
Unfortunately, after transferring the thick envelope, the other party did not show any desire to communicate and instead walked away to supervise the scene, to prevent any accidents.
The transport of anomalies roughly continued for about half an hour.
When all the transfer of Containment Subjects was complete and another member of the logistics group had him sign a confirmation slip, they waved and hurried onto the train, quickly departing.
“Why do I feel like we’re missing something this time?”
Watching the train start to move, Colin felt something was off.
It wasn’t until the train had left and disappeared that he slapped his forehead, recalling that the logistics personnel who had been hostile toward him for some reason was not seen in this transaction.
He wondered where they had gone…
Probably dead, he guessed.
Colin shook his head, collected his thoughts, and after bidding farewell to Xu Duojin and others, he went straight home.
He was quite curious about what was inside the letter that Lady Bunny had given him.
“Hope it’s something good…”
He took out the envelope, tore along the seal, and as Colin opened it, he found a thick stack of letter paper inside, no small number, totaling ten sheets.
He first spread out the top sheet to take a look.
“I have already received the information you sent about the employee from ‘World Code-13’. Unfortunately, transferring her over is extremely difficult, unless I’m there in person. Otherwise, without the ‘Subsidiary’s’ consent, I can’t move her…”
“After all, her creator has a high status. It’s hard to take action against her through company rules.”
“Besides, even if I really forced the issue, the cost would be high. It would significantly damage my company reputation, which wouldn’t fade quickly and would severely affect some of my arrangements…”
“So, concerning that employee in the area, there are some things that simply can’t be bypassed.”
…
‘So it really won’t work, I can only honestly be ‘drained’…
Colin pursed his lips but didn’t care too much. His gaze focused on the second paragraph.
“Creator” with a high status…
If “Lady Bunny” says the status is high, it must be Rosen.
Of course, he wasn’t surprised by this. He had already guessed it was related to him, just without solid proof.
Then Colin’s eyes continued down the envelope, and they narrowed slightly.
“Secondly, as for why it’s collecting points in large quantities, although there’s little information in this regard, the overall view suggests it might be because it still holds certain sentiments for Rosen…”
“Even though the situation related to him has been essentially determined, and his fate is sealed, there is an extremely important thing that has yet to find a place—the ‘heart,’ which is the most crucial part of Rosen and several ‘Flame Bearers,’ has not been recovered…”
“This may be the reason for its bit of luck, hoping for the return of that one, or expecting his heart to be found.”
“Theoretically speaking, if he truly is still alive and returns, then everything can be declared over. Unfortunately, this is an impossibility.”
“The ‘logic node shield’ it previously employed against you normally shouldn’t work. But since it did, it can only mean that its reasons are probably related to protecting some information about Rosen…”
“My guess would be that it shielded the direction of points usage to ensure you wouldn’t realize it might use those points to activate certain protocols in pursuit of Rosen’s situation…”
“However, as I’ve said, the related intelligence is basically clear, and there’s no significance in delving deeper. The investigation in this regard is extremely unlikely to progress until the ‘Flame Bearers’ reappear and the ‘Primordial Fire’ returns.”
…
“So that’s how it is, wanting to find its former master, hence the points. Then Lady Bunny feels it’s like throwing good money after bad and doesn’t want to delve deeper?”
Colin thoughtfully looked at this paragraph.
He had also noticed during this time that after the Corps had successfully taken away two “Hunger” Fragments, “Lady Bunny”‘s interest in “World Code-13” hadn’t completely vanished, but it did lessen by a large margin.
And the little that remained was likely just some attention towards the “Subsidiary” of “World Code-13”.
Unfortunately, this entity had its own thoughts. It didn’t cooperate much and didn’t want to be taken by “Lady Bunny”, oh no, it didn’t want to serve “Lady Bunny”.
Next, Colin continued to read on. The letter mentioned some other matters, like the next trade would be set for the week after the end of “The Descent Project”.
And from the next time, trades would be carried out weekly…
“The behind-the-scenes trading suddenly became frequent,” Colin murmured, his lips pursed as he felt that everything was starting to get urgent.
When he finished this part, he flipped to the back to see if there was any other content…
Unfortunately, these responses were all there was.
Colin’s expectation for “2044”, “the ultimate item from a certain company”, “Joyful Farmstead”, and such matters had no further mention.
It was at that moment, as if to confirm he had finished reading the contents, the piece of paper spontaneously ignited, leaving not even ash behind.
Colin then looked towards the other sheets, which one by one, each listed introductions of some items.
The items from the last trade’s feedback had arrived!
There were a total of thirteen items, and to Colin’s surprise, out of the thirteen, eight were Purple Items, with the least valuable among the rest being green!
“Is the quality this high with this batch?” he wondered.
Colin reviewed the item information, and a surprised expression spread across his face.

chapters.title: Chapter 734 - 734 527
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 734: 527 Chapter 734: 527 During those few times before, Colin remembered the items he acquired were either damaged or plain, with only a few green ones, let alone purple ones. He hadn’t expected this time to have the most items with purple names.
“That’s true, the quality of the things I offered in the last trade was pretty high, so it’s only fair some good stuff should come out of it.”
Colin muttered, although in terms of official offerings, all were “difficult problems,” the kind of anomalies that are hard to deal with.
But it’s precisely because they’re hard to deal with that they seem high in quality.
As he flipped through the dozen or so item documents like poker cards, his gaze skimmed over each document, quickly getting a rough idea of what these things were for.
“The effects are okay, but seem a bit lacking, and the overlap rate of some equipment effects seems quite high?”
Colin furrowed his brows as he held the documents.
For example, a purple-named item called “Surefire Rifle” – its effect stated that within three thousand kilometers, as long as you aim and shoot at a photo with the target’s birth date and name, you could snipe the enemy commander from eight hundred li away with a single bullet.
However, the bullet seemed impressive only on paper because it would fire from any random point a hundred meters away from the target. Though the bullet wouldn’t emerge from underground and would choose an angle that wasn’t obstructed on its own.
But this device couldn’t be enchanted with additional effects, and its power largely depended on the bullet’s material…
And for Extraordinary Ones…
Most bullets they can produce are enough to get a reaction within a hundred meters.
So it’s like it’s somewhat useless but also a bit useful – it’s damn tied up in complex rules. If you say it’s useful, it’s not greatly so.
“Out of the eight purple items, three are similar… rifle, bow, zither, huh?”
Colin was taken aback as he found something unexpected in the similar item descriptions:
“A zither? Playing a tune while targeting a photo of an enemy thousands of kilometers away? Every object within a hundred meters of the target can hear the instrument’s sound – what’s with this humorous effect? Don’t tell me they’re mocking me…”
Playing a song for someone from a thousand li away while you’re a thousand li away yourself?
“This is the first time I’ve seen such uselessness among purple items…”
He shook his head, feeling that these effects likely came from the same Containment Subject, pieced together with some other Containment Subjects.
It’s just that he didn’t know who the maker was, and once caught, would be in for a good talking to!
What he needs wasn’t shooting arrows from thousands of kilometers away; what he needs was something like a nuke or other explosive things that could be lobbed directly from a thousand li away – a long-range deployment well!
Taking a deep breath, Colin turned his attention to the other items’ information.
The few others were fairly standard and usually battle-oriented, such as a Severed Finger that could unleash a thunderstorm within a certain area, or a flag that could control Flame, or a brain tentacle that could mount a psychic assault on an enemy, and could…
“Eh? What’s going on, why are so many of these human body parts?”
Colin scratched the back of his head, who was the maker this time?
Not noticing was one thing, but once he paid attention, he realized almost half consisted of various limbs.
Looking at a document, which had a sketch of a Scepter that instead of having a gem at the top, was embedded with a brain, Colin was somewhat speechless.
No, more accurately, the Scepter was formed by the brain’s tentacles entangled together like twisted pastries.
The document specifically mentioned that this brain Scepter could be launched to automatically attack and so on.
“If you take this out for a fight, it doesn’t exactly seem on the up and up…”
Colin pursed his lips and after reviewing all the purple items, he then turned his gaze to the green ones.
Among these, there was a support item that could temporarily boost one’s physique.
Although the boost wasn’t very high for him, it was quite suitable for keeping the lives of ordinary people hanging on.
After going through all thirteen documents, Colin picked up his phone and notified Xu Duojin, telling him that the trade settlement had arrived and they arranged a time to come and collect it.
About half an hour later, Xu Duojin, wearing sunglasses, knocked on the door punctually – not a second early, not a second late.
Upon seeing Colin, he revealed a smile like that of a farmer reaping a good harvest—
He had been waiting for so long, and this little bro finally got some Explode Equipment again!
The equipment he had received before was worth far more than it seemed. Although a lot of it wasn’t fully understood, some of the design ideas gave them quite the insight.
“Have a seat.”
Pointing to the sofa, Colin handed over all ten item documents to Xu Duojin without missing a single one.
“The documents explain the items, as well as the items themselves. If you want to take them out, get an Employee to press their thumb in the blank confirmation space below, and the item will be retrieved.”
“As for usage, it’s pretty much the same as before, once taken out, ownership belongs to that Employee, but they can authorize in any way the use to non-company personnel…”
Colin briefly explained the purpose of these items.
“Alright.” Xu Duojin, still wearing his sunglasses, scrutinized the content on them.
He examined them in detail, nodding occasionally, mostly inferring from the described features and negative effects on the documents that these items were made using the Containment Subjects they had previously sent over.
They tried to destroy those things but couldn’t, only to find out that within a few days, the company had turned them into items again.
After looking through them, Xu Duojin showed a satisfied smile, as he was quite pleased with all the items listed there.

chapters.title: Chapter 735 - 735 527 Colin Brother Finally Explodes
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 735: Chapter 527: Colin Brother Finally Explodes Equipment Again! _2 Chapter 735: Chapter 527: Colin Brother Finally Explodes Equipment Again! _2 Although compared to when it was contained, its effect has significantly deteriorated and dismantled.
But the difference is, no matter how it’s used, there’s no worry about it exploding, unlike when it’s a containment subject…
It was just like the explosives from the earlier years, where any slight touch might cause an explosion.
“Don’t you feel some things are a bit… lackluster?” Colin looked at his smiling face and asked curiously.
Xu Duojin shook his head, “Not really, I’ve thought of some people who could probably make use of it, so it might not be that lackluster. Of course, how it will actually turn out, I’ll have to see when the time comes; right now, I can’t say for certain.”
Pausing for a moment, he asked curiously, “By the way, I have a question I’d like to ask: if someone who isn’t a staff member uses this thing with verbal authorization, can they tap into a level of effect beyond the item’s stated capability? You know, that thing… ‘Item Liberation’?”
The effect of “Item Liberation” is said to be only a few percent, but in reality, once liberated, the experienced effect often increases significantly…
Moreover, during this period, some officials they had in place had reached the stage where they should be moving up to D Level.
That is to say, they could start considering “Item Liberation.”
Of course, if given the chance, it would still be better to liberate it and then let some senior personnel use it; after all, once some sufficiently strong Purple Gear is liberated, even the lowest F Level can hold their own against Eighth Level Personnel in a couple of rounds…
If this were properly handed over to some high-level official personnel, one wouldn’t dare to imagine how useful it could be.
“No.”
Colin flatly refused, picked up the dried fruits from the table, tossed them into his mouth, and spoke while eating, “To put it simply, this is like overclocking use. In this regard, only employees are capable of doing it, as it involves applying for certain protocol permissions and whatnot… in short, this is highly bound.”
Perhaps legendary B+ employees or higher could “make an exception” and remove this restriction.
But that had little to do with Colin at the moment.
Anyway, he couldn’t do it.
“Alright then.” Xu Duojin didn’t dwell on it too much.
“However, there’s no need to focus only on this aspect; you can stimulate the item in your own way to let it produce effects beyond its inherent capabilities…”
Pausing, Colin continued, “After reaching Green Gear, the stability of the items is still quite durable.”
Unless “Red Moon” or some strong First Level Containment Subject intervenes, in general, it’s really hard to damage these things…
“So, if the integrity hits rock bottom, it won’t go out of control…”
“No.” Colin interrupted before the other could finish, “If the integrity hits rock bottom, it’s broken, there won’t be any risk of it going out of control, so you don’t really need to worry too much.
“Normally, when most items are destroyed, the anomaly also disappears and won’t emerge again.
“Of course, if some high-level lifeform far exceeds the item’s capability and deliberately manipulates it, then… anything under Purple Gear still carries risk.
“But most of the time, you don’t need to worry about that.”
“I see…” Xu Duojin nodded, indicating that he understood, then, curious about the mention of “under Purple Gear,” he asked whether everything above Purple Gear was permanently secure…
“Permanent is too strong a term, but even if High Order Containment Subjects took action, the likelihood is small.”
Colin remembered how Orange Gear or the Golden Card, the “Time Reversal” was corrupted by “The Night” for such a long time in a certain place, and it only went out of control a little…
Considering that there “The Night” is mostly sealed, it speaks volumes of its stability.
If it were left to the likes of “King of Savage Sound,” a disgrace among High Order Containment Subjects, Colin had no idea how many thousands of years it would take to see even the faintest advance past several zeros after the decimal point…
“And then there’s another thing, starting from next Monday, trading will take place once a week…”
“Once a week?!” Xu Duojin’s eyes behind his sunglasses widened, doubting he heard correctly.
“Yes, but each time, the number cannot exceed five hundred items, and contain no more than five Level 2 Containment Subjects with special traits, and no more than one First Level Containment Subject, also the transfer period must ensure the general stability of the containment subjects.” Colin relayed “Lady Bunny’s” response in this regard.
For “Lady Bunny,” even if she lost a hundred Level 2 Containment Subjects, she’d probably find it fairly simple to deal with.
After all, she can dispatch “Hired Staff” with First Level Containment Subject strength.
Just one of these employees could suppress a large group of Level 2 Containment Subjects…
But while in transit, the train might not hold up, or the logistic team inside the train might not be able to handle it.
‘In the end, it seems that it’s because the official’s current containment technology is too poor. Otherwise, transporting any number of them shouldn’t be a problem,’ Colin thought to himself.
Across from him, once he received confirmation, Xu Duojin’s face broke into a relieved smile:
“Good, good, good! Sure thing!”
Under proper channels, removing one of those dangerous items would further stabilize the world.
As for the limit on the number of Level 2 Containment Subjects.
If this happened a dozen or twenty more times, the part of Earth that’s already been contained would probably be emptied out.
After all, there isn’t much that they’ve managed to contain.
As for First Level Containment Subjects…
Mr. Xu thought for a moment, the official agencies hadn’t contained any of those, at most, there were only restrictions and banishments. Even if he wanted to take them for trade, the task wouldn’t be easy.
The most obvious example was in Africa, where there existed a super massive, active strange mist.
Its area was roughly over two thousand square kilometers.
This thing’s threat level had already reached the potential to destroy the world…
It took a hell of an effort, along with numerous sacrifices and powerful artifacts, to restrain it.
The idea of moving it was simply preposterous.
However, once other issues were resolved and they were free to act, there might be a chance.
Later, after exchanging a bit more, Mr. Xu left with the intelligence and documents for the artifacts, satisfied.
About half an hour later, he showed up at the outskirts of Base Number Five and handed over the items.
“New items from the Item Division, check them and then submit them, let them decide who should use them and how,” Mr. Xu handed the documents to an office employee.
“Okay…” The employee didn’t say much, took the documents, glanced at them, and then suddenly realized something was amiss, stopping Mr. Xu who was preparing to leave for other tasks.
“Mr. Xu, it seems there’s something wrong here.”
“What is it?”
“Look here, the page numbers at the bottom don’t match. See, from 4 to 7, 9 to 11, three pages are missing. Should we find the missing parts to verify…?”
“Smack!”
Mr. Xu patted him on the shoulder: “I have some business on my side that required pulling a few pages, don’t ask too much, understand?”
“Oh…” The new staff nodded, indicating they understood.
Mr. Xu taking a kickback, it seemed, wasn’t such a big deal…
…
Meanwhile, in Colin’s room, he took out two artifacts, one was a Severed Finger that could emit lightning, and the other was the Brain Scepter…
He didn’t plan to use these himself but intended to give them to two of his companions.
“You take this and use it.” Colin handed the finger, which looked like it belonged to some sort of beast, to the Little Maid.
The object would allow the Little Maid to use it—if it didn’t shock the enemy, she could use it to shock herself to enhance her own performance…
There was another item, the “Mental Storm Wand,” a strangely shaped wand in the form of a brain, which Colin intended for “Yukionna” to use.
The effect was quite good, able to enhance soul strength and protection, along with a series of related things.
And “Yukionna” was already largely immune to ordinary physical attacks like collisions…
By boosting the soul’s strength as well, all in all, it seemed quite fitting.
The only negative effect was that it could easily cause brain fatigue…
“I don’t think that counts as a negative effect. The real negative effect might be that it includes a certain intelligence enhancement.” Colin rubbed his head with a headache.
“Yukionna” was currently simple-minded, making her easy to control, but if she became smarter, it might not be as easy to control her anymore. To him, it was uncertain whether this was a good thing.
.
.
.
