chapters.title: Chapter 736 - 736 528
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 736: 528 Chapter 736: 528 Nowadays, Yukionna might be called an item, but as her human-like qualities increased, the restrictions of the Containment Protocol on her seemed to have been reduced…
The so-called possession and lethal freezing “negative effects” on the user by the original Yukionna were pretty much gone.
It felt like there might come a day when the ring could be directly smashed and released.
“No, you can’t release her either…”
Colin looked at the Yukionna who was twiddling the Brain Scepter like a propeller hat and had the dumb look of a foolish child on her face, and suddenly felt that this intelligence increase wasn’t too apparent.
The Brain Scepter spun in circles in the sky like a dragonfly and spread waves of a faint mental ripple.
With a figure as shapely as a young matron’s, and although her intelligence had clearly increased, Yukionna, who still held a child-like mentality, puffed out cold air around the scepter excitedly puffing her cheeks, making it spin faster while absorbing all those mental ripples, as if she were snacking…
Watching her like this, Colin felt that releasing her might easily lead to trouble…
Hmm, can’t release her.
“If the next mission isn’t too difficult, maybe consider letting Yukionna carry it out in full, with me supervising?”
Colin raised his hand to touch his chin, thinking it might not be a bad idea.
A fully unleashed Yukionna had strength that ranked high even among Third Level Containment Subjects…
If he encountered her in the wild, Colin would have to use a set of skills to take her out in a second.
After all, in the early days, Yukionna was a quite strong and able assistant to him; although she had fallen behind somewhat now, that didn’t make her completely useless.
Colin often let her merge with his body to gain some of the Containment Subject’s inherent abilities like levitation and phasing through walls…
“If we find something compatible with Yukionna in the future, we could let her merge with it to enhance her life attribute level. If someday we can raise her to First Level Containment Subject status, then… that seems quite good?”
“Yeah, and if she’s human enough, then maybe when I reach C Level and can have my own team, I could make her my employee to exploit her better, oh no, I mean, guide her to better serve human society…”
Colin felt a bit regretful he had only noticed these things now.
But finding something that could match with Yukionna wasn’t an easy task.
It’s not as simple as finding any item with an “ice” attribute to combine…
After briefly paying attention, Colin turned his focus back to this week’s “delivery” event.
The requirement was to arrive at a small village in the Yungui Mountains after ten o’clock tonight, find a well there, jump into it to reach a special area, locate a door buried deep underground and throw “Rosen’s Amputated Hand Copy” into it to finish.
No mention was made of the risks…
After briefly going over the information, Colin immediately went to Xu Duojin and asked him to bring over some data.
‘A rather remote area, if not for the mission display, the authorities might not even know there had been people living there…’
After briefly going over the data and having a meal, Colin set out directly.
A few hours later, he arrived at the target area alone.
An eerily primitive forest, and the so-called village…
“This doesn’t look like a village. Is it the wrong time?”
Colin looked around, only to see tall trees everywhere, with various loud insect noises non-stop, plus the ominous, almost imperceptible cold mist at night, which was rather creepy.
And in the upper right corner of his vision, a time display provided by the Little Maid.
It was about nine o’clock…
He had arrived a bit early.
He had been standing there waiting until ten o’clock when, suddenly feeling a sense of awareness, Colin turned his head and saw that a few meters away from him, where there had just been a forest, was now shrouded in a cold and misty fog…
One robust tree marked the boundary; in front of the tree was the normal world, while behind it lay something dark and strange.
Deep within the dim fog, with the reflection of the flame on his body, Colin could make out an ancient gate about ten meters tall, its plaque inscribed with faded vermilion, ancient text that was mottled and unclear…
“Little Food Manor?”
Colin murmured softly, though not with certainty. Then he moved his eyes, looking past the gate and into the depths, where he could glimpse the outlines of some ancient, low-lying buildings that were faintly visible through the thick fog behind.
“Hiss…”
Colin felt a shiver run down his spine.
The atmospheres of anomalous events within the country could be intensely creepy and eerie.
Originally, he had considered using this place for “Yukionna” and Little Maid to practice, but seeing the situation, it seemed better to take it easy to avoid any issues.
“Better find a task type abroad next time; they are more straightforward and easier to bully…”
Drawing in a breath, Colin gathered a ball of flame above his head, then strode forward, passing under the gate, entering this secret world.
“An independent inner world intersecting with reality…”
Feeling an indescribable sense of trance, Colin nodded and continued deeper along the path.
Soon, he came upon the village he had glimpsed before.
Dozens of ancient buildings constructed of earth and timber stood, some of them adorned with faded red lanterns and the like…
Following the mission guidance, from a distance, Colin saw a well in a large building resembling a clan ancestral temple; he couldn’t tell if it was dry or not…
He had pinpointed the target of his mission, but he didn’t act immediately.
After all, whether he walked or flew, he was likely to pass through that cluster of ancient and creepy buildings.
“It looks so sinister, makes me want to burn it all down…”
Colin didn’t sense any real danger, but the indescribable eeriness made him want to eliminate any potential threats.
If he were to start a wildfire here and everything was set ablaze…
His sense of security would be at its peak.
However, just as Colin was pondering the feasibility of doing so, he suddenly felt as if his flame had illuminated something bizarre…
Immediately, he turned his head, looking to the side, and his heart skipped a beat…
About a hundred meters to his right, there stood a massive, crooked tree with claw-like branches, from which hung a row after row of Chongzhen, no, bodies.
The number was astonishingly in the thousands…
“There’s not a single sign of life in the village; could they all be hanged here?”
Colin wondered briefly, then with a Flame Leap, he appeared in front of the crooked tree.
As he was about to raise the flame to illuminate and take a closer look at the bodies, he noticed a skeleton seated at the base of the tree, dressed in clothing that seemed almost modern.
And through an item scattered next to the skeleton, which popped up with the information, Colin immediately discerned his identity.
“An employee of the company?”
Colin looked from the skeleton to the bodies hanging overhead, frowning:
“How could an employee end up dead here?”

chapters.title: Chapter 737 - 737 529 Super Antique Employee._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 737: Chapter 529: Super Antique “Employee”._1 Chapter 737: Chapter 529: Super Antique “Employee”._1 “Hmm, doesn’t seem like anything major…”
“It feels like if the employees of the company go out on a trip, they’re bound to find a few bodies without any accidents, dead in every corner of the universe…”
“If this task wasn’t about delivering a package, I would have thought we were going to recover some limbs again. But speaking of which, what’s the situation with this old guy? His way of dying seems kind of… odd.”
As thoughts flashed through his mind, Colin had become accustomed to encountering the corpses of employees upon stepping outside.
He stood in front of the body and examined the old guy’s corpse, noticing that there were quite a few air roots penetrated into his skin…
Then, he looked up at the thousands of bodies on the giant crooked neck tree, each wrapped in air roots like a cocoon.
His first impression was as if he was using this strange tree to draw nutrients from the bodies to heal itself.
But his intuition told him that wasn’t quite it…
At this moment, the Little Maid suddenly made a sound, “The age of this corpse is at least over a hundred years, with the ultimate cause of death being organ failure induced by fatal injuries…”
Ignoring the latter part of what the Little Maid said, Colin listened to the first part and couldn’t help furrowing his brows, “Over a hundred years… Are you sure?”
“The specific year is uncertain, but he has been here for at least more than a hundred years,” the Little Maid affirmed again.
Over a hundred years ago…
Colin squatted down, his brow deeply furrowed. He knew that a hundred years earlier on this timeline, there was no such thing as the “Bonfire Company.”
So could this be “the previous batch”?
Combining the information he had with official content and discussions among some employees of the company, Colin had long felt that this world might have gone through a reset, and that the reset was incomplete.
That’s why there were all kinds of strange places.
Only this could explain how these “modern people of the twenty-first century” who had died a hundred or even several hundreds of years ago came to be.
However, it was precisely when Colin was staring at the corpse and examining it that he suddenly felt a surge of information from the company, like data in his mind that wouldn’t stop…
It seemed as if he was receiving some information from the corpse itself.
“Is this, decoding?”
Colin inexplicably felt like he was computing an exceptionally complex problem.
But as puzzled as he was, he didn’t shift his gaze and kept staring in cooperation.
About a minute later, everything stopped.
[Information reception and decoding complete, the following is the content left by the former company employee──]
“Current investigation results can confirm that ‘Little Food Manor’s’ generationally worshiped ‘Green-faced Kitchen God’ has an unusually close relationship with ‘The Eater,’ suspected to be one of the sources of turmoil, but it is uncertain whether it is a part of it or some kind of religious follower…”
“What’s certain is that ‘The Eater’ had appeared here and later left from this place, destination unknown.”
“Everyone in Little Food Manor went completely insane after Its appearance, without exception. If they were allowed to go out, they would certainly attract the attention of other calamities, so I have resolved them…”
“Additionally, in the original worship area of the ‘Green-faced Kitchen God,’ there exists a source of contamination, with some prohibitions on top. Although it will not erupt in the short term, in the long run… it still needs to be resolved.”
“Of course, if it is people who have fled here, and they truly don’t have any extra strength, they can ignore it…”
“Most areas here are safe, but not suitable for long-term hiding because it is impossible to grow food, and some weak sources of contamination that induce hunger, so it’s best to find a way to leave within a year…”
“I hope that one day, you can successfully leave and see the sun rise as usual again…”
“…”
“Leftover information…”
After quickly going through the information in his mind, Colin immediately extracted a few keywords.
“Green-faced Kitchen God,” “The Eater,” “turmoil”…
These words made Colin realize that the corpse in front of him might be that of a very early employee, really early, the kind from a long time ago…
He had a premonition that this turmoil was probably the “Black Turmoil” once experienced by humanity, as mentioned by Big C Teacher.
And judging from the content left by this former company employee, the turmoil seemed to be ongoing during his active period, not yet over, and the future remained unknown…
“Hiss, this corpse, really an antique here.”
Colin took a deep breath of cold air and then pondered the meanings of some other words.
“Green-faced Kitchen God,” he had no idea about the situation, but the “The Glutton” Buddha statue was greenish-black. Moreover, the word “The Eater” went without saying—if you just add a “Big” in front of it, it becomes the famous “0-09 ‘Hunger,'” feared by all demons and Outer Gods…
“Speaking of which, it seems that ‘The Eaters’ of this period might not have reached this level? And they haven’t been fully contained and rehabilitated by the company yet, still in a fugitive state? No, a wild state?”
Colin thought thoughtfully, knowing that if it had already been contained, the employees generally referred to it by its code number.
And not by some revered godly title…
This form of address hardly aligned with the company’s prevailing value system that placed humanity above all else.
‘That confidence in dealing with high-level Containment Subjects must have been forged during this calamity…’
With these thoughts flashing through his mind, Colin didn’t continue to investigate; after all, these events were in the past. While they satisfied some of his curiosity, they weren’t of much use to him.
The most critical thing was there wasn’t much mention of “The Source of Pollution” by this employee.
However, having learned there was a certain relation to “Hunger,” Colin couldn’t help but feel a bit relieved…
Lucky he hadn’t asked Yukionna to deal with it directly.
Otherwise, if a real issue arose, with the involvement of a “0” level entity, he might not be able to ensure its safety.
Then, Colin looked at the corpse in front of him, unsure how to proceed…
By his custom, given the choice, he’d definitely plan to eliminate all external threats first and then move inward step by step.
This naturally included the corpse before him…
But such an antique, it seemed a shame to simply burn it.
Perhaps it might yield some key information later on?
Just then, a task suddenly popped up…
[Temporary Event: Recover the remains of a former company D+ level employee.]
…
“D+ level employee? The rank is not so low…”
Colin murmured, pulled out a disposable glove from his pocket and put it on, then touched the corpse following the task’s direction, and instantly, some kind of guidance indicated completion.
An invisible whirl appeared, sucking the body and its broken artifacts lying beside it inside.
Task completed.
As Colin was taking off the disposable glove and getting up, he suddenly heard “crack, crack” sounds coming from above in the air.
He raised his head to see that thousands of bodies, once hung up by D+ employees using tree roots, were starting to shake on the crooked trees.
From beneath the roots came the crackling sounds of chewing…
It was like a mouth gnawing at something or a chrysalis about to break open.
Something was about to emerge!
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 738 - 738 530 Task 15.1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 738: Chapter 530: Task 15.1 Chapter 738: Chapter 530: Task 15.1 “Is this because his corpse was taken away, so some kind of balance was broken, and it started coming back to life?”
Colin stood up, his eyes on the things above his head.
It was at this moment that a larger “cocoon” cracked open, its shell made of tree roots, followed by a stream of blurred humanoid smoke that burst out quickly and attacked him.
Without any courtesy, he waved his hand and conjured a thick wave of flames.
As he had expected, just this one move should have been enough to severely damage that thoroughly contaminated humanoid monster…
But to his surprise, the smoke didn’t disperse when it met the flames; instead, it let out a scream.
Immediately after, a figure was forced out from the smoky state, its head and limbs were shrunken, but its belly was hugely swollen, and there was a large vertical mouth on its stomach, starting from the belly button and split open…
This mouth sucked in violently and actually devoured some of the bonfire.
Moreover, the commotion of the battle seemed to have triggered more “cocoons,” as the sound of cracking echoed one after another.
More and more figures rushed out, actually swallowing up the ball of fire he had conjured with a wave of his hand!
“Although the power form is a bit raw, it is indeed ‘Hunger’…”
Colin sighed inwardly at this scene, then unreservedly summoned a surge of frightening flames, engulfing the crooked tree, along with all the contaminated ones that had detached and those still attached…
At first, these non-human creatures with shriveled limbs and enormous bellies could swallow some of the flames through the mouths on their stomachs.
Even a few strong individuals, after consuming the flames, also gained some ability to control them, their bodies surrounded by swirling flames, resembling the bizarre creatures from The Classic of Mountains and Seas…
Though it wasn’t “Primordial Fire” but rather the characteristics of “Wildfire,” it was still shocking.
But as the flames continued to intensify, surpassing their threshold, one after another, they collapsed to the ground under the scorching fire, oozing grease, turning into charred remains, and eventually turning to ash…
Colin kept his gaze on the ashes without stopping, continuing to burn until even the ashes were consumed down to more primitive particles.
“Overall, this thing is definitely not as it was, but even so, it has about the strength of a Third Level Containment Subject, and due to the trait of ‘Hunger,’ once it feasts for a while, consuming some things, it can continue to grow…”
“If one weren’t several levels stronger, it would not be easy to handle.”
Colin gave a simple evaluation.
He had wanted to keep one for observation, but realizing that this thing’s hunger was stirring something deep within him, he chose to thoroughly burn it clean to avoid accidents.
Moreover, after clashing with these creatures, he felt that this D+ level employee had quite good strength indeed, capable of investigating alone and dealing with the incident on the spot. Despite the close brush with mutual destruction, the foundation of his strength was clearly solid…
At least compared to the current employees on the Earth side of the company, not a single one was confident they could solve it alone.
Even if a D Level team were sent over, if they weren’t well-prepared, the likelihood of failure was not small.
“Ah, the good news is, the D levels from Earth don’t seem weaker than those from outside, but the bad news is they’re all from the past.”
Shaking his head and collecting his thoughts, Colin observed his surroundings for a while, confirming there were no similar anomalies before beginning to lay on buffs for himself.
After a dozen minutes or so, Colin, wreathed in flames, pointed towards the sky. A fireball gathered at his fingertips and swiftly shot up into the sky, suspended in this world and radiating in all directions, illuminating this misty, dimly hidden world with light.
Under the flame perception, the area here was neither very large nor very small but spanned at least ten thousand acres, mostly covered by forest. The trees looked sickly, and aside from plants, there wasn’t a single live animal.
Even the chirping of insects was coming from the outside world…
“Since there wasn’t really anything alive to begin with, might as well be a bit more thorough…”
Colin glanced at the limp trees and felt that even alive, they seemed quite weary…
At once, he closed his five fingers into a fist, and the fireball in the sky exploded into dozens of pieces, trailing long tails of fire, plummeting towards the surrounding area.
The sounds of huge impacts came from all directions…
In less than fifteen minutes, firelight lit up the entire world, tree after tree twisting and burning in the flames, thick smoke gathering at the sky’s dome, forming dark red, magma-like flowing clouds of fire smoke.
The whole small world-like independent space was set aflame!
In the fiercely burning flames, faint, inhuman screams mixed in. Those seemed to be the howls of some aberrations.
But those howls did not last long and were consumed by the deep red, leaving only the whoosh of flames.
And at this moment, all of the original eerie and bizarre atmosphere was completely burned away.
“Good, good, good, the air is much sweeter now…”
Colin took a deep breath, feeling much more cheerful.
No, to be more precise, as the sky filled with flames, Colin felt that this small world was transforming into his domain, everything within it under his control.
This feeling was very strange and comforting.
However, a world completely covered in fire and smoke was not so comfortable for beings like “Yukionna.”
So, she hid herself well inside her ring…
And after the flames had sufficiently taken hold, Colin’s figure melded into the flames, and in the next second, several kilometers away, in front of the burnt-down ancestral hall, wisps of bonfire swirled and converged, forming his figure.

chapters.title: Chapter 739 - 739 530 The 15th Loop Task ._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 739: Chapter 530: The 15th Loop Task ._2 Chapter 739: Chapter 530: The 15th Loop Task ._2 When his silhouette became solid, Colin looked around to make sure there was nothing strange in this fire-red world. Then, holding his revolver, he walked step by step to the edge of an empty well behind the ancestral temple and peered into it.
“It seems there’s no water…”
Colin’s finger flickered, and a large amount of flame, obedient like an extension of his limb, poured into the well. Through these flames, which felt like his own tentacles, he quickly discovered a spiral staircase leading downward about fifty meters, ending in a bluestone passage.
The passage was clearly man-made, cut into the rock. As he moved deeper, he could see a hall filled with ancient pots, jars, and some steles and inscriptions displayed around…
If not for the flames filling it up, completely illuminating the interior, it would have been rather cramped and oppressive.
“Is it an ancient tomb?”
Colin had a hunch, feeling that the style of this tomb seemed quite old, possibly from the Tang Dynasty?
In any case, the style was quite different from above; it was likely not built by “Little Food Manor”.
However, not paying much attention to this, Colin controlled the flames to cover all places. While permeating continuously, he quickly got a clear picture of the specific situation of the underground area…
Soon, deep within, he saw a brass door that had endured an unknown number of years.
The brass door stood eight meters tall, constructed entirely of pure copper, engraved with profound and incomprehensible patterns that, in the light of the flames, reflected a dull glimmer.
With a thought, Colin once again performed a Flame Leap, materializing ten meters away from the large door.
Immediately, his gaze fell on the slightly ajar brass door which exuded a sense of heaviness. The door, nearly half a meter thick, was open about the width of two fists, with a hazy grey behind the gap…
“Gurgle.”
Colin couldn’t help but swallow, not knowing why, but he felt a strong desire to enter.
So fragrant… so delicious…
He always felt that there might be something tasty inside?
“Could it be ‘Hunger’s’ collection of ‘snacks’ from back then?”
Colin murmured to himself, took a deep breath, and suppressed the sudden urge that had sprung up.
But since he was targeted by “Lady Bunny” and specifically instructed to toss a hand inside, it’s safe to say that behind that door, things probably aren’t as peaceful as they look from the outside…
Although he was curious about what was inside, it was clear that entering was not an option.
Under these circumstances, to find out what was inside, he either had to send fire into it or use the “Book of Fate: Fragment”…
“Whichever I choose, either would guarantee an accident, and certainly a very tricky one.”
Colin hardly thought about it before he outright gave up the idea.
After all, “Lady Bunny” hadn’t asked him to go inside to check, and one characteristic of her missions was that they were fine until an accident happened, and if it did, it would become particularly troublesome.
Afterward, he withdrew his gaze from peering inside and, without hurry to throw the hand in, he took a second look at the brass door.
“The purity seems quite high. In normal history, even the recent few dynasties, casting such a thing would be difficult.”
Colin raised his head and scanned the door from top to bottom. The door could be said to be genuinely antique, and its age far surpassed that of the sacrificial offerings inside the tomb by many times.
But the problem was, the solid doorjambs about a meter beside the door were not something ancient people could easily make.
To create those, it seemed that Extraordinary Power must have been involved…
Looking at it this way, the appearance of extraordinary abilities might have to be dated back by several hundred years more than previously thought.
Colin pondered for a moment but did not dwell on it too much, for the oddities of the ancient past were more serious than those of the “previous generation’s” lost era…
It reached the point where they were known only by name but not in detail.
“It must have been rectified by the ‘Bonfire Company’ at some point. If time truly restarted again, then during the last rise of the Bonfire Company, the first unfortunate ones were probably the immortals and gods on Earth, as well as whatever buddhas and gods from outside…”
Colin felt that this was probably not far off from the company’s modus operandi.
Thinking this, he shook his head, took out the “Token” from his pocket, and threw it towards the gap in the door from a distance.
The light of the flames flickered and fell behind the door.
Immediately afterward, some horrific entity was awakened by this action, seemingly not expecting that upon waking from its years of slumber, it would set eyes on such a treasure, letting out a howl unbearable to mortals.
In Colin’s mind, vague abstract images came through, which, if translated into reality, would be like a person sleeping soundly suddenly feeling a disturbance and upon opening their eyes, seeing a swarm of roaches crawling all over, then frantically getting up and “going mad.”
The terrifying vibration kept attacking the thick brass door…
The breath that penetrated the grey-white haze twisted the sounds, sights, and the very space here.
With a “bang”,
Colin stepped forward, placing a foot on the door, leaning forward with his muscles tensed, and forced the door shut with one kick.
Suddenly, the scene fell silent.
And the vibration behind the door, from its initial intensity, gradually weakened after thirty or so seconds…
Soon, all the anomalies had disappeared.
“Struggled for fifty-one seconds, the longest struggle to date,”
Colin muttered to himself, the previously very loud “South Sea Bodhisattva” was just loud in its cries; in reality, it barely lasted twenty seconds before rolling its eyes back.
And many others didn’t last even ten seconds.
The way here was actually so quiet, I thought it was a minor affair, but it managed to howl for just over fifty seconds before quieting down.
It just goes to show, the dogs that bite really don’t bark…
At the same time, the words “Task Completed” popped up.
Colin didn’t hurry back. Instead, he reappeared outside the clan temple, watching a little world burning fiercely. With a wave of his hand and a call to arms, flames from all directions began to converge here…
In about ten minutes or so, the firelight gathered here to form an enormous fireball.
“Request to establish a ‘Bonfire point’…”
Colin sent out his request, exercising the authority granted in the “Outstanding Talent Plan.” He couldn’t establish a “Bonfire point” with special features, but a general one was still possible.
It was just that it wasn’t needed before, so it hadn’t been dealt with.
Now I feel, this place could be remodeled a bit…
Before long, the giant fireball began to shrink bit by bit, turning into a ten-meter-tall but incredibly bright Level 1 Bonfire.
“Looks good but not very useful; can’t even reach Level 2…”
He complained, but a Level 1 Bonfire was already sufficient. Whenever Colin needed, he could sense and monitor this place from any region on Earth, and use the special channel within the Bonfire to leap quickly to this location…
After confirming this, Colin didn’t linger; he went back home directly through the prompt provided upon task completion.
…
Upon opening my eyes, it’s the familiar ceiling again.
Colin shook his head and sat up, looking at the parchment, the Eighth Ring’s delivery task popped up.
“The transitions are really seamless, they didn’t waste a second; the ‘Flextime System’ is just amazing…”
Colin shook his head. After staying at home for a while, he became a numb task worker and began preparing for the next event.
Time flew by quickly amid the “monotonous yet thrilling” cycle of delivery tasks…
In the blink of an eye, more than twenty days had gone by.
A weary Colin was almost finished with this lengthy series of fifteen delivery tasks…
At the moment, aboard the “Train in the Fog” for six stops, he arrived at a broken world with disordered gravity. After creating havoc, expelling an incarnation of an Outer God, and freeing a large group of enslaved silicon-based humans, Colin completed the fourteenth ring task by dropping the “Token.”
“In the company’s eyes, as long as you consider yourself human, then you really are human…”
Colin looked at a crowd of unknown brown Crystal Stones forming a roughly human shape—Stone People—and reflected.
The fact that fishmen counted as people was one thing…
But that a bunch of Stone People could also be considered human was unexpected to him.
Shaking his head and gathering his scattered thoughts, he returned to the Earthly world amidst the kowtows and worship of the Stone People.
“Finally, the last task…”
Colin sat up and widened his eyes, feeling a mix of anticipation and nervousness, rubbing his hands as he murmured prayers for an untroublesome task, while opening the parchment to look at the final event.
When he saw the name of the task slowly emerging on the yellowed paper surface, his heart skipped a beat…
[Event: Go to the “Nonexistent Hospital”…]
.
.
.
ps: Updating first then editing.
The day before yesterday, it suddenly dropped from above 20 degrees to 2°C, and I caught a cold, feeling a bit under the weather…. I’ll take a leave tomorrow, and everyone also take care to stay warm.

chapters.title: Chapter 740 - 740 531 The Nonexistent Hospital Incident. _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 740: Chapter 531: The “Nonexistent Hospital” Incident. _1 Chapter 740: Chapter 531: The “Nonexistent Hospital” Incident. _1 “I never thought the fifteenth ring would actually be going to this godforsaken place…”
Colin was stunned for a moment.
This location’s name was all too familiar to him and the company’s employees, after all, there was a Brother there calling for help every day.
It had been almost a year of calling for help, yet no one had died, no one had gone mad, but the calls for help continued…
In a sense, this Brother had become something of a legend, similar to the “Stupid Robot”.
Of course, unlike the “Stupid Robot”, this Brother still had some logic in communication.
He might be sending out distress signals non-stop, but he also chatted with people on some fun forums.
The thing Colin saw most was that the other party would often tag him and say he wanted to go to “Descent Project-13” and work in the Other World.
What’s strange is that Colin had indeed tried to send a mission to the other party during his last expansion, curious to see if he could pull this guy out. The mission had been sent, but it seemed to have been rejected.
“He’s shouting to get out in the forum, but the missions seem to be rejected when sent, he says he hasn’t seen them when asked, telling us to send more… What’s going on…”
Colin sat up straight in bed, his face filled with confusion, feeling that this situation was even more special than he had imagined.
“Forget it, I’ll ignore him for now. The mission this time is probably not about rescuing him…”
“Thinking too much about him is simply a waste of brain cells. I’ll help him out if I can on the way; if not, then so be it.”
“Moreover, this last mission is also quite special; it’s not the same as the previous fifteen, which were about delivering messages, but rather… an investigation?”
Colin gathered his wandering thoughts about that employee and looked down at the mission content that had fully emerged.
[Event: Proceed to the “Nonexistent Hospital” for the relevant work.]
“Mission Description”: A special medical facility, wandering within are a large number of broken abnormal things, but the relevant documents have been lost and need to be reinvestigated…
“Mission Requirements”: On 28th February, head to the designated deep sea area with two selected assisting employees, wait for the train, get off at the third station, enter the facility, and descend beyond the ninth level for an in-depth investigation of the locale.
“Note 1”: The difficulty lies in how to enter the next level, please pay attention to some of the rules and signals in the lobby.
“Note 2”: After arriving at the target area, please leave “Bonfire Coordinate Points” on each level if possible.
…
“This, the content of the mission seems to involve more than one ring…”
Colin estimated that more content would appear after the investigation was complete.
Moreover, this was the first of the fifteen-ring missions that did not immediately require him to deliver a message up front.
And the mission was a multiplayer type…
“Leaving Bonfire Points should be for signal stability…”
“Rules and signals, I’ll have to see them on-site…”
“Also, this time I can actually select two assisting employees to join me? Hiss…”
Colin swallowed, feeling the gravity of the mission. In all those previous tasks, though employees occasionally participated, they were more like tangent lines alongside other tasks.
This time, being able to select his own team was clearly different…
After some thought, Colin opened communication with “Life Mentor Adorable” on the parchment, eager to know how much this know-it-all was aware of the situation.
If he wasn’t mistaken, he remembered hearing that some employees had tried to rescue, but they only made it a few levels deep before they couldn’t return…
“It seems quite a few employees have gone…” Since he had not thought about doing this Hellish task before, Colin hadn’t paid much attention, but now he was ready to learn more about it.
Shortly after the message was sent, “Life Mentor Adorable” responded.
“Boss, you haven’t rolled into a related mission, have you?”
Kawaii-many asked anxiously, following Brother Shunzi’s usual pattern; if it wasn’t for a related mission, he would typically just inquire to satisfy his curiosity…
And this matter seemed to have been discussed a long time ago, so it was unlikely to pique his curiosity again.
Suddenly asking like this meant it was relevant to the mission.
As expected, right after sending the message, he immediately received a response from Brother Shunzi, confirming this.
Seeing this, “Life Mentor Adorable” was speechless for a moment. Brother Shunzi, climbing his way up in the company, seemed to encounter half of the difficult tasks…
But complaints aside, his mind quickly sifted through relevant information about the mission and searched through a drawer full of paper documents, preparing to send the information to Brother Shunzi.
“This mission seems to have been accepted by others before, but there are no clear records; it’s unclear. It first became widely known through ‘The Unyielding.’ According to him, while performing a dangerous task at E level, he had to rely on ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’ to break the situation…”
“At that time, he managed to return safely thanks to the power of the ‘Book of Fate,’ but due to the misfortune associated with three ‘Book of Fate’ fragments, he accidentally accepted a task and somehow, during its execution, ended up in the ‘Nonexistent Hospital’… Of course, we’re not exactly clear on the specifics of his ‘accident,’ and he cannot explain it either.”
It sounded like someone had a bulb stuck up their rear, and the doctor’s inquiring led to an ‘accidental’ admission… Colin pursed his lips, his first instinct was that the lad wasn’t telling the whole truth.
But on second thought, such a story might fool oneself but not others.
If “Life Mentor Adorable” didn’t question it, it was quite likely that the other party really didn’t know.

chapters.title: Chapter 741 - 741 531 The Nonexistent Hospital Incident. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 741: Chapter 531: The “Nonexistent Hospital” Incident. _2 Chapter 741: Chapter 531: The “Nonexistent Hospital” Incident. _2 Moreover, “The Unyielding” not to mention his current situation, just by looking at how he shook off “misfortune” in a single day and ultimately overcame it, shows that his strength is quite formidable.
“At the earliest, ‘The Unyielding’ wasn’t trapped on the eighteenth level, but on the thirteenth. At that time, he promised some points and item rewards that seemed very tempting back then, in exchange for asking for help…”
Having said this, “Life Mentor Adorable” paused for a moment, secretly thankful for Brother Shunzi’s assistance. Without the big brother “cheating” to lead the way, by now, everyone would still be desperately poor…
After all, back then, over a thousand points and some item rewards, even in the eyes of D Level staff, were very coveted…
Then, he quickly composed a response while glancing at the arranged files next to him.
“I’m not sure exactly how many employees headed there, but as far as I know, those who did were a small team made up of four D Level Personnel. According to them, they eventually reached the seventh or eighth level before they had no choice but to withdraw…”
“Only made it to the seventh or eighth level? That’s it?” Colin sent a message back, surprised.
Four D Level, at least they should make it through ten or eleven levels, right?
After a pause, Colin added another message asking, “What’s their strength like?”
“I’m familiar with two of them, they’re probably a bit weaker than me before I was trained by Big C Teacher, but not by much. I’m not clear about the other two, of course, I can easily take on all four of them now…”
After Big C Teacher’s rigorous training, the overall on-the-spot combat level of the employees has increased significantly. If they were brass before, now they were silver or gold, a far cry from the past.
Seeing the analogy made by Kawaii-many, Colin stroked his chin, feeling that the mission would at least not be especially dangerous before the eighth level…
“By the way, can you still get in touch with those four employees who went there? Help me contact two of them…” Colin wanted to grab a couple of people to accompany him.
Having a friend familiar with the path would obviously make the journey easier.
“I can contact one, but two might be difficult…”
Before Colin could ask why, Adorable quickly explained, “When those four reached the seventh level, an accident happened, and they ran into some troublesome things, so the team got scattered. Two are missing and their fate is unknown, and two made it back…”
“But of the two who returned, one died recently due to an accident on a mission.
“So I can only contact one, and because of psychological trauma, he may not be willing to go. If it’s really necessary, I can try talking to him in a bit and ask…”
They actually died…
Colin was taken aback for a moment. During his missions, he seldom saw squad employees die and had almost forgotten about the company’s high fatality rate.
Looking at Kawaii-many’s last reply and thinking it over, Colin was about to respond when he noticed his responses in the chat group were nearing the limit.
Any more messages might bring some inexplicable danger…
‘Not sure why chatting with ‘Lady Rabbit’ would put on this kind of restriction.’
As the thought flickered, Colin didn’t pay it much mind. He closed his eyes and sank into the majesty of the “office” adorned with a great fireball, summoning Adorable down.
This way, there were no more posting restrictions…
As the figure appeared, Colin sat at a side seat, tapping the desk and said directly, “Talk to that person, and if anyone else has been in there, that’s fine too…”
“Okay.”
Sitting in the high-backed chair, “Life Mentor Adorable,” used to Brother Shunzi’s behavior of chatting online and suddenly pulling people offline, nodded at his request.
“Besides these four employees, some other employees also went there. I’m not quite clear on their situation, but if needed, I can try to contact them as well.”
“Life Mentor Adorable” was fully taking the initiative.
Having worked with Brother Shunzi for so long, he noticed that Shunzi usually didn’t post much on parchment… He thought it was just discomfort at first, but now it seems there could be other reasons.
As to what those reasons might be… he didn’t know, and didn’t really want to delve into it. Sometimes, knowing too much wasn’t good for you.
“Alright, then you go and inquire. It would be best to get a reply before the day after tomorrow.” Colin nodded.
The fact that this event was ranked on the Fifteenth Ring just went to show its particularity. It might not be very difficult, but it was probably complex. Better to prepare more before taking action.
Otherwise, if a real issue came up, there wouldn’t even be a chance to prepare.
Before long, after exchanging messages for a while, Colin returned to reality. It was only then that he had the chance to check the time.
“It’s the 26th today, the action starts the day after tomorrow. Time-wise, it’s still okay, and there’s ample time to prepare the supplies…”
Colin took out his phone and contacted Xu Duojin, requesting that he find some fuel of sufficient quality…
Otherwise, it would be quite embarrassing to run out of materials at the Bonfire Sacrificial Site when the time came.
“No problem, I’ll get it to you before the day after tomorrow,” Xu Duojin replied quickly.
After giving these instructions, Colin shut off his phone. Without further words, he opened the Trading Path and began to scan for some items.
In this past half-month, although the mission had not yet been settled, Colin’s points were almost depleted.
However, with the efforts of him and Shana in the previous period, the “Light” faith had established a fairly large trade with them, which somewhat alleviated the situation.
They sold gold-made BUFFs through Colin, and in return, this side provided some knowledge, scientific technology, and even special Containment Subjects…
Colin, acting as a middleman, could easily earn tens of thousands of points with each transaction.
Though this wasn’t particularly a large sum, it was enough to get by…
Moreover, Shana also benefited, becoming a genuinely wealthy lady, holding a significant number of points.
“Seems like she doesn’t really use this stuff much…”
Colin rubbed his chin. He had asked her before; the only things Shana could spend her points on were either buying some expensive special effects or repairing some of the company’s tools she frequently used.
The former she felt was not very useful, and the latter seemed too costly.
And compared to tools, she preferred using the “powers” of her seniors, as well as her own fists.
Therefore, aside from the necessary expenses to maintain her territory, Shana preferred to hoard her points for a time when there might be an emergency.
Of course, most of those points were held by Colin.
“She’s almost like a hamster hoarding for winter…”
Colin glanced at the over sixty thousand points that belonged to Shana and thought he could understand her choice. After all, with the significant lack and frugality at the “branch office,” Shana indeed had been scrimping and saving all along.
As for the “exposed” branch office…
Apart from no one doing the missions, things remained as they were, with an air of a dead pig not fearing scalding water.
Afterward, without further speculation on this matter, Colin began to look for some special tools to prepare for the mission…
During his missions in this period, he found that some white or green tools could be directly ignited by the “Flame Bearer’s” power in a way that would release a one-time burst of strength many times, even tens of times, greater than their own normal potency!
When he was liberating the group of silicon-based humans last time, Colin blew up three tools in succession, playing a vital role in driving back the incarnation of the Evil God, using them for a satisfyingly explosive effect.
The only downside, apart from the high cost of use, was that it wasn’t too friendly to the anomalies being made into tools.
But it wasn’t a big issue; to complete the mission, enduring a bit of suffering would probably not provoke too many complaints from them…
After a while of picking and choosing, Colin spent over five thousand points and bought three green tools that could explode, of both attack and defense types.
Then, time continued until the evening…
“Life Mentor Adorable” sent a message first:
“Things are going quite smoothly. I found an employee who has been there and is one of the members of our Incarnation Project. He is willing to cooperate, but there’s another D Level who, though he agrees, is asking for some reward…”
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 742 - 742 532
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 742: 532 Chapter 742: 532 “Five Thousand Points, plus a certain guarantee of safety, and he’s willing to make the trip…”
“But after talking with him for a while, I got the Points reduced. Now we only need Three Thousand Points, and what he values most is the ability to return. As long as there’s a reasonable guarantee of safety, I think that shouldn’t be a big problem for you, Brother Shunzi…”
“Additionally, his reason for wanting to go is to understand what happened to his former teammates and all that…”
“The reason I’m vying for him is that I’ve found they are the deepest explorers we can find currently. Our own team only made it to the sixth level, and it seems we can’t find the way to the levels beyond.”
Kě’ài duō’s messages came one after another, roughly outlining the reasons.
“Three Thousand Points as payment? That’s also acceptable…”
Colin had no objections since it was a highly risky, life-threatening task, and being able to lead all the way to the eighth level was considered decent.
Then, he asked another of his subordinates what their requirements were…
Kě’ài duō quickly replied that this person didn’t ask for Points, even suggesting they could do it without any payment.
Naturally, if there was a choice, they hoped to receive an appropriate ‘Bonfire’ Golden Mark or ‘Light’ Golden Mark either would do…
As for safety, there were no inquiries, as this group of employees, who had followed him for two or three months, were well aware of his nature and understood his strength, having a higher degree of trust in him.
After all, if Brother Shunzi couldn’t solve it, then any further assurances would be meaningless…
“Speaking of which, the Golden Mark somehow feels less worthwhile than just giving Three Thousand Points.”
A powerful enough Golden Mark, in Colin’s view, was definitely worth more than Three Thousand Points.
And crafting those things was quite troublesome…
He wasn’t particularly adept at it and usually needed a few hours to make one.
As for those specially crafted by Shana…
“I don’t even have enough for myself, how could I give them away? Forget it, I’ll find some time, spend two hours, and make a decent one.”
After thinking it over, Colin decided to craft one for the other party himself.
His own marks would be icing on the cake for him, but Shana’s marks, when used by him, meant a synergy of two kinds of powers and an explosive effect greater than the sum of the parts.
Without further thought, he let Kě’ài duō take over and agreed to the other party’s demand, and it took less than ten seconds for Colin to receive a private chat request from a stranger.
It was an employee named “Innate Ashen Holy Body.”
“Kě’ài duō said the matter has been settled, and he asked me to add you. It’s our first collaboration; I hope it goes smoothly. After everything is done, you can give me the Points…” Innate Ashen Holy Body greeted.
The main content had already been discussed with Kě’ài duō previously, and this request was just for confirmation.
“No problem, during this time I might ask Kě’ài duō to pass on some questions to you, and moreover, when it’s time, I’ll remind you to come for the mission, which will likely be the day after tomorrow at around nine in the morning. Until then, do some preparation on your own.”
Colin gave a simple response to “Ashen Holy Body,” and after taking some time to make the mark, he dove into the spatial office and pulled the other employee down.
“It’s all Orange Cat’s fault.”
This employee, Colin had some recollection of; if he was not mistaken, apart from the weekly “The Descent Project,” they had previously been on a mission in the “Thorn Lady” world together, and the individual was rather competent.
However, that time, the other party served as a signal booster; this time…
‘Yeah, seems almost the same, likely doing what we did last time, if nothing unexpected comes up.’
As these thoughts flashed through his mind, Colin shook his head slightly, gathering his thoughts before inquiring with the pulled-down employee about some specifics concerning the “non-existent hospital.”
He needed to know, at a minimum, what sort of monsters were inside…
However, a few minutes later, Colin furrowed his brow, as this inquiry had not yielded any valuable information.
“Hiss, it seems like after coming out, the related memories are somewhat vague. When I think about it carefully, it feels like experiences are as hazy as dreams, and I can’t remember the details, just a rough idea that there is a bunch of troublesome stuff inside…”
Orange Cat spoke and, noticing something off with Brother Shunzi’s post-battle aura, paused before adding: “Of course, I have a premonition that once I’m on the scene and see things, I’ll immediately recall some of the keys I encountered before.”
“Alright then.”
Colin waved his hand dismissively, guessing that “Innate Ashen Holy Body” was probably in a similar situation, able to remember only the gist of things.
It seemed that Bonfire Company had implemented some protective measures…
“By the way, one thing I do remember is that while the enemies over there are a nuisance, the real trouble is how to get to the next floor. It’s not as simple as just taking the stairs to reach the next level. I have an impression that finding the entrance to the hospital itself took a very long time during the last mission…” Orange Cat tried to describe as much as they could from their impressions.
The details were no longer clear, only the impressions remained…
‘Hard to even find the door, huh? But the door should not be a big issue since many people have already gone in. Moreover, the mission does indeed mention that the difficulty lies in how to get to the next level, not the anomalies.’
Colin recalled “Remark 2” of this mission, which had one more point than what Orange Cat mentioned, advising him to pay attention to the main hall.
‘Why does each one not seem reliable…’ he wondered.
After asking a few more questions without much hope, he directly concluded the brief meeting.

chapters.title: Chapter 743 - 743 532
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 743: 532 Chapter 743: 532 The situation in reality was just as he had imagined; the Ashen Holy Body and the Orange Cat were in a similar state, though the former had a deeper impression, mentioning some undying anomaly, “Be careful. Doctor,” “Don’t respond to it,” and the like.
But that was about it.
Tries as he might, it was like his memory had been veiled, and he simply couldn’t recall any specific details.
“The only person left not found must be ‘The Unyielding’…”
Colin opened the parchment and glanced over it, noticing that this old guy had recently posted a few sentences in a “stupid chat room” for amusement…
Then, almost as if clocking in, he @’ed Colin’s internal employee account name about a dozen minutes later: “@654321, I beg you, I can’t take it much longer, Brother Shunzi, just come and rescue me, and I’ll be yours forever, plus I have information on orange-grade gear, and tens of thousands of points…”
Right after he posted this, some people immediately commented.
“Oh, isn’t this Brother Unyielding? Weren’t you just trash-talking me fiercely? You seem to be in high spirits; how can you not hold on…”
“Exactly, just like those old folks scrambling for seats after dancing in the plaza, returning to Brother Shunzi, and then start acting weak?”
“Speaking of which, those points of yours, weren’t they from luring people in and then upping the ante to scam them?”
“Hahaha, don’t joke around, one of these days Brother Unyielding will transform into an anomaly and sneak right into your bed on the first day…”
“…”
Facing these slanderous remarks, “The Unyielding” naturally retorted, saying things like “Impossible, it’s all my own efforts,” “Just took the occasional opportunity to do some minor tasks,” “I’ve never tricked anyone,” and so on.
However, Colin couldn’t help thinking that this matter of transforming into an anomaly one day…
It honestly seemed quite uncertain.
He mulled over this while searching, trying to gather as many posts by “The Unyielding” as possible…
Compared to the beginning, Brother Unyielding’s words now seemed a bit slack, as if begging when possible and letting go when not, giving off a strange feeling of helplessness.
“Could this mean that his situation has now stabilized?”
Colin pondered, initially planning to have “Kě’ài duō” communicate with him…
But after thinking it over, he decided not to, given an indescribable unease.
The man’s situation was very complicated. If he knew Colin was coming, it might not be a good thing, and it was previously mentioned that during their mission, the two employees seemed to have come into contact with him, albeit uncertainly…
What startled Colin was that, although one employee had only reached level eight and another level six, both claimed to have had unofficial, private interactions with the “Brother Unyielding” on the eighteenth level…
That was rather eerie.
If that person could go as low as the sixth or eighth level, why would he need rescuing?
“Need to be careful, whether to contact him or not, we’ll see after the investigation is finished. If necessary, we’ll make contact, if not, better not to communicate, at least I can’t let him know in advance that I’m coming.”
Colin pushed down the urge to communicate with the man in his heart.
He also reminded Kě’ài duō not to make unnecessary moves and not to let the other party know even the act of gathering information itself, whether directly or indirectly…
Colin sighed after a few more hours with not much to show for his efforts:
“Seems like that’s about as far as we’re going to get with the information collection…”
After all that researching, it wasn’t that he’d come away with nothing, but neither did it seem he’d found any key information. The biggest impression he got from the whole thing was that this mission, if not delved into too deeply, might just be fine, but once deep involvement began, it was likely to be not much different from dealing with something like the “Out-of-Control Copy.”
And within the “Out-of-Control Copy”, strength was merely a ticket to entry.
Unless one could overwhelm the situation, in these kinds of events, greater strength did not necessarily mean more ease…
“Huh.”
After taking a long breath, Colin looked at the time and began making as much preparation as he could.
…
A day and a half later, on the morning of February 28th, somewhere over the seemingly endless, uninhabited open sea, Colin, shrouded in flame, plunged into the water like a seagull, then slowly began to descend.
After about ten minutes, in the dark depths of the sea, using the light from his own flame, he saw an arching seabed where, besides the dead corals, there were also some dilapidated ancient ruins.
An ominous aura was diffusing from them…
“Seems like the problem isn’t too big.”
Colin quickly landed on the ground as soon as he had confirmed that the surroundings had little effect on him, and it was at that moment, when he felt as if he had crossed some kind of boundary.
It seemed as though he had entered a sealed spatial area…
However, within the glow of the flame, the abnormalities of this region seemed to shrink back, as if instinctively fearing it.
About half an hour passed when Colin suddenly noticed a murky fog beginning to appear in the pitch-black sea around him, quickly growing denser…
Soon after, with the grey fog covering everything, a monotonous, hollow, and piercing sound of a flute echoed from the depths of the fog.
Following closely was a train that rattled on incessantly, “clang clang clang,” heading towards him.
The grey fog did not separate the seawater but merely spread and enveloped everything around, meaning that the train was submerged in the water at the moment. Yet, the immense pressure of the sea thousands of meters below seemed to have no effect on the train at all.
It was as if it didn’t exist, with not even the thin layer of the train windows being crushed.
“This thing… it’s still amazing,” Colin murmured to himself, then after a moment of stupefaction, he found that the train had slowly come to a stop.
“Click.”
The door slid open.
The seawater seemed to be blocked by an invisible force, unable to flow inside.
Seeing this, Colin was not particularly surprised. He didn’t waste time observing and took a few steps towards the entrance of the carriage and stood still. Then, with flames surging in his eyes, he swept his gaze across the interior, sensing a few shadowy figures.
“Please go to the corner and stay there,” he said calmly, politely extending his hand to point to the corner, with flames churning in his eyes.
Under the radiation of the flame, some of the “shadowy figures” sitting down hesitated for two seconds before reluctantly moving towards the bottom left corner of the carriage, under the heat of the flame, and sat down together.
After applying a barrier of flame to prevent them from escaping, Colin finally found a place to sit down.
These things in themselves had no real intelligence, being closer to instinctual. Yet, while being instinctual, they had a slight understanding of human language…
“It’s time to summon people.”
Colin took out the parchment for the current event and sent out the tasks to two employees assisting him…
In a few seconds, the two employees who had been on standby since the early morning immediately accepted the invitation for the “support mission” and appeared directly in the train carriage.
The instant they appeared, the train doors slowly closed, and the train started moving again.
As the train disappeared from the seabed, various strange, starfish-like black creatures began poking their heads out from the ruins, as if trying to ascertain whether the human who gave them an immense sense of oppression had left…
However, as soon as they emerged, they saw a pulsating flame at the original spot.
With a “boom,”
The fierce light of the fire erupted under the deep sea.
The flame, defying all logic, swallowed the area in an instant, purifying all that was unclean.
…
“Not bad, the threat has been removed…”
Colin’s gaze returned from the window, which was now obscured by the grey fog, and turned to look at the two people sitting not far away:
“The mission officially starts now, have either of you recalled anything?”
Both “Orange Cat” and “Innate Ashen Holy Body” looked at each other, shaking their heads. However, “Ashen Holy Body” spoke up first:
“All I remember now is that when we went there, it seemed that we arrived near the location through a ‘support mission’ directly, without taking the train or any other steps…”
“Me too,” Orange Cat nodded in agreement following the same line of thought.
‘Not by train? Could it be that the method ‘Lady Bunny’ provided is the correct way to enter?’
Colin nodded thoughtfully, trusting ‘Lady Rabbit”s arrangements even more.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 744 - 744 533
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 744: 533 Chapter 744: 533 “””
As the conversation went on, time ticked away…
After two uneventful stops, the train arrived at the third station.
Through the gradually dissipating gray fog outside the window, a broken city in ruins unfolded before everyone’s eyes.
Beneath the somewhat dazzling full moon, the city lay destroyed for unknown reasons, with collapsed skyscrapers, fissured earth, and the ferocious cross-sections of exposed rebar and concrete jutting into the air, leaving an impactful shake on one’s emotions.
However, within the cracks of the crumbling walls, brambles and vines were slowly enveloping and devouring this once fierce facade of the past.
If nothing unexpected occurred, perhaps in several thousand or ten thousand years, only a primitive forest would remain here.
“Is this the place?” Colin asked the two people beside him as he looked towards the luminous body in the sky.
It felt almost like a full moon…
But whether it truly was one was hard to say.
“Yes, it is.”
Orange Cat glanced at the celestial body that resembled the moon, as if struck by a thought:
“The light source here is quite magical. After setting in the east, it would rise again from the east; it falls in the west then ascends from the same spot, hopping back and forth like…”“Indeed, when it reaches its highest point in the center, it’s about as bright as an overcast day,” Ashen Holy Body said, nodding.
“Is that so.” Colin nodded, realizing there was a high probability this was a world under the company’s jurisdiction.
The thing in the sky must be artificial.
And this place probably wasn’t particularly far from Earth…
‘It seems that the farther places, not easily reached, would activate the “Descent Protocol,” while the closer ones could be directly accessed by train. Well, this isn’t entirely absolute…’
As thoughts flickered, Colin felt the train come to a stop, so he stood up and walked towards the door.
Just as he reached it, the door opened with a “click.”
A breath of fresh air, tinged with the faint smell of biological waste, hit him full in the face…
After making sure there were no issues, Colin stepped out, followed closely by the two people, leaving the train together.
As they departed, the train door closed with a “snap,” and the train quickly moved away to the sounds of its “clang, clang, clang” whistle.
“There doesn’t seem to be any danger nearby; it’s very quiet and clean…”
Colin conjured a fire to hover above their heads, shielding them from the direct rays of this land’s celestial body.
Sensing his surroundings through the fire’s illumination, he unexpectedly felt an indescribable tranquility.
As if not a hint of pollution existed at all.
However, considering the “nonexistent hospital” and the nature of the “Train in the Fog,” Colin questioned his own thoughts.
But their mission was not to explore this world, but to find the “nonexistent hospital.”
Colin didn’t waste too much time on this aspect. After a quick glance around and discussing with the others, they followed the mission’s guidance and flew across the sky above the ruins.
Numerous startled animals, feeling the deafening vibration in mid-air, frantically burrowed into their nests, quivering in fear…
“The animal life here looks like rabbits, roaches, and the like, nothing particularly strange,” Colin observed, without slowing his pace.
But about half an hour later, the great fireball carrying the three of them through the air came to a halt.
“Why does it feel like we’re not getting any closer to the hospital?” Colin asked, frowning as he looked around, sensing something was amiss.
The mission pointed forward, but no matter which direction they walked, the distance seemed unchanged, neither closer nor farther.
“Actually…”
Ashen Holy Body suddenly spoke behind him, drawing Colin’s glance before continuing, “I remember the hospital is right here…”
“Right here?”
Colin surveyed the surroundings, but aside from the ordinary residential ruins, there was no sign of any hospital.
However, Orange Cat, who had also entered it before, said, “I remember it’s around here too…”
With both people confirming this, Colin couldn’t help but think carefully about the reasons.
“Maybe the hospital is built underground?”
He tried to let the fire seep into the ground of the area. There were many underground structures, such as garages, sewers, and lower-level shopping malls, but still no sign of any hospital.
“Are you sure it’s really here?” Colin withdrew the fire and asked again.
The other two did not answer immediately but frowned and looked around thoughtfully. If their memory served correctly, the hospital should be nearby.
Not hard to find, just a bit peculiar…
“Does this hospital possess some kind of high-level stealth? Is its sense of presence so diminished, or is it some other situation?”
Colin leaped atop a taller concrete and rebar structure, gazing at the surroundings, pondering thoughtfully.
He immediately thought of an encounter with a rogue “Humility Knight” from earlier days, who had used lowering their sense of presence to several times behead him within the pages of the “Book of Fate: Fragment.”
With this in mind, Colin tried to let the flame spread out further.
With his current strength, if he encountered such a tactic again, he could easily break the illusion with “Bonfire.”
However, as minutes passed…
Colin reluctantly gathered the flame back, having gained nothing.
Ashen Holy Body, seeing the fire withdrawn, knew that Brother Shunzi had not been successful in finding it and couldn’t help but say, “Strange, I clearly feel it’s right here, but it’s as if some force is preventing us from discovering it…”
“To be honest, I feel it too, almost as if I can touch it…” Orange Cat even extended a hand to grope in the air.
‘I’ve checked the whole place, how could there be…’
Equally perplexed and feeling a vague chill, Colin remained unsettled.

chapters.title: Chapter 745 - 745 533 The Rules of Conflict Within the
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 745: Chapter 533: The Rules of Conflict Within the Hospital._2 Chapter 745: Chapter 533: The Rules of Conflict Within the Hospital._2 Both employees had a very strong feeling, but he hadn’t discovered anything at all. What was the reason?
Could it be that greater strength led to an inability to see that hospital?
Or perhaps, the feelings of both were entirely imagined, illusory?
“No, that can’t be right, it should be real. Combining the invisible guidance of the mission, ‘the non-existent hospital’ has indeed always pointed nearby. Theoretically speaking, I should be able to see it directly from this distance, yet I feel nothing…”
“If there really is a hospital here, then why is it that only I can’t feel it, while the others can… hmm?”
Suddenly, a flash of inspiration crossed his mind, and Colin abruptly looked in a certain direction.
But as his gaze reached out, there was nothing to see but ruins and vines—as if everything had been an illusion…
His eyes moved around rapidly, pondering the feeling he’d just had, and then he realized something and suddenly closed his eyes: “The hospital should be right here; since both employees are certain of it, there can be no mistake…”
“The hospital is over there, it’s right there, yes, the mission confirms it, it’s definitely right there!”
Just as Colin was murmuring to himself as if in a trance, he suddenly heard the voices of the two employees…
“It’s out! The hospital has appeared! Brother Shunzi, look quick!”
Upon hearing this, Colin held his breath, opened his eyes, and in front of him, a tarred road appeared out of nowhere.
At the end of the tar road, a grey-white medical complex building composed of many departments faded in and out of sight…
At the same time, certain insights kept arising, making Colin understand the reasons.
‘This hospital, it exists if one believes, and ceases to if one doesn’t…’
‘The reason why the two of them always felt it nearby is that they had been there once, probably knew the cause, and believed that it was nearby, but because I didn’t believe, it didn’t appear…’
‘Or rather, if it were just the two of them without me, then it should have appeared, it’s just that my spirit is higher than both of theirs, so I directly suppressed theirs; however, through continuous suggestions, it was finally able to appear.’Colin roughly figured out the logic behind the appearance of this entity.
If through some technique, he were to lose his related memories, it would probably disappear again, ceasing to exist…
“It truly lives up to its name of ‘non-existent’…”
Having figured out the situation, Colin retracted his thoughts, waved his hand, and motioned for the two employees to follow.
And as all three of them entered the tarred road, the bizarrely existing hospital once again disappeared from its place.
Everything on the tarred road was intact, showing no signs of destruction, and as they followed this road, the hospital, flickering in and out of visibility, became clearer as it was bathed in light.
This was an enormously large hospital, made up of many buildings, and even, behind almost one-fifth of the lit windows, the lights were still on, as if patients were being treated inside.
“The lights might as well all be off; the few that are on are quite unsettling…” Colin exhaled.
Looking directly at the hospital, he felt an inexplicable tension and a sense of oppression for no apparent reason.
“There will be shadows in those lights, but no people. Anyway, as long as you don’t touch those shadows, there won’t be any problems…” Orange Cat explained and then pointed in a direction: “Actually, there’s not much danger on the first three floors, and there’s even no one there.
“Let’s head to the outpatient department first and find a special staircase from inside…”
“Yeah, right, there’s nothing much on the front floors, you just need to find a staircase that’s a little special, then you can go up…” Ashen Holy Body added.
“What’s special about it?” Colin asked.
“Hard to say, but you’ll feel something’s off at first glance, a very uncomfortable sensation…”
“And what about those larger buildings in the back?”
“They’re just a trick to the eyes. The first time we came, we wasted a lot of time up there, and when it was finally time to withdraw, we found that the way to the next floor was right there in the outpatient department’s low-rise building…” Ashen Holy Body said bitterly.
“Fine.”
Soon, the group entered the main gate of the outpatient department, and they were greeted by the smell of disinfectant.
Unlike what was seen from outside, inside the hall was brightly lit. Other than the quietness caused by the absence of people, it looked like any normal hospital.
As Colin stepped in, he was just about to look for the so-called special staircase…
However, his gaze suddenly sharpened and he stopped, looking at a consultation desk in the middle of the outpatient hall.
There, stood the figure of a woman in a white uniform…
Noticing Colin’s movement, both men looked over at the same time, and they too were startled.
“Fuck! How can there be someone here!?” Orange Cat exclaimed in shock, with gusts of wind blades swirling around him, nearly shooting directly at the other party.
But Colin extended his hand, using flames to dissipate these wind blades.
“Don’t disturb the balance here…” Colin whispered; he didn’t feel any danger for the time being.
Moreover, not having much knowledge about this place, it was best not to act recklessly under these circumstances.
It was at this moment that the woman standing at the desk turned her head to look at them, a professional smile gracing her beautiful face:
“Hello, welcome to our hospital for consultation. Is there anything I can help you with?”
The gentle words echoed in the empty hall under the incandescent lights, chilling to the bone.
“What should we do? The last time we came, there didn’t seem to be anyone like her…” Orange Cat asked Brother Shunzi.
Before Colin could speak, Ashen Holy Body suddenly said, “That voice… it sounds like an employee we worked with before, her build and everything else too, no, it’s her!”
“Employee? What happened to her?” Colin frowned.
“She got lost after encountering some trouble last time; she was one of the two who didn’t make it out…” said Ashen Holy Body with a complicated tone.
One of his reasons for coming in was to find out the fate of his old teammates, and he didn’t expect to see one right at the entrance.
“Does that mean, if you run into trouble here, you might become part of this place?” Colin muttered.
“What do we do now?” Orange Cat asked, somewhat nervously.
Hearing his words, Ashen Holy Body also looked to Colin.
“It feels a bit strange, to be honest; she doesn’t look alive, but not dead either, more like a puppet of sorts…” Colin said, the light from the flames reflecting as he sensed something.
“If there’s no problem, we’ll just ignore her for now. We should focus on the mission requirements first, head down to investigate, understand the situation, and then consider her case.”
Hearing Colin’s decision, the two men voiced no objections.
However, before starting the mission, Colin remembered the task notes and began to look around, finally stopping at an LED screen.
“Welcome patients to… your consultation. During your consultation, please adhere to the following rules to avoid being deceived.”
“1. Please note, our outpatient department only has three floors; there are no additional floors. If you see any staircase that does not adhere to the rules, please retreat promptly…”
“2. All treatment in our hospital is fully automated and unmanned. Do not believe any person posing as our hospital staff, and do not respond to any of their words.”
“3. Please Ning…!??…??…???…”
Red fonts scrolled on the LED screen…
“What is this third point? Garbled text?”
Colin looked again at the first two points; the absence of additional floors—if combined with the employees’ experience—could, in a way, be suggesting a path to the next level?
As for the second point…
It conflicted somewhat with the existence of the woman who had turned into the front desk employee.
“What happens if we break these rules?” Ashen Holy Body and Orange Cat also noticed the text on the LED screen.
“Let’s not worry about that for now, let’s just get moving…”
Colin gestured, and the group began to search the outpatient building directly.
With information provided by the two, they didn’t waste time entering any other buildings in the outpatient department, greatly narrowing their search area.
About ten minutes later, Colin found a passageway near a corner on the ground floor. It was indistinguishable from other corridors but gave off the feeling of leading into an uneasy abyss.
“This is the place.” Both men confirmed at the same time.
Upon hearing this, Colin did not hesitate, enshrouded in flames, revolver in hand, he took the lead and walked at the forefront.

chapters.title: Chapter 746 - 746 534 The Weeping Psychotic Madman_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 746: Chapter 534 “The Weeping Psychotic Madman”_1 Chapter 746: Chapter 534 “The Weeping Psychotic Madman”_1 “Huff huff huff~”
The scorching fireball was at the forefront, providing Colin, who was fully armed, with a distant “view.”
However, the staircase leading to the next level, while feeling a bit more sinister than usual, had no other abnormalities.
Colin and his comrades made their way upwards, reaching the third floor, only to find another mirror-like staircase descending.
He examined it with the light of the flame and noticed that from this corner down, patches resembling black moss started to appear sporadically around the area.
“Going down from here, back to the first floor, we’ll be on the second level of the hospital…” the voice of Orange Cat came from behind.
Colin nodded, sensing no issues, and continued forward.
At that moment, Ashen Holy Body glanced at the patches and said, “It’s best not to touch these things directly, they have a very strong corrosive effect on flesh and blood, touching them with bare skin is almost like touching strong acid…”
“Can they really do that?” Orange Cat exclaimed in surprise.
They had bypassed these during their last visit without taking notice…
“Yes.” Ashen Holy Body added, “We’ve tested them. However, they only react to living flesh; corpses or anything that has been dead for a while and completely expired show no response to them…”
“Would clearing them trigger something?” Colin casually asked.
“There won’t be a problem, you can’t destroy these. If you don’t believe me, Brother Shunzi, you can try,” Ashen Holy Body stated.
“Can’t destroy them?”
Upon hearing this, Colin snapped his fingers and a flame flew out, landing on one of the black patches on the wall, igniting it instantly.
“This seems easily…eh?”
Colin was about to speak, but his expression suddenly darkened.
It hadn’t burned away?
After the flame vanished, the black patch reappeared in the original area.
With no change from before it was burned…
Undeterred, he tried several more times, yet the result was the same.
Even after burning the wall with it, within seconds, it too would return to its original state.
“There’s something to this, an anomaly that even the ‘Bonfire’ can’t burn away.”
This was Colin’s first encounter with such a phenomenon.
Nevertheless, after confirming that there would be no issue as long as one didn’t directly touch the black patches with their skin, Colin led his team downwards.
Descending the mirror-like staircase from the third floor, they safely made their way back to the lobby on the first floor.
To be precise, it was the lobby on the first floor of the hospital’s second level!
“I originally thought each ‘floor’ referred to a level of the building, but now it seems that’s not the case. Every time we pass through one, we reach a more ‘inner’ layer of the world, with a ‘nonexistent hospital’ on each level…”
Feeling the changes around him, Colin came to this realization.
At this moment, besides the dark patches, the scene in front of him looked almost identical to the first level.
Even the female employee at the front desk was still there.
Different from before, when she needed his gaze to fall on her to sense him and then turned her head, this time she was already looking over without needing to be seen…
Colin didn’t avoid her, but met her gaze directly.
He saw, on the professionally smiling face, a pair of eyes that became increasingly hideous as they locked eyes.
“Hello, do you need help? Hello, do you need help?!”
“Hello? Hello?…”
“You you you…”
The soft and polite female voice suddenly became rougher and shriller, as grating as nails on a chalkboard, causing a chill to run down one’s spine.
Colin felt a strong sensation of falling.
He didn’t panic; fire swirled in his eyes, pulling him out of the bizarre sensation and the momentary ‘distraction’ caused by the eye contact.
The voice by his ear vanished instantly, returning to its original gentle tone: “Hello, may I help you with anything?”
Colin paid her no more heed. With the fire burning on his body, he thoroughly severed that link, “Stay alert, make sure you are mentally stable. Don’t make eye contact with these things, otherwise you might run into some unexpected trouble.”
Big guy, we’ve always been cautious, okay? We wouldn’t dare to look around like you… The two of them silently muttered in their hearts, yet nodded.
