Upon seeing this, he reached out his hand, and flames spread like chains, performing a Bonfire sealing for everyone.
A few minutes later, he completed the seal and further reinforced it.
Colin glanced over at some scattered abnormal corpses in the distance, took out a “Fusion Card: Smiling Mountain of Corpses” from his pocket with his index and middle fingers, and held it in front of him.
The next second, with spiritual infusion, pieces of flesh from various places flew towards him, converging in front of Colin.
There was a bang, and dust rushed to the sky as a large black flesh orb fell to the ground. Muscular arms stretched out, and a toothless, gaping maw opened to let out a loud howl:
“┗|｀O′|┛ Wow~~”
“Bring them.”
Issuing the command, Colin recalled the “Fire Tree” and the Little Maid, put his hands in his pockets, and walked toward the yet-to-close “Bonfire Passage.”
The “Innate Ashen Holy Body” followed behind.
The massive Corpse Mountain was a bit slower, extending its crimson tongue to carefully envelop everyone in its mouth. Then, with the effort of its arms, it crawled after Colin like an obedient large dog, pushing the Ashen Holy Body aside and slowing down once behind Colin.
“It’s All Orange Cat’s Fault” had already returned from garrisoning the fourth layer.
“Goodbye~” Someone suddenly called out from afar, causing Colin to pause in his steps.
He turned back and saw that among the darkness, those ladies who chose to stay, were now emerging from the refuge onto the ruins above, waving at him vigorously.
Although they didn’t plan to leave, after Colin took care of the deep contamination, the chaos and contamination of the area had markedly decreased. There would still be some trouble refreshing, but it was no longer as chaotic as before…
Of course, the most crucial thing was that some of the hospital’s own anomalies still existed.
Meaning there would be no problem with food refreshing.
“Goodbye.”
Colin also waved his hand. “The Nonexistent Hospital” still had some secrets, such as the operating mechanisms of the hospital itself, but for a long time to come, these secrets were harmless and not necessary to explore further.
After responding, Colin turned around once more and left the twelfth layer amidst the gazes of the people.
As he departed, the “Bonfire Passage” slowly disappeared.
Before long, when Colin arrived at the first layer, he directly appeared in the lobby of the “Inquiry Department” on the ground floor.
Because of the recent battle, all abnormalities temporarily disappeared, and the lights in the hall went out, casting the area into pitch darkness.
However, the glow of the fire replaced the darkness after Colin arrived.
And as the female employee’s body was taken away, the hospital’s “reception” also vanished.
Colin didn’t linger, leading a group of people to the clinic’s main entrance, where carriages of the train were stopped not far from the door, the oversized carriages sheltering a tremble of terrified sisters.
“Is it resolved?” Lady Bai, who was clutching a greatsword, seemed somewhat relieved to see Colin emerge.
The signature flames of his, impossible to fake by anyone else, assured her it wasn’t a counterfeit, and she waved her hand to signal the other survivors to lower their guns and other such weapons…
Of course, the massive and ferocious black flesh orb following Colin, which also inexplicably seemed docile, still drew a couple of extra glances from her.
“Yeah.”
Colin nodded as he approached, checking to see which of the special carriages matched the requirements of his mission.
“Then… the other sisters now…” Lady Bai’s worried gaze passed beyond Colin and the rest, towards the direction of the hospital.
The recent battle was too terrifying, even leaving a noticeable impact here.
Huge cracks appeared in some of the buildings from the shockwaves…
And the sisters who were in the midst of the battlefield, their condition was also unknown.
“Don’t worry, they were all avoided before, and when I just came out, I saw some of them. They had minor injuries, but a little rest should be no big issue, and generally, there was nothing serious.”
Colin briefly explained, then found the smaller special carriage at the end of the train.
The carriage seemed to have a high level of protection.
With relatively larger seats inside, Colin placed the surviving employees one by one onto the seats and tied them down, considerately applying some protective measures to prevent the “Little Dark Ones” from possibly sitting on them later.
After putting everyone in place, Colin felt that now he could operate this train.
But he didn’t rush to leave right away and instead explained the details of riding on the train to Lady Bai and the rest who followed him, to avoid panic in the event of an emergency that couldn’t be handled on time, leading to casualties.
At the same time, he controlled the flames to bestow some “Bonfire Blessing” upon the several thousand sisters.
This way the “Little Dark Ones” would find them repulsive and would not make contact with them…
“There are plenty of seats in the carriages, don’t fill them all up, leave some for those black shadows. It’s essential that there is one shadow in every carriage. If you find one missing, use this flame to drive one over, otherwise something bad might happen…”
“Also, if you encounter an enemy along the way, don’t panic. Bury your heads and don’t look at them. Generally, anomalies won’t be able to breach the train, and since you’re on a special train, even if you are attacked, help should arrive very soon.”
“And if you meet…”
Colin went on explaining while also using “Inspiration” techniques to deepen their memory impressions, to avoid forgetting.
After all, traveling by the “Train in the Fog” would be fine if done by the rules, but a careless mistake could lead to casualties…
However, barring any surprise, “The Second Box Garden World” should not have fallen and retained a considerable portion of the company’s power.
So, there should be a complete version of the “Father of the Sea” or a “Lady of Thorns” grade “Administrator” garrisoned there.
Even the “Lady of Thorns,” who considers herself “civilian”, has the strength of a First Level Containment Subject.
Therefore, there should be no overly serious concerns regarding safety…
After patiently explaining the things to be aware of, under Colin’s supervision, Lady Bai rearranged the seating arrangement of the personnel. Once everything was settled, Colin left the train carriage.
The urgent, clanging sound of the train bell resonated incessantly.
In that moment, a mysterious haze of gray fog gradually thickened, filling the entire area.
With a “clack,” the train door closed.
The train slowly started moving forward, carrying a crowd of sisters filled with tension, excitement, and anticipation towards the new world.
“We should also be going.”
Colin waved to them one last time before confirming the mission was over and returning to reality through company channels.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 784 - 784 550 The Hefty Reward from the 15th Loop
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 784: Chapter 550: The Hefty Reward from the 15th Loop Incident. _1 Chapter 784: Chapter 550: The Hefty Reward from the 15th Loop Incident. _1 The familiar ceiling he had looked at countless times.
Colin opened his eyes, lay in bed for a while to dispel that inexplicable sense of daze, took a deep breath, stopped lazing in bed, and turned his head to glance at the clock on the wall.
“March 3rd, it seems like it’s been over three days and a few hours…”
Colin shifted his position to lean against the headboard, did some quick mental calculations of the train ride and mission duration, and it was roughly correct.
Then, he rubbed his hungry stomach, summoned the Little Maid, had her split off a part of herself to continue participating in various official experiments, and had her prepare some food ingredients to start making a feast…
Although, with his level of strength, his need for food was not high, theoretically he could go a long time without eating and it wouldn’t matter much, at worst he would look a bit thinner like the previous Saintess, without much impact.
But what was different from others was that he had “Hunger” inside his stomach…
If he went a long time without eating, it might cause problems.
And since he was eating, he definitely had to eat well; he couldn’t just settle for something random…
“Feels like once I reach C Level, I should be stable and not worry too much about losing control. If I become a ‘Flame Bearer’ later on, then there’s a high probability that I’ll be able to fully convert this part of ‘Hunger’ for my use.”
“Tsk, if ‘Hunger’ could be fully utilized, even if it’s just a fragment, it would be a huge treasure…”
Colin fantasized about the scene where he had full control over “Hunger”.
Even for a “Flame Bearer”, “Hunger” was still a powerful boost.
Otherwise, Rosen, who was a high-ranking member of the “Flame Bearer”, wouldn’t have used it as one of his main combat methods during his execution of super difficult missions.
But unfortunately, for him, the image in his mind was still a bit premature.
“Looking at it now, becoming a Level C Employee seems hopeful, but becoming a ‘Flame Bearer’ is still uncertain.”
In the hospital’s special effect of “Belief Materializes”, he had unwittingly summoned a trace of the Primordial Fire’s might, and now he had a deeper understanding of the current dilemma of the “Flame Bearer”.
What he summoned seemed to be a power from the past, not the current ‘Primordial Fire’…
Without the influence of “Belief Materializes”, Colin reviewed the situation in depth once more, and realized it was very difficult to describe the status of the “Primordial Fire” with his current understanding.
If he had to say, it seemed to exist in a state that was difficult to comprehend, a “neither present nor absent” status…
Or to simplify it, Colin knew that such a thing did indeed exist, but even though he was already using the associated power, he could not confirm its current existence.
Just bizarre…
And if he couldn’t confirm it, he couldn’t contact it; without contact, he couldn’t attract the “Primordial Fire”, and then he would not be able to become a “Flame Bearer”…
“‘Conceptual’ stuff is indeed a bit metaphysical; no wonder when I asked ‘Lady Rabbit’ how to become a ‘Flame Bearer’, she was so vague. The method she knew probably no longer works, so she is also clueless.”
Colin felt he was touching upon the truth.
According to the information he had gathered, “Flame Bearers” during the company era, though seemingly hard to achieve with many conditions, did not lead to a dead-end. However, after the company’s upheaval, this path seemed to have been severed.
The reason for this severance could very likely be related to the grand mission that Rosen mentioned, which the “Flame Bearers” at the end carried out together.
It also had something to do with “The Ultimate Moment”, or, to put it another way, 2044.
“I’m probably not the first person in this post-company era to take the ‘Flame Bearer’ path. I wasn’t sure before, but the moment I summoned the power of the ‘Primordial Fire’ in the hospital, I did feel a bit, as if there were other people on this path, only I am unsure of their fate, and it’s even possible that they sensed me…”
“But likewise, they seem to be reservists at most, just like me, using the power of the ‘Flame Bearer’ through some sideways means, having not reached the status of ‘Flame Bearer’, unable to truly mobilize the power of the ‘Primordial Fire’…”
“It seems that so far, I have not detected the existence of any living ‘Flame Bearers’. Did they all fail…”
Colin bit his finger, feeling led into a dead end.
However, the next time he had the chance to see “Lady Rabbit”, he would ask if there were other “Flamebearer” reserves, and if so, what their current situation is… He also looked forward to the other “Flamebearer” reserves being more capable.
If they could pierce through the last barrier with the “Primordial Fire”, it should make his becoming a “Flame Bearer” much easier.
Thinking of this, Colin suddenly let out a wry smile, strangely thinking, if there are other “Flamebearer” reserves now, wouldn’t they all be in a situation similar to his own, preferring to expect others to succeed rather than put in the effort themselves?
Then, Colin shook his head, stopping his train of thought, and excitedly pulled out the parchment——
This time it was a reward with fifteen rings stacked together!
Colin dared not think how many things there would be!
[In this event, your evaluation is: A-.]
[You have completed this event with an exceptionally excellent performance.]
[Below is the settlement of your rewards after this event mission——”Bonfire Points*412000″, “Special Grade Item Draw Ticket*1”, “C Level Genetic Compensation Medicine (Injection Type)*1”, “Golden Clearance Certificate*47″…]
…
The mission rewards looked plain and seemed no different from usual, but the quantities listed afterwards were clear to see.

chapters.title: Chapter 785 - 785 550 High Rewards from the Event at Ring
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 785: Chapter 550 High Rewards from the Event at Ring 15._2 Chapter 785: Chapter 550 High Rewards from the Event at Ring 15._2 Colin let out a slight hiss.
“Hss… over four hundred thousand points, more than double and quite a bit over the two hundred thousand I had in mind! The reward for an average regular task is close to thirty thousand points each, which adds up to a lot more than all my previous points combined…”
Clenching the parchment, Colin’s eyes widened slightly.
You have to know, within the Fifteenth Ring tasks, many could be completed offhand, and by Colin’s own estimates, they should at most only give three to five thousand points, definitely not over ten thousand.
And for the more difficult and complicated ones, like “Thorn World” or “The Hospital That Doesn’t Exist,” those few that are a bit tougher.
The rewards are likely around thirty thousand.
All together, Colin’s previous expectation was that anything over two hundred thousand would be a massive gain.
He hadn’t expected it to double!
“The points aren’t right, huh? They gave so much extra, did I get anything especially valuable in these Fifteenth Ring tasks?”
Colin was puzzled for a while, seemingly recalling that he hadn’t acquired any particularly valuable items.
“Whatever, it doesn’t matter if it’s too much or too little, as long as it’s in my pocket, it’s not going anywhere…” Colin calculated a bit, adding the points earned from the “Cross-Border Second-Hand Dealer” business he ran with Shana, as well as some points made from stockpiling “futures” in small-time trading.
In total, he had just over five hundred thousand points on hand…
Now there was hope for fixing the Golden Card.
“Should be just about enough, though it looks like I can only repair one card to the ‘Item Liberation’ standard, anything more still won’t do, this damn thing really does burn through money.”
Thinking about those points being almost gone soon made Colin wince.
But he didn’t dwell on it, instead he turned his attention to the other items…
The “Special Grade Mission Item Draw Ticket” mentioned a minimum of three Purple Gear with a chance to draw Orange, or a smaller chance for a Golden Artifact…
The “C Level Genetic Compensation Medicine” was as mundane as its name implied, nothing noteworthy.
As for the “Golden Clearance Certificate,” to be honest, there seemed to be some excess of these as well because, by Colin’s estimate, there should have been fewer than thirty, but there were forty something…
“Could this be some kind of extra subsidy for the ‘Bonfire’s Exceptional Talent’ or something?”
Colin scratched the back of his head, quite pleased, but while he was happy, there was a feeling that something was amiss.
Not overly fixated on it, after seeing these clearance certificates, he counted them and now had a total of sixty-five Gold Mission Vouchers…
“The ‘Gene Compensation Panel’ can be considered for maxing out; seems like after maxing it out, it can bring some improvement?”
Colin decided to max out that thing first and then summoned his own status panel.
[Name]: Colin.
[Strength]: 21.4. (Single-handedly capable of halting a high-speed Harmony Express train in motion.)
[Constitution]: 22. (Can bathe in lava without sustaining any harm.)
[Agility]: 17.1. (Freakin’ fast!)
…
[Discretionary Points]: 0 (3/18).
[Note]: The above data does not represent final combat power, everything should be based on actual encounter.
(Every fifteen hundred points + one Golden Clearance Certificate can be exchanged for 1 discretionary point.)
…
“Even though there’s some gap compared to Big C Teacher, it’s still pretty good.”
Colin nodded to himself; remembering Big C Teacher’s stats: “Strength 53, Constitution 77.1, Agility 19.9,” at first the discrepancy seemed huge, but even then he didn’t know what it really meant, until now…
Damn, he truly was a “stat freak”!
If he hadn’t been corroded and for various other reasons, there would have been no way to beat him!
Even if Colin now were to maximize everything and combine a large amount of items, while he could win, the fight would still be quite strenuous.
Any other Earth employee, dealing with it normally, other than praying that their corpse isn’t left in pieces, couldn’t really do anything else.
Without overthinking it, Colin looked at the remaining limit for discretionary points.
“Three points were rewarded when I went to ‘Passionate Paradise,’ which I’ve already used; a normal employee has 12 points, but I’m a Reservist, so I got an extra six, which is why it’s 18…”
“Speaking of which, this panel only required three hundred points within ‘Passionate Paradise,’ but after coming out for public testing, it jumped to fifteen hundred, an increase…”
As his thoughts flickered, Colin decided to directly spend twenty-two thousand five hundred points and fifteen Golden Mission Vouchers to obtain all the allocatable discretionary points.
Then, he intended to forcefully increase his Agility, but found that after adding 0.6, he couldn’t add any more.
[Do not arbitrarily ignore your own basic qualities in force-feeding points, please allocate them reasonably, otherwise, it may lead to the invalidity of added points…]
“There are even these kinds of requirements?”
Colin raised an eyebrow but ultimately followed the instructions, adding points one by one.
In the end, he added all the points.
[Name]: Colin.
[Strength]: 30.
[Physique]: 26.4.
[Agility]: 19.1.
[Available Points]: 18/18 (Reached the limit for version 1.0, look forward to subsequent updates.)
[High-Efficiency Talent Grid · Panel Specialization Unlocked]: None (Talent effects enhanced by ten percent).
[Comprehensive Evaluation]: Already very impressive, ranked among the top, at least ninety-three percent of employees at your level could not reach your current standard.
…
“So this is what it feels like to max out points and unlock a High-Efficiency Talent Grid…”
Colin felt his own condition, which was unprecedentedly good, tending toward perfect control over his body.
It was as if even the red blood cells were under his control…
Then, he extended his right hand, palm up in front of him, exerted just a little bit of effort, and clenched his fingers tightly together.
“Boom”!
A blasting sound erupted, and the entire room shook.
“Exaggerated.” Colin nodded in satisfaction, then got used to it, making sure not to exert too much force casually, lest he touched someone and injured or maimed that person.
In this aspect, the “Gene Compensation Panel” provided some passive assistance; he resolved related issues quite quickly.
“The ‘Gene Compensation Panel’ is quite considerate in its making.”
Colin then looked over at the Talent Grid, thinking that if he didn’t have any gains in the near future, he might consider removing “Wildfire Affliction” and then putting it back on.
An enhancement of ten percent might not seem much, but its effect in actual combat was still quite exaggerated.
“With my current abilities, if I encounter the lowest of the First Level Containment Subjects… never mind, it doesn’t seem feasible to think about it. I could probably take on avatars or incarnations, but the originals are definitely out of the question. Though, they wouldn’t find it easy to kill me either. If push comes to shove, I can fight to the death to escape. If it’s a severely wounded type, I might last a few moves…”
Colin wasn’t so optimistic as to think he could face those Ancient God-level lifeforms head-on.
After all, by company standards, even the lowest level of a First Level Containment Subject is a terrifying entity capable of causing destruction to a planet…
Perhaps unleashing “Hunger” could put up a fight, but just because “Hunger” can fight doesn’t mean he could; so if it really came down to it, it would probably end with “Hunger” winning while he died amidst the skirmish.
Afterward, Colin’s gaze fell to the bottom of the “Gene Compensation Panel,” and he was surprised, not that he surpassed ninety-three percent, but…
That there were seven percent of people at D+ level who were not weaker than him, some even stronger?
“What’s the situation? Does this comparison include data from ancient times, or is it just the present?”
Colin thought about it; aside from “The Light Chaser”, he really hadn’t seen many D+ level people stronger than himself.
“It should include people from the past, right? Otherwise, it doesn’t quite add up…”
Colin felt this was likely the case, then remembered “Lady of Thorns” once said that some people in the Corps were top seed players who, at D+ level, were even stronger than her, a World Administrator.
But such cases were definitely rare.
“However, this is just data concerning physical qualities. If you factor in equipment, then I wouldn’t say over ninety-nine percent, but it’s close.”
Colin estimated.
Considering the situation of the company back then, the mighty indeed were powerful, but the gear hadn’t kept up overall.
Orange and Golden Artifacts were likely only within reach for those above C level.
Average D level acquiring some Purple Gear with ordinary attributes was already quite good.
Like those seventy-some individuals on the train, the proliferation rate of Purple Gear seemed to be only around sixty to seventy percent, and some didn’t even have any…
Unlike employees nowadays, who are guaranteed at least one, and many might have four or five.
“If strength isn’t enough, make up with gear.”
Colin murmured and took out the “Special Grade Item Draw Ticket.”
…

chapters.title: Chapter 786 - 786 551 A Special Task _1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 786: Chapter 551 “A Special Task” _1 Chapter 786: Chapter 551 “A Special Task” _1 As Colin’s thoughts turned, he directly used the “Special Grade Item Draw Ticket”.
Soon…
A streak of golden light emerged in his line of sight.
Colin squinted his eyes slightly and saw a familiar design of a golden artifact’s information appeared before him.
[Name: “Force · Attraction”]
[Quality: Extremely Rare.]
[Status: Barely usable (Integrity 17%).]
[Energy Level: Class A.]
[Effect: Upon holding and activating the card effect, the user can temporarily control the concept of “gravity” within a 10m radius. The desirability of the effect depends on the item’s status and the cardholder’s proficiency…]
[Note: One of The Seventeen Gold Cards from the “Card Divine Kingdom”, capable of combining effects with other “Force” series…]
[In an interview, a “Mr. Kattu” who didn’t want to reveal his name pointed at a celestial body not too far away and said: See that moon up there? I just pinched it…]
[Status repair conditions: Consume Three Thousand Seven Hundred and Sixty One Points to repair to 19%, which will strengthen the effect intensity.]
[The item has been stored in the “Storage Room”, please check.]
…
“Gravity…”
Colin held the newly acquired Golden Card with a strange expression… It wouldn’t really be just these card-type items in the company’s internal golden artifact draws these days, would it?
He thought about it and seemed that so far, every golden draw yielded a card.
As for drawing a Golden Card, it wasn’t upsetting, but he wasn’t the same person he was when he first joined the company, especially after knowing some insider details about the draw tickets…
He was very clear about one thing.
Once the company started giving out super-level items, there was definitely a big catch waiting behind it.
Especially considering the mission just completed, which provided him with more than double the expected bonus Points and a Golden Clearance Certificate, plus his understanding of Lady Rabbit’s habit of issuing missions.
A vague sense of anxiety began to stir within Colin.
“But what’s given is given; I can’t exactly give it back.”
With the Golden Card in hand, Colin willed it into action and pointed forward, causing a ping pong ball and other various items, big and small, including the rack itself, to rapidly move and compress around the ping pong ball at a distance of several meters.
Everything within ten meters seemed to be affected…
However, just as everything squeezed together, Colin stopped using the item.
“You can choose which objects to attract and which to repel, but it takes a bit of effort to control. Plus, the ‘gravity’ endowed on an object’s size also determines the effect: the smaller the object, the higher the precision needed, the larger the object, the simpler it is to operate. However, lack of proficiency might reduce the effectiveness of the skill…”
After making a simple judgment, Colin suddenly heard the flapping of wings from outside the window.
It was the half-wild pigeon, which has been missing since eating one of its eggs.
It was chasing a male pigeon and flapping its wings on a landscaping tree outside the window. Just as it was about to catch up, Colin beckoned with a gesture and a gravitational pull took effect. The pigeon flew backwards and landed in his hands.
“Not bad.”
Colin, holding the plump pigeon that had fattened up from scrounging for food somewhere this winter and was now struggling in his hand, reflected on the feeling of using “Gravity”, feeling that the item was indeed very powerful…
As he contemplated, Colin tossed the pigeon into the air and produced another golden card, “Force – Repulsive Force”.
In a snap, the pigeon shot sideways and started tumbling, only to be pulled back by “Gravity”. Colin tried out multiple different usage scenarios in a few back and forth movements.
“The power of these two gold cards can cancel each other out or be used in combination, but the proficiency and precision required are quite high. Though, the ‘gravity’ attributed to an object will significantly diminish the effect when there’s not much around to attract…”
While waving his hand back and forth, pulling the pigeon like a yo-yo, Colin quickly familiarized himself with the Gold Card.
Of course, if the Golden Card’s status and precision were improved, theoretically, Colin could gather stars with a speck of dust, but now, applying gravity to something the size of a lychee pit was his operational limit.
Anything smaller made it difficult to lock on to the target.
While Colin was using the pigeon for his experiments, the pedestrians in the corridor below seemed oblivious to it all.
After trying out for about three to five minutes, Colin grabbed the pigeon again: “Next time you come to my window to relieve yourself, I’ll treat you to a meal.”
After muttering to himself, the merciful Colin—unwilling to kill—still threw it back outside.
“In a couple of days, I can go to Shana to practice with the ‘gravity’ card and even test it out in real combat inside the ‘Mist Disaster’.”
Colin started repairing the Golden Card.
Before long, after spending a total of just over eighty thousand Points and four Gold Mission Vouchers, Colin repaired its integrity from 17% to 49%.
[Status repair conditions: Consume 72140 Points to repair to 59%, and the effect intensity, range, and other aspects will be further enhanced.]
“What a ripoff; working myself to death to earn some Points, and two or three repairs later, nearly one-fifth is gone…”
Colin looked at his remaining Points, totaling over four hundred thirty-thousand, and could not help but complain.
Repairing this Golden Card with Points was not something an average employee could afford.
However, after repairing it to 49%, the effect’s range had increased to a diameter of one hundred fifty meters, and the gravity was much stronger than before. Moreover, an Inherent Skill had been added.
[Inherent Skill “Strong Aggregation – Celestial Body Creation”: Endows oneself or a specific object with a super-strong gravity effect, attracting all nearby objects to achieve protection or sealing.]

chapters.title: Chapter 787 - 787 551 A Special Task _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 787: Chapter 551 “A Special Task” _2 Chapter 787: Chapter 551 “A Special Task” _2 Displaying the effect, he could, if he wished, crush a building into a dense sphere in a matter of minutes.
“There’s nothing fancy about the ability, the core is ‘Gravity’, 49% is enough. The rest of the Points should be used on ‘Time Stasis’ as much as possible.”
With that thought, Colin was quite satisfied as he pocketed the item and picked up the parchment.
Then, he suddenly noticed something…
The second phase of the mission that usually comes after the first wasn’t popping up immediately?
“What’s going on?”
Colin raised an eyebrow, he hadn’t noticed this when he was checking the results of the mission earlier, but now he realized that normally, the next major phase of the mission should have appeared.
However, as he puzzled over it, the second round of the mission finally made its appearance…
[Promotion Qualification Event 2——]
[“A Special Event”: This is a special mission. What’s special about it is that it’s very special, whether it’s the rewards or the content are extremely special.]
“Huh?”
Colin stared at the mission, baffled. Is this… for real?
And wasn’t the second phase supposed to be a seven-day tour of the Joyful Farmstead?
How come it’s not quite what was agreed upon…
Confused, Colin clicked on the mission details to check the specifics.
…
“Mission Explanation”: This mission has no specific direction; complete the event, pass with a sufficient rating, and you will obtain C Level corporate privileges.
“Requirement 1”: Please repair your highest proficiency Golden Card to meet the “Item Liberation” requirements before the countdown of 57 days, 21 hours, and 29 minutes ends.
“Requirement 2”: Please repair your other “Rare” and “Ultra-Rare” items to above 69% before the countdown of 57 days, 21 hours, and 29 minutes ends.
“Note”: Subsequent requirements are ongoing, refreshing, please wait…
…
“???”
Colin frowned, looking over the mission again, realizing that the requirements were all about repairing his own items; in other words, they demanded that he quickly enhance his overall strength.
This… Colin thought for two seconds, feeling that “Lady Rabbit” probably intercepted the “Joyful Farmstead seven-day tour.”
Was it because she thought he wasn’t capable of completing the mission yet, so she wanted him to improve his strength before considering executing it… or was it for some other reason?
“And also this mission explanation, after completion, as long as you pass, you’re directly promoted to C Level, no need to queue for eligibility?”
Colin remembered that originally, completing this mission would just give the chance to qualify for a C Level upgrade.
As for whether or not one could get promoted to C Level…
That would specifically depend on what the requirements were at the time of promotion, and whether there were any slots available. If there were no slots, one would have to queue and wait indefinitely.
However, the dark comedy is that with so many high-level executives dead in the company, there should be slots everywhere…
Maybe because of this, one could get promoted directly upon completion?
“Just don’t know if there will be any other enhancement requirements after this part is done.”
Colin looked at the note, and it seemed like there were going to be more than these two requirements.
After some thought, he opened the company’s internal communication system and entered a small group, sending out a message.
“654321”: I have completed the first phase of the “Promotion Qualification Mission”…
As soon as it was sent, a bunch of people popped up in the group, bursting into cheers.
“Life Mentor Adorable”: Finally, it’s coming! I also completed the “Fifteenth Ring” mission a few days ago, now just waiting in ‘Joyful Farmstead seven-day tour’ on standby for Brother Shunzi to join!
“Only lewd images reign supreme”: Quick, quick, quick, I’ve been waiting too, just waiting for Brother Shunzi to make a grand gesture, and we can all charge towards that broken farmstead together!
“Superman when happy”: Count me in, count me in! I’ll call 6 so fast!
“Surprised Porridge”: @654321, wait up, Brother Shunzi, I’m just a few points short of “Item Liberation”, wait for me…
…
A bunch of the company’s “elite veterans” all came out. Although they knew that the missions Brother Shunzi took part in were likely to involve this or that kind of incident.
But at the same time, Brother Shunzi’s rate of success was guaranteed.
So far, the death rate among those who have teamed up with him was still “0”.
Plus, they have experienced Brother Shunzi’s combat power several times first-hand, so even if there might be danger during the “Joyful Farmstead Seven-Day Tour”, the employees were still willing to give it a shot.
After all, as seasoned veterans, they had carried out many events and could vaguely feel that something foreboding was on the horizon.
Before, there wasn’t an opportunity, and since the promotion task for Second Order D Level was so difficult, many people just gave up.
Now that there was finally a glimmer of hope, they definitely wanted to seize it.
However, what quickly disappointed them was that it seemed Brother Shunzi wasn’t part of this task?
Following that, everyone was taken aback upon seeing the description of Brother Shunzi’s task—it seemed a bit off…
Repair one’s own items?
Though it was true that there were other C Level qualification tasks besides the farm, none of them included Shunzi’s—
A new type?
“Looking at it this way, it should be confirmed that ‘Lady Rabbit’ gave this task to me specifically.”
Colin briefly communicated, then closed the chat group.
Then he opened up the task requirements to take another look, and immediately felt a headache coming on.
The requirements at first glance seemed not too difficult, just to repair items.
But the problem was…
“Within two months, all orange gear and golden artifacts must be repaired to at least 69%, this, if I’m not mistaken, just one Golden Card repair to meet the requirements is close to two hundred thousand points, including a need for an ‘Item Liberation’ repair to 85%… Where am I going to get so many points from?”
Colin didn’t even dare to carefully think about the points needed, because just the thought of it made his scalp tingle.
Currently, he had a total of four Golden Cards in his hand, and apart from “Time Stasis” which was just at “69%”, the completeness of all the others was at “49%”.
Then, besides the four Golden Cards, he also had a golden artifact, the “Shield Badge of Fairness and Justice”.
Although it was rented from Shana, but she didn’t seem to want it back now; rounding up, that was practically his own…
Plus, there were other various items.
“So, does this mean that I need to earn around a million points or so in just under two months to possibly meet its requirements?”
Colin opened his mouth in disbelief, how was this any different from setting “a small goal to earn first” in a short amount of time?
Upon further reflection, it seemed even more difficult than that “Fifteenth Ring task” from earlier!
However…
Upon careful consideration, if he went all out, it wasn’t entirely out of reach.
“Borrow some from the officials, take on some tasks, plus the weekly cuts from trades, and the income from task instances… No, still not quite enough.”
Colin estimated that he couldn’t afford to relax; whenever he had time, he would have to proactively take on tasks.
But before that, he sent a message to Old Master Wu:
“Are you there? Can I borrow some points from the officials? I need it for something urgent.”
“How many?”
“Roughly just a million points or so will do.”
“How many???”
On the other side of the phone, in a region of calamity, Old Master Wu stared at the message on his phone, wondering if he had started to become illiterate or was hallucinating?
Otherwise, how could he be seeing such an outrageous message?
It wasn’t until Colin sent another message to confirm this that Old Master Wu remained silent for a while before responding.
“In the entire Southern Region south of Huainan, there are a total of 249 employees of various levels, who, since half a year ago up until now, have accumulated a total of less than three million points, and most of it has already been spent on purchasing items and certain upgrades; the idle points are probably less than one hundred thousand…”
Old Master Wu did not reply directly whether he would lend the points or not, he simply stated the official situation.
However, between the lines, Colin felt as if Old Master Wu was implying something like:
Have a little shame, won’t you…
“Idle points are less than one hundred thousand? Is the official side really that broke?”
Colin, holding the phone in his right hand and scratching his head with his left, muttered under his breath before continuing to type, not giving up on borrowing points.

chapters.title: Chapter 788 - 788 552 With Great Power Comes Great Debt._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 788: Chapter 552: With Great Power Comes Great Debt._1 Chapter 788: Chapter 552: With Great Power Comes Great Debt._1 “A million points are definitely out of the question, even now, the points that can be gathered immediately, mostly by pooling national resources, would only amount to twenty or thirty thousand, and that’s after immediately cutting off some related plans…”
“I know you probably think that’s very little, but when it comes to using points, we have planned every penny, and aside from the necessary improvements for the employees themselves, there really isn’t much left.”
“For many official personnel, the materials gained through points are essential resources for many researchers, as well as crucial for many Extraordinary Ones to exchange for goods to maintain their sanity.”
“In short, even if you sold me to the company, I couldn’t come up with that many points…”
“…”
On the other end of the phone, Old Master Wu patiently explained the reasons for the scarcity of points—a single company employee’s points might be used by a whole group of people; a single dollar earned has to be divided into five or six portions for different purposes.
If they wanted to reallocate them, only the points earmarked for research purposes could be cut; other essential ones could not.
“Are points really that tight…”
Colin muttered to himself, but then, he noticed a key detail in the other’s words.
Did Old Master Wu think he needed to come up with the points all at once?
“Actually, it’s not like they must be produced right away…” Colin explained the situation briefly.
He informed the other person that there was roughly a two-month grace period, so time wasn’t particularly tight; the problem wasn’t especially big, as long as he could come up with the amount in this period.
However, upon hearing Colin mention the specific time frame, Old Master Wu’s brow furrowed immediately over the phone as if he had encountered something unimaginable.
“Fifty-seven days, huh…”
Old Master Wu counted on his fingers, pretended to calculate for a while, and then fell silent.
In his pair of deep dark eyes that seemed to see through everything, countless black threads seemed to squirm wildly…
After a while, he blinked, and everything returned to normal. He sighed and shook his head:
“Those guys at the top of the company, their estimated time is really accurate.”
Then, after pondering for a good while, Old Master Wu gave Colin a precise response: “In two months, we should be able to squeeze out around a hundred or a hundred and fifty thousand points…”
‘Only a hundred thousand in two months, huh…’
Colin pursed his lips, knowing this was close to the limit. There were probably around five to six hundred ‘Double-duty’ employees in the country, with each earning about a thousand points on average per month.
After deducting their own needs and various planned expenses, indeed very little could be spared.
Still, thinking of the remaining nine hundred thousand points, Colin felt it was quite a herculean task.
At that moment, he saw a new message from Old Wu:
“However, this matter concerns the whole world, it’s everyone’s responsibility; at times like this, humanity should unite to form an unbreakable human community of shared destiny…”
“I’ll help you contact the outside world; if all goes well, we should also be able to squeeze out a few hundred thousand points. Of course, if we forcibly plundered, we might be able to get more, but that would bring unnecessary karma, so we must proceed in a normal way…”
“I just did a quick calculation, to give you a baseline, a total of four hundred thousand points, but how much more than four hundred thousand I can borrow for you is hard to say, so you need to do some work yourself…”
Seeing this message from Old Wu, Colin was first stunned, then soon felt elated.
A million points became six hundred thousand points.
The pressure immediately lessened by almost half!
Even though it meant the ‘Double-duty’ employees around the world had to tighten their belts, if he became a Level C Employee, everything would be better!
For now, aside from essential expenses, the employees would just have to endure some hardship.
“Great, great, great, thanks in advance to the human community of shared destiny, I will not forget everyone’s sacrifices.” Colin hurriedly typed to cement this relationship.
“Don’t beat around the bush, kid; this is a loan to you, don’t make it sound like you don’t have to pay it back…”
“Yes, yes, yes, I’ll certainly pay it back when I can, definitely.”
Colin earnestly expressed his gratitude in response.
Then, he found himself missing the Fifteenth Ring task again. If another one came along, he might just have a chance to gather enough points…
Otherwise, normally, a month’s earnings, optimistically estimated, might not even reach a hundred thousand points.
“Right, the high-level employees at the company should be able to sort something out…”
Colin immediately got in touch with the group of old hands at the company, subtly hinting that he might need a bit of a point loan.
In this regard, the high-level employees were surprisingly cooperative, especially some of the D+ level employees, who even said they would empty their savings to lend him points, showing great enthusiasm.
Colin thought about it and roughly understood that they were probably hoping to be led through the ‘Joyful Farmstead Seven-Day Tour’ eventually.
To this, he had no objections.
But the problem was, if the task did not take the ‘Joyful Farmstead Seven-Day Tour’ route afterward…
That would be a bit awkward.
“Let’s talk about the future when it comes. Once I’m at Level C, squeezing out some powerful Golden Marks should get them through…”
Assuming the employees were at Level 69 and the ‘Joyful Farmstead Seven-Day Tour’ was a Level 89 instance, then afterwards, giving them a Non-Level Item of Level 159 should, give or take, get them through it.
At the very least, saving their lives shouldn’t be a problem.
Before long, Colin had obtained forty-seven thousand points from a dozen D+ level employees.

chapters.title: Chapter 789 - 789 552 With Great Power Comes Great Debt._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 789: Chapter 552: With Great Power Comes Great Debt._2 Chapter 789: Chapter 552: With Great Power Comes Great Debt._2 “I’ll sell some more stuff later, should be able to scrape together a few tens of thousands of points to use.”
Colin did a quick calculation and felt cheerful, having resolved another hundred thousand points.
The remaining five hundred thousand points…
In the previous month and a half, working with Shana selling golden beans, they split the profits fifty-fifty, Colin remembered that she had also accumulated a solid base, which was on him, about seventy-four thousand or more.
“I’ll mention it to Shana later.”
Colin pursed his lips, knowing that Shana would most likely be willing to lend, even all of it.
The pressure immediately eased up a lot.
But thinking of Shana, Colin then remembered the “King of Madness.” He recalled that even the “Mark of the Fire Tree” could save up some points, so the “King of Madness” might have some too, right?
“It is a high-ranking being, after all… Forget it, being caged up, it probably doesn’t have any, and even if it does…”
Colin thought of that “branch office.”
With its nature, if it had any points, they would surely be swindled out of it.
“Oh right, speaking of ‘Bonfire,’ how could I forget, some of the ‘summoning’ artifacts, those Containment Subjects turned into artifacts, most of them would have saved up a little over the years…”
Colin set his sights on the savings of these artifacts’ Containment Subjects.
He figured he could find some employees later, discuss the situation, and temporarily “sell” those artifacts to him. After extracting the points, he’d sell them back, sharing some of the received points with the others.
Although these Containment Subjects inside the artifacts seemed to be “underpaid,” over the course of a couple of hundred years, they would have accumulated at least a few hundred points, if not a few thousand, and if he was lucky, perhaps he could hit a jackpot.
“With my reputation, it should be no problem to carry this out, and as for what the Containment Subjects think…”
Colin had no intention of ignoring them: “I’m just borrowing, and when I earn more points in the future, I’ll repay them. As long as I become a Level C Employee, everything will start to look up.”
“Now down to four hundred thousand points, let’s see how much they can add to it, hm, any amount is fine, it’s all an unexpected windfall.”
After calming down, Colin lay on the bed, rubbing his hot forehead, feeling the pressure was still somewhat great.
Of course, the main reason for the pressure wasn’t just the points…
It was more about the vague hints of information behind this task.
“Some sort of big event is about to happen…” Colin felt especially uneasy at the thought.
This kind of thing doesn’t bother you normally, but as soon as you settle down and think about it, you can’t help but feel an inexplicable absurdity…
Who would have thought that a world that looks normal and seems to be improving would, perhaps soon, be facing a major crisis?
However, before he could dwell on it further, the Little Maid’s voice suddenly came from aside:
“Mr. Colin, your meal is ready.”
“Hmm.” Colin rolled over and sat up.
Things have come to this; it’s time first for a meal, to help relax after a good feed. After checking the time and confirming he had some to spare, he began to actively take on some tasks.
Currently, D Level Missions typically range from three to five hundred points each and you can only take on a maximum of three a week.
Of course, special talents get privileges and can do seven.
“Really too considerate, aren’t they…”
Colin pursed his lips, unable to help muttering softly: “Damn, this mission system is like hunger marketing…”
Then, he randomly picked a mission called “Old Mountain Ancestral House” and began to execute it.
Perhaps because he took the initiative in accepting the mission, Colin was surprised to find that there were no unexpected incidents the entire time, just an ancient, abandoned house in the middle of a little mountain.
Inside, some clay figures possibly revived the sealed Containment Subjects within due to weathering over the years.
However, after Colin set fire to the entire area, including that section of the mountain, the event came to an end…
“It looks like the tasks I usually receive passively must be carefully selected for me.”
“But seriously, is this the level of tasks that D Level staff used to do?”
Colin, watching the melted mountainside, shook his head with a sigh, no wonder they were all so lousy before.
The intensity is just too low…
Doing this kind of task every day, how can he lend himself money? No, that’s not right, how can he improve himself?
With a gesture, the flame that melted the mountain too, along with its heat, returned to Colin’s hand. Soon after returning home, he settled the points…
“A D Level Mission, get an A rating, and they only give eight or nine hundred points and two Silver Task Certificates? They must think I’m a beggar!”
Colin frowned, after two months here, he’d barely reached around ten thousand points, not even enough to cover the odds and ends needed for point repairs.
After some thought, his gaze settled on some “difficult team missions.”
These missions required ten people to carry out together, and because of the large number of people, the internal situation was complex, which is why not many employees were willing to do them, even though the points were two to three times the usual amount.
However, if they were successfully completed, one could at least get two thousand points, and the more one contributed to the evaluation, the more points one could get…
Of course, even on its own, it still didn’t seem high.
But when ten or more people did it at once, and each of those ten or more people could earn that much, the total was substantial.
And as long as employees had money, they could find a way to borrow some…
“Feels like I could start a team, recruit people, on the condition that a share of the points goes to me…”
Colin mulled it over and felt the plan was feasible.
Aside from points, Mission Vouchers were also important in a task, and while the points might be fewer, complex types of team missions could easily yield a Gold Mission Voucher.
Just having this single gold voucher in hand meant no loss.
Indeed, as soon as Colin mentioned this, many employees responded, expressing their willingness to follow him on the mission.
Colin first picked a D Level fifteen-person team mission called the “Terror Circus.”
The requirement was to locate the core, restart some of the old arrangements and re-stabilize that special small area.
The amusement park was quite large, it might be no smaller than some common cities, and it had various rules one had to follow or else get discovered by the myriad anomalies in the circus and then face the crazy attacks of strange and horrific entities—
Of course, this particular situation didn’t apply to Colin.
The anomalies’ attacks in the circus were simply approaches in weird manners followed by stabbings, or they involved mimicry, or turning into shadows, air, and so on, floating over.
But, in front of “Bonfire,” these methods were simply worthless.
Colin only needed to maintain the bonfire burning beside him in his normal state, and their tactics would be unraveled.
In this dominant state, the anomalies could only “despair” as they watched Colin and the others make their way to a tough and special black crystal.
By infusing new energy and restarting the old arrangements, all anomalies returned to the circus…
And transformed into roles similar to “NPCs.”
The most time-consuming part of the process was finding the core’s exact location.
“Large complicated tasks aren’t as complex as I thought.”
Colin casually assessed.
Upon hearing this, some of the employees who had entered the instance, split up to search for the core, and ended up injured by concentrated and intense attacks were somewhat embarrassed.
It wasn’t long before the event ended, and they returned to reality.
“Not bad, over three thousand seven hundred points.”
Colin took a quick look, checking on the parchment, where most folks’ points were around a thousand, the lowest being seven hundred, the highest one thousand and eight hundred.
Regardless of the amount, according to the previous agreement, fifty percent had to go to him.
In addition, twenty percent had to be “lent” to him.
With one thousand points, Colin would have seven hundred in hand.
“Life finally has some damn hope…”
Colin, who had been stressed and frazzled by the demands of the missions, looked at the tens of thousands of points in his hand and finally felt some confidence at the bottom of his heart.
If every large mission could earn this amount.
Then in two months, the points should be enough to meet the needs for repairing items…
At this moment, the only thing Colin needed to worry about was the scarcity of such ordinary tasks that could be actively undertaken and claimed to be complex maladies but in reality could be completed just by strolling down the street.
….

chapters.title: Chapter 790 - 790 553 The Stasis that Impacts the Entire
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 790: Chapter 553 The “Stasis” that Impacts the Entire World!_1 Chapter 790: Chapter 553 The “Stasis” that Impacts the Entire World!_1 Time passed quickly.
In the blink of an eye, Colin, who had become an unfeeling task machine, snapped back to reality from the relentless tasks and found that most of the time required for the task had already elapsed.
“Just one more week… less than that.”
Colin glanced at the task timer and then checked his progress.
Over the course of a month, he had not only secured one million Points but also exceeded the amount significantly. Old Master Wu had helped him obtain nearly five hundred thousand Points, and he had borrowed almost two hundred thousand from senior employees. Adding to that the weekly official trades with the company, as well as trades with “World Code -13” and other official transactions, there were also the Points that Colin actively accumulated from daily tasks.
In total, he had amassed over 1.2 million Points…
What surprised Colin was that, from the various “summoning-type” props, he had actually managed to borrow around one hundred and thirty to forty thousand Points!
Although there were those two stubborn ones who would rather die than relent, refusing to lend no matter what.
But many more “props,” upon hearing of Colin’s predicament and persuaded by his earnest reasoning and courteous treatment, eventually generously emptied their coffers to support him substantially.
Colin expressed his gratitude by saying, “Perhaps their assistance will fade from memory, but their contributions will never be forgotten!”
However, so many Points were still not quite enough.
Until now, with just the last seven days or a little less than six days left, he was looking at a gap of about one hundred thousand Points…
“This ‘Time Stasis’ from seventy-nine to eighty-nine percent, why is it so expensive? Aside from a dozen or so Golden Mission Vouchers, it’s over four hundred thousand Points just for Points alone…”
Colin let out a ‘hiss’ as he looked at the Points requirement.
Fortunately, other than this part of the Points requirement, the other props had all been repaired to 69% as required by the task.
Meanwhile, as these formerly tattered props were repaired, they began to reveal, more or less, the strange and mighty powers befitting their “golden names.”
Opening the “Storage Room,” he saw a pile of props faintly glowing.
Even Colin couldn’t help but feel an inexplicable sense of suffocation rising within him.
“It seems these things were probably derived from the abilities of First Level Containment Subjects far stronger than the ‘King of Mad Sounds,’ hmm, mid-level First Level or upper-level?”
Colin mused and felt they were just shy of “Level 0,” but also significantly stronger than the usual “Ancient Gods” he encountered.
They were certainly very powerful entities…
It’s just unclear where the company collected so many of these level Containment Subjects.
In addition, the only other non-Golden Card golden artifact, “Shield of Fair Judgment,” although not weak in its aura, stood among the other items in the “Storage Room.”
It was hard to say whether it looked a bit dimmer due to being outnumbered by the Golden Cards or if it genuinely fell short of the “Card Divine Kingdom” series.
“There are also differences among the golden artifacts.”
Colin took a look, then withdrew his gaze and started looking through the parchment, picking out a “team-type” task from those selected by his employees and casually calling on personnel to start on it.
Such tasks were usually never applied for…
Yet, with Colin leading, things started to change.
Thirty-person complex tasks that would normally take half a year to see a few volunteers were now filling up in mere seconds.
For the senior employees and some of the mid or low-level staff,
the past two months had been a roller-coaster ride of tasks.
High-level tasks that people wouldn’t dare look at twice for fear of being forced into became approachable.
And every time they performed, with Brother Shunzi behind them, they could band together and attempt the tasks to train themselves…
Even if they failed to complete the task, triggering some kind of “inevitable death” rule,
Brother Shunzi could easily break it now…
For the first time, the employees experienced the thrill of having a powerhouse lead the group.
In just two months, people’s comprehensive abilities improved faster than at any previous time.
Then, as a relentless “task completion” machine for a few more days, on the last day of the task requirements,
Colin had nearly enough Points, with just a small shortfall left. However, after carrying out “The Descent Project,” doing some second-hand dealer business, and borrowing a bit more Points…
“Finally, it’s enough.”
Colin’s eyes brightened, and he let out a long sigh of relief, looking at the four hundred thousand Points in his hand…
Some were his, others were borrowed from colleagues. At first, borrowing Points gave him some mental burden, but now… with the growing debt, he became numb.
Staking all his possessions, all for the chance to become C Level…
If he failed, he was prepared to face the consequences!
Taking a deep breath, he took out the shimmering “Time Stasis.”
After a quick confirmation that the Points and the vouchers matched the requirements…
“Upgrade!”
As the thought crossed his mind, all the Points and Golden Clearance Certificates were withdrawn, leaving Colin feeling an inexplicable emptiness.
Then “Time Stasis” began to float, blooming a golden light in mid-air.
The light, accompanied by the sound of a ticking ‘tick-tock’ reminiscent of a heartbeat, pulsed steadily…
And it became faster and sharper.
“Just don’t let me hear ‘repair failed’ now,” Colin thought, stirred by the emotion, feeling life would be unbearable if that happened.

chapters.title: Chapter 791 - 791 553 The Stasis that Impacts the Entire
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 791: Chapter 553 The “Stasis” that Impacts the Entire World!_2 Chapter 791: Chapter 553 The “Stasis” that Impacts the Entire World!_2 However, that bad outcome did not occur.
With a “clang,” a crisp sound appeared.
Colin saw that the completeness of the “Time Freeze” had reached 89%, gradually displaying its heart-palpitating might from above.
This might, merely a trickle seeping out, caused the frightened “Yukionna” to shrink into the refrigerator’s freezer compartment, hugging her head with both hands, tucking it between her knees, and curling into a shivering ball…
“Compared to the Golden Card I first obtained, it’s like a completely different card. However, this is the true might of a ‘Golden Artifact’!”
Colin stretched out his hand, grabbing the Golden Card floating in midair, intending to check the current information.
However, the moment his fingers touched the card, something unexpected occurred!
The recently repaired, nearly brand-new Golden Card, at this touch, released a wisp of its intrinsic might.
The next second, Colin saw an invisible force violently spread out, at an extremely fast speed, far exceeding its previous range, pulling everything Colin could perceive into “Stasis.”
This stasis was very brief, extremely brief, probably less than one ten-thousandth of a second.
But what shocked Colin was…
Its affected range was—the entire Earth?
“No, it might be even further. I can only sense that the Earth was affected; that’s my limit, not its.”
Following his shock, Colin felt a surge of excitement in his heart.
Does this mean that now the effect of the Golden Card could…
He hurriedly opened the item’s detail panel, his gaze moving to a few key entries.
“Time Stop Effect lasts for 13 seconds, effect range reaches 3,000 meters, three kilometers? Sigh…”
Colin suddenly felt disappointed; that moment made him think that the Golden Card could now freeze the whole Earth.
He didn’t expect it to be just three kilometers.
That was no longer unequivocally good or bad…
In high-level combat, many enemies could typically move beyond this distance in an instant, like Shana with her “Light Speed,” who couldn’t be confined without restriction.
But to restrict her, one must control her… leading to an endless loop.
Of course, not many anomalies or enemies were as fast as her, but they weren’t much slower either.
Colin couldn’t help but feel somewhat shortchanged, but setting aside the fact that the apparent effects weren’t as strong as anticipated, there was another unlisted detail, a significant increase in the strength of the Golden Card…
“Now, if this card were to encounter the power of a certain night and month, it should be able to stop it for at least a moment, not like before when they could pass almost unhindered during the Time Stop Effect.”
Thinking this, Colin nodded, feeling much reassured.
Just then, his phone suddenly vibrated. Colin picked it up and saw that it was a call from Old Master Wu.
“Did you just do something?” As soon as the call connected, the elderly man on the other end asked with a grave tone, as if he had encountered some tricky situation.
Did he somehow sense my recent Time Stop Effect? Old Master Wu is still impressive…
“Yes.”
Colin did not deny, but just as he nodded, he heard the other party interrupt and preemptively say:
“That’s fine then. I thought something formidable had occurred. Since it’s from your end, there should be no problem. You don’t need to tell me the specifics.”Upon hearing Colin’s confirmation, Old Master Wu’s tone was noticeably relieved.
He had felt, when that special and powerful force spread out, that somewhere on Earth, the source of all official extraordinary powers, a door sealed for who knows how long seemed to have loosened, beginning to be gradually pried open…
But fortunately, it was one of their own who had done it.
After a pause, Old Master Wu didn’t dwell on this matter further but continued with a cautious tone to admonish:
“I just felt that if nothing goes wrong, a suitable time should be approaching soon. It won’t be much longer, prepare yourself…”
“A certain time?” Colin echoed, puzzled.
“Your file for promotion to Level 6 should be getting approved soon…” Old Master Wu did not answer directly but hinted in an almost explicit manner over the phone.
Level 6 Personnel, “Lady Rabbit’s” request to investigate the “Book of Fate” behind-the-scenes and the status of the operation…
“‘Lady Rabbit’ mentioned that once the investigation starts yielding results, once we know the situation of that thing, there will definitely be a disastrous event erupting.”
Colin’s expression also turned solemn, and he couldn’t help but wonder what exactly would he have to face during the Level 6 Personnel promotion process? Why was it that others encountered no issues, but his involvement would lead to a major problem?
Was it because of his current Reservist status or something else?
Colin shared his doubts with Old Master Wu over the phone.
After a silence of a few seconds, the other party finally spoke, “I haven’t gone into specifics, because my situation doesn’t support me entering that place…”
“However, based on my abilities, I might indeed understand some things, but I am not at liberty to discuss them.”
“I can only tell you, some things, once known, can provoke dramatic changes, but it is because of this knowledge that we can begin to address the issues.”
Again, cryptic words… Colin felt helpless, and then he inquired further:
“What if I don’t go?”
“If you were still an ordinary person with a malignant tumor inside you, would you want to know now and take action at a critical moment, or remain ignorant, blundering through life until, when it’s too late, you finally realize you have cancer?”
Old Master Wu answered the question with a rhetorical question.

chapters.title: Chapter 792 - 792 553 The Stasis that Impacts the Entire
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 792: Chapter 553 The “Stasis” that Impacts the Entire World!_3 Chapter 792: Chapter 553 The “Stasis” that Impacts the Entire World!_3 Although he didn’t say it directly, Colin could sort of understand what Old Master Wu meant…
The investigation was probably akin to performing surgery and commencing treatment—
But as for whether the final outcome would be good or bad, no one could say for certain.
“I think I understand,” Colin said, holding his cell phone.
“Right, the time should be about a month later, which specific day, once I observe and find it suitable, I will call you. During this period, not only you but we should also make some preparations. In addition…”
“During this preparatory period, perhaps you can understand a bit about the changes this world has undergone under your influence since half a year ago when you brought the civilization remnants of the ‘Seventh Box Garden World’ here until now.”
“There are some things you should be clear about, to avoid problems later due to incomplete information.”
Listening to the old man’s arrangements, one sentence after another, Colin finally nodded, indicating he understood.
He roughly knew that there were some changes in society, but they did not seem particularly obvious; after all, most of the newly researched things were unlikely to reach the general public instantly.
They should still only be accessible in some cutting-edge areas, like certain research facilities, shelters, and so on…
After chatting for a while longer, Colin hung up the phone.
He sat in silence for quite a while, staring at the ceiling overhead.
Then, he blinked, pulled his thoughts back, and opened the parchment—now that the prop requirements were met, it was time to see what the next task entailed…
Upon opening the parchment, the overall content of “a special mission” hadn’t changed.
However, “Requirement 3” had been updated.
Seeing it, Colin felt it was within his expectations.
“Requirement 3”: In the coming period, understand the existence behind the “Book of Fate”…
…
“It’s definitely this thing,” Colin sighed.
Even though he had significantly improved, at this moment, he still felt inadequately prepared.
“About a month, with no specific time, but it should be right…”
Colin observed that there was not a little time left and also room for improvement during the preparation.
He opened the parchment, casually accepted a large-scale multiplayer team task, then went on the public channel to call for teammates.
“Here it comes, Brother Shunzi is back! Brother Shunzi is leading the brothers to form a group again!”
“Quick, grab a spot! My bag is starving for it.”
“This time I’m going to strip all the valuable stuff from the instance, leaving nothing behind!”
“Damn it, what’s this about? When did this instance get a rule that you can’t take items out? It’s totally bad luck!”
“Wait for me, Brother Shunzi. I’m almost D Level these days. Take me with you, take me with you…”
“+1, Brother Shunzi, I so want to improve, please, spare me a spot!”
“…”
The eager employees were enthusiastically greeting each other, competing for the task slots.
When the team was full, Colin informed everyone that from now on, boarding didn’t require the borrowing of 20% of the points, and the other half of the points that were deducted as a commission would no longer be taken but would start to offset the points borrowed earlier.
If they were willing, then come…
Facing the offer, the employees were too happy to refuse, how could they?
Soon, the event began, the personnel came together in both spatial and temporal aspects, Colin looked at the dozens of “senior” employees and said, “There’s one more thing, I couldn’t mention it in the chat channel, but now is the right time to say it…”
..

chapters.title: Chapter 793 - 793 554 The Beginning of Catastrophic Events_1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 793: Chapter 554 The Beginning of Catastrophic Events!_1 Chapter 793: Chapter 554 The Beginning of Catastrophic Events!_1 “What’s going on?”
In the train carriage headed to a large team mission, about thirty employees sat in their seats, staring intently at Brother Shunzi as if they were students listening to a teacher, awaiting his speech.
“If nothing unexpected happens, we may soon face a catastrophic event of massive proportions…”
Colin paused, then emphasized:
“This won’t take long, if you have any preparations, try to complete them within the next month, whether you want to leave Earth at a certain time or take some other measures…”
Hearing Colin’s words, except for a small number of “The Descent Project” personnel, who had frequent contact with Colin, the faces of the others clearly showed a realization that “this is indeed true!”
As for the “end of the world,” the employees were not too surprised since the related rhetoric had always been present.
And after executing various missions, they, whose spiritual intuition had far exceeded that of ordinary people, often felt a premonition of an impending storm.
These issues usually seemed like widely-circulated but uncertain matters; the rhetoric was always there, just without concrete proof…
Until now, with the appearance of Brother Shunzi, a heavyweight, all the “rumors” seemed to have finally found a definitive assertion.
“What will happen?”
After snapping out of an indescribable shock, one of the employees couldn’t help but ask immediately.
“I’m not sure about that… What I can say for certain is that when the time comes, there will definitely be various terrifying anomalies resurfacing or invading, but exactly which ones, I can’t say for sure…”
During this speech, Colin recalled some recent frenzied missions.
As a part-time “cross-world traveler,” he found that Earth had far more and more complex anomalies than many other places.
Even the most minor anomalies, if anywhere else, might be considered a small “elite monster.”
But here, they were inexplicably like trivial fish…
Their performance or strength always seemed inferior to that of anomalies from the outside world.
Colin had always found it odd, not knowing the reason, but as one mission after another was carried out crazily, he gradually developed some answers.
The reason for this situation might be because there are too many higher-dimensional anomalies at home!
It’s precisely because there are so many of them that lower-level anomalies are unintentionally suppressed, hence the bizarre situation where many anomalies have a decent status but lack the ability to show it.
It’s like in real life, some regional tycoons, having ten or eight million in their small towns, are already among the countable wealthy and can speak loudly.
But once these people go to the capital of a country, they’ll find that there are many like them, worth ten or eight million, as common as stray dogs, and above them, there are those with wealth amounting to billions or even more terrifying figures…
So their voices are inadvertently suppressed.
Perhaps in ordinary times, this would somehow be a good thing.
It could make anomalies easier to handle.
After all, our personnel, perhaps thanks to “Bonfire Company,” haven’t seen their strength diminish too much.
But now, when everything is about to erupt.
The benefits we “enjoyed” usually must all be spit out at once…
After thinking it over, Colin looked at the person who asked the first question, and said, “However, what will happen then isn’t completely without a trace; we’ve executed quite a few ‘Descent’ incidents recently… When you have time, you can organize and review the things you encountered during those missions.”
“Understood…” The employee nodded in acknowledgment.
During this time, Colin executed missions frenziedly, including several that were set in post-disaster scenarios, inadvertently also enhancing everyone’s knowledge and psychological preparation for the upcoming end times.
Seeing everyone calm down, Colin continued:
“Besides internal matters, it’s likely that distant worlds beyond us will also cast their gaze, so it’s not just internal troubles but external threats too…”
“External threats” may come slower than “internal troubles,” but they are inevitably on their way.
However, “external threats” and “internal troubles” are likely not on the same level; high-level beings are never a unified entity, and when they are trapped in a cage, they guard against each other to prevent anyone from closing the door after getting out, resulting in internal strife.
Not to mention if they bring in “external threats” for assistance; they’ll probably guard even more fiercely…
The conflicts among them may provide some space for exploitation… Thinking this, Colin heard an employee inquire:
“Does Brother Shunzi know about these ‘external threats’?”
Colin pondered for two seconds and then replied:
“I do know some things, but I know they’re not an issue since I can cut off their remote corruption through my power, but it’s not the same for you…”
Being seasoned employees with considerable experience, upon hearing his words, they prudently refrained from asking further questions, not being curiously fervent to ask “Why is that?” and the like.
If they were all that curious, they wouldn’t have survived to this level.
For a while, silence fell over the place as if everyone were contemplating the impending doomsday.
Even though Brother Shunzi hadn’t explained why he was certain that disaster was imminent.
No one chose to question his words.
Known for his integrity, Brother Shunzi might make mistakes, but he would never deliberately mislead them, and besides, there was nothing to gain from such deception…

chapters.title: Chapter 794 - 794 554
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 794: 554 Chapter 794: 554 Colin didn’t say a word, just gazed out the window at the surging grey fog and, seeing that they wouldn’t be arriving anytime soon, withdrew his gaze.
After giving everyone present about ten minutes to think, he suddenly stretched out his hand and knocked twice on the seat inside the compartment.
“Ting Ting!”
The crisp sound brought everyone back to their senses, and their gazes once again turned toward him.
“Having addressed this matter, let’s take this opportunity to discuss another related issue, about our relations with the officials…”
Colin slowly said, “From now on, if necessary, you may proactively contact the officials…”
Upon hearing this, some employees who had little interaction with Colin immediately thought of a phrase:
Brother Shunzi was placated!
It was unclear whether this was by coercion or not; no, with Brother Shunzi’s strength, it seemed that if he were unwilling, no one could force him…
Meanwhile, several of Colin’s subordinates who often went to “The Descent Project” weren’t surprised at all.
Considering the things Brother Shunzi typically brought out, people had long assumed that he might have had dealings with the officials long ago…
“Whether you want to leave or stay, you can seek their help, share information with them. In this regard, I can vouch for you to ensure you can fairly trade for what you need without being forced into doing something against your will,” he said.
After Colin briefly finished speaking and gave a few seconds for people to think, he added, “Of course, I can only ensure roughly fair dealings within our domain, promise there are no ill intentions, but I can’t guarantee the entire world.”
The internal affairs of the “Global Supernatural Alliance” are relatively complex, and not everything is good. Of course, this doesn’t mean everything outside is bad, but when it comes to his home, Colin’s influence is definitely high enough.
No one dares to lightly violate the “promises” he makes.
In this regard, with Old Master Wu and a host of internal “Fate Propeller” monitors, it’s ensured that even if someone harbors ulterior motives, they can be dealt with immediately.
Outside, although Colin could still exert influence and find solutions, it wasn’t as absolute.
The fear lay in the unknown.
Or, by the time he found out, some tragedies had already occurred.
Even though the likelihood was very low, it wasn’t impossible—some people’s selfishness far exceeded the average person’s imagination.
No sooner had he finished speaking than someone immediately asked, “Then… can people from other countries come to seek help?”
“Yes,” Colin nodded.
As the dangerous time drew near, he had to consolidate all possible forces.
Many long-standing D Level employees of the company were quite reluctant to have anything to do with the officials for various reasons, but some of the most common and crucial were fears of being forced into doing things they didn’t want to…
Ultimately, when the time came, it boiled down to either running away or staying, and from there they narrowed down their options.
There were always choices offered by the officials that would suit them.
…
It was while they were speaking that in a corner of the Earth, within a highly secret, independent spatial domain.
Not long before, as the effect of “Stasis” spread, countless incorporeal rats squealed frantically, making uncontrollable and unanimous noises that lasted a long while, eventually waking a rat as big as a person at the center position.
Its face faintly bore human features, looking eerie and paradoxical.
Yet, having just awoken from a deep slumber, its gaze seemed somewhat vacant.
“Who has qualified…”
After a good while, as if it had sensed the outside world, the air around its mouth vibrated as it murmured:
“Is it that dazed young ‘Flame Bearer’ reservist? Is the ‘appointed time’ finally about to arrive…”
The door that could reveal the truest facet of the world was about to open.
All that was needed was for someone to step through and commence the ultimate battle!
Afterward, its gaze shifted to the side, to the vat filled with various mysterious materials, where the “fuel” upon meeting its gaze either screamed in fear, cursed in resentment, roared furiously, or uttered perplexed questions…
It seemed they wanted to understand why it had betrayed them.
Some of the incorporeal rats around it, hearing these sounds, exploded like overinflated balloons.
The big rat looked into the vat without emotion.
For the sake of this vat of super dye capable of depicting all things, it had given up everything.
“No matter how you view me, as long as I succeed, all sacrifices are permissible. I will prove to everyone that I am right…”
“Only I can lead everyone to ultimate victory in the terrifying disputes of the future!”
“Only I am truly correct!”
“Not those fools who do not understand the current situation and still nurture unrealistic dreams.”
“Only I can lead humanity to victory, to become the supreme and greatest species!”
“…”
It stood erect, its massive rat body towering as it waved its hands, human-like in their dexterity, in front of a vat of dye mixed with countless things, proclaiming to the contents within.
…
