Another thirty-some days flashed by. Colin, having just completed his seventh proactive mission of the week and without a moment to rest, was getting acquainted with the current technological progress of the world when his phone suddenly received a message.
The message came from Old Master Wu, and upon reading its contents, his pupils shrank.
“In seven days, I will lead you to that place, to become a Level 6 Personnel. During this period, make your final preparations… We’re going to face it.”
At the mention of “it,” Colin’s breath caught, and he was suddenly gripped by an overwhelming sense of asphyxiation, a strange tingling sensation on his scalp.
It wasn’t the oppressive presence of any creature…
Instead, it was purely a colossal psychological pressure!
“Huff.”
Colin took a deep breath and slowly exhaled, finally managing to respond with a simple “Okay.”
“Right, from now on, I need to keep an eye on some critical matters, make sure there are no mishaps. I won’t be able to come out. If there are any substantial issues, you can contact Xu Duojin.”
“No problem,” Colin nodded.
After the brief exchange, Colin returned to his bed, laying face down, and dragged a pillow over to clutch it tightly.
Holding his breath for a good while to alleviate the pressure, he then sat up again and started organizing the things he needed to do.
“The reality-based issues have already been addressed officially, and I’ve gotten a fairly good grasp on the things I needed to understand…”
Colin thought. Using the various Other World knowledge he’d collected, the officials had created quite a lot of things.
In general scientific areas, things like superconductivity and miniaturized reactors were not a big deal, their feasibility having been successfully verified…
If time had not been of the essence, it was estimated that within decades, development could have spread into space.
However, even now the situation wasn’t too bad, having spread to most of the major sanctuaries…
Besides, there were various mysticism techniques. Colin was surprised to find that a technique similar to the “Twilight Angel” had been successfully replicated and integrated with the “artifacts” approach to become a system.
They succeeded in transforming a powerful Level 2 Containment Subject.
Specifically named “Fetal Angel,” its abilities were relative to “omnipotence,” but seemed to primarily relate to thought, consciousness, and the collective ocean.
It was said that, theoretically, as long as an ordinary human without extraordinary power was alive within the realm of Earth, it would be very difficult for the Fetal Angel to be extinguished.
Of course, this theory hadn’t been tested in real combat with Level One Containment Subjects, so it was uncertain whether it was truly reliable.
Besides, in this “angelic series,” there seemed to be “Plague Angel,” “Ocean Angel,” “Gun and War Angel,” “Dominion and Distortion Angel,” and the like, though none were as successful…
Beyond these, there were many other mysticism techniques worth paying attention to.
It felt truly powerful, but compared to the company’s technology, there was still much to be desired. During this period, there was a “Shadow Angel” that got out of control, and it was he who had casually dismantled it with his bare hands.
The situation wasn’t stable, so after understanding the basic circumstances, Colin didn’t pay it much further mind.
“Other than that, it’s the matters of ‘World Code-13’ and ‘World Code-4’…”
Colin sat, thinking. Over in World Code, they had already gotten on the right track thanks to their efforts over this period.
The food issue had been basically resolved.
People, having absorbed a few hundred thousand refugees, formed a special theocratic nation with a belief in “Bonfire,” guided by scientific values able to explain everything…
The only shortfall might be a lack of sufficient high-end power.
But as long as they stayed tucked away in their corner, and with the protection of “Bonfire,” there wasn’t too much to worry about…
What he needed to do was probably just say a simple “farewell,” and that would be about it.
After all, the preparations weren’t done now, but had started nearly three months ago, addressing various matters up until the present.
“I wonder how long this major event will last…”

chapters.title: Chapter 795 - 795 555 The Forbidden Knowledge that Made God
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 795: Chapter 555 The Forbidden Knowledge that Made “God” Lose Control. _1 Chapter 795: Chapter 555 The Forbidden Knowledge that Made “God” Lose Control. _1 World Code -13, originally a small “Light” Church chapel, now the Great “Bonfire” Cathedral outside.
Shana and Colin walked shoulder to shoulder on the path back to the cathedral hall…
All along the way, although Colin beside her occasionally greeted believers without revealing anything in particular, Shana still keenly sensed that the atmosphere seemed somewhat heavy—
There had been signs of this starting from some time ago.
However, the Bonfire Envoy had not explained the situation to her.
Without asking, Shana walked beside him, chatting idly now and then; she tilted her head up slightly, her delicate and fair face adorned with a pair of pure ice-blue eyes that looked towards the sacred cathedral spewing flames ahead.
Compared to earlier, the cathedral had expanded from a few hundred square meters to nearly thirty thousand square meters, and to a grand structure over a hundred meters tall. Its imposing presence aside, large-caliber cannons protruded from some “mechanical activity windows” on each level…
There were over a hundred of these guns alone on the building’s five levels, capable of harming Third Level Containment Subjects.
They would be difficult for anyone to withstand if fired in unison.
Added to that, the myriad of mysterious inscriptions, the defenses and might of this construct speak for themselves.
The entire “Bonfire Church” was basically completed within just a few months, which certainly could not have been achieved under normal circumstances.
Even if the two of them could use extraordinary means to erect a bare framework, they could not have accomplished something so refined and complete.
Yet Colin mentioned the need for a semi-permanent structure…
Thinking it over, Shana decided to take a risk and used a little trick with Colin.
That is, during the previous period, they ventured deep into the heart of the “Catastrophe of the Magic Fog” to a ruin she had discovered earlier and carried out a war sanctuary from the era of the Holy Light Court, eventually placing it here.
After some modifications and combining it with Level 5 Bonfire discussed by Colin, they achieved the current Great Bonfire Cathedral.
Using “Bonfire” as the energy core for the “war sanctuary”, they compensated for the missing power and thus reactivated the ancient war fortress’s mighty capabilities.
The unexpected compatibility between “Light” and “Flame” was evident.
As for whether this approach might draw opposition from “Light” believers…
Shana felt that in this regard, she should still have some say.
If she declared it as an ancient unclaimed artifact found in ruins, then it stood as unclaimed. After all, her highest surface status granted her final interpretive authority over various matters within the “Light” Church.
And as for the outside-elbowing behavior of their own “Saintess”, they all turned a blind eye and said little more.
After all, if you don’t let her create a stir, she’ll come to create a stir for you.
Choosing the lesser of two evils, plus with the Great Bonfire Cathedral poised as a formidable barrier against the divine calamity of “Magic Fog” before the disaster, it provided them substantial relief from pressure.
So, in the end, no one stood up to oppose it.
Walking into the grand hall, through the lengthy corridors, and arriving at the magnificent burning bonfire, Shana blinked, turned sideways, and asked Colin, who was somewhat “taciturn”, in a gentle tone:
“You seem to be troubled by something?”
Hearing her words, Colin did not respond immediately; he was silent for a few seconds before saying, “It’s not exactly a concern, it’s just that there may be a rather difficult mission coming up soon, and I might not be able to come here for a while.”
“Very difficult?”
Shana pulled up a chair for Colin, gestured him to sit, and then took a seat herself, sitting upright with her legs together.
So far, she had rarely seen Colin frown over a mission; given that it was singled out, this time the task would likely pose a significant challenge…
Shana pressed her lips together lightly and asked gently, “Is there anything I can do to help?”
“It’s hard to say…” Colin shook his head, took a seat casually, adjusted the collar of his custom-fitted “Bonfire” Envoy robe, and habitually crossed his legs.
Under normal circumstances, Shana could support by giving BUFFs or providing sufficiently powerful avatars.
Some of her powerful avatars were almost equal to her main body and could even contain “Level One Containment Subject” entities. Her power had a high origin, but it was not plentiful yet, similar to a “Flame Bearer”.
Using avatars of that caliber came at a cost.
And Colin anticipated that Shana probably wouldn’t make it this time…
But he was not here to seek help; after thinking it over, Colin took a bone spur filled with black rifts from his pocket and handed it over:
“I might not have many scenarios to use this item anymore, you can have it back…”
Upon seeing Colin take out the bone spur, Shana paused for a few seconds, then gently rose, extended her hands to carefully take it, and wrapped it in a clean white handkerchief.
After completing this, Shana looked at the man who had not yet answered her question directly, “It appears this event will be very difficult.”
Otherwise, knowing this man, he would not have abruptly returned the Holy Remains to her.
“It might be somewhat challenging…”
Colin nodded his head and was about to introduce another Shield Emblem-like item when Shana preempted him by saying:
“Keep that Shield Emblem… When I gave you this object, my main hope was for you to master it.”
Pausing for a moment, she looked into Colin’s eyes and continued, “This is an artifact representing a part of the ‘Virtue’ characteristics of the ‘King of Knights’…”

chapters.title: Chapter 796 - 796 555 The Forbidden Knowledge that Causes
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 796: Chapter 555 The Forbidden Knowledge that Causes “God” to Lose Control. _2 Chapter 796: Chapter 555 The Forbidden Knowledge that Causes “God” to Lose Control. _2 As for which Virtue it was, he had used it for so long that there was no need to go into detail…
Colin nodded, not surprised by this.
The materials that could become part of the Golden Artifact were mostly at the level of a First Level Containment Subject.
And that ancient legend of the “King of Knights” was a terrifying force unto himself, combining the eight “Virtues,” his strength even surpassing many First Level Containment Subjects—that part of the story was told to Colin by the King of Savage Sound.
In other words, he or she was on par with a god.
Moreover, because he was able to understand the notes on the artifact, he had a clearer understanding of many details than Shana did, knowing that the artifact was supposedly handcrafted by the enigmatic “Mister Huang He”…
“And the reason I want you to take this away is somewhat related to the current ‘King’ of The Kingdom of Knights, he harbors the desire to become a ‘True God’ once again and has planned some things that involve the use of this Shield Emblem…”
“But… I don’t think he’s worthy.”
Shana gave a negative assessment of today’s “King”: “He has some plans, which I don’t quite approve of, so I’ve always wanted to find the right opportunity to discard the shield, but I never had the chance, until you showed up…”
Upon hearing this, Colin suddenly understood why the “Shield of Fairness Adjudication” noted that using it more than once in “World Code-13” would attract certain beings…
Turns out, that’s the reason—using it too much would likely summon that certain someone from The Kingdom of Knights…
No—on second thought, based on the descriptions, it would summon the actual “King of Knights”!
“What’s the situation with that former ‘King of Knights’?” Colin asked curiously.
“His situation is very unclear; rumors suggest he fell in a distant past even earlier than the ‘Holy Light Court,’ but there are forbidden texts that indicate he also left traces of activity during the disasters caused by the ‘Holy Light Court’…”
“There are many doubts about him, but that’s not too strange, after all, such beings are very difficult to completely extinguish without specific measures…”
Shana casually mentioned the extremely “heretical” information insider The Kingdom of Knights.
Such words could only be shared with members of the “Bonfire Company” like Colin.
Even though the successive “Light” Saints destroyed the “Holy Light Court” with the hope of liberating the mysteries, the overall situation is still not great up to now.
As Colin listened to Shana’s words, he put away the “Shield of Fairness Adjudication” and couldn’t help but think to himself, ‘In a world where gods truly exist, unless it’s like the Lady of Thorns where a True God leads a rebellion, some things are indeed difficult to break…’
“Additionally…”
Shana changed the topic and lifted the Bone Spur wrapped in white silk:
“This Holy Remains has some potential that has not yet been shown; it might also be useful.”
As she spoke, Shana seemed to have made a decision, picked up the Bone Spur, and weak strands of pure white light began to flow from her hand into the Bone Spur, with mysterious glowing patterns moving on it as if some restrictions were being lifted…
“Saintess Krixis once said: ‘Those who light the way for others should also be bathed in light themselves.’
Shana placed the Bone Spur with some of its restrictions lifted in front of her: “I think, if it really comes to that moment, she might not ignore your plight…”
“Lighting the way for others? That’s a bit too much praise for me; I just don’t want my home to be stolen…” Colin pursed his lips.
He couldn’t quite articulate his thoughts, but whatever the reason…
He didn’t want to and couldn’t leave!
Colin had a premonition that if he failed to protect his home this time, no matter where he fled to, the outcome wouldn’t be favorable.
And it might involve his friends and so on…
Because as a “Flamebearer” Reserves, his location had been exposed.
Moreover, there were too many people back home, and no matter how much preparation was done, some would inevitably be neglected, and if he, a key combatant, left, the situation might become extremely dire.
Although Colin never thought that he could stir great upheavals on his own, what if—just what if saving the world was missing just him?
Seeing Colin’s “stubbornness,” Shana shook her head slightly, a tender smile spreading across her face. She reached out and took his hand, which was larger than hers, and placed the tip of the Bone Spur in his palm, not continuing this futile conversation with Colin:
“If you ever need me, just call, and no matter what, I’ll come to help you.”
The fair-skinned hands were soft, making it hard to believe that those hands had killed many people, as well as a large number of living anomalies.
“…” Colin opened his mouth but ultimately didn’t say much, choosing to accept the gesture and nodding in acknowledgment.
“Then, as for this artifact, should you need it, it can unleash half of, um, according to the description, a First Level Containment Subject of the natural phenomenon type. It’s in an uncontrollable state, and you can briefly manipulate it to confront your enemy. However, you need to be careful of the timing of its use, or it could harm you…”
“Half?” Colin noted the term.
Shana nodded lightly, explaining, “The being that is bound within was said to be a True God once worshipped by a now-extinct church in ancient times,
“Back then, it seems it became uncontrollable due to engagement with some forbidden knowledge possibly related to ‘Divinity’ while combating the ‘Holy Light Court,’ or for some other reason, and turned into ‘Rain of Filth’…
“Eventually, it was sealed by the ‘Holy Light Court,’ but it broke free centuries ago, corrupting many creatures. It was subdued along with the ‘Light’ Saint, Saintess Krixis, in a sacrifice-based sealing… That’s all the information I could gather about it.”
“Forbidden knowledge that could cause a god to lose control of ‘Divinity’?” Colin was startled.
What had it done? Had it not been peeking at the true nature of the ‘Night’ or the ‘Red Moon’?
Otherwise, Colin really didn’t know of any other forbidden knowledge that could cause a First Level Containment Subject to go out of control…
“I don’t know either…” Shana bit her lip, shaking her head.
Saints usually keep to themselves, and the information they retain is usually brief; she only knew some general life stories.
“Alright.” Holding the Bone Spur, Colin could indeed feel that with just a thought from him,
a terrifying existence would emerge from it…
If there were no strange hidden details within, then it was very likely that ‘True God’ that had seen something unclean.
For a short time, he could achieve a certain and brief guidance… but couldn’t do much.
It could be considered a ‘last resort’ in the general sense…
But also a clear double-edged sword, because if not used well, it would unleash a catastrophe.
“Thank you…” Once Colin roughly grasped the essence of the content, he sincerely expressed his thanks.
Shana raised her hand to adjust a stray lock of hair, tilting her head slightly, “You seem to still have two days left in your descent this time, right?”
“Yes.”
“Oh…” Shana nodded thoughtfully, not saying much more.
Meanwhile, Colin looked towards the other side of the great hall, to the figure who was sweeping in the distance, all the while pricking up his ears and sneaking glances over here: “Little Red, come here, stop pretending to sweep…”
The entire great hall was illuminated by the bonfire, usually not even a mote of dust to be seen.
“Oh.” Little Red quickly stepped forward, placing the broom back in its place properly, and then scurried over with her short legs.
Compared to several months ago, when she was first plucked from the refugees, Little Red obviously looked much better, her face no longer dirty and covered with new and old wrinkled wounds. Now, she wore a black dress with a scattered floral pattern, her black hair neatly combed by Shana, her clean and tidy face young and vibrant, and in her pure black eyes shimmered a spirited luster.
As the little girl with rare pure black hair and eyes in this world approached, Colin reached out to vigorously rub her head:
“Is there something you want to say?”
Seeing the hint of red flickering in and out of the girl’s eyes, Colin knew she probably had something to say.
The young girl, until now, whenever she had something on her mind or a noticeable shift in her emotions, would have a slight color change in her eyes, her thoughts relatively easy to guess.
Of course, she now had much better control than before; she was no longer as dangerous as she used to be.
…
…
Wait, there is another chapter.

chapters.title: Chapter 797 - 797 556 Light Saintess Shanas Gift._1
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 797: Chapter 556 “Light” Saintess Shana’s Gift._1 Chapter 797: Chapter 556 “Light” Saintess Shana’s Gift._1 “You, you don’t seem very happy lately…” the little girl hesitated and stammered.
“Ah?” Colin was taken aback.
He had not thought his demeanor had shown it, and while it was one thing for Shana to see through him—she could, if she wished, directly peer into a person’s soul and decipher what they were thinking by subtle changes—it was quite another for the average person, let alone Colin, to keep any secrets from her…
Little Red could see it… Was he being too obvious?
“Yes.” Little Red nodded vigorously.
Colin stroked his chin, “There might be a bit of a troublesome matter to attend to, so I guess I won’t be coming around for a while.”
Upon hearing this, Little Red clenched her fists and looked anxious, “Will it be a long time? Will it be dangerous? Can I help with anything?”
“I can’t say for sure…”
Watching the girl’s barrage of questions, Colin couldn’t help but chuckle silently, pulling out a big bag of Bunny brand milk candy from his pocket:
“Don’t worry about helping. Just focus on growing up and learning. And don’t think about slacking off while I’m away.”
Little Red, holding her favorite milk candy, still seemed uneasy, but nodded, “Oh, I won’t slack off. I’m about to master high school knowledge…”
Colin smiled, looking at the girl who had grown up to his chest, and thought of some things about her.
Without a doubt, the search by Sister Shana had revealed some truths about her eyes.
In the past history, these had indeed triggered certain traces, but without concrete evidence.
But… it seemed to have been neutralized for now…
And the one who seemed to have taken care of these matters was an old acquaintance of Colin’s, Rosen.
There could be some great terror involved, or there could be nothing, simply dealt with on the spot.
In any case, it had been handled quite thoroughly, with not much information leaking out.
To really understand, according to the snippets found by Shana, one would probably need to find the “Seed of Light” which recorded everything about this place…
But, even the “branch office” only had a bit of location information about this thing.
“Lady Rabbit” showed not the slightest intention to investigate; given the importance of this matter, even a sliver of a chance would have prompted “Lady Rabbit” to start making plans.
If she showed no action, it must mean it was either extremely difficult, or simply impossible, or perhaps it didn’t hold much significance.
Colin himself felt that even a “Flame Bearer” might not be able to find it.
Therefore, it was hard to delve too deeply into Little Red’s matters.
In any case, it seemed there was a relatively stable development, and possibly even the control of some extra powerful supernatural methods. Overall, it didn’t seem to be a big problem.
As thoughts flickered, Colin came back to his senses and, seeing the worry on the little girl’s face, he shook his head and smiled:
“Don’t worry too much. You can have two pieces of this candy a day. By the time you finish all the candy inside, I should be back.”
Saying so, he put a bag of Bunny brand milk candy into Little Red’s arms.
This bag had at least sixty or seventy pieces. Considering past incidents, it would take at most ten days to a fortnight, and at most a month, to resolve them.
At least, the most intense moment should have passed, and he could find the time to continue “The Descent Project.”
“Oh, okay, thank you, big brother…” Holding the milk candy she could never tire of, Little Red’s voice was muffled, and despite her worries, she wasn’t particularly happy.
At that moment, she suddenly felt a deep need for strength…
Strength like Sister Shana’s, even surpassing hers, otherwise, she was powerless to do anything!
As she pondered, a faint red hue began to glow from the depths of her dark pupils.
But before the red could rise further, Colin patted her head, rubbing it in a way that dissipated the redness:
“Go get the kitchen to prepare some ingredients, we’re having hotpot here…”
…
A day later, the day before he was to leave, Shana suddenly called Colin to the front of the Great Bonfire Cathedral.
There were hardly any people around at that time.
“These are the ‘Marks of Light’ for when the time comes. Even if you use them every day, they should last you around one or two months…” Shana said, pulling out some Golden Marks she had prepared in advance from her pocket.
Each the size of a palm, there were ten in total, with pure white light coursing over them, exuding an extraordinary aura.
“You… made preparations in advance?” Colin didn’t refuse and took the Marks as usual, but seemed surprised at the quantity.
These high-level Marks, it seemed, took Shana a day or two of complete concentration to craft each one.
“Yes, after all, our path won’t always be smooth. There will always be sudden moments, like now, which is why I usually work on crafting some items with multiple bodies, to avoid finding myself in an awkward situation. Fortunately, they have come in handy. Of course, just as unfortunately, they have come in handy…”
Shana spoke softly, her words seeming to carry a breath of spiritual purification.
Without waiting for Colin to speak further, she bit her lip hesitantly, yet without pausing her movements, she rummaged in her “Storage Room” and took out a pristine, white bone like mutton-fat jade and handed it to Colin.
“What’s this…”
Colin took it and could feel that the bone contained very strong “Light” blessings, skills, and so on.
The intensity of which even surpassed the combined total of the ten Golden Marks!

chapters.title: Chapter 798 - 798 556 Light Saintess Shanas Gift._2
chapters.content: ﻿Chapter 798: Chapter 556 “Light” Saintess Shana’s Gift._2 Chapter 798: Chapter 556 “Light” Saintess Shana’s Gift._2 As for it itself, it felt a bit like a Bone Spur, and similarly came from female skeletal remains. Colin, with his extensive experience, could even recognize at a glance that it should belong to the little finger of the left hand… ‘Is it the remains of Saintess Krixis again?’ The first thing that came to Colin’s mind was the saint from a century ago, but something didn’t seem quite right; this phalanx looked as if it came from an important figure but appeared new, not from the era of “Shang-Zhou,” but rather as if from last week. And inexplicably, it felt familiar, as though he had seen it somewhere before… No, more like he had seen it frequently? Huh? Wait? Colin suddenly realized something, casting a glance toward Shana’s hand, and a bold guess formed in his mind. Noticing Colin’s gaze, Shana subconsciously clenched her fist, hiding it beneath the long sleeves of her spacious Church robe, and unusually, both hands retreated behind her back… At any other time, this gesture would have seemed quite natural, and unlikely to arouse any suspicion. But now… “Ah, yes, hmm hmm…” Shana’s face reddened slightly, the leaping flames casting a reddish glow on her cheeks, as she stammered awkwardly for a moment, but she then composed herself and explained, “Once before, during an incident, my entire arm got frostbitten. I concentrated all the contamination into one finger to save the hand, but the finger couldn’t be saved—it was frozen off…” As she spoke, she seemed about to mimic Colin’s gesture of scratching the back of her head to ease an indefinable embarrassment, but seemed to reconsider, finding the gesture impolite to others, and dropped her raised hand back down before continuing, “Logically, I should have completely destroyed it, but it seemed a bit… well, wasteful, so I purified it and kept it. I meant to use it myself as material, but there was never really an opportunity to do so…” After listening to her explanation, Colin’s mouth fell open slightly, a complex sense of shock in his heart. ‘Uh, I feel like you should have been the ‘Flame Bearer’ Reservist. Maybe you’d have summoned the ‘Primordial Fire’ on the spot…’ Yet, in the face of the Saintess’s gift, he was deeply moved. Not just for its effects, but also because of the immense risks associated with the act itself… In the realm of the mystical, a single hair could lead to one’s demise. How much more so for a phalanx that came from oneself, personally gifted without much alteration? Especially the act of gifting itself. In the realms of the mystical, the risk was exceptionally high… And in the face of such a gift, Colin felt words of thanks were hardly enough. Colin raised an eyebrow, “That thing that hurt you back then…” “I’ve mostly taken care of it,” Shana began to say but then smiled and suggested, “How about we deal with it together when you return?” That thing certainly hadn’t been completely eradicated; the place where it was located was an area of “descent” for missions, not easy to access, but if they really wanted to go, there was always a way… “All right.” Colin nodded, etching the matter deeply in his mind. “This domain, the believers here, and Little Red, or… many unrealized plans, they all need you…” As Shana spoke, her figure grew larger, and huge pairs of pure white Wings of Light sprouted from behind her. They encompassed the entire hall as they flapped, before gathering to envelop Colin. The sacred light feathers that filled the sky seemed to descend from heaven, with the sound of young children’s hymns echoing in the ear. The soft yet icy feathers brushed his cheeks like hands… In that moment, Colin almost seemed to see a majestic construction clad in white with generous adornments of gold, atop the clouds; at the end of a wide corridor, a blinding light as bright as the sun hung from the heavens. And beneath this light, there seemed to be an indistinct glowing figure… Yet, when Colin subconsciously tried to widen his eyes, urging flames within them, attempting to see the details of that figure, all the “illusion” had already dissipated. Now he could only see Shana in front of him, dressed in a white and gold-edged outfit… There seemed to be an overlap between the two, and yet not exactly. And Colin felt as if he had just received a special blessing, suddenly filled with a sense of calm and tranquility. He was snapped out of this indescribable sense of spiritual comfort when he heard Shana earnestly say, “Anyway, I’m very strong, even stronger than you think. If you need help, remember, you must call for me!” Colin blinked, the flames swirling in his eyes, and nodded, “I understand.” Although he was still unclear about exactly what he had seen. But he knew well that it must contain some of Shana’s greatest secrets as a Saint. Of course, much of it was also about making her capabilities known, so that if he needed her help, he wouldn’t hesitate. The brief conversation came to an end. There was still some time left, and Colin needed to gather the believers, to also give them some explanations. Whether it was because of that “just in case,” or because he might not be able to return for a long time, He felt he owed them an explanation… Otherwise, Colin didn’t want to come back from Earth after clearing up an incident only to find that people here had started some sort of “God has abandoned us” scenario. Oftentimes, conflicts arise from misunderstandings… Colin had seen such things more than once or twice in other worlds.

chapters.title: Chapter 799 - 799 556 Light Saintess Shanas Gift._3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 799: Chapter 556 “Light” Saintess Shana’s Gift._3 Chapter 799: Chapter 556 “Light” Saintess Shana’s Gift._3 Resolving the issue actually wasn’t particularly difficult.
After Colin completed the “Thorn World” mission, he had discussed this matter with the “Thorn Lady” who disliked wearing shoes, inside a carriage.
Her advice was just to speak plainly.
Whatever problems might arise, whatever could happen, if there was an opportunity, just directly speak about it in advance.
You need to express your intentions clearly and explicitly, without too much euphemism, otherwise, people will wildly misinterpret them.
As for the Church’s “Gods” encountering challenges…
There’s no need to pay special attention to it.
After all, they don’t really need to create a supreme Church with absolute faith; they aren’t pursuing that believers must feel they are absolutely supreme, absolutely omnipotent…
Having been a “World Administrator” for countless years and with ample experience, the “Thorn Lady” quite dismissively told him:
“In the early days, I cared about these things like you do, but later I found that holding onto these things really doesn’t mean much. In the end, if the believers understand, then they understand; if they don’t, they’ll switch allegiances. It’s not a big problem.”
The main philosophy of her “Thorn Temple” was to take it or leave it—if you don’t believe, just go out the door and turn right to another place.
As long as you don’t believe in something twisted, praying to a chicken isn’t a problem, at most they would grumble that eighteen years of mandatory education didn’t teach well, not even knowing to worship something proper. Then they’d pull aside the employee responsible for education and give them a scolding just like that.
This didn’t hinder her Church from being the largest, nor did it stop them from continuing their work to enlighten and guide, save the world, attract more like-minded individuals, and pursue more things that were beneficial to the company, beneficial to humanity…
At this moment, Colin was controlling a majestic “Flame Giant” over five hundred meters tall, standing upon the Earth, conveying relevant information about the current event to all the congregated believers…
Shana was adjusting the brightness of the entire area on the side, ensuring Colin looked even more majestic and sacred without causing discomfort due to the excessively dazzling flames, preventing direct gaze.
After listening to Colin’s words, many believers showed reluctance on their faces, crazily wanting to help, expressing their willingness to do their part, to contribute everything including their lives, for the Church that saved them from the wilderness of ignorance.
Some even felt so distressed upon hearing that the “great” being was in trouble and they were unable to help, that they burst into tears and even fainted from crying…
‘They’re a little too excited.’
Colin began to use the comforting words he had previously prepared with professionals from Earth to calm everyone down.
…
On the other side, inside the Underground Great Labyrinth, the “King of Madness,” who was pressing his ear against the wall trying to eavesdrop on the outside world but couldn’t hear anything, was very anxious, using this to slightly relieve some frustration.
It’s more accurate to say that this anxiety had been present for some time, but today it had peaked!
A divine intuition associated with his “godly” status made him realize that the source of this anxiety might have something to do with the “Flame Bearer”—which made him even more anxious!
In the past period, aside from constantly using the newly learned human cognition rhetoric of “drawing big pies,” there didn’t seem to be any clear explanation from him…
He wasn’t thinking of reneging on the promise to let him out, was he?
It was during his distraught unrest that the “King of Madness” sensed Colin entering the scene.

chapters.title: Chapter 800 - 800 557 The Obscure and Difficult End of Time
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 800: Chapter 557: The Obscure and Difficult “End of Time”. Chapter 800: Chapter 557: The Obscure and Difficult “End of Time”. In the depths of the Underground Great Labyrinth, Colin had only just descended when he immediately heard the voice of the “King of Mad Sounds” ringing in his ears.
Following the sound, he saw the disgraced high-level containment subject already standing to one side.
“Mr. Colin, greetings…” the “King of Mad Sounds” greeted him sincerely.
“Yes, greetings to you too.”
Colin nodded a mutual greeting and then, without waiting for the other to ask anything, he directly said,
“This time I’ve come to tell you that the company has a rare opportunity for merit. If nothing unexpected happens, there will soon be an event which might present an opportunity for your involvement. However, the situation is relatively dangerous, with a considerable likelihood that a number of sealed entities, at least at the level of a First Level Containment Subject, will partake. I’ve come to inquire about your intention. I do not insist; you are free to choose whether you are willing or not.”
“Willing, willing!” The “King of Mad Sounds” felt that even a second of hesitation would be a betrayal to the suffering he had endured over the years!
Confronting a sealed First Level Containment Subject was not difficult for him; after all, separated by a wall, he could exert his full power, while the other could not, unless some special authority intervened. Otherwise, even an Upper-Level First-Class Containment Entity could be suppressed.
Dealing with five or six wouldn’t pose much of a problem…
Moreover, the “King of Mad Sounds” had already completed the necessary mental preparations during this time.
It wasn’t just about First Level Containment Subjects; he was even willing to take the risk if he encountered a “Level 0” threat—of course, under normal circumstances, how easily could one come across a “Level 0” Containment Subject?
Therefore, there was probably no need to worry too much about this.
As long as he could get out, everything else, whether climbing a mountain of swords or plunging into a sea of flames, was negotiable!
“Since you have no objections and are psychologically accepting of the organization’s arrangements, that’s good.”
Colin nodded, hands behind his back, approving of the “King of Mad Sounds”‘ attitude, “When the time comes, you will be notified. All you have to do is comply.”
Once he reached C Level, he could summon and release him without incident.
And at that time, Colin could also ensure with relative certainty that the “King of Mad Sounds” would be under his control.
Of course, when the time actually came to release this fellow…
Colin felt that he probably wouldn’t care whether the other was plotting rebellion.
After all, at least in the eyes of the enemies, the “King of Mad Sounds” released by him would certainly seem to be on his side, whether he wished to act or not, the enemies wouldn’t likely give him another chance to turn against them, so at the very least, he could share some of the hate.
As long as he could achieve that, obedience was not crucial.
It was similar to the half-natural disaster class entity hidden within Bone Spur.
“I, the ‘King of Mad Sounds’, am always ready for the company leaders’ dispatch! To contribute my strength to ‘humanity’, and to atone for my sins through merit!” the “King of Mad Sounds” responded with fervor.
He had a premonition that this time it was for real, that there was indeed a chance for him to go out!
After confirming the “intention” and receiving a “verbal agreement,” Colin pursed his lips, nodded, and without lingering, left the place.
‘C Level always feels as if it’s not far away. Once I become one, I should be able to summon half a dozen First Level Containment Subjects to boost morale, one ‘King of Mad Sounds’, and one from Script City’s Passionate Paradise, the First Level Containment Subject ‘Formless Mother’, and Bone Spur…’
Colin pondered for a moment, believing these two would be of great use.
Besides, “Lady Rabbit” might also have some kind of arrangement, but the intelligence on this aspect was still unclear; Colin felt it was better to rely on himself…
Shortly after, Colin returned to his domain and contacted the Little Mermaid, associated with “World Code -4,” via the “Level 5 Bonfire” on both sides of his domain, to provide some explanations.
Then, amidst the reluctance of the crowd, he bade farewell to Shana and the others.
A distant and ancient bell sound slowly rang by his ear…
In front of Colin, the rich gray fog enveloped everything around, blurring all scenes…
Amid the successive bell chimes, his gaze gradually grew hazy, and if nothing unexpected happened, upon opening his eyes he would return to his cottage and then begin to carry out that brief “investigation mission.”
However, just at that moment…
When Colin came to his senses, he abruptly took notice that he was still in a space swirling with gray fog.
The distant and ancient bell chime had vanished without a trace.
“This place…”
Colin looked around, not entirely unfamiliar, probably not his first time here.
He faintly sensed that something was about to happen…
Sure enough, at that moment, as if drawn by instinct, he turned his head and saw light blue dots floating in the gray foggy space, and then like a brush, they outlined the silhouette of a door.
And in the blink of an eye, the door gradually solidified from mere lines to become a heavy and ancient portal standing before him.
The door was covered with spotty, blood-like red rust.
Compared to the last time he saw it, there were more signs of war and decay on the door, and leaning in to listen, it seemed as if he could hear some sounds of combat and shouting…
Then, under Colin’s gaze, the door slowly opened, a dense white mist poured out from within, and all things behind the door were shrouded in a mysterious veil, unclear to the eye…
The two open door leaves appeared like a pair of arms spread wide for an embrace.
Inviting the one who had been summoned to enter.
Colin’s heartbeat quickened a bit. The last time he saw this door, he thought it might be a boss door, perhaps with a trap, or a dramatic villain inside…
It turned out, it seemed to indeed be a boss.

chapters.title: Chapter 801 - 801 557
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 801: 557 Chapter 801: 557 He wasn’t facing an enemy, but his own boss, a mysterious high-level employee within the company.
Even now, after having communicated by letter for a considerable length of time, Colin still found the other to be shrouded in mystery.
However, compared to when he was a newcomer, upon seeing the door again, he had become an old hand at the company, no longer naive and confused, nor harboring as much fear…
“Sigh.”
He took a deep breath, waved his hand, and flames surged around him, enveloping his body.
Then, he stepped forward with his legs, walking toward the great door.
At the same time, he pondered some things…
‘Come to think of it, this door appeared both times after I returned from the “Arrival” project. Is it because it couldn’t reach Earth?’
‘Or, according to some of what the “Lady of Thorns” said, is “Lady Rabbit” also not within a certain “wall”?’
As these thoughts flickered through his mind, Colin’s figure passed through the door and entered.
A momentary sensation of weightlessness swept over him…
Colin realized that in that instant, there had been a particularly special transfer.
When everything ended, the scene, engulfed in swirling dense grey fog, had transformed into a simple and tidy office.
Compared to Colin’s office, this one was clearly much more practical, devoid of even the slightest frivolous item.
Behind the solid wood desk, the sound of pen on paper resounded, and a female figure dressed in professional attire sat there.
Her figure was exceptionally fine, with long legs crossed at one side, and her face…
‘It’s still unclear.’
Colin thought to himself, only able to hold a vague impression of her being quite beautiful.
At this moment, “Lady Rabbit” did not cease her work due to his arrival, still maintaining a very proper posture behind the desk, meticulously handling the tasks in her hands.
She wrote on one sheet then moved on to another, as if the work would never end…
“Long time no see,” Lady Rabbit said while working.
“Indeed, long time no see,” Colin agreed with a nod, recalling their last encounter.
But now, as he looked at this lady who had “tortured” him through thick and thin, yet also enabled him to obtain substantial rewards far exceeding other employees, he couldn’t help but wonder this moment, was it an illusion…
Did he really feel like he had seen this person before?
The figure before him was clearly seated there, yet there was a strange condition—as if she didn’t exist at all.
This was a quite bizarre experience.
Previously, this wasn’t so apparent, but now, his intuition, much sharper than before, brought a starkly contradictory sensation when he contacted her, that was…
He was communicating with something that didn’t exist.
Without further thought, Lady Rabbit’s voice came again: “Please have a seat. In this conversation, I will clarify some of your doubts and also, inform you of certain matters to be cautious of.”
Her tone was as calm and composed as ever, seemingly unshaken by any event, rendering her innermost thoughts impenetrable.
Colin, somehow calmed down as well, ceased his rumination, pulled out a chair to sit, and spoke:
“Clarify my doubts?”
“Yes, you may ask me now if there is anything you wish to understand,” Lady Rabbit continued, without lifting her head from the documents she was writing.
‘Why do I have the feeling of having a last meal before execution…’
He couldn’t help but make a sarcastic remark to himself, then analyzing her words, a host of questions that had constantly occupied his mind surfaced.
Among them, the most persistent tags were “2044,” “Flame Bearer,” and the mention of an “Ultimate Artifact” in Rosen’s “Adventure Log”…
After a few seconds of rapid contemplation, Colin directly posed the question he was most interested in and had long been clueless about.
“I’ve come across quite a few mentions of the ‘ultimate event’ or the ‘year of 2044,’ saying that something will happen at a specific time. I want to know if these two are related and, following that, what exactly is the situation, and what will occur…”
After asking, Colin didn’t expect to receive any definitive answer.
After all, so far, regardless of their strength, it seemed no one knew anything…
Unexpectedly, however, Lady Rabbit’s smoothly gliding pen hesitated for a moment, as if considering the question, or perhaps surprised by Colin’s opening gambit.
But after less than half a second of stasis, she replied to Colin in her usual tone.
“Both ‘the ultimate event’ and ‘the year of 2044’ indeed relate to the same thing, in a way. The former comes from some once high-standing existence, while the latter is a more specific description from a key figure, pointing out a time point more clearly than before…”
“Secondly, it’s about ‘the ultimate event’ itself. There are two interpretations for this: one is the broad recognition of ‘the ultimate event,’ and the other is the narrow recognition of ‘the ultimate event’…”
“Next, I will start by explaining the former to you…”
Saying this, Lady Rabbit paused for half a second, seemingly allowing Colin to digest the information.
And Colin quickly straightened up, intent on listening.
He hadn’t held much hope for this answer, as even during their “correspondence,” Colin had occasionally attempted to report and inquire, but never received a response.
Either “Lady Rabbit” didn’t know, or his rank wasn’t high enough to be privy to such knowledge.
But unexpectedly, this time “Lady Rabbit” truly began to provide answers!

chapters.title: Chapter 802 - 802 557 The Obscure End of Time. _3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 802: Chapter 557 The Obscure “End of Time”. _3 Chapter 802: Chapter 557 The Obscure “End of Time”. _3 “In the broader cognitive sense, ‘The Ultimate Time’ is often proposed by life forms at a certain level of evolution, advanced civilizations, but one can only know this name, unable to confirm anything else, or even prove with clarity whether it exists…”
“Ah? If you can’t prove its existence, then how can it even be proposed? And it seems like I’ve always had this peculiar feeling, feeling like a terrifying event will take place in the future…” Colin said, somewhat perplexed.
The premonition he spoke of wasn’t about an imminent event on Earth, but about something much further away, perhaps an extremely large-scale event that wouldn’t occur until a decade or even longer had passed!
The vague premonition told him that it would be an event significant enough to affect the entire universe, and possibly even beyond!
“What you can feel is not this; what you can sense should be the ‘Narrow Sense of the Ultimate Time,’ but I will explain in detail later. For now, let’s continue to explain this…”
“The Ultimate Time in the broader sense cannot be perceived by ordinary things. People can become aware of it based on the same situation as you, over a very long period, unable to prove whether this thing actually exists or not.”
“However, later on, the company interpreted ‘2044’ from the concept of ‘The Ultimate Time,’ then further inferred that ‘The Ultimate Time’ might be related to this number. Combining the temporal description of ‘The Ultimate Time,’ many seers commonly believe it refers to the year 2044…”
“In actuality, this notion, although mainstream, is not rigorous because it could also be that on a certain day, someone glanced at the number 2044, or an object that was extremely similar in status, or perhaps a room happened to gather 2044 people, and then it happened…”
“And even further, neither ‘The Ultimate Time’ nor ‘2044’ are accurate because this is not something that can be described with exact words…”
At this point, “Lady Rabbit” stopped writing, pondered for a few seconds, and then said:
“As for its description, rather than saying ‘it is’ or ‘it isn’t,’ it should be put this way: It might not be time, it might not be space, it might not be an object, it might not have a physical form, it might exist, it might not exist, it might appear at the beginning of the year 2044, or it might emerge at the end of 2044. It might happen, it might not happen, to us it might not exist, to us it might exist indirectly…
“Just as I said before, we cannot describe what it is, we can only indirectly describe it with ‘it might,’ ‘it’s not certain.’ These ‘descriptions’ are already the limit of what we can observe regarding this matter…
“Inaccurate words are only possibly slightly more accurate than accurate words.”
After saying this, “Lady Rabbit” resumed writing something, leaving time for Colin to think.
But at this moment, Colin listened with a baffled face, scratching the back of his head:
Ah? Is this some kind of tongue twister?
Why does it seem like the more I hear the answer, the more confused I am?
If that’s the case, then how can you prove this thing’s existence?
More doubts emerged from his mind, almost overwhelming him…
Taking a short breath, Colin asked with particular confusion:
“So how do we actually know about it?”
Though he had not yet received an answer, he felt it must be related to the ‘Narrow Sense of the Ultimate Time.’

chapters.title: Chapter 803 - 803 558
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 803: 558 Chapter 803: 558 “You’re not being accurate. To be precise, we don’t know what it is.”
“Uh!”
Upon hearing this, Colin’s temples throbbed, feeling that if “Lady Rabbit” hadn’t appeared so formidable and wasn’t a woman, he would have rushed up to grab her collar and shouted:
“Speak fucking human language, will you! Say something people can actually understand!”
At this moment, Colin somewhat regretted delving into “2044”.
All these theories, once crammed into his head, not only left him more confused but also without any clearer understanding.
It was like listening to riddles. Better to point and shoot!
At this time, sensing that Colin had calmed down, “Lady Rabbit” continued with a voice that was calm and unrippled.
“‘Generally speaking’, ‘2044’ isn’t something you need to ponder too much over, because at this stage it doesn’t hold much significance for us. Only the major powers possess the ability to observe, study, and offer some explanations.”
“And ‘narrowly speaking’, 2044 is a point in time, based on ‘it might become known to all’ among other factors, deduced as when the more powerful a civilization or entity is, the more likely they have a notion that something might happen…”
“This ‘notion’ is not pronounced in us, but on the macro scale or when it comes to powerful things, it’s different.”
“For example, it’s been suggested that humanity’s own greed and aggressiveness are due to it, that as living beings we act ‘passively’…”
“For instance, ‘Red Moon’ instinctively believes that by recycling all biomass before ‘2044’, it can prepare for that time, place, entity, lifeform, or whatever else which may or may not exist for us.”
“Or ‘The Night’, which does the same, but its method is more radical, seeking to return the universe to tranquility, to the origin, reverting everything back to a state of ‘zero’, to confront it…”
Hearing this, Colin couldn’t help but click his tongue: no wonder “The Night” was more disliked than “Red Moon”. “Red Moon” just wanted to devour all the food, but “The Night” would flip the table!
“Apart from the examples I’ve mentioned, all other beings at the pinnacle of the universe or other dimensions are beginning to act in their own way, whether willingly or otherwise, and action is necessary. An analogy you might understand is arms race…”
“Some people have used this as a basis to observe and perceive that when these entities take action, whether actively or inactively, the point of greatest conflict is likely the ‘narrow’ ‘The Ultimate Moment’ known as ‘2044’.”
“And the reason it’s narrow is that compared to the ‘general’ sense of it, many existences don’t acknowledge the ‘year of 2044’… after all, they are the drivers, not the victims like us.”
“…”
“Lady Rabbit” simply explained this so-called ‘narrow’ version of “2044” as clearly as possible.
This was somewhat easier to understand than the ‘broad’ version.
Colin thought over this information and roughly grasped the situation; to sum it up:
That is to say, all contradictions originate from that generally imperceptible “2044”…
Because of it, countless entities and supreme beings have started to take action, and when their conflicts escalate to fever pitch, for ordinary beings, it appears like an “apocalyptic” situation.
That is the “narrow” “The Ultimate Moment”.
While Colin’s thoughts churned, he asked:
“Speaking of which, even if we successfully resolve their conflicts, in the end, we still face an unknown ‘2044’? Do we have any way to deal with that?”
“Lady Rabbit,” having apparently briefly finished dealing with her documents, spread her hands flat on the desk and looked up:
“As I said before, including us, all things, whether willing or not, are making some kind of preparations, actively or passively.
“Guiding the coming of ‘Primordial Fire’ and creating an environment where humanity’s virtuous side is the fundamental shared logic, is the main direction agreed upon by myself and quite a few others.
“Of course, there are some other opinions, but they are roughly similar.”
‘Myself and quite a few others?’ Hearing “Lady Rabbit’s” choice of words, Colin wondered if there were others who did not agree?
He thought of certain people and things, especially that “Rat”.
However, “Lady Rabbit” did not seem to want to bring up that group and continued:
“While ‘Flame Bearer’ as one of the company’s greatest masterpieces is indeed the right path, it wasn’t fostered in the suitable environment, leading to some fundamental issues…
“In that macro environment, ‘Flame Bearer’s’ most likely fate is assimilation by ‘Primordial Fire’, rendering all efforts beneficial to other purposes…
“And because of various factors, it was no longer possible to turn back at that point, and people were generally pessimistic, unable to find possibilities…
“However, at that time, there still were those who made a bold decision, leading the creation of an extraordinary item, seeking to break the stalemate.”
“What item?” Colin couldn’t help but ask, recalling the so-called ultimate item Rosen mentioned that could change everything, reversing despair.
As for the leader of the enterprise, it was likely Boss Huang He.
Just thinking about him made Colin’s head ache.
He was definitely a match for the word “bold,” and his items had a distinct characteristic: potent effects along with equally significant side effects!
“I do not know the name of this item yet, but I have a premonition that maybe soon in your investigative endeavors, you should be able to discover it.”

chapters.title: Chapter 804 - 804 558 News of other Flame Bearer
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 804: Chapter 558 News of other “Flame Bearer” Reservists._2 Chapter 804: Chapter 558 News of other “Flame Bearer” Reservists._2 “As for the precise intelligence related to it, it might be that I can’t remember, or that I never really came into contact with it, or perhaps the information was blocked. In any case, I can’t provide specific intelligence…”
“However, during this time, I confirmed some fragmentary information related to it, for instance, its initial activation conditions, which are extremely harsh. One of them is that within a short period of time, a person must throw eighteen consecutive ‘Luck’s stacked together, tilting the effect of the item in our favor.”
“Eighteen ‘Luck’s?!” Colin’s eyes widened. All stacked together?
Is that something a human could achieve?
He dared not imagine, after throwing it, how smooth one’s life must be.
Isn’t it practically becoming a god on the spot?
No, if it required so many ‘Lucks’, would things have come to this point?
Perhaps sensing his confusion, ‘Lady Rabbit’ said:
“Whether the effect was successfully thrown or not, only the executor knows. I’m just deducing the result from some events, such as, nowadays the ‘Book of Fate’ or some related items, may be fine when ‘Misfortune’ or ‘Luck’ is thrown the first time, but on the second throw, no matter good or bad, there’s a great likelihood it will evaporate, instantly merging into some macro level because of its cause…”
“Is it dead?”
“I don’t know, but it wasn’t like this before.”
“Alright.”
As he spoke, Colin resolved an earlier doubt in his heart—
He had once asked on the company channel whether ‘Luck’ could be renewed; the answer he got was that the second one would disappear, tracelessly.
Now he knew the reason, it related to that unknown super-grade item.
“Lady Rabbit” added, “Moreover, for the item’s effect to function smoothly, the ‘Flame Bearers’, as well as many company employees, had all paid a great price. This too was a condition for activating it…”
That’s for sure, in the past powers wandered everywhere, now there aren’t even two Little Cats left, almost completely annihilated.
Colin pursed his lips, unsure of what to say for a moment.
It feels like the cost of using this item is too great, among those eighteen ‘Luck’s’, there might be some padding.
Otherwise, it wouldn’t be so disastrously unlucky…
While he was thinking this, Lady Rabbit continued speaking: “Actually, for the company, the current result still hasn’t deviated because the scenarios that were originally impossible have now appeared…
‘The Primordial Fire’ has completed its final transformation. We have obtained the result we wanted. Now is the era when all things converge on ‘humanity’, only missing a ‘Flame Bearer’ to trigger ‘Primordial Fire’ to set the pattern…”
Hearing this, Colin nodded outwardly, but couldn’t help but internally retort, ‘That’s well said! So, where should we start looking for this ‘Flame Bearer’ now?’
He didn’t feel much for environments with or without “humanity.”
However, he now understood the situation quite a bit—
Simply put, without the ‘Primordial Fire,’ there wouldn’t be a ‘Flame Bearer.’
And without a ‘Flame Bearer,’ the ‘Primordial Fire’ couldn’t be invoked.
So far, no one had understood how a ‘Flame Bearer’ could appear without the ‘Primordial Fire.’
It was a dead loop.
Thinking this, Colin sighed and spoke, “If initially they had retained a ‘Flame Bearer,’ even the weakest one, we wouldn’t be in this situation. So, is there really a chance now?”
A ‘Flame Bearer’ might not be invincible, able to vanquish scores of First Level Containment Subjects in a second, but its real value was more than just combat power.
But also in its identity.
Today, if the first ‘Flame Bearer’ were to appear, it would have certain ‘uniqueness,’ because of some specific rules, it could command very high authority, able to reassemble the company’s power and prompt the descent of the ‘Primordial Fire’…
If they had kept one, we wouldn’t be in this situation.
Realizing this, Colin raised an eyebrow, suddenly aware that with the company’s capability, they should not have been unable to retain people.
Perhaps there was an underlying issue?
“I can’t answer your first question as there are details I’m unaware of, as for the second…”
“Lady Rabbit” spoke in a rare serious tone:
“It’s my ultimate demand behind all my current tasks to have a ‘Flame Bearer’ appear.
“I firmly believe it can succeed, and strive for this.”
Lady Rabbit’s firm words seemed to inject Colin with more confidence. Difficulties aside, just seeing ‘Lady Rabbit’ looking like this, it felt quite promising.
As for whether there was much hope, that was hard to say, after all, difficulties were aside…
However, having made a decision, Colin wasn’t overly troubled and, having clarified the issue further with “2044”, he asked about other matters:
“Apart from me, are there other ‘Flame Bearer’ reservists? If so, how are they doing? Can we establish contact and get to know each other?”
Hearing this, “Lady Rabbit” nodded:
“There are.”
Then, as Colin looked at her, awaiting further explanation, he realised “Lady Rabbit” had no more to say.
For a few seconds, as they were “staring at each other,” the atmosphere turned awkward, Colin suddenly realized—
His level wasn’t enough; a single “there are” was all he could know.
Other specifics like exact numbers, status, locations, were out of the question, very crucial secrets—probably only after getting a promotion or becoming a ‘Flame Bearer,’ could he know…

chapters.title: Chapter 805 - 805 558 News of other Firebearer Reservists._3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 805: Chapter 558 News of other “Firebearer” Reservists._3 Chapter 805: Chapter 558 News of other “Firebearer” Reservists._3 However, it was just a “yes,” and Colin felt there was much to conjecture from it.
‘I hope the others will also make an effort to pierce through this layer of window paper sooner rather than later. Heaven forbid they adopt the mentality of “why rely on oneself when one can hope for others”…’
Colin entertained the thought of others working harder for a moment, then posed another question,
“By the way, what is likely to happen after the investigation into the ‘Book of Fate’ is complete?”
“An individual derailed by minor setbacks will preemptively strike. His stance and demands deviate from our goals. You are not unfamiliar with him; the last accidental transfer was his doing…”
“That Rat?” Colin immediately realized who “Lady Bunny” was referring to.
“Yes, eliminate him directly if the opportunity arises. Do not give him any chances. I will not assign any tasks that might allow him to live a second longer. So, if you encounter him, ignore him,” Lady Bunny said calmly.
That decisive, huh… Colin pondered and then curiously asked, “Can you explain what the wrong path signifies?”
“Unless there’s an exception, it refers to the pursuit of human supremacy as a superior race of sorts, and it’s taken to an irrational and extreme standpoint.”
“Huh?”
Colin was confused for a moment. Human supremacy, wasn’t that the company’s direction?
Aren’t we all on the same track?
Seeing his expression, “Lady Bunny” tilted her head in thought before explaining,
“One thing you must understand is that we don’t pursue an extreme and singular human supremacy. It’s about all things gravitating towards ‘humanity,’ to become a fundamental logical commonality, not about elevating a single race.”
“To put it in simpler terms, consider an empire. Empires will fall, but as long as life continues, ideas endure, spread, and assimilate, rather than forcing a monkey to wear clothes and then calling it human…”
Is that so, creating an environment? “Flame Bearers” even sacrificing themselves entirely for it? Colin thought introspectively.
It feels like cultivating fertile land from a desert, using themselves as fuel for the soil—thus giving those who follow an environment to farm.
Only, the price paid for this “field” might have been too high; it’s hard to say whether it’s worth it or not.
“As for the one who strayed, although he will be the first to cause trouble, it does not mean his abilities are particularly strong, since his schemes are almost certain to fail. He might believe he has outsmarted ancient beings, but in reality, he may be overthinking…”
“Lady Bunny” expressed skepticism about the adversary’s actions, “You’re to kill him immediately because he possesses numerous factors that could spiral events out of control, causing unnecessary casualties and reducing our chances for success…
“Afterward, there are other matters to attend to. One thing you need to be aware of is that my current status is greatly limited due to the influence of a certain item…
“My own cognition, memory, and authorization are not whole…
“Furthermore, any actions taken in relation to your ‘Emblem World’ are particularly challenging for me.
“So, until you obtain any results from investigating the ‘Book of Fate,’ I cannot do much. After your investigation, I will be even less able to pay attention here… I can only try to offer what little assistance and guidance possible, which might not be very decisive. Therefore, you’ll need to try harder on your own.”
“Got it,” Colin nodded and then curiously asked,
“You mentioned you’d be too occupied to care about this place? Why’s that?”
“We have many enemies…”
“Lady Bunny” finished with a slight shake of her head, indicating it would be best for him to not delve further.
But that single statement, Colin understood.
Just how many enemies does the company have? Look up at the night sky, pick any planet, and chances are there could be enemies wanting to stab you twice…
It can’t simply be quantified by number.
But did “Lady Bunny” mean she would be going to guard the borders?
After some thought, Colin inquired about “World Code-13” and whether it might be impacted; he had some concerns about the situation there…
“In the short term, the effect isn’t significant.”
“Lady Bunny” affirmed, “There, I’ve left a few documents that can be used to intervene when necessary, so don’t worry too much.”
On hearing this, Colin felt moved, but also strangely thought, ‘Why do I feel like she’s saying “Don’t worry, I’ll take care of your wife”?’
At that moment, “Lady Bunny” looked at him. Her beautiful yet indistinct face took on a serious expression:
“Rather than elsewhere, you should be more concerned with yourself. Remember, even if the intended goals are not met, please strive to stay alive as much as possible.”
…
Wait, there’s another chapter.

chapters.title: Chapter 806 - 806 559 Global Disaster Broadcast Alert
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 806: Chapter 559 Global Disaster Broadcast Alert! Chapter 806: Chapter 559 Global Disaster Broadcast Alert! Upon opening his eyes, Colin didn’t immediately get out of bed, but instead, he stared at the familiar ceiling, recalling his recent conversation with “Lady Rabbit” and feeling his head buzz.
He had thought a simple inquiry would unravel some of his confusion.
However, instead of solving many puzzles, he ended up with even more questions.
Of course, the main focus was still on “The Ultimate Moment,” which was too abstract for most people to comprehend, even with an interpretation.
But aside from that, the rest seemed manageable…
Colin remembered the last part of their conversation in which he asked about the three leaders; “Lady Rabbit” said she could only recall so little.
She only subtly hinted that “the one you’re investigating is probably one of them.”
“Why do I feel almost certain it’s ‘Boss Huang He,’ yet why does she seem so unsure,” Colin wondered, raising his eyebrows but soon figured that there would be results before long.
He decided not to dwell on it any further.
“Everything that needed to be organized is nearly done; there shouldn’t be any significant regrets now…”
Colin sat up in bed, pondering the cause and effect of his current situation.
It seemed everything that needed tidying had been dealt with…
What remained was likely setting up the final arrangements before the event began.
He took a deep breath and pulled out all his tools from his pocket.
He checked each one…
“Contrarian’s Revolver,” “Time Reversal,” “Time Freeze,” “Force Repulsion,” “Force Attraction,” Enhanced Bone Spur, Enhanced “Mountain of Smiling Corpses,” “False Mighty One,” Max Kindness of the Firebearer (Haze Angel), Shield Badge of Fairness and Justice, Firebearer’s Grease* 1037.43L, Badge of Humility…
These were his main combat methods.
Among the dazzling array of orange and golden items, “False Mighty One” stood out in purple, looking a bit out of place in quality.
But so far, it had been quite useful for him…
After all, its upper limit almost equates the basic physical fitness of an employee with that of a Level C Employee.
Colin wasn’t sure which employee’s Level C standards it measured by, but it still proved quite effective in use.
“When it comes down to a fight, just blow it up in an overclock use; it could give more effects, though the side effects are a bit tricky to manage.”
Colin nodded, then glanced over his other tools.
Then there were pieces of kindling he’d collected from various levels of Containment Subjects, which, if laid out and burned, could cover the third-largest country in the world in terms of land area…
Of course, Colin couldn’t achieve this, so he only roughly estimated its effects.
Besides these, there were the “Widow Yukionna” and “Mark of the Fire Tree”; the former, Colin no longer used as a tool but rather held regular conversations with as an equal…
As for the latter, he similarly didn’t treat it as a mere tool but more like a healing pet that could understand human speech.
Though he knew “Fire Tree” harbored its own little schemes, often slacking unless snapped at, he didn’t know what exactly it was planning.
But Colin could feel these schemings were harmless to him, so he didn’t pay them much mind.
After all, a bit of thought made it clear that it was probably just plotting to escape.
Apart from this, there were also items like the “Analytical Lens” and other low-performance green gear, even some purple gear, which Colin regarded as “disposable tools.”
“The green gear is okay to blow up when overclocked, but even the worst ‘Purple Gear’ starts at a minimum of twelve or thirteen thousand points; exploding it seems a bit extravagant…”
Colin looked at the twenty-some pieces of green gear in his hands and the nine pieces of purple gear he had acquired through official and company trades.
Especially the purple gear, worth over a hundred thousand points just here.
But if a crisis occurred, Colin would not hesitate to blow them up to defend himself; hesitating even for a second would be a disrespect to his own life.
About an hour later…
Colin picked up his phone to notify Old Master Wu.
Instead of passively letting the other party inquire about him, this time he chose to take the initiative.
“Are you sure you’re prepared?”
Unlike usually waiting long for a message, during this period Old Master Wu seemed to be constantly by his phone, and Colin received a reply immediately after sending his message.
Facing the inquiry, Colin gave a confident response.
A few seconds later, it seemed the other end also confirmed something and replied,
“Okay, later Xu Duojin will come to pick you up, then, from a little while onwards, there might be some significant actions happening, you don’t need to worry, just wait.”
After a brief exchange, Colin sat silently in his room, thinking back to his last conversation with “Lady Rabbit.”
He pondered about “The Rat,” who was likely to show up first when the time came.
“According to Lady Rabbit, he’s quite adept with tools, likely possessing a super-strong golden artifact related to spatial abilities, and besides being able to evade her and ‘Fate Principle,’ he might have some secrets that needed attention…”
Of course, though his combat ability wasn’t weak, his weaknesses were quite clear…
His physical body was extremely fragile, almost like a regular person’s.
If only he could get closer, there was a high chance that just one wave of dispersion entering could directly kill him.

chapters.title: Chapter 807 - 807 559 World Disaster Broadcast Alert_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 807: Chapter 559 World Disaster Broadcast Alert!_2 Chapter 807: Chapter 559 World Disaster Broadcast Alert!_2 In this regard, Colin felt that the “Shield Badge of Fairness and Justice” might play a significant role.
However, before Colin had more time to think, he suddenly had a feeling and stepped towards the window. Just as he looked outside, he was startled by the huge wailing sound of an air raid siren…
As it sounded, it quickly drowned out the hustle and bustle of the city, involuntarily thrusting everyone into a state of tension and even fear!
“What’s going on? An earthquake?” someone asked, poking their head out with an inexplicable fear and confusion.
Yet no sooner had they looked outside than their pupils constricted upon seeing that the noise came from a line of sharp-angled green trucks, and a massive number of troops, usually only seen online, pouring into the city with weapons in hand.
“Something’s happened! Something’s happened! Evacuate quickly! To the nearest air-raid shelter…”
“Hurry up! Hurry up! Hurry up!”
“What’s going on? What happened?!”
Some of the residents, in the middle of showering and without even rinsing off the foam on their heads, rushed out in a hurry, staring blankly at the green camouflage trucks lined up on the streets.
Meanwhile, in a household, a young man’s game character flashed a taunting icon, psychologically striking at his opponent before preparing the final blow to destroy the enemy’s base.
However, at that moment, the screen abruptly changed…
“We interrupt for an emergency news broadcast! A strong seismic wave has been detected and is imminent. All residents must evacuate immediately according to the emergency drill plan!”
Upon seeing this, the young man showed a look of dismay: “Damn it, they’re running a drill now? I was finally winning against the wind, let me destroy the crystal first!”
But after being stunned for two seconds, he suddenly noticed the mournful sound of an air raid siren faintly coming from outside the window.
He flung the curtains aside, squinting as the natural light momentarily stung his eyes, but then his pupils shook as he noticed the row of large camouflage trucks outside. He didn’t care about his potential turnaround anymore and hurriedly packed up, grabbing the “emergency financial bag” previously prepared for drills and his only remaining pet—a tentacle mouse—and dashed outside—
This was not a drill!
On the way, he saw that all electronic devices he came across seemed to have been forcibly hacked and switched to the “emergency broadcast” channel.
“Damn, damn, DAMN, it’s for real,” he muttered, shocked as he saw the various military vehicles and armed personnel that one would only expect to see in the military.
“Stop dawdling! Didn’t you see the earlier news? They told us to prepare, I heard a massive earthquake is coming! They’re evacuating us now!”
“Damn, it’s really happening. Crap, I haven’t gotten my son out yet…”
“…”
“We still have time, no need to panic or crowd, please board the vehicles orderly after personnel have been checked as we practiced before…”
Hu Zheng, who had become a Level 5 Fate Propeller Teller, was now controlling the Lifelines of Fate on-site, ensuring that there were no mass stampedes or similar incidents.
However, while he was used to covertly influencing hundreds to thousands of people, affecting tens of thousands all at once was proving to be quite arduous, his forehead dripping with sweat that evaporated into mist.
During the evacuation, a beautiful female volunteer carrying an old man climbed onto a large truck, but as soon as she boarded, confusion spread across her face, and she glanced back at the residential area:
“I feel like I’ve forgotten something? As if there’s a patient I’m responsible for that I didn’t get out…”
She faintly remembered someone in a wheelchair, emaciated yet with an inexplicably firm and attentive gaze—a frail young person who caught one’s attention…
But then again, maybe not?
The images in her memory began to blur.
“No, everyone’s here already, hurry up and run, if the disaster strikes we won’t be able to escape…”
“Oh, right, right…”
“…”
And it wasn’t just in this one place.
The entire country, and indeed the whole world, was mobilizing in a short amount of time!
All kinds of alarms and broadcasts began to intrude through everyone’s electronic devices, sounding the alarm!
“Warning! The U.S. Government has declared all-out war on the Russian Government and plans to deploy to launch a full-scale nuclear strike. EVACUATE TO SHELTERS NOW!!!”
…
“Чрезвычайная ситуация! Правительство США объявило тотальную войну российскому правительству и планирует нанести полномасштабный ядерный удар по России, граждан призывают быстро эвакуироваться в ближайшее убежище…”
…
“緊急事態!多火山は活性化爆発段階にあります….”
…
“Alle Bürgerinnen und Bürger werden dringend gebeten, sich so schnell wie möglich in Schutzräume zu begeben, da die extreme Kälte einsetzt.”
…
“…”
Meanwhile, inside “Bonfire Company,” where employees had made preparations thanks to Colin’s earlier message, there was less panic, though nonetheless a sense of urgency.
“@654321, what’s going on, Brother Shunzi? It seems like the end of the world all of a sudden. Come out and tell us what you know!”
“Is that thing finally starting? But from what I’ve gathered, different countries are facing different disasters, and if there aren’t any, they create their own excuses. Especially the bears and eagles still at each other’s throats with their warnings, at a time like this, hahaha…”

chapters.title: Chapter 808 - 808 559 Global Disaster Broadcast Alert_3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 808: Chapter 559 Global Disaster Broadcast Alert!_3 Chapter 808: Chapter 559 Global Disaster Broadcast Alert!_3 “It must be correct; such a big reaction, brothers, prepare for battle!”
“I have a strong feeling that this time it’s really going to be a huge one! Hmm, may the ancestors bless us, no, rather may Brother Shunzi bless us. Even the ancestors aren’t as reliable as Brother Shunzi right now…”
“…”
Colin glanced at the information on the parchment, edited some content, and sent it out, confirming the inquiries of his employees.
Then, standing by the window, Colin quietly watched outside.
In the government’s action, people poured out of various buildings like ants, then walked onto large trucks under guidance and were transported to shelters in different areas…
Those in his area were luckier; most of them would likely be transferred to Research Facility No. 5.
Colin watched the departing people, his thoughts drifting somewhat.
As the top-level refuge, most people here actually didn’t have the qualifications to enter.
But as those who had come into contact with, or indirectly contacted Colin, they had to be properly dealt with to avoid any abnormal entities from using them as a springboard to launch some kind of remote attack on him.
In today’s world, such a thing was entirely possible.
“It’s a pity that after so many years of work and a huge investment of financial and material resources, Research Facility No. 5 can only support the survival needs of about ten to twenty million people…”
Tens of millions might sound like a lot, but within the scope of several provinces, it didn’t amount to much.
Only less than one-tenth of the “fortunate ones” had the chance to enter such large, high-level shelters. The arrangements were different for others, heading to “small worlds” with higher risk levels and the like.
Whether they could survive afterward was truly left to fate.
“However, the most crucial thing is, as long as we can withstand the first, most ferocious onslaught, ‘Lady Bunny’s’ contingencies will arrive, and some situations should then take a turn for the better…”
