Colin’s first priority after concluding his investigation was to lead the resistance against this or successive waves of offensives.
Save as many people as possible by all means.
Of course, the ideal status would be to expel the enemy down to the last one.
But the likelihood of that was not very high.
“‘Flame Bearer,’ ah… sigh…”
Colin shook his head, feeling that the object was close at hand, yet out of reach.
Taking a deep breath, he lifted his head to look at the sky again.
He could feel that, with actions beginning globally, the “world barrier” that macroscopically suppressed anomalies had been shaken.
Although the magnitude was not very large at the moment, the resulting impact was rapidly breeding adverse consequences…
However, some officials who were prepared in advance, or company employees, or even a few Heretic Believers, were quickly arriving at the scene, risking their lives to handle the problem.
This was also the cost of acting in advance.
Had they chosen not to act and maintain the stability of the “world barrier,” letting the general public be oblivious until disaster struck, society might have remained stable for a while, but then it would have led to an extremely exaggerated death rate with a sudden, unanticipated crisis.
By comparison, the current cost was still acceptable.
It was during the peak of the evacuation efforts that Colin saw a black sedan pull up on the other side, and the figure of Xu Duojin stepped out.
“It’s time to act.”
Colin nodded to the figure, took one last glance at the room he might never have a chance to return to, and then left without much attachment through the main door.
In a short while.
He was in the car, heading to the destination, beginning the investigation of the “Book of Fate” incident.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 809 - 809 560 Official Assessment
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 809: Chapter 560 Official Assessment Chapter 809: Chapter 560 Official Assessment “Mr. Colin, in about an hour and forty-six minutes, we will arrive at the assessment site, your record is spotless, no issues…”
“At that time, there will be some questioning, it’s part of the process, but you can respond casually.”
“After the process is finished, you will be led into a room or stay put. At that time, you should feel a strong sensation of being watched by something. Don’t resist too much, it won’t be long before your consciousness sinks into somewhere…”
Inside the cautious sedan, Xu Duojin sat on one side, explaining the upcoming procedure to Colin.
If it weren’t for Colin’s special circumstances, the assessment would only be a formality for other matters. For someone like him, whose power not just equaled, but surpassed most of the Ninth Level Personnel, there would be no need for an assessment.
He could simply receive a document and, without moving from home, be promoted and enjoy the top-level treatment…
Moreover, compared to the ordinary official levels, his position within the company would also reflect back here—
The F Level Staff who joined the company could enjoy supreme treatment, with Level Seven or even Eighth Level Personnel to safeguard them right from the start, not to mention Colin’s situation.
Of course, except for Old Master Wu, currently there was no one else to safeguard him.
Having listened to Xu Duojin, Colin nodded and asked curiously,
“Do you know where it sinks into?”
Xu Duojin thought for a moment, slightly shaking his head, “I’m not particularly sure, from what I remember, it’s a dark area that connects everyone’s ‘Threads of Fate.’ Usually, just one glance is enough, but evidently, your goal isn’t just to take a look…”
‘That’s so…’ Colin nodded.
“Actually, under normal circumstances, it would be best for Old Master Wu to lead you, but unfortunately, he currently has some more important tasks to handle, so I’m here instead…”
“What tasks?”
“To monitor some S Level Disaster situations and to ensure that these things do not erupt while he is still alive…” Xu Duojin said with a sigh.
Hearing this, Colin also fell silent for a moment, knowing that Old Master Wu didn’t have much time left.
But the exact timing, only he knew.
And Colin remembered, according to his own information, there seemed to be only two triggers for major turbulence in this world—one was during his promotion to Level 6 Personnel while investigating the “Book of Fate.”
The other was the time of Old Master Wu’s death…
But now, it seemed, the Company, or “Lady Rabbit,” planned to take advantage of the remaining time Old Master Wu had.
By investigating the “Book of Fate” in advance, they aimed to actively kick off this crisis.
Colin sighed slightly, said no more, and instead looked through the car window. At this moment, amidst the security alarms, a large number of camouflaged transport vehicles steadily moved back and forth on the main roads…
People screaming as they fled from the buildings, it seemed chaotic, but in reality, everything was proceeding steadily.
Under already established plans, the evacuation was generally going smoothly.
“‘Destiny Propeller’ truly far surpasses other Extraordinary Ones in maneuvering the general populace.”
Colin’s gaze swept over some “Destiny Propellers.”
The massive scale of urban population relocation didn’t see any serious pushing, trampling, or riots; it was mostly due to the guiding role of the “Destiny Propellers.”
Without them, Colin couldn’t even imagine the chaos that would ensue.
These guys might not be as strong in combat as their peers, but in guiding some kind of “major trend,” they indeed excelled.
“This kind of large-scale operation, actually, long before Mr. Wu was promoted to Ninth Level Personnel and foresaw a major event after his death, had always been under preparation, both domestically and internationally for many years…”
“If after preparing for so long, it still ended up a complete mess, that would be the real problem.”
Hearing Colin’s reflective remark, Xu Duojin promptly explained the situation briefly. However, while speaking, he seemed to think of something, paused for a moment, and then somewhat oddly added,
“But one thing that actually helped a lot was that Other World’s Black Box you brought along and your identity…”
“Oh?” Colin raised his eyebrows, unsure of what he meant.
“For the doomsday-type events, what would happen in human society, some information from that Black Box provided important reference samples, convincing us to enforce deeper control in the evacuations. After all, believing people would yield to one another right before a major disaster is almost impossible…”
Xu Duojin explained a bit more, then continued, “As for your identity… you probably understand, within official circles, both domestically and internationally, there are some ‘veteran’ personages who advocate ‘human elitism.’ These people too uphold human supremacy but do not regard ordinary people as their equals, not even planning to include many during evacuations…
“This group of people, although not numerous, controls vast resources.
“But because of the ‘Bonfire Company,’ these people currently also dare not oppose ordinary people too much and have coughed up quite a lot of resources, especially a lot of donations that have come our way…
“If it weren’t for this, the situation now might not look as simple as you see.”
Hearing Xu Duojin’s words, Colin initially perplexed, wondered what this had to do with him or the “Company.”
He indeed knew about “human elitism,” as this group planned to only take out a small selected group of “slaves,” possessing resources hundreds or even thousands of times more than ordinary people, to leave.

chapters.title: Chapter 810 - 810 560 Official Assessment_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 810: Chapter 560 Official Assessment_2 Chapter 810: Chapter 560 Official Assessment_2 Before, when he saw him, he also thought about taking the initiative to talk…
But because Xu Duojin indicated there was no need, he didn’t go, not expecting that resources had already been spewed out.
And does this have something to do with the company?
It took him only two seconds, and Colin understood the reason.
These guys must have been trying to curry favor with “Bonfire Company,” given that their disregard for ordinary people was contrary to the company’s philosophy…
After gaining enough understanding of “Bonfire Company,” they clearly knew that their behavior of hoarding resources and ignoring the lives of ordinary people could potentially offend the company.
And now, wherever one could possibly escape to seemed to somehow be related to “Bonfire Company”…
Plus, some of the “Extraordinary Ones” among them were employees of the company.
If one day they needed help from the company, they might likely be unwelcome because of this issue…
“It seems, whether they like it or not, they all must spit out something from their guts.”
Colin, while looking at the rapidly changing scenery outside the window, thought and then spoke in a gentle tone a few seconds later,
“There’s still some time, let’s find names of these forces and a list of some higher-risk individuals, I’d like to memorize them a bit.”
Of course, remembering these people was definitely not about returning favors.
It was because these guys were more likely to backstab, and if encountered, one could easily be stabbed without caution.
Xu Duojin clearly understood his meaning as well: “I’ve already sent the relevant contents to Ms. Silver by your side…”
“Oh, that works.”
Colin nodded, then, with a shift of thought, saw the Little Maid, who cooperatively transmitted the stream of information directly into his retina through special means.
An hour later, in a relatively remote town, Colin encountered an official venue used specifically for interview assessments.
A public park that wasn’t very luxurious but had a fairly large footprint.
At the entrance gate, the black official sedan stopped, and as soon as Colin got out of the car, the guards at the gate immediately looked at him and gestured for him to stop.
However, as soon as Xu Duojin got out and showed his credentials, the gates to the park opened.
“As we walk over, we’ll encounter some watching eyes, but don’t pay them too much mind…”
Typically, these observations were meant for the truly ‘new’ recruits, but obviously, Colin wasn’t really a new recruit…
However, as Mr. Wu said, all screenings could be dealt with formally but should not be negligent; they also had to carry them out.
Naturally, Xu Duojin also understood that, since it involved contact with the “Book of Fate,” it was best to follow the procedures, whether it was just for show or otherwise; the facade needed to be maintained.
If someone thought they were too excellent and chose to promote directly to Level 6 positions or skip grades without going through “assessment” and being watched by the “Book of Fate,” just to scrimp even a little, there had been such instances in the past…
As a result, that promoter had a rough time for a while, nearly dying several times.
Only after re-completing assessments, did he recover—As for why he knew this so clearly, it was because he was the unlucky fellow Mr. Wu had pushed forward to conduct this experiment.
Initially unclear why, but now, Xu Duojin vaguely felt.
Being highly bound to the official “Book of Fate” likely meant they were arranging something through them, which was why they enforced people through this stage of the three main pathways…
“Alright.”
Colin nodded at his words, followed half a step behind Xu Duojin.
All along the way, he did indeed feel some sneaky glances, but he detected all of them.
With a large enough gap in strength, even without Bonfire, he could still use some of the basic passives of Beast Transformation Syndrome, such as scent and crisis awareness, to lock onto the position and status of an enemy in his mind…
‘The strongest in the entire assessment venue are just two Level Seven Personnel and some mediocre tools, at this level, I might have sneaked a peek when I first joined the company at F Level, but as soon as I reached E level, in my presence, it’s almost like they’re skinny-dipping…’
Colin’s expression remained unchanged, but he couldn’t help thinking to himself.Everything within the assessment venue was basically within his perception; compared to these people, Colin was more curious about some related affairs of the “Book of Fate.”
It seemed, however, he hadn’t felt it yet…
And at this moment, as Xu Duojin led the way, he continued to explain the upcoming process:
“Sometimes, there are spies mixed within the officials, and these people might not even know that they are spies. During assessments, once they are glanced at by the ‘Book of Fate’, they go mad. To minimize the chaos they could cause after exposing themselves, the assessment locations are set in more remote areas…”
“That’s how it is.” Colin nodded and walked away with his hands clasped behind his back, slowly striding forward.
Elsewhere, a group of observers circled around ‘observation’, watching Colin’s leader-like demeanor as he walked with hands behind him. In contrast, Xu Duojin, who was supposed to portray a sage-like persona, was fawning over him with flattery, leaving everyone momentarily speechless.
Had they not known Xu Duojin’s identity, they might have suspected that the young man was the actual leader.
At the same time, everyone began to wonder about the background of this young man who could make Xu Duojin adopt such an attitude.
They speculated, one by one, whether this young man could possibly be Old Master Wu’s illegitimate son?
Otherwise, it really wasn’t possible.
However, they also knew beforehand that this assessment task was special; all they needed to do was to “deliver high praise” on a particular paper to attract the attention of something.
As soon as Colin and another passed into a building, the observers withdrew their gazes.
“In the presence of an elder, neither servile nor overbearing, extremely outstanding, a rarity in a thousand years…”
“Flawless jade, brimming with talent, a prodigy unseen in ages, the marvel of the world.”
“Holy crap, this young man is truly awesome.”
…
Several personnel, with mixed emotions and against their conscience, wrote their evaluations of that unfamiliar young man on the special paper.
…
Meanwhile, inside the building, Xu Duojin brought Colin to the door of the assessment office. He patted Colin on the shoulder, said nothing more, and turned to leave.
But he had not walked far when he suddenly felt his luck inexplicably improve.
Perplexed, he suddenly heard Colin’s voice from behind, “Wait a moment.”
“Uh?” Xu Duojin stopped and half-turned to look at Colin.
He saw him casually take something shiny and gold out of his pocket and tossed it over, covering a distance of about five or six meters.
“I’m giving this to you.”
“Holy crap…” Xu Duojin caught the airborne golden mark in mid-air and immediately grabbed it without any regard for his image.
“This precious item, what if it gets damaged if it falls on the ground! Gold is quite soft.”
Xu Duojin held the palm-sized object close, feeling the energy it contained, and realized what a top-tier item it was!
It had no significant side effects and could provide super strong bursts of power.
Just with these, Xu Duojin even felt confident enough to go toe-to-toe with some ‘Divine Strike’ type Ninth Level Personnel.
“Ha, even if you smashed your head against it, you couldn’t break it, let alone dropping it on the ground…”
Colin smiled. This was a rather special Golden Mark, solidly made and also a high-quality new item that had both “Light” and “Fire” properties, crafted with the efforts of him and Shana.
In the final period, aside from the “Light” sect being brought over as “assembly line employees,” the output from Colin and Shana had reduced as they began creating some high-quality products for others.
After understanding the horrors of this catastrophe, he did not wish to see his close ones die easily.
At the very least, he hoped that when pushed into a corner by these friends, he could still have a bit of “hidden backup energy” or a “microcosm” to burst forth and fight for one last chance.
Then, Colin slightly shook his head, gathered his thoughts, waved his hand, turned around, and walked towards the “interview office.”
Watching his figure disappear into it, Xu Duojin felt a strong sense of possibly parting ways forever…
He took a deep breath, turned around, and left, carrying the Golden Mark in his hand and heading to his own battlefront.
…
One more chapter!
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 811 - 811 561 Drawing the Attention of the Book of
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 811: Chapter 561 Drawing the Attention of the “Book of Fate”! (Long Chapter!) Chapter 811: Chapter 561 Drawing the Attention of the “Book of Fate”! (Long Chapter!) The room was not very big, similar to the usual arrangement for interview work. In front of the seat designated for the test subjects, there were seven tables and chairs, on each sat a person, both men and women, generally over the age of thirty, with the oldest having white hair and a face full of vicissitudes.
After Colin sat down, an elderly man with white hair and a face full of vicissitudes spoke:
“Mr. Colin, shall we begin the assessment now?”
“Okay.” Colin nodded and, out of habit, crossed his legs as he appraised the “old man” in front of him.
Aside from some documents, there was nothing on the table that indicated the other party’s identity or name.
Furthermore, his rich experience told him that this was a “Fate Propeller,” which meant that, despite the elderly appearance of the man, he might actually be two years younger than Xu Duojin, who appeared middle-aged.
“Snap snap.”
The “white-haired old man” picked up a stack of documents, tapped the edge on the table creating a crisp sound, and then asked seriously and sternly,
“What do you think about salty tofu?”
“…”
This isn’t how you just go through the motions… Colin thought to himself, but he pursed his lips on the surface, pondered for a moment as if considering deeply, then responded:
“I don’t know, I generally drink sweet.”
“Good.”
The “white-haired old man” nodded seriously and wrote on the paper in front of him: ‘Stable personality, prudent in action, not panicking in the face of difficulties, not rushing to give immature responses, but giving answers after deep thought, strong decision-making ability, capable of making correct decisions swiftly under complex situations, he is the most skilled person I have seen in my life…’
While he was seriously writing this, another assessor spoke up:
“If an elderly man fell by the roadside and waved at you for help, would you help him?”
“The situation is too vague, I won’t answer,” Colin replied offhand.
“Are you sure that’s your response?”
“Yes.”
Hearing this, the assessor nodded seriously, revealing a relieved look as he glanced at him, then also began to write:
‘Faced with things he considers unreasonable, he dares to question, challenge authority, and pursue truth, possessing a strong will and high consciousness, his character has already led and surpassed the top standards of the current era…’
At the same time, another person asked seriously:
“If you had money, would you give some to ordinary people?”
“No, giving a man a fish is not as good as teaching him to fish, I would teach them how to fish and take a proportionate fee.”
“Good!”
About half an hour later, the assessors all stood up, tidied their documents, displayed smiles, clapped their hands and offered congratulations.
“Congratulations, congratulations, welcome the highest score ever recorded in written examination history!”
“Yes, yes, it’s an honor to interview such an excellent young man like you!”
“My evaluation of you is perfect, young man, keep it up!”
“…”
‘Though I know it’s all for show, but…’
Even Colin, who was used to hearing flattery, couldn’t help but feel his cheeks heat up.
It felt like he was caught doing something wrong and publicly trolled mercilessly…
‘According to Xu Duojin, a rarely high evaluation like this will likely attract the attention of the “Book of Fate”. However, even under normal circumstances, I should pass…’
Colin thought to himself.
“Alright, let’s hand in the documents first, and Mr. Colin, please stay here for a while.”
After the “white-haired old man” finished speaking, he left the office one by one with the documents and the other six people.
It was about ten minutes after they had left.
The office suddenly fell silent.
All earthen sounds seemed to be cut off at this moment.
‘It’s coming!’
Colin’s heart shuddered.
Perhaps due to the relevant documents being entered and “uploaded,” some indescribable entity seemingly cast its curious gaze towards this place…
Curious about who would receive such high praise.
At that moment,
Colin’s senses suddenly jumbled; he felt like he saw a book with his tongue, smelled the book with his ears, and touched the texture of a book with his nose…
His perceptions were twisted!
“Whoosh!”
A hot blaze erupted from his body, and Colin’s jumbled senses were forcibly restored to some extent.
Following this, he saw the surroundings severely distorted.
And within this distortion, the light emitted by the flames outlined the book…
However, just as Colin saw it, the book opened from the middle, like a gaping mouth, swallowing him almost without any chance to resist.
‘Holy shit, Xu Duojin still told me not to resist, but I literally couldn’t if I wanted to!’
That last thought faded, and all consciousness sank into darkness.
At the same time, within several kilometers, all workers near this park area, including Xu Duojin who had just left, either clearly or vaguely heard the sound of a book slamming shut.
“It seems, the attention has been successfully drawn.” Xu Duojin halted his steps and muttered to himself.
As one of the high-ranking members of “Fate Propeller,” he knew well what that sound signified.
He also knew that Colin would enter a sacred place in the hearts of all “Fate Propellers,” gaining knowledge of the deepest secrets unknown even to this Eighth Level Personnel.
“Oh, it was supposed to be me first.”
He jokingly half sighed.
Then, turning around, he continued towards the area soon to be a battleground.

chapters.title: Chapter 812 - 812 561 Drawing the Attention of the Book of
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 812: Chapter 561 Drawing the Attention of the “Book of Fate”! (Long Chapter!)_2 Chapter 812: Chapter 561 Drawing the Attention of the “Book of Fate”! (Long Chapter!)_2 …
Colin couldn’t tell how long had passed when he snapped back to reality, only to realize that although the surrounding darkness remained, it no longer felt utterly intangible…
“Just what was that book? The ‘Book of Fate’? Was I swallowed by it?”
Colin was full of doubts, but he didn’t have the luxury to think further. He looked around and could clearly “observe” that numerous odd things surrounded him.
These things gave him the feeling they were about to engulf and cause him to lose himself…
Immediately, he instinctively “whooshed” up a flame, blocking out the suffocating sensation of being overwhelmed.
Following that, he saw those odd things were actually black threads, trembling and writhing; some were thicker, like iron wire worms, others as fine as hair…
“What the hell is going on?” Colin frowned, standing still.
But then, a voice reached his ears: “For ‘Bonfire’ to ignite here is surprising. Nonetheless, it helps me find you…”
“Old Master Wu?” Colin asked in surprise.
Yet there was no one to be seen around?
“Right, I’ve seen you through my abilities… Don’t panic. Control your consciousness and walk forward. While things haven’t truly started, I should still have some time and energy to guide you…”
“Right, thank you.” Colin nodded.
But no sooner had he finished speaking, Old Master Wu abruptly said, “Be careful later. Although your abilities won’t fail here, to prevent accidents, I’ll give you a loophole to exploit.”
“Ah?” Colin was puzzled and was about to ask “What loophole?”, but he swallowed his words upon feeling a sudden inspiration.
Next, he heard Old Master Wu say, “There’s no danger here, but, of course, if possible, you’d better keep ‘Bonfire’ in check, as it might inadvertently burn ordinary people’s ‘Threads of Fate’…”
“Thanks for the warning, I’ll control the flame.”
Colin nodded, then saw an invisible “person” ahead.
He propelled himself forward with a thought, following the figure.
Passing through an endless ocean woven from “Lifelines of Fate,” he suddenly smelled a faint yet unmistakable stench of decay…
Oddly, even the ‘Bonfire’ couldn’t mask the odor!
At that moment, Old Master Wu’s cheerful and gentle voice rang out again: “Hehe, that scent is directly fed into your senses in a certain way, so it’s unavoidable.
“For example, if I write on a piece of paper ‘you smell something,’ then you will indeed smell it. You can’t avoid it with normal means.
“However, if you disperse the ‘Bonfire’ now, the smell of decay may be ‘corrected’ to a pleasant fragrance.”
Is this also a technique from the “Book of Fate”? So magical, yet under the ‘Bonfire’, it reveals its true nature… Colin murmured to himself, then, after hearing the last of Old Master Wu’s words, shook his head:
“There’s no need for that.”
He had a vague feeling that there might be something off about “Old Master Wu.”
But when Colin felt that something was amiss, he couldn’t seem to muster any guard against him.
However, it was during their casual conversation and deeper exploration that the surrounding “Threads of Fate” gradually vanished and, as the flames cast their light, Colin saw an old neighborhood in the darkness.
The neighborhood appeared very old, seemingly built in the last century, with many white ceramic tiles already fallen off.
Despite its eerie atmosphere, it also strangely gave off a sense of warmth.
“Do you know where the ‘Book of Fate: Fragment’ came from?”
Upon “hearing” the other’s words, Colin’s pupils subtly shifted as if he had noticed something, but then he covered it up as though he had not noticed at all, decisively turning the discovery into “Inspiration” and concealed it.
He had a premonition that what he saw would become key information later on.
Then, with curiosity on his face as if trying to freeload knowledge, he said, “I don’t know. Is there a story behind it?”
Honestly, he used it more in the early days, but not so much now.
Just gave some extra ‘Points’ to employees, and after a time gap of seven days, used these points to understand the things that needed to be understood…
“Hehe, do you see that oil stain on the ground?”
“Right.” Colin nodded, then as if realizing something, promptly heard the other explain.
“That is ‘Corpse Oil,’ as well as the origin of the ‘Book of Fate: Fragment.’ This Corpse Oil flows into a special area in the real world, which we call ‘Area No.1,’ as it was the first unusual area to appear…
“After collecting the Corpse Oil, it’s added into the wooden pulp in a certain ratio during the paper-making process, to create the ‘Book of Fate: Fragment.’ Ordinary people who use this paper extensively absorb a minute amount of active ingredients from the Corpse Oil, which gives them the opportunity to become basic ‘Fate Propeller’ users, and then it’s all about experiencing events and getting closer to the source of the ‘Book of Fate’…”
Shh, ‘Fate Propeller’ actually has such a secret, huh? Thinking back, when he first saw the official version of the ‘Book of Fate: Fragment,’ indeed it had an odor, but he never thought it was Corpse Oil… Colin clicked his tongue in realization.
However, he had no aversion to Corpse Oil, since he often used products made with it…
Just that after proper processing, they don’t smell.
“Alright, I won’t say much more. Just keep following this trail of Corpse Oil, and, of course, ‘Bonfire’ may accidentally ignite it. If possible, it’s best to extinguish it without worry about not being able to see…”

chapters.title: Chapter 813 - 813 561 Drawing the Attention of the Book of
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 813: Chapter 561 Drawing the Attention of the “Book of Fate”! (Long Chapter!)_3 Chapter 813: Chapter 561 Drawing the Attention of the “Book of Fate”! (Long Chapter!)_3 “I’m fine, I’ll control it well.”
For some reason, Colin felt a strong resistance against putting out the fire, as if it was an untouchable bottom line for him.
After saying this, he walked towards the direction of the residential complex…
A few minutes later, in the darkness of an uninhabited building within the complex, he actually saw a window on the 13th floor lit up, casting a dim and warm light that appeared extremely eerie against the darkness.
And the grease on the ground, which was emitting an increasingly intense smell of corpse decay, was flowing out from the wide-open doorway of this building.
Colin followed it inside.
He saw corpse oil trickling down from the emergency passageway next to the elevator door…
He looked around and then continued walking in.
The narrow, cramped corridors were filled with an overwhelming stench of decaying corpses.
At this point, “Old Master Wu’s” voice continued to appear, as if he were a good friend, “Climbing the stairs is very tiring, you can actually take the elevator without ‘flames’, it’s a lot more convenient.”
“I don’t exercise much, it’s good to walk a bit more.” Colin still did not agree.
As he climbed the stairs slick with corpse oil, after just a few steps, he felt an incredibly strong sense of exhaustion. After only a couple of steps, he was panting and his body was too weary to straighten up.
But he had only reached the eighth floor…
“I said it’s tiring, right? How about… the elevator?” “Old Master Wu” suggested.
Colin shook his head and continued upwards.
Finally, after completing the 13th floor, he was so tired he sat down on the steps, his mouth dry and his tongue parched from exhaustion.
“Why am I… so weak?” Colin panted heavily, his eyes filled with confusion.
“It’s like this when you don’t exercise regularly and then do a lot of exercise all at once,” “Old Master Wu” said beside him. “If you disperse the flames on your body, you could save a lot of effort…”
“No, no.”
Colin took a deep breath, braced his hands on his knees, and pushed himself to stand up, then he walked out of the emergency corridor.
Outside the door, there was just a hallway, and at the end of the hallway, there was a door that was already open.
When he arrived there, Colin looked through the door and discovered what seemed to be a very large, luxurious penthouse with a solid wood style, which was greatly at odds with the aged exterior of the complex.
And on the ground, scattered among many items, were some books, some documents, and so on.
However, what really caught Colin’s attention was…
From the slightly ajar door of one room, he could see the dim light still quietly glowing, and the sound of a pen scratching across the paper, as if someone was writing fervently inside.
“Is there someone?!”
In an instant, Colin felt a wave of nervousness.
But after a moment, he decided to push open that door and enter—
Although he didn’t know why, he felt this was probably the purpose of his visit here.
“It’s very rude to enter someone else’s room with flames, don’t you think? Look at all those documents on the ground, what if you burn them? Better extinguish the flames before entering. It’s not good if this old complex catches fire, and there might not even be water in the fire hydrant…”
“Seems… reasonable…”
Colin felt a very strong urge to disperse the flames on his body because it all made perfect sense.
Yet, another emotion was resisting this urge!
At the moment of this dilemma, Colin had a flash of “inspiration,” realizing something suddenly, and he reached out to grab something next to him.
He seized an invisible “person” out of the void.
Then, the flames flared up, instantly igniting and burning it to ashes…
At last, the air around him grew quiet.
The impulse to extinguish the flames had also disappeared.
“Damn, that was close.” Colin’s eyes cleared instantly, and feeling the damp sweat on his back, he realized he had broken out in a cold sweat.
If he hadn’t spotted a flaw earlier, he might have actually encountered a problem.
The “flaw” was that when the other party verbally mentioned the “Book of Fate: Fragment,” they actually said “Book of Fate·Fragment,” not “Book of Fate Fragment”…
This made him realize he hadn’t heard anything but saw the other person’s words on his retina.
And with this “flaw” as a clue, he could immediately sense other things that were amiss!
“Fuck, come to think of it, I shouldn’t have said I exercise less when climbing the stairs; I should’ve said I exercise a lot and can climb easily; then I wouldn’t be this tired now…”
A strong burst of inspiration made Colin realize that his current fatigue was because that thing, “Old Master Wu,” had literally taken his words at face value.
Say less, and that “whatever it was” would settle it, and then his exercise regime was really less…
As a result, an entity that could confront a First Level Containment Subject nearly died climbing a staircase.
“But speaking of it, I should thank ‘Old Master Wu’ for that help, or else something would have definitely happened…”
Colin exhaled.
Then, after dealing with that “Old Master Wu,” which may or may not have been related to the “Book of Fate,” he moved his eyes, looking toward the interior of the room with the slightly opened bedroom door that was scattered with many documents and books…
The “tap tap” of the pen tip touching paper occasionally sounded, and the person inside the bedroom didn’t seem to notice anything lurking outside the door at all.
Colin shifted his attention slightly downward, noting.
At the bottom of the doorway, there was thick, foul-smelling corpse oil, trickling out bit by bit.
Now he was certain that behind this door might be “Lady Bunny” and other objects of interest to many people.
By pushing open the door, the true nature of the world would be revealed to him, and the peace of the past might disappear forever.
For a moment, he even entertained the notion of backing out.
“No, can’t hesitate now, it feels like… I’m being influenced again…”
With thoughts flashing, Colin stepped into the room.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 814 - 814 562 Descending God
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 814: Chapter 562: Descending God! Chapter 814: Chapter 562: Descending God! Colin felt an uncomfortable sense of unease as he stepped into the room, reminiscent of the feeling he would get as a child visiting a stranger’s home.
“Thump, thump…”
His heartbeat inexplicably quickened, and he felt like a thief, but a deep breath helped him adjust considerably.
At the same time, after entering, he noticed that he could now clearly see the scattered books and some of the document content beneath his feet.
“Gene Control Theory: Selected Edition”,
“Extracting and Applying the Power of Stereotypical Thoughts on Public Perception”,
“Liberating Mysticism: From Beginner to…”,
“Material Deconstruction and Reorganization Guidance”,
“Information and Matter”,
“Human Body…”…
“Some things are still unclear, but speaking of which, ‘Extracting and Applying the Power of Stereotypical Thoughts on Public Perception’ seems…”
Colin paused, his gaze lingering on the book, a vague inspiration flickering in his mind—
This thing was probably talking about “Divine Strike”.
“So, this thing really came from the company.”
Curious, he turned the “Revolver Reverser” into a stick and poked it at the book, trying to lift it to see its contents.
However, he found it completely immovable…
With slight force, the object would collapse downwards, like a sponge.
“Originally, ‘Divine Strike’ must have been taken out from here, but it’s unknown how ‘Fate Propeller’ and the like absorb effective knowledge from these things.”
Colin murmured, taking in everything he could see, thinking that taking advantage of anything he could was worth it. After nearly completing his survey, he approached the door that was opened by a sliver.
He tried to peer inside, but could see nothing…
“Tap tap—” the clear sound of a pen dropping on paper came intermittently.
In his mind, Colin could picture someone sitting at a desk, continuously writing under the cozy, warm yellow light.
Although it was still unclear whether the occupant was the owner of the “Book of Fate” or one of the company’s three giants.
But even if not, it was probably not a small player.
After all, the Corpse Oil flowing out of this room not only nurtured the “Book of Fate”-related item but also developed a whole “Destiny Propeller” and many similar system pathways.
This… Even if not a giant, was probably at least an A Level employee, not much lesser than “Lady Rabbit”!
‘”Lady Rabbit’s” exact level is uncertain, but likely B or B+, or maybe a non-permanent A Level, while the “Book of Fate” seems to surpass a level standard, or even higher, and those who can completely use or carry this level item on missions, considering Rosen’s ‘Hunger’…’
‘Rosen’s tone when he talked about “Lady Rabbit” seems like he was describing someone of a not very different level, so his combat ability may be stronger than “Lady Rabbit’s”, but the position level should be quite similar…’
‘This person here… even if not a giant, is likely an A Level person, just below a giant.’
As Colin’s thoughts spun, he scanned the room again, viewing what could also be a special office?
Why did it feel like the high-ranking members were all so down-to-earth, so “back to basics”…
However, he didn’t dwell on this too much. Realizing the possible rank of the person inside, he took out all his equipment, maximized his BUFF, and prepared for the possibility of having to fight as he pressed his hand on the door and pushed hard—
Immovable.
“Hmm?”
Colin tried again with more force but it remained firmly closed, making him raise his eyebrow: “Something’s up.”
It was then that he suddenly realized from the inspiration transmitted from his mission:
Only those qualified to face the consequences of pushing the door could open it.
He needed to demonstrate the corresponding qualifications!
And his level was, theoretically, supposed to meet the minimum qualifications to handle this situation.
“Damn, ‘Lady Rabbit’ really likes to assign tasks that push the edges of personal capacity, just like Rosen mentioned… I’ve been in the company for less than a year, yet I’m set on apocalyptic-level missions!”
With that thought flickering, Colin instantly activated “Item Liberation” and held four Golden Cards in his hand, not triggering their effects but instead channeling spirit into them, simply releasing their energy.
The emitted power from multiple high-quality items even caused some regional disruptions in time and gravity within the room.
However, these disruptions didn’t affect the room as a whole…
Seeing the situation was almost set, Colin again pressed his hand to the door, ready to push with all his might.
Unexpectedly…
“Creak~” The door was effortlessly pushed open.
And surprisingly, the room inside wasn’t a bedroom but a spacious study, about forty or fifty square meters large. Under warm yellow ceiling lights, rows of books cluttered the shelves, and at the very back by a floor-to-ceiling window, there was an executive desk chair…
However, no person was seen.
Colin, on full alert, saw no adversaries; moreover, the previously intermittent “pen tip” sounds had suddenly disappeared.
Instead, a slight noise of a thick liquid dripping onto the floor took their place…
Pausing for a moment at the doorway, Colin stepped towards the executive desk.
Surprisingly, the rotting smell in the study was quite faint.
And it grew even fainter as he approached the desk…
“Hmph.”
Colin wiped the sweat from his forehead; to ensure he had “qualifications,” he had to continuously maintain full output of the effects of five advanced items, including the “Revolver Reverser”.

chapters.title: Chapter 815 - 815 562 Descending of God_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 815: Chapter 562: Descending of God!_2 Chapter 815: Chapter 562: Descending of God!_2 Even so, it was still a difficult effort for him.
But he had no choice but to do so, Colin had a premonition that if he relaxed, he might be “kicked” out the door in an instant.
After a few large strides, he finally reached the desk and saw an open notebook on it.
The content was written in a diary-like style.
It was very fuzzy, and he couldn’t see it clearly.
Colin, thoughtful, closed his right eye and channeled his energy into the left eye that had been imbued with the “Kindness of the Firebearer max,” and then he was finally able to make out the words.
“…The corresponding preparations are finally almost done, from the first cry of humanity to the emergence of the first ‘Flame Bearer.’ I thought that all problems would eventually be solved, and the few Dark Clouds on the human edifice were only minor troubles…”
“This edifice was supposed to shelter us through storms, to face everything, to break through that so-called final Time point…”
“But unexpectedly, while the edifice is indeed sturdy, embarrassingly enough, the foundation was not firmly laid…”
“And even more awkward is that, even if the foundation had been solidified, the ‘earth’s crust’ began to act up, and even more problems were exposed in the collision with those things…”
“And now, when we cannot turn back, under the scrutiny of various enemies, where any small issue can be magnified infinitely, we simply don’t have the chance to tear down the building and lay a new foundation.”
“The only path before us now seems to be the one where a few ‘people’ ascend to become ‘Divine’ creations.”
“Choosing this means picking up ‘Divinity’ once again.”
“Which is to say, it would be the end of humanity…”
“I will certainly not choose this, the path of humanity, which is based on humans as the fundamental carriers, does not require the involvement of Divinity.”
“But without choosing this, everything seems to have fallen into a deadlock…”
“However, I’ve come through so many ‘deadlocks’ along the way, this one is no different.”
“As a human, I will not allow anything ‘Divine’ to reappear and rise above us!”
“I will not allow humanity to fall into an era of moral decay, loss of ethics, and enslavement like livestock under its torment again!”
“Either we succeed, or they fail, there’s only one possibility.”
“For this…”
“I will initiate what is currently my life’s greatest achievement!”
“The only item the company has ever created that goes beyond its specifications, the only tool that can break the current stalemate!”
“It will trigger a series of unforeseen consequences in a far-fetched, abrupt manner, completely disrupting the stalemate, and during this time, let us fundamentally transform, of course… although it comes at a great cost, I believe we can overcome it.”
“I named it ‘Accident,’ no, that’s a bit lacking in gravitas, although this is a major part of its effect, the standard is not quite there…”
“Ah, I’ve thought of a better name…”
“…”
That was where the page ended, and Colin’s eyes scanned it several times before resting on that last part.
“A bit costly?”
Thinking of the current situation, Colin couldn’t help but make a sarcastic remark. Is this what you call a bit costly?
It’s nearly a complete disaster!
But then, he steadied himself, guided by some kind of spiritual foresight, reached out, and gently turned the page of the notebook, immediately coming upon the four characters that an employee had given as the specific name for the artifact on the next page—
“‘Mechanical Descension’!”
It was at the moment Colin saw these four characters that his heart lurched!
A strong consciousness told him that some kind of disaster was about to erupt!
Just then, a surreal, long unheard but startling sound of dice reached his ear.
No one knew the result of the dice.
However, as the sound of the dice faded, a line of Narrator-like font appeared before Colin’s anxious eyes.
[The true reality of the world descends because of you…]
…
Meanwhile, all over the world, everyone suddenly felt a terrifying pressure descend!
A heart-stopping roar came from the sky.
Terrible things were happening!
“Stability factors are declining rapidly, about to fall below ninety percent…”
“No, it’s already below ninety percent! A large amount of abnormal events is about to break out!” someone shouted in horror.
Ninety percent might sound high, but in reality, it was extremely dangerous, with hundreds of thousands or even more minor events about to erupt. Level 2 threats, entities akin to ghosts and specters, would be everywhere!
“Damn it! Be careful!”
In the halls, some people, always watching the instruments, were yelling, but at this moment, many others had no time to care about it.
Garrisoned all around the world, regardless of where people were, if they were still outside, they could clearly see the day turn dark instantaneously while a bright moon suddenly rose to the center of the sky…
And the once pure moonlight, at this moment, began to give off a faint Red hue.
It was as if this was its most authentic color!
“Ah!!!”
Inside some shelters, bursts of screams suddenly erupted.
“Monsters, monsters! Some people are turning into monsters!”
Among the crowd, someone suddenly puffed up, their twisting muscles ripping through their skin to transform into a three-meter-tall muscle monster, and then, as if mad, lunged at the people around him, with a crazed expression, swinging his fists violently downward…

chapters.title: Chapter 816 - 816 562 Descend God_3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 816: Chapter 562 Descend, God!_3 Chapter 816: Chapter 562 Descend, God!_3 Some people couldn’t dodge in time, and their entire upper bodies exploded instantly.
Blood mixed with viscera splattered everywhere…
The level of gore frightened many who had never witnessed such a scene and who possessed no mental preparation; they simply stood frozen in place, staring dumbfounded, while a few even vomited on the spot.
“Damn it, the ‘consciousness body’ has temporarily failed!” an official Extraordinary One immediately realized the cause.
If it hadn’t failed, these people would continue to “rationally” flee rather than stand still and vomit or even become immobile!
Such a reaction was like the dross within human bodies; once stimulated by danger, this would occur—as if they were born to be cannon fodder, selected by their genes…
But in this moment, this would only make things even more troublesome!
The raging muscle monster continued to smash several bodies, growing larger and heading towards a denser crowd of people.
However, just as a new round of slaughter was about to begin,
a figure with a long sword charged directly into the midst of the battlefield, halting it.“I’ll deal with this Believer contaminated by ‘Red Moon’; take the civilians to another quarantine zone that’s still functioning…” shouted the man wielding the special long sword as he joined the fight.
Merely minutes later, he had defeated the enemy, but when his long sword sliced the opponent’s body into several pieces,
he suddenly felt a strong sense of unease…
The next second, as expected, the corpse fragments burst into a dense red mist.
He couldn’t dodge in time and was directly engulfed by it.
Within the entire “E-29” area, anyone who came in contact with the red mist had their fear and unease erased in less than a second, then viciously lunged at others with wide, manic grins.
Although they hadn’t transformed into the same kind of monster as the “Red Moon” Believers, they had completely lost their minds, akin to humanoid beasts!
Having lost all rationality as humans, they pounced and attacked others on all fours.
Anyone wounded by their bites or splashed with their saliva, blood, or any bodily fluids lost their sanity and went mad…
This demonic madness spread quickly through the tens of thousands of people like a plague.
Amidst the chaos, a dense, white light suddenly emerged.
“Move forward, leave through the main gate, go into that room; someone will save you…”
As the few survivors left, the figure of the official, leaning on his sword, stumbled against the wall and transmitted intermittently through the communicator:
“E-29 is completely out of control, immediately close, fully, the main gate, blockade…”
A golden granular object on his chest emitted a white light, holding back the red mist.
The pure light sheltered his remaining sanity…
But as he watched the gold substance evaporate rapidly, he knew it wouldn’t last long.
Standing at the corridor door, frantically disposing of the occasional out-of-control person acting like a wild beast, he was anxious that the outside world hadn’t received the information.
Fortunately, he didn’t have to wait long; upon hearing a loud “boom” as the great alloy doors hit the ground, he knew his message had gotten out. After the departing gate was completely sealed, he emotionlessly severed his own head…
The headless body, spurting blood, slid down the wall onto the ground, powerless. Yet in the crowd of uncontrollably frenzied, attacking and biting each other, this act barely made any waves.
And it wasn’t just here; anomalies had erupted in all areas.
…
One more chapter

chapters.title: Chapter 817 - 817 563 Red Moon Entity
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 817: Chapter 563 “Red Moon” Entity! Chapter 817: Chapter 563 “Red Moon” Entity! “All those hidden ‘Red Moon’ Believers, for some unknown reason, just lost control completely! Once they kill a certain number of people, or after they die, their bodies turn into a special red fog. Ordinary people and even mid-to-low-level Extraordinary Ones below the Fifth Level, once they come in contact, lose their sanity within ten seconds, and currently, there is no way to treat them…”
“Damn these ‘Red Moon’ Believers!” someone cursed upon hearing this.
“Notify everyone, if a rampaging ‘Red Moon’ Believer doesn’t die immediately, do not kill them, just hold them off. In addition, all contaminated ordinary people may be allowed to be killed…”
“Notify everyone, do not look up at the moon!”
“Notify all personnel to begin a search immediately…”
“Report! In Area 325000 of Z City, a special anomaly has occurred, with a large number of unknown creatures approaching, requesting our support…”
“Report! In Area 374000 of B City, an ultra-giant creature has appeared, requesting Eighth Level Personnel…”
“Attention! Emergency situation! Emergency situation! ‘Shelter No. 4’ has lost contact!”
“Attention…”
…
Faced with a series of unexpected events, people in the command center were scrambling in a state of utter panic.
The incidents caused by the infiltrated ‘Red Moon’ followers had just barely been resolved when a multitude of other crises erupted!
What made some high-level Extraordinary Ones with the ability to predict, deduce, or divine feel even more palpitation was their spiritual intuition telling them that these events, even before the real catastrophe arrived, didn’t even count as an appetizer…
At this moment, on a darkened seaside, an old man looked up at the moon hanging in the sky at noon, feeling that this celestial body, which had always shone throughout the ages, was so unfamiliar at this moment.
“The world has been sealed…” he muttered to himself.
He had originally felt a subtle connection between ‘Bonfire Company’ and the outside world, but now it seemed totally cut off, though most employees hadn’t noticed, as they hardly had any dealings beyond Earth.
The old man looked up, gazing directly at the celestial body, and although he had guessed it a long time ago, what he hadn’t expected was…
Part of the ‘Red Moon’ entity was actually the very one above their heads!
As he pondered, not far in front of him, a modernized city covered in shadows flickered in and out of the vast sea, and within it, a scarlet, colossal entity silently leaped atop the city walls, seemingly gazing up at the moon as well.
It seemed to yearn for its return…
The old man narrowed his eyes slightly. He was unclear why part of the ‘Red Moon’ had been sealed here and why it was erased from the world along with the entire city.
But he knew very well that once it successfully reattached to its body, it would signify the ‘Red Moon’s’ victory.
…
“Hahaha, it’s finally here! It’s finally here!”
In a park, under the bright moonlight tinged with a barely perceptible crimson, countless shadows of ‘The Rat’ surged out like a tide, almost instantly submerging the place.
Abnormal creatures that wandered in the park were covered by shadows and were immediately devoured.
The shrill “squeaks” were ceaseless, sending the scene into a chaos of frenzied revelry.
But then, all The Rats fell silent, prostrated themselves in devotion, and parted to form a path as if to welcome a king…
A towering humanoid monstrous rat emerged from the darkness.
As it appeared and looked up at the moon, it suddenly made a piercing, raspy human laugh:
“Hahaha, it’s finally here! Mother! My great Mother! I will become the leader of the future, hope… give me a little help! Hahaha…”
By this stage of the events, it felt as though it had almost secured its victory!
With its words, all The Rats shrieked, enraptured by the future it described.
At that moment, the giant humanoid rat waved its hand, and a vat of huge, demonic dye was brought out from the space where they had hidden it.
The already active bizarre dye became even more lively under the moonlight.
And a massive canvas was also brought out by using Spatial Displacement from another place.
The canvas already had some basic outlines sketched on it.
“Only the last step remains, under Mother’s ‘rebirth,’ to paint my glory!”
“What I paint shall become reality!”
“But the power of the ‘new birth’ is still lacking…”
“Hehehe, with so many dangerous events erupting in the world now, as part of humanity, I should contribute too!”
While the giant humanoid rat spoke, it seemed to activate something.
It was at this moment that all over the world, in areas affected by disasters, people began to “awaken” new abilities, new Skills!
“It’s the ‘System’! I’ve awakened the System! Haha, let the System lend me its strength!”
“Magnetic awakening! The rotation of the magnetic field! Watch me blast all you monsters to smithereens!”
“Step aside, bro, I’m going to exterminate all these fallen beings!”
“Kill! Tear down this shoddy shelter! They didn’t let me in before; now, I’ll return in the posture of a king, and everyone must die!”
“Hahaha! This power is fantastic!”
“I am reborn? Right, there’s a secret…”
“…”
“What happened?!”
Some official Extraordinary Ones looked at these suddenly emerging Awakeners, who mostly seemed to be aiding their own side, and were more or less stunned.

chapters.title: Chapter 818 - 818 563 Red Moon Entity_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 818: Chapter 563 “Red Moon” Entity!_2 Chapter 818: Chapter 563 “Red Moon” Entity!_2 Despite the fact that most of them had thus received help, instinctively, they didn’t feel it was anything favorable.
And it was at this moment that a voice quickly transmitted through the headphones,
“Attention! Cognition is being rapidly destroyed, the ‘world barrier’ is about to fall to eighty-five percent…”
“All personnel please note! A third-level threat is about to emerge and be universally present!”
“All personnel please note…”
And just as these “Awakeners” appeared en masse, the “world barrier” was once again being charged.
The moon was faintly reddening, growing gradually denser, and some humans with higher inspiration felt an inexplicable lightness and liveliness in their bodies, with their minds suddenly brimming with numerous new ideas.
Outside countless shelters, big and small, some of the ordinarily common creatures, whether birds or beasts, their eyes gradually began to develop a cruel and intelligent wildness.
And they continued to undergo anomalies.
“Eighty percent now, this speed…”
Following this trend, this thing will very likely fall below fifty percent in the not too distant future!
The thought alone made many observers slump in their chairs, their faces filled with despair, for they clearly knew that this meant the reappearance of most of the high-level anomalies that had been sealed or even exterminated.
All containment seals on Earth would fail…
Countless disasters and anomalies would, in an instant, replace humanity as the actual rulers of the world!
No, even whether Earth itself could continue to exist under those horrific things
Was an unknown.
…
“Tens, hundreds, even thousands of ‘Awakeners’ you all can handle, but what if this number reaches ten million? Hahaha!”
The Rat in human form laughed madly, but listening to the panicked words around him, it was as if having a conversation through thin air,
“But rest assured, I’m not some madman who would let the world truly collapse.”
Everything now was just minor sacrifices…
Its actions were all for humanity; people might not understand now, but when it succeeded!
When all returned to unity, then everyone would understand!
By then, the people would know “Bonfire’s” true face, understand that it was never any savior, he was the true savior!
At this very moment, as the barrier’s effect rapidly decreased, the pristine white turned crimson.
The time, had finally come!
“With pigments made from the essence of gods, I paint my colors, witness my greatness!”
It stretched out its clawed hand, which was both human and non-human, dipping into the dye vat to smear the pigment onto the vast canvas.
Under the crimson hue, many anomalies instinctively attacked this location…
However, amidst a wave of countless rats, most mundane anomalies were utterly devoured.
Some of the more powerful heretic factions, inspired by the revelations of their beliefs, attacked in this direction, intending to directly deal with the source of the disaster.
However, compared to those looking over, the large, humanoid Rat didn’t care in the slightest.
Under the illumination of the “Red Moon,” even the “Bonfire Company’s” communications had been severed, making it difficult or outright dangerous for them to come!
Within this world, it was unlikely for any anomalous phenomena that could catch its attention to appear until the “world barrier” fell below fifty percent.
And mere believers would probably not even get past its rat minions…
The only slightly troublesome one might be that agent of the “Book of Fate,” but he was preoccupied with preventing the return of “Mother’s” consciousness to give this place any attention.
Then there was that “Flamebearer” Reservist.
But the guy hadn’t even gone through the official “Flamebearer” Reservist training, his methods were all over the place; in its eyes, he barely counted as moderately skilled.
Just as it continued to smear the painting, it suddenly felt something, and immediately dozens of pitch-black arms shot out from a certain direction, yet they went straight through its body without touching it.
“How could this be?!” Xu Duojin, who had arrived on the scene, was shocked at the sight.
“An Eighth-Level ‘Destiny Propeller’? Good, take care of it first, establish authority.”
The giant Rat spoke, a golden light flickering in its hand as space twisted and turned, and it quickly ended the battle.
…
Meanwhile, under the cozy daylight lamp, Colin snapped out of his daze, and noticing the “World Descends Because of You” in front of him, he immediately felt an overwhelming weight.
He realized that something monumental must have occurred outside!
Colin glanced at the notebook, which actually had quite a bit of content left.
However, reading every single word in this thing was strenuous, and now, if something really was happening outside, he had no spare time to continue watching it.
And most importantly, at this very moment, the demand in his mind to investigate the person behind the “Book of Fate” had shown as completed upon seeing the words “Mechanical Descension.”
It was just that the task seemed to be offline, completed yet unable to be submitted…
“No, it really is ‘offline’.”
Colin furrowed his brows; he suddenly realized that all contact with the outside world seemed to have vanished at this moment.
Even…
A strong premonition told him that “The Descent Project” might have failed at this moment!
He needed to leave!
A huge change must have occurred outside.
With a thought, Colin withdrew the power supporting the “Golden Card,” and at that very moment, he felt as if he had lost the right to stand in the room.
In a span of a single thought, he returned directly to the room he had entered before.
However, as soon as he appeared, Colin found that the room had vanished, turned into ruins, and then, as if sensing something, he looked up to see hanging in the dome above, dark as a curtain, a slightly red… moon?
“Boom!”
Scorching flames soared up instantly, engulfing and protecting Colin.
‘This feeling is…’Red Moon’? No, it doesn’t seem right, it seems like ‘Red Moon’ yet not exactly ‘Red Moon,’ devoid of any signs of the real ‘Red Moon’ stirring…’
‘And why did the ‘moon’ suddenly change like this?’
‘Was it contaminated by ‘Red Moon’?
Colin’s brows knit together, but he couldn’t dwell on this thing…
Because, compared to the perhaps contaminated moon above, the surrounding scene was the real disaster area!
His former “assessment office” had turned into utter ruins.
In the air, unclean breaths drifted everywhere, carrying barely tangible, horrifying presences, along with dense, nauseating stenches of blood…
The personnel previously stationed here seemed to have all evacuated, not staying because of him.
Colin didn’t care about that; after all, it would be quite unrealistic to expect the officials to send protection for him.
However, the sudden change now left him unsure of what to do.
“No new tasks, electronic communications seem to have failed, and original psychic communications appear to be malfunctioning as well, so first, head to Research Facility No. 5 or those shelters to understand the current situation and deal with some anomalies…”
With these thoughts, Colin acted decisively.
Already in full BUFF status, he bent slightly at the waist, legs storing power, and flew up into the sky, diving towards the set destination.
But, before he could fly for two minutes, distant screams reached him.
Colin changed direction, diving towards the source, and saw a large group of people on the ground being chased and attacked by a horde of dark, small, bipedal creatures resembling dogs with gelatinous skin.
“Shouldn’t everyone be in shelters by now? Why have they run out? Were they breached?”
He extended his hand, and flames surged forth, instantly resolving all the anomalies.
“Mom! Wake up, please! Waaah…” A teenage boy was sobbing, holding the top half of his mother’s body, almost torn into pieces by the claws of the beasts.
“Help, somebody save me, I don’t want to die, I don’t want to…” Some were lying on the ground, staring at their ruptured abdomens, wailing continuously, their voices fading more and more.
“…”
Having just arrived, Colin heard the wails, screams, and desperate cries of these dozen or so survivors.
After a moment’s thought, he sighed and activated “Time Reversal.”
The next second, the time for some ordinary people “reversed” by varying amounts, from thirty seconds to a minute prior!
“Stop crying, I’ve revived your mom.”
Colin approached the sobbing boy, summoned the “Fire Tree,” and started emergency treatment for these people.
Hearing Colin’s words, the boy was stunned, then realized his mother was whole again, seemingly truly revived, and started to cry even louder from the overwhelming relief.
Ignoring them, Colin’s gaze shifted, looking at the only severely injured Extraordinary One in the group.
Colin had to quickly understand the current situation.

chapters.title: Chapter 819 - 819 564 The Bad News About Xu Duojin
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 819: Chapter 564: The Bad News About Xu Duojin Chapter 819: Chapter 564: The Bad News About Xu Duojin “You, who are you, what have you done to me?!”
The official Extraordinary One, severely injured and slipping into semi-consciousness, became instantly alert when he opened his eyes and saw Colin.
However, before he could resist, he suddenly found his whole body riddled with branches.
In response to his questioning, Colin simply pulled out a document and placed it in front of this nearly Sixth Level official:
“Don’t worry about who I am, I’ve just finished dealing with a troublesome matter. Tell me everything you know about the current situation.”
On the special paper, stamped with over a dozen direct seals from the highest authority.
And these seals’ inspiration matched up with the man before him whose body was flowing with fire.
“I understand…” the severely injured Sixth Level Personnel sighed with some relief.
These things, at least to his knowledge, could not be counterfeited…
As a Sixth Level Personnel, a mid-to-high-ranking official, he knew a fair amount, though not everything was completely clear to him.
What surprised Colin was that eight or nine days had passed since he had entered that district and seen things, not just the one hour or slightly more than two hours that he had felt.
However, the exact amount of time that had passed was unclear to the severely injured official Extraordinary One.
Since that time, disasters had been occurring continuously, and with the night sky permanently obscured, even the passage of time had become difficult to judge.
Up until now, a large part of the region had lost contact, and many shelters, ill-prepared and lacking in strength, had been seriously damaged…
However, compared to the anomalies that had no significant awareness,
More terrifying were some areas where non-human heretic alien species had begun to invade, arriving by unknown means and, compared to common abnormalities, these heretic civilisations’ actions were more targeted.They carried out indiscriminate slaughter, control, torture, and corruption of all human lives, regardless of gender or age…
And what made people even more desperate and troubled was that these weren’t even the most serious problems.
Above their heads, the light that was gradually turning crimson as the “World Barrier’s” integrity continued to collapse,
That was the truly troubling and desperate matter…
However, no one had much of a solution at hand: they could only watch helplessly as disasters destroyed the world.
After listening to the other party, Colin nodded and then asked, “Where do you plan to go next?”
*Cough cough*, to the Takasugi Shelter to seek help…” said the Sixth Level Personnel, somewhat weakly.
“Takasugi Shelter…”
Colin murmured softly, then immediately, information about the Little Maid flashed across his retina, giving him a general understanding of the shelter’s condition.
Among the official shelters, there were seven star levels, and the five-star Takasugi Shelter was already one of the higher-level shelters.
It would be garrisoned by multiple Level Seven Personnel and possibly Eighth Level Personnel.
The five digital shelters Colin was more familiar with were the highest, seven-star shelters.
‘This ranking system feels like that of hotels…’
As thoughts flitted through his mind, Colin surveyed the surroundings, roughly assessed the injured people, looked far off observing the intensity of some anomalies, then pulled an irregular lump of coal wrapped in gold from his pocket.
At the same time, he took out five “Colorless Crystals,” infused one into the other party’s body to ease the injury and strengthen his condition, while the others were sent into the bodies of the over a thousand people present through fire.
“I don’t have the time to escort you right now. When you move later, you can ignite this, and within the range of the flames, no anomaly will dare to attack you easily.”
Deep within the black char wrapped in gold, faint wails could be heard, seemingly originating from some terrifying creature left behind after being processed and burnt in a special way.
Once burned, it could maintain a flame for at least a month or more.
Among the heretic anomalies that had appeared before the “World Barrier’s” integrity fell below fifty percent, those carrying fire would instinctively flee and avoid them, and most would not attempt to breach the flames to harm them.
Because their value was insignificant, the costs and benefits weren’t proportional.
Moreover, thanks to some kind of energy source and the Bonfire Blessing, they might be plagued by extreme hunger for a considerable length of time.
But it wouldn’t particularly affect their physical abilities…
“Thank you…” After receiving most of the information, the Sixth Level Official Personnel was taken aback, knowing this definitely counted as a valuable item.
However, just as he was at least going to properly thank the man, he found that the man in question had already disappeared without a trace.
…
At the same time, up in mid-air, Colin flew like a stream of flames toward a certain direction.
While talking with that worker, a new mission request had emerged.
The content was: to solve an imminent hidden danger…
There wasn’t much information, but it provided a direction, not very far but definitely not close.
After exchanging information with “Lady Rabbit,” Colin had a strong premonition that the hidden danger mentioned in the new request was probably that “The Rat.”
And at the same time, he could truly sense something brewing in that direction.
Many indistinct gazes were casting their attention there…
“What exactly is up with this moon…”
Colin sensed above his head, his heart heavy with concern.
The night sky had been perpetually covered and the moon hung in the exact center never changing.

chapters.title: Chapter 820 - 820 564 Xu Duojins Bad News_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 820: Chapter 564: Xu Duojin’s Bad News_2 Chapter 820: Chapter 564: Xu Duojin’s Bad News_2 At that moment, Colin could feel that no matter how he moved, his position remained unchanged, always at the center of his sight and on a mental level.
This moon was definitely the same moon, yet, it seemed somehow different…
Meanwhile, as he traveled along, Colin saw that within his field of vision, the entire world had been shrouded by an ominous calamity. There were roaming xenomorphic beings everywhere, their types remarkably diverse, almost making him think he had returned to Great Britain.
Of course, even so, the situation was still much better than in Brython…
He incidentally dealt with several abnormal entities he encountered along the way.
These things were easy for him to handle, but for ordinary people, they would be nothing less than a disaster…
“Unfortunately, the area is too large, I can only solve a small part of it.”
Looking at a small shelter that had been completely hollowed out, Colin sighed, waved a hand, and incinerated the aberrations and the insane humans inside, then continued on his way.
After a while, he paused, squinting towards a location nearby.
In that direction, there was a group of twisted, deformed heretic beings…
They were laughing wildly at the moment, each holding a fork-like weapon, each fork impaling a large piece of shattered human limb, circling around a glowing formation, raising and lowering the forks, with the heretics in the front holding heads, and those in the back holding arms, thighs, thoraxes, etc., running around like lion dancers.
Heretic races, bathing in human blood, celebrated like primitive humans at a bonfire party, bloody and barbaric.
However, before they could continue laughing, a bonfire fell from the sky!
In almost the blink of an eye, most of them were completely burned away.
Only one survivor remained on-site, and Colin extracted a white cloth prop from his pocket, an item obtained from official and company exchanges, effective in forcefully extracting an enemy’s memory under complete control.
Its method was similar to the “Memory Search” method…
The side effect was that the object of the search often had their brain damaged, but for Colin, this was essentially no side effect.
Next, without hesitation, he covered it over the face of the frightened creature, extracting information from its mind.
“The ones who died here, some were armed personnel, along with a fourth-level official…”
Colin pursed his lips, looking at the fragments on the forks.
This xenomorphic race thought that by killing the strong and performing rituals like this, they could gain power and become stronger through the ritual.
“Fire Tree, put them together,” Colin sighed, giving the command.
He continued to press his palm against the white cloth, extracting more information in this manner.
“Hmm, a nearby shelter was breached, some people have escaped, are being chased, not bad, a large part although captured…is not yet dead.”
“However, these things seem to have had their origins cut off, can’t find…”
“The only thing visible is coming out after crossing some channel.”
Colin roughly understood the situation of these xenomorphic races.
Their strongest individual was just barely approaching the standards of a Third Level Containment Subject, any D Level elite or Eighth Level personnel could have a chance to manage them.
Unfortunately, that shelter lacked somewhat…
But no big problem.
He casually punched down, the strongest individual of that enemy race still owed him several dozen tubes of blood.
At this time, “Fire Tree” approached, “Mr. Colin, it has been taken care of.”
Colin nodded, turning to look, there were five corpses in total, three men and two women, their bodies roughly put together. Seeing this, he casually summoned a surge of flames, incinerating them all.
“First, let’s deal with this heretic race before I move on to my mission; otherwise, many people in this area might die.”
Colin stood up and rushed in a certain direction.
Before long, as a hundred-meter-diameter fireball crashed down, a large number of xenomorphic races merely glanced at it before being ignited by the flames, screaming in agony as they rolled on the ground, their lives gradually extinguished.
“Don’t, don’t come any closer! If you come any closer, they will die!” one xenomorphic being attempted to threaten with hostages.
But this move had no meaning for Colin:
“You’re about to die yourself, and you still have time to care if others die?”
“Huh?” Hearing this, the xenomorphic being was taken aback. How did that come across backwards?
Watching a figure approach with an immense aura of pressure, he hastily said, “This place has thousands of hostages, if you kill me, they won’t survive either! Do you understand what I said, do you really want to kill them all?!”
In the midst of speaking, a streak of flame flashed before his eyes.
Then there was no after that…
The bullet passed through and instantly incinerated him.
As this most powerful entity turned to dust, the restrictions applied to ordinary people similarly detonated.
Within the vicinity, everyone’s heart exploded in an instant, and horrific agony ensued, each clutching their chest about to reveal an agonized grimace…
But at that moment, Colin waved his left hand, and time reversed.
Before the crowd’s pained expressions could even manifest, they suddenly realized it seemed as though nothing had happened.
Their hearts, once ruptured and dead, revivified as time reversed.
However, the objects of the reversal did not include that unknown magic responsible for the cardiac detonations…
“Hold this kindling, light it up, it can burn for at least a month. Head to the nearest high-level refuge, it should take about five days on foot, you might get a bit hungry on the way, just bear with it.”
Colin found the Level Seven Personnel, who was leading a partial group in escape tactics and guerilla warfare, repeating words he had said many times before.
“Thank you…” he nodded, taking the kindling from Colin’s hand.
But upon receiving it, he did not immediately start moving, instead, he looked at Colin, hesitating to speak.
“What’s on your mind? Spit it out quickly,” Colin said.
“Are you, by any chance, headed in that direction?”
“Why?”
“It’s really dangerous there. Several high-ranking personnel have lost contact and have warned not to go there…”
“High-ranking personnel? Who?”
Colin asked casually, but immediately received some very bad news.
“Two ‘Divine Strike’ Path Eighth Level Ambassadors, Mr. Xu and Mr. Lin, ‘Destiny Propeller’ Path powerhouse, Mr. Xu, Grand Talisman Grandmaster, Yao Shijie…”
“Wait, ‘Destiny Propeller’—is that Xu Duojin? How long has he been there?” Colin frowned suddenly with a bad premonition.
“Yes, it’s Mr. Xu Duojin, roughly three days ago…” the Level Seven Personnel continued to caution, “The threats there, their techniques, are enough to deal with most of the Ninth Level Personnel, but…”
“That’s enough, I understand.”
Colin waved his hand, cutting him off, “Continue with your escort mission, don’t worry about the rest.”
After finishing, he grabbed his revolver and quickly moved in the opposite direction of the crowd.
Originally, he thought if he had just gone, or even within half a day or a day, there would still be a chance to rescue them, but upon hearing it had been three days, he knew it was difficult.
That place was confirmed as the troublesome spot mentioned in the mission.
Even for him, there was no certainty in resolving it.
Let alone for Xu Duojin and others…
“Still, the enhanced mark I gave before should last a long time. I could use it at full strength for a day, his consumption and output might be less than a fifth of mine, it shouldn’t let him be instantly killed, and if he’s lucky, he might even hold on…”
With that thought flashing through his mind, Colin no longer delayed and started moving at full speed.
Along the way, he encountered some research facilities, some intact, others under attack.
Although Colin was in a hurry and did not stop, he still offered considerable help.
Like a meteor’s vibration, within the radius illuminated by the firelight, all heretics were utterly incinerated.
The majority of abnormalities that appeared didn’t even qualify to gaze directly at him before turning to ash.
.
.
Another chapter follows
.

chapters.title: Chapter 821 - 821 565 The Madman Plotting Red Moon
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 821: Chapter 565: The Madman Plotting “Red Moon”! Chapter 821: Chapter 565: The Madman Plotting “Red Moon”! During his journey, Colin encountered a large number of “Awakeners.”
These “Awakeners” are hard to classify as having good or bad dispositions, as long as they didn’t do anything against nature, Colin didn’t kill them, but he left a trace of a weak flame clinging to their bodies.
This flame served not only to “monitor” them but also had the function of temporarily stabilizing their mental state.
After all, most of these so-called “Awakeners” are just ordinary people who have obtained a talent or similar company ability, those ordinary people who had not injected “Gene Compensation Medicine.”
Using this thing, they wouldn’t have any problems in the early stage, but as time went on, they would start to have mental issues…
In addition, some had their desires inflated due to suddenly gaining power and committed unforgivable acts such as rape and murder. Regardless of their status or reasons, Colin chose to casually execute them.
Meanwhile, some of the “Awakeners” below looked up at the abnormal life that had endangered them now engulfed in flames, then looked at the large fireball streaking across the sky, their faces showing shock.
“How could such a powerful Transcendent appear just after the ‘Spiritual Energy Resurgence’?”
“No, it shouldn’t be, the authorities seem to have had Extraordinary Ones long ago…”
“Perhaps there have always been Extraordinary Ones in this world!”
They whispered among themselves, feeling that the world seems to hold many mysteries they couldn’t understand, full of curiosity about everything behind the scenes.
