From within the light door, a hand could be dimly seen slowly reaching out…
It was at this moment, seeing this scene when Yukionna felt utterly powerless and desperate.
Suddenly, the space around her warped, forming a vortex, and from the “vortex”, dozens of hands capable of manipulating fate reached out, pulling her and Colin, perched on her shoulder, into the vortex first.
After an unknown duration, when Colin once again opened his eyes, he found himself in a storm-swept, fiery desert wasteland.
The “nuclear blast” seemed to have stopped, and many fragments above the dome seemed to have fallen; the world everywhere was filled with anomalies and terror…
Moreover, whether it was an illusion or not, the world seemed to have become much larger.
However, without pausing to think further, Colin suddenly had a realization. He saw, not far away, an elderly figure with white hair standing there, seemingly observing something.
At that moment, the figure also seemed to have sensed something and turned around.
When Colin saw that face, he was stunned for a moment and then immediately understood why “Yukionna” had been able to find him!
Suddenly, he couldn’t contain his emotions and joyously exclaimed:
“Old Master Wu?! It’s great! You’re alive; I thought you were dead…”
“Thank you for your concern…”
Old Master Wu nodded expressionlessly and approached, saying, “I still have some unfinished business, very busy, so I haven’t had time to die…”
In fact, he was both himself and not himself, at least in a certain sense. When he appeared in this world again as a “safeguard”, as the formal executor of the will of the “Book of Fate”, it meant that his own fate had reached its end.
But these weren’t things he needed to discuss with Colin now…
The other party just needed to simply consider him an old man having a final flicker of life.
In a flicker of thought, Old Master Wu continued, “Additionally, there’s something to tell you, ‘Yukionna’ really did find you because I asked her to… But wait, this isn’t the place to talk…”
The moment his words fell, a profoundly oppressive gaze descended from somewhere, and behind the gaze was a terrifying presence emitting a strange pale light. Countless wings enveloped a red eye filled with blood vessels, shedding infinite brilliance in the air.
Old Master Wu, unafraid, grasped Colin with his left hand and raised his right hand as if holding an invisible book…
The pages within the notional book fluttered rapidly.
The book documented exceptional techniques from other creatures, which he accessed, simulated, and borrowed at that moment.
Amidst a tolling bell sound, the space began to exhibit some strange changes.
The next second, he and Colin’s figures disappeared from their original spot, appearing at a very distant location.
Without staying longer, with several similar rapid spatial jumps, they eventually stopped on the penthouse of a building situated halfway up a hill.
This place was one Colin remembered from before, known as Institute Number Three, one of the five major Numerical Research Institutes.
However, Institute Number Three was now a collapsed ruin, all its plans seemingly failed, devoid of any life…

chapters.title: Chapter 847 - 847 574 Guidance of Fate_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 847: Chapter 574 “Guidance of Fate”_2 Chapter 847: Chapter 574 “Guidance of Fate”_2 A shattered Twilight Angel lay dead some kilometers away, emanating a dimming amber glow similar to a setting sun.
Clearly, the battle here had employed the latest achievements, those mighty mystic arts and various technologies once acquired from other worlds…
Yet the result seemed no better for it.
The old man gazed at this scene for a long while before finally sighing and approaching Colin’s side, observing the young man who had once again fallen into unconsciousness. Then his right hand slowly lifted, as if cradling an invisible “book”, from which special, intangible “Book of Fate” pages fell like leaves.
They landed on Colin, wrapping him in layers so dense light could not penetrate.
Before long, Colin came to and found his body much more comfortable:
“It feels much better…”
The negative effects persisted, but his head was not as throbbing, and most importantly, his cognitive ability and speed had returned to at least a normal human level, and he could hold a simple conversation.
Not as before, when even speaking was a luxury.
“Mm…” Old Master Wu nodded, pupils moving with black lines that seemed to check Colin’s injuries, before he continued to speak.
“Your situation is dire, and I can’t solve it, but to offer you some concealment, to prevent those extra-specimen entities from targeting you, that I can manage—if you refrain from using that Flame explosively, they should shield you for a while. I don’t know how long, but, as long as possible.”
“I can sense you seem to need to break through the Blockade, to reach the ocean, but now is not the time. Their divine powers have not fully dissipated, so I advise against moving now. At least in the future I glimpsed, it’s virtually impossible for you or me. And afterward, I can’t offer further help. When the timing is right, I will have run out of Time…”
“The path ahead is yours to walk alone.”
“Moreover, you seem to have the slightest inclination towards throwing in the towel. Remember, do not choose death lightly. I’ve sacrificed much to save you, not just me. I sense others, unknown to me, have made sacrifices and rushed for your sake…”
“We may not necessarily win, but please do your utmost. Next, take care of yourself. The right time will soon come. I guess, it should be when the ‘Red Moon’ fully lands and its pollution covers the world. Those so-called ‘Gods’ wouldn’t dare move during the ‘Red Moon’s’ period…”
“After that, pinpointing your exact location, They won’t risk an unclear cost to target you directly…”
“The aura of the Red Moon will take at least half a year to fade, slower, and it might be years…”
“When the time comes, you can strive… set sail for the ocean, and then, I can no longer see…”
The old man droned on until there, then fell silent, seemingly finished with his instructions, as if waiting for Colin, who was affected by negative effects, to digest his words.
After a moment, Colin, having pondered with difficulty, nodded slightly: “That’s enough.”
It was then he belatedly realized Old Master Wu seemed somewhat off…
“So, Colin, I wish you the best of luck…” said the old man with a sigh.
“Is that ‘good luck’?”
“No, it’s just a blessing, a regular one… My power is no longer sufficient to sway your fate.”
Colin reflected silently for several minutes: “Seems like it’s not something good…”
“No, it’s one of the few good things.”
Old Master Wu said with a headshake and a smile, not explaining why, but instead, he turned and walked step by step towards the edge of this deserted skyscraper, closing the conversation:
“It seems, I’m going ahead of you.”
As he spoke, he stood at the skyscraper’s edge, overlooking the vast and desolated land, his smile slowly fading.
Those eyes, as if reflecting ages of settlement, worn but filled with a strong will, mirrored everything ahead like panes of glass.
The once thriving city before him, now seemed low and empty in the wake of the disaster.
Who knew if the hundreds of thousands or millions of buildings collapsed into utter ruins, leaving countless people crushed to death, buried deep, only corruption and the stench of death flowing…
Among such a hellish landscape of ruins, he saw countless Lifelines of Fate…
In those innumerable threads, the resentment shown by people in extreme despair, the immeasurable hardships and choices, the incalculable deaths and helplessness…
Countless Threads of Fate snapped here…
Like reaped straw…
The weight of life, so trivial.
“These people, shouldn’t have just died here.”
Old Master Wu supported that phantom book, and with a tone as calm as it was roaring, declared as if making a proclamation:
“As the Bonfire witnesses! I shall commence another round here, to grant those unwilling to fall here another life, to transcend their doomed fate, to challenge this catastrophe that for them, is utterly undeserved!
“Now, regarding their ‘death’…
“I, with the witness of ‘Bonfire’ and the ‘Book of Fate’, shall pronounce it null!”
During this declaration, he no longer concealed himself, exposed to the countless “unknowns” below, engaging directly with the “Gods”!

chapters.title: Chapter 848 - 848 574 Fates Guidance._3
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 848: Chapter 574 “Fate’s” Guidance._3 Chapter 848: Chapter 574 “Fate’s” Guidance._3 Yet facing his opening move, not a single “unknown” dared to casually intervene…
For, a blurred book had appeared in his right hand.
Whether it was the mysterious and strange “unknowns” holding supreme authority, or any other entity, at this moment, willingly or not, it was difficult to step in and interfere…
The moment after the book appeared, a hard-to-observe yet omnipresent “human fate agglomeration” reemerged in the world.
It was so vast that it seemed to cover the entire world, the fine threads stemming from it entwined with countless individual humans.
Even if their bodies were rotted, from the viewpoint of the “Book of Fate,” they were not completely dead.
Countless threads of fate rose from the ruins like smoke, instinctively encircling Old Master Wu like a school of fish, seemingly lost and unsure of where to go.
At that time, the elder lifted his head, gazing at the sky above.
Directly above, shrouded in crimson, an obscure red celestial body, about twice the size of the Moon, arrived in response to his call, in an incomprehensible way.
This was an elusive and perplexing astral body, like the fate of a person’s entire life.
In the past, it had an ancient name unknown to the masses—”Blazing Mars.”
However, the celestial body was just its facade, a symbol in the physical world. Under the elder’s gaze, the dark red star appeared unchanged to the naked eye, but on another level, within human cognition and imagination, it violently expanded like an explosion, revealing its true form…
An entrance to a horrifying and swelling world made up of numerous elements, like an abscess, layer upon layer of active strangeness.
Countless things struggled to break free from it, while unceasingly others were being dragged into it from other dimensions…
The moment it revealed itself, aside from a few rare beings, all other prying eyes hid away, not daring to look directly.
But not all were timely, some existences, terrifying for mortals, failed to avert their gaze in time and were pulled into the veritably alive and bizarre world by its intangible tentacles.
This was the greatest secret and ultimate countermeasure controlled by the “Fate Propeller” after reaching the Ninth Level!
The portal connecting “City of Scripts” with reality.
It had descended.
In the past, when confronting insoluble beings, Old Master Wu’s approach was to pay a certain price, set up layers of traps, and eventually cast them into the world once called “the confluence of fates,” now named “City of Scripts” by the company’s employees.
Only in this way could he prevent the return of those dreadful powerful beings.
However, this summoning of the portal was evidently not for the simple purpose of banishing an entity.
Old Master Wu took a deep breath, his tone heavy as he spoke,
“Fate continues on!”
While speaking, he lifted his hand, slowly yet with unwavering determination, pointing towards that active and bizarre world…
In the next second, countless threads of fate left by the deceased seemed to find their direction, beginning to move…
Billions of fate threads, snapped during calamities, charged forward wildly, like numerous ships sailing towards their destinations, ceaselessly entering that massive agglomerated world, to fight for another chance at extension!
Seeing this scene, Old Master Wu let out a slight sigh of relief.
Although that place was no safe haven.
At least, their abruptly interrupted fates would not merely end here…
Stop at this sudden and terrible disaster.
At the same time, this also satisfied the payment required by the “Book of Fate”: the extensive participation of humans in the scripts of the “City of Scripts.”
Indeed, the initial contracts signed for “voluntary” participation in exercises, creating the “human consciousness agglomeration,” was all in preparation for this moment.
Other matters such as making rational beings obey arrangements were nothing but a facade, the current request was the true and ultimate aim.
And in repaying this cost to the “Book of Fate,” for the people, at this moment, it wasn’t entirely a bad thing.
Anyone who had signed and harbored resentment or regret about their death had the chance to live a second life in the endless world of scripts.
Although this arrangement came from the “Book of Fate.”
Under the premise of “living,” letting them enter for whatever other purposes the “Book of Fate” might have, was acceptable.
He believed that people would ultimately triumph, break free from it, and return!
It was long after, when every ship had sailed past, that this great ship, which had sacrificed all to show the way and block the storm, slowly submerged.
Old Master Wu stood there, still maintaining the gesture of pointing forward, motionless, under the gradually dimming twilight, like an eternal statue…
The strongest “Fate Propeller,” born in death, and thus concluded.
Who knows how long passed when the red light once again covered everything, the celestial body in the sky vanished without a trace, as if it never existed.
.
.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 849 - 849 575 The 3rd Day of Descent
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 849: Chapter 575: The 3rd “Day of Descent. Chapter 849: Chapter 575: The 3rd “Day of Descent. “Goodbye.”
Colin’s eyes flickered, wanting to say farewell, but due to extreme fatigue, even as his mouth opened slightly, no sound came out.
And at that moment, fearing “Old Master Wu,” the “Yukionna” hidden in the shadows reappeared.
By the time Colin’s eyes opened and closed again, a lot of time had apparently passed.
Because the scene had once again changed…
He had been taken by the “Yukionna” into a hiding spot in some unknown corner.
However, since Old Master Wu had helped mask some of his scent, he was no longer like before, sporadically sought out by cultists or even some high-level Containment Subjects.
Moreover, the pollution from the “Red Moon” served as a sort of natural canopy in a way, deterring high beings from descending.
Now, at last, he finally had a chance to catch his breath…
But, Colin also noticed that the duration of his unconsciousness seemed to be getting longer and longer.
He used to wake up several times a day, but now he might not even open his eyes once in an entire day.
And the intervals between awakenings were getting shorter and shorter…
…
Meanwhile, beneath a world covered in crimson,
Deep inside a shattered refuge, within the only channel of clear water, suddenly a “squeak squeak squeak” sound emerged.
Before long, a figure covered in scars and extensive burns emerged with a splash, their hands stretched out onto the bank from underwater.
Then, aided by a host of unseen rats, he crawled out.
Lying on his back amidst the ruins, he struggled to lift his head and peered through the cracks at the dark red world outside, his eyes filled with hate.
If it weren’t for that guy, none of this would have turned out like this!
“Colin, the world has collapsed, countless lives have been lost to this, is this what you, is this what you ‘Flame Bearers’ wanted?!”
“We’ve all lost!”
“What ‘Flame Bearer’?! A bunch of long-dead souls, only dragging others down! There’s nothing but empty promises, no actual substance to prove success, just blind faith… What’s the difference between this path and a pyramid scheme?!”
“The fate of humanity should not be left in the hands of such scammers…”
“No, I haven’t lost, I still have a chance, I can still succeed, no, only I can, only I can make it…”
“Only I can lead…”
His spirit seemed tangible as he spoke with resentment.
Towards the end, his whispers turned somewhat frantic.
After a while, he seemed to notice something, and all sound instantly vanished.
He turned his head toward the nearby corner, where he saw a group of survivors huddled together, shivering as they watched him…
“Hey, hehehe, truly, lucky, at this time, to still encounter such high-quality, biological material…”
The horribly disfigured figure began to speak:
“You, come here, you are very lucky, you will have the opportunity to become an important part of humanity’s great plan again, come, give me your biological matter…
“I promise, your sacrifice will be forever remembered by me, your contribution will be remembered by all…
“I will live forever with you!”
He uttered an extremely persuasive and amiable whisper, trying to call those ordinary people to him.
However, unexpectedly, these people showed no sign of being swayed by his power…
Was it because he was too weak?
“To sacrifice for me, is to sacrifice for humanity’s great fate, what are you standing there for?!” he said, somewhat anxiously.
His power was clearly still present, so why weren’t his words having any effect?
Why weren’t those people coming forward to devote themselves to the great cause?
Nearby, the few rats that remained squeaked as if issuing threats.
Nevertheless, the survivors didn’t budge, just staring at him from the shadows.
“You…”
Before he could finish, the old acquaintance, now somewhat calm, noticed the strange emotion on the faces of these ordinary people who lacked a sense of the bigger picture…
There was both fear and hatred…
Why would they hate?
At that moment, an angry shout came from the crowd.
“It’s him! It’s that Rat monster, I remember, it’s him who killed Uncle Liu, killed my father, made our refuge disappear!”
A teenage girl, with tears streaming down, yelled angrily, ready to charge forward.
She clearly remembered how, that Rat monster, with some incomprehensible talk of “sacrifice,” had killed all the Extraordinary Ones in the refuge, drained their blood, poured it into a large cauldron, and then left.
It was because of this that the refuge was destroyed, and countless people died…
The few remaining people could only hide in this deepest single room of the refuge, surviving on their last morsels.
In that moment, she wanted to rush out and fight the monster, but before she could, she was pulled back by her equally enraged mother.
However, her brother, unnoticed on the side, actually broke away from the crowd, clutching a brick he had picked up at some point, and rushed towards him.
“Be careful…” the mother cried out in desperation.
But by then, the little boy’s brick had already viciously struck the ghastly creature.
“Die! Die, you monster! Monster!!!” the little boy screamed heart-rendingly, swinging the brick with all his might, smashing it repeatedly onto the monster’s head.

chapters.title: Chapter 850 - 850 575 The 3rd Coming Day. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 850: Chapter 575: The 3rd “Coming Day”. _2 Chapter 850: Chapter 575: The 3rd “Coming Day”. _2 “You…” The Rat-man wanted to say something, but he found himself dizzy and disoriented from being hit by a child—
How could this be possible? How could he be so weak that a child with no extraordinary means could knock him out with a brick?
And at that moment, a burst of footsteps suddenly emerged.
He saw that, upon witnessing his weakness, the fear in the eyes of the people hiding behind vanished, replaced by a chilling hatred…
This hatred consumed all their emotions, driving them to seek some kind of revenge.
A chaotic assault came from all directions the next second; amid his dizziness from being hit, he seemed to finally realize the reason:
“Fate…!”
“No, you can’t treat me this way…” Amidst various attacks, he struggled to extend a hand, trying to crawl away.
But in the end, under the stormy fury of the people, his hand fell to the ground and was trampled and broken.
Unaware to those still furiously venting their anger on the corpse was that, at that moment, a line of secret, inconspicuous text appeared on their retinas.
“[Those who choose to sacrifice others, in the end, die at the hands of those they sacrificed…]”
“[To die so meagerly in a remote, narrow ruin, unknown to anyone.]”
“[And the avengers, from that point on, harden their hearts and continue to exist in this world.]”
…
At the same time, in a barely functioning basement, Colin, who Yukionna had stuffed into what she considered the safest place—the freezer compartment of a refrigerator—suddenly opened his eyes slightly, revealing a flicker of confusion in his turbid gaze.
For some reason, he felt much lighter, as if some indescribable danger had suddenly disappeared…
But he couldn’t quite put his finger on what it was exactly.
‘It must be… a good thing,’ Colin thought groggily.
Taking the opportunity, he routinely sensed the outside world and could confirm one thing: the world had indeed grown much larger, possibly due to all those small worlds, inner worlds, and the like…
Because of the “Red Moon,” these worlds were all exposed.
Consequently, Earth’s area had expanded to an extent previously unimaginable, and the anomalies and Heretic Races emerging from these worlds mingled together, creating an even tenser situation…
The good news was, this also made it harder for those things to find him.
The bad news was…
It was now an era of unprecedented chaos.
In Colin’s mind, under the strong sense of spirituality, he could vaguely glimpse scenes unfolding in various worlds—
On a continent aglow with a strange light, countless kangaroo-like creatures burst forth, trying to spread beyond the world, but most sank into the sea without traveling far.
Underground, odd, mucus-like creatures surged out in hordes and spread themselves out as much as they could to bathe in the red light, voicing their praises…
In some regions, every few kilometers felt like entering a different world—one moment it was a land of snow and ice, the next it was an endless flow of lava, or a bizarre area devoid of gravity…
From a distance, it looked as though different worlds had been stitched together, with clear boundaries.
Some surviving humans whispered in the dark, praying, unwittingly drawing the unsettling gaze of others…
…
“It feels like I can almost imagine the sea now. Looks like the blockade has dissolved a bit…”
Colin’s thoughts were fragmented as he remembered the time before he had come out of “Hunger” and the “Red Moon” pollution hadn’t spread, when the power of the Gods was still present…
There was a time when he had forgotten even the concept contained in the word “sea,” and had it not been for a mission hanging over him, he might have forgotten the word “sea” entirely.
But now he remembered much more, at least he recalled what the ocean was.
And he had a sense of where this thing might be…
“Once some time has passed, the blockade weakens, and my body feels a bit better, then I can try to have Yukionna take me into the sea…”
Colin thought drowsily; he was very sure that these negative effects on him could not be cured by rest alone.
Only by following the mission and entering the sea could he be cured.
But before that, it was time to sleep…
No, to think about how to escape the nightmares after falling unconscious.
Inside his dreams, he kept repeating very rigid and monotonous actions, like endlessly climbing stairs with his body out of control, then feeling a magnification of fear, or even biting himself…
After waking up, he didn’t find it to be terrible, but in the dream, it was as agonizing as the torture of water dripping.
He was once again lost in a coma, his eyebrows tightly furrowed from the intense pain and all the confusion within him.
…
“World Code-13,” “Bonfire” Church’s only grand cathedral.
Sister Shana, clad in holy white cult robes with golden trim, radiated a pure light as she stood in front of the deep hall’s Bonfire, her eyes closed as if she was napping, her beautiful and fair face faintly visible in the glow of the flames.
Since the last time an employee had arrived from Earth, more than ten days had passed.
By the current understanding, two “Arrival Days” had gone by.
But on both occasions, no one came here.
The third one was coming soon…
However, there was no sign of anything getting better.
Thinking of this, Sister Shana’s brows furrowed slightly, and her inner anxiety deepened.
Through some indescribable inspiration, she could distinctly feel that something unimaginably horrific was happening on the other side—yet as for the specifics, especially Colin’s current status, she was almost entirely in the dark.
This made her even more uneasy…
On the other side, Little Red sat holding her knees in her room, biting her lips despondently, her swollen eyes red as she stared at the last White Rabbit milk candy.
Big Brother Colin had said that he would come after she finished the candy.
But now…
She was down to the last piece.
It seemed that finishing it would reveal the outcome.
But she dared not eat it, afraid of obtaining a result that she neither wanted nor could accept.
“You haven’t really eaten anything in days, have some food first…” Sister Shana’s hazy, shadowy clone came to her side and comforted her.
“Okay…” Little Red replied with a nasal sound but didn’t move, simply burying her head deeper.
Shana reached out and rubbed her head, about to speak, but Little Red suddenly looked up with a woeful face and tear-filled eyes:
“Sister Shana, if, if I finish this candy and Big Brother doesn’t appear, does that mean… he might never come?”
At these words, Shana fell silent for a few seconds, then reassuringly said, “Don’t think too much, it’s just…he’s been busy, there won’t be any problems.”
“Sister Shana, I don’t want to do these problems anymore, I want to gain power, I want to help him…”
Shana wasn’t sure how to respond; she wasn’t really adept at offering private comfort with insincere words, so she could only say:
“You need to become smarter to help him, and of course, if there’s a chance, I will teach you some things…”
Little Red had a sort of extraordinary talent related to biological knowledge and the methods of esoteric studies.
She could easily grasp the essence of some of those things…
It seemed related to the special trait inherent in her being.
But, that trait in her wasn’t very stable, her emotions, once disturbed, could easily cause problems, making it risky to attempt.
Hearing Shana’s words, Little Red finally felt a bit better. Then, worry flickered in her eyes as she recalled some past attempts…
In certain statuses, she might even attack Big Brother!
This…made her fear herself.
“Don’t worry, it’s just a simple trial, don’t be afraid, if you can’t trust yourself, then trust me…” Shana rubbed her head again: “For now, you need to get your body in shape…”
Hearing this, Little Red nodded vigorously.
Not long after, under Shana’s comfort, Little Red finished eating and fell into a deep sleep.
“Have a good sleep.”
After speaking, Shana sat beside the bed, her hand stroking Little Red’s head, her legs swinging, as she hummed a light lullaby, waiting for the third Bonfire arrival time to come.
After a while had passed…
She thought this Bonfire would remain as silent as before.
But just then, the flames suddenly began to shake!
…
Wait, there’s another chapter.

chapters.title: Chapter 851 - 851 576 Boss Huang He
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 851: Chapter 576 “Boss Huang He Chapter 851: Chapter 576 “Boss Huang He The grandiose bonfire began to shake rapidly, followed by dozens of ash streaks erupting from the base of the flame, quickly taking human shapes within the hall…
“Have they arrived?”
Startled, Shana’s emotions fluctuated ever so slightly, causing her eyes to brighten, as a flash of pure white light darted across the depths of her eyes.
But in the next second,
After sweeping her gaze across the crowd, her ice-blue eyes, as beautiful as gems, swiftly filled with a hint of disappointment.
The staff who had arrived totaled forty-seven, among whom she did not find the figure she had hoped to see.
Moreover, judging by the emotions reflected on their faces, Shana had a very ominous premonition.
With her thoughts in complex disarray for some seven or eight seconds, she turned to a female D Level staff member with whom she had a somewhat better relationship:
“What happened over there?”
As she spoke, she took caution to isolate and protect certain information from being overheard by others.
Listening to the woman’s account, Shana’s heart nearly sank.
Indeed, a major event had taken place in Mr. Colin’s world, a god-level calamity had erupted, launching a pursuit against Colin… Although the staff present had not directly faced the battlefield, the D Level Personnel still had a general understanding of the overall situation.
In addition, there was the existence beyond comprehension, the “Level 0″…
After the chaotic disaster continued for over half a month, they had finished handling matters and managed to come here first.
Others would be following them later.
But…
Even if more were to come, the likelihood of Colin being among them was slim.
After hearing her out, a silent Shana immediately realized something – with Colin’s abilities, there was no way he could handle such an immense apocalyptic event without outside interference…
This was not belittlement, but rather because during this time, many of Colin’s combat tactics had practically been imparted by her.
Therefore, regarding Colin’s level of strength, Shana had a relatively clear understanding of this man who could almost be called her disciple.
Even though he possessed some trump cards that startled even her, they probably weren’t enough to change the entire situation—otherwise, these people wouldn’t have needed to flee here.
At the same time, her rich combat experience made her well aware of just what level a First Level Containment Subject occupied.
“You all… go and rest for a bit.”
After sending them off, Shana let out a sigh.
She had some guesses as to why Colin hadn’t called for her… firstly, he probably deemed it too dangerous; secondly, without surprise, even if he really had summoned her, it likely wouldn’t have made a difference.
Too many fearsome incarnations existed, and a clone going over wouldn’t provide any real help.
She might even provoke certain entities due to her interference, bringing crisis to “World Code-13.”
Standing in front of the seemingly eternally blazing “Bonfire,” Shana pondered for a while…
“Since a clone going over is unlikely to be of any real help, then I will go myself!”
Shana’s gaze flashed, making up her mind.
As for how to get there, she had no method, but she knew of something that could do the job—
Parchment!
Aside from the occasional necessity of entering that world, there was practically no need to use it during the rest of the time.
“I need to go to ‘Earth’.”
In front of the Bonfire, Shana looked at the parchment in her hand and spoke softly.
Long ago, she had learned of the name of these people’s home from the staff…
However, in response to her inquiry, the parchment showed no reaction, as though it were unable to operate.
She frowned, refraining from repeating her words, but a burst of pure white light emerged in her eyes, and behind her unfolded wing after wing of immense Wings of Light:
“When I came to understand some of the true nature behind things from Mr. Colin, I somewhat realized that you probably don’t belong to this world, right?
“And my current authority is enough to banish you from here forever, should you refuse to aid me…
“So I hope, it would be in your best interest to assist me with this.”
She stated calmly.
It was right after she finished speaking that she finally saw some text appear on the parchment.
[It has been detected that your current decision is rather rash. Countdown will conclude at 11:59. After you have calmed down, we will then respond to your query…]
“I have considered it thoroughly; there is no need to wait.”
However, after this text appeared, no matter what she said, it stopped responding.
Shana had no choice but to wait, until the deep hours of the night arrived…
[The world you wish to go to is now shrouded in numerous evil threats. The senior employee who previously protected it now faces a multitude of external enemies, as well as those beyond “Time” and “Spatial” boundaries, and is unable to offer any more assistance…]
[Under current circumstances, the success rate of your action is less than ten percent. Any incaution could result in perishing in this calamity.]
[…]
A multitude of words emerged, together with some inspired thought, making it clear to Shana that indeed, the danger was immense, yet she did not waver much.
She tilted her head slightly, the gold ornaments on her earlobes shimmered dazzlingly with a subtle sway:
“What else?”
As a Saint who had risen through the ranks, she wouldn’t shrink back just because she was intimidated.
And furthermore…
When this thing had urged her to face an Ancient God while she was still not very powerful, why hadn’t it warned of any danger back then?
[In addition, that place is within the “wall.” Without special permission, no one outside of the “wall” can directly arrive; one must travel through a series of transportation points. Even under the most favorable conditions, it would take at least six months to reach your destination…]

chapters.title: Chapter 852 - 852 576 Boss Huang He_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 852: Chapter 576 “Boss Huang He”_2 Chapter 852: Chapter 576 “Boss Huang He”_2 [During this period, there will be many entities that reject the “Primordial Fire,” and upon perceiving you, they will launch an assault against you.]
[And at least half a year later, even if you successfully arrive, it’s highly likely that everything will have already concluded.]
[…]
As she read these contents, Shana fell silent—half a year’s time, indeed, things were likely to tend toward tragedy.
But still…
“This does not dissuade me,” she slowly spoke.
Upon hearing this response, the parchment rapidly revealed numerous pieces of information.
[At present, trying to resolve the crisis there, aside from the birth of a “Flame Bearer,” there are virtually no other paths… Despite that employee’s belief in the possibility of a “Flame Bearer” being born, realistically and objectively speaking, this likelihood is extremely slim, and now nobody knows how to attract the “Primordial Fire”…]
[Theoretically, anyone, even an ant with humanity, could potentially kindle the “Primordial Fire.”]
[But in practice, up to now, such an event has never occurred.]
[Compared to this uncertain outcome, there is another method at present—to find the “Flame Bearer” ID number 18 or other key remnants related to it…]
[…]
“There’s no need to speak further on this matter.”
Shana shook her head: “You’ve been pursuing this for more than a moment, and since the predecessors haven’t succeeded, I don’t believe that I alone can achieve it…”
In times past, Colin had mentioned that the parchment collecting a great amount of points was likely preparation for finding someone or something.
Now, it seemed to be so.
However, since this has not been successful for so many years, she didn’t believe that she could simply intervene and make it work.
Compared to the “Flame Bearer” of ancient times that she had never seen, she believed more in the “Flamebearer” Reservists of current times, which she could see and touch and about which she had adequate knowledge!
[His chances of success are incredibly slim, almost equivalent to none…]
“I don’t care about that,” Shana gently shook her head, saying, “Throughout history, whenever a Saint has emerged, there has always been responsibility, I originally thought that the Disaster of Magic Fog would be my final journey, but now it’s been contained and to a certain extent unveiled, and other disasters are mostly under control…
“Perhaps, my appearance is to ensure that this small flame can grow.
“This glimmer of light is still very weak, it needs protection, to wait for the time it can set the world ablaze.”
Of course, should she fail, that too was okay…
For this unique individual who had once entered the heart of the Disaster of Magic Fog alone to save herself,
Shana could not simply let go!
Whether dead or alive, there must be a conclusion!
After a pause, she added, “Assist me, and then, for your actions before, I personally choose to forgive…”
Finally, the parchment did not counsel further, instead, a few words appeared on it.
[Before taking action, you should make adequate preparations…]
It was at this moment that Shana felt as though she had received something.
From the ten-liter spatial dimension she possessed, she took out a piece of paper, and looking at this paper, confusion appeared on Shana’s face, because this was almost a blank document.
However, at the very bottom of this document, there were a few characters written by someone unknown.
“Boss Huang He…”
With the knowledge of writing she had previously learned stealthily from other employees, Shana deciphered the meaning of these characters.
It looked like a signature, perhaps?
And this position in the lower-left corner, indeed was where signatures are typically placed on a document.
But a signed blank document…
What use could that have?
Shana’s eyes were filled with speculation; she could sense that the person behind the signature was extraordinary but it seemed to be limited to that.
It was during her confusion that a burst of blue light suddenly emerged on the parchment.
This blue light illuminated the blank area of the document and swiftly wrote out some content…
“A most special event is being executed, we have urgent matters and need to proceed to the ‘Emblem World’ Earth,” please allow passage for all units and provide convenience,” read the document.
…
“Is this a pass document?” Shana roughly figured out its purpose.
This thing would be the key item once she entered the “wall”!
After these words were inscribed, the pale blue light retracted from the parchment, and then, inspiration surged in Shana’s mind, helping her realize that this was not enough, and she also needed some employees’ signatures for notarization.
However, this issue was relatively easy to resolve…
Soon, in the “Notary” section of the document, there appeared signatures and thumbprints from “Life Mentor Adorable,” “Miss Nell’s Dog,” “Play○Play…” and the like, with a total of forty-seven employees.
After resolving this matter, a blue light orb flew out from the parchment and landed on the document, transforming into a stamped seal.
It was at this moment that Shana suddenly felt that the ordinary piece of paper seemed to start having some form of validity!
With this item, she could travel through the various mechanisms and subsidiaries of the “Bonfire Company,” crossing many areas and passing through who knows how many worlds, eventually arriving at the place she desired to go…
“Compared to them coming here, it’s a lot of trouble.”
Shana took a deep breath, regardless, she at least had a way to depart.
Next, it was a matter of taking care of the territory’s affairs here before she could start her action.
Everything in the domain was relatively stable, a large refugee population had gathered here, forming a nation with considerable strength, and with the addition of the company’s cross-generational technological products…
People’s concerns about food, clothing, housing, and transportation were not a problem.
The only thing to worry about was that other kingdoms might have some less than favorable ideas after she left.
However, a cluster of “Level 5 Bonfires” along with various war machines were enough to solve most problems, and with company employees stationed here, there wasn’t much for her to worry about.
Moreover, what was originally the most worrisome “Disaster of the Magic Fog” seemed to be extremely well restrained by the “Bonfire,” making it difficult to impact this “Nation of Refugees” even in an outbreak.
In other words, her actions could almost be said to be free of any significant worries…
In a clean and tidy room, Shana reached out and stroked Little Red’s head: “Trust me, no matter what, I will bring back the final result.”
She didn’t want to keep this action hidden from the young girl, to prevent her from overthinking and causing unwelcome trouble.
Little Red opened her mouth, wanting to say that she wanted to go together, but she knew that right now she’d only be a burden; she could only nod vigorously: “Then… Sister Shana, you must be careful!”
“I will,” Shana nodded with a smile.
Here, she planned to leave a duplicate’s coordinates; it could be useful if anything happened.
Of course, through this avatar, she could also understand the latest information about that world from potential employees who may arrive later.
Following that, before the “Bonfire,” Shana once again entered that ancient sanctuary through the parchment.
She used all her points towards enhancing herself.
Even some effects she felt were “flashy but insubstantial,” she purchased—
Because according to Colin’s words, they might elevate her permissions.
After a while, done with the distribution of power, she prepared to return to the “Light” church’s holy land to dig up some useful Holy Relics from the tombs… no, the sleeping places of her predecessors, and to arm herself as much as possible.
After all, the danger level of the place she was heading to this time far surpassed any she had ever visited!
Just when her preparations were nearly complete.
The information from the parchment suddenly appeared in her retina…
[Before your action, enter that underground relic and communicate with a certain being; you may find some unexpected assistance and gains.]
“That underground labyrinth?”
Hearing this name, Shana suddenly remembered that impressively high-ranking being.
Seems like it was called something… “King of Savage Sound”?

chapters.title: Chapter 853 - 853 577 Bullying Our No. 13 Containment Realm
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 853: Chapter 577: Bullying Our No. 13 Containment Realm Unchallenged! Chapter 853: Chapter 577: Bullying Our No. 13 Containment Realm Unchallenged! In the complex twists and turns of the Underground Great Labyrinth, a streak of light descended, coalescing into the blurred figure of Shana.
This time it wasn’t the actual body that entered. After all, it was Colin whom the “King of Madness” had submitted to, not her.
Still, caution was something to be maintained.
While entering, she hadn’t sensed the presence of that higher being. However, while she was about to call out for him to appear, a peculiar silhouette formed from frequency bands emerged in the corridors of the labyrinth.
Without any pleasantries, Shana looked at the form this less-than-serious Ancient God had taken and got straight to the point, “I’m preparing to go to the location of the ‘Bonfire’ Agent. Do you have any advice?”
As she spoke, she observed this being and quickly noticed something…
This guy had become much weaker than the last time she had seen him.
And it wasn’t just a simple fatigue. It seemed as if the very foundation of his higher existence was shaken!
And it was so obvious that even she could perceive it!
What exactly was going on?
“Advise…”
The “King of Savage Sound” spoke with a voice filled with weakness, “I recently answered a call and went there to participate in the battle, and I’ve only just returned…”
“Hm?”
Shana furrowed her brows, not understanding immediately, but in a matter of seconds, upon grasping his meaning, she hurriedly inquired, “What happened there?”
Though she didn’t know how the “King of Savage Sound” had managed to travel there.
However, as a First Level Containment Subject, he must certainly know more than those ordinary employees!
And hearing Shana’s question, the “King of Savage Sound” fell silent for a while…
Now back from the battlefield, he had probably understood why he had been previously “mocked.” The “Bonfire Company” was actually in a state of collapse!
There were no “Flamebearers” in existence in the current world…
No wonder those things dared to start a rebellion, attempting to overturn the company’s rule.
Even though today’s environment was starting to lean towards a kind of “humanity,” the foundation of this “humanity” was not yet settled, leaving much room for manipulation…
However, after pondering for a good while, the “King of Savage Sound” sighed, and regardless of everything, he was bound to the “Flamebearer” Reserves and had no other choice.
If that group of Ancient Gods were successful, those beings like himself, currently in containment, could only be taken out to be fodder in the future.
After all, the relationship between “God” and “God” was not much better than with the “Bonfire Company.”
So even though he felt it was all but over and he might as well give up, he still had to give it a try—what if?
With this in mind, after being silent for several seconds, the “King of Savage Sound” suddenly got motivated again; he wanted to gamble once more!
Next, while rapidly considering various possibilities, the “King of Savage Sound” began to explain the situation briefly: “The battlefield there is beyond imagination. That ‘Bonfire’ Agent Mr. was besieged by a multitude of Incarnates created by the higher beings…”
Using “multitude” to describe Ancient Gods felt slightly dissonant to him.
For there weren’t that many Ancient God level beings in reality, a major galaxy might not have many under normal circumstances—
But regardless, the high beings gathered there could indeed be described as a multitude.
“I fought side by side with the ‘Bonfire’ Agent Mr., we were ultimately outnumbered, but before leaving, I voluntarily tore a part of my authority to assist him in invoking ‘Hunger’ to deal with a multitude of enemies…”
“Right now, I can feel that the Agent Mr.’s life is critical, and the situation does not seem very optimistic.”
At this, Shana felt a jolt of alarm in her heart but then relaxed slightly upon hearing what the “King of Savage Sound” said next.
“However, based on my residual connection with my authority, I can affirm that it should still be in the ‘Bonfire’ Agent’s hands and has not been taken by something else.”
“So, he’s still alive,” Shana interjected.
“Yes, theoretically, that’s the case. At least I think that he is alive, but his status is not optimistic.”
“As long as he is alive, that’s good.”
Shana breathed a small sigh of relief. She hadn’t even left yet and receiving news of his death would be…
No, such thoughts should not even be entertained!
At this time, the “King of Savage Sound” continued: “As for your journey there, theoretically, it’s not possible for you to go, as something equally transcendent covers that area… But you came to me, so you must have a way. May I know about it beforehand?”
Shana remained silent for a moment, omitted some key information such as the matter of the transfer document, and simply outlined the process of her journey.
“Passing through various transfer stations will take some time…”
For the “King of Savage Sound,” a year or two wasn’t considered long, but the battlefield situation changed in an instant, and everything could be different in the blink of an eye.
However, recalling the fragments of the “Red Moon” he had seen before…
The “King of Savage Sound” might have surmised that his “leader” could indeed hold out until then.
After a thought, the “King of Savage Sound” opined, “Looking at it this way, you already have a means to go. So what remains, you’ll probably need some practical combat assistance…”
“Yes,” Shana nodded.
Compared to other types of assistance, if she had a choice, the best would be a faster means to arrive there. But unfortunately, there was none at the moment, so the next best was combat power.
Thinking this over, Shana also gained a new recognition of this being…
Earlier, when he had appeared before Colin, he had almost always been in an undignified, seemingly sly and flattering form.

chapters.title: Chapter 854 - 854 577 Bullying Us No One in Containment
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 854: Chapter 577: Bullying Us, No One in Containment Realm 13!_2 Chapter 854: Chapter 577: Bullying Us, No One in Containment Realm 13!_2 But now, without Colin, it became much wiser all of a sudden.
Perhaps, only in front of Mr. Colin would it show that kind of behavior again…
Shana couldn’t help but ponder.
It was then that the “King of Madness” spoke, “In this regard, I myself can no longer provide much help, but to get assistance, there are ways, though they might require you to make some promises…”
“What do you mean?” Shana asked, puzzled.
Instead of answering her directly, the “King of Madness” explained:
“The vast majority of high-ranking life forms contained within ‘World Code’ were forcibly imbued with certain seeds of human reason back in the day, which granted them, including me, a modicum of human intelligence and corresponding ways of thinking…
“Of course, these human ways of thinking aren’t necessarily beneficial, as they could also lead to resentment towards us, just like the hatred that exists between ordinary people…
“But likewise, because they are filled with a certain human logic, their patterns of behavior will no longer be so inscrutable, giving you a chance to persuade them through some means.
“Pointing out the pros and cons, promising enough benefits, could make them exert effort on your behalf…”
Hearing this, Shana nodded her head, understanding the tactic, though the specifics of how to proceed were still up for debate.
“In terms of interests… Although they greatly dislike you, dislike the ‘Flame Bearer,’ dislike the ‘Bonfire Company,’ they hate the prospect of those other ancient beings from different worlds succeeding even more…”
“Because if those beings succeeded, we who are imprisoned would surely die, with no other possible outcome.”
The “King of Madness” then described the relationship between themselves.
To put it simply, with the ‘Bonfire Company’ there, they might not necessarily die, they could suffer a bit but at least live; as long as they hadn’t committed any grave crimes, they might end up joining the ranks of the workers, cooperating as experimental subjects…
Being fished dry sustainably, there was still some hope.
Who knows, maybe one day they would be made official and join the company in exploiting others?
Just like the direction in which he was currently striving.
But if those other beings succeeded, it would be a straightforward fishing dry, all contained entities would be stripped of all will, put on the table as “fish” to be devoured, becoming part of someone else.
“When it comes to interests, what they desire most in their trapped state ultimately boils down to ‘living’ and ‘freedom’…”
“These two can be achieved by one means…”
“And that is to obtain an ‘official position’!”
At this point, the “King of Madness” paused, logically pointing out:
“Of course, ‘official positions’ aren’t easy to come by; you certainly can’t promise them. That would need approval from the upper levels, then go through internal auditing and so on…
“And as key containment subjects, they would naturally not be easily released.
“However, there’s a chance now; if one can provide certain assistance during the disasters of the gods and succeed, then perhaps there’s an opportunity for redemption, or at the very least, a chance to survive.”
Why had the containment subject of “World Code-13” been increasingly active?
Was it not because it knew that it might soon be trapped to death?
Before “2044” arrived, simply being “neutralized” by the remaining mechanisms within the containment unit.
But if it could “accumulate merits,” the situation would be different.
Plus, that would mean assisting the “Flamebearer” Reserves to succeed; though risky, the greater the turmoil, the larger the potential gain!
In such a scenario, if there were official positions to be had, they would be given priority consideration!
But still…
While the “King of Madness” spoke logically, Shana still felt it was somewhat surreal—such anomalously terrifying containment subjects like him, she had only ever encountered one.
Other existences…
“Is he really going to be persuaded by something like ‘position and benefits’?”
“If that’s the case, why didn’t they choose to defect before?” Shana voiced her doubts.
“Before? Before is before, now is now…”
“The King of Madness” explained, “Before there simply wasn’t a way in, to defect? To whom would you defect? And who could promise you anything? It’s different with a ‘Bonfire Company’ agent, he does have the capability to accept defectors…
“And there’s another key point, which is that even with their instinct to seek benefits and avoid harm, they wouldn’t want to see those ancient beings succeed…
“Also, compared with the past, this incident is something that can pass internal scrutiny; it’s a real opportunity to make a mark.”
After hearing his words, Shana nodded thoughtfully.
Of course, she still had some doubts and found it hard to believe that beings high and mighty would choose to help, or even pledge allegiance to, a company all because of a “position”…
You see, a position might sound nice, but bluntly put, that’s… going to defect and be a workhorse, and the catch is you have to fight for the chance to be that workhorse!
It’s a bit absurd…
Hmm, but as absurd as it is, it’s not completely unbelievable, because there indeed is a “precedent” right here.
Shana glanced subtly at the “King of Madness.”
At that moment, she heard him add,
“Of course, you have to find the right targets; not just any fellow can be swayed this way. Some beings have committed serious sins, and no amount of merit could save them. They’re not killed now simply because they hold special authority; it’s just not easy to kill them right away, and given time, they’ll be worn down eventually.”
“I understand.”
After nodding, Shana brought up another question, “In that case, how can we ensure that after they join us, they won’t be seduced away by other beings?”
Since ancient beings could be swayed by threats and temptations from her, couldn’t they also turn against them for the same reasons?
Speaking of this, the “King of Madness” suddenly seemed a bit wistful,
“Because the Ancient Gods can’t trust each other, any promises made between them can be broken, it’s just a matter of what cost is paid. But, the ‘Bonfire Company’ has some special agreements that can guarantee promises made by the company will hold true, and it’s not something you can break by just paying a price. It’s like a certain ‘fact’; once promised, it must come true!”
This was a paradoxical matter, despite countless high-degree beings hating Bonfire Company to the core…
Yet, undeniably, “Bonfire Company” was one of the few beings that could be trusted.
“Reputation” was one of its foundations.
Otherwise, the company couldn’t recruit so many high-level containment subjects to its cause.
Of course, the company’s approach towards “demons” was a different story; when dealing with things they define as “demons,” they tend to deceive and con, essentially making no promises or setting traps within those promises.
“The King of Madness” only knew that there were some deep-seated grudges between the “company” and so-called “demons,” but the reasons were unknown…
At this time, Shana, who understood, asked,
“So, what do we do? And how do we select and persuade the targets…”
“This isn’t a hundred percent guaranteed to succeed, but I can try to pull some basics for you first, then continue to shake people down the line…”
At that point, the “King of Madness” seemed to remember something and spoke through gritted teeth, “Damn it, last time a bunch of them ganged up on me to fight! It’s as if they’re picking on us ‘World Code’s containment realm for being undermanned!”
Although the number here might be an order of magnitude less than there, if we could pull a group together, we wouldn’t have been pressed and beaten like that…
It was in thinking this that some “knowledge” suddenly appeared in his perception.
An analysis of sorts — who are friends and who are foes?
…
Wait, there’s another chapter.
.

chapters.title: Chapter 855 - 855 578 Branch Office Open the Door Free Trade
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 855: Chapter 578 “Branch Office”: Open the Door, Free Trade! Chapter 855: Chapter 578 “Branch Office”: Open the Door, Free Trade! He didn’t think too much about the knowledge that emerged from Xinduo, and after discussing some matters, the “King of Madness” took action…
In a short while, Shana suddenly felt a terrifying will descending from outside the labyrinth.
Large expanses of soil suddenly melted and then crystallized, transforming into an active green irregular polyhedral crystal, its light dispersing, corroding and dissolving all things that it shone upon rapidly…
At this moment, even though its body was bound, even though it couldn’t truly arrive…
But the immensely strong aura undoubtedly revealed the other’s identity—
A being worthy of being called a God by the people!
“‘Disciples of Resurrection’ worship ‘Lord of Corruption’…” Shana’s eyelids twitched, recognizing this being; she had personally killed many of its followers.
Relatively speaking, this was a group that liked to steal corpses.
All the stolen corpses, in the end, would be “reborn” through the power of this being.
But to say it was rebirth, Shana felt it was more like a new soul being stuffed into the bodies, infesting them.
When she first sensed Colin through the daughter of a great noble, Helena, she had suspected that he was a “Disciple of Resurrection”, but then the flame made her overturn her own thoughts.
Overall, this was a big event with constant minor incidents and was unfriendly to humans.
However, because of the “King of Madness”, they weren’t likely to come to blows.
At this moment, upon its arrival, the “Lord of Corruption” greeted the “King of Madness”, along with some mockery—after all, Shana could see that he had suffered serious injuries, not to mention a being of the same level.
“I’m just here to give you more choices…” The aura of the “King of Madness” surged and expanded, confronting the other head-on.
Regardless, he was a member of a higher life form!
He shouldn’t be stepped on by just anyone!
For a moment, the whole area trembled nonstop, as if a violent earthquake had occurred.
But this confrontation, in Shana’s eyes, was just like prisoners of one prison clashing with those of another through the air, mostly harmless unless one was within a hundred miles of the center of the site.
Shortly after the atmosphere had somewhat eased, Shana spoke, proposing to the other party to assist her, when suddenly, terrifying corrosive power rippled out from the irregular polyhedral crystal, like a volcanic eruption…
Shana frowned, thinking her words had “offended” the other.
After all, these “Gods” always had an unapproachable aura of majesty…
Just when she thought the negotiation had failed, she suddenly heard a mental message from the other side,
“What terms or treatment can you offer?”
Could it really be, is the company structure that magical?
Shana paused inwardly, hesitant to speak immediately when mentioning treatment, as she was uncertain about what she could promise.
Then, from her sleeve pocket, the parchment seemed to offer some inspiration.
With this guidance, she promised some things she could achieve—
For instance, ensuring that He would currently not be “neutralized”…
Then there were matters about organizational positions; mostly… it was pure negotiation, bluffing with high hopes. Although Shana wasn’t experienced in this area, she wasn’t completely without skill, as she made several generous promises afterwards.
The first assistance came smoothly!
Shana looked at a “Token” in her hand, her expression slightly peculiar.
This item, guided by the parchment and made through cooperation with the other party using her own authority, was a kind of small avatar of an Ancient God that allowed her, under appropriate circumstances, to summon the other party through certain internal channels of the company, ignoring distance to achieve a “God Descent.”
Not a full descent, inferior to the original form and slightly worse than “World Code-13”, but still significant.
At this moment, Shana, becoming more familiar with her own authority in this world, also increasingly understood why the Ancient Gods always wanted to target her…
Because apart from her or some Saints whose authority reached those levels, these beings really found no other way to break free.
Of course, there were other methods, like forcefully breaking containment or accidental descent, but for the former, if they had the power to break containment, they wouldn’t be trapped.
And the latter, the far-reaching event happening now was considered an “accident.”
She had to grasp it well.
After negotiating the relevant conditions, another being called “Shadow Tree” descended under the guidance of the “Lord of Corruption”, its branches hung with numerous eye-like “Plentiful Fruits”.
Another “old acquaintance.”
While she was being chased before, Shana had met this entity before.
But, this spiritual state was not very stable, barely arriving before attacking her, seemingly mad, but it wasn’t long before it was driven away by three beings present at the scene.
“Continue, next one…” said the “King of Madness” looking at the “Lord of Corruption.”
Most of the time, he could only move within the labyrinth, and each attempt beyond it was extremely exhausting, especially given his poor condition, he couldn’t have called unless the place where the “Lord of Corruption” was confined overlapped his…
Not long after, another being was summoned…
And it was while Shana and others were trying one by one.
In other regions of “World Code-13”, among nations or powers where individuals of certain strength and sufficient inspiration existed, they were all watching that world with intense unease.

chapters.title: Chapter 856 - 856 578 Branch Office Open the Door Free Trade
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 856: Chapter 578 “Branch Office”: Open the Door, Free Trade! _2 Chapter 856: Chapter 578 “Branch Office”: Open the Door, Free Trade! _2 “‘God Descent’?! Another ‘God Descent’… That’s the seventh one, what are they doing over there!! What is the Saintess doing, does she want to destroy the world?!”
A high priest of the local imperial state religion said anxiously.
Since earlier, breaths from higher beings had been arriving continuously, but nobody had reported in advance, nor did anyone know exactly what was happening; they only knew about the presence of some “Evil Gods,” appearing one after another.
It wasn’t that their abilities were strong enough to spy on “Gods,” but those breaths weren’t hidden at all…
That’s why they were able to observe some situations.
A minority with predictive abilities sensed that the matter was related to “Bonfire,” no! More accurately, it was related to the current Saint of the “Light” religion, and one might even say she was actively summoning it.
What sudden provocation had she received?
Even though they were in different nations with different powers, they all simultaneously thought that the Saint summoning Evil Gods ostentatiously couldn’t be planning a rebellion, could she?
Compared to some orthodox nations, there were also heretics feeling complex emotions at this moment.
Among those who had descended were beings they worshipped.
A certain crystal-clear “God Revelation” even led them from then on to abandon all sacrificial rituals, cease all acts that harmed life, and go to a certain area to care for the people there.
Moreover, a significant portion of people, who had previously committed numerous sins by defying the ‘Master’s’ will and creating untimely slaughter…
Were directly erased by the “Master’s” power.
Many heretics clearly realized… the heavens were about to change.
…
Eventually, after consecutively summoning the consciousness of twelve “Gods,” including the “King of Madness,” Shana successfully got six higher beings to go all-in on this event.
The rest either were not in a state to serve, or they were too weakened by certain reasons to take on a major role.
“The ones we could find are basically all here; there are others left, but it’s very risky…” the “King of Madness” continued to inform Shana about the current situation in this containment realm.
“World Code-13” functioned as a kind of large transit point in the past, amassing dozens of higher beings.
About one-third of them had already died…
“Disaster of Magic Fog” had a certain connection with the deaths of Those.
As for the remaining beings, up to now, they were mostly just the “old, weak, sick, and disabled.”
“However, on your way, if you manage to reach other ‘World Codes’ or anything within the ‘Light’s’ jurisdiction, you can try to recruit through similar means.”
After the “King of Madness” had spoken, another ancient life form that was a recruit spoke immediately after:
“But once you cross the border, don’t try it. Once you reveal yourself, the risks will be very great. You will be intercepted by many beings, and some of them might even descend in their true forms…”
Listening to these mighty life forms speak, Shana nodded in acknowledgment.
After making sufficient preparations, she left the place and then answered some people’s anxious inquiries.
Following that, through some special devices, she led a group of reinforcements desiring to clean the regime toward the so-called “Emblem World.”
…
It was only about half a month after Shana left, that some parts of the employees who chose to stay and confirmed their stay thrice saw information suddenly emerge on their retinas…
Seeing this scene, everyone was startled—since then, they had ceased performing any missions for a long time.
But it seemed like more had come now?
Before long, after deciphering this content, each of their expressions became somewhat strange.
“It seems like they want us to interact with the ‘Light’ religion and some imperial mages, knights, and such, asking them to… assist us in creating marks that use BUFFs?” someone said, perplexed.
Some others noticed problems inherent in the mission itself:”This isn’t officially issued by the company; it resembles something Brother Shunzi mentioned about the ‘Subsidiaries’…”
Regarding this “Subsidiary,” they knew something but had not engaged with it.
“Let me sort this out, ha, the request is that some of our employees here provide gold, then our area exerts effort, and then it acts as a platform to sell it?”
“Is this to restore the previous BUFF trading? Create a little golden bean, and split three to five points among us…”
“Damn, what kind of slave treatment is this? I remember Brother Shunzi got thirty points for one golden bean, isn’t this just about one-tenth of the reward?”
An employee couldn’t help but curse under his breath.
But… after cursing, he couldn’t help but ponder, as they no longer had any income from points.
Still, doing this could increase their income a bit.
“Damn, let this ‘Subsidiary’ learn…”
“Life Mentor Adorable” couldn’t help but mutter to himself.
This “Subsidiary” used to be known for luring people into using physical means to rob and such, its methods of making money were relatively primitive and backward.
But from what he could see now, it seemed to be starting to seek out trades…
Although he didn’t know where it planned to sell…
But once a systematic market was built by it, this advanced free trade could earn much more than the primitive methods of robbery!
“Alas, a fallen tiger is bullied by dogs, prepare to be a slave…” someone sighed resignedly.
For them now, this was at least an income source, and if it grew, they could probably make some money.
And those employees who still traveled between realms did not refuse, after all, it was just collecting some gold, which was relatively easy to find, and they could pick some up on the way back when they went to inquire about Brother Shunzi.
As days passed, the trade began to establish, and the employees didn’t feel much change.
But the various local forces that earned quite a benefit from it began to feel something strange, encouraging more people to join and work at the “Extraordinary Factory.”
Some forces even unprecedentedly opened the path downward to extraordinary powers, to cultivate more Extraordinary Ones.
The originally intense national situations even began to ease and calm down…
Some visionaries began to realize that the civilization of this world seemed to be developing in a strange direction.
…
On the Earth that had expanded who knows how many times its size.
Colin, covered in scars, barely managed to deal with a group of pursuers, and then “Yukionna” led him into a somewhat safer place, immediately plunging back into an unspeakable nightmare.
In this time, the negative effects on his body, after a period of outbreak, gradually turned into a “chronic” phase, and his condition began to stabilize.
Taking advantage of the slightly better situation, he found a direction and tried to enter the ocean.
But unfortunately, after two failed attempts, he remained pursued until just now when he finally shook off the enemies.
Then, the suppressed negative effects burst forth again…
And this time, for some unknown reason, his consciousness sank deeper and deeper, and everything around became dark.
Cramped, narrow, with little room to stretch his limbs…
There was a force suppressing and limiting Colin’s awakening.
He felt as if he was trapped in an iron cage, sinking into the deep sea, breathing obstructed, increasingly suffocating.
Even, a terrifying fear arose in his heart that he might never wake up!
However, just then, outside the nightmare, the finger bone hanging on Colin’s chest suddenly glowed, and its soft light seeped into his body. As he “sank” in the nightmare, suddenly Colin saw:
In the blackness, a dazzling ray of light appeared, and from the light, a familiar yet incredibly comforting soft voice came:
“Colin, don’t be afraid, this is my hand, grab it…”
Colin blankly reached out his hand towards the light, and as he touched the light, layers of glowing wings slowly folded around him, pulling him out of the dark nightmare.
The next second, a strong smell of blood came, Colin realized something, abruptly opened his eyes, and woke up from the nightmare!
…

chapters.title: Chapter 857 - 857 579 The Covert Attack from Behind
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 857: Chapter 579: The Covert Attack from Behind Chapter 857: Chapter 579: The Covert Attack from Behind A massive block of ice enveloped the area he was in…
Through the hard, semi-transparent ice, Colin saw that this must be a rather spacious room…
And on his body, the flame that had once covered him had now grown markedly weak.
“Is ‘Yukionna’ using this to preserve me?”
Colin pursed his lips and then moved his body. Amidst the cracking sounds of the ice shattering, he broke free from some of the frost’s binding, only to find that his body had also accumulated many irregular, pitted wounds.
The culprits of these injuries were some strange insects.
They were like beetles the size of fingernails, penetrating the surface flames and nibbling at his skin in wriggling motions as though they were munching on leaves and twigs.
However, it seemed due to the activation of the finger bone at his chest, most of the insects had already perished.
A few were still wriggling under his skin…
Colin inserted his fingers into the wounds, dug around in the flesh, and removed all the now almost inactive insects, crushing them to death—
These creatures were not fatal to him, but were just slightly uncomfortable, compounding the severity of his injuries.
“It’s a bit like some kind of plague. The reason I couldn’t wake up just now seems to be because of them, but fortunately, now that I’m awake, that’s not a big problem…”
“It’s just that after so many battles, there are so many enemies that I can’t even remember where these insects came from or who attacked me…”
Colin rubbed the insect corpses in his hand, wiped them aside, leaned against the ice wall, and tried to get up, planting his legs on the ground, but felt somewhat powerless. His previous attempt to reach the ocean had not been successful, and to escape, he had spent a lot at the cost of using numerous items.
Moreover, for fear of using the bonfire and melting the seal set by Old Master Wu on his aura, which could make him reenter the sights of those higher beings, he could only use items throughout.
As a result, his body was now in an extremely weary and adverse negative state…
Gently shaking his head, Colin recalled the luminous hand in the darkness and the words still ringing in his ear that gave a strong sense of security…
“Shana?” Colin uncertainly looked down at the necklace made from her finger bone that he wore on his chest.
He felt like he had heard Shana’s voice, but was not entirely sure…
Because logically, she should be in “World Code-13,” which made it unlikely she would appear here.
Yet, just before he opened his eyes, he harbored a certain expectation, but upon opening his eyes and stabilizing his condition, once he calmed down and saw the coldness all around, not a single shadow he wanted to see was in sight, everything seemed like a dream.
The sense of discrepancy made Colin feel an indescribable discomfort and regret.
However, he couldn’t afford to spend more energy on this now…
At this moment, a strange commotion suddenly erupted.
A gust of cold wind accompanied by a howling roar faintly made its way to his ears.
Colin, who had just barely managed to stand up, staggered a few steps forward, pushed open the room door, and looked through the hallway towards the outside, belatedly realizing that it seemed some enemy had followed them.
And “Yukionna” was about a hundred meters away, engaging the enemy together with “Mountain of Smiling Corpses”…
The roar from just now was emitted by “Mountain of Smiling Corpses.”
At this moment, it was larger than any he had seen before, composed of three house-sized black mass of corpse mounds. As it moved, the ground vibrated, but it seemed that due to the enemy’s attack…
One of the corpse mounds had half chopped off, motionless.
As for “Yukionna,” she hovered in the air, creating widespread frost and ice spikes among other methods, attacking from the side and occasionally using the massive body of “Mountain of Smiling Corpses” as a shield.
The enemy’s strength was not particularly weak this time.
It was a female figure in a gray hooded cloak, and beneath the hood was a rather delicate face, but at the very bottom, instead of feet, stretched out were numerous worm-like shadows, acting as roots to support her body…
“Is this something similar to those fishmen that underwent a transformation like before…”
At a glance, Colin recognized the situation of the opponent.
Such enemies, within the usual heretic groups, are typically of statuses like High Priests or God’s Favored Ones, with very formidable powers…
Had “Yukionna” not strengthened herself significantly, they would have probably already lost.
At that moment, the cloaked female figure held a long sword in her right hand, its blade wrapped with numerous “threads,” which connected to a terrifyingly menacing ancient specter, puppeteering it to launch attacks on Yukionna.
Meanwhile, in her left hand, she wielded a silver cup, brandishing it now and then, from which new imps appeared in twos and threes…
“Yukionna” focused primarily on freezing these dark spider-like imps that crawled everywhere before taking the opportunity to launch sneak attacks on the main body.
“Where is he? Where is he! Hand over that damned man to me…”
“Why would you help a sinner who has caused the world to be destroyed to such an extent…”
“Hurry up, hand him over, or you all shall die…”
The cloaked female figure murmured to herself while fending off attacks.
From her own body, there were also frequent outpourings of mental attacks, causing “Yukionna” to sometimes scream in agony…
Right now, facing the joint attack of “Yukionna” and “Mountain of Smiling Corpses,” she even showed signs of counter-suppression!
It was foreseeable that if things continued this way, defeat was almost certain.

chapters.title: Chapter 858 - 858 579 The Hidden Attack_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 858: Chapter 579: The Hidden Attack_2 Chapter 858: Chapter 579: The Hidden Attack_2 At that moment, she suddenly sensed an extraneous gaze, and a ferocious smile appeared on her face, “Found you!”
As soon as she finished speaking, she violently crushed the silver cup in her hand. The shattered pieces quickly evaporated, forming a curtain-like barrier that sealed off the surrounding area.
The next second, she dashed toward a building in Colin’s direction.
Soon, she saw Colin, looking frail, at the lobby…
“It was you! It was you who killed our great priest and disrupted our ritual…” The woman in a gray cloak, upon seeing Colin, seemed to have bloodshot eyes.
However, in response to her accusation, Colin, leaning against the wall, simply shook his head indifferently, “Your priest? I don’t know him.”
“Don’t know?” Upon hearing this, the woman in a dire state paused.
Colin nodded, casually and honestly saying, “There are too many enemies, might have encountered and killed him on a whim, I really don’t know which priest you’re talking about.”
To be honest, during the last attempt to break out, those enemies, because of the “God Revelation,” came in droves, making it really impossible to remember the so-called priest they mentioned.
After all, he was easily dealt with.
If it weren’t for his severe injuries now, this individual, who might barely qualify as a Level 2 Containment Subject, would merely require a glance.
“You deserve to die!”
After coming to her senses, the woman in the gray cloak seemed to explode with anger, her hair standing on end.
Her body tensed, then she dashed swiftly in front of Colin, swinging her long sword fiercely down at him.
However, the strike ultimately landed on a shield formed of intense light.
Colin’s gaze became murky for a moment because the light originally used to suppress his negative effects was partially drawn for defense, causing him a slight daze, entering a state as if one’s vision darkens suddenly after standing up from a long crouch.
Almost simultaneously, Yukionna, sensing Colin’s vulnerability, dashed over and launched an attack from behind the woman in the gray cloak.
In the chilling wind, the woman in the gray cloak instantly froze into an ice sculpture.
Then, struck by the chunks of ice tossed by Yukionna, she instantly shattered into a pile of corpse fragments.
“Lalala!”
Yukionna stuck out her tongue and made a face, wanting to celebrate her victory. But before she could fully rejoice, she suddenly saw Colin yank her figure back.
It was at that moment that an ancient armored Evil Spirit appeared and attacked where Yukionna had just been.
It opened its huge mouth, seemingly wanting to swallow everything.
“Boom!” Colin punched out, and dozens of “spatial fissures” burst forth from his fist.
Amid the tooth-grinding sound of shattering glass, the Evil Spirit entity, which could face off against three “Mountain of Smiling Corpses” and even had the upper hand, was directly shattered into pieces.
Even though he could access only a small amount of the power of this authority, it was undoubtedly overkill to use it against such an enemy.
It was after slaying this mysterious Evil Spirit that Colin’s head swayed a little, and as he barely steadied himself, he couldn’t help coughing twice, spitting out a mouthful of dark blood.
The spilled blood quickly ignited from some faint flames on his body’s surface…
Then it was absorbed back into his body.
