Through this “Fifth Disciple,” he saw the giant statue of “White Night” suspended in the sky, scattering countless glowing feathers, like an unparalleled round white “Little Sun,” with eyes shut, facing him.
Although its eyes were closed, Colin knew it was watching him.
Immediately afterward, a tremendous force came from the “Fifth Disciple’s” hands, lifting Colin’s body, which was still only that of a ten-something-year-old child, high into the air.
Compared to the “Disciple’s” hunched but very tall stature, the lifted Colin was like a baby compared to an adult.
There was an extremely strong contrast…
And at the same time, other “Disciples” arrived in succession, thrusting the tails of their scythes into various parts of Colin’s body.
“Thud thud thud…”
The sound of flesh being pierced made Colin’s eyes somewhat bloodshot.
The terrifying “Repulsion” erupted again, and all the “Disciples” nearby were blown away.
Colin landed on his feet once more, but unlike a second ago, in this brief moment, he had gained hundreds of pounds, his body still carrying several heavy and strongly corrosive scythes.
Blood, like a fountain, slid down the scythes and dripped all over the ground…
And those “Disciples” who had been blown away showed no mercy, quickly recovering in half a second to ten seconds.
“Receive my ‘Master’s’ mercy and love, and you will be reborn.” The first “Disciple” to recover screamed with a message, fluttering his youthful wings behind him, swooping at Colin.
“Are you really seeking your own death…”
Colin’s eyes were frosty, and the next second, he slightly tilted his head, triggering one of the talents within him.
“Wildfire Addition”!
As the thought sparked, a huge hand made of raging flames descended from the sky.
The swiftly approaching “Disciple” seemed to sense it, looked up at the sky, then tried to dodge…
However,
With a “slap”!
It was like a mosquito squashed against a wall, flattened harshly by the great force.
“Ah ah!!!” Under the scorch of the wild flames, the “Disciple” no longer had the indifferent expression it had before, regardless of the wounds it received, but instead emitted a painful scream.
“Heh heh, feels good, right?”
Colin’s mouth curled into a twisted smile, also enduring the terrifying burning pain—
This time when he used “Wildfire Addition,” he did not invoke the power of “Primordial Fire” as a prerequisite to activate it, resulting in his body suffering immense agony.
However, his tolerance for this kind of pain was far greater than his opponent’s.
Therefore, he could ignore it for a short time…
And at this moment, Colin, while pulling the scythe from his body, faced the disciples charging at him and a half-formed giant of “Wildfire” appeared above him.
At that instant, he managed to block all the enemies outside.
But, it seemed like this barrier wouldn’t last long.
“Sigh, in the end, I still have to use this power…”
Muttering to himself, Colin watched as the blood spilled on the ground, like little pits, began to burn fervently.
At his left eye, something akin to a long-installed “hot-swappable” device again came into play…
“W’ldfire’ has not attracted attention, I don’t know what the power of ‘Primordial Fire’ will do, let’s try…”
Colin finally made a decision, preparing to use this power in small amounts.
And in the sky above, the giant statue that White Night had transformed into seemed to sense that Colin was willing to risk it all, so its eyes cracked open slightly…
Through that slender gap, one could see pupils red as flowing blood beneath the eyelids.
“Come on! Come on!! Today I am going to turn you and your ‘Disciples’ into kindling, and I’ll arrange you all together neat and tidy!”
Colin spread his hands and shouted, but before the two sides could erupt into a decisive battle,
Above the dome, an intensely pale and glaring light suddenly beamed down, directly shining upon the twisted giant statue of White Night.
At first glance, the coinciding colors of the light made Colin think that his opponent was about to unleash something big.
But he quickly sensed something else, slightly lifting his head to see the previously overcast sky cracking open above him.
The light that shone through immobilized the giant statue in mid-air.
This beam of light did not come from White Night…
At this moment, someone else had entered the battlefield!
“?”
A question mark popped into Colin’s mind, feeling as if it were someone very familiar and crucial, but someone who shouldn’t be here…
Then, without time to think further, he saw the Angel Envoys in front of him suddenly get blasted away without reason, spinning as they flew through the air…
“What’s this, a new technique?”
He paused, unsure if this was the wind-up to some special attack.
It looked rather perplexing anyway.
But the next second, something inside him, something “stored” in his stomach and seemingly related to the concept of “vibration,” resonated with something else.
Then, a familiar and very excited voice resounded…
“Leader, don’t be afraid, I’m coming right away!!!”
From this voice, Colin detected a lot of emotions—reunion after loss, excitement, tears brimming with joy, and…
A great deal of subtly mixed nuances primarily leaning towards “happiness.”
‘Fuck, I didn’t have any unclear messy entanglements with this thing in my past memories, did I?’
Colin was stunned.
As far as he remembered, he didn’t seem to have had such a good friendship with anyone.
However, soon he could almost recall that it didn’t quite qualify as a friendship; strictly speaking, it seemed to be an undefined superior-subordinate relationship…
But for some reason, that relationship was enough to make the other party so happy.
“Daring to hurt our leader like this! You’ve got a big problem coming your way, I’m telling you!”
An imposing, terrifying projection, composed of various frequencies, unseen but as massive as a mountain, descended upon the scene, protecting Colin.
However, without paying attention to this overly enthusiastic guy, Colin looked to the other side.
A vision formed vaguely in his mind…
A terrifying figure of light, at incredible speed, traversing countless lands, disregarding all stares, was “rushing” towards this place.
Even from a distance, Colin could faintly hear that voice speak to him in a gentle tone:
“Colin, this time, you won’t be fighting alone…”

chapters.title: Chapter 884 - 884 591 Shana
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 884: Chapter 591 ‘Shana? Chapter 884: Chapter 591 ‘Shana? “This sound…”
Colin’s heart skipped a beat the instant he heard it, his pupils dilated slightly.
His emotions, which had been relatively stable, showed a significant fluctuation.
Though a profound sense of emotion occupied most of his feelings, at the same time…
For some reason, he felt a slight reluctance to hear her voice here because it always seemed too perilous.
Coming here might not be a good thing.
Yet, at this moment, she had already come…
Along with the gentle sound, in the next instant, when a huge crack ripped open in the dome, the intense light further amplified, brightly illuminating the dark, gloomy world.
Under this light, not even a shadow existed.
Even placed within ruins, it was akin to arriving at a broken God Kingdom.
Colin even saw something resembling an “umbilical cord” on every single “Disciple,” connecting to The Pale Colossus’s body which enabled continuous repair much like carrying a spring of water.
Colin had more or less felt these things before.
But then, being held by the head while being hit, he absolutely could not free his hands to cut these off, at least not without using the “Bonfire.”
Colin slightly squinted his eyes, flames leaping from his left eye, as he pointed toward those “Disciples.”
He prepared to coordinate with the not-yet-arrived light, to sever those umbilical cords.
To prevent them from continuously regenerating…
“Haha, such a small matter, why would you need to step in?”
“You?” Colin, instinctively skeptical, questioned.
The next moment, the giant, comprised of various vibration frequencies, exerted its force, an explosion of terrifying vibrations spreading in all directions, making the entire space momentarily seem solidified.
Following that, dark “rifts” spread everywhere, severing all the “umbilical cords.”
Several “Disciples” were blown away.
Despite still being alive, they had sustained serious injuries.
Seeing this, Colin felt somewhat surprised; just like four-legged creatures that beg pleasingly, yet expressing a special ability to chase mice.
‘A First Level Containment Subject against life beneath “Authority” usually shows an overwhelming effect.’
It was indeed the essence of a Higher Life Form, resembled a child of few years.
Even without much learning, it could easily crush an ant.
Only when both parties are on the same plane, with equivalent power, then considerations about which side has stronger combat abilities are pertinent…
Otherwise, it’s just a dimensional reduction attack on levels of existence.
However, speaking of which, Colin wondered why such a strong entity had a crucial part of “Authority” inside his stomach.
‘It couldn’t have been from previous parasitism, could it?’
As the thought flickered, some vague memories started to clear up…
Oh, this thing is called the “King of Madness.”
As for the authority, he couldn’t recall it for the moment; it seemed voluntary anyway.
Though he didn’t know exactly where the “Authority” had come from, it seemed like a good thing; at least through this part of “Authority,” the “King of Madness” had descended earlier, preventing him from choosing the worst outcome.
In that moment, a slightly gentler burst of light erupted, and the white colossus resembling a fetal angel suddenly unfurled petals-like wings around itself.
On the ground, the injured “Disciples” turned into glowing fragments, flying high into the sky, transforming into numerically numbered halos from “1” to “13” around him, encircling him.
This also allowed it to temporarily escape the pale light descending from the sky.
“Apostate, back off… you are not my match,” The Pale Colossus spoke in a slightly childish voice.
“A middle to lower tier First Level Containment Subject with potential for advancement… If I encountered you alone in non-corporate territory, I would definitely turn and run, but sadly, this is a crucial facility of our company!”
The “King of Madness” responded bluntly.
“Heretics, protecting him, even though the chances are low, you are pushing all of life’s future into the pit of fire, are you truly prepared to face the consequences?”
“The possibility of ‘Primordial Fire’ descending again is extremely low, thus far, not a single ‘Flame Bearer’ has emerged, and, moreover, today’s ‘Flame Bearers’ are likely not the same entities as before.”
“The fate of the world should not rely on such an intangible future.”
The colossus issued a childish voice, “Compared to them, even though the environment has changed today, we still can make a choice, shaped from the newer-born ‘Divinity’, absolute reason, that can lead people towards the right and successful path…”
“Fuck off!”
The “King of Madness” cursed loudly:
“Don’t bark there; it’s just fear after all. If it’s as you say, that the chances of a ‘Flame Bearer’ emerging are very low…
“What are you afraid of now? If you’re not afraid, then why do you still persecute?
“It doesn’t look like you’re as indifferent as you claim, are you trying to manipulate the outcome through the reality-bending cognition of Higher Life Forms? Impossible! ‘Primordial Fire’ will surely descend! You can’t stop it!
“And only an environment of ‘humanity’ created under the leadership and support of ‘Flame Bearers’ born from this era’s big shots and designated by the corporation is the future; all else are aberrations!”
During the rapid dialogue, he unleashed terrifying shockwaves in a ferocious assault at the enemy, protecting Colin.

chapters.title: Chapter 885 - 885 591 Shana_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 885: Chapter 591 “Shana?”_2 Chapter 885: Chapter 591 “Shana?”_2 However, all the charges scattered when they reached the wide wings of the entity in front of them.
Following that, the colossal figure opened its eyes, and a beam of intense light burst forth from its blood-red eyes, piercing through the “King of Madness” and heading straight for Colin.
But at that moment, the light that connected heaven and earth suddenly dissipated…
Colin, sensing something, turned around and saw a humanoid figure formed from extreme and pure white light approaching.
Just like in the depths of his memories.
Sacred, pure, difficult to gaze at directly—at least, this life form would be hard to look at directly if its light’s intensity hadn’t been adjusted specifically for him.
The brightness was too high…
“Are you… Shana? When did you get here…”
Almost subconsciously, Colin uttered that name.
Corresponding memories were somewhat vague for some reason…
But he was certain she was a very close person, and perhaps because of this, his memories of her were even more blurred?
He wasn’t sure why…
That figure suddenly flickered and split into two.
One of the stronger avatars charged toward the colossal figure in the sky, which was shining like a white sun.
The other came to Colin’s side.
“Sorry, I’m a bit late…”
Shana, almost completely transformed into a “light” state, appeared in front of Colin and spoke softly.
At this moment, seeing Colin alive, her hanging heart finally settled a bit.
Although Colin’s physical appearance had changed drastically, he might only be waist-high, but she remembered all his scents. She could recognize him even if he turned to ash, let alone if he just shrank a little.
The only issue might be some minor problems on his soul level…
But upon inspection, the problems weren’t significant and were reversible.
Moreover, compared to the previous uncertainty of his life and whereabouts, seeing him alive now far exceeded expectations.
However, she slightly lowered her head at that moment, looking at the hastily unremoved scythe crosses on Colin’s body, and frowned.
Then, half-kneeling down, she reached out to touch the crosses on Colin’s small body.
“Crack!”
During the touch, all the crosses instantly shattered. Before any blood could gush from the wounds, a large amount of light flooded in to heal them, then some blessings were applied.
After performing some emergency treatments, Shana looked at the “shrunken” Colin and suddenly opened her arms, gently enveloping him in a hug…
A very tight hug!
Colin even felt a little breathless in his chest; in his memory, this sister-like figure had never been so “out of character.”
However, from this somewhat suffocating and slightly painful embrace, Colin felt a full sense of security.
But before he could say anything, he heard her speak.
“It’s so good that you’re still alive.”
At the same time, while speaking, she slightly suppressed the stirring flames.
At this moment, drawing the “Bonfire” at this inappropriate time point…
Would lead to incidents she might not be able to resolve…
Over the past few years, while she had been traveling here, she had encountered numerous attacks. There would always be unknown higher entities, through some inspiration of their own, who felt she might be doing something “dangerous” and would attack her.
Either they came in person, or they sent civilizations with high technological levels under their command to pursue her.
And this “dangerous” thing was apparently to save Colin, who had a unique status…
This was still based on their vague premonitions, not knowing specifically what she was doing. If they knew, they would likely stop her at any cost.
The situation worsened after passing through a certain station, through some sort of “wall” that required a “pass” for entry…
Because the civilizations and higher life forms behind the “wall,” once partially or fully liberated, focused on the newly emerged “Flame Bearer” reservists with over half of them fixated on these entities.
There were strong indications of a relentless pursuit…
The driving force behind their actions was not hatred, or rather, hatred was not the main component but rather “fear” – a type of “fear” dominated by the company that even transcending eras couldn’t erase…
And then another part, with more dispersed attitudes, mostly watched and stayed neutral, seeming indecisive.
As for the friendly ones…
Some of them told her that if the “Flame Bearer” were born, they would be willing to intervene.
That was probably the most friendly attitude.
As for going all-in like the “King of Madness,” there were few.
After all, the possibility might indeed be small…
But even so, it still made many beings uneasy and countless lives obsessed.
So much so that even while saying it was impossible, they kept arriving to stop that “impossible.”
A few seconds later, after suppressing the flame inside Colin’s body, Shana released her embrace and gently said:
“This place will be dangerous, but I’ve already suppressed some of the aura for you. Find a chance and leave first, and after I clean up some traces here, I’ll come find you. Don’t worry, we won’t be apart for long.”
There was a weak presence of flame around…
It wasn’t a bonfire, but it was enough to prompt their arrival to inspect and ensure the elimination of all possibilities…
And if they did come, they might really discover something and trigger a massive battle.
However, fortunately, this giant statue had probably blocked off the area to ensure Colin wouldn’t be detected by other beings, intending to handle him alone, preventing the escape of the aura.
Otherwise, things might have been very complicated…
Now, what needed to be done was to clear the aura cleanly, turning the conflict here from Colin to her and that “Heretic Light.”
“Okay…” Although Colin wanted to stay a bit longer, he knew the priorities.
Seeing him nod, Shana pulled her consciousness from that part of her humanoid light shadow, turning into countless particles of light that rushed into Colin’s body to further eliminate any negative effects et cetera.
Then she began battling with that being above halfway in the sky, which seemed very similar to her.
In fact, not just similar, they came from the same source.
Both belonged to “Light.”
Just like different ethnic groups, they had some differences…
But Shana didn’t feel any friendliness toward it because “Light” was once also a key member of the “Bonfire Company,” and many places indeed had their lingering effects, not all of which were friendly.
Moreover, this one seemed even more special than usual…
Apart from “Light,” it seemed mixed with other terrifying entities.
Most likely, it was another experiment done by the administrator in the containment unit here.
The universe’s administrator seemed quite keen on various terrifying or dizzying transformations…
“Heretic of the Counter-Light…”
As the embryo giant with numerous broad wings suppressed the “King of Madness,” it called out to Shana: “Are you still going to make an irrational choice using this power of absolute rationality?
“I still believe there could be cooperation between us.”
However, before Shana could reply, the “King of Madness” on the side cursed: “‘Saint’ Sir, he just aims to maneuver the ‘Source of Light’! And, this guy counts as part of ‘humanity’ too, but he’s more hateful than external enemies, there’s nothing good to discuss with such a heretic, let’s finish it together!”
“Regardless of my choice…”
While speaking, recalling various horrific injuries on Colin’s small body, Shana bluntly said:
“Today, all your ‘disciples’ will be disqualified!”
With the being before her, they had erupted into numerous conflicts before, and today was the day to settle both new and old scores.
While speaking, she gestured, and a beam of strong light descended from above her head, like a door that was about to open, and from behind the door, the sound of trumpets from heaven seemed to resonate.

chapters.title: Chapter 886 - 886 592 The Group Fight for Justice
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 886: Chapter 592: The Group Fight for Justice. Chapter 886: Chapter 592: The Group Fight for Justice. A chilling horn sound swept across the land…
crushing all traces nearby, shattering everything into fragments.
Following closely, an extreme and intense light flashed, purifying many things in an instant, covering a large area and cleansing most of the encompassed space to a “clean zone” where almost no microscopic life existed.
The white giant avatar hanging in the sky fluttered its wings to block these attacks, and beneath each feather, different powers burst forth.
These powers had some connection with the previous Angel Envoys.
However, no matter the battle, at least in the short term, it was difficult for either side to determine life or death, let alone a significant, substantive victory or loss.
That Pale Colossus was just an incarnation…
Shana was well aware of this, so she focused on intercepting the enemy “Disciples” who were attempting to retreat to this location.
If it weren’t for the “Light” pathway, it might not be easy to intercept the enemy’s retreat.
But in some ways, they all sprang from the same source. Although Shana was not as high on the life hierarchy as the enemy, her understanding inherited from the formal organization was not low.
With the assistance of the “King of Savage Sound,” she easily cut off the enemy’s retreat route of the “Disciples”…
“Boom!”
With a terrifying vibration, the “King of Savage Sound” seized the opportunity, tore off a wing, and forced out a “Disciple” that had been absorbed into its body.
And then further tore it apart on the spot…
The Pale Colossus didn’t mind this because at that moment, several “Projections of Light” formed through the torn gates of light and, after completing the simulation of “Authority,” burst forth with a terrifying aura.
Multiple beings with the power of “Level One Containment Subjects” had descended!
“Judging by some of the disturbances left on the scene, you guys took advantage of my weak leadership phase, liking to gang up in greater numbers, right! Now you get to try it too!”
The “King of Madness” called out, leading a group of allies gathered along the way in a righteous siege.
For some reason, both the “King of Madness” and Shana noticed that the entities behind the summoned “Projections of Light” seemed to be suddenly more empowered, displaying more autonomy, and there was a much more significant effort shown…
Even their mental states seemed more resolute!
Not at all like the previous period when, almost immediately after being summoned, they felt sick and lethargic, barely having the strength to fight.
Before this, Shana had guessed that it might have something to do with the price they paid to help escort Colin into the sea last time.
After all, it wasn’t long after that battle that they all seemed a bit off.
But this time, the fundamental reason for their condition seemed not to be what she had guessed.
Quickly thinking, Shana had a rough guess at the real reason—
It was still because of Colin!
After all, these guys came mostly to swear fealty, because only by doing so could they have a chance to escape their predicaments.
Halfway through, they lost their object of fealty, so their spirits started to dwindle.
“My faithful ‘Disciples,’ prove your devotion to me…” The Pale Colossus that had lost a wing murmured something like an oath.
Then, in the sacrifice of the “Disciples,” they transformed into clusters of “Projections of Light.”
It was summoning those lives it had once encountered, with which it might possibly have a basis for cooperation.
Shana acted, preventing the formation of some of the light shadows—the enemy was different from her; she directly put the “Projections of Light” into the “gates of light” for storage, readily available when needed.
The enemy was creating on the spot, and with the arrival of the enemy “Level One Containment Subject” light projections, there was still a chance to interrupt.
Meanwhile, she no longer focused all her efforts on that white giant avatar…
Instead, she began to eliminate any presence related to Colin as much as possible, a presence that was inappropriate to appear here…
Even though they had been erased several times before, if necessary, it could be done a few more times.
After all, Shana had made her way here almost without concealment; and if the Heretic Forces noticed, they might become suspicious and report to their “Masters”…
There was a certain probability that some entity might be drawn to investigate.
Of course, her current reason for acting in this world was to expand her Believers and to vie for control of the company’s inheritance…
Not much different from those higher beings.
The only trouble on the scene was “White Night,” but Shana estimated that it was highly likely he wouldn’t reveal Colin’s whereabouts; and even if he did, other beings might not be willing to come without actual proof.
And there was another important point…
Shana originated from the same source as White Night, allowing her to pretend that both sides were fighting for each other’s “Authority” power, seeking to assimilate and devour the other.
“Take this chance, Colin, to leave. I’ll come to find you after I finish things here.”
Shana’s voice came into his ears, Colin nodded slightly, a little reluctant, unsure if it was because he had physically shrunk that his personality had also become more childlike, or due to some other reason, he wasn’t as decisive.
Looking at Colin’s demeanor, caught between his original maturity and childlike nature, Shana stepped onto a light shadow and gently touched his head with a warm smile:
“I’ll bring you some gifts later.”
“Okay.”
Colin responded with a childlike voice, took out “Space: Transposition,” and after confirming a certain coordinate, he immediately transposed away.

chapters.title: Chapter 887 - 887 592 The Righteous Group Fight._2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 887: Chapter 592: The Righteous Group Fight._2 Chapter 887: Chapter 592: The Righteous Group Fight._2 Seeing Colin leave successfully, Shana breathed a sigh of relief.
With her understanding of the effects of the “Space Displacement Card,” such a transfer would be very difficult to track without prior marking, even for her.
Its cutting was a true severance; ordinary methods simply couldn’t keep up.
Once he had run, they would have to start searching all over again…
And just now, she had confirmed that, apart from the scent marker she had left on Colin, all other traces had been cleaned by her, so there wouldn’t be any more issues.
It was also after confirming Colin’s departure that the intensity of the battle at the scene almost instantly increased by several degrees.
Previously, everyone was somewhat holding back to avoid injuring this “leader,” and many were more focused on Colin, to prevent any unforeseen ambush.
Now that the person had left, they had no more concerns, each beginning to exhibit the horror and dominance befitting higher life forms!
And while The Pale Colossus had managed to summon a few beings through the sacrifice of its “Disciples,”
compared to those with a stronger will to fight, they didn’t stand a chance!
The battle here, although not yet over, could more or less be seen heading towards an outcome.
…
Meanwhile, in a special little world, Colin’s figure appeared out of nowhere, and upon landing, he looked around.
The place was quite empty and seemed as if it had been scorched by a massive fire, appearing barren…
Overall, it felt relatively safe.
“Not right, I can’t say it’s safe, just that I always have the feeling… it seems like this place is connected to something that makes people hungry, and because of the scent of that thing, many beings are simply unwilling to turn their gaze here.”
Colin had some guesses.
Rather than saying it was safe here, it would be more accurate to say that it was the slumber of something even more dangerous to the higher life forms, which made it seem safe.
And with some remnants of the aura left by that being, they could easily cover up their own issues…
Next, he looked down and saw many footprints on the ground.
Sniffing the air, he could tell from the remnant scents that these were left by the survivors he had transferred here before.
“It seems like I’ve picked the wrong place…”
Colin mumbled, having chosen the most “safe” location based on his intuition.
Unexpectedly, he had arrived at the same place where he had sent others before…
However, he had not transferred the believers from the Aurora Society here earlier, and even if he had, it wouldn’t have been a big problem because the strangeness here was enough to hide them.
Then, Colin took a step forward, intending to check on those people.
But after taking just one step, his head spun, he became sluggish, and he staggered to sit down on the ground.
The various negative side effects surged up following multiple uses of the Golden Artifact in the previous battle.
“Huff, huff…”
Colin shook his head forcefully, feeling not only bad control over his body but also a great disturbance in his sense of time.
Fortunately, there was no danger here at the moment.
Even if he sat still, nothing could threaten his life.
He could endure and release these negative effects to the fullest…
He lay on his back on the ground, closed his eyes, and silently endured this dizzying discomfort, occasionally retching, until after an unknown amount of time had passed.
His body felt slightly better, and then, still groggy, he opened his eyes to find that he was no longer lying on the ground, but resting on a pair of thighs.
“Are you feeling any better?” a familiar voice sounded.
Colin instantly became alert, but after regaining clarity and seeing it was the female doctor from before, he relaxed a bit.
“Thank you, sister, I think I’m alright now,” he nodded and replied politely.
“No, I should be the one thanking you, if it weren’t for you… I might have ‘died’ in the literal sense.”
The female doctor said with some lingering fear, then checked Colin’s body:
“Your injuries, they should be okay now, although there are still some scary wounds, although they’re all in vital areas, it doesn’t seem like there’s heavy bleeding, so it’s fine. As for the rest, just be careful not to get an infection, and you should be alright…”
She paused, as if remembering something, and smiled, “But you probably don’t need to worry too much about getting infected.”
Having such close contact with the Extraordinary Ones, only now did she fully realize just how exaggerated their physical conditioning could be…
Regenerating limbs wasn’t an issue, let alone wound infections.
“Okay, I will be careful,” Colin said, nodding while lying on her thigh.
At the same time, he also took the opportunity to observe her a little, as she had been previously selected as a participant in the “Disciple ritual.” He wondered if she had been brainwashed by something.
Soon, after confirming that there were no issues, he redirected his attention and adjusted his position, continuing to lie down.
Then Colin noticed that, aside from her, there were a few other people around, including the government employee who had demonstrated Sixth Level strength not long ago.
“Bro… I mean, brother, you made it out safely too, that’s really great,” the other said with a sigh of relief.
Previously, when the Aurora Society’s great being performed “God Descent,” he thought their chances of survival were slim.
He hadn’t expected them to actually manage an escape…
“I should probably thank you as well,” Colin recalled how the other had given him a certain “gaze” before being swapped, which had successfully resulted in Shana arriving…
Otherwise, the current situation would be a bit difficult to predict.
“I’m glad you’re okay…”
After speaking, he curiously asked about the situation on the other side, wondering who had come to the rescue and managed to pull them out of the hands of the Ancient God.
To his knowledge, up until today, there weren’t many with such clout on the “Light” path.
That senior employee from another company, or those individuals who had embedded “Light” within themselves to stabilize their power, they didn’t quite measure up in his view…
After all, we are dealing with an Ancient God here, even if it’s just an avatar, not someone ordinary people can easily deal with.
Otherwise, they wouldn’t be at the brink of civilization extinction right now.
‘If only humanity had a few more powerful figures, it wouldn’t be this helpless,’ he couldn’t help thinking.
The only ones capable of exerting such force within the path of “Light”…
And excluding those people, the only remaining option…
Seemed to be just one.
The young man held his breath for a moment, faintly realizing who that person might be!
Someone with numerous representations, rarely known by many in terms of origin, gender, etc., but one thing was certain, a prominent person on humanity’s side, a purveyor of the path of “Light”!
“It’s okay, you don’t need to worry about them coming over anymore, you can survive here for now…”
Colin didn’t say much. Looking around, although the place was bare, he vaguely remembered storing quite a few things here before the disaster struck, as an emergency shelter.
“Are there other people here?!” the captain of the team that had first discovered Colin suddenly spoke up at the mention.
“There are… but I’m not exactly sure where,” Colin nodded.
Years ago, after killing someone and seizing the Spatial Displacement artifact from them, he had transferred a few people here during his escape.
Seeing their nervous expressions, Colin lifted his head from the makeshift pillow and sat up, soothingly saying, “There’s no need to panic, just tell them that you were transferred here by me, and they’ll welcome you…”
He understood why they were anxious.
In the post-apocalyptic ruins, although food wasn’t scarce, confrontations could still erupt violently due to potential differences in belief systems among survivors.
He briefed them on the situation, and everyone breathed a sigh of relief.
Then, the young man hesitated, curious to ask about the person who had observed through him in that particular area.
But at that moment, Colin suddenly looked towards a certain direction as if sensing something. The others, noticing his abrupt gesture, also turned to look.
And then their expressions changed.
On the clearing there, light began to converge from all around, condensing into a pure, pale radiance.

chapters.title: Chapter 888 - 888 593 Sister Shana
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 888: Chapter 593 “Sister Shana”. Chapter 888: Chapter 593 “Sister Shana”. In the open space ahead, a pure, white light slowly transformed into a beautiful and sacred human-like entity.
Among those present, aside from Colin, even the Extraordinary One of “Light” couldn’t make out the specific figure of the humanoid light-shadow.
In different people’s eyes, its gender and appearance varied.
However, when the white light first appeared, the few on site were all shocked and immediately assumed a guarded stance.
The female doctor quickly scooped up Colin like a teddy bear.
The others also readied themselves for battle, stepping forward—
Despite the aura emitted by the light, suggesting they stood no chance of victory, they couldn’t just die without doing anything.
But soon, the Extraordinary One touched by the “Light” realized this might not be an enemy of the Aurora Society?
He was somewhat uncertain, having never seen such a high-level powerhouse within their ranks.
Just then, they heard Colin speak, “No need to be so tense, it’s a friend.”
As his words fell, the tension eased significantly, and then Colin saw, emerging from the light, Shana, tall and clad in white with gold trim, waving to him.
Colin instantly wriggled out of her embrace and dashed towards her.
Although the doctor’s embrace was large and soft, he still preferred a sense of safety and affinity.
Catching Colin, who flew into her arms like a swallow returning to its nest, Shana let him sit on her left arm, his hands kneading her neck. She turned her gaze to the people present.
Gleaning from the remnants of “Light,” Shana pieced together how Colin had come to be there.
She realized these people had helped Colin through his initial “confused phase.”
After nodding slightly in thanks to them, Shana, with one arm around Colin, cast several orbs of light toward the people present.
Each orb contained substantial power, enough to greatly enhance their physique.
And to some extent, it allowed them to wield extraordinary power in small measures.
Their strength approximated that of the local Third and Fourth Level Extraordinary Ones—not much, but for ordinary people, it represented a significant leap, as if they had one foot on the path of the Extraordinary.
For the one already at Level 6, Shana offered an opportunity of “Light.”
Whether he could ascend was up to him.
But even if he didn’t ascend, his power would be further perfected and supplemented.
“Thank you for this great gift…” The Official Level Six Personnel, sensing the power within him, expressed his sincere gratitude.
It included not only a portion of the qualities of “Light,” but also the accompanying knowledge inheritance.
Once he successfully steps into Level Seven, his strength would far surpass that of newcomers.
After he finished speaking, the others offered their belated thanks, only to realize that the figure had already left.
“Who was that…?” the female doctor asked, blinking, as she felt the light emanating from her body.
Hearing this, the Official Level Six Personnel fell silent for a moment before speaking somewhat uncertainly:
“He has many identities. Some more obscure ones, like ‘Messenger of Dawn and Light,’ or ‘Person of the Dawn,’ among many others… However, the one known most broadly here is usually ‘Pure Light Bodhisattva.'”
As for the origins, there were several theories, because, appearing shortly after the Deep Sea as well, some said he was a pre-catastrophe human powerhouse or a local individual who grew rapidly during that disastrous period.
Beyond that, some speculated that he was a human from a world outside of Earth who came to offer support.
Whichever it was, there were examples of each by now, and more than one.
Just that they usually weren’t this famous.
But since this belonged to the domain of mystical knowledge, they wouldn’t understand even if it were explained, so it wasn’t mentioned.
Across from him, as people heard what he said, they took a sharp breath.
“This, isn’t this a True God descending to Earth…” exclaimed the leader of the explorer squad.
While they were unfamiliar with the first few identities, the last was well-known, if not universally so: “Pure Light Bodhisattva,” an entity many prayed to in the post-apocalyptic world.
Because many times, He truly manifested!
And He was the most frequently manifesting one!
…Actually, he was also human, just one that stood above Level Nine, infinitely close to the power of a highly dangerous Containment Subject. Compared to calling Him a god, he probably preferred to be referred to as human… the official thought to himself. However, from the perspective of ordinary people.
Such a being could indeed be described as a divine!
At the same time, he was puzzled; according to some of his not entirely accurate information, this preacher of “Light,” accounting for those “small worlds,” was at a distance that could circle the Earth’s equator from the past several times over.
Who exactly was this Returner from the Deep Sea?
Why had such a major figure crossed a vast distance to get here?
For a moment, he wondered if that kid named Colin was the child of this individual?
…
“Sister Shana, where are we going?”
…Sister Shana… Hearing little Colin call her that, Shana’s ice blue eyes blinked, a barely perceptible smile tugging at her lips. Hearing that word from Colin’s mouth sounded rather novel.
She planned to record this moment in the light, to show it to him later… if there was a later.
Then, refocusing her thoughts, Shana spoke, “I’m not sure yet, but first, we should probably leave this place and find a safe haven…”

chapters.title: Chapter 889 - 889 593 Sister Shana. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 889: Chapter 593 “Sister Shana”. _2 Chapter 889: Chapter 593 “Sister Shana”. _2 Discussing this, she hesitated slightly because in a certain sense,
for Colin, who was a reservist of the “Flame Bearer,” there was nowhere that could truly be deemed safe. The presence of the “Red Moon” was a temporary protection, but it also presented an opportunity for the “The Gods” to escape.
Because its descent had destroyed some of the arrangements that once existed here, allowing them the possibility of breaking free soon.
This meant, once the presence of the “Red Moon” completely faded, calamity was inevitable.
And where the “The Gods” appeared, disaster would follow Colin.
Although their primary target would probably be to vie for some of the “legacy” here, during or after this period, they would certainly not mind initiating revenge against Colin.
Now, if one were to say where was the safest, this place, for the time being, could be considered the safest.
“There’s always a place to hide first after all…”
Shana seemed to be answering Colin as well as reassuring herself as she spoke, pausing for a moment before continuing:
“For now, we’ll just roam around, and leave when the time comes. Is there any place you’d like to go? I can take you there to have some fun…”
“Oh, okay, Sister Shana, wherever you want to go is fine with me as long as you’re there,” Colin said, sitting in Shana’s lap, hugging her slender neck like a koala, his face expressing his youthful innocence.
Shana laughed, “It’s hard to imagine, you saying something like this.”
“Ah?” Colin responded as if he knew nothing.
“Hmm…”
Shana raised her hand and pinched his nose, then set him down and took his small hand as they walked along the shattered streets.
Though she had been in this world for more than half a year, this was the first time she carried such a leisurely mood to really look at this place.
It was evident that this place was far superior in various aspects of life compared to her hometown.
But without dwelling on it much, as Shana walked, she mulled over the ideas she had come up with these days about how she could keep Colin safe if she found him.
For example…
Heading to the so-called “Radiant Angel” Corps encampment that had some arrangements left behind.
Or, finding the location of the mysterious superior behind Colin…
As well as some places she had seen along the way.
But, after thinking about it, Shana quickly dismissed most of them, as they didn’t seem quite appropriate. Going to the “World Code” areas was also akin to seeking death, as it was beyond the “wall.”
Even with remnants from the Corps, it might not be very effective…
As for that superior behind Colin, according to some information Shana bought from the “World Code-13” branch, that place was likely not a safe area either.
According to “World Code-13,” Colin’s enigmatic existence is powerful but in a strange state… “World Code-13” described it as “a group existing outside of time and space.”
Everyone who has reached her level at the company shares a similar status.
Not just him, but other great beings also exist in this state…
The reason, possibly, is related to some special tool initiated by some tycoon.
Shana didn’t quite understand, but she knew not to expect any help from here.
What remained was a few directions given by “World Code-13.”
If no “Flame Bearer” was born, to keep Colin safe,
the first was, if she had the capability, to find and rally a group of remnants and forces making up about ten percent, and stick together.
That being said, at least before the great calamity of “2044” arrived,
the likelihood of keeping Colin safe was not out of the question…
But that was unlikely too.
Not to mention how to find people, where to look for them, in this day and age, even the existence behind Colin couldn’t keep the “branches” and external employees aligned, let alone her.
The only way to get the majority to agree was if there were a “Flame Bearer” with a special status within the company, enabled to enact specific authoritative laws.
But if there were a “Flame Bearer,” then why would she seek help?
In that moment, those needing help, from their perspective, would turn to those ancient entities, perhaps causing the “Ancient Gods” to reunite and form an anti-“Bonfire” coalition again…
But for now, that was just a thought.
Next, came the second suggestion…
She had found the “Seed of Light”, fully activated the “Light” including its subordinate “Corps” among other forces…
It could preserve Colin as well, but this condition was no simpler than the success of the “Flame Bearer”.
Theoretically, the “Seed of Light” would appear, but it was deeply entangled with the “The Ultimate Moment” in premonition—to put it plainly, it was most likely that it would only reappear on that day.
Of course, nothing was absolute, if she could assist the “branch office” in acquiring a large amount of points, activate something, and then travel to “World Code-1”.
If she could find Rosen, or more of his remains, there would be a chance.
According to some premonitions it revealed, if the “Flame Bearer” were to appear, it was very likely to be linked with Rosen.
But, Shana had to take care of Colin, so it was impossible to agree, and based on some information Colin had previously provided, Shana felt the “branch office’s” idea was as good as daydreaming.
According to Colin, they were all dead down to the bones, even the bones were eroding, and yet it still dwelt on these memories.
There was a third way…
The branch office indicated there were other ways to preserve life, but it was not certain.
…
With each thought flickering, Shana felt, aside from knowing more useless information, she didn’t really have many practical things.
However, no matter what, she couldn’t just sit and wait for death…
Shana continued contemplating more reliable shift plans.
In the following several days, she moved through the post-apocalyptic wasteland with Colin.
Occasionally entering amusement parks that hadn’t been completely abandoned, powered by props electricity, just manageable to use, sometimes lending a hand to some survivors, or visiting various areas for observation…
When the Ancient Gods were absent, and avoiding some dangerous taboo areas, she and Colin could basically roam freely.
During observation, Colin noticed that the world had become abnormally vast, with various small and large patchwork worlds, and many peculiarly special human races.
Maybe due to environmental impressions, despite different environments and customs, the general values leaned towards the positive and conformed to humanoid ideals.
In the peaceful days of slaying demons and exterminating heretics.
Time passed quickly…
Another ten days went by, Shana felt it was about time to leave.
To leave through a small world to a “branch office” domain, and ultimately try to go to a place that might be safe.
But, while she was contemplating this, Shana suddenly seemed to notice something, turning her head to look sideways.
She saw Colin standing on a piece of steel-reinforced concrete, looking somewhat dazed.
“What’s wrong, Colin?” Shana flickered over.
“Shana, it’s okay, I just don’t know why, looking at these scrap metals, I always feel it’s a pity. When I was young, I always thought, if I picked up one more piece of rebar, I could buy another ice pop. Now seeing these scraps all over the streets, it actually makes me feel very upset…” Colin spoke, his voice getting lower and lower, until finally he fell silent.
At that moment, Shana reached out to rub his head, about to say something, but she suddenly paused the next second.
Colin spoke first, in a very familiar tone:
“Sister Shana, well, Shana…”
Shana blinked, staring at him blankly, knowing what his statement meant…
Colin had regained all his memories!
But she still couldn’t help saying, “You, you’ve recovered your memory?”
“Yes…”
Colin nodded, his memory had just come back entirely, it felt nothing special, it was like waking up groggy, and then suddenly becoming completely clear.
As thoughts flickered, Colin took a deep breath, steadied his emotions, then looked at the glowing figure in front of him, somewhat unsure what to say.
This “childhood” memory, he definitely still had it, Shana hadn’t hidden it from him, to come over here, they had traveled for more than half a year, the journey tough but they finally made it.
This favor, and her intentions, it was no longer about whether to return it or not…
Although they hadn’t finally determined their relationship yet, Colin felt like he was already Shana’s person now.
..
Wait, there’s more
.

chapters.title: Chapter 890 - 890 594 Brother Shunzi
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 890: Chapter 594 “Brother Shunzi! Chapter 890: Chapter 594 “Brother Shunzi! “My memory has been restored, but my body is still a bit off. It can recover, just that it would require the power of the ‘Bonfire’ to do so immediately, and once I do, I’ll have to face quite a few troubles…”
Colin paused, seemingly recalling something. He gestured for Shana to put him down, and then complained somewhat:
“Speaking of which, I was almost damned by that cursed ‘Sea God’ successor.”
“What happened?” Shana lifted her hand to brush a strand of hair aside.
“I had a vague sense of your presence, so even though I was in deep sleep at the time, I let him throw me towards a place with ‘Light’. But the guy, he tossed me right next to ‘White Night’…”
Colin couldn’t help but complain.
It was nearly a direct throw into the tiger’s mouth.
“So that happened…” Shana said, a bit surprised.
“Yes, fortunately, nothing serious happened; otherwise, that little runt would have doomed me.”
As Colin spoke, he realized the possible consequences, feeling somewhat apprehensive.
“What exactly happened in the sea? How did it come to this?” Shana asked, curious.
At that time, not only did Colin have a slew of negative effects on him, but he was also branded by various Ancient Gods.
Then everything disappeared after soaking in the sea?
“Probably that guy, using his own ‘authority’ combined with some corporate functions I still can’t quite grasp, diluted me completely, and then gradually released the problems from my body into the sea…”
Colin briefly described the process.
This also led to his body “shrinking” and temporarily losing most of his memories.
However, he then thought of other matters and didn’t dwell much on this issue as his expression gradually became more solemn.
“There’s something I might need to mention, it might not be as hard as you think for me to survive…”
Colin said, seeing Shana listening attentively, he continued:
“In general, I would have two options. The first is to find a suitable place to enter a deep sleep and withdraw from the world with my current identity…”
“If I make this choice, it means I give up becoming a ‘Flame Bearer’. Then, as long as I hide far enough away, those gods and ghosts will stop hunting me.”
“At the same time, it also means I’m handing the possibilities to someone else.”
Colin briefly explained the situation.
However, it was obvious to Shana that this wasn’t his choice…
“Although I always like to say I believe in the wisdom of later generations, the more time passes, the more difficult it becomes. If I choose this, it’s almost as if it’s all over…” Colin explained.
Perhaps the corporation had other candidates lined up to follow him.
But that would no longer be his concern.
“The second option is to fight, to fight for everything I have! When I ascended to C Level and connected more deeply with the ‘Bonfire’, I already had some rough ideas…”
“If I fight, it will probably involve reigniting the Bonfire. In this process, I will be back to normal. Additionally, through some means, I’ll be able to control a large portion of the power and try to forcefully confront the ‘Primordial Fire’…”
“See what kind of situation it really is.”
Colin paused and added: “By doing so, there would be many potential outcomes. The best, of course, would be to become a ‘Flame Bearer’, where I can preserve everything and even look forward to 2044.
“The next would be failure, but driving them out, shifting the battlefield, and making this place pure.
“Or, find a safe zone and take as many people away as possible…
“Or perhaps…”
Colin laid out all the potential outcomes he could think of.
“The worst outcome doesn’t require thinking—it’s total annihilation, which is the inevitable result if no action is taken when the ‘Red Moon’ passes…”
Although at the time, while collaborating with “The Gods” against the “Red Moon”,
Colin demanded that they should not harm ordinary people actively…
But if they decided to pay a certain price, they could still cause significant harm to ordinary people, even without direct actions.
So…
“What I can ensure is that if I intervene, there’ll definitely be a ‘safe bet’. Meaning, no matter what, I can make sure to move a large part of what’s left to another world, thus leaving more Sparks behind.”
“Who knows, they might succeed…”
“After all, this fight, whether I live or die, if I don’t succeed, there’ll be no chances later on.”
“The only piece of good news might be that if I fight and fail but survive, I’m unlikely to be hunted down desperately. To put it in certain terms, failing to achieve the path means complete failure.”
“To them, such a person is no different from a dead man.”
If that time comes, one has to trust in the later generations whether they believe in them or not, as there would be no other choice.
Sitting to the side, Shana, with her elbow resting on her knee and her palm supporting her chin, gazed at him quietly as he finished speaking. Then she asked:
“No matter what, it’s good that you’re alive.
“Then, that means, you can be sure that you’ll inevitably be able to obtain a strong enough power for some time?”
“Yes.”
Colin nodded, “I have it. It’s a one-time move. I had this feeling when I advanced to C Level before, but due to severe injuries and being targeted, I wasn’t sure and couldn’t use it. Oh, the ‘Red Moon’ influence is also a key factor…
“I have to wait for the ‘Red Moon’s forces to fade. While it’s present, the effect will decrease, even the success rate isn’t guaranteed. Only after it subsides, I’ll be able to try.”

chapters.title: Chapter 891 - 891 594 Brother Shunzi_2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 891: Chapter 594 “Brother Shunzi!”_2 Chapter 891: Chapter 594 “Brother Shunzi!”_2 “At that time, I’ll try to give this bunch of guys, who are fighting to get out and lay their hands on me, a big surprise…”
Of course, that still relies on when the interference subsides, the signal connects, and he gets a little help from Lady Bunny.
He would acquire Rogue, as well as some other things from the “Flame Bearers.”
After talking it through, Colin finally asked, “Shana, are you willing to take a gamble with me?”
“Sure, I am willing.”
Shana replied, as expected.
Hearing this, almost without a second thought and deeply touched, Colin stepped forward, hugged Shana tightly, and couldn’t help but kiss her on the cheek.
Surprised by his “bold” move, Shana paused for a moment, then smiled and, taking advantage of Colin’s distraction, lifted him up and with a “pop,” returned the gesture in kind.
“It’s a pity, you’re still too small like this…” Shana pursed her lips, gave a wry smile, then put Colin down.
“Let’s talk about it later.”
Colin nodded and clenched his fist: “We will win.”
“I believe in you, and you also need to believe in yourself, don’t give up, I will face everything with you,” Shana promised.
“Yeah.”
Colin nodded earnestly, indicating he definitely wouldn’t give up easily.
“Yeah…”
Shana said, then suddenly changed her tone, as if it was no different from usual, yet with a peculiar undertone, “So, Mr. Colin, is there anything else you would like to talk about?”
Hearing this, Colin had a bad feeling and thought carefully.
All the preparations and possible consequences seemed to be just what he’d mentioned…
But seeing Shana’s tone, Colin hesitated and said with uncertainty, “It seems like there’s nothing else…”
“Hmm-hmm…” Shana’s expression carried a rare special meaning, like she was up to no good, and she smiled slyly, “Would you mind if I ask you something then, Mr. Colin?”
“Uh, go ahead,” Colin nodded.
“Do you mind talking about Miss Liu Yun?”
Shana asked with curiosity.
The lady who had gambolled everything on her own to escort Colin, staking her life, Shana remembered quite clearly and was somewhat moved by it…
“Oh, her…”
Colin came to his senses, then glanced at Shana but couldn’t discern her expression, and he spoke with a mix of emotions:
“There’s nothing I can’t talk about.”
After briefly explaining the situation, Colin wore a face of melancholy complexity.
The information collected previously in Passionate Paradise indicated that even without losing control, its success rate was not high. Back in the day, many companies’ “elites” charged in, shouting challenges at their own weaknesses, confident and brimming; yet one by one, they all came to nothing.
Colin didn’t quite understand why before.
Now, he sort of understood…
Although many things in it were fake, were staged, it didn’t play false with you, once the “characters” inside, like Liu Yun, “awakened,” their emotions became real, autonomous and unique…
How could anyone bear it?
It’s impossible to guard against, absolutely impossible…
“Is that so…”
After listening, Shana said, “I remember, she seemed to have sunk to the bottom of the sea, maybe we could save her?”
There were no thoughts of jealousy, only the feeling that it was a pity to lose a life.
“I’m not quite sure, maybe it can only be known after contacting that little guy in the sea, if she was swept into the sea back then, the chances of survival are high, but…”
Colin shook his head: “Even if she’s alive, she probably wouldn’t want to wake up.”
This might already be the best outcome.
Thinking it over, Boss Huang He, the instigator behind this Passionate Paradise, truly caused no small harm to others.
After speaking, there was a brief silence on the scene.
Then suddenly, Shana raised her hand, rubbed Colin’s head forcefully, breaking the silence, and began talking about other things.
For example, the current state of some employees as well as the world…
Colin quickly got a clear picture of what condition the world was in now.
First was the size, it couldn’t be said to be infinite, but at least, from six months ago to now, Shana had not yet seen a definite boundary or end, with various overlapping “Inner Worlds” visible every once in a while.
Some could get out just by walking straight ahead, others might get turned around variously, making the landscape of the world extremely complex.
“No wonder this world always has all sorts of anomalies popping up, never completely eradicated,” Colin couldn’t help saying.
If nothing else, these things seemed to be the masterpieces of the “Bonfire Company”—
Even if it wasn’t, it couldn’t be entirely unconnected to them.
Secondly, regarding the employees, according to “Life Mentor Adorable’s” statistics, about forty or fifty percent might have been sacrificed, which, compared to the mass casualties of ordinary people, couldn’t be considered a lot.
But to say it wasn’t a lot, that certainly wasn’t true either…
Many people Colin knew had died, like the cheap apprentice “Professor Cute Cuddle” of Adorable, like someone with a Martian name, like many…
At the height of the crisis, even Parchment had once come to a standstill, not reopening until “The Deep Sea Era”.
Various functions were also limited, like shopping in the marketplace with purchasing limits, communication functions only working in certain areas and not reliably, most of the time there was nothing…
Like now Colin couldn’t even turn it on.
Besides that, the only thing worth being glad for was that the crucial “mission” mechanism was still running, and those who were still alive had basically all been promoted to D Level.
Elite D-Level employees with extremely rich combat experience!
“One bigger problem is, after the disaster, it no longer actively selects and recruits,”
Shana shared the intel she had understood: “Now, many employees who left this world through ‘missions’ or other means, are trying as much as possible to return, to support this place…”She continued mentioning some things, like how originally quite a few people had entered “non-existent hospitals,” “Abyssal Blood Pool” and the like for special missions.
Where they had avoided the most dangerous moments of the disaster.
“It seems like ‘Brother Unyielding’ might have put his strength into it there,” Colin felt somewhat heartened.
But he couldn’t feel heartened for long…
Because, including the “non-existent hospital” and so on, a lot had completely disappeared without a trace during “The Deep Sea Era”.
Not knowing whether they were dead or alive, the surviving employees couldn’t uncover any information…
Colin picked up the Parchment, and using his C-Level authority, tried to sense the situation of these missions, attempting to gain some inspirational knowledge.
But quickly, he frowned, he didn’t feel anything.
It all seemed to have vanished.
If it were simply a disappearance that would be one thing, but more critically, even the mission records…
Seemed to have been wiped clean.
This was not something an external enemy could accomplish.
“Seems like there’s a bit of a problem.”
Colin instinctively felt that something was amiss.
He couldn’t speak for those other places like blood pools that he hadn’t visited, but after sensing the anomaly, Colin even had a feeling that something wasn’t right the last time at the “non-existent hospital”.
However, without any leads to track, he could only put it aside for the time being.
In the following period, Colin accompanied Shana on the post-apocalyptic wasteland, enjoying the last bit of leisure time.
After feeling the “Red Moon” presence as if the tide was retreating.
Colin and Shana came to a crumbling dam near the sea where they set up a bonfire.
Next, while grilling some recently caught large squid, sending them as Qingming offerings for an old friend, he took out the Parchment.
After waiting for a while, the communication function was restored.
“Brothers, up for the final winning chicken dinner match? Winner eats chicken, loser eats shit. Anyone joining me?”
After editing and sending the message, other employees, intending to query its meaning, halted upon seeing the ID that had been longed for and overlooked for over two and a half years.
Each one paused, incredulously rubbing their eyes, then widening them to the fullest!
Brother Shunzi, logged in?!

chapters.title: Chapter 892 - 892 595 The Disappeared It
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 892: Chapter 595 The Disappeared “It”. Chapter 892: Chapter 595 The Disappeared “It”. “Is this for real?! It couldn’t be a trap, could it?”
“So far, I’ve never seen a fake account! It can’t be fake, it’s Brother Shunzi’s account!”
“He’s back! They’re all back!”
“@654321! I just knew it, Brother Shunzi, you’d definitely come back. Where are you now? Let’s charge once more together!”
“…”
In an instant, the surviving employees exploded with excitement. After struggling so long in this oppressive doomsday world, there was finally some good news for Pete’s sake!
Instantly, noticing Brother Shunzi’s message, they all started frantically asking questions.
“Life Mentor Adorable”: @654321, what’s this about a chicken dinner? What’s going on? Whatever it is, Brother Shunzi, count me in!
“Loafing Immortal”: Add me too! I want revenge!
“Happiness is Superman!”: Me as well! I’m still alive, simply surviving on my hatred for these darn things. As long as I can get revenge on them, death doesn’t matter!
…
One by one, employees swiftly spoke up, a stark contrast to their previous “timid and afraid of death”.
Now, their beliefs had drastically changed.
The catastrophe made people grow, but the cost was way too high.
They had lost too much…
Colin looked at the familiar IDs, shadows of their corresponding figures flickering in his mind, and couldn’t help but sigh.
From the first announcement of refuge to now, it had only been a little over three years, but everything seemed utterly transformed.
Even, from his perspective, it seemed to be about half a year…
Since he had been asleep for a long time.
Upon waking, many things were simply gone.
Silently shaking his head, Colin typed back “Hold your horses,” and then informed them that he needed to check up on everyone’s situation before making further arrangements.
Like confirming locations, for instance.
Otherwise, even though employees said they were on Earth, the Earth was as vast as ever.
Bringing everyone together would indeed be an arduous task for him.
Moreover, when it came to location confirmation, Colin had to be careful. He could only use landmarks in his mind to ask if any employees had seen similar objects. If so, they would discreetly confirm the details.
He wouldn’t let either party disclose their current positions, just that they would meet at a certain place later.
But as he thought this through, Colin suddenly realized something was amiss.
Just then, an employee chatting with him sent over a message:
“Actually, that ‘Stupid Robot’ has disappeared. There are risks to reporting locations now, but it’s not as dangerous anymore…”
“Disappeared?”
Colin was taken aback, thinking carefully, he realized he indeed hadn’t seen those things making any noise.
He sent out a query about this and quickly got an answer: at the start of the disaster, those things were around, but then one day, they simply vanished.
As if they had disappeared in the blink of an eye without any trace.
Currently, the employees were clueless about the situation, not knowing whether to take it as a good or bad thing, but most actually preferred it when these things were visible every day in the chat channel.
Not because they felt affection for it from constant contact, but because, for many corporate employees, this damn thing was like a cockroach.
It was terrifying to see it one moment, and then not see it the next.
Especially since it was a tremendously dangerous and horrifying entity.
However, compared to the clueless employees, Colin had some guesses…
“The disappearance timing is somewhat close to when Old Master Wu summoned ‘Script City,’ but I’m not certain if it’s related.”
“I currently can’t detect its specific location, although I’ve never been able to sense it. ‘Lady Rabbit’ once said that solving it might require higher clearance, yes, the key is clearance, not power…”
Colin pursed his lips, suspecting that during the disaster, it had perhaps achieved some unknown objective and left the internal group chat.
Now, immediate problems obviously didn’t concern this.
Unable to track it, he would put it aside for now.
Later, when he had a chance, he would see and confirm whether it had escaped, been snatched by some entities, been completely sealed, or something else…
“Brother Shunzi, do you not need me over there?” “Life Mentor Adorable” suddenly asked.
“Your location isn’t quite suitable. For now, just focus on taking refuge, and wait for the results,” Colin replied succinctly.
After being promoted to Level C Clearance, his speech restrictions had been lifted.
No longer did he feel an eerie unease when he added a couple of extra words like before.
‘From what I can see, it should be some corporate response mechanisms left by this world, targeting specifically…’Lady Rabbit’, or rather, including her and all ‘outsiders’.’
Colin raised his hand to stroke his chin, feeling that Earth’s defenses were somewhat “unrecognizable.”
Somewhat like a non-intelligent mechanical execution system…
It wouldn’t play on the fringes of manipulation like the “World Code-13” branch office.
It is what it is.
At this moment, “Life Mentor Adorable,” seeing Colin’s response, sent a message that appeared quite regretful: “Alright.”

chapters.title: Chapter 893 - 893 595 The Disappearing It. _2
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 893: Chapter 595: The Disappearing “It”. _2 Chapter 893: Chapter 595: The Disappearing “It”. _2 Colin was somewhat aware of the other party’s thoughts, though the details of Lifecoach Kawaii-many’s family and loved ones were unclear.
However, internally within the company, Kawaii-many had good relations with many people; otherwise, it wouldn’t have been possible to gather intelligence.
But in these few years, a good number of these people had died, either indifferently at the hands of “The Gods” wielding their authority or at the brutal hands of the invading Heretic Races and all sorts of anomalies…
Currently, if there had been no contact, the prospects were generally bleak.
“However,” Colin said, “once I start taking action, the whole world will probably be in turmoil. To stop me, the noise from those Containment Subjects being produced might not be less severe than the ‘divine disaster’ at the beginning of the catastrophe. You all need to prepare…”
“No problem,” Lifecoach Kawaii-many saw the message and immediately became serious.
“There is half a month or a month left, prepare yourselves…”
After finishing, Colin thought for a moment and sent another message:
“There’s another matter. Organize a team to compile all the information on the current Heretics causing trouble, anomalies, and some of the more active Containment Subjects, including everything they have done…”
If there was a chance, he would selectively target these troublemakers.
“No problem, it should be resolved very quickly,” Lifecoach Kawaii-many responded.
Such matters were not difficult because actually, every time the “internal group chat” was restored, someone would post some new anomaly information, alerting others to be careful and avoid pitfalls…
Over the years, a large amount of data had accumulated.
All he needed to do was to organize it.
In no time, he had finished and sent everything to Brother Shunzi.
“There’s quite a bit of data…” Colin held the parchment in his left hand and stroked his chin with his right hand, reading the content.
The higher life forms had not taken active action; by and large, they were mostly lying in wait, with very little activity. Even if they did act, it was mainly involved in “Agent” wars…
Similarly, various anomalies were generally passive, lacking any real intelligence, just mechanically moving like stones by the roadside—if you didn’t kick them, your foot wouldn’t hurt, not really targeting anything specifically…
So their impact wasn’t particularly significant.
The greatest current threat to people was from some strange species that emerged from nowhere, wielding more advanced technology or possessing special mystical abilities. Using various means to reach this place, they continually captured or slaughtered the already few survivors…
Colin remembered seeing some space vessels as big as things hanging high above the dome not long ago, but at the time he didn’t have the leisure to deal with those things.
Of course, apart from capturing or slaughtering humans, they also preyed on various anomalies, special metal resources, and even some extremely weak higher life forms!
Their actions indirectly led to the destruction of many safe havens and gathering points in the aftermath of battles with powerful beings.
After all, this was not their homeland; it didn’t matter how much they destroyed.
“A bunch of opportunists.”
Colin summed it up simply.
Besides these, there were also a small number of friendly ones, but not many…
Following that, he looked at a report about “Fetal Angel,” and his brow furrowed slightly.
It had been confirmed that during the Deep Sea calamity, “Fetal Angel” had for some reason turned against them, becoming an existence named White Night.
“‘For some reason,'” Colin repeated these words, vaguely forming some speculations…
The entire line of “angel” technology was derived from “The Seventh Box Garden World.”
If he remembered correctly, there was a high-ranking Containment Subject called White Night in that world at the time.
“This guy, did he dig a pitfall in the technology…”
Colin surmised the reason for White Night’s appearance.
He just didn’t expect that the pitfall dug by this guy had escaped the company’s “disinfection” screening…
“Or maybe there’s no problem with the technology itself, and it’s only when manufacturing certain special ‘angels’ that pitfalls arise… It gambled on a probability and actually won,” Colin guessed. White Night, after appearing, had clashed many times with some of Shana’s avatars or her subordinates among the Extraordinary Ones.
It obviously showed an interest in Shana…
Or, more accurately, an interest in Shana’s extraordinary traits.
However, it clearly lacked the strength to take her down; should it appear, it would likely be driven away.
But no matter what,
“This guy, given the chance, I must take it down first.”
Colin recorded this at the very top of the first line in his notebook.
Then, he roughly organized the current information on the heretic anomalies, promising his employees that when the opportunity arose, he would not let a single one escape!
“It’s up to you to welcome our guests, Shana,” Colin said, turning to Shana beside him before picking up a skewer of nicely grilled squid and handing it to her as she sat at the side.
Though the squid looked somewhat abstract, it was still safe to eat and free from any peculiar contamination.
As for the old acquaintance, it was the thought that counted.
“Sure, you don’t need to be polite with me.”
Shana took the food from Colin, confirmed their direction, and while her body remained seated, vague and hazy figures emerged from her and darted off in different directions, transforming into streaks of light as they rapidly departed.
Watching Shana finish eating, Colin fed her a few more, feeling considerably more cheerful.
For the next few days, neither of them talked much about the battle that was about to erupt soon.
They spent their time wandering aimlessly through these ruins of the apocalypse.
Colin acted as a guide, explaining various things to Shana—though she had already grasped most of them, having rapidly processed a vast amount of network information due to her special nature.
And so, she had come to understand most things about this civilization…
All knowledge was categorized and stored in her mind as if filed away in folders.
But even knowing this, the experience of being introduced by Colin gave her a different feeling.
“Some methods that use ‘light signals’ to transmit information are very important to us…” Shana said, holding Colin’s small hand as they walked and talked:
“I and most of the Extraordinary Ones from the ‘Light’ Conclave can directly decipher the information within the lines. If every Conclave is connected through these ‘light signals,’ the entire world’s ‘Light’ Conclave could even be unified.”
“Heh, the rulers of your nations will start losing sleep over this soon.”
Colin chuckled at the thought of the various countries and congregations that were highly vigilant against the “Light” Conclave.
“Exactly, but they cannot deny the appeal of such a thing: ultra-low-cost, long-range communication… But more than that, I think the value of ‘science’ as a thought and a way of understanding the world might be even higher than these…”
“This world had no Extraordinary Power for a very long time, but through a certain thought, a new way of understanding the world, it achieved…”
Shana paused, her gaze falling upon the broken world, revealing a sense of regret and a sigh, “a transformation that was almost earth-shattering.”
She had been to many worlds, and to be honest, Earth’s overall level of civilization was not particularly remarkable…
But most of it was either “ancient” legacy or the result of prolonged and exaggerated evolution; few could show continuous self-driven progress and a “technology explosion” like this one.
The simplest example: if we went back ten thousand years, this world would have been dominated by the Extraordinary Ones from her side.
This timeline extended to eight thousand years, three thousand years, a thousand years ago, and there wouldn’t be much change.
But starting a few hundred years ago, the transformation in thought was reflected in reality, with civilization rapidly ascending until the recent modern era, by which time the situation had completely reversed.
From a historical perspective, this was virtually the blink of an eye.
If it weren’t for the sudden catastrophic event, this world might have been on the brink of the next “technology explosion” due to the emergence of the “Extraordinary.”
By then, only a few on her side would have been able to protect themselves…
.
.
And another
.

chapters.title: Chapter 894 - 894 596 Infinitely Close to Primordial Fire
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 894: Chapter 596 Infinitely Close to “Primordial Fire. Chapter 894: Chapter 596 Infinitely Close to “Primordial Fire. “You didn’t say anything, but I haven’t felt particularly anything,”
Listening to Shana’s words, Colin thought for a moment. Being in it, he indeed didn’t feel much, especially knowing about the peculiar entity that “Bonfire Company” was.
However, talking about these things, Colin looked into the current status of “World Code-13,” then his expression involuntarily twisted.
That place, after Shana left, had been taken on a very strange developmental path by the “sub-branch.”
Most churches began to participate in crafting disposable extraordinary items, which were then sold through the “sub-branch.”
From what he could see, they weren’t sold here only, some went to other places too…
“Why do I feel like this guy is now like an arms dealer?” Colin raised an eyebrow, discovering that over there it had almost turned into a super-sized “factory.”
A factory specifically for producing disposable extraordinary items.
This situation made Colin feel a mix of amusement and dismay, but, these weren’t particularly important things, just casual chat and he didn’t plan to intervene for the time being.
A few days later, Colin suddenly felt something special and then stopped wandering aimlessly.
Instead, he had Shana take him towards a certain place.
Before long, in an open area, Colin saw a total of thirty employees.
It was only when he approached them that Colin could feel that here, at last, he could attempt to actively contact the outside world…
But he wasn’t in a hurry to act.
When the group of employees saw Shana leading Colin to the scene, they were stunned for a moment. In the several major operations previously, they had generally seen the flames on Brother Shunzi’s body.
So, the glowing could be ruled out.
In that case…
“Brother Shunzi?” Someone uncertainly called out to the “child.”
“Mm.” Colin nodded, causing everyone to widen their eyes.
Was Brother Shunzi actually just about a ten-year-old child?
No, that’s not right…
“Why have you turned into this?” someone curiously asked.
“My appearance isn’t important, what’s important is what I plan to do soon…” Colin pursed his lips, and hearing this, everyone’s expressions turned serious.
One employee voiced everyone’s thoughts: “Alright, do we have a mission? Just command us, Brother Shunzi!”
Before coming here, they had prepared themselves to carry out an event with no return.
…Although I appreciate your readiness to face death, it seems like the things you could do are almost done… Colin couldn’t help but mutter to himself internally.
“Stable signal,” that was the greatest value of the employees’ presence.
However, Colin wasn’t so blunt to say it but instead said: “When the time is right, I’ll start doing some things. It will be very dangerous here, and you must preserve your lives at all costs.
